name: Dome Keeper
detailed_description: Check out a friend's mining survivor game! About the Game Defend your dome from wave after wave of monsters in this innovative roguelike survival miner, Dome Keeper. Use the time between each attack to dig beneath the surface in search of valuable resources and artifacts – use them carefully to choose powerful upgrades and bonuses. Set on beautifully crafted pixel art alien planets, Dome Keeper offers a captivating atmosphere, music tracks fusing melodic and synthetic creations together with a sense of wonder meeting the jet age that makes you want to come back for more. Drill tunnels beneath your dome in search of precious materials or to uncover powerful hidden artifacts. Watch the time, you need to get back to the dome and be ready when the next wave of attack comes. How deep will you get this time? How much can you carry back? Take control of your defenses to fend off the alien attacks. Air and ground, slow and fast; the attackers must be prioritized and dealt with before they tear your dome apart. Utilize your mineral harvest to unlock powerful upgrades: augment your weapons, enhance the impact of your drill, boost your jetpack’s max speed, and many other upgrade paths -- each of which gives you and your dome the best odds for survival!

_childDocuments_.review: Are you old? Did you play a stupid flash game called Motherload in the early 2000s, where you had a crappy mining ship, dug your way down to hell, and fought the devil at the end?What if you could play a version of that game that was actually good? One with audio that's not awful, with actual artistic intention, and with real game mechanics instead of... whatever that old stuff was?Now you can. It's called Dome Keeper. It's Motherload, but actually good. And yes, you can also just go play Motherload, the internet still has it lying around. But remember: Dome Keeper costs money while Motherload is free... and both games are worth exactly what you paid for them.

_childDocuments_.review: As of 12/8/22 with 207 hours played, I have mixed feelings about this game. On one hand, it started out as a lot of fun and I've clearly spent a ton of time playing it. On the other hand, it's changing rapidly, there's no in-game explanation of changes, and I'm not sure why, but ever since the last big update, I find myself on the wrong end of RNG over and over and over again.The relic mode is a fun introduction to the game, but you rapidly find yourself realizing that if you're ever going to have fun with all of these other abilities you could theoretically get or gadgets you could max out, you need to play on a bigger stage, so the map size gets bigger and the difficulty gets harder and it didn't take long before I was able to beat a huge map on most difficult setting, and I STILL didn't feel like I was really getting to enjoy ALL of the abilities. So I looked to prestige mode for my time when I wanted to chill and dig some holes.Some of these runs in prestige have been a great time, and others have just become an annoying slog. In some runs, the waves of monsters are inexplicably more difficult than in other runs (enemies are more numerous right from the first wave, and they appear on opposite ends at the same time), or the rocks are thicker and I can't find iron, then I finally do and crack open a bunch of duds, frequently getting just 1 iron. Also, does every run still yield a hidden room with a seed? I can't tell if it's just that on some runs I'm not finding it and am instead finding the new rooms, or if they're all always in there and it's just a big dig site. Or are they switched up depending on the planets? If so, it would be nice if there was something other than the aesthetic to differentiate these planets, like a planet name somewhere on the screen or some kind of indication so that the people who aren't pulling up faqs or steam guides can also be clued in. I don't think it's hand-holding to provide some of this basic info somewhere.In terms of gameplay, it seems like whenever there's a gadget with 3 options (thinking shield or repellent), there's always one path that's clearly better than the other 2 paths. Why not just have that path instead of offering wayward options that yield poorer results if you aren't going to make those other options any better?There's a new alternative to the engineer that I haven't gotten myself to be willing to try out yet because I've invested so much time into the engineer.There are a lot of random "game modes" and options that are clearly intended to inject more life and staying power into this game. It's just a shame there isn't a campaign mode with missions or "planets" so the developers could offer the player passive exposure to different modes and relics and things while they work through the campaign. Instead we find ourselves becoming entrenched in specific ways of doing things and we have zero incentive to try out these modes that make the game more difficult and yet don't offer any reward.I also think the game could use some streamlined mechanics to inspire different upgrade pathways. For example, what if the game rewarded the player for following through one upgrade path without altering it by giving cheaper upgrades in that path unless the player deviates? For example, a player could get the basic lvl 1 upgrades they always get, but then they can decide to just focus on their laser until it's maxed out, or they want to max out speed so they can move around super fast, and this is benefited by slightly cheaper upgrades or even by offering to allow water to take the place of 2 irons each or some such thing whenever a player remains in a focused upgrade pathway.The WORST THING in this game... bar none... is the Teleporter gadget. It breaks the game. I avoid it and turn it into cobalt now because the game is no fun with this damn thing. The game is all about zipping around a cave, digging, and dragging stuff around. That's where most of the fun is found. Why build a gadget that wholesale destroys these gameplay elements and allows the players to completely ignore what are considered ESSENTIAL speed and carry upgrades with any gameplay style that doesn't involve the teleporter? If I was the game developer, I would highlight all the code that has to do with this damn gadget and press delete. Easy choice.A few closing random thoughts:1) It's too bad there's no gadget or minor ability that tells you "you need to head back this instant or you're going to be too late" or any other way besides the repellent to get more time in the dig phase (if there is another, I don't know about it. Is that my fault?).2) There are multiple abilities that nobody gets (inventory display and wave indicator). This was recently changed to where they now cost water instead of iron. Still can't afford to get them, even when I have a water abundance, unless I'm playing in relic mode. Why not quit ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around with these and just remove them as pay abilities and grant them to the character at the start? We're never going to spend our precious resources on these so you as may as well allow us to have them since you bothered to develop them. They would be NICE to have. They're just not worth the resources.3) I don't think there's a single gadget that doesn't need either one expensive (for early game) upgrade or several inexpensive upgrades before it's ANY good at all. This is really annoying for prestige mode. I'd rather something take up both gadget spots in my dome than pick something that needs those precious early resources in order to get going. Incidentally, the only option for most gadgets in prestige mode is to turn them into cobalt and gobble them up.All in all I liked the game a lot, and would have shouted nothing but praise if you caught me in my first 100 hours. As it stands, I'm a little irritated with the game lol since it feels like it's actually gotten worse rather than better since I started playing it. Still going to give it a recommend as it's a great casual game for at least a while. For me right now though, speaking as a laser player... I'm thinking I need to find another game to play when I'm looking to chill. I'll check back after a few months or a year or so and see if it's improved.

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant gameplay loop makes  a perfect roguelike—for the right kind of player.  Don't be fooled into expecting a relaxing mining experience out of this job; every underground excursion is conducted with one eye on your watch as you hastily carve out and collect your findings before returning to the surface chamber just in time to fight off a fresh wave of shadowy beasts intent on ousting you from your invasive venture.  As the machinery within your dome eagerly grinds up the backbreaking resources you've hauled in, you slump in front of the nearby console for a quick rest and decide whether to invest your iron in improved defensive lasers or a superior drill before getting back on the clock and back in the dirt.  At least down there you're safe.'s beating heart lives in the tension between mining and defense.  You are continuously being drawn back and forth across these roles—rhythmically, predictably, like a pendulum—with your seat at the upgrade/battle terminal serving as a neatly connective transition point between the two sides of the game as one fuels the other.  Everything you do has a touch of tactility and weight and nuance, from the drag of the ore slowing down your jetpack to the need to visit a recharge station for your pulse scanner to the design choice of having wandering orbs pull your misbegotten goods up the lift rather than just letting them float up some boring beam.The soft pixel art is muted and moody, and the fanfares and periodic ambient melodies of the soundtrack are wistful and warm; alien but inviting.  The more time you spend in the tunnels and caverns, the more they begin to feel like home.  Maybe you'll move in—after you've finished your conquest, of course.

_childDocuments_.review: First off: Get this in a sale. imho, this game is not worth the full price for what it is right now. Most negative reviews you see are because of the price since that is to high for what is on offer. Disregarding it's price, for what this game tries to be though, it is a fun gameThe game's presentation is great with nice moody backgrounds, good looking effects, atmospheric music and satisfying sound effects. Everything is crisp and snappy. Controls are good/decent and the game-play is nice for a quick game-session. The upgrading is also satisfying and there are a few nice bonus things to find like a stun laser, a creature that digs for you etc.However; the game-play is also somewhat limited and the loop gets samey. You will quite quickly feel like you experienced everything and new stuff you find/unlock after that is nothing wild or crazy. During a single round the different bonus equipment you can find are quite limited which means there is not much variety during play. Add to that the limited enemy variety and after a few minutes playing you will feel like you are  not really progressing anymore. This would hardly matter for a <10 dollar game that you play in a quick burst between something else, but not for it's full price atm.Get it on sale and you will enjoy it. Get it for full price and feel like maybe you could have gotten some other game for the same price with more depth.Alternatives are games like Vampire Survivors or Dig-N-Rig (not on Steam)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, but for being a roguelike there is very little variation between runs. There just isn't enough variety in the number of gadgets, equipment, characters, dome types, etc. And the mining itself, which makes up more than half the game, is very simplistic with only 3 resource types, very few underground anomalies/powerups. And there is a very obvious tier list in every choice. Automated Dome Defenses are OP, the teleporter is easily the best gadget in the game, the resource lift is extremely powerful early on and never really stops being useful. But drillbert stops being useful in the lower levels of the mine, bombs are extremely situational, the resource converter and water condenser are too slow to be overly useful most of the time, the tree dome and artificer characters suck...This makes the game suffer in 1 major way: replayability. Which is a major problem for a roguelike.There just isn't enough content to make it interesting between runs, even when challenging yourself with the sub-optimal gear. Once you've played 5 or 6 relic hunts, that's it. You've played all the content from the whole game. There's nothing more for you here besides increased the difficulty and playing endless mode to try for a high score.Plain and simple, if the game had more gadgets for each slot that could actually compare in utility, more characters that are actually viable, more weapon and dome types, then this game would be fantastic. One of the main draws for a roguelike is trying out all the different variations of builds and playing multiple runs, each one playing out differently from the last. But with the current game state you only have a dozen or so different combinations of gadgets, and the pool is small enough that you can really pick and choose what you want every time, which just defeats the purpose...tl;dr: Game is fun but lacks replayability which means it sucks as a roguelike.

_childDocuments_.review: 42 hours to unlock all achievements. The enemies are diverse and challenging, and the game provides the player with multiple tools depending on your play style. I enjoyed figuring out the best way to get a high score in prestige - in my last run I almost got 2.000. High scores seem to be so high that they are probably hacked (40.000+). _childDocuments_.review: It's fun... for about one to two runs. And even then it's not that great. The main problem is that the core loop is simply not that interesting. The game tries its hardest to squeeze the absolute maximum fun out of it, but there's only so much water you can squeeze out of a rock. Digging seems like it should be fun, but the maps are rather empty, especially the larger ones. Mostly just rock. Yes, there is ore, upgrades and other fun stuff to find, but it's entirely possible to go an entire cycle without finding anything at all. And even if you do find something, it's probably going to be a pittance anyway, and you'll have to carry it all back (or not, if you have certain upgrades). I don't know; I like mining in games - a lot, in fact - but here it felt frustrating rather than fun.And the combat isn't much better. The default laser dome can do only one thing: rotate the laser and shoot. You can buy an active skill, which will either damage incoming melee enemies or reflect projectiles - but they can't really be relied upon, they're more like "once-a-wave little helper". The enemies seem like they offer some variety - there's quite a few types - but I don't know, it all just boils down to "keep firing until they pop". No matter if it's a small rhino-type dude, a floating mass of... something, or a hulking, slow-moving monstrosity. Later on I found one enemy that actually felt different - some kind of teleporting wraith - but for the most part combat felt like a slog.So why did I play for 5 hours? Like I said, the early runs are fun, when you're still learning what is possible. After every successful run you get to unlock a new loadout - a new character (there's only one so far), a new type of dome (again, only one), a new game mode (ditto), different gadgets (there's more actually!). And I tried them out, but they don't really change all that much, and they don't solve the main issue - that the gameplay loop simply isn't that engaging. The sword dome is pretty cool at least, even if it feels unwieldy.Also, the game has this... polish. It looks fantastic, there's a lot of little things that make the world feel alive - critters, plants growing, cool little hidden powerups such as a speed boost or a helper that carries your loot back to your base. And the soundscape, wow. It's really good - including the music. This feeling of being stranded on a mysterious world with only the walls of your dome protecting you from unknown danger is delicious, even if it fades away after a while.AAA games have been sacrificing their depth and playability in favour of visual polish for a very long time, and now they're too expensive to make and boring to play at the same time. It's troubling to see the same trend happening in the indie world, too - and we're falling for it all over again. Or maybe I'm just reading too much into it and this is just a game that I personally didn't enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Dome Keeper has become one of my absolute favourite games, and it's easy to see why. It's just a super fun, addictive game that scratches that SteamWorld Dig itch I've been having. The core gameplay loop of mining for resources, upgrading your dome's defences, and fighting off waves of alien attackers is seriously satisfying, and the tension between exploring deeper caverns and getting back to defend your base is always keeping you on your toes.I'm really digging the "A Keeper's Duty" beta right now, especially the new guild assignments. It would be awesome if the devs added custom assignments in the future.One of the things I love most about this game is the devs' dedication. There has been a constant stream of free updates with new features, game modes, and cosmetics, which keeps the game feeling fresh. And the mod support is a huge bonus, letting the community create their own cool stuff.  Did I mention the game has a killer soundtrack and gorgeous pixel art to boot? It's the full package.Overall, Dome Keeper is a must-play for anyone who enjoys resource management, tower defence, or just good old fashioned digging games. It's addictive, rewarding, and always evolving, making it a real gem in my gaming library.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute gem of a game that has devs who are committed to listening to community feedback and actively improving the game post-launch. I saw that there was a new massive update and thought, "Wow! That looks awesome... but why isn't it showing up in the store's DLC page?" Well that's because this massive boon to the game's replayability is absolutely FREE. I'm sure there will be plenty of other reviews that cover the gameplay side of things, I just wanted to gush at how much I've seen this game improve since launch. In an era where games are being talked about more as products, Dome Keeper sticks out as a passion project from days gone by.I'd recommend this game to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: It's an incredibly satisfying game and a ton of fun to figure out! The art and sound design are really stunning. It reminds me of the simple fun of Flash games but juiced up with really high production values and a pretty interesting strategic layer.A note on replayability: Even though it has a roguelike structure, it plays more like a strategy game single-player campaign. You'll have a lot of fun figuring out how to rise to each challenge level, how to play with the different combinations of gadgets, how to macro and micro better. Eventually you'll hit a point where you feel like you "beat" the game and there's not too much more interest in it. (There is a highscore mode, but to me it just feels like a grind, because runs are ultimately pretty similar - there's not really that combinatorial-explosion infinite depth you see in many roguelikes.)
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I don't agree with all the reviews saying "you've seen all there is within a couple of hours". You don't even unlock most of the gadget upgrade trees in the first couple of hours let alone discover all the synergies between the relics. You definitely don't get to see all the monsters in one run since they mix and match the varietyBut there's still tons the devs could, and do plan to, add to the game to improve variety. Sometimes RNG with the relics can screw you over hard and not give you stuff that works together at all but most relics have functions that help you out greatly once they're upgraded. I'm also looking forward to more characters being added because while the single drill character is fun, the planned one sounds even better. I really hope they support the game for a good while cause there's a really good framework for a lot of variety in upgrades, monsters, characters and cosmeticsBut the game is still fun enough and addictive in that you always want to try one more round and push your limits. I found my limit soon enough but I'm hoping I can unlock more upgrades to win some more rounds

_childDocuments_.review: This game was on my wishlist for a long time and with the free major update in Juli 2024 I finally bought it.And oh boy was it worth it.The game is very polished and coherent in its style and mechanics.It is overall very well executed.It gives players a lot of small micro decision to make, like - do I drill left, or right, or down, What pattern is efficient, what is most fun?- when do I return to the dome, do I risk coming back late by drilling too long or carrying too much stuff slowing me down? Greed will be your downfall at least once!- which monster do I need to target first to minimize damage to my precious dome?This gives me as the player power and responsibility and feels rewarding because of it.I never had the feeling the game is unfair, because in the end all my tiny decisions led to the outcome I got.Every small action is satisfying, like- drilling has a nice rythm and also a nice crunchy sound when destroying a block. You will find yourself wanting to destroy every single block, just because you can.- carrying of resources makes wind chime sounds - the plopping sound of monsters when they die in your laser (or sword, or whatever dome you prefer)At first, I was a bit disappointed that there was no story mode and I could not learn more about the universe, but the guild challenges made up for it. I did all of them and they are not too hard in retrospect when using the right tools, but they feel hard every time. Again super rewarding when you've beaten them.The developers are true Indies and are very active and responsive to everything the players have to say.A wonderful gem of a game made by wonderful people. You should try and buy. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Dome Keeper is a Survival Base building Rouge-like game where you have to defend your dome against waves of alien creatures. In between these waves of attacks you have to dig under your dome to find 3 basic resources to upgrade your dome and your weapons to fend of the creatures.Pros- Very easy to get into.- Beautiful pixel art & music- Multiple difficulties and map sizesCons- Could use a very basic tutorial for people who may be new to games like these.- Nothing else as such for me personally.I am very happy with the game. Having said that the game is going to get updates so might make more sense to wait a bit and get it when there is more content. Currently there are 2 main modes in the game. Also for a game like this a little sale would help a bit as well. I get good regional pricing so its fine for me but I can see where the other reviewers are coming from.Overall this is one of the best Indie games I have played and will check it out more when there are a few more updates.Gameplay Example :

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game that's perfect for those moments when you just want to unwind and lose yourself in some fun, Dome Keeper is exactly what you need on your Steam Deck. This game is an absolute must-have, offering an engaging and addictive experience that’s perfect for wasting time in the best way possible.What makes Dome Keeper stand out is its incredibly engaging gameplay loop. It brilliantly combines elements of exploration, resource management, and strategy. As you dig deeper into the game's world, uncovering hidden treasures and valuable resources, you can't help but feel a sense of excitement and discovery. The constant need to adapt your strategy keeps things fresh and challenging, ensuring that you never get bored.The sound design in Dome Keeper is top-notch. The atmospheric soundtrack and satisfying sound effects of mining and collecting resources really pull you into the game. The audio cues are not just great to listen to; they also help you stay aware of what’s happening in the game, adding another layer to the experience.The mechanics of Dome Keeper are both fun and intuitive. The controls are smooth and responsive on the Steam Deck, making it easy to dive right in. There are plenty of tools and upgrades to experiment with, allowing you to tailor your playstyle and keep things interesting. Mining in Dome Keeper is more than just digging tunnels. Thanks to the procedural generation of the game world, each playthrough offers new surprises and challenges. This keeps the game feeling fresh, as you never know what you’ll find next. The excitement of discovering rare resources or hidden chambers adds a thrilling sense of anticipation to every session.The Steam Deck is the perfect platform for Dome Keeper. The game runs smoothly and looks fantastic on the device's screen. The controls feel natural, making it easy to play whether you’re on the go or lounging at home. Whether you have a few minutes to spare or want to dive into a longer session, Dome Keeper fits perfectly into your gaming routine.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! Of course it goes more in-depth than that, but overall, I cannot think of any particular thing that I am really unhappy about. _childDocuments_.review: The Good: Music, sound and art design are all excellent. The mechanics play well and digging just feels good.The Bad: A lack of variance and content -- this is a run-based game that can go stale quickly. It makes no effort to explain the controls, UI or mechanics.Fun game but this really feels like an Early Access game released as a full title. The core loop is rewarding but repetitive. With no hazards or meaningful variance down in the mines it's just mindless searching until you find more ore, dig dig dig and haul. The combat above is fast and engaging, I enjoy the Sword Dome. The game keeps you busy and switching between tasks near constantly.I enjoy a lot of roguelikes. I find that it is rare that good mechanics alone can cover for a lack of variance and content in a run-based game. Dome Keeper unfortunately goes stale quickly. Loadout options and the range of Gadgets you can find in your run are limited. There's only one Engineer currently with the other billed as "Coming soon!" Very Early Access, yes. Overall, I think this game is half-cooked and needs more time in development before it's ready to be released as a finished product.

_childDocuments_.review: Dome Keeper is a real gem of a game! Imagine Minecraft and Starship Troopers having a super addictive baby. You dig, you extract resources, and you prepare to fight waves of aliens who want to turn your dome into a colander. Each game is a tasty cocktail of strategy and survival, with just enough stress to make you forget you had to take out the trash. Basically, Dome Keeper is the perfect mix between a mining game and an alien attack simulator. A must-have for any roguelike fan who enjoys digging holes and kicking alien ass!
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, but shockingly barebones. Great art, but it's stretched over extremely thin gameplay. The fighting gets very repetitive and it doesn't feel that engaging to get into, I routinely found myself rolling my eyes when the little timer went off and I needed to return to the surface, but then when I imagined what the gameplay would be like if I didn't have to, I realized how hollow the 'mining' aspect is. Two sub-par halves don't suddenly make a particularly enjoyable whole.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Dig Dug was a roguelike, right? I mean, I guess every arcade game was kind of a roguelike by the loose definition we now use, but that’s not important. What is important is that Dome Keeper is like Dig Dug except instead of the enemies being cute dragons and weird diver dudes underground, they’re horrible shadowy blob monsters that try to assault your dome-y home.Abbreviated Review: The premise of Dome Keeper is simple, you come blazing down from space in your vaguely spherical home and slam onto one of those aforementioned blob creatures just minding its own business on the surface of an alien world. That’s essentially all of the narrative there is to glean from the entirety of the game. Yet, there’s plenty to discover and explore within the depths.The gameplay is split between two very distinct facets, digging underground and maintaining the dome on the surface. The surface doesn’t have a lot of interaction outside of the times when it’s under attack, but it’s the part you do everything else to maintain. When it is attacked, your initial counteraction is to take control of the massive laser that tracks along the outside of your dome and use it to blast those alien creatures. After each wave, you’re treated to a pleasant reprieve where you can repair any damage and head back down to dive into the heart of the gameplay underground.Despite the game-ending importance of maintaining the integrity of your dome, the majority of the gameplay involves you grinding through rocks underground. It’s as simple as pointing your pixelated engineer in a direction and letting them bounce their drill off of the surface until it breaks. The various densities of the blocks determine how long it takes for you to make it through, similar to Minecraft, so it’s advantageous to try and pick a route that affords you the most progress before the next wave approaches.The goal of all of this digging is to find veins of resources, crack them out of the rocks, and haul them back up to the processor in your dome. You can attach as much iron, water, and cobalt to your character as you can find, but you’ll limit your movement speed until you can’t move at all, so there’s plenty of discretion in this process. Part of the strategy is balancing your load with the time remaining before the next wave – as those aliens will attack regardless of your presence. The resources you obtain can be used for several types of upgrades including those that make it possible to drill faster, move faster, and carry loads more efficiently. However, it is equally important that you upgrade your dome and its defenses to survive each wave.During your mining expeditions, you’ll also come across special glowing blocks that, once returned to your base, will reveal a selection of special abilities or tools to aid you in your adventure. These can be as simple as a bomb you can place on a surface to carve out a huge area instantaneously or the incredibly useful cargo elevator that slowly hauls resources back to the surface for you. They also join the upgrade page with separate trees used to make them more effective and efficient. This cycle of digging, defending, and upgrading goes on for as long as it takes to find the main alien relic buried deep underground.The initial (and primary) game mode is all about you finding that relic and dragging it back up to the surface like all the rest of the goodies you’ve obtained. Once you do that, it’s essentially the end of the run after a scary final assault. However, that’s not the only game mode. As you complete these relic runs, you’ll unlock numerous additional gameplay features and functions. Things like a crazy harpoon sword and deflecting shield replacement for your laser and a “repellent” alternative to the secondary energy shield for your dome are interesting ways to add variety to the experience. You’ll also unlock bigger maps with much more digging and resource gathering and variations on the existing gadgets you have obtained.The biggest divergence from the initial gameplay you’ll unlock is that “Prestige” mode, which is basically a high-score game mode. Here, instead of looking for a relic, your goal is to get as many resources as possible and send them back to space on a rocket for ‘prestige’ point bonuses. Then it’s all about surviving waves and ultimately putting yourself on a rocket and getting the hell out of there. Whether you succeed there or die horribly before ever getting close, whatever points you obtain will put you on the leaderboard to be judged along with the rest. It’s a stand-in for an “end game” experience since there’s not necessarily a way to “win” the game. It’s quite easy to find the relic on the normal difficulty and the small map, but you can very easily ramp that up with bigger maps and two more notches of difficulty.I was a little concerned with the lack of a campaign when I first started the game. Usually, when left to my own devices, I don’t feel like I’m good at crafting my own best experience. I’ll either make it too easy or too difficult and then it’s my fault for not making the game fun for me. Dome Keeper made the lowest difficulty “normal,” which of course is just a clever way of disguising “easy”, but it felt pretty satisfying to play from the start. The map sizes can change the difficulty slightly but are more about letting you better explore the upgrade tree and determining how long you want to play a round. I’m not sure if the difficulties have any bearing on what is unlocked each time, but every completed Relic mode has resulted in an unlocked item each time – which is rewarding.Dome Keeper is much closer to the classic roguelike design than modern roguelites. Progression is entirely in the form of modifiers to a fresh run rather than slowly buffing yourself up to beat the game. You’ll always start falling from the sky and face the same basic challenges you had in your first attempt – similar to games like Spelunky. Yet, the variety provided by the different starting options and modifiers can make each run feel distinct and the Prestige mode is always there to tempt you with leaderboard legacy. While I do think it would have been nice to have some kind of initial campaign or some narrative to tie all of this together, what is available is fun and approachable for almost anyone – and it leaves plenty of room for additional content in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: The idea is simple. You have a dome, attacked by aliens in waves. You have a drill. You have the ground beneath the dome that you can extract resources from. Your goal is to do so, bring the resources back up in time to upgrade the base before the next wave of aliens attacks, and push tme back. Rinse, repeat, defeat the boss.The visuals and physics of the game are nice enough, and the core loop is surprisingly engaging. I had a lot of simple fun with it.The only thing I found odd were the unlocks. They're not presented as upgrades — more like sidegrades — but I ended up never using them anyway because they are... finicky. The new options you get are always much harder to control. I wouldn't be surprised to learn that a player who masters them becomes way more powerful, but I failed to do so.Still, this game is unassuming fun even if you only use the basic options. A good game if you simply want to chill.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: The most important element of a game is the primary gameplay loop, which is what you do most often in a game. If a game has a good gameplay loop, much can be forgiven. If a game doesn't, it could be the most beautiful game ever and still feel lackluster. Dome Keeper's gameplay loop is simple, yet addicting and frankly genius. First, you mine materials and special stuff I won't spoil underground, but be careful, you are on a time limit. When monsters attack you have to quickly rush back to the surface and defend your base, using the materials you mined to help defend against the increasingly dangerous enemy attacks.The first thing that impressed me about the gameplay loop is the combination of turret base defense and mining. Both have been done, but I am unaware of a combo like this existing before, and how it was missed for so long is sort of surprising given how well they work together. The problem with pure mining games is there is little tension, and trips back to the surface are only for banking your minerals, they are really just there to pad gameplay time. The problem with turret defense games is there is only tension. Fighting waves of enemies until you die to get the highscore is great for an arcade, but not great if you want to make a game that people want to play for hours at a time.Combining the two, you get a very pertinent reason to travel to the surface (you are going to die if you don't defend) and a great way to get upgrades, through mining. In every action there is a tradeoff, from perfectly timing the length of your mining underground vs being ready to defend before the attacks start, or in the attack vs defense vs mining vs speed upgrades, long term plans vs short term need. Tradeoffs are so important to allowing creativity in a game, and this game is chock full of them.The only downside to this game is there isn't enough of it! I want more upgrades and secrets. Luckily there are already alternate game characters and upgrades that aren't released yet, and this type of game makes it comparatively simple to add extra stuff.Even given that caveat, I haven't been this into a roguelike since . If this game could add a fraction of the extra content/random stuff that game has, I'd be very happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't review games as i believe every person experiences something unique and different with each game, however that being said i can't really recommend this game....First lets talk about the price, for a game under 20 but above 10 i feel like you really aren't getting enough 'Bang for your buck"I bought this for $17.99 and after playing for awhile and advancing to the secondary dome it feels lackluster for the price.Don't get me wrong the atmosphere, the art, the music and mechanics are 10/10 ! it plays smooth and looks and sounds beautiful but after you get in it , you find that beyond the glits and glammer leaves a bittersweet experience lacking a satisfactory play though. it feels like there could have been some story element added in with some text boxes or more lore for the situation while mining, discovering more than just resources. Instead you get this feeling parallel to waiting in an elevator to reach you floor, enjoying the trip and the music, but all to eager to get the experience over with. it feels like this should almost be a mobile game or an idler rather than a rogue like.I do feel this game has potential and can be a great game, the game play and survival aspect doesn't have to change, just provide a reason to survive and thrive for more than just to fire a laser or swing a sword. maybe multiplayer? maybe lore? maybe a wider range of mechanics? whatever it may be , its so close to gaining that missing piece of the puzzle. until such time i can't recommend for the price. maybe for $10 but not for $18. i'll keep playing and edit this if it ever changes my opinion, hope this helped the developer or another interested game lover.Edit: Fixed some spelling errors , sorry if it bothered anyone!
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of care was put into development of this game over the years and it shows.From the simple color changes each run, the small critters found within the cave systems, the ever expanding arsenal of weapons and gadgets and the downright enchanting sound design, Dome Keeper has grown to be a great game to pass the time while still keeping me engaged and challenged at every turn.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: It is a shockingly fun game. I'll admit the price is a bit steep when you compare it to other indie titles in terms of content and that is my only real complaint. I personally would consider $10 to be more fair.  Other than that, its a blast. It is a wave defense game with really good artwork, surprisingly good sound and music, with addicting mineral fetching and upgrade managing. Don't let the difficulties scare you either if you get it. Normal is incredibly easy and is pretty relaxing, hard is pretty much medium, and brutal is 'hard' with another setting pass that which I haven't tried yet. I am bringing this up because brutal sounds intimidating, but it really doesn't take long to get the hang of - I am usually not great a games like this but even I didn't find it OVER the top hard on that setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Fun your first run or two. Then it gets super repetitive. There's not enough content and what's there isn't even that addicting. The game has some interesting concepts and ideas but it's just way too lacking and slow paced. Runs should be longer with more upgrades to profit on that engine building mechanics but instead the game ends when you're starting to have fun. Doing a new run all over "so soon" makes it extremely tedious and not worth your time in my opinion.6.5/10 - Not recommended in its current state (version 2.3).
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent rogue-lite miner. You mine for resources, balance upgrades between more efficient resource gathering and being able to defend the base every so often. Presentation is nice and gameplay loop is pretty self explanatory. I did find the game becoming pretty repetitive after 4 hrs or so, so I am just getting a few more achievements before calling it quits. I do not regret buying it, but for a game of this genre it has fairly small amount of content. The runs do feel sorta samey and unlocking new stuff is very few and far between, this could have been done better imho.  Still, overall a fairly good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Dome Keeper is a mining game meshed with elements of old classics like Paratrooper, Load Runner and Brick Breaker. You play the keeper of a dome on a hostile planet. The game play is split into defending your dome against waves of aliens, and mining for resources underneath your hatch. Visually both activities are pixel perfect, the feedback on the screen is great. The controls with a keyboard are simple and sufficient. It's easy to get into a rhythm playing Dome Keeper, keeping the pace, and suddenly forget you've been playing for hours.When you begin under a new dome, the first steps are to upgrade your dashboard, mining iron, water and cobalt. A good game is a game where mining is done quickly avoiding harder rocks to mine. The mining game is simple, with these 3 primary resources, you'll need to find gadgets and relics in one of two gaming modes. The dome offers upgrades for the various tools and defenses used.Relic hunting is the first game mode, where a game ends when you bring back the unique relic hidden on the map. Prestige is the second mode, which involves lasting as long as possible against the waves of aliens attacking your dome. Defending in Dome Keeper is done with various weapons against a good variety of alien behaviors. Aliens attacking your shelter change depending on the map randomly selected when you start a game.Currently, you have the choice between defending with a laser dome or a dome equipped with a sliding shield/sword combination. Both configurations are well balanced against the waves of baddies. I've never made it past wave 52 on relic hunt with the Sword dome. Both profiles have a good set of upgrade choices which you'll want to try on alternate games. There are very little flaws with the game mechanics, everything is easy to figure out on your own, which is great.This is a fun game to play! There may be improvements to be made on the map generation, some of the sprites could use better defined models, but overall this game is very easy to recommend full price or otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: -  There is some great sound design in this game. Everything you do from mining to picking up resources all feels very good.-  The tech trees are varied and, at least at first, most of them seem useful. Some of the quality of life upgrades seem necessary to play optimally. I’m also happy that you unlock the HUD later so you don’t have to spend resources on them. Which is a little strange but I guess it prevented me from being overwhelmed at the start. There are many different angles to upgrade: Do I go for fire power, defence, moveability, resource gathering etc. It’s not clear what the best choice is. And every tool you find gives you an extra tech tree to think about.-  The pixel art is pleasant to look at together with the visceral animations of the enemies, like one that charges up a scorpion tail for heavy damage. There is also some cool VFX for special moments that breaks the pixel art style.-  I only played on brutal difficulty which says its the recommended. I had some close calls there.-  There is a nice game of enemy prioritisation. Some hit harder than others and there are upgrades that make you reconsider your targets. If you have a shield that reflects damage back to melee enemies you will focus the ranged and vice versa if you have the pole that shoots down projectiles. They also have a wide variety of behaviours that require different strategies. Like one that flies to you from the sky but gives a warning before it happens.-  It’s tempting to mine a little longer but that might make you lose more health or even die because you get back to your turret too late. Most of my deaths were because I got greedy.-  The physics applied on the resources you find allows you to abuse it (pull forward with momentum) or be negatively impacted by it(it drops in a hole). The player character you unlock later gives even more ways to manipulate resources.-  When you succeed in a run there is a cool cutscene and a nice build up with finding the relic.-  The other player character, Assessor, is interesting to play. Very different from the straightforward starting character. Manipulating the orbs to bounce efficiently and “guiding” resources back to the dome are interesting skills to learn.-  With the new update there is a nice little environment to test the controls and set your game before you start. Although I had to search for a little while for the start button and it wasn’t immediately clear I could move the character with keyboard and mouse. Maybe the character should fly in. Overall it's a positive though.-  Moving the laser is a bit iffy. I found it best with the mouse. But at the start I kept accidentally moving it too with A and D. With the controller I found it awkward to move it with the d-pad or analogue stick. But that might be a preference thing.-  It’s not entirely clear how gadgets work at the start like the prospect meter. I guess its part of the game to figure it out.-  Especially at the start I often accidentally mine a block because I’m moving in that general direction. This slows me down a bit. Not sure how to fix this but it causes some annoyance.-  At the start it was not clear how the overcharge for the shield works.When I looked it up you had to interact with the shield within the dome before a battle starts. It doesn’t look interactable though. I read the dev was looking into fixing this though.It’s a great little game. It got me hooked for a while. If you like a little hectic rush for survival that doesn't take too long with lots of upgrades give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: After my first taste of victory on a brutal difficulty, which no doubt there will be more to come, I am ready to share my initial thoughts on Dome Keeper and will update this review as time goes by. Right now, it is a strong recommendation if you enjoy pixel art roguelike action game. The design of the game is good and engaging. You are constantly racing against time. The game is challenging but you will improve as you play and will beat it eventually. It is hard but fair. I don't feel frustrated at all when I lose (which is pretty often).It is a roguelike action mining game. You are a Dome Keeper, which is also a Relic Hunter. Your dome landed on an alien planet and accidentally squashed one of the indigenous creatures to death. That must have triggered a revenge attack. Your dome is going to undergo waves and waves of attack from various types of creatures. Should you manage to find the relic before the dome collapses, you win. Otherwise, you lose. Come to think on it, that game opening reminds of the movie Avatar.At brutal difficulty - the intended difficulty for this game - the game is pretty challenging.  There are two levels below for more relax game play and one level up (need unlock) for the veterans. You have to constantly prioritize how to allocate resources to the tech trees that improve yourself, your dome, and your gadgets found in the map. You have to constantly make decision on where to dig and how much to carry during the "peace" phase and which enemy type to take down first during the "war" phase.Gadgets are game changers and they can dramatically change your strategy and approach to the game. You may carry forward one gadget of your choice from your last game to the next one. You can also find new ones as you explore the map. Gadgets have their own tech trees for improvement. Depending on the gadgets you have got, you may approach the tech trees differently as well as how you would play the game. Some gadgets seem to be more valuable than others. But I found the combination of gadgets makes the game fun. Since gadgets are random though limited in number at launch, with the randomness in resource hidden placement, you may say no two games are the same.Progress in this game comes down to map size and difficulty, as well as various unlocks (including current and planned ones). A small map on brutal difficulty usually takes around 20-40 mins to end (win or lose). You may save your game at any time and continue from where you left off.Keep up the good work, dev!For those of you who are interested on videos, here is my Dome Keeper playlist.My Dome Keeper playlist is

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:I purchased for $18 wanting to support an indie title and hoping that more content would be added. Since then, lots of content has been added, and now it feels totally worth. I've been going back to it more and more. Some story elements, lore, secrets, have gone a long way. Can't wait for multiplayer.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Instantly feels like a classic arcade game. Bought Dome Keeper just 3 days ago and I'm already plotting more paths than a mole on espresso! It's like SteamWorld Dig had a lovechild with a tower defense game - you dig, loot, upgrade, defend, and then dig some more till you're clutching relics like they're your first paycheck. If you dig deep and love defending your turf, this game's your new addiction. Just beware: time will vanish faster than a pickaxe through dirt!
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game, somewhat limited in scope/progression, but plenty fun for people interested in "best practice" gameplay. Excellent roguelike basebuilder, well worth the money, and all time spent is a joy.After a certain point, the game stops presenting new unlockables, and it's up to the player to make the fun in the form of points on the leaderboard or to hone their skills. It's always fun, the controls are excellent, everything is predictable and skill based- even the RNG elements. You have to work with what you get, but nothing ever feels totally overpowered or unfairly bad. Some combinations are incredibly good, but the game is always quick to give you a choice to pursue said combinations. Legitimately, it's one of my favorite roguelike games. It's completely unique and I think everyone should try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: You remember that time when you played a flash game about mining back when you were a kid? If you kept going back to it back then for the mix of managing resources for upgrades, optimising your time underground, and finding resources and relics... well, you will be OBSESSED with this game.+++ PROS+++-Learn as you play tutorial, mechanics are shown as they present themselves.-Small help boost for when you lose, death is part of the learning process.-Progressive unlock of new mechanics and modes for every successful run, REGARDLESS OF DIFFICULTY (you don't miss out on anything if you want to play more casually)-Modes that pull you back in, removing aspects you don't like about the game, adding some more, or making it different altogether---CONS--- -Tutorial does not give you any hints about mysterious locations or relics, some things are only learned through trial and error or experimentation (you will waste some runs just to experiment with something you found just to understand or try to make it work).-Only two types of miners to play with, either a simple and boring one or a complex and interesting one. The simple miner will have you burning through resources just to make it functional (non-skill based), while the other barely needs any so you can invest it on something else (almost exclusively skill based).-Only two types of domes... simple laser dome that will burn though resources to make it usable... other .... (same situation as the miner)Overall, this game will be mysterious enough for you to keep coming back early on and be customizable enough for you to keep coming later on. Dome Keeper stands as an example of great game design!
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere alone sells this game. The pixel art, the animations, the phenomenal soundtrack, the sound effects in general, even the light story elements, all of it is so detailed yet understated and so full of character. This game has vibes.The gameplay itself alternates in waves between being a simple horde-defender type game, and a "Motherload"-like 2D mining game, with some soft roguelite elements like. It's a simple yet satisfying core gameplay loop, reminiscent of Kingdom but significantly harsher.The biggest weakness of this game is the lack of content. If you are looking primarily for a roguelike, this game might disappoint you a little, as there are only 10 different gadgets to find at the time of writing. But the game still has replayability in its different modes and characters, which is nice.All in all, if you like atmosphere and some difficulty, def pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun game, but not one you will get many hours of. I got about 7.5 hours of fun gameplay, and I beat every size of map on brutal difficult (the 2nd highest). I don't think trying the max difficulty would be much fun.After a few hours you kind of know what to do... dig patterns, best technologies, etc.The game could really do with more types of domes, more types of items, more variance in gameplay, but for now it's just a solid 5-7 hour game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Dome Keeper has one of the most satisfying game loops I've played in a long time. Dig for Resources -> Upgrade -> Defend Dome-> Repeat. It's clear a lot of effort and time went into make sure this was the case. I've played for nearly 30 hours and still plan to play a lot more. If you've read the negative reviews here on Steam, you'll notice two main criticisms over and over that I want to address. This is despite agreeing to an extent. Those being:- The game is too repetitive- There is a lack of contentI think the game is well worth your time and will certainly be well worth your money once more content is added. It is true that the game lacks content at release (but is far from the "unfinished game" comments you'll see around). Most notably, there isn't enough to find while digging and not enough variety in the Gadgets that you can dig up that alter how you might approach things. I believe this is why most people find the game too repetitive despite the gameplay loop itself being very satisfying. The lack of variety just makes it a bit samey sometimes, even with the 4 difficulty levels, 3 run modifiers, 2 types of domes, and 3 types starter Gadgets that currently exist. There's also a few different worlds you can spawn in, but their differences aren't immediately apparent (it's mostly enemy types).This doesn't mean there isn't depth in the game though, far from it! This become evident in the Score Attack mode named "Prestige" where the depth found in all 3 facets of the game are required to be learned to gain a very good score since it allows you to give up resources (and thus upgrades) for a better score. Even the simple act of digging has more depth than it first appears. During the main "Relic Hunt" mode, these aren't as necessary (Unless you play on "You Asked for it" difficulty), so I can understand why some people may not recognize the depth in the game currently. However, it is absolutely satisfying to get better at this game. It is well designed and has great presentation from the artwork and music. It also sounds like the main issues with the game will be ironed out over time as it seems more content is on the way (there is, at the very least, a new character coming). There's a lot of potential here and I can't wait to see what comes of it. I certainly recommend Dome Keeper!Positives:- Satisfying Gameplay Loop- Great Artwork and Music- Plays very well, has good performance- Plenty of Depth to master- Solid options of customizing each runNegatives:- A Lack of Content- More Options would be nice, especially in the controller department (no Playstation icons, though the controller works fine)- HUD Elements aren't explained and move around sometimes, takes some getting used to- Minor Bugs, though most I've run into since release have been patched already
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is a very well polished game that reuses same formula from the genre but reworks it in a way that feels super fresh and innovative. While you have resource gathering to upgrade your character, you're threathened by enemies that come in waves that get progressively harder. This forces you to pick between your upgrades or defense upgrades, but it also makes finding any valuable resources feel amazing because upgrades bring  so much  to the table. Combine this with random powerfull upgrades that you can  find which will define your complete run and you've got a perfect formula.It's very enjoyable, balanced and besides story mode, it offers challenges which are actually amazing too. Such a fine game  it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I was quite looking forward to this release actually, and there's a lot of good to it, but at the same time, some, in my opinion glaring flaws that ultimately stop this game from being enjoyable. Let's start with what's done excellently. The general quality and polish of the game is fantastic, the art is stunningly beautiful and really quite cute! There're a lot of little details here and there in the animations of the various pieces of the dome that make it come alive, and you can get little pets that hang around your dome. The atmosphere as well is brilliantly captured. The soundtrack helps to make you really feel the tension of crash landing on an alien world with hostile locals that are  happy about your presence. It really does feel like I'm playing a Metroid game in certain ways that are just perfect. That feeling and atmosphere of exploring an alien landscape, or in this case, alien mine, is perfectly captured. And it's exemplified by the general polish and feeling of the graphics, soundtrack, and best of all, controls. Which are again, finely tuned and feel great to play with. The controls lend themselves to the simplistic nature of the game, you simply run into the blocks you want to mine to break them, which to me, was quite a joy and innovative. And I loved the little jingles and unique sounds each ore makes as you mine them / pick them up, etc. Attention to detail like that is great! So yeah, there's a lot of really solid base here that makes it really shine in some ways. Now for what I have issues with. Honestly, it feels like there's a lot of anti-fun design in the game. If you're looking for a relaxing experience where you're super over-powered and blow through all the enemies, or you get this game and are waiting for that moment to happen, then in my opinion, this is not the game. That moment of crazy over-poweredness never came for me. And I don't think it ever would, that's not what the game is trying to be. It's always a race against the clock to collect more resources and complete the objective  before you inevitably die. It feels like the game is too much of a resource / time scramble to really be fun. Sometimes you'll get really unlucky and find no resources where you choose to dig, and it basically ends your run. Not to mention how expensive the later upgrades are. And most of the upgrades feel so bad that it feels pointless to get them. They sound really good on paper, like "oh wow! I got a resource elevator that will ferry resources for me!" Or "Oh, now I can teleport anywhere I want!" Until you realize that both of them are so restricted in their use, or take so many resources through upgrades to be useful, it almost feels like they're not even there. I saw some early release footage from some YouTubers and some upgrades have been changed to make the game even harder than it honestly feels like it needs to be. There's one particular resource, cobalt, that you generally use to repair your dome, but it's so hard to find, and you'll generally always take damage due to the nature of how scarce resources are, that you are basically pigeon holed into using them to repair, always, which really isn't fun. That's the whole thing, you might look at the upgrade paths and be like "wow! There are so many different ways to play! So many different upgrades!" But the amount of resources you're able to find and the high cost of each upgrade, in tandem with the overwhelming force of the enemy after even just a few waves, culminates in the player practically being forced to choose a certain path of upgrades, or die otherwise. Those upgrades being character mining speed, resource carry speed, and weapon damage. As such, you never really have time to play around with the more "fun" upgrades the game has to offer, and the experience ends up feeling more like a claw to the finish rather than a relaxing, fun delve into the depths of the planet for resources. Of course, if you enjoy that kind of oppressing feeling of being pushed to your limit and stressed, putting out fires, then I'm sure you'd enjoy it quite a bit, but I didn't find it enjoyable. And this is coming from someone that has played over 150 hours of Factorio, where you similarly have to put out fires against an unstoppable force. To me, all of these reasons combined make the experience feel like it has an anti-fun design. Personally, I'd make resources more plentiful, or easier to transport back to your dome and make the various artifact upgrades you can find more relatively powerful, given how hard they can be to even find in some runs. Just in general make the upgrades more meaningful / impactful, if they're going to be so costly, they need to really feel like they're worth the cost. Either way, I do quite enjoy it for what it is though. And I do still think it's worth a play if you get it on the cheap, as others are saying, just for the fact of the level of polish, and it certainly is fun to go mining for different ores! So it'll certainly scratch that itch for you, if for but a moment. And again, all that said, this is just my opinion, and I'm not trying to be too harsh to the great work the developer has put in. I certainly couldn't make something this good. Thanks for reading, hope this helps someone!

_childDocuments_.review: Dome Keeper is a roguelite mining game where the player must find a relic buried deep below the surface of a strange alien world, while waves of increasingly more powerful shadowlike creatures try to destroy your dome.As you dig deeper underground you’ll need to collect resources and carry them to your dome, which then allows you to purchase upgrades for drill strength, movement speed, dome shield and weapon strength, and special abilities for various gadgets that can significantly alter your tactics.These gadgets include a bomb which can quickly clear large areas, a probe to scan the nearby area for resources, a lift to carry resources up to your dome, a teleport which can reduce time spent travelling back and forth through deep mines, a dinosaur like creature who can help you mine, and a stun laser which automatically targets enemies during combat.There are a few different enemy types, including ground based enemies who will try to smash your dome in melee range, and flying enemies who shoot energy bolts from overhead. You can fight enemies with a laser beam or a sword (which can be fired out to hit distant targets), and you could equip a shield to protect from damage, or use repellent to delay enemy waves so you get attacked less often.While each run takes between 1-2 hours, there’s a good amount of replayability provided by different map sizes and difficulty levels, a second character who has a different mining technique, and a prestige mode where instead of finding a relic you’re chasing a high score earned by sending resources home.The pixel graphics are basic, but good enough to understand what is happening. I haven’t had any problems with bugs or crashes. The game’s menu says it plays best on gamepad, but I think the keyboard controls work just fine.Dome Keeper is a simple but fun game which is worth checking out if you’re looking for something a bit different.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: pros: + audio is very pleasant, from the soundtrack to the upgrade unlocks+ interesting art style and enemy variety+ very focused gameplay loop+ addictive upgrade gameplay designcons:- lacks gameplay depth (no pun intended)- controller is a must- only one controllable character at release, the other option says "coming soon"- some rare graphical bugs during attack waves- final wave on default artifact mode is an auto winI'm torn on this game, its well made and addictive for what it aims to deliver. You dig, gather resources, buy upgrades, gathering artifacts for equipment used during that run (if you die you get to keep 1 equipment for the next run), and defend against enemy waves and repeat. Unfortunately that's all there is to it, what the game does it does extremely well but that's not enough value for me at this price point, as I cant see myself playing this for more than 10-15 hrs. if it were 10-13 $ then it would be an easy recommendation. I've already clocked in 5-8 hrs on the demo and thought maybe the final release would changed my mind but I can see this game getting very repetitive after 10+ hours. Using a controller is a must, I started the demo with k/m and it was not enjoyable. By winning players can unlock new worlds, equipment and new difficulties. The new worlds is basically a backdrop of art and a few color changes on your characters and resources and some different shadow type monsters. Each wave gets more difficult, however on the default mode in which you hunt for a game winning artifact, once you find and bring it to the dome a final wave is triggered and it does not seem to matter what upgrades you have you will win no matter what, just before death the artifact kills everything. This is a bit of a let down as the final wave would be considered the big boss style challenge, however there is a achievement for surviving without the artifact triggering. After beating the game on brutal I was able to unlock a prestige mode which says you rack up score by sending resources home before you die or win, and while i was unable to play it I interpreted it as some sort of endless mode to try and beat your best record. I also explored some of the unlocks you can customize from the main menu and the game advertises a second character but that its "coming soon" which is weird considering this is full release and not early access. The devs(s) seem pretty active on the forum and have indicated post launch content so this is not a huge deal.There is a lot more equipment to unlock which was not available in the demo, however because i'm at the point of no return for steam refunds I cant determine how much extra equipment/content there is or how much of a difference it makes in the games longevity.

_childDocuments_.review: At the start, this game is deceptively simple. After around 5 hours I felt that I had seen all it had to offer. It was a fun little mining game with simplistic combat. After a few more games though I realized that it was much deeper. there are two completely unique domes and characters that completely change the game depending on which you play as. The dozen or so gadgets also have a big impact. You can customize the experience to make it as challenging or easy as you like. Different tech trees paths encourage experimentation. The more you play the more game modes you unlock, most of which can change the game in drastic ways. All of this is to say that the game never really feels stale, at least not yet for me. Not to mention that the devs still regularly update the game. I strongly recommend this game for anyone interested.

_childDocuments_.review: Dome Keeper is a great game that I struggle to enjoy.I really want to love this game: the visuals are gorgeous, the design is charming, the mechanics are polished, and the mining experience is wonderful. With that said, the gameplay loop just isn't for me. The constant juggling of the two different parts of the game, mining and combat, is stressful in a way that doesn't feel good, and the combat itself is varied in approach but ultimately too limited to be a main feature of the game, and in fact takes away from the mining part. Whenever I'm fending off hordes of monsters, I don't get excited, I get annoyed by what feels like no more than a dangerous interruption. When you're in a flow state mining, you get an alert that you have to stop what you're doing, fly all the way back to base, and click on a monster for maybe 20 seconds or so, and then do it all over again.That being said, this game is full of love and polish in a way that I rarely see. Given that my distaste for the game's weaker half is mainly a matter of personal preference, I can't claim that this game doesn't deserve the credit it's gotten. If a frantic balancing act of a game (a perfectly reasonable style, even if I don't care for it,) sounds fun to you, then this is a masterclass in that, just know what you're getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: I first started playing this game a few months back with the demo that was released on Steam. I found the demo from a Youtuber who plays multiple Indie games. From the get go, I fell in love with the art style and the game play. It felt beautiful and unique at the same time. Reminded me a lot of Dig Dug as a child.Although I love playing the game and think it is fantastic, I do feel that the release was sort of lackluster. The demo I had played had most of the items that were featured in the release except a few things, such as:- Modifiers- Several Gadgets- Map size- Sword Dome- Pets- Skins (map and character)Now looking at the list that sounds like a lot, but when you break it down most of these items don't do much for the game play of Dome Keeper. In the current state of the game, Modifiers are broken and seem to give you all the modifiers at once, or always give you the maze modifier. On the note of Modifiers, once you unlock them there doesn't seem to be a way to turn them off. Which takes away from being able to change and customize your runs. Map sizes is also a great way to expand on the game, but adds nothing but a bigger map and a longer play through. Much like the map sizes, pets do nothing but add a collectible that changes nothing in game, same as map/character skins. Moving on to the gadgets, the release shows several gadgets in the game that can change how your run is affected based on RNG. However,  I find Drillbert, the Probe, Blast Mining, and Condenser to be almost useless in every play through compared to the Lift, Stun Laser, and Teleporter. I would love to see an improvement to the useless gadgets to justify using them or just new gadgets that serve a better role in the game. Finally, being able to choose your dome's weapon is the biggest change to how you play the game when choosing your loadout, however, there are only 2 choices available, and the sword choice has been known but not playable for several months now. Meaning that during all the development they pushed the biggest feature of game play last.Let me just say, I LOVE the art and game play, but I do not believe the $16 price was justified when most of this content was available on a demo months ago. I'll more than likely change this review once more updates come out, but as of now I feel the game is incomplete.
_childDocuments_.name: Dome Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Good concept and artstyle, but feels very incomplete and as a result, tediousIt feels like they had a concept for a really unique base defense game, but instead of fleshing out the endgame they just added a reset button to take you back into the tedious early game. At its core, this game is about time management. There's two main gameplay segments, mining and combat. The combat just serves as a pressure mechanic so you can't spend all of your time being productive. When the combat timer ticks down, you have to fly all the way back to the top of your base or else the hostile mobs will destroy you.The mining starts off slow and tedious, but by the end of a run you will have unlocked enough upgrades that mining is now just tedious. The mining never gets more interesting than strip mining in Minecraft. There is no danger underground. You just hold a single direction until you find a resource, bring it to base, repeat until you find the area's special upgrade.The special upgrades are the coolest part of the game. You can add special systems like an elevator, teleporter, or digbot to your base. I would really hope upgrades like this would reduce the amount of tedium in mining, but they're usually so unimpactful that they just serve as a minor additional revenue stream instead of something you can adapt your gameplay around. The combat is alright. It is a bit challenging at times, but only if you fall behind on the upgrade tree.  There's only 5 or 6 enemy types that I encountered. I can't say the combat is exciting. It feels more like a DPS check than an interesting battle. The alternate defense and weapons systems you unlock (there is one of each) by completing a run are also not very good. Either I played them terribly wrong, or they are in severe need of redesigns. They felt vastly inferior to the base loadout in regards to both killing enemies and avoiding damage. I feel like there's a decent foundation on which a good game could be built, but as it stands it's just a tad dull. There was never a point where I thought "this is cool!". Just incremental upgrades until the end so I could upgrade my weapon enough to survive the combat sequences.

_childDocuments_.review: Dome Keeper is such a satisfying game and I wanna tell you why.!!! The sound design in this game is impeccable. There are so many small details that could be easily missed but just to list a few I love: - The resources you dig up make sound when they collide with each other or walls while you carry them and all of them have a very pleasant ring to them- If there's a storm outside your dome, when lightning hits it there's a satisfying FOOM sound that is accompanied by a little rumble if you're playing controller.- The music is intermittent so when you hear it come up it really hits different and feels special.I could go on but those are some of my favorites so far, all the sounds are pleasant to experience and well designated.!!! The art and design of the game are beautiful. The game knows what it wants to be and does it well. The pixelated style really pops where it wants to and is very easy on the eyes.!!! The digging in this game really satisfies the same part of your brain that enjoys digging in Minecraft, and it really makes leveling up using the resources feel like a treat. Will you choose to move faster overall or be able to carry a heavier load? Or maybe you'll just dump all your resources into your drill and be able to break through anything in your path in no time. The choice is yours! You will, of course, need to balance leveling up your mining equipment with upgrading your dome itself for protection but because it's a roguelike, you'll probably try a few variations on what you prioritize and it might change based on the circumstances of the run.!!! GADGETS AND DISCOVERIES: I am NOT going to spoil anything here but there are devices you can find called gadgets that will VASTLY help you on your runs and each in a very unique way. And the best part is that you can choose to keep one gadget if you die on a run so it can help you from the get-go on your next run! Not only are there gadgets but there are also some very very cool random things you will discover while you mine that can also help you along your way.!!! Customizeability : The game has many ways to play and there are options to unlock for larger maps that take longer to play as well as different dome types and ways to defend said dome; AND there are modifiers you can unlock to make the experience more tailored to what you want (My personal favorite is "longer wave timers", it makes the waves of monsters more spaced out but it makes the waves themselves tougher) and so this is really a game you can get into a rhythm with and then play how you like.My final remarks are that Dome Keeper is a very fun roguelike base-defender that will definitely appeal to you if you like that hypnotizing satisfaction of mining in games like Minecraft and the team who did the sound work for this game deserves an award.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the rare games that I come back to over and over. The mining/upgrade/combat loop creates tension in just the right way. There's a feeling of racing against the clock to mine and upgrade quickly, but you always know exactly what you need to do because it's such a simple system. There's a good variety of upgrades to play with and builds to try. It has never kept my attention for more than 15-20 hours at a time but it's a game I will always be willing to pick up again when there's an update.
