Luckily I got used to the maelstrom palette using the crt-setting on value 1.That being said: I think this is a great game.** Old review **I was really hoping this would be a great game, but I am unable to play this long enough to feel what it's like. The problem I have with this game is that it is too hard for me to distinguish background, platforms and enemies. I've tried every palette there is, but the all suffer from the same issue. It is straining my eyes. Too bad, because I think this could have been a great game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: B.I.O.T.A.

_childDocuments_.review: B.I.O.T.A. is more of an action platformer than a metroidvania. You can go back but there's not much reason to other than to purchase items from stores specific to each area. That is, if you were collecting everything in each area prior to leaving it. The gameplay is really tight and there are a few characters you can unlock. They just change their weapons and visuals, none of them will change movements or give you any special abilities that will help traverse certain areas.The aesthetic is a cool retro style with only a few colors, you can even change the color palette from a wide variety of options if you have trouble seeing with the default color palette. The music is surprisingly good. Overall, it's a pretty fun action platformer. Definitely worth a playthrough if you enjoy retro style platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: B.I.O.T.A.

_childDocuments_.review: If you played Astalon: Tears of the Earth from last year, then you know what a small indie team of good devs can do. This is one of those retro Metroidvania games that raises the bar like Astalon did. Run, gun, platform, and explore an 8-bit alien asteroid full of danger and mystery. There are dozens of items, characters, vehicles, and areas to unlock on your journey, and the rogue elements are very lite and forgiving. B.I.O.T.A. hits all the right notes for anyone looking for an immersive retro world with lots of character and replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: B.I.O.T.A.

_childDocuments_.review: Crunchy, compact, satisfying as hell. Experimenting with the characters in different situation is enjoyable. Enemies are threatening and fun to deal with. Currency is something to keep in mind, but you'll never find yourself stuck in a long grind for it. The story is brief, simple, but quite charming, absolutely capturing that retro feel. A very good deal for a very low asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: B.I.O.T.A.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first play through and man that was fun! I pretty much got sucked in right away and couldn't wait until I was done work every night so I could get back to it. The feel of the gameplay and 8-bit design really brought me back to my childhood in the 80s and early 90s. That nostalgia vibe always is a plus for me. While there's many 8-bit games available now, a lot of them still have a more modern gameplay feel and that's where this one really excelled because a lot of the gameplay aspects really felt retro as well. I loved being able to switch between the different characters. While their weapons didn't really change the way the game feels as a whole, there were certain situations where the perks or weapons for each character were better suited for different biomes with the layouts and enemy design and positioning so choosing the right character for job felt rewarding enough. All the different palletes were cool, but honestly, a lot of them made things really tough to distinguish on the levels so I only tended to switch between a couple of them.To sum everything up, clearly, I loved this game. For you guys that grew up on Sega Master System and NES then def pick this up. Might be the best $10 you spend all year. For those of you that didn't then the choice is yours, but you may want to skip it if you prefer the more modern feeling metroidvanias that require much more exploration and play time as this was relatively short and while there was some backtracking, it felt pretty linear for the most part only having to go back to an area for a minute or two to grab something you simply didn't have enough currency for at the time you first discovered it.
_childDocuments_.name: B.I.O.T.A.

_childDocuments_.review: ProsGreat VisualsExcellent Boss FightsDiverse Enemy Pool and Solid AnimationsConsPoor Environmental Hazard Placement (Dom Area with Electrical Hazards)Constant need to Collect ViridiumWall Jump Not Always ReliableB.I.O.T.A. takes heavy inspiration from titles like Metroid as you venture deep into a mine now crawling with deadly aliens and infected. The story is teeming with 80s nostalgia with players taking control of 1 of 8 characters that resemble the badass military heroes of the era. Each character is a viable option and uniquely designed with a different weapon and unique ability such as C4 or shielding to name a few.The design and presentation is exceptional and will attract those who grew up with NES, SNES, or SEGA Genesis. Everything from the sound design to the boss fights were crafted with this in mind. The boss fights are simple affairs but not pushovers, being cocky will end up with you dead but the patterns are usually simple.Despite being a metroidvania the game is more linear. Upgrades are mostly only available through the blackmarket and rarely are items available in the map. This includes items needed to progress which means grinding for currency to obtain it. Much of the "upgrades" are just containers needed to increase what you can hold, think the original The Legend of Zelda The Wind Waker when you went on a treasure hunt for the Triforce, where you constantly have to hunt for these containers. Fortunately the map isn't complicated and every area is shown to you. Rare is there a hidden room and usually only houses the only optional collectable which are specimens that unlock new color palettes.The game does mix up the platforming and action with vehicle sections that include a mech, submarine, and airship. Much of the game will have you exploring the various biomes in the mines. You can leave at any time using a teleporter but if killed you restart to the last save. Since health is only available through specific containers this option is a god-send if you need to get out or need to exit the game and save quickly. There's a elevator that you can use to access unlocked areas for fast-travel as well.The biggest issue I had was with the environmental hazards. Some are prudently placed like lava pits or dark areas but the electrical traps are the most vexing. In the Dome level the placement of these things are just annoying. 1 mistake and you're dead and since they're placed seemingly everywhere it becomes an vexing battle of attrition as you just try and move through.Overall I did enjoy B.I.O.T.A. and if you grew up with games like Metroid there's little reason you won't enjoy this. The boss fights are fun, the environments are diverse with unique enemies, and the playable cast is wonderful to experiment with.
_childDocuments_.name: B.I.O.T.A.

_childDocuments_.review: Would highly recommend this game for anybody who is a fan of metroidvanias or run and gunners.  Particularly if you have nostalgia for NES and SNES era games this will be up your alley.  The controls are incredible smooth and the game loads you back in really quickly when you die so its easy to jump right back in.  Absolutely worth your time and money if this style of game is something that you generally enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: B.I.O.T.A.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good platformer with a nice difficulty curve, cool storyline on a derelict colony/asteroid with a developping problem. Secrets to find, not a lot of backtracking and when it happens, its not unpleasant.  Graphics are 4 colors and the game allows you to chose your favorite palette, which is nice. You can choose from a group of heroes, I personally played through using only the shotgun wielding martian; there is a level that forces you to use an alternate character, but overall allows you to go with whichever play style you favor(shotgun guy is short range with a fan shaped bullet range, but his extra weapon is an enemy damaging shield and he has a nice purchasable add-on). Music is also pretty good, with the proper mood accompanying the romp through the base.
_childDocuments_.name: B.I.O.T.A.

_childDocuments_.review:
B.I.O.T.A. is a 2D metroidvania action-platformer, in which you command a team of mercenaries and investigate a mining colony infected by an alien plague.

Explore a pixel art world packed with mutant monsters and deadly traps. Try to survive using a multitude of guns and various crafts, including a mech, a sub, and a starship.

name: Heading Out
detailed_description: It's not about the destination, it's about the journey. Heading Out is an immersive driving game meets visual novel passionately inspired by cult classic road movies. Escape your fears by taking off down American highways on an emotional trip of discovery. KEY FEATURES Your Adventure - What's your motivation? The fears, dreams, ambitions and choices of your driver pave the road ahead so each run is a unique combination of races, chases, hazards and colorful characters. Your Path - Will you, or won't you? Each strategic decision impacts a variety of systems including who you meet along the way, what radio hosts say about you, fuel consumption, car condition and wanted level. Your Legend - When and where does it end? An eclectic Americana soundtrack backs each road trip playthrough as your experience expands across the unpredictable western frontier.

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly a interesting and amazing game amazing voice acting, art style, story, diving feels nice but it has a MAJOR problem.  The game may not be exactly what the store page leads you to think this game is, this game in its majority is a 'visual novel' at its core and much less to do with the driving or racing that's seen in the majority of the videos and screenshots.  Also the description just seems vague AF now that I look at that alone.It leaves out the fact that your not actually driving through your journey like in the majority trailer videos and leaves out the fact that this is a visual novel, a good portion your actually just looking at the map and watching as your icon travel across it like they VERY briefly show in the video. When you hit cretin event markers on the map is the only time you get to do any driving/racing for approx. 2-4 minutes.I was expecting more driving from city A to B, speeding down the road weaving through traffic while listening to the radio and talk broadcasts, encountering other drivers that challenge you to a race, finding stops with people, shops & towns in-between your destination all while running from your fear thats trying to catch up to you, like the videos, screenshots and description make it look like.I personally cant recommend this game as a driving journey game, but if you like a good story where you can make choices with a little bit of driving gameplay here and there this is for you.Comment response edit 5 - 09 - 24I would give this game a solid 10/10 IF they described this game as a visual novel, I'm personally not into that type of genre i'm more into consistent action instead of well watching a icon cross a map and stopping to sit and listen to some radio talk to then continue watching a line progress hoping I run into a race or intentionally speed past a cop to trigger a chase scene which was the impression from the videos IMO.  I know I'm not the only one that had a similar misunderstanding what this game was based on other reviews .Comment response edit 5-28-24This is my favorite argument, it makes no sense but I love it anyway.  I hope you enjoy that "steak" that just so happens to be great ice-cream. <3 Yea I can tell your working really hard on the description that at most could of took 30 minutes to add a sentence or two, just hit me up when you do that, it's been almost a month now and I got other things to do then check a game description once a week. _childDocuments_.review: It's early days for this review; will update as I go along.  I bought this game thinking it would be a driving game with narrative elements; I wanted to cruise around the US, listening to the radio, avoiding cops, living out a Smokey and the Bandit fantasy.But right now, I cannot recommend this game for purchase.  Despite the trailer, the game is not really a driving game; it's not really a narrative-choose-your-own-adventure game; it's not really much of anything.  Why not?  Let me tell you.First, the actual driving in the game consists of approximately three-minute long levels that are more or less always the same.  You race against two or so other cars, it's incredibly easy.  But these racing events happen only once in a while.  The majority of the game takes place on a big map of America, with a small icon representing your character.  There's a (pointless) mini-game where you have to hit a button to "hide" from random roving policemen, but that's about it.Second, despite what you might read, this isn't a narrative game with meaningful choices.  Why not?  Because there are none.  It's already been discussed elsewhere, but the game takes (for no clear reason) an extreme political stance in all its small interactions.  In encounters, you have a bit of narrative dialogue and then get a choice A or  a choice B.  Both of these interactions are approximately exactly the same.  There's no branching out of the narrow worldview of the developers.  You're not living in a world you're creating, you're living in theirs (compare to Disco Elysium, where numerous ideologies were present and where players were forced to wrestle with the ethical / human consequences of following one ideology or another).Third, the game really isn't much of anything.  If you want to know what it is, it is a mishmash of three different minigames:  a driving game that stutters on Steam Deck and where the events end in about three minutes; a narrative-driven choice game without any real choices; and a overland map game where you get to watch a little icon creep along a big map while occasionally depressing a button to avoid total boredom.Sure, I guess there is some mild resource management thrown in there, but, who cares.Anyway.  Right now, I can't say I recommend it.  Only about 45 minutes in and I think I've already seen the majority of the game I really want to see.  Too bad, because the premise of the game is really cool, but the execution is honestly a disaster.
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: good game, very immersive, but bad writing, especially for political topics. I found the game to be fun in its resource management/driving aspect: the driving is the speed races from need for speed ProStreet but a bit slower and more slippery. That change, however, actually makes the prostreet model better because you can actually predict and strategize. It requires some time to master but it's pretty good when you get it imo. Avoid using the Daytona-looking "European" car. It's trash. Resource management provides some challenges on balanced difficulty and gives a sense of being chased but abusing the police chase mechanism is OP.The game did well immersing the player into the movie-esque 1970s American road trip setting with the graphics, having an American map that you can travel in, and mechanisms like the songs and state borders. However, the writing has much more potential that is just untapped. The idea of letting the player choose the MC's backstory means that the MC becomes intentionally vague and mysterious. Yet the writers also decided to make MC's backstory essential to the story, which makes the protagonist not relatable as a character and the character growth arc to be confusing. The small stories on the road are good, but I feel like they can be more: they all feel pretty plain, don't have twists and surprises, and often just depict the world instead of building on it. The politics part is weird as well: the writers haven't done their historical research as real events like the Nixson scandal, queer rights, racial equality, Vietnam war protests, Cuban missile crisis, the ENTIRE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ COLD WAR and so much more have so much storytelling potential yet are rarely mentioned or ignored. (like bro, just listen to We Didn't Start the Fire and like you get ten good stories just from the '70s news headlines) The writers put two over-the-top and stereotypical "evil conservative" and "good progressive" and called it a day, which also made the radio hosts incredibly annoying. (especially when Riley repeats the same lines SO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MUCH AAAAAAAAH) (Joy and JC are less annoying since they have a much more personal story, which the narrators are better at writing) The writers are only capable of "depicting" and not "building": not really having a message instead just following the current media narratives. Apparently, they are not American so it makes more sense. I am not against politics in gaming, nor even the political views that the writers holds(just look at my avatar lol) but I am against bad writing and lazy faux-discussions of political topics. And, unfortunately, that statement applies to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: Let me get this out of the way first. If you are using a Linux based system (that includes the Steam Deck) DO NOT BUY THIS GAME! I have had countless crashed and twice it locked up my computer completely. Otherwise let me get into the actual review.So Heading Out appears to be a comic like The Crew game on the store page. Well its not... Yes you will be going across America but, in the context of a map and not actually driving. The driving sections don't exceed more than 4 minutes in length per session and are rather short. They aren't very in-depth but, its...fine. The car handles either like the twitchy model out of Gmod or like a brick in molasses. The handling lacks consistency and often times causes you to take turns incorrectly. Bump's can often times be a 50/50 gamble of weather you'll be fine... or darting off the road. But, I'll save me thoughts about this later. I want give a breakdown so, that I can give people a proper decision. The very bottom will be a TLDR of my overall thoughts of the game.So... what did I like:- First off I wanna give props for having a dyslexia mode. As someone who suffers from dyslexia a great deal. And often times has to just cope with the fact of re-reading the same line 5 or more times till I get the real context... this was awesome. Sure it makes the game look off but, if it allows me to follow along with the story... I'm cool with it.- The art style is awesome! I love the cell-shaded comic book like theme going on here. A nice mix of Initial D meets The Fast and The Furious.- Car section is nice. I will give a small breakdown. (Note you unlock a new car every act upon completion. You need to use the left analog stick to oddly wack your way over to the section to make a choice.) The cars (year not withstanding) are as follows.1973 Dodge Challenger (You will have this by default)1952 Chevrolet Bel Air with Blower (1st Act Finished)1964 Ferrari GTO 250 (2nd Act Finished)1970 Nissan Skyline GT-R (3rd Act Finished)Now while I think some of the choice of cars are a bit odd (The GTO and GT-R due to one only ever having 34 made and the other never being sold in America) I like the selection. Naturally they don't go by the licensed names but, that's not a strike against them.- Finishing a chapter is great to see. It shows you your choices and events performed. Like a highlight reel! - Music may not be the best. But, I have heard way worse.And that's all the likes I have to say... So lets get into my gripes that are not game crashing issues. Now mind you these comments are coming from someone who was playing on "Balanced." They may not reflect other difficult levels.- About the driving... Beyond the lack of feel it has it can be boring... Often times you are left unchallenged. Detours feel like a no-brainier instead of a risk/reward situation.  Get fame in a Burnout like style is often touchy at best (You could dive a few inches from a car and get a near miss one moment. The the next time nothing happens.) And the car really likes throwing a hissy fit with the slightest of bumps.- The Cops... or the lack there of... For the most part the cops (apart from being the bad guys for the most part but, we will get into that later) are terrible. If you end up in a chase with them it is often Speed + Detour + Something Else + Repeat = Win. Seriously they are so bad at posing a threat it makes the cops in NFSMW 2005 look like they are cheating. Better yet if you get arrested instead of it being a failure condition its a reset. No drawbacks, no getting held up, no needing to panic about fear, and defiantly no major issues. Just... drive. - FEAR... Well more like fear... It's meant to be the games way of making you move forward and be a fail state but... I never once had an issue with fear. Sure it would shut me out of a city once or twice but, whats the big deal? Didn't stop my run and overall just felt like some pointless fail condition to keep me from thinking about going somewhere else... speaking of which...- The East Coast! Or better yet the lack their of. The roads exist on the map but, you can not go to any of the states that line the Atlantic Ocean. They don't even have the abbreviation on the map! Why do you hate the East Coast Serious Sim? WHY?! (Mind you I come from Texas that is in the game... But, the point stands.)- Game length is a bit short. Wanna do another run? Too bad... start from the beginning! Sure you don't really need to worry about unlocks as this is more of a rouge-lite than a rouge-like. But, I wanna be able to use the other cars still!- It's re-playable! Or not... Look once you've done one run thought the entire game. It's highly unlikely you will want to come back. Perhaps that's an issue with the game wanting to have a story but, I doubt it.So... without further ado... lets take about the one major opinion I have that makes me not want to recommend this game to someone else.So I hear you like politics..? Let me set a president I was more interested to get into the muck of the mess of the 1970's America but... one big issue. You only get to do what the developer thinks the good side is. I don't need to tell you the America in the 70's wasn't a nice place to be if you were a minority or at the very least not white. Sure it may have came after the Civil Rights Act was passed but, that only meant civil liberties were protected. It had no control on how people had to behave personally.But, here's the rub. The developer doesn't let you do remotely anything right of Stalin as a good thing. Or at least it feels that way. People have pointed out that Disco Elysium does a better job of letting you see the pros and cons of political ideologies over this game (Mind you that DE was made by actual Communists) and I will have to agree. Personally I will most likely never play DE as it's just not my game (but, kudos to the guys and gals who made it.) I wanna give a breakdown of this games outlook in the 70's. And if you wish to skip to the TLDR by all means go right ahead!-So... the game wants you to focus on 4 radio stations. I will not really name the people manning them beyond one (as the name of the person is also the station but, not?) And is somewhat important to the story... Somewhat. At the base level they will comment about the world and some of your actions. Good or bad and the spin they have on them. I wanted to comment on each one in depth but, I hit the text limit. XDIn a nutshell all of them have the vaguest of political views minus two. One who is very left wing (even for the time) and one who is basically Alex Jones without the aliens and the waters that turn the frogs gay. The other two stations; while meant to have differing political views from the two extremes, really spend the time for the most part taking the piss out of Steve Landry. Even the game wants you to know that Steve Landry is a douche-bag. It's a tip actually... The issue is... I actually like Steve. How did you succeed in making the person whose meant to a douche into the one I am glad to hear from? Well mostly by having a horribly set up world. The politics of the 2020's in the 1970's. Look I'll keep it short. I wanted a bit of historical accuracy but, you won't find that hear beyond the style. So my advice. just take it for what it is and assume this world takes place with a really progressive society. For god sake they called the Iron Cross for a Nazi marking. And they don't let you deal with him nicely. I could go into a rant but, I'll pass.TLDR: Game fine, story bad, choice do not matter, right wing bad.STEVE LANDRY FOR PRESIDENT 1974!I can't refund it so I'll just enjoy what I can.Edit to fix errors. Again Dyslexic.

_childDocuments_.review: Its advertised as a stylized, roguelike inspired, open-world driving game. It is actually resource management ala oregon trail with interspersed five minute driving sections once or twice per stop. You only catch a glimpse of what the bulk of the gameplay is actually like in the trailers. That gameplay is watching a dot on a map slowly move to event spaces.It's more of a visual novel but marketed as a driving game. The radio is the focal point more than the driving and the radio's focus is on the DJs. The music is phenomenal. No complaints. The DJs play their parts well but the overt political tones stick out. I'm not going to chastise the game/devs for their politics but rather the inability to hide their bias. The main narrator is toeing the line between a good grizzled performance and pure mamamax toned cringe. It's a tightrope. Sometimes the dialogue hits and other times I'm laughing at the game. The jabs at the right wing are both immature, cliche and frankly, out of place. I'd be saying the same if it was full of Andrew Tate/Jonesian dunks on the left wing. I didn't buy a driving game to have politics shoved into yet another piece of media where it has almost no relevance on top of barely driving. Very cool art style, music and the driving (when there is driving) is pretty good. The script is the weakest aspect which is compounded by the game being very dialogue/text heavy. I mostly enjoy the game and I like the nods to Initial D and other media. I just wish there was more like, racing. Dodging traffic on two lane highways gets stale quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: It has so much potential and I tried so hard to enjoy the game, but overall the game is extremely boring, the stories are simply forgettable, and the radio hosts' dialogues are downright ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥Even better the publisher/developers are actually  with the gamePros:- Most of the random encounters are intriguing- Unique comic like art-style- The fear system: gameplay wise it introduces another element you have to take into consideration when making choices and I think it has a lot of potential, but the implementation of it is lowkey broken, there are way better way to design this system. Story wise the way they portrayed Fear made little to no sense at all.Cons:-  The majority of the time for playing the game is going to be you idle watching the dot (your car) moving around on the map heading towards next destination, it is unskippable and the idling is painfully long, unnecessary, and serves almost no purpose besides wasting your time. If you watched any of their trailers, or saw the 10 out of 11 screenshots they showcased right here on Steam, they intentionally depict the game as a cross-country road trip game, and making complicated choices while not driving. The reality is more than 80% of the time is you starring at the dot.- Awful scripts: The voice actors they picked are fitted for the roles, but the scripts are so bad they ruined all the voice acting, effectively made everything unmemorable and dismissible. The main problem is with the radio hosts and their dialogues, unlike the main story I can't tell if the writers were trying to be corny but took themselves way too serious or the other way around, it's like a college professor went substitute in a high school and decides to act like the most unprofessional class clown so he can be "cool". In addition, the dialogues are excessively political and every radio host is as stereotypical as it gets, they successfully managed to make everyone from left to right look like an egoistic, idiotic, narcissistic smug- The minimal driving portion itself is bad as well: the driving physic itself isn't that bad, it's mediocre, but the races became repetitive very quickly. The races themselves are supposed to be generated every time you enter a new race except for the one at the end of each chapter, in theory the ever changing environment should have great replayability, but the reality is the developers put so little effort into developing assets, roads, environments, etc. and I quickly lost interest after three races.

_childDocuments_.review: Driver meets visual novel meets choose your own adventure meets roguelike progression and item management. This game has been a joy so far in the time I've spent with it, it gets personal, it gets deep, and it gets dark. But its also full of humor. Driving itself is fun and gets more and more challenging the more you progress in the game, and the chases and races remind me alot of the old Driver games.This is definitely a gem and a sleeper hit of the year, highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the reviews here seem to claim that the tactical portion of the game was supposed to be less present and that the game isn't advertised correctly. I outright disagree, if you take a moment to actually look at the various marketing material for the game you'll quickly find out that the map portion of the game is a fundamental part of the experience that's being offered here. I find the mix of resource management, visual novel and genuine racing elements to all flow really well together. It might not certainly be for everyone but it's a core part of the game which i think works. Furthermore the driving itself is satisfying with a mix of arcade and simulation physics(leaning a little more towards arcade)My only gripe with the game so far is some of the writing. The premise, psychological elements and most of the little stories you stumble upon are intriguing (out of the ones I've seen so far, plenty more left to see) but some of the dialogue really takes me out of the whole thing sometimes, I'd say it comes off as a bit immature given the whole tone and setting (and supposed 70s/80s era)I've been following the development of this game since i first heard about it a few years ago and i can finally say that as a big fan of Vanishing Point, Interstate 76 and the Driver games, this game has my approval.
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, amazing soundtrack, looks really pretty, and I think the driving is pretty good (can sometimes Jank out), and the main story plot-line and most of the Side stories really tie this world together. I only really have one problem with the game, and its the Rainbow Radio station girl, feels completely out of place for a game that takes place in the 70's (mid Vietnam era). I am extremely left leaning and gay, but stating "I'm gay" and "DAMN MEN" every time she is talking gets a bit annoying. Again that's my only problem besides some driving jank. Also your a ♥♥♥♥♥ if you won't play just because of "Woke", you can skip the radio stations if it gets your panties so much into a twist. Get this game if you can!

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately the game is just not what I was expecting. Heading Out is mostly played from a map view while I was expecting more of a third person driving experience than what it offers. There are also performance issues and some pretty bland storytelling. Pros:++Soundtrack is 10/10+Art style works well+The narrator has a cool voiceCons:-Not a whole lot of driving-Story choices don't really matter-Some events do not respect the agency of the player-Crashes frequently-Driving segments are over too quickly4/10, kinda bad. Although this score is below neutral I do want to add that the game has a lot of potential, and if you're into map view games this is definitely a game you want to check out.

_childDocuments_.review: Indeed "It's not about the destination, it's about the journey."And what a journey it was even if a bit short it was really fun with good music tons of events that kept the game interesting  with funny quirks on the radio or from the random events that made me smirk or laugh, I wanna address what other people say that the game is misleading in what its is about. While yes is true the description would not do the game justice in reality the game is a split of a resource management / visual novel / driving game and I think is better like this then what people expected it to be just a driving game mostly... but hey that just my personal taste there is enough driving to not make it boring.There are however some small nitpicking stuff about the game that I did not like.Firstly is kind of short and once you done with the last act the game locks you out of the save file... so you cant do the other event quest n such needing to start allover unlocking the stuffs again... hopefully a post lunch update with New Game+ or an endless mode where you don't have the fear mechanic ? and generally speaking hopefully there will be some more content in the future for it because the game core and foundation is really nice, has a nice loop to it would be amazing if it would be expanded upon it with more stuff... A Second thing would be a bit of clean up on the graphical side. Like the comic art style is amazing but it should/could look more sharp, there are some blurry details inside the car dashboard and in general... the grass popping in as you drive gets annoying and anti aliasing being it on maximum settings looks sometime like is not there at all...In conclusion even if short and with a few flaws here and there overall the game is a really nice experience maybe a bit stingy at full price but if they will add post lunch content it is definitely worth it... or if you think a mix of resource management / visual novel / driving game where you run from you fear would be your jam its still a worthy purchase.( I finished the game on the 'challenging' difficulty and it was just good mix of challenge without getting annoying and also turn the setting 'hide consequences' to ON, makes the experience soo soo much better and immersive, that setting should be default to on.. )

_childDocuments_.review: The problem for me is: There is nothing much to do for that price. I enjoyed the game for sure, but at the end I was dissapointed how narrow this game is.  After my first playthrough I simply dont see why I should play this game again. My understanding from Rouglelike is simply some sort of random generation each playthrough. But it bearly changes anything and after going through the Story once and start again. All I do in this game is watching at my map while a point moves from A to B and wait for some events to happen. While trying to get there before the schizophrenia catches up to you.The good things I can say are:I enjoyed the story of the game. _childDocuments_.review: I am probably sure this is a nice game, but as a whole, I simply cannot recommend it. For a game focused on driving, there is a shockingly very small amount of it.The story is... certainly a story. It's good in some parts and meh in others. Several locations to choose from to travel to, but of course you only ever seem to see the city you start in. After that, it's watching a dot on a map while you "drive" it to the next story piece. What fun.The driving itself is by far the worst I have ever felt. It's like the focused on storytelling and "driving" on the map over the actual driving experience. The game will randomly reset you saying that your "fear" (whatever the ♥♥♥♥ that is) is catching you... while driving at 150MPH and dodging everything. The slightest turn causes you to drift, and your braking distance is ten feet, meaning the best course of action to slow down is to lift and coast, then under/oversteer into a wall/car/tree because your brakes are too strong.Radio stations seem to have decent voice actors behind them but with one of the worst scripts I have heard since NFS Unbound. They're calling me the Interstate Jackalope. Okay, cool, there's some context there and I'm getting some background. I do not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ care that the radio host has found a cookie after a week and is now spending more time talking about that than she did talking about exposition for the story. They haven't caught the Interstate Jackalope yet, oh no. How about instead of explaining what a jackalope is, you expand on this news story I heard about when I started the run. A Canadian Civil War? The Mexican boarder being closed? I want to hear about the world around me.The idea is there, but it is so poorly executed that I cannot ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ believe this game managed a Mostly Positive overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this, but I can't. The gameplay is pretty cool, I'd see myself replaying it for hours and hours, but the story and novel are soo poorly written that I just can't stand it. And don't get me started on the radio host. It seems to focus more on politics than it's own story. It's a hard pass for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: As other reviews have mentioned the trailers are pretty misleading, there is way less driving in this than you would expect. That being said that criticism takes a big backseat to the main issue with the game: It's boring. I only played 44 minutes of this and it's literally the same 2 lane road over and over and over and over again. Sometimes you detour onto a dirt road. Sometimes there are trees, or rocks or buildings but it's always the same with slightly different curves. A rouge lite should have some repetitive elements but this is taking it way too far. The second thing that really makes this game bad is the absolutely insufferable radio show personalities that drive the story forward. The devs thought it would be a great idea to inject modern politics into a game set in alternate timeline 70s...for no reason. It is grating and annoying and the writing actually some of the worst I've had the displeasure of listening to. Since this game is trying really really hard to emulate the movie "Drive" I would ask the devs to go watch that movie again and try to understand what made it good. It was a dark, brooding, slow burn that was driven (no pun intended) by it's atmosphere and the the situations the protagonist got into. It was NOT "lol  look at all these WACKY characters, and listen to the them talk for 90 minutes straight". If for some reason you have to inject politics into your game, at least make the set piece relate to the time frame and drive what ever point you're trying to make. This is just cringey and lazy. This had the potential to be fun but what ever point the Devs were trying to make with the story got in the way of an actual gameplay loop, atmosphere, and concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: Heading Out isn’t just another game you pick up and play for a few hours before moving on to the next big thing. This game is an experience. It’s like a love letter to those of us who have ever dreamed of dropping everything, getting behind the wheel, and just driving until the road runs out.From the moment you start, you’re pulled into this beautifully crafted world that feels both nostalgic and fresh. The way the game weaves in elements of classic road movies is nothing short of genius. It taps into that universal yearning for adventure, for escape, and for finding yourself out there in the wild unknown.What I really appreciated about Heading Out was its depth. It’s not just a driving game where you steer a car from one point to another. It’s a journey of self-discovery. Your driver’s fears, dreams, and ambitions aren’t just background noise they are the very essence of the game.So, if you’re looking for a game that offers more than just a quick thrill this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little disappointed with this game. I thought this would be a game where you spend most of the time driving coast-to-coast, but instead it becomes a road trip planning visual novel game where you have to manage icons and numbers on the screen to avoid losing immediately. The driving sections can be fun, but the physics are dodgy that I find it hard to grasp it. Hitting the side of a barrier pushes your car a little too violently, and this is obvious in the first mandatory driving section in each run (oh, and this is a roguelike game). The car can drift, but it regains grip too quickly during drifting that I ended up counter-steering too much way too many times than I wanted.And probably the aspect that I don't find to be really good is the roguelike aspect of the game. It doesn't make me wanting to play more like other roguelike games do, exploring other shenanigans the game can throw at me. Probably because I don't really find the road trip planning aspect to be that engaging to me as I was more interested into the driving part, and I was disappointed to learn that the game is mostly about the road trip planning than driving.The characters in this game are some of the most boring ones I've ever seen. In this game, there are radio hosts that will comment on your choices and actions, but they react in the most plain way possible that neither of them are engaging at all. Even the radio hosts that condemn your behaviors have very shallow personality that it feels like a teenager is writing them. And the worst part is, you'll be listening to these radio hosts talking after every race or when going through radio icons on the map which happens fairly regularly. It's a miracle there's a skip button to skip these radio talk segments.The 6 hours I had in this game is after I completed one save file. Yes, it is that short to complete the "story" of the game. It may take longer for you because I was quite lucky to first-try each act at balanced difficulty. However, I'm not going to continue any further because this is not the game I thought I expected it to be.

_childDocuments_.review: When reviews complain about a game being woke or progressive it makes me want to buy two copies. They've become more annoying then the "sjw" people ever were. So when I saw "progressive malarky" in a review I knew I needed to check this game out. The game is good. The racing is ok, probably it's weakest element. The radio stations are ok, with a "Alex Jones" like character on one station and a young antifa girl on another. The music is solid and enjoyable. The story is fun and probably the strongest aspect of the game with a solid narration throughout. The meta game on the map is simple but works fine. I would love to see what this dev team would do with a higher budget sequel. It's a solid 7.5/10, something fun to lose 9 hours to and move on with your life. My one big complaint is that there wasn't enough progressive malarky for my taste. I'm fueled by red pill tears you see and they just weren't salty enough for my taste! The next game needs gay pride parades, anti fascist propaganda, and trans people that want to be excepted and treated like real people. Then I'll buy 20 copies!

_childDocuments_.review: The driving itself is mostly fun (not challenging, but that may be because I asked for refund early to face any serious difficulty). Unfortunatelly, the driving/racing/police chase is smaller part of the game. The larger part is about playing FTL-like map run with resource handling, where you react on storytelling  decision making "encounters". If these encounters were OKish, neutral filler between the actual driving the car, that would be tolerable, but it is not the case.The encounters are poorly written, not believable cringefest. Examples:You hit and kill a dog while speeding (you are speeding most of the time, that is the point of the game). You can run away (bad) or stop, hug the lady-owner of the pet and burry the dog together. That costs 1h of game resource and it is considered good option increasing your reputation. In which universe that could happen - you hit someone's beloved pet while speeding and it increases your reputation, because you hug the owner (who is very happy to hug you and burry her beloved pet with you - the cause of all this)?Another one:You accidentally hurt feelings of 12yr old boy. He wants a fight. You decide - lose the brawl (good) or win in front of his friends and girlfriend (bad). I felt real cringe here...But it is even worse - big portion of these encounters are leftist propaganda. And mostly modern day progressivist/woke one - i.e. not really related to late 70s or early 80s USA. The main character is very feminine and soft - hardly to be believed as rebel from that era.And to add even more - you are told that listening to the radio may be important (yes, the game is taking inspiration from Vanishing Point movie). The radio is called Rainbow Revolution and it is exactly what you think it is.I am just surprised, that there are leftists, who like speeding with high-fuel-consumption cars listening to 80s rock music (i.e. boomer music).
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: Graphically interesting, good performance, and solid mechanics.Your time will be split between the map view of the USA, travelling from point to point, and sometimes actually driving for 2-5 minutes at a time on the streets from driver-view. Sometimes these will be races against other (CPU) drivers and sometimes they'll be police chases.The concept is that you're a bad-ass woman driver fleeing from... uh... your fear?Unfortunately, you don't feel like a bad ass. First of all, your name is "Jackalope" *eyeroll*. Second of all, you don't do any cool stuff that would make you feel like you're immersed in the movie 'Driver', 'Cannonball Run', 'Death Race', Gumball Rally', or anything else. Instead, you're presented with series of interesting encounters that are presented like a comic book that often offer you a choice upon which will depend the raising or lowering of stats like fame, reputation, focus, and cash. The mechanics are part arcade racing, part visual novel/choose-your-own-adventure.What kind of badass stuff will you be doing? Listening to brief lectures about global warming, consumerism, reproductive rights, sex-workers, inflation, the industrial military complex, conflicts in Israel and the middle east, or helping a woman flee her groom during a wedding.The music is enjoyable enough, but entirely forgettable. The "radio stations" don't feel at all like radio stations. It's just the music tracks interspersed with all-too-crisp-and-not-at-all-processed-like-a-radio-sounding-audio segments by mostly zoomer-DJs with almost nothing interesting or amusing to talk about.Overall, this is a positive recommendation because of the mechanics. I could take or leave the music and "radio stations", and narratively, it's trash.How could it be improved? Music that doesn't sound like it came from Udio, fewer soap-boxes, and more badass events and choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: Big warning, you're gonna be playing that map picture 70% of the time. Each icon is in its way a visual novel experience of choices.Nothing is connected through the driving experience, that's more contained within small procedural missions like outrunning cops or racing other drivers that I'm sure will update over time.This is NOT what I was expecting this game to be based on everything shown. All of the actual mechanics are tied to the 1 map screen pic where you accelerate an icon across a line trying to fight to have fun with the actually good driving.Now if you're here for the visual novel side and not being a Racer on the endless winding road, then this game has a lot more to punch for you with the choices in the events that are well written and provide different statuses on your journey against the ever creeping closer fear. You also need to figure out if you click with the radio hosts or not as well because they're gonna be holding the story on their shoulders.
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: Heading Out has to be one of the best releases this year that I've been able to play, And I didn't expect to see myself writing this review or wanting to care this much about a game i picked up for only $20Starting out I didn't really know what to expect from this game; I hadn't followed the game's development and looking through the screenshots, game play trailer and earlier reviews my initial understanding for what the game would be like was a narrative based driving simulator with the ability to decide parts of your characters story. I loved the sound of that, purchased the game and spent the first bit of it falling in love with the visuals and aesthetic of it all, the almost comic style of the colors and flashy visuals paired with the 70's setting made the game feel lively all throughout for me even to the end.Game play wise it isn't anything spectacular, well from a normal persons point of view I'm guessing. To me the driving felt much different than anything I've played in a racing game before. I didn't go into the game believing I'd be able to drive completely all over the USA like in 'The Crew' with how cheap the game was or even expecting complex driving mechanics comparative to most racing games of this era, Instead what I got with 'Heading Out' was loving the game driving for not how it felt to drive but for how it made me feel when driving. The setting is perfect for me, spending countless minutes managing cash and your drivers energy make you feel the rush of being on the run, ducking in and out of cover as a cop nears your location along one of the maps many roads before speeding off to the next blip in front of you; whether that be a brand new story for your character to flesh out their ongoing journey, Road Races that keep you on the edge of your seat to get into first place hearing the cars pass by exclaiming "There he is! The Interstate Jackalope!" letting you know just how widely known and important your characters actions are to the people around you as you gain infamy and reputation. Cash from the races always doesn't seem like a lot but enough to keep yourself moving even just a bit further on your path and running through traffic or escaping police chases combined with those races shows you leaving a trail of increased wanted levels all over the map in your wake, just you and your car managing to escape anything in your path or even behind it as your characters fear follows you slowly filling up the roads you drive and leave behind. You always get to keep the feeling of being on the run, whether it be from the aforementioned police officers wanting to tear you off the road, the fear of your  past lingering right behind your tread tire marks or as the game eventually makes you realize, even yourself.That's where the narrative really comes into play. You start off deciding your characters backstory, or well as much as you can in a game where the mystery really carries the story. From that point on, whenever you enter a new chapter you get to continue building that character and the history they have or traits you want them to have. This was one of my favorite parts of the game, even though the driving felt so rewarding; the feeling of building this driver and making the traits as relatable to myself as i could made certain pieces of the game stick with me more then they maybe should have.Before I forget to mention this; Jesus Christ this game's score is wonderful. Serious Sim really did do such a great job with everything on the OST, From the games main track of "Same Old Road" to "Aint No Hero" even "Disco Gal" is such a banger for me. No matter what your taste of music is, the songs that were chosen for this title really put you in the place the developer wanted you to feel you were in; listening to some western track or hard rock while I'm gunning down a California interstate anticipating a turn, there's not a single way i could think of being able to make someone feel like a road ruling street racer outlaw then the way it was displayed in this game.The way the topic of self hatred and running from your issues were approached really hit home for me as well; the way that fear speaks to you through the radio preying on your vulnerabilities and problems you've been through mocking you for the issues you have and belittling you is so reminiscent of what it's like to have depression. No matter what you do sometimes you cant help but doubt and be the one person beating yourself down in any given situation. The one voice you know so well in your head telling you the same things over and over and you just have to deal with that, to keep pushing it off.The struggle of maintaining that mental escape while trying to distinguish what the good things are around you whether that be the people you meet along your way, the accomplishments you make or even the situations you can decide to aid or hurt. Every single one of these things i experienced in this game made me understand how I could relate to the character I was building and the struggles they faced along their own journey in their own life. Every step of the way we have so many different voices in our ear; from the doubt and cynicism our fear speaks, Riley giving us adoration and pressing her own problems down, JC venting about his regrets and past decisions, Joy dealing with the pain she had from her ex husband, and even Steve Landry beating us down for anything we decide to do. All of these characters have their own unique and distinct personality, and even if we don't see eye to eye with any of these people about everything they believe certain radio snippets show the relations of problems that our character and these troubled people can all sympathize with. At the end of the day, opinions are opinions. We all will spout and spew what we think and what we believe, shouting into an endless void believing our thoughts will matter more than someone else but our hearts will always empathize with feelings we can relate to. That's what being human is all about. Even just thinking about the things we go through as people; the things we lose, the people we hurt, the ways we get hurt, there's so much i felt hit home for me in this game in so little time. The feelings i got from this game will not be the same or maybe even close to what you felt, but feeling every single part of the things I was able to describe and even the things i wasn't able to put into words made me adore this little narrative rogue-lite so much. The ending was amazing, your character pushing from day to day reliving the same stuff over and over, very obviously so tired of it but never giving up as he pushes towards his goal. One of the scenes i experienced having low focus and driving over one of the conversation blips showed my version of Jackie so tired, so stressed and so emotional behind the wheel. He pulls over in the rain and he just cant go anymore. It was the one scene in the game i feel that i have felt a million times over in my day to day life. Making the choice between screaming and crying and then being forced to just go back to it, like nothing happened. Being able to let a bit of that pain out before you are forced to do what you have to do. This game is beautiful, from the driving to the narrative we are able to build and experience to the ending where you finally get to realize that running from your issues only perpetuates the cycle of never escaping them and the only real way to handle the things that we try to escape is by turning around, and facing them. That's the only real way you can get through to that light on the other side.To every other "Interstate Jackalope" that played this game I hope you enjoyed it more if not as much as I did. Whenever you hit your lowest of the low, you cant go anymore and you feel terrible about yourself, remember the person you are the things you're capable of and get yourself back on that road to defeat the "greatest driver alive", your doubts!<3
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: For a story that tells me it's all about me (the character in the game), nothing really relates to me, beside some meta game outputs. I felt more involved as the protagonist of need for speed underground.The driving feels uninspired and off. After you've seen the three basic types of races, they are just a chore with rubber banding enemies. The feeling of speed is all over the place, and while the little animations are cute, they are super boring after the tenth time that you saw them.I didn't get what the map screen was supposed to add to the game. Could've thrown that out and kept people in character, in the car, and on the road, and there would've been nothing lost.The fear mechanic is such a non-issue, it might be not there. Maybe you have to crank up the difficulty as much as it goes, but if you just drove with mildly high speeds, you can easily outpace it.The radio hosts and vignettes were about what you get today. Either it's cheap shock or pretentious "HAHAHA, NONE OF THESE WERE GOOD" type of story telling.You are probably going to have a better time watching a let's play of this game while it's just you, your car, and the road... in The Long Drive, Jalopy, or even Truck Driving Simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good, racing feels good, cars are weighty and feel like they're barreling down the roads. The story is pretty good. My biggest issue is that the "hours until fear gets you" just genuinely doesn't work well. There's been more than once were I've rested for 7 hours and I've been ahead of fear by 9 hours and it still somehow hits the city I'm resting in and loses me the run. If it's not accurate why have that as a feature? Other than that though this game's fun. Super stylized, love the story bits and the narrator, I love that some of the radio hosts think youre a woman and some think youre a man. Really good story building and world building
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun but holy ♥♥♥♥ they need to fix some things with it !- "Police barrage" game mode is straight up unfun and a run killer, you can't beat the cops at spawn fast enough so you'll be losing, generally losing 2 out of your 3 lives just there, and after that even if a cop is 10+m away behind you and you're doing 130+, you'll still get busted because... reasons?- Driving with manual gearbox is really fun but wasn't tested enough as the game will show the gear you were in when you finished the last drive instead of the gear you're currently in when the car spawns, and unpausing the game using "A" will make you downshift when coming back- Going next to a barrage in any game mode sometimes doesn't register as you were to far from the barrier- Big jumps are very random, sometimes the car will fly straight, sometimes it'll land on the hood damaging it, sometimes it'll do a barrel roll and finish on the roof losing you a life even when jumping straight- Braking while still holding the throttle will cause the game to ignore all throttle input, forcing you to release the throttle before applying it again- Opponents are ruber banding like crazy meaning a mistake close to the end is a lost race- Position changes takes a second to register meaning to can't pass an opponent just before the end of the song and win, the game will still think you're behindIt may seems like small stuff but the frustration of losing a 1-2h+ run due to things like that is really buzz killingThen there's the smaller stuff like dialog between racers not being numerous enough leading to a lot of repetitions even before starting act 3 of 4, police chatter bugging out due to a line not playing audio, which will lower the music volume for the whole race and just play faint static, the interface when starting a run is just plain horrible to interract with using a controller, vibrations are too strong and can't be turned down, roads are way too straight for the gameplay with only the final cities having some twisty mountains...It's a good game at the core, I really like the idea and the execution, but it needs some polish to really be enjoyable
_childDocuments_.name: Heading Out

_childDocuments_.review: Heading Out is an interesting concept for a driving game, something that intrigued me and my friends.However, it just seems... boring?It's a driving game, so you'd obviously expect to be doing a lot of driving, right?In the 30 or so minutes I've spent playing I had 2 VERY SHORT driving segments, both of which were basically just me holding RT and maybe once or twice swerving to the left or right to avoid traffic.The radio commentary didn't help, I thought it'd be cool, but instead it just TRIES to be funny and fails miserably (maybe it's just my sense of humour though?). At times I genuinely just wanted to go into the settings and turn the radio down, it's like this oooOoH i'M SO qUIrky type of humour that just makes me sit there staring at my screen with a blank face. "OOOh I found a cookie!!!" stfu jesus christ.Pacing is also just kind weird, I drove through the city for like 3 minutes and got into a short-lived police chase (one that seemed completely insignificant as I gapped the police almost immediately), and the next thing you know I have a radio station giving me a nickname and later on (if you decide to join a race, which is by the way, completely optional, I know, a driving game with OPTIONAL driving, how funny) the racers somehow KNOW YOU, acknowledge that you're the "INTERSTATE JACKELOPE" or whatever the name is and exclaim how proud they are that they raced with you.I literally just started my journey how am I this famous lmao???Besides that the A.I. is just genuine ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Maybe it's the difficulty I chose, but Christ almighty the decision making other drivers have just blow me away. It just seems like they have a set path they must follow and WILL follow it even if it means they will take you, themselves, another driver, and an innocent family of 5 in the process.The game tries to be this awesome, rebellious commentary on how you run away from your "fears" (literally the red thing in the game is called "fear"), you answer personal questions and then as you progress you get to answer various other personal questions which I'm guessing is supposed to let you LET GO!! of your past grievances or whatever. Unfortunately it's just... mid... The artstyle is cool but the white slowly started hurting my eyes genuinely I couldn't continue playing because my eyes started getting way too tired of the bright look this game has. Overall 3/10, wouldn't drive in the USA ever again.

_childDocuments_.review: While I did not experience any crashes or major glitches during my just under six-hour playthrough, I did experience some minor issues such as audio crackling and visual oddities such as fairly awful pop-in and distorted shadows.Heading Out’s graphics need to be separated into two categories: first, the persistent comic panels, which are the game’s main vehicle of storytelling. Therein, as you are making your way through America, you will frequently encounter brief road events that present a handful of gorgeously drawn panels that offer the player a choice. While these artworks are consistently amazing, the regular gameplay—the racing—is less good. A persistent black-and-white filter sets a decent atmosphere that is further supported by a good, but not terribly diverse soundtrack. What is noticeable to me is that this black-and-white filter also tends to hide some of the more uglier textures that eventually just become apparent as you replay through the various acts. The skybox is flat, there is an abundance of pop-in, and there aren’t very many unique cars on the road either. It’s serviceable, but not great. You’re the Interstate Jackalope, a nickname for an outlaw driver making their way from Indiana across the United States to challenge the best racer alive. However, it becomes apparent that there is a little more to it than just a 70’s outlaw story, as you are constantly pursued by your own fear, literally enveloping the roads behind you and threatening to end your run if they catch up with you. Events repeat. You meet the same people again and also repeat the same race against the best racer alive at the end—each time you reach the end, unlocking one further act and thus gaining a little more insight into what led your character to this point.HO competently ties the roguelike element of replaying the same basic journey into its own story; however, it is also a little too ambitious with how it attempts to coax the player into self-inserting into the Jackalope. More specifically, the game tends to ask personal questions such as one’s childhood trauma, their greatest fears, dreams, or friendships. Though it also fails to meaningfully incorporate them into the greater narrative and, as such, ends up feeling more like flavor text than anything else. Sidestories are a lot more intriguing, wherein the player encounters both mundane events, such as stopping by a decrepit gas station and choosing how to spend their time there, to utterly nonsensical, like actually encountering a Jackalope and deciding how their character feels about it. These blur the line between the facade of the outlaw racing and do a good job of building anticipation of where the story is going. Nevertheless, each of these is only one to three paragraphs long, and multi-part sidestories are difficult to finish due to runs being as linear as they are.Heading Out is a visual novel pretending to be a management game, pretending to be a racing simulator. That is to say, the minority of the game is actually spent driving—much more so, each act begins with a brief comic sequence during which the player sets some additional information about their character and is then introduced to a map of America, with their goal being reaching a certain city to challenge the best driver alive to a race that, upon winning, will lead to the next act. On this map, the player gets to choose the next road to travel down and is granted a preview of events along the way. These may include the aforementioned story events, but also racing challenges or radio exposition. Furthermore, the player manages the main resources of ‘Focus’, ‘Car Condition’, and their money through this map screen. Focus drains as time passes and represents your character becoming tired, which is represented by them dosing off during actual racing segments, whereas Car Condition could be considered a soft hitpoint system. Racing is a less nuanced, as maps tend to be fairly linear, with few challenges being unlocked throughout the different acts. While it was all serviceable, I can’t claim that the driving was genuinely very engaging and, frankly, felt lackluster due to an incredibly incompetent enemy A.I. Cars, similarly, felt all fairly same-y, though the game also makes a decent effort to make the driving segments feel as immersive as possible due to the inclusion of similar comic panels.Heading Out is a very niche title that can only really be recommended to people who are very specifically looking for this sort of narrative experience. It’s short, and all three major aspects of its design feel underwhelming in their own way—but it has a charm that is difficult to deny and kept me engaged throughout my playthrough, if not for any repeat runs. It can’t be recommended to people who solely desire a racing simulator, a management game, or really a visual novel, but to players who are looking for a decently straightforward, though heavily thematic, story about self-discovery.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, if you don't, then ask yourself this:As long as the answer to either of these questions, the more the merrier, is yes  you just openly identify as Ryan Gosling (he's literally you, after all), then it's safe to say this game is for you., please note that this game is a visual novel/racing game, not just a roadtrip simulator. There's about a 50/50 split when it comes to the actual gameplay  choosing a route/moving along the map; it's not a map you can just open up while driving, it's a separate element.The trailer definitely does a poor job at pointing this out, so if you think regular pauses between driving sections (the latter of which usually last a whole song, i.e. 3:30 min.), are too immersion-breaking for you, then that is definitely something to consider.Still, I honestly think that including the map the way they did, having to manage aspects like your speed, because it directly affects gas and how much it will cost you, the events you come across, including cop cars you have to react to and stop for (or not!) and all the little scenes when you meet all different kinds of characters, do a lot more good than harm to the story.The latter are voice-narrated, which adds to the game's feel quite a bit, usually prompting you to make a decision as well:, you'll also need to manage things like your "focus" by resting in cities, which might lose you a bit of time, sure, but it'll also make sure that you're fit for the long road ahead.Alternatively, you can take some... uhm... "substances", that's the word! They'll do the trick too. More or less.Last but definitely not least, you obviously have to manage your car's condition as well, which can be damaged by crashing (duh..) in the aforementioned driving sections. _childDocuments_.review: Had a great weekend running away from my fear.The core game and mechanics just work great. There's a brilliant thematic consistency in building on music (for races) and talk radio (for stories) so much, it really throws you into that road trip feeling. And then there's (so many) layers on top of it that turn it from a novelty into a worthwhile, wholesome experience. The end is worth fighting for, and I watched the credits with satisfaction, thanking all the wonderful people who created this work of art. Spotted some repetition of smaller story elements when retrying a couple of runs, but generally this game is very forgiving to failure and won't get boring too quickly. I don't blame anyone who fails to put this game into a category - I can't. Oh and if you're scared of "woke" games stay away I guess this will have a lot of triggers for you.

_childDocuments_.review: opening disclaimer: i don't really recommend for or against this game, it's decent but not great or terrible, i have to pick one for a steam review, i also might sound angry, mean or upset but that's just me all the time, i like this game lol.this game is very curious, it is a good classic racing game, it's a pretty nothing roguelike, it's a somewhat lacking visual novel and it's got some really nice visual art, as well as music, but the story is nothing special, the plot devices are extremely literal; how you're running away from your fear, racing against (totally not yourself) someone in the same car, that no one knows anything about except that they're really fast, which is .... suspiciously similar to the main character you'll be thinking the first time you see it, then the second and the third it becomes a bit grating, why have the game play out the same 3 times, to the MC's absolute non-reaction, (atleast in other timeloop games like for example alan wake's american nightmare alan is very clearly somewhat irritated and confused by it) until the MC realises the obvious loophole in the contract that i personally already figured out by that point, it's a fun experience with likeable characters (other than the player character which is literally a character you select your exact experiences to fill in, which again is neither great nor awful) haven't finished part 4 yet but if they actually make the player character a woman no matter your choices then bonus points for having some amount of rigidity and commonality to any player's story which i think all games should have SOME of, i don't like the blank slate protag concept in these extremes where it makes the character feel too generic and like a vessel even though they aren't explicitly supposed to represent an empty vessel for the player in a meta sense, if they have a past of being a famous racer why do they have no personality or deeper history? this to me feels like a weird and largely non cohesive character design, i feel that although it's an interesting choice to do this it would be better in a more silent hill 3 or until dawn way, or even fallout NV where you answer generic, psychological profiling questions in a more medical environment where it's an in universe thing rather than basically a settings menu selecting whether you had a good relationship with your family, i mean it's nice that the things the villain taunts you for are personal and actually targeted, more specific words are often stronger and more emotional than generalised things of course so i see what the idea was but it seems somehow wrong or forced that the game explicitly asks for them at the start of every act just to then immediately try to make you shocked when it told you it wanted to use them to make you feel something or whatever, this could be slightly alleviated even just by having the questionnaire be a big blank file you fill in ALL at the start before you play, it could even be the villain's contract that the MC has signed, there are ways this aspect of the story could have felt less forced and corny and more like creating your characters backstory, which in games like fallout is part of the appeal (though that is an RPG, you don't need this in a visual novel or racing game) i feel like the customisation of a character almost entirely was misunderstood, it exists for a reason in games it exists in, and when it doesn't, which we can see in games like.... idk the EA WRC games or something it feels hollow and pointless and like a waste of time, point being that it's a clear risk not very worth taking in this project and therefore confuses me, it feels like the idea guy was also the development guy, which is fine and i still think it's a good game but maybe there should've been a 'we're not trying to reinvent the wheel' guy there too because i do like the minor characterisations we get in roadside events where you have 2-4 options for a given situation, which of course then have pre written responses and actions that i think are a charismatic, well written character for the tiny ammount they give us.this game also has some actual problem problems, there is a bug where sound is attenuated as if someone is talking, so the car and the radio are quiet to let you hear them but it's bugged for the whole stage and no one is talking anymore and infact all future voicelines in the stage won't work, also the UI doesn't show everything you may need to know, like for example i lost a run because i made the mistake of not selecting to pause the fear because i thought i would make it to the end, since it said it was a few hours behind me, but seconds later it overtook the end, there is no indication of when it will do that other than guessing and the way fear works on the map is slightly confusing so it's hard to know. another problem is that the driving physics feel like an oldschool racing game, like outrun or something, this is a problem. because as important as those games were, they kinda suck, it feels bad to drive a car that is unresponsive and weightless, i'm driving a muscle car that weighs probably close to two tons, why does it feel like it weighs 20 lbs and simultaneously 4 tons, it also suffers from the classic racing game issue of ''useless-brake syndrome'' brakes do not slow the car down at all and you drift the car by letting off the gas, not letting off the brake, it will, confusingly, not really drift while accelerating, which doesn't make any sense, not just in terms of realism because this game is clearly stylised and arcadey, but it doesn't make sense to play, think of the driving in grid 2, this game should feel like grid 2 or burnout, those games atleast to me feel a lot better and more intuitive to play, arcade racing games done right, or at least, in my opinion, better, another problem is that once i crashed and got reset onto the road automatically but i was unable to accelerate quickly enough to evade police capture and they stunlocked me twice, i got reset from crashing once and then instantly lost my entire run on the final road because i was physically unable to escape the police cars the game reset me directly into TWICE, please atleast add a buffer for resetting and not getting instantly arrested or make police move away slightly when you respawn, also sometimes you will hit small wooden gates/fences at 150 miles an hour and spin out uncontrollably, i can't believe i am saying this but that is not in fact how multiple tons of metal would react upon hitting a small piece of wood and this is a very irritating quirk that screwed me over several times, please make it so that the car is not as sensitive to small collisions with fragile objects you have, intentionally, no other choice but to hit like gates and wooden barriers in police roadblocks, atleast if the brakes aren't going to slow you to a speed where you can control the spin.at this point i don't think i would choose to spend £16 on this game, 8-10 is definitely a more realistic price point for mecliff notes: don't try so many things that no one has done, there's a reason no one made a visual novel that's a racing game that's also a roguelike, it doesn't add much really.don't be afraid for your character to have a character.take the aesthetic/feeling of oldschool racing games and leave the physics, outrun feels weird to play, this doesn't have to.likes are the writing, characters are charismatic and funny, the woodstock '69 bit really got a good laugh out of me.also the music is somehow mostly period accurate for the 70s and somehow good, which is already shocking, but it's very inetersting how the music is so varied and yet all of similar quality, it's very good.and the sound design, non protag characters and the car choice are all stand out, good, quality parts of the gamealso i'm by no means a game designer so these are probably all stupid criticisms in ways i don't understand.
