_childDocuments_.review: I totally loved the old Dungeon Keeper. Previous Dungeons 1,2,3 I have missed, but 4 after the positive reviews I had to buy. This game is definitely the neighbour of Dungeon Keeper and War for the Overworld.The strengths:+ Perfect voice-over present everywhere, even in the menu+ Story is memorable, with a lot of outside references+ Gameplay is not repetitive - in every level you will probably choose different strategy+ A lot of choices to make (mostly in later levels, when you have learned how things works)+ I have struggled in some levels, so I had to learn how to better or choose better strategy+ Necromancers dance in Necrodancicon (I spend some time just watching them :D)Comparison to DK:- It is not so "seriously" dark as DK, but instead in fun manner with a dark humour- I don't feel connected to my creatures as much as in DK (player focus is more based on overworld and dungeon events, to stay alive and protect the dungeon, so it is understandable that there is not much space to babysit creatures more - for example, they don't fight between themselves and usually in fights it is best just to pick all and let them fight, also all creatures can return to life if they die and you can easily buy new one - so  the game is more about your strategy than doing the best with available creatures you have)- It harder to switch between 2 maps- There are 3 creature factions, each feels different and has it's own needs and combat style- There is dungeon hearth and Thalya (would be nice if you could create your own dungeon lord, to be something like champion of certain creature type and bring some bonuses based on that, maybe in Dungeons 5?)- Traps are more thought through, at level 17 I still haven't tried all the complex ones, also some traps are placed on walls, they are definitely more advanced than in DK- There is always path to dungeon hearth, and only more can happen, and enemies are eager to test out all the traps in the way - in later levels, they can still pass through somehow, which is nice, you can just add more and more of them ... if you have enough money)- There is real story. In DK, it was just raiding all the good land, here there are nice plot twists along the way, more varied objectives, and even some cutscenes- Creatures have synergies - usually it is about finding the right composition of many of each type to pick (for example, having no healer is no go for orks, while demons doesn't even have any, and necromancers just require their graves to not be destroyed by evil heroes while they die)- There are spells, but also potions, it is faction based- A pity, there is no "possess creature spell" (those DK levels with traps were kind of cool)- I don't understand why Blizzard does not release rights to Dungeon Keeper franchise, I miss the Bile Demons and Mistress - and they just don't do a sequel to DK 2, but I am happy that Dungeons 4 is unique successor to the genre and looking forward for 5 (if there will be any, but I hope they have still plenty of ideas to implement - and haven't tried multiplayer yet, but if I am right, you cannot play against each other, only in co-op withing one dungeon)

fun out of any of the games. potions are defently overpowered and can be spammed to win any fight but there fun and the horde feel like a strong faction to play and there evolved versions all feel like natural advancements. bringing in some old and new ideas was very nice. the demons though i dislike there resurrection taking evilness now and missing there ability to convert are insanely interesting to play as. there max damage output is rather insane the spells are also very useful and also can cause moments of being overpowered. the undead's infinite hero revival is a fun mechanic. talya feels stronger then she did before with alot of really powerful abilities and can recall back to the dungeon heart when something gets through. (there is no cancel button for the recall button which has caused some annoyances) the story is good however i wish they brought back some more of the hero's given the story line we should be going on a world tour of every hero in the franchise. having 30+ snots is a godsend and I cannot say how much I enjoyed it. this game is still a jolly good time wit  its flaws. now id like to state my hate for level 16 partially does come from I feel it could be one of the best levels in the franchise if it just had a few minor fixes. its so close to being fun but 8 swarms of spawners with elite gaurds and 50 damage per second ground is kinda making it hard to enjoy it. its a level of attack and defense but it feels more like your attacking gains you nothing as I cleared half the map and my highest level was 3 and the defense was watching 30+ of them charging at you. another thing the level could do to make it a puzzle would be making the ice pillar thing nullify some of the fire damage or freeze the ground. (edit: either im jsut dumb or they added it shortly after the fact but its now in there and i must say doing the level again did feel much better so thats another thing off the list) that automatically makes the fights far more engaging and not watching as you your armies at 1/3 health by the time they finish standing up after you placed them. its such a interesting concept of a level which I really love but I feel it drops the ball by making a few small but really annoying changes. it probably doesn't help the level suggests the undead faction which are the most expensive faction on a resource starved map which you cant gain evilness half of the time because there's a eruption. I do need to account this game has been out for a month and I'm comparing it to dungeons games which had years to be bug fixed. this game had a excellent start it just needs to fix up some of its blemishes. some of these are easy fixes like with unit control and a bit more resources on some levels. the evilness needs a more reliable gathering method then prisons which give 5 per hero killed and torture which is very late game. the carts give big boosts but theirs nothing that really allows you to just build it up while your doing other things. a slight cut in the big boosts and a way to get small trickles consistently would probably help a lot of the resource starvation as it feels like feast or famine with no real in between. this game very well could far surpass any of the other games in the franchise. I'm sure some people already believe it has. this isn't a bad game its a game that's missing a lot of the small stuff. I also would like there to be at least some mod support (Modders greatly increase a game's longevity), so if changes could be made to accommodate the modding community that would be absolutely lovely!Something I felt lacking in D3 that could still be done here in D4 is more building/room types and more minion types. _childDocuments_.review: Dungeons 4 REVIEW ( GAME FINISHED ON HARDEST DIFFICULTY )To start, played all 4 Dungeon games beat all 4 dungeon games so I like to think Im pretty experienced :P      (Also beat WotO) Ile go through each aspect and give it my honest thoughts.Campaign - Story wise it was pretty good. Nothing that will blow your mind but the humour is on point with all the pop culture call outs from the last several years. Its not quite as murderous as the last title tho. Its 20 missions, each one will take you 30 minutes to an hour based on difficulty and if you are going for challenges or not.   I would give it a 6.5/10.  Its nothing AMAZING , but it will keep you entertained and it does have some tough challenged.Base Building - Not bad , it gives you all the tools you need. One big change is almost all the devices are run by your Snots ( I cant think of 2 exceptions). So that really free's your units up to be and do whatever you need them to do, which is fine because this game has a LOT of busy work. It has all your favorites like Torture Chambers and Undead Dance floors.  5/10. Its about the same as the last one, and comparing it to WotO, it really lacks substance.Unit Roster - A few added, a few taken away.4 units for each faction, The biggest loss for this game was they removed the 3 super minions. I wont get too far into it here as I want to write a guide for the units and traps, fair to say tho you will end up finding a combo you like. Personally I find demons were the big losers this game but thats just my personal experience.   Roster wise 4/5 . It felt like it was just missing another an entire tier and no super minions .Traps building - They reduced the amount of traps by a lot, but i see it more as they cut the fat (tho not quite enough IMO) . What you have for traps suffices for what you need , and there are 1 or 2 infinite traps if you know what your doing. I feel Dungeon Master games have long since moved away from trap based tho.  Traps wise 5/10. Everything you expect to find is there , and there are a few REALLY interesting new additions as well as some extremely lackluster options. Again if you want a deep dive, go find my guide ( when I post it )Gameplay - I wish I could say this really shines but honestly, its really just a "Run your army into the enemy and hope you win".  There is a bit of finessing around in some maps but ultimately its smash rock into other rock till 1 breaks. 4/10 It lacks depth a lot, and with 2 of the factions having healer units there really isnt any reason to not just run face first into the enemy.Unlockables - There is actually a decent amount. Each level ( after the first 3 I believe) has 4 challenges, 1 of which will give you perks you can use after you unlock them.  They range from "X faction is cheaper" to "Thalya has bigger ... dps". 7/10 for this, I found quite a few of them quite challenging and ended up having to go back and pick certain ones up in order to get the MUCH harder ones.Overall, I would give Dungeons 4 a 6/10. Humour was fantastic, I could listen to the narrator and Thalya back and forth all day. Where it falls flat I feel is the units and battle gameplay. There is no real strategy to this game when it comes to army battles, you just run stuff into the enemy and see if its enough to win. I will be very interested in where the DLC's take us. Again if you want a DEEP DIVE into the game, look out for my guide. Will be posting it in sections when I can.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I completed the game, I can give a complete review.I always love Dungeons for it's ridiculous over-the-top humor. It has a lot of meet and brings a lot of nice features to the "Dungeon Keeper" game style. At its heart there is a lot of choice of how you want to succeed in a situation and I think that's what keeps me coming back.The gameplay boils down to a race to get resources before you are overwhelmed and destroyed. Levels each add unique gameplay experiences that mix things up to make the race difficult. It ramps up difficulty pretty well, I think.The three major resources are gold, evilness and mana. Gold and mana can be mined, and manage can be generated by your minions. Evilness requires you to do, well, evil.This usually means running into the surface and killing goodie people, but there's a few ways to get it past that.The monsters you get end up three categories. You get horde monsters, Orcs, Goblins, Snake People... Demons which are Imps, Succubi, and so on... And Undead, which are Banshees, Skeletal Warriors and so on.Horde tend to be pretty sturdy, but it takes a lot of resources to keep them alive if they die, losing their experience progress. Demons and Undead just respawn when they die making them better in some ways, but they have trade offs. Demons are pretty squishy and have no "Tank". And Undead need blight to summon mini-undead to assist them in order to be the most effective. Usually a mix ends up most effective, but then you are spreading your resources thin trying to level up multiple monster trees!This ultimately means you're changing gameplay styles in a lot of ways.Defending your dungeon also means deciding how. You get traps you can set up, or you can try to use monsters to do it. It's strategic in that manner.Tactics, I think, is where the game faulters a bit. While the units are tanks, healers, DPS, etc. Often you are just selecting everything and right clicking. Now and then you try to prioritize targets, but I think micromanaging fast paced combat like it has gets to be difficult and it lack the tools to make it very easy.Overall, it's a strong addition to the series!

_childDocuments_.review: I have had experience with every Dungeon Keeper Style Game from the start and enjoyed mostly all of them to one degree or in some aspect. Dungeons 4 feels like a very bad copy of Dungeons 3. I honestly think that they have done nothing better or as good as in Dungeon 3. Pros: -Coop works good-no crashes-Speaker is the same as in previous gameNeutral:-Musik is ignorable-Creatures have been modified with new specialities like the undead minions-There are a lot of kind of funny references to pop culture thingsCons:-Most levels have more then one limitation like: time limit/ enemy spawn/ space to build/ or any of the level  specific mechanic (I don´t want to spoiler you if you really want to give this game a go)-The new way to get evilness is more of an anoyance, you can only get it on the surface and if you are bound with your creatures in the dungeon you wont get more. The oportunities to gengerate it inside the dungeon come so late in the game, that you either have won already or have nothing more to research. -Commands given to your creatures are laggy or some of them just ignore it, compared to Dungeons 3 it feels buggy.-In some fights creature that are further back (both in the dungeon and on the surface) just ignore the fight and either stop following or venture away.-Balancing between the horde / demons / undead is off.No map has made me want to do it again and i have to say most of the time it felt like doing a chore and a very frustrating one at that. _childDocuments_.review: Here we are again. Dungeons 4. Larger maps, more creatures, continued story and a few changes.Dungeons 4 takes the essence of Dungeons 3 and tweaked things here and there. Dungeons 3 was very well received so might as well continue on that path.Jokes and dialogues are funny, at least for me. But I embrace this type of German humor and the references to pop culture. Of course you're not allowed to be upset when one of your favorite franchises gets a little side joke ;-)Pressure for the missions? I don't have any. I spend about 2 hours building up my dungeon and when I had enough of the mission I have enough firepower to crush the goodness. But that is my personal gameplay style, you might differ.Also I  might be only a 6 year old as I really like the simplified research menu, as another review suggests.Overall this game is solid and fun. My only wish would be more multiplayer. For example I would love to play with a friend, each their own dungeon and then have the options either fight each other or fight up to two bots or other players.While playing I have not found any bugs yet or they are so minor that I didn't even realize they were there.Good job on Dungeons 4.

_childDocuments_.review: Good:- Better graphicsBad:- Bad skirmish mode is a static map. After 2-3x you will be bored. You cant select anything much basically- You need to get maximum achievements per each mission, to get "bonus". You can view the achievements only at the start of the mission, once the mission starts you have no clue what achievements you are meant to do, or if it is completed. This makes getting the "bonus" difficult and annoying. You can select 3 "bonus" for each game you play in skirmish.- Troop types is unbalanced. Some troop types is totally useless, some overly powerful. IF you can figure out which troops to use (hint: AOE Bombing), you can one shot almost anything- Traps is useless against wardens or "enemy tankers", so don't even consider making traps- Don't even consider making guard rooms, cause it is bugged. Your troops will not patrol or stay in the guard room but wander around, and you have to individually find and select each and every single troop of yours to fight- Snots AI is bad. They will put your resources in the top most area, even if it is in another room. Imagine having a 10x10 treasury, they will walk not to the nearest available but furthest spot. Imagine beer production, they will walk to another room 10 square away to put the barrels- Way too many bugs+ Factory that makes tool boxes will shoot out tool boxes at "tool box stacks". This will make tool box stacks (as in stacks of tool boxes) collapse , sending them flying to every other room . Snots will pick them up, stack them up in front of the factory, then the factory will shoot out tool boxes , repeat+ Snots will stack resources in a pile, at random in a room. IF your room so happen to have a door, chances is, the snots will run through the stacks of resources, causing the resources to fly to other rooms,  causing more snots to rush in to pickup the resources, causing more resources to fly, repeat+ Your troops tend to ignore enemy, and do whatever they want to do, leaving just 1 unit of troop to face an entire enemy mob. Only way to fix this is, to manually micro manage each battle/fight+ Enemy Hero AI is horrible . Place a "slime wall" at the other side of the lava, the Hero will walk all the way to "kill a wall" that isnt anywhere near its route to your dungeon heart, making the Hero die . You can also kite any mob of hero across the world for some reason .+ Balancing issue again, spells is too over powered. 2 bat spells (lowest rank spell) will wipe out 3 mobs of wardens. To do this, you need at least 15 units of level 8 troops without deaths. Highest rank explosion potion does almost the same damage as the bat spells , as in it takes 2 bat spells to kill 3 mobs , versus 2 explosion potions. Explosion potion is extremely hard to get compared to bat spells.+ So many other issues

Developed by Realmforge Studios, this dungeon-crawling extravaganza not only continues the legacy of its predecessors but elevates the humor to new heights, delivering an entertaining and laughter-filled gaming experience.Dungeon 4 doesn't miss a beat when it comes to humor. The game is a comedy goldmine, packed with clever writing, witty dialogue, and absurd situations that will leave players in stitches. The humor, a trademark of the series, is not just an afterthought but an integral part of the gameplay experience, making every moment enjoyable.The characters in Dungeon 4 are as quirky and amusing as ever. From the bumbling heroes to the devious villains, each character is brought to life with charm and personality. The hilarious dialogue is delivered with impeccable timing, and the voice acting adds an extra layer of comedic brilliance. The interactions between characters create a lighthearted atmosphere that enhances the overall enjoyment.Beyond the laughs, Dungeon 4 impresses with its creative dungeon design. The levels are not only challenging but also filled with comedic elements that add to the overall amusement. Whether it's navigating through trap-laden hallways or encountering eccentric creatures, each dungeon is a blend of fun and strategic gameplay.While the humor takes center stage, Dungeon 4 doesn't neglect its gameplay mechanics. The game introduces innovative elements that keep the experience fresh and engaging. From quirky puzzles to unexpected challenges, the gameplay seamlessly integrates with the humor, creating a cohesive and enjoyable adventure.Dungeon 4 is a treasure trove for fans of pop culture and gaming. The game is peppered with nostalgic references and clever Easter eggs that add an extra layer of enjoyment for players in the know. Discovering these hidden gems becomes a delightful part of the gaming experience, rewarding players with a sense of shared humor and camaraderie.Visually, Dungeon 4 is a treat. The art style is charming, and the animations are smooth and expressive. The attention to detail in character design, environments, and visual gags enhances the overall comedic impact. It's a game that not only tickles the funny bone but also pleases the eyes with its vibrant and well-executed visuals.Dungeon 4 is not just a game; it's a comedy spectacle that excels in delivering laughs without compromising on engaging gameplay. With its hilarious writing, memorable characters, creative dungeon design, and innovative gameplay mechanics, Dungeon 4 is a must-play for anyone looking to embark on a dungeon-crawling adventure filled with joy and laughter. Get ready to chuckle your way through a game that proves humor and gaming can go hand in hand, creating an experience that is as entertaining as it is amusing.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I don't think I can recommend this game. If there was a neutral option I would pick that, cause the game isn't terrible or anything, it's quite average and uninspired.I love Dungeon Keeper, I think bullfrog has definitely been among the best of the software developers of all times and it pains me to see what kind of games are coming out nowadays but I digress.I thought this game could have filled that kind of craving for something similar to DK but it's nothing more than a shallow copy that tried to mix things up with some "RTS" wanna be vibes.The idea in itself wasn't bad, but it fails to deliver on it.The main attraction and beauty of DK was about building your dungeon, watching the heroes trying to invade it and dying horrible deaths while trying, enjoying the placement of traps, attracting the best creatures, converting the most powerful heroes and so on.The problem with this game is that it's not like you "can't" do the above mentioned things (although the quality does not compare favourably to this one, for one I do not like one bit the whole concept of "evilness" as a currency and the costs required to buy and upgrade the chance to build advanced rooms, summon creatures (they no longer come out periodically as your dungeon evolves and fits their needs, you need to pay and buy them...).What makes the game fall short is the wanna be RTS part and the above mentioned "evilness" currency that forces you to take your creatures to the "overworld" to kill and destroy in order to gather the "evilness" required to make the dungeon building part work. The main issue with that is, the story missions will be forcing you because of "PLOT" (nonexistent, the game knows it and tries to make fun of itself, but it just doesn't work for me, it's so bad, cheesy and cringe that it makes you want to skip every single cut-scene) to constantly come to the "overworld" because of time based events.You end up spending the majority of the time on the overworld, watching your creatures fight on their own with their auto-cast skills, hardly requiring any input on your side barring a few fights against "boss" creatures to avoid an "AOE" attack or two (feels like a bad MMORPG sort of thing), and even then the controls are clunky and nothing to do with a real RTS. It's all half baked.It's just bad and annoying having to constantly pick up your creatures from the dungeon, drop them in the "overworld", run around doing what you have to do there with the clunky controls, and quickly bring them back down to defend from the hordes of heroes, rinse and repeat every couple of minutes.Also unlike DK or other DK clones, there's no real AI opponent that can create a dungeon, break into yours and try to invade you. Not even in the skirmish. It was quite the disappointment when I found out, as I thought the main campaign was all about fighting against the forces of "Good" but in skirmish you would have been able to play against AI opponents, my fault for not researching more into it.The creatures available are also underwhelming for the most part compared to the original DK, some of the rooms are pretty useless (like the guard room) because of the above reason (your creatures are basically all the time in the over-world and under your command until you need to teleport back down), others like the torture room I hardly get to use it because the mission will often be over before I have the chance to, again due to the time based nature of the missions.What I liked the most is the sound track, they did really well with that.I would say get it if you really crave some DK like game and you have already tried all the rest of them, but only if you can get it heavily discounted (50% or more), it's not worth the full price/25% discount.

_childDocuments_.review: As a first-timer's introduction to the series, Dungeons 4 is a solid game. Scratches that Dungeon Keeper itch while retaining its own identity in terms of aesthetics and mechanics.  Playing through the game on hard is an engaging challenge, and there's certainly enough going on here to promote a variety of play styles and replays given the achievement mechanics, skirmish maps and online community content.I will say this (and this may come down to personal preference), but I would have loved to see some dungeon vs dungeon focused campaign maps. I also think the overworld mechanic is great, but would have benefited from some more inspired map work - they're often restrictive and feel MOBA inspired, and I can't help but feel some variation in overworld buildings, such as more structures to sack and open areas to explore would have really nailed the mechanic for me. Again, minor issues attached to an already very enjoyable game.Very keen to see where the series goes next - might even be a day one buy for the next game if they keep expanding on the already solid mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale but it was still expensive, about half the price of baulders gate 3 so it should be atleast a 5/10!I really like this game but some campaigns feel like the dungeon isn't the focus. There is almost no reason why you should focus on dungeon defense and traps when you can send out minions to the overworld and prevent monsters from even entering. Investing in traps is also really expensive and compared to spending and leveling minions, I don't think the dungeon is good value.You need to listen to the voice overs as there are key queues. Focus on the quest and try to finish within an hour. Some levels ramp up in difficulty over time so if you haven't been pushing the overworld the minions entering the dungeon become overwhelming. If your army dies, it can often be game over.Some helpful hints;- try to finish early, the game shouldn't go past 1 hour in time- try to increase your gold storage, having 10k in the bank means if your army falls or if you get some evilness you can spend and build right away.- try to get minions out on the overworld in the first 10 minutes, clear the mobs around the dungeon entrance to get some early evilness- focus on overworld objectives, if you did you 10 minute overworld clear, you should be able to access some of the objectives easily because the cart will be passing close to the dungeon enterance and you have already cleared the path to the objective.- split your army up, you really dont need more than 10 minions to fight, when you hit 20 minions, you just steam roll.- NEVER let manavores feed. I have lost a game after 40 minutes because 1 manavore got to level 5 and would swipe my army to death.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons 4 is a delightful return to the dungeon-keeping genre, bringing back the beloved Absolute Evil and the Dark Elf Thalya. This game masterfully blends complex strategy with intuitive design, making it a must-play for fans of real-time strategy games.Pros:Top-notch Voice Acting and Hilarious Dialogue: The game is filled with endearing sarcasm and witty lines that keep you entertained throughout.Stunning Visuals: The graphics are impressive and don’t sacrifice performance, making the game visually appealing without any lag. Engaging Gameplay: The game offers a perfect mix of dungeon management and real-time strategy, ensuring that you are constantly engaged and challenged.Cons:Inconsistent Pacing: Some parts of the game can feel a bit slow, which might affect the overall experience for some players.Overall, Dungeons 4 is a charming, fun, and endlessly quotable game that is worth every penny. If you’re looking for a game that combines humor, strategy, and beautiful visuals, then Dungeons 4 is the game for you.

Highly recommended for couples or best buds to take out their sadistic pleasures on smug goody-two-shoes heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated to a HUGE Negative. Kalypso really screwed the pooch on this one! I originally gave this a thumbs up UNTIL I got to the mission "Doom Hill". I played all of the missions on normal difficulty including this one. Never had a problem finishing each level and was having fun until Doom Hill. Some of the missions were challenging at times, but still mostly fun. But for the Doom Hill mission, the only way to have "fun" is if you're the sadistic type that likes to be punished for playing. I'm not!How are you punished in Doom Hill? Well, you're in the belly of a volcano? Why? Who knows, truly. I mean why would your character "Thalya" choose to setup shop there? To make it tough on the player. Don't tell me the story explains it because it is still lame. And frankly I don't remember now IF the story did explain why you're in a volcano. I got about 35 minutes into it on normal difficulty. Constantly had problems with my Undead creatures beginning to die on me. Why? Because the Volcano slowly heated up before blowing. While it heated up internally, your creatures begin to cook until they die. No problem. Undead can't really die unless their crypt is destroyed. But, the heat begins to burn these too. Once that is burned up, your Undead also die. Now, some will say well you're supposed to move ALL of your creatures to the surface until the volcano blows, then move them back down below the surface. Problem with that is in the mean time the "spiders" the narrator calls them (though they are some kind of flying lava creatures) begin marching to your dungeon heart to attack it while eating gobblers along the way. Why do they attack your Dungeon heart? No particular reason other than to punish the player. Why did I even have Gobblers? Because I had one of the specials to cause your creatures to eat gobblers instead of going after gold on payday. And don't say to move your creatures back down to protect your dungeon heart. Because your creatures will begin dying from the heat. And your level 1 or 2 vampires can't keep up with the healing to save your creatures. Especially if they are trying to battle the lava creatures also. Yes, I know about the magical crystals that allow a certain area to be protected from the heat. But, you have to find them by sending your snots digging. I found two of them, but the problem is while your snots are digging around everywhere you end up finding about 6 to 8 large nests of those lava creatures. Some of you are like "oh all you have to do is this, this, and that". Easy mission. Well, as I said before some of you are sadists. That's ok. You can be a sadist. I choose not to be because I don't enjoy being punished for playing a game. And in the end I even tried the EASY difficulty and still lost creatures to the heat. It's just not worth it. I truly enjoyed Dungeons 2 and 3 and started to enjoy Dungeons 4. Doom Hill ruined it for me and I wont' be back for another beating. The developers are lame for allowing this mission to pass.Original Review Below.Another great entry in the Dungeons series. The humor continues, which is nice and entertaining. I'm enjoying it, although there are some annoying elements like the Manavores. And I like to pace myself through each mission. As a result, you can quickly tap out various gold veins, which you then have to randomly search in other parts of the dungeon until you find more gold veins. The most annoying thing is when you're minions go on strike and get uncooperative. Yeah, you can dismiss / kill the rebellious ones, but do you really want to do that when they are at higher levels?Anyway, it is still fun overall in spite of some of the annoying parts described above.

_childDocuments_.review: Unique and fun RTS game. Playing the game on highest difficulty and unlocking the achievements is a satisfying challenge. Controlling your army is low APM micro but there's a lot to keep you busy between expanding the dungeon, staying active on the overworld, and casting spells in battle. Each army type (horde, demons, undead) has a unique feel to them and fun in their own way. Horde charges straight in to smash smash smash.  Smash buff potions to enhance your brutes, charge straight in, smash healing potions until the enemy forces break. Demons are more manipulative and my favorite. They can kite with hit and run tactics using area slows and range attackers. Combos very powerfully with spells. Slow spells helps make kiting even easier. Thunderclap knocks down the enemy group and pulls them into a single spot which allows your small aoe demons to roast the whole lot of them in a flash. Or, for an even more spectacular bang, one demon type makes them weak to fire which greatly amplifies the destructive power of the ultimate spell, meteor swarm. Undead is a relentless massive army where each creature can summon 2 to 4 additional minions for an endless army of death.  Then it's further augmented when you resurrect your choice of enemy heroes you've defeated as ghost champion versions.I loved Dungeons 3 and Realmforge Studios has managed to further improve the experience for Dungeons 4. If you've played the previous entry the changes like dungeon controls, hotkeys, and tech tree design can be a shock to get used to. I feel they're all an improvement though once given time to become accustomed to them. I like the streamlined tech tree redesign as it needed to be organized better because you'll discover it includes 4x the unlocks as you progress through the campaign. I like how snots take care of operating all the rooms instead of needing to use certain army creatures because that was a pain when trying to grab your whole army while also wanting to leave the specific operators behind. Dungeon controls are also improved with how you can slap a group of snots around, hotkeys for building rooms or casting spells, and interface in general is well designed. The intentionally hamfisted humor I could take it or leave it but it does get a chuckle out of me once in a while.Overall I highly recommend the game!

_childDocuments_.review: The Completionist Evil writes a review of this new installment of the Dungeons series.After beating the campaign, then getting all achievements, then unlocking all the skills, and then beating the campaign on Hard mode I can say that this is a great improvement over Dungeons 3. When I went from D2 to D3 I thought that D3 was the definitive, final version of what Dungeons could be. I thought the same thing when going from D3 to D4. There's a bunch of QoL upgrades in this version over D3 that greatly improve gameplay, such as sweep picking up resources or having more than 20 army units. There's a number of changes to how the dungeon works too, like how advanced trap building works and a new potion system that is very powerful yet balanced. Something that's difficult to adjust to is the lack of continuous evil income, because the islands of evil are removed. I don't like the change but I see how it's necessary and how it makes the work you do more rewarding in the end.Overall, the game is fantastic and I would love to pick up any DLC that comes out for the game. Even if D3 maps are ported to D4 I'd play those in a heartbeat as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good continuation of the series. Dungeons 4 made a lot of improvements and streamlining since Dungeons 3 in various areas, such as tech tree (this specifically is a big improvement) and dungeon management. It plays differently from #3, in which you had to leave members of your army behind or loaf around while work got done. Now snots do practically everything. A lot of the same humor and dialogue you'd expect. While random seeded maps are gone, a map editor and easy way to download player-made maps is available. There are a few good ones right now, but not a ton of maps.There are a few things that did not make its way into #4 from #3, such as the random seeded maps and playing as the heroes. "Converting" heroes still exists in #4, but because they're ghosts now they lack that nice aesthetic from #3 and instead just have an ethereal look and lack the name change too. It isn't bad per se, but I do think the prior aesthetic was better.If you want a hefty amount of details, user SilvasRuin made a thread which details a lot of what to expect in this game under steam discussions in a thread labeled: "What's changed between Dungeons 3 and Dungeons 4? An answer."Overall, it's a solid game and if you liked #3 you'll probably like #4.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeons 4

_childDocuments_.review: It's an improvement on Dungeons 3 (graphic improvements, game-play, & rooms, but all-in-all it's the same game in the grand scheme).   The over-all just streamlined the game some.  It's worth the buy.A new story with some cool unique twists and some rooms have been changed & improved upon.My biggest beef with the game is that it takes a extremely long time to build up your dungeon with the high-end rooms, only to have the campaign chapter near the end or at the end.  The gold balance I think is decent, but the evilness balance in my opinion is not. _childDocuments_.review: Dungeons just has everything I want in a game. Its a solid game with very few issues. In my entire playthrough I ran into like 2 minor bugs, and it runs very smoothly with minimal performance issues. I would recommend you play dungeons 2 and 3 first and then jump into dungeons 4, as there's some story elements you might miss.Some things I enjoy are how you get evilness now. Before you had to capture certain locations that would slowly give you evilness, sure they would try and caprure it back but it took the good guys a while and you really only needed 1 site to get all the research you needed. Now you actually have to venture into the overworld and fight in order to get evilness, meaning you have to constantly leave the comfort of your dungeon if you want to scale up and get stronger.I also like how there is much more enemy variety. Sure at the end of the day you can kinda see them as healers, tanks, and DPS. But you tend to see most of them as their own unique threat and you would want to focus certain enemies down over others.A few things I disliked is how broken the horde faction seems to be. I would honestly say there isnt any reason to train anything other than horde units. They are the best early in the game due to how cheap they are to train. Sure they can die and you have to train a brand new one, but if you manage your troops properly you can prevent pretty much all of their deaths and wont have to train very many of them. They also have the best mid game, since once you get them to champion status, they get such an absurd power boost that they tend to beat everything with minimal effort until the best of the best heroes come out. They even have the best late game due to how good their potions are. Horde strength + speed boost just makes them roll over everything, and you will eventually be able to revive them so even if you somehow manage to lose a unit they just get revived. The other 2 factions really need a power boost to make them on par with horde.Another thing I dislike is how troops no longer work in rooms. In dungeons 3, you were encouraged to train units from each faction for 2 reasons, each faction had units you wanted in your army, and each faction had rooms you wanted in your dungeon since they made it better. In dungeons 4 however, you dont need troops from each faction as you can easily only go 1 faction and thats enough to beat the game, and since they dont work in rooms, you dont even need them to unlock everything you would want. You can easily go horde only and still get spells to max level and not suffer at all.Despite these issues, I still 100% the game on the hardest difficulty, so its still a very enjoyable game.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Had a lovely time playing trough campaing in coop with my son (6yo), he playing on Xbox me on Steam. Solid cross platform coop experiences and very enjoyable game.Was a bit sceptical at the beginning but was hooked after a few levels, with more rooms unlocked and starting to understand more how combat etc worked.Finally a modern dungeon keeper, that is most things a new dungeon keep should be. Good:- Good variation in the campaign, probably just long enough and with lots of different objectives.- Liked how every level ramps up and becomes intense and difficult in the end.- Achievements and how they are presented encourage you to play in different (often fun) ways and try out different factions, helping variety a lot.- Really fun building traps, and that it's more or less a constant flow of enemies into these traps (as original dungeon keeper didn't if I remember correctly. Would be fun to have more variation/even more trap types though.- Some graphical elements are really really nice, especially things down in the dungeon, for example the gold. Something really cozy about these types of glimmering treasure piles. Overall good looking game (important in the genre I'd argue) - 3 different factions is fun and pretty well made.Bad:- Narrator, and humour overall is annoying and awkward, the meta and pop culture reference writing is so done before and feels like it's written by a teenager. Unfortunate as it ruins the experience a bit. you have to just endure the cutscenes and VO, turn of narrator and enjoy the gameplay.- Would love to see more physics and hit reactions from traps, felt a bit immersion breaking the just walkthrough all things without flinching, but you get used to it, and at least the high level traps can move heroes around.- Gorgu summon too strong and cheap, avoiding using it on all levels where it was available. Felt like cheating.- Not steam game related, but xbox (X) performance is horrible. Final level looked like it was running at 10fps.Son absolutely loved the game. He needs some serious detox from it now I think. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I played a lot of Dungeons 3.  This is very similar.  Probably more similar than most sequels I can think of.  The story line continues with Thalya. Maybe you never played Dungeons 3, and like the idea of managing a dungeon.  Sounds like a possible fit for this game.  Maybe you loved Dungeons 3, and want more of the same.  This is your game.   You can play this pretty chill, on easy, making it more about doing whatever it is you want.  On harder levels, you are more constrained.  I think the traps are a bit better.  Spells are similar, but I think a bit better.  Potions add another tool in your toolbox.  One thing to note that if you love big armies, this game is better than D3. _childDocuments_.review: It's Dungeons, similar to #2 and #3 in the series, but different.I didn't care much for some aspects of the UI.  It looked fiddly at times, hard to see what you're clicking on.  And just not a very Dungeons style theme.  Likewise, the music didn't match too good.  One of the big UI complaints is that the stat boosting potion bottles are not visible on the minimap.  They can get stuck inside walls even after digging them out, so only a snot can grab it, and only if a potion room is built.  However, if you build the work stations there, normal potions make it hard to find the stat potions.  Gameplay, the stat potions are always consumed, never returned when you accidentally give a second potion to a unit that already had one.  And when you summon the Crowley demon, he does not appear on minimaps, nor does the Dungeon lord.  Otherwise, the gameplay seems ok.  Undead might be the best option, as it uses less evil, and can do the most damage, especially when you stack up all the minions, and make a massive (limited only by 3x3 dungeon space or crypts) army of undead.  MASSIVELY OP!  Mix with the Thalya perk that gives +1% damage for faction research, permanently slapped snots for faster economy, and evil heroes for faster research.The big failure of Dungeons 4 is the lack of map generation.  There's a map editor.  Good luck spending hours upon hours trying to figure out how to use the undocumented editor.  In Dungeons 3, enter a number from 1-65536 on most maps, and it randomly generates a map.  A user spends 5 seconds and has a new map.  This aids replayability MASSIVELY.  After 3 months, there's 17 maps made by users on mod.io, most of them are empty or duplicates of in-game maps or new maps, or otherwise really simplistic maps.  EPIC FAIL!  Rather than make a seed generated map, they opted to just bundle the map maker, and gave some excuse about auto map generation being too hard or impossible, boo hoo, excuses, excuses.  The text files of the map seem straightforward, but the map editor also generates some cryptic binary files.  If I or someone else can reverse engineer the file format, it'd be almost trivial to have a JS or Python script or something run on the web or cmdline and generate maps.  The real trick would be to include custom load screen and TTS auto generated voiceover assetts.  No excuses, just do it.

Orcs are ironhides your tanks, goblins turn into wolfriders with knockdown and very usefull buff to boots physical damage dealt to target, aka horde dmg. Naga serve again as healers and naga oracle is better in every way. New unit for Horde is Gnome, essentially Gob-o-bot AOE, very squishy but usefull for clearing clusters.Demon units suffer a bit if you want only demon army. Since Titan units are no more and arachnids are replaced demons have no dependable frontline fighter to hold the enemy. In return demons are dps machines, many have burn dots and new Gazer unit boots in AEO fire damage taken on enemy in AOE, which can be upgraded even further and since all demons have fire damage a good demon core and chew through early to mid game without any problem. Imps return as long range high dps snipers, infernals are some of the best AOE for your money, Gazers debuff enemy so your demon do more damage and succubi are valuable utility, beguiling with upgrades up to 2 units and reducing enemy armour, perfect for denying the enemy their beefy frontline, even if only for a while.Undead recieved the most love in Dungeons 4. With new units and mechanics full undead army is not only viable but one of the best you can have. No zombies or skeletons as regular units and not titan as the best tank but new units more than make up for it with their new mechanic. Each Undead unit can summon little minions who often benefit from unit upgrades and full undead army can become really large and ridiculous. Banshees are back and now very important debuffers since they reduce enemy cold damage resistance (as Gazers do for demons) and summons wraith minions. New Bone lord is similar to swordman hero, tanky and doing good damage with skeleton mage minions. New undead Vampire queen is the most important unit in entire undead roster since she can AOE heal ALL undead units in range, with upgrades her healing improves and even her minnions AOE heal, So if you have enough of these ladies your army becomes all but invincible to most enemies and can deal with enemy AOE. Nercomancer is a good debuffer and can provide healing too, good unit to fill the roster. Also you can turn enemy heroes into undead who can be upgraded to a real menace.Corrupted heroes are no more, only ghosts remain of them. You no longer convert enemy heroes and pray to RNG to get those you want. Now with new Ice tomb building at least 3x3 you can get 1 hero of your own choise, provided you have their corpse or imprisoned (and since you can teleport dead Overworld heroes into dungeon it's not hard to get who you want) so as long as you have room in dungeon you can legit have a true "hero" army 20+ units and not bad at all since they can be healed with Vampire queen and can be upgraded to cold damage. My ONLY gripe with ghost heroes is that unilke with corrupted they looks very simmilar (since all are ghosts) while in dungeons 3 corrupted heroes all have distinct colours and can be recognised with onle glance (with 5+ ghosts bunched a little close it becomes hard to see which unit is which) and although it's a minor thing it's a bit shame that your evil heroes look so lackluster compared to enemy and corrupted in dungeons 3EnemyForces of good now provide significantly greater challange, often coming with greater packs where focusing the squishy is often mandatory or their AOE and healers can grind even very durable armirs to dust (though I speak mostly late game, all tier 3 hero armies), new dryad hero gives you a good reason to invest in early AOe since their summon treants if massed enough can stall even early-mid armies while new warden elf unit provides a middle between swordman and stone guardTowers are now much more dangerous and not to be underestimated but you can now dodge some attacks.Base buildingCompared to dungeons 3 now EVERYTHING is done by snots, gold, mana, toolboxes.Creatures no lorger work AT ALL. So be carefull, ewvery building that needs operating can take snots wime from other tasks like building, gold mining ect. In my opinion it's a shame since now creatures in dungeon only fullfill their needs and aside from undead do nothing for the dungeon (in dungeons 3 brewery for example could be operated my horde creatures or snots), undead can generate blight for minion summons. Almost criminal misstep is however removal of magical toolboxes and automated magines, now you can only produce battery which provided TEMPORARY automation and must be dome manually (or at least I have not found out how to automatically, only finished 5th mission in campaing at this moment). So unline in D3 where every faction had a purpose (Horde with traps, demons with mana and undead with ressurects and magic toolboxes) now no faction is udefull in the dungeon aside from defending it (since you can get auto blish pretty easy)Presentaion (story, sound)Here is as at the start, if you liked D3 you will like D4. The story is classic Dungeons 3 humon (though a bit better imo, Tristan is a lot more entertaining than Tanos) and soundtrack is quite fitting and good combat music. ConclusionIf you finished D3 already then you can go full for it and probably with no regrets. But I do recommend you do Dungeons 3 before since quite a bit of the refferences are on the previous game and the previous game offers a lot of scirmish, good campaing and especially clash of the gods DLC are really worth it (although I enjoyed all DLC)8-9/10 depening on how much you played D3 since here there are some QoL changes for the better but is not as polished since it's much younger game. IMO worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: A really big improvement on Dungeons 3! The essence of the game is the same, but you can tell that they went and rethought all the game mechanics and how they fit together. The mechanics feel very cleaned up, e.g. being able to queue buildings without enough resources to build them, a much better research layout, factions that make a lot more sense (Dungeons 3 seemed to want you to diversify between factions while simultaneously punishing you for doing so), streamlined pop mechanics (no more ~5 different types of units which you had to maximize all of for popcap reasons), much roomier and more interesting dungeons, better-feeling traps, etc. The new graphics are gorgeous.By far the biggest change is how much more chaotic the games feel. In dungeons 3 you could kind of get away with rushing a few islands of evilness, turtling in your dungeon while you built up, and then clearing out the map in one big swoop. Dungeons 4 does a fantastic job of addressing this. It isn't super clear in the early missions, where things are still pretty easy, but all the new systems really come together to put pressure on you. Dwarves/Spiders/Lavalumps aren't that scary on their own, but when you're busy with other things they can be a constant and annoying thorn in your side. Due to the lack of passive evilness you have to be much more active on the campaign map, both doing things at your own pace (e.g. killing good creatures and hero bases) and at the game's pace (intercepting construction crews and shipments). Things can get really tense on the highest difficulty, with more threats than you can manage at once!The factions feel a lot better now. In dungeons 3 I felt pushed towards a horde-focused build every game with maybe a few supporting demons, because the other factions didn't really have much of a frontline on their own and the undead in particular were just underwhelming. Demons feel the strongest in 4, but all the factions still feel rewarding to play. The spells and new potions are super fun to use.In general there's no one thing which you can point to to say "this single thing makes 4 a huge step up from 3," but as you see more and more of the new mechanics you really come to appreciate how much they've improved.The game isn't perfect--there are a few issues, like arenas and torture chambers feeling a bit vestigial. The difficulty is spotty at times: there are a few missions which I just sort of steamrolled, in particular many of the earlier ones. But overall it feels great, and if you liked 3 you're in for a treat.

_childDocuments_.review: Realmforge have done it again. They've produced another fine instalment of the Dungeon's saga and it's brilliant. It retains consistency with previous series but with changes that keep it feeling 'fresh'. Personally, I love the comedy - the designers clearly had some fun making this and the narrators continue to ensure we have a chuckle too along the way. I feel they've listened to previous feedback too. This time the little snots did all the work, including mana production and traps, and so freed the creatures. The developers also looked to address Dungeons 3 feedback where people generally felt it was a bit too easy - not me but then I'm rubbish. This time I think they tried to allow more flexibility so people can find their own balance of challenge vs patience. So gone are the colossus of Dungeons 3, this time you don't have the same power units and also I found the traps less effective.Improvements? Maybe I have the attention span of a gnat but I felt many mission features weren't properly explained and so took me a while to realise - like what to do with the crystals or the artefacts. Anyway. Looking forward to D5 in another 4-5 yrs time.

_childDocuments_.review: A definite improvement in (just about) every area from Dungeons 3.  They did this right.  The missions are more varied, the dialogue no longer makes me wish for a corkscrew to puncture my eardrums with, the play is more active and engaged (you can no longer turtle below ground and just wait to grow stronger), there is now a skirmish mode (albeit with fixed maps).  The snots even level up, something that was in games like this 20+ years ago, so snot management is no longer a large part of the game.There are of course, a few annoyances.  The "enemies in the dungeon" announcement is inconsistent, so you have to monitor the dungeon map even with fighting in the overworld.  The skirmish maps are fixed, so once you master one, there isn't much more to do with it.  The horde tree is the new undead, I develop it last, if at all, as the larger armies somehow translate into losing creatures more easily, and they are the only ones who do not come with an immediate way to revive (and the potions just don't seem to be worth it).  The traps are less effective than in 3, which is probably a good thing, as it means that you cannot make an impregnable dungeon and just ignore it while above ground, but when coupled with the "enemies in the dungeon" announcement bug, leads to rushing back to defend a dungeon heart under attack somewhat frequently.  Lastly, while I figure everything out eventually, an intro or explanation of changes between games (in things like how evil is gathered, the fact that diamond veins are not the end all of money generation, the torture chamber now just generates evilness - conversion is in the undead tree, etc.) would have been very welcome.But that is all nitpicks.  The "Meet the Spartans" style jokes, where referring to something everyone knows is supposed to be funny, are blessedly, incredibly rare.  The game is more fun than the previous one, and that's what really matters.I'd love to see more skirmish maps, and even randomly made ones.  I'd love for a dungeon vs. dungeon mode.  But those are hopes for the inevitable deluge of DLCs (if this is anything like 3).

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute joy to play. It has all the terrific bits from Dungeons 3 and mad it even better and more enjoyable than ever before. The little Snots and a the evil creatures under your control will get you hooked on the game in no time. The developers nailed it, this was exactly what I was hoping for from a sequel to the mighty enjoyable and hilarious Dungeons 3 and oh boy did they deliver. Lastly the co-op experience is just as streamlined and awesome as the previous game. TL:DR: If you enjoyed the previous installment than this is a must have. The upgrade paths for everything is just too expansive and you end up feeling like you are playing a managerial/sim type game  rather than a straight out dungeon brawler. Resource management and levelling up was always part of Dungeon Keeper , but it was not as in your face as what it is in this game. Lots of the upgrade choices seemed quite pointless during gameplay , while others were a necessity . _childDocuments_.review: Dungeons 4 is a safe sequel.  It revises aspects of the previous game and demonstrates why those revisions were necessary to improve nearly all aspects of the game play.  There is a major balance problem that, although not a review-killer in itself when the majority of your hours will likely be single player, does impact the diversity of choice or the perception of that in the least.The balance of the three Creature factions against each other is underwhelming in that there is little to be thought of outside of what works best in the context you're in and then following the upgrade path down.  That is, each faction works well in different situations but outside of a couple powerful options buried deep in their research tree there is little reason to invest in multiple Creature types.  You might want to get some Hero killing done ASAP and begin with Demons but later on in the Mission you could pump some Evil into the Horde tree to get potions that make up for the lack of healing and buffs.  Likewise vice-versa for the Demon's utility Spells and the Horde's generalist play style.  Where this becomes a problem is in the third faction, Undead, who are overwhelmingly powerful after a small period of necessary scaling in the very early stages of a Mission.  They exponentially raise in DPS, defence, and healing after completing just a few simple "Intercept", or "Good being", side objectives and go on to crush almost everything with little input from the player outside of clicking in the direction of your objective.  They even have their own built-in Evil generator to get the snowball rolling as soon as possible with their Prison.This means that outside of completing the many challenging time-sensitive achievements that amount to optional difficulty there is little reason to avoid mainlining the Undead faction and not having much to do since there is no additional mechanic that supplements the click-and-attack style of combat in the main meat of the tactical portion, the Overworld, as the other factions do with Spells and Potions.  Instead of a list of abilities tacked on to the side of the screen with many options after researching and building the appropriate Room, you instead are encouraged to research one point into the Undead's equivalent of the corrupted Heroes from the previous game and dump as many bodies there as you like for an endless ghost army that only adds to the snowball effect putting any other method of completing Missions to shame.This remains a positive review because this is the only problem with the game I have encountered so far 20 hours in and completing the majority of the available Missions including their achievements.   This state is hopefully temporary with the game receiving patches.  It's unfortunate that something like releasing a game that works upon release is something worth praising today but Kalypso gets the benefit of that I suppose.

_childDocuments_.review: Mega Dungeon Keeper fan here. Pretty sure I’m one of the 1 % of people out there who has played that game the most. JUST GUSSING, but I have hundreds of hours in DK 1.Why does that matter here? Well, DK-esk RTS games are not exactly a commonality. I have DK on GOG which is great whenever the urge hits (which it unbelievably still does).Dungeons takes the DK formula and makes it its own thing. It does not hide its inspiration; nor does it need to. This is a modern twist on DK. Dungeons 3 is the only other entry in the series that I’ve played besides 4. 3 is amazing, and I strongly recommend you go there first. Not because of story reasons or anything like that. It’s just fantastic.I was so excited when I saw Dungeons 4 was coming. I’m glad to say that it does not disappoint! I have about 200 hours in 3. I’ve beaten it thrice, twice on hard. All the DLCs. 4 changes some things, most are for the better. There is a deemphasis on microing which I don’t love, but respect. 4 instead focuses more on interesting choices for how to upgrade, and develop your dungeon and your strategy.I’m not going to write you a guide for how to play, tempted, but it’s not the place for that. The game is good, but there are some bugs, no game breaking stuff, but some annoyances. For example, I missed out on at least three perks despite achieving what they asked. Though it is possible I misinterpreted the “achievement”, but unlikely.Dungeons 4 is really, really good if this is your type of game. There are more options, and the game has much better unit balance than 3 where it was all about Orcs, Nagas and Imps (and some titans); the rest of the roster just wasn’t really worth it, and there were at least a few units that were genuinely bad, and unplayable on hard (more or less).The game play loop of defend, attack, build, maintain and upgrade is still there. Yet, all the new stuff and the changes to the rosters, upgrades and enemies – forces you to adjust and rethink. The dungeons themselves are also more exciting adding bodies of water and lava to the mix as well as better layouts and other secrets worth your time. It’s not DK 1 level of smacktacular dungeon layout, but it’s a huge step up as that is a very lacking aspect of dungeons 3. They could have done a bit more, and I expect they will in, potentially-hopeful, DLC.The only real negative I have is that it runs worse in late game. If you build out your dungeon a lot, and max out your army: the game will struggle a bit. It’s not game breaking, but it does feel a bit bad to be punished with poorer performance just because you want to ♥♥♥♥ around, and build out to max. It could be my PC, but I doubt it. I fall well within the recommended system specs, and I got a decent PC that I built myself two years ago.I could ramble on, but they only thing I can really say is that if you like DK and those types of games – this is a great one, and I’m extremely happy with it so far. If you are more into traditional RTS games, or modern RTS games that doesn’t even have any type of base-building; this game could feel off. Check out some video reviews, and get a feel for it.Questions about the game? Leave a comment, I’d be happy to assist =)

_childDocuments_.review: I completed Dungeons 4 over the weekend, and yeah, it's an enjoyable RTS / Management game and a good addition to the series.I have completed Dungeons 2, I have played quite a bit of Dungeons 3 (but got distracted and stopped) and therefore Dungeons 4 was pretty much an insta-purchase having enjoyed the games in the series.Dungeons 1 doesn't count as it is a very different game and the 2nd title is where the series actually starts really 😊If you know the Dungeon Keeper games from the 90s, then you know what this game is, however if not... essentially in a role reversal of all of the classic games you have played were you take the role of the hero raiding Dungeons and killing the bad guy, in these games you are the bad guy (Ultimate Evil), running the dungeon, stopping heroic incursions and mustering your evil forces against the power of good! You also play as Thalya (pictured) the Ultimate Evils Dark Elf general, which joined the forces of badness in the previous game.As your Dungeon is under ground, running the games namesake takes the form of mining through the underworld to find gold and other treasures (or perils), building rooms to keep you minions happy (such as fighting pits, torture chambers or even an undead disco), creating arcane spaces store and harvest mana which fuel magic spells, workshops to build traps and other contraptions (such as the Frankenstein inspired lab to resurrect dead creatures) as well as a number of other rooms and things to manage.Where the Dungeons series deviates from its "Dungeon Keeper" inspiration however, is that you can also leave your dungeon and send your forces out to the overworld, taking the evil fight to the forces of good directly.When doing do, the game turns into a command & conquer style RTS, ordering your minions around, attacking hero strongholds and murdering light infused mini bosses such as unicorns and elemental crystal giants.Personally, I think it's great and works really well. Minimal micromanagement, for the most part you can tell your forces what to attack and leave them to it, while you switch back to the Dungeon to continue it's management (or whatever)Your rooms and forces are upgraded via research, across 4 separate research trees, 1 for the Dungeon itself, and 3 others for the 3 groups of evil minions you can recruit.These themes would be the Horde (i.e. Greenskins of various types), Demons, and the Undead. All have their strengths and weaknesses and all level up through battle, learning new skills and abilities as they go.You are free to mix and match your troops between all 3 groups, however of course each group requires their own rooms and management to stay happy and ready for battle, so... pick your poison.The whole series is very tongue in cheek and self aware, it isn't serious at all, and is very much the moustache twirling big evil laugh version of fantasy bad guys versus such heroes of virtue and nobleness that they are also a parody of themselves.Whether the comedy lands for you will be a matter of taste, but I liked it's light hearted jokes and digs at fantasy tropes etc.So yeah, good game. But so is D2 and D3. It isn't a complex management sim by any means, but it's engaging enough and entertaining enough to be good evil fun.

_childDocuments_.review: . .Realmforge Studios and Kalypso Media continue their Dungeon Keeper-inspired saga with Dungeons 4, a game that treads familiar ground while offering a devilishly delightful experience in the world of dungeon management. Let’s take a look at the game’s narrative, gameplay, humour, and overall performance, exploring whether it successfully builds upon its predecessors or falls into the trap of repetitiveness .The fourth instalment kicks off with what seems like a decisive battle gone awry for the Absolute Evil and its minions. As they seize control of the land, a few valiant heroes persist in resisting their tyrannical rule. Notably, Thalya, the Evil’s most trusted servant, and her not-so-brilliant brother play pivotal roles in the unfolding chaos. The game weaves a humorous tale, laden with comedy, pop culture references, and meta elements that are cleverly integrated into the scripts.The abundance of dialogue, both from the narrator and in-game characters, contributes to the comedic atmosphere. However, the option to adjust the frequency of these dialogues proves essential, as the charm wears thin, occasionally bordering on distracting and annoying.Dungeons 4 follows a straightforward gameplay loop – progress through the story-driven campaign, which strikes a balance between length and engagement. The campaign introduces new gimmicks and situations regularly, preventing monotony. However, the game grapples with the common issue of repetitiveness found in many management sims. Waiting for resources to accumulate or manoeuvring armies through convoluted paths extends the levels artificially, occasionally testing the patience of players.The core base-building and combat systems, honed over four games, remain robust. New additions and streamlining enhance the overall experience, making it addictive. While managing the dungeon, the role of Snots, diminutive goblin-like creatures, becomes crucial. Their tasks, from farming resources to maintaining the system, contribute to the intricate web of gameplay mechanics.Strategic decision-making, inherent in most management sims and RTS titles, becomes prominent as objectives escalate, requiring effective multitasking against mounting pressure from adversaries.Despite the complexity of scenarios, the game provides numerous opportunities to exploit its mechanics. The developers encourage players to discover unconventional strategies, be it rushing to find endless diamond deposits, leveraging specific trap combinations, or exploiting the F2 key shortcuts. While not a cakewalk, the scenarios demand effective multitasking, offering a smooth ride for those well-versed in the game’s mechanics.Beyond the Campaign mode, Dungeons 4 opens avenues for cooperative play and a flexible Skirmish mode, offering different scenarios based on the campaign. This mode accepts modifiers unlocked through story progression, allowing dedicated players to experiment with dungeon builds and systems. The performance on the PC version is commendable, with no crashes or stuttering observed, showcasing a game that runs smoothly even during busy and resource-intensive moments.The PC version of the game delivers near-perfect performance, with no crashes or stuttering and a consistent framerate even during intense moments. The slightly dated technology behind Dungeons 4 contributes to its stability, with a colourful and easily readable art style reminiscent of Warcraft III. While some might perceive the game as sticking closely to its roots, it manages to achieve a clear vision without unnecessary complications. The intentional continuity may be seen as a strength, maintaining a delicate balance that has proven successful over the years.In the realm of RTS and management sims, Dungeons 4 stands as a testament to its legacy. The game offers an enjoyable experience for players familiar with the series, striking a balance between innovation and preservation. While some may yearn for more drastic changes, the deliberate approach taken by Realmforge Studios and Kalypso Media ensures a game that stays true to its essence.The success and enjoyment derived from Dungeons 4 hinge on players’ expectations. For those anticipating a continuation of the series’ evolution, the game delivers a satisfying experience with room to grow into something more memorable. Conversely, those looking for something new may find themselves disappointed. As the Absolute Evil reigns supreme once again, Dungeons 4 remains a worthy addition to the dungeon management genre, embracing the dark legacy with humour and strategic depth.

I wouldn't buy until they fix the stability issues.---You've already wasted enough time reading this review. Go buy the game, full price or via a Humble Monthly subscription for 20% off. You know, I grew up playing Command and Conquer. The dad-jokes and humor written as playful sci-fi badassery really stuck with me. It had a vibe I can only call "90's optimistic goofiness" present in Hercules: The Legendary Journeys, Xena: Warrior Princess, Star Trek, etc.This game passes the vibe check, from the badass metal title music with samples of chanting and evil chuckles to the continued banter between the narrator and on-screen characters. Nothing in the game is remotely hateful or bigoted. It's just straight up a delightful experience.I bought this at near full price and fully support purchasing it at full price. At $30, it will be an absolute steal. It beats the absolute tar out of Starfield.The only con is that there will be DLC, which if it's like Dungeons 3 will be voice acted, goofy, and well worth buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't gotten far yet, just the demo and the first chapter beyond that (life got busy) but so far I am VERY happy with a lot of the changes they did to the game. :D1. More units for each type of monster! The undead now have bone lords and vampires queens (so far,) the demons get infernals and beholders, and gnomes join the horde (no not that kind of gnome.) _childDocuments_.review: Played the demo back during the Next Fest so I knew what I was getting myself into, I tried going back to playing the 3rd game in the series that I bought on sale recently, but found it much more clunky to play. Personally I love the improvements they have made in this release, might not be for everyone but mechanically to me it feels the best the series has ever been, gets an easy thumbs up from me, and is an easy jump in point for folks who might not have played much of the series so far. And yes I played Dungeon Keeper back in the Bullfrog days before EA murdered them, and I don't get why everyone seems to want a rehash of an older game in every dungeon management title, however good it was, the year is not 1997 anymore and games aren't the same as they were back then.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished the last mission and unlocked the last achievement so now I can totally tell more about the game.First of all, the experience was very enjoyable, I really loved that, and I was not disappointed at all after the perfect Dungeons 2 and 3 games. The game is not revolutionary, in fact, it feels like a great stand-alone addon to Dungeons 3 which felt great on its own and was a great improvement to Dungeons 2 and a quality-of-life improvement to Dungeons 3. This game lacks the feeling of being completely unique. However if you've played Dungeons 3, this game fixes all the hiccups that game had - for example you can build traps WAY easier and faster than before. The story is fun and interesting and it's really great to meet Thalya and Narrator once again! But I guess the ongoing joke of 'game designers and writers did a bad job designing this mission' went a little bit too far since it was repeated way too often which made me feel like this is true in a way. But other than that I really loved that. The humour still rocks so much!!! The characters and their voice overs are just something else. Love all the jokes and the dialogues between the heroes and Narrator, been laughing a lot during this game. The game improved already great formula of Dungeons 3 in every way: it's more beautiful, it's fun, it's interesting and addictive, it's relaxing and enjoyable. It offers much bigger maps and armies which might include almost a 100 units in your group which is impressive. The game is still easy to learn, basically the horde is cheap and weak, the demons are more powerful and expensive and the undead are the most expensive and strong. Basically you can learn one or two tactics that work for you and use those in every mission. There were some units I never ever hired at all in any mission through the game. I wish there would be a PVP mode with two dungeons fighting one against the other or one player being the absolute evil and the other playing as the dwarves or as the good ones on the surface. Some generated maps would be great, too, so each experience would be even more unique. It took me 47 hours to complete everything this game has to offer and I loved that. The only thing missing for me is the ability to build on each and every square which is currently limited by lava / water. Thanks for keeping the series alive! It was fun and I would love to see new installments in the series in the future and some DLCs for this one.P.S.: a couple of words about console version, too, as I bought D3-4 for Xbox as well. D3 was a VERY questionable low quality port with serious performance issues and hard to learn controls. D4 fixes it all! Works like a charm and it's way easier to control! So for console versions I'd say that D4 is a more significant change from D3 compared to PC.

_childDocuments_.review:
The Absolute Evil and its trusted *cough* servant, the Dark Elf Thalya, return in Dungeons 4 after the events of its fabulous predecessor to bring about their triumph over the forces of good once more.

Build a cozy and comfortable Dungeon to suit your creatures' needs and rule over them, then send them out into the Overworld to kindly remind the good people living there that the Absolute Evil rules over their lands.

Gather your Evilness in new and dynamic ways and unleash it upon the lush green forests and plains of the Overworld to turn them over to the dark side. But make sure that your Dungeon is well-secured by traps and defended by your creatures, for those pesky Overworlders won't just twiddle their thumbs while you turn their land into the Absolute Evil's most pleasurable holiday paradise.
