_childDocuments_.review: Woah, this is 20 bucks normal price? I'm all for being paid for your work, but there definitely isn't $20 worth of content. It's sad, because this game seems like it has tons of potential, but potential isn't really value. The loddle growing system is oddly barebones for being the game's namesake, it felt like a good idea that wasn't fully realized. Where most growing sims have multiple stages between child and adult, this one jumps straight between the two in a tiny amount of time, no more than 30 minutes.The main game (which is somehow almost completely divorced from the loddles) doesn't have a whole lot to offer. It's cozy at face value, but when you play it for more than a couple hours, every little error becomes blazingly apparent. If you've cleaned one object, you've cleaned them all. There's nothing that really gives you a fun visual progression like similar games do, you pretty much just delete blobs off of an object with no change to the thing besides a couple procedural plants growing on the surface in the exact same way as everything else in the region.The 'limiting' mechanics are mostly just annoyances that shatter flow state. Oxygen management is only a chore that causes you to pivot every few minutes to go refill. Even at max capacity upgrades, it's just short enough that it would be an annoyance if it wasn't for the constant inventory bloat that causes you to trek cross-map to deposit your items. There were plenty of times that I looked at early-game trash on the ground and said "no" simply because it'd end up taking up the inventory slot on my way to pick up the other item bloat. That seems kinda counterproductive in a game about cleaning, doesn't it?It's sad, but this definitely doesn't pass the dollars to hours requirement, that's for sure. Looking back, I'm glad it doesn't, I don't think I'd want to play it that long.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: ***SPOILERS FOR ANYONE THAT CARES ABOUT THE NON EXISTENT STORY AND GAMEPLAY***€20 for less than 4 hours of gameplay. Mind you, over an hour and a half was probably spent cleaning up non-essential areas. I also left it running in the background while eating dinner, so that's another 30 minutes. Basically 1,5 hours worth of gameplay, and that's including the probable 30 minutes where I was just running back and forth to my base to recycle all the trash. Sure, you can evolve your loddles and tend to them, but that was barely implemented to the gameplay. They actually discouraged you from helping loddles. Because if you don't have a bubble ring to clean them, they will follow you around if you get too close and contaminate things around them, wasting your time. So I just cleaned the place up and left them there until I was completely done cleaning.Graphics are pretty good, story is non existent unless you're a literal toddler, no plot twist because it's revealed in the first 15 minutes of playing if you just read the first two holos you find. The gameplay gets lame really quick. You get new tools, but they are just there to stretch out already boring gameplay. I also forgot to empty my new tool multiple times because you barely use it. The inventory restriction is just there to extend the gameplay. I don't even know what happens when you run out of oxygen, but I'm assuming it puts you back at your base, because I ran out of oxygen while being AFK for 30+ minutes. So, yeah. Not a challenge in any way shape or form.The game hints at you getting fruit harvesting robots. The game hints at you seeing a huge sea creature. The game hints at you getting to investigate a dubious chemical leak. None of these actually happen. You just find their HQ and find out that the CEO tried bringing a loddle to the next planet they were gonna trash. Then the game is basically over.This game has less content than Hades 2, which is still in early access and costs €30. Not the best comparison, but it's a relevant one. There are barely any upgrades for your equipment. It was 2 upgrades for your first tool and 1 per tool for the other 2 you get.TL;DR Graphics are good, story sucks, loddles are not implemented well, many elements of the game are made to waste your time, there are not a lot of upgrades to chase making all materials abundant half way through the game, the soundtrack isn't very impressive (does it have one?), the game teases upcoming content and then the game is over, the cleanup gets boring real quick, the cleanup is 90% of effective gameplay, your assistant is really annoying and thinks you're a moron, lacking content, waste of time, money and expectations. TL;DRx10It's lame and your expectations are way too high.

_childDocuments_.review: The only saving grace of this game is that I got it basically for free thanks to Humble Bundle. I just finished the game, 100% completion, in under 4 hours. _childDocuments_.review: Loddlenaut is a cutesy third person adventure game where you clean up the ocean floor on an alien planet, and there's not much else to it really.  I think there's a scope for cutesy cleanup games if they're made well, but Loddlenaut is not made well. One important note is that even though this is an amateur project, it does seem to be sincerely and genuinely made.  I couldn't find any flipped assets, plagiarism or any other kind of insincere actions from the developer, but unfortunately genuine intentions alone are not enough to produce a brilliant PC gaming experience.The biggest problem with the game here is that the developer simply did not bother to test the game on Windows (yet it never got the console release it seems to have been intended for).  If they had tested the game, they would have noticed they locked out the mouse from the menu (it's always in the middle of the screen), but improperly, so no matter how you try to navigate the menu, because the mouse pointer is in the middle of the screen, you can't choose any menu option apart from the one in the middle.  It's ridiculous they didn't test their game properly.  What this means is you can't customise the controls or visuals, making this an immediate, utter failure.  It doesn't meet the absolute minimum standards for any PC game. The game assets are fairly mediocre/low quality, in some places they appear mismatched... Ultimately the quality of these assets, and thus the overall visual quality is lower than average, and low quality always makes for a less than optimal gaming experience.  Remember, we're looking for the best of the best of 100,000+ games on Steam.The game features lazy low-polygon "retro" assets with crap 2D retro pixel "art" filters on them, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the early 1990s.  This very poor quality visual style is a method that lazy devs often use to disguise their lack of talent/interest in doing the graphics properly and trying to disguise it under the name of "art", or "We made it look bad on purpose", which really isn't something gamers should have to put up with.  It's unclear why the developers weren't willing to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets and high resolution textures for the game.  It looks bad as a result of their decisions, worse, it doesn't authentically recreate the 1990's vibe the developer is hoping people will accept instead of doing their job properly, and that's just another reason to avoid it.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Loddlenaut has the pathetically optimistic price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.For comparison, the $20 asking price for this game could get you games like "Ghostrunner", "The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt" or "Dead by Daylight".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so simple and cute; it's easy to get lost in the music and graphics and spend hours just floating around, cleaning trash and, finding loddles. The premise and controls are straightforward.I had a lot of fun figuring out what I could do with the different loddles and just exploring. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Now THIS is a cozy game. Calm, open ocean exploration, simple cooking, adorable critters, and feel-good environmentalism to boot! This is everything I wanted Subnautica to be and more. I want to be able to say I wish it was longer but I actually think the length was perfect for the number of upgrades you can get to equipment. My only qualms to the devs: I wish you could see how many times a loddle has already laid eggs because otherwise it makes for tedious guesswork when trying to max out the biome populations, and I wish it were possible to feed follower loddles without releasing them--I feel so bad for babies I find in new biomes but I don't want to have to backtrack to drop them off. Otherwise the perfect way to spend a couple evenings.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun and cozy game! Enough there for those who love to collect, as well as those just looking for a short story. The only downside was that I didn't balance the game play well enough and had to spend a couple of hours (after finishing everything else) to get the last achievement, "Loddles Rule the World".
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: If you like chill games to play whilst you're doing something else or just to relax to this game is for you. The entire game has a comfy vibe even when its dirty and it makes you feel amazing when you help clean up the environment and get rid of all the trash. Would fully recommend and absolutely loved playing this game. Can't wait to see what else the studio comes up with.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

I kept running out of oxygen when I first started playing.. but after pausing to read a few online guides I learnt to manage that better, THEN the game became pretty relaxing to play.

I see the relation, given the real time changing pet feature. I do wish it were a bit more fleshed out, maybe requiring 3 of fruit type A and 1 type B, rather than 1A, 1B, 1C = unique. Inspired by Chao's evolution, based on highest stat, and changing in real time as stats increase / decrease.80% of game play is power washer simulater, scan for mess, point and click to clean. Remaining 20% is achievement hunting and loddle raising.*achievement for maximum loddle population includes your home base. But I do not believe they can reproduce in base. As such, you have to bring Loddles to your home to fullfill 100%. (Took me a  short while to figure out)

It has an addicting game play loop, cute characters There's no violence in it.  It's a charming game.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: A great, sweet little game, absolutely recommend it. I got it half off on sale, which felt like a good price, since it is a short game. I finished the game in about 7 hours but I'm looking forward to going back to complete it.  A nice, calm resource management game without the stress of min maxing things. And you can pet the cute animals.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I saw that the creators said they were inspired by the Chao Gardens from the old Sonic games and I ran to buy this game. I was not disappointed. I enjoyed every minute of this game. The mechanics are perfectly built. The cleanup aspect is not too hard, just enough to be REALLY satisfying. The Loddles are adorable and collecting he different forms and colours is so fun. I hope these creators make more games in a similar vein to this!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: There aren't many games that I simply wanted to go on forever. This is one of them.You are an astronaut on an underwater planet, which has been left polluted with debris. Your mission is to clean up the planet, and make it clean again. Incidentally, this planet is inhabited by "Loddles," whose populations you're able to care for and help flourish.The gameplay was relatively simple, and the atmosphere was among the most relaxing I've played. It gave me a very similar feeling to playing "Lake," by which I mean it was very easy to find yourself simply puttering about and relaxing, worried less about any goals in the game and more about enjoying yourself, which I feel is high praise.Gameplay wise, I felt like there was some mix of Powerwash Simulator, as you clean up the planet, combined with a Pokemon game, because you're collecting and protecting the Lottles as you go. (Specifically, I thought of Pokemon Ranger, since your interactions with the nature are less ones of capturing and training, and more about interacting and caring for the Lottles.)Overall, this was just a great game, and all I wish is that it were longer!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game. I played the demo a little while back and waited for the game to go on sale. I bought it a couple days ago and have since beat the game. It's relatively short but it's super calm and relaxing with nice music and a fun design. I don't think I would have ever purchased at the full price as the game does not have enough content for its price tag. Still, it's a nice game and I'd definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: The game is amazing and I enjoyed playing it, nice and relaxing like most cleaning games. But, this game honestly isn't worth $20 for how little there is. I beat the actual game in only 4 hours and only spent another 5 hours to 100% the game by getting all achievements which was more tedious than fun, but did it to try and feel like it was worth buying. Luckily I got it on sale at $10 but you really shouldn't consider buying it at full price, just wait until it's on sale. Other than that, amazing game with a nice story, just wish there was more content. Maybe they'll add more eventually but in it's current state, only buy it when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game! It is very relaxing, very chill, the graphics are nice, and there's nothing scary. It's a small game, it took me around 8 hours to finish the whole thing, but I didn't get all the achievements either. It's worth buying at a discount. I would 10/10 recommend! _childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely adorable! I received a copy as a prize on Twitch while watching a friend play it, but I will absolutely be recommending it to all my friends in the cozy gaming space. It's a wonderful blend of a cleaning simulator, crafting game, cozy swimming adventure, and raising the Loddles feels very similar to raising tamagotchi creatures. It's quite short, but so simple and comforting that I can absolutely see myself 100% this a few times, like coming back to it like a good book from time to time. The biggest thing for me personally though, is it's attention to conservation awareness and the way it's designed to remind you how good you can feel for doing something that is good for other creatures. I think this game could be a wonderful learning tool for young people that's also super cute and fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: such a lovely cosy game. i had so much fun playing this, i got super invested and honestly didnt want it to end. i might end up replaying it in the future! managed to snag the game for a pound on cdkeys as well so i have no complaints at all. i love the fluidity of movement and how smooth everything is, it is very satisfying <3
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing and adorable game cleaning a planets ocean and taking care of the Loddles (alien fish), which you can feed the babies to make them into different forms of Loddles!I also adore the new update, I already cleaned almost everything possible before it and getting a little reward of golden equipment and an updated ending was really nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adore this game. I loved it when I played it the first time around--the music, atmosphere, art, everything was top notch. There was initially no organization for the loddles, but in the goddles update, you now have a "loddlepedia" to track which variations you've discovered as well as how to create more of a particular evolution. For a game that is only supposed to give you 7hrs of playtime, I got way more out of it and so much enjoyment as well. I found it a little hard to feed a loddle particular kinds of food to get them to evolve into a certain loddle because you'd either have to have space in your home cove or have them follow you as you feed them. Maybe this was just an issue for me because I liked having all the loddle variations in my home cove so I had no extra space, but overall it didn't detract from my play through. It is such a relaxing experience, there's so much to explore and cleaning the pollution is super satisfying. Plus the loddles are just so stinkin cute! I highly recommend this game! 🩵

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really cute and fun game to play! Loved the cleaning and upgrading parts, but I didn't enjoy the creature part as much.. I wish there was more customisation and plants in the home cave, to make it more fun to look after the creatures. I finished the game but will definitely play it all over  again,  no doubt :)
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, the core gameplay of Loddlenaut is surprisingly addictive. You get to swim through beautifully rendered underwater landscapes while cleaning up trash and nurturing cute little creatures called loddles which make for a calming yet rewarding experience. I loved how each task, from cleaning up pieces of litter to feeding my little creatures, felt like it contributed to restoring the ecosystem. The progression system is well-paced, with each new upgrade bringing meaningful enhancements to my tools and the environment.Secondly, the narrative, though simple, complements the gameplay perfectly. It’s nice to play a game that raises awareness about ocean pollution and how Loddlenaut makes it better is it shows how small actions can lead to a big impact.The gentle soundtrack and soothing sound effects create a calming atmosphere that makes this a perfect game to unwind with after a long day. Hearing the loddles chirp is actually one of the cutest things I've experienced playing this.Although Loddlenaut leans more towards relaxation than challenge, the steady progression and satisfying visuals give it plenty of replay value, especially if you enjoy completing every achievement and fully restoring the ocean. While it doesn’t have the survival elements of Subnautica, Loddlenaut shares a similar appeal in exploration and discovery, focusing more on relaxing gameplay than high-stakes challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Talk about a gem of a game! So relaxing and cozy... I was hooked after the first 10 minutes. I used a PS5 controller and it worked flawlessly. You can remap every action on your keyboard or controller which was nice. The music was a perfect fit and sometimes made me not want to switch zones so I could keep listening. I would've loved to keep playing if there was more stuff to do :)
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful, amazing, feel-good, adorable, satisfying. What more could you want? Also, I played it on launch day and had a bunch of feedback, and everything I asked for was fixed/implemented in a game-appropriate way. Some attentive devs right there. I came back to play the new update, decided to play through the whole game again, and was so impressed to see all the quality of life things they'd implemented. My playtime per file was roughly 6 hours, but I could easily see it being longer or shorter depending on your play style (and how much time you invest in loddle farming).
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute, relaxing and colorful. This game is my power fantasy. Cried at the end. ;_; <3Although the world seems like a very dark place, and feels like greedy, rich polluters are getting their way despite all the resistance, we gotta keep fighting the good fight for all dem critters of the Earth and the people who make adorable games like this./smuggles a loddle off the planet
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I restarted this game because I loved it so much. It's very much a chillax/cozy game about swimming around and cleaning up the ocean. You can even find cute little creatures to hang out with as you work. There is some resource management to upgrade your suit/cleaning tools but it's so rewarding when you recycle all the trash you collected. Highly recommend, especially if your special interest is the sea/marine biology or you just want a nice cozy game. Also yes, there is an oxygen meter, but it's super easy to combat when you unlock a certain tool! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Randomly came across this while looking for fish keeping games and oh my gosh what a diamond gem i stumbled upon! this is exactly the type of game i was looking for. i LOVE the breeding and farming aspect, especially all the shapes and color variants you can find or make by cross breeding. even though the story part of the game is relatively short i know i'm going to get hours more just perfecting my sanctuary! this game is the perfect blend of other games i've spent countless hours on like abzu, subnautica & slime rancher. if you like taking care of creatures, growing fruit, uncovering mysteries and powerwashing goop off of surfaces with cute little tools this game is a MUST play! Super highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: As I finished it I said out loud without meaning to "what a lovely game".Worth the full price? YMMV. On sale? If you want a cute cosy game, absolutely. Power Wash Simulator meets Slime Rancher, but cuteness multiplied by 100.Got all achievements in about 9 hours without looking anything up, main story quest is probably 5-7 hours depending on gameplay style.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Loddlenaut is a very relaxing mix of PowerWash Simulator and a pet simulator. The game takes place entirely underwater where you are tasked to clean up pollution left behind by a large corporation. In removing the goop, litter, and microplastics in the area, you can also encounter loddles to rescue, feed, and evolve into different forms based on their diet. However, the game doesn't pressure you into spending all your time on the loddles; you can spend your time cleaning as you please and leaving the creatures mostly to themselves, which I think is a wonderful choice as I was more invested in the cleaning aspect of the game. That being said, the loddles are adorable, and most of their various evolutions happened organically as I was playing rather than intentionally feeding them specific foods. The game is very fun and peaceful, the controls are perfect, and the sound and art make you want to sink into the world and stay there. An absolutely wonderful treat of a game!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Loddlenaut is an absolutely adorable and heartwarming game that combines exploration with environmental cleanup in the most charming way. The cute little sea creatures called "Loddles" bring a sense of companionship as you work through the ocean restoration and make the game all the more lovable, especially watching them thrive as their habitat is restored. The game's visuals are bright, colorful, and relaxing, which makes the experience of watching the once-polluted waters turn crystal clear as you clean up trash and nurture the environment feel truly gratifying and rewarding. Perfect for anyone who loves a blend of eco-conscious gaming and lovable creatures!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. Apart from your 02 going down (which is easy to refill) there are no timers and you can go as fast or as slow as you like through the whole game. Being able to grow different Loddles with different colours and abilities added a nice touch for when you want to take a break from the clean up. Honestly I would clean up planet after planet like this. I hope they continue to expand the game and if not then at least a sequel :)
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, cozy adventure where you play an underwater diver cleaning up the mess of a corporation, who has since abandoned their posts, on an alien planet named GUP-14. You are accompanied all throughout your journey by the recovering local fauna, a diverse group of Axolotls. With some great equipment progression, some fun breeding mechanics, and a few secrets to come across I definitely feel its worth the cost!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Very cozy game. Non stressful, very relaxing , A game anyone of any age can play and enjoy it. If you're not sure about the purchase, play the demo. I played the demo for a full hour and knew after the demo was over that this was a game I wanted to purchase. I do hope they consider making DLC content for additional maps/areas to explore. The game does have replay value for sure. It would be cool if there was another map and makes it more important to go back and forth to tend to the areas.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable, charming, relaxing and wholesome.It's not a massive game but I really enjoyed cleaning the whole area and unlocking every achievement. Its cool that there are a nice variety of creatures that you can create by feeding the right food. Once when I tabbed back into the game I was surprised to see my screen was full of fruits that had been spawned by one of my little loddles. I highly recommend if you like this type of game and are happy with something quite short and sweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: the focus of this game is clearing up the ocean after a corporation trashed it, which admittedly sounds a lot like other cleaning simulator type games but is done well in this one. alongside the cleaning, you have to manage taking care of these little axolotl-like creatures who need your help to restore their home and give them a better place to live. you pick up the ocean rubbish and clear away pollution in different zones with a little laser ray. there is a small upgrade system to progress in as well as one of the mechanics i like a lot in the game: the recycling system, surprisingly. the recycling system was interestingly well thought out for something you wouldn't really think twice over after the tutorial but it makes the game more interesting as you sort out your litter into seperate bins and get processed materials back to upgrade your tools- however you are also encouraged to keep the original trash in order to upcycle and reuse some function in them to create toys for the loddles and helpful secondary kits to aid with clearing up. this adds a little material management to the game but personally i just find it enjoyable to sort my inventory and get something back from it. the loddles are arguably the best and most important part of the game, not only because they are the reason you are clearing up their habitat but also because they are so adorable and rewarding to play with. after finding my first baby loddle, goopy, sad and hungry, cleaning it up and feeding it until it was happy felt like a huge step and i was instantly hooked :,) they evolve differently based on how you treat them and you unlock more things to do with them when you rescue more babies, but i found myself only wanting to spend my time watching them play and eat because they were so charming. as for the actual gameplay, cleaning the zones is fairly simple with a few things to watch out for and if you enjoy powerwash simulator or other repetitive task based games i would really recommend this game. i cant find much at all to say negatively about this game other than i wish it was longer because i dread finishing it
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Just some thoughts;I think if there is a co-op option it would be nice! Me and my best friends have been talking about this game and if we could explore together, that would be so much fun (or do quests together)!It was so hard to leave, I loved this game. The art is cute, the music is amazing and the game all in all is gold. Kudos to the developers for this gem. Would revisit this again, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This cute game has really mastered the relaxing yet engaging feeling of the cozy game genre... I wasn't expecting too much when I bought it on sale but I am so glad I did because I was instantly hooked on Loddlenauts visuals & mechanics and I pretty much binged at least 5 hours the first day I played it. _childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game. Had a really relaxing time cleaning up the ocean and exploring. The Loddle portion of the game wasn't quite as robust as I wanted from a true pet sim, but as a cleaning sim with a pet sim flavor it was awesome. It's a short game, and the story isn't much, but there weren't any glitches and the mechanics were fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: i love this game so much!! i got completely hooked and couldnt stop playing once i started haha, i only wish id played it at a slower pace to enjoy the first playthrough for longer. the music and the art are soo lovely, and the worldbuilding and story are really interesting (and the new content was great too!) anyway my first loddle malelo i will always love you
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful and delightful game. If you're looking for a relaxing cleaning game then I cannot recommend this game enough. The cute art style on top of the gorgeous environments makes this game pleasing to the eyes. The creature and plant design in this game is also a delight, as well as the evolutions of the Loddles, so freaking cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: It scratches a certain itch that only cleaning games can scratch. Like power washer simulator or viscera cleanup detail. Combines it with a very straightforward but satisfying progression system, to make a perfect and chill little casual game. But it really doesn't have any sticking power.. I was eager for the game to end so I could move on to bigger and more ambitious games.It's a good game, perfect for a little refresher game, but isn't going to be anyone's new obsession.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly wholesome and cute game with amazing visual-, audio- and game design in general. The message is great, the gameplay loop is satisfying, the narrative is just there enough to be interesting but not overwhelming. Loddlenaut does not overstay it's welcome but the 20€ price tag is a bit much for the 4-6 hours of gameplay it offers. A lovely game for all ages <3
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★Loddlenaut is a charming underwater open world clean-up/pet-collecting game, you clean up trash, and oil, before introducing the local plants and wildlife. The loddles, aka space axolotls, come in many different colors and what you feed them determines what type of loddle they become. There is a few cosmetic variants that hatched loddles have a chance of becoming that you can try to coax out with special diets and actions, as these are all cosmetic traits this feature is more for the pet focused players but it's nice when you hatch a variant unexpectedly. The story line is nice and simple and while there's not much replay ability outside of collecting new loddles I still think it's worth checking out if you're even a little bit interested.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: very cute gameplay. You clean up the ocean and also breed cute fishies. _childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I bought a steam deck to play Elden Ring. Instead, I've spent most of my time since purchase in Loddlenaut. I really love this game. The art design, mechanics, music, and mission progression are all so fun. Just cleaning up an area is super rewarding and the feedback makes it all feel so pleasant. This is perhaps the only game I've ever hesitated to upgrade my equipment, because doing things in the game--from zapping up goop from swimming into air bubbles to replenish oxygen--simply feels good. I'm having the nicest time and couldn't recommend it more.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely gem of a game. Great palate cleanser between other games at around 5 hrs taking my time and trying to 100% (two achievements seemed like a time sink and i'm OK on that lol). This game encapsulates the magic of gaming. No bloat, fresh art style, great loop, dreamy world, fun for fun's sake, GREAT and responsive controls. I would love a sequel with more stuff to check off of a list and more traversal options (I loved the first Subnautica for that very reason).The Loddles are super cute, but I did not want to sink time after completing the game into evolving them all; maybe if this was a little more straight forward or easier to do I would have engaged - but totally not a deal breaker. Reminded me of Chao Gardens ALOT. Play this game if:you love indiesyou love colorful and vibrant worldsyou love great gameplay with a satisfying loopgives you that "just one more" feelingyou love underwater and a plethora of colors

_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cozy I teared up. okay not literally but I have loved every second playing this. Cleaning is very satisfying and rewarding; it makes you feel productive. _childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: First off let me just say wow what an eye catching game (for players like me). I saw this game on TikTok and they advertised it as a "Chao Garden" mixed with Subnautica, cozy, cleaning sim and that just NAILED the description. Honestly I came for the Loddles and stayed to fully clean up their planet and 100% the game in just 12 hours. Pros:This game is cute and lovely to look at without being too pixelated and hurting my eyes during long periods of game play. The controls were easy enough to learn and weren't highly complex. I didn't feel like I was having to grind for items for my loddles or my biomes. The story was simple and quick to play through without having to go too far out of my way to finish the achievements list.Cons:The only thing I can say was a con for me other than not being able to move on to other planets and keep playing, was the evolution. I wish the fruits told you which attribute they changed. Maybe not specifically telling us lily bananas are flippers and kelp hearts are fancy, but maybe just telling us which ones change the body, head, or style? Just so I'm not getting 8 jumbos because I just keep changing their antennae to gills and back lolOverall I give the Loddle Garden 11/10 I couldn't wait to pick it back up and keep playing!

_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I received the game as part of Humble Choice. The game itself is quite fun and there is a decent amount to explore and Loddles to find. Picking up trash and cleaning the areas with the tools you unlock is enjoyable. The game itself is quite short but I will be replaying in the future to unlock the rest of the Achievements I missed during my first playthrough.The game is relaxing and has a nice soundtrack. I would say it’s definitely a cozy game. It played perfectly on my Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adored this game! As a little Loddlenaut, your job is to zap, scrub, and vacuum up all the goop and litter left behind in the ocean. The cleaning itself is super fun and satisfying- I found it really relaxing and ending up just zoning out and zapping away for hours~ Each different area of the ocean is unique and pretty, so clearing out the junk and grime is extra rewarding! I ended up cleaning 100% before I even knew it!Even better than the cleaning, though, are the precious lil Loddle friends you find along the way! They follow you around while you clean, and you can pet, feed, and play with your new friends to your heart's content! Just don't forget your main cleaning objective hehe~ There's 13 different types of loddles, and how the babies you find evolve depend on what fruits and snacks you feed them as they grow! It's too hard to pick a favorite type of Loddle, so it's better to just collect them all! \(^w^)/ There's a limit to the total amount of loddles you can have hanging out, so be sure to try and diversify before you wind up with too many Jumbo loddles (they're so cute, but so useless) and wind up having to release some >_<Overall, it took my about 16 hours to finish the game and collect all the achievements- but I spent a lot of time just wandering around and trying to make a bunch of cute, pink loddles, so it's definitely possible to complete it in less time! I definitely recommend giving it a go~ :3
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: A cute cozy game I enjoyed/enjoy playing. It's nice to sit down and basicly do nothing but look at cute loddles and collect trash every now and then. That being said, there's sadly not much to do past the point of cleaning all the biomes. I wish and hope for there to be more content in the future that adds either a function for replayability or more content in general :)
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so nice to just sit with after a day of work. I've been searching for a good while for a game that is low stress but still fun and this scratched so many itches for me. Just chilling in the ocean, keeping it tidy, taking care of my loddles.That said, outside of being a completionist, there's not a whole lot to do once you've cleaned all the areas once and gotten all the upgrades. The dev's just released a content update though, so there may be more to come and considering how much fun I've had for the price I'll gladly buy some DLC if it gives more areas to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE THIS GAME!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I've been waiting for it to come out for YEARS, and I couldn't buy it until now. I played the demo, I followed both the discord server and the tiktok account, and I was SO excited for it to come out. I love playing it, and the story behind it is amazing. I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short, decent, cozy game that doesn't really have anything out of the ordinary. There was an update on the 19th of september that seems to have changed the game a lot and removed a lot of the frustration. I think you should look at reviews after that time if you want to make a proper opinion on this game.I'd say this game is about as low in complexity as you can get without getting boring. It's nothing challenging, even getting the different breeds isn't too bad with a guide and remembering you can put them in your  base as a controlled environment. The plot is similarly simple, but it's not completely barren with some implied stuff to  think about.The loddles are cute, though the pixelated filter strained my eyes after a while. Thankfully you can disable it in the settings. All around the game was pretty without obscuring what you had to do.I personally like a little more complexity in my "cosy" games, but I can understand that this could be a nice one for people that want a very relaxed experience. I could also definitively see people obsessing over the loddles,naming them and making up stories about them. Maybe the next game will have you play as one... In summary, I'd only advise you to play this game if you like easy, cosy games, and if the time spent to money spent ratio isn't too bad for your taste. Still, if you do fit the criteria, it's a nice game to spend a few days on.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by far one of my favorites that I've ever played. I know that's a lot to say considering how long I've played it for, but it's quickly becoming a favorite for me. The concept is so well thought out and I love pretty much everything about it so far. It does not overstay its welcome and to be honest, I could see myself replaying the game some time in the future. It's not really tough to 100% either, it is pretty much just a play to chill out kinda game. It also isn't annoying the way Power Wash Simulator can be in that when you scan, it is pretty obvious on your screen, where dirt in PWS can be tough to find even when highlighting it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Such a good game!! So relaxing and calming to play whenever. I do wish that the game was longer with more map areas to clean and explore however as the game is still relatively new, I'm sure they will add more locations in the game in the future like they have done recently with the new update. The graphics are simple but so cute and cleaning up and collecting items is so satisfying. _childDocuments_.review: Loddlenaut is an absolute gem! 🐳💙 You get to explore a gorgeous alien ocean, clean up trash, and take care of adorable sea creatures. It's super chill and satisfying, especially watching the ocean come back to life. The little critters are the best, and it feels great to help them out while making the world prettier! If you love cozy, relaxing games with a positive message, this is 100% for you
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really cute but I felt like it was too short. I was hoping for a bit more. It felt like an abrupt end. Some of the story implies there might have been more but then there was nothing. I got it in my humble bundle so that's fine, but I definitely wouldn't have paid $20 for it. I stretched it as long as I could and still only spent 10 hrs on it. Definitely could have finished the game faster. I don't know if they plan on updates.. But I hope so. I was hoping that some of the machines you happen upon could be refurbished with the recycled trash and collect fruit for you to feed your pals. Maybe a final upgrade for your airtank that lets you never need to refill so you can just wander the whole landscape cleaning stuff. Maybe ability to customize the landscape a bit more, set up little cities for your buddies. I dunno. Something.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a way to rate this a 10/10 cause this is the first game in my entire life that I believe truly deserves it. There is not a feeling or idea that comes close to what this game is, and what it has done for me. From the sounds and music, to the nice game play and message. Everything about this game is perfect, my only real issue is that is isn't longer. A few more worlds to go across would be amazing, but i understand the creative process to basically make more maps is to make a Loddlenaught 2 (Which I wouldn't complain about). All in all I would recommend this to anyone and everyone. Truly my favorite game now. 11/10 if there ever was one. My friend bought it for me, but if they made 20 of these games I'd buy them all myself. I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game!Loddlenaut is a game about cleaning the ocean and helping the loddles grow and populate again.It's a lot of fun and satisfying cleaning the areas, feeding the loddles and seeing them be happy.There are some little things I would like to have improved1. a way to see if a loddle is 100% grown (like using the radar and seeing the number)2. seeing if the loddle is either hungry/full and happy/sad with the radar.besides those two little problems, I loved it and can recommend it to everybody who loves underwater cozy games.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game. Relaxing and a good way to pass the time. I got it in a humble bundle, and I'd suggest that getting it very cheap is the only way to play it. I'd finished the "story", cleaned all biomes, got all upgrades and saw the credits roll in 3 hours. There's so much more potential here, but the game is lacking in depth. _childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I've never seen or played a game like this... This is a work of art. I usually don't like anything that includes the sea, but I wasn't even scared a single second while playing this game. It's simple, cozy, and so fun to play. I love cleaning games. _childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Love cute animals? Want to clean up the ocean? Love satisfying dings and pings of completion? Then this is ABSOLUTELY the game for you! Super cute, incredibly satisfying, and all around an adorable cozy game. Truly enjoy all of the aspects of the game, from oxygen management to the different ways to clean up the ocean. I've played it to completion at least 3 times at this point, and will likely do more once the update is here!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: If you like cleaning and caring for nature, then this is the right game for you. I love the satisfaction of cleaning the goop and picking up the trash. The helmet sensor comes in really handy to look for remaining litter/goop for people who are easily frustrated when they dont reach 100% cleanliness for each biomes. im very picky when it comes to cozy games, but i really like this a lot and made me want more. this game definitely made my top 3 for cozy games! i hope the developer is working on coming out with its sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: this game is lovely! the experience of cleaning the ocean is both relaxing and rewarding as you get to see how your work cleans the environment little by little!im having a great time playing and i have a couple suggestions for the developers:id love to get some sort of cosmetic shop for the lodddlenaut. it'd be a great way to get more objectives and to personalize your experience for more replayability id love to see some short of challenge mode (like having to clean one of the enviroments in a limited time, or using having some short of race using the oxigen rings, boost and those plants that give you yellow boost)right now the game is great but i feel it has a lot more potential! i cant wait to see the switch update and i hope you keep working on the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

Also pretty simple and achievable achievements for everyone. 10/10 would loddlenaut again

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and relaxing game all about cleaning up the ocean and collecting new loddles. The mechanics are very easy and the achievements are pretty easy to get as well. There are guides out there to help when trying to get one of every type of loddle for the achievement if needed. I would say get this game on sale if possible as its a very quick play through and should only cost like $10 max.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game a whole lot more than i thought i would. Super cute and lots of fun. Its very soothing and cozy, the art is cute. There isn't a rush to do anything either which is a plus. Personally, i would 100% play this game again if i ever need something relaxing to do while i put on a podcast or something else. I'm really glad there are different levels of pixel resolution as Loddles are cuter with smoother shapes. It is a little annoying sometimes when your newly cleaned area goes from 100% to like 92% in a few minutes, but i've found that can be easily remedied by putting certain loddle types in each area. (It's got similar vibes to the game "Donut County", but with more freedom and things to do.) The controls are really nice on a controller, very intuitive and easy. (Not sure about keyboard since i didnt try)My main gripe with the game though, I would love love LOVE to be able to change my dive suit colour or my spaceship colour. Idk i just think it would be cute. That's it really. Just a cosmetic thing rather than an actual gameplay thing.  Now, this game did require a bit of talking myself into spending $20 since that is a fair amount. I love the game, but I would wait for a sale. Otherwise great atmosphere, relaxing game play and no crazy achievements :)
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite cozy game experiences, Loddlenaut mixes mild exploration with a variety of resource collection and cleaning tasks. It introduces enough variety to not overstay its ~5 hour playtime and subtly promotes a sustainability message without being preachy about the subject.Simply a joy to play and a great experience on the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I went into playing this game with no expectations, no idea what it's about and finished the game really feeling like this is arguably the best cosy game I've played in a long time.From the calming music, to the charming graphics, the simple yet entertaining gameplay and little quirks thrown in that you have to discover on your own, all of it was just such a great experience. Just when I thought I'd seen all the game had to offer there was a little secret thing thrown in that I'd find right at the end after playing through the entire game. I didn't want it to end, I wish there was an entire other planet and more tools, more creatures to nurture and snacks to make.It's so nice to see a game idea from seemingly a couple of guys develop into such a cool little creation.I really didn't expect to enjoy it so much, I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: such a good game, super cute style, super relaxing and easy to understand but not to easy enough to be boring. Its not just a cleaning game, it also has lore as to why you're doing what you're doing and why the wold is the way it is. You progress more in the story as you continue to unlock areas and discover hidden items. Upgrading equipment is super easy and not grindy, since you just gotta play the game and use the rubbish u collected to upgrade stuffits also fun feeding the loddles different food to see what evolution they will grow into, and the game also encourages 'biodiversity', so you get more stars if you have different loddle evolutions in one area. theres nothing scary in the game such as aggressive sea life or whatever, the only way you can die im pretty sure is if your oxygen runs out, but that hasnt happened to me yet since its quite easy to prevent.im about 4 hours in whilst writing this review and i believe im on the last area of the map, however i still have a lot of loddle evolutions and ID cards to find.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute and simple game. Idk why but I love video game swimming (terrible swimmer irl, ftr).  I started it while I was sick and felt productive after hours of cleaning up this alien ocean** (**sitting on my couch, swaddled in blankets and sweaty).  There were moments where I felt nauseous in the ocean, but I think that has nothing to do with video game ocean or being sick. I am just getting old.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Got this in a Humble Bundle. Decided to crack it open while suffering from Covid. I needed something kind of low-key, low-brain energy that would still keep me interested enough in it to stop me from thinking about being sick. This game delivered in spades. It's a short, but enjoyable little romp that will scratch your itch if you like playing games that "defragment" things such as Power-Wash Simulator, but it's a lot more cute and has lower stakes and a pet mini-game that comes along with it. The music is nice, the graphics are perfect for what the game needs, and the story line is just enough to keep you moving forward. A perfect palate cleanser between your 100 hour epic monsters.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Loddlenaut is a fun game about restoring the environments, discovering new creatures, and relaxing throughout it all.At the beginning, I found myself worried about how I was going to get far enough to clean before running out of oxygen, but that quickly became much less of a problem without upgrades, and with the ability to place extra oxygen devices, it's really not much of an issue at all. If you do run out, you'll drop some items and they'll be waiting for you when you come back. Crops regrow and biomes will continue to build up grime over time, just like in real life. There is no permanent solution, and that is okay. Upon cleaning a biome to 100% you unlock a permanent fast-travel spaceship (and storage) at that location. This is an excellent feature and I used the storage many times through adventures.Your Loddle's will breed, grow, and evolve independently, or with your help. You can feed them special foods to have them change into specific breeds, which you may need to do for the achievement. A full guide is available here, and it was a huge help for me.All in all, this game is well-worth the purchase and I highly recommend it. I hit 100% completion in 7 hours and I would definitely play again if there were an update.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game! Had a lot of fun cleaning up the different zones and making Loddle friends. I actually cried a bit finishing the game and leaving them behind, so maybe I got a bit *too* invested, lol. Highly recommend giving this one a go :)P. S. Much love from a fellow Austinite! Dunno why, it just makes me happy to see creative projects from people in my hometown 💜
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game!! It's so cute and calming, and the art style for the game is amazing. For me, the game was well worth full-price, but I am incredibly slow at playing games and typically have a lot more play time than the average user. I think my favorite part of the game was experimenting with Loddle evolutions - it reminded me so much of the Chao Garden mechanics from Sonic!! I would highly, highly, HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone looking for something cute and cozy that doesn't require a whole lot of mental effort. One of my new favorites!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer, the following review is based solely on my opinion, therefor you may have contrary thoughts and opinions and are welcome to your interpretation.Overview:time is taken to complete not including the collecting of all lottle types-  4 hours 43 minutes.do I recommend playing?- yes, why not?Is it worth £15.99?- not in my opinion.The game has about 4 hours of content if you do not include discovering all the loddle species, the game itself is simple and easy and a good recommendation for first-time gamers or someone looking into getting a relaxing no thought game. whilst the loddle species is cute I didn't find them pretty enough to want to collect them all as I felt there wasn't any benefit. regarding the upgrades, I don't feel like there was enough. once you are fully upgraded the act of cleaning up remains tedious. it is also straightforward to upgrade your equipment quickly and there's no real challenge behind it however judging by the rest of the game I feel like there's not meant to be a challenge at all it is just meant to be a calm and relaxing game.whilst I did enjoy just relaxing and killing time I feel like there could have been a lot more potential to take the game further not only with the story but just the general mechanics as well because slow boosting everywhere very quickly becomes annoying especially if you haven't unlocked the fast travel option yet, so in reality there is likely way less then 4 hours of gameplay since most of the time you are just boosting back and forth from your base.at the end of the day, this is just my interpretation, I liked the game it was alright but it is not something I see myself replaying in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare that I pick up a game and genuinely can't stop playing. After abut 15 minutes I was hopelessly lost in the game loop, and only sleep stopped me from playing. After that though, I woke up and completed the rest of it. It only took me about 4 hours and I don't feel compelled to play more, but they were 4 great hours. I wish there was more of this game and more games like it. Very well designed in the context of how quickly I got addicted to it. The intro was a bit unappealing, but as soon as I left that area, I was all in. My only very minor complaint is that the process of recycling could be streamlined a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a fan of the ocean? Cute little friends? A simple game play loop while exploring a world made with love? Then I'd HIGHLY recommend Loddlenaut!
