I think there have been some tweaks and updates to it since then, which is a shame that I didn't get those, but hey maybe your experience will be better? Highly recommend still.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so flipping adorable! :D I love the ocean I love picking up trash and I love cute little sea creatures!! Picking up trash in the ocean and depositing it into separate receptacles is so satisfying and fun! You get to upgrade stuff by recycling heck ya! Also the Loddles are SOO FREAKING CUTE! I just wanna squish their little faces! Really awesome chill cute fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game!!! Relaxing and cozy without being boring. Perfect for easing anxiety or just feeling soothed. The soundtrack is lovely and calm and it is very satisfying to pick up all the trash and especially to zap up all the goop. The fact that litter slowly creeps back over time means that you can also go back to biomes you have saved to do maintenance. The loddles and cute and it was fun to have their different abilities help me with my tasks or feel like they were taking care of their environment.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: You get to clean up ocean goop and pet little ocean friends, I couldn't ask for more. Super cute, super cozy, super satisfying game that's the perfect length to sit down and 100% in one weekend.(for anyone who's favorite part of Sonic Adventure 2 was the Chao Garden, definitely recommend checking this game out)
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Loddlenaut is a cute, cozy, 3rd person pixelated game where you clean up a polluted planet and take care of alien Loddle fish. Loddlenaut's pixelated art style and chill soundtrack create a relaxing atmosphere as you use your bubble gun to clean up contaminated plants, scenery and Loddles. By finding and collecting trash, you can bring it back to your home base cove and recycle them into Bits. These Bits can then be used to order upgrades and new tools for your Loddlenaut. Loddles have unique evolutions that can be influenced by feeding them certain foods. It's also fun to see Loddles evolving themselves by eating what is naturally occuring in their own environments. Although I absolutely recommend this game for a chill, relaxing time I have to say that this game is disappointingly short. I managed to 100% the game in under 7 hours. Some of the aforementioned mechanics such as upgrades and tools are also somewhat surface level; I managed to max out everything in the first hour or so. I could say more of the things I'd noticed during my play through but I don't want this review to come off as too negative. Sufficed to say, this is a very chill, simple game so don't expect to get much more than my playtime. That being said, I still recommend this game. I played the demo and picked it up during a sale and had a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Loddlenaut for what it is. A few hours of playtime with relaxing atmosphere and the satisfaction of cleaning up each biomes. I loved the upgrade system... but really once you upgrade everything you have no need to recycle because there is literally no crafting needed anymore and no rewards for doing so, which for some people can be a deal breaker but I try to enjoy short games for what they are as long as they have a good vibe to them and this game did it for me :) -----> I definitely WOULDN'T pay full price for it but it's worth when on SALE for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed both the story elements and the game play. With a story that is both well written and easy to understand, it doesn't feel like it took over the game. The game play is relaxing and enjoyable, with the player feeling to a sense of peace washing over them. Even me as someone who feels they need to complete everything, I didn't feel overwhelmed with getting the little story badges or getting all the loddles. 10/10 game will prob play again
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: So upon playing it seems fairly shallow but that doesn't subtract from the enjoyment. It is a cozy game that is relaxing and enjoyable but upon a closer look the Loddles have actual perks and grow into different loddles depending on the diet. The loddles then have useful effect while in biomes helping keep it clean or helping produce grow among other things. Honestly surprised by how in depth the game was. I do feel that 19.99 is a bit steep for this game unless you're going to take time to 100% the biomes with loddle wildlife and build the eco system. I finished the story content in about 5 hours give or take. I got the game on sale which was a great deal but full price seems steep.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: amazingly well done. you can name the Loddles and they follow you around and you can feed them. the mechanics are well done and easy to get the hang of. the ending was very bittersweet. this is a relatively short game. i completed it within 5 hours but did not necessarily 100% it. if there is a dlc or second game with a second planet and creatures i would absolutely buy it. until then, i might just have to replay it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: + Such a lovely game, really helped me calm my nerves after work a few times :) If you ever played Sonic Adventure and liked Chao Garden, this is a game for you.+ Latest update added few more things like Loddlepedia and plants that help you keep sprinting, I think they both were the reason I finally got to finish the game +/- Music and gameplay are both calming but might get repetitive after a while. +/- The game is short enough, so previous point might not be an issue at allPersonally I didn't mind repetitiveness here and there. I took my time with it and got everything I wanted out of it!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely adorable. A bit on the shorter side, but a cozy/chill game involving cleaning an ocean and making friends with the cute wildlife. Even though I just finished it, I'm so compelled to play it once more just because of how satisfying it was to clean out the ocean. You can also change the amount of pixelation the game has to your preference, which was an awesome feature! I hope to see more content come for this game, I thoroughly enjoyed my experience and recommend it to anyone looking for a shorter chill game!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Loddlenaut is a wonderful, colourful and thoroughly entertaining journey through a fantastically designed, beautiful alien world.The gameplay is satisfying and simple, the music is upbeat and pleasing, the designs are adorable and creative, and the price is fair for the 8-10 hours of game time.The loddle evolution system is surprisingly in depth and while some may need a guide to figure out some of the more complex parts (like I did), it's not too difficult to discern and once it clicks in your head it really stands out as a unique aspect of a fantastic game. Each type of loddle has interesting and cute designs that tie together a nice little side objective that feels satisfying to complete and definitely felt very fun to discover each loddle type and all the different types of colours and characteristics they can possess.Anyone who is a fan of cute, cozy indie games that you can enjoy for a quiet but pleasant few hours, I would highly recommend them Loddlenaut, I'm excited to see what this team of devs will put out in the future and will most likely end up replaying this game more than once.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: i LOVED THIS GAMEIt's got the cozy cleaning vibes together with little creatures (loddles) you can befriend and lead down evolution paths. If you're looking for a cozy game to chill and relax to this is definitely it.Also, the game was updated recently to include much requested features and the devs seem passionate :)
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I totally recommend Loddlenaut if you want to sit back and relax. Its cute, cozy, and there is almost no rush.The only downside to this game is that you get to clean up one planet! I want mooooore! I want to be able to play this game fore hours and see new areas or have the ability to travel to different plants.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Loddlenaut is a cute cozy serene game about saving a planet and making cute little friends. This game is relaxing yet incredibly addicting. It sadly is on the shorter side but I think that it makes up for it well in all its other qualities. As a 100% completionist, I can proudly say that this game is more than worth it for a short curated experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing, no-stress game. You can probably 100% it in 5-7 hours, faster if you don't care about the trash in the transitional areas. Fair warning you will probably need to consult the guide on how to get some of the loddle types, though I was able to get all but 3 without having to look up what to feed them.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game was recommended to me by my awesome friend and i am loving it !! i love the loddles and every evolution and the satisfaction that comes after cleaning each area. I hope the would be a new area to clean other than GUP-14 like another GUP location for future updates, new upgrades, customizable suits/gear and more. I'm almost done with the map T.T makes me sad, I wish there was more....
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: It's a simple, cute, chill little game. Good for turning off your brain and just playing. It's pretty short - I beat it in 5.5 hours - but you can squeeze some more time out of it by trying to get all the varieties of Loddles if that's something you're interested in. The controls are easy to pick up, especially with the little tutorial dude there to guide you through the new tools.It does take a little common sense here and there - the recycling machines show examples of items they accept, but not all of the items they accept. So if you have something you picked up that doesn't seem to be good for anything else, see if it's recyclable.Seriously, though, the only thing worth complaining about would be the price tag. It's a little bit too short to be worth $20. But that's just my opinion, and honestly I got this through Humble Monthly so I'm thrilled. I wasn't sure if that qualified as getting it "free" since it's a subscription.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game may feel a little slower going but I still found myself absorbed for hours making my way across the ocean ecosystems and doing my part in cleaning up. It is very relaxing and cute and I had a great deal of fun seeing the different Loddles and their colors and variants. they are so darn cute and you can pet them!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: A great game overall. I love the story building and how cute the little Lottles are. i do wish there were more biomes to explore. I feel like the game ended too quickly, and for the price of 20 dollars I wish there were more things to do. I left the game feeling unfulfilled and a bit disappointed. I love the aesthetic and game mechanics I just wish there was more to do. Possibly a big update, or even a DLC because I would be willing to pay a lot for one if it expands the world and story
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect performance on Deck.A cool little chill game. The Steam description is astonishingly accurate. It's not trying to reinvent the wheel, but it's great at what it does. There's no combat, only cleaning. There's an oxygen meter that can be annoying to some, but you quickly get ways to build oxygen dispensers so it's okay.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute and fun. You can customize little friends, have them help you clean and farm food, adventure around the map at your own leisure, and the replay value is so good!Only thing I can think to add would be more bioms (likely already in the works) and different difficulty levels. Then the replay would be even more fun with more to cleaning up to do on harder settings, no oxygen for easier, or a timed version to really challenge yourself to clean the planet as fast as you can!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: if you like whimsy and delight and joy and having fun with your friends you'll like this. as much as i like cozy games, i find that few tend to hold my attention past the initial cuteness - totally not the case with this game. i could not put this down. takes around 7 hours to complete, my only complaint is that i wish it was longer. the first time i pet a loddle i genuinely teared up.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: A fun cute little game. I love the little Loddles and what they can become. I like how there are different tools you need to use to clean up the map, not just one tool for everything. I definitely recommend it if you want a nice laid-back game about cleaning the ocean and caring for little Loddles.P.S. would also love if devs added DLCs for more planets or parts of GUP-14 to clean.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This is an AWESOME game. It's a really good game to just chill and play while you're watching a show or movie. It's a really nice relaxing game that you can just load up and play when you're bored. There's not many lightweight games with not too many strings attached that I own. Many games you can't just casually play and have to be fully attentive. This game you can just play while you're doing other stuff. In a Zoom Call, Watching a Movie or TV Show. It's a really fun game and I highly recommend it. Maybe wait till it's on sale or you're able to get it in a bundle because I wouldn't pay $20 for it but it's a really good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Wish there was a mixed option for this one as I enjoyed my time on Loddlenauts but it was way too short - only taking a few hours to complete and that was while taking my time with the game too. They could really do with adding more areas or another planet. I hope this is something the developers will consider.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: A cute adventure game where you explore an ocean planet and clean up all the pollution and litter left behind by a giant corporation, and befriend the little fish that inhabit the planet named Loddles. You can convert the polution you clean up into upgrades that let you clean more and harder. A straightforward game, enjoyable and short.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful and relaxing ride where the biggest enemy is running out of breath and getting a little dirty, i loved the low stress vibes of taking care of the little Loddle dudes and cleaning up the ocean. Wonderful for all ages and really intuitive.I really want to see this game expand with more of everything that they're already doing but its otherwise perfect, like the feeling of an amazing meal but you just want more. Loddlenaut 2?
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little game I 100%ed within 6 hours of playtime.Very wholesome till you start achievement hunting, with one of the achievements requiring to see every possible loddle growth path.Then you end up kidnapping loddles from their homes and hiding them in the only place lacking food, your proverbial basement/home base, for the sole purpose of guiding their growth with strict diets.10/10, would recommend as a weekend relaxant.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: The coziest of relaxing games. Short, but satisfying. It scratches the same tidying itch that Powerwash simulator does, except it is very cute and underwater and there are also cute fish you can rescue and mutate. Damn it, I just scrolled down and read RPS gave this game pretty much the exact same review! How dare they simultaneously read my mind and time travel to the past to post it first. Outrageous!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: i bought this game during a high discount and honestly would gladly pay 20-25 pounds for it. a lovely casual/cozy game. stress free time cleaning up an ocean on planet whatever. the only thing needing monitoring is your oxygen which is easily done as there is many plants that produce  oxygen bubbles. a cute game to wile away the hours with even cuter little fish friends. its a 10/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: loddlenaut is an adorable, cozy, cleaning/pet(?)-simulator for gamers of all ages, with an interesting premise and sweet little creatures called loddles (that look similar to axolotls). definitely recommend for anyone who is interested! just be aware that the game took me about 6-ish hours to finish with 100% of the achievements, so it isn't a super long game. i would recommend getting it on sale like i did just because, imo, the story is a little short for the $20 price tag.edit: they're adding a loddlepedia! i'm so happy! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I've mentioned this in my other reviews and it applies here as well: This game reminds me of one of the many legendary quotes by Danny DeVito: 'I'm the trashman!', only in this game you are an underwater trashman, there are adorable little creatures known as Loddles and the game is super addictive. And you get to clean up the sea in various ways which adds to its appeal! So yeah, highly recommended! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually adorable !! I don't think I ran into a single bug throughout the entire thing except for like two (one of them just being clipping), and I enjoyed cleaning up everything so so much. It was so satisfying to see all that gunk removed and it makes me want to clean up the ocean in real life as well :]] Too bad I don't live close to the ocean, sigh. AND DON'T GET ME STARTED ON THE LODDLES THEMSELVES ??? Literally the cutest things known to man and i am SO HAPPY you can pet them. I want to kiss all of them. Great graphics, great colors, great ideas, great everything. ♥♥♥♥ you Guppi if you put ANOTHER PIECE OF TRASH IN THE OCEAN I will destroy your headquarters from the inside out. My only complaints are that the ocean keeps getting relittered after cleaning everything up (but I understand that's so you still have materials to make things with), and I think it'd be interesting to have Guppi be responsible and send down their trash to you to be recycled into loddle toys. Another thing is that it's hard to find individual Loddles, especially in places where they're all the same color. I can search for like thirty minutes for the one Loddle in an environment that hasn't been named yet and still not find it lol. Otherwise, THE PERFECT GAME GRAH!!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: One of the cutest games I've ever played! I had so much fun scrubbing the ocean clean and recycling the stuff left behind, while making friends with the local loddles. No enemies to worry about, only scrub... and maybe keep an eye on your oxygen meter. It gets progressively easier to get more oxygen as you move to different sectors, though it took me a bit to realize that some of the sponge-like structures actually blow oxygen bubbles for you. Though, after completing my first run through, I'm left wanting more. I anticipated this game to be progressively harder or introduce more complex challenges, or maybe even travel to other GUP planets and work with new biomes! But I still had fun beautifying GUP-17 and playing with loddles, much to the chagrin of Dave. I want a plushie of one, now.Loddle is a fun word to say out loud. Loddleloddleloddle.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: -Soothing to watch the progress as it cleans up. Music adds to vibe very well.-Mindless fun, no enemies or things to avoid just grab stuff and clean.-Cute loddles and cute diver. I love the lil arms going up on the diver as you dive down in place.Cons:-Not super clear instructions but easy enough once you figure it out. Not a clear connection how food affects Loddles. So, it's a lot of guess work when figuring out Loddles diet and what to do with stuff. -No real story line as far as I can tell (but lets be real are you here for a storyline or just the cuteness? Thought so)
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: it's a very short and sweet game. I enjoyed it as a breath of fresh air compared to the other games I play. The Loddles are cute and seeing the all the different transformations they can go though is fun.I would like to see more of this game in an "endless" mode where you complete one section of the ocean and then you keep moving to the next procedurally generated area for you to clean and a small chance for you to meet the Loddles you let go again. this way the game had nearly infinite replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: A fun short indie adventure, the only real complaint I have is that I wish there was more! A larger map, more upgrades, more gadgets, just... more! And that's a great major complaint to have because that means there are zero major issues with the graphics, story, mechanics, or anything else! I'd love a more in-depth element to the Loddles as well, like actually needing to keep the population balanced or even some log of how to get them to turn into different forms. More coloration for the Loddles would have been great as well, some sort of color hybridization mechanic would be super cool.This game is a great example of a game that knows exactly what it wanted to be and achieved that very well. It's got a pro-environmental message without being preachy or depressing, even if the intensity of the post-human-occupation pollution is striking at times.I beat the game in just under 5 hours and I wasn't really trying to beat it super quick, so the $20 standard asking price might be a bit steep for some, (I got it from a humble monthly, but it's also on sale for less than $15 as of this review, which I'd say is  worth it) but honestly I see myself playing this again, and probably multiple times. it scratches the same kind of itch as games like Power Wash Sim. Honestly it might even be a fun game to give speedrunning a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, relaxing game. I can't wait to see what else Moon Lagoon releases!I kind of wish there was another zone or 2. Just a little more to justify the vac and scrubber since you get those pretty close to the end of the game.Near the end of the game you may begin to wish there was a way to craft basic items in the zones instead of returning to home. I'm a little torn there, it's convenient but resource collection does require some traveling anyway.Resource scarsity is balanced pretty well so you'll always be looking for things to grab while you traverse the zones. I wasn't caught waiting for things to spawn or stuck with a massive stockpile of one thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really calm and easy, but also cute. I just wish it were longer. I suppose I can always do another run! I beat my first playthrough without ever using the ship storage, both as a challenge for myself and because I was worried I'd forget about something if it wasn't in my inventory (this is a personal issue - it has happened with Minecraft a little too often). Play this game if you want something chill with occasional silly creatures.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This is an awesome game!  The gameplay loop is fun and relaxing while the graphics are cute and light.  However, I experienced a critical crash in the game that deleted an hour of my progress.  It occurred when I was depositing materials in the recyclers.  The setback was enough to make me want to put down the game for a bit, which was very disappointing as I was hooked until the crash.  I recommend this game in spite of the crash, hopefully it was a fluke accident and doesn't happen repeatedly or to other people.  Try not to overwhelm the recyclers though.  There are no cats in this game though the whiskered loddle may count...it is certainly cute enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I got this with humble choice. It was one of the least likely games for me to love from the bundle, but I downloaded it first cos it was smallest. I really expected to be bored or not into it. AND I LOVE IT SO MUCHon paper I should hate this, so why would I love it so much? it's weird. it's just so cozy and satisfying and relaxing. I do think full price is a bit high though so I recommend a sale
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I wish this game was longer. It was so cute and fun. The visual style was a little surprising at first, but after some time you get used to it. The controls are pretty simple and the game has a nice little series of tasks that it runs you through to help you progress. I did 100% it in 6 hours though so as I said before, I wish it was longer because I was really enjoying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this are why I subscribe to Humble Bundle; I never would've sought a game like this out on my own, and I doubt the algorithms would've pushed it at me, but now that I have it I really enjoy it. A simple game, just explore, collect mats, and craft upgrades to craft more upgrades. I completed the story in a little over 4 hours while I was chatting with friends on a voice call, and I think that's what's kind of great about this game? It's super chill, an easy thing to keep my hands busy while my attention is elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet and relaxing.Definitely not "challenging" in any way but not every game has to be something you "git gud"  at :DThe loddles are adorable, the game goal is "cleaning up the mess".There's even a smidge of story told through the holobadges.Some 10hrs of fun for the price of about two movie tickets is definitely worth it. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful cosy chill game! I played the demo last year and I am super happy with the extra things they have added. It is a simple game with just enough progression to keep it interesting while keeping it calming and simple fun. Would recommend for anyone in a summery water mood who wants to swim about and make some fish friends
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: This was a lovely experience - Whilst semi-short, I didn't feel like I wasn't getting enough out of it. I think it would have gotten too repetitive without new mechanics if it'd gone on for another 3 new sections. For me it was the perfect length and I enjoyed myself very much. Would absolutely recommend if you're a fan of Powerwashing Simulator, the chill vibe feels very similar.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Ended up unintentionally speedrunning the game after completing the main story and grabbing most of the achievements in just under 3 hours, but only because it has so much charm and is super chill that I didn't want to step away from it. I do wish there was a bit more depth to the game in regards to tools and cleaning things up, but only because I am a sucker for these types of games.You could wait for a small sale, but I'd still heavily recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Great time waster. You're an astronaut on an aquatic planet tasked with cleaning surfaces and picking up trash from the environment. You craft upgrades and materials with the trash. You can take care of "Loddles," including feeding them and evolving them. It was satisfying to clean up environments and see progress. The whole game only took > 5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Cleaning and tidying up is therapeutic, I should do it more in real life! :PCosy little game, relaxing game mechanics, with enough upgrades and variety to be interesting yet not overwhelming. I appreciate the minimalistic and charming art style, conveys atmosphere without visual clutter, reduces sensory overload, very calming indeed :)
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game I'd pick up on a sale as it's really short and not much to do beside the same repetitive task of cleaning. Having to manually ascend and descend in the water and not just swim around with the camera in each direction was really annoying. Two somewhat grindy achievements to 100 % it, if you are a completionist.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Quick, chill cleaning sim with a simple pet sim on top. Cute graphics with charming little characters, even the advice giving character, who felt halfway between a soulless corporate drone and a parent barely keeping it together. ADHD Multiscreener/Tasker friendly. The distance between the worksite and the storage drop-site/home base was sometimes annoying and the upgrades ended far sooner than desired. This could easily have done with three or four more zones, but it was still a satisfying amount of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: Play as an interstellar custodian sent to clean up a polluted ocean planet. Pick up trash, explore the vibrant waters, and take care of axolotl-like alien creatures!
_childDocuments_.name: Loddlenaut

_childDocuments_.review: I hate Square Enix.Just shadow dropping this game on Steam one day before Persona 5 releases.This is just evil, really. This game is not as good as the first game, but it has the same charm.The quality in the writing of the dialogue and character development is the same as the first game I'd say.Soundtrack is another banger to listen to  it has the original OST - although most of it remixed.The Story has some flaws and it just kinda does things sometimes just for the sake of the plot moving forward, but it's still a very fun ride. It drags on unfortunately, the game does have a lot of padding. Every mission with time travel involved is just a drag and not very enjoyable.That said, the gameplay is really unique and interesting and although it takes up-to the second half of the game until it gets really interesting, I would still say it's really fun (when the enemies you fight aren't annoying that is, because there are some that just love to waste your time and energy).So, where do we find ourselves?We got the first game with no definitive way of playing (since the DS version has the best gameplay but misses the extra content and the higher quality OST and visuals) and then the sequel which Square Enix just refused to market in any way. Oh, and we have the mediocre Anime that does a poor job of re-telling the story of the first game.It's a shame really, this franchise doesn't deserve it, but that's just how it is I guess.I recommend to play the Original TWEWY first on either DS or Switch (the mobile port as last resort) and then come back to this.It is worth it.I just wish they'd remake the first game (even if it won't be able to replicate its original gameplay due to no dualscreen), but I think I got my hopes too high up for that :')

_childDocuments_.review: I should start by saying a few things.1: I played the original The World Ends With You after a recommendation from a close friend just a few months ago. I am not a die-hard fan who had waited for over a decade for this game to be released, and I do not have formative memories tied up in the original. I also streamed the original and this game live to my friends.2: I played the original DS version using an emulator, and thanks to my drawing tablet, the experience was quite close to what it would've been had I run it on original hardware. I did not play the Switch Final Remix, nor the android Solo Remix.3: I completed TWEWY only to what I wanted. I got every secret report and beat (original TWEWY post-game spoiler) . I did not 100% the original game.And finally 4: I came into NEO with some relatively dampened expectations thanks to my previously mentioned friend's opinions (he said the game was fine but not as good as the original). Heck, I didn't even mean to play the game, it was just a happy coincidence that NEO TWEWY released in the middle of my original TWEWY playthrough.So, with your expectations and some of my background set up, let's talk about NEO: The World Ends With You. If you want it, the tl;dr is that NEO: TWEWY is a very good modern JRPG which you should play if you're a fan of that genre, that's the sequel to an exceptionally great modern (for 2007) JRPG.Overall, NEO has a few standout features. The art direction is outstanding, the music is fantastic, the dialogue is flawlessly modern and realistic (even if half of Sho's dialogue is utterly bewildering to people who haven't taken Calculus 2 or above, because that's the point), the character design is great (even if I think that Fret's spine is an eldritch abomination that cannot exist), the story is very solid, the appearances of the original TWEWY cast are done very well and tastefully while giving the new cast some room to shine, and the world itself is simply cool to run through. The gameplay is also exceedingly interesting, feeling like a frenetic combination of your standard 3D action RPG with the added uniqueness of using multiple attacks at the same time dramatically increasing your risk of death.In fact, I really rather struggle to think of things that NEO falters in on its own merits. The most you can say is that some of the characters don't get a lot of time in the spotlight and feel a bit underwritten.So... alright, on its own merits, is this game worth playing? I mean... maybe? It's hard to say. I think it's better than the other big, modern day JRPGs: Persona and SMT, since I believe the gameplay is more interesting, the music is better, and the characters are more believably written, but a solid part of the game is how it calls back to and evokes/subverts expectations of the original game. Without that context, a small portion of the game is darn near incomprehensible, and you won't really get a lot of the coolest stuff. I think the game is a very solid and well-done 8/10, with a few flaws and some fairly under explored characters, which ultimately feels a bit like it doesn't have the thematic resonance of some games, but there's nothing glaringly wrong about the game.But then comes the question of "is this game good as a sequel?", and here's the thing. It's fine.Like, with all those things I listed about the game, the dialogue being excellent, the art direction being great, the music being flawless, the gameplay being cool and unique, and the world itself simply being interesting and fun to walk through... the same applies to the original TWEWY too. And unlike in NEO, the original TWEWY's characters are exceedingly well written, with only a few characters feeling genuinely like they were underwritten or underdeveloped (original TWEWY spoiler) , heck, even the side characters like Mick or Ken Doi or The Prince or the major antagonists like Kitaniji or Sho or Higashizawa or Uzuki/Kariya, they all feel like they were interestingly explored and fulfilled a solid role in the story. Comparing that to NEO's cast, where (NEO major spoilers) , that's a total of just 2 of the party members: (more NEO major spoilers)  who feels like they got a significant and interesting amount of writing/development. This is still better than the other major modern JRPGs, but it's not good.So, when you look at it as a sequel, NEO has a few flaws because of the things it does worse than the original, most of which show up in the form of the characters. Much of this can be explained with writing time constraints, they tried to tell a whole new story of whole new characters, but also wanted to find time to pay homage to the original cast, and also didn't want the game to be entirely reliant on people having played the original TWEWY. These goals are cursed, you can't have all three at the same time without an exceedingly large amount of development time, and they only had so much time. In the end, this game's only real faults lie in its own near impossible goals, and in the end, the game is still absolutely worth playing if you enjoyed the original TWEWY, and even without that context, if the game looks cool, if you're a fan of action RPGs and modern day JRPGs, if the OST sounds good, then I'd recommend playing it. Just, you know, buy it when it's on sale, because $60 is too darn much.

_childDocuments_.review: Square Enix marketing absolutely failed this game. While it doesn't quite hit as deep as the original TWEWY, it's still a very effective story told with the help of some pretty clever gameplay integration.If I had a nickel for every time Tetsuya Nomura made a game about Fighting Against Fate (TM) I'd be richer than Elon Musk, so some of the thematic material (especially near the end, as you'd expect from a JRPG) is a bit boring and predictable. But NEO does succeed in tackling the core message of TWEWY (connecting with people) from a different angle: while Rindo isn't nearly the misanthrope Neku was, the struggles he endures with his larger social circle are quite compelling. The side characters receive varying amounts of development (mostly near the end of the game), but are all ultimately deeper than their dialogue quirks, which is much more than I can say for other games of the genre.The combat is certainly quite button-mashy, but it's designed in such a way that each of your 6 attack buttons (!) must be mashed/held/charged in a different way, so there is a kind of mechanical rhythm to fall into that's pretty unique to this game. The preparation elements of gameplay (pins, food, and threads) are all fleshed out even further from the original game. It's just as satisfying here.My only issues gameplay-wise lie with some questionable enemy and boss designs. NEO is, for the most part, an easy game (which I have no problem with, as you can increase the difficulty and lower your own level to gain more rewards), which makes it a bit jarring when an enemy on normal mode suddenly has a borderline one-hit kill with a surprisingly unforgiving attack window.The visual style is rather low-detail but is in my opinion the best possible way of translating the original's artstyle to 3D. Besides, this game's presentation is mostly carried by its art direction anyway. The character designs/outfits are top-notch; literally every character is drippier than a monsoon.Also, THE MUSIC. It is as good, if not better, than the excellent soundtrack of the first game.It's Linkin Park: The JRPG and it's freaking incredible.It also has Sho Minamimoto, who is the single greatest character in fiction!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid JRPG.  Reminds me of a strange combination of Kingdom Hearts, and Persona.  The aesthetic is unique compared to most other games, and the music has no right being as good as it is.I love the pin system as well.  Anything that contributes to character growth that isn't just basic levels, and gear is always a plus for me.The price is a tad high so I don't blame anyone for waiting especially with how many other PC JRPG's are releasing this year.  There definitely isn't a shortage of things to play.  Although I definitely can see myself getting my moneys worth if I aim for a 100% completion.  It also runs great on Steam Deck so far, the default controls were kinda weird to get used too (I fought with the main menu longer than I care to admit).The only nitpicks I have so far is that the story can be a bit hard to follow if you haven't played the first game, but the narrative as a whole is still decent.  Hopefully they release its predecessor on Steam someday.  I also think Square did a poor job with marketing this game, and shadow dropping it only mere days before Persona 5 Royal drops on Steam.  Although this in no way affects the actual quality of the game.Can't recommend if you aren't into JRPG's.  If you despise anime like presentations then this also definitely won't be for you.  Although this is a fine addition to any library for fans of the JRPG genre, and I highly recommend it if you are.

_childDocuments_.review: The World Ends With You (=TWEWY) has become a cult classic and over time its reputation grew to be the best game on the Nintendo DS. NEO does not need to hide as it is a worthy sequel which is not a straight upgrade, but a side grade in comparison. So TWEWY is a DS game and has over time become a legendary game that holds perfectly up to this day. In preparation for this review I played through it and was delighted to see a game surpassing my expectations to such a degree. TWEWY is a game about bonds and identity. While this motive has been discussed to death, the way it was told, has been perfected. TWEWY always plays in the now, the time it was released. For TWEWY it was 2007 and it captured its cast and Shibuya with style to build a narrative of how characters shape their own world and grow as a result.All the while connecting these motives with a colorful cast, ludo narrative resonance (=gameplay and story feel coherent) and outstanding design in music and visuals, especially considering it was on the DS. No wonder that Square Enix definitely wanted to make a sequel for this widely successful game, right?Well, it was mildly successful. 1 million units sold is not bad, but not great either. And as such the IP laid dormant for a decade. In the meantime the team always pushed the game to get re-released, to get a sequel and just kept it from getting forgotten. TWEWY quite literally survived by the passion of its developers and fans.And finally it paid off, NEO The World Ends With You got greenlit.So before we get into the game, I have first to explain the gameplay and why you need a controller. NEO uses a button attack system. Every character in the game can be equipped with one attack and can execute it in battles which play relatively similar to the Tales of series but a lot faster and more airborne. More characters mean more buttons and more buttons means more attacks which then lead to combos and this is when the game starts to open up. I have to stress that the gameplay is superb and while button mashing works for most enemies, NEO has quite the learning curve for the experienced player who wants to test their respective limits. You don't need to, but you can. There is a lot of to get into, but I would recommend just going with the flow as experiencing the battle system is something completely different from any other game I had played before that.NEO is arguably extremely stylish. It uses a graffiti color palette with a comic book art style that uses the general visual design of anime and manga. Framing this with large black lines and large monochrome surfaces (with subtle texture maps for the environment). While NEO is in-between AA and AAA, the style is enough substance to characterize the whole town. The game uses many clever tricks that give Shibuya a soul that is difficult to imitate. Shibuya really feels like this place where people can be whatever they want and express themselves, because everything feels like it is an acceptable part of this world.Now, let's talk about the big one:The OST.NEO is insane it terms of music variety, having 51 tracks, many of them with vocals. And every OST is used perfectly to characterize every given scene and mood which makes the respective set pieces hit that much harder. Even without the context the songs remain completely listenable. Without even referencing the variety of the OST, NEO dabbles in so many genres lacking any symptoms of failure.While I praise NEO most of the review, because the other elements are without much to criticize, the story is the only decisive point in the fandom.On the one hand, it is a great sequel which introduces new characters while also bringing back fan favorites and tells a gripping story with many relevant elements that are perfectly executed. Wait a second, so where does the critique stem from?Maturity and character development. TWEWY did a lot of strong character development for its cast and never stopped giving strong plot beats which encourage the player to keep engaged, while also being genuinely funny at times. NEO is still about character growth, although it handles it differently, we do not see the characters continually evolving, we see individual strong points which finally push them over the edge to better decisions. It is arguably not worse but different and making such a drastic change in a sequel which touches every story element of the game is a bold and respectable move. Yet it will disconnect people who wanted more of the former structure.Additionally, NEO is still a direct sequel:While the new cast is important and strongly characterized, the focus somewhat shifts over the course of the game to the old cast which makes this game bad to start with. It would be enjoyable without getting the references, in spite of that you absolutely should play the first game first. Yeah, NEO is the most fun I have had last year in a game. Which is also the year I played Elden Ring. Not to say that NEO is better than Elden Ring. But for the target audience of this game, NEO is as close as to perfection as it could get with the resources it got, if the marketing is anything to go by.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, I love it a lot, and I'll say right out of the gate that if you're a fan of the original TWEWY, you should absolutely play this game because as a sequel, it's stellar.Generally idk what people's perception of this game are if they've never played the series, and honestly it's really hard for me to say if this is worth playing if you haven't. What I can say is that this will definitely be one of the more unique AAA games you can find on the steam store and a lot of that comes down to how this game, and the original, look at basic mechanics.For instance, levels in this game only increase your health. You can lower your health to increase your enemy item drop rate, which can be further increased by chaining fights together. Stats are increased by eating food, and food is worked off by fighting so you can digest said food. And a lot of what I like about this series is how it constantly adds features until the end, which keeps you playing and looking forward to what you can do next.Also this game has a banger ost and originally I was literally gonna just post the lyrics to one of my favorite songs in the game, , as my review. I'm not gonna talk about the music like, at all, I'm just gonna post some of my favorites.I will say that overall I like this soundtrack more than the original's. Partially because a lot of songs from the original are in here and remixed, but also because it just feels like they went more out of their way to make a higher quality soundtrack and bring in more singers and I really appreciate that because I was honestly worried that was one area this game wouldn't stand up to its predecessor.In fact, I feel like other people kind of cover the game enough, I guess for me rn I just wanna kinda talk about why this game hit so hard. Originally I didn't really know if I'd like this, hence why I waited so long to play it. The original TWEWY is one of my favorite games because it's just so bizarre and unique, it just feels so itself. Like, before this came out I couldn't recommend a The World Ends With You fan a game like The World Ends With You. It's a game that kept surprising you with ideas, one moment you're fighting frogs and bears in the middle of Shibuya, the next you're playing in a beyblade-like tournament, followed by getting lectured on the nature of fashion and trends- a mechanic that melded so well with the idea it was trying to portray that I still think about it a lot. It had a battle system where you were playing on two screens at once and used everything imaginable as a feasible option for how attacks would work on the bottom screen. It just felt like something that they were excited to make and just had fun making.And this game feels like an extension of that. There's a lot of love here and I can't count the number of times while I was playing where I said "" or something similar just because this felt like a game that basically never stopped thinking. There's just so much to unlock and do and the story felt so insanely cathartic after waiting like...14-ish years for this game. It feels like a game that knows how long its been and tries to pay that time back in full which makes some moments hit so incredibly hard.I'm just kinda rambling but to be honest, this is my GOTY, I voted this for most innovative though because I think that fits it best. While I do think some ideas fall flat, particularly the territory wars and fighting other players, overall I was hooked on this game from the moment I turned it on. It's a fantastic sequel and, hell, if you're just looking for a really unique ARPG then you'll probably enjoy it regardless. Huge recommend.---Also, Square Enix like really wanted this game dead and stealth dropped it on steam after leaving it to rot on EGS along with the Kingdom Hearts games that are apparently really well ported but also no one played them, likely because all of the games in question are like, way more expensive than they are on console. So this game being half-off only 2 months later's a big surprise. Totally not complaining, would definitely recommend it at this price but like...why not just release it at this price then? Anyway, love this game, happy holidays~

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore my playtime, I put around 90 hours into this game on Switch.The World Ends With You is one of my top 5 favorite games of all time, so I had really high hopes for Neo. It absolutely lived up to my expectations, and I'd put it just below the first game in terms of quality. The combat's a ton of fun and really unique, the story's engaging, the characters are all some of the best in any game I've played, and it has what is hands-down my favorite video game soundtrack of all time. If you're a fan of the original, play Neo. If you haven't played the original, I'd highly recommend finding a way to do so before playing Neo, but if you can't, I'd still recommend playing Neo because it's that good. It's a passion project that has been treated poorly by a complete lack of marketing, and it's too good to let the franchise die due to the lack of advertisement. If this game interests you at all, please give it a shot. You won't regret it. It also runs really well on Steam Deck if anyone wanted to know about that!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright SE does its best to try and kill this game just because they're icky towards AA games now. Now that that's out of the way, let's talk about the game itself. The game does a good job containing the story for the sequel. If you've played TWEWY, you'll know which character(s) is returning, but if you're playing only NEO, again, the game does a good job introducing the returning character(s) and incorporating them into the new storyline. You might wonder if playing the first game will enhance your enjoyment, well my answer is not exactly. I played the DS version again before playing NEO last year, and what increases my enjoyment is actually the nostalgia I had for TWEWY (I did finish it when it was first released), and in NEO case, again, the game did a superb job in making me love the new casts and loving the interaction between the old and new casts to the point I can't believe SE made this game. But basically, unless you've played TWEWY years ago to develop nostalgia, playing the it won't add much enjoyment when playing NEO. Nevertheless, both TWEWY and NEO is a good game so you should try both when you can.So don't worry, if you want to play NEO only, you can do that and still enjoy NEO in my opinion because of the reasons I mentioned above.One thing that you need to note is that the game will have some slangs and interaction between characters while in battle, so unless you understand Japanese without subtitle, some thing might fly pasts you. I tried using sub, but the difference between what is being said and the subtitle is pretty jarring so I decided to go back to dub. The dub is fine and not bad, despite what people online are being up in torch about the localization.Imo, when taken out of context, it might look like the localization is bad, but honestly, they are not in anyway ruins the game whatsoever when taken with context. If you can read and understand Japanese, then by all means, go for the full Japanese 'buya experienceTWEWY is a game that utilize the DS control to the maximum, but since NEO is multi-plat, the dev took the ARPG route. You will control several teammates at once, each teammates will have the corresponding button assigned to them. The button used is decided by the pins they equipped - which also serves as your skill attacks, so some pins will have different input, skill  and effect on them. Each pin also has its own usage limit, and once it is depleted, it will goes into cooldown before you can use it again.The game also has beatdrop system to make you avoid mashing button and actually consider how you want to use the pins. If you use a pin attack until its finisher, the enemies will have beatdrop counter which you will need to hit with other pin for the beatdrop bonus. This will fill up the beatdrop meter faster and once the meter is at 100%, you can use an ultimate skill. The ultimate skill is decided by the finisher pin, which is the pin you use the last to 100% the meter. If you can't use your favorite ultmate skill, you can trigger another beatdrop at 100% and use your favorite pin to change the ultimate skill.Down the line, you will unlock 300% beatdrop which will trigger a remix attack that will also heal you. In NEO, your team have a shared health pool, so any equipment and health stats you have on your teammates will go into said health pool. The interesting thing is that level only increases your health pool, while stats can be increased by eating certain food that will raise certain stats. You can shove food to your teammate and raise their stats respectively, and of course there's a limit on how much food you can give them. Once they are full, you will need to battle a few times to 'digest' the food before you can eat more food. The equipment in this game are clothes and accessories that you can equip. Each of them has certain effect that can only be activated once your style status meets the requirement, otherwise they will only provide extra status. And as status can only be raised with eating certain food, you gotta eat stylish food to raise your style status. I hear eating a can of air is really really stylish.Oh yeah, each character will have their favorite food, which will gives extra bonus when they eat it. Don't worry, if they eat food they don't like, no penalties will occur except them looking dissatisfied or even outright puking.This is something that I believe more rpg or arpg games should use. Difficulties can be customized to your hearts content at any point of the game, so long you're not in battle. Difficulties like easy, normal, hard and ultimate dictates the damage and what pin will be dropped by the enemies, while lowering your level will only reduces your health pool but increases drop rate so it will make grinding for certain pins much more easier and faster.Once you feel like you've seen everything the gameplay has to offer, the game then throws new stuffs at you, whether through the storyline, unlocking certain skills or something you discover yourself. As an example, at certain point of the story, you will be given the ability to soundsurfs, which is basically a small rhythm minigame. When you're exploring around shibuya, some OST will play, and with soundsurf, you can tap X (on the PS3 controller) to make Rindo 'surf' according to the beat, which will gives you beatdrop meter bonus before starting the battle aside from being fun on its own. As I mentioned in the beginning, the story of the sequel isn't that related to the first game, bar several things that carried over from the extra stuff from TWEWY's switch port, which I recommend you to just watch on youtube if you need it. NEO's story start with a new problem and doesn't depend on you to know the detail of the first game, since most of the time, they only mention "something happened in the first game's reaper game and a player handled it so well he's basically the legendary player, and now word on the street is, he's back in this reaper game", and that's it. Aside from those, the old cast is integrated to the new casts and interacts really well both in cutscene and in-battle interaction. There're some moments that might goes past you, but you can clearly see that it serves as fan service and doesn't contribute that much to the story. So yeah, imo you can enjoy NEO as it is without the need to play TWEWY, but again, both NEO and TWEWY are good so play both of them if you could.The story is also told in a comic book VN style, so still images with word balloons, and some cutscenes in between for the important moment. The battle and exploration is done in 3D area so you can freely explore each area. This is a rare instance where a long awaited sequel is actually good. There're a lot of stuff that can be discussed but the main point of this drivel is for review. And hopefully, what I've told you above is enough information for you to decide whether you want to get this game or not. As for me, the game is a worthy sequel and a great stand alone game too, the gameplay is immensely fun and actually pretty deep(have an ). The story is fun, the casts is lovable and the interaction is fun to watch. I strongly recommend this game whether you're a TWEWY fan or not, the game is simply a fun ARPG with fun story in tow.

_childDocuments_.review: An RPG that sees you hitting the streets of Shibuya and trying to survive the Reaper's game. It's a sequel to The World Ends With You though it is still very enjoyable without having played the first, even if I'd also highly recommend going through it.For those coming from the previous game you get to enjoy this game's rendition of returning elements, such as enemies and abilities, made especially interesting with the change to 3D (for the overworld and battles mostly, the game retains the visual novel style story sequences of the original).Newcomers can expect an adventure through the many cool and interesting locations that comprise Shibuya, that will need you to solve (fairly simple) puzzles and overcome increasingly challenging battles using your party's abilities. Combat in this game has you assigning each party member an ability, which also corresponds to a particular button, and you can use it a number of times before it has to recharge. Each type of ability has different mechanical characteristics and there are many variants of each with different stats that further change how they feel to use, so there's lots of room to experiment, though you can't have more than one character with a psych using the same button, which can feel limiting but is also understandable balance wise. You'll also need to boost your party's HP by levelling up and boost their stats by eating around Shibuya's many restaurants or equipping a variety of clothing items (that sadly don't change your characters' models).And as engaging as the mechanics are they definitely don't take a back seat to the story. It's very engaging and might even make one reexamine oneself, though it does make a few missteps compared to the previous game, and the characters and their interactions are always fun to witness. _childDocuments_.review: I'm actually surprised there was not much advertising for this game because this is one of my favorite games of this year so far. I've played the prequel on the Nintendo DS and also some of the ports and remasters of the original. I had very low hopes because the ports did not do right by TWEWY by any means. To my review:Surprisingly, so far (as of 15.4 hours of gameplay) I am addicted to this game. The visuals, the music, and the gameplay is extremely engaging. Very much in the vain of the prequel the game presents dialogue and story in comic-book style and the visuals still have that manga feel as the first with 2D renders in the story dialogue, but brings the action in 3D. The aesthetic is charming and it's amazing to see what was once a 2D world come alive in 3D as well.The battle system as we know from TWEWY is very complex and engaging, it's interesting to see that even in a more straight forward manner they were able to captivate the complexity of the original blueprint of the game. Moving from touch screen controls to each pin being mapped to a button press allows for fun and interesting strategies in battles, but also makes the usage of the pins less convoluted. Battles are an action beat-em-up style of gameplay but you're using your abilities via pins. Movement takes getting used to as using a pin gives you immediate control of that character and the range of movement is related to the placement of the enemy. Sometimes this makes for weird camera interactions as enemies will be automatically locked onto after one is defeated and the camera will spin wildly or zoom out. It rarely happens, but ti still happens.The story so far has been very fun and exciting and feels similarly to TWEWY but fresh and the voice acting is well done. The characters come to life and present extremely colorful and fun personalities. The beginning has a lot of story to set up, so it can feel a bit like a drag at first, but the first part of the game just as was with TWEWY is mostly for story set up, tutorial, and learning mechanics. It gets you into the action quickly though, it is a bit aggravating to have all of the hand holding, but I'm sure the game can be over stimulating for people new to the franchise.Not going to spend too much time on the music, it lives up to the prequels soundtrack and even features remixes of the songs we've known before. Another soundtrack that works to bring the streets of Shibuya alive with electricity.As for performance, the game is installed on my SSD and I have not had long load times or start ups and there have been no freezes or stutters from my experience. The games runs extremely smooth and even with alot of effects from the battles it feels seamless.The game is very fun and I recommend it especially if you've played the first one, but even if you haven't the game is still very good as a standalone. Knowledge of the previous games story isn't required but there are a lot of cameos and references that make having that knowledge worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: NEO is a remarkable ARPG shinning with so much personality that I didn't want it to end.Controlling a party of outcasts and nerds, your goal is to complete missions in a deadly game with your life on the line. All the characters, mayor or small, are either infinitely likeable or inhumanly despicable, with every second of their interactions and dialogue on screen being a delight. I cannot overstate how enjoyable the core party is, developing a story shinning with wonderful arcs and memorable moments.Combat and sightseeing are the meat of the experience, with shops providing upgrades and stats in forms of food and clothing, while scanning the environment hands over increasingly difficult clashes against the hidden noise enemies. The battles are a simple button mashing frenzy if you like, but the combat mechanics rewards experimentation, team builds and good use of the skills for best effect.The presentation also deserves some mention, with an incredible soundtrack, good voice acting by the cast of the original game (as well as a Japanese audio option), trippy world design and a striking art style tying it all together.Subjectively, this game can however not click with you, particularly if the characters are not enjoyable (due to the amount of story involved), or if you find the combat too repetitive or grindy, which is perfectly understandable.At the same time, while not needed to fully enjoy the story, playing the original game or watching the anime is needed for the sake of getting the most out of the experience.But to me, NEO: TWENTY was an excellent game from start all the way till the finale, that constantly kept itself fresh and exciting. It's a shame it was basically doomed to fail, but anyone who is interested should absolutely give it a go. This is by far one of the best games SE has put out in the past decade and the flopping won't change that.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on sale on a whim because I heard the first one was a somewhat of a cult classic. I never played the first one, and I couldn't really identify with the style, but I decided to jump over my shadow and give it a try.It was worth it.This game is one of the best games I played in the last years and really stuck with me even after the credits rolled. I was laughing about the characters' antics, and while at first I felt they were one-trope cutouts, they did soon show to have heart and problems and depth, that I really enjoyed. I also laughed at the somewhat weird way of speaking some had, like Fret's constant puns or Nagi's olde English expressions. The combat feels great once it clicks, and the music is amazing. The look is super stylized and flows very well. Both the full motion cutscenes as well as the more common comic-like cutscenes are nice, and you get into the story super quick - which is also amazing, btw. I was constantly making room to play because I wanted to know what happens next.There are some problems, that are - in my opinion - minor.Not every cutscene is voice acted, which is a shame, but it's fine. The voice acting itself I really liked, every VA did a great job, even for minor characters.The fights can get a little grindy, especially when you get the ability to link 10+ fights together. It can take up to 10 minutes to resolve them sometimes. But I never felt that grinding is really necessary, and by the end, I just focused on the story fights.There are just a tid too few dialogue lines for combat actions - especially when you only have a small party in the beginning you will hear the same phrases over and over again, sometimes in the same fight. That said, if you like modern action-oriented JRPGs, give this a shot, whether you like the otaku-style or not. It's really, really good. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I first played the original The World Ends With You through its Switch-reworking. Back then, TWEWY had basically become an artifact of a very specific time: it had a very contemporary setting of fashion-hip Shibuya, with themes of modern life loneliness at the advent of phones. It was a peek into a time when anime was growing but not yet really mainstream, and all the little gems could be found on the DS. Then, the unlikely sequel came in a changed world. Now, the game is competing with anime and RPGs being more mainstream, experimental games are dime a dozen on even the Playstation 4 store thanks to indies, and even Kingdom Hearts 3 looks like a big budget Pixar movie. In this atmosphere, Neo The World Ends With You tries to go big while also trying to stay true to its own idiosyncrasies, and the result is a game out of time.    The game puts its best feet forward thanks to the great basic combat loop, translating the iconic fast-paced and unique pin gameplay. You now play as a party instead of two characters, and instead of touch screen controls use your normal controller to (rapid)-tap, hold or single-press a button to activate a pin, each pin getting assigned to one input (with the exception of the B-button being reserved for dodging, the L-stick for moving and the R-stick for locking onto an enemy). Complementing this setup, and enabling the theme of teamwork cooperation, is the combo system: successfully attacking with one character eventually pops up a short combo timer, and if you attack with another character, you build up a combo percentage. Hit hundred-percentiles, and you can launch a strong combo attack. It's a satisfying flow that keeps combat fast paced, especially once you find pins that work well together.Unfortunately, it is the meta-game that stretches this fun gameplay into an odious loop. If you get good at the game, you’ll quickly run into limitations: pins get stronger by levelling them up, but there’s a cap on how many levels they can gain (including levels via evolution) and after that they don’t get stronger. Thus, you’ll need to swap them out for pins with a higher base power on level one. Unfortunately, they will run out and be replaced by Uber-pins, which you can only equip one (or two) of at a time. So, while this meta-system encourages you to experiment by swapping out pins constantly in order to level them up, eventually you will run out of fun pins to swap.It is emblematic of NEO: TWEWY’s ethos of taking everything unique it can from the original and stretching it to its breaking point. You’ll quickly grow tired of the return of Shibuya, as the glacial pacing of the story means you’ll be revisiting the same streets over and over again, punctuated by the stupid inclusion of a bare-bones time travel mechanic, making you even replay parts of the mission again and again. Add in a story that in the middle is blatantly padded and often forgets about the new characters in favour of its lore/politicking, a massive need to grind for the best items to unlock, and a chain-encounter mechanic that just begs you to balloon the playtime even further, and the magic of the original quickly evaporates behind this extremely mixed experience. NEO: The World Ends With You proves that certain great things were lightning caught in a bottle, and it would be folly to try to bank on these wonders.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the first installment of the series way back in 2008-ish when the english dub/version was first released and thoroughly loved almost everything about it. Though, I do personally feel that the sequel falls short of its predecessor. To me these are the selling points: Story: > Decent story telling > Events of the past game that lead to this current one aren't fleshed out that well though they    are explained> Certain plotholes are answered in game, whilst some are left for the player to decipher    themselves> Still leaves a bunch of plotholes in anycase > Will probably love the game if you are a fan of the prequel> World Building is decent with the story sometimes going out of its way to flex it> Grey-ish feeling type of ending > Will leave you wanting for more if you're the invested type of story gamer> Comparison to TWEWY DS:Combat (X-Box Wireless Elite Series 2 Controller): > Takes time to get used to> Unique to the point whereby it would be best to watch a video of it. Some may not enjoy it    as it is very button-mashing > The dodge in the game sometimes feel a bit sluggish. Probably the game design intent so    as to not abuse i-frames. It is however still very forgiving. > Fingers might have to be placed in an awkward position in order to pull off most efficient    amount of burst damage (This does not count if you are remapping keys for easy of    gameplay) > Also every time you change a 'weapon', you may have to reposition one of your fingers> No Tin Pin (Prequel enjoyers will know this mini game)Difficulty: > Personally, very easy even on Hard as you can grind stats really easily  > All of the attacks in game are the type where you just have to time your dodge and i-frame    throughArt: > Every aspect of it is unique, from the world design, to the characters> Only a few cases here, you will either love it from the start or dislike it> It's not exactly persona-ish or kingdom hearts as well > One gripe that i do have is that, i wish some of the characters were designed less gaudy, an    example would be the character's coat and  parka. They feel a tad unnecessary. World:> Exploration is very linear as the game is limited to a few areas> There isn't much to do honestly speaking in terms of exploration aside from hunting specific    enemies > Per single chapter might include 1-3 side quests with some not having any at all, highly    recommended to do them as the rewards they give are impactful and actually contribute to   QoLs and gameplay Soundtrack/Music: > Easily has of the best soundtracks in the recent gaming scene > Everyone should be able to appreciate something from their wide collectionAll in, the game is still good and will put a smile on your face if you loved the prequel. I will only be providing a word for word review as per written above since I do have my biases in providing a scored review.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the low Hours, I've played and beaten the game on Switch.First off, for anyone still confused by this because Square Enix refuses to market this game properly: . This is not yet another version if The World Ends With You, it is a  set three years after the events of TWEWY .As it is a sequel it will contain massive spoilers for The World Ends With You. Specifically it spoils post game content. While it stands well enough on its own as a standalone title, it definitely works  if you come into it with the knowledge of the original game.NOW To the actual review:NEO was my GotY for 2021, easily. Combat is chaotic and immersive, full of bright colors and varied abilities. Not quite as varied as the original game, and taking a very different form, but playing it made me grin from ear to ear. For those familiar with the original it isn't nearly as difficult. I played through all but 1 day and 1 boss fight on Ultimate Difficulty: The Day because the game literally forces you to play on Easy for the missions and the Boss because he is a difficulty cliff for no readily apparent reason.The story has all the classic TWEWY charm, focusing on the Reaper's Game, but not as old fans remember it. Something's different this time around. Something's . While there are plenty of returning cast members (every old major character returns as at  a cameo), the focus is on the new kids as they navigate this new Game.However, the story does feel like it needed a little more time in the oven, feeling more editorially rushed as the game goes on, and it's clear where they ran out of their surprisingly slim budget in the final rush of the game. There's one day at the end that is as long as the entire rest of the Week combined and you  be feeling the Fatigue of it.I love everyone in the new cast, even the ones I hate.Except Kubo.Kubo can get eaten by a shark.In proper TWEWY fashion the music is absolutely . NEo features more Metal and Hip Hop this time, as opposed to the more techno sound of TWEWY. Several songs have been added to my personal playlists and I have a copy of the official soundtrack that lives in my car.The background details are wonderful, and even side characters feel fleshed out and developed.Localization is excellent except for one major quibble I have where a major cast member was uh... De-Gayed (a certain character is Gay in the original Japanese version, and in English is instead portrayed as having a very strong romantic and sexual attraction to a female character). However, the rest of the cast is Queer and ND enough that I can forgive the Localizers for it.There is one big issue I have with the game and that is a lack of a "minigame". The original had Tin Pin Slammer, and that seems to have fallen out of style since then with nothing to replace it. Instead we have field abilities.Oh and time travel.Huh I could've sworn I just saw a bird...

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, NEO TWEWY good.I had a hard time gathering my thoughts on this game, so let's get the superficial out of the way first:This game oozes style. It does a beautiful job translating the art of the original into a 3D environment, thick lines, nice effects in combat. Love the dialogue being expressed through dynamic paneling. I'm particularly in love with how the geometry and perspective shifts as you walk through the streets of Shibuya.Great soundtrack as well. I will definitely be listening to that back and forth over the coming weeks. The remixes of old songs are a bit hit or miss. Some I prefer, others at least don't defile the original and can exist seperately from them.Next up: Combat. Idk how they did it, but they translated the 2D beat-em-up combat of the original into a 3D format as if it was easy. Tons of pin combos you can play around with, tho I feel like the balancing fell flat a bit. Some are just objectively a lot worse. Combat itself is good. A bit tough to get the hang of at first, since you have to keep track of multiple buttons at once, but once you get the hang of it it's really fun. I wonder if there was a way to make it accessible tho. Unfortunately people with motor function issues are left out of experiencing this game.In terms of story, there's a lot of old ground being treaded here. Makes sense, since it's a sequel. But because of all the similarities, for a while, I thought this could be used as a good entry point for new players, up until the game makes absolutely sure you know that this is a sequel and you don't have the full picture if you've missed out on the DS game.Now where the game doesn't tread old ground, it's a bit complicated. A lot more subtle compared to how aggressively overt the first one is. This is neither criticism nor praise, but I found it worth pointing out that difference. Overall I have to say, though, that this game had some impossible shoes to fill and made the best of what it could give. That's as far as I want to go in talking about it for this review.And with that, I think I give NEO a good recommendation. A shame I passed on this game for so long because I was under the impression it wouldn't be worth the look. I'm glad I was wrong.

Graphics are very colorful and stylized, it will not age and will always look incredible.Lots to do, side-quests everywhere with tons to unlock and you have a nice menu for tracking.Replay value is through the roof, custom difficulty selects even changing your own level for higher rewards.Cons:Your hands are going to hurt. ♥♥♥♥♥ fast paced man and you may have to withhold jerk/rubbin off for awhile.Party size gets BIG to the point where depending on your controller style combat can get tough to nail down.Some songs play WAY to often than others to the point where repetition starts setting in.Teammates try their best to be smart in combat but they will still stumble and take damage which hurts you.Literal game-play mechanics are locked behind certain side quests, some of which are crucial.Again the games amazing, worth playing at least once in your life.
