_childDocuments_.review: A very much needed sequel to a game that struggles to have its play style replicated the more its ported.NEO: TWEWY is everything you could want out of a sequel.While the story is connected to the original game, it can be enjoyed fully without needing to play it.Legacy characters appear constantly throughout the game, but not to the point its suffocating and the new ones get sidelined for the purpose of jingling keys in your face.The combat especially has been revamped without compromising the feel one could expect either.and best of all, for the folks out there whom all I've mentioned clicks with, the game incentives you further and further with rewards to try everything if you feel inclined.I'll also throw out very quickly, No, KH is in no way connected. What happened in dream drop distance, stayed in dream drop distance. like everything else Square Enix related in the KH games.the big question is, what version should you buy?Either PC or PS4. if you care about physical media would be the only real reason to recommend the console versions of the game. The switch version is fine, however the slight dip in performance, while not terrible by any means, does eat away enough of your time if you have hopes of being a completionist. more so if you're having your first blind run of the game.Combat incentives you to consecutively fight monsters back to back without breaks. In between each round theres a set loading screen, the switch version noticeably takes 3-5 seconds longer everytime. Spread that upwards to the maximum you can unlock of 20 fights in a row (provided win and dont have to start from the beginning), it stacks up over time. Combined of course with the switch versions biggest flaw, controller options. Simply put, neither the joycons or the switch pro controller feel right to play with, especially for a game like this that practically requires you to press as many buttons as you can rapidly.The PC version of course can have the best performance, with the added bonus of supporting your controller of choice. having done 2 full runs of the game, the switch version ate 60-70 hours of time, while playing on pc, with a better controller to boot (xbox series x/s specifically) I was not only able to shed 20-30 hours off my time, but was able to nearly 100% the game by comparison. All I had left where a couple collectibles I missed because I wanted to wrap it up, and the entirety of post game since I was ready to move on by then.As far as the gameplay itself, it works and feels great to play, for about 20 hours. the closer you get to the end game, the more I would get antsy wanting to wrap it up, but being an RPG thats a bad idea as levels and lacking money can very quickly work against you should you decide to B-line the story with no side objectives. the whole time, the game is giving you more and more ways to fight enemies and chaining together battles consecutively, making it all take even longer to get through that the charm sadly wears out after a while.ultimately the games an 8/10, and I do intend to go back into it again for 100% completion as I never truly finished the post game before. I cant overstate that enough, as much I may ramble about the fun running thin after a while, its still good enough that I've not only done 2 full runs, but still want to go back and 100% after I've had some time to play something else.TLDR: 8/10, buy the PC version if you love controller freedom, buy on PS4 if you value physical media

_childDocuments_.review: This will be a whole lot of yapping but a TL;DR is YES PLEASE PLAY IT BUT PLAY/WATCH THE FIRST TWEWY BEFOREHAND.NEO:TWEWY single handedly beat Fire Emblem Echoes as my favorite game, after it was my favorite for over 5 years. This was genuinely the best gaming experience I have ever had in the longest time, everything this game had to offer was amazing. The beat-em-up like gameplay with rhythm aspects to reward you for taking your time and syncing attacks, the absolute BANGER set of songs with a comtemporary feel to them, the amazing story, the memorable cast of characters, the visuals, graphics, EVERYTHING about this game is amazing. The only real flaw to me is that the first week of the game can be a bit slow, but honestly I was so focused on the amazing gameplay and extremely appealing artstyle that i pretty much didn't notice at ALL that the game's story was slow. I've been praising the game, but I do want to say that the only real flaw to me is that the world-exploration CAN get a bit repetitive, but the game is very beautiful so i didn't mind re-visiting areas much at all. There's simple puzzles you have to complete (things ilke fighting enemies, or solving questionares to test your memory of the game) in order to traverse, so it feels as if you EARN each piece of the world that you unlock. The fact that the only flaw is so easily defended is what made this game so amazing to me. The story past the first week is absolutely memorable, but you DO need to have knowledge of the first game beforehand. For the quickest summary, I'd recommend The World Ends With You: The Animation! It's definitely not a perfect summary by any means, but honestly it will get you updated enough to quickly be able to understand what's going on in those weeks, as there's some returning characters that wouldn't be as satisfying to see otherwise. It's such a shame that this game didn't perform well, but I truly hope that someday this game will make its way to popularity like other JRPG series managed to!

_childDocuments_.review: NEO: The World Ends With You is the follow up to the cult classic DS game of the same name (minus the NEO). As Rindo, you are taking part in the "Reapers' Game". In order to avoid getting erased from existence, you must complete objectives in this 1-week competition. Utilizing the pins you get, you must fight the "noise" and level up in real-time combat to make your way through the game. With a gorgeous art style and some enjoyable mechanics, it is certainly a good time! But how good is it on the Steam Deck?The answer is a resounding yes! It makes sense, considering it is a Switch game first, but nonetheless, it is still a wonderful thing to see! The game doesn’t have many graphical settings, but it does work fantastically right off the bat! Without changing anything, and setting a TDP limit to 6, you can expect around 11W - 13W of battery drain for 4 - 4.5 hours of battery, temps below 65c, at native 1280x720 resolution and 60 FPS! It looks gorgeous and feels like a perfect fit on the Deck. There is some stuttering that happens during the game, which seems to be from running around or getting into combat, but this alleviates itself pretty quickly so it doesn’t impact the gameplay that matters.The game does start the game out with the A and B buttons switched. This means that hitting A will cancel and B will confirm. This makes sense as the ABXY layout on the Switch has it reversed. You can easily change the inputs in-game though, which I recommend doing. If you decide not to, it isn’t super jarring and not necessary, but it did make going through dialog and confirming things much easier.NEO: The World Ends With You is a really fun game and if you’re a fan of the series, or JRPGs in general, this is definitely one to check out. I am happy to report that, on the Steam Deck, it runs like a charm other than the minor stutters here and there.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from the PS4 version, I have put at leave 40-50 hours into grinding out pins and am currently on Week 2, Day 3. PLEASE give this game the support it needs, as SQUENIX just doesn't seem to care at all.As for an actual review: The combat is pretty solid imo, the pin selection gives you a lot of variety to how to take out your opponents, from long ranged attacks, closed ranged physical attacks, to setting trip wires to bind your enemies. One thing that I love about the combat, is that each teammate is assigned to a button, and your mission is to find out which pin synergize with each other, cause the more you do so, the more damage you can do, and max out your Groove Gauge, all in all, the combat is a solid 8.5/10 for me.The sound and music, top tier. Buy the soundtrack, it is that good. A lot of variety with rock, pop, and the occasional heavy rock. 10/10 easily.As for exploration, it's pretty decent. You unlock more areas throughout the game, but it limited, as this game works on a day-by-day structure. For example, what you can explore on the 1st day, you may not be able to explore on the 2nd or 3rd day, but there are times where you can explore a lot of areas in 1 day, particularly the . Just a small nitpick. I'd give it a 7.5/10As for Story, while I can't comment fully on it as I am still working my way through it (and starting over on PC lmao), I can say that the story is pretty entertaining so far, it even got a few chuckles out of me from some of the character interactions. There is at lease one thing that you participate that can be irritating on a first playthrough, which would be the  If anything though, I would HIGHLY recommend playing the first TWEWY, as things in the sequel won't make sense unless you played the first game. All in all, story is a solid 8/10 for me.And that is where I will leave my review for now, I apologize for it being basic, but this series seriously needs all the attention that it an get, cause SQUENIX just doesn't care, considering that they shadowdropped it HARD. All that's left is for the Kingdom Hearts games to come to Steam. It's been over a year and a half now, SQUENIX. If NEO:TWEWY after a little over a year, and FFVII Remake after  can come to Steam from EGS, the KH Series can at least be shown some love.

You can avoid all optional battles if you want; stat increases aside from HP come from eating food, not leveling up. I played the whole thing on Hard without much grinding. Boss battles can be somewhat frustrating if you die due to length of fights and unskippable phase transition scenes.Story and Character - 8/10 Starts off slow and ramps up fast after the first week. It's a very anime-y story and the characters are purposely over-the-top, but like the original, it has a heartfelt message to convey about humanity and empathy. I find the cast to be very charming.Style and Soul - 10/10 These games are all about the style to me, and that's what makes them enjoyable. It's a visual treat even in 3D with the bendy perspectives, and the soundtrack gets you tapping your feet as you're walking through the city. Relax, listen to the music. _childDocuments_.review: The short and sweet of it is that if you played and enjoyed the original TWEWY, NEO is an enjoyable, if far from perfect, sequel experience.Set three years after the events of TWEWY, NEO starts you off with a new cast of characters. Unlike TWEWY, it's not a new partner per week, but rather a slowly accumulating party that you get to use in combat, each member with a pin of their own. While it lacks the charm of using the Nintendo DS' dual screen functionality, the controls feel much better (at least for noobs like me) and more intuitive, and a lot of minor gameplay frustrations from the original have been addressed, from figuring out each party member's favorite foods to being able to replay earlier chapters soon into the game. The visuals and music are as top notch as ever, much as might be expected from the series.The main potential sticking point is mostly the plot and characterization. The new party cast is a fun bunch, but Rindo's character and development arc fall a little flat compared to Neku's, even if the latter had a fairly predictable one. The side characters and villains generally aren't outstanding characters, but they perform their function well for the most part.The slow reintegrating of the old cast throughout the story and their increasing involvement in affairs is a mixed bag - on the one hand, it's sweet as an old fan to see them come back, older and wiser; on the other, it lessens the attachment and impact of the new cast we're supposed to fall in love with. The story also generally is worse about appropriate foreshadowing, with events all the way up to the ending appearing out of seemingly nowhere and justified with "higher powers at work".All in all, it's a fun and reasonably satisfying experience, but you can't help but ask a few questions, like a good meal that had some odd condiment choices. Regardless of its flaws or questionable choices, NEO is something I think every fan of TWEWY owes themselves to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% lives up to the original. Combat is obviously different (especially compared to the DS version) but there's a lot of QOL stuff that makes it much easier to enjoy. Namely, a map that actually helps, actual side content, and having your team be able to dodge on their own. The multitasking was part of the appeal for me in the DS version but in this one you have several more party members. It's a little thing, but not having to worry about the character you aren't directly controlling? Great for peace of mind. Also the story is... on par with TWEWY? It didn't resonate as much with me as the original but it felt more well put together. And the difficulty and level system carries over here - you can lower your level and change difficulty at any time in exchange for better drops. Lowering level doesn't change damage output, so it just comes down to how familiar you are with enemy patterns etc. Being underleveled doesn't make any encounters impossible. The buildcrafting can be a bit obtuse, especially with the party size, but once you get the hang of it, it's... neat. I wasn't blown away by the options but I do appreciate the ability to lean into playstyles I prefer. In particular, those were charge attacks and vortex saber, with a small amount of rapid fire projectiles and auto melee attacks. the directional control attacks you'd find around the game didn't click for me, so I could just avoid 'em entirely. And the localization is funny. You can, like, pinpoint almost the exact year this game was localized by reading the dialogue alone. It's awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: NEO:TWEWY is a masterfully crafted game. If you are allergic to RPGs, then you should try NEO.This game might seem like your usual RPG, but it is actually more of an action game with RPG elements than a pure RPG.Combat is simple enough for starters, but not braindead boring. The skill ceiling is high enough that the gameplay will keep you hooked for a very long time, plus it looks cool as heck!Visually speaking, the game looks amazing despite running on Unity. Nomura did a great job of elevating the original's street fashion looks- the new character designs feel modern while still maintaining the first game's charm.The OST is zetta great, too. Just go listen to it.The current age of gaming is so dull and braindead, and, somehow, NEO:TWEWY manages to subvert all your expectations. This is truly a breath of fresh air, and you can tell how much effort and love was put into this game, the devs did a phenomenal job, so much that they deserve all the praise in this world.Amazing world, fantastic art direction, funky OST, addicting gameplay- a 10/10 for me.Plus, stan our lord and saviour, the mathematician catboy himself, Minamimoto. <3

_childDocuments_.review: I 100%'d this game on the PS5 at release. I haven't yet played much on steam other than to check out how NTWEWY plays on Steam Deck; I'm planning to re-100% it over the holidays.Overall the game is a pretty fantastic sequel to TWEWY. It's got a banging soundtrack and visuals yet again. The story is reasonably good (with a different message & focus than the original - so yes, the story has a different vibe to it, since we have a different main character!) and all the characters are generally wonderful.The game plays pretty great on steam deck (albeit with some questionable default input binds, e.g. A being cancel and B being confirm, due to it mapping to Switch/PS5 button locations) as you'd expect, given that it launched on Switch and PS4/5. The main issue with the game stems from how SQEX did not market this game at all. This is a sequel to a 14 (now 15) year old game and the initial launch was given 0 coverage by SQEX due to them going hard on Marvel content at E3, the initial Epic release had 0 lead-up or fanfare, and then the steam release was also just stealth dropped a day before the Persona 5 Royal release, with 0 prior announcement or anything. If you're wondering why you haven't heard ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about this game, it's because Square Enix *wants* TWEWY to die, apparently.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kind of obsessed with this game lmao. So far, its been a fun, linear JRPG with an entertaining and interesting cast of characters. You can customize your moveset, making new combinations to enact different strategies. It isn't a strategy-heavy game, but certain power combos and elements may be necessary.Also if you want to go in blind I'd recommend not looking at Steam community stuff concerning the game. _childDocuments_.review: **Originally played on Switch**NEO does an incredible job translating all of TWEWY's crucial systems into something possible—and palatable—on a standard controller layout, without compromising the variety, complexity, and soul of the original. If you loved TWEWY, you'll love this. And if you didn't, you might find comfort in the knowledge that NEO is far more accessible and refined. TWEWY is my favorite game of all-time. For 15 years, not only did I clamor for this experience, but I also built up an expectation that I genuinely never thought could be met. Believe me when I say, I went in expecting disappointment, and I left with a fulfillment I can't quite describe. However, Square's minimal marketing and seemingly-negative view on the title has been heartbreaking to watch. NEO has absolutely not been treated with the same level of fairness and respect as other titles released in the last year, and has performed abysmally as a result. I doubt we'll ever see TWEWY again because of Square's typical, head-in-ass philosophy, but I'm happy I got to see all my friends one more time.

_childDocuments_.review: NEO Twewy might be one of the best game i purchased, and maybe even on Steam.Its a sequel to a very unique DS game, The World Ends With You, the game that is played on 2 screens at once and tries to make the most out of DS. Buttons, Touch Countrols, even Voice are used in combat.The reality is that there will never be a game like that again unless someone makes a 2 screen system like a DS. Infact the newer versions of the original game for phones and Switch remove a lot of the combat aspect due to them being 1 screen only [and Switch version even removing Voice attacks]NEO Twewy has the ask of being a sequel to something it cannot really be. With that said.I adore NEO Twewy, i love the map, i enjoy the characters, combat is fun, visual style is fantastic, music is top notch just like the first game, the Devs really did a fantastic job on making the sequel, although again not as unique as the first game.Your attacks are tied to pins, which each have a different input [on PC this being the I O P J K L yes its as weird to play as it sounds] There are pins that are simple sword like slashse, pins that shoot, pins that heal, pins that you hold a death ray, pins that drop bombs, pins that drop objects, charging pins and then each of those has variations, different healing pins heal differently and different slash pins also work in a different way. These all go really well together, you could be holding a pin that burns someone while at same time shooting them with some balls of fire or charge up rockets. Although you do have to play a bit to get larger variety of said pins.Story and characters are cool, it ain't entirely up to the first game in this part, characters are weaker however there are more of them, and Story while it is pretty cool especelly more you spend time in it, first game had a better hook in. In this series as best as i can explain, people that passed away are given a second chance, or well will be given after playing a week of The Game, that potentinally leads more likely to their death.Tho rather than the first which was about said people being in pairs of 2, it is now groups of people. Now i think both have their upsides and downsides, i do think pairs are better however in the first game you did not know many pairs of players besides yours. In this game along with the group of characters you have you also meet other groups, which is really nice since it kinda felt like you were the only one in the first game minus some parts of it.The music that goes along with this game is some of the best ive heard. Its mix of variety of genres, and it even has remixes of some of the tracks from the first game, my only problem with this is that they did not remix ALL the original tracks. It is a weird complaint but considering how many are remixed from the original, it is a bummer not to hear something like Emptiness or Deja Vu in NEO with a re-do.The visuals of the game are fantastic, although i do have issue with the camera. While you are exploring the map you are stuck to couple of camera angles, while in combat it moves freely. which is really odd. Also more of a complaint coming from the first game, certain spots in the game are bit re aranged and all it does is confuse me when trying to get to some of the spots and then seeing i went a different way.Overall while not as unique as the first game, i absolutely had a blast playing and i would reccomend everyone to not only play this, but also the original game.

I'm basically forcing myself to continue so instead  I'm going to play something else. I'm guessing there's some kinda twist or two that happens maybe with , but it's unfortunate because I can't keep going with the motonony of it all. _childDocuments_.review: Some mixed feelings about this game.I loved the original TWEWY, and this feels like a decent sequel. Apparently there was some extra content added to the original game with some port. which made me feel loss on what was going on from time to time, which made me very salty. Nothing you can't grasp through osmosis, however.What really bothers me about the game is the actual gameplay. They tried to translate the original's system to a 3D environment and I don't think they did a great job about it. Specifically, they replaced the puck that bounced from top to bottom screens with a "groove" system that basically rewards alternating characters when doing combos. This is alright at first, but I am 100% sure it's the indirect reason for my main complain, that is, enemies have way too much HP.You see, the puck on the OG game was dependent on the player on the top/bottom screen, not on the enemy they were attacking. This means that if the enemy died before the puck bounced, it wasn't a big deal, just punch a different one. In 3D, on a single screen, and with the groove being on the enemy being hit, if it dies before the combo's over, he takes the puck with him, meaning you don't get any groove. I am willing to bet the devs tried to solve this by making sure absolutely nothing died before you smacked it around for five minutes, which makes battles really drag on. In single battles it isn't that bad, but in like the OG, in Neo you can chain battles. Up to 20 battles (And maybe more in the postgame?) can be chained at a time, but then you better be ready to spend half an hour fighting the same battles and hearing the same songs over and over and over. Now lets talk music.Music in TWEWY was amazing, absolutely loved it. It had a couple of meh songs, but overall it was a top tier soundtrack. It was so great in fact, that they chose to recycle it for NEO. This would've been fine, except they also "neo remix"'d them all, and 9/10 times for the worse. There's a couple that got better, but frankly I wasn't impressed. The game does bring it's own unique tracks that don't quite compare with the originals, ut frankly fit well enough that I didn't hate any of them... except one of the battle themes. One specific song that has lyrics that go something like "one hundred thousand people blah blah blah" is so bad, but I wouldn't single it out if it wasn't a battle theme, one of the possible themes that you'll be hearing for 30 minutes in a row at a time, if you're grinding money, which you will have to by the end game if you're a completionist. At the very least that specific song is only added to the playlist late game. Other than that, the story felt about par for the course, but the beginning felt off. Something about the first two or three ingame days have this awkward pacing, with the main characters reacting in very weird ways to the information they're given. At points I seriously wondered if I skipped a cutscene by mistake. Thankfully eventually it gets going, and once it does it's alright. A bit of a retread of the original, but different enough to not bother me. Overall, I really want to give this game a much bigger recommendation than I think it deserves. It's frankly not a very good game, but it is one I really enjoyed, in no small part thanks to my love for the original. So if you liked the OG TWEWY, NEO is worth a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: NEO: The World Ends with You

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this review by saying that if what you want is to-the-letter gameplay copy pasted from the original, that's not what you're getting. I can't speak for the remake, as I have not played it at the time of writing.This game is *unbelievably fun.* However, character dialogue is very 'new age,' I guess? A character calls something 'sus' once early in the game for example. Turn off for some, myself included really, because it comes off as cringey. However I can excuse it since the combat gameplay is truly something special.You'll be doing a lot of simple cycling between using different characters (each with only one ability, making it much less complicated than it sounds) for maximum efficiency and a lot of theorycraft for the best combinations of equipment. It can get pretty challenging too at the higher difficulties.Overall? 8/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't really recommend the game. I will finish it, eventually (currently in the middle), but I am already sure it will be a chore more than it will be a fun experience. As expected, the game presents some obnoxious youth culture. No problem there. I knew what I was buying. And although I would have liked at least one grounded character to absorb the barrage of cringey comments and behaviours, I do respect that the game is consistent in its general atmosphere.Apart from surprisingly frequent and long loading times, my biggest problem is the massive and mindless grind. The battle system is at the core of the game and therefore, it should be the part of the game that is the most fun. But I think it is poorly executed, despite some interesting ideas. At the start, you will be excited about some challenges and strategies, but the more the game drags on, it will become more of the same with every fight.So if you are no completionist, you may have fun with the title because the grind will be tolerable. Otherwise, prepare to do pointless tasks over and over again with little to no gain, reward or feeling of accomplishment. Apart from bosses and special encounters, there are about 12 different types of monsters (noises) as long as you don't count their differently coloured versions. And the attack pins you can collect also give you a relatively limited set of moves if you do not take the visual effects into account. It may have a different colour or particle effect or range, but a dash attack always remains a dash attack and pretty much works the same.Wanna master a new barrier skill that you found? It has a slow progression and 10 levels, so prepare to fight approximately 100 fights with one character being unable to do damage.Wanna get all of the clothes available in the game? Here is a store that sells some 100.000Y clothes and items for which you will have to fight even more of the same battles.Wanna have that special pin to complete your collection? Just play the turf war event and try to consistently chain battles of 20 fights each together (about 160 fights in total). And keep that multiplier high all the time, because if you fail to do that once, you'll have to try again.It's not that there is no variety in the purpose of those fights, it's just that those fights are never any different from each other.Edit: Finished the game. Wasn't fun. But I think that with the right mindset, there might be some fun to be had.- corrections: Winning the turf wars is not as hard as I thought, but it is still nothing I'd tell my grandkids about... Prices for clothes go into the millions towards the end. For some pins, you have to farm money, specific pins and also rare materials. Additional nuisance: The most important QOL improvements that would make the game much more enjoyable are only available end- to post-game. Especially the option to repeat boss-fights immediately instead of playing through the entire day again, solving riddles you have already cracked and clicking through endless dialogues that were already mostly redundant the first time. Also, ultimate mode. It is not that much harder than hard mode, and when you unlock it, you can already bodyslam everything up to the last few days, even on ultimate mode and with your level reduced to 1. The loot isn't even anything that would break the game if you could get it early. I have mentioned that in another review: I really don't get why developers consider putting crucial stuff at the very end of the game a good idea.In my opinion, if you want to enjoy the game:- Do not try to 100% complete the game. There is a "secret ending" for finishing a lot of tedious tasks, but you can save several hours of your life by watching a 1 minute video on Youtube. It's not even special, just a voiced dialogue in which a guy says to another guy that he likes a choice the main character made.- Get only the pins and clothes you find useful. Gatto Nero (and Hog Fang) have the definitely best pin sets.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game's grind was pretty killer for me. Not having beaten the first game, clearly I have some bias and confusion when it comes to entering this one. That's on me. However, they explain the world-building well enough and carry some life in the conversation with how the characters interact that I'm fine with the pacing of the story.However, if I can't get into the combat, it's pretty freaking hard for me to enjoy it. Lots of it is just mashing buttons and running around to make sure I'm not about to get creamed by some scrub's attack. Your best attacks are the ones you can spam too, so waiting around until a character's able to use a move (since they can only use one pin at a time) sucks balls.I put up with the experimental music but it got repetitive and sick for me after awhile that I tried my best and just put on Spotify and put the normal music on mute.And I really wanted to make use out of my money so I slogged through until I literally felt my hand developing some form of tense pain from spamming the buttons, and I'd swap from keyboard to controller to try and mitigate that. So both my hands got messed up grinding.There probably is a much better way to play this game which is a shame given how I loved the innovative mechanics of new pins through different difficulties and nothing being truly missable. So when I found myself unable to launch the game again I was very disappointed. That's just me though. Hope you enjoy it more.

_childDocuments_.review: The second week turf war completely killed the fun. So many grindy battles using the same moves over and over. I find the game good with annoyances, but would've regretted getting at the full price.I don't play many games like this, so I don't know how the combat system compares in general, but for me it was quite interesting.You equip combat moves on your characters. Each move is mapped to one of six buttons, which you then press in combat to use the move. There are different types of moves, such as press repeatedly, press and hold, press and release. This creates a kind of fun and chaotic combat, coordinating the different buttons. You can only have one move equipped per key, so this creates interesting choices in what to equip.The problem for me is ultimately there is too much combat. I found many moves just weren't worth using, and with the restrictions on equipping, it was actually quite difficult to improve setups. This resulted in using the same kind of succesful AOE setup for every battle, making every battle effectively the same: Charge bomb, start punching and throw bomb, perform the finisher, switch to another punch, charge bomb, release bomb, use flame/ice/whatever AOE your fourth move is, charge bomb, switch to first punch, release bomb... At some point reach a point when all your moves are on cooldown, so evade until ready. It doesn't matter who you're against, big monsters, swarm of monsters, human enemies, works every time.Killing enemies makes them drop more combat moves, and finding new moves is always fun. And you need to upgrade often to keep your setup competitive, so there's that aspect.The story seemed quite interesting. I figured I will probably never finish the game so I spoiled the story for myself, and ultimately it seems like a generic JRPG plot. Beat down baddies until evil plot is revealed, then beat the evil baddy, get the revelation that there's actually another evil baddy mastermind and beat them as well. The setting is more interesting at least, and the story, when told by the game, is probably better.There is also a ton of needless dialogue that tells nothing and adds nothing, sort like: "well here we are, what do you think guys should we just keep doing what we agreed to keep doing two minutes ago or change plans? Keep doing what we agreed to keep doing? Alright hear YA, we'll keep doing what we agreed to keep doing two minutes ago! Alright, let's do it. Yeah let's do it. Go. Oh he's already going. Yeah he always just does that. We should probably go as well. Ready to go after him? Yeah, let's go after him!"The storytelling seriously should've been compressed by half. So many pointless cutscenes pop up at every opportunity.The graphic design and style are very good, and I like the soundtrack as well. I especially like the cutscene style.

_childDocuments_.review: NTWEWY is easily one of my favorite non-indie games from 2021. It had huge shoes to fill as a sequel, and yet it met or exceeded most of my hopes and expectations.If you're worried that it may be too difficult to get into as a sequel to a DS/Mobile/Switch game with no PC port, you can put those worries to rest. Just about everything that needs to be known about the original game is gradually revealed to the player alongside the new main characters, and while knowing the original gives a lot of extra context it's never required to understand the story. For those who have played the original game, it's a great expansion of the themes of that game that also plays with some of the details of the setting that were previously relegated to the optional "secret reports".Just like the original game, NTWEWY focuses on a group of teenagers in Shibuya who struggle with their personal issues while being forced to play the "Reapers' Game", which requires the players to survive a week while gaining enough points to earn themselves a chance to return to the world of the living. The game features even more named major characters than the original, exploring numerous themes related to the struggles of young people in today's society. Topics like parasocial relationships, agency versus reactivity, and social networks (both literal and digital) feature prominently in the story.As for the gameplay, NTWEWY adapts the Action RPG combat system of the original game to 3D and a large party of characters. Each character in the party gives you another potential input button, and each character is equipped with an ability that determines how they act in combat. Controlling 2-6 characters at once sounds complex at first, but it's actually fairly easy to learn once you give it a try. The game's theme of urban youth is represented in the gameplay by making shopping for food and clothes a big aspect of progression: clothing serves as the "armor" or "accessories" of most RPGs, while food is how you raise character stats.Visually and aurally, the game is very stylized and fun to experience. Some of the 3D cutscenes feel a bit awkward, but everything else in the presentation is thematically powerful. Story scenes are shown in a motion comic style, battle results are presented as graffiti, and the soundtrack is filled with vocal music that evokes the feelings of the characters and story. (In particular, some of the vocal tracks that aren't just designed to fit a certain mood could almost be considered spoilers for certain characters and plot points with how relevant they are to the story.)Regarding the port, I've yet to run into any issues while playing with a controller. Keys and buttons can be rebound, making it relatively easy to set up a comfortable control scheme if the defaults aren't working for you. I've not attempted to play the game with the keyboard, but from my experience with the Switch version I'd highly recommend using a controller, as a keyboard button layout may become unwieldy as the player gains more characters. I have yet to experience any major bugs or crashes in the PC version.Whether you're a fan of the original or new to the franchise, I'd highly recommend giving NTWEWY a shot. Both the story and gameplay are exceptional and inspiring, and the series could really use the support.

_childDocuments_.review: (Honorable mention before we start there is an anime that briefly recaps the previous game I would recommend watching if you want a better understanding of whats going, or play the previous game first I would recommend the phone port, unless you plan to pick up an original 3DS copy.)---Graphics/Art Direction and Soundtrack---The World Ends with You as a franchise is known for its heavily streetwear, and music inspired style, and just like the previous game it can back up the feel its going for quite well. The overall graphics of the game are nothing crazy but everything feels very inspired and you can definitely see the time that when into planning out every detail of the world and the characters you will be spending all your time with. If you aren't looking for something graphically realistic but want a nice RPG with its own style this is the place for you. The real winner is the soundtrack, it alone could feasibly sell this game with little to no other marketing and if I wasn't already a fan of the series and I heard it well its the type of thing I would be putting on a playlist. I found myself listening to it in my free time and it even surpassed all my other music for a month, I would specifically recommend Breaking Free to anyone interested in a true taste of what it has to offer but I feel like there's something here most people will enjoy and the soundtrack really brings the entire vibe of the game together especially when you access an ability called Sound Surfing later on.---Gameplay and Story---For a brief spoiler rundown The World Ends with You as a franchise follows individuals called "players" the players play through whats known as the "Reapers' Game" for a week and whoever wins the game gets a wish granted. That's a very bare bones description but just to give some context, in this game you will play as Rindo who ends up in the Reapers' Game with his best friend Fret. The overall story I would say is pretty good, I found myself still being caught off guard in the final moments of the game and for any who have played the first game there will definitely be some things you remember and that keep you smiling all the way through. It is a bit corny but I would say that is par for a large part of the Square Enix catalog and that's not a bad thing I like it and if you have played something like Kingdom Hearts then this story may be what you are looking for. The gameplay is okay I never found myself upset with it but it definitely becomes much more enjoyable later on when you get some upgrades in what is this games version of a skill tree. Combat revolves around pressing multiple buttons at once each aligned to a party member and their attack, you deal damage and through their attacks cause "drop the beat" popups if another character who didn't trigger the popup hits an enemy you will increase what is essentially your special ability meter called "Groove." The gameplay isn't anything to insane just that coupled with dodging, but I would recommend taking it easy on your hands especially later when you unlock the "Killer ReMix" because if you're like me I promise your hands will hurt if you are someone who can really mash well.---Game Time and Price---To finish the game and its story it will take a rough 20-30 hours with minimal actual grinding, much much longer if you plan on doing a full 100% run for achievements and then it will for sure turn into non-stop grinding, however I did find myself farming money at times so its something to note you may not be able to play through the story start to finish without doing anything else and honestly I wouldn't recommend doing that anyways. This game is rewarding with getting to know its characters most days have additional skill tree nodes you can unlock by interacting with characters, doing these and going back for ones you miss will help you but obviously will increase the runtime a bit. Overall I would say the game earns its price point but only if you already know what you're getting into and are a fan if you are at all on the fence or just have a different idea of how much a game of this length should be then get it on sale for sure.---Final Notes and Bugs---To start off I encountered a single bug in all my hours and it happened twice and it was just a simple game crash, it did happen to me at rather bad times but just keeps your saves up to date better than I did and you shouldn't have any trouble at all. Overall I think the game is worth your time if the art style and music are up your alley, the gameplay isn't gonna win any awards but the game nails the theme its going for and pulls everything together nicely across the board.Below is the basic steam chart of my thoughts.--- Graphics ---☐ You forget what reality is☐ Beautiful☐ Good☑ Decent☐ Bad--- Gameplay ---☐ Very good☐ Good☑ It's just gameplay☐ Meh☐ Watch paint dry instead☐ Just don't--- Audio ---☑ Eargasm☐ Very good☐ Good☐ Not too bad☐ Bad☐ I'm now deaf--- Audience ---☐ Kids☑ Teens☑ Adults☐ Old people--- PC Requirements ---☐ If Chrome runs you're fine☐ Potato☑ Decent☐ Fast☐ Rich kid☐ Super Computer--- Difficulty ---☐ Just press 'W'☐ Easy☑ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Significant brain usage☐ Difficult☐ Cruel and unusual--- Grind ---☐ Nothing to grind☐ Isn't necessary to progress☑ Average grind level☐ Too much grind☐ On that grind forever--- Story ---☐ No Story☐ Some lore☐ Average☑ Good☐ Lovely☐ I'm not crying you're crying--- Game Time ---☐ Could probably play and refund☐ Short☑ Average☐ Long☐ Years off your life--- Price ---☐ Free☐ Worth the price☑ If it's on sale☐ If u have some spare money left☐ Not recommended☐ You could also just burn your money--- Bugs ---☐ Never heard of☑ Minor bugs☐ Can get annoying☐ Constant, atrocious, bugs

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really amazing, making this series one of my favorites. The only problem (with both games in my opinion), is how annoying and stupid the writing of the characters can be. Sure the world building, the idea, the plot, the story is all there, and its pretty amazing (and well written), but some of the characters feel really annoying and Stupid, like really really stupid. Most of the mysteries regarding the game, were pretty much easily solvable by us the players, but the writing made the protagonists feel stupid. However, as much as I hated how the characters were really annoying at the beginning of the game, I appreciate the development that each one of them underwent (in both games), as 75% of the time, I hated them so much, but by the last week, they easily became some of my favorite written characters. Regarding the plot twists, this game has some of the best plot twists, and unpredictable moments to the point that I was getting goosebumps by the end of each day. Regardless, this game is pretty amazing, and I really hope we get one last installment for a 3rd game that would end the story once and for all, especially with how niche this game is.

_childDocuments_.review: Square Enix refuses to aptly advertise this game. The original TWEWY was a DS exclusive that was never ported to modern systems, the anime was released in a bad time; timed alongside some giant animes. NEO barely got any advertising, and was released alongside more giant games. This port was released a day, or the day of? I don't remember, the release of the popular JRPG Persona 5 Royal. _childDocuments_.review: Even with all its jank and weirdness, the first TWEWY game succeeded because of its genuinely novel combat system paired with great characters. NEO fails at both of those things and I can't say it was worth playing at all.Moving from touch screen controls to a controller had its benefits particularly be removing the chance that the game would misinterpret your inputs as happened so often in the original. But it came at too huge of a cost, minimizing the combat system's depth thanks to a conjunction of more standard controls and reduced variety in the activation methods and effects of the various pins. The biggest differences between your combat at the start of the game and the end is just the damage numbers and a small increase in the number of pins you can use concurrently. Its just not engaging, and terrible difficulty scaling plus very little enemy variety mean the combat system just isn't engaging enough to last the full runtime.But far worse for me was the story. By far the best part of the first game was its characters and their emotional turmoil and growth throughout the game. NEO's characters are awful by comparison. They're completely one-note, barely grow throughout the story, and they're all complete idiots who need even the most basic concepts explained to them and fail to make deductions even a child could manage. Even the returning characters fall flat because they just reek too much of fanservice and lack any of the emotional tensions that made them so compelling in the first game.NEO failed to engage me on any level. The combat was too simple, the story uneventful, and the characters forgettable. Apart from visuals and music, there isn't anything about NEO that I actually enjoyed overall. Unless you really loved the first TWEWY game and are willing to put up with an inferior sequel just to see how things progressed after the first game's ending, I don't think I can recommend bothering with this.
_childDocuments_.name: NEO: The World Ends with You

_childDocuments_.review: Does have a lot of things I like, but...I absolutely hate certain aspects of the game.Forced camera positions and shifting cameras, so if you are running around trying to gather mobs, you end up having to change directions repeatedly.Somewhat random feeling cutscenes (no warning marker) where mobs chasing you can still move (and will often just disappear because the cutscenes take so long that they return to their original locations).Timers still run while cutscenes happen. Not sure if this is intentional or not.No way to skip cutscenes that I've seen so far, only fast-forward. Sound effects can't be skipped, so if there is a long sound effect, even with fast-forward, you have to wait for it to finish playing.While it is a neat effect (that mostly stops happening past the tutorial with one exception), the conversation pop-ups disable the rest of your UI while it happens. There is one of these that can reoccur every time you pass a specific type of shop under specific conditions and covers up almost half your screen.Really annoying when you finish an objective early, which means you have to reset the map in order to do the objective. (ie. get 5 chain, but you already did a 5 chain and killed all the enemies on the map).If you play in JP audio mode, make sure you know a reasonable amount of JP. It isn't often, but specific cutscenes are not subtitled.Be warned that button spam (Not necessarily the same thing as button mashing) is a thing here. Instead of an option to hold down a button to fire multiple bullets, you have to click every single shot. On the other hand, you do have 'hold to fire' attacks in the game and 'charge up' attacks where you hold then release to fire, so it isn't as if it wasn't possible to have a hold option (There is one thing I haven't unlocked yet that might change that). No option to semi-reassign similar buttons. (For example, if it is a RT, you can't assign it as a LT without doing a button remap. Some games would allow this. (RT would be the 'slot', but you'd be able to reassign RT slot to trigger on LT press without a complete remap of the buttons).There is a lot happening on the screen during battle, so you can get pretty overwhelmed with the characters dashing around as you use skills.There appears to be an option for clothing loadouts, but you don't unlock it before the quests that require you to wear specific clothing.There are also minor things like asset flips where if a non-key character is facing the other direction, instead of editing the image, it is just flipped. So text is backwards in one scene. Or things on one side of a character are suddenly on the other side.Now, I do love some of the stylistic stuff. It is just that the way they are implemented is in a way that bothers me. I feel like they could have streamlined things quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILER WARNING: Love this game, I played it at launch on PS4 and I couldn't wait to play it again on PC. The new characters are immediately likable and relatable and they're just as great as the characters from the 1st game. The introduction of our old characters was a great call back to the 1st game and the mystery of discovering Neku, who ended up being Beat was a great plot twist. I love Beat, I'm glad we could have him on our team. The grind of the game for 100% was crazy intense, so much to do and way too much time spent, but that was probably just me being stupid.

_childDocuments_.review: IGNORE THE LOW PLAYTIMENEO: The World Ends With You is my favorite game of 2021. An absolutely wonderful entry in an amazing series. While technically being a sequel, you don't HAVE to play the original game. Certain story beats will impact you more if you have played the original, but it isn't 100% necessary.NEO's story is incredible and full of well-written and enjoyable characters. The combat is extremely fun and dynamic, especially later on in the game. And the music... OH MY GOD THE MUSIC. People say Persona 5 has a catchy soundtrack, then they must have never listened to NEO's. (Seriously, even if you don't pick up the game, do yourself a favor and listen to both the OG TWEWY and NEO's OST)That's not to say that the game is without it's flaws. Some characters feel poorly used in the grand scheme of things, certain chapters of the game feel bloated for no reason, and one specific mechanic is WAY overused. But none of the games flaws are so bad that it doesn't make for an incredible experience.All in all, NEO: The World Ends With You is an incredible video game and one that anyone who plays JRPG's would regret missing out on. Play the game. The series needs all the help that it can get right now.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun ARPG with a great soundtrack, funny ass dialogues, really interesting puzzles and a very pretty aesthetic and presentation. The game also runs very well on PC. The combat is a bit repetitive and spammy but its still pretty fun with a whole lot of attacks and skills to try out (in the form of equippable pins). It has some similarities with the persona franchise in terms of hanging out in the city, levelling up your friendship, and fighting monsters that are born from the human psyche (just called noise instead of shadows). If you like RPGs like persona or the previous game you will definitely enjoy this game.Unfortunately the main issue with this game (and the reason I dropped it) is the tedium. The game can be frustratingly slow at times due to weird annoying puzzles with a lot of backtracking, very slow dialogue and initial story progression. The enemy variety is also pretty limited at least for the first 10 hours of game play. The game isn't very challenging even when you use the optional difficulty settings.  The game is fairly long too so the tedium might drive people crazy.If you like slow burns then this game is for you. If you hate backtracking, slow dialogue and progression as well as tedium in general you won't be able to play this for long.

_childDocuments_.review: Started off liking it, but it was dragging a lot. Combat is unique and kinda interesting. But you have to do it so many times that it stops being interesting and becomes a tedious never ending grind. 10 hours in of doing the same thing and you suddenly notice that you’re not even 1/3 through the story. I reached my limit of boredom and had to quit the game more than twice. And it’s always the same thing, the location is the same city and its 20-ish districts, which all look very similar, as city districts would. Game makes you grind for money and exp, but it’s tedious fighting the same monsters forever, even if they're different colours now.The music is good, some tracks are sick. But again, same problem. You hear them over and over so many times that eventually you have to turn off the music just to cope with the game. Most of the pins (combat abilities) are either useless or bad. And there’s at least a hundred of them. I tried to explore as many as I could, but once I realised how similar they were, I gave up, found a winning combination and stuck to it until the end of the game, only upgrading for the same type but with higher damage.This part I want to really highlight. What I found personally off putting is the NPCs. They remind me of NFTs. Once you notice it you can’t unsee it. They are 3-4 templates that get reused hundreds of times. Their clothes and accessories change a tiny bit sometimes. In time I learned to really hate these eerie, off putting, creepy NFT boys. The pacing of the story is terrible. For a game about music and rhythm, it has no flow. You get interrupted and bombarded with comics out of nowhere. It’s especially irritating when the comic itself is very short, but it stops what you were doing just do deliver either nonsense or irrelevant sh1t. You can’t skip them, you can hurry up the animations, it has to load it and the text/panels must appear before you can go next. It happens very often. It’s always text and still images, almost always the exact same still images. 20+ hours of this. Half of them feature the NFT boys. The truly egregious part is when it’s not interesting text, which is the majority of the time.Half way through the game it starts blatantly wasting your time for the sake of “plot”. Go here, go back, go here, go back, times 10. That’s a chapter. Is the pay off worth it? No. In many ways the plot is meandering without a clear goal, which makes me think that it’s all to pad out the run time. You could most likely tell the same story without missing out on anything important by cutting out 60% of it. Most of the redundant “plot” is written around shoehorning in the abilities of your friends. Those abilities get overused like crazy, but they’re not engaging or interesting after the first few times. And I’m sure I’ve used each of them at least 30 times.The writing itself commits 3 sins. It’s contrived, contradictory and “then this happens”. The “and then this happens” type of writing just makes me sigh in exasperation. It’s not even the kind of game that you can breeze through without paying attention. The game quizzes you to make sure you’re paying attention to the incredibly boring and repetitive dialogue.Just when I thought the game was getting a bit more interesting in the last couple of hours, the last boss fight turns into a sh1t show. The pinnacle of visual diarrhea, where even targeting the enemy becomes annoying. It’s like it was purpose built to kill people with epileptic seizures. And worst of all, it’s badly integrated with the existing combat mechanics. 300 groove just makes you shoot into the void, because you can’t target ♥♥♥♥ because of how the game is made, how the camera works.Characters don’t have arcs or growth. The way you meet them is the way they stay throughout the game. They are incredibly consistent, which is a plus. But they adhere to their tropes very strictly.  Otaku girl acts like an otaku, chara boy is always upbeat/head empty/joking, main character has main character syndrome. There’s hundreds of pages of dialogue, but it stops being interesting when I can with certainty predict what the characters will say. It’s like they’re all pre-programmed AIs with specific traits rather than people with personalities. Villains are also one note moustache twirling cartoons. In the last 2 hours there was finally some meaningful interactions between characters, but that's about it.The premise of the world is very flawed, considering how you’re supposed to believe there are these teams full of so many people, but unless it’s mandated by the story, you don’t ever see anyone outside of normal humans and monster enemies. There are supposed to be enemy team members running around at the same time as you trying to complete missions, but you never see them unless you have to talk to them to progress the story. It’s weird and doesn’t make much sense. You also never see any reapers doing their jobs, so the world always feels empty and it feels like the reapers aren’t doing anything and serve no purpose. They say they do, but you almost never see it.And that’s on top of the fact that the existence of the game is stupid to begin with. How it works is stupid. The fact that somehow Reapers, iphones and badges are integrated into it. The more you think about it, the more it falls apart.Some spoilers to drive home what exactly I mean by contrived, contradictory and “then this happens” nature of it.Shiba shouldn’t remember Kubo after Kubo got erased, which also erased everyone’s memory of him. But he somehow does, even though he shouldn’t, which enables the plan. If he didn’t conveniently remember, then it becomes impossible. The girl that talks to him after somehow figured out the existence of angels, despite it being impossible, since there are no angels and the only one that was there was hiding his identity and then got erased. That’s just a few contradictions in the span of 1 minute of dialogue. The entire game is full of them. The whole part of them “coming together, joining forces” is incredibly contrived, because despite the fact that the MC is time travelling, by the time he talks to the characters, they’re somehow ready to listen to his plan, despite being hostile the last time. The biggest example is the Shima guy, who pulled the “I retained part of my consciousness” card. An example of the contrived and “and then this happens” combo. A lot of characters from the previous game show up, but honestly I just couldn’t care less about any of them and the game doesn’t give me a reason to. And there’s absolutely no reason why some of them would’ve picked that exact time to show up, exactly  when their help was needed. Then at the end, the mass murderer Shiba gets treated like a good guy. That’s super weird. In the end, the only bad guy according to the narrative is the ugly old guy. Oh and nobody kills Shiba, the tyrant mass murderer just gets to be in charge forever. So he can keep pulling random people into his death game where he erases people from existence after an unfair game. And there’s no reason to think he won’t try to genocide Shibuya again. It’s so stupid.Then they suddenly pull the BS “composer” card out of nowhere, as though this game didn’t have enough useless nonsense concepts. But thankfully, once again, it just happens to be exact perfect thing to make a thing in the plot happen. Then Shoko becomes human out of nowhere, yaaaay. Makes sense I guess. No it doesn't.It started to really piss me off when all of the side characters, who are powerful reapers and players, would aggressively avoid helping you, despite it meaning they would get murdered. TL;DR: It’s a very style over substance kind of game, but style isn't even good enough to redeem it and the substance isn’t worthwhile at all. I honestly have no idea what this game was going for, what I, or anyone, was supposed to get out of it. It’s badly written nonsense about people in somewhat fashionable clothes.

_childDocuments_.review: As a sequel this game is kinda meh, most of the best parts of the game comes from all the returning characters, the new characters are overall kinda weak. What makes it worse is the, honestly, horrendous localization.Ignoring the minor political differences and stuff, some of the translations vary from making the dialogue cornier to make it "more interesting" for English players to outright questionable. Shoko goes from a pretty decent girl who's a bit sarcastic to a total ♥♥♥♥♥ in the localization. In the original script, where she would just kinda jokingly make fun of you but not be a ♥♥♥♥ about it, she'd instead be a total jerk to the entire crew in EN. Now this wouldn't normally be very egregious.... if by the end she wasn't supposed to love the cast yet hurls really bad and hurtful insults at people she considers irreplaceable friends, and especially to  by the end of the game. It makes the entire situation less believable and makes her far less compelling as a character and only serves to bog down the entire experience as u now sit there and wonder why everyone is so nice to her despite her being an insufferable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to everyone for no real reason.Gameplay is passable, the only major annoying feature is the difficulty. Higher difficulties don't always net you better rewards and each difficulty has its own unique drops. This wouldn't be a huge issue normally but it's a nightmare for completionists as you gotta replay entire days to get, potentially duplicate, pins from the bosses that only appear at the end of the day. It also forces u to juggle difficulty constantly as playing on hard religiously can potentially screw you over by not giving u as much money as it should as some money pins get replaced by material pins which can't be sold.The story is overall just boring as well, most of the cool stuff doesn't happen till the very last week or so and, even worse, there's like no stakes at all until the last week. Since Rindo's entire gimmick is that he can turn back time, there's legitimately no real stakes involved and it honestly causes tons of plotholes, as the game relies on the cast being total idiots with 0 awareness of their current situation to force constant rewind use for the later twist. TL;DR the game is fine, nothing amazing, it's a solid 7.5/10 at best, but as a follow up for TWEWY I'm personally sorely disappointed as this game barely feels the same. Aside from how cool it is to see the TWEWY cast all grown up and carrying over their character development from OG, the new game's cast are sorely lacking overall and pale in comparison to the returning cast. Good game to get on a sale but with how SE rarely has regional pricing it's hard to recommend for those who don't have the money to spend on it.

_childDocuments_.review: The best I can say for this game is, for what it is, it's... Fine.  Is it a completely broken mess?  No.  Is it annoying, frustrating, repetitive, shallow, and badly-written?  Well...  The game is flooded with Wheadon-esque over-writing, back-to-back, overlong, and frustratingly-redundant dialogue sequences that grind the gameplay to a cryogenic halt, and shallow, button-mashy, zero-strategy combat.  The lead characters, Rindo and Fret, are utterly insufferable idiots who spend the first several hours of the game rapping out "I'm so clever" lines back and forth while everything falls apart around them.  I get this idea that they aren't entirely sure there is a ticking clock and their lives are literally on the line, but then why are they taking so easy to fighting giant gorillas and flying jellyfish with magical pins?  It makes zero sense, story wise.  There is a mountain of quality action RPGs out there.  NEO: World Ends with You does nothing particularly well enough to set itself apart, especially for the full $60 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, don't listen to the people who claim the localization was bad - they don't know Japanese social cues that had to be translated for this game. As for the rest of the game, it's fantastic, an amazing sequel to a great action RPG, with a story focused on character growth and learning to step outside your comfort zone.Alright, so let's go into the real review. Already posted much of this on Amazon, so I'll just copy bits from that and hope it fits the character limit.Let's get one thing straight: Neku Sakuraba's story from TWEWY is over. He's taken lessons to heart that he will never forget. But NEO isn't about Neku. Instead, it's about a teen named Rindo Kanade, who lives in a Shibuya that's become much different from the one Neku knew. Miyashita Park's been rebuilt, the most famous ramen shop in Dogenzaka has closed down to be replaced with a curry shop, new clothing brands have sprung up to replace fading fashion trends (including Gatto Nero, created by Shiki Misaki), and the most glaring of all, flip phones have been replaced by smartphones. Rindo Kanade is a young man who is glued to his phone half the time, rarely ever interacting with others. His two best friends are "Swallow," a stranger who Rindo met through Fantasy GO, a Final Fantasy-themed take on Pokemon GO, and Tosai "Fret" Furesawa, his classmate who can make new friends easily but can't stand heavy topics. Rindo and Fret are pulled into the Reaper's Game, which is now a team-based game, after Fret buys a pair of "Reaper Pins" for the two. Before long, they meet the mysterious Sho Minamimoto, a man who doesn't play by the rules but wants to help the two survive in the Reaper's Game, and Nagi Usui, a college student obsessed with a mobile dating sim who judges others based on her observations of them. The whole team has a lot of growth to do, except Minamimoto, who is only there for a short time. Either way, I won't spoil anything else beyond Day 4 in terms of story.The gameplay is an evolution of the original game's. All attacks are represented by pins, each with a specific button, and they're split into six different categories, all using different buttons. When one team member's attack does something specific, a meter appears that begins to decrease. If another attack hits before the meter completely empties, a Beatdrop combo happens, building up your Groove meter, which replaces the Fusion Level mechanic. The last Beatdrop that happened will determine the kind of Mashup Attack you unleash once your Groove is at 100% or higher, and there are many different kinds, one for each pin element. Around the halfway mark of the game, the game begins to feel more about mashing buttons, since Beatdrops seem to happen more often when you do. In battle, you are tasked with taking out Noise, monsters based on tribal tattoo designs. Your team's HP is always full at the start, and it's all added up, though the Noise's HP isn't. You can also take on enemy teams playing the Reapers' Game, all with their own tactics.Random encounters are not a thing in this game. You can only see Noise with your "scan" ability, then fight them by drawing close or using a special magnet ability unlocked later in the game. Noise are represented on the map by skull-like symbols, and absorbing one will send you to battle. However, you don't have to battle right away! While a certain amount of time will pass before you need to battle, you can also absorb more symbols. With each one you absorb, the rate at which enemies will drop pins will be doubled, but you'll need to take on another battle where your HP from the previous one rolls over. As the game progresses, you'll be able to take on up to 20 of these chains, with every "reduction" adding onto the drop rate more and more up to 20x. If you combine that with the fact that you can lower your level at will to get a higher drop rate, you can get a nearly-2000x drop rate!Stats are similar to how they were in the original - leveling up only increases your HP, while eating food increases your other stats, and some characters will get higher stat boosts from certain food. You can only eat a certain amount of food before your characters get full, and you drop the hunger meter back down to 0 by battling. There's also clothes that improve your stats, but the main one that they don't change is "Style" - instead, it unlocks a different ability for each piece of gear if it's high enough.While you can activate abilities by wearing certain clothes, you can also activate abilities by doing side quests. There are four different types of side quests: helping people around the city the way only a Player can, getting Gold Ranks on a Dive mission by erasing sets of special Noise as fast as possible, fighting special Pig Noise, and Scramble Slams. (More on those later.) Helping people will add them to your Social Network, also giving you Friend Points to unlock the ability associated with them. For example, Rindo's Social Network perk displays a health bar above enemies. Gold Rank Dives will earn you six FP apiece, two for each rank. Finally, Pig Noise are special Noise that drop rare pins, and once defeated, won't respawn. However, they have their own gimmicks; some are only vulnerable to one pin affinity, some are in a herd of two different colors that must be changed to all be the same, etc.I haven't even brought up the most obvious part of the World Ends With You series: the aesthetic! The game takes place in a very stylized Shibuya, where certain parts are exaggerated or dialed back to keep it looking fresh and unique. The game is designed to look like an action manga/anime, with a distinctive art style and cel shaded graphical engine. The game's style is directly inspired by the culture from 2019-2021, much like how the original was inspired by the culture in 2008, so a lot of outfits, food, and even slang may feel like a time capsule of 2021 culture when it's revisited in 2030. (Terms like "sus," "cringe," and more are used sparingly, thankfully.) The design is very inspired by manga and graffiti, like an RPG version of Jet Set Radio.The art design paints a punkish look at the most stylish district in Tokyo, and the music complements it perfectly. Takeharu Ishimoto, a composer on games like Kingdom Hearts, Final Fantasy Type-0, Crisis Core Final Fantasy 7, and Dissidia Final Fantasy, returns to provide his amazing musical talent to the game. It's nice to listen to hip-hop, punk rock, general rock, and even screamo as you explore this strange Shibuya and clash with different threats. My personal favorite was Last Call, one of the boss battle themes in the middle third of the game.In the end, I think this is an amazing sequel to a great game. It did a good job of making clear that, while characters from the original are still around and play a significant part in the story, this is Rindo, Fret, and Nagi's story of personal growth and self-discovery. I would be happy to see this game become a franchise, each one focusing on a new Reaper's Game player/group.

_childDocuments_.review: Each character is equipped with a pin. The equipped pin defines the action that the character performs. NEO TWEWY’s combat involves chaining these actions together to create Beatdrop combos, building up the Groove percentage then executing a special attack. Initially, the combat is very basic. Fortunately, it does improve later in the game as the player gains access to more party members, a larger variety of pins and a skill that adds a timing window bonus for executing Beatdrop combos.NEO TWEWY features more than 300 pins. If you’re a completionist, you will need to level up and master all of these pins. The combat system is fun when you’re using a set of pins with good synergy, however much of the game will be spent playing with pins that you’re leveling. Unfortunately, many of these pins do not feel good to use and the combat suffers because of this.The combat system suffers from some contradictory design choices. Many pins can only be acquired through playing on harder difficulty modes. Drop rates can be increased by chaining together Noise (enemies) and delevelling your party. Battles get progressively more difficult later in the chain. Combining harder difficulty modes with a delevelled party and big Noise chains leads to long, frustrating battles.NEO TWEWY is extremely grindy. The game features Dives (time trial Noise battles) and Scramble events (high score Noise battles). While technically possible to complete on initial chapter playthrough, they are extremely difficult and will most likely require the player to replay the entire chapter once they’ve obtained the skills designed to make them easier. A lot of optional and post game content is also gated behind replaying chapters. I did not find the combat enjoyable enough to justify the amount of chapter replaying that’s required.I liked NEO TWEWY’s unique take on gearing, skill and stat progression. The game features a Social Network, completing side quests or frequenting shops expands the Social Network and allows the player to unlock new skills and special items. This really helps build immersion in NEO TWEWY’s world. Stats are permanently increased by eating food at restaurants. Each meal offers various stat boosts, this allows you to build your character stats in very specific ways.While not gameplay related, the soundtrack is absolutely phenomenal.NEO TWEWY’s story takes place over an in-game three week period. The story pacing for the first week and a half is extremely slow. The story doesn’t really start to pick up until midway through the second week. For me personally, this was around 25 hours into the game. I found this part of the game to be a drag and not enjoyable. The story really picks up in the third week and it does get good, however I am not sure if the late story pay-off is worth enduring everything that comes before it.Some design choices really hurt the pacing of the story progression. The main character, Rindo, has a time travel ability. This ability allows the player to replay previous parts of a day to change the outcome to progress. The Scramble events mentioned earlier involve battling huge Noise chains to score as highly as possible. These Scramble days sometimes took me several hours to complete because of this. Both of these design choices, as well as a few other minor things really felt like they were holding up the story.The majority of the story is told through visual novel style talking heads and speech bubbles. This isn’t really an issue but it would have been a much better experience if there was more voice acting and fully animated cutscenes.NEO TWEWY visuals are a high point for the game. It has a unique visual flair. The cell shaded graphics really compliment the art style of the game. The character designs are also very good.At 1440P, some textures, specifically UI textures are noticeably blurry. I do not find this acceptable in a modern game.When combined with NEO TWEWY’s obnoxiously grindy gameplay, the extremely late story pay-off makes NEO TWEWY very difficult to recommend.
