_childDocuments_.review: Realtime exploration + tactical, turn-based combat + RPG elements. On par with Mutant Year Zero.If you were a fan of  you can stop reading here and just buy the game, it's the same developer and the same style; just a new story and a new publisher.---I could almost copy & paste the same review. This is as you might predict a turn based tactical combat system, not terribly different from XCOM and others like it. The main difference with this (and MYZ) is the open roaming (only becoming turn based when combat starts) as you explore and search various zones.It's not fully open world, you just have adventure zones to loot and encounters in those zones to stealth past and/or into and then fight.The story is mostly linear but well presented, and though the replay value for the story may be limited by this there are different difficulty options to challenge yourself with and even two different tactical styles you can pick from (including one that is less random with auto-hits on flanked enemies, it's explained before choosing)Sound design and voice acting are decent with some amusing character designs and a relatively interesting narrative even if it doesn't stray far from some of the standard sci-fi tropes.Day one release and a couple of hours playing, no major glitches or crashes, it's functional out of the box and is compelling enough that I'm entertained and planning to keep playing through to the end.---Bottom line: If you're a fan of turn based tactical games this is a fun little diversion.---

_childDocuments_.review: I've now finished the game so I will state my views on it.The good* The combination of turn-based combat and real time out-of-combat movement together with the ability to set up ambushes gives the game a far more tactical feel in my view than most games of this sort which rely exclusively on turn-based movement. A lot of games feel as though every encounter is the same and all enemies instantly knowing where you are feels a bit silly to me. In this one, you can most of the time decide how to approach every encounter before combat even starts, luring enemies away and picking them off one by one silently or engaging a full squad or outright using stealth to ignore encounters.* The various factions feel like they approach conflict in distinct ways, forcing you to adapt while they still having some consistent core elements within them. The game is also pretty clear about the fact that some factions are harder than others and will remind you of this a few times.* The story itself is decent, but I find it undercut by the voice acting and story inconsistencies.What can be improved* It would be really neat if stores refreshed their consumables and chips. Kind of a bummer that they don't.The bad* The voice acting feels a bit too theatrical for my taste and while the story is mostly good, sometimes the script and story feels kinda off. Like characters having strange reactions, rapidly moving from love to hate to love or having no reactions at all to some pretty significant pieces of information.   * The weapons also feel kinda meh. There's not really any scaling or variety among them. I was hoping for all characters to at least have one silent weapon, but never managed to find that and some weapons I had from the start were still viable at the end.In conclusionI think it's a great tactical game with an overall decent story (although some question marks). That said, if you mostly prefer games such as XCom, I would look at some videos first as it in my opinion plays a lot differently from those kinds of games. Overall, if this doesn't scratch an itch for you, I'd wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first bought my PC a few years ago, maybe more, Mutant Year Zero was coincidentally on the Steam home page. I had no idea what it was, but something about a cartoonish duck, and hog, carrying guns excited me. I purchased it, and had a hell of a time. Eagerly approaching each encounter, looking at it as a puzzle to solve, made up consecutive evenings for many weeks. And the story; I was enthralled. Colour me excited as I found they were releasing a similar game; Miasma Chronicles. Overwhelming anticipation surrounding this game and, now having the chance to play it, I can assure Mutant Year Zero fans that it doesn't disappoint. They cranked it up to 11. It's on steroids. All the metaphors for something being bigger, and better, applies. The graphics are gorgeous, the gameplay exactly what I loved about Mutant Year Zero, and the story is brilliant.Being somewhere around the D.R.C at the moment, I have become acutely aware of how well versed I now am with multiple different Miasma powers, and general abilities, since Level 1. I reflected on the scale of dwellings like the D.R.C., the surrounding environments, and the enemies within. Over the course of my journey with Miasma Chronicles thus far, Elvis and I really have come far.I forsee being left craving DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: To put it simply, this is a game that appears to have been made great on the first draft but had no one to revise or give feedback to iron things out. Technically, I had one graphical glitch and a handful of reaccuring animation issues but other than that no problems. The overall art style is fantastic and the post-apoc setting is nicely realized for the most part (the droids you can find feel like a real missed step for potential worldbuilding).However, so much just feels like it could've been fixed with some extra feedback and revision. The characters are close to being great but there's some real out-of-character moments and contradictory things that take you out of moments that were clearly designed to be impactful. The combat is extremely unfun for the first half of the game and even has some moments at the end that had me rolling my eyes. You can specialize your characters, changing that at any time (huge plus), but half the abilities are lackluster or weak and the other half are play-defining and must-takes (shock glove, tackle, and turret for example).Overall, I can't recommend this but will keep an eye on what the devs make next as there's real potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game to be enjoyable.  I like the characters, the story, and the combat.  The game does have one somewhat glaring problem which I seriously hope they will address.The only way to heal effectively is to use the heal pots, which are prohibitively expensive.  Unless you are playing on the easiest mode, which heals 100% after a combat, you will likely spend the majority of cash you collect on heal pots.  This leaves little cash for anything else, especially in the early going.I play on easy because I found the cost of healing on high difficulties prohibitive.  But that said, at this difficulty level the combat is easy as well.  They need to do one of two things.  Ideally you would be able to set difficulty parameters.  Here you could allow full heal after combat, or, when you return to a city.  At the same time you could have a combat difficulty slider to determine how difficult combat would be.The other option would be to tune the economy so the heal pots are not so dang expensive.  Dev's please address this.  Clearly I am not the only one reporting this issue.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is forgettable, guns are so imbalanced: shotguns are so strong, hit multiple enemies with great crit chance, why the hell should someone use a sniper? Combats are repetitive: try to stealth kill as many enemies as you can (sometimes you can stealth kill them all in 1 encounter), and then engage the rest. Hit rate is stupid. Don't be fooled by the high cover, low cover ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. If you don't get 100% hit rate, you will almost always miss. If you hide behind a low cover, you will almost always be hit. The game compensates this by giving you strong miasma abilities though, so combat is not too difficult.Skill trees are ridiculous because it doesn't affect much how your characters will work. Skill descriptions are poor. There's a passive skill that says reflect 35% of range damage to the attacker, I thought it was meh because my character will need to get hit to benefit from that skill. Only until late game when I level that skill (I have no other skill to put skill points into), I realize it reflects 35% of range damage AND fully neutralize the attack, so my character gets 0 damage while the attacker gets 35% damage reflected back to them. If I had known it was that OP, I would have leveled that in the beginning. Another skill says it allows character A to transfer 60 energy to another character. In my mind "transfer" means character A will lose 60 energy while the other character will gain 60 energy, but no, that skill in game only means the other character will gain 60 energy, character A doesn't lose any energy, only 1 action point! Because of this misunderstanding, again I didn't level that up until very late in the game. I wonder if I misunderstood any other skills as well.The story is so so poor. There are some "plot twists" that you could see from miles away. All characters are annoying to a certain degree, everyone has a secret they withhold until the very end for no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason. The protagonist is a little ♥♥♥♥♥ that shows no character development until the end, where he does the bitchiest of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing, of course, for no reason. The person writing the script for this game should be fired and replaced by chatgpt, it surely can do a better job.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing on Challenging(2nd to hardest difficulty) | Full tacticalNeed some serious balancing.Not a fan of the combat design;* No damage variation, everything is multiples of 10. For both you and enemies. HP upgrades are meaningless until you hit breakpoints.* Consumables are way too important for how much they cost, especially healing nades(medipod). I'm not sure how the post-combat healing works, sometimes my guys will heal to full, sometimes they will be left injured until I finish the quest line(?) idk* Since the game offer stealth approach before engaging the enemy directly, almost every combat encounter designed around that, you 3 vs anywhere between 8-12 enemies(some encounters are forced and the amount of enemies you face will reflect that). It's getting boring after a while.* Enemies that can summon other enemies can do so throughout the entire battle, now they won't summon each and every round, they will however always spawn new ones after you kill the old ones and the worst thing is, the spawns don't die along side the "host". You will need to kill them separately. All in all, if you're into story driven games, play this game on normal difficulty  and enjoy the story. I'm not that kind of a gamer, and this game is not for me.  I will still finish it because of sunken cost, but only once and move on.

_childDocuments_.review: Miasma Chronicles is a Tactical RPG set in a post apocalyptic America. We follow Elvis - a young man looking for his mother, Diggs - his mechanical "brother" and Jade a mysterious one-eyed girl as they try to save their home from the Miasma and the the First Family.Game play is tactical turn-based like most CRPGS. Though tactical mostly in the sense of preparation over combat. It is always best to take out stray enemies with stealth ambushes in order to whittle down the enemy forces before engaging with the rest. I thoroughly enjoyed the combat although there are some enemies near the end that can be a tad bit frustrating. Overall though, it's pretty good.The story is one of the best parts of this game as all off the main cast are compelling in particular, the main character Elvis. He spends a portion of the game looking for his mom and trying to comprehend who he truly is. The darkest hour is amazingly well done though I was hoping that it would drag on a little longer and take more time to resolve. Overall, I really like the story.7.5 out of 10 -  too much Miasma
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game from The Bearded Ladies. If you are coming to this from Mutnat Year Zero there a few differences that might turn you off, but stick with it and I think you'll find that its every bit as enjoyable as MYZ if not more so.If you're unfamiliar if MYZ then you should check that game out as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked 'Mutant Year Zero' you'll probably like this one, too. Made by the same devs the game has many similarities with its predecessor though there are some differences. For instance I prefer the "circle mechanics" of MYZ when eliminating enemies in stealth, but then again the skill deck system of MC is better than the skill tree of MYZ. It makes it easy to redo your skills against different enemies when/if needed. At normal difficulty the game is a pleasure to play and importantly, I faced no bugs at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I only have a few hours in, but this is what I got so far:Pros:- Environment looks great- Combat is fine. There seems to be many options available, though I of course haven't unlocked most of them yet.- The overall background story sounds interesting, or at least anything that is not related to the main character.Cons:- Main characters are very cringeworthy- Controls and menus are very cumbersome and clearly designed for a controller- Difficulty balance is off. I'm playing on the normal difficulty, and it ranges from way too easy (no need to bother with cover) to very difficult (enemy ambush one-shots whole squad on the first turn).- Menus are a bit buggy: Every time I open the menu a random set of "new" indicators are shown.- No way to listen to codex entries on the background. Clicking anything or closing the menu stops the playback. The people on the recordings also speak so slowly that it is faster to just read it instead of listening.I'll wait for some bug fixes and balancing tweaks.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Bugged out during the Arena fight round 4/5, which happens to be, for some godforsaken reason, an area where you can't manual save or EVEN HAVE AUTOSAVES.This is incredibly stupid design. Want to stop player from saving manually? tolerable. but no autosaves for a long sequence of fights that appears to be highly bug prone is utter nonsense.I teleported the greenfingers enemy to be in range of Diggs to try and tackle him for CC. Doing so made Diggs share the same Square as the enemy, and the game froze.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: First impression: Amazing graphics, OK combat, lame writing. "What are those things!?""Frogs!" "No, those are not animals!"Literally, it looks like my 14 year old niece wrote these conversations for her English lesson at school. Also the main dude Elvis sounds like he was smoking pot all day or at least had a minor stroke just a few weeks ago and sounds NOTHING like he actually looks. Casting 1/10. In general the main character is just an uninspiring kid. For me, a 40 year old dude, that is not cool at all.His robot "brother" is overly sassy, sometimes aggressive out of the character (first Mayor scene) with the hints of a black guy stereotypes in his speech.Are those character features contribute to the story somehow or are they just added for the sake of robot being "different"? Now combat: as many of people already said - only 1 "right" path is available, so you will be loading the save game again and again until you find the way. I play on Normal, although the description encouraged to play on this level if I'm new to these tactical games. I'm not new, I'm kinda good at them, but in myas*ma I keep dying all the time.But I ain't gonna lie that when you find the "right" way - the feeling is rewarding.So the first impression would be around 6/10 but I will keep playing and will change the score accordingly.EDIT: OK, weeks passed, but I never wanted to go back to this game. So I guess 5/10 is more accurate.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: It's perfect for the person that loved Mutant Year Zero/Wasteland 3 and wanted more after the game ended. Definitely a better experience on a controller as others have stated. 10 hours in, no bugs/crashes. The story and world have me hooked and always exploring just to see what's next. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game...very atmospheric and beautiful graphical style.  Great follow-up to Mutant: Year Zero.  I enjoyed this game so much that I've already bought  their other game called Corruption 2029 (wish it was on Steam, but it' only on Epic).  Looking forward to their future games as well.  My one requests are:1) Add more silent weapons, or let uses attach silencers2) If player ends an Ambush, don't make the other teammates regroup.  It's annoying when you've placed them far apart strategically, but you they leave their spot if you exit the ambush for any reason which could cause an alert or take more time to reposition them.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly fun even if the writing isn't the greatest. Though there's just one problem i had, i just got a tier 3 sniper stashed behind some enraged enemies. I didn't want to sneak past them so i decided to just fast travel to save myself some time and then my game crashed. I figured i'd take a break cause i had been playing for awhile, but when i came back to continue it crashed again and again and again. My save and the checkpoint before the autosave are both either corrupted or broken. My last save was around 16 hours before where i currently am in game and i'm not doing every side quest and quest again. I tried restarting my pc, game, and validating my game files but no luck. Is the game fun, yes. But i can't leave a good review because this one problem has made it so I can't experience the ending without a major time investment replaying all the content on the hardest difficulty again
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Been holding off writing a review to get some hours in.Beautiful, b. e. a. utiful! The environmental effects and models are gorgeous. Miasma has a deep, terrifyingly plausible history. The main character story is a little reluctant hero campy, and the companion histories are thorough. Combat (playing on level 3 of 4) is challenging, every win feel earned, like, gee golly, you're playing a game set in a hostile wasteland that wants you dead.There have been a few, and I mean a very few, visual glitches. A hat not lined up on a head, clipping in a cut scene, model misplacement.One huge kudos. Huge, HUGE! I bought a fully made game on release date. None of this alpha/ beta/ early access or emergency patch bullshart. Game was released. I paid the money. I'm playing a finished beautiful piece of Artitainment.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game and you should play it BUT:If you haven't played Mutant Year Zero: Road to Eden, you should play Miasma Chronicles first, MYZ second.Those who have played Mutant Year Zero, shouldn't view Miasma Chronicles as an upgrade but a sidegrade.It's best to meet the game on it's own terms, not compare it. And as with every good advice I give others, I won't follow it myself.Pros:The devs did a good job to fill the world with believable combat arenas. You always get a sandbox feeling and it's realy fun.Also the stealth is unique to MYZ and MC, where you thin out the herd before engaging in the real battle.Also I liked most charakters or disliked them for their charakter. Now this is no RPG with choices. Dialogues are linear and have always the same outcome.The graphics and worldbuilding are pretty good. Animations are a bit stiff but it didn't bother me at all.The scaling to lategame is unique: You get skill points and a few max. HP with every levelup. Your skills are often passives or a few dots, but nothing incredibly overpowered, despite a few skills. Damage progression comes purely from equipment, wich works pretty well, because you can't get to op.Now the Problems:This game feels rushed at the end. In one area you get 2 major reveals and 1 major plot point. After that you have the last boss fight. This gets a bit weird because Elvis dislikes what is revealed but still cheers, when the mates he dislikes score a crit. Good sportmanship I guess.It is buggy and I mean it had no "small" bugs for me, but 2 pretty major bugs. Once I lost a weapon after an arena fight. Reloading solved it. The second one was more important. I got XP everytime I entered stealth combat and left it, without any action. If I'd wanted, I could have been max level in act 1 of 3.The Miasma powers are what makes Elvis (the protagonist) stand out among everyone else but most of your powers are pretty underwhelming. Especially considering that it uses a resource that can't be simply regenerated, just with consumables or skipping a turn (if skilled) or with special weapon attachements. But once you got the ressource it's simply the... most underwhelming thing I've ever seen. You can summon stuff, wich is nice, you can do a chain lightning with 20 dmg (your starting weapons do 50 ?). So chain lightning with 20 dmg or just a shotgun doing 60 dmg where you can combine it with a dot. Considering the Miasma is what killed the world and those who could control it fought a war against giant robots, I was disappointed.The cover system is a mess. In all 30+ hours I played the enemy missed twice or thrice. I missed more often with 80+ chances. However, I got reliable crits as long as I got the chance over 50 %. It's a mess. My guess is, that the AI only shoots, when it KNOWS it will hit. So it doesn't if it knows it would miss. However this gave me the impression that I could simply stand out in the open and get shot there instead of being shot while in cover. Cover should have dmg reduction effect as well. This fact made me give everyone a shotgun and just run into the groups of enemies.Lastly you could just watch the trailer for MYZ and MC and compare the fights. Both have the same mechanics but MYZ has dynamically destructable enviroments. I had fights there, where half of the buildings where destroyed. And you don't get to fight a giant robot...To be clear: I am not mixed in my opinion, I definitely recommend it. It just lacks a few things, you get from MYZ, but it is still enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those again... We defenitely need a "meh" button!After having played "Mutant: Year Zero" (the Developer's previous work) i was exited at first.And don't get me wrong, the Gameplay is still what you would expect:A 3D, isometric Strategy-RPG, going turn-based whenever you enetr a fight, but is free-run in exploration.You command a team of 3 characters with one (the main Character: Elvis) permament, plus one Human (also with "Superpowers" like yourself) and one Robot (with no Superpowers).Both of your Teammates are eventually interchangable with another alternative character.I did like the little touch, that you could lure away Enemies from a Group with throwables and then kill them off silently in 1 or two smart turns and then go back to scouting again. But the biggest negative for me - and let me tell You it almost ruined the Game for me - is how absolutely unlikeable every single character is in this Game!Boy... oh boy... not just unlikeable... outright idi*ts! Everything just turns into cringe right from the get go. Neither Elvis, nor Diggs are really people who i want to hang out with. Granted: Diggs is a Robot.. but that's beside the point!They are trying so hard to make Elvis this kind of "edgy", "angsty" teenager and Diggs his lovable but stupid Brute-Friend with a Heart of Gold.... or should i say Motherboard? And don't gat me started about Elvis' supposed "Mother" and all the other wooden Characters.It's not just the voice-acting. The whole thing is just terribly written.This hit me especially hard, because in "Mutant: Year Zero" I really liked the Atmosphere and Story and the Characters came well together. But here... I am sorry. Do Yourself a favour and skip the Cutscenes. this is something I very rarely do but the Story is as predictable as it can get and the Characters are simultaniously too stupid and mr. (or mrs.) obvious.It's really sad thinking that we could have had Mutant: Year One instead...
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: i want the game to do well, i want that out front, the story and mechanics of game play are very nice. i have 11 hours in and the game has crashed 4 times, the audio randomly starts to repeat and some cut scenes are completely whited out then the main story line broke and i can no longer proceed in that save file, i am so disappointed. i was so looking forward to this. I want to leave a positive review but this sort of thing is so frustrating. i get it this is a smaller developer but this is the sort of basic level crap beta testing is for. i did not pay 50 dollars (which used to be a price point reserved for AAA titles) to muck about in an unstable version of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I really came around on this game. I got it because i liked the dev's past work (Mutant year zero..  which was fun.. not amazing, but i had a good time with it.) Miasma Chronicles started pretty weak.. yes pretty looking.. and fun combat - but my god.. not likable people in the game. poorly written.. from the story beats to the every bit of dialog. Why is everyone such a dummy!?!?!?While the story didn't get any better (so lazy and predictable), the people grew on me (a bit) - I did have fun. I can't put my finger on it, but it was better than the sum of it parts and I enjoyed it.Hopefully they hire better writers next game. If you like turn base combat and liked Mutant Year Zero, pick this game up.I didn't have any issues running the game and it played great with a controller. (I played it on my TV.)oh, do save scum the hell out of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical combat is good, with a stealth assassination mechanic is a nice spin on an old formula. While the post-apoc setting is interesting, the story is absolute garbage. Plot line is a fever dream and the characters are cringe worthy. Still a good game, just make liberal use of "Press A to Skip" and save yourself from the cut scenes of chaos
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent tactical game. On the harder side compared to what devs are putting out these days.  Forces you to engage into its systems, even on  standard. Story is fine robot has its funny moments. You start off weak but as you play you start to kick butt. That being said as you are getting stronger you are going to  have  to pick your battles and come back to a few if you are in over your head.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write many reviews, I'm lazy, however, I enjoyed the game so felt it deserved a positive review.I struggle to play games start to finish, although this I was able to keep playing. Some cheese and predictability in the story, but that is a thing in every game.Its not too much Xcom as it has the kill from stealth elements too which I really liked, my only negative regarding this was the lack of variety of silent weapons (two in the whole game!).
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Very original feeling and challenging turn based tactical game. I like the blend between real time exploration and turn based combat. Environments are great (if somewhat monochromatic), NPC companions are interesting and the creature design is creepy. Encounters are tough and you really have to minimize damage because healing only happens when you level up. If you like XCOM or Chaos Gate Demonhunters, you'll like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I've actually liked the game a lot, nice sci-fi plot and settings, nice character progression and nice characters too. I liked the way story is passed through interaction with old world artefacts in a cosy way (you don't have to read long papers and books). Tactical component is kind of limited, cover systems is really not leaving much to the tactics, but battles are still quite entertaining. My only problem with 505 Games is they controls system, why for the love of god you'd do WASD navigation system in turn-based tactical game ?also something for consideration for those who want to buy, I found it's quite expensive since the  game is quite short too. I'd expect 40¬ hours of main story gameplay for these money, but had 27 including ALL side quests. Maybe wait for the discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Mutant Year Zero was a pretty great game. A hidden gem.But Miasma Chronicles is such a big disappointment. Almost as bad as Corruption 2029.Graphics seem a step up, but design is much uglier than Mutant Year Zero and even Corruption 2029.Voice acting is terrible. It's really bad, some of the very worst in any game I played. Writing seems ok, but it's not enjoyable when the voice acting is so painfully bad. Sound is decent, although there is a bug that turns off some sounds during gameplay.Combat is similar to Mutant Year Zero, but somehow, it's less fun. During exploration, movement is clunky  and slow. And the final battle is a broken pile of excrement. The game uses FSR1 and it looks really bad. Since this is an UE4 game, it's best to just use Epic's TAAU.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't get why would they limit Unreal engine to such a console-type controls. Game looks awesome and I guess it is interesting enough to play, but not on PC. Add normal for the genre point and click, zoom in and out, map dragging ability and so on - type controls and I will definitely try it again. So far it's a slap in a face of old school PC gamer. Shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Love the aesthetic and the world building so far however, ran into a broken main quest mission which means I literally can't complete the game until it is fixed (unable to talk to a main NPC following an ambush). Even tried loading an earlier save and re-fighting the two fights prior but still doesn't work. Can't recommend this game until they sort out the bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: The setting of this game is fun. While nothing exactly ground breaking, the world building is done well and the conversations between background NPCs bring life to the world. This is a game where you'll get a nice chuckle reading some of the item descriptions. The writing of the main story could have some improvement, the twists are either overly foreshadowed (leading you to wish you could avoid something in the linear plot that you can see coming) while one in particular seems to come out of no where. But overall is a fun scifi plot. If you're expecting this to be exactly like xcom combat you may be dissapointed. Engaging directly with all the enemies will have you quickly overwhelmed and draining resources. If you engage with the game's ambush mechanic though it adds a great puzzle element to the usual formula. Sneaking around the map picking off isolated enemies is a nice little challenge to make the main fight of each level more manageable. The game is a decent length, you can likely complete all side quests and the main story in 15 to 20 hours depending how much you run around in circles. I think this is a pretty good length as this is around the time the combat starts to become repetitive and luckily the game ends before it actually gets boring. Overally I'd be excited to see a sequel to this exploring the rest of the setting, though hopefully with a few interesting tweaks to the combat and a bit tightened up writing.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: After nearly 12 hours, game breaking bug. I really liked this game, until I got to the mission "The Other Side". Now, the game is not telling me where to go, I watched a walkthrough and went where they went and I'm not given the option to "investigate" so the place I'm supposed to go after that isn't open. Which means I can't progress. Extremely disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Game has a great environment with a rushed story-line. The intro left me underwhelmed with the dialogue and motivation of the characters. Most of the immersion faded out after a couple missions but the combat system and level design was enjoyable. They give the player a lot of versatile options for attacking and defending zones. UI was easy to navigate and switch between 'heroes'. Overall I'd give the game a 2/5 or 3/10. It just doesn't have the quality to be worth the price. I HIGHLY recommend trying other TBTs like: Mutant Year Zero, Gears Tactics, Wasteland, Darkest dungeon, Nowhere prophet. I've put multiple hours into all 5 and will vouch for each ones replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Throwing in my hat to the lack of tactics and difficult imbalances.  The devs have stated they are going to patch addressing these concerns.Playing on the 2nd hardest difficult the only thing I can purchase is medipods because every shot enemies hit on me requires healing.  Exploration only fuels my need for healing as loot is sparse.  No healing outside of combat whatsoever even on normal.  Even XCOM 2 didn't dare do this.  XCOM 2 balanced around enemies being overpowered but players being able to out think them.Miasma balances by assuming you kill half the enemies in stealth before engaging.  Tactics take a back seat to resource acquisition.  You can only kill a few enemies in stealth because enemies have too much health requires two shots and you only acquire one silent weapon 4 hours in.The game also is throwing a lot of sidequests I'm not the right level for so I cannot even attempt them.  Even killing every enemy I could in stealth I was forced to leave the map and come back later when able to take on the enemies.Let me be clear.  No amount of tactics would allow me to win the fight after I exhausted every tactical stealth kill the game afforded me.  I needed to level up before progressing these quests.  I question a game about tactics where level ups outweigh tactics.I've beaten XCOM handily with one death on Commander (the second hardest difficulty).  Every other fight in this game somebody dies.  There's too few resources to properly recover let alone actually build my characters.  The skill tree is also weird.  Early on I got my robot companion the ability to act as cover for the other party members.  However, he doesn't have any armor or any different in health compared to other party members.  I have to wait for multiple levels to be able to even give him some armor so he can actually serve his purpose as a wall.XCOM 2 mechs have a similar functionality except they start with an absurd amount of health and armor to allow this usage.Why offer me tools I cannot possibly use?TL;DR  The game isn't actually hard it's just overtuned.  Difficulty is only a matter of resource spending rather than bette tactics.  I cannot use tactics I cannot afford.  Hopefully the patch fixes this.

The story was very enjoyable and the characters are easy to fall in love with. Hoping they come out with a 2nd game to follow up on the story line ending or release some DLC's. _childDocuments_.review: This game was a delightful little game for me, YMMV of course, but, if you liked Mutant Year Zero : Road to Eden, it's a fair bet that you'll enjoy this.It was very accessible as far as getting into it, and, there's no grinding, no random battles, and enemies don't respawn. Somewhat linear but, in this case, that helps the story maintain it's impact.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of Mutant Year Zero: Road to Eden. I've been waiting for this game since the announcement. I bought it on the first day of release. The world is beautiful, the plot is exciting. But I'm angry.Tactical RPGs are not such a difficult thing to develop in order to make so many mistakes. Pachfinding was the weak side of Mutants, but then everything went to another level. My character fell through the floor during the fight and could not move and shoot the next moves. Another time, the character began to run around and fall behind the map just while moving. At the same time, it became impossible to select him, and the menu stopped working. Then, loading save after the fight with the "ents" in the mine, I could not move to a new location, so I will have to go through the fight again. Erratum in the description of the healing core: It says heals 50 extra points, but in fact 30.The game also has illogical things borrowed from the JRPG. During combat, you can steal "plastic" (game currency) from enemies using a special skill, but if you just kill an enemy it will not be in the loot. You can summon a healer, and then it will be a good idea to leave one weak enemy alive while healer healing everyone, because you can't do that outside the battle. Same thing with restoring energy (mana) by skiping turns in battle, "one weak enemy".And this is a game that has a "hardcore mode". Are you kidding me? I would recommend waiting until they fix the bugs and buy the game later, at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I have now completed all three games of this developer nearly back to back. I would say for the weapon variety for end game, Mutant Chronicles felt better however you can easily see the improvement in all other fields in this game. Although the end of  story feels very rushed, world building and characters remain interesting throughout the game. I would say this is a must play for any tactics fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: The base game is a fun tactical game. The stealth/ambushing mechanic really does make it feel unique, letting you choose your approach to most combats.It might not reach too far beyond that initial impression but I appreciate the free respeccing to mix things up if you want. Being able to kick up the difficulty midway through the game was also a great option.There are a decent number of bugs but they didn't get in the way for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Miasma Chronicles is a work of art. The visuals, the sounds, the music, the universe are breathtaking.Many times I just walked up to a ledge just to admire the scenery. It makes you feel small with impossible odds of survival, yet always pushing through.The story is alright, very contemporary.The plot twists are not great: you see one with a certain character coming a mile away, the other one is just disappointing.The cons:- Combat is repetitive with few valid options on higher difficulties.- Most guns you find are useless, and it feels like you only ever upgrade once near the end.- Controls and UX suffer from several small design flaws that pile up. In UI web design, you learn that people spend most of their time on other websites, so you need to respect some basic principles. It feels the same in a game set in an established genre: players spend most of their time playing different games.So playing a tactical shooter with reloads, you expect R to reload your gun, Tab to switch between different targets, right click to move, etc. This leads to reloading a save for dumb UI manipulation mistakes.- No replayability. When you've completed it once, there is no incentive to go back. It is all linear and you get the extra companions so late.Overall the creative minds behind this game did a fantastic job,Miasma Chronicles came close to greatness, and is a beautiful experience with great value for money.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique game. I usually find dialogues in video games boring and I can't stand them, but this game got me engaged and made me want to listen to how the characters describe their world, interactions, and their dialogues fit their personality pretty well. The combat difficulty might not be for everyone since it requires you to spend a lot of time to plan carefully before engaging, but I do enjoy games that are very harsh and punishing. Exploration in this game feels fun and the world is beautifully crafted, it got me engaged the whole game. There are a few bugs here and there, but nothing game breaking. 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: We're going to start off with the things I like about this game and then go into the things that made me want to rip my hair out but beware of spoilers later on. Side note, I have finished the game.Things I like:- Environments and overall world-building I think were done very well here, the areas with settlements actually feel lived in unlike other games of similar premise and they do feel very unique to one another. The areas you find yourself in can vary significantly even in the same region which is always a plus, little to no copy/paste environments from what I played.- Diggs is hands-down the best character in the game. His combat banter is done very well and his dialogue during cutscenes and world exploration is legitimately funny. - Sound design is awesome, from the ambient sound of the miasma to the music when you're in combat they did a very good job here.- The silent kill system is a nice addition and really allows you to avoid some fights entirely if you play them right. This makes Jade indispensable as a party member, in my opinion.Things I don't like:- You will receive a lot of weapons that are absolutely indistinguishable from each other. Under normal circumstances this wouldn't be an issue as you can take that back to a trader, sell it, and get a better one. The issue with that line of thinking is that those vendors have the exact same weapons you are carrying around. Why? - The game is not optimized for keyboard and mouse. I have no doubt this will be fixed in the future but this lack of optimization leads to some very frustrating encounters.- This combat system is supremely frustrating. For starters there appeared to be little to no reason to put my party members in cover as the AI will have no issue hitting them and it does nothing to mitigate damage. I played through on basic tactical which admittedly directly lead to some of my frustrations. That being said I can count on two hands in this entire game the AI missed a shot on one of my party members, and most times they hit you from positions of cover that are impossible for your party members to hit as the percentage is too low. If I play through again on full tactical though I will update. - Bha Mahdi is the Nazeem of this game and everything she says is equivalent to the cloud district line.SPOILERS AHEAD:This story makes no sense. So the beginning of the game is you trying to break though the miasma wall to find your mom. Solid motivation in and of itself but the reason you want to find her is so she can tell you who you are and who you need to become which is not so solid but I was willing to put this aside cause there's frogs' need killin. You save the town of Sedentary twice; once from frogs, once from miasma. This also makes sense as its the town you were raised in and so its home. And the townsfolk thank you by electing you Mayor... as a teenager. What the ♥♥♥♥. Even better is for your first act as mayor you leave the town to fend for itself while you go find your mom... again what the ♥♥♥♥. Through the miasma wall to meet mom and turns out she's not your mom... what the actual ♥♥♥♥ is this. Turns out your the reincarnated all-powerful founder of her religion and you need to stop whatever is making the miasma mad. Now you might be thinking its to save Sedentary but the town is never mentioned again until the end game. Now I could go on but suffice it to say that the storyline in this game makes absolutely no sense, with characters doing things for seemingly no purpose whatsoever.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, with excellent graphics, sound and lore.  Xcom like game.Tips for Getting Started:                                                                         Combat And Skills- The combat in Miasma Chronicles is turn-based, and understanding the mechanics is key to winning battles. One critical mechanic is the rage system, where you gain rage for every kill. Once your rage bar is filled, your next attack is a guaranteed critical hit, granting you an additional action if you kill an enemy with it.- During combat, movement is key. Reposition often and try to set up crossfires with your team. Overwatch is an extremely powerful skill for this purpose, allowing you to set up traps for moving enemies. The sprint and shoot skill is also beneficial for maneuverability.- Your first magic-like abilities are miasma powers. These are powerful abilities that can be modified with red and blue slots at the skill icon. The red slots add damage effects but increase the kilowatt costs, while the blue slots reduce the costs. Remember, cooldown times for skills are long and even carry over between battles, so it’s crucial to use each skill judiciously.                                                                  Stealth And Ambush Mechanics- The stealth mechanic in Miasma Chronicles allows you to thin out enemy squads before you engage in open combat. A character like Jade can sneak around and snipe unaware targets, breaking up enemy formations and making combat engagements significantly easier.- It’s important to scout your surroundings, take out as many targets as you can in stealth, and bring your team into a good position before initiating open combat. Glass bottles can distract enemies, offering you the opportunity to separate and eliminate them individually.                                                                     Manage Your Resources Wisely- Resources are scarce in Miasma Chronicles, so manage them wisely. Grenades, health packs, and alternate weapons are all quite expensive. Always ensure that you have enough health packs on hand. Consider using your resources to buy these items if you’re running low. - Also, save up for the ultimate weapon, EDZ-COL: ASSAULT, offered by the NPC Pontius Pychart in Club 14 for 7000 Plastic. This powerful weapon can be a game-changer, so it’s worth saving up your resources to buy it.                                                                   Locked Doors And Keypad Clues- You’ll encounter doors locked by a keypad with clues given in text locks close to the locations. For example, the old keypad next to the new one might have blinking hashtag symbols which indicate how often they blink – a hint towards the code. In other instances, you might find codes marked on walls close to the cage.                                                                      Miscellaneous Tips And Tricks- Explore every corner of the map to find in-game currency, plastic, and occasionally, consumables. Try not to spend your money on guns early on as you’ll find better ones as you progress. Instead, consider purchasing weapon attachments like the energy gain mod, which gives you 5 kilowatts per hit.- As you progress through the main story, two shops will be unlocked in your starting settlement.- In Miasma Chronicles, there can be potentially awkward racial dynamics to navigate, particularly in the first act. As your main characters, Elvis and Jade, try to assist a predominantly black community, they may end up being seen as ‘white saviours’ who are needed to solve all problems. Keep this in mind when interacting with NPCs and try to ensure that interactions are mutually beneficial and respectful.- Exploration isn’t limited to what’s immediately visible. For example, you can climb vines to access rooftops when ladders aren’t available. This could lead to strategic vantage points or hidden loot, so always be on the lookout for these vines.- In terms of skills, don’t worry if you haven’t decided what skills to put your points into. The game allows for free refunds on skill points, so feel free to experiment until you find your perfect setup. You’ll also find side quests along the way, but they are often higher level. It’s recommended to focus on the main story early on until you complete the Data Drive retrieval mission.- Save Frequently And Reload When NecessaryEnjoy this good Tactical RPGCheers

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I can recommend this game. There last patch was over six months ago. They updated this game for a month and then ditched it. There are a lot of weird design decisions that I mention that should have been patched. Mutant Year Zero seems to be the better game and so I hope to pick that up soon.*Mild World Building Spoilers*The premise and setting are really good. It's a post-post apocalypse setting(?).The world starts to succumb to climate change and is saved by this one mega-corp. Edezen goes on to basically run the US, Canada, and some of South America. They use the "Miasma", or the precursor to it, to eat plastic and save the world basically. Miasma turns evil and becomes the catalyst for the current apocalypse. Some OK humor for the setting. A penis joke here, a Homer Simpson joke there. The usual post-apocalypse, "they worshiped something called the Inter-Net" type of humor. I chuckled at some stuff.Some of the characters I enjoyed. Elvis is the main character and he slowly starts to unravel the plot and how he fits into the world. The "twist" at the end of the game is out of left field. Diggs is my favorite out of the cast. Diggs stays pretty consistent in tone and character progression.Elvis and Diggs relationship develops steadily.Jade kind of throws a wrench in that as she is the typical badass who doesn't care about anything. She barely opens up throughout the game and then in the final bit of the game, gets all chummy with Elvis and calls him her brother. ABSOLUTELY not earned whatsoever.Bha is only OK. She is kind of one note throughout the story. She has one goal and does everything to reach that goal. Aside from a couple lines of dialogue at the end of the game, she never really questions what she did to Elvis.Mason is pretty much a non-factor in terms of character. To say anything about him would be spoilers and so I dislike him. None of the other characters in the game really matter. The final boss is limp ♥♥♥♥ in terms of impact to the story aside from a mention in the early game, some cutscenes after chapter completions and end game. Gameplay was only alright.I like XCOM-likes. I really liked the hub area gameplay in this. I would love to see an XCOM game use this in a kind of offshoot with rebels during and before XCOM 2.The puzzles were mostly easy, but I liked that as the combat was more what I was wanting to play. There is some jank during gameplay. The stealth system is weird. Only your currently selected party member can be detected so if you have the group following behind you they can never be detected as long as you don't switch to them. Completing an ambush puts everyone back in the standing position and I have accidentally swapped over to another character and been spotted. Very frustrating. Also only two stealth weapons. A lot of oddities during gameplay that I feel should have been found by QA and ironed out before release and especially after launch. I played the difficulty that reloaded your weapons and refreshed your cooldowns after every encounter. Playing the harder difficulties which don't do that seems like it would involve a lot of skipping turns so you can reload and wait out your cooldowns. The upgraded versions of consumables that can heal or regenerate watts on multiple party members can only do so in combat. You can't heal or regen for everyone in the backpack. Weird design decision.You can reset your skills at any time, but don't get enough skill points to max out every tree. This just felt tedious. It felt like I had to micromanage my companions before every encounter. Really throws you out of the immersion having to menu constantly.There's more I disliked but I just finished my campaign and am tired of this game. I don't really recommend it, especially because they only gave it one month of updates before ditching it. Some good ideas that I hope other games take away, but all-in-all an AVOID.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game.  I've played others like it, but this game has frustrated enough to quit playing, which is a rarity.  The main issues I have with it are the difficulty and the economy.   Having my 3-person party ambushed close-in by 20 foes is ridiculous, not to mention that some of those enemies can summon more, 2 at a time.   Even in normal conflicts, the enemy seems function at a higher level than my party members.  Some can move, shoot, and move again.  They hit way more often than my party, given the same apparent hit chance.  I believe some of this imbalance could be mitigated by using more consumables like grenades and upgrading weapons, but my party spends all their credits on ridiculously priced med packs.Stealth/sniping attrition is supposed to be the only way to success in this game.  Maybe I'm not seeing the best approach to attacking a group, but I think I'm an okay player with experience in other games in the genre.  I hope the developers see this and similar reviews and release game-play improvements soon.

_childDocuments_.review: i dont regularly write reviews for games but i had such a fun time with this one that I felt compelled to let others know how much fun it was. the good: combat, world, graphics and overarching story felt satisfying until the very end. the world is just gorgeous. it's worth buying and playing just to enjoy walking through the desolate world and experiencing a fully realized post apocalyptic Kentucky. the combat felt satisfying and was definitely challenging (i played on "extreme difficulty, which is the hardest without doing ironman). this isnt a pure xcom style game, so be aware that the combat loop largely revolves around stealthing around and taking out as many enemies as possible BEFORE the actual combat starts. if you ignore the ambush mechanics the combat is EXTREMELY challenging, but not impossible. i found it to be largely pretty easy IF you regularly visit the store and stock up on items like acid grenades and medipods. regular use of backpack items are an absolute must. the bad: the dialogue and difficulty. the dialogue oftentimes feels like it had entire sections cut, which is par for the course on budget titles such as this. i didnt interfere with the overall narrative, however, and was largely (for me at least) forgiveable. just be aware youre not going to get Shakespeare here. the difficulty curve is all over the place, and many people have wrongly said that it's a puzzle game where there's only one right answer. the game is hard, so if youre not a gamer who's very familiar with xcom mechanics you likely want to play on an easier difficulty. that said, im a 33 year old game who's played xcom games for a decade, so i found the hardest difficulties to be challenging but not impossible. i played on extreme and lost around 5 fights total before the end of the game which was about ~10% of my fights i had to restart and try something different. if youre struggling, use ur backpack items and spend all your plastic on consumables to be used in combat. the game is near impossible if you dont utilize your grenades and medipods.in summary, i do recommend this game, even at full price. it's a budget title and shows it sometimes but it's well worth the $30 to play through even once. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid  game overall. Took about 18 hours to complete. Pros: Graphics, Environment and art design, Combat, Story, DIGGS and the voice actor.Cons: the cover system is a lie. the percentages are not even close to being what they say so be prepared for full cover or none. Limited weapon customization (They could have added a third weapon mod option for plentiful combinations). Very limited skill trees for development (some skills felt really pointless but you need to take them to get the more useful ones). Mason and Bha Mahdi (characters). _childDocuments_.review: This game is very two-faced for me. The characters start out as charming, but throughout the game remain the flat and superficial archetypes they are. The setting has an intriguing and a mysterious start, with plenty of environmental story telling and bits of lore to put together. Then the second half everything gets over-explained with no character development and very obvious plot developments. The story comes across as very formulaic and generic. I don’t mind the linear story, but I do mind the poor writing. The graphics have a unique and gorgeous touch to them, animations look solid. The sound design is juicy and nice. But the dialogues are filled with sloppy design and forced exposition… very immersion breaking to me. At some point the one-liners started annoying me: all potential danger was "Disneyfied" and "Marvelised". The combat starts out amazing with a cool stealth mechanic and challenging tactical decision making. It was challenging for about 10 hours, the enemies felt threatening and overwhelming. But then halfway, resources become abundant and I could just waltz through hordes of enemies, without careful positioning. To some the power fantasy might work, but for me it takes away any wanted tension.The cool turn-based combat is just enough to save this game from a negative review. The predictable story, poor scaling into late game and cringy one-liners let me quit and not complete the game (which is rare for me). But I can see this will entertain others.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is a good game, but it has flaws and does not hold your hand. If you like serious TBS/T games, then you will probably appreciate this game. It is hard. You have to really strategize each encounter and snipe as many baddies before an encounter as you can, or you will be doing a lot of battles over and over again. Compounding this is the fact that there is not tutorial or mini map to guide you along the way. It's trial and error, baby.  You also better be ready to scavenge because you won't be able to upgrade your weapons or buy medipods for low health during battle if you don't. All that said, the graphics are good, the story is interesting, and the gameplay is satisfying. However, it is buggy. It crashed on my Steam Deck about every hour, and I would have to reboot it. It probably works better on a gaming computer, but it's unstable on the Steam Deck. Also, the comments about cover during combat being broken in favor of AI are true. If you have to choose between a good shot or good cover, choose the good shot with no cover, and you will find out that this helps you win battles more often.

_childDocuments_.review: I should make it clear that I absolutely adored Mutant Year Zero. I also hate the RNG of XCOM games. This game scratches that tactics itch, without dice roll difficulty.Very by the numbers plot, and serviceable characters (although the kill/crit dialogue could go).Game is hybrid stealth/tactics, which if you want pure XCOM style combat I'd give this a miss.I enjoy being able to spend some time a garrett in the shadows, picking off patrolling guards until I can sweep the map. Because of this the game is very balanced (or even a tad easy), and will enable you to clear out zones while under levelled and ill-equipped, provided you use the game mechanics. This also balances some of the more frustrating RNG elements of XCOM style games I don't particularly enjoy.My only complaint is that the optimisation is a tad questionable. Some areas chug out of nowhere and for no reason (but it wasn't enough for me to get annoyed).To the developers, I hope you continue making these sorts of games, and telling your stories (selfishly because they're fun).

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fine TRPG with great visuals, good writing, various side missions, and some stealth elements, but don't come expecting too much: after all it's a AA game with its share of issues.First of all, it's main difference from other XCOM clones is an option to lure away and stealthily kill enemies one by one (by throwing bottles or activating speakers). However, the game has only two silenced weapons and only a couple abilities that can be used without alerting all the enemies. Thus, these stealth eliminations quickly become too repetitive.Secondly, while the game has a selection of several weapon types (assault rifles, sniper rifles, shotguns and bouncing disk weapons), the main difference is not even damage, but attack distance. There are assault rifles and even shotguns with bigger range than some sniper rifles! And since SRs only have one bullet in a magazine (ARs have 3-4), they are mosltly useless.Then, aside from the main difficulty, the game offers a tactical mode. Essentially, with this mode enabled you are not guaranteed to hit the enemy even if he's standing in plain sight, and chance to hit also depends on the weapon type you are using (SR have higher chance at big range, AR at close range, and shotguns at medium range - yes, at the same range as AR shotgun is more likely to hit the target).But that's fine, XCOM fans will understand missing with 99% chance to hit. The real issue is that in this mode covers seems to benefit only enemies, but not your teammates. I went through the whole game, and regardless of the covers I used (low or full), enemies pretty much always hit my characters even from a huge distance. So, basically, instead of hiding behind covers, this forces you to be aggressive and control or quickly kill enemies instead. Not sure if this is intented or a bug, but this makes the game significantly different from other XCOM clones, and not always in a good way.And, of course, there are tons of bugs, and some of them may make you lose the game (for instance, while using a specific ability, one of your characters may run across the map and aggro more enemies than expected), so I would not recommend playing on the Alpha Editor (Ironman) difficulty. And given the length and amount of content, I would also wait for a sale: the base price seems way too expensive for what the game offers. Still, it's a good TRPG, and if you like the genre and the visuals, you should grab it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: The Bad:The story is so far rife with cliches. The main protagonist is just some painfully generic dude named Elvis a team of middle-aged dudes from some gated community would come up with. Diggs, your one vaguely ethnic friend is your robot brother with a caricatured kinda weirdly racist voice. It's like they told him to sound as "urban" as possible while cracking jokes that don't land. I struggle to imagine listening to that and the dull protagonist for thirty hours. Him and Jade feel pulled from some pale YA novel. Characters needlessly exposit things to each other that they'd already know to the point they feel like empty vessels to inform the player as opposed to actual people. Diggs fall into the writing trope of informing the audience that Elvis is his little brother by constantly calling him "little brother". Nobody talks like that outside of bad scripts. Finding your mom isn't a compelling enough plot device to pull forward & Elvis' tired saviour role isn't either, so you'll likely just be playing to see how powerful you can get.The fact cooldowns don't reset after each fight is an odd choice. It isn't enjoyable, but perhaps it's simply a skill issue on my part which finds it a nuisance. Locking me out of doing the better moves arbitrarily like this doesn't seem conducive to having a good time though.The Good: -It's a nice looking game, albeit potentially unoptimized as I hit only 60-70 frames on ultra on a relatively powerful gpu.-The ability to pick certain enemies off lends itself to rewarding tactical approaches. I can see how this can become tedious later.-The systems are simple enough yet give room for experimenting.Was playing on iron man & had a unit hidden. Switched back to have it stuck outside of cover and triggered combat leading to my death. Not sure after that if a replay is worth it. You might have an entirely different experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- fun tactical gameplay with lots of skills, weapons and mods (respec is also free, fun to try out different builds)- challenging but rewarding- many different unique maps- good variety of enemies- nice looking environments and character models- fully voiced- some cutscences for the story- kinda unique story for this genreMeh- music not very memorable- main character's voice acting could be better- while game runs well on my PC, the gpu usage is very high even in non-demanding environment (increased room temperature in summer, not great)Cons- some minor annoyances, such as audio codex entry not playing automatically when picked up- sprinting speed is a bit too slow for me- map is sometimes unclearThis is a game with a slow start.In the first 2 to 8 hours (depends on difficulty, skill and experience) you will have a difficult time - enemies hit hard, healing meds are hard to come by, you don't have a lot of tools yet and you do not have a lot of skills yet. However as you progress there are a lot more things and resources at your disposal and combat will feel easier and much varied.It takes time to learn the combat and stealth mechanics if you are new to this type of game. When outside combat, you move in real time to explore and scout ahead. You have the ability to ambush enemies, and silently take them down if you have the appropriate weapon and damage. You can think the herd this way and make the subsequent fight easier when you go loud. The catch is many enemies are in each other's line of sight, so you will need wait for the chance when they are not looking, or distract them with some in game mechanics. Contrary to what some claimed here, stealth is not a must; with careful planning, the degree of freedom in combats is actually very high.One more point - while it has xcom like cover-based tactical combat system its quite different due to different skills and tools. The enemy's AI are quite aggressive too. You cannot play this game like xcom and go gun blazing.

_childDocuments_.review: A new game from the developers who made Mutant Year Zero, which has a few improvements to the combat. The game is heavily based around sneaking and eliminating enemies silently to thin down the actual fight. Sometimes you are even capable of clearing a map without the enemy reacting, if you plan it well. For some reason that feels rewarding, although "guns blazing" has quite a bit of impact upon it, yet more dangerous.The story makes an interesting perspective upon the climate with a solution made that goes wrong. Your little pack of characters traverse the world in order to fight back the Miasma, but also those who seek to control it for the worse.Despite the world is torn from Miasma, then it's made with good detail. The town of Sedentary seems lively with chatter in all corners. The Miasma itself is "alive" with a weird twisting and swirling presence in all the zones you explore.One small downside to the game is the use of cover. This may only be present in Light Tactical Mode, but it's weird when you have a "Full Cover" on a character resulting in a 20% chance of being hit and surprisingly that seems to happen rather often when enemies shoot at you. It could be different in Full Tactical Mode, but due to this it's definitely best to exploit as much as possible by eliminating enemies silently, or use skills to control a fight to avoid taking damage.Overall a fun and engaging game and I look forward to any possible sequel, if it happens.

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best games in the genre, although t-rpg might not be the right tag. The Bearded Ladies pretty much copies their core gameplay loop into every original IP they create; if you are not familiar with their design: yes, it's kinda always a t-rpg, but with a more restrictive general design. encounters are more or less not centered around combat and in-combat choices, but preperation (aka snipe/silent kill enemies during real-time-stealth segments) and a more puzzle like approach. but i feel like this time around, unless you play on the hardest difficulty, it's gotten slightly "better". i mean gun-blazing, e.g. strict combat focus will still drain your very limited ressources like there's no tomorrow, but the heavily expanded character-progression and customization optiones (equip sci-fi-magic, with it's very own gem-system, level up and spend skill points, equip different gear with weapons beeing modable and equip "power cores" similiar to passive perks) you get away with mistakes a lot more than you did in their other games. there's also a lot more choice and options when it comes to actual combat: the miasma powers where a great choice, both narrative and gameplay-wise; you get a notable pool of sci-fi-magic, which greatly expands combat options.audio-visualy this game is a master piece. the screenshots barely do the game justice and it stands proud next to CP2077 and the Ascent. everytime i boot the game up and pass an area i've already seen dozens of times i discover new tiny details everywhere. it's not just that the world-building and enviromental story telling are great: it's the whole picture. colors, design, lighting, fog, SfX and the fantastic OST make this definitly feel more AAA than many "real" high budget AAA games. and let's not forget the great general sound design. beeing it the combat effects or athmospheric backround audio the sound-design is quite impressive. the VO in general is also very high standart...i mean on a personal level you might "love" every actor, but objectivly the VO is very competent.the studio always had a hand for creating very deep, rich and compelling worlds, with this itteration probably beeing their best depiction of an original new IP. you get some western/Borderlands bits, some Fallout, some Cyberpunk, some The Surge (nanotech galore) and even some fantasy pieces. the fact that they managed to include the line "dream about electric sheep" without it feeling fan-servicy or tagged on says it all. narrative, world design, gameplay and even the U.I. just show how much experience they got and i cannot imagine how much blood, sweat'n tears went into this project.however there are issues. first: there's bugs'n glitches abound (this long after release...). from your companions getting stuck in the enviroment during exploration to weird behavior when starting/closing ambushes (as you would when you try different position to start an engagement), to companions not sticking to your imputs (like staying seperated or crouched, problems here again are often related to the ambush behavior). i also encountered very rare UE4 crashes, mostly in specific quest moments (side-quest mostly)second: as much as i commend how competant they got their core gameplay-formula down...it's an aquired taste. yes, pro-gamers might love the puzzle approach to combat, but for "normal" gamers this just turns the game into feeling very on rails and unresponsive. Stellar Tactics would be my example on how to do it better: you got the choice to grind and get stronger to make encounters way, way easier or you don't do that and instead plan every singel move for days and enjoy a more challenging gameplay...it's the players choice, which is how rpgs did it back in the day, and imho a way better approach. i get that the studio wants to implement the silent-kill/snipe, etc. mechanics in their titels, and i get that you need more challenging encounters, to make this even a viable gameplay aspect: but this can become quite repetative aswell.the option to "outgrind"- or overpower content could make this aspect more feasable for the masses. again: i think rpgs/t-rpgs before all this auto-scaling and "every game has to be basicaly rogue-light when it comes to difficulty" just did it better...it was your choice. that said Miasma is definitly the most approachable The Bearded Ladies games, the start might still be somewhat challenging, but come midgame you can get away with a lot, even on harder difficulties. as a whole package Miasma is fantastic game, definitly one of those games i won't forget. it's fun tactical combat, mixed with a lot to tinker around with (gear, skills, magic) set in an interesting, well designed, world and filled with characters and a narrative that might not surprise you, but both the narrative and the party will grow on you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my second attempt at writing a review of this game and while I still do not recommend it, I thought it was important to acknowledge that my dissatisfaction with the game was more due to personal bias and experience.This game was hyped as a "XCOM"-like game.  And while that may be true in the loosest possible comparison as it does have turn-based combat, that actual hype is what causes the largest amount of frustration.By that, I mean that XCOM has always been about combat.  You develop your team, increase their abilities and improve their weapons and skills.  All of this is in order to be better at your primary function of killing the enemies faster and more efficiently.But that is not what Miasma Chronicles is all about.  And that focus on combat will cause a ton of frustration and unnecessary stress until you step back and realize that this game is more about puzzle-solving than any kind of tactical expertise.Let me give you an example.  Early on, you pick up Jade, a sniper/assassin type whose primary weapon is a silenced rifle that does 70 points of damage and that can be increased to 80 with a weapon mod.  This is fantastic because many of the "cannon-fodder" mobs have 70 or less health and they can be killed with one shot.  And that's where the deviation from tactical combat and puzzle solving comes in.  Instead of setting up kill zones, you have Jade sneaking around the entire map, picking off isolated low-health mobs until the only ones left are those who have more than 80 hit points and then you simply use multiple attacks on each mob to burn them down.  When you get a second silenced weapon you tag-team the mobs that you can't one-shot.  Puzzle solving, not tactics.Once you understand that basic principle, you can more or less waltz through the various scenarios and side quests, swapping out your companions as necessary depending on the type of enemies expected.  Thanks to a couple of people who responded on the discussion page and explained the non-combat emphasis, I was able to go from level 6 to level 18 without any further mishaps or stress.  This game is not really my cup-of-tea, but I can see where people who enjoy a more puzzle-solving type game would find it entertaining.  Still not worth $50 and still not recommended for more tactic's oriented people.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing this game, I am certain that I cannot recommend it.  The gameplay is extremely difficult and I wouldn't consider it remotely fun on any difficulty other than the easiest.  The tactics are thoroughly broken as the hit calculations for your team and the enemies don't match, nor do they match the values presented in gameplay.  On the light tactics mode, partial cover should cause you and your enemies to have a 50% chance to hit, but in practice you have about a 10% chance and your enemies have a 90% chance to hit.  Critical hit chances are equally ridiculous.  On full tactics, the hit chance drops further to the point where you almost can't hit anything unless you are flanking them on an adjacent square with a shotgun.  At higher difficulties, your squad doesn't heal (as much or at all) between battles, and the enemies have more hitpoints and do much more damage.  This might appeal to some hardcore gamers, but unless you like a ton of save scumming, avoid it if you are a casual gamer.Now for the worst part, the writing and plot for the main story.  I have family from Kentucky and I was initially very impressed with the voice acting and writing.  The satire and commentary of modern society is hilarious and very on the nose with many points.  When it comes to the main storyline, however, it is so filled with overused tropes, poorly explained or justified situations, and it just doesn't make sense or feel reasonable to anyone with a brain.  I don't know what the writers were thinking when they came up with the plot, but I almost quit playing the game 3 times because of how bad it got.In summary, between the bad writing for the main plot and the poor gameplay experience, I would struggle to give this game a rating over 3/10.  It might be a good game for some people, and I'm glad I actually finished it, but I was extremely let down and frustrated by the way the game ultimately resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Mutant Year Zero: Return To Eden, so I was looking forward to seeing how the same developer had progressed, but Miasma Chronicles is quite different, although also the same!MC has more hubs than MYZ, and the mechanics are somewhat changed. Gone is the circle of awareness, replaced by a glowing grid system, which I thought worked quite well. There are shops to buy and upgrade gear, and you have a skill tree for each main character, of which there are five, with two being your main characters and one of the remaining three being your companion.I started playing on normal difficulty, but I found that too time consuming. If you really love the format then I imagine a good time could be had thinking your way through each encounter, but eventually I was getting bogged down and changed it to the easiest setting, which turned out to be very easy indeed!Characters are nicely fleshed out, with good voice acting (although zero lip synch). Perhaps they are a wee bit generic, and interactions between them were scripted and barely interactive. I didn’t get the feeling that there was any kind of branching story, although I did miss out on two treasures and two watchers. Also, I never found all the pieces for the big gun, and I did feel that I had explored everywhere.The story is reasonable, with the post apocalyptic nature of the destroyed America fitting in nicely with the narrative conceit. There were one or two inconsistencies, but just the usual kind of sci-fi trope nonsense.The AI was pretty lame, and there was a weird mechanic that I couldn’t decide was a glitch or a feature - when you change guns they automatically reload, which doesn’t cost an action point, whereas loading your gun does? Why have loading at all if it can simply be bypassed?The art style is nice, if not particularly beautiful. There is so much blackness about (in the form of the titular Miasma) that after an extended session I did feel like I had just worked a shift down a coal mine. The camera controls are nice, but with no zoom, and the whole control system very intuitive on controller.I enjoyed my 30 hours, but not quite as much as Mutant Year Zero.
