_childDocuments_.review: Miasma Chronicles is a tactical RPG that offers an beautifully crafted immersive world, with some limitations. The storyline is very "narrow", the gameplay is slightly repetitive, and the story itself suffers from a disappointing final act that lets down some of the strengths of the game's writing, leading to some (fortunately brief) dissonance as the story demonstrates an absurd gameplay/character development dissonance moment that really leaves a sour note in the last act. However, the world still holds up the game and I think it's worth giving a try if it interests you.Overall: B+I would recommend this if the world sounds interesting to you, you want a tactics RPG but may be hesitant to try the genre for the first time (difficulty settings are very accessible but allow for more experienced players to face a challenge), and the story and world are compelling compared to average game stories. Gameplay: BI call Miasma Chronicles a tactics RPG because it checks the boxes. However, as a warning for those who might want to dig into stat allocations and robust skill trees, there is fairly limited options for build development. Each character has sixteen skill options in four small trees, unlocked by spending skill points that will allow you to get most, but not all, options for each character. There are a couple dozen weapons with a selection of modifications that range from extremely useful to pretty trivial. It isn't super robust, but it does allow for a sense of progression throughout.There are six major groups of enemies, with a pretty standard pattern of small, expendable enemies, more durable enemies that pose more of a threat, and the occasional boss type for a total of probably about fifty enemies, though many feel pretty similar. A lack of diversity holds things back here, though the difficulty settings are a nice touch and allow for a more tailored experience. I played most of the game through on normal and thought it felt mostly fine, with a few weird spikes up or down in difficulty because of side quests, until I dropped the difficulty because I had reached level cap and there wasn't a lot of variation in enemies, at which point the game became, well, extremely easy. Narrative difficulty is for the narrative, if you want more depth or challenge I would recommend normal+.The side quests are fine, but limited in scope and mostly serve to revisit old areas with new enemies or offer challenging fights. They serve more to bolster the storytelling than the gameplay, which is fine, but don't expect repeatable or farmable side quests.Additionally, vertical design is cool and makes the world interesting, but the tactical engagements don't always leverage them well- lines of fire get murky, the AI doesn't always seem to know what to do when fighting across multiple levels, and targeting across levels is wonky sometimes.Story: B-The story is mostly fine, held up by the characters, let down by some of the predictability. There are some things which are supposed to be plot twists that go from being foreshadowed to being painfully obvious to everyone except the characters. The final act is downright painful, with the main story beat being a character making some pretty frustrating decisions that seemed suddenly out of character. The fact that this is at the end is especially painful, because I generally liked the rest of the story and worldbuilding. While I suppose this was the easiest way to add some tension to the story, it feels rushed, out of place, and like they just wanted to finish the final act with a twist, which, to be fair, does lead to an interesting character development moment for the supporting cast, but could have been done much better if they had found a way to do this without so much dissonance between the excellent combat banter and character development and what seems like an abrupt story twist.Environmental design and graphics: A-I have nothing bad to say about the environmental design other than a few places where the Miasma is represented by a floating car or something with no visual effects, which felt jarring. Everything else felt good, though, with a few moments of physical implausibility hand waved away. The special effects chosen to represent things do a good job, I didn't encounter any noticeable glitches that stuck with me, performance wasn't an issue for me. Did have a few odd UI issues- like an enemy marker persisting from the final fight's first phase all the way through the ending cinematic (which detracted a bit from the cinematic). However, the aesthetic and design feel good throughout.Sound design and voice acting: B+I have some mixed feelings, in part because I encountered a bug where alt-tabbing sometimes broke the audio, so a few sections where I alt tabbed during a loading screen to check something. A lot of the sound effects are generic, but generally work and are reasonable and don't hurt immersion. The banter is great, really tells the story and sells the world when characters respond to context, share jabs or compliments, and generally I would rate this very highly, though sometimes it does feel a little bit rough. Towns are lively because of dialogue barks and there is a real synergy in the characters carried by excellent voice acting. Polish and quality control: A-Mostly very good, like I said I didn't encounter any bugs that really stuck with me besides the audio bug when alt-tabbing while loading which is not something I would hold against the game since that isn't "normal operation". However, there are a few typos/subtitle mismatches, including in at least a few storyline central moments, and I felt like the final act was rushed as if they just improvised a reason to make a certain event happen. I think I would say the quality is entirely within acceptable parameters, with a lot of the issues being easily missed or ignored and not detracting from the gameplay.Value: B-There is a lot of competition in the $50 price point, and I don't know if this would be my first pick at that price. However, the quality and gameplay live up to expectations for the price point. That said, I don't think you should be entirely deterred by this if you prefer shorter games you can actually reasonably finish in a few days- I think 15-18 hours is a safe estimate of playtime, though higher difficulties may pad that out longer. I would have loved to see a more content, particularly to explore different enemies in different arenas (something like a skirmish mode or random encounters to allow for exploring different abilities without just repeating encounters), flesh out the world a bit more, and a slower final act that didn't rely on an abrupt twist. However, since I grabbed the game on sale for $20, I would give it an A+ at the price I paid.

_childDocuments_.review: Watching U-tube videos of this game I found it was extremely interesting and entertaining, which led to the purchase of this game. Unfortunately, the actual game dynamics are wholly eccentric and do not play well with other aspects of the game. The combat mechanisms are nothing like the XCOM features aside from being turn based and cover oriented, which limits damage. The control configuration on the PC keyboard are exceptionally difficult to understand and memorize, not to mention that the tutorials are essentially garbage and do not give actual instructions on how to manipulate the players actions, like which button to press to go into ambush mode, etc, which has previously led me to refund games. After purchasing Miasma Chronicles which I regretted for obvious reasons. For one the game lacks a lot of the attractiveness and game-play ability of both XCOM and Dishonored, two of my favorite games. Miasma lacks continuity and is exceptionally difficult to progress beyond the level of beginner for obvious reasons, We all like a challenge but miasma is much more than a challenge, it is a monstrosity of epic proportions.There is no way that I, of humble video game nature, will ever be able to play miasma chronicles  despite my efforts. It is cool story, with engaging characters and a proper goal, etc. Unfortunately, unless you have a 195 I.Q. and a photographic memory, Miasma Chronicles is probably not a good game for you. Let us not forget, that we are talking about games, not life solutions here, I am revising my Review after playing for 15 more hours, I am still quite inexperienced at this game and I still have some misgivings about the mechanics of this game. Nevertheless, I am progressing and I have discovered much by essentially trial and error. I feel like some of the voice acting is crude and uninspiring, saying nothing about the typecast stereotypes, which is a little condescending and annoying. The story-line is a bit strange but at least it's not another zombie hack and slash rehash. Thank God!! The combat mechanics are somewhat bizarre, and nothing like XCOM and the genius simplicity of that Rock-God of a title. It is nowhere near that good, however, there are some cool nuances in this game that are attractive and enticing, I love the fact that a player can snipe enemies on the down low and thin the herd prior to engaging in all out existential combat. The tricks of the trade are brilliant. What I fear at the end will most assuredly be too short of a game which I struggled through for the first 12 hours only to find myself struggling through the entire game. However, I will have to leave the rest for a future rendition. After finishing the game, I realized it was far too short for the money I spent. I still haven't completely grasped the nuances of the controls and they oftentimes seem to lock up or lag in execution. I also spent a good deal of time trying to mend my accidental movement mistakes for pressing 'E' instead of 'W' on the keyboard. Furthermore, I do believe that supplying more game revenue, in this case it is "plastic". and revising the cost of certain weapons and other items would have made this game a bit more enjoyable. All in all it was decent, but for the hours played, it was hardly worth it. I have over 1,000 hrs on XCOM, and despite how old it is getting, I still occasionally play. I will probably play this again maybe a couple more times, but I fear it will be then forgotten like many other games.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it enough to play through it once, but I will unfortunately never play it again after these 20 hours. I have played some games for only a couple of hours and still thought I got my moneys worth out of them, but with this game I don't feel that way. I bought this on sale for 30 €, but this game should have been priced at 20 € without any discounts. The other negative reviews have already explained the negatives, but just a few main points:- The starting hours of the game feel slow. Once you get through them, the game does introduce a lot more fighting. So I would recommend not giving up in the beginning if you have already bought the game.- The gameplay is decent. All the actions, guns and powers feel like they are missing something. In XCOM I really get into the gameplay, but with this game the actual gameplay became a chore after a few hours.- Replayability just isn't there for me unfortunately, which is a big reason I regret buying the game. If the game was 20 € and especially if it was 15 €, I probably would have given it a positive review. The pricetag doesn't remove the negatives, but this doesn't feel like a complete game, so the pricetag does lower expectations.- The story is predictable, the acting isn't good and the writing is poor. All the worst and most predictable story elements and "twists" are here, with the most stereotypical and boring characters possible. I just absolutely hate how the story is set up and forces unnecessary drama.- On normal difficulty (full tactical) I never felt like I was in trouble. I never had to save-scum or anything like that, mainly because the stealth gameplay is so overpowered, that you can clear entire areas without the enemies ever even getting a chance to attack. The game knows this and throws you into forced fights, where the enemies appear in a cutscene when your party is in the middle of an open area and the enemies can attack you without you even getting a chance to react. Again, these battles are easy to win, but these tries to pump up the difficulty in this way is extremely irritating. Especially because every enemy "ambush" (just like all the "plot twists") can be seen a mile away.

_childDocuments_.review: Miasma Chronicles offers a solid tactical gaming experience accompanied by an average story-line. While it initially captures your interest, the game-play can become repetitive over time. Additionally, the game's economy includes odd choices, such as glass bottles being priced higher than grenades and unrealistic sell prices, which may leave you scratching your head. Despite these flaws, the game is enjoyable, although a few improvements could have taken it to the next level.As you progress further into the game, you'll notice that Miasma Chronicles leans more toward a puzzle game rather than a tactical action RPG. Combat encounters have a single predetermined solution, leaving little room for experimentation or alternative approaches. This design flaw forces players into a trial-and-error loop, where any deviation from the intended path leads to failure. The lack of freedom and flexibility in combat encounters is a significant drawback for a game aiming to provide tactical action.Despite its limitations, Miasma Chronicles still delivers an enjoyable experience for casual gamers. If you appreciate tactical gameplay and can overlook the repetitive nature and lack of flexibility in combat encounters, this game may be worth your time. However, if you seek a more open-ended and adaptable tactical-action experience, you may find the game's limitations to be a dealbreaker. Miasma Chronicles offers a satisfactory casual gaming experience, but needs to become an exceptional title in the tactical-action genre.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, Updated review now that I have just completed the campaign. Before I get into the details it's worth noting that, while I enjoy the Tactical Turn-Based genre, I am by no means an expert. I really enjoyed this games "predecessor", Mutant Year Zero.Overall I really enjoyed the approximately 32-35 hours it took me to complete the campaign (I played on skill level 2 of 4 and on light tactical). I felt that the game was very well balanced and remained challenging throughout. No single fight felt easy yet it felt rewarding to defeat each group. Some enemies do have some pretty unfair seeming skills (like summoning enemies every 2nd or 3rd turn) and player characters don't have any god-level powers.Still, the gameplay kept me coming back and I enjoy the exploration aspect, although limited compared to most games. Several areas are gated by more powerful mobs and guard better loot. One critique I have is that when it comes to your loadout, it never feels like you can have exactly what you want. I guess this adds to the challenge and at least you can swap mods, skills, etc on a whim so you can tailor your characters before each fight. The art style of this game is phenomenal. Extremely detailed and truly unique environments make wandering through the world a delight. Voice acting was very good yet gets underhanded by the fact that accurate lip-sync for dialogue only exists in a few story-driven cutscenes. Not enough to be a big detractor but a little disappointing for a 2023 release. The game has an interesting story that takes a few unexpected turns and is filled with little tidbits of lore that often have bits of silly humor. Nothing groanworthy, though, and I did laugh out loud a few times during the game.Overall I would recommend this game to fans of the genre or even newbies. It's RPG elements are pretty simple and the gameplay is straighforward enough that the learning curve is pretty quick. I will definitely play through this game again in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: I know I've barely played it, but I can already tell that the writing is extremely bad. Not only that, but for a game that's trying to be so firmly rooted in its Southern U.S. setting, it's a very strange choice to have the interface localization done by someone who uses British English. (Yes, we can tell, even when the words are not spoken aloud.) Also, I'm weary of sassy, slang-spouting robots. It's not cool or funny; it's just dumb. Were they going for some kind of American Fullmetal Alchemist vibe? I don't know, and I don't care.On a more technical level, the mouse-and-keyboard controls are extremely awkward and unpleasant. I have to imagine the entire team somehow managed to input all the code for this game using controllers, because it's clear that none of them understands how a mouse is used by normal humans.The gameplay elements seem fine and polished, so if you don't find the above problems as jarring as I do, you might enjoy the game. Just remember I did warn you about the very bad writing.

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed this on Extreme difficulty, Full Tactical mode.  I took my time exploring every location, completed almost every side quest and finished at about ~50 hours.  Awesome game overall.  I knew this would be a must-play since Mutant Year Zero is such a hidden gem and actually introduced me to the tactical stealth X-COM-like RPG genre.I feel the game could've been a bit tougher.  Some of the miasma abilities were a bit overpowered, especially the transmuter and teleport ones when used together. Using these abilities, I could repeatedly spawn an explosive barrel right in the middle of a pack of enemies at the start of basically every encounter, which seemed a bit too strong. Transmuter has insane casting range and potentially uses zero AP if you use the chip that negates the AP usage of the power. This wouldn't be so OP if there weren't so many ways to recharge your kilowatts.  It'd be more fair if you could only use those abilities maybe once per fight encounter.   I found the economy to be perfectly balanced and I never had a problem with money, especially if you loot every location and make sure to take advantage of leveling up to heal your squad rather than wasting medkits.$50 well spent.  I'd love to see a Miasma 2 and/or Mutant 2 in the near future!

_childDocuments_.review: (Spoiler free) Miasma Chronicles is not only a good story and game play, but a worthy addition to the growing "Xcom" style games. It brings some thematic qualities, refinement, and improvement to what mutant year zero created.   The Story strikes a very interesting balance thematically. Its gritty and dark while also preserving some of the best qualities that make us human while still acknowledging the needs that we feel that sometimes conflict with our altruistic nature. Each of the main characters are deeper then they might seem initially and with time open up as bonds are forged and secrets revealed. All this makes the story very relatable for the player in my opinion.Game play, if you like xcom or mutant year zero, you'll like this enough said. If you haven't here's what i'll tell you. Its a turn based grid strategy game where some of the most important parts of combat are how you prepare for it. It may challenge you, leaving you frustrated, but it always feels rewarding when you get the hang of it and have your "A Team" moment when the plan comes together.

_childDocuments_.review: Miasma Chronicles has been everything I hoped for and more as a spiritual successor to Mutant: Year Zero. The game still maintains the same core gameplay loop that made Mutant great, but it implements some new mechanics to spice things up a little bit.Miasma Chronicles is not a hardcore turn-based RPG with expendable characters like XCOM, etc.. Instead, it is a more simplified turn-based experience with dedicated story characters. However, the game is still plenty challenging, with 'Normal' difficulty providing enough heat to keep me on my toes. Upgrades to the game include a new power system, full-range hit percentages (compared to mutants quarter-chanced system), more side content, and unlocked FPS for the visuals. Combat is very fun with somewhat varied abilities and strategies, though there could be more. Furthermore, the AI feels improved, leading to some seriously challenging battles.As for the negatives, there aren't many to speak of. There are a few bugs here and there but nothing that forced a full reload or major loss of progress. The skill tree and ability system implements the fully refundable skills mechanic to encourage plug-n-play creativity. Personally, I am not a fan of this system as I prefer the hardcore nature of being stuck with my skill tree choices permanently. However lots of folks do enjoy that mechanic so it is what it is.The game runs very well, with no crashes to speak of. So far, it has been worth every penny!

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game because I like beautiful graphics and turn based game play. It is definitely a challenge. After reading the other reviews, I think many people don't like to think, they just want to play. As with Mutant year Zero, stealth is necessary to get through many missions. Taking out lesser health enemies or isolating the ones that will give you the most trouble is what is needed if you don't want to wipe your small three man team or use a million healing potions. If you blast in without thinking, you will have a much harder time. Yes there are times that to me was unfair, like the surprise in the gator area after you just came from a big fight. If you take the time to get your team fixed up before even revisiting the mission giver, you won't be unprepared for what comes. There are parts of the game you are meant to sneak through that map to get to the next one, not to fight the high levels before you can.I think the bad reviews are from those who fit in that category. I do think there are parts that are unbalanced. But its doable.What I don't like and I find totally unnecessary for the story and the game, is the gore in places. This is off putting to me.The story has many surprises, twists and turns. Before the last boss fight, was a shocker what you find out. I do think you should be able to use your whole team. I did not have any big glitches  or lock ups during game play. I had one item I could not pick up so I checked my driver to see if it had the latest update. It did not, so I took care of that and then I could pick up the items.If you are having a problem like that, always check your driver. It makes a huge difference.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game.It's not the perfect game by any means. The controls were a little wonky, there's a number of bugs and I felt that the finale was a little bit stale. But for 95% of the game I was totally hooked. I was curious, I was motivated, I felt like there was pressure on me to succeed. You're constantly thrown from the frying pan into the fire before a cathartic release.I've no idea what the complaints about difficulty are for, as that's part of my enjoyment. It is a hard game, but that's part of the fun. On the second hardest difficulty I got wiped once (Damn Tragul) and the rest of the time I was mostly teetering on the edge of failure and success. Which is exactly where I wanted to be. The exception being the final fight which was an absolute cake walk compared to everything else that had come before.If there is to be a sequel I'll definitely be picking it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun X-Com-style Turn-Based Strategy/Tactics game set in a post-apocalyptic Earth. Gameplay provides a lot of detailed and enjoyable depth and options. Graphics look quite good the only odd thing is that an overwhelmingly large amount of voice-actors and characters are African-American. No issue there, representation isn't bad at all BUT when it's wildly skewed in any one direction, it just feels awkward.I chalk it up to a foreign-based dev team (Sweden) who wants to force diversity into play instead of allowing it to happen or be depicted naturally.  It's the only real detraction in an otherwise enjoyable game but it is one that feels fairly jarring, imho.  It kind of reminds me of the goofy and fairly bizarre depiction of the mafia and organized crime in any of the GTA games by Rockstar, the UK-based company.  I think if you want to try to create a game set in or focused in another country, you may want to simply not bother because you're never going to get the balance quite right.Also, because I'm more than familiar with the overall intelligence level of the basic Steam gamer, I'm turning off comments so I don't have to listen to whiny and inaccurate "that's racist" remarks - because nothing about what I'm pointing out here is racist.  I have zero issues with representation and diversity but when it's clearly been shoe-horned into the game for its own sake, then I take notice.  Other that that bizarre design choice, this IS a fun TBS experience.EDIT - Didn't take long for some pea-brained numbnuts to throw a clown award my way.  Oh no, show us on the doll where the mean review hurt you (albeit an accurate one). But what I really love about pasty Steamers is that they're giving me awesome points to use in the Points shop, so thanks!  ROFL

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game in it's current state. It's close but not quite there. First off I started the game on Hard and full tactical because I'm a huge fan of xcomlike games. I don't recommend that. A lot of save and reloads.Pros: Story is kind of neat. Combat is good if you like turn based tactical games. Free refundable skill trees for experimenting on what's good and what's bad. Different enemies require different skillsCool miasma powers to help with combat. Stealth combat is fun. Bouncer guns are also cool. Being able to shoot people behind cover is amazing.Cons: The story. One of the pros is also a con. The story had enough to draw me in but didn't satisfy me. When the game ended I wanted more. They make such a big deal about what the miasma really is and yet you never find out. You don't know what it is or where it came from.The scaling. Often a quest will say recommended level 6-9 but when you get there and see the squad of enemies it says recommended level 14. That could be a side affect of me playing the game on hard.Not enough energy. I had some cool miasma powers but Id be lucky if I got one shot off. There are a lot of attachments to modify the powers but they usually increase the casting cost. This felt very counter productive.Not much reason to heal people to full. Some enemies hit so hard even in cover that it doesn't matter. There's 2 tiers of healing items but tier one is more practical due to the cheaper cost. Tier 2 items don't heal enough to prevent being one shoted by end game. I found it better to carry a bunch of cheaper healing items and use them to constantly revive people over topping their health to full.The game puts heavy importance on stealth combat. Which I like stealth when given the option but damn. You are required to try to kill half a squad to stand a chance in the early-mid game. Most enemies cannot be killed by one silenced weapon. When you find the 2nd silenced weapon it is a god send but there are still enemies you can't pick off without going load.Cool downs only recharge during combat. I understand why they made it that way but it sucks to kill a bunch of enemies in stealth and when you have to go loud, all your abilities are 3-5 turns on cool down.Backtracking. The game makes you sneak past a group of enemies because they are too powerful. Often there's some goodies but you can't get them yet. When you come back at a higher level to clear them out. The goodies would have been good, if you had got them the first time you visited. Which at the time was almost impossible. There were miasma powers I had to walk past because I was too weak. Then I forgot about them and went the rest of the game without them.The shops. On hard your health barely recovers after a fight. There is also no inn or rest feature to heal yourself besides leveling up. 90% of my currency was spent on healing items. I bought a new gun once and instantly regretted it. Any gun in the shop you can find somewhere in a chest or something better.The companion system. It's okay but you can only swap out your 3rd character. Your forced to bring Elvis and Diggs. This makes you have to make a hard decision who your 3rd char will be. One character I never got the chance to use because I was so dependent on my sniper.The game ended too early. Time wise I spent 33 hours. Which is about typical for what I paid for the game. However most of that is sneaking around trying to pick off enemies without alerting the entire squad. If you took out all the sneaking and back tracking to find items I probably spent 20 hours. Content wise it was lacking. At one part I thought it was the half way point of the game. Turned out it was the ending and they ended it on a cliff hanger. Left it open for another game or an expansion. If it's as short as the base game, I'm not tempted to get it.Crashes. The game crashed on me a couple of times throughout my play through. Worse is they happened at very inconvenient times. Like when I killed the last enemy and it froze when trying to play a cut scene. Forcing me to reload a previous save and do it again. As of writing this, even after a few patches, I still had a crash and had to redo the final boss battle. There's one part where you have to fight 5 waves of enemies back to back. Saving doesn't count. If you reload you have to fight all 5 waves again. It crashed on me at the end of the 5th wave. I went to sleep and tried again the next day.The game was good but it felt like the devs were told to stop halfway. I get the impression they deliberately ended it sooner than expected so they could sell us an expansion later. If your a fan of turn based tactical games you might enjoy it but feel hollow after completing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Eden Mutant Year Zero was an inferior X-COM like game with poorly balanced and frustrating combat, though it had an interesting setting and engaging characters.This successor is an inferior Mutant Year Zero. Enemies dispense with tactics and simply run adjacent to your characters, relying on their large health and armor pools to tank through your attacks while they shred your team.  The cover mechanic is awful, rather than damage protection it's a flat chance to miss, except I've never once seen it affect enemy fire. Perhaps it is a poorly explained or implemented mechanic.Available weapons are poorly balanced, some vastly better than others, and there are few of them. Sniper rifles are mostly useless due to the bizarre range accuracy penalties. They barely have more range than an assault rifle in the game, but take massive accuracy penalties if you are even a few spaces inside their max. Range is also frustratingly short for most weapons, the shotgun has 4 less spaces than some of the sniper rifles, but hits an arc, making it the obvious choice.Line of sight mechanics don't seem very consistent. I've been unable to shoot an enemy 2 spaces away because there was a low wall or bit of trash in the way, but I've also been able to shoot and affect enemies through walls and vice versa.The upgrade system and skill systems are shallow and uninspired and progression is tediously slow. Thanks to the bad decision of trying to shoe in some kind of poor stealth mechanic, which can either overpowered or useless depending on the map and enemy groupings, is only eclipsed by the awful decision to retain damage and skill cool downs between combats.The characters are more annoying than interesting with some some questionable decisions and racist overtones related to the "brother" bot,  and the plot is dull, dull dull. I might be able to ignore these things if the core of the game, the tactical portion, actually held up.As a fan of this genre I tried very hard to like this one but I found it more frustrating and annoying than enjoyable. So much potential here, so poorly implemented. If you can tolerate or work around the serious flaws you might have fun with this one, but I doubt it. I couldn't get past the 10th hour and I try to give every game a really fair chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty simple really. If you liked Mutant Year Zero, you'll like this. If you're a hardcore XCOM fan, as I am, it takes some adjustment but eventually it'll grow on you. Maybe not now, maybe not today, maybe not even yesterday but it will, eventually. It took me good amount of working up the courage to enjoy MYZ after a couple failed attempts (as in WTH is this kind of game) and in the end it paid off. This game also had the same effect, I'd been playing other turn based games before giving this a try and I couldn't hack it at first, not because it's hard... it's just weird mechanics. It's not your average turn based game, it has it's own mechanics, mechanics you'd do well to learn ASAP otherwise you'll sit around wondering what's happening and why you can't win a battle. It's not about just going straight into a battle-zone, you need to plan your approach, take out the easy targets without getting caught, explore everything first, get a feel for the area and what's going on. Early game is probably more difficult than once you reach say level 8. By then you'll have much better tactics/skills/weapons at your disposal. It's not the sort of game where you're expected to complete every side mission from the minute you come across it, you cam come back later when you're better equipped. All in all, I'd say give the game a chance, a real chance. Play Mutant Year Zero first if you have to, get yourself into the mindframe that this game wants you to be in. I found it very hard to shake off old habits from XCOM and the like but it'll pay off in the end.

These were to do with issues coming out of and being in ambush, visual glitches in the ending cutscene, the eternal bah mahdi floating head, and 3 crashes throughout 30h of gametime). I played this on the hardest difficulty and won on my first try, and let me tell you there is nothing like being 15h and down to one hero with no medipods, six full health enemies alive and managing to come out on top, because you know if you lose, its campaign over, 15h of progress lost. Unlike XCOM there is no possible way to savescum, so when you run out of medipods again 30h in, in the final fight, ♥♥♥♥ is intense. Real stakes, great artwork, well though out gameplay, room for dlc or a sequel. Everyone that complains about lack of ambush weapons/crit chance is misunderstanding the point of the game.I think for the price tag, there ought to be a bit more to the game, more side quests or a 45h storyline instead of 30h for the £45 I paid for it. Regardless, its well worth it in the stale era of gaming nowadays, one of the few good new releases.

_childDocuments_.review: I came to Miasma Chronicles after finishing and loving Mutant Year Zero. While Miasma (and Mutant Year Zero) is a Turn-Based Tactical game, it's significantly more approachable than Xcom games. This is incredibly story focused, where you work through the game in real-time, with snippets of Turn-Based activities. Both games are incredibly focused on stealth, with the game being almost impossible unless you move around and take out some enemies before actually beginning the battle with the remaining enemies. Battles are a natural part of the environment, and you aren't "preparing your loadout" before each battle.I've waited to play Miasma Chronicles until a few patches came out, and had very few bugs (except a weird one crashing the final battle when using my REWASD configured PS5 controller). I also played at the higher difficulty level, which I enjoyed a lot mainly because I came from Mutant Year Zero.Battles are really more like puzzles. Each enemy is specifically positioned within the environment, and you need to look into different distractions, high/low shielding, and getting up higher. Through the final battle I really felt like I had to think about the limited resource I had, the abilities assigned, and where my characters were before starting the battle.Similar to their other games, resources are really limited almost to the point of making the game incredibly difficult in the beginning. It remains difficult, and can definitely put people off if you're used to normal turn-based games.One of the hardest things to get past is that you get very, very little experience from battling enemies. Experience comes from completing quests and finding the hidden items. It took me a while to realize that after each battle it made no different in my experience. Then I started clearing out the side quests and suddenly rocketed my levels up.Pros- When a character dies, they come back to life when the battle ends, or can be healed mid-battle (good since there are limited characters)- Great, linear story with orchestrated battles that feel like puzzles- Really unique characters with distinct build options- Enemies don't respawn, making it impossible to "farm" resourcesCons- Really difficult almost from the start- Resources are pretty scarce

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited to try this game as I enjoy XCOM style games and really enjoyed Mutant Year Zero. However, after 3 hours, the balance just seems awful and leaves me with a lot of frustration. I'm playing on normal difficulty and I'm getting rocked every fight. There are too many enemies that seem to have much better accuracy than your characters and they deal too much damage. You get Jade in your party rather early and she has a silenced sniper rifle that you can use to pick off enemies that walk away from their group to make a fight easier. This is absolutely required to do because you won't win the fight if you don't. The problem here is it doesn't feel challenging or satisfying to do, it just feels tedious. Even after you pick off as many enemies as you can, with how much better the enemies' accuracy seems to be, you'll find yourself saving/reloading after every miss in order to stand a chance even on normal difficulty. Another thing I dislike about the combat is how much of the abilities are locked behind the upgrade tree. Some of the abilities will be very familiar to you as a tactics fan. The main problem is the whole skill tree is just uninspired. Some of them are just "Get 20 extra HP" while others are "unlock overwatch." Overwatch shouldn't be something one character has to unlock, that has been a staple in tactics games for years, everyone should have that! It's just frustrating for no reason. The game looks great but the combat is a bit uninspired and feels like too much of a chore.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so let's start by addressing the elephant in the room. The difficulty, now I've pumped a fair bit of time into this game as I've always been a fan of games like xcom and Troubleshooter: Lost children so far yes this game has proven on multiple occasions that it is not afraid to punch you in the nuts. From teleporting melee units that one bang your squishy units to dime a doesn't grunts that whittle you down with numbers and status effects. This game doesn't hold your hand and for good reason. For all the BS the game puts you through you can equally give as much back for example take Elvis' Miasma powers (Minor Spoiler ahead)I've been making use of his tornado and healer summon abilities which can move enemies out of cover and help him keep everyone at full health (even after getting hit with a super lucky shot from certain tougher enemies) but as I'm sure you're about to ask "But how do you use you're power's when there are limited energy cells?" Simple make use of weapons and modifications that regain KW energy for example give Elvis a shotgun and equip it with the KW regen mod for every enemy hit. With this you can pump out steady Damage and regain resources and Assuming you've given Diggs your best Shotgun with the rage mod (Which if you haven't wtf are you doing man's a freight train with it) you can line up some insane kill zones that can even the playing field a little doesn't mean you're a god now or anything (Just ask Red Death who absolutely loves to remind me that I am still mortal) But you can start to enjoy the game a little better (It took me 3 restarts to figure this out btw X-X) If you made it through my rambling I applaud you and I highly recommend this game if you enjoyed their previous work Mutant Year Zero You can tell they are improving and the worlds they create are always entertaining and filled with little easter eggs that'll make either roll your eyes or burst out laughing.

_childDocuments_.review: Miasma Chronicles is a science fiction RPG with turn-based tactical combat a la XCOM in an end-time version of the USA. And unlike the previous two games, there is no indie team behind this title, but experienced developers with a slightly larger budget, so it’s more of an AA game.Due to initially unknown circumstances, the formerly corporate-ruled world is broken and haunted by a strange threat called Miasma. This substance causes all kinds of destruction as well as a kind of dimensional shift. And on top of that, there are strange beings who worship the miasma as some kind of deity and want to exterminate all humans.(German voice-over, CC in ENG and many other languages)But I see all kinds of problems in the balancing because the fights are really crisp. And sometimes it gets frustrating to the point of pulling your hair out. The enemies are numerous and deal out a lot of damage, while healing material is very scarce and our hero group is often massively outnumbered. The cooldowns are usually way too long, and even for distraction skills you have to find empty bottles first, and they are strangely rare to pick up, although there are plenty of them everywhere as decoration.In addition, even simple actions like healing and reloading consume our extremely scarce action points, so you’re often simply overrun. And regenerating between fights doesn’t work either. So, even if you know your heroes are badly banged up, you can’t just go home and rest. You have to go into the next fight wounded, and first use action points and the rare consumables for that again. I find that very, very strange and not nice.On some maps, you can make up for it by sneaking, sneaky ambushes, or clever use of the environment. And if you manage to resolve the almost puzzle-like difficult combat scenario of some maps and use the environment to your advantage, there’s fun and satisfaction in having accomplished something.But the story also often throws you into battles unprepared with half HP, where there are no opportunities to perform special placements or ambushes. This may certainly provide a great challenge for some tactics fans. However, I found it a bit too intense for my taste, even on difficulty 2 out of 4. There is also a story mode where the battles are then dialed down even further, but my goodness, can the game kick your butt sometimes.So after 10 hours into the game, I’ve played some battles twice or four times and am far from having seen the end of the game. But always I was wavering between “I want to see more of the fancy world and learn more wacky miasma skills” and “boah, been surrounded and wiped out again, completely out of healing potions and not really had a chance, that sucks”.While the presentation is mostly high quality, the price of €50 or $ seems reasonable. However, with the high frustration level due to what I see as immature balancing, you somehow can’t fully enjoy this fancy world. And that somehow leaves the price tag with a very, very pale aftertaste for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 30 hours of playtime and overall... the game's OK. I'm enjoying it enough to keep playing, but it definitely has issues. Sadly, there are too many negative for me...===============PRAISE===============1. Mapping, lighting, and overall textures look fantastic. They do a great job immersing you in the world.2. Music is great! It really fits the theme. Exploration is mysterious and calm but combat is upbeat and sets the mood.3. Plenty of side quests, hidden secrets, and places to explore/unlock!4. Weapon mods, 2 power cores to add additional perks/benefits, miasma (magical) powers that you can customize further, each character has their own skill tree, and you get a lot of nice abilities.5. Combat has a nice variety of abilities for each character.6. The town has a lot of interesting characters and shops.7. Lighting and shadow is done very well.8. Character models look good, animations are smooth, and controls are easy to understand/use!===============GRIPES===============1. None of the characters are really likable, unfortunately. The main character (who's name is ELVIS btw LOL sorry) is a whiny teenager that just moans and groans about everything. Your robot companion, Diggs, is the comedic relief and verges on annoying at times. Jade, the "mystery girl" is cliche. Who is she? Kinda rude. But then she grows, becomes soft, and opens up. Been done. And then there's "Mama." She's loud, stern, and strict... typical teacher/mentor behavior.2. The story is interesting, but the dialogue is really bad. Poorly written, cheesy, bad jokes, and many conversations make no sense. Just filler talk that serves no purpose to the story. Also... with Elvis being a whiny baby all the time... listening to him gets old fast.3. The main character is dumb as hell. He's so oblivious to, literally, everything. He asks stupid questions that the rest of his party know the answer to. For example... a man asks him to find antibiotics for his sick daughter. Elvis still acts ignorant to the fact they're in a hospital, what is this place, let's find these "healing sticks."4. Combat is, unfortunately, bad in terms of other turn-based tactical games. The game is built around a glitchy and poorly developed stealth system. You have to sneak around and "silently" take some enemies out, assuming you have enough guns with silencers. If not... you have to face a massive squad of enemy soldiers, which is nearly impossible against your party of 3.5. Stealth and splitting your party up is a big annoyance. It's slow, the AI is dumb, and it just makes no sense. You can take enemies out, practically, right in front of their friends... and they have no idea what just happened. Bodies also vanish, so you don't even have to worry about a patrol finding their dead corpse. It's just pointless, bland, and repetitive. The game would have been much better had they just balanced combat around not having pointless stealth.6. Reloading adds a nice strategy but guns with only 1 ammo slot... really hurts the experience. I get that, in real life, sniper rifles need reloaded between each shot... but this IS a video game.7. Not a fan that you can only take 3 characters into combat. So many turn-based tactical games give you large squads of 4-6 characters. From what I understand... you only get 5 heroes... so why it wasn't built around letting us take all 5 into battle... no idea. This would have made combat more interesting as the game progressed.8. They reference America a lot... and talk about "Ancient America" or the "Saviors of America." It just sounds cheesy. I mean, set your game in a post-apocalyptic USA, but you don't have to consistently have characters be PRO-'merica every 2 seconds. This takes place around 150 years after the collapse of the United States, so I can't imagine people would STILL be this patriotic in this new wasteland LOL9. You have an OUTFIT slot and vendors have an OUTFIT category (that's always empty)... making you think you'll be able to find or unlock a lot of new armor/clothing. However, outfits are very difficult to find, there aren't many, and they're purely cosmetic. Not sure of the point then. If they're so rare and hard to find... why not give them some benefits to health, armor, movement range, etc?===============Is the game worth playing. I've been on the fence about it. Yes, it's getting great reviews, so you may not pick it apart as much as I do, but I found myself frustrated with the cheese-fest dialogue and story, boring stealth, and just uninteresting characters. Combat is... just OK, too.

_childDocuments_.review: Only played a little so far, but after almost 40 years of gaming... my gut instinct is pretty sharp as to whether I think it's going to be a winner or not - and I absolutely believe this is on target to be one of my games of the year.My favourite game of all time is Wastelands 3 - a decent part of the enjoyment came from the co-op. BUT I do think this is going to prove an extremely enjoyable one player experience that will keep that part of my gaming appetite satiated nicely.The main two starting characters are definitely a bit 'Hollywood' for my liking - but I absolutely love the aesthetic and the control mechanism - which goes from free roam with your joystick as you would in a top down shooter to turn based for combat (this is actually an improvement on Wasteland 3s, par for the genre point & click character movement - some may not find it better, but at least it's different - and more importantly - it works).

_childDocuments_.review: My thoughts as I uninstall this game, sad that it could have been so much more than what it is:- This game is probably going to do well with people who like XCOM style games, but with smaller party members. I don't know how many more you get, but you start with two.- There is something super forced about the characters and story in this game that feel wrong, and off putting.- I could not get invested into the story line.- I could not get invested into the characters.- I could not get invested into the protagonists mommy issues, had a literal eyeroll, and found myself saying, "Not this again?". The added NPC's piling onto the trope like Mommy was some sort of legendary person did not help at all.- Game feels super woke? Maybe? That's a hot button topic. It just wasn't for me, but I appreciate what they were trying to do.- I could not get invested into the robot with a black man's voice. Seriously, why make him a robot? Just make him a beefy black dude that can do the same stuff. Hell, give him a robotic arm, or make him a cyborg. The generic repainted tin can felt like a gimmick. Besides, it would have been much more authentic to have the robot sound more robotic and/or to have the robot develop a "personality" over the course of the game.- I could not get invested into combat. The constant 3v2, 4v2, 5v2 combat for literally every single encounter (I had at least 10 encounters) got old, fast.- I was majorly annoyed about the WADS controls (or lack of), how I was locked into selecting my opponents in combat (I am playing on a mouse and keyboard, why do I need to arrow around?), and the biggest cardinal sin is that stupid fixed camera. I prefer a more isometric top down view. Sure, I can swivel it side to side with the EXTREMELY ANNOYING middle mouse button (who the hell wants to click that? Just let me use Q and E!) but I can do nothing for the up/down perspective.I played the dev team's last game, which this clearly takes a big cue from. I enjoyed the last game more before getting burnt out, I didn't finish it. But that one grabbed me more than this one; I found myself falling asleep for this one.If you don't love this game within the first hour, refund it. You're unlikely to change your mind.

_childDocuments_.review: During narrative sections, the player character walks SO SLOWLY that it is impossible to believe anyone actually played this game. It is ponderous and plodding tedium, wholly unnecessary. Ah yes, I know, it gives the world a "heft" and "weight." That's what I want to do for fun, be weighed down.Similarly, the combat system hops between key binds - is it tab to cycle choices, or Q/E, or numbers?Finally, I dare you to ask five random TRPG friend to try this game, and watch them go through three combat encounters without tipping them off to the following. The characters are bland and stereotypical, and Diggs is... well, let's just say it sure was a choice to make the only black main character a robot programmed to serve the white boy in the south. The world is the traditional fallout style - everything is still destroyed like the apocalypse happened two days ago, and despite having mining robots the starting town is still more of a ramshackle corrugated aluminum junkyard than a settlement. Finally the gameplay - comparing it to XCOM really isn't doing it any favors, because XCOM EU had better gameplay a decade ago. MYZ had the same issues, where the gameplay was slow and plodding, and miasma chronicles doesn't even have the shallow appeal of a shotgun-toting duck who can fly.If you liked MYZ, then probably just go back and play that again. Did you know there's a TTRPG? Go buy that instead of spending money on this. There are better xcom-likes out there, there are better post-apocalyptic mystery games out there, and there are definitely better stories out there. 5/10, if you held a gun to my head I'd play through the entire thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted to play a Sith Lord in a medium-low tech, post-apocalyptic story? This is your chance! (Sorry no lightsabers) Story is a slow build though, and characters are so 1-dimensional that they would be a blank sheet of paper on a Rorschach Test. Those ~10 hours are a bit bland, but then the real fun begins, and it’s worth it. starts strong with a cool opening sequence but quickly grinds down into low gear. First couple of fights are fine, but like a lot of games, you don’t start with any cool skills/items. Fights are pretty much move-shoot-next-->. Then you return to the same rundown small town that you’ve seen in every dystopian novel/game/TV/etc. The story is painfully lackluster at this point (got to find mama!). It isn’t likely to hook you.I know, I know. I’m not really selling it. This was all to say, it will be easy to get bored/distracted early on. Stick with it. After ~10 h you’ll be glad you did…and those hours aren’t a slog…they’re just a little bland.Turn-based combat is fun and interesting, especially once you level up a few times. At its core, combat is pretty stock standard. 2 actions. Turn ends when you attack. Cover good. Getting flanked bad. All the normal stuff. Building on this foundation is what makes it engaging. Skills and gear provide fun and interesting ways to approach combat. Sometimes I equipped the ricochet gun just for funzies. Some characters can manipulate the Miasma (a semi-sentient, destructive swarm of…nanobots? Alien insects?). Miasma powers come in 2 categories:  and . The powers that don’t summon something feel like they were designed by Darth Vader or Darth Sidious. See…told you things would get interesting. is very similar to their previous game,  It successfully breaks away from the tried and true  formula. First, stealth kills are heavily rewarded…which might be an unfair statement because some tough fights are almost impossible if you don’t knock off a third of the bad guys before you trigger the alarm. Second, you do not heal between fights. Third, skills only cooldown in fights. Finish a guy in stealth with a 4-round cooldown? Combat ends there and you need to spend 3 rounds of combat without that skill. No…other stealth kill rounds do not count. Skill and HP management are crucial.World building and visuals are very cool. I get it, building a good, in-depth world takes time. It needs to be slow so that you don’t overwhelm the player.  also does an excellent job of telling the story with visuals and interactions. The game almost never uses that tropey dialog at the beginning of each episode to explain: “If we don’t get the  back, the town will be teleported into space by  and John Connor will never grow up to be a real boy!” The world was a real pleasure to play through and experience. Tactically moving through a ruined skyscraper (in and out of stealth) still sticks out as my favorite set piece.Story gets a B/B- in my book. I know a bunch of people loved it. Pacing is a bit slow for my taste, but once you get past the “this is the start to every other dystopian story you’ve ever read” it comes alive. Other than an unnecessarily slow start, I also did not like how some of the twists were portrayed. They felt super contrived. Lastly, no story can be completely separated from the characters…My one major complaint is that the characters are 1-dimensional MEGA-tropes. They are so ground into their particular trope that what little personality (obtained from great voice acting) was crushed like Admiral Ozzel. I found nothing unique or interesting about any of the playable characters. Sure, there is one that is goofy-fun…but still no personality outside of the trope.I wasn’t sure I was going to do this, but here it goes…time to piss off Some have complained that the game’s robots represent an offensive racial stereotype. Portrayed as a servitor race, the main robot character also has a stereotyped black-person’s speech pattern. There is not enough there for me to claim intent. Later, robots have different speech patterns and live in a town where humans are the servitor race. Unfortunately, the only other major robot character also has a rapper-gangsta name, the stereotyped speech pattern, and is an actual gangsta. What sealed the deal was when the character was presented as blinged out with massive gold chains and a bejeweled initial of his name. That was a clear, conscious, artistic choice. Was it egregious? Offensive? Maybe that’s for you to judge. For me, it was a clear portrayal of a harmful racial stereotype. Enough for me to think “cancel this game?” No. But if I have any sway over you, I encourage you to play to this point in the game. Pause and consider how portraying the stereotype is harmful. We can’t become better if we don’t examine these issues, both the extreme and subtle. Then lets all ask  to do better next time.

_childDocuments_.review: At current time of playing, I'm not even a full quarter-way through the game, so this review may be subject to change.  That said, I absolutely cannot recommend this game enough. Even if I did get this game from a friend (thanks to their Humble Bundle codes.)  Some of the themes and whatnot are, admittedly, a little milquetoast throughout, but there's genuinely a lot of fun to be had if one is willing to engage with the setting of the game as well as it's gameplay at it's core, Miasma Chronicles is incredibly amusing and the combat, while relatively simple even on the "Full Tactical" setting, is rather endearing and rewarding.  As for a proper review, sometimes it feels like the progression and game is a little slow and disjointed -- quests that are far beyond your level at the time of receiving them, but I quickly realized it does not put them beyond your reach. With the proper application of consumables, abilities, and tactics (and a bit of luck), you can actually pull over some fights that are upwards of 3 levels beyond your reach otherwise. The Voice acting is, while sometimes coming across as odd, also very endearing in the very natural way it comes across -- the lines bouncing off of each-other don't often feel disconnected or uneven, so it flows nicely. Really, the only complaint I have so far is the currency economy -- Quests do not often given monetary rewards, so the only way you can earn money (Which is Plastic, in this game) is by scrounging it off of enemies or by finding it randomly in the world during exploration. This can make getting upgrades for your team a little bit of a pain, but I've also reached the point where I've just found enough weapons through progression and exploration (generally through weapon crates behind keypad-locked doors) that it's not as much of an issue in the immediate moment.     I will give this review an update upon completing the game, but this game has achieved the rare case of getting a review out of me at all outside of a Steam Seasonal Event. I cannot stress how good this game really is.

_childDocuments_.review: MIASMA CHRONICLES is a mix of X-Com-like strategy game coupled with the RPG trappings of a young boy and his robot out to save the world, set in a unique post-apocalyptic America where a deadly Miasma consumes most of the country. Wish I liked this more.There is a "correct" way to play this game, and it involves sneaking around stealth-killing lone guards out of the sightlines of their teammates. I'm all about that stealth life, but when that tactic isn't viable (ie sticks you in an arena) then you're in for a punishing time.The story is also unbalanced: the first act runs for considerably longer than the rest of the game; so by the time our heroes' journey REALLY begins, the game is 2/3rds over and so much plot and plot twists gets crammed in the last couple of hours it becomes a little hilarious.I enjoyed those first hours of the game when the world was all steeped in rich possibilities with a twist of mystery - but by the end of the game it all seemed so... small. And the characters kept fumbling the idiot ball among themselves. Voice acting was pretty great though!

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and enjoyed myself a lot. Hunting achievements and doing all side quests was just as much fun as following the main storyline. At times, there is a quirky kind of humour in the dialogues which I liked. I have a lot of hours in the game but for maybe 10-15 hours the game was idling while I was doing something else. If you're more of a streamlined gamer (unlike me) you'll finish it probably in 40 hours or less.This is no doubt a really good game. It is not without its flaws, but it does most things really well:Pros:+ Very cool visuals - great artwork with attention to detail, all aspects of the game have polished visuals.+ Nice level designs and layouts. The areas are varied and lend themselves to intricate turn-based battles.+ Sound design is one of the strongest parts of Miasma Chronicles. The voices are well spoken and relatable, dynamic music and sounds are spot-on and atmospheric. It all sets the mood nicely.+ Kills and hits in battle scenes are often animated from the shooter's perspective, which helps immersion nicely.+ Apart from one area where there is a known bug issue (see forums), the game runs pretty flawlessly.+ Combat mechanics are pretty solid - you can easily tell how much damage you will make unless your hit chance is low. Positioning is everything here.Cons:- The game seems to have resource-hungry spikes that make some of the activities on-screen stutter or lag at times. This happens mostly during combat, in particular when the game engine tries to play out the action in first-person view.- The user interface could be more intuitive and logical. A lot of aspects of party and inventory management are quite clunky. For instance, if you want to customise weapons, you can't do this from the inventory screen, but only in the party screen, and when said weapon is equipped. This could have been implemented better. Likewise, when accessing the backpack in fights, you need to scroll through all the consumables with the Q and E keys, which is cumbersome. There is more but these are just 2 examples.- While the voice acting is pretty darn good, the dialogues can be corny and "too much" at times. I hated it at first, but when you get to know the main characters it isn't that abrasive any more.All in all I can confidently recommend Miasma Chronicles for any fan of story-rich games with turn-based combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the game for the first time.Wow.I loved their Mutant Year Zero and Corruption 2029. In this game they took all their experience in game design, world-building and art and pushed it to the next level. This is a legit RPG with deep and interesting plot, characters and game world. With very cool turn-based/stealth puzzle combat system on top.I would describe the game world in terms of "Final  Fantasy meets Fallout meets Star Wars" in a GOOD way. You've got a post-apocalyptic world ruled by an oppressive  First Family with scattered and almost wiped out at some point order of "knights" capable of taming the , , Miasma. How cool is that? I can tell you that in THIS game this is beyond cool!In all this mess you are just a young boy (although with kick-ass brother robot) looking for his mother. And boy, you are in for an adventure of a lifetime.You travel the world (beautiful locations), pushing the main quest, taking and completing side quests, meeting new people and characters to join your party.Combat system is a mix of turn-based "X-Com style" battles with Commandos-like stealth puzzle elements. If you can find and kill an enemy silently without being seen by other enemies -- they won't be alarmed. This is a third game of theirs with this mechanic and I have to confess that I enjoy it tremendously every time I play it. Regarding the technical side -- I played with ultra quality on my 4 year old gaming lap top. In all my hours of play I had almost zero problems. I encountered only one crush later in the game (and no it didn't happen during the gauntlet!) The game was running for like 6 hours straight at that point. I'd say that's OK, considering I was able to run a world-class looking game with max graphics on my not-so-new PC.So my verdict -- a great RPG -- a breath of a fresh air and a hope that we have another developer to rub shoulders with all time greats of the genre.Now I'm looking forward to DLCs, part II, you name it. Fingers crossed and I highly recommend the game!

_childDocuments_.review: 50 hours of gameplay for 20 bucks, whats in it for you:Story: 5/10Pretty forseeable storyline, medium length/depth, simplest of plot twists. Even side quests are more or less straight forward with a bit of thinking and patience. Weaponsystem is ok-ish, some variety, nothing really out of the ordenary or special to it compared to other games of the genre. I personally find the tactical battle menu system a bit cluncy, confirming every move with "space". but once you get a hang of it, it works ok.graphics, 5/10:even though its unreal engine, lots of areas look pixelish or simply not good, while others look absolutely stunning. its a shame that most of the landscapes are so ugle due to the miasma.Bugs, 10/10:This game seemed to be bug free, if we do not count one crash I had the whole time of play, which might not be related to the game, but to my PC itself, which I did not bother to find out. any other mechanics, quests etc, worked as designed and did not interrupt gameplay, which made this game a smooth experience.overall for me a good game for the price, worth of play for a week or two and for hardcore fans, it might give the edge in higher difficulties hunting for achievements.7/10 overall for me personally and a good recommendation for the price.

If you're a fan of tactical, turn-based games like XCOM, Chaos Gate, Hard West, and Mutant Year Zero, this game is worth buying at a large discount.Unfortunately, the story is really poorly written. The main characters are all cliches and the villains are one-dimensional. Dialogue is extremely cringe. It's like the writers were writing a story for kids, while the rest of the dev team was making a really brutal post-apocalyptic world full of death and body horror. It just completely misses the mark. Even the title of the game sounds like the name of a crappy, self-published YA novel on amazon. It's a real shame that this cool-looking world gets such a crappy story.There are also some baffling design decisions. On higher difficulties, there's an overreliance on consumables and save scumming, which makes combat more frustrating than challenging. Character progression is very underwhelming, and "magic" is cool and powerful, but can only be used sparsely. No idea what they were thinking, but I hope they aren't going to stick with it in their future games.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game mechanics-wise. Story and setting are pretty average but not too bad, strong enough to keep you interested but I found it tailed off in the last third. The mood is played fairly straight (minus the juvenile quips from your team, though that can almost be passed off of as a product of their world, almost. Also Jade's accent and delivery grated on me like sandpaper.) until you reach robot town. I don't know why but all the robots are voiced and scripted like cartoon characters, it would have been better if they'd kept the whole tone more to the serious side, I guess they were worried about falling into pomposity, but then again: Bah Mahdi. There's a little pacing issue where you don't get a full compliment of companions to choose from until right near the end, making you not want to try new characters as you've spent the lions share with your current ones, until the game forces you to do so that is. Also they're just unlikable, you feel no connection to them as a result, it would have been better to bring them all in earlier or just not include them as team members.All in all though it's good, I really enjoyed the battles. You can take your time setting up ambushes and luring out enemies one-by-one if you like, or just go in guns blazing, it's all possible and totally up to you. I never felt like I had to play encounters exactly one way or another. It's great that games like this are being made and I look forward to more from these guys.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it on sale at a pretty decent discount. I can recommend it at that price, but definitely not worth full price. I have pretty mixed feelings about this game. The gameplay is solid and challenging. The world is great and I would love to see more of this setting. The game itself looks really good. However, the approach is more stealth based than all out combat; until the last third or so where your stealth weapons start failing to keep up with enemy HP. The cast and writing in general are pretty bad. The last couple hours of the story are awkward, the arcs unearned and feel extremely rushed. There's not a lot of development going on for each of them and it leaves the cliched moments weak and transparent. The voice actors seem fine overall but the directing and tone is odd at times. The skills themselves are fine but the leveling system is frustrating, as it's slow to gain new skills and most of them are passives anyway. You can't get every skill, even at max level but it still didn't feel like there was any true build variety. Loot is uninspired but not not bad. It seems like they wanted to encourage swapping weapons for fights but failed to put enough weapons and variety (especially end game) in to actually make it matter. You can also instantly kill the final boss on the first turn of the fight, which didn't seem intended but does fit with the mechanics of the game up to that point and is a bit funny. 6/10?

_childDocuments_.review: Whether you'll like this game depends on your attribute preferences.  This game looks great.  The graphics are AAA.  If you like that, that's a major plus.  The post-apocalyptic atmosphere is well presented.  There's a lot of story, as our main characters try to unravel the mystery of their world including the mystery of the miasma.  So far the combat is fine.  It emphasises getting your units into position to get a good start in the battle by ambush damaging the alien enemy.  This is critical, scout the battle scene stealthily, study the enemy, and position your team carefully.  I enjoy that.  The game has Save Anywhere, so you can experiment with the game mechanics to help learn the game.  I would say this game has a more relaxed feel and pacing, than say an amped-up turn-based game like Showgunners.  I play this game when I want some relaxed game time.I got this game on sale to give a try, as the negativity of some reviews had put me off.  I decided to buy it on sale and see it for myself.  At this point I think it's good and I'm happy with my decision to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Miasma Chronicles is a deep, turn-based combat puzzler with a poor but skippable writing. I thoroughly enjoyed it despite its flaws.Tactically, Miasma Chronicles (MC) improves on Mutant Year Zero (MYZ) in every way. MC allows each character to have multiple active abilities to swap between, giving the player an interesting choice (on the hard difficulty) of which ones to put on cooldown to get through each fight. Spending and building up Kilowats for impactful miasma powers and Rage for killer gauranteed crits adds even more tactical depth.Also, the distinct functionality of each weapon type was very engaging and satisfying to use, which was a big improvement over MYZ where I used snipers almost the whole game. On a related note, they fixed high ground to now give an offensive bonus but no defensive bonus. High ground sniping was so effective in MYZ that I had resolved to not use it in MC until I realized that they had just redesigned the mechanic.Miasma Chronicles also improves on the real time stealth of MYZ by including the rage mechanic, preventing cooldowns from ticking during ambush rounds, and by introducing the glass bottle consumable. These changes make every stealth kill more of a tactical decision and more satisfying.The main downside is that the characters are somewhat annoying and the main interpersonal conflict feels very contrived. But, you can skip almost all dialogue and just enjoy setting up killer ambushes while making tactical tradeoffs between 5 different resources (cooldowns, kilowats, rage, health, consumables).
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, because I like turn-based strategies and this one is (unfortunately) not great, but a good one. The gameplay is decent. The powers, weapons, etc are put together well. It's fun to play, trying out different tactics, different approaches. I loved the open-world approach, sneaking around the enemies, ambush them and wipe them out. The world is very well detailed and it's a visual orgasm.But...The story is a different story. It starts good, misterious, figuring out the far future world is fun. Then, as the story unfolds, it turns to a Z-category sci-fi fantasy. The citizens of the former world are called "Originals". The airplanes are "Flying Whales". The hospital is called "Dying Place". But everyone wants to save the good old America... WHY?! Why do they have to "save" America? Why it's even America? That's very disappointing and very low and the characters are talking way too much about it.Also, the voices are a disaster...

_childDocuments_.review: Combat initiation can be done after ambushing to pick off some stray enemies, and with silent weapons/skill you can string together multiple ambushes to really cut down on the enemy before the fight even starts.In highest difficulties, cheesing through as many ambushes as you can get is almost required. Health regen after combat is inefficient and resources are always scarce. This means micromanaging items and abilities and non stop to make sure you can successfully ambush when ready, but also that your ambush skills aren't useless on the occasional surprise attack that can result in a teamwipe.It is still satisfying to execute an ambush, and I'm still enjoying the core experience enough to continue, but the story/characters leave room for improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: This is like the interesting parts of modern X-Com, with a more unique story. (Assuming the tactical battles are the part of X-Com you find interesting, not the base-building.)The skills from leveling up are a bit weird in that some of them are massively better than others (e.g. a passive 20% bonus to critical chance if you're on high ground is not worth more than the ability to use overwatch, which effectively gives you multiple shots per turn. Critical hits aren't even that great, so a 20% chance is worth about 1/10th of a shot, whereas overwatch frequently gives you a whole extra shot and sometimes as many as five in a single turn, but the 20% chance skill costs more than the overwatch skill.) But that's okay, the skills and weapon upgrades are, for the most part, subordinate to the tactics, which is nice - there's not really any grinding.The before-battle stealth element is an interesting twist (if you can take out a bad guy using only silent damage, in a single turn, and out of sight of his companions, it's free, essentially).The only really negative thing I have to say is that the hardware requirements are pretty aggressive for a turn-based tactics game - I had to turn it down to 720p resolution and medium quality, with a laptop 3060, and it was still a little sluggish on the framerate. It's possible that this is related to Linux/Proton, but most games don't struggle this much under the same conditions.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good tactics rpg which on the max difficulty settings felt like a fun puzzle with a lot of tools available to use, and being able to easily swap skills created a lot of variety. Anti-typical. The impact of skills and variety of items are minimal so it's mostly a focus on how to use what's currently available to overcome what's next. Can run around grabbing everything, but clearly it's not necessary, and same with a lot of stealth. Enjoyable gameplay.Despite various bugs, the "Load Latest" and stealth mechanics are pretty forgiving so most things can be undone/redone even on Iron Man, with about 9s load times.Amazing visuals, runs smooth as butter. Interpreting the world through the environment design was infinitely more enjoyable than following along with the characters and their story. The direction and flow of miasma, and the path of destruction along with whatever was caught in it had my imagination going. A variety of light or crude humor in there too. A spectacular job was done here, and a shame not too many will probably appreciate it or care.Voice acting was refreshing for the most part but... after having beaten the game I have to say that the characters and their story really falls apart in the 3rd (Final) act. Everything felt rushed and had no impact, and what occurs felt nonsensical mostly, very much like a placeholder. I can now understand why the story doesn't get much regard, because at first while I was asking questions it was kind of interesting, and as those questions got answered, suddenly less so. But at the same time, while the world is fascinating, our actual story in it felt out of place... and reminded me a lot of Conker's Bad Fur day. Take Mayor Mason, for instance, clearly a parody of a John McCain type when regarding how he's talked about... sounds exaggerated, then you meet him and realise he's literally a head in a jar. Mason Jar. Also, goes full Futurama Nixon. Funny, if we don't take it too seriously... but the ending was lame in so many ways. Would've preferred a derailing into a series of popular movies.This game seems underrated.
