_childDocuments_.review: 3 hours in, I'm starting to like that Brobot.Another turn based tactical RPG I can sink my teeth in for the next 20 hours.Still not a fan of BS RNG though...EDIT: I was going to edit this review after I at least beat this game but now I just... don't fuggin care anymore.I can't recommend this game, they prioritize more on teh purdy graphics over everything else, like optimization. Granted, I will take the L for trying to run this game with my low spec PC and MY GOD, even on the lowest graphical settings, the game runs like molasses.Yeah, I can give the devs credit for the world design but that's about it. The story, as interesting as it is, will not leave a strong impression on me after I beat this game (and I will). Thus giving me no incentive on playing this game again afterwards.In short, this game has a VERY LOW replay value.Combat system was brilliantly thought out but the characters I am given to work with did not click with me for the first 10 hours. _childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of DNA from Mutant Year Zero, and I really enjoyed that. They both fall prey to one of the same mechanical problems, in that you really need to be stealth killing enemies to bring the fights down to manageable levels. so playing stealth archer is kind of necessary at least in the early game. I found I did a lot of save scumming to make sure the stealth went the way I wanted it to, which isn't great. However, I love the world design, most of the character design is really good too. I enjoyed that this wasn't as deeply complicated as some of the other turn based combat games out there. I also enjoyed how the threats your facing in the game evolve. At first I thought I would be dealing with the games initial antagonists for the whole game, but then you take on a mission to put them behind you and that actually happens. Its a nice flourish that those enemies really were a regional threat you were faced with that were separate from the big bad of the story. I encountered two bugs throughout my play and one crash that didnt happen a second time. occasionally one of the late game companions fires his weapon without any sound effect and then the attack resolved at the end of the turn.

_childDocuments_.review: It's in the same style as their earlier game Mutant Year Zero: Road to Eden.Though it was less polished this time, had it crash a few times and journal entries not registering (was missing Tutorials and one enemy, the enemy i restarted until it registered, only noticed as i liked reading the entries after fights)I found Mutant to be more fun in a puzzle kind of way, missing a silent weapon this time (max of 2) made encounters harder to prep and more reliant on RNG, positioning also affected crits less so had to restart fights until i got the right outcome or the whole map would get alerted -> Death.Still fun though but some really questionable decisions, skills cooldown compared to Mutant where they lowered on kills is now tied to rounds of battle, so assassinating enemies with silent weapons no longer help get skills back thus the "best" way to prepare for a tough encounter is simple run away from a smaller one until cooldowns are over -> tedious compared to Mutant.Some fights are Ambushes, which would be fine if they didn't get a cheapshot in and kill one or even two characters which more or less demands a restart, if they just got into defensive positions it would be more fair as they also outnumber you.The story was fine enough but the way it was worded was mostly funny, reminded me of a comedy sketch "The neutrinos are Angry!" but here it was Miasma instead that was angry.They nerfed some stuff in a dumb way ex a late game weapon got it's stats lowered but didn't change it's cost compared to the next best option so you got 1 more shot and a little more crit for almost double the price, really should have lowered the cost as well a bit.But asides from the small annoyance it was a fun ride and greatly recommended if you like tactical puzzle games, though might want to try Mutant first as it's the older one and probably on a better discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: All the good stuff from Mutant Year Zero developers. Solid voice acting reflecting each character's (even the NPCs) personality and nuances. Variations of weapon mechanics and enemy dynamics. Hard to believe such an excellent game for this price.A very intense ride among 3 comrades who have to survive through it all. 4 if I am added :)
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I dunno how to say this. I have very mixed feelings about this game. On one side the story is really good an kept me playing. _childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Fun gameplay if you enjoy turn based tactical games with rpg elements. It's similar to Wasteland.Polished game - didn't encounter any bugs. Cover doesn't work for you, though - it only works for enemies. At full cover, hit chance should only be 20% unless flanked, yet enemies hit with 80% accuracy. If this is intended, then they do a poor job of explaining the cover mechanics.Terrible story. Terrible characters. Laughable dialogue. Feels like it was written by a child.I enjoyed Mutant Year Zero much more than this game, but this game is still not bad. I recommend if on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Mutant Year Zero is the GOAT for me. I got all them vibes with Miasma Chronicles as well.  I love the game design.  Too many games think throwing lots of loot at you is a good thing.  The bearded Ladies games are the opposite.  Just like in Mutant Year Zero (I play on hard & full tactical) things are scarce.  When you find a new gun it feels like a real reward.  When youre desperate to heal & you find a medkit its a mini fist pump.  When you level up it feels worthwhile.  I absolute love it & not many games hold my attention.Not all good though.  Half cover never seems to work & ive lost count of how many times the game crashed on my steam deck & each time I had to hard reset the console.In summary though this game is so enjoyable & its up there with Mutant Year Zero.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I like games like X-Com, Jagged Appliance and all the other sqaud based tactical games.I liked this game, pushed all my buttons and the style and levels are nice.Combat is great ... as always it get's a bit bored once you have the good stuff and the correct skills. _childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I First read about Miasma Chronicles about a year ago, and decided to wait for a sale, unsure of the entertainment value. Too many games have collected my money undeservedly, and as such I air on the side of caution. The price dropped to 20 bucks and I started playing, it was when I took a small break and realized it was morning already, this game is truly epic. _childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely deserves a neutral rating. But i decided to keep it a thumbs up.Another potentially great game, "consolified" and became mediocre. People always say why are you hating the consoles? Just play it on your favourite platform, it is available on PC too right? Well guess what, in order to make it playable on consoles, devs usually reinvent the wheel, try to find a control scheme that is applicable to gamepads. And ruin basic controls in the meantime. This is one of those games.If you are planning to play this game via keyboard and mouse beware:You move with WASD out of combat, i'm ok with that, nice change even. You can use your mouse to move in combat that's good. BUT you need to press 3 to 4 keys in order to take an action. Which hinders the games flow. So you want to shoot an enemy? You first need to go into shooting mode by pressing 2. Because by default you are on move mode. Then cycle through the visible enemies with Q and E just to find the right target. Press spacebar to execute the shooting. Yeah, not ideal. I highly recommend using a multibutton gaming mouse and assign some keys to those extra keys. It becomes playable.Graphics (apart from the overused sharpening effect), effects, world building, voice acting, all very good. FSR is unusable.Story is ok, it grows on you. RPG elements are very shallow, game practically wants you to play stealth. Which extremely fun.You cannot toggle UI elements with the same key which i find FRUSTRATING in any game. You press M for the map f.e, but need to hit Esc to get back in the game. This lack of feature needs to die, come on it's 2024...Cover system is a complete mess and needs rework. If you are expecting an xcom level cover system here, you are going to be dissapointed.There is no healing out of combat without using any medkits (except for leveling up) which is kinda rare. This is not a good design and can make you stuck somewhere, if you are not careful and plan ahead.I recommend getting it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: If you are hesitating - to buy or not to buy, let me tell you hesitate no more, because this is masterpiece of a game. I bought Mutant year zero + expansion and corruption 2029 liked them both very much, but miasma chronicles is even better. It has better story, looks beautiful, you can upgrade your characters in a great ways and every character has rage (similar to adrenaline) where you deal more damage when its full and some characters have energy (similar to mana) and they can cast really cool spells besides shooting their guns. The only problem i see with this game is that after you beat the story it ends completely. There is zero replayability other than start completely new game which is a real shame. They could easily prolong gameplay by just adding tons of enemies in all zones again so that we could enjoy combat fully geared for many more hours.Overall really great game and for me its 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Overwhelmingly Positive:Only about half way through, but the story is fleshed out, the world is interesting, the loot is well distributed, the characters are diverse and voiced well. _childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a lot of fun if you spend a bit of time learning the mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved the game play and story. During the 38 hour play through (finished all side quests) the game's story kept me interested and engaged. _childDocuments_.review: While I was initially concerned Miasma would be plagued by difficult combat approaches (requiring a lot of stealth and positioning) and often dull discoveries like Mutant Year Zero, I was pretty quickly proved wrong. The powers and abilities introduced after the first few hours add lots of different ways to approach combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Started out fine but encountered more and more bugs the more I progress, almost wanted to drop the game but was already invested so finished it in the end. I guess I expected this game to be 100% turn-based strategy but no, it involves stealthing and taking down lower hp mobs which are not in range of others or distracting them before u finally engage the rest which takes alot of time tbh so do take note on this if you are looking to play this gameList contains spoilers, read at ur own accord. Pros:-Nice graphics, was amazed-Music was nice and fits the environment-Has quest tracker and pathing-Plenty of EXP to help you hit max level, also lots of side quests with their own stories-Level recommendation is stated for the area so I know if I can handle the mobs-Game pauses when you alt tab even for cut scenes-Lots of weapon choices & free skill reset to customise build freely-Can teleport to any map from anywhere-Dialogues get played as you travel nearer to them which are related to the current story progress instead of random stuffs-Lots of throwables to utilise during fights-Able to buy back whatever you sell to NPC, though at higher cost-Puzzles to get those weapon crates were challengingCons:-Camera view is fixed, cant zoom in or out nor turn/rotate left and right, only could use WASD to move screen to look around, which kinda feels restrictive-No mini map or marker to show where I am, spent quite some time navigating towns due to this-Backtracking with no way to mark the map/area and I had to teleport to every area to find as the area requires much higher levels to attempt, by that time I don't remember clearly wheres the location anymore-Only 2 stealth weapons given the whole game, and they are only tier 2 so damage is limited and you need to land critical hits on both weapons to take down mob stealthily in some cases-No loadouts, so forced to equip the above mentioned 2 stealth weapons & equip them with attachments before every fight which at one point I just gave up and used them as part of my main setup as I am not gonna keep unequipping attachments every fight-Failing stealth kills is very punishing that you feel like saving before every attempt to kill to not miss the for example 90% shot to hit + 50% critical chance, which feels necessary or most of time you will just fail the fight due poor positioning from just trying to stealth kill and not in a position to engage in a all round fight-Miss-able side quests if you don't travel back to old maps, some which are nice rewards though not necessary-Story felt ok at the start then quickly went downhill, then had some nice parts but the ending was bad imo so overall was below average for me-Just when I thought I am gonna have a nice final boss fight with actual lots of hp & mechanics, but nope just spawn lots of mobs which I just one shot everything with the Alpha Editor's Miasma skill-Lack of indicators like: Miasma Barrel skill doesnt show the AOE before planting it, no weapon range indicator before ambush, number of enemies on screen and in range if engaged-Plastics aka the currency feels lacking as you only can get a limited amount throughout the game, farming Arena is possible but I don't feel its worth the effort and time-Limited to 3 characters in your team & fights although you have more, weird but I guess thats how they do balancing but I ended up not using the others, only during the final fight when forced toBugs I Encountered:-Alt tabbing breaks the sound effect of the game, had to alt tab a few times for it to be fixed, sometimes it comes back after awhile-Characters were dropping into the ground and unable to move, encountered this a few times and had to re-load saved files.-Characters getting stuck on debris or rocks on the ground and unable to move, encountered this a few times but managed to solve but running far away and it auto teleports over. Was annoying as once I was hiding from enemy and this happened so I had to re-load saved file as being spotted.-Enemy moving over to attack but got stuck in animation and did not attack and nothing could be done and had to re--load saved file and restart the whole fight-Cover do not work most of the time for yourself but works for enemies, only had a couple of missing through the whole game whereas the enemy always gets the high miss chance-Cut scenes animations were scuffed for my playthrough not sure if bugged or its just this way, one good example is during breaking wall part i think there was suppose to be a beam effect but there was nothing on my screen so i just watched Elvis raise his hand to the wall with nothing coming out-When enemies are knock downed, I have seen my character shooting the air instead of at the enemy when the screen zooms in for the animation-Not sure if this is a bug or intended, I split my team to prepare for ambush by positioning them nicely but realised that I was not in range after I enter amubsh so I proceed to turn off ambush but my team decides to run back to my main character and I have to reposition them again, annoying af as I had to keep doing this just to check if I am in range to ambush properly-During the Arena fight for my main story progress, I got kicked out of the Arena because a cut scene got played and was teleported out before I could loot any of the Plastics, there were plenty and you can't even go back to loot as the path was blocked intentionally, not sure if intended or not. _childDocuments_.review: Miasma Chronicles is an underrated gem. The graphics are visually amazing and the level design is excellent. I love that there are adventure / exploration sections in between combat encounters- it helps with immersion and it allows you to explore the world and learn about it at your own pace. The turn-based  feels solid so far and challenging (I am playing at 'Normal' difficulty level). I have only played the game a few hours, but I would have appreciated the opportunity to complete some missions avoiding combat and using a stealth-only approach instead (maybe there are going to be more opportunities for that in the future though, I still don't know).The UI design is top-notch, elegant and informative - I am really enjoying learning about the game world by reading through the  various pieces of journals, character and items descriptions, etc. I am playing Miasma Chronicles with an Xbox controller and I found that it takes a little while to get used to all the different controls as they are mapped on the controller. But this is probably due to the fact there are so many options (both in and out of combat). The weakest part of the game in my opinion is  that feels simplistic and cheesy. I appreciated that most dialogue has got , that's a great added value to the game - though the voice acting can often be as cheesy as the dialogue.Level design does a great job of "show, don't tell" when it comes to the world's story.Generally speaking a more adult approach to story-telling would have really lifted this game to the rank of masterpiece. But I appreciate that maybe the developers were catering for a (much?) younger demographic than mine (I am an old geezer!).All in all I am really loving this game, I find it engaging and relaxing, as I can enjoy it at the pace I choose to.It is evident that the devs poured a lot of passion and attention to details into this game, so kudos to them.If you like visual adventures and turn-based combat, Miasma Chronicles is a definite must-have.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a casual gamer looking for an immersive tactical gaming experience, Miasma Chronicles is a good pick up. The post-apocalyptic world setting is beautifully crafted. The character designs look great with excellent voice acting. The gameplay itself is satisfying specially when your hits connect. I wish the game was twice as long with more side quests, outfits and weapons to collect. Although the base game has a pretty decent amount. However I found the in-game credits to be lacking, so I would advice using the in-game mod that steals plastics from enemy units. Overall fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Not too complicated, just an enjoyable game. Beautiful maps, fun story and setting. So many rpgs have super complicated character build and leveling systems, nothing wrong with that, but i gotta admit i like a system that's a little more streamlined, something along the lines of Xcom2 where the depth isn't so much in the character builds but in the combat/gameplay itself, ♥♥♥♥ i hope i'm actually making some sorta sense here.Absolutely loved this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Miasma Chronicles is a strong successor to the developer's previous game, Mutant Year Zero. It's a story-driven, post-apocalyptic sci-fi turn-based tactics game with RPG elements and an emphasis on stealth. The gameplay loop revolves around stealthily dispatching enemies before going loud and committing to fights. Once you're committed, it's a pretty standard XCOM-like affair, though you do have some cool powers and abilities to spice things up. There's enough enemy variety and challenging encounter layouts to keep the combat engaging through the game's 30-40 hour duration (if you go for 100% completion on the higher difficulty). Outside of combat, you'll spend most of your time exploring the levels, looking for loot and talking to NPCs. The writing is generally solid, with interesting lore and characters, though the dialogue can be awkward at times. The graphics are quite nice, with highly detailed environments, atmospheric lighting and some lovely vistas.All in all, I had a lot of fun with Miasma Chronicles. I'm not sure why it got a worse reception than Mutant Year Zero, as Miasma seems like an improvement in most regards. Maybe people are getting tired of XCOM-style combat?
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this adventure. It has involving story, great XCOM-like combat, interesting characters and really cool visual direction and style. There are few things I didn't like, f.x. dialogues and character interaction as well (and especially) the Diggs character, but other than that - all in all pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played either of the Bearded Ladies previous release. Corruption 2099 (not on steam, why?) or the more successful mutant year zero, you should be instantly comfortable with the game mechanics as they are but for a few changes the same.Of those three games Miasma Chronicles seems to full in the middle. it doesn't have the charm of Zero and feels for all the world more closely aligned to 2029. It's a solid enough game with decent mechanics and solid story. My main issue with the game is the wildly uneven difficulty through out the game. Even on normal it throws a ridiculous amount of enemies at you in basic encounters forcing each encounter to feel like an exercise in frustration. Weapons don't really get that much better as the game progresses and i never felt even when at max level i was much stronger than at the start, I merely had more tricks to use.I would love to give the game a neutral rating here as there is fun to be had but as it's either good or bad I need to recommend the game on sale knowing it might frustrate.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to Mutant Year Zero.  I do wish they had tied MYZ into the lore/world-building of this game since there are mutants, but know knows, maybe DLC?The good: 1. Turn-based combat has been improved and is generally much smoother.2. There are a bunch of new tactical options, but the general map clearing strategy is the same: Sneak, Snipe, Ambush whatever remains.3. The characters are interesting and generally well developed. VA is well done, even for random npc chatter, which I enjoyed running around discovering after each major event happened.4. The maps were very well done, with unique zone specific flavor, and are believably post apocalyptic.The meh: 1. Most later enemies are immune to half your tactical options. Not very fun to customize skills and weapons just to have them be useless a couple maps later.2. Unique weapons are great, but most of them are found too late, and/or they are outclassed by late game 'generic' weapons because most unqiues are tier 2 or lower and their damage is sub-par.The bad:1. The story does a good job feeding you tidbits and slowly laying out more of the puzzle that is the MC's story. UNTIL it nosedives and the MC pulls a 180 and becomes the last boss basically. If this event was going to happen, it should have been before the final stretch, when you basically lose the MC as a playable character.  That way he gets some sort of redemption instead of the truncated/forced ending we got.

_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Very similar to their prior game; for a value proposition you have to ask if it is worth 50% more.  For some of you the answer is probably no. The combat is very fun, several paths to success, many more to failure.  For most of us picking the enemy apart before combat is important.  Like their prior title, each character has things it specialize in; there is enough flexibility where your sniper doesn't have to be a sniper but on the same note you can not field three brawlers.There is enough variety in enemies to make it interesting. AI is decently done, some flank, some charge, they'll use specials.I have had several bugs, none have been game breaking but it can get irritating. Your mileage may very.  UI/inventory bug where you have to get in and out, in and out, in and out, to modify weapons.  Once I had the overlay stay on after the start of combat where I couldn't hit E to close the pop up or control the action, had to kill the game.I've just about rage quit due to follow/group.  Game is designed for you to scout the field and pick your point of attack.  So many times I test line of sight, decide to keep looking and everybody magically groups even though I had them ungrouped and hidden elsewhere.  Not really a big deal from game play but annoying time waster.Elevation is 1/2 baked.  One weapon can bounce shots but it can not do elevation change; it'l bounce of the empty air if you are on top of something like the second level of a building.  There are talents for boost if you have elevation but no penalties for shooting up.  Being up high isn't that great most of the time benefits are limited, coverage is often missing and there are no penalties for them attack you up.Speaking of coverage.  It might as well not exist.  Deductive reasoning, if full coverage gives 65% reduction and I get hit 4 out 5 times in full coverage then their base change to attack needs to be 145%.  I know it is fun to complain about RNG; this is literal, my experience is they very rarely miss.  I assume it modifies the AI so they don't try shots quite as often as if you weren't in coverage so coverage isn't quite useless but yea, expect to be hit and position accordingly.  Kind of the opposite problem from Xcom where 99% chance to hit would miss.To be fair, a 55% change to crit seems to be a functional 80% so it goes your way sometimes.  Frankly being able to pick off enemies quicker probably works in your favor as your always outnumbered.  If there are modifiers being applied to make this make sense it isn't displayed. The mechanic of crit + kill restores 1 AP is inconsistent.  I get it without killing sometimes and don't always get it when I do make a kill.  Despite all these minor bugs, still fun. _childDocuments_.review: I was very much looking forward to this, after mostly liking Mutant Year Zero. Sadly, so many of the little annoyances found in that game are present here, save only a select few(you don't have to return to a hub to change your weapon attachments anymore, cutscenes and subtitles are overall improved). I really want to finish it, but I don't think I can bring myself to keep pushing. The game is getting worse as it goes on, and the mostly-fine tactics combat isn't enough to keep me going. There are so many small game design choices that irk me, but listing them all out right here would just feel like a waste, so I'll save you the trouble. I also, just, fundamentally can't wrap my head around the sniper rifle having less range than your standard assault rifles. The percent chance to hit being tied to how far away you are, closer=less accurate, is fine, but I sincerely don't understand the benefit of having a sniper in the game if you can rarely take advantage of high ground, since you'll be too far away from the action! I just played Showgunners, another tactics RPG that came out this year, and maaaan that sniper felt so much better. It did a lot of things better, actually, but I will give credit to Miasma for 1 cool idea: the overwatch in this game is very fun. It being a narrow field of vision but allowing for multiple shots to be fired is neat!

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a 7/10. I would probably rank it higher if I wasn't comparing it to the previous game from the same developer, Mutant: Year Zero. Overall, I feel like this game was built to protect the player from ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up too badly, which unfortunately takes away a lot of the freedom that made the previous game enjoyable. I think this game had a ton of potential, but it suffered from uneven pacing and a predictable plot. Still, it is a pretty tightly designed game that does what it wants to do well, and doesn't overstay it's welcome.One other thing that bothered me on a meta level is that this game relies on the same basic joke that M:YZ relied on, which is that characters in a post-apocalyptic setting misinterpret artifacts from pre-apocalypse times. It's basically Ariel from the Little Mermaid thinking a fork is a hair comb, and then that same joke over and over for an entire game. Sometimes it's really funny, like the line about the founding fathers fighting dinosaurs, but it gets old after a while. Normally this wouldn't be a big deal, but a narrative game like this sinks or swims based on the humor and storytelling, so I think it's relevant. If you never played M:YZ, I can also see this humor staying fresh longer.  Pros: -The character writing is solid and funny. The characters have unique personalities and good dialogue, and the voice acting is quite believable. I wish the Mayor got more screentime; the main character is kind of bland.-The art and environments are great, although I think there could have been more variety in locations.-I like the stealth gameplay and exploration. However, engaging with this mechanic forces you into certain builds. Enemy AI is very basic and enemies have very predictable patrols. Would have liked to see more distraction options, stealth powers, ways to pit enemies against each other, etc.-The turn-based combat is solid with some unique interpretations of familiar firearms that incentivize you to reposition enemies. Cons:-I didn't like the exploration as much as M:YZ. In that game, most of the areas in the game weren't locked. You could progress through a bunch of sections, stealthing around enemies with much higher levels than you, and gather powerful resources that would help you a lot. It felt like you weren't "supposed" to do this, which made it feel like you were getting away with something, which was a lot of fun and made the stealth mechanic seem worthwhile. Abusing Dux's flight ability to traverse the map was also a ton of fun in that game.The exploration in this game is more parceled out by progressing the story. Areas are locked until you reach the appropriate story milestone. Strong enemies that are higher levels than you hang out in their little corners of the map and you don't have to engage with them until you're ready. There are never really enemies that are so powerful that you have to go our of your way to avoid them (except for one memorable encounter in the swamp - that was great!). There are a few strong enemies at the very end of the game, but they are just reskins of enemies you've seen already, with too much HP. Not really scary in the same way the big-ass, fast robots were in M:YZ-Less party variety. The main character Elvis and his robot brother Diggs are always in the party. Eventually, you can put one more person in the party. For me, I literally played through the entire game with the sniper character as my third party member because she had the best stealth ambush abilities, which are basically required if you want to use the stealth mechanic at all and pick off enemies to make fights more manageable. M:YZ let you have any combination of 3 characters in your party - I think there were 5 or 6 in total, which allowed for more experimentation and varied playstyles.-The actual plot structure. I think the characters were written well, but the plot itself is so generic. They could have taken this in a lot of different directions, and it's just another "you are the chosen one and you have to save humanity." A little third-act twist doesn't change the basic structure. The main character abruptly does something stupid, and then changes his mind for no real reason a short while later. M:YZ had such a cool plot! You were a weird duck or pig monster, and you were trying to figure out why. That was an engaging mystery. -The pacing - It feels like you spend half of the game in the tutorial area fighting frogs. By the time the world opens up and you start getting some lore, the game is almost over. -The magic system. Spells cost too much MP (electricity) to execute. For most of the game, you can only use maybe one or two spells before you have to use a consumable, or skip a bunch of combat turns to recharge your batteries. This led me to hoard battery consumables in case I needed them later. The spells are also just weird. You can pick up an enemy and throw it at another enemy, but this doesn't do any damage unless you equip a modification chip that inflicts a status effect, but makes the spell cost more to cast. You get a spell that allows you to mind-control an enemy, but by the time you get it, all of the enemies in the game are immune to the spell? You get a teleport spell, that is like the pick up an enemy spell, but cheaper. The only spells I used for the entire game were the ones that let you reposition enemies, which I used in conjunction with the spell to summon an explosive barrel. Summon barrel, move enemy next to barrel, shoot enemy and barrel with a shotgun. Worked in every fight in the entire game. - The last fight of the game - you have to crowd control a powerful enemy while fighting a bunch of other enemies. If you do not, this enemy will stunlock 1 or 2 of your three characters every turn. Don't have any of the 3 abilities that let you crowd control this enemy? I guess it's time to reload and respec your characters (which is free, thankfully). The powerful enemy cannot be killed, but the game doesn't tell you this. The enemy just returns to full HP after every time you attack it. I honestly could not tell if this was a bug or not the first time it happened. Just annoying and dumb.-Bha Madi - She was just insufferable. Shut up, Bha Madi,

_childDocuments_.review: Miasma Chronicles is a game that offers a great mix of turn-based strategy combat and stealth mechanics. The game presents a good story with characters that are likable, and the villains are interesting as well. The gameplay mechanics successfully combine strategic decision-making and stealth tactics, making it enjoyable and engaging.However, there are a few things i Didn't like as much. One major drawback is that players can only have three squad members at a time. This anoying since you I ended up liking Jade, and didn't want to replace her with any other squadmembers. Additionally, the controls in the game can be convoluted and may take some time to get used to, which can detract from the overall experience.Another downside to Miasma Chronicles is the difficulty in acquiring resources in the game. Since there isn't much available in the wilderness, players may find it challenging to gather the necessary resources, such as grenades, healing items and powercells. The game only provides two vendors, which further restricts the availability of resources and potentially limits the options available to players.Overall, Miasma Chronicles delivers an enjoyable experience with its engaging combat and stealth mechanics. The story and characters are well-developed, and the variety of villain types adds depth to the gameplay. However, the limitations on squad members and the challenging resource acquisition may be disappointing to some players. Despite these drawbacks, Miasma Chronicles is still worth playing for fans of turn-based strategy and stealth genres.I give this game an 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: While I have not played Mutant Year Zero (same studio), I do have a fair bit of experience with the genre. This is a turn-based tactical action game with a heavy emphasis on story and visual presentation. Overall, it's a solid game I'd recommend it to fans of the genre. My time here was well spent and the main critique would be that the "normal" difficulty needs balancing (I found myself switching to narrative at times). People considering this title should note that this is a game that centres around stealthily eliminating enemies BEFORE entering into turn-based tactical battles - I had more fun when I understood this.+ Stunning visuals for the genre - gritty dystopian settings and interesting character designs+ Strong effort into world-building and a cast of characters (relative to others in the genre)+ A good range of weapons and powers that allow for a range of tactical options (the latter hampered energy being scarce)+ Great soundtrack+ Versatile controls - very easy to use on a controller + Flawless ultra-wide support+ Rock solid stability and great framerates (100+ on a 4080 @ 3440 x 1440)-  The effort into the story is terrific but the actual story could be more compelling and the characters more nuanced                  ( a lot of tropes and tonal issues)-  Difficulty needs balancing, the use of Miasma powers is hampered by energy cells being scarce and expensive early on.-  Shader compilation issues (not traversal for me) when certain effects are used for the first time e.g. miasma powers. Probably needs precompilation like most UE4 games.Would love to see what this studio puts out next! There's a solid foundation here.

Overall a good game, you know exactly what to expect if you played Mutant Year Zero. Very simple mechanics for new players. Recommended! Just do not expect much in terms of character development, plot twists, RPG elements etc... it is a very uncomplicated game :).
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy games with tactical turn based combat, something that is not very common today, so Miasma Chronicles really fills that void. The game has a unique story and a feel similar to the old Fallout or the newer Wastelands games. The story is interesting and the combat is challenging. It is sometimes a bit hard, but I prefer that to super simple games and I know that they have lowered the normal difficulty a bit now (I play on Extreme). What I feel is unique with the game compared to similar games it that it includes puzzle elements, both in and out of combat. For instance you can be failing a fight over and over again, until you finally realize there is a way to get the enemies to get close to an explosive barrel and hurt them all with a well timed explosion. There is also ways of separating the enemies and taking them out silently before the actual fight and that way make it easier. Really recommend this game if you like this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Game, and good sequel to their last game M:YZ. Didn't see any bugs from day one and on, so already a better game than most that have been released this year. Quite a few changes to overall game play and mechanics that make it more challenging than M:YZ such as not being able to use whatever ability regardless of action points or pretty much having to maneuver your way around enemies or fight them because silent weapons are near non existent. Not as good of a story but not bad either still very much an enjoyable game with little easter eggs through out from the previous installment. Overall give this game an 8.0/10. Take this review as you will I am biased since I am a huge fan of their first game and was awaiting for any future game from them.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I liked the game: 7/10But there were too many things that almost made me to stop playing. Constant glitches with enemies spawning in places where I can't shoot them, heros getting stuck, etc.The elements that supposedly have to enrich the story (ancient robots, terminals, etc.) take too much time to operate and to many clicks to get through. There wasn't single one that I was able to sit through without skipping parts of text.The idea is great (even if the storyline is a bit predictable), but the UI could have been much better.If you are ready to suffer a bit, I definitely recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting evolution of what these same developers did in Mutant: Year Zero. I found myself quite immersed in the "guerrilla tactics" gameplay loop. It felt like I was exploring and surviving a true post apocalypse by tooling and re-tooling weapons, gear and abilities to overcome different combat challenges. Stealth is king however, so don't expect a traditional Xcom experience from this one. Going in guns blazing in the early game will end in a quick game over. Story and presentation is marginally improved from their previous work, but there is enough here to keep you interested. I'm keen to see where this franchise goes in potential DLC's or sequels. Has the potential to be something special, if you don't mind a few rough edges. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like it and played it to the end but, overall, disappointed. I loved their MYZ but this feels like a step backwards. Limited skills with very long cooldowns that don't refresh between combats means you have to constantly reconfigure your character after every battle to select different skills not on cooldown. The Miasma powers are the same. You have so little energy you can only use 1-2 in an entire battle w/o adjusting your entire build (and taking multiple skip rounds to regen energy). And you have have 1-2 slots for skills so give you little flexibility DURING combat. If you don't preselect the right weapons, skills, powers BEFORE a combat you are often screwed and reloading. Feels like I spent half my time reconfiguring and reloading which was no fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with a congratulation to the graphic team.The game in 4K looks extremely good!I have a buffy config and the visual shines - no optimization issue - It runs well.Environment/Atmosphere of the game is also top notch.artistic direction department was also performing a good job.Game-play wise it is a standard TPT with an emphasis on ambush mechanism.You choose when you engage most of the time.There is enough variety between miasma power/different weapons to spend a nice time on the tactical map.No real customization, Builds per character are not really diversified but let's say they all have their uses.For veteran of the genre the game is not that difficult and i will recommend to go for the higher difficulty level.Story wise is okish - the teen vibe is not really a material i appreciate(a touch of global warming propaganda but well modern game what can we do...) however let's say the darkness of the world compensates.Did not reinvent the wheel but miasma brings a nice touch to the story.I have never played Mutant Year zero so cannot compare but i was positively surprise by the game and the high standard at a graphical stand point.Recommended - In the same vein as King Arthur Knight tale's somehow.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable game. Not overly long, and doesn't overstay it's welcome.Great characters, fairly interesting and unique story, and good gameplay overall. Similar to a mix of an RPG and Xcom like tactical fighting. Not overly in depth, but just enough to keep character and story progression rolling along.The only "negatives" are that I had a few crashes here and there at 4k max settings. You're also nearly required to stealth kill as many enemies as possible before engaging into a large battle. This is fine, but silent weapons that don't alert other enemies are incredibly few and far between. Stealth attacks also aren't guaranteed, which means you'll simply be saving and reloading to get the desired outcome.Beyond that, no complaints!! Well worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable tactical game with a cast of entertaining characters, though it does have rough points with some encounters being much tougher than they should with what you can reasonably prepare for and despite giving you a lot of tools to encourage you to use miasma powers you will rarely have the energy to actually use them in combat for a good chunk of the game.One noteworthy issue I personally experienced was that stairs gave issues with characters not being able to traverse them in combat occasionally and one instance where a character started combat on stairs and could not be moved for the entirety of the encounter.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Same developers that made "Mutant year zero - road to Eden". And If I compare those titles I have to say that Miasma Chronicles is slightly better in many ways but not on all levels. One thing remains though - the bugs! My game has crashed 5-6 times - occasionally freezes during death cam and whatnot. But I can live with that because Miasma is a really fun game. Interesting story so far and I got a feeling I'm in for a surprise of some sort at the end. The graphics amazing runs fairly smoothly on my pretty old computer. few fps drops here and there but nothing alarming. I've invested 74 hours so far. (*edit* finished the game.)Healing equipment, as in MYZ-Road to Eden, is scarce. The scraps you farm, especially in the beginning, go exclusively towards any means necessary to boost your squad's HP. The Cover system in Miasma Chronicles is one of the concerns I have as many other gamers have already stated: it's unbalanced. And overwatch shouldn't be a skill you need to unlock as a trait.. that is just dumb. Weapons are a waste buying because you will sooner or later loot a box containing a similar weapon anyway and since scraps do not come in huge piles you have to be careful about what you purchase. Some of the weapon- mods are useless if it's not Crit- /range-, kilowatt-, or rage-based while the two first ones are essential, and the latter I m o more situation based or optional.I recommend but I think you should wait for a sale and give the Bearded Ladies a chance to fix many of those bugs. I will most likely buy and play upcoming DLCs. 7.2 / 10 I recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This is my 1st TRPG..  Unusual play style for me.  I particularly like the lore and the multiple varied locations available to explore.  Multiple different enemies to fight that requires re-thinking tactics and weapons to use.The game lends itself to possible expansion, so there is that.Downside: -  Damn hard to find enough plastic to pay for consumables that you will burn up during firefights.  After a while fights become somewhat predictable yet remain reasonably tough.I like the fact you the player have a choice to play as easy or as hard as you like.  Stealth tactics and weapons work well until enemies become alerted to your presence, then watch out.  Choice of the right Miasma powers during battle are freakin awesome.Overall, I'm enjoying the game..  I did try a previous TRPG from this producer but simply couldn't get the hang of it at the time.  This game may help me re-visit the previous offering.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the "this game is too hard" reviews. Yes the game is hard but, if you give yourself the time to strategically plan out your attack you will find yourself achieving satisfactory victories. I'm playing on challenging (one before the hardest difficulty) full tactical so I cannot speak for those who are playing on normal but,  if I can do it so can you. Save scumming, picking off enemies, trial and error are your best friends. This is a stealth-strategy game after all. If you want something instant and brain numbing go back to fortnite. p.s Diggs is mah diggaedit :I am changing my suggestion. I cannot suggest this game right now. I was really enjoying it up to about late game. I have experienced two crashes and frequent UI bugs. One where Bha's coach buff aura will persist around the characters I cast on. It's annoying to see a HUGE yellow aura following the characters. Another game breaking bug is when I lose control of movement. Sometimes I cannot click on a square during combat. For shame. I was hyped for this game and considering uninstalling until its all patched up.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Tactical choices matter - starting with ambushing guards who wander a little too far from their groups to kill order/cover/weapon and ammo types and more. That makes it a good turn based game, in my opinion. I enjoyed Mutant Year Zero but had a hard time getting into it due to what I felt was some poor encounter designs. They have obviously learned from developing that game - Miasma Chronicles is a step up in every way. Yes, there are some things that could be improved (just a little too much scavenging required for gear and I dont like how the game approaches energy regeneration, imo), but it is a game I happily recommend.Dont go into this expecting an XCom clone. Yes, there are a few little similarities in the combat, but this game does offer a fairly unique experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: It has been far too long since we've had a decent tactical strategy that could live up to that standard set by Xcom and I can wholeheartedly say that Miasma Chronicles ticks that box with flying colors! The game, quite refreshingly, offers two levels of tactical gameplay; Full tactical (like Xcom) and a soft tactical for more forgiving gameplay. The characters and weapons have limited customisation but you'll find a comfortable set fairly quick so I don't see that as a downside. The story and characters are engaging and intriguing and develop nicely to a satisfying conclusion with just enough wiggle room left in case a sequel is made (although i doubt one will). My only criticism is that it needs some patches to better optimise the game
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best games I have played in years.Story: level of Warcraft 3 10/10Battle: 6/10 very poor battle and stealth mechanics where you have to rely on supps, such as grenades and meds... which cost way too much at the store. Basically if you wanna finish the game you will spend over 90% of your money on those... instead of buying guns or gun attachments.Sounds: 10/10Graphics: 7/10 more like something from 2015Atmosphere: 10/10Length: 30-35 hours if you do all objectives including special missions where you search for gun parts. 15-18 hours main missions only.Cost: buy it on a discount... not worth the price it is at.

_childDocuments_.review: From the creators of Mutant Year Zero, so if you played that you know what you are getting into. Pretty good game, story and world is great, tactical wise for same as Mutant Year Zero pretty basic, for any tactical fans set it for challenging and full tactical for at least a little bit of challenge.Took me 39 hours to beat the game, only had maybe 4 side quests left uncompleted. _childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is super similar to Bearded Ladies previous title; Mutant Year Zero: Road To Eden, which is a big positive for me. Haven't gotten very far, but just based off of what I've played so far it's an enjoyable experience, especially if you like figuring out how to best approach any given combat situation.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it. It's very nice to play a game that is finished and pretty much polished on day one. Sure here and there some balancing is needed, some small UI issues which are already being fixed like the ability to remap WASD but it's small fry. I didn't encounter any crash or major bugs.The story is ok and the characters are not especially interesting (it's no MYZ...) but it does the job. The art style is very pleasing.A bit expensive for the playtime and I don't think there is much replaybility but for sure others may disagree on that regard, that said my playtrough of 74hours quality gaming it's acceptable value for the expense. Looking forward to the next offering by this crowd, hopefully a sequel to MYZ with the improvements in the tactical game like in this one or a sequel to this.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it. The gameplay is mostly an improvement on Mutant Year Zero if you played their previous games. Once you get a good collection of Miasma Powers, each encounter doesn't feel like a puzzle compared to MYZ. This game has a satisfying gameplay loop combining stealth sniping with the tactical turn-based shooter combat system codified by X-Com.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game. The character development was done very well compared to most games these days. The voice acting was amazing as well. I didn't skip a single conversation or wish for things to hurry up. The Pace was great and completing all side quests will have you get maxed level right before the final fights. All the enemies felt unique and sometimes overwhelming, but with some smart stealth actions before some of the larger fights you can reduce the onslaught be a few enemies. 5 out of 5 stars for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Review of Challenging (second hardest difficulty) and 'Full tactical'. I don't know how other settings play. About me: I play a tonne of games in this genre.The game is great. There are multiple ways to take on a group, the variety in skills and weapons opens up the possibility of multiple strategies. You can refund skills at any time meaning you can swap out depending what's best for the situation (for example, enemies immune to acid? remove your acid attacks and put those points elsewhere, about to fight a horde of melee? put points into the counter-melee punch etc).I also swap weapons/mods constantly depending on what works best, for example, 80 HP enemies I'll use the +10 damage mods so that they die in one hit to the 70 base damage weapons, or for the 130 HP enemies I'll use the +20 crit damage so they die in one crit to the sniper. The game starts off difficult, but felt well tuned to me. I haven't see the game over screen once, and this is only the second game where I've never had to save scum once. I do make HEAVY use of the stealth portion of a battle though, scouting out the entire map and taking out every enemy I can, I also spend all my money on 'Bottles' (they pull enemies away from groups) after I got the silenced weapon. I haven't been in a single fight or been ambushed where I've felt 'this is impossible'. Later on, you get another silenced weapon, and things become pretty easy from there.Story-wise I've found it good enough to make me want to keep playing to find out what it's about and where it's going. Weapon variety is good with each weapon having a very unique feel and use case.One thing is: this game is not XCOM. Many of the same strategies you use there do not work here. I've found overwatch to be useless in >90% of my fights, for example, usually it's much better to take a shot. I take MANY more low% shots in this game then I ever would in XCOM, and I've never been punished for it.Later on you get more characters and it opens up the strategies even more, for example I'll use one character if I'm fighting the collectors, and a different companion for the miasma creatures/humans.TLDR: Overall the game is excellent in my opinion, different enough from XCOM to not feel like a copy but similar enough to scratch that XCOM itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 8/10Played around 30h at the time of review, around half of the game in full tactical + alpha editor.I gave it a shot since I wanted to play a Tactical turn based combat game and I must say it was a pleasant surprise to find this coming out.Recommendation: Play once or twice, I might finish it when it gets some additional balance patches.+ Quite polished for release+ Beautiful graphics, soundtrack, immersive world+ Interesting story line+ Interesting puzzlesThere are some points though that I found out could be improvedCombat mechanics:  - Distances feel wrong, there's no way to accurately know if the enemies reach you or not and if you'll reach the enemies with inventory objects, or to heal your squad member if they're apart.  - In Some encounters you get "surrounded" by enemies so if you're not prepared it can be deadly on Alpha Editor (basically you need to have played the game beforehand or always be prepared when playing the main story line).  - Height offers low tactical advantage; besides critical hits, you don't get any cover bonus and many enemies can jump at least one level, making it even a bad choice.  - Poor variety of choice: You need to get a shotgun ASAP, you need to go around doing silent kills, you need to min max your skills according to the type of enemy in the zone and your level.On world, trading, inventory, companions:  - Game economy feels wrong to me. Like in the previous game from the same developers (Mutant Year Zero), this part of the game is really not appealing. Feels like you need to run around in search for the main resource (plastic), and then you need it in high difficulty levels to buy provisions, making buying weapons hard or unlikely in the beginning, except if you grind the side quests later on & use some abilities.  -  You need to play half of the game to get to your second companion so there's not a big repertoire of team composition since the beginning and then you find the team is capped to 3 .  - Additional AP mechanic: It's quite hard to make it happen when you need it so, most likely you can never count on it. - Some dialogues are a bit lacking and dumb but overall the story is great.Alpha Editor difficulty:  - It doesn't say but it works like a 1 save Iron man mode (It only says that there are no manual saves; any miss-click can be heavily punishing.) I was expecting it would be possible to at least, roll back to the beginning of a zone.It's a game that tells a story and has fun mechanics but doesn't have a unique experience, worth a buy on sale for me, or if you're into tactical RPG's and have the money atm buy right now.Edit: The creators really show care for their product and made updates that are described above 7-> 8 / 10I'll definitely replay this at some point. It is a rich immersive world :)
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Solid gamePros: Graphics (some fps drops), UI/presentation, combat, the in game world, stealth aspectsCons: A few technical issues (crashes, glitching party members or enemies), character build diversity is limited, level spikes on side missions and such doesn't feel rightMeh:  Story is cliche (but is ok), 3 member squad means limited strategy, VERY linear game (low replayability)
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Surprising depth and very fun and unique mechanics for combat for a tactical strategy game.  If you liked Xcom you will probably like this game a lot.  I've been playing on full tactical mode on the second hardest difficulty and have been having a blast  It's a challenge with some unique and surprising mechanics that took some getting used to, but its not too hard.  You have to pick your battles and create setups that are advantageous for you.  You can completely sneak past groups of enemies, trim groups down in size by silently striking from the shadows without alerting the rest of the group - you can even create distractions to peel off individual members or simply distract them so you can sneak past.Contrary to what I'm seeing some people claim there are a lot of ways to handle situations and many different loadouts and combos that can be used including character skills, power cores, weapon mods, weapon choices, miasma abilities and squad members, besides loads of gear stored in a shared backpack that your whole squad can access during combat.  Leveling up tops off all of your characters health, so use that mechanic to your advantage.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Love the atmosphere. I've missed the possibility to choose the enemy I want to attack in a free camera instead of using Q/E, but I got used to it after a couple fights. The combat always feels challenging and needs the be thought through the whole way. The progression is a bit too linear, you always get a +10 damage weapon or a better miasma skill, could be more interesting. Overall, a great game! 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Lets first talk about the bad:- The story is pretty mediocre- Most of the playable characters are pretty uninteresting- There are some small glitches/bugs (nothing game breaking)- The game forces you to play in a certain way (don't heal after fights/need to abuse the stealth mechanic/cds persist after combat)Now for the good:- some interesting plot twists- Great turn based combat- Interesting abilities- fixes that turn based cover shooter itchOverall it is a good game. Nothing great or amazing but you get your moneys worth of content out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: i have played through the Story from start to finish and i can say that i had a genuinely good time and would recommend others pick it up.The Good.- The mechanics are fun. If you like Xcom and other games like it then you'll like this. - The stealth game-play brings a new element that made me think about how to approach every fight and who to pick off. - The characters themselves all had interesting back stories that made me want to learn more about each one. (albeit a little obvious for some).- Graphics were awesome.The bad.- The variety of weapons and abilities felt like it was lacking. - The writing fell flat at times and left me with a sense of "What the hell?".Overall it feels like there's room for improvement but the overall game was awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: To start with its hard and i would suggest u go on easy mode if u want to enjoy the game as a its quite hard on other modes and not much fun, as u get into the game its gets easier, but healer is a big issues as u don't heal after each fight, its hard to get plastic to by heals as they cost a lot as well as getting up bit, worse part of the game is not auto healing and lack of plastic for equipment, but this is such a good story and i would buy the next one. one last thing it would be nice to be able to have a better map once your in each section so u can see where u have been or where to go.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A simple yet pleasant blend of XCOM combat with free roam as seen in earlier reviews. Definitely feel the challenge of combat regardless of how prepared and geared you are, this ensures the game never feels stale or unrewarding. The plot and gameplay is a bit linear with a very strict managment of ability cooldowns and resources but I'll consider it as intentional by the devs to balance the combat(maybe some fine-tuning is needed). Exploration of the world as well as few interactions within it are satisfying to stumble upon as it leaves me curious and wanting to learn more.However, I do find myself heavily reliant on the stealth mechanic since enemy AI just overwhelm you with numbers and sheer firepower as well as some units(non-melee) having strangely high amounts of mobility that cover large distances. I'll just chalk this up as intended design to make any player re-evaluate how to approach certain situations and enemies.Edit: (UPDATE) So after progressing further into the game I am sad to be confined to a 3 man team and was looking forward to  4th or 5th  member thinking the squad grows as the plot progresses with higher stakes.  Progression of abilities feel lackluster as I find myself heavily reliant on stealth, the free and on demand refund system of skill points  helps manages abilities once im done ambushing but at the moment I find myself feeling the burnout of fumbling between ambush and hard engage perks/abilities. In it's current state this game is a 6.5~7 out of 10, personally I want to give a better rating but im not getting the impression of squad tactics or to put in another perspective its 70% stealth puzzles and 30% squad tactics.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Being a fan of the turn-based combat that X-Com brought, but looking for more of a story driven narrative, I instantly grew a liking to Miasma Chronicles.The combat is challenging even on Normal, but it's almost the perfect blend of fun with frustration at the maths, when Diggs still misses with an 89% chance of hitting...but it's those moments that make it all the more satisfying when you beat the encounter.Abilities are strong and necessary in later game, with stuns and ways to peel armour off targets being the most important. The game also rewards you for exploring, offering free weapons, items and XP gains to become much stronger. I've now finished my playthrough, but plan on revisiting for that Alpha Editor difficulty and take on the real challenge!I will say the story initially is a bit on the lacklustre side, but it clicks into gear near the end, explaining it all away with how everything is linked. I personally did enjoy the story once I had completed it all, but I can see why the slow start would be a turn off for people.Performance wise, it's been great. 1 crash throughout my whole time in-game, and very rarely any ever dips in FPS. The art is stunning, and the outfits are all worth grabbing just for their appeal alone.Honestly, Bearded Ladies and 505 smashed it out the park and I can't wait to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A good RPG with decent turn based combat, real time exploration, stealth/snipe, good basic story, intresting world/lore and almost big enough.There are two problems in my opinion:1: 30 hours  from start to finish and do/see everything is too small for a RPG. There should have been 1-2 more "areas" (14-20 maps) filled with quests and story. I simplyy expect more from this kind of game.2: The main story is over arching story is good and worth exploring, BUT the writing is truly terrible. Main character are written like an idiot, not understanding basic things in life (no spoilers so can not say more). There is a scene close to the end that was so completely out of character and against all the game try to tell you I had to turn the game off and rest for too days before coming back. It feels like the writers have not read a good book, seen a good movie or tv show. Just feed up with trash and thinking "oh that is how people talk and behave".The game is still worth playing, but there will be moments where all logic goes out the window and you go "WTF happened!?".
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of xcom type games, specifically Mutant Year Zero. Then you will love this. There are alot of complaints going around about ability cooldowns not being what people want and characters all having the same skills. The first complaint is an opinion, I personally have had no problem with cooldowns at all, I am in the final stretch on Alpha Editor/Full Tactical and have had zero problems with cooldowns or game mechanics. If something is on cooldown you need to be more "tactical" about when you choose to use the abilities, do not spam abilities.The lack of variety is also partially invalid as each character has things they excel at better than others, but I do agree with it as well in that they could be more unique. There are scopes and weapons that have increased crit damage and crit% against different racial types of enemies. This fantastic and very useful late game when you are being outnumbered 20 v 3 sometimes. Usually, if you utilized the stealth mechanic you can whittle down those numbers to something a little more manageable before kickin off a big fight, but sometimes luck is not in your favor on that. Where I think the devs could have expanded variety would be to have added 2 more skill trees to each character. One skill tree being minor racial bonuses. The second being major racial bonuses. Racial bonuses would apply an increase in crit % or crit damage or base damage against racial enemy types. This mechanic already exists on some guns and scopes, adding it in for characters as well would allow for better specialization as well as an incentive to use late game characters. I will not name names due to spoilers but there are characters that you will get 15 or 20 hours into what is essentially a 25-30 hours game. By the time you get those characters I have already devised working strategies around the characters I have, to change it would be an unnecessary risk for me when in combat so those other character will likely never be used. The inclusion of racial bonuses as a skill tree for each character would guarantee I would use some characters in certain fights while not in others. That said that is my only real critique, that and for the love of god why are empty glass bottles both expensive and rare? Seriously, only 12 can be bought in the whole game and they sell for 200 plastic each, which totals 2400 plastic... thats ALOT of money to drop on a single use distraction item. Doubly so when you need to min/max crit%, crit damage, and damage output to have a prayer of the silent shot dropping your targets to make the distraction worth anything at all. Awesome game, I personally love it and give it 9/10, but for gods sake, make the glass bottles more plentiful and cheaper!
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: love their first game. this one is too difficult i think. im not a total tactical noob and beat their first game and xcom just fine on normal difficulty. this however, man you get flooded with enemies and the usually 2 shot you. either the game is too hard or it does a really bad job at guiding you into the gameplay mechanics of it.if you're into hardcore tactics and wanna tweak at the perfect difficulty then this might be for you.graphics are top notch. gameplay should have been more user friendly.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a lot of fun with this game as well as the previous ones. Everything works perfectly and looks amazing on my oled 55 in 4K I'm using xbox controller so no issues here. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game so far, really only 1 complaint that I have is with the combat. The assault rifles are very under whelming (not sure about other weapons). The combat graphics and sound don't give any impact to the weapon. You hear a weak pew pew sound (like an old 80s / 90s sound effect) and the visual is just like a floating ember floating towards the enemy. Anyways other than that, the graphics are very nice the art style is great. The story so far is pretty interesting. I really like some of the themes for the maps. In addition some of the powers you eventually get are pretty cool. I do hope that there are more varieties of enemies to fight. In the 2.5 hours I've played its all been the same race (mutant frogs). Also Im not sure about replay ability. If money's tight you might want to wait till its on sale.  Pretty solid game so far 7 out of 10. I'll update my review as I go deeper.

_childDocuments_.review: Setting, story, character and mechanics are all pretty good in this game but it has several balancing issues mainly health recovery and enemy hit change when your characters are behind cover to the point when it seem they arent following the same rules. _childDocuments_.review: "yet to beat the game" was not too sure about this game after playing the first missions. "Either  i am really good at this game or its just to easy" is what i started to say to myself. "on hard, full tactical" they give you a lot of good equipment early it seems. as i progressed i started to realize this is not just a tactical game like xcom and others in this genre.  skill management is key swapping your powers for certain situations is important very different from a regular skill tree. the game is very interesting in that it makes you think differently about your choices. it make you utilize everything that you have instead just finding one cool weapon and sticking to that because its the better weapon. i appreciate that every item matters and every skill matters.  if you stick with one skill set through out the game im sure you will have a very tough time. also stealth is important before a battle. in other games your more like Rambo with the mini machine gun. in this game your more like Rambo with a knife.  the difficulty is ramping up but i just went through what was suppose to be the hardest match with out taking any damage. i found that funny  because i took damage from mostly every other fight prior. but then i found a side match that gave me my honest first L.  i am not fighting those guys im go level up first. i love that i cant just take out any team of monsters. or if i do i would need alot of health packs. but i dont want to do that because i may need to buy other things. yes the weapons kinda seem the same but some have modifications that make them you unique, again this game is not about having a dope singular weapons its about using the right tool for the job. especially when comes to the powers. i hope they make more like this. i think they really created something unique with the skill deck "is what i heard it was called". its refreshing from a regular skill tree. looking forward to see how much bigger this game gets and if the story can drive it home.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely an improvement on Mutant year zero which was a decent game in it's own right. A decent amount of content for the price. And nice to see the light puzzle elements with the keypads seem to be new with each keypad. I'd like to see a little more gun variety, and really hoping they add some DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions in the first few hours of game-play:Sleeper HIT of the SUMMER!!! What's not to like from this XCOM/RPG style game? The interface is easy to navigate and use. The story is well written so far, along with a great plot! Memorable characters, excellent graphics and the sound is top notch! THE GOOD: Well designed levels and maps, graphics are amazing, multiple difficult levels, fun exploration, great plot, comedy and writing, memorable characters, awesome XCOM style strategic fights with real time exploration, awesome stealth mechanics, easy fast travel options (the game doesn't waste your time backtracking!), innovative and new ideas to the genre too. THE BAD: The only bad thing I can see is the difficulty level can't be changed without starting the game all the way over. I started it on standard and i've had some very difficult missions that I have had to keep restarting to beat. I'm afraid I could get stuck and just not be able to beat a mission and then will rage quit as I 'm not going to start all over just to lower the difficulty. There also could be more loot and weapons to choose from. I'm level 8 and still using the same gun I started with. So i would like to see some crafting options and more random events while exploring would be nice too. AFTER 10+ HOURS:After restarting battle after battle, I find myself getting frustrated as the difficulty is too tough. AND there is NO way to lower the difficulty without a complete game restart!! Wow.. this is seriously a MAJOR oversight! I'm probably not going to finish this game as I refuse to restart. So unless the developers allow changing game difficulty in the middle of a playthrough I'm  not going to see the rest of this game. I'm disappointed because I really did enjoy the characters, game play and the story/plot a lot. It's sad that game companies make simple mistakes like this and ruin the play-ability of their game. PLEASE FIX!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Game was going good til the frog boss fight. then it froze 4 different times and wouldnt let me finish the fight. graphics are good gameplay is very similiar to mutant year zero which i expected. characters are complex and very different. many ways to approach each fight. damage scale is a little fundamental but overall an awesome experience. just need to get the glitches fixed at frog boss fight.
_childDocuments_.name: Miasma Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This game is off to a great start. Very smooth experience. I love how systems are slowly introduced as part of the story. I'm in the mines now and have some tough fights up ahead. It's been tactically challenging and I feel I just scratched the surface. Next to gameplay the game is a beauty to look at.

_childDocuments_.review: A breath of fresh air to see this game, still in development, be amazing already compared to many new games being released lately that are considered completed and are garbage. _childDocuments_.review:
In the not-too-distant future. America has been torn apart by a savage force known only as the 'Miasma'. Meet Elvis, a young man brought to the mining town of Sedentary as a baby. Left by his mother in the care of a robotic older 'brother' and given a mysterious glove with which he can control the Miasma.

Join the brothers on a quest across a post-apocalyptic wasteland to find the answers they crave. Answers which may change the course of human history forever.

From the creators of Mutant Year Zero: Road to Eden, comes a beautifully crafted tactical adventure you won't forget.
