_childDocuments_.review: Hunt the Night is a standard singleplayer 2D action rpg. Negative:- Getting lost, even though the game is linear. You'll have to open a walkthrough guide or the wikidot page sometimes.- Related to the previous point, the game has no 3D shading, causing elevations and objects to blend into the terrain.- There are a few points of no return that come without warning.- Some of the endgame bosses can oneshot you with bullethell chaos and gimmicks where it is not obvious how to avoid them. Takes some trial and error.- Occasionally, aoe magic attacks spawn right on top of you before you can dodge them.- The endings are disappointing. It's just a few images. I expected more, considering that the whole game builds up to it.- There isn't much replay value.Positive:- Combat is fast and fun. - There are a handful of different melee and ranged weapons for variation. There is no leveling system, so you never lose efficiency by trying out the equipment that you come across.- The enemy difficulty is adequately challenging.- The music is alright. I like the calm tracks, but sadly there aren't many unique combat themes.- The story is decent, even if they payoff isn't great. There is some lore if you like theorycrafting.- The level designs are good. Checkpoints at places where they make sense and shortcuts that bring you closer to them.- Exploration is well rewarded. Aside from the occasions where I was completely lost, I rarely felt like I was wasting my time by checking every corner.- The game doesn't waste your time with filler content. It has appropriate length for what has to offer.Verdict:It's fine. If you like edgy games with challenging combat, then you'll get your money's worth out of it. It took me 14 hours to beat it and I was never bored while playing it. I  wish the endings were more elaborate though.

_childDocuments_.review: Released on April 13, 2023, Hunt the Night is a retro RPG with a dark narrative, gothic atmosphere, and fast-paced gameplay. The game offers a nostalgic experience, exploring a haunting world and immersing players with immersive music and sounds.The pixel art graphics are smooth and well animated, complemented by a stunning color palette. The game's strong point is the freedom of exploration and material collection to progress through the levels, providing a rewarding experience. Additionally, the variety of combat options, with dash abilities and melee and ranged attacks, allows players to customize their strategy.However, the initial narrative is lacking in detail, and progression can become tiresome and lengthy, with long stretches without relevant information. Furthermore, the game presents a considerable difficulty level, with challenging puzzles and numerous enemies.Overall, the game offers an engaging and challenging experience with interesting gameplay mechanics. However, the narrative could be further developed, and the difficulty may pose an obstacle for some players. It's important to note that everything stated here is subject to change.

_childDocuments_.review: You can read my other reviews Video review: Most of the time good and evil are hand in hand in a dispute for the supremacy of the forces, here represented by Day and Night, trying to achieve the ultimate goal of controlling everything. Hunt the Night follows a path of despair in an atmosphere surrounded by pixels in a top-down action adventure with a steep learning curve.The player will follow the story of Vesper, an integral part of a group called "Stalkers", in the world of Medhram. This group was created to defend humanity against nocturnal creatures that were attracted by the eternal Night. One day the Stalkers, discovered an artifact called Seal, which allowed them to imprison the night and grant humanity eternal day, but with one catch… the Seal will have to be fed periodically through the sacrifice of Stalkers. This prosperous period saw its days over when Blackbone, a former member of the Stalker, betrayed his group and broke the Seal, thus bringing a new era, the era of Night.The adventure begins in this troubled period, where humanity has almost all been decimated and the Stalkers see their numbers greatly reduced. Vesper is not just another member of the group, as she has powers that are quite different from the rest. Vesper is, in a way, possessed by a being of the night and although she cannot communicate with other people, as she is mute, she can communicate with Umbra. These story notes are presented during the course of the adventure at key moments. It is undoubtedly an interesting process, this one of uncovering Vesper's origins and connecting all the dots with the characters present in Hunt The Night.One of the first things that stand out in this title is without a doubt its presentation. The whole environment is full of delicious pixel art notes, which even leave a taste of Bloodborne, ranging from decimated forest areas, icy areas full of contrast with trees with orange leaves, to a giant cathedral haunted by beings of the night. Speaking of enemies, there is a very interesting repertoire of different beings, which of course, have several different attack mechanics. Not being a very difficult title, there is in fact a learning path, but without ever going to the boring side of the thing. Of course, it is possible to cross areas without having any kind of confrontation with key enemies, which helps a lot in moments of exploration.Gameplay in Hunt The Night relies on fast movements combining melee combos and ranged attacks. Vesper has the possibility to use one of five different types of melee weapons, presenting different types of attacks that also print different types of damage that can even leave enemies with poison. These weapons can be a rapier-type sword, which essentially sees its speed and range as a main feature, a greatsword, which sees the moment of impact as its main point but is extremely slow, among others. In the field of ranged weapons, there is the possibility of using a pistol, a crossbow, and a shotgun. They all share the same type of ammunition, although they use a different number of cartridges, which are recovered either by applying damage to enemies, or at specific points scattered around the map, essentially at key points of movement between cliff areas.In addition to the weapons repertoire, Vesper will be able to acquire and equip various types of Armor, Dark Power, and Moonstones. Dark Powers offer additional damage, buffs, or summons. Moonstones apply a buff to Vesper's stats and can also provide unique benefits that cannot be found on any other equipment. The boss fights are quite interesting. They all feature different and interesting mechanics and attack patterns. It's up to the player to find their favorite weapons and most favorable pieces of equipment for specific situations. Although it is not the main point, it is interesting to realize that it is really possible to make different types of builds, whether they apply more damage, or on the other hand, a more defensive build such as, for example, more armor or life.This is a linear title, however, with the non-implementation of a map, or small indications about where the player will have to move next (other than when talking to the characters who present them with their new task), there is a possibility of encountering a barrier to progress. Of course, as I mentioned, exploration is always the key to this barrier, but there were times when I really felt lost in the world of Medhram. It is also very important to memorize the places where you passed before, as it is quite likely to pass by the same place several times.Hunt the Night is an experience marked by visually stunning areas that make its entire world vibrant. Despite somewhat frustrating moments in terms of exploration and combat, Medhram's mysteries are quite interesting and serve as a fuse to keep the player interested until the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat over all felt really good and the mix between getting up close to the enemy and then shooting them from far away with the recovered bullets is a lot of fun. A few times it felt a little bit unfair due to enemies straight up one shooting me, and the moves sometimes not being well telegraphed, though it wasn't too bad after learning the enemies patterns. Sometimes the gunshots, especially from the shotgun, felt really inaccurate though and shot in a completely different direction than aimed. Almost all the Boss fights were really well-made and a lot of fun to fight.The only points that could have been made better are the Duo-Boss fights and the Story, which itself wasn't all too interesting. The Duo-Bossfights felt more like they were added for the sake of having it, instead of actually being made for it. All of them were just 2 bosses thrown in 1 arena with no effort made to synchronize their attacks. The story was pretty disappointing due to it not being delivered all too well and feeling pretty flat.It also slightly lacks in enemy variety, but due to it being a pretty short game, it's nothing that was bothering me too much. World- and sound design is where Hunt the Night shines though. The entire game is filled with atmosphere and the gothic horror is really well-made.TLDR: Hunt the Night is a pretty fun game. The world is fascinating, and I love the gothic horror aspects of it. Combat feels responsive and the Boss fights in this game were, with a few exceptions, really well-made and fun to fight.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed the game on Kickstarter in 2019, because it promised the looks and feels of Bloodborne in combination with games like Zelda and certain Metroidvania-elements. And it did deliver on that promise!Graphics: clearly a 10/10 if you are into pixelart. Animations are fluid, atmosphere is fantastic. The game has a clear vision of what gothic horror should look like. Sound: 7/10; the game has a decent soundtrack, but only a few standouts. Gameplay: I expected the gameplay to be much more combat-driven than it actually is. I also expected it to be a lot more linear. But combat is only half the fun: after the first big area there is a semi-open world with a lot of exploration and some puzzles - all of them rewarding with new gear or abilities.Combat is hard, but fair. It takes time to get the move sets of bosses down, but every move has it tells - you just have to be careful and not too greedy. I would rate it another 10/10, but just be warned: it is a hard game!Can I recommend it? Yes, definitely.
_childDocuments_.name: Hunt the Night

_childDocuments_.review: Hunt the Night, in short, is a crossover between Blood Omen and Bloodborne. While the aesthetic and writing don't even remotely try to deny the Bloodborne influence, the gameplay, atmosphere and exploration reminded me of the first chapter of the Legacy of Kain saga, especially in certain areas like the Cathedral. It's a little janky, not extremely polished and frustrating at times, but its heart is in the right place. I enjoyed the game thoroughly and I'm glad I backed it.The game looks very good and the soundtrack is, for the most part, fantastic, even though the game doesn't handle the looping of the tracks with enough grace. The gameplay loop is mainly fighting and exploring, with some pretty easy puzzles thrown in the mix. The combat is snappy and fun, exploration is made rewarding by the numerous rewards and the game does sport excellent atmosphere. Boss fights are generally very entertaining. The writing is so-so, but it's enjoyable nonetheless. Hunt the Night is competent in every area, it just lacks that polish that would have allowed it to really shine: the balance is not perfect, not by a long shot; the hitboxes aren't always precise; and so on.So overall, as a debut title, this is very encouraging, and if you don't expect perfection, you'll probably have fun with Hunt the Night. Cheers, devs, and here's to the next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend.   Taking my time with the game.   Really like the lore, pixel art and gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: I will preface this by saying that Hunt the Night was on my wishlist for a long time. On the surface, it looks like a mash-up of oldschool Zelda and Bloodborne. It checked a lot of boxes for me; challenging combat, lots of gear & collectibles that reward thorough exploration of it's intriguing world, and how can you ignore that delicious pixel art aesthetic? With that said, the game isn't without it's flaws. Enemy balancing sometimes felt a smidge off (though, who among us hasn't gotten stuck on a boss in a game, yelling "That's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!" as we rock our 5th death in a row?) As with any game that pays tribute to the Souls series, overcoming those struggles also felt equally rewarding. There are some minor areas that could use a bit more polish - getting stuck on random edges or behind fences I'm pretttyyy positive I wasn't supposed to be behind. With that said, I never encountered anything that hampered my positive experience with the ~11 hours that I spent with the game. I'm currently sitting at 21/22 achievements. The last achievement I have to unlock is "Unlock all achievements" - which seems to be a minor bug.Side note: I split my time between both my PC and Steam Deck and the game played fantastic on both, if you're thinking of exploring that route - and the devs have already added Cloud Saves shortly after release. Why are you still reading? Play the damn game already. :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely doesn't deserve it's mixed review. It's a pretty darn well made game that's held back by some clunkiness and QOL issues. Hunt the Night is a hardcore top down action rpg, imagine mixing the Legend of Zelda with Bloodborne's setting and Castlevania looking characters.  I won't beat around the bush, this game is tough as nails and you will die a lot, so if you're after a more casual romp, please turn around immediately. Combat is all right, it can be clunky and frustrating at times but it can also be exhilarating and very satisfying when you're weaving dashes in between melee attacks to then unload you guns onto the enemy before finishing it off with your dark magic, the bones are well structured, it just needed some more polish. Enemy variety could have also been better, especially since this game loves to throw you into wave gauntlets.The game doesn't have a map, which can be annoying for some, who don't pay attention or talk to NPC's so they end up not knowing where to go next,  but there is an NPC in the game that will tell you which direction to go, so it's not really a big deal.  If anything Hunt the Night's biggest flaw is balance, which is probably the best flaw to have because it can be easily patched, the game starts pretty darn tough, a bit too much, but gets much easier mid gameOverall Hunt the Night might not break any new grounds, but it melds together well tried formulas into an intriguing dark fantasy world filled with challenges to keep you coming back for more and conquer them once and for all. It has a few QOL and polish flaws here and there and I would say maybe wait for a balance patch down the line, but don't overlook this gem
_childDocuments_.name: Hunt the Night

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't happy with the game at first but it grew on me.Bloodborne aesthetic with Hyper Light Drifter's style of combat. Good art and music. Some interesting puzzles and I think the combat is actually pretty good. Lots of people whining about the combat but it really does boil down to "Git Gud" as annoying as that sounds. The hardest room encounters and bosses only took me a handful of tries at most. The game is only about 10 hours long but has some extra content to unlock if you're a real masochist.My most frustrating gripe is a lack of a map. The game has the Soulsborne approach to progression and exploration where you only get a general hint about where to go but then you're on your own. This would be fine but the game doesn't have enough visual cues in some dungeons to direct you toward the goal and you can totally miss that one door you need to walk through if you just didn't happen to scroll the screen far enough in the right direction. There's a couple minor bugs like being able to dash out of bounds occasionally and sometimes the menu stops working. These were few and far between for me.All in all, totally decent game at the correct price point.

_childDocuments_.review: First I wanted to mention that I did experience the line of sight beam disappearing while using a controller. If I’m perfectly honest this didn’t bother me much. And it did not prevent me from completing the game. Aside from that I didn’t experience any other bugs.The story of Hunt the Night is fairly light, limited to a handful of conversations. However the true depth is in the environmental storytelling present in notes and destruction throughout the world. In addition, the backstory is set up through a world concept of infusing feathers with memories. These provide a lot of detail. And there are about 30 of them in all.The sound in the game is excellent. The combat sound effects feel appropriate and provide lots of feedback. And the soundtrack is very fitting for the atmosphere of the different biomes present in the game.The gameplay loop of Hunt the Night is quite fun. You generally solve a few puzzles on the way to the boss room in the five dungeons. The puzzles break up the combat nicely and they are not too difficult. You’ll end up facing 10 main quest bosses and optionally 10 hunt mini bosses, which are supped up versions of normal enemies. As for the enemies themselves there are 17 types that I could count. Every boss encounter was a challenge except for 2 of them. And even the hunt mini bosses were a challenge at times due to the mobs that would also get thrown at you. The 5 dungeons are connected by the overworld which contains a few side quests, lots of hidden items to collect, and some of the mini bosses.Overall I really enjoyed this game and felt that it was worth every penny! If you enjoyed games like Morbid: The Seven Acolytes, Unsighted, CrossCode, or Tunic, then I think you would like Hunt the Night as well :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hunt the Night

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game a bit blind. I have played Souls games, Bloodborne and Nioh so I have an idea of game difficulty. The game is excellent. The difficulty is up there along with being a bit infuriating and annoying (the whole point of playing these games). Unlike the aforementioned games where if you are killed in game and lose your (souls etc. whatever currency) HTN does not do that. You keep what you kill. Another big plus is save points are right where you need them just before a boss. The music is good, the art is SUPERB. The combat is quick paced. The story is so-so. The lore is excellent. Creepiness and jump factor is definitely in high in there. The few janky or bad things about the game are quite minor. From using healing items and spell use if you get hit you can get cancelled (normal in many other games). HTN can use more spells and weapons. I found the layout of your home base of Ravenford  a bit strange with the merchant a bit out of the way.Overall I really enjoyed this game (as of writing this I'm about 3/4s of the way through the game). I recommend this to all those who are very casual and determined.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a beautiful bloodborne inspired soulslike with metroidvania aspects. It has a lot to love, the amount of lore, the attention to detail, beautiful animations and scenery. The combat is fast paced with some depth, similar to bloodborne there is no blocking but instead an incredibly strong dash. It gives you 3 ranged weapons which you can switch between at will and dark powers. There is also a large focus on platforming which has its ups and downs.Unfortunately I wouldn't buy the game in it's current state to be honest. It has a lack of polish and a decent amount of bugs that, while not frustrating, can easily bring you out of the atmosphere. There is no map despite the game having content that is inaccessible until you obtain certain powers. Backtracking is fine because of how powerful the dash is and the inclusion of fast travel spots, but it adds a layer of tedium trying to remember a location that is fairly off the path. The combat can very easily become frustrating depending on the enemies they throw at you and even more importantly the terrain you are fighting in. The enemies aren't very diverse, melee enemies all act the same minus one more challenging enemy that acts as a mini-boss, and even then it's usually because of the terrain you have to fight him in or because it summons ranged enemies. The problem with the ranged enemies is the fact that their projectiles go through terrain and are plentiful, it makes dealing with platform combat more frustrating than engaging. The boss fights in the game are incredible and I've enjoyed every fight versus boss enemies minus certain mini-bosses.The game also gives you plentiful equipment and you begin to get different options almost immediately. I appreciated the ability to find my own play style instantly despite the lack of overall variety in the weapons. There are about 5 weapons types in the game despite there being 20 different weapons in the game. So after the first area you explore, you'll begin finding weapons that are the same weapon but with an extra passive. The armor selections, however, were truly diverse, only seeing maybe 1 armor set that had the same effect as another. All these armor sets also effect your characters visual appearance, something I can appreciate as pixel art games usually don't do that. Lastly, the games story seems fairly generic to me. I'm not the most story focused player so take this with a grain of salt. It just seems like the usually dark vs light story and it makes the story and it's endings blatant almost immediately.I'd definitely keep an eye on the game as developers are very active within the community it seems. They are planning on fixing most of the bugs that you'll hear spoken of in other reviews. Once the game has gotten more polish and bug fixes I'd believe it'd be a solid 6 or 7 out of 10. Currently however, I'd recommend you wait or get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say this is like a... 6 or 7 out of ten. It is top down hack and slash with difficulty akin to dark souls. You have a simple array of weapons you will find (Sword, great sword, daggers, spear, claws) with various elements. A couple of 'dark powers' and three guns which you can enhance with some effects. Enemies hit hard, and you're expected to dodge them, while using a limited amount of roses to heal. You'll explore various dungeons as well as the overworld of this bleak world in search of 5 seal fragments to restore the day. It is very nostalgic with similarities being given to Zelda : Link to the Past, and puzzles can be rewarding if you're paying attention. But it fails and is very much a letdown with the bugs and general... 'unfinished' feeling that it has.The game started to get tiring about halfway in with various bugs that were coming up. One issue that I adapted around was never being 'above' an enemy. The sprite will look like it's out of the way of an aoe attack, but the graphics don't have a proper sense of 3d environment so you get hit anyways because the animation touched you as it came down. Extremely unfair and very poor programming that they should fix up, And there were a few situations I had were items got bugged or achievements got bugged. I finished all of the hunts, but never got the achievement for it. Meanwhile, after back tracking and trying to find the 'missed' hunt, I find that one of the hunts still has its mini-boss arena play out. The hunt is still there and I can kill him again but for no achievement progress or reward. He's just bugged out. And I had a couple of fights glitch out that either resulted in an unfair death or me needing to restart the game. And then the game begins to rush itself after the second dungeon. :What was a proper lengthy dungeon immediately dumps you off into the 3rd dungeon that is maybe 1/5 the size. :You realize that the overworld is incredibily small (if we refer to Link to the past, imagine you only explore the zones on the southern part of the map):A narrative moment has you fighting with someone, but the conflict is ignored and you magically make up somehow with no gameplay reflecting it either.:An NPC definitely shouldn't have died at a certain point in the story, but they will die when you find them in a certain map that is not blocked from you going there right off the bat. They will actually disappear from your base. But later in the story, other NPCs will tell you to chase down the NPC who has long been. The story makes alot more sense at that pivotal moment, when you realize the NPC should've been alive up until this point. But the way the game is programmed enables you to just wistfully explore and find him and thus kill him preemptively.:Your character never gets their backstory explained. Which, if they were going the dark souls route and making you want to piece together things, then that'd be one thing. But the game actively brings it up as an important thing, and pushes you to remember. All while an important choice will be coming to meet your character, whom, has had no growth and no realization and no struggle and no development leading up to make that choice more meaningful.Overall, I found the game enjoyable. It challenged me and beat me a good number of times and I kept returning until I could beat various bosses. I entertained the idea of 100%'ing the game, but in the face of various bugs that prevent me from doing so, I will not be. With some more polish and bugfixing, I would definitely elevate the score to an 8. It's a solid game despite the bugs. It certainly has the potential to do alot more, had they made a bigger world and gave you more abilities akin to Link to the Past. Maybe DLC?

_childDocuments_.review: Hunt the night is a top down souls-like that, especially in regards to the lore and environmental storytelling, delivers an amazing experience. The music and art of this game are exceptional, and the exploration is very satisfying, especially when any part of the environment could be a key to understanding a key piece of lore.The game does an AMAZING job of encouraging the player to engage in the lore, with many puzzles being tied directly to it. I dont think they are so complicated that you need a full understanding of the lore or anything close to it, but by asking the player to even lightly interact with the lore to progress, it gives a base level understanding of the world and story being told even to a player who may otherwise not be reading things or thinking about it.Now, I know not everyone is into the storytelling side of things, and as far as game play goes, I have been thoroughly enjoying learning the combat. For me, the combat is secondary to what really makes this game so amazing, but it is still fun. The boss fights have been challenging but not frustrating so far, which I always appreciate.Hunt the Night is absolutely worth your time, and if they add full steamdeck support with cloud saving, it will take it to the next level.

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed this game; its the first game I've been engaged enough with to try and beat in one sitting (it took two). Gorgeous pixel art, interesting lore/worldbuilding, solid combat, unique and challenging bosses. There are enough different weapons/abilities and enough variety of environments/enemies that I actually felt compelled to try different options, which doesn't always happen for me in these types of games.  I've seen a few negative reviews that dislike the feel of the combat, but to each their own, I suppose. Overall, if you're searching for a minimalist 2D indie Bloodborne, or something that feels a bit like a very challenging Link to the Past, Hunt the Night may be worth checking out.

name: RIDE 5
detailed_description: SPECIAL EDITION About the Game Rev up your engine and get ready to hit the track with RIDE 5. An adrenaline-filled gaming experience that is so authentic it will make you feel like you're truly racing at break-neck speed. Find your favorite bikes and check out new ones in the ultimate motorcycle game! Race on over 35 tracks and collect more than 200 motorcycles from world-renowned manufacturers, each element is designed to feel like you're riding a real bike. IT'S A LONG ROAD It's not just speed that wins races - Endurance mode rewards perseverance and strategy. Time is no longer the issue, ride to your heart's content with the option of saving, exiting and jumping back in later. Just make sure you keep an eye on fuel and pit-stops - these helplines can quickly become your worst nightmare! FROM ZERO TO HERO Start out in your garage, climb the ranks and become the best world racer in the new Career mode. Race against increasingly skilled Rivals, true obstacles who will stand between you and the finish line. Learn to master different bikes and handle every situation. It won't be easy though... The road to victory is laden with challenges and it's up to you to decide which one you want to take - the harder the challenge, the greater the reward! WIN UNDER ANY CONDITION It doesn't matter how good you are, there is always one factor you can't control: the weather. Clear blue skies can turn into heavy downpours and then back to sunshine, rolling clouds will follow you as you dash through the bends, giving you ever-changing views and landscapes. You will have to deal with unexpected situations and use your skill to tackle both wet and dry conditions - the improved physics makes for an even more life-like experience! TEST. LEARN. RIDE. Not sure which line to follow or when to slam on the brakes? Use the new riding aids and get customized support when needed the most. Learn to better handle the bike and the tricks of the trade to become the best rider you can be. TAKE CONTROL You can tell a true motorcycle aficionado not just from the bike but also from their garage - collect your favorite models and customize them to your liking. _childDocuments_.review: After playing Ride 4 for more than 300 hours and cracking 5 lap time world records in that game I have a good grasp on the physics of Ride 4 which in my opinion were the best since Ride 2.Ride 5 however feels wonky, unresponsive, there's no real feedback from the brakes, no vibration in the controler to tell how much I'm pushing the brake lever, especially for the front brake. The rear is bouncy and steps out way too much on corner entry imo. It feels like I have MotoGP style engine brake in a bike from the 1980s.Very little has changed from Ride 4, apart from content that could've been brought in as DLCs like the newer models of the litre bikes, a few tracks, etc.The story mode, especially starting out with that narration (which I personally don't like, but oh well) had more potential. Why am I on a 1980s Endurance Racer just 5 'cups' into my career? How do I transport my bike on a trailer from wherever I live (assuming it's what you put in in the rider info - in my case Germany) to Suzuka, Japan when I'm just starting out racing? It feels very weirdly put together, without passion, without thought or regard how the ladder of motorcycling could or would work in the real world.Also, and this is a personal issue of mine, I feel like small bikes don't get the recognition they deserve in the Ride titles. We have SSP300 championships on a nationwide and international level virtually all over the globe, so why don't we get Ninja 400s, Kove 300s, etc. in these games anymore? I remember the days of Riding Spirits 2 for example that basically had all bikes your mind could think of and your heart desired. I understand it's about licensing, but man, I'd be fine trading in some of the very similar looking MV Augustas for some more variety immediately, don't even get me started on Bimotas or Vyrus models.Overall, this game is the biggest disappointment in gaming for me so far this year. I was really looking forward to it and now regret not having waited another week and reading the critiques before buying this 40gb of software. At least I didn't get the cash grab Season Pass that's going to flood this game with more of the same looking bikes and same old boring tracks we got in Ride 4... Not worth the money right now, wait for a sale or just get older titles on key sites for more enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: Ride 5 In Depth ReviewThe developer has created a game changing type of game. Ride 5 has a Career mode that can provide many hours of enjoyment in itself. You have a chance to collect over 200 bikes which have been painstakingly modeled in amazing detail. On top of that you can ride them on realistic near perfect models of some of the best circuits in the world. There are a few circuits I have ridden and I can say they it gives me goosebumps of how accurate they are. If you have a decent gaming pc, some of the gameplay is easily mistaken for videos of real racing. My advice is try out the Career mode and collect some bikes while getting to the point where the AI is easy to beat and you can finish 3 laps without crashing. When you have reached this level, you will be comfortable diving into Multiplayer, which is another world inside this game. I have met a ton of great people through the Ride games who are helpful and fun to ride with. For the cost of this game, I can go out to eat and get a movie (once). Think about it, the justification is simple. If you race bikes or want to do trackdays, this game can even be a tool to familiarize yourself with a circuit you have to ride on in the near future. Hope to see you online. There are some really cool new bikes like the Superleggara V4, Aprilia RSV E5 (super smooth), many more BMW S1000RR and M1000RR. is a real Pro mode where turn indicators, auto-shift, off track aid + all the riding assists must be off. In Ride 4 you could be in realistic with all that stuff on. Look at the Time Trial leaderboards now and you see not everyone can do those times in Pro... Sometimes in Ride 4 it is a nightmare when collisions are on, if someone is intentionally crashing into others. In dynamic mode, they can bump you, but it won't instantly crash you. This can also be used in Career with the AI. are 20 minutes for the most part. Rewind is available so you don't have to throw away your time if you are trying to get gold on every race in Career mode. If you made a bad choice on your pitstop, you can now restart from the pitstop. I am a busy person and for me rewind and restart from the pitstop keep me interested in doing the endurance races.The way the rear tire spins is more dynamic now. You can do some fun sliding if you are into that. Also you can back it in waaay better than Ride 4. Very satisfying IMO. seem better now. In 4 if you don't have a perfect setup and riding style, you have to run H front on a lot of bikes/tracks. Now you can run soft on a lot of those same bikes/tracks.  like fork oil level, slipper clutch, swingarm length, chain tension.Can have 20 in multiplayer. (adjustable to 120%). is better. There are no more invalid laptimes in career, only time deductions.You can modify the liveries on BMWs now.The editor allows twice as many layers and I found a new way of getting credits to buy bikes by sharing some bike liveries. Not new to Ride 5, but I never used it in Ride 4. are better. ABS has 0-4 settings now. For me ABS 1 feels like Ride 4 with ABS toggled on in Rider Aids.Bikes are cheaper when in the beginning of Career mode. No need to hack the game like some did in Ride 4 to get money. is a whole new venture, which I have not tried yet, but sounds interesting.My experience: 35 years riding 2 stroke/4 stroke. Ride R6 and Duc twin regularly. Have been a licenced racer in the last 15 years. Still do some trackdays. One championship on 250 MX. There are no games currently available which are just like the real thing. Unless you are in a very small group who own an actual road racing sim, you are playing from a controller. These games do challenge you by making you put your body position in the right vicinity, use the gas and brakes correctly and hitting the ideal trajectory of the turns. When I go back and play Ride 4, I immediately go off the track because I slowly got used to the arcade abilities. I see people do 1:44 on Mugello on old R6 bikes in Ride 4. That isn't very realistic, unless you are telling me you are faster than Marc Marquez on his factory Honda... The real non-MotoGP record on Mugello is more like 1:54 on a V4 Panigale. For me it feels like Ride 5 is more like how it should be and for us jaded Ride 4 players, it is hard to accept slower lap times. With that said, I see some of the guys laying down some fast laps still. Those super fast guys you see on YouTube seem to be finding ways to do the super fast laps. We just have to work harder, but in the end you will be a better player. Hurry up so we can do some racing online.Missing weekly challenges - I enjoyed a new challenge each week and seeing which of your friends could get the top spotI Like adjusting electronics on the starting line, for doing starts in TC0 and then turning it up if needed. It is possible in Ride 5, but you have to remember to do it in setup, then toggle Y as soon as the race starts.No tuck. Not really a bad thing. Not having tuck in Ride 5 allowed me to move to manual shifting, so it was a bonus in that aspect. But I keep pressing the tuck button and it upshifts the bike at bad times.

_childDocuments_.review: I've sunk 32 hours into this game so far, and it's given me enough time to really express how disappointed I am with Milestone's 5th attempt to iron out this series.I'll start this off with a list of bugs, glitches, and general gripes I have with this game:1. If you use rewind during an endurance race, you've pretty much broken it, and the race will never end.2. Replays after qualifying and after a race with a qualifying session don't work.3. When track lights turn on at dusk, the entire game stutters down to single digit frames before recovering. If you're in the middle of a turn when this happens, good luck.4. AI bikes are so loud, you can't hear yours if you're in a pack...which you will be for every career race since you always start 10th if there's no qualifying session. There's no option to change this in audio settings.5. "Rival" NPC's are obviously overpowered, and will perform 2-3 seconds faster than anyone else on track, including you on the same bike. Sometimes, if they group together, there will be a 6-7 second gap between the rivals group, and the rest of the pack.6. AI bikes still do not detect the player at all, and will ride through you. Even if you crash, the AI will keep turning into your riderless bike until it disappears, with no attempt to avoid it. This is exacerbated by the fact that you will always start 10th in career races that don't have a qualifying session.7. AI difficulty is wildly inconsistent. I'm a top 10 leaderboard rider in Ride 4. At Road Atlanta, I can barely keep up at 70% difficulty. At VIR, i'm 4 seconds ahead by turn 3 at 120%.8. Resolution scaling is broken. 50%-200% provides no change.9. Turning off motion blur still creates ghosting, just as it did in Ride 4.10. The "warbling" engine sound when in the mid-range of the powerband is still there from Ride 4.11. In order to obtain multiple liveries for a bike, you now must buy the bike in that livery. Bike affinity no longer grants this. If you're gifted a bike in a livery you don't like, too bad because...12. You still cannot get rid of gifted bikes. If you don't want multiples of the same bike in your garage, too bad.13. The rear brake is now useless at any lean angle. You can no longer use it to adjust your line in a corner. It only aids in straight line braking. Mash it to 100% at max lean, and the bike does nothing.14. The menu navigation has been changed for the worse. In career mode but just want to turn a few laps on your own? You have to back all the way out to the main menu, and then change the mode. Some menu selections also make no sense. Sometimes you press "A" to select something, sometimes you press "Start". Was that really necessary?15. The "career" mode locks your progress to a linear set of races. You cannot progress at your leisure like in Ride 4 by choosing what types of bikes you'd like to race. You must race the bikes it tells you to in order to progress to the next set of races. Want to race 600cc bikes? You'll have to race 1960's 500cc's first to unlock them. Don't want to race endurance races too early in your career? Too bad, you're racing them by your 5th set of races, and you're not going to race anything else until they're done.16. The "career" progression makes no sense. The game tries to paint this picture of an up and coming rider just starting out and trying to make a name for themselves, but you're globetrotting around the planet from the get go. Rather than starting off in your desired region, and then unlocking races in different regions like in Ride 4. It just makes no sense.17. The narration is abysmal and cannot be skipped. This includes "rival" introductions before some races. If you have to restart the race for any reason, you're getting the un-skippable intro every time.18. The track selections for some of the races make no sense. 1000cc bikes on a tiny twisty track is not really that enjoyable. The bikes are heavy, hard to change direction quickly, and you never get out of 2nd or 3rd gear.19. Finally, bike handling has changed dramatically. While in and of itself not a bad thing, there are some definite odditites that now exist. The bikes are defininitely more difficult to turn, and have too much grip, especially on corner exit. It is now VERY difficult to high side. You have to intentionally slam the throttle wide open in 1st or 2nd on a 1000cc bike in order to get any rear tire slippage. Braking is...ok, but seems somewhat inconsistent. Sometimes you can brake deep into a turn, sometimes you can't even breathe on the brake lever. The bikes also seem to headshake VERY easiily, and recovering from it is near impoissible unless you stand the bike up and ruin your race. Maybe steering dampers should be an adjustable setting?20. They've removed some enjoyable entry level bikes (KTM 390, Honda CBR300, etc.) for some reason. These would be great introductory bikes for those small twisty circuits early in your career. No idea why these were removed...Well, there you go. These are just mine and some of the reported issues with Ride 5. You may be able to over-look all of these things and have an enjoyable experience. If so, that's great and I'm glad you're having fun! But for me, having dumped so much into this franchise, I was expecting an improvement on what was probably Milestone's best attempt at a true motorcycle racing experience to date (Ride 4). But instead, they decided to remove some of the things that made that game good (open career progression, satisfactory bike handling, good UI), and introduced others that add no value (narration, rivals, etc. See list above).The game still looks pretty good, and runs well on my hardware, so I'll still keep playing it despite the list above. They've added some new tracks that are a worthwhile addition (Autopolis and Le Mans especially). The bikes still look amazing, and turning laps is still an fun way to burn some time. However, the races are simply rage inducing (again, see list above).In the end, there's still no alternative for what is basically the Gran Turismo of bikes. But at this point, 5 games later and with all these issues, I really wish there was. RIMS racing was close, but has since been abandoned. Shame.

_childDocuments_.review: You can see my playtime, I've given this game a decent go and been through a few patches now. Here's why I can't recommend it:- The physics are really tame. Even with all assists off, it's quite hard to lose the rear wheel. There's almost no risk of an endo if you smash the front brake even at 160mph+- The bike selection might be 200+ bikes, but most of these are ten variations of the same model. Counting two different years of the same model with a tiny change, then the race modification and the endurance modification seems a bit cheap. There's a distinct lack of smaller CC bikes too- The graphics are a mixed bag. Bikes look great, but shadows of the bike on the track aren't quite connected to the bike and make it look like it's floating.The skybox looks like it's from a 2003 game, especially in overcast evening weather- It's nice having a day/night cycle, but bad that the game absolutely chugs and will make you crash when the track lights come on- Increasing the resolution slider does precisely nothing- FRUSTRATING endurance race bug, which supposedly has been patched but as of today is still occuring. Look forward to spending at least 20 minutes racing before crossing the line and the race doesn't end. I did manage to find a workaround but this no longer works since the patch- The career mode gets really stale really quick. There's some tracks in the game that just don't get used (no exagerration, some tracks haven't been in a single race in the career) and others that are seriously overused (and it ALWAYS rains!)- The AI can set god like qualifying times. Sometimes they will be at least 20 seconds faster than your best effort in the dry, when qualifying is in the wet!- AI still tries to kill you, regardless of the new behaviour settings- The majority of career races stop you from using race tyres, but permit the AI to use slicks. They'll be on soft tyres in the rain while you're on stocks and they lose no pace whatsoever from this- During autopilot (leading into a race, time attack or in and out of the pits), there's a good chance the AI will straight up crash you into a wall or slip across the grass/sandThere's more than that but you get the point.Really disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review to put what I've been seeing mostly in the review section to rest. Like most I was double checking reviews because I wasn't impressed with the last two MotoGP games that dropped but I've always been a fan of the Ride games. So I'll reference the review I'm smashing on so everyone can read about the original review on top of this one.   I doubt this guy even looked at the bike settings screen for someone who "tracks bikes" seems odd to miss the electronics section of it. I will agree that when the ABS setting is max you can't brake like you should. Put that on one or zero and that problem goes away pretty quick. As for the stoppie I've done one at my settings but it's not that big before the front locks up. As for turning/steering that might be getting affected by the TCS or AW depending on the throttle. As for feel I'm not sure what he means because I get plenty with my settings similar to the MotoGP games so I don't know what to say for that. As for impossible to lose the rear I'm not sure what he means because you do if you try. This game is better than it's predecessor in a few different way but the same in some as well. The physics from what I can tell are pretty much the same as the last few in overall feel with some minor changes which is fine for being the game it is. It's not meant to be the hardcore game that MotoGP is and that's fine. It has the same difficulty slider as before but now there is a AI behavior drop down now so they will even behavior differently even if the difficulty stays the same which can bring it's own challenges if you play around with it.  I'm not a big fan of the current career system compared to the prior game but it makes more sense for a "story" mode I guess. You can still gain credits and experience from single races and time trials so that's a good way around the story mode if you don't want to do it. Overall if you were a fan of the previous games like I am you'll enjoy the changes once you figure out the settings a bit because that can be weird if you're use to a certain setting like I was. It seems a bit lack luster in bikes without the DLCs but that normal for Milestone to drop the free and paid ones over time. If you're new to the title give it a chance and mess with the different setting before hanging up the towel on it. It's a pretty decent game and a slight step up from the previous titles which is the normal trend for this title. This is a much easier game to get into and enjoy than the MotoGP games due to the wide spectrum of bikes to use along with tracks. Nothing against those games it's just not the same and that's how it should be.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME!!!It has been nerfed into oblivion. _childDocuments_.review: Don't make my mistake. I told myself I wasn't going to get this game but I got it anyway, and I'm disappointed in myself. Feels like another Milestone game where the physics don't make much sense, the AI are all over the place and ram you off the road, with the slightest touch to your rear and you'll go flying off into space. Handling is basically a mix between Ride4 and motogp23. You get the standup physics on acceleration of motogp23 with the bouncy/lightweight suspension physics of Ride4 (which don't go together well imo).I came off of Ride4 to play this, and I actually want to go back to playing Ride4. The graphics are close to Identical to Ride4, and there is very little feeling in vibration and feedback when using a dualsense controller. Under braking, with certain types of corners, you will lose the front out of nowhere because there is no feedback in the brake. A couple of positives: The motogp23 physics model means the rear doesn't want to slide out at every turn or bump like it did in Ride4. AI seem to be a lot more competitive at 120% difficulty compared to Ride4. The improved curb physics are probably the biggest positive.BUT, there are just too many negatives (albeit subjective negatives) to justify this game at this price. I've had very little fun in the minimal time I have played which really shouldn't be the case for a brand new Milestone game...Edit: Played 10 more hours trying to make the most of a bad purchase...My opinion of it has only gotten worse. 2 gamebreakers for me:1) The physics is really bad imo. On Road America, your bike will bounce its way along the track through the bumps and dips as if it weighs 20kgs, but will still feel like you're wrestling a 2 ton buffalo trying to change its direction in the chicanes. Slow turns are particularly painful because the bikes just don't turn naturally even at a crawling pace in 1st gear.2) The feedback from the front is nonexistent. You can literally lock your front wheel under braking so that it is physically not turning, and you won't feel the vibration in the controller. When you do feel the feedback, it is usually too late because you are already sliding out...I've uninstalled until they do some physics/game engine changes. Its not a fun experience. This coming from someone that has a few top 100 times in motogp22 and 23, so I am not bad Milestone games. Again, don't make my mistake...Edit 2: As of patch 5, its still not great at all imo because the controller feedback on dualsense is still borderline nonexistent until you are at the point of crashing...I don't understand what is so hard about devs testing their games...or at least learning how to play the games they make at a relatively competitive level that they can have an honest opinion about critical game mechanics...

_childDocuments_.review: Much of the issues have been detailed by other reviews but I would list a few points that bother me- Smaller class (A1 and A2 or 125cc - 500cc) bikes have been cut from the game but also other bikes from Ride 1-4 are also missing, no Bonneviles, no R90T, W800 or Adventure bikes or anything where you could have some fun. They have the 3D models, the sound and handling files, they know how to do the licencing- what's the problem here?- I didn't check in detail but I'll think also Supermoto is gone?- DLC roadmap came out and I don't get it, nothing there that is really interesting or that they haven't already done before or that fixes the above points on first glance, except for the Italijet Dragster (that's 1 bike out of 6 DLC packs!)- Narration pre-race is tedious, those who have been playing racing games for years have had to go through this format for way too long, we just want to race. If we want to watch a video, then we'll stick to YouTube!- Many are saying this is a Ride 4 with some new 1000's, I'm guessing it is based on Ride 4 with the learnings from SBK and MotoGP added into the handling. - If this was Ride 1 we could let it slide, but this is the 5th game in the series, by now all bikes and tracks from the other games should be ported over with the additions of the last 2 years. Overall, if you have Ride 4 and all the DLCs, and/or all the other Ride titles, then you can honestly skip this unless there does happen to be a bike you're absolutely interested in riding that you don't get from the other games.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, Ride5 is a shadow of Ride4! The vehicle handling feels rubbery, and there’s no sense of the machine – it feels like they’ve introduced simplifications to cater to players who want to chill at their computers rather than immerse themselves in a realistic motorcycle racing simulator. Just a minute ago, bored with Ride5, I launched Ride4, and suddenly the boredom vanished, replaced by the joy of handling sports machines and the urge to keep playing. As a result, I felt compelled to write this comment, hoping that Studio Milestone S.r.l. might read it and that it might somehow influence their future work. If the physics of Ride4 were combined with the graphics and enhancements of Ride5, I believe it would be a step toward an even more perfect simulator. Unfortunately, the physics, the feel of the motorcycle, and the dynamics that accompanied every session have drastically suffered. In the end, while a few enthusiasts might be replaced by dozens of casual players for short sessions, in the long run, the overall quality and prestige created by Ride4 will decline! I do not recommend the game so that my comment gets noticed and reaches someone who cares about improving the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start... they like their made up physics.... a rider stands the bike up to get onto the fatter part of the tyre.... not the bike.... in the game, if you apply throttle the bike automatically starts lifting onto the fatter part of the tyre.... doesn't happen in real life (even with increased chain tensions).  Also slipping down into first gear if geared correctly should not lock your front or cause a major/minor slapper, may cause your rear to chatter (of course not modelled either in the game).  Bikes feel more planted? unrealistically so! They have removed so many Ride 4 qualities and made this a 100% throttle pile of crap.A.I are playing bumper cars.... don't worry... they can ram as much as they like without penalty.... but you will go down without fail.  Braking is starting to feel a bit more controlled..... now this is the weird thing.... as mentioned before bikes don't stand themselves up onto the fatter part of the tyre on the throttle.... but braking.... yes they do....not in Ride 5 though... brake pretty much as deep and hard as you like.... it will tuck eventually, but without any feedback or feeling for a made up "planted tyre". Again, even stranger is such a planted tyre seems to have you running wide on turn exits even once your clip your apex and start feeding in the throttle. You can't square the turn off.... as the levels of grip are superglue status along with the stupid standing the bike up mechanics they have introduced. Killed the sim and brought in the arcade really.I hope they can revise some of these physics issues.... seems like they have tidied up some of the game... finally liking building my own championships...liking the penalties for leaving the track better, tracks are stunning and accurate as ever, Career mode is as it was before but at the moment with the current ass hattery of the A.I, I rather just do Time Trials against a ghost.Overall, could be an improvement but a lot of work is required on refining the "arcade feel" and this damn annoying ramming A.I. _childDocuments_.review: Ride 5 is decent. Not sure if its because they already patched out the issues on launch when I bought it. I'm fresh off Ride 4 and I ride both street and track in real life. Overall, your better off getting Ride 5 when on sale if you already Ride 4 as the differences IMO aren't enough to warrant full price.  This is my take compared to Ride 4+ Better physics and graphics (except background scenery)+ Newer bike model generations to choose from+ More track options+ They finally fixed the metric to US units bug so you don't have to change back and forth every race+ Slightly harder and more unforgiving than Ride 4 Overall, Ride 4 feels more arcadey now compared to Ride 5. Engine sounds though sounds better in Ride 4.Some have said the handling is more slugglish and slow vs. Ride 4. I found this to be mostly untrue. The animation is slower compared to Ride 4 but after riding the same bikes and track in Ride 5 as I did in Ride 4, same config and everything, I was getting the same performance in corners and lap times. The experience just felt different due to the slower animation and less controller feedback.I play with all rider aids off. I like that it is more unforgiving than Ride 4 when it comes to braking and cornering as in Ride 5, it's similar (but not completely realistic) to how it is in real life. You can low side pretty easy in corners if your hitting the front brake too hard if your not trail braking correctly like in real life. You can also high side coming out of a corner if you accelerate too hard (especially on the higher CC bikes) when you have all the electronics like TCS off or set to the lowest. The only thing I really dislike is the lack of controller feedback. In Ride 4, controller would vibrate some depending on how much and how hard your hitting the brakes. In Ride 5, you'll get some vibration but only when your slamming the front brake hard instead of gradual as you apply pressure to the left trigger.

_childDocuments_.review: I asked for a refund pretty quickly.The game looks decent but nothing spectacular, still i wouldn't expect great graphics from a realistic sim oriented game.i got a refund for some of the reasons i'll mention.Physics are pretty weak and everything is made to make the game somewhat easier (maybe to compensate some flaws i'll mention later). Even with all assists turned off i didn't manage to highside even once despite a full front break at 260km/h. Even with all assists off i didn't manage to lose the rear when exiting a turn at full throttle.. Even with all assists off i didn't manage to feel the existence of a clutch other than for revving, also show that even on stock bikes, the engine brake literally doesn't exist in the game.The overall feel of the bikes, after trying a few in all ranges of power, including ones I actually used in person, is decent but I always have this feeling in games like Ride or MotoGP that I have to call the brakes and handle a few minutes before I use them or the bike won't turn. This feeling doesn't appear in GPbikes or trackdayR and obviously, doesn't exist in person.The game is pretty obviously made to be played in third person despite the modelization efforts for first person. The game lacks a functioning first person camera that looks where a rider should be looking in a turn : at the exit of it.Why would I look in front of me without knowing when the turn ends ? It's an issue that would either be fixed with an automatic head turning option or with an actual head tracking like flight sims use with TrackIR/openIR support. (VR would also work but after trying, it's pretty vomit-inducing to ride in VR with controller)Rear brakes feel like engine brake but worse, I know it's weaker on most motorcycle but I swear you can feel the difference between a free wheel and a rear brake on a M1000RR or other insane motorcycles. You can't really feel it in game, the rear brake is here to make the front brake work harder.The AI ...I could deal with all other issues quite easily considering the game as yet another simcade. It's what actually works after all, actual sim is a niche, even Isle of Mann didn't pull the sim notch all the way up.But damn the AI is absolutely ruining it, it's not agressive, it's actually a bunch of murderers, no matter the settings or difficulty, if the game was actually realistic, most pilots would die in the first turn of a race.It's not even funny I literally saw one go push against 2 other to move them out.Contact with AI already is a shame in a racing game but can be understandable since the player is unpredictable.But AI actually going for a push with other AIs ? that shows how absolutely terrible this AI is.And I don't really want to mention it but still will, I have no idea why they even give you the choice to equip your motorcycle with slicks. You're stuck with regular tyres in most races and categories. Also i saw an AI H2R actually performing a sharp turn at a rather low speed and it almost made me laught, that thing turns just as well as a busa with swingarm extension or just like a freakin bus in real life.Oh and last but not least, the motorcycle choice feels limited but very much FILLED with potential microtransactions as i can already see 3 paying packs available and lots of motorcycle that were in Ride4 are not here.Also i know it's not everyone's favorite but lower cm3 bikes seems to be lacking.Overall the game is a disapointement, while it could have been a decent motorcycle simcade, the AI ruined for me what little could be enjoyable.I also feel some frustration in an issue that isn't one with the game.Isle of mann added an open world that was ultimately useless but still enjoyable, but I felt frustration because I was limited to SBK class monster motorcycles.Ride has actual factory branded motorcycle and could offer a "forza horizon" esque experience with an enjoyable open world, it's frustrating as the only other real options for open world motorcycles are in game that failed motorcycle handling (the crew) or are starting to get old and are not supported anymore (test drive) TrackdayR offers openworld modded maps but it's just an early access limited game on empty maps.Anyway dont buy ride5 at full price, game doesn't deserve more than 25€

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do. It's the only real option for a "Gran Turismo" experience for motorcycles since Tourist Trophy. I've also owned every version of Ride since they came out. But there are so many things that frustrate you about Ride 5 that even as one of the diehard fans of this niche motorcycling community (in the US especially) I can't bring myself to recommend it to other riders. So what does it do right? Faithful visual and audible reproduction of the multitude of bikes. This is the one thing that keeps me coming back. The bikes are modeled pretty darn good. I've owned several of the bikes in this game and I can say that, visually, R5 gets it mostly right. The audio does sound better than previous versions of Ride. There are very distinct exhaust/engine noise differences between the vtwins I love (RC51, TLR, 998, Mille) and other engine configurations so kudos to Milestone for putting in the effort on that end.I also have noticed and appreciate the differences in various power bands of the bikes I've ridden so far. Your average I4 600 hits its power differently than an early '00 big twin. Side-to-side transitions are also better in R5 and weight reductions make a difference.If you want to play R5 solely to experience different bikes then you won't be disappointed. What makes it difficult to recommend is the racing experience. And you gotta race to make money and buy more bikes, so there's the dilemna. First off the difficulty spread is wildly random. 70% AI difficultly is absolutely not the same between tracks. Road Atlanta and Cadwell come to mind as the more obvious examples so far. AI does not see you or adjust their lines when you're there so don't expect a realistic racing experience in that aspect. The racing options so far are linear with no option to try different race series without unlocking them first. You're stuck racing in the order the developers have defined whether you want to or not. Also, the overall game interface is awkward at best, too many actions are required to get to different parts of the game. Want to back out of the career mode to do a random time trial? It takes too many clicks in my opinion.Honestly, they need to just remove all of the transitional animations in the career mode. Who loads a bike onto a trailer with two front wheel chocks? How does that even work? Why are the trailer fenders mounted backwards? Why do your avatars show so much teeth in every scene? Why do I have to watch this every time I start or win a race series? I can imagine the conference room meeting at Milestone where some manager who's never ridden a motorcycle made the call to move forward, but c'mon. This is embarrassing. Thankfully, you can skip most of these scenes, but again, too many clicks.Other minor complaints - why can't I adjust electronic settings in the few seconds before a race start? Why does the AI automatically resume to near impossible to beat 100% difficulty with the "pressing" setting at every race? I know I can't hit every line perfectly, I don't need some npc mindlessly plowing through me at every turn to remind me. The bikes in general have so little edge grip at low speeds it's painful, with or without slicks. Maybe we could have 10% less exhaust burbling and 10% more edge grip? Other reviewers have mentioned and I have noticed the high tendency of the bikes to run wide on the gas. While this is true to an extent in the real world, it feels a bit oversensitive with stock settings for most bikes. If Milestone wants to appeal to more folks maybe they can dial this back a few notches.So I guess if Steam had an option somewhere between "recommend" or "not recommend" I'd probably select it. This latest evolution of the genre definitely isn't a game changer as it gets some thing really right and other things really and frustratingly wrong. Let's just call it the "bold new graphics" of the virtual motorcycling gaming world. You know you want to try it, just don't spend too much on something that's not terribly different than the previous version.

_childDocuments_.review: Update after playing a fair amount: My original review still stands for the most part and by far the most frustrating things are still AI related. They at least don't run out of fuel in Endurance races now but they do magically gain 10+ seconds on you during pit stops. And they're still wildly inconsistent at the same difficulty level: absolute aliens on some tracks and 3-4 sec/lap slower on others. Also, multiplayer is pretty much dead for the most part which is unfortunate but not surprising.I have to say I'm pretty disappointed with Ride 5 given how long it's been since Ride 4 came out. Let's start with a quick overview then dive into some details.For those of you who have played Ride 4, It's basically Ride 4 with a different selection of bikes and tracks and a career mode that is effectively identical with some absolutely nonsensical rival "stories" tossed in. The visuals are not improved, the bikes handle just like they did before, and the AI is still aggressively bad.For those of you who haven't played Ride, it's basically a feeble attempt at Gran Turismo or Forza Motorsport except turn the cars into motorcycles and make it a full contact sport played by immortals, or at least make the AI operate like it is. That is not to say it doesn't have enjoyable moments for hardcore motorcycle enthusiasts, because it does, but some of the bike/track combinations combined with the suicidal AI are enough to put more than a few game controllers and screens at risk of serious damage.There is a large variety of tracks and bikes and if you've ridden a decent variety of bikes in real life you will notice they tend to exhibit at least some of the characteristics of their real world counterparts.This is more of a personal preference, but I find racing in first person view to be much much better than any of the 3rd person cameras and is genuinely fun. You get a better sense of speed and it's a lot easier to get a sense of what's going on under hard braking. You see things get a bit squirrelly and can let off the brake a bit to stabilize. I found it incredibly challenging to notice these sorts of things in 3rd person.When races are on an appropriate track & layout for the size of bike, things can be really fun. You can have some occasional decent 2 or 3 way battles with the AI once the field has stretched out and you're not being knocked around constantly.As much as Milestone would like you to believe otherwise, Career mode so far is basically the same as Ride 4. They've shuffled some menus around and called some things by different names but really you have the same formula. There's a bunch of series you have to get through, and the series are restricted by type of bike and performance class. The presentation of each individual series is effectively identical to Ride 4, so changing up the menus of how you navigate to the series really makes no difference.Bike customization is also exactly the same as Ride 4. You can add 2 upgrade "kits" to both the engine and brakes, switch to racing slicks from stock road tires, and upgrade the exhaust and wheels. All other changes either just unlock tuning options like suspension, or are purely cosmetic. I would love to see something closer to the depth of RiMS, maybe a happy medium between the simplistic customization we have now and the part-by-part customization of RiMS.The attempt at creating some sort of a story or narrative has also not really added anything of value to the game. It doesn't affect it negatively, but it's cheesy and honestly has no bearing on the game whatsoever.The number one issue, as many others mention, is the absolutely atrocious AI. For whatever reason it seems so much worse than in MotoGP 23. For starters, the AI does not seem to care that they are on motorcycles and at risk of bodily harm or death. They will gladly slam into the back of you, send it up the inside and take you out, and just constantly run in to you every chance they get. This is regardless of the "aggressiveness" setting.The AI is also VERY inconsistent and at the 70% difficulty I've been playing, seems to randomly switch between entirely incompetent/slow, and absolutely godlike. Head to head race against a rival? Win by 5 seconds easily. That same rival on a regular race on a different track? Gaps you by 2 seconds in the first lap alone. In general it seems like the rules of racing AND physics don't really apply to them. They can cut corners to pass you and basically just ride wherever they want without penalty and they can seemingly brake HARD on stock tires on a superbike with significant lean angle without letting the front end go.On endurance races, the AI suddenly becomes incomprehensibly stupid. In a 20 minute race the riders that do actually make it to the pits wind up doing so with a couple minutes left. The riders that run out of fuel (5 or 6 of them each race I've done) turn into ghosts and slowly swerve their bikes left and right like they're doing a slow riding skills slalom course.Outside of the AI, although I'm sure this is made much worse by the AI, some of the combinations of track and bike class in career mode are simply NOT fun. Primarily what I mean by this is large powerful bikes on small, narrow, twisty tracks. Any of the GP-sized tracks are actually reasonably fun even with the AI.So overall, I wouldn't spend your money on this at full price. Milestone is not in the habit of making groundbreaking improvements to any of their games after release so I would skip it until it's at least 50% off and don't make the mistake I did in ordering the edition with the season pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Wowee I haven't been this disappointed in a game in a long time. First up I really enjoyed the past Ride games so this was a big shock to me as honestly it wouldn't have taken much for me to be happy with a new Ride game. All I really wanted was some new tracks, updated bike models, and maybe a new mode or two in career. But at its core the handling of the bikes are broken. That alone ruins this game and leads me to a negative review.In a nutshell, it doesn't matter what bike you are riding, they all handle like a 400 kg cruiser stuck a metre deep in mud. The bikes just understeer like you wouldn't believe, with only the smallest lean angles possible. What this means once you get into races is that the AI will completely out corner you as you attempt to trail brake in vain to create even the tiniest semblance of cornering ability; utterly in disbelief as to how many gears you'll need to drop to not end upside down in the kitty litter off the asphalt. Even the rear brake won't help you out in tight bends. So racing is a no-go, and even more so as the AI will run straight into the back of you, often within mere seconds of the race starting. If by chance you do get ahead of the AI, they'll simply hit the "I win" button and breeze right pass you on the straights with what appears to be a healthy dose of NOS. Even tweaking the bike settings didn't appear to do much except upset the stability of the bike under braking and acceleration so your only option is to drop the difficulty and hope the AI are too busy fighting each other so you can slip down the inside of a corner.Then we have the career mode which is split up into 4 tiers, but tbh I don't know why they bothered as within each tier is simply a long list of career events with a certain bike type like "American Litre Bikes" or "Naked 765's". In past Ride games the vast selection of career events offered you a great choice so if you felt like riding a certain type of bike you could scroll through all the available events to find one you liked. Not so anymore. Now you are simply locked to the current event in the list. Each event requires you to complete the previous one, so you must do them in the exact order they appear, even if you really don't feel like using that certain type of bike for the current event. So the whole career mode just feels like a chore. I finished the first Act, saw the format continued for the next act and sighed. Just why would they do this?!!Also visually the game is lacking in texture details. The track surface in particular just looks very grey and bland with only the occasional tyre marks in braking zones to break up the visual eyesore.The best thing I can say about this game is that the engine sounds are pretty good and riding side by side another bike you can hear the metal scraping as you touch bodywork panels which is nice but that's about it.There's simply no reason to buy this game. The woeful handling will put you off in 10 minutes of playing the game. Buy Ride 4 instead if you haven't and feel like 2 wheel racing.Really wish I had refunded this.

_childDocuments_.review: Only reviewing because some other reviews decided to put people in boxes here:As someone with multiple top 10 times in Ride 4 (all assists off and on highest physics setting) AND someone who frequents actual, real-life motorcycle riding on tracks in A-class track days and events....this game is unresponsive and downright ♥♥♥♥♥♥ - the braking marks are inconsistent at best, trail-braking makes this even worse, when you actually FOR ONCE are able to slow down enough for the corners it feels like snail-pace and boring (and sometimes all of a sudden you're going too slow and cut into the grass?), there is literally no concept or feeling of carrying speed through a corner whatsoever (so much so it's not even very easy to distinguish corners are fast, medium or slow...) Exit grip is just stupidly easy to find, the auto-pickup of the bike on exit makes the actual input from the player's controller exaggerate the movement even more which completely ruins any hope of carrying speed through (why would I want to sit back and let the game lift the bike for me?), can't put even the slightest bit of throttle down after the apex of a corner without being sent off the track in the opposite direction....the list goes on. Not even mentioning the state of the cringe voice overs, irrelevant cut scenes, horrible facial models, erratic behaviour of controller inputs within the menus......and this is from someone who tries very hard to be a fan of this series, I'm an even bigger fan of irl motorcycle track riding both on tv and in my own hobby (competitively riding both 600cc and 1000cc) around 3 local racetracks.There's nothing "pro" about this thing? Entry is ♥♥♥♥ (layman's: Leaning is vague and braking is dull throughout the entire braking pressure applied) Exit is boring and crap (layman's: Acceleration is easy yet unreadable oddly enough?) If these principles were applied to real motorcycle riding then it wouldn't be nearly as exhilarating and it probably wouldn't even be a sport anymore...there's absolutely no room for finesse and accurate use of the momentum, throttle and brakes, it sucks.All my question marks in this review describe the game exactly, the entire time felt like one massive question mark, there's no feedback from the bike underneath you whatsoever which sounds strange but Ride 4 achieved it....But I think overall what applies to most of these reviews is: Instead of attacking the fellow players of the game for their opinions, give yours and that's that. (There's a reason the reviews are mixed)

_childDocuments_.review: I mean this in the best way possible - Ride 5 makes me want to play old school Gran Turismo.That's definitely the vibe they're going for here and I think it's the right move. Actually I hope they lean into it even more if the series continues. With the Moto GP series providing the career-focused motorsport experience, Ride should really look into emulating early Gran Turismo even further. Right now the spread of bikes is decent, but certainly weighted to sportbikes in that 2017-2023 window (how many Fireblades do we really need?). Some of the best fun had in the GT series is thrashing the weird Kei cars and econoboxes around race tracks. There's room for that here. Heck let's add some minimotos. More retro bikes too! Not just for the sake of padding the count, but for adding variety and stuff that the playerbase might be more familiar with. Right now KTM RC390, CFMOTO 450SS, and Yamaha R3 are three of the most popular entry-level bikes for new riders. None of them are in Ride 5. If Milestone could capture that broad-spectrum GT2 feel in a future game, I think people would stop clamoring for a open-world free mode - which  is very much a "be-careful-what-you-wish-for" request. The age of festival games came and went for a reason.
