_childDocuments_.review: Put almost 200 hours in ride 4 and fell in love with it. It definitely had its flaws but I was looking forward to the sequel for improvements. After playing motogp for an hour, I got worried the physics would carry over into Ride 5 and sure enough, it does. The bikes just feel like they are riding on rails. In a bike sim I would expect to be able to lean too far into a corner and be punished for it, i.e., lose traction to the front wheel but no...instead it just greets you with ridiculous oversteer where slowing down doesn't help and you just continue your giant parabola off the track. The improvements from ride 5 include, the braking, more realistic traction under acceleration, the perception of speed is vastly improved from ride 4, and lastly the bike classes make more sense. 600cc vs 1000cc actually has a tactile difference in weight and power vs ride 4 with 600cc just being slower. Milestone took the criticism of ride 4 being to hard to the full extent and made the handling easy for the masses which completely ruins the experience for me. Who wants to ride around tracks at a safe pace?? It's a racing game not a life sim. I want my butt to pucker not have it pampered driving on training wheels. Haven't bought a game for full price in years and I regret paying full price for this one.

_childDocuments_.review: It seems Milestone still haven't made their focus on quality AI in Ride 5. It is definitely more about getting your yah-yahs with drooly shots of licenced bikes, razzing your dream bike around scenic tracks, and experiencing some, to-be-fair, good simulated riding. Though, the above focus of the game gives it a cheesiness, that seems to appeal more to the flashy, mid-life crisis rider, who is probably more familiar with your local cafe car park, buying ACF-50 by the pound for their - less than 10k miles - 2023 "Panigal-é".The announcer for example.. it borderline feels like dirty talk, when he starts talking about "eras of racing", spitting out this nonsense that just makes you feel like throwing up in your mouth a bit - and you cant skip it, which feels almost like borderline abuse. Also side note: Why no subtitles? - Very lazy to those with accessibility issues..As you continue in the game, this "style over function" becomes more apparent, where for example AI never actually register where you are. You can be infront of one, slam on the anchors and BAM! Here comes Lenny, rear ending you at full throttle, throwing you off your bike like a flailing fish, all the while him staying on, and riding off into the sunset. They also dont get affected by sim settings, set all your aids off, and the AI still stay as straight as a board at all conditions with not a care in the world. This makes you pretty much fearful of ever turning off rewinds, or upping their difficulty setting under sim conditions.The unfortunate thing is that the game relies heavily on AI to get your fun out of it. Online is not a thing, you'll find a couple games going at once. Coupled with this, everyone seems to LOVE the full aided setup (ABS, TCS, and other clicky abbreviated electronic jargon), which really turns matches into a dull repetition of full aid riders being always at the front, and simulation riders at the back.The final little thing that bugs me is there is no damage system.All in all though, if you can look past the above, and are looking for more of a casual racing game to focus on the bikes, good graphics, good customisation with the livery editor, and the fun in learning simulated riding, it is a good contender.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game alot. I played every Ride game and this is by far the most fun i've ever had in any Ride game. Ride 4 was good at the beginning aswell, but then the physics got changed up after a few patches and since then the game was not as enjoyable anymore, sadly. I never really liked the Ride 4 physics after they nerfed it.But anyway, now onto Ride 5. The most important thing in any racing game are obviously the physics.The new physics feel amazing, better than ever. At the beginning it may be difficoult to feel the front, but after an hour or so you will improve more and more, and it will progressivley get more fun the more time you put into it.The bikes feel planted and they have some weight to them, the rear is not floating around like in Ride 4, you have a very good understanding of what the bikes are doing. You can now no longer hammer down both brakes while going full lean angle into a corner, the game is taking on a much more realistic approach than previous titles, wich i like.Every bike has different characteristics, every bike feels different. Slower bikes are also very fun and dont feel ,,slow'' like in previous games, if that makes sense to explain.They absolutley nailed the sense of speed in Ride 5 and thats a reason why lower cc bikes feel quicker now.Here are some points what i like about the game summarized:• Dynamic weather• Realistic bike prices• Race creator mode• Improved physics• Improved graphics, the bike models look stunning• Improved engine sounds, much better than in Ride 4• Improved AI • Improved rider animations, the movement looks very smooth and dynamic.• Better presentation of the career mode, menus and UI.In summary i can say that Ride 5 has been a good upgrade from Ride 4 and i do recommend it for everyone who has a passion for motorcycles and likes to test their skills on the virtual track.

Bikes are more planted to the grount and that floaty/hovercraft feeling I had in Ride 4 is gone. Different bike classes handle according to speed, inerita and weight of the bike. There are however some issues. One is a feeling of big input deadzone. Especially superbikes feel to have delayed input. Another issue is that some bikes (especially Race Modified) feel very understeery and it is almost impossible to turn into corner ifnyour speed is above 100 kph. Standard tire also have way more grip that slicks what is very bad and confusing.Another improvement is grpahics with volumetric clouds. Everything looks more realistic and not as cartoonish as it was i. Ride 4.Sounds were also improved. Some bikes sound so good that itnis super enjoyable to accelerate out of corner. The biggest negative of Ride 5 is amount of bikes and tracks. For such game I expected to have more tracks and bikes. Despite the amount is still impressive it is not enough for Ride 5. Also promised online endurance is very limited - its just maximum 60 minutes. Damn its not even endurance…AI is fine. Not as annoying as in MotoGP23 but does spoil the fun racing against it. Last positive thing is that game really feels polished with minor bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really freaking good. It is not a Ride 4 clone. I don't have a lot of hours yet but I just absolutely LOVE motorcycles and my Honda VTX 1800 is almost my daily driver. I wanted to get this review out while its on sale cuz I'm telling you, its a steal. This game actually has so many subtle things about it that make it incredibly immersive as a rider myself that I can just appreciate so much.Graphics\Immersion: First andf or most, wow. I use a RTX 4070 with a 1920x1080 monitor. I cranked the graphics to the max and then was even able to run it at 3840x2610 and just made it even better. The reflections, the weather, the light, its the newest game so of course its gonna look better right? What I wasn't ready for was how realistic the movements of your driver are. You  stack that on top of the graphics and jeez, your almost there. Like I said, I ride my bike ALOT and when I saw my rider move his but around in the seat down the straightaway after a set of tight turns, I felt that. No lie, I 95% would have done that there because you gotta find your seat sometimes. If you get bumped, your guy looks  exactly like you would, body does the wave as you hang on to the bike. Hitting your max speed down a straight away and watching your ride just gripping through those beyond highway speeds as the camera shakes ever so much with the intense wind. You just really feel it. Its just amazingly helpful for the immersion and I have not seen better.  Game-play: The  career mode  is really cool. It offers a great sense of progression without the sense of a burden somehow. I actually found myself turning lap after lap after lap on Monza time attack just so I could get  better. No other racing game would you ever catch me doing Time Attacks more than I absolutely had to. Its just fun to get better and learn the track and breaking points. It has a button press to enter rewind mode so if you suck or if the AI gets too aggressive, it has a generous amount of rewind time so you can back your self up and give it another go from where you want. It even has a little slow motion effect for a few seconds while you can ease back into the action instead of you just having to have the controls already pressed when you hit Resume. There is a bad, when you wreck or fall off or what ever takes you down, your rider rag dolls kinda but it just looks...off. Its a little immersion breaking but no more than hitting the rewind button when it happens.AI: (on  Medium) These dudes don't give one care about you or your feelings. If you are slow and in their way, you will be moved. I find this irritating at times but only usually  when I fall off the pace or  make a mistake, they just have a hard time avoiding me. Honestly tho, with the rewind, I can see what I did wrong, correct it, learn from it and not get hit again so it, so I don't blame them as much as myself.  I don't know how much you can make an AI on this bike react without just messing up the whole field or immersion, ya know?  So I am ok with the AI. Online: I'll update this when I do it but for now, you can download liveries other people have created and put it on your bike.Customization: Its better than I thought. There are so many brands and variations of gear to wear from visor colors, helmet types all the way down to the gloves and boots. You buy these with in game currency you earn from participating in races. Your bikes are pretty basic, you can purchase rims, remove mirrors and the plate and such. However, you unlock paint jobs via purchasing the bike with the paint job. I tend to find the online liveries better tho, I have yet to try and construct one. Physics: This is a "SIMCADE" type game. I find it much more enjoyable than Ride 4. There are also a ton of assist options  you can manipulate to help you race and get into the groove, learn the track, braking points and your bike. You can easily turn these off one buy one and some even have levels of effectiveness so you don't can ease out of the assist vs just going "cold turkey". On top of their awesome and effective assist systems, they will reward your progression away from these system with money from racing. Each degree of assists you take off, will net you more money per race. It will even break it down after the race for you to show you what you are getting and why you are not using for example, off track assistance that makes it easier to control the bike if you run off.  We have rewind tho so I find that better.This is the best time to buy this game. I watched reviews and was on the fence and now its my favorite bike game ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Things I look for in a Sim (even a survey sim like this) aside from realism are fidelity and feel of the equipment. I like feeling personally connected. Ride 4 definitely did that.Something that really breaks that feeling for me is having a "Career" or little virtual dude to manage and play house with. Ride 4's "Career" was basically just a progression, so no big deal. I certainly don't want some player-character talking to me and saying trite and vacuous stuff like it's a movie. I don't want to be in some person's head as they monologue. Not in a Sim. I want that person to get off my bike. Out of my garage. Leave and don't come back.I feel it's unfortunate that the good idea fairy comes around and this stuff gets pushed. Maybe it's not a big deal and it's actually a selling point for younger players. It's fine for something like GTA or Forza Horizons. Kills a Sim for me. I didn't even stick around for long enough to see if you could turn it off. I just imagined I'd be getting text messages from the mechanic or some love interest or whatever. "Good luck today! XOXO" Refunded.What I'd like to see is more Sim. Head tracking support? Make it so damn good they start making dedicated handlebar controllers like they do with wheels.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel there should be more for $60 than just a graphical update and a physics change, and even these qualities aren't finished yet. There are many graphical bugs spanning from flickering textures, lighting popping in and out, and overall poor optimization that results in low fps (sometimes sub 60fps on 1080ti and 5600x). I do think the motogp physics they transferred to this game are better than what ride 4 offers. The braking actually feels good, and with brake upgrades you actually have brakes to slow down. Improved stability on curbs is welcomed and the collision physics are much more forgiving (unless you get rammed from behind mid corner at mach 5 thanks bots). Acceleration and sense of speed are more exhilarating and realistic, as they are in the motogp games. *The major problem with the physics is leaning. comparing to ride 4, I feel like I'm trying to turn a semi truck into every corner in this game. It takes too long to transfer body weight and initiate the turn and you can just forget trying to set up body weight on the edge of the seat before a corner. When I am turning into a corner and trail braking, that should reduce the radius of my turn but the bike stays on a uniform path and that doesn't feel right. I run wide almost every corner and when I do miraculously get it right, giving power on corner exit stands the bike up itself and makes me run wide anyways. While it is realistic the bike wants to stand up on power, it is too exaggerated and makes corner exit unpredictable (if I give it too much gas on exit just make it spin the rear out). The bike list is mainly the same as ride 4 minus some bikes from dlc which is understandable, but why remove entire categories of bikes?? I can live with no supermotos (rip dank wheelies) but there are no 300-400cc 4 stroke bikes. No Ninja 400, ZX4R, or even previous bikes like the R3 or KTM RC390. There are not enough variety of bikes on release, and I think we'd all like to play around with older machines from the 70's and 80's as well (give me the OG Kawasaki H2 pls). New maps are cool: Blue wave is pog, Sonoma is perfect ty, Autopolis is cool with many variants, and lemons is neato (90% of the ride 4 maps are here too). IMO the story mode is cool idea but done poorly and production seems rushed. The garage setup is cool but the animations for prepping a race are a bit wonky and the voice overs are trying to tell a story that's not well established. Overall game looks good, plays ok, and wait for sale.+ New bikes like R7, RS660, 2021+ models+ New tracks are good+ Acceleration and braking physics+ Stability on curbs (I don't combust on touching a pixel of kerb anymore yay)+ Extra assists for non-gamer irl riders should bring more ppl into the game+ Graphics look good- Not enough variety of bikes- Leaning physics need rework (pls make trail braking work and give more control over throttle/lean)- No 300-400cc class whyyy (give me RC390)- Seems like the additions of this game e.g., physics, graphics, etc. could of come as a 2.0 update to ride 4- Almost all playable content is the same as ride 4* I would change this to recommend if the leaning gets reworked

_childDocuments_.review: As a frequent player who enjoys spending my evenings honing my skills and shaving that 0.0010 off my favorite track to compete with other passionate racers online, I have to express my disappointment.Following the announcement that "Ride 5" was launching this August, I was incredibly excited about the potential for new tracks and bikes. I attempted to contact Milestone to share my enthusiasm for the launch and provide suggestions for improvements, but I received no response – not even an email acknowledgment. I assumed, like many others might, that they were likely receiving valuable feedback from racers and experienced riders who had spent thousands of hours on the previous game.Sadly, I was mistaken. The game was an absolutely gut-wrenching disappointment. If it weren't for the graphics, I would think I was playing a motorcycle game from the early 2000s. This isn't merely a step in the wrong direction.. it feels almost like a mockery of the previous titles. I've also tried the MotoGP games, which seem to have faced the same fate. Many previous reviewers have detailed the game's shortcomings, and I find myself in full agreement.While I usually leave reviews to the "professionals" (gamers with thousands of hours of playtime), I felt compelled to write this in hopes that Milestone takes notice. Please get back on track and deliver the quality games that we've come to love. You've done it before... I believe you can do it again!But sadly, I had to request a refund this time.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly believe most of the negative reviews about this game's physics are coming from people who were turned off by the tutorial and didn't dive into the settings. When the game starts out, it introduces itself assuming you're brand new to the series and is very heavy-handed with its driver assists. It almost feels like the game is playing itself and your inputs are a suggestion- the game seriously holds you back and fights you for control of things like throttle, braking, and even steering correction. After that, you are also run through a bunch of unskippable cutscenes and introductions to the basic career mechanics... This intro is the worst part of the game. Its a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and I wish for series veterans you could just skip this from the start. However, after the first hour once the game opens up, if you go in and dive into the settings to turn off all the driving assists and turn down a bunch of your bike automatics like ABS and TC, the game feels way way better. The driving mechanics are just as fun as Ride 4, but the AI feels way less suicidal blindly rear-ending you off the road chasing its own lines. Its a small iterative step for the series, but after a couple of years, I think its a worthy successor. If you still love Ride 4, this isn't a massive leap that demands you upgrade, but it is a tiny bit prettier and has some small nice QoL upgrades.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, a RIDE game that actually feels like trying to ride fast.... You have to break BEFORE the apex!! You can't just get on and go fast if you're a die hard RIDE 4 fan. I'll be blunt about it, the games expensive as hell for what they offer at the moment, their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ move of 4 days early access to console.. (I know I still won't let it go ;) ) I intrinsically dislike milestone and hold quite a bias against saying anything good about them. BUT they got a game that feels like it has so much potential going forward and let's face it those of us that play RIDE we will inevitably rack up x00s of hours into the damn thing anyway.There are some severe lack of feedback issues on controllers under braking at the moment, might be something possibly remediable by steam controller settings and the Haptics being cranked for the left trigger. But as for the riding, well people say the bikes unresponsive etc etc go watch motoGP or SBK or MotoAmerica, not often will you find anyone brake at the apex but start to slow down at the "braking markers" you know the 300 200 100m signs that denote a corner approaches slow down and be ready etc etc Here are a few words of wisdom from far greater men than myself; Slow is smooth, smooth is fast.SLOW in FAST out.TLDR; I think it's an overpriced pos for the level of initial content re bike numbers wise and selection in terms of displacement, would I recommend it 5% yes I would.Plenty of the initial issues have actually been fixed!

_childDocuments_.review: Not without its flaws, but pretty good overall. If you're looking to ride a ton of cool motorcycles that both look and sound great, and go through the campaign the game offers or do custom races and set new lap times, you'll likely get your money's worth. The AI will just run through you sometimes, and the difficulty they provide can vary wildly with the same settings from track to track. The handling feels pretty good with the assists off, even if slightly forgiving at times, and you'll feel a difference between the bikes. The campaign is lengthy and offers a lot of different races that give a lot of variety, constantly changing bike classes and types and going through different tracks, though the unskippable narrated scenes can be hit or miss depending on how you feel about them, and personally I don't think they add much value.Overall, if you're mostly looking to ride your favourite bikes in some cool tracks, you'll get plenty of that here, and the experience is fun enough to recommend for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Great driving mechanics and physics let down by without doubt the worst AI I've ever seen in a racing game. They simply refuse to acknowledge your presence on the track, and as a result every single race is determined solely by whether an AI rider randomly decides that the tarmac currently under your wheels actually belongs to them. Think I'm exaggerating? This is how bad the AI are - you will witness multiple bike pile-ups at the starting grid so often it ceases to even be a noteworthy event. Your position in the race for the first lap will be decided by whether the riders in front of you actually bother to accelerate or not. Your survival of the first lap will be determined solely by whether there happens to be an AI anywhere near you on any corner. You are not even safe on the straights, rubberbanding will launch AI riders directly into your back wheel at practically double the speed even possible at that section of the track, even if you took the last corner perfectly and are sitting right in someone's slipstream. Buy it only if you can accept that the game is only fun online, and there are not always online lobbies available to race in.

_childDocuments_.review: This game falls short of expectations. What baffles me is how it manages to regress from its predecessor, Ride 4, which offered decent AI, physics, upgrades, and other essential features. Let's start with the AI, which is disappointingly lackluster. The so-called "difficulty slider" might as well be labeled a useless gimmick. It's either far too easy or ridiculously difficult. Adjusting it to, say, 80 out of 120 (a peculiar choice of range) results in AI opponents who seem disinterested in competing. They offer no challenge, allowing me to effortlessly pull ahead by 40 or 50 seconds, which simply feels wrong.Turning up the difficulty doesn't solve the issue either. The AI suddenly becomes faster on straights, as if they've engaged an imaginary seventh gear straight out of a Fast and Furious movie. Endurance races are similarly underwhelming, with AI opponents seemingly unaffected by fuel consumption compared to the player. The disparity in fuel efficiency, despite identical conditions, is reminiscent of driving a 2014 Prius versus a sports car.The bike physics contribute to the overall disappointment. Instead of being engaging or challenging, they often feel erratic and unpredictable. Even on gentle turns, the bike can inexplicably lose traction or refuse to respond, leaving me feeling as though I'm riding a stretched-out Hayabusa. Wheelies and stoppies lack the finesse and realism one would expect.Despite my initial hopes, this game has failed to impress. Even after getting gold on the first two tiers, I find little motivation to progress further. While I haven't ventured into online racing yet, I'm not optimistic about its quality either. This game had the potential to offer a compelling motorcycle racing experience, but sadly, it falls short in almost every aspect. I hope this game can be better thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: RIDE 5 has arrived and it has been well worth the wait. 20 riders on track and a more competitive A.I for the stock and smaller classes, a revamped dynamic weather system for quick races and endurance modes to change the complexion of the race in an instant.I'm much more impressed with the new physics here in RIDE 5, a closer representation of the MotoGP games with some RIDE 4 elements really allows players to pick up and play both games seamlessly without much adjustment.The brand new race creator mode is a game changer for many, allowing you to customise a full championship to your desired liking. You can change the A.I's rider gear and bike to fit the style of your vision, sadly I didn't see an option to customise the A.I's names which would the experience just that much more immersive.Layer limits increased for our livery designers out there and the ability to customise and change the liveries of all BMW bikes are a blessing!There are additional tracks such as Almeria, Sonoma Raceway, Le Mans and Autopolis but sadly Phillip Island, Imatra and the iconic Macau didn't make the jump to RIDE 5.Finally I'm really enjoying RIDE 5 and I highly recommend, if you would like to see my full video review check here:

_childDocuments_.review: +++ EDIT (will be updated with new issues) +++[EDIT – 2023-10-20]Sooo, they cut content that was in previous RIDE games – like Supermotos – and are now adding it back as paid DLC... just sad.I personally don't care for Supermotos but it still sucks. However, the DLC also adds scooters for the first time in RIDE and some people (not me) have been long waiting for that.[EDIT – 2023-08-31](  ):They confirmed they're gonna bring back tracks and bikes (copy-paste) that have been in previous RIDE games as DLC, like the Stelvio track and Suzuki Gixxer K5...[EDIT – forgot date][FIXED according to patch notes] So, endurance races make up way too many career events AND THEY ARE BUGGED! Sometimes, the clock runs out, but the race keeps going infinitely until you lap the rider that the game sometimes displays as first position. You can also try to cross the finish line, reverse back over it and cross it again. GG Milestone. No quality control...Some events tell you to un-equip slick tires because the weather doesn't allow them...but the schedule shows no rain and during the race, the AI uses slicks -> WTF? Also the slicks have a rain version with profile anyway, so this makes 0 sense. And sometimes, you won't be able to equip slick on the bike again without restarting the game.Also, tire wear makes 0 difference. I kept riding Interlagos for several laps in the rain with both tires at 0% and red, but the bike handles exactly the same.The AI, especially the rivals rubberband so much, it's ridiculous. You can be several seconds ahead and in the last lap, the AI suddenly overtakes you on the finish straight -> WTFI'll still have fun with this game, since there's no real competition, but these practices are just scummy.+++ EDIT END +++##########Bought every RIDE game so far and don't regret buying this one, either.RIDE 5 likely has some of your favorite bikes and tracks and I spent WAY more time in RIDE than any other motorcycle game, ergo I'll keep supporting the series so they keep making these games.For me, Milestone – even though they are far from perfect and there's lots of copy/paste involved in their (bi/tri-)annual releases – basically make the only playable motorcycle simcade games that feel somewhat realistic. Isle of Man TT 3  is decent now, but the bikes in RIDE 5 feel WAY less wobbly/janky and much smoother; also goes for the rider animations which are terrible in IoM TT.##########- The HUD: Please make the gear number blink red when the RPM is about to redline (that way it's easy to see in the corner of the eye). Also, add a gear indicator to the HUD in 1st person cameras (pretty sure, RIDE 4 had that?), some bikes' gear indicators are hard to see or they don't have one. I don't see a reason not to offer this feature.- Why do we have to buy the same bike several times to get a different original livery? Just unlock all liveries for the owned bikes. Sucks especially for bikes you get as winning prize and can't choose the first livery. .- Let us test ride bikes before purchase to give us a feel and for immersion? Even if it just loads one specific, same track regardless of the bike? E.g. Mugello. Or, at least, let us turn it on and rev the the engine?- (more of a suggestion for RIDE 6, I guess) A garage we can walk in? The new 'walk around bike' feature is cool but how about a full garage where you can display a couple bikes and walk to different stations for mechanics/setup, paint/livery, etc. Maybe even a dyno (I guess the telemetry is calculated by the game anyway so might be 'easy' to add)?- (probably out of the scope of this game series) A free roam area, maybe with the beginning of roads that lead to the different tracks/countries. Maybe even a whole game like a 'Forza Horizon' with motorcycles ('The Crew' has terrible bike physics where they just steer like a car, before anyone suggests playing that)##########- Season pass (didn't buy) is too expensive for a bunch of basically copy/paste bikes that are similar to existing ones apart from the year, or bikes that were included in previous games. At least there now is a season pass on PC for those who were gonna buy the packs anyway. Might get it on a steep discount.- Why not finally put ALL the good tracks in the newest release? The new additions are cool, but where is e.g. 'The Snake'? As long as the Nordschleife keeps being included, I'm gonna buy every RIDE game, though. Wish they had the license for the Isle of Man TT, too... - Apart from some lighting, the graphics seem pretty much a copy/paste of RIDE 4 – I expected more after 3 years...- Some copy/paste is apparent in bugs. Example: (Not sure what exactly triggers it) Sometimes, when you ride over curbs, the curb/gravel/grass sound keeps playing until you ride over a curb and back onto the track, again. Maybe it happens when you ride over a curb and then rewind and the game doesn't 'notice' that the curb sound should be turned off?##########-/+ The bike handling is vastly different from RIDE 4. Bikes are easier to handle but feel less realistic. I appreciate that e.g.  the bumps at the Nordschleife don't instantly make you crash anymore (tried a ton of suspension setups), because the bike kinda sticks to the track, but also diminishes realism elsewhere. It's easy to get used to and I still enjoy it, though.-/+ There's only 'naked' ad 'sports' bikes in RIDE 5, I think. No cruisers, supermoto (no supermoto tracks either) or adventure bikes. I personally don't miss any of those, since I'm only into sporty bikes, but others will be left disappointed.-/+ I feel like endurance races shouldn't be mandatory in career mode. I don't like having to race a track/bike I don't enjoy for 20 minutes just to progress the career. Should only be an extra category to unlock for extra rewards after clearing a part of the career.-/+ Fewer customization options compared to previous releases. No aftermarket handlebars, triple clamps, etc., just chain and rims can be painted, apart from the livery. I personally don't care that much but it was a nice feature to have and after all, RIDE is marketed as a motorcycle playground/make-it-your-own-experience...##########+ Sounds are improved compared to RIDE 4. Most bikes sound more realistic and less like an '80s synthesizer, even though it's still audible in the background for some bikes. Could still be better but there's so many bikes and this game probably doesn't have the budget of a 'Forza Horizon' and the likes.+ Career mode feels like less of a chore and you can purchase more bikes, sooner. The 'story' bits, rivalries, cutscenes and photos could be regarded as cringy, but you can skip them. At least they tried some more immersion than just a string of races for a career.+ You can restart endurance races from the last pit stop entry. Can save you if you messed up the pit stop. Which I did in the first endurance race in career mode and was about to complain until I saw the option...+ Menus look pretty good and put an emphasis on your selected bike's presentation

_childDocuments_.review: ______________________________________________________________UPDATE SEPT 1: ______________________________________________________________So I didn't give up on this game, I put some work into re-calibrating my entire MotoSim and got the game feeling pretty good now. I'll admit, I've actually never played a Ride game with a controller... ( the way milestone intended).  So to be fair, it's not Milestone's fault that their game didn't come perfectly tuned to my custom MotoSim I built for it.I think Milestone's biggest mistake is the two bikes you start out with; a 1991 RGV-250 and a 2020 GSX-R 1000R (gifted if you played Ride 4).  I immediately went for the GSXR and the thing just will not steer. It runs wide with any amount of suspension tuning you do. Litre bikes are heavier, I agree, but not THIS boaty. Any bit of tuning you try and it still feels terrible. This was a complete buzzkill for Ride 5 and I *almost refunded it before the 2 hour mark of play.When I turned enough laps to purchased a 600 (R6), the game had a COMPLETELY different feel. So, I bought another bike and another bike and another bike, and noticed that the play-ability is dramatically different from bike to bike. The gas-on gas-off in corners feels pretty close to my actual R6 with everything tuned.So, I'm going to change my original negative review of Ride 5 to a positive one. If you're just starting out, my advice: leave the GSXR in the garage, earn some points to get a better mid-weight bike, do all the upgrades, tune the suspension, and I promise you'll actually come around to this game. Next up, we need VR and a Track Builder in Ride 6. Looking at you Milestone... ;)_____________________________________________________________FIRST IMPRESSIONS REVIEW:_____________________________________________________________Sighhh. I was so excited for the release of this game. I NEEDED this game to be good.  I designed a full-on leaning motorcycle simulator that I have been calibrating/tuning for the last year to Ride 4 and MotoGP 22/23. As a gamer/designer that has actually raced motorcycles, I’ve done everything in my power to make the simulator experience as realistic as possible, but the problem is in the game physics/mechanics themselves; they are just inherently laggy and non-compliant. I was expecting Ride 5 to be the release where they finally get it right… Here’s a marketing quote directly from Milestone:  “Get ready to be blown away by an unprecedented level of realism.”This is not it…This one is worse, much worse. The biggest frustration is the understeering coming into corners. On a real race bike, if you come in hot, you scrub off speed by trail-braking all the way into the apex and then smoothly roll on the throttle from the apex to the exit. It’s the same brake/throttle pattern almost every corner on track. Too much brake you’ll tuck the front, too much throttle and you lose the back; it’s that simple. In Ride 5, It’s seems like as soon as you touch the brakes, the bike runs wide. This is not how bikes work on track Milestone… Please, please fix this! I’d love to share my moto sim publicly one day as a consumer product, but the dream is starting to run wide as well…As far as I'm concerned, this is a BOAT simulator...Milestone, please reach out if you need help/feedback fixing this mess.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so my first review was misplaced because of settings and the bike being quite frankly ass! Tampering with the electroincs pretty much almost removing them all and the game became way better and more fun. It also comes down to the bike, some bikes just go super-wide which is a bit boring in general. Not sure why milestone is on this crusade with understeering bikes. It always have it to some degree but it's acceptable and you get used to it, would I want it fully gone? Absolutely! But there is a trade-off here to feel and fun factor which seem quite balanced. Sound is improved in this game, it's far from perfect and some bikes still sound goofy but there are also some that sound much nicer and brings some immersion. Graphics is hard to tell, Ride 4 already looked so nice but it looks great.I started my career yesterday on stream and it just took a few laps with these weaker crappy bikes until i had a grin on my face and was actually enjoying myself. It was just superfun to ride around these short circuits of Mugello and Oulton Park against the AI, 75% felt like a great starting point if you have some experience and ride the bike non-upgraded. It didn't feel like I was playing against AI, they gave a good but doable challenge and it never felt artificial which I definitely would have noticed since I am sensitive to cheesy computer behaviour. I was immersed in the race and had a blast, the starting bike you get for second place in the tutorial race is wonderful little bike on these short tracks. My current electronics are ABS 3, AW 3, TCS 0, EBS 0, I will try tamper with the other 2 as well maybe I lower them but it felt really nice so far with TC and EBS on low, the bike started to respond a bit better in my opinion.Things I would like to see improved is the sound further, more tracks, normal clothing like jeans jacket, leather jacket, normal jeans etc. Everything feel very race oriented and I saw no Harleys and other such bikes but maybe they are added later. Also motocross would be cool like small 80cc, 125cc, 250cc cross bikes on cross tracks, I can see that being very fun against other players and also against this AI. I see no reason to not do it, there is so much to do with this Ride game but they seem to be holding back. The understeering I think could be fixed further so you can actually take a turn before it feels like your bike is standing still almost. It's very deceiving with the speed you have and how you can take a turn and it's the same in MotoGP 23. The speedometer show 90kmh which is fast the problem is that it feels like 25 kmh and kill the wow factor a bit, luckily this game have great acceleration and sense of speed to compensate so you enjoy the straights a lot when they arrive. Also the side by side switching of the bike could be faster it feels quite heavy compared to Ride 4 which was maybe a tad on the twitchy side but it made it very snappy and fast on tracks like Nordschleife.Overall I think the physics are a bit more enjoyable and stable even though I miss some Ride 4 aspects. The braking seem to be on the easier side, you can floor it in RIde 5 and my memory was that you couldn't do that in Ride 4 without sliding. So from the braking standpoint alone it feels a bit cheap, it is weighed up with the very satisfying lean feel and overall physics of riding. But coming in no matter what speed and just step on the brakes is a bit silly maybe. I don't want MotoGP 23 sensitivity either but something in between, it should be dangerous to push your bike to the limit but it rarely is here because of these forgiving brakes. The difficulty in this game will be calculating your braking distance and lean in early enough at right speed. The rest is not hard, you don't fall over easy on 0 TCS, you rarely slide if not touched or hit dirt etc. With that said the game is excellent fun even with it's problems and a pleasure to play, I rather have easy brakes than somewhat annoying ones like in GP 23 where I had to put saturation on 95% otherwise locked up tires and stoppie arrived instantly. Hopefully further DLC will bring us some cool motorcross tracks and bikes to use. Normal clothes, more bikes both sport and casual boomer bikes etc. Also more tracks, real life country side, city places and so on. Like I said there is so much they can do with this game, only their imagination set the limit.Check out my time with it on stream  I highly recommend it now even after my initial crash n burn review. Thank you Milestones you are on the right path even if your changes are too drastic in some areas and weak in others where it need to be drastic. At least it's not 3 years wait for another version that is good since this is good enough.Edit: Ok now after 29 hours I can honestly say this is the best bike game I have ever played, it is incredibly fun and satisfying to ride these bikes in both third person and first but in first person it sure is something else. Wow what a crazy immersive experience it is and it sucks you in to just keep going. I could not put this game down tonight, I did like 30 laps on Road America and the more I played the more I wanted to play. Thank you Milestones, you really created some magic here with this game. Sure we can discuss understeering being a bit too much at speeds that feel very low on but beside that and some bikes sounding a bit dull and boring compared to others this game is a winner in my eyes. If you're hesitating, reading mixed reviews and believe these people then it's your loss. They are not true in my opinion, lots of hate train mentality towards Milestons in general and people playing 40 minutes and refunding. The game is really really exciting to play, great sense of speed and acceleration, the thrill of riding and being close to a crash is always present when you push these bikes. It's a highly recommended from me and is a must in any gamers library if you enjoy great games in general.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a realistic motorcycle racing sim, do yourself a favor and start playing on the highest difficulty setting, and then also turn off all the assists on your bike (TC, ABS, etc.) On any lower difficulty, the handling is very arcadey and clumsy. With the most realistic settings, this game turns into a highly accurate sim. Anything on a real bike, you can do in Ride 5. You can high side, low side, slide out the front wheel, and feel every shake and rattle in the bike as you accelerate and brake. Even the simulation in rain is spot-on, accurately capturing how wet roads affect grip and cause the bike to steer differently.So far, I am very impressed by the quality of the physics engine, the graphics, and the wide variety of bikes and courses to choose from.

_childDocuments_.review: Anytime I play a new Ride or MotoGP game, there is always a learning curve. I think many with negative reviews may have made a knee-jerk reaction (I felt very clumsy the 1st hour I played, and I was a little concerned). However, the overall PHYSICS ARE WAY MORE SATISFYING than Ride 4. Turn off all rider aids, turn the difficulty to 120%, dial in your bike and get going! The bikes have real weight to them, the kick out is manageable and enjoyable as you get your feel dialed in, and the trail-braking felt VERY REAL to riding my bikes in real life. That "oh ♥♥♥♥" feeling is definitely there when you mess up your braking zone or screw up your line. Now more than ever, smooth is the key. Also, though more challenging, it is great to see that you can't make large, mid-corner adjustments like in R4 without disturbing the chassis in a big way. Big thumbs up for realism in that regard!As far as negatives, the lack of feedback/feel in the front brake is a thing (left trigger haptics). I imagine they will adjust that with a patch soon. Also, the race leaderboard pops up way too often while entering left turn 1 in general. I like to have it, but maybe they can have it appear on the 1st righthand turn so it doesn't interfere with looking through the curve. The bike selection is definitely a little weak at the moment, but that will also improve with DLC. The lack of modern small displacement bikes is a bummer. Where's my KTM RC390, Ninja 400, Ninja ZX4-RR, CFMoto 450SS?! I know most of us race 600s and 1000s online most of the time, but sometimes you want to ride a small bike fast.If you are a big RIDE fan in general, you don't mind putting in some hours to adjust to the new feel, and you understand that games are generally going to need a few community notes and patches to get to 100%, buy it. If you are on the fence, wait for a sale. This feels like the best RIDE game, and it's just getting started.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 5

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a casual player of ride since the first game and this one doesn't disappoint. I used to be significantly more competitive in general back in the first few games, but now just play ride to more or less relax and enjoy some time trials and cool bikes that ill never own. Ride 5 is significantly easier and more enjoyable in my opinion then ride 4. The physics seem more relaxed and it is much easier for me to be smoother then in 4. I will say the first race I was super disappointed, the S1000 felt like a boat and unresponsive with the brakes out of the 60s, it was a struggle bus. The next race I turned all assist off and put to manual and what a difference I could actually control the bike. I am overall much happier with the physics of this game then the previous. And yes it feels like a video game, but I kind of expect it to be like that. It reminds me more of horizon then assetto on the video game scale of realism. But I think it is literally impossible to make a motorcycle game feel like real life. You can't cram the full body experience of riding a bike into a controller. But this does a great job overall especially when I want to just chill and enjoy bikes. The AI is actually easy on easy which is awesome so you can chill and ride with the group instead of being hammer down like in 4. A game breaker for me that 5 does a great job on is the sound of the bikes. Huge improvement over 4, the 4 cylinders actually scream like I want them too. Twins like the R7 and TL1000 have the low rumble that pulls through the high rpm like I expect.  But will say kinda upset with the 3 cylinders like the mt-09 and trident 660 don't have that wail i've heard in real life they seem muffled. The Brutale 800 sounds like a 3 cylinder should though. So other then that sound is much much better in Ride 5.  My only real disappointment with Ride 5 is the selection of motorcycles. They have some great bikes and the TL1000 is back so i'm happy about that, but there seems to be a huge amount missing. Gone are the 300s and 400s, and why not some 650s. The entry level and mid level bikes are missing in favor of the 600s and up, not a huge variety of the smaller bikes. Adventure, touring, dual sport, I could go forever there are so many good bikes that are gone. I could write pages on pages of bikes that would be fun to have, that even the previous Rides had. So i'm hoping like crazy they go hard with packs and DLC to bring more to the game. I still believe Ride 5 is a great game and will leave a positive review but some more variety and larger selection would be amazing.Oh and prices of bikes, gear, and upgrades are actually realistic which is amazing. Slip on exhaust 800, full system is 1500 which is realistic. Boots 400, helmet 800, all similar pricing to things I've bought in real life. The bikes actually match what I would expect to pay for one new. 11-13k for a 600/750 13-20k for a 1000 like 9k for an R7. The SRAD is 10-12 unlike in ride 4 it was 200k. Super happy with the realistic pricing compared to ride 4. Overall really happy with the game. Oh and cool they brought back split screen.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Just wow. They finally fixed so much from Ride 4. For instance, in Ride 4, you could be going the same speed as other riders. Using the same bike, same rider positioning and taking the same turn, but you would go out way wider than they would. The rider wouldn't go down all the way and the AI would zoom past you. You were taking turns at 60 and they we're blasting through at 90. It was ridiculous. In Ride 5, they revamped all of that. The rider now gets lower, more realistically. You can maintain speed through your turns. I used to race motorcycles. Amateur stuff, nothing pro level at all, but I can personally tell you Ride 5 is way more realistic now. If you get any of the Ride games, it needs to be this one. Bravo Milestone. You finally achieved realism.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure what people are on about. The game feels different to ride 4, but that's a GOOD thing. It feels much better. Those complaining about braking don't understand how brakes work on a motorcycle, and in Ride 5 they work so much better than 4 if you understand how physics work. If you don't manage your weight transfer correctly, bike isn't going to brake correctly. Content is a lot of carry over yes, but that's how racing games work for the most part (look at forza...) they've got some new bikes as well, and most DLC content from the previous game, I'm excited to see what more gets added. But so far the complains that originally had me hold off on buying this game are silly, it feels miles ahead of Ride 4 as far as realism. But it does have a steeper learning curve to get the hang of it.

The graphics are nice, but the level of detail on the tracks doesn't seem to have been improved one bit, so they really don't look great.The bikes look better than ever, but i noticed that even with the "improvements to chain physics" the chain STILL doesn't actually move in accordance to the wheel. _childDocuments_.review: Ride 5 is without a doubt my favourite in the series. They've really nailed it this time around in my opinion. The game is involving and enjoyable. You can find yourself really getting into each race, noticing the AI competitors names and cursing them when they outbrake you into turn one. I've found myself more than once calling out "Gunther" for his quite frankly poor riding etiquette and crazy overtakes...The AI itself is pretty fantastic. Vastly improved from the previous games of which I've played all (including 2, although not on steam). Maybe I'm, giving the AI too much credit but they do seem to try and outbrake you when you are alongside and will run wide on corners in an attempt to overtake you, at which point if you take the right line you can slip up the inside. Not experience this in previous ride games! Normally they all follow one set line and don't differentiate from each other. This one is a fair bit different. I've also noticed that certain AI players seem to have their specialities, such as late braking, faster mid-corner, etc. Again, this may just be me giving them more credit but it's certainly something I've experienced. Where the AI does fall down a touch is their aggressiveness. I have the AI set at 80% and the "pushing" setting. They do seem to (a lot) rear end you? It can be a bit annoying.. Sometimes the AI rear end you and have absolutely no chance of actually making the corner, so I'm unsure of what the intent was. For example, lets say for example you are doing a race and your bike excels on corner entry but the mid-corner speed is down a touch on other bikes. The AI will simply push you off if you are mid-corner, it's a bit annoying!The sound from the bikes is the most accurate to date. They've really nailed the majority of bikes and it adds a lot to the game itself. You can actually hear the difference in the crossplane engines as opposed to traditional inline-4s. Endurance races are a fantastic addition to the game, strategically selecting tyres and pit times really adds something special to the game and makes the 20mins fly by. The bikes feel accurate to life, in my experience. Bikes I've ridden in real life feel somewhat like they do in the game. Obviously it's a huge difference, a controller compared to a set of clip ons but it's certainly not miles away.The game itself is well optimised, I believe, I'm running a 6950xt and a 7800X3D which runs the game fine, as I would expect for the hardware. At 4K, ultra everything I'm still around 100fps.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; If you are interested in bikes, and in general more sporty bikes and sporty track riding you will absolutely love this gameFull review:Ride 5 tries to improve on its predecessors by trying to balance out riding physics and general improvements that earlier entries missed out on. It is extremely hard already for driving games to nail the feeling of driving while still being accessible for newbies, for a riding sim, like ride 5 even more difficult. If you are coming from earlier versions you might need to get used to some changes in simulation but in the end the translation from controller to on-screen action really hits the nail in ride 5. The downside is that is can have a steep learning curve for new players.Personally I ride with most assists off, while challenging, eventually you will get that "feel" of riding this way. You really do need a controller to get that feel. I ride in real life and it's still a lot of work compared to playing a game like ride 5. With the flick of your controller thumb-stick you will flick the bike in the the game. In reality, you need to nail a certain technique and really need to work for flicking your bike at high speeds, impossible for a game to achieve. But the presentation and outcome of your controller actions translates really well and very believable. You will get punished for braking too hard in a lean or when you transition directions too aggressively, like its supposed to be. Brake hard in stable straight lines, and while you transition your weight and lean angle you build off on your brakes, called "trail braking", used in fast riding. Eventually you hit apex and from there anticipate on gradually increasing throttle and reducing lean angle to blast out of a turn. It's beautifully translated on screen. When riding on the edge, you will notice all the small effects of riding hard. Speed wobbles, drifting and the potential risks of low and high-siding your bike. A lot of presentation details like your rider's characteristic lean angle and foot out just before a turn, are even customisable. Of course every bike has its own handling characteristics as well, based on power, weight and customisable bike settings. Every track with its unique layout. The challenges that these different combinations bring are numerous.Talking about customization, you have a sticker editor to personalize everything from rider stickers to helmets and bike liveries its all there. If you're interested in the history of the bikes and all the technicals you will not be disappointed here. From movies on tyre manufacturers , bike manufacturers and models, as a gearhead you will love this background information.graphics wise it looks beautiful. A lot of unique and key details on the bikes. The tracks and surroundings are true to life. Only the character models look like the sims 4 at best. But most of the time they luckily have a helmet on.Soundwise its a hit or miss. Some bikes really nail the character of their engines. 600cc's come to life beautifully at high rpm, vtwins or v4's get that linear power and sound great as well. But there are situations that you get that bland lawnmower sound that does not translate well unfortunately.While this game is not an official MotoGP game, with all the presentation bells and whistles, it does have a huge listing of road production bikes and racing modifications alike. All of them with their unique handling and tuneable setups. If you want adventure riding or cruising harley davidsons this game is not for you. The game is about track riding or sporty riding in general and you will get a lot of fun out of it even though it can be challenging at times. Ride 5 is an absolute recommender, the best in the series and your best option to date if you are into sporty/race riding.
_childDocuments_.name: RIDE 5

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I would recommend Ride 5 if (and only if) you are like me and you just want a halfway-decent motorcycle game to play.  The riding "physics" feel better than in Ride 4 by a noticeable margin, particularly sliding out of corners is a little bit more controllable (and fun) now.   It is not all roses though, where fast, flowing tracks now feel better than ever, slow and narrow corners feel bad and sometimes terrible.  There are a few spots in a couple tracks where you have to brake down into speeds where your bike will just literally fall down if you don't tap the gas a little bit (looking at you, caldwell park penultimate corner.)  The other *still unfixed* problem with the riding "feel" is the kerbs, they are bumpier and nastier than ever, I don't think the devs of this game have watched much motorcycle racing, because I don't remember seeing anyone get launched into outer space just for touching the inside kerbs at imola, for exampleThe additions to "career" mode are mostly horrendous, especially the unskippable cutscenes, these are just awful, please let me skip them!  The introduction of more qualifying rounds is a good step forward, but its not available on every round, if you can't give me qualifying rounds then give me a free practice button that just lets me run laps to learn the circuit, how is this still not in the game?  I also despise the "auto-pilot" sections, please delete this crap from the game, let me start from pit lane, no one wants to sit through 12-20 seconds of unskippable AI riding for any reason.  Stop it.The AI is still bad, it is still not really playing the same game you are, they do weird stuff mid corner, this hasn't changed from Ride 4 I don't think, not much else to say here, guessing no one cares since racing games all suffer from this, but it is extra obvious on a motorcycle game where every little misstep can send you off track.Wait, why am I recommending this game?  Oh yeah, well the riding is still fun, the tracks are generally still very faithful to what I generally like to play on and the motorcycles still generally look and feel the part.  Its a shame that VIR, UMC and Caldwell Park are still in this game because they are absolutely awful, but there's plenty of other great tracks available to apologize for these crimes....Maybe buy it on a sale a couple years from now once they have all the DLC in one bundle for like 8 dollars. I'd give it a 78%.

Everything loads a little faster. All loading screens show the track! Appreciate the little video clip showing city highlights from where you're racing. $36 is still a lot for what essentially feels like polishing/physics tweaks. So corners are about giving your self the best entrance so that you can get back on throttle as early as possible without jeopardizing your racing line. Also, the braking feels different in this one and figuring out the braking points for each track and bike has proved more challenging than i thought. Nonetheless, its a great game if you are into motogp and want to race road bikes.

_childDocuments_.review: This has all the ingredients for the perfect Ride game yet it fails in the only area which matters. The physics. When you're able to turn all traction control off yet use maximum throttle on every corner with +200hp bikes there's a problem. This game has removed any physics difficulty options and locked everything to the extreme arcade mode. It begs the question, why bother using the realistic (and amazing) physics engine - as an arcade game the Ride 4 engine did far better. It's not like it's incapable - riding in the extreme wet feels about where the dry should be.The revolutionary trigger feedback is there but highly muted (why bother if the bikes rarely lose traction after all). The dynamic weather and time is amazing. The game is beautiful, though could do with some optimising particularly with lights. So much has been improved and done right. However AI is still very bad as always, the upgrade system could do with some real work but has been carried exactly from Ride 4.I'd love to recommend this game. I really would. But if the core loop of riding bikes around a track just doesn't work I can't really call it a good game. I'm taking a hiatus from the newer MotoGP releases after seeing the same downwards trajectory, I'd just hoped Ride wouldn't make the same mistake too. Yet whilst neither can simulate riding a bike (for that their own MotoGP21 is king), at least Ride 4 delivers the sensation and joy of riding missing from Ride 5.

_childDocuments_.review: My observations are without any assists and I'm running on a 4k LG OLED TV and it runs amd looks great on my mid-spec systemDespite what some others are saying I think this is the best version of the Ride series so far.The graphics aren't a huge leap forward but there are improvements to my eye especially the lighting and reflections. The bikes looked beautiful in Ride 4 and they are beautiful +1 in ride 5. The tracks look much the same except as I mentioned earlier the improved lighting helps.I like the physics as you can back the bikes in to the corners etc. and they are still quite controllable in that state. The front brakes don't give much warning as to when they are about to 'let go' but I was playing with the ABS turned off. Some of the bikes will need some anti-wheelie dialled in as you'll get nowhere otherwise.My only negative with the physics is that flicking the bikes from side to side does seem a bit laboured and it could do with a little tweaking by the devs in my opinion but all in all physics wise I hope they don't give in to the 'whiners' and alter things to make the game too easy.Being able to set up your own races with 20 riders and choose which bikes the opposition rides is a real nice touch and as I love the 2 strokes I'll have many hours of use out of this feature.Another slight downer for me is they have left out the Kawasaki KR1S 250 which I think was included in Ride 3 but there is a huge choice of others so not a big deal.I also think the Career mode is much improved.Is it worth getting if you already own Ride 4? In my opinion yes or if you are skint wait for a sale but I'm happy with my day 1 purchase.Note:- Come on guys! I've just read through some of the negative reviews and some are slating the game after 30 minutes of play time! : / The others are mainly saying it isn't worth it over Ride 4 and moaning about the physics as usual...they just need to spend some time with it and 'git gud' Difficult for some I know as they have a 5 minute attention span!

_childDocuments_.review:
Rev up your engine and get ready to hit the track with RIDE 5. An adrenaline-filled gaming experience that is so authentic it will make you feel like you're truly racing at break-neck speed. Find your favorite bikes and check out new ones in the ultimate motorcycle game! Race on over 35 tracks and collect more than 200 motorcycles from world-renowned manufacturers, each element is designed to feel like you're riding a real bike.

IT'S A LONG ROAD
It's not just speed that wins races - Endurance mode rewards perseverance and strategy. Time is no longer the issue, ride to your heart's content with the option of saving, exiting and jumping back in later. Just make sure you keep an eye on fuel and pit-stops - these helplines can quickly become your worst nightmare!

FROM ZERO TO HERO
Start out in your garage, climb the ranks and become the best world racer in the new Career mode.
Race against increasingly skilled Rivals, true obstacles who will stand between you and the finish line. Learn to master different bikes and handle every situation.
It won't be easy though... The road to victory is laden with challenges and it's up to you to decide which one you want to take - the harder the challenge, the greater the reward!

WIN UNDER ANY CONDITION
It doesn't matter how good you are, there is always one factor you can't control: the weather. Clear blue skies can turn into heavy downpours and then back to sunshine, rolling clouds will follow you as you dash through the bends, giving you ever-changing views and landscapes.
You will have to deal with unexpected situations and use your skill to tackle both wet and dry conditions - the improved physics makes for an even more life-like experience!

TEST. LEARN. RIDE.
Not sure which line to follow or when to slam on the brakes? Use the new riding aids and get customized support when needed the most. Learn to better handle the bike and the tricks of the trade to become the best rider you can be.

name: Loopmancer
detailed_description: Follow Us For immediate game information, please add it to your Wishlist and follow us: Discord： Twitter： About the Game Year 2046 / Dragon City Neuro-comp interfaces, bionic prosthetics and nano-biotechnology have all become commonplace. Society is highly developed, but the gap between the haves and the have nots has only grown larger. Xiang Zixu, a brilliant private eye, is killed while investigating the disappearance of a famous female journalist . Immediately after his death, he wakes up with a start in his apartment bedroom. Before he can process what happened, his phone rings and his colleague at the agency tells him of a new case: the disappearance of a famous female journalist. Eye-pleasing Maps and Stages; Cyberpunk-style Eastern Cities This game features 7 finely-crafted large stages, including: Dragon Town, which comes alive with holiday spirit in the evening; the bleak and gloomy Shuigou Village; the luxurious Tang Dynasty Hotel; the maritime Bionic Beings' Training Base; and the Biotech Company... Developed with the UE4 engine, this game depicts an eastern cityscape with cyberpunk aesthetics. Fast-paced Battle Action Unlock new weapons and abilities through endless reincarnations to solidify and enhance your fighting skills. Unlock over 100 weapons, cast skills with prosthetic limb chips, and use tech items to defeat the enemy. Face over 30 enemies with unique behavior patterns: vicious gangsters, well-equipped mercs, crazy mutants whose neuro-comp interfaces have been hacked, highly trained bionics, etc. The list goes on, and none of them will be easy to take down. Certain areas will change at random after each life loop. Select your favorite battle mode and investigate the ultimate truth. Rebirth Loop: Real or Fantasy After each death, Xiang Zixu will awaken in his apartment and begin a new loop. As the story progresses, reviewing what seemed like the correct choice in the past may lead to a different conclusion. Every decision you make will alter the fates of in-game characters and rewrite your ending. Are you ready to initiate a new loop?

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this a sideways thumb. It has potential but just feels poorly designed and artificially difficult.- At the beginning, you have no moves at all against bosses that seem to basically require parrying, grinding or both. Once you do the grind for the parries, they feel unresponsive and don't even reward invincibility frames. I have been hit twice in a row during a parry, which should not happen, especially when the game forces me to grind for the right do use it in the first place. In any skill-based roguelike, you want to make sure the player has full control over the character to the point that they feel it's their fault if they take damage. In its current state, this game fails to accomplish that.- Lots of cheap hits from things like enemies blending in with the scenery, tons of hyper armor and bosses that attack relentlessly while your character doesn't have the stamina to deal with it.- The progression system is underwhelming and makes the mistake of making the player grind for things you would expect to be unlocked by default, like the perfect dodge, ground pound and parries. Almost everything else is just stat increases, so it feels like the stuff you're grinding for is what you need to actually have fun playing the game instead of new tools to make the runs more interesting.- The overkill mechanic, despite its name, ironically can get you killed. It has barely any i-frames and since the animation varies depending on the weapon being used, sometimes it just puts you headfirst into danger. Bosses can block it too, which just feels awful considering this mechanic is supposed to encourage not taking damage. In a game with lots of super armor and defensive options that refuse to work like you'd expect, having the reward for fighting through all those mechanics give out on you just makes the gameplay loop feel flawed.- The player can unlock new weapons and abilities by spending coins in runs, but for some reason this game shipped with over a hundred items. This means that an item you unlock (or worse, upgrade) may not appear for several hours of gameplay. It would take an immense amount of grinding and luck to get the build you want, and while that's not uncommon in other roguelites, you're still spending a lot of time upgrading things you might not ever consistently see again.- Combat is one-dimensional with the melee weapon only having one s-string and nothing else to work with. With how many weapons are in this game, I don't see this aspect being improved in a patch. The gameplay is fluid but it does get boring when all the weapons basically feel the same with different animations. In a game where all you do is run and fight, it's disappointing to see yet another melee combat roguelike fail in this department. There are other games in the genre that both have better combat and better overall game design. The defensive options not feeling good or consistent to use just makes the gameplay loop feel even worse.The presentation and setting of the game is great, and it's clear a lot of love went into this, but I have to admit I find this game more frustrating than fun. Some of these things could be fixed in patches, but things like the shallow combat likely can't. Check back for patches, but right now this is a hard sell at its current price and level of polish. It really feels like this game could have benefited from early access to get the combat and gameplay loop where it needs to be, instead of what the game is like now where it may or may not improve.P.S - The enemies swear as much as we do when we get pissed off at games. It gave me some entertainment when I was frustrated with the rest of the package, but I would advise turning it off in the settings after a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Loopmancer is a classically based sidescroller with fighting elements in a contemporary twist.Watch my first gameplay here: Loopmancer can easily be compared to games like Metroid but with slightly less complexity.The battles are mainly fought in close combat, be it with bare fists, your feet or blunt weapons of all kinds, in addition firearms and other attack options such as throwable weapons are used.The range is really good here. Weapons and equipment can also be leveled up.You start a run and will almost certainly die sooner or later. The game is also very challenging, you notice that from a certain point.Oh yeah, and also very important, the controls with a gamepad are as they should be in a game like this, it doesn't feel clumsy or slow.The courses you have to take are also not complete, just from left to right,you will also have to observe often to find the route because regularly you have to climb, descend, go back, turn around again, etc, but in the end this is not that difficult and who knows, you may also find some extra items this way.In terms of sound and graphics I also found it very interesting, the atmospheres that the sounds, music and scenes create fit very well with the cyberpunk environments and backgrounds,whether you like good hack & slash sidescrollers or just the whole cyberpunk style then I can definitely recommend this game.ps: I tried to play the game at an ultrawide resolution but it didn't seemed to support that, it would be great if it would via a future update.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game but there are many issues with it at the moment. The John Woo style cinematic ballet of death is fun, the scenery is gorgeous and the gameplay satisfying, but the issues hold the game back from achieving it's full potential.1) (Fixed)  Lack of i-frames- I lost count of the number of times I used the hook to jump onto a ledge and immediately got knocked off by an enemy. Even the overkill does not have i-frames at the end of the animation, making this a situational skill, rather than a cool move you get to pull off after not getting hit x number of times. 2) Lack of readability: The enemies blend in with the scenery and I got whacked many times by someone I could not even see. (partial fix)3) Cheap hits: Right now, in level 2, there are multiple trip wires that stun lock you after explosion and you get your butt kicked by the enemies for accidentally walking into one of them. Bosses have cheap moves which are difficult to read and there is a highway level where cars hit you if you can't find a safe space in time, and you cannot defend yourself. 4) Weapon viability: So in many games, some weapons are more OP than the others, and this game takes this to an extreme. The longer range melee weapons are almost always better than short range ones, to the point I stopped unlocking weapons after getting the quarter staff, pipe wrench and the spear. I should theoretically be able to beat the game with any weapon, but I can't see myself beating the game with the punch. 5) (Fixed) Enemy expletives: Every time you hit an enemy they drop the f word and I had to entirely turn off enemy sounds in the game because it got so annoying. (There is now a civilised mode which turns off the expletives)I hope the developer fixes some of these issues, I really think the game should've been in Early Access before release since these issues could've been ironed out by early players. This game has a buttload of potential if they manage to patch out these issues.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is freaking great.I dunno what the negative reviewer is talking about, this game goes hard. I've played some janky indy rougelikes, this is NOT one of them. Note that I played this for the steam games fest, so I've a lot more playtime than my 2.9 hours on record attest to.First off, unlike most rougelikes, each level is one fluid level, just like a normal single player game. Not a bunch of connected squares. This alone would make me love the game. I'm getting seriously tired of the 10 mini arenas making up a level gimmick. Quick, difficult, extremely varied. You have melee weapons, guns, gadgets, and a special attack. How you chain that together is up to you but there are a buttload of each to unlock. You starting loadout is randomized, but you can purchase weapons and abilities for the current run when you get to a shop. There are a few shops per level and you can teleport between them to come back later.How do you unlock the weapons and abilities?Well, during a run, you come across these item terminals. You can choose to put some of the coins you have toward unlocking the item. This persists across runs and once you pay the full price, any time you come across that same item it will be free for you. These are not static terminals. They change what items are available and where they are between runs so you never know if you will get access to them or not. Better so far than any other rougelike I've played.  Its a detective story mixed with a sci-fi "reliving the same day over and over" scenario where the detective is trying to solve a mystery by putting together the clues he gathers each time he goes through the loop. The order you choose to do these levels in and I'm assuming a few other things will affect the outcome at the end of the game. I'm only into the second area so no idea how that pans out yet. Also, there are huge lore dumps lying around everywhere. POV stories, histories, Wikipedia-like entries, and they are well written in perfect English (no idea what other language translations end up like). They are also pretty damn long. Someone put a lot of work into this.  There is permanent progression for things like health, health vials, stamina, keeping money when you die, a free res, etc the normal rougelike stuff. But also you can unlock a bunch of different combat abilities that enhance how you fight like the ability to repel ranged attacks or do slams from the air and things like that.In addition to the unlocking weapons thing mentioned in the combat section, here are a few more I've seen.You have checkpoints that you can teleport between like normal, but those stations can be used to heal yourself with some restrictions. First its only a bit at each and if you use it all you have to pay to reload it if you want to use it again in that run. They make for nice little boosts to heal up after fighting a big group of enemies, but not wanting to waste your precious potions.  Boxes that refill ammo are 1 use each, but you can teleport back and grab ones you left for later if you didn't need it at the time you first passed it. I REALLY like this. Keep an eye on my total play time if you want to see if the game is actually good or not. Some people leave a good review no matter what so they can build up a reputation to get free games and such. I'm not one of those people. I like rougelikes, I play the ones I have fun with, and I'm going to be playing this one a bunch.Here's some short  clips if you want to see what the combat and lore of this game looks like in action.
