_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a review before because English is not my native so I'm not so confident about writing one. I usually just click the Yes or No in the recommendation section. BUT... This game has received a lot of negative review which I don't think it's fair.TL;DR: The game itself is good, the battle is so fluid, the scenery is astonishing for a platform game, have no problem launching and playing it, multiple endings (7 in status, don't know if there's hidden ending or something)Positive things:+ The Devs definitely love us, they listen to what seems to be the cons of the game and update it (been receiving 2 update in last 2 weeks)+ Very fluid movement. I play with controller and there has been no issue or what else. Indicators are there for when you need to dodge or parry.+ Cyberpunk, futuristic theme! Who doesn't love this???? I'd love this game in 3D to be honest.+ Skippable cutscenes or dialogue if you guys don't like the story or just want the action stuff+ As a non-English-native, I found the translation or script is great. Easy to be understood.+ Lots of side story, including the enemies' side of view.+ DLSS. No drops in FPS. Stunning!+ UI is not cluttered, and perhaps I can say it's clean.+ Tutorial and fighting tips are everywhere.+ CATS! I love pets =p+ Side game like flappy bird (in this game sedan) to get some start money to upgrade your weapons in the beginning of the loop.+ A LOT OF WEAPONS! But it's also the cons NGL...Cons:- Weapons, although it's a lot (140+ I think?), I only love some because there's not much of an impact choosing other. And I found no interest to spend coin in them other than just to collect it (giant fish MF!) - Some enemies and mines are hard to be seen, maybe because it's the background color. Maybe adding some contrast can help- -- + Update 1.02 already patched this, so you can bind the controller buttons all you want --> Can't rebind controller buttons. You only have 3 presets of the controller. Though Keyboard and mouse has the rebind options - Lip and dialogue are not synced, so for you OCD person, beware.So I don't know why all the negative review, but I think this is a great game and might put a new standard of a beautiful platform roguelike games

_childDocuments_.review: I understand why people are thumbing this down, but I'm absolutely loving it. Yes, it's a bit janky and the localization isn't the best, there are a lot of names that sound very similar thrown at you rapid fire and it can be hard to keep track of them. The UI and explanation of the perks and systems leaves a bit to be desired.  The voice acting is wildly over the top (in a great, campy, B sci-fi movie way)... BUT, the setting is amazing, and so far the story is engaging. If the Cyberpunk genre is your jam then this game is for you. If you love Neuromancer or Snowcrash this game is for you. There is a ton of lore and world building and I find myself wanting to read every note / diary entry etc... I can. It's a gorgeous game as well. I can't speak to how this game holds up as a roguelike because I'm fairly new to the genre, but I'm enjoying it more than I expected. I'm very happy with the cost to fun ratio!My biggest gameplay issue is that the screen is SUPER busy. There are visual cues that indicate when an enemy will go into an unblockable or special state, but those visual cues get lost in the background scenery and the particle effects. When the whole city is glowing red, and the enemy's visual cue is a quick "flash red" and there are 4 or 5 enemies on screen....well you get the picture. Still, I'm having an absolute blast.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a big fan of 2D fighting platformers, nor am I very good at them, but I really enjoyed Loopmancer mostly because it’s also  a detective game with interesting twists, several different choices to make and many different endings!You have an option now to keep reading if you prefer written reviews or you can check my video review on Youtube if you prefer watching and listening instead: The story in Loopmancer is interesting and exciting. The choices you make are between two levels, because most of the time you don’t have the time to visit both places. Other choices depend on how strong you are so for some of these options you will have to get stronger first. The game has 7 endings in total, but for me personally it was way too many. I already had enough when I had 4/7 endings achieved. The game became easy and repetitive at that point so rather than wasting more hours on something I didn’t enjoy as much anymore, I looked up the last three endings. Why? Why bother? Because I felt like I needed to get the final happy ending and some kind of closure before moving on. Unfortunately “the happy ending” was very disappointing and I got no closure anyway. I recommend you getting a few endings when the game is still fresh and fun for you and then stopping. If you decide to go for all the endings and you need some help, you can check my full playthrough on Youtube:   or you can send me a message and I will try to guide you.The gameplay in Loopmancer is fast and fun. You have 4 different types of tech - a melee weapon, a ranged weapon, a tactical gear and a skill. There is a huge variety in all categories. Some options are hilarious - for example a pink dildo I really liked to use as a melee weapon. Some options are really powerful - I loved all the melee weapons which give enemies negative status effects like poison, electricity or fire. The level design is a little bit different in every loop, also weapons you can find and purchase in levels are changing.I absolutely like the visual look of the game. The levels are so charming and atmospheric. I wish the game had more levels. For the amount of endings, it would make the game so much better. Loopmancer also has high quality cinematic cutscenes and full voice acting in English. Even your enemies speak, swear and scream ridiculously when you are fighting them. It was all very funny.The biggest issue with the game right now is that it doesn’t save your progress much, so if the game crashes during a level, you will have to play it from the beginning of that level. That was not the worst. Even when you finish the level and beat the boss in the end and your game crashes during the cutscene after, you still have to play the whole level again! At that point I almost felt like uninstalling the game. Luckily it only happened once.Things get a bit messy after a couple of loops. I no longer knew what’s new information when talking to people and what I already heard. Also in the case of cutscenes, I never knew if it’s a new variation of a cutscene or if it’s something I’ve already seen before. I wish there were some kind of indicators for differentiating between old and new. Diaries and notes you pick up could also be easier accessible. At least a few seconds to open them with pressing a button after picking them up. I got absolutely bored going through menus to read each of them and this annoyance made me give up reading them.I loved all the different outfits for the main character but why not let us change them between levels? He can change equipment at work so why not clothes? I wanted to roleplay a bit with him and blend in as a detective by wearing the appropriate clothes to certain environments like a hotel or a muddy village.In Loopmancer you make yourself stronger by permanently upgrading your equipment in levels or at work and by purchasing permanent tenacity skills at home between loops. There are also temporary power ups in levels and they last until you die by the hand of your enemies or environment. If you keep looping without dying, eventually some of your stats will reach maximum and some power ups will then have options like increase of healing sodas from 7 to 7 or melee attack damage from 48% to 48%. At first I thought it was a visual bug so I chose a couple of them without increasing anything at all. I believe that it should be more clear. If there are two options where one is maxed out, you should only have one option showing. If you got it all, remove the power up completely or give us some currency instead. I recommend Loopmancer because it’s really fun, especially the first hours of gameplay when everything is still new and exciting. The developer really did a great job. They got it all right, well almost. All they need to do is to push for perfection and fix the endings. Remove some of the bad ones which feel like very small variations of the same and add some final ending with a closure and explanations. And they should really fix the saves and game crashes, because those are really frustrating!

_childDocuments_.review: Link to video review: Loopmancer is an oddly harshly criticized roguelike timeloop detective game. It's got a slick and faithful artstyle, keeping its cyberpunk roots close to the chest. It also has flashy combat that's generally quite smooth. This however doesn't mean it's perfect. If you advance too quickly, the game seems to skip a few sets of dialogue with the loops, which can leave you in a position of hearing how you've been in the loop forever, even though it's loop 2. Also the story's nothing to write home about. A mildly intriguing disappearance of a journalist will get dropped for a bigger conspiracy that's just too big for its own good. The biggest issues mentioned in the reviews are either irrelevant after the 2 notable updates or are kinda weird to hear since they criticize issues that stem from the lack of usage of gameplay mechanics. Saying how it's easy to get knocked down is weird when the game's surprisingly generous with the amount of dodging you can do even from the beginning. I don't mean to make it sound like a "Git gud" issue, but I personally just never had those problems and the solution seems clear on surface.Honestly a great time overall, but it's also not perfect by any means. Expect the budget and price to reflect the expected product.

_childDocuments_.review: I had very low expectations for this game considering how low the percentage of positive reviews are, but I still wanted to give it a go since it looked very interesting. And let me tell you, it surprised me in a good way. But first of all I will mention this: the game crashed a lot with RTX on. I have a 3080 and it was not a framerate issue. I think the game is not optimized to handle video memory that well. That said, I'll move on to some brief thoughts.Graphics and art style are pretty. The cyberpunk atmosphere is well made but there was something about the character models that looked cheap in my opinion, especially when they talked in cutscenes. Voice acting was a big plus and the overall sound design was solid. Gameplay is where the game shines, offering some fast paced hack and slash combined with many upgrades in a roguelike-esque manner. I had a lot of fun slashing through levels and performing combos. And speaking of roguelikes, this game reminded me a lot of Sifu in terms of the game design, so if you liked that, you'll see some similarities here. It's not the same, but it makes the game not so heavy in the roguelike aspect. I don't generally enjoy them and I was able to blast through this game twice.There aren't many levels (just like in Sifu) but they are different enough. Minibosses or something like that would have made them a bit more special, but I'm not complaining. And the story... It's alright. There are like 7 endings to get but unless you are a completionist, you might just want to look them up on youtube and that's it. I don't think the story is told very well. The game tried too hard to get me involved in a character for whom I had no feelings and neither of the 7 endings are completely satisfying. As far as I can tell, there's no "true" ending.Last but not least, as I said before, I played through the whole thing twice because after beating the game a first time, I still wanted more. Things do not change much between playthroughs, except that your upgrades and everything remain. There's not a lot of content either besides the endings so replayability is low in my opinion. It is a good idea and I think it's well made, I don't understand why it is sitting at 72% positives at the moment.4/5 - It's not GOTY material, but it's good enough for you to spend an afternoon with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Received a review key for this game a while back. I was immediately impressed with the visuals, gameplay, and narrative, but but was disappointed with some balance and performance issues. Thankfully, the team behind Loopmancer have been dedicated to improving the game, and they have displayed an effort to listen player feedback and use that feedback to improve the overall experience.This is a fun action roguelite. If you're familiar with the genre, you'll feel right at home. The game builds on the standard action roguelite formula with varied and interesting loadouts for your character, and a complex narrative with multiple paths and layers. There are a lot of little features in the game that show there is a lot of care going into the title. It's good!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is rad!  I generally don't like rogue-like games but this one is an exception.  Most likely because I suck at them but I also get bored doing the same thing repeatedly in the same area.  Not an issue with this game.Beautiful graphics, ray tracing, incredible set design.  Graphically this game is a power house .  I have personally never played a side-scroller that looks this good.  The aesthetic is very reminiscent of Cyberpunk 2077 along with the music.  I am running Epic settings on PC with RT on and most settings on high on the Steamdeck (with FSR).  Locked 60 in 4k on PC and almost a locked 60 at 800p on the Steamdeck (60 most of the time with some occasional drops to the 55-59 range).   Overall the game performs great.  DLSS and some other Nvidia settings are available as well on PC.The gameplay is very fluid and responsive.  Quite a few different weapons (and I am still very early in the game).  Action is very fast paced and the fighting is tons of fun.  In your arsenal, you have melee, firearm, special (like fire or electricity), mines, and other options.  The enemies definitely pose a threat particularly in bunches.  I have only made it to the 1st boss (and died a bunch of times) so far but the fights have been exciting.Also a pretty good story thus far.  You are basically a detective in a time loop fighting a mob boss.  Story is told both by NPCs and documents throughout the level.  When you start a new loop, the NPCs generally have new info to give too although you eventually run out of new dialogue in the same areas.  Overall very engaging.I give it a 9/10 and I am not a fan of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I did not like this game....at first. Now its 2 days later and I'm loving it does it have some issues? Yes however keep in mind I don't know how it performs on Consoles. I have a PS5 but anytime i have to choose between a game that's on PC and PS5 I go with PC hands down. I'm playing on keyboard and using a mmo mouse which comes in handy (for me). I wont ruin the story (I cant stand reviews where the person tells you the whole plot) but basically the main Character is experiencing a "Ground Hog Day" scenario and every time you die you retain memories of your last run and you can change the path you choose. This is the first game I've ever experienced where the voice acting is so bad but the plot (To Me) is good. I enjoy reading the notes, and diaries which by the way gives you hints on maybe what path may be easier. At first you may seem overwhelmed by all the weapons and how leveling works but after an hour or two I got the hang of it. Game play is the best thing about this game because you unlock cool weapons which changes how you fight and you cant just button mash your way out of trouble (at least not after the 1st couple of levels). This game may not be for you but if you enjoy hack n slash platformers then I say give it a try if you don't like it just make sure you don't play over 2 hours anything under that can be refunded.
_childDocuments_.name: Loopmancer

_childDocuments_.review: Loopmancer is easily one of the best roguelikes of the year so far and I can easily recommend it to anyone who likes beat em ups or action games. The story is genuinely interesting, the combat is fluid and addicting, the animations are phenomenal, the art style is visually striking from start to finish, the power progression is very well paced, the weapon selection offers genuine variety, and considering this is the first real game from this developer it is so much more impressive. That being said, there is one genuine issue with the game that even after 10+ hours I can't seem to find an easy solution for and that is the gun wielding enemies. I'm not even on the hardest difficulty and these enemies feel somewhat broken. There are a lot of things going on visually at any given time so projectiles in general are very hard see, making them difficult to parry which in itself isn't even completely reliable because the attack parry doesn't knock back ALL projectiles which means any gun wielder can still hit you even if you land the parry perfectly and this is amplified by the fact that many encounters will have multiple gun wielders on all sides of you AND they can hit you from off screen as well which also feels awkward because melee adds seem to have their AI deactivated once they're off screen. Add to that the fact that they also aimbot you and will hit you no matter where you are during combat AND the fact that they can hit you through the floor (if you're on the level above/below them), through other enemies, AND the fact that they are some of the tankiest enemies in the game, the majority of your runs will end because of these nearly broken enemies. That being said, My experience is with the 3rd highest difficulty option (out of 4). I would recommend anyone who plays this game to go with one the easier settings especially if you're not as familiar with action games or beat em ups. I'm not sure what the developer intentions were regarding the gun wielding enemies, but they feel completely at odds with everything else happening in combat. I'm going to push through on the same difficulty because it genuinely feels so well balanced outside of that one issue and I'm so closed to the end, but it seriously does not feel good to have a perfect run die to being stunlocked by gun wielding enemies that you can't even see yet. Seriously, I had one gun wielder ledge guarding me and no matter how long I waited to climb up to deal with him I would get shot right as I got up and knocked all the way back down again. I was even able to beat some of the bosses on this difficulty first try, but the gun wielding enemies are literally the biggest obstacle in the game. But EVEN with that, I still think this game is worth a shot. With no technical issues or bugs to speak of, I would consider this is a very polished experience. These developers definitely have talent. Considering it just dropped, if the developers see my criticism as a legitimate issue, they can address it in a patch. But if this is their intention, like I said, just try one of the easier difficulties if you run into the same issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Loopmancer

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hesitant recommend, while it is a good game, it has some really fatal flaws that I think it's probably not for everyone.First, this is not really a traditional roguelite, this is more like a repetition of an action RPG. Usually roguelike you focus on your build, you will have relics and skills to enhance a certain build. This game is not. It does have different weapons...but that's it, there is no build. You unlock some weapon, and that's pretty much you can get. No relics to support a certain build, you just have to pick a weapon that you find you like and stick with it for the rest of the game. You have upgrades, which is just your hp and consumables that you can carry. So stripping out a core game play from rougelike, but you still need to start at the VERY BEGINNING starts to get tiring REALLY quick. Since weapons are more or less the same, really, it's your skill. Which is kinda like dark souls feeling, It's doesn't matter what weapon you use, if you know how to beat it. So forcing the roguelike starting over gamestyle doesn't add on anything valuable to the gameplay I would say. It's mostly just dragging out the length. This game would be much fitted to be a short metroidvania with new game+ for different weapons and raised difficult and multiple endings.  Second some enemy placement and just the sheer amount of effects going on screen really bothers me. For example, some times you have to crotch through a door, but guess what, the enemy literally BLOCKS that door, you can only shoot while crotch, while is dumb. Other times when you have to jump on roof, guess what, there will be 3-4 enemies at the EDGE of the roof where you have to jump on, if it's an enemy with a gun, well, good luck getting on there cuz when you start to jump, they will shoot, and once shot, you fall mid-air, trying to jump again? They start to shoot...see the problem here?? Same happens when you land on roof, sometimes there will be 3-4 enemy waiting for you right at the edge of the roof and the second you land...well. I don't know who thought it's a good idea to either not have i-frame when landing, or put the enemy right at the edge (and they will NOT move once they see you). Besides the ridiculous enemy placement, the effects going on screen is also insane. You have enemy throwing stuff, enemy shooting stuff, you shoot stuff, traps on the ground, explosion, your special attacks...these are all going on at the same time, it's even worse when you have to face 4 or more enemies cuz sometimes you just can't tell WTF is going on. But despite the above problems, it is still pretty fun to play (if you can accept the repetitiveness), it's has stunning visuals, everything is just beautiful to look at, the art style definitely nailed the cyber punk feeling. The plot is pretty interesting. I love the customization you can have in game (different outfits). All the characters are voiced, the level of detail and love is just awesome, and tbh, rare nowadays. If you like a metroidvania, like RPG, like story driven games , I would say try it. But if you are looking for roguelike and builds, don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: After 28+ hours and some 30+ loops in the main game I can say this has become the most addictive roguelike for me and the genre as a whole will never be the same.Gameplay is dynamic and extremely addictive with some nice depth thanks to melee, guns, skills and gadgets, all of which tend to synergise quite beautifully. Character air control is tight, we have counters, knockbacks, seamless action cancels and all physics in general feel spot on. Gore and gibs are aplenty which is a bonus for those who enjoy them. Once you get used to everything you become an (almost) untouchable killing machine executing everything along your path in the shortest amount of time. Doing challenges left and right, collecting weapons, logs and filling that gallery. Weapons are distinct and their physics feel just right, albeit some fall into the category of "NOT THIS !@#$ AGAIN".Each level consists of a predefined number of pre-made-random-order "fight" tiles connected by not-so-random "connection" tiles which serve to teleport around and as story or shopping places. These tiles follow the level theme and each section is completely different from the next. Enemies, traps, gears, upgrades are randomised as well but follow the level theme and this keeps things fresh for the nth loop. Mini challenges on each combat tile add interesting twists and make you utilise various techniques to deal with the enemies. Restarting again and again makes you learn from your mistakes and you actually get better at fighting the enemies you know - until you get your ass kicked by the ones you don't or start getting careless.Finally finishing a loop completely without dying allows you to retain all skill upgrades and weapons you were carrying and they can scale up the more you loop and perfect your death-bringing collection.The story is quite elaborate and has a good flow. The groundhog day twist gives us some interesting situations and is nicely implemented by itself. Have to stop here to say "No" to spoilers. Just a tip: don't skip all after-boss cutscenes as they change a few times depending on how much you've uncovered or which paths you have taken.The art design is stellar - a sight to behold. The attention to detail is incredible starting from level foregrounds and backdrops, it extends to enemies, animations, effects and even menu and icon styles.English voices are fine, however I can recommend the Chinese voices for a more authentic experience.Everything said, I've been itching for something like this for a long time and am glad it was made.
_childDocuments_.name: Loopmancer

_childDocuments_.review: This is an honestly good game from an indie developer.  It has all the things that strikes me as fun:  A Cyberpunk themed world, an in-depth story, and a semi-punishing (yet still very rewarding) combat system.As a note to anyone reading this, the first thing I did was change the voiced language to Chinese, the NA Voice Actors are interesting, but really don't fit in the world.  Do yourself a favor (you can only do this in the start menu, if you're in game, you can't change the voice over).Because of the nature of the game, I appreciate that dying doesn't feel as much of a punishment.  Sure, you'll repeat the first level so many times, you can almost do it blindfolded, but the levels themselves have a bit of randomness, and as you progress in the story (and unlock better weapons and upgrades), more difficult enemies from later in the game will start to show up.  You gotta be quick on your toes.  Remember your past loops and let your weapons do the talking, and don't forget to pet the cat!Speaking of weapons, the various tools, guns, and abilities feel different and unique in their own way (and certain combos are really fun to play around with), including the "Data Lost" weapon -- a seemingly fun nod to Saint's Row and other games with a giant pink floppy dildo as a weapon.  I've discovered that interweaving melee and gunplay with tech and skills provides the best way to beat even the most painful of enemies.All in all, for its cost, it's a great game to get lost in while still enjoying every loop.  I appreciate this game (even though I haven't finished it).

_childDocuments_.review: Visually great, fun combat with multitudes of different, sometimes hilarious, weapons to choose from. It's a Rogue-lite so it may not be for everyone as you have to restart from the beginning with each death. Although you keep some progress and slowly level yourself up with each loop. Story is fairly simple if not cheesy but honestly in a good way. Voice acting is hit or miss, except the Director, that man can do no wrong.The game is pretty difficult, I decided to play on Challenge mode as I had played the demo and felt a false sense of confidence. I've played for nearly 20 hours and the game tells me I'm less than 30% through. If that sounds like a problem, maybe choose an easier difficulty to begin with but no complaints from me there, I love a good challenge.Overall I would give Loopmancer an 8/10. A few fumbles here and there but certainly an entertaining experience! I may be a bit biased as I happen to have worked on the game, but everything I've said has been divorced from that process.- The man who may or may not have voiced the Director

_childDocuments_.review: Overall impressive game that plays like an homage to Hong Kong action cinema, with fast and furious combat, some great cut scenes with fantastic direction and choreography, and I'm totally digging the plot, which puts an entire new spin on the whole Cyberpunk mystery thriller angle. Roguelite elements come in the way of weapons you can invest currency in when you find them (these become unlocked when you buy them and are a permanently part of your arsenal, though some randomness is involved), and Cores that you get from objectives, bosses, and your Director when you complete stages. You also roll over any Buff Bot Upgrades you find should you successfully complete a loop (by getting an ending instead of dying). Weapons appear randomly, and what's available from the weapon vendor in the Detective Agency changes each time you report back before a stage. You can skew a loop in your favor by quitting to the menu and hitting continue to refresh the options available before you head out though, since the game saves any item you've already selected in your inventory. This allows you to reload for the optimal kit, and I've started loops with a full set of orange (i.e. mythic) gear this way. Controls can be a bit finicky with the keyboard, especially the jumping/platforming parts, and because I was playing primarily with a melee spec using an elemental damage weapon, I had to rebind my melee parry to my mouse to make things easier. (Hopefully the devs are looking into tweaking the parry mechanics so they're more intuitive and fluid). Gotta say that the best experience overall comes from playing the game with Chinese VO. The English dub just doesn't cut it if you know Chinese, and there's a lot of nuance that gets lost in translation. (You also get to hear gangster mobs in there that shout "KNNCCB" and other Chinese expletives before they attack you, which is a win in my books).Also, I'm guessing that the date the story takes place on is a secret Wong Kar Wai reference, given the time loop concept of the story (Is someone in the game studio a Wong Kar Wai fan?). Unlocked all Endings so far, and they're all kinda depressing. There's definitely some missed opportunities to tell a more complete and fulfilling story, especially with so much lore and world building invested already. Looking forward to seeing more content and support from the creators.

First things first, the dialogue in this game feels SO out of place, the enemies seriously drop the f-bomb for every quip. I'm not exaggerating, every single line of dialogue from the enemies has at least one f-bomb in it, like "Wow you f-ing, f-ck, that really f-cking hurt!"It was really funny when there was a group of 3 or 4 enemies clustered up because all you would hear is stuff like that. _childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: The easiest way to describe Loopmacer is "Cyberpunk Dead Cells". Those are two terms that instantly excite me so I was excited to try this out. While it does deliver on that promise and has a lot of depth and amazing visuals, the combat system is definitely not as polished or fluid as Dead Cells, though it's still satisfying. I also haven't found this as hard, though it's definitely still a challenge.Where Loopmancer excels over Dead Cells is in the story department. There's a fairly deep narrative here, with various choices you can make throughout your runs that will impact events and potentially what characters will be available to you in the future. Your choices and progress are also reflected in dialogue and progression in future loops. Everything is voice acted, but unfortunately, it's also heavily overacted, making for dialogue that's often very cringey to listen to. Cutscenes do repeat between runs, though they can thankfully be skipped. You'll also pick up a lot of readables in your runs, if you want more flavour in the world.The world and levels are positively gorgeous and the game generally runs quite well and includes support for many features offered in modern GPUs. It does support raytracing, though I can barely notice a visual difference so depending on your GPU, it may not be worth the performance hit.I'm surprised this hasn't gotten more attention with the depth that it offers. Does it play as well as Dead Cells? No. Does it make up for that with its stunning presentation and deep, choices matter narrative? Voice acting aside, I think so. If you like looping Roguelites, don't pass on this.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game and it was amazing to invest hours into Loopmancer.Here's my written review, the video review is currently in progress. I will update this review with the YT link, once it ready this weekend.STORY:The game narrates the story of Xiang Zixu. Xiang Zixu is a privately hired investigator and he needs to find a kidnapped reporter. In your quest to find the kidnapped reporter, you come across a gang leader Wei Long, who is enjoying his annual tour of the 6th month of the Lunar Calendar known as the Parade of Penate, where a rich and colorful parade is organized by the temple crews. You meet Wei Long on the bridge, where he tries to flee away. On your way, you fight a cyborg, or a modified superhuman and chances are you may get killed at your first attempt. And next thing is that you find yourself in your apartment, and you see vivid images of your wife and your daughter, who met in an accident. And this wakes you up.  The day has restarted, but your memories remain intact.Liu Xin is a police officer who tries to brief you about the situation at hand but is surprised to know, you are well aware of the details due to the previous loop. And this continues until you end the story, and yes, there are multiple endings.GRAPHICS:This is one of the areas where the game shines and does so brightly. Cyberpunk being a culture with a distinct style of "High Tech, Low Life" is portrayed in the best possible way in Loopmancer. The poor are getting poorer and the rich are getting richer, creating a larger and larger divide. The opening segments introduce you to the neon-baked low streets of this cyberpunk low life and then you move on to the Parade of Penate, mentioned earlier. Here, the ambiance, the fireworks, the drifting pieces of the aftermath of the fireworks, and the computer-generated visual fish swimming in the air, are a sight to behold.Then you move on to Longxi Town, where you are greeted by the fast-paced traffic that will not avoid pedestrians. Then you will find yourself in a cyber city, where your ride gets hijacked and you are forced to travel on foot and visit the modern Kouga Industry and its interiors. So, the locations in Loopmancer are varied, pleasing to the eyes, and the highlight of the game. It's a good-looking game.GAMEPLAY and COMBAT:Considering the length of the video, I will combine the Gameplay and Combat elements into one segment.We expect some fine gameplay from a rogue-lite game and in this Loopmancer does not disappoints. Being a Metroidvania game, there is back tracking but this does not make the game monotonous since the locations are an absolute eye-candy to revisit. Xiang can use melee combat to his advantage and ranged combat via guns. All of these can be upgraded at ChangXu Detective Office's Equipment Depot when you meet your buddy, Dave Ray. Also, you earn cores that you earn by completing challenges. So you upgrade your weapons with currencies earned by killing enemies.Cores on the other hand upgrade your health, stamina, and combat abilities, including the ability to block and parry attacks. And you retain them even if you die. Also, cores allow you to customize the visual aesthetics of your character, like changing your outfits. And there is a wide range of weapons at your disposal.I mean there is a huge list, and some unique ones too. Melee weapons range from a Katana to slippers, fish, and eh... something I cannot mention haha to straight forth reference to the popular Manga Berserk and Guts. The same applies to ranged weapons. You can jump, double jump, press Right Analog to cling to surfaces, down press the Left Analog button and A simultaneously to move up or down some platforms. So the gameplay is very fluid.Combat is Loopmancer is fast-paced, fluid, less flawed, and engaging. As mentioned earlier, you gain access to melee and ranged weapons. The variety of weapons makes the gameplay interesting. It's challenging and colorful, and always pleasing to the eye. Apart from melee and ranged weapons, you have access to Tactical Gear and Skill Chip. Tactical gear is a powerful offensive tech but the downside is it has limited capacity. And you also get an ability called Overkill. Once you hit enemies and reach the combo limit, you can press L and R analog buttons to get some glory finishers. The best part is it's different for every melee weapon. It just satisfying to see the body parts flying off your enemies when the moves are executed. CONS:Ok, I need to address the elephant in the room first which is voice acting. It is pretty stiff, with not-so-good, lip sync movements. The cutscenes can be pretty long at times and seem a bit janky or of poor quality. I have a minor issue with progression. So remember you need to earn cores to upgrade your character. You need up grinding cores for moves like dodge and parries. I wished they were unlocked by default. The overkill feature looks great visually but bosses can block it. It feels a bit weird since you work all the way to save the moveset for a boss fight only to get it blocked. This does not make much sense.The load time is something that needs to be fixed. Also, the enemies keep dropping F-Bombs at you and they swear a lot, I mean a lot. If possible there should be an option to turn off this feature in the menu.Since it's a rogue-like game, you are expected to upgrade your weapons and get stronger. However, the weapons are quite random. Let's suppose you upgrade a weapon, you may never come across that weapon during your entire run. So this needs to be fixed.Another turn-off is the fact that enemies blend in a great deal with the background and it's easy to miss their attacks quite a bit.VERDICT:Despite all the cons discussed earlier, Loopmancer is a commendable effort by EBrain Studio, and it's their first game. They are talented, with only 20 developers on the team creating a game as visually and combat-rich as Loopmancer. I could see inspiration drawn from Metal Gear Solid, for example, the scene where Xiang Zixu does a standoff against a boss, very reminiscent of Metal Gear Solid Revengeance. Loopmancer's fight, die, and repeat may not be fresh but the game's randomly generated enemies and levels will keep you engaged. Set against a Cyberpunk world that looks so amazing, with flashy movesets and some amazing boss fights, I can recommend Loopmancer to my viewers easily.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand the mixed review score - not at all. This isn't supposed to be a AAA game. Its price is a third of a AAA game. For this relatively low price, I had as much fun as with Cyberpunk 2077. Yes, it still needs some bugfixes. The crashes during the loading screen are annoying but I haven't lost any progress so far because they always happen during the loading screen towards the next level. The artstyle and world building are amazing. The models aren't always as granular but I think it's as beautiful as the artstyle of Cyberpunk 2077, might even surpass it in certain places. Ray Tracing really makes a difference for Cyberpunk games. For a 20 bucks game, it's impressive that you get a progressive story to invest in, voice acting, cutscenes. The world gradually develops with every loop, everytime a little bit different. This makes the game more repayable than Cyberpunk 2077. It's an Asian game, so I don't expect perfect English in every lore text. The voice acting is fine, I've seen much worse. I like that the game occasionally switches to a 3D angled perspective. The overall loop system is great. If you don't like it, the game also has an easy mode where with different rules. But it's so much fun because you always play a little bit different and because you don't really see where it's going and how long you'll have to keep playing. You have flying cars, which is better world building than Cyberpunk 2077, which makes flying cars a privilege for the super rich. The combat mechanic is a bit clunky at times, mostly when attempting to do double jumps and when the second jump or the movement won't be recognized. Other than that, it's really fun. The unresponsive jumping should be improved though. There is a wide variety of upgradable weapons with the typical rarity system you know from other games such as Cyberpunk 2077. There is a great variety of enemies, mechs, biotics, different powers. There are different story branches which can be changed and revisited during every loop, always with slight changes. The dialogues change as well during every loop. The story is really fletched out, also with supplemental lore. It's a must have for every Cyberpunk fan. But don't expect a lot of music.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS AWESOME!!! As a sidenote, I jump straight into "Challenging" difficulty, the hardest of 4 settings, so that's what my experience is based off of and I am quite content with the actual level of difficulty!Getting this out of the way first. My ONLY issue with the game is the stamina just feels weak when you really really need it. Stamina depletes when you sprint, jump, or dodge (attacks as far as I can tell don't cost stamina). Most of the time the stamina really isn't that bad but when it is an issue, it feels like a stun lock. This mostly is on two of the boss fights. You need to do a lot of dodging which drains your stamina fast and sure there's two upgrades to help (attacking enemies gives a little stamina back and also crouching recharges a little faster) but still that bar will be empty quick leaving you no more evasive actions; no jumping, no dodging meanwhile you still got LOTS of things to dodge. Also the fact that your stamina depletes outside of combat is iffy, like as an example just sprinting/jumping through a level to the next combat and you come across a group of enemies and you're out of stamina without realizing it so can't dodge. :( I would recommend just a slightly faster regen for the stamina bar (maybe even having the stamina upgrades in the level also increase the regen rate) and also not depleting when in between combats when there's no enemy aggro.Now that that's been said, there's SOOOO many great things about this game! Visually it's stunning! The combat is really fun! Story is very intriguing and keeps you wanting to explore all the different storylines! There's a great variety of weapons (you have 4 slots for a melee weapon, gun, tactical, and skill chip) and I love how they set up unlocking and upgrading them (though upgrades could have a bit more variety but still not bad)! Level design is awesome! Also the hidden stat upgrades in the level are nice to reward exploration a bit! There are also combat challenges to attempt while going through levels to gain more rewards which I enjoy (when they don't get me killed XD )! Soundtrack is banging! Cut-scenes are nice and I enjoy how there are subtle changes to them based on loops and choices you make!Some other reviews mention crashes, but I have yet to experience any game crashes and I'm 16hrs in! Some of the loading screens can take a teeny bit long but not too horrible.Overall though IMHO the developers did a phenomenal job with this game! It's definitely a HOT HOT recommend in my book and I will definitely be spending much much much more time with this game!P.S. Fair warning, enemies drop the F bomb A LOT.....like A LOT ALOT! BUT there is a setting to turn off the expletives if you so choose to do. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game, definitely worth the money. I feel like this game has everything: - extremely high replayability from roguelike elements and the challenges present in each level, - a challenge similar to Hades where it might take a few runs to even get to the final boss let alone beat them, - multiple paths to take with 7 different endings that don't require extensive changes in each run- good level design that provides variety and several ways to use the environment to your advantage- lots of weapons, skills, and tactical items- a stamina bar to force you to be careful with dodges and jumps- good graphics where reflections can be seen in some areas even without raytracing- optimized well and fairly polished (I never had any frame drops or problems like that running on a laptop 2070 on Epic graphics settings, no raytracing)- decent voice acting and localization, though the translation had some funny faux pas and weird choices here and there. Still done better than some other Chinese games that came out relatively recently. I'm pretty sensitive to bad voice acting so most of it here wasn't bad, but once again, the main character has some of the worst somehow (you'd think they'd be able to pay more attention and recognize his overacting before putting him in the main role...) The main problem I have is the high RNG factor for achievements and such, but you need to make multiple runs anyway and can restart each level. I don't know where or when the last items I need to collect are or can show up, so not sure if I'll be able to get all of them. Not a deal breaker for me though.Like I said, solid game; fun, challenging, decent story, lots of options. Worth the $20

( LOL ) The combat is HARD in the beginning because you have really no combat skills to start with, and the enemy's do not pull there punches. _childDocuments_.review: I played in Loopmancer around 8 hours and think I need a last loop.So what can I say about the game: Positive.- Very stylish game with good visual effects and ray-tracing. - Many interesting and funny weapons.- Not bad cut-scenes with animation very similar to F.I.S.T.: Forged in Shadow Torch.- Can carres a kitty and get boost!- Nice battle flow.Negative.- Boring dialoges and a lot of text information which take down temp.- Strange FPS jump's in gameplay and cut-scenes.Total: I liked this game. _childDocuments_.review:
Year 2046 / Dragon City. 

Xiang Zixu, a brilliant private eye, is killed while investigating the disappearance of a famous female journalist. Immediately after his death, he wakes up with a start in his apartment bedroom. Before he can process what happened, his phone rings and his colleague at the agency tells him of a new case: the disappearance of a famous female journalist.

Loopmancer is a 3D platformer roguelite action game with realistic graphics that takes place in a cyberpunk universe. Players play as a detective who comes back to life after an unexpected death, and battle in this lifelike and futuristic city of the east.

name: Fabledom
detailed_description: Welcome, your Highness! A vast land awaits your settlers and is ready to be colonized.  Fabledom offers an accessible and intuitive way of playing City builders, the game is easy to pick up and play for anyone but can still offer a challenge for more experienced players thanks to its difficulty settings. Set in a strange world where Fairytales become reality, you will witness the growth of your village; follow your citizens’ lives and watch the rise and fall of your relationships with the neighboring kingdoms. From a small village to a bustling Fairy tale Kingdom Find the promised land, settle, and flourish! You will need every resource available to you to expand and thrive. Build and shape a city worthy of your citizens! Meet & interact with magical creatures Experience a fairytale world filled with flying pigs, giants, gnomes, and much more. Explore every nook and cranny of this magical world but beware of the witch sisters and the looming dragon if you don’t want your kingdom to become a cautionary tale itself! Adapt your playstyle to find true love! Romance will strongly shape the way you play and enjoy the game. Fabledom’s focus on love and candor will provide fresh city building mechanics as you can choose between 6 different rulers to interact with, get unique quests and buildings for your Kingdom! Build an Army to protect your kingdom Make it rain coins on your Fablings by building a Mystic Mine but do so at your own expense as trolls have an appetite for such endeavor. Gather your army and hero to protect your kingdom from their malicious invasion! Tales of trades, feuds and partnerships Build your economy, exchange rare resources to grow and evolve. Fabledom offers numerous ways to interact with other kingdoms. How you handle diplomacy will shape your progress. Fabledom is inspired by amazing games like: - The Settlers - Foundation - Kingdoms and Castles

short_description: Set in a wholesome fairytale world, Fabledom is a laid-back City builder. Enjoy the growth of your settlement, interact with your neighbors and defend your kingdom from magical creatures. All to find true love and live happily ever after!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that I did not realize I NEEDED!! I bought it a few nights ago and I have been addicted and can't seem to stop playing. I appreciate the pace of the game too, I don't myself feeling overwhelmed like other titles within this genre. I personally have not run into any bugs or glitches either, which is a huge plus for it still being in early access. AND OMGGG, the graphics are so cute and adorable. The music is so relaxing as you plan and create your thriving and forever expanding kingdom. I cannot wait to see what else the devs do with this little gem of a game, from what they've shared regarding the road map, I am SOOO excited to play more!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little game.  The charm and style makes you smile, growing your city keeps you engaged, and optimising your building placement gets you immersed.  Game has no bugs, runs smoothly, and according to the road map still has much more to come.  You wont regret buying this if you like city builders.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: It's just not for me.  It is great as it sells itself to be.  Laid back, slow, has minimal interaction with neighboring kingdom, but the management tools that it has is just not quite there yet for me.  I would prefer if you could upgrade homestead to town homes similar to the mechanic that the Anno series has.  The penalty/range for having homesteads close to townhomes is way too harsh.  First playthrough really screwed me on this and adjusting buildings takes way too long since the whole game is slow-paced.  If I need to constantly be playing the fastforward button to adjust things, it takes away the lay-back, relaxing element that I was looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: My review may very well change down the road, but at the moment I would say wait for more to be developed. Once it is fully released, I hope that it will be a fabulous, well-rounded game with a large variety of options. I see a lot of potential right now, but you start hitting roadblocks pretty early on where you might think to yourself "Gee, I wish this part was developed already". In which it isn't currently. And that's OK! Like I said, I'm sure in a year or two, this game will be great. But right now there isn't enough variety to keep me engaged for more than a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: A casual city-building game (set in a classic fantasy kingdom, fairy tale style, in this case). In that sense, it delivers what it promises. The graphics are simple but well-crafted, made for a children's story. The gameplay is calm and slow, very relaxing. The game ends when you complete the main mission, which is to marry one of the other leaders. The systems are simple and easy to learn. It's practically stress-relief therapy. Highly recommended if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: A game with crack-like addictive tendencies, when is the patch??? *itching the neck* I wanna keep going ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ REEEE. I want to have the rest unlocked, I not only want it but I NEED it. A building game with a touch of crusaders king, the art style is 10/10. Best building game i've played in a while. So erm, yes, you should buy it and get addicted too.  Ofc some unbalanced things here and there since its early access. But you don't care, its that good. (At least for me)
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: tbh, I am very disappointed with the devs moving on to new games. From both the amount of reviews and their score and how active the discord was post release, I was hoping for more content - when I asked in discord pre release, main dev's answer had been "depending on how the game does", and the game did very well from what I can tell, and yet the main dev is moving on. There will be a 1-2 person team working on dlc apparently, but that's it. They also said it was their "last patch". While I understand wanting to move on after 4 years, I am disappointed with the promises "we will continue if it does well", and then still abandoning it, because from what I can tell the devs who remain for dlcs are graphics designers, and with only graphic designers the content is gonna be... well, not deep. There were several things that I wanted from this game post release - planting new trees, more indepth map generation tools, official mod support and a LOT more decor, because that's the most appealing part of this game. Dlc miiight cover the decor part, but I doubt there'd be a lot of pieces. Modding support would have kept this game alive for a very long time, so I just feel disappointed. Perhaps someone from the community will take over and integrate something but... Well... It all honestly leaves a bit of a sour taste. I'm not gonna change my review from positive because I feel like I got my money's worth in hours, but I have not found any interest to replay post release cuz I feel like there was just not enough new stuff to warrant a replay.I will honestly not buy anything from this dev team again until way after their releases and seeing what happens with the new games.=============ORIGINAL REVIEW:The most chill and one of the most beautiful kingdom builders that I've seen or played. The wedding chateau update that added palaces and castles added leaps and bounds onto the game - without it I do see how there wouldn't be much content, but this update fixed it imo. It consumed my whole weekend before I could even notice.If you're searching for something difficult - I don't think this game is for you. This game's biggest charm is its fairy tale looks and beauty, the ability to build a sprawling kingdom and decorate it to your hearts content. There isn't really any difficulties in managing the domain.One thing that I think this game really needs tho is more decoration pieces - for homesteads, for palace, for free placement... imo there just isn't a very big selection of pieces for decorating. I really do hope for mod support in the future (tho I didn't see it mentioned anywhere) because modders would take this to a whole another level with detailing, but for now we can only sit tight and see what happens on release and in the future roadmap.Also, need a lot more fairytales and quests and interactibles on map because they really do run out quick.Also, devs are actively fixing bugs and communicating on discord so I've had a very pleasant time with this game overall!Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: For $21 I can't be upset, and the game is currently $13.64 when posting this.  I enjoy the graphics and colors - it's fun.  I did NOT play EA and didn't have any expectations.  I grew up playing Caesar 2 & 3; Settlers; Sim Tower & City.  This lacks some of the complexity, but overall enjoyable.I'm not sure if I'd completely start over again.  The pacing feels okay at the beginning, but in the later stages feels slow even at the max speed.  The food / starvation mechanic could use improvement as there isn't any kind of indication similar to happiness, sewage or water access.I enjoy the game, and while there is room for improvement, I find it difficult to fault for the price.  There are enough elements to consider without being too complex; relaxing and engaging w/o being stressful.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game and can't wait for all the content in the finished version. It already feels like a cozy and cute version of the settlers and hope the finished game will add extra challenges. You get more and more teasers as you play further and it did not bother me while playing. But, I did get this game in with the spring discount and the amount seems fair for the content of the game so far.

You should be able to upgrade certain buildings say like on a scale from 1 to 4. Like each house that gets upgraded would be upgraded to house 12 people to work In the buildings like farms or sawmills. Sawmills should also be allowed to be upgradeble like to produce on a scale from 1 to 4 1 produces 2 boards. 2 produces 4 boards , 3 produces 6 boards, and level 4 would produce 8 boards.  What about adding like a traders dock where traders come to trade goods or where you can buy goods from the trader.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the concept of this game so much that I put 30 hours into it trying to succeed. Not that each new map erases the previous map. I made at least 6 different maps trying this game.  It is full of bugs, beware!  The game constantly interrupts your train of thought with popups in your face asking you to do things to take away from your storage. Supplies are always never enough of anything no matter how hard you try to fill up the storage of everything.... every item is important. The quests do the same thing... take away needed items.  I finally gave up.  Good luck to you, The game kept telling me that my map was not good enough.

_childDocuments_.review: The game works, but it feels like they got it to 1.0, realized it wasn't the next Civilization sequel, and finished it off as fast as possible before abandoning it. Missing a lot of QoL features other games of similar genre have, like building relocation, ways to cross water longer than two squares wide, planning, and the combat function feels vestigial. _childDocuments_.review: What is there is enjoyable and hints at what is to come with more development time. The art style is charming. The UI is clean and easy to navigate. The game does a good job of introducing the new mechanics in bite size, easy to understand portions. The framework is there for a great game. There are some interesting elements that i havent seen in this genre before such as a player controlled hero which has equipable items. It also seems as though they will be adding armies later. There is political relations with neighbors with which you build either positive or negative relationships with. I hope that multiplayer is added at some point. It seems doable at some point and would be interesting to see in this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great game, it just lacks certain needed content and it takes to long for certain aspects of the game to progress. For example, Lumber camps cannot be replaced and the sawmills only have the option for one worker rather than 2 to 6 workers. Moreover, there are some game breaking bugs such as commoners dying from starvation despite there being plenty of food.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I'm excited Fabledom has entered early access! This is a lovely city builder so far. Definitely more on the cozy side; you have to balance your resources but I wouldn't call it a punishing game at all. Much more content will be added as early access  continues, so my best advice if you're on the fence is to read the early access roadmap and see what features are most important to you. As it stands now, you can spend hours building a cozy little kingdom, but if you want a more polished complete experience, perhaps until the early access period is further along.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: When I came across this game I was very suspicious of yet ANOTHER city builder...I gave it a chance and read into the details:The Art style is INCREDIBLY cute, and unique. The game is brightly colored, many flowers and the water is fun. You can also click around the map and it reacts to your click (I loved this a little too much...) The animals are SO cute and I am looking forward to seeing more added in eventually...(Horses are my favorite winkwink Grenaa Games)The Narrator is SO funny and very cute with the little comments he makes here and there, but by NO means is he overbearing or annoying like some games have. The tutorials give you rewards instead of just being blunt and annoying, and the jobs they give are very calming and peaceful. As someone that suffers immensely with mental illnesses, PTSD, Depression, Anxiety and more...This game is a god sent. I cannot wait to see where this game goes, if you're looking for a great one to relax to this is it, consider supporting it's growth!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Still very barebones at the moment, but shows a lot of promise. The art style and humor are charming and on point, and the gameplay is relatively simple, but still offers a bit of challenge - but as I said before, it's far from done. I've played a little under ten hours and I've basically seen everything there is to do, almost twice over, so if you don't want to support something in it's infancy, the game might not be for you.That said, really looking forward to where this goes from here. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Very basic city builder. Fun theme and commentaries from the NPC narrator. There's a weird mechanic called "Head of Household" and some other subtle things that you have to pay a lot of attention to. Apparently residents aren't capable to get their own food, coal, or other materials to survive. Played for 10 hours straight and had a ton of fun. It encourages a separation of rich and poor and there are a lot of little mechanics that are nuanced and so much to pay attention to in order to be successful.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting this game to be released for $20 - $25 but wow, thank you devs for a much better price. Sometimes these prices increase as the EA game grows, and I would say especially right now it is worth it.Very cute, chill, plenty of challenge for now...while the roadmap for development isn't specific as far as timing goes, it does show there is a lot more on the way. If it's already this good, then I eagerly await for more.Bonus: It has winged piggies.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I'm obsessed with this game! I grew up playing SIM City, and Fabledom has all the same fun elements but the fantasy setting is so much cuter. I love creating beautiful spaces and scrolling through town, watching my fablings till soil, care for tulip fields, and cart goods back to their home. So relaxing!I typically play on casual mode but have also enjoyed many hours in creative mode (instant builds, no worrying about resources or cost; just relax and create a beautiful fantasy world). Some tips for success: - Prioritize getting lumber (lots of lumber!)- Manufacture coal early and don't stop (keep expanding with your populations)- Add lots of desirability boost items so more visitors will want to stay in your kingdom

_childDocuments_.review: You can read my other reviews The dream of living in an enchanted land, filled with fables, mystical beings, and a lush, endless forest, has always captured the imagination of many children. Fabledom allows players to experience a piece of this magical world, letting them build their own enchanted kingdom.I stumbled upon Fabledom in my Steam search feed unexpectedly. Although the City Builder genre isn’t my usual choice, this game stood out with its unique graphic style and overall charm. It creates an enchanted world where humans can live harmoniously with fairies, cyclops, knights, and princesses. From the beginning, players are welcomed by a guiding voice that accompanies them throughout the adventure, referencing well-known tales and becoming a friendly narrator, commenting on choices and telling the story of the player’s created adventure.The game’s objective is to build a city that can withstand different seasons and fend off unfriendly forces from neighboring kingdoms, all while seeking love in those kingdoms. Although it doesn’t feature a “flesh and blood” main character that you can actually see, Fabledom invites the player to enter this enchanted world with its method of creating diplomatic relationships and even allowing the choice of a preferred romantic partner. This is an unusual but quite fun mix, where the story ends up being shaped by the player’s small choices.Building a city, managing resources, and maintaining friendly relations with neighboring kingdoms might seem daunting, but it’s actually quite relaxing. The game introduces small challenges gradually, allowing players to adapt to new buildings and residents, without ever leaving the player confused and without direction. However, some resources take time to produce or gather, so maintaining a balance between the population and resources is crucial to avoid shortages. There is no sense of pressure to build a certain building, although there are small side quests that can be a bit tricky due to resource logistics and lack of time to complete them.Regarding the story, its direction is entirely affected by the player, by their romantic decisions or the enmities they will build with neighboring kingdoms. In this sense, I believe there is some replayability, and the player will be embraced by different lines of text, bringing a laugh or two throughout the process. These romantic relationships also impact the kingdom itself, as courting a certain character requires building something to please them. For example, to court the local Bard, you need to construct musical elements throughout the city, such as a building that will be occupied by kingdom residents, turning the town into a daily party.Fabledom is perfect for those looking to escape routine and relax, spending hours in a peaceful experience of building their own fairy tale. I genuinely believe this is something that can appeal even to those who don’t make City Builders a regular “diet.”

It's adorable, seems to be balanced and has a lot of interesting mechanics that I can't wait for the developers to flesh out.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and chill city builder.I love how the game handles the various housing/citizen levels. You initially have your peasants and build a nice little rural area with little gardens for each house.Then the housing system shifts slightly with Commoners. Here you have a main building and can then lay foundations in the area around that building and place your houses and shops anywhere on those foundations and they automatically merge together to look great. You have a lot of freedom here to create cool internal courtyards between the houses for people to move through and for other decorations and buildings.The last set is your Nobles that all live in the Palace. This again shifts the system slightly, you place down your main palace and then have a bunch of other buildings that either attach to the palace or sit in the grounds around it. Again, a lot of freedom to create cool compounds and gardens within your palace area.There is still a few buildings to be added and some balancing needed, but overall a very fun experience. You can definitely see the love the developers have for this game and it is on the right track.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a classic city builder game. I love the cute romance story and the cute animations, there is lots of details when zoomed in. Started the game, the Tutorial is very ez to understand, the game is very user friendly.  I made it to the end of what early access gives us and I was very happy with what I got and how smooth it all plays. I love that you can break anything and get all resources back, makes rearranging your city simple and effective. The world events are nice bonus, loved when the village turned to cute skeletons.  I hope the rest of the game features come out soon as I had a ton of fun, I just worry about the resources, seem like so little for such a big map, and where will you get more stone if its all gone? There also needs to be more happiness buildings as only two get boring quick.  Would be nice to have a graveyard and tombstones for the dead Fabledoms. Overall I'm super happy with this game, as I have played many city builders over the years. Good job.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't the kind of game I would normally play, but this is made so well, that I've been totally sold 100% on it.The game play is seriously addictive due to the interface and learning curve being so simple and straight forward. The housing designs are absolutely fantastic and piece together perfectly.I'm truly looking forward to new additions in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Easy and relaxing game to play, I also like how you can change the speed of the game, pause it and save. I love the narrator. I have come back to this game a lot on and off, trying out different layouts.Looking forward to more updates and added features to this game develops.  I can see this gaming staved in my favorites list for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: A really cute city builder, it took me around 15 hours to complete doing everything. Fabledom is really engrossing and I highly recommend it! The only issues I had was with starving villagers which seemed to happen when they were jobless or the head of the household (with around 1k food). I also really think the Nobility system could be better as I seemed to spend the whole game with 0. There was an encounter to banish witches that needed 30! I was lucky to get to 25 once. I don't feel like you shouldn't lose nobility for failing quests. I also feel that missions were introduced too late into the game and were kinda pointless by the end. _childDocuments_.review: It's a really fun and really pretty colony sim that succeeds in many areas, but there are a few concerns that have begun to frustrate me after many hours. It's gonna sound like I hate this game, which couldn't be further from the truth. I just have some issues that I hope can be addressed in the future, so that this game can blossom to be a true gem.My biggest problem is the amount of resources required for many buildings in the mid to late game.I'm constantly battling building more homes. I'll be running out of food, so I build more farms, then I'm running out of wood, so I build more lumber yards, then I'm running out of stone and food again. but I don't have enough homes. Then once I have enough homes and everything else, all my fablings start getting sick and dying, so I'm perpetually in limbo trying to save enough resources to advance so that I can build hospitals. I just never have enough. I feel like the population requirements to advance are too steep, or the materials gained from farming/mining/cutting trees is just too low. The few times that I have successfully made it to the point where I can build a palace, I really start getting overwhelmed. I appreciate the dynamic nature of how most things are built, but the palace system just falls flat. None of the pieces fit together in any sort of logical way, which makes the foundation of the palace totally arbitrary. These buildings should all just be individual pieces. and the palace should mostly be for housing like the previous tier. It's really confusing. Even worst of all, is that even if you manage to build all of them together in one cohesive clump, you can't even have enough nobles to staff every building. And there doesn't seem to be any way to place more homes for them.Mountains are a huge hurdle that can hardly be overcame due to being unable to modify terrain, or build ramps to access the tops in useful ways.Walls should just cost gold, and should be built instantly like roads. They are purely aesthetic until you are placing ballistas and the like. They don't even provide beauty.The map selection is also pretty pointless. There is no difference between any of the choices other than the a few randomly selected sizes and frequencies of things that should just be selected from a drop down instead of rolling over and over for a large map, with few hills, medium ocean, and dense forests. The proximity of other kingdoms to your location make no mechanical difference in game either. your messengers reach each zone at the same speed. This could be more useful if you could provide some kind of image of what the zone will actually contain, so that you aren't starting games over and over again to get a map that you actually like. It would also be nice to zoom out more while you're in game.There doesn't seem to be any real trading with other kingdoms either, which seems like a missed opportunity. let me use my surpluses to gain resources I'm lacking.My final complaint is that you can't place any resource nodes or modify the terrain in any way within creative mode. That would really seal the deal for this game type. I'm sorry if it sounds like I'm just tearing this game to shreds, but I'm just critical of things I love. This game really is amazing though, especially for the price. It's hard to beat a deal this good.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but it is a city builder with a few unique cool twists. Become the ruler of a fantasy kingdom! Build up your small empire right from the start by erecting the first building with a few settlers on a meadow and then adding newer and better buildings and connecting them all with roads. If necessary, your people can also walk across the grass, but it's quicker on paved roads. The more attractive your city is, the more new inhabitants (called Fablelings) will come to live and work here. So not much has changed in the essential game principle since the great-grandfather of the genre, Sim City (Maxis, 1989). What has changed, however, is the graphics. Today, the graphics are in 3D, can be zoomed in and viewed from all sides. It looks good, but my computer's fans are roaring like in Cities: Skylines II, even though my RTX 3060 graphics card is well above the minimum requirement (GTX 1060 / RX 580).First, we build a small farmstead and assign a head of family. Heads of families make sure that the inhabitants of the individual villages have everything they need to be happy (especially food). Add to this a well that supplies the entire immediate area with water, and the first new Fablelings arrive in our developing village. Basically, new Fablelings arrive every eight days as long as you have enough living space and your kingdom appears attractive to new settlers. You then always have to decide whether you want to accept them or not. If you don't have a residential building, you will have to turn them away. As soon as you have a farm, you can decide what you want to grow there. The first industrial plants will soon be added, starting with a logging camp. So far, Fabledom plays like one of the usual city-building simulations.One of the special features of Fabeldom that you won't find in any of the other city-building simulations are the princesses (or princes...) who would like to get to know you better so that they can rule your country together with you. In the beginning you are single, and as the game progresses you can marry a suitable partner. Of course, you can also organize a lavish fairytale wedding in your town.Keep track of a variety of different buildings required for production chains, build the necessary infrastructure (especially a tavern) so that your fabulous people are happy and pay taxes well. With enough tax money, you can continue to expand your settlement and build a circus or a huge theater. Military buildings are also a must, because if your settlement is doing too well, there will soon be enemies who want to share in your wealth. Just building a wall around your territory will not be enough to fend off the riff-raff or vicious fantasy monsters. The administration soon becomes quite complex - many inhabitants, buildings and a balance of the necessary resources (vegetables, wood, stones, coal, money, grain) have to be managed. Fortunately, there is a very useful overview menu that shows you your inhabitants and buildings at a glance. With a little money you can buy neighboring regions, which you can then also colonize. A special resource in the game is your nobility, which you receive for particularly noble deeds (e.g. donations).Cozy city-building simulation. Build your village and watch the lovingly animated inhabitants go about their daily work, construct new buildings and manage complex economic cycles. Defend yourselves against attacking monsters, watch out for mean witches and employ noble heroes. Establish diplomatic relations with neighboring kingdoms to trade. You are king in your fantasy realm, and in addition to managing the realm, you must also take care of your own love affairs. Fabledom plays like a mixture of Sim City and Die Sieder 2 with a few dating sim elements. Suitable for players who just want to settle and build in a relaxed way, as well as for fans of more challenging city-building simulations.
