_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game - definitely looking forward to when it has been built out more. Currently it is very bare bones and not much here for more than 8 hours of play and little incentive for replayability. There's a bunch of opportunities for this game to make the game feel better.1. Needs to be a clearer explanation of where income comes from - if it is only from the citizens then I believe we should be able to generate gold from buildings, or depending on the quality of worker (peasant vs commoner) we should be able to generate resources faster - so we can trade (sell) to other kingdoms for gold. 2. We need to be able to relocate people to different houses.  I have 2 areas in my city for housing vs workplaces. I would like to make sure my people work closer to home so I can manage happiness. But population automatically fills older built houses instead of houses closer to workplaces. I should be able to relocate people so I can move them to houses closer to workplaces I need to fill. 3. Stockpiles - it would be great if stockpile employees worked to distribute resources amongst other stockpiles - so that we we don't end up with 1 stockpile on 1 end of the map with all the coal - for example.4. Labourers Hut - more than 1 labourer should work on a building at a time. If there is only 1 building being built, all labourers should be working on it - not 1 working and the others sitting around. If there's multiple buildings, then a fair distribution of labourers if fine. However, if a building is prioritised then all labourers should focus on it. 5. Buildings should be able to be rotated once built. It's a small QOL thing but it would help. Condomoniums are the worst for this. If the townhouses have a door facing another building or a wall then people can't access it and get stuck all the time. 6. At around 100 pop gold generation is too slow (if you've kept up with jobs and everyone is employed). It takes 10 minutes to save gold to do 1 action, then you just wait around. Very disengaging part of the game. 7. Walls don't seem practical. Given cities are built in a sprawl and extended out based on tiles purchased, I don't understand how walls would be an appealing aesthetically as they would be going everywhere. 8. Pathways should have an upgrade option. If I want to upgrade my dirt road to cobblestone I should be able to just select and upgrade, or have an upgrade tool similar to the destruction tool. Also upgrading should be discounted (eg. dirt to cobblestone would cost 3 instead of 5)9. I'm sure this is planned for when the fishing hut becomes available - but fish tiles in the water should actually show fish (think Age of Empires)10. Finally we should be able to place buildings down even if we don't have the resources for them (but not able to click build) so we can do "town planning" with the buildings' outlines.  Overall I think this city builder has a lot of potential, the devs just need more time to put more meat on the bones. Excited to see where it goes.

_childDocuments_.review: So, Fabledom is a really fun way to kill time for people who enjoy city/colony builder/management games. I'll lead with that so you can tl;dr if you want. The humor isn't the greatest ever, and kind of repetitive, but still amusing to me even fifty-some hours later. The graphics are appropriately cartoonish for a game featuring flying pigs as a visual gag. Having said that? There are some problems with the game's back end that become evident the longer you play.The most immediate concern of mine is that the regional maps don't actually show you anything about what your region looks like. In fact? Your region isn't even spawned into existence until AFTER you pick a map region. Regional maps also don't inherently follow the descriptors given for them on the map either. They seem to be 'suggestions' rather than rules. I've selected a map region that stated it had 'None' for ocean. Technically true, but it was flooded with lakes to the point where half of my starting grid square was unusable (because you can't even start fishing until later in your city's development). There's an option to select to NOT spawn any mountains or hills. But there are times I've selected that option and they still spawned into the map anyway. So, the map itself has some problems. I'm sincerely hoping that fixes are coming for those, because they seem like glitches to me rather than features. That'd be a horribly feature for a game like this.Next is the Hero mechanic. While it does have its uses? It is horribly, and I do mean HORRIBLY underutilized. There's zero focus on the hero at all, he's just a useful tool to clear out 'encounters' on the map, and doing so gets you some interesting fixtures for your city as a reward. The primary problems with the hero mechanic is that there is zero visual variance in the hero, and what few customization options you have are pointless and boring. You can equip a hat and a series of three amulets. That's it. One hat buffs health and regeneration, the other hat buffs damage and attack speed. Furthermore, the options to get additional amulets are basically self defeating. You can kill Bob Barkskin to get a regeneration amulet, sure. But why would anyone do that when befriending him gives you a global buff to wood production? The choices aren't very competitive, which makes them basically non choices to begin with.And then there's the Nobility system. A system in which you, as the ruler, make choices and either gain or spend nobility accordingly. You help people, you gain nobility. You spend nobility? You remove threats or get stuff. Pretty simple and straight forward, and I love it as a thematic component of this game. The problem is that it is horribly unbalanced and unless you're playing on the easiest difficulty? You will basically never have any nobility to spend when you need it because the events requiring you to spend it are far more frequent than the ones where you can gain it. And half the time, the events where you gain it are 'one and done' events you'll never see again, where almost every single Nobility expenditure event repeats ad nauseum. This is kind of a blunder on the devs part, but I don't really view it as a deal breaker, even with all the others, because the system allows for many other ways (at least at normal difficulty and below) to overcome the challenges that spending Nobility would get rid of anyway. The witch wants to starve your people by making them twice as hungry? Cool. Ramp up produce development and flood your graneries with vegetables.Which brings me to another opportunity lost. You have five different kinds of vegetables you can plant, but there is no distinguishable incentive to have variety. All five are simply lumped under 'vegetables' in terms of your food production and consumption categories, and for that matter? There's no real point to making pork farms, chicken coops, or fishing huts either, really. First of all, none of them can even remotely keep pace with the vegetable farms, and again, there's no mechanic that requires you to have them in the first place. The only real reason to make pork farms is just to move a herd of winged pigs out of your way when you're building something else.In short? While this game is hilarious to me, and still fun to play? It has a lot of little problems right now, and many a little makes a mickle as the saying goes. I'm going to keep playing it anyway, because the fun aspects of the game still more than make up for it's deficits, but these might be deal breakers for anyone else looking the game over.

_childDocuments_.review: In a few words: Charming, but not without issues.Having only played up to town houses, my partial impression is that the primary game play loop is healthy, if a bit basic. There are not too many resources to manage right away, and the production chains are very simple. New citizens trickle in slowly and the margins on production per worker feel fairly thin, I don't think I've ever felt like I had an overflowing stockpile of anything most of the time. While this does feel fairly balanced it I also felt like I didn't have much agency in selecting what resources to pursue, every new citizen already had their job decided the moment they arrived since allocating them to any other resource would quickly guarantee a shortage.I don't think the margins being thin would bother me as much if it wasn't also necessary for me to manually assign them to the specific job sites. This problem becomes particularly egregious in winter when farming tasks can no longer be completed, but the citizens stand around at their assigned farming job sites anyway requiring a tedious UI dance each year to temporarily reassign them one-by-one to other work.I haven't touched much of the systems related to diplomacy or martial stuff, if there's much to be said for it then it's not apparent during the early-mid phases of the game, if the structure/development tiers are a reliable read on it.On a few positive notes, the overall design is endearing and the artwork and little cartoony details are cute and fulfill the fairy tale theme nicely. The interface does a serviceable job and tells you most of what you want to know in an intuitive way.As a platform for future development, I think it has excellent potential, even if it's excusably rough in some spots at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Gave me Settlers III vibes when I first saw it, but it's different.  There's cutesy graphics and basic production chains, but this is by no means a "relaxing" city builder. Certain mechanics are not explained very well, and it takes trial and error to figure them out. I didn't like how the fablings seemed stupid sometimes, going to a storehouse instead of to a production site that is right near them.There are no forced battles in this game. There's something you can build that will invite invasions if you want some defense action, but there is no going forth and conquering territory. My army was basically there for embassy missions (which reward resources).There's some fable elements in the game, which I guess is all part of the cute element to the game. _childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend it? MAYBE.It's a chill city building game, slow paced with no consequences (not in a good way). The marketing material is misleading, the witches and dragons for example are just "events" and serve no purpose but to give some debuff to the city which can be removed almost instantly. The Cyclope, you would expect to protect the city when someone invades you, but in practice it just walks around and "spreads joy" as there are no invasions and you don't really need any army or walls or fear of any danger as they are "optional". The flying pigs (which just walk around on a 2x2 square) are just a resource for the slaughter house. You can either anger or befriend the other kingdoms, nothing really happens, maybe just some price increases when trying to trade with them. Also, no end game content - the game feels somehow unfinished towards the end. For example, It tries to slow down the pace of the game itself (even more) by increasing the time you get more Fablings (citizens) which doesn't really matter as they are all unemployed because you got too many buffs, too much money, too many materials and not much space left to build production as you don't need it anymore. Honestly, I think it's a wasted opportunity to create some very good city building game as the game mechanics are well though and play great and the premise of the game is fun, Shrek style fairy tale world with much potential.If you want to play a game for about 20 hours that's chill with nice aesthetics, try it out. Otherwise look for something else. I don't think it's a bad game, I just think it's just not what I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: For being early development, I have already clocked 8 hours and continue to add more. The game is extremely cute, easy to understand, and accessible for casual gamers. Due to the nature of it being in early development, it does lack content and has a couple bugs. A couple suggestions to make this game more enjoyable without over complicating it would be:Content:- multiplayer to trade with friends- a cathedral (solely for the aesthetic purpose, could possibly boost happiness)- being able to move a building without having to completely demolish it- horses or carts to allow stockpilers to move resources more easily- more decorations/having decorations improve happiness- more events (such as the witch)- a night cycle (could have unique events or limited jobs like a tavern?)- being able to replant Bob- a flower shop to use flowers and boost currency- allowing the villagers to use the dice table (or at least see them interact with their environment)- showing a range on storage such as the granary or stockpile (able to be toggled)- being able to place decorations on top of pathingBugs of notice:- the villagers consistently starve even when you have a surplus of food- villagers constantly get stuck (this may be "where is my body," but I am not sure)- the pigs cannot be moved or killed so you have to build around them- certain buildings will not demolish (such as the condo)Overall, this game is 100% worth your money. My friend and I have an hour/dollar rule in which a game is worth it's money if you play for the amount of hours you spent on the game ($1=1hour). I can easily see this game going over it's hour/dollar limit, as I have only had it for two days, clocked 8 hours, and it is still in early development.

Being told a villager died and having to see if he was working for that one vital Inn or mill is somewhat annoying.- The game should give you more info on which buildings are inactive, what stockpile is full, which parts of the city are unhappy, etc. Now I'm constantly guessing.

_childDocuments_.review: Strongly recommend trying this game out! If you're a fan of light, simple city-builder type games, then you'll feel right at home with this one. I've been following this one since its early days on Twitter. It's had a LOT of polishing up and feels very well put together, and the dev team is fantastic and very receptive to its fanbase!GAMEPLAY: ★★★★Almost perfect, for what this is! It's your typical square-grid builder type interface. UI feels good, it's simple and to the point. Placing buildings isn't terribly finicky, and has improved a fair bit since the game's initial EA started. But there's more to it than placing buildings and making your citizens happy by giving them access to resources. On the side, you can direct a hero to interact with event items scattered throughout your area. Often, this yields rewards. In the future, heroes will have a much greater role in terms of gameplay. Lots of potential that's actively getting realized, bit by bit!GRAPHICS: ★★★★★Fantastic stuff! It's very cute and stylized, has a low impact footprint on systems, and does a very decent job giving off that cartoony fantasy vibe. The shaders and particle effects integrated in the environments are very well done and textures blend seamlessly in with each other in a very organic fashion. I'm excited to see what other visuals we'll get as the game grows.SOUND: ★★★★Music is nice and fits the vibe well, changing dynamically with events as they come, they did a decent job keeping the feel of a fantasy hamlet without going crazy on the brass and string section like you find in so many other games to feel "epic". Maybe that's a personal taste of mine, but I like that the music is a little more understated and subdued to feel relaxing and immersive. The sounds of the villagers, buildings, and environment ambiance is also very well done. Nothing's loud or too plosive on the ears.STORY: ★★★Okay, so there's not much to tell, but it is pretty charming at premise! You take on the role of a lord, new to the region, and start off building a settlement for your little villagers. Shortly thereafter, you'll begin to integrate in the community of other local empires as a new neighbor, while seeking out a cute, romantic bond with one of the regional lords and ladies! Along the way, you'll solve dilemmas for your people and send your hero out to investigate mysterious events in the realm. Right now, it's pretty simple for what it is, but the devs have much more in mind for this game as it grows. The game's trying to tell a story with you at the helm, after all.ACCESSIBILITY: ★★★★As this is an early access game, there's still a lot to improve upon and give us as users. Right now, unfortunately, there isn't a ton in the way of accessibility features. But the devs are listening in discussions and are eager to jot down and use feedback to improve the game. No colorblind support as of yet, but the game does allow for personalized controls. Newbie experience with the game makes learning how to play as a first-timer to city builders a breeze, and you can disable such tutorials if you're already practiced at it. And the UI's got a fair number of languages supported! (English, traditional Chinese, simplified Chinese, French, German, Russian, Spanish, and Portuguese) More can be added as time goes on and development focuses on these QoL additions.OVERALL: ★★★★Definitely worth picking up and trying! It feels great to play and it'll only get better with time and more feedback from the community! This is a much smaller dev team and they're very eager to make this game go far.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really like this game. I actually love it. It's exactly what I was looking for. I like a good, challenging game like Warcraft III, or Age of Empires, or whatnot. But I've always wanted to play a version of those games that were more open-ended, lower-stakes, and lower-stress.  This is that game.I'm actually a bit nervous that the developers will increase the difficulty.  If they do, I hope they keep this "casual" experience an option, because it's the very reason I enjoy it.  That's not to say there's *no* challenge, or *no* risk inherent to the decisions you make in-game, but they're generally not game-endingly serious. Winter comes, and if you're poorly prepared, maybe you'll lose some of your population, but your game won't suddenly end.  Looking forward to playing more :)

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is a nice, relaxing city/kingdom builder for more chill gaming sessions. It's easy to learn and understand, and not too complicated for people who tend to get overwhelmed by the management features in other games of its kind. Unlike other games of the same genre that only have one speed setting, Fabledom allows you to speed up time in order for the Fablings to walk and work faster (similar to the functionality in the Sims). This is definitely not the kind of game to speedrun or grind for more serious players who enjoy other city expansion games like Cities: Skylines and SimCity.There are a few features of the game that could use some tweaking and adjusting, such as the ability to prioritize the construction of different buildings. Whenever I have had this box checked, it does not seem to make the Fablings "prioritize" the selected structure, and they continue to distribute resources to other buildings instead. I also read a review mentioning the capability to decline courting other rulers. While I do enjoy the feature of discovering your own "happily ever after", I agree that there should be an option to simply remain friends with the leaders of surrounding realms. Finally, there seems to be a lack of efficiency with resources being moved from one place to another, as I have found my Fablings sitting around with "nothing" to do, despite there being ongoing construction and expansion.Regardless, the design and roleplay aspect of the game is a cute and fun integration for a city builder, making it a simple yet entertaining game to play when you have a few hours to spare. If you're interested in this game, I would wait for it to go on sale, or for more updates to be released to justify the listed price, as it is quite high for an early access game. I believe there is plenty to do between updates, and a lot of fun to be had. This fantasy-esque city builder is straightforward and quite easily addicting, and I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to Banished but with heavier emphasis on fantasy. Take in peasants, commoners and nobles to grow your ever expanding kingdom. Build armies to aid or hinder nearby kingdoms or fight off domestic threats such a troll and dragons. Once you've amassed enough wealth and power start the courting process of one of the many princes and princesses of the realm to obtain even more power.Overall Fabledom is a great little game. With a colorful palette, soothing soundtrack and unique bubbly art style Fabledom is a pleasant experience for the casual player. The only complaints I've have with Fabledom is the various bugs some of which are easily ignored others makes the game much more difficult. Major bugs:Encounter NPC's don't disappear after encounter.There's been a cyclops standing in my Kingdom for the past 15 years. Speaking to them only spawns more cyclops that pile together in one spot.Happiness:Moving a noble from one building to another in the palace can cause Happiness to drop by a lot.Fabledom is a great game though could use a bit more elbow grease. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is genuinely the most charming city builder I have played in recent memory (or ever). The designs of the world, the buildings, and even the people have a personality to them that is so distinctively "Fabledom". I honestly don't have any complaints that can't just be attributed to the game's status of "Early Access" at the moment of writing this review. I do hope the final version has some form of map/kingdom maker (grid, preferably) for more replayability. Cause, dang, i'm planning to play this A LOT. Maybe, a really basic (and, I mean BASIC) character creator for yourself to really have the feel that you are someone to the kingdom and not just a faceless god trying to get hitched to an equally immortal being, that unlike you, has a face and personality. However, that's more of a want than a need for me to play this already amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have the pleasure of spending 6.8 hours playing the demo alone and the early access release did not disappoint. Absolutely adorable and comfy game that isn't so easy that you fly through it. I spent almost 8 hours just taking my time on a single run of the first stage of the early access. If you're looking for a finished game though definitely wait and allow the dev's to complete it which I can say they 100% will. But regardless if you're looking for a cozy game or a simple strategy city builder this game will definitely appeal to a large audience.As updates continue to come out and I consistently fall in love with the game, it was easy to decide to nominate it for some of the steam game award categories. _childDocuments_.review: I’m holding off to make a proper review once the game gets released, but I think it has a good amount of features for a first impression. The first thing I noticed is how striking its visual identity is, everything looks so cohesive and pleasing it is really a feast to the eyes with its Aardman-style animations and welcoming yet witty narration. There are two modes: the sandbox mode and a proper city builder version with resources management and progression. Once you learn the proper controls it gets easier to make the realm you wish and it even has things like hero units that might be further expanded in future updates.Every update they add a new layer of gameplay, the most recent one is the ability to build an army that will eventually be expanded upon and I can notice improvements in the game’s overall performance too. I can’t wait for the Elixir of Love update with the promised fairytale elements, if this game writing is anything to go by this will be a blast to play.This is a promising title made by two people, yet the quality and the solid foundation shows promise.

_childDocuments_.review: There are many like it, but this one is mine.This city builder is just it. It's what I've been trying to find in the last 10 city builders I've purchased.The gameplay/loop is wonderful, and yet there is so much depth missing (I'm still loving it). It's very "magical" in the graphics and fairy like - some people might think it's cringe but it's alright, it's calming in many ways.The game shines by doing the small things right. Like 100% perfect. How to place things, details within buildings, population and more. I can't wait for the military to get into the game. I'm missing a lot of buildings now.Well done to the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is adorable and like other reviews state, the first few hours are kind of fun and give the impression that the game is going to get more interesting as you unlock more things and see more events. It didn't.My three biggest issues:There is only one generic "cozy" music track that plays over and over again. It became grating after a few hours. I'm sure there are people who are cool with just popping on their own playlist but I personally would appreciate at least a small rotation of immersive and unique music.Events are anticlimactic, you just get what you get. Other than a positive or negative effect depending on what you choose, they don't feel very immersive or satisfying. You just wait out the timer or plop down your reward on the map. The beanstalk, for instance, was heartbreakingly disappointing for me. No giant, no scene, just a themed schematic and it was over. It was my first seemingly big event and after waiting so long for it to grow and then again for the hero to climb it, I was completely disillusioned.The map has a few interesting little things on it, like a missing shoe and the occassional fairytale visitor, but even if there were more, they too are anticlimactic. The shoe, for example, can be given back to the owner that you never meet for one currency or sold for another. That's it.There are other issues, like being unable to relocate some important structures like houses and your heroes not interacting with the town (or even moving without your input) and no one watching the entertainers, but the game would be so much more interesting if these things were expanded on. A negative or positive effect can make the game more challenging, but not necessarily more immersive in my opinion. As it is now, it's a sweet little builder that needs more TLC before it can really shine. The artwork is lovely, the narrator is genuinely funny and the builder aspect is easy to get into.Also, the pigs don't fly. The wings are cosmetic. :(
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential, but the resource aspect of it is terrible and extremely slow. I don't know how much I'm producing or consuming. You have to build many farms, but the more farms you get the more workers you need, and the population to resource ratio needs balancing. Also I dislike the fact that the "head of household" doesn't count as someone you can assign as a worker. I would also like to be able to move homes and objects without destroying them first. It's hard to build up happiness when it depends on how good of the area the home is located in, it wouldn't be a problem if you received the resources you spent on it back. Other than that I'm looking forward to the games development.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY! Unfinished product, rushed from early access, abandoned by dev already!Only 1 year in early access, abandoned 2 months after full release.It has same bugs as in early access, still very bad balancing, but this time the other way around: before it was way too easy, now it's not-hard, because you cannot really loose (when out of food, someone suddenly will give you a lot).Amount of people joining village cannot fill all required jobs for producing resources/food. This is due to weird idea, that every home has to have a worker that cares for that home (forgot the word) and, at the same time, lives there. Basic home allows for 3 people living, new ppl are joining your village always in pairs (2 new villagers every 8 days - always). With this mechanic, you will very quickly fall short on production workers.During single gameplay on one map (~3h), grid system for placing objects (buildings, chests etc.), bugged out several times, showing objects between the grid, with final placement being in completely different area then i chose.BEWARE! This game is not even worth -50% in current state. It will not get better, it will not receive updates anymore. This was announced by dev in most recent update. Besides, it's bland and boring, feels more like puzzle game, finding best placement of buildings in relation to workplace distance/home desirability/unwanted areas/happiness.Graphics are ugly even on ultra - especially foliage, all the grass and bushes are 2d sprites. The only thing that changed since ea is a bit better performance. It's still very high for a game looking like that.Music is nice, but gets boring quickly, soundtrack is very poor, i have a feeling it's actually a single song. Game audio is also badly mastered between levels of music/effects/narrator/interface.Narrator in menu is annoying and mostly unfunny, saying something every few seconds, making it really hard to focus before you start the game (choosing map, designing your banner etc.). To the point that i mute all audio until i start the game.Also, designing a banner is very limited, but that doesn't matter much.I also get a feeling that "wand" jokes are dirty, you might consider that before buying it for the kids. There is basic information missing for all buildings. Makes it hard to manage. You will not be aware of a lot of stuff until you build something or encounter an issue. Like in many similar games, worker home distance to their workplace matters (supposedly), but the game won't tell you that until you place such worker in job far away from home.Editing existing fields of a farm building is cumbersome, you need to remove single square one by one while maximum field can have 40 of them :)Generally, it's missing a lot of quality of life enhancements.Anyone who already has it can go to Overview (O) -> Event log; it's full of pages containing:"Bla Bla finished construction, this this and thatBla Bla finished construction, this this and thatBla Bla finished construction, this this and that" - this is a quote from the "fully finished product" that left early access.I wish the developers all the unhappiness and problems in their future endeavors. No need to thank me, you deserve it all.I bought this game for exactly half of current full price, during early access discount, and i still feel ripped off.I will get my refund somehow.

_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: So I sank a ton of hours into this game because WOW it's easy but fun and satisfying! Nothing is difficult, just cozy building and kingdom-sculpting! I've started about 6 or 7 kingdoms at this point to try different things or go about different ways and I haven't gotten bored yet: it's easy to just spring up your kingdom the way you want and let your fablings take care of things as you keep an eye on the big picture. I particularly love that nothing in this game is tedious and repetitive: that's what has made it so easy for me to start new kingdoms, it's just set up and go with no grind to get to the good parts!I cannot wait to see what is added in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: ★ ★ ★ ★ ★ - meFabledom is by far one of the most beautiful, relaxing, and enjoyable games I've ever played. Whilst in Early Access until full release this week, it was also by far the best Early Access entry I've ever played too, with regular updates, and a very well-established variety of features. From the graphics and art style, to the cute and minute-to-minute details in the gameplay itself, I haven't felt this well-catered for thematically since we last had a Discworld game... way back on the PS1! For a more modern comparison, imagine Kingdoms of Amalur having a meet-cute with Tropico, but with a far better support-cycle, and you have the joy that is Fabledom! I haven't played a city builder this attentively in such a long time, and I think it's a great throwback to the old days of Will Wright's Maxis, with all of my favourite genre trademarks of Terry Pratchett, the Fable series, or the Settlers, thrown in too. It is very VERY clear throughout the whole development cycle and play-through of the current core objectives, that this game is being made and updated with a lot of love, every item has a well-themed and humorous description, with an amazing (occasionally voiced) narration to accompany it. I really don't want to spoil the little details, as they're such an engaging part of the game for me, but you can find them elsewhere if you need to know more before you buy.There are still some mechanics and occasional bugs that crop up every now and then, BUT- like I said, until this weekend, this was an Early Access title, and the patches and hotfixes are consistent, not to mention the content additions, which never fail to make the game a more enjoyable experience. And it really is the evident ongoing love going into this game by its developers that keeps you patient for the next patch when the odd bug does happen.If ongoing development isn't your thing, I'd just say wait until the next major release mark happens, but, as someone who played Stardew Valley from the very beginning, I'd say there's a great experience to be had getting into a game like this early on, when you can see the good in it before it becomes popular, as you get to play witness to a very unique experience of growth, and almost feel like a proud parent when it becomes as celebrated as you think it should be. Small honourable mention to NerdCubed for introducing me to this game via a livestream that came up on Youtube a couple of weeks ago!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent addition to anyone's citybuilding library! The setting is extremely refreshing, and beautifully presented. The gameplay is satisfying, with no noticeable bugs or glitches, and the romance is inclusive of LGBTQ+ people!It is also encouraging to see a roadmap for where the devs intend to take the game going forward. All in all, an easy and hearty recommend, especially at the price they're asking.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: A nice light-hearted, family friendly take on the classic city builder. I played a campaign through on classic difficulty, which was a comfortable challenge level for me (I've played quite a few games like this but I'm not the greatest player). Tip: Make sure you have a strong economy and plenty of resources before you go for the third date mission, it can throw extra challenges at you!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: FabledomPros :- Relax, play at your own space- Beautiful game, cute graphic- Good humour- Very casual (maybe not a Pros for everyone.)Cons ;- No challenge. Did it at very hard. Because you advance at your own space, even if everything is more expensive, it is not more difficult, just take more time to advance.- The economy is not clear. You are not sure how many food your fablings need or other kinds of ressources. If I look I'm low on something, I just build more.- Lack of quests and special event.This is a good game for a casual. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to rate this game, but first I wanted to put some hours into it and do some of the achievements. 50 hours later and with all the achievements received here I am: strong 7/10, and the best type of 7/10, because it has all the potentials to go up to a 9/10 with some work and 10/10 with realistically speaking a year of work.  Here is what makes it a 7/10 for me: - Anxiety? What anxiety? Throw it out the window. This game made me relax like no other in a long time. Simply cute light-hearted fun is what you will get for your money. - Unique city builder with this little fably atmosphere. - The narrator is hillarous.- The pigs have wings, like how good is that. Extra points What I think this game needs more of:- Fixing the graphical issue. It takes away from the cute play doh-like graphics, that the anti-alising is bad for some reason even on high graphics. I saw that the team is working on it so big-ups for that, can't wait the finished thing!- As one of the great philosophers of our time, Britney, one said: Gimme gimme more, gimme more, gimme gimme morrreee. This what this game needs: more of everything: more characters, more heroes, more fable, more buildings, more events, more bioms, more more more. You get the point. - Some things are a bit inconsistent for me. You can have a love relation, but you can still flirt with anyone else, without any issue. I think it would be good if some characters reacted to this in different ways, a.k.a the characters also need more personality. Same for the relation. If you are courting a character, you can do any amount of quest that has a bad impact on the relation and the love will never be gone. I don't think this is optimal. You should lose relation points for being bad. - The trade system is just baaaad. Clicking and trying to guess the prices is sorta annoying even after 50 hours in. If I say I want 100 coal and I put my gold against it, it should automatically give me the number of gold I have to spend. Relation also has no effect on the price of stuff or the willingness to sell stuff so I'm not sure that is very logical either. As said earlier, if you fix these it's a 10/10. I recommend this game, but for now a strong 7/10. Good job, good luck in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: At this stage, the game still has incredibly slow progression, particularly due to how few and far in-between new citizens show up in your town. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: The game lacks general polish.When allocating workers to a building, it requires you to select a person, rather than the quantity of people working there. This creates inefficient city layouts and the need for you to do "housekeeping" with your workers and reassign them periodically from scratch, to ensure everyone is working as close to home as possible. This would not be an issue, if it did not take 1 click per each worker fired and 1 click per each worker hired. My kingdom has 400+ fablings, which means 800+ clicks (not counting many of the menu navigation clicks) just to make sure my city works.Furthermore, the gameplay is a bit... stale, to say the least. You could have had SO MUCH more story that could have been extracted from the "fairy-tale" concept, but chose to base every encounter with anything magical on a couple of textboxes. UNDERWHELMINGThe list goes on, for 20€, this is just quite frankly one of the worse games you could chose.

_childDocuments_.review: While it says I played almost 10 hours, most of it was AFK. I don't recommend this game as it lacks content. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Really just a solid and fun city builder. It's very much like a simpler The Settlers in setting up towns, making your people happy, keeping people fed and producing the resources you need to keep the town expanding. What makes it special is twofold: first, an absolutely charming overlay of fairy tale themes in events that happen and obstacles to deal with; and second, your main quest being to find a prince or princess to Happily Ever After with, and the city building largely being support for that. It's cute and fun and built on a solid core of a game with a large number of decorative elements to play around with.The only complaint I have is that the management tools are a bit basic for telling you how much stuff you need and how much you're producing, and for managing who does what job in a game where travel time is a major impediment to effectiveness, so problem solving is sometimes harder or more tedious than it should be. Still hasn't stopped me from playing it, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access but I still managed to fall in love with this game and can't wait for it to be finished.Relaxing background music with realistic hints of water, birds, wind and working sounds.Cute graphics. Funny storyteller. And even a creative mode.Lovely little details on every corner which are totally unnecessary for the story or the process itself but make the game so much more fun to look at.I really do recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Good, casual city builder game, needs a little polishing.  At times it almost feels like an idle city simulator.  It doesn't really have a lot of replayability currently, in terms of variety or content.  You can marry all the different rulers but the real essence of the game is the building of the city and managing of the resources.  Maybe they're planning to have more events in the future, such as army attacks, that sort of thing?  Reminds me of the old zeus or poseiden city builders from the 2000s, which i loved.  To that, they could modify the granaries and storage depots a bit.  In Zeus you could specify specific items for storehouses/ granaries to either get rid of or actively seek.  Right now you can just empty a storehouse but have a little less micro.  Having to hand automate, later on when your colony gets huge, where each colonists work can be hassle. Would be nice to see an autopause on event functions.  Like I said, at times this feels like an idle game, you set up what you want them to do and let them slowly work towards it.  But events happen such as new colonists without autopausing.  Right now the biggest bottleneck to growth is the rate at which new colonists come in.  More events, more intrigue, they have a fun, solid city builder.  With some polishing it could be fabulous.  Maybe variety maps, different campaigns, different resources dependent on each map?  Dunno.  If not, still a solid play.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I love city builder games and this one is really enjoyable. I especially love the narrator-he's hilarious! I look forward to future patches so I can continue to play and see how the game develops now that I've done all I can with early access content. I'm hoping for more events and quests and hopefully a bit of combat at some point. There are a few minor things that I hope get worked out too with pathing issues and a few items of inconvenience- like being able to replace gravel roads with cobblestone without destroying them first would be nice and save time. I still highly recommend this game if you want a cozy, fun, city builder to play and look forward to the update.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a beautiful relaxing fantasy city builder game that is not complicated in terms of game play then look no further.The game is still in early access but it will not stop you from training your creativity to make a beautiful kingdom. _childDocuments_.review: It's relaxing but engaging at the same time, like a jigsaw puzzle. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: So the game is excellent and has a lot of potential, but when they say early access, they should say demo because that is what this feels like. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game.The game is not as easy as it may first seem. This is a city builder with hidden logistics that you will need to learn. Until you do your town/city will suffer. You may not get to the stage where you learn enough to begin to enjoy your town/city building because some things just seem to make no sense. I hope the developers add more hints to help people with this. However once you begin to see the patterns in the game you will be able to relax and appreciate the fact that this is a good game. Not perfect, but good. City building games are a niche type of game. I think some can fall into the trap of seeing them as survival games, and that can mean you miss the patterns of city building. Fabledom looks cute but don't be fooled, you'll have to have your wits about you to succeed.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I've sent red riding hood on her way to her grandma's house in exchange for 70 bread. There is blood on my hands.(Bread in my tummy though, so like, you win some, you lose some.)Other than that, there's many buildings that should be making me money but, instead cost me upkeep. (Market, Adventurers guild, Laborers guild, Hospital, Town shop for example).Family support is a very cheap/bad/easy way out mechanic in order to "increase difficulty". The problem with this is that it DOES NOT make the game more difficult, it just makes it so that you have to micromanage your buildings (turn off hospital when there's no sick, other buildings when there is no direct need for it). This in my opinion goes directly against what a CITY BUILDER is. You're trying to create a beautiful, thriving and well functioning city, now because of this management instead of having a thriving city we have a city where 1/3rd of the buildings are semi-permanently unstaffed and closed.The laborers guild, upgrade of the laborers hut, does not replace the laborers hut. The game forces you to keep at least 1 hut existing.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: At the current moment, Fabledom is a very basic city builder game. It lacks content, I can probably play a game for about 2-5 hours at most without it feeling redundant. However, after that it feels like you're doing the same thing over and over. The graphics and story is cute, light, and fun. If you're looking for a city-builder that has more sustenance, I would look somewhere else. I will say I do look forward to seeing more from the game and what kind of content the devs will push out.

_childDocuments_.review: Love it already. Less individual-villager focused than games like Founder's Fortune but more personal and less systematic than games like Kingdoms and Castles. Some serious missing features as of now: no iron, or wool, etc. Also small things like no way to build upgraded roads over the old ones, and no way to delete roads en masse, only one block at a time. Also no way to assign specific villagers to a specific homestead, etc. But given the trajectory this early on I am excited to see what they continue to add. If you like colony simulators that are cute and fun, this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: So this *IS* as the reviews say, a relatively low key sim-colony-management game, with cute graphics and fairytale flavor. It is also just demanding enough in the details to regularly break the zen I'd get going and frustrate me.Why can some buildings be moved but not others? _childDocuments_.review: After playing the game more in depth I am giving a more detailed review of the game. I will keep it as short and easy to follow as possibleSummaryIn short, this game is in very early development and is still missing some important pieces in the early game, and has basically no mid or late game yet. If you are looking for experiencing a fulfillling story/charming and developed building experience, the game is not there yet. The designers are working fast and transparently, so I'd take a look in a few months and see if there is enough content for you then (I'd say after the 2nd roadmap patch it would be playable enough to enjoy more deeply). As for what the game offers now is an introduction and baseline to play around with and is engaging enough to keep me testing it.Pros- Charming theme with a lot of character and style. There is potential to be fleshed out more in a way a fable-esque game should be- The main foundations of the game in terms of resources and UI are clean and easily understandable. As the game develops, I am hoping for more unique or rare/useful items with the intriguing heroes system.- There is a charming story and larger map you can interact with that I am hoping to speak on more as the game develops. Promise of trade, war and love with neighboring kingdoms is a very exciting concept to me in this game.- Haven't seen any game breaking bugs or issues which is a huge plus for a game so early in developmentCons- While there are fantasy elements, its missing the trolls, goblins, fairies and other fable creatures that would really elevate the game. I am expecting to see these creature included after the next patch as enemies to fight.- There are some vital management views and options that are missing. Adding in additional overlays to see happiness and routes would be beneficial. Also adding negative/positive seasonal or yearly forecast yields would be immensely beneficial for planning the city or a district.- Not a lot story or interactions happening for a game based on stories. While it is early development, I'd love to see cutscenes of important benchmarks with the main story, and more importantly, interactions of fablings in the city. Seeing them attend street theatre, go to the inn, slack off at work, or interact with other fablings, buildings, and environments would be a huge boon to the theme of the gameCritiques/FeedbackWhile I listed out some of the more pressing feedback in the cons above, there are some other pieces that could use a touch  mentioned below.- Give Fablings experience in their set jobs, the longer they work the same job the better they are- Have different aged fablings, maybe even kids in the city who can't work or take up household spaces but hang around the city or at home to give more life to a city.- Give buildings upgrades, give storage workers a wagon to move more resources around the city faster. As the main source of resource transportation at the moment, they seem a bit slowIn conclusion the game looks great and feels great. I am giving a positive review as the game development is good and the designers are very active. I am hoping as the game reaches completion I can come back and remove all my cons! Hoping this game goes far.

_childDocuments_.review: I was in love with this game from the moment I loaded the demo. It's relaxing, easy to play and rewarding. Building is satisfying. Resource management doesn't grind to a halt in a split second like other games I've played. The world feels rich and vibrant. Having a hero you send off for encounters is brilliant - as are the choices you can make during these.The only negative things I can think of are likely just limitations of early access and some of these have already been changed in a patch. I'd love to see the ability to relocate buildings added - sometimes I've miscalculated my space and don't realise until much later. I'm sure we'll also see more courting options and combinations in the weeks to come.Overall this is an overwhelmingly adorable, satisfyingly cozy game and I cannot get enough of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Long time city builder player here. Pros:No bugs, glitches, everything works as expected (some balancing issues aside, obviously)Atmosphere is great - music, graphics, decorations, no complaints hereRelaxing gameplayThe initial beanstalk quest? Great. However, it is the only one in the gameplay at the moment that I've found, after 11 hours.Cons:Very little content. It's a great start, with a lot of potential. However, adding the "romance" encounter seems like jumping way too far while not taking care of other content issues first. Exploring ruins, meeting other NPCs, very shallow. There is no point of having the royalty "crowns" if all you do with them is click buttons yes and no. Make it more meaningful. Even if you simply add mini games to events it would make a world of difference. Right now, except for the beanstalk event, everything else is pointless and unrewarding. Other rulers - again, extremely shallow content.  UI issues:* When building anything, including decorations, the game forces you to go back and re-select the same item over and over again. Add an option to keep the current selection active (e.g. building a garden patch, I don't want to have to re-select the flower patch 15 times).* Please make the "do you really want to turn newcomers away" disappear. It is beyond annoying. If someone needs new settlers, trust me, they will keep an eye out for them. * Please stop changing the gamespeed without a notification. If I have it set on max speed, it's there for a reason. It should not be reverting back to snail pace without my input.* Replace the stockyards with actual warehouses, or barns or something. Anything besides the tiny platforms, of which you require 50247523 of in order to accumulate enough resources to build the castle. It is _really_ annoying.* The buildings menu needs to be changed to be more clear and organized. One long line for all the decorations is a no-go. * There is no way to tell while building how far away the commoners' townhomes need to be from homesteads to not get hit by negative decor*  Deleting content: if you delete a road with benches on it, it ONLY deletes the road OR the bench, requiring you to delete a second time. First pass leaves you with road patches on which the benches were set on. Best suggestion, allow to UPGRADE the roads instead of having to delete them and re-do everythingSuggestions:* The "romance" content, and all the interactions with the neighbors, the pop-up quests - they all feel like an afterthought, and are absolutely abysmal.  Making a game work is one thing, making the content enjoyable is another. Hire a good, creative writer for the scenarios, quests and personalities. I know this is preview, but I can see there has been a lot of effort put into the game already when it comes to gameplay details. But if your non-graphics non-gameplay related content is dead as a doornail, it won't hold anyone's attention, doesn't matter how cute or adorable it looks. If you had a good writer, it would show already.I will wait for an update before playing again. The game has a LOT of potential, however, I would have waited longer before releasing it to the public for a preview. The whole premise/selling point is the magical whimsical content - but apart from graphics, I don't see it being delivered as advertised.

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad, not great.  I wish it offered more variety for progression.Fabledom is just another game that makes you seasonally shift labor. Turn off farms because they don't grow in winter.  Move those workers to the things that get food in the winter like bakery and fisheries. Reverse this process in the Spring.  Put everyone back into agriculture.With a large population, this becomes tedious.Game wants you to constantly add more people, leading to unemployment or idle workers (due to seasons or waiting for resources to respawn).Progress is locked behind 'total population' so you have to saturate your space to unlock things.Map has limited resources, it is linear growth with a conclusion (stone and iron do not regenerate). Your citizens get unhappy if they have to walk too far, but the game wants you to expand expand expand.You finesse everything to fit into your land space so you can unlock more stuff to make it fit until iWin the game. Once you exhausted a map, you can start a new map and do the same things again.Exploit, Saturate, iWin.The characters, events, and story are repeated, always the same things, same characters, same events, same progress benchmarks.  The map is procedurally generated, so where you find stone or an event is somewhat randomized.Events are RNG, but based on current resources.  If you are failing, you get free stuff.  If you are winning, you get disasters.If you aren't exploiting the map enough, you get events that encourage you to exploit the map more.At first this game seemed pretty chill and cool, like you get to build a village and make it look neat, fun and fantastic story.. but no.  Not really.  It is just another game that makes you clearcut forests and saturate the lands with standardized buildings until you reach a certain quantity for victory.You get some gimicky things like a cartoon hero, some pseudo-fairytale events, but in the end it is just another reskin of any other game that makes you hack and slash resources for maximum gains while smothering the land with as many generic buildings and roads as possible.Creative mode is ok, since it has unlimited resources and all tech is unlocked.  My take away is since the game doesn't cost a lot, it isn't bad considering what you paid.  If you don't enjoy games that make you clearcut and saturate the land with generic buildings while micromanaging labor and resources, then maybe wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, but not replayable. It feels unfinished like it's still in early access.I binged this game hard during the weekend. I really enjoyed the mechanics. It was something I wanted to keep playing. I clearly enjoyed it enough to play it for 11 hours between two days. However here's what makes me give it a negative review:- There's no incentive to replay again. No collectables, no unlocks, nada.- Some mechanics don't work nor are explained like bridges. (You're telling me a long bridge won't cover this gap so my people are walking all the way around? What is the bridge even for?)- The relationship system is hardly a relationship. I screw people over all the time for any mission and it doesn't affect the relationship. If it becomes "not as happy smiley face", I just send a messenger to them and give them whatever they want.- There's no graveyard or children system so it gets to a point where you're waiting for time to pass so more people can move in. But depending on where you are in the story, it can take a while if you have low happiness due to unavoidable debuffs.- It got really repetitive. "People unhappy? Okay, let me drop all this money I have to give you guys some flowers. Oh look, you're happy again and I can move in 5 people at once." It's a waste of my time. I'm sure some people love doing this, but it gets old.- Not sure what an army is for. I never got invaded. Trolls appeared but just hung out. Easy to take out. I never won "The best army in the land" even though I was slayin like Meg Thee Stallion. - The beanstalk was the only cool thing and encounters stopped popping up. Is it a simple game? YesIs it meant for low maintenance people? It can beIs it too simple? YES. Is it worth the pricetag? NO. Please get it on sale. I paid full price ($20.99 and it's not worth that. I won't pick it up again unless if there's a major update.) I paid about $2 an hour to play this game. There's better out there if you're looking for something a bit more engaging with replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is absolutely loaded with charm and an equal amount of potential. If you're interested in a relatively laid-back city-builder, this one's for you. My Pros and Cons:Pros:- Easy to get into and maintain- Relaxing environment- Cheap!- Minimal/No bugs, certainly not gamebreaking ones- Easy mechanics- Mechanics generally work as intendedCons:- No ability to direct Fablings (like in Keflings) so sometimes it seems like they don't listen to prioritized builds- Minimal content (Obviously, being early access, this makes sense, but I feel I've seen mostly everything to see with around 6 hours played)- Repetitive music (Like 2 or 3 tracks)- Curse mechanic, which I'm not entirely sure is avoidable, that can happen at the worst times, frequently (Doubles food drain)There is a ton of potential to be tapped here. If I had to rate it right now, I'd give it a 7/10. Its very fun for what it is, but I feel for the most part that the money I put into it is stock for the future (which is good, because its a cheap entry point). There's enough here to give you some enjoyment for a day, and I recommend it, but don't expect to be bogged down for days on end just yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: The game, in this early stage, is simple, but very cute and laid back! The narration and literal storybook introduction sets this apart from other similar games. Some item descriptions are quirky and funny, and in my short 30 minutes of play time before writing this review I was blown away! This is a game I feel I'll come back to over and over as a comfort game. I'll again point out the narrator, it is REALLY nice to have the tutorial read out loud instead of reading page after page of text. The graphics, as simple as they are this early on, are very pleasing to look at, I was especially impressed by the snow on the ground! I look forward to seeing where this game goes. In my mind, all it needs is a bit of polishing, so far it is very enjoyable! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is my first attempt at city planning/management. At first, I was intimidated by the concept of planning the building of a kingdom and the management of the folks called Fablings and the industry. As time went by, I found the management tools provided in the game easy to learn since they are understandable and; I might add; cute. This game is very clever and cute. The battles are adorable and quite fun to watch. Beware of the witches, dragons, and trolls. These cute little critters can have a devastating effect on the kingdom and its people. No fear! The kingdom has a hero with his swordsman and archers to save the day from these tricksters. I would highly recommend this game to those who are beginners in this genre of gaming. The graphics are adorable and very well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game so far, and I really enjoy playing a more of a relaxing take on the city builder/colony sim genre, I know it's in early access and still in development but I would love to see these suggestions into the game.Add more animals for huntingAdd fruit trees, berry bushes and herbs (and maybe wild vegetables) for your people to gather when you don't have farms yetmore environments from the hot deserts to the cold tundra, for people who want more of a challenge (With harsh weather in those environments to boot like sandstorms and blizzards)Cultural architecture. What I love seeing in games in this genre is seeing different types of cultural architecture I'm able to build and admire. Wishful thinking on my part but I hope to see this features implemented in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only city builder where you place a building and then place the foundation.  My complaints are mostly of this nature - grammatical errors bad enough to actually mislead or stall the new player, because the words being used are inappropriate.  The tutorial messages tell you how to use features that haven't been introduced, using terms the game has not defined.  For example, it explains how to stop the game from putting attachments on buildings before attachments have been disussed or defined.  So when it becomes relevant, you wish you could bring back that tip, but you can't.  The "peasants" live in large, well-furnished homes.  All of them own dogs.  Pet dogs in this game take the place of constables in any other game.  They keep the populace from rebelling by digging up the flowers and barking all night.  Or something.  The game forces you to build non-square housing plots, since every peasant house occupies one tile but has four tiles for optional features.  that's five tiles, total.  Just try making a few space-efficient rows of those.  Really, if you have even the slightest literary sense, or some amount of common sense, avoid this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended for players who want a city builder at a comfortable pace. In comparison with Settlement Simulator (which I found really fast-paced and complex for what i can handle), Fabledom progresses at a comfortable pace, so that you have time to plan things out and enjoy the aesthetics and humor without worrying about things getting out of control. I enjoy the whimsical encounters with fairytale references and it's enjoyable just to watch your fablings(?) going about their day.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to choose No, but if I could go back I would not purchase this game. It's super fun, yes, but you get a weekends worth of gameplay - if that. It becomes very repetitive and i'm bummed to see they released a "final" patch when I myself still find the game lacking as well as encounter many bugs. While none of them have been game breaking, I don't think i'd pay full price for this game. Wait for it to go on sale for around $10 because it's worth that much! Maybe with the port to console they will see the love the fans had for the game and continue expanding it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really cute and calls back to obvious inspiration from old school castle builders like stronghold, but lacks much of the depth those games possess. There is a very shallow breadth of content in this game, and all of it is accessed in a slow, linear fashion. Selecting territories on a map is largely irrelevant, as you cannot enter another person's territory. You have an army, but cannot fight. You can build walls, but there are no soldiers to attack you. Even the economy and town building isn't very complex despite being the main focus. Worse yet, the UI is not very informative and many of the mechanics are highly illogical, such as characters dying of starvation when your granary indicates you have years worth of food because they happen to not be close enough to their home to eat.It's really a shame, there's a lot of good ideas here and it was a promising foundation, but the game feels like it's in pre-Alpha. I would much rather recommend you pick up Stronghold (2001) or The Nations (2001) which are both fief buidling sims with an emphasis settlement management and economy over combat, though Stronghold does have some combat centered modes. They are almost 25 years older than this game, but somehow manage to have greater depth in every aspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: If you like resource management games, this is THE game for you. I'm simply obsessed with the amount of information, from managing the distance between production buildings and the residents' houses to deciding which buildings should have the maximum number of workers in each season. The overview board, with graphs and information about your kingdom, is simply amazing. Anyway, I've played a little, but I could already spend hours talking about this game, so I definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great. It's beautiful and it feels nice to make cosy villages. I like the mechanics as well; it doesn't just looks nice, it also brings some fresh takes such as how reputations work and how the larger city homes work.There are a lot of small bugs though; every patch breaks a few things, and the devs notice them and repair them, but they seem to always have some gameplay impacting bugs in the game at all times. Also balancing could be done a lot better: If you build a nice looking place instead of a boring perfectly planned grid you will notice that resource production might be really slow. Luckily as soon as you build a hospital there are no negative things that can happen without your interaction. So you can just press full speed and let it run for a while, while you go make lunch or something
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10The game shows promise with its engaging gameplay, but it suffers from notable bugs. For instance, the roads I meticulously build disappear whenever I reload my game. Additionally, I've encountered issues where citizens starve despite having ample food supplies.I'm hopeful that these issues will be addressed in future patches. If the developers can fix these bugs, I would gladly update my review to a positive rating.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute disaster. Despite owning a high-end computer setup (Windows + RTX 3060 Ti), it crashes relentlessly. I've tried everything—posting on Steam forums, reaching out on the company's Discord—yet no one bothers to respond or fix the issues. The crashes are unpredictable; sometimes it's after something as simple as rotating the map using the mouse wheel in the tutorial, other times it happens randomly after 30 minutes to an hour of play. I attempted to get a refund through Steam, but they refused, leaving me feeling utterly robbed. Save yourself the frustration and avoid this game until the developers show some basic competence in fixing their game-breaking problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I love the feel of this game and it is very satisfying to build and develop your town. It is currently lacking depth and features, but the foundation of the game is very solid and extremely fun. I love the art style and audio as well. Happy to pay for this game up front because it shows great promise, is already very fun (although not super replayable rn) and the devs are releasing substantial updates regularly. This game also has a great tutorial that lets you play the game properly from the start.I have also been playing Against the Storm these days, and I wish that game pulled off the same feel of this game when it comes to the City Builder feel. The core building experience in Fabledom feels way better imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute, the music is calming, and the overall management of the "kingdom" (a tiny one at that) is done well. I think the only caveat I have is making it easier for folks to get around to their jobs: dunno if there needs to be some kind of shuffle option to automatically move folks around, or if there needs to be some kind of cart/horse fast-travel system added.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: For frame of reference, I've played Banished, City Skylines, SimCity (multiple), Settlement Survival and a number of other city building games.In comparison, this is a super watered down and laid back city building game. The art and animation style is cute and sweet, the narrator is quirky and breaks the silence of the game otherwise. A rather two-dimensional and straight forward game, but that's not to say it's a bad thing - on the contrary, it fills an interesting niche in the city building genre that caters to a more casual and easy-to-pick-up style.There are a few things that are not super straight forward. Fortification wall mounts are upgraded on stone walls after they are built and you click on the wall to resize it - the option to mount a ballista or likewise appears after that, provided you've unlocked it via city-size. And building an Embassy is vital to story progression or you sort of get stuck in a diplomatic/romantic flat zone for a while. Embassy also allows you to trade because stone and iron depletes permanently (though events can come up to replenish them for a while).All-in-all, for the price of two bubble teas, I had a good run - I'm not sure there's a huge amount of replayability with regards to new content - there is not much strategy involved besides some logistical placement and building (no tech trees or building upgrades for instance), but it definitely seems like the sort of game I can have running semi-afk on the side while doing something on the side. Very forgiving and you can end up spending a lot of time making stuff pretty and crafting a cute little kingdom.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's cute. Initially sweet .. then .. bugs . bugs bugs everywhere. 'prioritize construction' - yeah, villagers do whatever the duck they want to. totally ignored.
