_childDocuments_.review: I have to start by saying that this game is almost uncomfortably similar to Foundation in aesthetic and mechanics. Many of its features, like expansion into adjacent areas through purchase and modular buildings, have appeared in other games and proven to be deep and interesting mechanics that are worth reusing, but this specific combination of them with this specific presentation left a bad taste in my mouth. I wouldn't normally put a lot of stock into this sort of thing, because city builders can only have so much deviation, but even really basic stuff like the design and layout of the UI, down to the color and shape of the dropdown boxes, are eerily similar. I'm not necessarily opposed to looking at an interesting idea and making some tweaks, but you have to actually do it better to be successful.Unfortunately, a major part of this game's similarity- deliberate or otherwise- is every new world starting with a mandatory quest-based guided experience that locks off buildings until the tutorial is ready for you to place them, hand-feeding you rewards to compensate for the fact that you have no control over your own income for the first hour or two. Even if I set aside the fact that I feel like I've done this before, I have to do it on the pretense that most city builders necessarily follow a similar formula, so locking off obvious inclusions like farms and woodcutters until I'm ready to handle them feels like a waste of my time.The places where this game does innovate are arguably marks against it, because the two immediately obvious from the first minute are a grating narrator you can't opt out of and the predefined goal of finding a romantic partner. I could just turn the voice volume down, but honestly, the urge to turn off the narrator is more an urge to have control over what I'm doing. The storybook presentation, framed as a flashback retold from after the end of the game, highlights that my goals are pre-defined- and that I've done this all before. I understand the drive to present a more narrative-driven take on city builders, and assuredly there is a point where the game opens up and gives the player more to work with, but so much about this game conspires to highlight that lack of input.Maybe my gripes are personal ones, and other players can look past them. For me, this formula just isn't what I come to city builders for- and even if it was, I've gotten it better elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this for a little while but so far I'm enjoying in very much! It's a cute, fun and relaxing game to play. I love the aesthetics and the color palettes and the background music is so lovely too.There are couple of small things that I'd like to see get better, ie. better resources management, ability to move built houses etc and more content story-wise as well as more different buildings too. That being said, I have not regretted the money I spent on it and really like it overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This is Kingdoms and Castles with a splash of the Anno series.  It's got a great style and a good early experience.  But while a lot of the game's features seem promising, they are implemented in an underwhelming way.  The insult comedian narrator makes a quip and disappears for an hour, like an afterthought.  Your marriage partner is a checklist.  There's not much for your military units to do.  Citizens don't have very many demands for variety in food or happiness buildings, so many of the mid-game buildings are not strictly necessary, and what few late-game options unlock have little practical use once you've gotten that far.This is fun while it lasts, and a reasonable value at 30% off, but a bit disappointing as I feel like it could have been amazing with more time and attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I'll come back to write a better review, but this game is ADDICTING!I'm a sucker for a farm sim, romance sim, town builder sim... this game has it all! Navigating building a kingdom is fun because you kind of just put things where you can to start with, and then have to either come back and rebuild whole areas (a challenge) or just learn to live with them and work around the artefacts and vestigial pieces of your initial hamlet (which is exactly how city building works in real life, so that's fun). The only critique I have is that trying to make the palace/castle work in a pleasing way is... kind of a nightmare, because basically once you place it, you can never move it due to the attachments. But... that's literally the only issue I have. I love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: An impressive and entertaining little city-builder, filled with cute fairy tale-like characters and fun quests. A relaxing pace which is a nice break from similar types of games that tend to be really full on and stressful.I highly recommend the game for those who like the genre. Of course, its in early access so who knows, this could all change (but I doubt it).
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely LOVE this game. I got it for passive light fun to pass time but have become actually obsessed with it. I really wish the 3x speed made the little dudes run faster, but overall the mechanics and game play are great. I would enjoy being able to design my princess and see her roam the town with her wife Agnes! Highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice low stress city builder and the fairy tale elements provide a great framing device so it doesn't devolve into feeling like a grind too quickly. While playing and finding the little references and following the story, I found myself smiling quite a bit. I'm really happy I grabbed this game and I'm excited to see how it continues to grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This has definitely been a much needed brain off game for me. It has the good existence one comes to expect from a city builder while still feeling like there's a sort of goal to it too in its relationship mechanic, similar to that of the Civilization games while adding to it with the missions and romance. Definitely a fun, relaxing game to play after a long day.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I have restarted this game a few times to play through - and I'm very excited for the finished product. I'm sad that there's not a timeline because I would be setting phone reminders on the dates it would be updated. It's such a fun strategy and simulator. I see inspiration from Civilization, Age of Empires - both games I love. However, the desgin and animations are phenomenal. Yes, there are different bugs that need to be ironed out - but what I think is one of the coolest aspects of this is that they built the feedback feature into the game itself. In the top right hand corner, you can provide feedback, your email if you want, your comments and then it will take a screenshot to try and capture what you're talking about! The human centric way of obtaining feedback from end users while they're playing the game live is a wonderful way for QA & User Research. You can tell that there's a lot of love and care that is going into this game. I look forward to the final version.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I am playing on 2560 X 1440 and I cannot read the in game text without getting up to stare at my screen. _childDocuments_.review: Its cute very simple like other sim builders. Sorry no lore early game if that is something you are looking for, can't name cities/countries which is kinda meh. _childDocuments_.review: Currently on my first playtime, so not sure how many hours im in but certainly enjoying it, much easier then other city builder games but the art style is stunning and game play is brilliant if you want a game in which to relax too with not seriously over stressful events i would highly suggest getting this. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best city/town/colony games I've played in a while.Shades of Anno, Settlers, Majesty, and even Black & White in a way.Music is pleasant and calm.Voice dialogue can be funny, and I've yet to find it annoying or jarring.Visuals are not mind blowing but are perfectly suited for the type of game.Tutorial and new player experience is great, guiding you into the systems of the game in a very natural way.Controls are sensible and familiar. Quests are neat and you'll see a lot of familiar fairy tale references or tropes.So far I only have nitpicks for things I don't like, such as game speed resetting to 1 whenever you get a dialogue. Little things. Many of which I will submit to the dev discord which seems to be very in touch with its community. Lot's of stuff already in the game with promising updates on the horizon.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I normally wait until I get $1/hr of game play before I review a game positively, but since this just released on ea, I want to give it a positive recommendation so others tempted for a fun little city builder would know that it's pretty good. I've pretty much played through everything available at the moment. I've unlocked all the territories available, built a kingdom, and essentially just building up resources until the next parts of the game release. I look forward to seeing what comes next
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about this game, but there's also quite a few quirks that can make it a frustrating experience once you get your city past certain milestones. I'm currently late into the game and despite being wealthy and having bountiful food my pawns are starving, and  beginning to drop dead all over the place. Assuming it was perhaps something I'd done with the layout of my farms, marketplaces, and granaries I decided to completely bulldoze my kingdom and start again, this time ensuring there was a Granary, marketplace, or at least somewhere the pawns could get food, within a short walking distance of every household. With that done, I'm still finding my pawns are beginning to starve the minute my population rises beyond around 150-200. An abundance of food, and accessible storage for it, does not seem to be resolving the problem. I can only assume it's some kind of balancing issue, or something else that hasn't been explained by the game. In addition to that, I haven't really fully understood the purpose of 'family aid' within the game. As far as I can tell it seems to be a set value that rises when your city hits its next tier, and isn't something that's related to employment, or something you can reduce. This can at times make it hard to plan your expansions if you are opening businesses as you recruit pawns, as you can quickly end up in the red without much warning. It's quite easy to find yourself at, say, +25 gold only to recruit 3-4 pawns, open a business for them to use, and then find yourself suddenly on -30 gold because you've had an unexpected increase to family aid on top of the business cost.Those things said, it's a nice game to look at and I've mostly enjoyed my time playing it. On that basis I'd recommend playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: It's very cozy and cute. The gameplay is not too complex for casual gamers. The art and aesthetic is everything! I love taking screenshots in this game. The "creative" sandbox option is a big big plus!! Devs know their audience fr. W devs.Some of the things that can be improved:WALKING PATH:  it'd be nice to be able to select multiple tiles at the same time because it's a pain to delete one by one. COMBAT: for hero and soldiers, i feel there needs to be a tad bit more tweaking because it's not very smooth (like the hero not going to the tile i want him to go which i think might be a bug). I don't think this matter much anyway since combat gameplay is very little and it's not the focus of the game.MORE CONTENT FOR COURTING: This is a request from me <3. Please PLEASE make more content or more DLC for the game. Take my money and give me more romance options (let me court the witch)!! U-U

RelationshipsObviously this is work in progress, but I'm thinking, since befriending our kingdoms is relatively useless at the moment, maybe consider adding buffs if a kingdom is befriended, or: when the other kingdom is a friend of foe, certain magical elements or incidents occur to add to the fable feeling of the game. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: The greatest strength of this game is also its greatest weakness: it is a relaxed, not particularly lengthy experience. Most of the chains of goods are simple and don't require a great deal of planning or understanding as is the case in other titles of this genre. As a city builder, it is a great game for beginners, but will quickly become too simple for more experienced players. At the same time, it has absolutely no lategame, no later challenges you could try, even if you start too understand or enjoy such games.Personally, I still have a few problems with the UI. Although there are already quite clear interfaces here, there is still a lack of fine-tuning and flow in some places.But overall, i think this game has a great potential. I needs a tiny bit more depth, and more challenging objectives.To summarize:+ good for beginners of this genre, very easy in standard mode.+ Simple economy or chains of goods+ good overview/UI with minor drawbacks+ nice cartoony look- UI needs fine-tuning/flow (If you want to find out where unemployed residents live, you simply have to click around too often instead of there being an option that clearly displays this)- absolutely annoying messages (every few minutes you are informed that witches/dragons/fairies have done something somewhere and you have to pay gold or suffer the consequences)- little creativity within these messages, very repetitive after a few minutes of gameplay. I wish for more creativity here, maybe more references/small easter-eggs to old fairy-tales or fantasy franchises?- Announcer is sometimes quiet for several hours, only to suddenly comment on something loudly, which can be a bit startling. - No lategame, no higher challenges.So if you're looking for a relaxed experience, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxed, enjoyable atmosphere with clean, cute graphics. Fun resource manager/city builder, but only really as taxing as you want it to be as you can choose to accept additional quests as you go. Don't have the resources? Don't commit to the quest! _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Promising. Too early to say, though.If content is added at a reasonable pace so as to that it becomes a fully fleshed out game rather than just an alpha with one patch every 3 months and providing development is stable and timely this game will be amazing, it just lacks content that makes the game feel whole right now.If not, it's just another one of the 'in the bin' games that are promising but ruined by slow development turning it into a waiting-for-the-next-patch simulator.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is cute and cozy, but it doesn't offer anything new to the genre.I've played a lot of colony sims and city builders. While Fabledom is enjoyable for the first couple of hours, it gets repetitive pretty quickly. It has resource management, supply chains, and city design mechanics, but there is no depth to any of them.If you've never played a colony/city game before, you'll enjoy it. If you have, you will probably get bored after learning the basics.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is officially my favorite city builder! I've been looking for one with cute graphics and a play style that isn't overly complex. I've finally found it! The fantasy elements are adorable and the romance is a fun little added bonus I hadn't really been expecting. I'm also very excited about how often we've been getting updates and love seeing devs sticking to their promises/roadmap and I can't wait for full launch in spring!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so much fun. Building up your empire from a tiny little village to a huge, map-sprawling kingdom was a real treat. The game is set in a lovely fairy tale world full of winged piggies, clumsy ogres, magic trees, and mischievous witches. This game is overall a resource management, organization, efficiency builder. In order for your kingdom to thrive, you must be smart with how you place and layout your buildings, where you choose to have people work and live, and what you do with the resources at your disposal. The game didn't overstay its welcome. By the time you get everything made for your castle, you're probably reaching end game. It wasn't too hard, but I will admit, there were a number of winters where I didn't know if my villagers would have enough food and coal to keep them warm and happy till spring.Game's optimization could use some work, but it looks like the developers will be tweaking that with the upcoming patch.If you can get it on sale, great, if not - that's still not bad.Very satisfying game to come home and relax with. I got a lot of joy zooming in and watching all the goofy little villagers go about their day and I was able to make some pretty aesthetically pleasing areas as well!Glad I bought this. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Full review here: Fabledom still has a long way to go but it's already noticeable that it has some potential. For now it's a short game with little diversity of options, and the practically absence of economy makes it a bit reductive. It makes up for it by being gorgeous and quite polished.PROS:- beautiful;- few bugs or glitchesCONS:- virtually no economy options;- lack of diversity on gameplay.Follow my curator page:
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming civ builder. Feels simple when you first start out, but gains more complexity as your village grows and you unlock more buildings and types of villagers. The game does a great job of not overwhelming you with too many systems to learn right out the gate. I also enjoy the humor and light hearted cheek it has.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game because of how simple and easy-going it is compared to other city builders I've played in the past. The mechanics and strategy of the game are fairly simple and easy to catch on. The fairy-tale theme makes this a warm and cozy game! There are some bugs in-game, but the in-game Feedback button allows you to easily report them and they quickly get resolved! The Discord server is also a great resource for tips/help when need be!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: omg Im so excited to see where this game goes!! I am at the end of early acess and I can'y wait to have this game develop. One of the things that has impressed me the most about the game is the potential it holds. The game is packed with unique features and mechanics that set it apart from other games in its genre. The gameplay is addictive, and the graphics are stunning,While I've already sunk hours into my kingdom during its early access phase until I reached the end, I'm eagerly anticipating the full release and what it has in store. The potential for new content, features, and improvements is vast, and I can't wait to see how the game grows and develops. The end of early access is just the beginning, and I'm excited to be along for the ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Cute but boring. Soooo boring.Everything takes ages. The UI is not helpful either. Game: You want to move a building? OK. It cant have any resources in it. Me: Ok I empty it. Game: Sorry it cannot have any workers in it. Me: Ok I fire them. Game: Sorry this building cannot be moved because F U. Logistics is a nightmare. You have to make little villages since you cannot upgrade the houses like for example in Anno. Once you put a farmer small village that is it you are done with it nothing will need to be done with it. Either raze it to the ground and get rid of your fabelings or put a whole new village that will do 1 specific thing. If you want to make a big village like in the trailer with a castle and evetyrhing. You have to make it from scratch. Put it in a empty plot next to your existing production village. Since the fabelings will have to take 90% their work time getting to their work space.Also good luck transporting something from one side to another as the little guys take their sweet time going from one place to another. So if your stone hub where you make stone and stone slabs is on one part of the village and you need it to the other. Well tough luck they will take their sweet time moving it. Maybe a year maybe less. NOBODY KNOWS. There is no way to move anything faster (Except upgrading the roads wich gives you some faster movement but not that it would make much of a difference.) Stockpiles do not share their contents. So if your fabeling needs stone slabs it has to go either to the stone slab stockpile or the mason. so they have to treck all the way to it. And they pick up 5 slabs at max. And most of your buildings need 10-30 or more.You can edit what each stockpile takes but still it needs to get there. And that means one of the two little guys needs to get it. And since each stockpile can have up to 10 materials you need 5 stockpiles next to each other to have it optimized. And that means that you have a stockpile hub the size of a small village. That still will be slow. Since they need to travel whooole town at a leasury pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great addition to this genre, really carved out a space for itself! The graphics are incredible and it's so fun to just sit and watch the villagers interact with the world. It's early access, but with a clear roadmap for future content, and I personally can't wait to see how it grows. It otherwise doesn't feel like early access and feels very polished already. There's also a creative mode option which is fantastic! Definitely worth picking up if you're looking for a new city builder/management game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Game is no longer receiving updates, as such I cannot recommend it.This game feels like the first 30-50% of a really excellent game, where it just needs to further flesh out some of the weaker mechanics and add some more content to make it one of the best city builder games.This was actually originally going to be a glowing review, as I had assumed that the devs would keep releasing updates to it. I can understand if maybe finances were a concern, but at that point I would have preferred to pay an extra 10 euros/dollars if it meant that the game got another 6-12 months of development.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game. Peaceful to play, but you still need to manage your resources. I think it needs some tuning during EA. My citizens are often starving despite there being plenty of food. One citizen just stood in the lumber yard and starved to death. Looking forward to the additional features and content.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is super cute, watching the villagers walk around, busy with farming, mining, transporting goods, and building houses—every action is adorable. It's quite an interesting management game, but the current content is not rich enough. hope more interesting updates will be added in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely medieval town builder. It's still very early access but the foundation they've made is incredibly clean and smooth. If you're not in a rush it's got around 8-10 hours of game play for now. I'm excited for more!Post release edit: They definitely gave more and it's so freakin' charming! Great little town builder. Definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: ADORABLEbut!Makes 4090 sound like a jet taking off for some reason, literally THE hottest, loudest experiencecp77 63 degrees, this 76 degrees lmaowowAND THATS POWER LIMITED DOWN TO 45OW FROM 600Wwhile looking as a cute mobile game from 2018.kingdom looks sane though, classic take on a European fable thankfully, so at least that.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for a low-key, small-scale city builder for many, many years now, and Fabledom really delivered for me. The game has a lovely aesthetic sensibility, with fantastic lighting and weather effects - I frequently stopped to admire the way roads were impacted by rain. I really enjoyed that I could arrange things in ways that were both efficient and pleasing to look at. The romance and diplomacy aspects are very lightweight, but I like that the quests they provide give some direction to your city-building without being overly prescriptive. And I quite like the fantasy elements, though I wish there were more of them.My only complaints are polish and quality-of-life items. I would love if clicking on a resource like stone or iron popped up a button for the appropriate harvesting building like in Against the Storm. I would love if I could manually select the specific design I wanted for any building with a randomized appearance. Sometimes after save/loading I'd notice weird behavior with manually placing and removing attachments on foundations. There are other complaints I could make on that level, but honestly? They're all nitpicks. I eagerly dumped over 100 hours into this game to get all the achievements and I was delighted the entire time. I look forward to any updates that may invite me to come back. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game, the music and everything. I think things like food should be easier to monitor, for example food, I would like to know how much food per day/season is needed and how much I am currently producing. And I would like more status besides food, maybe crime, education (imagine the variety of things that could be unlocked using the population's intelligence, creating more products for commerce, or for the very quality of life, changing social classes through this system , I would love it), sanitation (sewage, garbage in the streets) more ways to earn money like rallies and wars, maybe managing popular revolts, slaves... The initial film talks about being feared, but this is not an option yet, I would like also to make better use of road mechanics, currently there is not much to do with them if not for a decorative reason. I know that a lot will still be revealed and released, but so far this is what I have to say
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Get this, having to see the game add things that gives you possibility to grow your kingdom, and I thought that you could do so much more when it comes to other kingdoms, like stealing, having alliances, dealing with wars.. It can still be cozy game with those stuff added, I waited for so long for proper game updates. Very little content and now told that there will possibly be no new content. Game did promise so much more and did not deliver.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Many times I wish there was a meh button. I enjoyed my 20 hour play through, but it really lacks re-play ability IMHO. I love city builders so I was going to put a lot of hours in no matter what. it has some cute spins on the classic genre but not enough to for me to strongly recommend. My recommendation is wait for it to go on sale, then buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is a really relaxing city builder with cute, fairytale-esque graphics. The maps are randomly generated with each new save file, so there's always different terrain challenges to work with that keeps it fresh. The developers have done a great job developing the game, and it's really satisfying to play. Can't wait to see what else is added throughout early access, highly recommend it even at this early stage/
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently not worth the money. For the price that it is, even on sale is not worth it. The game is at it's best a 2-3 hour demo where you can easily get everything that is available done. You can't even fully romance any of the prince or princesses available. It has so much potential but seeing as almost all the stuff you can unlock is still in "development" this should have just come out as a demo rather than early access.Will update once more things are actually playable.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: Give this game a wishlist and wait to buy for some time. Good premise, but early in the making.I can see what this game is trying to go for, and I do think it's actually really good for what it's going for. This game is like a pie cooking in the oven, but not even close to browning.Pros: Clear theme that is acted on and supported by design and gameplay.No noticeable design bloat. Every piece has a function and fits together.Pathing works well, no noticeable bugs, no crashes, functional balance, and good interlocking systems.Devs chose making the game work over content first. Very good, but this means limited content as they make sure it works before putting it in.Cons: Devs chose making the game work over content first. Very good, but this means limited content as they make sure it works before putting it in.I do like like how *fast* this game goes compared to it's theme of children exploring new lands. 11 years in 6 hours is fine gameplay wise, but feels a bit rough when nothing ages or how you take so long to marry.Fishing is planned, but this makes water maps hard for space.When my cons are basically "Wow it's early access." That's a good sign for it's future. Hope it doesn't get dropped in the future because this is clearly a gem that can became a staple for citybuilders like banished.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing city builder, no stress like many other city builders like storms or civil disorder... Just peaceful building, expanding, making sure everything works as it should. Very excited to know what they will all add during EA. For those who are looking for a challenge, you might want to skip this game. For those who love the city building genre and just want a relaxing experience, this might be your game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderfully cozy city builder with a lot of potential!Dev team is very responsive and active on the discord, and listens to the input of their fanbase.Game content is current a couple of hours long and does definitely need more, but roadmap looks promising. If you have 15 bucks to spare and just want to play something relaxing, this already does the job! If you prefer a 'fuller' game, wait for full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very SIMPLE game! If you're looking for something quick, charming, easy-going, and cute, then this is for you. It's NOT challenging, creative, doesn't have long play times, nor end game content. I beat it (married) in about 16 hours and spent the next 5 hours creating extra goals for myself because there was nothing else to do. This game is GREAT as an introductory to city building simulations as there's not much to manage nor maintain. I hope they add more content because I wanted to see and do more in this fable style game play.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I have almost completed the story at this point, but I have come upon an issue where all of my Fabletons are dying from starvation. I have a multitude of food production buildings, but something in the late game is not functioning. I have just under 470 population. Maybe I have to liquidate some houses.So aside from that, when I first started playing, I was impressed by the graphics and game play. I have played my fair share of city sim games and I was pleasantly surprised with it at first. I do like the no-pressure/low-pressure military side of it. I was playing on "Classic" mode. I am not into war games.It's difficult to tell how many resources the farms produce in any given time, so I wasn't sure how many farms support a certain population. I like interacting with other realms and performing missions that get me rewards. Some of the game play can seem slow or unproductive, though. The armaments are lacking. There should be more options for the military, especially if you want to play on the tougher settings.Nobles are difficult to obtain. Nobility is also difficult to obtain. The ogres that are spawned by mystical mines don't really do anything. I had expected them to start attacking my very poorly fortified village, but they didn't. They were easy to defeat with a small squadron of archers and sword fighters. And I thought there were going to be more "heroes" but there is only one and the isn't much in the way of upgrading him. Why is there no armory?I would have liked to have been able to see on a layer where all my unemployed people are so I could better plan where to place production buildings. I also wish it were easier to move houses without having to kick out the inhabitants and destroy the attachments.There could have been other types of buildings like for spirituality or artistry. There is also no school. It would have been nice to be able to upgrade the peasants to commoners through some advanced track and then also be able to upgrade their houses. But since the commoners live in "town homes" that have to be built as a cluster, I am not sure how that would work anyway.There are a number of bugs that I don't think will be addressed. One being that the Overview give irrelevant information where everything is identified as "BlahBlahBlah." And when I place a farm, I have to click away from it and click back on it to actually place the vegetable farm next to the building. And I have experienced ineffective trades. I would spend resources for items I needed and those resources never ended up in my inventory.It's a nice little game for someone who isn't familiar with city sim games and resource management. There is a very low threat level for danger. I wanted to like this game. I do like it, but it has been left half-baked. It has so much expansion potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: great game, better than settlers imo. hoping for fishing and cows for dairy and boots and shoes soon.have played the game several times from start to finish.. you can choose different starting kingdoms but basically it will be the same game no matter where you begin. I found the game fun and engaging partly because it was a low stress building game that the only things you need to worry about are having enough food and very easy to play and keep up with needs.The art style and graphics are very well done imo, and the game is worth the time and money i would recommend this game for anyone looking for a less stressful game and it would be enjoyable for children i believe.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is very cute graphical game. pretty normal slow expansion of the city with a lot of resource and supply line management, with milestone unlocking of content based on the size of your kingdom/queendom. all the AI rulers have very unique looks and personality's. you can marry any of them each giving you unique items and buildings as you progress through the game. it has some light combat aspects with a hero that is semi customise-able  with equipment and items you unlock/find in the world. and city defences like wood/stone walls and towers, which can be equipped with cannon and ballista.  its not perfect by any means but it is very enjoyable. still a few problems here and there with balance stuff and bugs, the dev team is only a few people. and they are pretty quick on fixing game breaking bugs and issues. so yes i would say its worth picking up. if you enjoy slow methodical city building in a fantasy setting.After the 1.0 update and the devs saying they are no longer going to be pushing anything apart from bug fixes is a joke. its a shell of a game. and clearly not finished. combat is horrible towers fire globally. so you can just stack a bunch of towers in a tiny area and kill anything. honestly is a shame. the game is not worth it as it stands at full price. i would only get it at 50% off or lower moving forward. because there is basically no replay ability to the game despite a bunch of ai rulers the game is still the same. they don't change enough its just bonuses to certain things. overall i still enjoy it, but its not done and you can clearly see that. extremely disappointing with the short production cycle since EA.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This was a difficult one because there are many good things about this game; it is cute and relaxing. Not too easy and not too hard. Complex enough mechanics that are pretty easy to get your head around and optimise. However, some of the goals were boring and frustrating and I spent much time just waiting for fablings to collect material. I waited a lot.. even when they were sped up I just sat and waited. Moreover, I finished the main quest fairly fast (15hours) and I always spend more time than most others. There is not a lot of replayability as it is mostly just the same functions again and again.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I often never leave a review, and reserve it only for such an occasion. This game is special. And a dev specifically asked for this as a favor in their Discord, so, ya' gotta do it!Just to make it easy - great music, fun city builder, a great voice actor/narrator, and a wonderful combination of silly/cartoony and realistic as an art style. And at $15 or $20? Nah, go for it! Give it a try. A bit more in-depth - this game is made by a two-man dev team. Which is as mind-blowing as learning Manor Lords is a one-man dev team. With Fabledom, you feel the love they put into their project. There's a story here that will be fleshed out along with the game's development - delivered by game mechanics and a fantastic, sort of nostalgic narrator. The art style is very well crafted, allowing an indie team to seem like they're competing with PIXAR. The game has hints of Banished, Manor Lords, and in some sense, ANNO 1800. The game is calm and easy-going. I saw one comment that was pretty on point - Fabledom feels like how the new Settlers game should have felt.And my top compliment - this game allows for travelling the map, and does a great mix of cute, cartoony city-building, with later-on added elements of combat. You can eventually build a castle and the surrounding walls, with both footmen and archers. Overall, support the game, support their art. Give it a try!To note though - two negatives. One, as with most city-builders, the game is too easy. Again with other city builders, I doubt there's an End screen. The focus is of course actually building, designing, and decorating a city. But it needs far greater challenges and true game-ending events, if the player isn't focused or strategic. This might be mitigated slightly when combat is introduced soon.Two - so far, nothing is really new here. You can tell there's love from the devs from this project. It feels like a game from the 90's or early 2000's when devs really, really were trying. I'm reminded of Halo...... But anyway, the game's great and it's fun to play. Buuut, aside from the story line, there's nothing really new here. Hoping to see what happens later on though!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Like: atmosphere, UI, the narrator, and the simplicity of it. It does still pose some minor challenges but you can control difficulty. It’s very much what I expected: an easy-going, aesthetically pleasing, relaxing game. Dislike: very limited on military options, each new game has the exact same encounters, so it has limited replayability. Also it contains The same recurring characters without any way to customize the way you can in other “similar” games like anno 1800. I tend to gravitate towards colony sims and city builders, and it scratches that itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

Its worth the small price for 35hrs of entertainment.No bugs in anything i tried except Eric Jr keeps spawning.  that was just annoying, but didnt impact gameplay for me.Cute game.  very relaxing.  fun to examine your kingdom when complete.  Not sure it has replayability for me.
