Like the wood cutter will run out and they have no forester so theirs that so just keep in mind on the way you build and the game is a bit of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable; visually unique and appealing, the "cuteness" of the art style betrays how complex this game can be.There's something here for everyone - whether or not you like grueling games like Banished or want something more relaxing like Dorf Romantik. Or well --- just want to make cool maps for your D&D campaign.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: It's just another one of a million town builders. Farm food, feed people, make coal, survive winter, repeat. This one has a dating system though. For a gem called Fabledom there's very little fable in this game. A hero checks out ruins, but nothing really happens. A witch turned my villagers into skeletons for a bit. Other than that it's almost exactly like any other town builders where each citizen is tracked on a map. Seems like it's being updated regularly, but mostly to add in stuff other games already have anyways.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are adorably cute. Very pleasing to the eye and relaxing to play. The only reason (and it's a BIG reason for me) for deleting this game is because in the process of wanting to be different from other city builders, the devs put in the objective of courting and marrying a suitor to rule together and expand your empire. You have the choice to court a male or female, whether your male/female (which is great!) but you don't have the option to NOT court another ruler so you can rule alone. This may seem petty to some folks and that is understandable, but I feel like a game that gives you choices that other games don't...why not also give us the choice to remain friends with other rulers and rule my kingdom alone? I suggested the ability to skip an objective so I can rule alone...and the admins basically said nah, we want to to be different. It is within their right to do so, of course. But sometimes the attempt to be different ends up being more oppressive to the player. I don't play city bulders/colony sim to be forced into a linear game, I play it so I can choose to play it however I choose. Some people may enjoy it, others may not. I did not.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I got this as soon as it was available, and I love it.It's relaxing, cozy and so is the music and the artwork.While it is still developing, I have already had hours of fun, and the only reason i haven't played more is because I am waiting for more to be done.But with each update, i am back streaming it.This is already wonderful work from this small team.Also the narrator is amazing and funny. I love him. Great choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Even for early access, this is pretty bare-bones for a city builder. There's not much more content outside what you see in the demo.It is very cute though, with stylistic decisions I can get behind. I also like how they're making some of the structures less static than just placing squares and rectangles. They do need to extend this to more buildings than just housing and stockpiles though.The biggest problem right now is that the "fable" part of the name is fairly cosmetic at this point. We are dealing with pigs with wings, there's a princess, and a talking tree somewhere on the map. Otherwise, it's just a regular city builder like you've played before. I've built the well for my houses in so many games. I've built the tavern to make my people happy countless times before. I've built the wheat farms for my windmills for my bakeries every year since playing Settlers II back on windows 98. Let me build and set up actual fable stuff. What about needing to build mushroom huts for gnome citizens, and then I can employ them to spin straw into gold? Or trying to host a coven of wicked witches but trying to put together a sufficiently spooky swamp in time?Ultimately, this game has potential, but in the same way that a lump of rainbow playdoh has potential. It's kind of nothing right now except, appropriately, castles in the sky.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: The most cozy, most adorable, most fantastically unique city building game I've ever played. You'll get to watch your Fablings' every step of the way as they work hard to turn your struggling little hamlet into a mighty kingdom. It's not all tulips and festivals tho... if you don't keep good stock of things you may lose some of your precious Fablings to hunger and sickness, which will in fact break your heart because they're so danged adorable. Win over rulers, or frustrate them with sneaky... "resource acquisition" missions. Interact with world events as you please (but I swear if you chop down Bob, so help me....)Build the biggest, most colorful, most flying pig filled kingdom your heart desires. Cannot WAIT to see what they have in store for full release, tho I will say there's already plenty of content to keep you busy for quite some time with where the game is currently.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this in early access hoping it would expand into a bigger game but after completing the game (marrying once and getting all achievements except the other marriage ones) it became a grind game... What should be an easy quest (Giovanni's debt) has taken an hour because of how sparse the npc events are. An hour of sitting here clicking buttons is not fun gameplay, thankfully I had art stuff to pass the time. It definitely needs more events, npcs, just general things to do towards end game. If I wasn't so stubborn I would've skipped getting the other 5 marriage achievements. Another kicker is the quality of the game mid-play, I have to have the graphics on the lowest setting and even then when you reach small city status the game freezes ridiculously often, sometimes even crashing. The loading screen also gets stuck for around 5 minutes. I can run Skyrim on high graphics and with multiple mods yet I can't run this on the lowest setting?... Definitely needs fixing.TL:DR Fun for the first 3 hours, waiting/grind simulator after you marry someone, graphics are great until you're nearing the end, don't waste too much time on this game or just don't get it at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: There is nothing heinous about this game. Is a well-built city builder medieval game with a cute art style. The reason I am leaving a negative review is because the game brings nothing new to the table. It is becoming a negative trope that a medieval-style, banished-inspired, city builder is: place house, place road, place farm, place woodcutter, place stone quarry, etc... until a messy grid of said buildings occur. I just found myself becoming bored, very quickly, because I have done all of this before in games of the same genre. The few mechanics which are unique, such as the world map, are not well-developed (yet). The diplomacy is shallow and adds very little. The resource management is generic. The "hero" feels like something out of clash of clans or a cheap mobile game.The game is well executed but just uninteresting. I am looking forward to other projects in this genre, such as Manor Lords and Going Medieval, a lot more because those projects try to bring more uniqueness to their mechanics and gameplay in a genre which is already inflated with generic, Banished-inspired, grid-based, city builders.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: 8 hours in and I love this game. I am a fiend for city builder and resource management games, and I was so excited to see a city builder that is fairy tale themed. Like most city builders, there is always some level of replay value if you want to start new maps (which are randomized each time!), but the available number of buildings max out pretty quick. Visually, the game is well designed and everything is rendered beautifully/stylistically in a way that is perfect for the theme. I actually enjoy reading the dialogue - and there isn't too much, it's a perfect passive injection of narrative that leaves me to my own devices and choices (which I appreciate). I really hope that this early access game doesn't fizzle out over time and that the devs continue to build on it - there is so much exciting promise! After trying a few maps, I would recommend the following to the devs:- For resource collection and creation buildings, offer a way to "level" them up - doesn't need to be anything drastic, but it would add a layer of something to build towards and improve. Bonus points if it also changed their appearance upon leveling up.- I love the random encounters, more would always be welcomed!- More decoration options are welcomed- Adding more 'attachment' options to buildings like the bakery and the inn, giving more resource options like a distillery to the inn, or more baked goods options to the bakery- More map diversityThat being said, I genuinely enjoy this game and I'll keep playing it with hopes for more updates and additions to come. I recommend this game to anyone who wants to play an engaging city builder with a dash of charm and low pressure to engage in battle scenarios. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Great Graphics.  Cool Concept.  Gameplay is fun.  Revising my review from previous play testing - the game has gotten more stable.  There's still bugs/ but it's gotten to the level of forgivable.  This is understanding being at this phase, but I feel like the devs are making positive improvements to the game and really investing in something that is conceptually fresh and fun.  The mechanics are a bit... dry at the moment; but I loved the art style and the concept - I do wish they'd try to wrack up the difficulty a bit throw in more event based actions.  those are awesome; really unique and it's so fun finding and taming an ogre - stuff like that make this game charming and I get a sense that there is a lot more to come;  I definitely recommend you try it out as well and see how you'd live your fairy tale :D
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game, and got some cute ideas.  But wasn't enough to hold my attention long term.I wish the devs had leaned more into this game's USP.  Make the quests and random things around the map more impactful, give you a reason to build defences etc.  Even the diplomacy and "romance" etc felt very tacked onto an otherwise middle of the road city-builder.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I love city builder games, but this one gets pretty tedious pretty quickly. The first few hours are mainly just building homesteads, waiting for new citizens to show up, and then building more homesteads. After getting to the next tier of citizens, it feels like more of the same. It does not feel like there is enough depth to the resources or building to be worth investing additional time.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game sadly. I want to, and I wanted to love it. It's a really fantastic start to a game. However even if the few objects in the game like bridges and castles get added in later, it's no where near enough. I feel like realistically for this to be more than a $5 couple hour experience the content needs to doubled or tripled. I've basically ran through it twice now in 8 hours, and while it's a filthy casual awesome city builder, it's just missing way to much to make me want to play much. There story/fable aspect to the game is actually extremely minimal. You've got a giant bean stock you tell the singular hero to inspect.... Other than that the hero inspects a few other things on the map. The romance aspect also appears minimal, a few clicks to send dowry type goods followed by a few missions later. TLDR: A couple hours of game play, and feels like if the rest they show gets added it's still a couple hours to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: It's SO hard to give this game a 'do not recommend' rating, but I have to.  Because my thoughts are that you shouldn't buy this game YET.The core game play loop is fantastic, don't get me wrong.  The graphics are gorgeous, the sounds are wonderful.  There's so much to love about this game.BUT... then there's what's wrong with the game.  It's just not balanced yet.  The time you wait for gold primarily is the major sticking point.  For some reason you have to pay a family fee, which drains gold out of your budget, and I feel like if it weren't for that, the game might be perfect.  But as it stands, you just wait and wait and wait and wait and wait and wait and wait.  Want to build condos?  Have fun waiting for the 300 gold you need, as you earn 24 gold a cycle.   This game is supposed to be a village simulator, let us build and play with our village!  Stop with the economy drain just to lengthen the game play loop!I'll come back and give this game another go at some point in the future, but it really needs to let people play the wonderful game that they've created, and not just be stuck in a waiting sim.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: So far it's been very addictive & casual fun even in early access. I'm excited for more at later stages. Was looking for a game with these vibes. Hope there is a smidge more complexity by then too, with heroes, the nobility points (w/e they're called), and/or maybe the decorations (which are technically pointless at the moment).
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game, at this point in its development.I thought I was buying a game where I get to create a nice little city for some little peoples that wasn't focused on combat or conflict, where I could do some fun things to build a pretty and balanced city with everyone working together to make the place a pleasant town to live in. Instead, I got a game about gentrification and elevating the wealthy. The poor Peasants do not pay as much in taxes and have ugly homes without plumbing (not like you can give them access to it, when it becomes available for Commoners) so you are, when Commoners arrive and you can build an army, better-off press-ganging Peasants in to the military to send off on Quests and leaving just enough Peasants to run the dirty jobs (like farming) while maxing out your tax-income from Commoners, which are also more-densely housed.The "romance" aspect of the game is merely just another framing to runs quests... Which are just resource-based. There is zero roleplaying involved. There is zero substance to the system. All it does is reinforce a goods-based economy of emotion (your worth is only as great as your material means)Building the city is very samey, with little flavour or customization to how things look. With how housing placement works, as well, you need to build densely, as well, or else your workers will be too far from their job to be of any use.Over-all, the game is "alright", but, for myself, it falls apart with the gentrification, lack of personality to the city and the complete lack of substance with the romance system.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright, my 20 or so hours are two and a half maps full play through, if I didn't have to replay from early access it would be half that. My first play test experience in early access was positive, I was excited about the game, but as other have said the final release did feel a bit empty. It's fine for a easy cozy game, but if you really enjoy city builders, its not much for you. I wish they had a neutral recommend, but I'm giving it a yes, as it is a decent cozy game, but I wouldn't pay more than $10 for it. I don't want to pick it up again, and its shallow as far as city builders go.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an enjoyable city-building fable-style simulator with a lot of potential. However, there are some areas that need improvement to enhance player engagement and reduce the downtime spent waiting for resource generation. The game doesn't lend itself well to replayability due to the grueling and time-consuming endgame.One major improvement would be to increase the number of villagers or commoners arriving, as the current cap of five can feel frustratingly slow.The graphics and overall quality are impressive, but the game could benefit from taking inspiration from titles like Northgard and Age of Mythology. The higher difficulty levels don't feel truly challenging; they simply require more resources, which results in more waiting.Overall, I would rate it 4 out of 5 stars. I would gladly return if the game introduced mission modes or unique gameplay elements where multiple nations compete for resources, similar to Age of Empires.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing I liked about this game (aside from what I consider a clever name) is the art style.  This rich and beautiful art style that carries through all annual seasons and the detailed animations of working, building, waiting...its fun to just watch what you've built run for awhile every so often.But what about getting started?  So for a game created by just two guys, I'm STUNNED at how well done it is and this is brought across early when, aside from adopting standard controls, getting them communicated is so well done.  So let's talk about gameplay.  Like many city builders, you know you're going to need resources, housing, farming, etc...and this is all present in Fabledom, but you also must maintain relationships with other kingdoms.  I have found there might be a balance or AI issue in that I am not getting enough focus on the most critical needs (wood, stone, building), and to that end it would be nice to see a few QOL changes like letting us know how each day is passing.  We don't get a clue as to if we're in Hour 1 or Hour 20 of any day.  And if you're waiting for taxes to arrive, that makes it difficult.Another QOL would be I'd like to know if someone left or died.  I've seen my kingdom go from a max population to missing several citizens with no word to me that they're gone or why.  But hey, its Early Access.  All of this is to be expected.So to summary, I absolutely LOVE this game!  To be this good, work this well, and be this complete in Early Access is very promising!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very chill, easy-to-learn city builder game. Fans of the cottagecore style will probably like it. I like the tutorial mode and the fact that you don't actually have to control anything during battles -- the game does it all for you. Standard mode is just challenging enough to be "not easy", which is what I want.There are a few minor bugs that I've seen reported but I've only come across one in my travels.It's a bit resource-intensive (my computer sounds like it's going to launch into orbit when I play) and in the late-game (20+ years in) the resource-intensiveness makes it a little annoying to play because sometimes the left-click action won't register in the Overview or Building menus.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I think the developers have nailed the feeling of a storybook village with this game.  After 5 hours or so, you will likely have done everything there is to do in the game (taken the romance as far as you can so far with the content, built every building (even though the Bank doesn't actually do anything even when fully staffed... it just says it needs to be fully staffed), cleared all of the little hero missions on the map, etc.  There are also definitely bugs, like if you exhaust a stone or iron resource and move the building, the building permanently has an alert saying the resource is empty even if it's pulling correctly from the new resource.  The game is also outrageously simple for a city builder, and if you've ever played other games of this type you'll likely never be low on food or resources (you may have to wait a while to save up coins to build new stuff if you build a military or something, but it's not like you're ever out of money... just have to wait a bit).Still, when I was shutting down last night because there was literally nothing left to do, I took a look at my village and thought, "Goodbye storybook town!"  In terms of the feel, I think it's right where it should be, and once the game is actually complete this may be a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is a lot of fun and has great replayability. I love city sims but it can become boring after learning how to optimize play for the best outcome. Having several types of romance partners and/or warring enemies available, plus random encounters, it keeps me entertained all day long and looking forward to playing again.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed what was there, but finished everything there was to do in a single day. This is early access, of course, so there is plenty more to come, I'm sure! Hopefully they will add a lot more than what you see on the "coming soon" section as well.I did two playthroughs. Money was very difficult the first time, but I had a more solid grasp of the mechanics and what to do first for my second attempt. You absolutely want to get a lot of food going as soon as you can, and pay attention to what costs upkeep versus what makes you more taxes. Rush food and coal so that your people survive the winter. Don't rush some of the other things until you have a solid economic base to draw from. Random events will drain your coffers or nobility points. Those nobility points will surely mean something at some point? I am sure there will be more princess and princesses in time, as well as other encounters. And, of course, you'll someday be able to actually fight, as well, if that's what you want to do.At the moment, you have a prince who is all about money to woo, and a princess who is all about crops and flowers to woo.  I personally found the princess to be far easier and less annoying to deal with than the prince. The narrator is amusing. It's a solid day's entertainment, and hopefully will provide a lot more in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good starting point and a good game. However, it does need more work.The game is not fully optimised for certain hardware specs, which the devs are aware of.Fabledom lacks much of the "Fable" with few and far between Fable elements besides a "Hero", pigs with wings and a medieval era feel. Content wise, it's a bit thin too but that is because the game is currently in very early access.Also, not sure if this is my fault or the game's, but I have noticed that villagers will often say they are starving despite having plenty of food available with no obstruction to either home or food access, often leading to them dying of starvation with no way for the player to change this.Having said all that, I still enjoy playing this game and, to me, that is what a game should strive to be above all else, enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Full Lets Play Walkthrough - I AM SPEECHLESS !!!!  ITS SOOO GOOD !! Imagine Mount and Blade Banner Lords and bit of an Age of empire but In a Cute fairytale world with a bit of City builder elements to it 1 - This is a very fairy tale esque unique world full of cute mythological characters 2 - You start with a small pair of two men and women and with time and patience turn it into a massive empire 3 - You can talk to the kings and queens of other regions and even get married to them or fight them and takeover them , destroy them 4 - This is also the world of magic so expect magic spells and curses from time to time 5 - You can also espionage on other kingdoms 6 - There are world events that keep on happening throughout the game that will affect you in many ways in a both positive and negative sense 7 - You can also build a massive army 8 - You have hero camps in this - Heroes can travel in interact with interesting objects in the world , you can control the heroes yourself , although they can only walk in your area so you have to expand your region 9 - You can expand your region easily by purchasing the nearby lands 10 - Dynamic weather systemOverall - 10/10 ( GO FOR IT )
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Spent a good few hours in the game and so far I've enjoyed myself. It's a nice whimsical take on the city builder with a nice chill vibe. Despite it's simplistic nature it does have a lot of depth underneath the surface and can get quite complex as you figure out the best way to layout your kingdom, especially with the different housing types. Having fun, still more to come as it's in Early Access to worth a look if you're into this sort of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, even though its a tad limited and could have more content. It took me about 12h to complete the game on easy mode (to learn the game first time). It was easy to just play along while watching a movie in the background. Its a great chill game. However i do feel like its limited and not much to do bar click a few buttons, build houses, assign jobs and wait. The game could use more buildings in general, more hero quests as atm there are so little, bridges that can be build over big rivers so there is better access to other resources. A lot of resources drain super fast as well so the production vs spend is not well balanced.I will play more as I am excited to try different locations and map sizes. I would recommend it for chill gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This has promise of being an excellent game, I've already lost several hours playing early access. There's clearly a number of features not ready yet however what is available works really well, I'm looking forward to diving in deeper when more is added. It's not a quick management game as it's challenging to bring in the coin but I'm hoping once more resource management and facilities are added this will become a little easier. The game runs really smooth, the graphics are pretty charming and there's an interesting story to this city building game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really hard game to recommend for me. There is nothing wrong with the game, it's very adorable, the humor is alright, all the systems work as intended, worker management wasn't too annoying, there are nice graphs to show production/consumption, i didn't have any crashes or bad experiences while playing it (apart from my fps tanking over 300 population, but that's not really surprising + i was playing on pretty much max settings over 1440p resolution). The problem is, i don't feel like there is much replayability. Your biggest enemy is running out food and coal in winter, everything else is super chill. From midgame onwards things slow down considerably (you need to do missions + everything needs a ton of resources to build). and at that point you are pretty much done with everything.Conclusion:if you just want a very cute and pretty city builder to chill and make some cool towns (and you can make some very cool towns, i really like the building systems in this game), this game is a big thumbs up.But if you want something deeper, something to keep your attention for multiple playthroughs, this is not the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Only other city builder I have really played much since Emperor: Rise of the Middle Kingdom. Others haven't clicked for me, but this one has. Super relaxing, love the graphics, and generally a fun game. Could use some more features (like happiness mattering more, houses upgrading based on their surroundings, etc.) but overall am having a blast. Played 7 hours straight in a single sitting for the first time in a decade.That said, the missions and random events that happen keep things feeling lively whilst you build out your kingdom.Big fan; excited to see how it grows.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: After sinking a whopping 100+ hours into Fabledom, I'd be a bigger liar than the game's storyteller if I said I didn't enjoy it. This city builder is a laugh riot, with the narrator cracking jokes that are almost as good as the zoning laws. I mean, who knew building a kingdom could be this much fun?The game offers endless replayability – I even tried romancing every ruler just for kicks. But don’t get me started on creator mode. It's like a silent movie without the charm. Seriously, where’s the witty banter? Where’s the drama? It's like building a city out of cardboard cutouts.That said, if you're into masochistic map challenges, creator mode might be your jam. But even without it, Fabledom is a total steal, especially if you can snag it on sale. Just don't blame me if you end up neglecting your real-life kingdom because of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game for players who are looking for a laid back experience of building and designing your own perfect fairy tale village. The graphics are pleasing and adorable with great color. The game is still in it's early stages of development but based on what's accessible at the moment this game has a bright future. Fun, addictive and just plain refreshing.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing for a early access game by a 2 man development team. I've played a lot of City Builders and I really enjoy building in this one. The added RPG elements are great and the developers are really responsive towards feedback! I am sure this game will just become better and better over time! Currently the game is only optimized and balanced to have around 200 people, but I am rocking almost 600 and have had zero crashes, I get some stuttering, but the developers have already addressed and are making changes to sort that.The gameplay is great, yes it still needs some balancing but I've already played for 24 hours and haven't been bored yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Play style is a fun mix of managing a city like Civ, resource management like Age of Empires, a beautiful art style, and a forgiving game loop. Makes for a relaxing, enjoyable, but still challenging (if desired) city-builder with engaging fantasy elements. Would recommend if you enjoy:- city-builders- cozy games- beautiful art and atmosphere- strategy that doesn't feel punishing - creating a kingdom without being forced to fight other civs- fantasy or medieval settingsOverall 9/10 - haven't been able to put it down since I got it. Can see this replacing my Civ itch when I want something more laid-back and cozy.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: It's nice to see and play a relaxing city builder that's much more forgiving than others in the same genre. Graphics are cute and fit the storybook/fairy aesthetic well. The devs have been quite transparent in their roadmap and respond to a lot of questions over their discord too. Very excited to see further development into the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up seemingly ages ago following a test version via Steam, enjoyed it so bought it and like many games in my library it got put aside for something else, picked up again recently &quickly becoming a favourite game, Fabledom is charming and interesting and challenging all at a relatively relaxed pace, starting to understand there are deeper levels and lots more content than I've touched already with 19 hours on my latest game it's really getting interesting, feel I will be spending lots more time in Fabledom, especially with the version 1.0 only days away now. Definitely worth the full asking price and the devs seem to have their hearts in the game so that bodes well for future updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun little city builder for a couple of hours.The main focus is to build an aesthetically pleasing city and have some fun with the story-teller. "This is a butchery where you can get meat. What are they doing with the pigs there? Ohhh... Oh no!"The game focuses much more on the relaxing rather than challenging aspect - typically the worst thing to happen will be that stuff takes longer.  This isn't necessarily a bad thing tough, I had my fun with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good but it's a text book early access game. Needs a lot more development there are many things inside the game that are there with an "coming soon" text on it. If you aren't looking to be an early adopter and have to come back later I would just pass on this for right now. Wait for a large update and join in on HOWEVER, I will say for the amount of content in the game for the 10$ I paid right now it's not anything terrible. The dialog is decent from the game and it's basically city skylines with a more cartoonish theme. I think coming back to this for the next major update is something I will do for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried several city builders this year, and many were too complex for me and quickly became stressful to play. Fabledom was the only one that clicked with me, because it simplifies things to the point it's very fun to play.Only con right now is that being EA it is scarce in content (in about 5 hours I saw pretty much everything there is to see) and while I really like the fable theme, it feels very underutilized right now making the game more generic and less fable-like than it can potentially be. Looking forward to the 1.0 release.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This is still in early access, and I will amend if need be, but right now this lands on my "must have" list of city building games. I've played through all the early access story content thus far and the creative mode content as well. Here's what I think so far:Not only is this game SUPER cute, the artwork is really well done and the continuity in style as your city grows is great. I find that in some city builders that the jump from one type of smaller town to the upgraded bigger town buildings is sometimes jarring in style, and your city tends to look disjointed because of that. Every time you start a new story a new map seed is created, which keeps the orientation of the lands fresh and new for each playthrough. I love the layouts I've seen so far, but I do wish I could find a way to get up the hills with roads. Because of that I've strayed away from lands with too many of them. I'm not sure if that's a future feature or not, but it was a pain point for my first town as I had to build everything around them, and I found it a huge waste of space.The UI is easy to navigate and pretty intuitive. It controls much like other city building games. I haven't had any issues so far with this at all.The narrator is funny. You hear him mostly in the very beginning as you're first starting out, and less so as the game progresses, though he still pops up from time to time. I do appreciate that you're reminded he's still there without him chatting all the time as some games do. It keeps his witty comments fresh without wearing him out and making him annoying. I hope this continues into full release.Also eager to see more world events than just the witch turning my villagers into skeletons (which, by the way, while super annoying and tears through my food stores, I love how the ambiance of the game changes and turns all spooky). Now, something I don't like - I'm not a fan of the merchant prince. And this is fine, as I'm pretty sure we'll be introduced to more than him and the harvest princess (who I do like). I just don't like his overall character and demeanor. I also wish my hero had a bit more to do, though I understand that there will be as time goes on. I just hate to see poor Fergus standing at a crossroads in my town in his little straw hat looking bored. I've sat him next to Bob Barkskin for the time being so he has someone to chat with. Other than that I've really enjoyed the small chunk of game that has been offered to us so far. I can't wait for it to grow so that I can wrangle up the sheep and use their wool, finally mine that iron that's just up the road, and see what kind of wheeling and dealing I can do with other royal figureheads.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly? City Builders aren't usually my thing since they get to a ridiculous point where I personally can't keep track of everything XD.But with the small amount of time I've played this game, I can definitely recommend it!Getting the hang of things is simple and you find once you really start getting into the game and gathering resources quicker, it's really fun to sort of plan out how you want your kingdom to look with the space around you.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: As a millennial who grew up playing Sim City & is now well into adulthood, I crave the fun this genre brings but don't necessarily have the time or energy to sink into grinding or managing complicated mechanics. Fabledom brings the perfect mix of building/management, but balances it with fun, humor, style, and is absolutely dripping with charm.  You can totally play at your own pace, opt out of events and take your time, or opt in and challenge yourself.  I also appreciate that it doesn't bleed over into "farming sim" and stays in the lane of city builder.  I'm already enjoying it as it is, so I'm excited to experience it at full release.  I'll definitely keep coming back, and thankfully the game does make starting over quite fun since you can choose different maps and try different strategies.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute, a lot of fun and pretty well balanced for an early access game as well!You either plan new things to build, balance your resources or watch the cute little chicken run around in their backyard.Very relaxing and feel good.I started playing and suddenly it was 8 hours later and I ran out of content.Looking forward to the release!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Game is quite peaceful. Kinda like Foundations but with a bit more focus on decorations and laying out your village but not so much about crafting your own monistary/keep structure. Large maps are quite small and so when I go to 300 pop I ran out of room and can only trade so long for food. Fun game needs some Quality of life improvements
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I will say I usually run away from games like this, not because I don't like them but because they are usually a bit difficult for me and make me feel overwhelmed. Fabledom has only made me feel overwhelmed a couple of times. It is much less daunting than other games in the genre. It's a nice relaxing game, nice music and some challenge. I play at a snails pace, so being able to play at your pace is really nice. They're adding stuff as the weeks and months go by for this game, I got it on sale but believe it's worth the full price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: The game was released on May 13th. On July 24th, the developers provided an update:'Patch 1.06 is expected to be the final patch for Fabledom.'WHAT???I initially believed in the game's potential, but the decision to abandon development so early makes me hesitant to support any future projects from this studio.Considering the high price for what the game currently offers, and with no further updates planned, this game is a no buy right now. Despite the potential of the theme, the gameplay feels shallow and extremely repetitive, leaving little to no replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: All in all I would consider this a pretty good game! The resource management develops slowly enough on your first play that you get an idea of what you will need, but it definitely becomes more and more complex making you reconsider your original builds to be more efficient. I really enjoy the aesthetic of it and the ramp up, but think I'll probably enjoy it more the second go around now that I have a better idea of what things do.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are great, the chain of buildings are good, easy to play and great UI.However being in Early access the game feels limited and looking at the ROAD map i'm disappointed this game doesn't have much more to offer into a larger game as noted in the early access post. My experience has been positive, however i feel DO NOT BUY YET.As it's been a whole month since the last major patch and nothing in between.I fear this may turn out to be those games that will stay incomplete for some time.Shows good promise.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Game has promise, but will not entertain you for more than 3 hours. Had everything built and saw everything after a playthough. Might be good in time but in this current state I would wait. Game advertises as a story driven chill building game. After the opening scene there is next to no story or any development. Building management is square and simplistic. Which I do enjoy although felt no reason to continue playing at all in its current state.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game. A strong 3 out of 5 star. One lost because it's simple, you get the point and snowball very easily. The second point lost is lack of things! The fairytale villains are great, but why is it always the same? Always the same shoe, always the same red riding hood, etc. Wish there was more diversity in that aspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom scratches an itch I've been trying to satisfy for quite a long time. I grew up loving the early games in the Settlers series and have been forever chasing that feeling again (since that series isn't as good as it used to be). I've finally found that joy in a settlement building game again after so many years.This game is so cozy and relaxing. The music is wonderful, the art style adorable, and the different buildings and their interactions provide a fun challenge for building your settlement how you like. Sometimes I just like to lock the camera on a fabling and watch them go about their day. There have already been some great quality of life improvements to the game, as well as new features, since releasing into early access.Fabledom already delivers a fun experience, and a dedicated team that is open to feedback has me looking forward to what the future holds. If you enjoyed games like The Settlers, you will love this.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game. Pretty fun. I find myself restarting a lot to make things perfect and I guess that adds to the fun of it for me and allows more hours to be put into the game. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game and I keep playing it, but I really don't think I can recommend this game to people. It isn't finished. There are just too many little user interface issues that prevent me from really enjoying it. For example, you click on a building to build it. The build menu vanishes, but you don't have a building to place. I have to go through the motions 3 or 4 times before I finally get a building to place. That happens a lot, and not just with placing a building.There are far too many instances of the game just not picking up mouse clicks correctly. There are also interface issues where multiple dialogs will pop up, making it difficult and confusing. Not only can deleting a building take 4 or 5 tries, the dialog to do so pops up in inconsistent places.And based on comments on reddit, if you aren't playing on a pc or a steam deck, don't even bother.Based on the way one of the few update messages was phrased, it seems like the problem is that the main dev had a good idea, got most of it implemented, then got bored and went to do something else. I get it. I hate doing all the little boring bits to polish an app.  But when the app isn't finished, I can recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Cute is an understatement for this game. It still lacks features and content but thats somewhat okay i guess, since it's early access. It was fun playing this though and i have high hopes regarding the further development and the roadmap. Please don't disappoint me. Unpolished gem right now. Perfect for winding down though.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Every time I launch Steam, I immediately check to see if there are any updates from Fabledom yet. _childDocuments_.review: I got this delightful little game a day or so ago ( a week and change since this edit ) and I'm so stupidly hooked it's silly. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is a feel good game and it does its job with great competence. It's a city building game in a fairy tale complete with a beautifully detailed and functional palace.It's full of wonder, with little stories and side quests/tasks and you can also choose what difficulty you want to play.It has dragons and witches, princes and princesses, pumpkins and :} taxes.I think that from the all building games I've played, this one is the most beautiful, i.e. you can build the most beautiful kingdom of all.Pros:- you can build the most beautiful kingdom ever- you can live happily ever after in it- tasks and side quest plus some guests (like Red Riding Hood) give you a sense of wonder- humour everywhere- mechanics are classic city building- you can choose the difficulty and the pace of the gameCons:- there are some bugs (like one with the stuck granary and frozen people) which will maybe never be solved because the devs had announced that the last patch was the final one.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game! Can't wait to play the rest of it as soon as the game updates.Love the look of the buildings, everything is designed very cute!The fairytale theme is a nice take on the genre and something i haven't seen before.The city building mechanics are easy, so is the general gameplay.It is an easy paced game and not so stressful as others in this genre when it comes to management.You won't be punished that hard for mistakes, which makes it a great game for a more casual play.As it is in early access it is not yet complpete, so for now buy when on sale.On sale it is worth the price, so don't shy away from this little gem in the making :)
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly love this game so far. I'm not going to talk about the common issues people have with the game. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: It's simply a really chill city builder. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Please note that this review is for the EA build of the game as per May 2023.I suppose most of the core features, such as building, diplomacy and courting are already in the current build; however, it lacks more content as it is. For example, when you employ your hero, there are at most 2-3 points of interest within reach that your hero can explore. Otherwise, he just stands outside his tent, vacant.When it comes to building and progress, they both are tied to how much money you have, and you never have enough unless you spend time to wait and collect more, and more, and more, and... nope, still not enough. I suggest the devs introduce more ways to make money early in the game, such as trade, increase monetary gain from tasks etc.Apart from the necessity expansion of the content, the game features really good and cute graphics, a good variety of things to do in the game, some sort of a story, replayability and a very nice and relaxing soundtrack.Overall, this is NOT your typical medieval city builder sim; the focus is more on diplomacy, courting a noble from another faction, interaction with the surroundings and generally having a good time.I give it a thumbs-up and recommend the game if you're looking for a relaxing and simple building sim. I invested in the EA build and have not regrettet it since.Looking forward to 1.0 version.

Food and coal are the main things u need. Like the twist about finding a wife. Thats not normal in a city builder. Now diplomatic systems are in many of this games and is also here. All in all a good and fun game. Not to much in it at the moment. Played for 4 hrs and now i have built all i can build as far as i get. _childDocuments_.review: A solid base with the makings of an excellent city builder, I'm looking forward to see what it can turn into. -Compared to others in the genre, Fabledom is most similar to Foundation, but the aesthetics and laid back atmosphere are arguably even better here, which also makes it more accessible. -There is a modular building element like in Foundation that is satisfying if limited only to housing structures; it would be great to see that expanded upon.-At present, with a little over 4 hours in, however, I'm already running up against a dwindling number of new structures. So this will definitely be one to watch improve as new additions are rolled out.-I haven't explored much depth in the "courtship" mechanic. So far it seems like a glorified Civ-style diplomacy system which is currently more distracting than anything else, but I'll refrain from making a judgement until I discover more and see it fleshed out.Overall a good time with some solid room for expansion. FINAL FEEDBACK NOTE TO DEVS: Please, please make it easier to understand how the desirability of condos are impacted by their proximity to homesteads; this is something that is not properly explained at the start and yet is a huge penalty (-10 per homestead). I had to figure out by trial and error that the minimum acceptable distance is... more or less 7 spaces? This should be more clear from the start so that you don't do what I did and build condos. It would be nice if there was also the option to upgrade homes to higher levels and unlock additions to housing hubs.Keep up the effort!

Feels like you're waiting forever.And there is basically no point to training an army, feels a little wasted.But the biggest reason I give it a thumbs down, is apparently the developers are done with the game.They released their final patch, and it still feels like half a game.A few other big gripes I have, is that there is only one type of hero, no customization for them.And the quests are very repetitive with little variation or impact on gameplay.Also basically zero replayability. No unique challanges depending on the type of map you play on.If you can pick this up for half the price, I'd say it might be worth it.Maybe you can even get more out of it than I could.I know it also depends on how you value your money.But for me, I will say: very, very close to a yes, but sadly still no

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game, its allot of fun but the building system at the moment sucks big time. What ever it is you are trying to place down will randomly change shape regardless of what you the player want. Add to that with a game bug that will delete foundations and undo fences to the farms you place when you load/reload a save due to its random build system, it gets pretty annoying fast. I have spent most of my time rebuilding the same thing over and over and over and over again to try and make it just look okay. Thats my biggest issue with the game at the moment, other then that its currently missing some buildings that will be added later, currently there is no fishing so no point in building on a map with any water. This makes food a bit tricky to deal with, expect to starve to death at least once before you can get a stable village running.The hero system is a bit wonky, he can only stand on and move to grass tiles so if you do roads he cant use em at all for some weird reason making him feel pretty useless at the moment, you can send him to investigate ruins but there is no real reason to do that and you can only investigate what is on your territory limiting what you can do with him even further.Like i said earlier the building system in this game is pretty annoying but i would not call it bad, with some work it should be a great game to play, what i hope to see is the ability for players to choose what they place down and what direction they place it as well as placing down decorations on the road tile or have a new tile that match the road tiles so you can properly make the area look nicer. And decorations should in my opinion make the area more desirable to live at so that you actually have a reason to place things and i hope they add more decorations in the future as what we currently got is limited.Update, 15.05.2024The game is finished yay? Well the first thing i got for returning to the game was a bug, no audio for the game, not a great start to be honest. And the build system is still as awful as the last time i played, how the heck did nothing change about the game? Some people might not see a random building system as a bad thing but for people like me that actually want the entrance of the fenced yard to the house on either the right or left side etc of the house its a pretty big deal when the game decides for you where it is or to not have an entrance at all.Will edit as i play but so far this is not that good but not that bad either, they did change the game for sure and for the better so far, if they change the build system then i will be happy with it tho right now the random system is still as annoying as before.

_childDocuments_.review: (DISCLAIMER! SKIP TO PROS AND CONS FOR SHORTER SUMMARY!)I am an avid player of colony sim and management games. From the vast libraries of Paradox titles (Stellaris, Crusader Kings, Hearts of Iron, etc) to smaller titles like Going Medieval or Kingdoms and Castles, I always love this genre of games. This game, if I had to summarize it into a single word, is - quaint. Everything about it is well made and well executed. In just a little under an hour I am fully engrossed into the world and invested. Despite it's minimalist approach to management and mechanics, this is not a bad thing. Not every game needs to be as thorough or complex as others within the genre. It hits that nice balance between critical thinking and forgiving game play. However, clearly this game has a problem with expectations. To be fair, no where did the developers oversell the product. They are, in fact, very generous and straight forward (this game is a steal for $15 bucks). But I can see things about how the game operates and plays that bothers me and hasn't stopped nagging me. My enjoyment of the game and it's potential makes me want for more, but also wince at what's missing just as much. Hills that make building frustratingly impossible at times, but also ridged coastlines to both lakes and the ocean that limit building near water. These make it really hard to build attractive, yet functional layouts sometimes. Plus the inclusion of detailed models for rivals, whilst yours is completely absent, really impacts the player immersion and agency. No one likes to be a faceless prince/princess. This is YOUR fairy tale. I should be able to at least customize a simple portrait for my royal. Perhaps even take it one step further and make a character model inside the game similar to the hero? Even a cameo at your castle/palace would be a nice touch.But enough about that. Here is my list of pro's and con's, along with my conclusion.Pro's-------------*Endearing artstyle*Rewarding romance systems*Ease of access for newcomers to the colony sim genre*Good music, narration, and sound effects*Comprehensive tutorials*Mutli-layered tier system (peasant, commoner, nobles)*Full models for rival rulers with unique stylesCon's----------*Impassable terrain (no terraforming or accessibility like quays or stairs)*Small worlds, despite being called "large"*Nobility feeling redundant and tacked on*No model or avatar profile for the player*Singular hero with surface level customizationConclusion---------------I think Fabledom is a very solid game and is absolutely worth the price point. However, if you are looking for immersion and to be in full control? You may just want to play Crusader Kings, Bannerlord, or even ANNO. This game has a goal and it clearly meets, and sometimes even beats it, when it tries. But I would really like to see it flesh out more of it's world and mechanics. Particularly when it comes to it's building.Below is my wishlist for additions. Feel free to comment what you'd like to see included! Whether you agree with me or not, please be respectful in the comments. Enjoy the game!Wishlist-------------*Player avatar customization*Kingdom hero customization*Terraforming and/or structures to allow versatile building (stairs and tunnels, quays and docks, etc)*Larger generated maps (large doesn't feel large to me)*Further development for both fortifications as well as forts/castles.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun, casual city building game.  I first played in early access and recently started playing again with the official 1.0 launch. _childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable and laid back city builder.  Interface is easy and the game itself--especially if you follow the tutorials--if easy to learn.  The difficulty settings definitely play a part in your game, so it caters to any play style.  And the random map generator ensures countless possibilities. No real complaints.  Only a couple desktop crashes, but those were confined to loading a game and didn't effect play. Only quality-of-life improvement I would like to see it a little better Fablings management screen.  Right now, when you get a bigger town, it takes a bit of looking and clicking to find a certain fabling and move him from one job (or house) to another. Beyond that, though, very fun game.  Highly recommend for those liking this type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game, peaceful music, cute graphics.  Definitely worth the $13 I spent on it.  Two things I wish they'd fix, add, change.  The choices of male rulers should be better, and please, add bridges that go over water!  The text says they do go over water/rivers, but when you try, you cannot place them down.  Bridges should be one of the most basic of things.  Those are my only "complaints" so far.  Overall, love the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly well made, very chill and simple with strong focus on visual aspect, you can tell it by looking at detailed buildings. In terms of gameplay it`s not complicated at all for that kind of games. For your kingdom to prosper all you need to wory about is to make sure you have enough food. Unfortunately, the developer abandoned this game with latest and final patch. However, i still would like to address some minor bugs that requires fixing:Everytihng mentioned above doesnt ruin experience at all, but fixing it will make game smoother.There are two things this game lacks: Simple terraforming and load button when in game.Overall its a gem that requires a little but of polish before becoming a diamond.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a great, laid-back city builder. Think Foundation or Banished but much more relaxing. It's very difficult to get yourself in trouble in this game. The mechanics are interesting. The addition of courting a neighbouring faction adds a very unique charm that no other medieval settlement/survival game has and doesn't make you feel all alone in a vast wilderness by knowing you have other kingdoms nearby.My biggest gripe with this is after recently purchasing it I learned that they had released the "final patch". The game still feels somewhat early access. I'm not going to call it "abandonware" because it is a fully fleshed game with all the development promises. But you can tell that there are some gaps. Having a small militia is pretty pointless except for a few skirmishes throughout the map, clearing out the usual enemy-type camps that dot around and offer a small barrier to expansion. But there is no real war mechanic (asides from helping your neighbouring kingdoms by sending them some troops). Your hero has no real equips. There could be more to the "fantasy" random events that happen. There are also occasional graphical, UI, or general bugs. Despite the above, it is still a good game and something laid-back to play with lots of unique features that sets it apart from the dozens of similar games.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This game may have been given a v.1.0 stamp, but it's still very much what I would deem an alpha, maybe a beta level of polish.There are so many bugs in it, and loads of features are missing.Just to name a few:- Quests don't give rewards.- Ballistas can't hit and just spends all your resources missing the dragon.- You can't really manage resources. Some foods you may have 2000 of but they insist on eating the other foods you need for quests.- They insist on workers home and distance to work is important, but there are little to no way of changing where they live, only where they work with great difficulty.Tha game looks lovely though, and I wish it was polished and recommendable, but at the time of reviewing it at 1.0 launch I rate it a 4/10. Give it a year, maybe it's fixed by then.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Concept of the game is very appealing. The graphics are very cute. And the building mechanic is very straight forward. I also enjoy that it's a very relaxing experience when it comes to managing things. You're not being bombarded by a 100 things you need to keep an eye on. I know there are only 2 devs working on this game. But I just have to be honest about how the game feels and what it offers.

_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This game has massive potential and it's clear they have a lot of big plans for this game. A lot of it seems to be fully realized and ready for production. I'm assuming they're just working out bugs and making sure of balancing. It's a good blend of challenging and relaxing. The art style is great and I can easily see the potential. Buy it now to support the devs and I'm confident this will be worth much more in the next 3-6 months. As it is, it's a bit lacking. I've done two cities and played about 5 hours a piece. That's about as far as you can make it without running into serious balance issues and lack of content due to early access. I wanted to get 15-20 hours out of it before getting bored. I might do one more city but it's already getting a little stale. _childDocuments_.review: Fabledom is simply Fabulous.It is a very laid back experience on normal difficulty, but I can see how it will be challenging on higher settings. I feel like this is what the first Settlers games were all about. You get a total of 17 resources, gold, nobility, people happines and relations with 6 other rulers to manage. Not so few to be trivial and not so many to ovewhelm. There is some fighitng but it is secondary to the main goal of finding your love and marrying a prince or princess of your choice. And to woo them you will need to build your own little kingdom of wood and stone, feed your fablings a variety of foods, keep your subjects happy with decorations and entertainment and fulfill quests straight out of a fairytale (more of a Shrek kind of fairytale to be honest). To perform some of the missions you will need to equip your hero and arm some soldiers. You can also build fortifications, but so far the only use I had for them was to fend off a dragon that happened to wander into my land.Overall the core gameplay could use a bit more polishing. Manually assigning fablings to workplaces gets tiresome after a few hundred times, and switching them around so they don't work too far from home is just annoying. Too much micromanagement spoils the fun. There are some bugs here and there, like area of effect buildings not affecting all houses in the area correctly. I am also missing some features that I feel would make sense: I cannot prioritize where the goods will go (eg. wood for construction, planks or coalmaking), I cannot plant new trees (even though a forester can replant ones that were cut down long ago), I cannot relocate fablings to another home, and I cannot release soldiers from service (I wouldn't even mind if it meant losing their weapons).I adore the cartoonish graphics, there is some clipping here and there but it's not really noticable unless zoomed in all the way. Only the flat sprites of plants feel cheap. But the pigs, oh the pigs are so lovely. I want to cuddle them. And look at those tiny wings. And you can build an arc of pigs! WEEE! The music is wonderfully chill, although somewhat repetitive. The game could use a few more tunes. Overall the game is an 8/10, great with a bit still left to do. I really hope it will continue to be developed!

_childDocuments_.review: Fabledom offers a familiar and enjoyable experience for fans of recent City Builder games, adding a unique twist with fun fables and nostalgic elements from pre-2000s childhoods. The game features a mix of city building and light combat with random encounters, making the initial growth phase engaging. However, it suffers from poor communication regarding gameplay mechanics, such as the advantages of Commoners over Peasants, which players might miss without deep exploration.Like most City Builders, the fun is usually in the beginning, you know – the growth phase. Fabledom does it great. But it doesn’t do a great job at letting you know things. Like for example, at some point you move up to Commoners, and they can do almost every job the Peasants can do, but better. However, you won’t know that unless you really dig deep.The encounters are very easy, but with how Armies are, you will lose Troops, and it will suck. But no fear, you just need to craft a specific item from the Tier 2 and you can revive fallen troops, so there is no real ‘downside’ to combat, as once you have your Troops (1 Troop takes away 1 Pop) you don’t ever lose them, you just revive them. This also goes for your Hero. It’s a bit of an RPG in some respect.The end game is rather dull, unfortunately. Once you reach here, you will likely have a better time restarting at a higher difficulty. You will find yourself in a terrible loop of: I need Coal. It is very fun ruining knowing you need at 300 population, roughly 20 Coal Makers to stay above water while also producing Armaments for new Troops. It does not RUIN the game, but it makes you just want to restart.Some things I think this requires is a Copy and/or Blueprint mode. It sucks having to manually build each home when it would make it so much easier to Blueprint builds or Neighbordoms. I wish there was more to the Special Tiles. They give some decent buffs, but I would like to have a mission to to Climb the Beanstalk more than once, make it some form of “event” to get special Seedlings, or something, anything!
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: Oh joy, what a fun city builder!7/10 Cons:  -Somewhat buggy camera/visual glitches 'rarely' and npcs glitching in place for a few moments before returning to normal -It should be easier to reassign fablings to closer work but I'm not even sure how they'd do that -Lack of settings, though important ones are there -Seems to be poorly optimized, it shouldn't be running 30-40 fps on a 2060 with medium graphics... -Tutorial could be more in depth but works well, this is more of a personal like to see improved -Could have a little more depth(hero exploring, quests, combat, etc...) but I think this is the draw of the game so that's kind of a personal thingPros:  +Music! +Humor and cute/peaceful aesthetic +Simple but more than enough depth to explore and spend plenty time in +Not completely unique but different enough to be something special +Only (almost) 10 hours in, but seems to be a well balanced game(classic difficulty)    +I'm a sucker for ANY romance +Randomly generated worlds Would be an 8/10 if they fixed some bugs. Hope to see more added and more fixes/QoL improvements!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm coming into this game straight from Wandering Village and Against the Storm. I am enjoying it, but I would not say yet that I love it. Still I am giving it a thumbs up. As someone who started building sims with Rollercoaster tycoon rather than Sim City, I admit to being more of a casual player. Pros: I like the pacing. It is a slower more casual colony sim. It gives you the time to stock up on resources before you really need to focus on expansion and improvement. I also really enjoy the whimsical aesthetic. For those who are saying they cant understand why people are starving or what not, it is because you are going too fast. You need to slow down and gather more resources before bringing on more people. If your manager of one household takes 30 food, that food will be given only to that household. Other houses cannot access that food. So you need to have enough food by twice over for your people to sustain them without issue. Cons: The management of the colony is through one menu and I dislike that. Not only is this menu very limited in what it tells you, it can be visually overwhelming for people like me that struggle with too much information in one place. I would prefer to have an overview of the performance of a particular structure be outlined in that structure's menu. For example, if I want to know how much food a particular structure is producing I can go to its menu and find that information. Rather that view the management system and see how much food overall is being produced. Also the aesthetic choices are wonderful, but there isn't as much sandbox play as I would like. For example, the gardens have a lovely tile foundation that matches if you place then next to each other, but that foundation is not available by itself, so if you place the gardens kiddy-corner to one another, you will have gaps of weed covered grass sticking out. For those players like me who enjoy the game play as well as creating a work of art, I would like to see more aesthetic options. As things are compartmentalized into foundations, why not unlock a garden foundation to play with? That way there can be fully courtyards of that beautiful tile? Maybe more colors. Also, do all aesthetics offer the same buff to the area? If so, then why make some more costly? It should say in the item description how much beauty if offers to the surrounding area. In all it is an enjoyable game that gives you just enough dopamine to continue playing, but not enough to truly sit and relax with and carry that relaxation on to other activities. It only gives enough to manage itself.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is so incredibly similar to "The Universim" which makes me wonder if it will have the same fate as The Universim, which is the game does not have much replay value, and gets boring once you reach the end-game. that is my main concern with Fabledom but like The Universim, the game is worth your time and money, even if it might get stale within 50 hours. it's super cute and fun and one of the few cozy games my attention span has no issue with. at least, at first you pretty much constantly have something to doi do wish the villagers themselves had a bigger role: personalities, marriage, children, illness, death, etc. that is one area The Universim does better. because of the similarities to The Universim, i subconsciously expected the villagers to at least marry, have kids, and die. im only 2 hours in though, so maybe they do die eventually lol ... anyway, one of the most fun parts about The Universim was personalizing your village; giving the villagers names, seeing them get married and have kids, giving them jobs, events, and finally, die. this means i could give a villager a cute name, observe them throughout their life, and then be sad when they die. and if i really liked them, i'd make sure the villager who'd take over their job would be worthy ~ and often, that'd be their own children. and Fabledom doesn't seem to have any of that, which is a real bummer! i'd even love them to expand more on it than The Universim did.this game has amazing potential. i really hope it will grow into a game that can be played for hundreds of hours without getting boring. of course, not all games are meant to last you hundreds of hours. but Fabledom is so fun and interesting, that it does have the potential to indefinitely entertain me. i'd even say they could come up with cool DLCs, tbh. nonetheless, it's a great game as it is right now, and truly feels like it's already a fully fleshed game. am very excited to follow its journey.edit: the villagers can die!!! i sound crazy for liking that! lol. but my feedback still stands

_childDocuments_.review: Right now with the game being in early access, I would recommend just buying it on sale. While it's a beautifully stylistic city builder, it only has about 5 hours of content unless you start over or play in sandbox mode.That being said, the soundtrack is amazing, the narrator is a lovable addition, the animation is striking, and it's tracking to be a promising game. If you're looking for a cosy city builder with fantasy elements and a lot of heart, this is the pick.I think a nice touch would be if the town could expand via families instead of only having new town folk appear once every ten days, but maybe that's in the works.In the end, I can't wait to see where the end product of Fabledom takes us.

_childDocuments_.review: It's early access - so there's still a bit to go. That said, what I've seen is incredibly promising. It's a competently made city builder, very "Settlers" (for better or worse) so if that's your jam keep an eye on this. I chewed through the EA content fairly quickly (about 3 hours) but I'm quite eager for more.What jumps out at me is there's clearly a lot of heart in this project. Fabledom is comfortable in its style and the unique goal of maybe dating your neighbours. The game is cute and has a good sense of humour that'll pop up just frequently enough to get a chuckle without wearing itself thin.There's a couple of issues with your little dudes getting stuck and they can die of starvation if your food storage is too far away from them but the team is aware of this and I'm confident in their ability to address it.

_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to review... As a city-builder it's very light so I thought it was maybe more story driven. But then as a narrative based game it's ALSO very light - Although the setting is charming and fun the few events that happen are SUPER brief and not in the least bit immersive. Basically you get a text box saying something is happening (Like a witch is cursing you) and you can either choose to take the curse or buy the witch off. That's it. That's the extent of the immersion. You get one sentence and a choice to take a debuff or pay some resources.But saying all that I don't feel like I should give this game a thumbs down as they HAVE got the promising bones of a game here. The mechanics are ok, the art style is great and it feels like it's just a couple of tweaks away from being something special. And this IS early access after all so with any luck they'll actually flesh out both the city-builder side of things AND the story side of things (I really hope they do the latter, it's such a waste of a good setting otherwise).So I think I'm gonna give it a thumbs up for now. There's enough playability to it and it's polished enough to get recommended. It is very charming and not overly expensive. But if in 6 months time the game hasn't moved on I think this review will have to switch to a thumbs down as it's 'potential' is doing a lot of the heavy lifting.
_childDocuments_.name: Fabledom

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend it but it has issues. Pros: graphics, music, fairly easy interface, easy mouse only controls. Cons: 1) you're encouraged to add more people to your village pretty much every 5 minutes and made to feel horrible if you refuse and 'dismiss' them.2) the seasons change far too often, pretty much every 15 minutes which means you have to constantly change workers from farmers to coal burners to provide heat for homes and then back to farmers again after winter. Winter lasts around 5 minutes so every 20 minutes you're changing roles of workers. 3) You're sent requests for items/food from unknown beggers and made to feel bad when you reject them4) My village only got to 40 residents then around 5 died during winter? WTH? can you not skip over the death part, it's meant to be a relaxing game?!I'll update if I think of more. Not sure if I'll play this game again though.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't call this a relaxed 'cozy' game at all. It is a citybuilder with a cute theme - but the focus is on min-maxing production and supply chains just like every other city builder and yes, unfortunately you will end up with a dozen coal producers, a dozen woodchoppers, a dozen farms, and have to keep building more just to survive. Late game inflation means you have to build more and more and more of everything. So long as you aren't expecting a relaxed 'design-my-ideal-fantasy-town' game, but want a city builder with a web of supply chains for everything, then this is for you. Personally the city gets so large and complex by mid to late game, I generally end up not finishing any games. Sigh ... really hoped this game was different to the usual. But all gripes aside - not a bad citybuilder game, just very much the same as all the others.
