_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic gameplay, I honestly loved how charming the characters are, the comedy is on point, as well as how fun and addicting the combat mechanics were. It's relatively short, coming in at around 4-5 hours of content, but it's design and difficulty makes up for it. Take it with a grain of salt but personally I've run into a few issues in the arena mode where my game would crash seemingly out of nowhere, might just be me, but just a heads up. Overall super fun ^^
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know sapphic swashbuckler games were a thing, but I need way more of them.This game is super fun. I really enjoy this game combat that forces you to use the entire map and utilize the environment - it was such a blast to kick barrels and throw bags of chili powder at enemies. The story is simple but well-written and the characters are charming. I'm kind of burnt out on long games currently so it's refreshing that the story doesn't drag on, though at the same time I want more. The arena mode helps to itch that scratch somewhat.This game was obviously made with a lot of love and it's incredible that this originated from a student project. I understand people's complaints about the price, but I don't mind paying for a short game when it's at this quality. I do hope we get more En Garde in the future, though.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I only played the first two chapters, but I had SO much fun. It's such a pretty game, the lighting, art and environmental details make it a wonderful place to explore. The dialogue is great too, I love the sass of Adalia. There were a  couple of spots where I was struggling with coordination but I was able to just turn on the accessibility features to help out when needed. I'm looking forward to when I can play next!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this with no expectations. It seemed like a promising indie game when I first saw it, then kind of forgot about it.But after playing through it, and giving myself a challenge of only completing the game once, all whilst going for the 100% achievement trophy.I succeeded, and whilst it wasn't easy, it was never frustrating.This game did so much right, because it didn't need to check all the boxes to be relevant.A simple story. No need for a 740 document story, which in order to understand, you need to play the game 100 times. No, just a simple heroic story with snarly comedy. And by not trying to be something it ain't, it didn't fail in that regardFlowy combat. You do not need million armour pieces, three thousand weapons and charms, rings and what not. No need to level up, rest at bonfires, nothing. It makes the combat all the more enjoyable. It's measured on your skill alone, and whilst I recommend playing the game on Hard difficulty, it will probably not be as hard as Dark Souls tho. But it doesn't need to be.Catchy soundtrack. The music fits so well with the enviroment, and even when the music is silent, the enviroment stays catchy regardless. Kind of a nice change of pace from the aggressive choirs of the Souls Games.Original Enemies. Enemies don't have a lot of variety, but on their own, every enemy is very easy to beat. But that's the point of the game. You're not a killing machine, you're a duelist, and you can't really duel a group of 5, you have to split them.No-Cheap Comedy. I love the fact that you never kill anyone. How you compliment / insult the guards in a playful manner and how they often admire you after you defeat them. It's no "funny" oneliners, it's the stupidity of the situation that's funny.Simple Story. In all honesty, I much more enjoy simple stories like this. An easy to understand villain, being evil for the sake of being evil. A double crossing lady that always doublecrosses, a false hero that's always a false hero. It feels like a fairy tale, for no one truly changes throughout the story. And it's lenght would agree with that.PS : I got chills at the end when Adalia said "En Garde!" at the end. Such a predictable one liner but so well fitting. The only thing I can take away from En Garde! is the lenght, but as a person that does not have a lot of time to play games, I enjoyed this bite sized game. I wouldn't be against it if there was an En Garde! 2!Thank you for reading my review, stay swashbuckling!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this, I'll confess I wasn't expecting anything overly special. Colorful cast, flashy combat, goofy dialogue, and an overall lighthearted romp.A lot of games make you look like a badass, but it takes a special touch to make you truly  like one, and by God this game delivers in spades. The combat system, in all honesty, defies description; I really don't think I can do it justice with words alone. It's hard to pick up at first, with enemies quickly overwhelming you and seemingly designed to counter your every move, but once you start to understand how the mechanics function and interplay, you quickly go from helpless fencer to daring swashbuckler, systematically tearing apart encounters and turning entire squads of royal guards that would have once overwhelmed you into absolute chumps. It's certainly not easy, not by a long shot, but the feeling of exhilaration you get from ripping through a room and turning a seemingly impossible situation into a beautiful symphony of chaos worthy of the silver screen is truly magnificent.If you have any interest in this one, give it a go. You will not regret it, I promise you.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: -Link to a video below-TLDRThis game feels  with its balance of combat, story, and comedy. The combat is super fluid, with the ability to parry or dodge-roll mid combo or action. The art-style is polished and the voice acting is top-notch! 10/10 highly recommend!   In En Garde!, you play as Adalia de Volador, a fencing champion/vigilante who is constantly fighting against the Count Duke and his goons to bring justice to your city. You play through episodes, with each one having a slightly different premise, locations, and challenges.  En Garde is a hack and slash story game, and it does it ! Playing on medium difficulty, I found myself dying a few times each episode (Don't worry, there are easy and hard modes, too!). The combat is completely fluid, and you have the opportunity to use your surroundings to your advantage! Dash across tables or over crates, kick bad guys into weapon racks, or knock them down the stairs to disable them for a brief time. The sound effects and the voice acting only add to the game, bringing comedy and satisfaction to everything you do.  Overall, I highly recommend this game to those who are considering it! There is replay value in trying to find all of the hidden collectables in each episode, and the higher difficulties are something I will absolutely be checking out. Thank you for watching/reading!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A cool idea brought down by janky combat. Enemies in mid attacks are kind of "sucked" towards you when you try to move out of the way. Blocking feels more like they want you to hit it when the blue light flashes rather than when the enemy is about to hit you which feels way too earlier and very different from other parrying done in games. I played Sifu, got my ass kicked for the first 15 or so hours before I became confident in clearing crowded rooms and it seriously raised the bar for brawler type games for me. The combat en En Garde seriously falls short of that bar in terms of smoothness and flowing combat. I can see why this is overall rated given the aesthetics, music, and comedy, but the swordplay just kind of kills it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Player-driven Loony Tunes physical comedy combat integrated with streamlined swordplay, all coated in a thick layer of borderline-cheesy quips? Was this created in a lab just for me? I started replaying before I even finished. The devs clearly know the main draw of this piece is the combat and have kept the game nicely focused.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I would sum up En Garde! as a short fencing experience with unique visuals and a story that's told in a very humorous way.Fencing is the key element and the combat feels fluent and clean. Standard parry and dodging red attacks is what they were going for here and for me it felt very crisp with a gamepad. The story is nothing revolutionary, but the way its told in a funny and comical way really nails it, rounded up with colourful visuals. Also, voicing of the characters with spanish accent and the guitar soundtrack lend this game a really authentic athmosphere, that really suits the fencing setting, well done.Its a short experience of about four hours in main campaign. Besides, there is a rogue like arena mode which also has potential for another few hours of fun. Overall another love letter of an indie game that it doesn't always have to be a triple AAA game experience.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game does a lot of good things but unfortunately also misses the mark on other things.My favorite part about this game is mostly how it looks and feels. The animations are smooth and feel cool. The art style is nice to look at. There is an option to set the controller button layout which is something so simple yet so amazing. It baffles me that other games do not have this yet.I also love the voice lines of the heroine. She very confident and playful. Some lines made me genuinely smile.The music is nice and you can jam to it while playing. Though it does get a bit generic after a while.This game is very lighthearted. It has a lot of humor. This is both a good and a bad thing. The bad thing is that it lacks depth. There is nothing meaningful to anything happening. The game doesn't take it self seriously. So neither could I. If you like lighthearted games then props to you. I like them too but they never seem to stick with me and I can't play them for long amounts of time. My first session of a lighthearted game is usually also my last.While the game does look and feel nice. Everything gets generic. Nothing really sticks in my memory as "that one cool thing that happened". Every new place feels and looks the same. It goes from a corridor to a big room to a corridor to a big room. The bad guys are also very generic. They don't really have a personality from what I saw. All enemies and bosses seem to talk and act the same.While I do say their lines are actually funny.The platforming doesn't feel good. Jumping around is cool. Especially with grabbing poles and ropes. It just feels a bit snappy while the running jump also feels a bit uncomfortable to control. This makes jumping from a bouncy net to another feel very awkward. It also feels a bit inconsistent. The one time I jump towards a pole and my character seems to gain another 3 meters in height and fly towards the exact center of the pole while the other time she does a regular jump and misses the pole by a pixel and I flop to the ground.Now for my main issue: the combat.What I do like about the combat is how it slowly introduces more mechanics while it also feels smooth.The animations and voice lines are also very satisfying.What I do not like is that it gets repetitive too quick. This is a huge deal breaker for me.I like games that give me a combat experience where I am on my toes and feel like I have to pay attention. One other thing I like is when games give you multiple ways to tackle a situation. This game does neither.(people might disagree with me on the 2nd point. I will elaborate*)Some items are just too strong to the point I find myself kicking crates or tables at the enemy the entire time. If you do enough blunt damage to enemies they gets guard broken after which you can spam attack on them until they die.All enemies I found only had 2 attacks. A blue parryable attack and a red dodgable attack. Though you can just spam dodge and you won't get hit ever. (unless you try to dodge into a crate). I found myself liking the parry more but using the dodge more on bosses and groups of enemies because I just get hit otherwise.There's too many enemies that stick together insanely hard. If you run anywhere for a solid 10 seconds and turn around they are all as close to you as 10 seconds ago. They are constantly in your neck.I kind of hoped that I could manoeuvre around. Maybe single out an enemy and duel them for a bit but unless you go stunning enemies you cannot.On the flip side if you DO go and stun everyone: They can't do anything back. While I kick crates or throw things at them they are completely helpless which makes the game feel a bit too easy and boring. This is why I would like to duel some enemies a bit to get off ripostes. However the constant ganging up on me makes this basically impossible. If you attack any enemy at all, another guy will immediately do a red attack on you. The enemies recover their health/guard while you are not attacking so it's absolutely not recommended to sword fight them while nobody is stunned.This makes me run around, kick crates and throw objects basically through out entire fights. I even found myself just kicking a table towards 3 guards for about a whole minute.*I said earlier that I don't think there are many ways to tackle a situation:I want to add though that there are a lot of ways to stun enemies (kicking, throwing, even jumping over an enemy makes them look track of you which is actually hilarious). But it all comes back to stunning. You are forced to go out of your way to stun almost everyone every time.With variety in strategy I mainly mean that I would prefer if I could choose to fight the guys head on in any way at all or try to use dirty tricks. Not always resort to stunning.I honestly wanted to keep playing to see if there would be more to this game but I did not want to hit 2 hours on this game because of the refund policy. After reading a bit it seems that this game is about 3-6 hours long with 4 episodes total. I finished 2/4 episodes in 90 minutes on normal difficulty (I didn't rush I spend time looking around. I found some cave with spoons). I do not see myself playing this game more after I finished the main campaign.I wholeheartedly believe that this is a passion project by developers that are genuinely trying to make a fun game. I also think that these developers are very competent and have a lot of potential.While I think they nailed a lot of things. The things that matter the most to me in video games were the parts that I did not enjoy. I think most people will enjoy their first playthrough of this game and then forget about this game forever.This game is definitely for some people.But not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Short and uninspired. Combat is on positive side, yet enemy hp recovery made in rather janky way.Art direction is really great, voice acting is on decent level, whole environment gives really good vibes, which are ruined within minutes of "story" progressing.There is no story really and characters are as transparent, bland, shallow, and personality lacking, as a bucket of water.If you're fan of arcade decent melee action combat - worth getting because of arenas.If you're here for the whole thing packaged with the story and character development - Bulletstorm does better job in that department.Most boring protagonist in action games.Most boring villain in action games.Most boring support cast in action games.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played Sifu, you'll feel right at home playing this... after you've gotten used to the controls being different, anyway. And much like Sifu, the story is pretty short and there's an arena mode to keep you busy afterward.Story and dialogue are pretty funny, too.My main complaint is just that the game kind of encourages playing like a scumbag most of the game. In sifu, if there's like 5 enemies, they can all crowd you but you can still just parry everything they do, and there's only a few throwable items lying around. in this game, if there's 5 enemies, they'll just all attack you at once and kick your ass so a lot of the time playing is spent running around the arena and throwing items at people - especially later in the game, where the arenas throw several elite enemies at you at the same time.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is a very fun little 3rd person-action-adventure-fence-em-up game from the brilliant developers of Sifu. Clocks in at around 4 hours of play time and doesn't overstay it's welcome at any time. So you can easily finish it in 1 or 2 sessions. After completion there's an Arena mode to test your combat skills some more. Don't go in expecting a deep story about a woman in fencing or anything like that. This is a game focused on it's highly stylized and timing-based combat and first and foremost - fun. The tongue-in-cheek humor might be a little too much for some people here and there, but the slapstick comedy you (un-)intentionally produce in combat is something I haven't seen in a while. Chaotic and hilarious at the same time.The art design is very pretty with a swashbuckling-mediterranean flair. Similar to Sifu, but more cartoony in my opinion and kinda reminded me of the old Asterix and Obelix games.  The gameplay has a heavier focus on light platforming and "puzzle" solving in between the different fighting arenas/encounters compared to Sifu. Controls and movement in general are very tight, fast and forgiving with little downtime windows when missing a parry for example, making everything feel very snappy. You can tell that the budget was a little lower as there aren't any really fleshed out cutscenes or facial animations, but the voice actors seemed to be having a lot of fun and more than make up for it. I got this game on sale for 10 bucks (euros in my case), and I'd even recommend getting it for 20 if you're a fan of the genre or want to support the developer. Definite recommendation!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing work for a game that started as a ... student project.The Art (yes, with a capital A) is just wonderful. So is the lighting and level design.Is it fun? Yes, absolutely. Some sassy dialogues, use of environment elements (the bucket trick is my favorite), etc.I was expecting a nice little game but got a great great game!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: things that i have done in this game:-blinded a guy by sticking a turkey on his head-kicked a jar into a group of my enemies, spilling its contents onto the floor and causing them to comically slip and fall.-cut the cords of at least three giant chandeliers, sending them crashing down on my enemies.-threw a grenade at a pot of soup and the resulting explosion not only stunned a bunch of nearby guards, but also threw the pot high into the air, and when it came down a few seconds later it landed squarely on the guard captain's head, knocking them out.the combat expertly straddles the line between crisp action and off-the-wall comedy. it's great.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is trash. There's no rhythm to the combat whatsoever. You just get piled on with multiple dodge/parry attacks slapped right on top of each other. There's no way to really engage with the combat. I have to assume most of the positive reviews come from people playing this game on normal or easy. Playing on hard just breaks the game. There's no flow to the combat and enemies just attack right on top of each other. I don't appreciate games that break their own systems when you up the difficulty. _childDocuments_.review: It's by no means a bad game. So it hurts me a lot to give it a thumbs down...So why do I do it:Gameplay is at first real fun and has a good learning curve... but it gets repetitive really fast...Measured with the playtime and the price... there you got your thumbs down...All in all a nice game with a cool and intuitive gameplay, but the short playtime and the repetitive missions with a playtime around max 5 hours... absolutely too expensive.If I could I would give it a thumbs mid in conclusion... around 6-7/10 if you do the equation...So get it on sale and have a good time... but never at full price.All the best to you and keep playin'!

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun Sifu style combat, but with an emphasis on using the environment and splitting up your foes.Character banter is funny and top tier. Also, I think the devs like star wars because I've detected many prequel refrences in the lines, so thats good.Finally, the roguelike arena mode is fun and adds much needed replayability for such a short game.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It is a rare joy to find a game that knows exactly what it is, exactly what it plans to be, and goes for that goal as hard as possible. It is even rare to find one that sticks the landing as well as En Garde, where the few rough edges can be overlooked by the power of simply having fun. It would be a cliche, but an accurate description to describe this game as Sifu, but it is also Zorro, an arena based brawler about throwing roast chickens onto people's head and kicking the table out from under them, a rollicking saturday morning cartoon with heaps of personality and accessible mechanics that provide a decent amount of challenge over the length of the game, which knows not to overstay its welcome. En Garde knows what it is, provides it to you with style, then leaves with grace. Rarer still, a videogame that is actually funny (intentionally), and has given me more genuine laughs than any other that comes to mind. I feel like this is the kind of game that Rare are making in an alternate universe.Solid mechanics, an absolute banger of a soundtrack and an engaging artstyle round off the package, along with of course buckets and buckets of Zorro's most powerful weapon, charm.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: has plenty of style, an elegant simplicity to its combat, and swashbuckling for days—or, at least, for a few . It’s short, sweet, and to the sword point, but what’s here is beautiful to look at, fun to move around in, and a joy to listen to.Each level  have its own assortment of challenges to complete and secrets to find, and there  an Arena Mode to hone your fencing skills. For the story-focused player, however, these might not be enticing enough reasons to play beyond “The End.” Even so, I would still very much recommend giving  a shot, especially when it happens to go on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say, it was a surprise!Gameplay is smooth and hectic: running and jumping around, kicking baddies, throwing them buckets and mugs... using the various items scattered as weapon is really fun to do. Even if linear, the combat section give a lot of freedom.Best thing for me though is the light-harted humor.You know? This game gave me memories of that old Disne's show of Zorro, that I used to watch as kid...The downside is the its lenght. While secret objective can give an excuse for a second run, it still remain short (my time record is for 2/3 of the game, by an action noob).I still recommend it, as its innovative and fast combat system and humor.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A short but very sweet little game that actually plays remarkably well in terms of both humour, gameplay, and artstyle! I encountered a few bugs here and there, but nothing of further note than a minor hiccup at best!'En Garde!' slots into a very certain niche on the games-market with fencing-style swordplay that (I think) is rarely seen nowadays. With a beautiful presentation and giggle-worthy wits and humour, along with high-energy swordsmanship that can sure make you feel like Zorro - outsmarting henchmen and combatting them using all sorts of tricks to do so - it's very easily a game with a good recommend from me!The only woe I would have is that it isn't longer! I was struck with sadness when I realized I was playing the final level, yearning for more. The Arena Mode is nice and all, but it sadly tends to get old a bit quickly... If Fireplace Games continue with what they have going here, expanding on it with more levels, more detailed fighting-freedom with more options to tackle encounters they could easily make something truly incredible!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good, however I've decided to go for a refund after playing just a bit. I saw right away what kind of public they were going for. The main reason why is that there is way too much hand holding and the story just doesn't click with me.Let me say that there isn't worse tutorial than the one that requires you to "do that things 2 times" and then "do that other thing 4 times" and just spawns things infinitely until you do exactly what they want. I know it's just the tutorial, but I have way too many things on backlog to bother.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is a fun quirky game that hearkens pack to classic linear arena beat-em-ups from the ps1 era while feeling modern. Solid game-play, voice acting, sound track, and mechanics. Very short but very sweet! Most people will finish this game in an afternoon or two if we include the arena mode. Main story is four chapters of engaging game-play and humerus dialog. Voice acting and soundtrack is 10/10 and surprised me coming from an indie dev. The first 2 chapters are about 45 mins to 1 hour each (I beat these in 45 mins each I played on medium difficulty), chapter three took me 1 hour or a little over and chapter four took me just under 2 hours to complete with around 45 deaths. Difficulty goes up gradually (largest spikes being boss fights and small area fights) and the devs did a good job of introducing new enemy types throughout the short experience. Overall the fights feel challenging but yet attainable. I would recommend playing with a controller and on medium the first time through for the funnest experience. The difficulty is frustrating in a good challenging way where the game wants you to hone in on game mechanics, strategy and a tad bit of swashbuckling luck to progress. En Garde! shines in its arena fights. This is the pinnacle of the game so I'm happy the devs put in a separate arena mode with its own challenges for replayability. My only criticism is in chapter four and part of chapter three where it becomes more boss fight and small area fight focused which takes away from the core appeal I have in the game and what I think is the pinnacle of the play experience. The final boss of the game has a good balance of arena minion and boss fight. Pretty much all of chapter four is boss fights one after another from the games previous boss fights. While it's not my cup of tea it didn't feel low effort or like you were just rehashing the fights from before as they are unique to the area. Others will love this aspect of play more than me. Definitely worth the sale price on this. 100% would recommend and I'm very happy with my $12 going to this game. Pick this up if your looking for a fun unique throw back that is more friendly and lighthearted than sifu. Great game to fill a weekend with and revisit from time to time. Streamed for my buddies and they enjoyed just watching the game play.  The major drawback of this game is that once you beat it you do want more. While that sucks it does make me want to follow this dev team and see what other projects they turn out. Solid 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having a blast playing the game , the art style is really charming and makes the whole experience feel unique and lively. The game has a great mix of strategy and fast-paced action that keeps you on your toes. The beautifully painted locations and witty dialogue feel like you're in a classic adventure story. If you love games that mix action with comedy, En Garde is definitely worth a try. It's full of charm, laughs, and a ton of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll throw my review on the pile, considering there're not many. This was a wonderful, incredibly charming experience backed by strong combat mechanics and fun story. The fights reminded me of the swashbuckling fun of Arkane's Dark Messiah and the presentation strongly (at least, to my eye) associates with the Shrek movies, all in the best way possible. The only problem – it's very short, the main campaign without rerunning for challenges and achievements will last you around ~5 hours, which is hardly a complain for the price but still merits mentioning. I ardently recommend this one and will be holding out for a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Good but short. Campaign took me about 2.5 hours with several deaths, arcade mode 2 hours with 1 defeat. If you subscribe to "$1 = 1 hour" theory, this game isn't worth $20, but it is very fun for the short time you have with it.Besides rock-solid fundamentals, the fun of using the environment to screw over your opponents and unlock openings to take down enemies (who actually defend each other and don't just fight you 1 at a time, because that's what Adalia De Volador wants!) is unmatched.Absolutely oozes with flavor, having the Puss-In-Boots-esque Spanish swordfighter story of a daring hero fighting against a corrupt governor, with plenty of comedy that is actually quite good.The only real downside is how short this game is, so unless you're down to replay the same story or do the story-less arcade mode multiple times, I would wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AWESOME. I'm so glad I picked it up. I just regret not having bought it at full price. When I become a trillionaire, I'm funding the studio to make a fully fleshed out sequel with even better environment design, even more expansive voice acting and definitely a larger set of episodes. 10/10, up there as one of the best indie games I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this a lot. Ok, this game is short, the moveset is simple, i get that. But guess what ? That's what makes it super efficient. Swachbuckling at its best, and not long enough to get bored.Besides, it's a game in which the pleasure comes from overwhelming your opponents with environmental hazards rather than getting Gud "souls-like style". Plus, the atmosphere is totally in that boast-and-jump-around style.Oh and guess what ? ALL OPPONENTS ATTACK AT ONCE. No "taking turns" like in AC-like games. So you better sharpen thy rapier, and En Garde !If Inigo Montoya could make a game he would make this one !
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This is as close as it comes to perfection, for me at least. A tight action adventure game with a beautiful art direction, short but very replayable story mode, a challenging and expansive arena mode and a soundtrack that just makes you wanna swing on a rope while slashing your sword in both directions violently. The game devs have managed to re-create the feeling of a 1950s swashbuckler movie, The Princess Bride and the works of Alexandre Dumas perfectly while filling every line with charm and endearing humor.It does not only play well, it also just sounds good. It's buckets of fun, plain and simple, and I cannot get enough of it. The game devs also deserve praise for making a very lgbtq+ friendly game, I'm sure I'm not the only bisexual who sees the inspiration for Adalia in Julie D'Aubigny, and appreciates the representation.If there is any minor criticism to be had, then that the voice acting sometimes seems to lack direction - the voice actors are all doing a very fine job, but some lines could have used another read. Honestly, thats nitpicking on the highest level tho, as the only real problem I have with this game is that there isn't more of it.I love this indie darling, it seems to have been made specifically for my tastes, and I hope this won't be the last we see of Adalia de Volador!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, cute, charming, engaging. I just completed chapter 2 and I'm ready to reccomend this game. I heard that it's pretty short for the price, so do as I did and wait for the sale. 10€ is more reasonable in my opinion. However, I'm having very good time with this game. It satisfies my need for action sword combat. The combat is pretty satisfying.If you're looking for a Assassins Creed or Prince of Persia clone, this is the game you're looking for.+ Arena mode is cool
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those games where you could say something like "This is a like a PS2 game (complimentary)". It's focused on what it is while still exploring the possibilities. It doesn't take itself too seriously, while also being sincere. It's just a Fun video game. The mechanics are fun, the writing is fun, the voice actors sound like they had fun. It's a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely delightful from start to finish!The music, art design, sound design and animations are incredibly fun and charming, and the actual combat is as fun as it looks!The swordplay is kept pretty simple - attack/parry/dodge - and won't get you very far on its own, because the game quickly throws large groups of enemies at you. This is to push you into using every part of your environment to win, which - once you embrace that approach - leads to beautifully chaotic fights. You kick a chandelier into one lackey's face to stun him, distract another by throwing a bucket on his head, then parry and riposte an attack coming from a third before you slide over a table and kick the stunned lackey off the balcony.While the game has the charming and family friendly vibe of a saturday morning cartoon, the combat is actually tougher than I expected. To some degree it has to be, to push you into the environmental systems, but I had to turn the ending of the final episode down to easy. It's pretty short, but very well polished, tight and focused. I prefer a game that spends a shorter amount of hours well over a game that takes longer but wastes most of that time.Absolutely recommend this one, it's genuinely wonderful and I can't wait to see what Fireplace Games do next!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute joy to play! I loved the characters, the music, the art style! Gameplay is both simple to learn and hard to master. The writing is hilarious. It also doesn't overstay its welcome and can be beaten pretty quickly which might be a con for some but I liked the shorter run time. I did get a little frustrated on the final boss because it felt much higher difficulty wise than anything else in the game, but perhaps I am just a scrub. 8/10 would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, and relaxing... Well, not that relaxing, the sword fight can be intense if you face more than 2 enemies.I bought this game mainly because of the bright color and likeable characters, turned out to be a nice mini-Prince of Persia game with a female protagonist, decent sword fights and good humor. 1/2 of the time you do wall jumps to reach the other side, the character will automatically swing on the rods, meaning you won't miss a grip nor lose your way. The rest 1/2 will be sword fights so prepare to polish your skill.I need to focus on attack and counter because this part of the game is serious, missing a few times meaning face down on the floor. Luckily, the sword fight is not too hard to master, and the environment contributed a lot to the fun, like you could kick enemies into river/into a weapon rack/down the stairs, or use cannon on them (LOL), loose the rope to drop chandeliers on them etc, there are a variety of items can be useful and to interact with. What's more, most lines are designed to be funny even during combats, enemies being defeated would say "I wish I never got up this morning" and there are unexpected actions to discover like you can .The gameplay is a bit short with a limited kind of enemies, but okay for a nice little game.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Game got off to a good start, but became frustrating by  the later acts.  The environment in integrated well into the combat, but you quickly run out of crate to kick and  lutes to throw.  By the end the enemies have unblockable attacks, regenerating guard, and the fights become very Benny Hill (run in circle looking for a quick environment.  Also, the camera struggled to keep up so you'd often be clipped by someone off screen, which is a deal breaker given that the focus is on acrobatic combat.Personal I don't mind the short gameplay, but too repetitive and the combat should keep me feeling like Errol Flynn the whole way instead of feeling the need to cheese things.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Lot of fun. Game is polished, the voicework is fantastic, characters and writing are endearing. I wasn't particularly good at it, and got through the main campaign in under 7 hours, so it felt a bit short for the price point. There are a few things to pad out the playtime for completionists, but I'd recommend getting it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde is a short but very fun game with a lot of charm. You play as an honorable swordswoman who is fighting against the guards of the evil villain who took control of your city. These fights start of really easy but get increasingly difficult to a point where I needed many tries just for a single fight. The fighting mechanics are relatively simple but in most fights there are many opponents at once and you have to use boxes, barrels or stuff lying around to get an edge by stunning or weakening them. Also, while fighting (and even after), you and your opponents are constantly mocking each other and the voicelines are hilarious! This is the first game in a while that genuinely made me laugh out loud.The game has a great soundtrack and even better voice acting. Don't expect too much out of the story, though, it is very predictable and full of cliches.If the fights get too monotonous for you, there are some challenges that you can try to do for some added difficulty and you can also roam around the levels and try to find some hidden areas.After you finished the story, there is an arena mode where you just fight waves of enemies but with some modifiers to the mechanics that add some more variety.Completing the whole story took me about 6 hours, and getting 100% of the achievements brought my gametime up to around 14 hours.Summary: En Garde is a charming and entertaining game with easy-to-learn but hard-to-master fighting mechanics, hilarious dialog and voicelines and generally good vibes. I absolutely recommend playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Good game about sword fighting.A little on the short end for its price but i liked the enemy progression.Played it on hard and tbh, it was getting a little messy in some of fights due to the aggressive enemy AI, but you can learn to deal with those situations.Fighting with the environment took a while to get used to but felt worth towards the second half of the game.All in all: pr good.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough! You can feel the love in every aspect of this game. The swordplay is so responsive and allows for creativity in your approach to all situations. I'm excited to hop back in and find all the secrets, complete the challenges and play arena mode. The charming characters and beautiful setting make for a world I want to return to many times and I'm excited to go back! For less than $20 (or slightly less if you purchase before 8/23), this is well worth it. If you enjoy exciting sword fights and dancing between/riposting enemies, throwing pots on peoples heads and things of that nature, you will love En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: The game on its surface is fun, charming, and engaging. With many unique environmental interactions and creative moves, you can fight with some flair and panache. There is a lot of humor in the game and quite a bit of lighthearted fun. However, even after a three-hour campaign, the mechanics can wear pretty thin. As others have said, the game tends to only increase difficulty by adding more enemies or having more and more waves in a room with rapidly dwindling resources. The game, generally speaking, is not that difficult, but it can be incredibly frustrating seeing the mechanics interact. This is especially true with enemies whose stamina is instantly refilled if you mess up fighting them (e.g., you dodge when you should have parried, or they hit you). This is all good, but when you have 5 of those enemies fighting you, and you mess up an attack from one of them, all of them fully regenerate their stamina. While this really incentivizes the usage of the weakening mechanic, your opportunities to engage with it can run out in prolonged fights. These difficulties can be overcome with enough time and skill. Still, I think the final boss fight especially makes it really frustrating to engage with the core mechanics. Still, these are just light frustrations on a fun and lighthearted game. If you want to feel like a swashbuckler who uses flair, panache, and the environment to outwit your foes, this is a fun three-hour journey for you. You will undoubtedly feel like a master duelist and a true swashbuckler as you swing off ropes to surprise foes and parry enemies for that perfect riposte. If that sounds like something you would be into, give it a shot. However, again, be warned, the main story is four chapters long and, at best, around three hours if you’re not that great at the game like I am.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Sekiro but want something more cheery and less brutal, this is it. It gets a bit silly by the end when they throw a bunch of enemies at you instead of making single encounters more difficult. Overall a well made game that can be completed in only a few hours which is good as it doesn't overstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: The storyline is short but enjoyable throughout.  The combat and banter are all great fun, and the vibe is overall quite charming.  Overall, this is certainly a hidden gem.I'm writing this review mainly just to give the game some love.  Don't let my hours decieve you, I intend to keep playing.  There are some challenges I can pursue in replaying the story, and also arena mode is a lot of fun because the combat and dynamic banter is so enjoyable.Edit: Also I should add that it seems a lot of the negative reviews just don't understand the combat and thus have a bad experience. _childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game with enjoyable combat and nice visuals although a bit too short and not that much variety, also its a shame the cutscenes are just still shots and there's no mouth animations in the game so that's a bit weird, voice acting isn't too bad though and there is achievements and secrets and other little optional things you can do if you want to get more out of the game. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite nice, made with love, very very interesting graphical stuff where things far away don't blur but rather fade into watercolor. I do hope to see more content to come as it is on the shorter side.And the comparisons to Sekiro are very tenuous... You can see the surface level similarities, but En Garde's combat is just much *flatter*, less depthful, and it never pulls you into a flow state like Sekiro can
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is the main offering of this little game, and they nailed it. You'll feel just like you've stepped into a lighthearted rendition of the Three Musketeers: it embodies all the gusto and comic relief of an Errol Flynn film, dialed up to 11. The swordplay encourages lightning-fast reflexes and thinking on your feet, because you will almost always be outnumbered, and the enemy does not play fair. This forces you to see every item or piece of furniture as a potential distraction or weapon. The devs struck the perfect balance between challenging and fun: the game makes you feel like a boss, yet always keeps you on your toes.The "campaign" is regrettably short, but the arena mode provides challenging replayability where it counts. This is not the kind of game I find the urge to sink large sessions into, but it excels in quick, bite-sized bits of swashbuckling fun.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! has some things in spades and other things swirling the toilet, but the experience is overall good enough for me to recommend it.  The combat is quite fluid and well-conceived.  Despite having very few actual moves and zero progression (through leveling or equipment improvements), it has a very interactable environment which provides the player with a whole host of options for improving gameplay through your own ingenuity.  The game also has a ton of style and charm with its setting and voice acting.However, there are some small and large negatives.  On the small side, the game is rather short--about 5-6 hours.  This is probably flirting nearer to the edge for gameplay time to dollars being too low for some people, but I think it's still priced alright.  I also do think the lack of some kind of progressing unlock/level system/equipment upgrades would even further help flesh out combat and provide players the ability to craft their own unique style.  It's pretty apparent by the end of the main game too, when the Arena mode has modifiers you can apply yet the main game doesn't have anything.  The main game is playable without it, but I definitely felt it lacking.The plot is pretty trash, maybe even sometimes a touch idiotic.  It felt infused with ideologies at every turn through regularly terribly dumb writing.  I get it:  rich guy bad, and you want to feel like Robin Hood.  If the story had just stuck with that and dropped the pseudo-economic buffoonery, the shoe-horned romance, and 'men are all dumb' undertones, it would at least get a pass.  It's enough that I won't be returning to the main game, and plan on just sticking to arena mode until I beat that.Keep trying developers.  Keep improving.  Keep moving forward.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly silly sword-fighting adventure starring Adalia, the sapphic swashbuckler who does whatever she can to help the people of her home under the oppressive rule of the Count-Duke. Featuring tons of banter, relevant commentary, big personalities, and a heroic tale,  is a game with a whole lot of heart! It's got plenty of action and exploration with a compact yet immersive story. Great for gamers who enjoy putting some extra thought into their actions. The game demands resourcefulness.This review is split into sections and further organized under each section. The gameplay is mostly focused on unique combat maneuvers and level traversal. You continuously learn new tricks and encounter new items to interact with all throughout the game. The game keeps an updated codex of all the information you learn so you can easily refer back to that for a refresher if needed. It is all about beating your opponents with style and, frankly, embarrassment—like tossing a bucket onto their head so they can't see and then kicking them down the stairs to clamber into a weapon rack which falls on them, cartoony sound effects and all. Much fun. You learn to use the environment to your advantage, and with enough style, you will fill up your panache meter which allows you to perform special moves. There are a total of 3 special moves. A full meter = 2 moves. On easy mode, the meter is already half full at the start of each level section, allowing you to already use 1 move. You will encounter several enemy types, each with unique attack & defense styles you must learn play around. It becomes a tough challenging when everyone is charging you at once. Split them up! As a former completionist, I had a hard time resisting the urge to search every nook and cranny. The level designs are quite tight, so it was never overwhelming, but they packed enough content into those spaces that even when I was actively hunting for secrets, I still missed a lot. I finished the game and want to go back to find everything I missed and complete the challenges I failed. And get more of the Steam achievements. I played on the normal setting until the fight with the Count-Duke while he . After dying an unreasonable amount of times in that fight, I had to turn down the difficulty. Good news: Easy mode reveals the secrets and challenges you need to find in the game menu so you don't have to find them by chance or guess what they will be! Otherwise, they appear as a "?" in the menu until you unlock them. I played on keyboard and mouse. I'm a devout ESDF user rather than WASD, so I basically did a fully custom keybinding. I can't comment on the default controls. However, the ability to customize your keybinds is a win. The game opens up with a screen saying it plays better on a game pad, but I do not have one of those. It did get a bit clunky at times with aiming or dodging in the right direction or kicking crates where I intended to kick them. But I had fun! Valiant spirit and kind heart. She fights for what is right and feels protective over her town. A protagonist should usually have the best voice acting out of an entire cast, and Adalia certainly does! Her voice and delivery are believable and appropriate. Some of the quips can be a little cheesy, but I think that is an intentional part of her personality. As brave as Adalia is, she is also portrayed as lighthearted, silly, and even bashful. Also a very believable voice performance, and I only wish we got to enjoy more of her! She has her own agenda and may not align with Adalia all the time, but it's clear she has excellent rapport with her. Zaida is a confident, cunning lady who knows how to get her way while also knowing when to concede. I love when she says "princesa." Okay, I just love Zaida lol.Despite not having much backstory known by the player between Adalia and Zaida, I felt their...let's say "history" is clear enough for now. I would LOVE to know more about them, maybe through a prequel or sequel—or some other form of media that explores their obviously more-than-platonic relationship further. This man is so over the top you may just love to hate him. His voice acting is  exaggerated to a comical degree. He's the big-bad villain with a penchant for excess (in tax collection, lawmaking, etc.), so of course he should be spoken like a raging temper tantrum! Quite dramatic as well! For someone who puts on a different outfit and expects his own sister to not recognize him (multiple times, even after it's clear she knows it's him), I'd say his silly act of drama is quite appropriate! That and his habit towards reckless actions.Four episodes in total, the first being more of a tutorial. Each episode felt like a self-contained story within the  universe over a period of time with gaps between each episode, all distinct yet separate points in the story working towards the final mission of . In other words, the start of a new episode was not inherently picking up where we last left off—but maybe with some breaks in between, if that makes sense. I have no way of knowing if this was intentional, but I do know that it didn't hinder my enjoyment of the game at all. I had a blast going through each episode's story and satisfying ending. Even though they may not be directly linked in a typical linear way, they absolutely  linked chronologically. You could probably play each episode independently and still get the gist of the story, but you  all episodes (in order!) to get the full picture of the worldbuilding and characters as you build up to the finale. Flashy and colorful, just like the cast of characters and their personalities. Adjustable settings to suit your needs. I played with the graphics pretty high, but I didn't know what settings were optimal for my setup, so any issues were likely my own fault. Overall, I found the graphics to be quite beautiful, and I was able to run the game rather smoothly. Impressive. The game uses a lot of vertical space, sometimes leading you to end up in a high-up place later in a level that you never noticed was there in an earlier part. The map designers included lots of vantage points for you to either scope out an area in advance or look back on where you came from. I felt amazed almost every time. "Oh, that's where I was at the start! I didn't even see this area up here before!" I wish we had fully animated cutscenes. The characters may change position here and there to better convey what they are saying, but I found it odd to watch characters speak without moving their mouths. There are a few scores throughout the game, but the main theme is most memorable. It is very catchy, has an upbeat tempo, and feels rather heroic in tone. It perfectly captures the setting and energy of the game as well as Adalia herself. Right at the start, you may notice the classic "clack" of castanets when you hover over menu items. It is very pleasing and cleverly blends in with the music. While exploring levels, the environmental sounds fill each map so that they feel a bit more alive. Combat is where the sound design goes off the rails—in the best way possible! Boinks and yoinks, clatters and clambers, just like the classic cartoons of days past. I had a joyous time humiliating the guards and the Count-Duke over and over again, and I credit the sound effects for making it all the more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Very creative and fun game, worth the full price for the experience.It relates to a category of "beat them all" with a twist: you are supposed to split the hords of ennemy with elements of the decor (much like how you would face multiple people in real life). Funny thing is you can that in tons of way : kicking barrels or boxes to knock them down, throwing buckets to blind them, exploding bombs to stun them, burning them with lamps, ...But it's just the appetizer, the main dish being the 1 on 1 fight. Adalia (the hero) moves smoothly and fences her way through her duels. She can either dodge or parry, depending on the receiving attack.The game puts us in all the situations it could think of and when it's running out of ideas, it just stops without trying to drag (which is in itself a reason to buy it).All that is served in a humorous story with memorable characters and funny situations.However, it's not all perfect: the target system can be imprecise in the middle of the fight and I have had several (3-4) crashes while having a current-gen computer, fortunately not in the middle of an important fight.This game is truely for anyone and an experience to play, perfect pick for a week-end :-)
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Just an all-around great, fun game. Combat has plenty of depth and varying venues of approach, yet never feels mentally overwhelming, stifling, or clunky. The attention to detail in the way the AI behaves and speaks makes the setting feel more alive. The whole game has a pleasant, somewhat "campy" vibe to it all the way through, despite looking Dark Souls inspired to the outside observer.The only downside is the short length of the story mode for its price, but at least there's a basic, mini-roguelite "Arena mode" that unlocks after finishing it, which could easily keep the average player busy for several hours more. Even still, the story itself is worth replaying on different difficulties and for specific challenges difficult to achieve on a first playthrough. It's been a long, long time since I played a game that felt this .
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is a fun game that puts the emphasis on swordplayThe gameplay is very interesting in the sense that it follows dueling mechanics while also adding elements in the environments that can be used to defeat the enemies. Furthermore, the different enemy types demand each different tactics from the player to effectively defeat them. The gameplay that is stimulated by this game can be enjoyable to those who wish to fight with sword mechanics, to defeat enemies with style or to achieve perfect victories.The story is greatly inspired by swashbuckler classics such as Puss in Boots, the Three Musketeers or Zorro. In this case we have a charming female sword fighter who embodies the cliches of swashbuckler heroes. Those cliches are not a negative thing since there are clearly Romantic notions behind the plot of En Garde!, which I quite enjoy. The only negative thing I have to say about this game is that the story mode is rather short with a duration of 2-3 hours. Nonetheless, this is quite natural for such a fast-paced game where the most important values are speed and perfection.The game is accompanied by 3D graphics that offer a great colourful environment and by great music that evokes the hispanic charm of the space and characters.I had a really fun time playing this game so I can easily recommend it, especially for sword-play fans and perfectionists.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Need more of this combat plzThe, heavily encouraged, addition of using the environment to defeat enemies (kicking barrels, pushing down the stairs, dropping chandeliers, etc.) is such a welcome addition to this typical combat system that it makes this one of the most fun to play games that I have played in a long while. The only real issue with this game that it is pretty short campaign and only rouge-like arena mode attached to it. Not painfully short, and you can get some millage through the arena mode + completing challenge/secrets, but you can finish it in 3-4 hours These developers have, along with colorful graphics and corny-fun dialog, a really good foundation to build something really good
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A very charming, Spanish themed fencing Sekiro-like. The visuals and soundtrack fit the setting very well, and the enemy banter is actually quite funny. The mechanics are there for good 1v1 combat but when it comes to fighting larger groups the difficulty was a bit much for me, as by default the enemies regenerate their stamina/posture if you don't keep attacking them which makes fights really tedious; a lot of it devolves into kiting and meticulously picking enemies off. I can respect the creator's vision but thankfully they added in an accessibility setting that turns this off, as I don't think I would have enjoyed this game otherwise. The length of the main story was perfect, and if you want more there is an arena mode.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Silly fun short game, with a great fighting mechanic, a game where you are Zorro a like across bright fun maps with amusing dialogue. The Count-Duke being a camp villian with some amusing lines. Self aware but not too much so. Fun interested where these developers go next as short and could be fleshed out more. Combat loses some of its fun towards the end with all the enemies special attacks and enviroment requirements.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I will never get over how much I love this game(apart from not being able to kick people when swinging on ropes). So much fun to play(even when you can't kick characters while swinging on ropes), charming characters(who can't kick characters while swinging on ropes), laugh out loud moments both in the writing and naturally occurring in game-play(Unfortunately none of which are kicking a guard while swinging on a rope). I really hope they do a sequel, as I would love to see them try a more complex plot with same tone and develop the characters further, along with developing the combat and platforming they have created (Not sure how, probably something to do with ropes, swinging and kicking, yeah that sounds good)In conclusion, this game is worth a look at the minimum, I feel this game will show you if you're gonna love it or hate within the first hour or so. If you are willing and able to buy a game, this is a great choice as you'll either find a fun, bite size adventure to enjoy or a realise this game is not for you within time for a refund (Note; not being able to kick people while swinging on ropes is a reasonable motivation to refund, although if that's annoying you, you'll probably love the game so much you'll play it past the refund deadline)
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good BUT BE AWARE if you intend to play it going through the campain once and never play it again you'll probably find the game very short and overpriced. I would say that in terms of content En Garde is kinda like SIFU meaning the campaign will be short but most of the fun comes from mastering the mechanics of the game and having fun doing spectacular combat and the game does that really well and truly captures that Zoro/puss in boot feeling.     The arts are really pretty with vibrant colors, the distant objects appearing like in a painting is smart and beautiful, and still it's never difficult to spot the interactive elements during fights. The story is lighthearted, funny and yet engaging. The biggest flaw of this game will be that the story will be filled with rythm breaking platforms part that are quite uninteresting. There is an Arena mode to hone your skills with a bunch of modifiers to give yourself a challenge or just have fun or both. Also, worth mentionning the OST is really cool. Overall great game that does what it wants to do really well and that's it, which coming from a small indie dev team, we can't ask or expect more than that. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde is intensely charming and fun.  The game consistently managed to expand on the mechanics and keep things interesting. The level design was just as good and went a long way in helping things seem fresh throughout. The art and writing which (I think) aim to emulate a Saturday morning cartoon are so charming and well done. The only real issue is the game is kind of lacking in polish. I wouldn't say it's buggy, but I did encounter some bugs during my time with the game. One especially annoying one was when the music would just go mute for no reason, which sucks cause the music rules and is integral to the game's experience imo. Overall though, the game is short, sweet, and great.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of the most fun games I've played this year. Lighthearted and fun with an engaging combat system. The game is pretty short if you don't do any challenges/secrets; I finished it in 3.6 hours. The final level got a little tedious because of the amount of enemies with janky hitboxes and faster than flash speeds, but it doesn't last very long, so all good.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game. Fantastic combat that feels fluid and fun and utilizes the space and environment well. Absolutely gorgeous art style, there were multiple times that I just stopped to take in the scenery. Fun characters and dialogue. That said, it is a very short game and the last chapter leaves a lot to be desired. It doesn't utilize the environments as well as earlier chapters, reuses bosses from chapters you've played within the last hour, and the final encounter is kind of a crap shoot of the devs throwing everything at you at once with very little nuance. I enjoyed it a lot overall, but I would recommend buying it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun short game with a simple and comedic story, gameplay feels incredibly smooth and well polished with pretty much everything in the environment being interactable to give you an advantage over large groups of enemies. my only two complaints are i wish the campaign was longer and maybe give the enemies more combo strings. Im really excited to see any new content the devs are cooking up.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but really fun adventure with a great soundtrack, colorful environments and excellent fencing mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: Such a nice game and a good challenge. I enjoyed it on my journey to 100% it. Fun gameplay, good story, amazing soundtrack and surprisingly good voice acting!The game gave me some Kena: Bridge of Spirits vibes, though it has a totally different taste and touch. _childDocuments_.review: En Garde! has the soul of a classic and timeless linear adventure, reminiscent of Spyro the Dragon or something else of that ilk, and the brevity of modest indie budgeting. Gameplay mechanics are simple and elegant, and you can assuredly have them down within a span of time between minutes and a couple of hours. The gameplay itself is genuinely fun; the story itself is comprised of 4 short episodes, each one upping the difficulty via enemy types introduced and which ones are surrounding you. The characters, though all are limited in their dialogue and appearance, are all rather endearing with their witty, innocent banters and honest goals. Music and art style of the game work in merry harmony to deliver an uplifting and swashbuckling-primed atmosphere.The adventure is a brief one - it is no exaggeration to say you will finish the story in 3-4 hours. Doubtlessly faster if it is all intuitive to you. To account for this there is an arena mode that you unlock by progressing through the story, and this may well serve you to renew your interest in playing as it is a varied sort of game mode with multiple levels of difficulty that promises to test your ability to adapt, endure, and stay on the move.At the time of writing this, I've bested the story on its hardest difficulty and conquered the arena at its hardest difficulty. All in all, this was the fruit borne of roughly 6 1/2 hours of playtime. I enjoyed every moment of it and am likely to dabble in the arena from time to time as the game is mechanically fun.I recommend the game - I've spent far more money on momentary pleasures that were not half so charming and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't enjoy En Garde! While it's a beautifully crafted experience, it's also frustrating, and this overcame my excitement.It started nicely, the characters are funny, and the gameplay is enjoyable with light platforming and fast-focused combat. There are some smart ideas to make it more interesting, with the addition of new enemies adding their own spice to the game.However, the experience falls down at the midpoint of the game with the introduction of a mechanic that will follow you until the end. Suddenly, you need to do exactly what the game wants you to do because the enemies have set patterns that you need to dodge and parry before you can attack and decrease their poise. If you let them go for too long, they will reset it. You end up in a whole different gameplay experience, and it's massively frustrating; beating it isn't especially rewarding as you just want for it to end.And if that wasn't enough, the game adds another layer where these enemies can protect each other, and you have to isolate them to beat them. That makes the last chapter a game of run, dodge, pick an object, throw it, attack, and repeat. So the biggest game's selling point, the combat, becomes an experience that isn't enjoyable unless you're 100% focused and follow the inputs given by the game.On top of it, playing on the Steam Deck, the performance is all over the place; there's frequent frame drops, and the game struggles to keep a steady 45 fps on Medium settings. The camera is stiff and can be really annoying to move when you're circled by enemies. The platforming is okay, but the camera is not enjoyable, mostly in the last chapter. I would recommend this game if you can overcome these issues; it's well crafted, well acted, and the universe is engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game in a deal with Sifu and let ME tell you that this game is more polished and mechanically sound than a large number of high end/AAA titles and runs amazingly. IDK how long the game is so far but even if its only a few chapters/hours this game is an absolute BLAST!!! An easy game to jump into, not too technical and ( in my opinion ) has better fighting and parrying than all of the arkham games. The reason why i say this is because arkham enemies have a timer while these enemies in En Garde! seem to have more of a random time frame of attack and can also all attack at once. ALSO the game has responsive controls you can parry and dodge in an instant while other games limit you to one action at a time which feels less intuitive as you ( the player ) can most likely do more than one action in a few seconds time. In conclusion i really hope to possibly see a new and improved En Garde! 2 because so far I'm having a great time and I hope this review reaches the people who debate on whether to get it, $20 dollars seems fine at the moment but ON SALE its definitely a MUST BUY for a more casual tech fighting game comparable to Sifu and Sekiro.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I won't be spoiling anything here beyond very vague mentions that are along the lines of "This is a game that involves fighting npcs"I'm only two missions in, and I gotta say this game is just beautiful. The combat is amazing, with every fight essentially being a pseudo sandbox puzzle where you are free to take on enemies in any method you wish. The dialogue is just mwah mwah, it is funny, witty, goofy, and overall just fun. There wasn't a moment in the game where I wasn't smiling, and at the minimum, each remark got a sharp exhale, with a special few so far having prompted real, legitimate laughter which is rare for game dialogue to manage, especially so often.The performance is fantastic, I've tried the game both on my laptop (with a mobile 2060), which ran highest settings 1080p with no stutters. And my workstation pc with a 4090. Obviously the 4090 had no issues but I expected to have to downgrade the settings for the laptop at least somewhat, even if it is at 1080p. For how good the environments look they've done an amazing job optimising it.The animations are superb, nothing felt like it was animated just to get a task done. The character acting carries through, the attacks are sharp and impactful, they are full of life.The voice acting is similarly great. I can just hear how much fun the voice actors/actresses are having with their lines.Overall, just an absolutely amazing game, even only as far in as I am right now. I'll be buying a Steam Deck in the next couple months and this is going right onto it as something to play again and again.

_childDocuments_.review: Great little slapstick action game!Combat is fun, flashy, and has a few great ideas sprinkled in. For example, skilled enemies have a special posture bar that fully refills if you mess up or run away. This means you have to play clean and beat them resoundingly, which is very satisfying and evokes the swashbuckling vibe.The writing is whimsical, and although not every joke landed, nothing made me groan so I'll consider it a success.The main sticking point would be the play time. I finished the story in about 4 hours on Medium difficulty, which I feel OK about but I got the game in a 60% off sale. I might have been less pleased if I'd paid full price. As with any character action game you're supposed to replay it for secrets/high scores/higher difficulties etc. There is an arena mode which helps with this. I appreciate that the devs kept padding in the campaign to a minimum. I would call it short but sweet.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a fun experience. The artstyle looks amazing and the story, what little there was, was good enough for an episodic adventure, like this was. Combat was really fun. The basics were solid and the numerous ways you could stun/surprise your enemies were fun to use. The only issue with combat, in my eyes at least, was that it got a bit tedious when a lot of enemies were in the same area. This was mostly seen in two boss fights, that threw tons of enemies at you  and separating them took a bit of running around the arena and at times some luck.The weakest part of this game was exploration/parkour. Although controlling the character during fights felt fluid enough thanks to the dodge ability, movement felt slightly rough when having to explore/move to new areas. This was mainly due to the characters movement midair feeling awkward. But, as this was a linear episodic story, there was not a lot of this and so this is a minor issue.

_childDocuments_.review: A friend bought this for me to play and we had a blast playing through the first few chapters before calling it a day. I know that 'En Garde' may not be for everyone but its a silly indie swashbuckler game at it's core. Among the voice-acting, story, and music, everything was so charming I can't pick a favorite part!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: "Good stance!How dare you mock...wait, was that a compliment?"En Garde is as many describe it like the Zorro movies. A quick jab in both using a sword and insulting the enemies.The game has 4 chapters of story, which isn't much. However you may end up repeating them several times if you want to hunt the achievements. The overall style of the game is dueling the enemies. What is off on this part is that duels are one on one, but the enemies won't allow this. In fact if you end up facing several enemies, they are much more aggressive compared to when split up. This is where the swashbuckling part come in, where you use the environment to separate enemies. Throw buckets, mugs, lanterns, cut down chandeliers and kick away to make things easier for you. You'll need to stay on your toes as enemies attacking will often mix attacks that require parrying or dodging. All while both sides do various chit chat insulting each other in a gimmick way.Despite the campaign is pretty short, then you can challenge yourself in the Arena mode. Here you will have random modifiers active both for enemies and yourself.Short, but fun game :)
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Though short, En Garde is a fun and fairly challenging melee combat game with a lot of heart and humour. Combat encounters rarely go the same way twice thanks to the variety of abilities and environmental opportunities you have at your disposal. The arena mode also adds on some value for those who want to experiment in different combat scenarios.A fantastic effort from the studio's first game!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It was half price and i thought why not. Completed it on medium pretty quickly but it is definately challenging enough. A game for thinking quick on your feet for sure. _childDocuments_.review: I'd love to recommend this game but it's just too repetitive. I couldn't even make it past the first chapter before getting bored. You fight the same two enemies over and over again, and combat boils down to "block with sword or kick an enemy into a thing, rinse and repeat, but sometimes you get new things to kick them into!"As weird as it sounds, the game doesn't take itself seriously enough. It leans too hard into "this is all very silly" and it feels like the characters are too aware that they're just characters to really feel all that compelling.Maybe I would have enjoyed later chapters more, but at the same time the game is supposedly maybe 4 hours long at most. _childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is basically a fencing version of Sifu with simpler mechanics that takes place in Spain during 16th-17th century and also has a much lighter tone reminiscent of early 90s cartoons. The game is fairly short (I think I completed 3/4 of the game) but that is actually a good thing unless you like the mindless filler missions of Ubisoft games. Since the main mechanic is fencing and light platforming having a shorter game actually is better since it ensures that the game does not overstay its welcome. As mentioned, the variety in the gameplay is somewhat limited but it does what it intends to do really well. The art style and attention to detail in En Garde! are truly amazing.  Characters have animations for falling down the stairs, a lot of the swashbuckling movies' classic moves are beautifully implemented, and environments also look great and fairly detailed with paintings that are era-appropriate and also fit with the game's art style. Another evidence of attention to detail in this game is that characters you have beaten say really funny things when you are nearby; even more impressively, I rarely heard them say the same thing twice so developers must have recorded hundreds of lines of dialogue just for this feature. I noticed this while reading the reviews for this game but the main villain of the game (Count-Duke) is a real person from Spain's history and makes the story even more amusing.  Overall, En garde! is a brief and entertaining fencing game that does not overstay its welcome. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was made for . _childDocuments_.review: Charming and cute game with solid gameplay. They did absolutely nail the feeling of nostalgia that so many games try and fail to achieve. The AI could be better but thats more a nitpick since its usually totally fine. Just in an ideal world it could be amazing but they struck a good balance (mostly). The devs should feel proud. _childDocuments_.review: Art style is very nice, dialogue is very cheesy in a good way.
