_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: OK, Overall it's a reccemend but I have a few gripes.First the good: - Colorful, high energy, relatively fun game-play. - Decent dialog mostly, and well voice acted. - cute premise and story. - Straightforward, fair game-play...mostly.The bad: - If you sword fight in real life (I do) or expect the game to reflect real blade / fight interactions, you will be led into taking damage all the time. You play by the games fight rules, which play out a bit like a continuous, unreliable, poorly telegraphed (at times) Quick Time Event. - It is REALLY obvious that a DEI leaning group of some kind made some changes to the characters and story late in the game, because some of the old lines and art are still in the game and don't like up with other things.  Some dialog tries to play on tropes they took out or 'subverted' and no longer works at all because of it. You can tell it was written by a good, clever writer, and then some idiot, no-talent hack came in an DEI'd all over it and ruined it. The changes stand out against the canvas they were pained on like a rainbow colored turd on a Bierstadt painting.TLDR - If you fight IRL you will have to unlearn timing and tactics, but it's still a fun little game.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: 4/12 (Dropped)Game is neat on the first playthrough and its woke, but the scripted encounters become such a drag when you're retreading the same four levels multiple teams each to mop up some missing collectibles, especially when there's nothing to indicate where in the level you might be missing them. There's no checkpoint select which is depserately needed when there's missable items and each level can take 30 minutes to an hour. I tried to do it without a guide and just got burnt out to the point I don't even want to attempt it with a guide. The combat is fun but gets stale fairly quickly once you realize you can option select roll and parry for most types of attacks and the enemy variation isn't really there to be engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: offers an authentic experience of the good old swashbuckling comedies and brings fresh air to a setting which didn't receive much attention during the last years.Each of the four adventure episodes is a gem of storytelling and game design done by a small yet talented developer studio. The arena mode provides a lot of the else much needed replayability by setting up various more or less randomly created combat scenarios.The gameplay feels smooth (apart from very few pathing issues) and doesn't need much to get used to. For me as a melee game enjoyer the combat system could be deeper, but together with the other gameplay elements it is enough for creating a well-rounded experience of both funny and challenging moments. The bugs i experienced were in such little extend that they didn't impact the experience in any significant way. looks visually appealing and invites you to stop by to enjoy the scenery. I really like the art style and think it adds a lot to the overall enjoyment. Warm, bright colours and lovely designs create a romantic atmosphere of the early 17th century Spain. The background and objects in the distance are displayed in the style of watercolor until you get close and they become the new location of interest - an awesome trick to save GPU and make the game look nice at the same time.The whole audio part is 10/10. The spirit of the swashbuckler setting has been caught on point with the game soundtrack. It creates an authentic feeling of hispanic rhythm and has both epic combat and relaxing background tracks in it. In fact i regularly listen to it in my freetime. Go and buy it now, then return to reading this review with the track  in the background! Apart from that the voice acting has been done with much passion and the  will invigorate the fights with a wide range of random voicelines which actually fit to what is happening. The humor itself feels natural and genuiley makes you smile.With all of that  leaves you with a somewhat strange feeling, because all of what you encountered was of such a quality that you think it would be suitable for a much bigger scaled game. In short: The quality of the game doesn't match the time you actually spend playing it. The arena mode is great, but sadly it doesn't let you change any parameters of the scenarios except the difficulty. There could have been so much more for this game; even for a potential multiplayer mode  already has a good fundament and wouldn't need that big of an overhaul.If i could wish for anything and should name three things i want the most for , it would be ...I know that two out of these three points sound ridiculous, but come on, i really want an autograph of El Vigilante! I would pay a lot! Honestly the best videogame character i had the honor to meet since a very long time ...Lastly i want to mention that i hope the success of  will encourage other developers to create more games around the swashbuckler action of the 16th and 17th century. This has to be one of the most underrated settings i can think of. Thank you Fireplace Games for your gorgeous creation! :)
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a wonderful art style, a really fun combat system that is both ridiculous and challenging, and bags and bags of flair and charisma. Short, but sweet, if you grew up watching any brand of swashbuckling movie, as I did, you owe it to yourself to pick this up in a sale and blast through it!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely game with a lovely artstyle, soundtrack and sense of humor.My go-to Zorro gaming experience if you ask me: the gameplay is simple to grasp, yet not that easy to maintain or master, which is an absolute positive in my book as looking at gameplay footages alone you might assume that it gets old fast. It doesn't. Combined with everything from the first sentence it presents an amazing experience. If you believe that you got the jist of it and let your garde (:D) down, you'll suffer significantly, I promise you. Somehow it both is and isn't as simple to handle as it looks from the first glance. Pacing is extremely good too, the game takes the effort to build itself up reasonably slowly so you have the time to understand it's mechanics and doesn't waste it a minute longer than necessary. It's got an almost perfect length to it, you could tell that the devs didn't want to unnecessarily drag it out just for the heck of it, instead they just closed it the minute they ran out of ideas. Even so the game's 3 boss battles each get their own semi-recycled "harder" variants through the second half of the story which is fine, because they're all at least somewhat if not significantly more challenging than their earlier versions, resulting in unique experiences on their own.I personally didn't bother with the arena mode tbh, I prefer my gameplay integrated into the vanilla gaming experience itself, but I understand the need for it to be available for those who want to experience it in it's purest form without narrative pacing holding it back and all. If you want the gameplay after the fact and nothing else, then it's your place to visit.All in all, I loved this one, definitely recommended! :)
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why, but this game out of all the other modern 3D games really takes me back to my childhood. Something about it just really reminds me of the 3D platformers I used to play as kid.It's really fun using the environment to take out enemies and I love how over the top all the dialog is. The game has a clear vision on what it wants to be and I feel it executed that idea really well, maybe not the longest game but with the amount of polish the game has, I feel the price is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game had an absolute blast. The main story content isn't super long only ~5 - 7 hours I would say. The story although short has a wonderful cast of characters and made me smile.All and all despite its short length I would highly recommend En Garde.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game perfeclty captures the swashbuckling fantasy we all deep down crave so much.The fighting mechanics feel great with a controller in hands and work almost flawlessly, leading to an experience that gets better as you master all the skills offered by the game.The writing is a classic evil count against heroic vigilante type of story and doesn't pretend to be anything more than a reason for the action. However, the delivery of the lines is both incredibly well written and voice acted !Presentation wise, the game looks very good in terms of artistic direction : colour palets are fantastic and the aquarel look to the far away landscapes is amazingly done. The soundtrack is so great I just bought it after completing the game. Definitely buy it if you need inspiration for your swashbuckling stories during tabletop roleplaying sessions.The only downsight to this game is it's length : it is way too short ! The main story is finished under 5 hours or so, and the Arena mode is entertaining for a while as a simple Rogue Light type of game, but the perks unfortunately do not allow enough novelty and fresh air to the game mode for it to last for too long. Add to that a few secrets and collectibles to the main story and a achievement hunt (which I typically never do, and only shows how much I crave playing this game) and you have a ~20h complete experience. As I said, it's too short but I will always take a focused and unique experience over a 100h hours long watered down open world type of deal. Let us hope that En Garde will serve as a nice tumbler for the developers to create a longer and deeper experience for their futur game !Overall, it was my favorite playthrough of this summer and I highly encourage people to try it if they are into swashbuckling stuff (and who isn't ?).
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely enjoyable and creative and I highly recommend it.The story felt a bit disjointed at times but it was still enjoyable and full of humor.The gameplay is the prime hook of this game: battles are intense and exciting and take place in interactable arenas that add another layer of strategy to battles.I also enjoyed the platforming segments sprinkled between battles, they're a nice change of pace and very enjoyable.There aren't many secrets to find, from time to time you'll find items you're able to press a button and a prompt will pop up saying something usually sarcastic about the item you've interacted with, it's nice but tangible secrets would have been better in my opinion.In short, I've really enjoyed my time with En Garde! and I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Also fair price.It's a colorful, funny and lighthearted swashbuckler game where not only the combat, but also the comedy is central. You attack enemies with your sword, but as the game progresses you learn more mechanics to deal with enemies. You have to use every trick and tactic available to deal with large groups of enemies.Both the combat and the comedy complement each other, since there are a lot of environmental objects to interact with, resulting in funny reactions, animations and sounds.The sound design is very well done. From enemy reaction to the overal environment and music, everything works well.It took me under 4 hours to complete the story, but during the episodes there are challenges that you can complete, which is great to replay the episodes to complete challenges that you missed the first time.  The parkouring, while not difficult, is a nice change of pace for a minute in between the combat sections.Overall a great game with replayability. Well worth the asking price and I'm curious to see what the developers do next with this concept.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Will: You didn't beat me. You ignored the rules of engagement. In a fair fight, I'd kill you. Jack: That's not much incentive for me to fight fair, then, is it?-Pirates of the Caribbean (2003)I think alot of people will love this game. It's a three musketeers type fighting game with the color commentary to match. The story and animation are light hearted and endearing. The music is a nice touch too!It's a swordfighting game, but the fighting is different. There is a heavy emphasis on swashbuckling and parkour over hand-to-hand combat. You will be significantly out numbered in combat as the game progresses and parrying, dodging, running away, escaping to higher ground, surprising enemies, and throwing random objects, are just as important to staying in the fight-if not more- than just striking with your sword. In other words, in the Pirates of the Carribean scene when Will Turner and Jack Sparrow first spar, you'll be fighting like Jack, not Will. My cons are: -The dialogue has become annoying over time-The lock on/enemy targeting system is frustrating when surrounded by a group of enemies and will get you killed  -The difficulty increase from boss to boss is a bit steep-The collectibles add nothing to the story or game playTbh, these are all little things.  There were no serious technical issues and the storyline is exactly what you'd expect from a swordfighting comedy based on movies like Pirates of the Carribean, The Three Muskateers, The Princess Bride and Don Quijote. Overall, the first couple of hours were great fun, but the game is beginning to feel a little tedious, like I'm playing just to complete it and not for fun. I'll update if anything changes.7/10 for me, but the reviews are glowing, so most players seem to really love this game. Be warned though, the game is very short.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A game with heart and love. The graphics are beautiful and the game is challenging! I played on normal and it got me sweating real hard at some bossfights. This is no game where a lot of clicking is bringing you far. It took me around three hours to finish the story. But it has side content in form of an arena mode. It was worth it on sale for me. But i would not pay more than 20 euros for it. For that there should be a bit more content.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: So I got this game on humble bundle and I can't recommend this game enough. It starts out easy enough, but gets more difficult as you go on. Requires a lot of strategy and maneuver when there's a lot of enemies and the combat is just amazing. The animations feels very satisfying and really sells the dueling setting.If I had to compare this unique game. I would say it has  the fine tuned combat of dark souls combined with the fast paced and action packed combat of sifu.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little action game that solves two major problems in the Bad Mike Tyson's Punchout environment we find ourselves in:1. You're active. Flynning means going on offense (like Sekiro) and doesnt mean you get armored thru.2. There's tons of fun cartoony swashbuckler stuff to do people in like buckets on heads, kicking people swaying on cliffs, or the satisfying chandelier drop, all of which makes adds fun rather than a bad pacing mechanic.Its also quippy as hell, again, living up to the Three Musketeer/Insult Swordfighting trope perfectly.The one real problem is, that despite its apt and breezy 4 hour playthru, the last level sans final boss is entirely recycled despite the setting just to pad.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely enjoyed this game for its exciting environment and engaging combat mechanics, which I found pretty cool (10/10 ngl tbh). However, it's worth noting that the game is relatively short, around 4 hours for all 4 episodes (the first of which I presumed was a tutorial for the most part). If a DLC is coming, I am 100% coping that.P.S. love the relationship between Zaida and Adalia :>
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A game not for me...- 2.6 hours to finish the game, really short game, 25% of the game (4° chapter of 3) is just a repeat of 75% of the rest of the game- Too pricey for what it gives you- The style and design of the game is exquisite, but you never can explore it- Rail Road, no exploration- Light-hearted narrative.- Combat is... goodish, but the perma target block in combat can be pretty annoying and... well there is an auto-aim- You never have the feel to combat different enemies, only an upgraded version of them. Their moveset is just an evolution of the first enemy... even the bosses.It's a costly game for kids, combat could be good but it's too easy and can be frustrating, enemies are just copy-pasta with some additions, and can't explore enough the cute and wholesome scenery of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game, Short and Sweet.Amazing level design and visualssolid platforming (although awkward bounce physics)The combat is mostly straightforward and rewarding.But by the end it devolves into an unfortunate dodge fest and the mechanical inconsistencies become glaring (last fight especially) Beat it on hard so maybe the enemies we're overly aggressive as a resultBut I would get clobbered after rolling and running wouldn't be enough and the enemy hit sequences would just catch you (through geometry high to low ground and vice versa as well as through pillars) But for 10 bucks it was absolutely worth it, and I love the concept and lighthearted story, if the game was more consistent and fleshed out. It would come close to a dream game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of a yes, but really no situation. The challenge ramps up pretty much from 0-100 immediately, which is mostly made worse by the fact that there's attacks you *need* to dodge, and other attacks you *need* to parry. Unlike many other games that keep swarms of enemies from attacking you all at once, you'll get surrounded and 3 or 4 of them will attack simultaneously with both attacks and you WILL get hit. Running away is a little inconsistent because she will lock on to nearby enemies and you have to keep hitting the run button. On a similar note, picking things up feels oddly clunky, and throwing them often doesn't work the way you'd expect. You pick something up to throw at an enemy you're targeting, and instead she just throws it at a wall or something. Similar thing happens frequently with kicking boxes, instead of aiming at the nearby enemy, just kicks it at nothing and gets you hit.I was hoping the full release would fix some of the combat clunkiness from the demo, but... it really didn't. This game seems like another one of those in the Stranglehold category of "cult classics" that were *almost* really good, and instead are just very short, but neat, games.I honestly wish the game was easier, this seems like something kids should enjoy with the humor, but if I were a kid the combat would make me angry and I'd stop playing it. As an adult... I might do the same. It's a shame, it's really close to being good.Oh, and of course it's LGBT, because why couldn't it not be?
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of heart. The art direction is great, with everything looking appropriately sun-drenched, and the voice acting has plenty of amusing lines. The combat is fun and makes you feel like Errol Flynn. However, it's pretty short - you could probably finish the game in under two hours if you rushed it. Still, there is a randomly-generated arena mode to mix things up.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine, but a bit disappointing. The devs have come up with a good fighting system, but the design of enemies and encounters means sword skill isn't a viable path to victory. All the emphasis needs to be on throwing projectiles and kicking barrels. If you want a game with good parry based combat you can actually indulge in, try the shadow of Mordor games. Oh, and the writing is gratingly unfunny.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game with enjoyable combat that's complex enough to give you lots of tools to work with without being too daunting to keep everything in your head, a lovely art style, and very entertaining character with humorous writing. Although the campaign is a bit short, it has multiple difficulty modes and a pure arena battle mode for replayability!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Look, this game was graphically polished but not properly balanced. The game runs but the mechanics of combat are fighting each other the whole time. The individual features work but don't work TOGETHER. Controls are very clunky, the camera is too slow in combat, and the camera is too close to you and too low to see the combat properly. Too many strong enemies are attacking in tandem, the dodge mechanic is extremely forgiving when you active it but the rolling leaves you vulnerable for attacks that should miss. The kicking animation is too long and does not point in the direction you are looking but the direction you are moving. You're expected to pick off enemies by isolating the out maneuvering but they swarm you and leave few opening to parry and dodge without being hit by an attack you didn't even see from an enemy that is out of sight. Mechanics for climbing and traversing out of combat are HORRIBLY forgiving to the point you just snap to objects that are out of reach but still in the intended path of travel. It is jarring to think you are too far from a rope and will fall only to suddenly grab hold of it and swing with no effort. The climbing and acrobatic features have training wheels on them. It isn't fun to run an obstacle course when the obstacles are just painted on the ground and offer no real challenge, so why did the programmers make it so effortless to overcome terrain obstacles but massively punishing in combat?I admit that I only played the game a little bit but from what I could see the writing was very lazy too. I am OK with some bland characters and weak humor so long as the game is fun to play. But the bad gameplay makes the bad writing pop out like the colorful world they tried to make. Despite dialog trying to convey a cheeky, nearly self aware world whose lines read like a parody of a Spanish soap opera there isn't much personality beyond it's setting. The heroine is plucky, confident, and has an edge of humor to her dialog which is good if not a little too common nowadays. But the villain is plucky and confident, the guards are either slightly cowardly or confident with an edge of humor, and El Vigilante is slightly cowardly with an edge of humor. The point is that this world and the heroine are both built with the same three characteristics and the other characters share two of those characteristics with little if anything else to add. The characters are bland and watered down in the very world they were written for.Bottom line, combat doesn't function well, obstacles are too easy, and the writing is too weak. I wanted this game to be much better than this but it wasn't. I bought this game on August 23, 2023. I hope that it is fixed by the developers after the fact but it is not fun to play as it stands.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet game. Originally a student project fleshed out into a more full game, split into 4 Episodes which took me roughly 30-50 mins each to beat.Each level has secret areas, hidden challenges and lore to uncover. With an optional wave based arena mode with randomised perks and debuffs for some extra replayability.The combat boils down into Dodging Red attacks and Parrying Blue attacks in between using hit and run tactics with the help of the environment, objects / interactables and gauge spender attacks to create openings on tougher foes. As you progress in the story, a handful of harder foes come into play where you have to learn to use objects and throwables to create 1v1 opportunities, and are punished for just spamming the basic attack and dodges.Personally what stood out to me was the visuals of the game. Beautiful and charming environments to progress through. I feel like a lot of love went into making this game, and the games length does not overstay its welcome. If you are looking for a short, well crafted game to enjoy for a day or the weekend. This is worth its price.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. the combat is responsive and smooth. The use of the environment is next level. I really felt like I had to outsmart my foes instead of beating them straight up. The soundtrack is fantastic. Every chapter the game brings in some kind of new opponent that shakes up the way you approach every fight. The only thing I have against this game is that it is over so soon. I will definitely be trying to complete every challenge. Looking forward to whatever the devs do next!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is like a shorter, easier, and less fun version of Sifu. Fun at times, but more often frustrating.  I really liked using the environment in the combat sections. It was fun to kick barrels and tables at people.There are sections of this game where you have to fight 3+ guys at the same time and if you dodge instead of parry they get all they get all their health back. That is Stupid and frustrating. Also this game is very short.I got this for $10. I would only recommend getting it if it's $2.

_childDocuments_.review: The opening is great. The second episode is ok. The third episode has been the weakest yet. Between getting lost, finding alternate paths that aren't actually paths (just bugged ledges), chandeliers that don't have ropes (I checked the whole room twice), and the hero turning into a fawning idiot even after being betrayed...it's just not as fun as I'd hoped.Hopefully it gets better, but right now I regret buying the soundtrack edition so soon.EDIT: I just finished the 4th episode, which is the last one. _childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Just so delightfully fun. The story is very silly, tapping into over-the-top swashbuckling stories of old. The sword combat has that fun "parry the hell out of your enemies" challenge that I liked about Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. If you're concerned about difficulty, there are some customization which let you tweak a few things like the time you have to successfully parry an attack. And on top of that, you not only can but should kick a table out from someone to make them fall on their face. It's a bit short, only 4 chapters, but they're expansive fun levels, and there's an arena mode on top of it where you can stab and kick to your hearts content. It's worth $20 without question.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A very cool game. Combat is fun, visuals are super stylized and soundtrack is awesome. All the enemies are engaging and diverse and there are not any gimmicky or unfair fights. Even the most annoying enemy the granny with bombs you can turn to your advantage.Only problem is that there are only 4 levels each taking about 35-40 minutes to complete. There is an endless arena mode but still something to consider. If the game is on sale it is a non-brainer purchase however at full price length is something to consider. Another thing is that some levels are better optimized than others. Nothing too serious but I did have minor stuttering on the third level.Would absolutely love to see a sequel with more levels and perhaps a different setting. Some people have suggested a pirate setting but I also think a French Revolution or Feudal Japan or Ancient China could work. As long as they keep the core combat the same and maybe add some moves and variety of animations.Overall I am very positive about this purchase
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde is a game with good visual design, an interesting premise.. and gameplay that is INCREDIBLY dull. The game is basically Sekiro-lite, where the combat is a puzzle: enemies will use attacks that have to be parried to do damage, and if they get into groups will start using attacks that have to be dodged instead, with the focus being on managing groups of enemies so they do not become a Dark Souls ganksquad. Unfortunately, due to the mechanics not always working the way they should, the game is instead a slog.Most enemies have several health bars and a stagger meter that is slowly depleted every time you land a hit, with a few mechanics (such as poise crushing via kicking objects into enemies) allowing you to land a few more. The problem is that a lot of the mechanics are meaningless: sure, you can poise crush an enemy, but that doesn't mean anything when the enemy recovers from being stunned the moment you land a hit and still isn't hittable unless they're "open" after a parry. Combat boils down to meticulously stunning every enemy but one, slowly parrying that enemy and hoping you get their poise down, and then meticulously stunning everything again. It gets very repetitive very quickly. Worse, enemies regain their poise INCREDIBLY quickly, so if you aren't pressuring them constantly, they'll just completely reverse the last several minutes of combat.There's also the problem of enemies "stacking" attacks, where one enemy uses a must-dodge attack while the other uses a must-parry, which means that you're taking damage no matter what and can sometimes be stunlocked to death that way. This game needed another several months of balance testing in the oven, and it didn't get it.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this lovely game. Charming, humorous with great gameplay and colorful environments. The overall feel of the game is very uplifting, combat is slick, you'd be surprised how greatly it works against different types of enemies. Adalia de Volador is a good solid protagonist. Voice work is nice, game has a nice, soothing charm to it. The sound is also great, from crisp environmental sounds to clinging of swords, it's good.Such games should always be encouraged, especially when developers put their love and labor in the project.Also if you have Steam Deck, all the more reason to play it!

_childDocuments_.review: I beat En Garde! in a short 3 hours and loved every minute of it. Crisp combat, beautiful environments, and hilarious dialogue. If you loved Sekiro and/or Lies of P, you'll love this combat. If you're looking to get into those games but are wary of the difficulty, En Garde! is a great place to start to learn the rhythm!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A nice short Zoro like adventure game with souls like inspired mechanics. It's silly and embraces it head on. The game play revolves around parrying, dodging attacks, and using the environment to your advantage. The environment aspect is the most aspect of this loop. The parrying and dodge windows are pretty generous as well. There's a minor inconvenience where sometimes the camera angle is not ideal, but you can quickly adjust it by moving or moving the camera.Replayability: The arena mode is pretty nice. Deepens the fights even more. It's a rogue-like mode where you select perks and go through the arenas from the main story. The best part of this package. Will at least add a few hours to your time.

_childDocuments_.review: i honestly didn't know what to expect but thankfully i saw a YouTuber that goes by the name ironpineapple and he did the demo for this game and it looked amazing. now the game is released and i can say i had a blast playing! the aesthetic and comical appeal for this game is enjoyable. the story is 4 episodes which can take up to 30 minutes to complete but they offer a lot of hidden things to find and a awesome arena mode. if you are looking for a fun game to kill some time you have come to the right place. if u want a full play through check out my channel 420BLZKN on YouTube as i complete all 4 episodes.

_childDocuments_.review: Great art style, great game play, and fun story. _childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of parry based games, this was meant for me. While it is on the easier and forgiving side with its indicators and generous parry window, it innovates more on crowd control which enhances its tone and appeal. The new enemy stamina meter compliments this new layer on managing enemies such as kicking them towards environmental hazards or other enemies to keep them away as well as weaken them to easily and safely damage them. Given its budget and scale, its linear combat arenas, light platforming and few stages makes the most sense; however, I do find it a bit short on content, variety and challenge to be a memorable experience.At its low price point, it is a justifiably short experience consisting of four chapters/episodes left me underwhelmed. What made me truly lament about this game is its lost potential specially on how much fun I had on its arena or roguelike mode. The (potentially broken) positive and negative modifiers adds a strategic and tactical depth that I feel the main mode lacks or could emulate with its comedic tone. Beyond the arena, I find no real reason to replay or learn the game at a higher difficulty despite the challenge which is one of my key metrics for an action game.As an action game, what holds this back is the zoomed in camera, unclear lock-on and messy object interactions that make the experience frustrating than rewarding. First, the camera is quite close to the character making it hard to see enemies approaching from behind. When backed to a wall or corner due to dodging or parrying, the camera goes behind a wall and obscures incoming attacks. Second, the lock-on feels so random or uncontrollable at times with clusters of enemies. It happens so many times that it breaks my immersion and flow. Third, so many objects on the ground can hinder movement both for the player and specially the enemies who get stuck. Tables in particular can cause dodges to be unintentional slides that can reset elite enemy meters. All these problems are not unique to this game, but it made combat a sloppy experience.For smaller issues, I am not a fan of the humor and tone of this game although this may be the right approach for its short experience. Even if the corridors are linear, some tangible rewards such as costumes or cosmetics could be hidden instead of small notes or references. Better indicators for the exit and interactables would be nice because it is hard to know at times.As for the , I really only have one issue which I mentioned in the demo: performance. Playing on the lowest graphical settings, I can play around a stable 45 FPS. The fight arenas are small and segregated by loading screens, so I am concerned why it is not hitting a stable 60 FPS or sometimes having hiccups. Perhaps some configuration can hit those numbers or perhaps  verification is not intended; regardless, I do suggest playing on a stronger machine for a better experience.It is still overall a good casual indie game and hoped to support it, but I hesitate to recommend this for players looking for a meaningful and rewarding challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was such a blast. As a lover of indie games, this one's unique fighting style really drew me in. It was so much fun to play. Once I got the hang of it, I couldn't help but want to master it. My only problem with this game is that it was not long enough! I did all the achievements, and I want more!!!In terms of recommendations, I would definitely recommend this game for anyone. The cost might seem a little high for a short game, but I thoroughly enjoyed it and am happy that it will forever be in my steam deck if I ever want to play through again in the future. I hope the developers make more or more like this. This was a phenomenal game, and I will definitely be buying any DLC/sequels. Fingers crossed!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This has been my most anticipated title from Steam Next Fest and it doesn't disappoint. You'd think the game would start to run out of tricks, but it keeps adding enemies to defeat with new strategies, and environmental objects to exploit to defeat them more easily. You can really get some Zorro moments out of this game if you're inspired enough.The setting feels ripped straight out of Puss in Boots, leans deep into cheesiness, and somehow all the humour lands. The dynamic dialogue between Adalia and the Count-Duke's minions feels natural, and there are so many lines that I doubt I'll get tired of hearing them.I haven't had any BS encounters that I couldn't eventually outsmart when I had enough time to plan my counterattack. This is even encouraged in the Tips & Tricks page for individual enemy classes and how fighting them in groups can be problematic. The game will give you a challenge on Medium difficulty, and you'll probably die more than once to boss fights, even if you can get through regular enemy encounters just fine up to that point.Replayability is high, because there are challenges to complete, secrets to hunt for, objects to examine and get Adalia's thoughts. And they're in easily digestible chapters, so it's not like you need to start the whole game over or backtrack across an open world to get it done. With the gameplay as good as it is, I could even see myself picking it up again on occasion to have some fun in the Arena.Loved this game from its Next Fest demo a few months back, and definitely looking forward to 100%'ing the game. Be sure to pet the chickens.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and short game. Does need some polishing when it comes to certain things but overall it's a good game.The combat system offers some very nice feedback (visual and sound) on hits and parries, is super easy to play and tough to master. It plays very similarly to Sifu so if you liked Sifu you'll probably like this game as well.The atmosphere is very light-hearted and every character is whacky and entertaining.The game looks really nice and is cleverly minimal.There are some issues with level design, the sections end simply with you opening a random door and losing the controls of your chraracter, the screen fades to black and loads the new area.Often the areas are not well connected together and the levels don't offer many interactions. Yes you can pick up stuff to throw to the enemies or kick boxes but that's it. There are loads of doors that just can't be open, jumps that could be done but bring nowhere and in general many missed opportunities for more variety in arenas.Maybe a bit too many reused assets.Rapid movements of the L stick may sometimes result in an imprecise input which becomes a problem if it happens during a fight.The lock-on target could be clearer in some instances.The character automatically grabs ledges or ropes and I think the gameplay would be a bit more interesting if you had to press a button to perform those actions.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: $20 is a lot for a 3 hour game, so I would only recommend purchasing this during a sale.En Garde! is basically Puss n' Boots the game except you're human. Although the main characters are static, I adore the written notes and enemy dialogue. The combat feels similar to Sifu, and the optimization and world design are buttery smooth. Besides length, my complaints are: 1) special attacks feel like a tacked-on mechanic, where one attack is just a better version of the other (there are 3 total); 2) difficulty is poorly implemented because individual enemies are trivial but groups of enemies turn combat into something akin to COD zombies. Overall, it's a short, solid, kid-friendly game. Give it a try if you're craving something like Sifu, but understand that you won't get much bang for your buck.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I strongly dislike this game. The easy battles are just counter and kill, often repeatedly against stronger enemies. Then the boss fights are pile ons where you run around, get hit because your roll didn't work or they attacked from off camera, and just generally feel like the game doesn't respect your attempts to play it. Then there are long, quite dull boss fights which are simply reaction memory games: red means evade, blue means parry, do that until their string is over then reply. 4/10, I wouldn't recommend.Edit: I beat the game! It was too often grindingly annoying and repetitive to be fun.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is brilliant. It's not just button mashing, you have to think tactically and use various tools. And it is also satysfying and makes you feel like you're good at sword fighting in real life. Travelsal and platforming is very smooth and fluid. Graphics are beautiful, bright colorful and models are fantastic and this game will never look old. Story, dialogue and characters are super charming. This game is perfect, but too short. I can't wait to see a sequel or another game like this from its creators. En Garde - definetely one of the best indie games ever.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game had all kinds of fun stuff to it from the colorful palette to the dialogue, but the gameplay was what killed it for me.The game's two biggest and most immediate issues are the dodge and targeting. So far I saw two attack types (grenades not included) being parryable white and unparryable orange. The parry felt quick, responsive, and reliable, but the dodge felt like I had a 50/50 shot whether or not I would actually dodge an orange attack while almost never succeeding on a white attack, and most of the time I would be assaulted with both.The targeting in this game has got to be one of the most frustrating and handycapping things I have ever seen, and this comes from someone who beat the Four Forcemen in 'Let It Die'. The lock on didn't even work in the tutorial and I could only get past it by destroying the dummies. The game boasts a LOT of resourceful environmental hazards to exploit against your enemies, and it has that in spades, but I could not use it to its fullest because auto lock. In my under 2 hours, the lock on has:1. Pulled my view away from the mob of enemies I was trying to fend off and 180 to a lone mook2. Refuse to look away from said mook  leaving me unable to properly react to what was behind me3. send my grenade to an isolated fire pit leaving the massive horde of enemies unexploded4. have me kick a box out left field in spite of the enemy being right in front of me (auto lock did NOT engage the one time I needed it)5. pull my camera away from the guard-depleted enemy and force me to hit a shield captain6. send a barrel into a cooking pot instead of the mob after meThe weird, short, unreliable dodge was NOTHING compared to the issues I have had with the targeting. The targeting alone made a game that could easily have been a short, fun little adventure into a mind numbing slog because so much of this game even though "family friendly" relies on precision. Precise timing of the parry which you can't do if your back is turned and can't see the enemy, precise timing of the dodge which at its best was questionable (this could have been because of the camera as well), precision in knowing what person your throwing a bucket at, or where to chuck a grenade. The targeting ripped of that away in my playthrough. For those that can work with the targeting or even better, get it to work, more power to them. But If I'm fighting the controls for near 2 hours can't really say I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun. If you like games like Dark Messiah you'll enjoy it. If you think DND combat but in videogame form is a cool idea play this. This game is about creatively using your environment and outsmarting a numerically superior force who in most cases are also better fighters than you. Though dont play this game like Arkham City or something. It's not built for that. This is a game about making people slip on puddles, and then kicking them off cliffs. Or throwing buckets over their head while you deal with the weaker guys. Or my personal favorite, throwing bombs into cauldrons of stew which explode, launching the cauldron into the air where it will conveniently land on someone's head knocking them out instantly. If you play this game by perfectly parrying every attack, dodging every unparriable, and whatever you probably wont have fun with this game. There are better games for that and this has nothing to do with that kind of playstyle. You can do it but you wont have fun imo.I especially like this game to occupy my mind while i'm listening to a youtube video or chilling out with friends. It is pretty funny but after 10 hours or so you've heard every joke there is to tell.  The game is very short though so I'd suggest getting it on sale. 20$ imo is pretty steep for what is essentially a 10 hour experience+ a pretty bare horde mode. If this game had DLCs or Expanded upon the story mode it'd be worth 20$ imo but in this state just wait for it to be on sale. It's currently 10$ for me which is more than reasonable for this experience imo. I say it's a 10 hour because that's how much time i've played it though I can see it only being a 4 hours game. Just keep in mind how little there is. You're in for a good time just not a long time. I would love to see a possible DLC story or expansion on the story. A sequel as well could be great so long as the story is told in a longer way. I want more gameplay. More unique locations, with different gimicks, and villains and jokes.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Lemme get something out here real quick to celebrate this accomplishment.The title is super slick. (On Deck, where it plays wonderfully, I can get a solid 40 FPS by changing the anti-aliasing to TAA.)The writing, given great breath with convincing VO, has a high  charm--on behalf of its setting, producing smiles and giggle. Zero cringe.Nicely difficult on the recommended Medium.The flamenco guitar soundtrack is as clean as it should be, and super fitting and enjoyable.--Minor gripes: the keybinding option is a little screwy, for I couldn't remap as desired; the tutorial videos don't loop; and model's mouth's don't move when speaking.--A gem.--Additional thoughts:On Deck, launch with DirectX 12--as offered on startup, or the tutorial videos won't load (displaying, instead, as white).I'd further moniker its charm as " gone Spanish."After playing the  demo, it's nice to be able to use another rapier in a video game so soon.Combat is reaction-based, but it's not nearly as demanding as .
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a game that lets me channel my inner Errol Flynn! It's not easy - the boss of Ep. 2 took me a dozen tries - but it's fast and funny, the banter never gets old, everything about it is just light-hearted and puts a smile on my face, reminding me of those pirate movies (or Robin Hood or Zorro or the often quoted Princess Bride of course) I loved so much as a child. Optically it's not very ambitious but pretty and colorful - it's fitting and performance is not an issue. The game mechanics are smooth and well taught. Simply completing it probably doesn't takes very long but it's a game I can see me coming back to just to have a good time and find the secrets. And the price is very fair. So highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is an exceptionally charming action game. It's not overly complex, and on their own none of it's individual components are of note, but as a complete package it's a wonderful experience. This is one of those games where you can tell everyone involved was passionate and enjoyed themselves during it's creation, and that elevates En Garde! above what it may have been otherwise. It's quite a short and easy game, but I believe that to be a strength.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 - Fun soulslike, with dark souls 2 type difficulty.Pros:- Great soundtrack & artstyle, perfect dialogue & voice actors.- Great concept to utilize environment objects.- The first 2 chapters are perfect.Cons:- Spammed with trash mobs, especially when within a tiny room or environment. FOV is horrible in such situations (would've been good to have a setting).- The camera speed is limited to 5 with controller (This can be edited in EnGarde/Saved/Config/Windows/Settings.ini, set Input.Sensitivity=8).- Disabling camera tracking doesn't work, as it always tracks enemies that are close.- Enemies often attack at exactly the same time, while requiring different counter attacks, which is impossible.- Limited variety of enemies, gets very repetitive by the end.Maybe the game required more chapters to figure out how to deal with spam mobs with limited resources.Looking forward to any DLCs!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game in just under 5 hours on hard with the default settings. It does just enough to be entertaining throughout and the world is really fun and pays homage to a ton of classics, and its short run time keeps things from getting frustrating while playing on harder difficulties. Unfortunately this game can be a bit of a mixed bag. The kicking mechanic can have some very, obvious auto aim towards targets can take you out of the immersion and fantasy the world creates and the final episode feels more like they're reusing bosses to save time than it does a grand finale, as you fight every single major boss in the game during the episode. If you like Sekiro, or Fallen Order you'll like this game, it does a lot to keep the fighting interesting and flashy. If you're looking for a quick, fun and funny game to play you should pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't sleep on  this. If you're worried about parrying, the game is rather forgiving and I say this as someone who is really terribly at it. There's also an easy mode that I actually started on (see terrible at parrying), but I actually found it too easy and switched it up. The game is basically Zorro without the IP in all the best ways. It's rather short, but very enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great little action game - feels like a mix of Sifu and the Arkham games, encourages more interesting playstyles over just getting the parry timing perfect, full of Spanish guitar and fun voice acting, vibrant colors, just a charming package all around.You'll win fights against huge groups of enemies in ways that feel like you're getting away with something, not just hacking through goons.The main story is short, but there's an Arena mode I'll be playing a lot of now that I "get" the combat.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely. That's really one of the better words I can use to describe it.Almost feels like a Disney-Soulslike, which sounds awful to say, but I promise that's as close to a proper review as I can get. The voice acting is charming and the story are very cheesy but fun. The music and art direction is beautifully stylized to fit with the Spanish setting. The gameplay is a little floaty with movement, but the combat feels snappy and properly rewarding/punishing when you get the hang of it (very alike to Sekiro). I've yet to find the secrets or do most of the challenges, but they're fun little extras that offer replayability if you want to go back to achieve them.A bit shorter than I anticipated, as I beat it one sitting of about 3 hours, but honestly? I prefer games with more love put into them that are shorter than bigger ones with not as much passion. Definitely get it if you're looking for something with some good charm and some great swordfighting gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is a delight.  I am historically very bad at third-person action games and En Garde! is not, alas, an exception to that rule, but the game's charm more than makes up for it.  As a life-long fan of swashbuckling, I couldn't be happier.  I am also pleased to say that the game, while very difficult, at least on the default settings, rewards both practice and thoughtful play.  I am definitely much better now, some thirteen hours in, than I was when I started.  It's a nice feeling.I haven't beaten the final boss fight yet--it's tough!--but if I had to give one piece of advice to potential new players it's that while En Garde's combat might seem reaction-based, you can get by even if your reaction time isn't the best if you're willing to learn enemy patterns and sequences.  You don't have to be fast enough to respond correctly to each individual strike as long as you can anticipate the rest of the sequence based on the first strike.  I learned that the hard way trying to clear the boss fight at the end of Chapter 3.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet, in every sense of the word--this is by far the most wholesome action game I've ever played.  The combat is fairly simple, but it feels great and can get pretty challenging when there are a lot of foes at once.  The characters are adorable and well-voiced, the henchmen are downright hilarious at times, the art is appealingly stylized... I don't know what to tell you, it's just fun.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Like Zorro before, this is all style--don't think about it too hard, or the story falls apart. Look sharp and use your rapier wit--and witty rapier--to inflict bloodless cartoon violence on the bad guys.Also like Zorro, it's all surface, and any attempt to plumb the depths reveals a great deal of frantically running around behind the scenes, setting up the next cool shot at the expense of the principles. If you can sprint->dodge-roll->sprint past the unblockable gangbang pain train, you can reach the bucket and inflict hilarity on the gormless villain while you make mince of his minions.If you can't? Well, hope you like rehearsing the same four jokes every time you hit the green room, because Adalia sure does. Get it on sale and enjoy the fun.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I waited a long time for this game and now that i have played the first level i sadly have to say that the gameplay, even on hard, is piss boring after 15-20 min. I will definitly play through the game to see if it improves, and if i will change the review, but the gameplay feels like a 0815 game from the 90s: attack, block, dodge and kick enemies into environment, fight 2 waves of enemies, exit area, jump over a wall, fight 2 waves of enemies, exit area, repeat, repeat, bossfight. i cannot bring myself to play the game atm, because i was so bored yesterday that i had to quit and play another game.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Swordplay feels great and parrying is easy enough to use regularly. More important than swordplay is crowd control by using the environment, the enemies do a good job of building off of each other and supporting each other in a way that keeps you from falling into a routine like you might in other games with similar melee combat.You can also pet the chickens and fight tyranny.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Crisp gameplay, charming environments and an excellent mood overall.En Garde! knows what it does best and strikes through the heart of it without unnecessary fuss, a commendable quality. Throwing a bucket to neutralize a pesky guard in order to kick his friend off a table before finishing off a third with aspecial move feels  and that's all one should ask from it.It  short though I do believe the extra effort that went into all the little details one can encounter during an encounter (?) pays off at the end and makes the game into quite a tightly-packed adventure. Whether that is the lively dialogue between the antagonists and Adalia, or the micro-mechanics permitted by the use of the environment, or the different enemy reactions to the aforementioned micro-mechanics, one still ends up feeling pleasantly surprised several chapters in. I'd recommend this to anyone who likes swords, hats with feathers on them, beautiful Mediterranean sights and chickens (preferably with feathers on them). Good stuff, devs!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: The measly 6 hours I put into this game have not only stuck with me for months, but have also soured me on the combat mechanics of other games. I never write reviews, but this feeling hasn't hit me since I played Half Life 2, so of course something had to be shared. Silly story with immense gameplay depth that doesn’t outstay its welcome. It’s simply satisfying, and I’d throw money at as little as a Kickstarter for the sequel. The most prominent, long-lasting memory from my experience encapsulates the essence of this game perfectly: fighting all of the main bosses at once by stunning them with chickens, tricking them into slipping on puddles of goop and falling into combustible barrels, then kicking each one of their enflamed egos to death, all while parrying attacks from the few remaining goons dumb enough to stay within reach of my bloodied sole.Now don't misinterpret the domination described above, it's not an easy game, you'll fall to a brute a few times before perfectly aligning a chain reaction of boom doom. But the moment-to-moment strategy of aligning the environment to your advantage is just as satisfying as the final explosive outcome.Wrapping this back around to my HL2 comparison, En Garde! is one of those rare games where I truly felt like the developer gave me a set of tools, then actively requested a lengthening of the limits past what could have ever been previously envisioned. Peak combat puzzle gameplay, for those of you who enjoy mentally stimulating table kicking pick this up immediately. If they release a Spanish vocal dub I’d call it perfection and replay the whole thing in a heartbeat.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It's awesome. Sounds great, plays great, looks great, artstyle is great, dialogue and characters are great. Everything is great. Sadly it's only 3 hours long to beat but you still have an arena mode to scale up from easy to hard difficulties, random runs with random modifiers.It's half sekiro half platform action/adventure game, I know it's only 3 hours long but that's a plus for me, short condensed extremely fun short game.I want to give the devs a hug
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 : Some good ideas but with too little content... The 1st hour of the game is glorious, I had a lot of fun, but the game does not bring much to renew itself apart from some little addons gameplay wise.76/100 : Metacritic+ Beautiful art+ Good comedy+ Arenas with a roguelike aspect- Very little content- Very short- Always the same 2 musics- Hard to say it doesn't worth the price because there is still something good, but I sadly can't recommend this game to anyone other than young kids.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Pet the chickens and kick guards into the river! Swing up buildings as FemZorro! Be a sword lesbian who runs headfirst into situations!....Okay, Really I have no idea if Adalia is a lesbian, but a gal can dream. The  little I've seen has been a lot of fun, I love the colorful painterly style and the camp. Oh the camp. Road to El Dorado would be proud.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It's running with the standardized attack/parry/dodge melee setup, but the emphasis on using the environment in combat and the fiendishly responsive controls alongside all the delightful banter means En Garde ends up being a fantastic swashbuckling adventure with lots of charming flair. Also note that any game with a dedicated 'kick' button is likely to have an understanding of what fun is.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the combat system it is so fluid and really brings the immersion of a swashbuckling pirate style dueling would play as in a video game. I love the comedy and humor mixed with the cartoon-ish feel. Reminded me a lot of the Puss in Boots movie. The game is short, however, i still think you can find value in it and i hope the developer expands on this even more! (updates, v2.0, DLC etc)Honestly a really fun game! If you factor out the time played solid 8/10 and the combat IMO is a 9.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid game, with a very enjoyable combat system, but also very short - to a point, where it took me 3,5 hours to beat. You will still have access to arena mode for a bit of "extra" content, but I don't think I would recommend it at full price. 12€ or less - sure, no problem.Where the game really shines, is with its combat system and how it utilizes elements in the environment as part of the interactive combat arenas. In a weird way, it reminds me a bit of what Dark Messiah of Might and Magic achieved, since the game not only makes you focus on what attacks the enemy is performing and whatever to doge or counter them, but also how to position these enemies, so they can be pushed into traps, off ledges and such. And just like with DMoMM, this is also really fun... even if significantly more restrictive. In between these arenas you will do some platforming - which works generally without problems and is very forgivable. The game's humor is also pretty fun. Even if some of the randomized jokes, repeat a bit too often. That is, if you can hear it, cause default sound mixing in the game is pretty bad and requires you to modify sound volumes quite drastically in order to have voice lines being audible and not drowned by music and sound effects. That and the standard UE4 stutter (again!) are two of my biggest issues about the game.Overall, I recommend this game, just - again - not a full price.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Very good voice acting, made it seem like I was playing the heroine in a cartoon show, decent graphics with a very very cool environmental battle system, but "En Garde!"s Story felt really lackluster and boring. Almost like it came straight out of a bad cartoon pilot. The combat was the best part and felt really smooth. The hard gamemode doesn't really make the game more interesting. On Hard Mode you just get swarmed completely instead of actually being challenged with more Shielded enemies for example. All in all a pretty short, but cute game. It won't win any awards, but it was quite hard to beat without dying, though I do think that swarming isn't a well done method of making games harder, I did personally enjoy it enough to recommend it. Get it with a discount though, 20€ is a stretch.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game, after completing the first two missions, is amazing. The combat works wonders, the movement feels fluent, and in general, feels fantastic to handle. My gripe, at least as a first look, is hordes of enemies can get a bit overwhelming, especially in the battle with the duke. You can use your environment to stagger them, but your breathing room is very limited, and on occasion, you get hit with an attack off screen my a henchman or lackey. Still, this does not bring down how much I am enjoying this game already.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Never have I ever wanted to learn Spanish so badThough it is a really short (just finished the story, I haven't tried the arena mode yet nor discover all the hidden objectf from the campaign), this game is really good all aroundFirst, the graphics are honestly gorgeous, great atmosphere and lighting, with a nice spanish music that doesn't get boring.The writing and dialogs are really great, literally the first enemy you encounter says "I am not in danger. I am the danger". There are a lot of funny jokes, I was playing this game with a smile on my face most of the time.The gameplay is simple and effective, controls are responding great whether you are exploring or fighting. Lots of people are comparing this to souls like, it is completely unaccurate, Dark souls didn't event the action/fighting genra.You will probably die a couple of time (i played it in normal difficulty), but it isn't that hard honestly, it is not a die and retry. Most of the time you will run around like in a disney movie to isolate enemies and surprises them with the environement, create weaknesses among them.I honestly recommand it, it is more of an experience, but a very nice one. Get it at a discount though, It isn't worth more than 15€ considering the lifespan (even though the devs really put their heart in it you can see it).
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It is what I was looking in a game. No sandbox. Just go forward. No open, inmense, void areas. Just go forwards. No exploration. Just go forward.  Not objects to collect around the map. No crafting. No losing time. Just fight. Fight a lot. Fight like in the old capcom games. The combat system is a tunned version of Batman AA. In which you really can appreciate the swords, because you can be killed very easily, and also, kill more or less easily. (In hardest difficulty), and all depends in how you and the enemies, block, or dodge, unlike Shadow of Mordor, in which you use weapons, but you feel the weapons are made of wood, because you need many hits (or do an elimination ) to actually kill. It will make you need good reflexes, to choose when to dodge or block, due to how the combat has been designed. I need more games like this. I love it.Also NO PROGRESSION tree. No choosing which ability to upgrade. No upgrade points. Just play, and your character will increase its abilities autmomatically. Oh god. Just play. Some platforming, and a lot of fights. Simply Awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and immersive. The dueling gameplay, lighting, models, effects, atmosphere, and dialogue are all finely tuned and showcases the unbelievable talent at Fireplace Games. Amazing game, a must-buy at any price.I also love the dotted oil paint-like effect of objects as they get further away.And chicken <3
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is 90% combat and the rest consists of very light platforming. The combat system is very fun and wants you to play in ways that felt cheesy in other games. Running around, throwing objects, kicking barrels, climbing stuff. One-on-one the combat boils down to parry, dodge and slash, but facing just 2 or more enemies forces you to rely on you surroundings. There are different enemy types which require different strategies and it makes the encounters varied and interesting.My only criticism is that beating the main game took me just over 3 hours. I felt like there was enough variety to stretch the game a little further. But the upside is that it never got old and ended well before things started to feel repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun swashbuckling adventure!! does basically everything you want, the combat and movement feels great and fits the swashbuckling vibe. The story and setting were both really fun, and i loved that all the characters were voiced! also loved the art style, it was gorgeous. hope to see more from it!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet. This game has some really fun combat mechanics, well designed levels and beautiful environments. Its story is simple but charming, and it keeps its encounters varied and fun throughout its 4 hour or so runtime. There's also an arena mode where you can keep playing around with the combat to your heart's content.Also, sword lesbians.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! captures a sense of joy that few games succeed to with both its unique and dynamic combat design and a tone and script that are expertly crafted to enhance the free-wheeling fun. While there are a few hiccups with the controls (namely Adalia's auto-targeting not being the best at predicting which enemies and environment targets i'm aiming for), the game generally provides enough leeway for the player to escape and attempt a different angle of attack, befitting of its swashbuckling, plucky protagonist.The main mode of the game may be modest in length compared to what one may come to expect from a linear action game, but i felt that Fireplace Games made the most out of its short time with the player, exploring both the historical setting (with very pleasant environmental art and an engaging cast of appropriate opponents) and the combat loop to the fullest. The exceptional performances of the voice cast elevate what would otherwise be rather simplistic dialog-box-based cutscenes as well. I think the game industry at large could stand to learn from Fireplace Games' deft usage of limited resources, and I hope they have more chances to show off their skills in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I found that sign in my first minute of game-play and  knew I would love En Garde. I was very surprised to find out the studio that developed it, Fireplace Games, is based in Montpellier, France. The game oozes Spanish culture and references. As a Spaniard myself, I find myself marvelled at them, from a portrait of Charles the Second to names like  and . These fellows really did their homework with the setting and I bow to them from Spain. Well done.Combat feels like a mix of classic parrying games like Sekiro or Ghost of Tsushima and the good old Batman games, with their different enemies and ways to defeat them. It's fun and satisfying and the diverse difficulties make it approachable. It's simpler than its references, which helps a lot. The scenarios look very appealing. The graphics are very stylised, but it's the lighting that makes the city look warm and cosy. The music is very enjoyable and fits the setting perfectly. But it's the texts, dialogue and banter what wins it for me. From the "Do not... it's illegal" signs (Apparently, it's illegal to swim, pile up more than three barrels or steal spoons) to the dialogue coming from defeated enemies. That "" line had me laugh out loud.The character are cheeky and the dialogue is cheesy as hell, but t works perfectly fine. Having the "Conde-Duque de Olivares" as a villain is interesting, especially given that I live mere meters away from the Prado Museum, which displays the Velazquez painting of the noble that was used as the main reference. As I said, the setting hits home quite nicely.En Garde! features interesting combat game-play, nice and cosy graphics and very funny dialogue, all wrapped up in a very well done Spanish setting, which relies, of course, on stereotypes, but works well and is done with care and respect. Oh, and a female protagonist is always a positive for me, especially one based on "La Maupin"
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: As others have pointed out, the game has charming visuals and voice acting, and solid if simplistic core gameplay mechanics, but there's just not enough content to justify the pricetag - only 6 enemy types and 4 levels (including the tutorial one,) can be completed in a few hours with not much replay value. Also, there are some really weird difficulty spikes, I wonder the game design logic behind creating a laid-back game with casual vibes and cartoony graphics, and then throwing in a boss fight in the middle that would make sweaty souls-tryhards sh*t out their liver. Perhaps they hoped to pad out the playtime with this (?)
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: An overall simple, but also fun combat system and rather enjoyable banter makes this game quite fun to play. Not the longest game in the world, but replaying to find secrets, complete challenges, and take on the arena mode still provide plenty!Just...Unless you're a completionist, maybe try to avoid going for the damageless achievements. Those were brutal.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Did not enjoy the full game as much as the demo. The combat gets repetitive fast, the dodge function is unreliable and unresponsive and the frequency of unblockable attacks just ruins any kind of flow in the combat. Often you end up fighting three or more enemies at the same time and as you get an opening to damage one of the enemies another does an unblockable attack forcing you to dodge out of combat. Annoying more than challenging and in the end not really fun.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is a fun little game you can finish in a weekend. It is done by a small team of newcomer developers who started this game as a student project, which makes me excited what their next fully fledged project will look like. It has funny and cheesy dialogues, fun combat, great environmental interactions and more. Just keep in mind before buying this is a short and fun game so keep your expectation accordingly.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, fun, joyous little action game that was clearly made with lots of heart. The action is difficult and engaging (if a little slippery and awkward at times), the characters are charming, and the painterly visuals are gorgeous. I also love a game short in length and small in scope, fully confident in its own 3-4 hour campaign without stretching mechanics and systems beyond what they were built for. Definitely worth playing on a lazy afternoon, especially for fans of Sekiro or classic character action games!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde is packed full of heart, silly banter, swordfights, and a big emphasis on using the environment to your advantage. You also can throw a turkey on someone's head and incapacitate them straight out of a Mr Bean sketch. If that doesn't sell you on it, maybe this one isn't for you. I finished the story on hard in 3 hours so buy it at a price you're comfortable with for a good, short game.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: "IT'S A SWASHBUCKLING GAME AND YOU DON'T EVEN GET A BUCKLER, 0/10"In all seriousness, this game is wonderful. The art and design of this entire game is gorgeous, the dialogue is charming even when it's dorky, and combat genuinely feels good once you realize you're supposed to be a tricky rogue instead of some heavily-armored knight. This game has one of the most vibrant and enjoyable color palettes I've seen in any game ever mixed with what I'm pretty sure is an abiding love for the classic Zorro-style swashbuckler films, and I love it. It's fun, it's unapologetically goofy, it feels like you're playing in a very specific Saturday morning cartoon in a really good way, and you should absolutely get yourself a copy of this game.The amount environmental objects you can bring into combat cannot be overstated, either: this is the first time EVER where I've seen the absolute goblinry of a swashbuckler's fighting style get rewarded so well, and it's very refreshing. You can throw buckets onto enemies' heads, kick enemies into weapon racks or off ledges, light and fire cannons at groups of enemies, or even slide across a table before flinging it at the enemies who are chasing you. This game does not take itself seriously, but it does take your deep emotional need to pelt a dude with an entire bag of chili powder during a sword fight VERY seriously, and I for one really appreciate that.Also, possibly most important of all for a specific niche of gamer, .
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, the game looks and runs great.  It still amazes me that these small, independent game developers are better at optimization than AAA studios.  The art style and lighting in this game are very reminiscent of Sea of Thieves, in that the style itself is very animated and cartoony, while the lighting effects are allowed to be center stage and add gorgeous depth to its scenery.  Meanwhile it runs at a smooth 60fps on maximum settings (granted, I do have a 3070ti, but I've had poorly optimized games run like trash on it), with no dips to be seen, even in more demanding scenarios.Now gameplay-wise, it's an absolute blast.  Combat is incredibly smooth, responsive, and satisfying.  They even managed to make platforming during combat feel fun, fluid, and useful in every scenario.  This game is a combat sandbox that's insanely fun to experiment with, and there's really no right or wrong answer to how you can approach each combat scenario.  Plus, you can blow enemies up with black powder canons.  Good stuff.Story-wise, it's nothing new, but it's executed with an eloquent charisma and wit that makes it feel fun and fresh.  There's no socio-political commentary or agenda here, and the protagonist genuinely feels like a badass without being forced.I've only had one problem so far, where it crashed 20 minutes into the first episode, but it hasn't crashed since.  Also, a couple of times the dialogue, which I really like in this game and want to listen to, gets cut off mid-sentence when a cutscene plays, or it loads into a new scenario.All-in-all 9.5/10.  The very small issues it has can be fixed with a small patch at some point in the future, and none of it ruined the experience for me.  For the small price of 20 bucks, you should absolutely check out this gem.
