_childDocuments_.review: Zorro meets Puss in the Boots: The GameIt is extremely charming, atmospheric, the story is over the top and the game in general doesnt take itself seriously, rather, it embraces its sillyness. The vibe of this game is just fantastic, standing ovation for every dev, especially the people behind the visuals and sound/narration. While the game doesnt do anything groundbreaking mechanically, the combat is solid and smooth like butter, and using the enviroment and items in fights is really fun.The story levels are quite linear from a level design perspective, but there are secrets to discover for the keen eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun action game with light platforming sections to break up the combat. En Garde has a vibrant color pallet and oozes style; the developers definitely nailed the tongue in cheek Zoro vibe. Another interesting twist is that you play as a female protagonist and there are hints at LGBTQ romance which is underrepresented in video games. Another person put it best - this reminds me of a game you'd rent from the video store for a weekend, have a blast with, and then forget about until it's mentioned in an obscure Youtube video.En Garde is a fun romp from start to finish that doesn't overstay its welcome, I'd put length for the 4 chapters at around 6 hours total. There are some collectibles but the game is mainly running from one combat arena to the next in order to progress. Good thing the Arkham rock, paper, scissors style works here although some enemy types can feel extremely cheap to play against.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure what spurred me to buy this game really. I hadn't heard of it, but it was on sale and I decided to give it a go. I was pleasantly surprised by it. It's a game that doesn't take itself too seriously, and it really pays homage to older third person platformers as far as level design. I think it's one of those games that just fits together. It looks great artistically and the art style and humor really play off of the gameplay here. I don't think there's a game that better does the swashbuckling type of swordplay where you use your environment to such a degree.  It's mechanically quite simple, but there's always so much around you that it encourages you to really play in fun ways. Especially on hard, you need to use that environmental stuff in fights, and so it leads to you as a player being constantly aware of the stuff around you, jumping over tables, kicking boxes at people and knocking them down the stairs. I think it's an overall well polished game with systems that cohesively mesh together incredibly well at every level.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: The game ends quite suddenly, and is overall very short (I beat it in about 4 hours). I would have preferred a bit more of a narrative arc. As is, it feels like watching the middle few episodes of a cancelled adventure serial: A few loosely connected mini-stories, but missing any kind of rising action, consistent throughline, or character arcs.Still, what's here is an absolute blast. Every arena is a joyful medley of cartoon crates, bombs, chandeliers, and other conveniently placed traps, and every tiny detail of En Garde is designed to encourage you to make clever use of them. The tone is unique and spot on - each character in the game is having fun and playing along, from the heroes and scoundrels swapping banter, to the guards who play dead when defeated.Fans of Dark Messiah or other games that encourage creative use of the environment will adore every second of En Garde.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and it's 4AM so excuse if I'm incoherent, but this game is absolutely amazing. I was imideatly captured by its charm, the artstyle and writing is delightful and theatrical, which helps pull you in, though the gameplay quickly enough becomes interesting enough that it could have carried the experience alone.You play as a swashbuckling insurectionist, and your primary means of combat is basically kicking boxes at people, or at least doing so lets you stun people so you can manage the otherwise overwhelming number of enemies attacking at the same time. As for the direct combat it's evasive with a parry and a dodge with just a single basic attack, but the fact that your kicking around people and envirenmental objects, while throwing buckets over peoples heads all the time makes combat engaging and fun at all times. I got a real challenge on hard mode, while the game is short I spent a lot of time stuck on some of the bosses, and I'll even admit I struggled and had to replay parts of the first level which is bsically a tutorial, so if you want a challenge it should be there at least untill you master the game mechanics, but even then the room for creative espression though how you use your environment leaves endless potential for improving your flow and technique, which I'm sure comes into play in endless mode, but I haven't tried that yet.The story isn't particularily deep, but it isn't trying to be, instead going for a cartoon-y hero vs villain plotline with a delightfully nasty and pathetic villain in the form of the Count-Duke. There are also a few supporting characters involving your brother's obvious alter ego, and a pirate lady who's your love interest, providing a delightful opertunity for lesbian sword fighting, which could be added to any game and make it better (looking at you tetris). There are voicelines and moments that imply a lot more detail, but I think their descicion to leave most of the events implied was a good one, such as the noble status of our heroine, the conditions of the Count Duke's rule, what has happened to the rest of the heroine's family, etc. It doesn't feel overlooked either, it feels developed and consistent, just understated, which I think is good for a game that is primarily about a fun vibe and gameplay experience.I can draw a paralell to the Assassins Creed series, specifically drawing on my experience with the second game in the parkour traversal and the style of the sword fights, but it's definetively a level type game, and the fights are better due to the whole environmental thing.Ultimately the game is absilutely amazing, though I will say it's very short, and even with my slow-ish clearing on hard mode it has taken me under ten hours, but even factoring that in, I still think it's well worth the price for the high quality fun the game offers, and having been stuck a few times having to repeat the same boss over and over I can also confidently say that this is a game you can play many times and still enjoy, as every single minute spent playing has been a blast, and the vibe of the whole game has made me fall in love with it, a truly amazing game I'm highly reccomending.I will also add that it manages to strike that balance of being both kids friendly, and yet entertaining and enjoyable for adults. I haven't tried the lower difficulties yet, but they do have an easy mode, and the settings menu has accessability options that also help reduce difficulty quite considderably, I saw an auto-parry option which alone would have made most bosses trivial for me so the range is threre for players of most skill levels.A rare case where I can't justify to myself rating it anything lower than a 10/10, and I sincerely hope more games or content is to come, and I will check out what else the devs have done because this is truly inspired.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A charming game, and I'm genuinely baffled by some of the complaints. Combat is challenging, but very rewarding if you approach it tactically rather than assuming you're a one woman army, and while the platforming is forgettable, I had no difficulty with it whatsoever-- it does its job of pacing out the action.My only complaint is that it's relatively short, but not egregiously so for a $20 game. Especially not for one as polished as En Garde.(For those struggling with combat, pay attention to the tips! Use kicks+projectiles to isolate enemies, and duel them one at a time! )
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is , I went in thinking I needed perfect precise timing with each parry/block but the window for it is very forgiving. Also, I enjoy that overwhelming swarms of enemies encourages you to constantly use your surroundings and mix & match various objects to gain an advantage over big groups. It's much more fun that way than to brute-force through every encounter.Story is pretty simple but the characters and their witty dialogue didn't bore me and actually gave me a few chuckles along the way (which is great because I'm so deadpan when it comes to playing linear single-player games), especially the Moon conspiracy bit, so that was fun!  Such a concept and beautiful art-style mixed in with fun platforming could've had me stuck in this world for hours yet I've managed to finish the story in a day. The Arenas gamemode is fun too although it can get old quick so I'm hoping devs add more stuff cause 'En Garde!' has lots of potential.Minor gripes include certain dialogue being cut off by another but that can be overlooked. When displayed on Discord, it still says demo, so if fixed, thanks!Otherwise, a short and sweet hack n' slash with fun and intuitive combat mechanics!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: The game also does a fantastic job of blending humor with competitive elements, keeping the atmosphere light-hearted while still providing a satisfying challenge. Additionally, the diverse environments and dynamic interactions enrich the overall experience, making every match feel fresh and exciting. Overall, "En Garde!" successfully captures the spirit of swashbuckling adventure, making it a fun choice for players looking for an entertaining and unique gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Great fighting gameplay (know your basic attack, parry and dodge :D), lovable characters and many interactions with the environment make this game a pure pleasure to play.The story is a bit short (3-4h) but it's a very enjoyable experience. There is also an arena mod and multiple challenges to do if you are not ready to stop playing after these hours :)
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Step into the shoes of a wise cracking Spanish fencer as you bring down innocent guards and cause insane amounts of criminal damage all in the name of JUSTICE. ✔️ Very well written... unlike my reviews.✔️ Great voice acting, Great Humour the acting really brings the game to the next level.✔️ Combat is ironically better than the UFC games, its fluid, fast and really gratifying.✔️ Looks great, Low poly clean art really has a nice Spanish Style.✔️ After playing the game you will speak in a Spanish accent for about 3 hours until you snap out of it.✔️ Somehow feels nostalgic of games of the past, it feels like a PlayStation classic.❓A DLC or a Part 2 would be awesome, the odds are by the time you've grasped the combat the games about to end, which is a real shame!❌ A bit overpriced at full price, but its a small indie team so give them the money they deserve it you tight ♥♥♥♥♥.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with decent dueling combat but most of the fun is in environmental combat. Would have been nicer with more of a variety of enemies rather than throwing more and more duelists towards the end of the game. Also the boss dueling fights have moves that are seemingly random and hard to counter, and remove all environment moves that we are taught to use, making it frustrating, but overall a very nice game that I had a great time with!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This was ok. Combat is pretty simple with one main attack and parry/dodge with generous timing windows. The hook is almost every encounter is a big group brawl and you have use environment to isolate enemies from the group to take them out. This include kicking people into weapon stands/off ledges and throwing water jugs on enemies heads. It is enjoyable but I was starting to get tired of it near the end of the ~4 hour game run time. The problem is fights are mostly the same; because of the enemy groups overlapping attacks you need to run around find an item to isolate one guy, burst him down repeat. However the game is super beautiful with a good soundtrack, doesn't take itself seriously and is short enough to be a worth while couple of sittings.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This was quite a fun game. I really enjoyed the combat and mixing in attacks, parries, and dodges with utilizing the environment to my advantage. I think the combat really shines in the smaller group settings but learning how to deal with the mobs was also its own challenge. Add to that the amazing graphics and absolutely hilarious dialogue and this game is definitely one to play.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably one of the more enjoyable 'quick reaction' combat style games I've played in a long time. Whenever you get frustrated from a loss of some type, you go back into the fight, use your environment, and realize how easy it could have been. Pros:- Combat system is fluid/very satisfying. - Story is lighthearted and enjoyable, same feeling you get from a Puss & Boots movie.- Environmental fighting is great, you're not confined to play only parry/dodge simulator if you choose not to. Two people playing this game may have completely different experiences from this alone.- Arena fighting makes you feel strong, it's interesting to see how much combat changes from a couple of perks.Cons:- Game is way too short, this is my biggest negative with the game. I have 2.7 hours on record as of this review, finished the story and two of the arena fights. I hope that they add more to this game, because even the platform filler/collectible filler doesn't justify really delving further into the game.- Enemy HP is sometimes odd, you think you kill an enemy only to realize they have 0.1% HP still available. I don't really have many cons, but this one was frustrating when keeping track of groups of enemies.-Item throwing & lock on mechanic. This just gets frustrating sometimes when you're trying to attack an enemy with broken shield, or throw a projectile at a grenadier. If they can make this fluid, I'd be surprised though.Overall, I recommend this game to play. I think the average person would have a great time playing, and have the exact same issues and still enjoy the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite a title that’s explicitly a fencing term, you won’t find the word ‘fence’ anywhere in this game’s description.  Before ‘En Garde!’ is a sword-fighting game it’s a swashbuckling game—a distinction made manifest from a dual focus on multi-enemy encounters and environmental interaction. The primary skills being tested here aren’t mastery over its swordplay, but target prioritization and item-usage-improv. It’s a joyous blend that will have you grinning not solely for the delight of striking down a villain, but also for the heroic rope swing you did to close the gap.Its story never pretends to be anything more than an excuse to get you into new arenas with baddies, but it still delivers its themes with charming vivacity.“En Garde’s!” critical path clocks in at around three hours, but it justifies that brevity with a focus as narrow and sharp as its heroine’s weapon.Each of the game’s four missions is a long daisy chain where each daisy is a combat arena, and each chain is a hallway demanding basic platforming. The latter is simple by design; jumps are forgiving, swinging timing is practically automated, and falling prey to a bottomless gap lets you off with a slap on the wrist–you’ll be brought right back to the ledge with all you’re HP intact.It's a definitive statement: these non-combat sequences are pretty and breezy palate cleansers in between the dedicated swashbuckling focus.The combat shares DNA with Batman Arkham. Basic attacks magnetize you toward your foes, and when those foes strike back you’ll be parrying or dodging respectively depending on how red and flashy said strike is.This combat grows its beard in the few subtle ways it deviates from that Arkham molding and the most significant way it does that is in how strongly it punishes indiscriminate blows.Enemies have low health, one to two HP at most, but they’ll always have a balance and/or shield bar protecting them. While enemy HP will never regenerate, those meters will; the end result demands you to pick targets and land decisive strikes before moving on to the next. You can’t just slowly rot away at everyone’s HP by gliding around randomly and smashing attack—none of it will stick.Late-game enemies can even fully and immediately regenerate their meters if you switch targets. It may sound like a poor fit for a game that inundates you with dozens of goons, until gain mastery over the style it pushes you towards—to stop relying on sword swings exclusively and start using all the interactables that litter the arena.“En Garde!” isn’t just a classic Spanish adventure film in game form, it’s also a slapstick cartoon; our hero can do anything just shy of dropping anvils on heads. Throwable jugs will always perfectly strike your enemies, and kicking over wine containers will have grunts comically slipping on the contents. Enemies who stumble near a ledge will linger on it, arms flailing at their sides, for more than enough time to ensure you can Sparta (Espana?) kick them off. You can even see this over-the-topness in sound design as well: knock an enemy into a wall and their stun corresponds to a loud *BONK*, and the long descent of airborne projectiles will have a slide whistles pitch descending along with it.It’s goofy, hilarious fun: the game’s systems push you towards using everything other than your sword and it rewards you with comedy and slain enemies.Maybe not even technically slain? Despite the fact everyone’s wielding exclusively sharp weapons, there’s a playful and lighthearted energy that implies non-fatality. Your defeat screen will usually have a guard barking to “fetch the manacles!”, presumably to lock our heroine in an offscreen cell she will no doubt escape from to thwart the villain yet again.You get that impression from the episodic nature of the missions, too. They’re each distinct micro-stories with the same recurring characters: most important being our fearless and selfless protagonist, Adalia de Volador,  and our all-but-mustache-twirling antagonist, “Count Duke.”The conflict between their black-and-white ideals plays out through mid-mission dialogue but also through dedicated cutscenes. These cutscenes don’t have full animation but offset that limitation with some smart usage of key poses: heroically defiant pointing and ominous finger-tenting are the backdrop for playful monologues that hint at multiple seasons’ worth of Saturday mornings we missed.It’s tonally excellent writing in line with the morally unambiguous adventure films it’s based on and fits the cartoon hijinx of the gameplay well.And it ties that package together with a beautiful painting aesthetic: the streets are colorful and alive, and there are even some clever touches like distance-fog being replaced with paint smudges.“En Garde!” is a wonderful little game that knows exactly what it is and exactly where it wants to strike. Its runtime may be similar to the movies it’s inspired by, but like those movies, it’s well-paced and endlessly worth revisiting.There’s even a robust post-game arena mode that remixes the story's combat rooms with roguelite power-ups. But it’s worth playing even for its campaign alone. It takes a traditional combat system and nudges it in the right spots to make something that feels entirely new—something that will make you want to don your cape and make a heroic entrance. A lot of games could learn from how confident “En Garde!” is in its execution, and I wouldn’t mind more that let me circumvent challenges with a well-timed chandelier drop to the head.

Story is generic but it has nice humour. I'd have liked a couple of level more, and more complex platforming, but overall it's a solid 7.5/10 for me. 4-6 hours to finish it, more for achievements

It can be tough as nails at times, but ultimately not the hardest game out there once you get the hang of it. I just wish it were longer, as I've completed the whole game on hard-mode in about 4-5 hours. Multiplayer would also have been amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a VERY short game (not including the arena mode), but i still loved it, it looks, feels and plays (mostly) amazingly, i would love to see a continuation of this game as a series! I had 1 problem with the game, - the way 2 bosses were made, nothing to change the mechanics and just crank up the punishment for any mistake, to the point where it just feels annoying, instead of challenging. The good thing that the devs probably understood that, and added a no damage mode, but, cheating your way through the last boss is kinda silly. Overrall, great pretty much everything, too bad it's so short, would love to see another game like this, with the same character, ideally with a more open world.

I recommend the game but as i said its very short dont expect it to even hold a day8/10, would be higher if more content added or price was/is lower

_childDocuments_.review: perhaps the pirates of the caribbean game ive been needing, in terms of buoyant swashbuckling anti-authoritarian escapism ofc but also just the Physicality of ecstatic and yet inherently comedic action spectacle. so many combinations of actions and fast reversals of fortune that are just Inherently Amusing!!! and the written jokes aint bad either, on the whole they give the game a much more lighthearted and breezy tone then the movies im comparing it to and it works perfectly well for this,,,i can easily picture a worse version, but its all exuberant action movie giggles completely sold on the gravity of how Awesome ur character and her accomplishments are. just pure joy!!! and one of the best swordplay games ive yet come across, as fantastic as the main crowd control stuff is i was always happiest to just sink my teeth into a good one-on-one duel...lots of promises fulfilled here

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! A bit challenging, especially startin off, but eventually you will begin to understand the flow of the game and it becomes one of the most engaging and entertaining experiences I've ever played. I really hope for DLC or something more to add to this game, cause its criminal its not more popular.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm impressed with the level of difficulty tuning available. If I want a challenge I can turn up the difficulty but if my daughter needs an easier time I can turn on more assist options. The story actually had me chuckling quite a few times. It's a truly lovable experience for gaming veterans and novices alike. The story mode is short and sweet, it seems, but there's an arena mode for additional challenge. Overall, this is one of my "must buy" games for the year.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game that made me fall in love with it inmediately.There are a lot of good things to say about this game. The general mood is a mix of action and comedy that is reminiscent of old series and folklore like the Three Musketeers or el Zorro. The characters are really well done, their dialog is amazing and the interaction with the enemies, even the weakest ones, had me laughing for a good while. As a Spanish speaker playing in English, I found that the times Spanish was used in the dialogue were correct, not like other games that simply smack Spanish words randomly. Even the accents of most of the characters are Spanish! Visually the game is stunning, the colours are beautiful and the designs blend perfectly into the scenery. Nothing feels out of place, not even the protagonist with her vibrant outfit. Combat was fun, innovative and easy to pick up. It's not straight up fencing, but playing with the environment to grant yourself advantage. Keep in mind this is not a fencing simulator or else you're up for a surprise.Bad things? Not many, but I'd say that as a level transition you sometimes open a door and find an empty corridor that is no more than a few steps long before the screen fades to black. Game is a bit short, but since it's a student's project and it has an arena mode, it's completely understandable.In general, I think this game is a short and fun masterpiece! Can't wait to see if we ever get a sequel! I give it a 9/10!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely swashbuckling adventure in the spirit and tone of The Princess Bride and Zorro, biting back and forth insults and banter while fencing, daring leaps, dodges and ripostes, and kicking everyone into walls, tables, pillars and down stairs. Throw a turkey on someone's head and poke them in the butt.I can't stress enough how charming and joyful this game is. The music, the atmosphere, the playful dialogue and setpieces. It looks very nice, with warm colours and soft edges, a gorgeous painterly effect on environments in the distance. The defeated guards muttering to themselves as they lie on their face on the ground is one of my favourite little touches.It's a breezy, fun experience, but it can get pretty hectic with bigger crowds of enemies. The combat is a lot about positioning, crowd control and using everything in the environment to your advantage, as the later enemies are absolutely relentless, and you can't mash your way through most of the tougher encounters. If the combat proves too frustrating, there's multiple difficulties, and a number of assist options that will make the experience smoother if you so wish. Sometimes the lock-on will fail you and you take a swing or kick at the wrong target you weren't intending to go for, and you get punished, but then you just try again. There is an ebb and flow to the fights that takes a moment of getting used to, because you don't (at least you shouldn't) play it like a character action game, you often have to back away and look to isolate enemies before attacking them, and initially it can feel demanding.If there is one thing you could complain about, I suppose the game could be considered "short" as the four chapters do not overstay their welcome and the whole game can be completed in 5-6 hours, depending on how quickly you get past the tougher fights. There is a really fun arena mode, which pits you against increasingly tough combat encounters, and there's a bunch of readables and easter eggs in the levels I'm planning on going back for.All in all, it's just a really charming, joyful adventure that everyone should experience. If you're unsure of the length, pick it up in a sale. I hope in the future the developer gives us more adventures with Adalia and Zaida, I would certainly welcome it.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brief review of , an action adventure game taking elements from both the hack and slash genre as well as most precision based titles such as Sekiro to create a precision-based combat system which thrives when the player is faced against multiple enemies. This is an important point, because although the game is usually compared to Sekiro due to the nature of the combat being reaction-based, Sekiro shines most on a 1v1 setting against an enemy, while En Garde! is built so the player feels right at home in a 1vX situation, giving tools to crowd contol, slowly chip away and fight against multiple enemies at once. This does not mean that the combat in 1v1 situations is bad, in fact it can be quite compelling when it comes to harder enemies like duelists(enemies found later in the game) or certain bosses, but simply that the game  with simpler enemy movesets to allow more comfortable group fight situations. Not only that but there's a big emphasis on movement which opens opportunities for the player to create space, separate fights and find advantageous positions, which together with the use of the environment and objects in it, which can help deal damage and CC enemies, makes for a fun combat loop in which you move around the arenas presented looking for the right moments to face off against whichever enemies are incoming.Other than the combat, the game is rather short, which I prefer personally, and has a lighthearted narrative in which the player takes control of a swashbuckler ally of justice named Adalia de Volador, as she fights against the corrupt Count-Duke's schemes for the good of the people. The narrative is simple, loaded with dumb humour and cheesyness, and that's what makes it so charming to me. En Garde! isn't afraid to be cheesy or stupid, rather it embraces it, and in that process allowing, in the short story, the characters to have charm and be endearing without necessarily the player learning much about them. If there's one complain I have about the game, it would be how the enemies can sometimes have a ton of tracking on the player, sometimes closing off massive amounts of distance in an instant during an attack aimed at the player, sometimes resulting in the player taking hits that feel undeserved, but it doesn't happen too often, and is avoidable once you get used to staying in the fray and using the mechanics the game offers to deal with multiple opponents at once. Overall, to me,  was a fun, mechanically compelling, charming and light hearted short game which I would recommend to anyone who likes real-time combat with some depth.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, Inigo Montoya: the game.Finally, an answer to the question: "What if Kitty Softpaws was human?"You know that meme of Sonic going "I want shorter games with worse graphics and longer dev cycles and I'm not even joking"? Yeah I think this game is exactly what that meme was asking for and it's wonderful.En Garde! feels like a PS2 game, and one of the greats. One of those games you come back to twenty years later and find it still holds up. If you ever wanted to play a video game with expert fencing delight after watching characters like:•	⁠Cyrano de Bergerac•	⁠Inigo Montoya•	⁠Zorro•	⁠Puss in Boots•	⁠Captain Jack SparrowThen you will love this game.I was obsessed with The Mask of Zorro and The Princess Bride's fencing scenes as a kid, and always wished there could be a video game that recreated that kind of lighthearted swashbuckling feel. I always dreamed of a game where you could improvise silly sh*t like this. It feels like something Arkane would make if they stopped being so in love with wacky superpowers. Dark Messiah was almost that kind of game at times.  The story is built in an episodic format, with relatively simple mechanics, but executed perfectly. It's a really lighthearted action game but the combat is very entertaining. Even a bit hard sometimes. The movements and interactions with the background and set pieces really lend into the aesthetic. Devs should be applauded for keeping a laser focus and making a tight experience.En Garde! has something that I think is missing from almost every swashbuckler archetype in gaming (Both tabletop and otherwise). Being an Errol Flynn style duelist at the end of the day isn't really about swordsmanship (Although it does help), it's about outwitting your opponent, luring them in and humiliating them, not stabbing them to death. The sword isn't a weapon, it's a distraction to draw their eyes to the left while the bucket you kicked at them comes in from the right.The game emphasizes the use of props a lot, because you need to fight each enemy one-on-one, which means using props to distract or in some way incapacitate his 5 buddies for a few seconds. And you have to use not only the available props, but also the layout of the area itself. So you can throw buckets (or even whole rotisserie chickens) at guards' heads, so they're stuck with them, comically cursing in a muffled voice as you go fight someone else. If an enemy is standing on a table you can kick the table away so he'll fall on his face. If a guard's back is against a downward flight of stairs and you manage to kick him, he'll roll down the steps and become easier to defeat. Is there a canon or box of explosives around? Kick a brazier which will light a trail of gunpowder to said canon or explosives, and any nearby enemy will feel the effect. And then there's the always enjoyable insta-defeat by pushing enemies into a body of water or off a bridge (which is somehow still non-lethal).So yeah, there's a really big emphasis on constantly using whatever improvised weaponry you can get your hands on, running all over the place, kicking and throwing stuff at enemies so you can have some breathing room to have a proper sword duel with a particular enemy, and pick them out one by one.The combat in this game shines a light on just how much positioning has fallen to the wayside in a lot of other combat systems. Nearly all games I play with combat really only work on a one to one level, as in it’s you and your opponent(s), and considering that most combat systems have some level of Move Assist to help nudge players to the next target, it seems that a lot of games don’t trust the player to keep their surroundings in mind.This game’s entire point is positioning. It’s about understanding the entire battle field and never losing track of your position on it, melding enemies, your own skill of play and the environment seamlessly. All in incredibly appropriate presentation that understands the best way to capitalise on its gameplay by way of its aesthetic, bringing to mind old Western Swashbucklers.It’s not super fancy so the big AAA gaming fans probably won’t be won over and it isn’t polished to high heaven so the indie crowd probably won’t love it either but a game that is able to see an under-utilised feature like positioning in combat, understand it’s strengths and make a gameplay loop that takes advantage of it to force the player to think creatively in a fight, all with an appropriate aesthetic to boot! It’s a winner in my book!It’s a fantastic game, one that absolutely deserves a sequel which builds on the excellent combat and the fun platforming to make a modern action masterpiece. And having its scope be a bit more bite-sized is a plus for me. Too many games need 80+ hour playthroughs and oftentimes a 5 hour romp is just what I want. I encourage everyone to give it a try if you like classic action adventure with a nice sword combat system and enjoyable characters / dialogues that makes your heart smile. I guess what I'm saying is…You can kick a man into a column, and then the flowerpot that was on top of that column falls onto the mans head.10/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth it at a larger discount (I got it for 10€/50% off)A game with a quick to learn combat system that puts emphasis on spacial awareness, environment and a calm mind.  You're a duelist in a brawler, you're at your best when singling out enemies but they come in waves (finite amount per room) and the AI is intentionally coded to be disruptive to not let you easily try and rush down one guy at the time. Whether it's synchronizing attacks or doing different ones (essentially there's blue and red attacks. Blue can be parried, red ones must be dodged).The game is lighthearted from its colorful and soft visuals, lively background music and silly dialogue. Where it falls short from being worth 20 bucks is the length of the game. 3 hours gets you from start to finish, not including hunting down secrets or doing challenges. There's a "Arena mode" for those that wants to enjoy the combat a bit more after the story (replayable) with different degrees of difficulty. If the game had 3-4 more episodes of hijinks introducing another 2-3 new enemies over that span, I think it'd be worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, stylish, fun and hilariously Spanish!The only potentially disappointing aspect of this game is the length of the story mode, which is approximately 3 hours for a non-completionist playthrough. Everything else is impressive: the charmingly silly story, the colourful cast of characters and recurring enemies, the fast-paced split-second decisions you make in combat, it's all there, polished and is an absolute treat!Outside of the story mode you also have an arena mode with randomized modifiers, which i'll definitely be coming back to play every now and then.How does it play? The game runs like a charm, it's responsive, and feels great when you beat a challenging encounter.it really reminded me of Sekiro, the gameplay very linear (you travel from arena to arena) with some hidden secrets and revolves around breaking the enemies' posture to land a the killing blow, you can do this through parries, ripostes and strikes, or taking advantage of your environment and swashbuckling maneuvers. The fights are not fair and you're often surrounded by enemies, which is why you must resort to all kinds of dirty tricks to even the odds.I'll be keeping an eye on this studio, and look forward to whatever they're working on next.If you want to sit down for a few hours and simply have a blast, I would strongly recommend doing so with En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 9/10 perfect bite sized action game like sifu but easier that hearkens back to the ps2 era.OverviewEn Garde is a tribute to stylish action adventure stories like Zorro, princess bride and puss in boots. All of the characters are larger than life, witty and light hearted. even the game's villain is a moustache twirling cartoon jerk with petty ambitions. The jokes land, everyone is likeable and story never takes itself too seriously.GameplayThe real meat however is the gameplay. En Garde is a fairly linear action game with combat similar to batman arkham, sifu and sekiro although considerably easier than those last 2. Enemies have very little health but protect themselves with guard meters that must be worn down with repeated strikes or parries. Unblockable attacks need to be dodged and the game's many enemy types all introduce their own quirks you need to keep track off in order to overcome them. the game also lets you fully rebind the control scheme for both controller and K&M and it has button prompts for playstation and xbox.what sets this game apart is a heavy emphasis on environmental interaction. You can pick up jugs to toss at enemies and stun them, kick enemies down stairs or into hazards, swing on poles and chains to surprise the enemy and leave them vulnerable for a moment. all of these things combine to make every encounter feel somewhat unique based on what's available to you in any given arena and keeps the game fresh through it's short run time. at it's most intense the combat is a serious adrenaline rush and boss fights in particular are very satisfying duels that require you to learn your opponents every move.GraphicsWhile very beautiful and charming, this is a game that is relying heavily on artstyle over fidelity. Character models and environments are akin to something from the late ps2 era, cutscenes are mostly static images of the models posing and lip sync is non existent. This is the area of the game where it's most obvious that this is very much a small team indie title. that said this I didn't take issue with any of this, I'm very much of the mentality that I want games to look worse and play better.lengthIt should be noted this is a brisk game, There is no fat to it at all. The game consists of 4 very different levels that all take roughly an hour to finish casually with a number of secret objectives to complete or documents to find and read for lore. Once you're done with the main game you can replay those levels for the various challenges or speedrun achievements but the main side content is Arena mode.Arena modethis is a rougelike where you fight in a series of randomised rooms from the campaign with each new room giving you a negative modifier like enemies dropping grenades when defeated and giving you a choice between 3 positive modifiers like healing after kicking an enemy or stunning all those near you when you dodge an attack. eventually culminating in a boss fight and unlocking a harder difficulty.gripesWhile I greatly enjoyed the game, I do have some complaints. Despite there being many challenges and collectables to find, there are no unlockables besides harder arena mode difficulties. there are no costumes, no concept art, nothing. Which is unfortunate because I was really hoping we'd at least get her original design from the student project version as an unlockable, even if it was just a recolour.My other complaint is a nitpick but I'm not a fan of the default control scheme. it's very similar to batman arkham with the attack and parry on square/triangle (xbox X/Y) but trying to do that and also dodge with circle in a combat system that requires you to constantly turn the camera to find escape routes and objects to use against enemies quickly became unmanageable for me. I would recommend switching parry to L1 and attack to R1 so you can keep your thumb on either dodge or the camera.

_childDocuments_.review: An impeccable but short swashbuckling adventure. En Garde is a title where you play as a Spanish Musketeer by the name of Adalia Valador as she takes on the counts guards and conspirators in a colourful, delightful adventure. The main part of the game consists of running through areas engaging with enemies and using items and the environment to split up encounters and stagger enemies. You fight enemies through parries, dodges, attacks and special abilities as well as a kick. All in all there's nothing complex here but everything in the game is fine to a point. Engaging with enemies is fun, especially with all of the environment elements such as chandeliers, bombs, pots, buckets etc etc. The arena mode is especially fun if repetitive as it plays like a roguelite where you can buff these elements. One major flaw in the game is that it's really short on content. The tutorial/demo is 1/4 of the game. There's 4 levels in total that, if rushed, can be beaten in under 30 minutes each. My first play through on hard took 3 hours and a half. The enemies variety is decent for the amount of levels but more variety would be appreciated. Arena mode as well as secrets and challenges add some extra replayability and things to do but all in all I really wish there were more content and hope that down the line there's more added to the game. In terms of Aesthetic the game is an absolute delight A*** the writing is cheesey and fun, the games audio is fantastic both the soundtrack and sfx. The game visually is stunning with all of the visual flair and design of enemies, areas and effects. Everything is on point. Having done everything in the game, all I can say is that I want more added to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: No game (that I know of) has ever caught the spirit of the cloak-and-sword adventures than En Garde. Its masterful combination of engaging combat, ineractive environment, and mild humour leaves no soul wanting. All the dodges and parries are as elegant as they should be (however, I cannot help but lament the lack of a feint, available to some AI enemies). Its simple, but captivating story and limited graphics do not take away from it at all. Fantastic work of art.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, the "you have to recommend or not recommend with no nuance" system on Steam causes problems. people commenting seem to make it through En Garde! 's main 4 Acts in less than 5 hours (and usually about 3 to 4). If you're that kind of person, then the game's light humour, swashbuckling adventure, and panache-based environmental combat system will probably remain fun for the entire period, and you might even get into the challenge Arenas and start asking the devs for DLC., playing on Easy, took almost 8 hours to complete the basic 4 Acts - this isn't really my genre of game, and certain enemy types are particularly wearing (plus there's a bridge section I kept falling off). At that length, a lot of the humour runs its course - especially Adalia's "death" quotes, which I heard an awful lot at some points! - and things start to look a bit "thin". (I also found that - playing using Proton on Linux - no achievements triggered for me.)That said, this is a great game for a first time studio, and they've been very responsive to their small community. So, I wish them well in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:  I'd rate this a 10/10. You won't regret purchasing it.Edit update: After some extra hours in, and a sub 1 hour completetion of the whole game, I truly wish everyone gives this game a shot. I've replayed all episodes almost 10 times, and I am still finding new routes and new ways to defeat the enemies with.I casually completed the game, (not 100%), in about 3 hours and 10 minutes while exploring different paths and more. But I have put over 40 hours into speedrunning the demo, so I would dare to say that I played through it quicker than the average player would.The witty humor, the funny characters and the loving aesthetics makes this game a modern classic in my opinion. You will no doubt have fun all through the game.The combat is excellent, it feels so incredibly polished and there are so many ways you can approach fights.I'm playing perfectly fine with KB&M and there is no reason for you to use Gamepad if you aren't comfortable with that.The game is broken into 4 episodes, each longer than the previous, making it easier to play through in sections but also allows you to play your favorite parts over and over again.There is also an Arena mode in which you can test your skills against waves of enemies, if you want even more swashbuckling action!I already see this as a game akin to Portal, a short but amazing game with an immense replay-ability. Even if I weren't intending to speedrun this, I could see myself going back over and over to replay it for years to come.*And some wishful thinking*As the game is broken down into episodes, I would assume a successful launch will probably spawn future episodes as DLC, as there are tons of stories the devs could explore in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: The game seems more like a proof of concept than a finished thing. It is enjoyable, but it is also really short. I died over and over and finished it in 3h40. I do not recommend it for its cost, it is too expensive for what's in it, even at half price.The negative :-A lot of the time, you struggle to do what you want to do in fights, target the right ennemy, grab the right item, jump on a table or a pole... all of this can be quite random. -The duel base is nice but you spend most of the game being outnumbered, the improvised brawl is also nice but the ennemies are designed around their duel capabilities. I get the idea but both system don't really mix well. -Ennemies can't platform and end up being locked in place if they fall on an un-connected platform like the top of a cage.-There is platforming but it is kinda pointless, you just press forward and your character automatically grab the next thing.-No side objective or progression, the game is 100% linear.-The difficulty curve is quite brutal. -The game is really short.The positive :-Combat is snappy in duels and strategic in mass fights. Both sides are enjoyable despite the whole not mixing well.-The game is pretty, love the artstyle and the presentation.-The sound design helps the gameplay and is overall good-The tone works for the genre, it's whimsical adventures like Zorro. The neutral :-Writing is nothing special, doesn't capitalize on the tone passed some referencial humor and expected banter-Feels like a prettier PS2 game, like prince of persia without the platformingOverall, it feels like the basis for something else rather than a finished game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, there is not much of a story or immersion but it's just fun to play around with the combat system.You have a jump, a dodge, a parry, an attack, a kick and several special abilities. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun romp of a swashbuckler. Fencing is very fluid and reminiscent of the Arkham series with how you soft-lock onto targets, weave between blows with a mix of parries and dodging, and execute your simple combo or special moves - but with a touch of Dark Messiah in how you can freely kick enemies and objects around to stagger, stun, and knock them around into eachother and other hazards. The stagger mechanic makes for tense fights as you try keep pressure applied to specific foes to wear them down, all the while managing the rest of the crowd too.It's camp in a fun way, never taking itself too seriously and maintaining a tone of playful silliness throughout, with some really beautiful environments and good music too.

_childDocuments_.review: A female lead that has a face of a man. A game that really feels like it's cheating. A light-hearted story that drags on. I just don't like the game. How are you supposed to really play this game? Sometimes I get good RNG and I can dodge, parry, and attack like a pro. Other times I get stuck on a simple fight where every guard does an attack an infinite number of times and I just have to lose. There's no fair feeling fight to this game. Either you get good RNG or you have to restart a scene a dozen times. You might lose 5 times in a row to 4 guards, only to then take out 15 guards in the next room on the first try. I just don't like that feeling. The feeling I'm not making progress. I don't feel like I'm learning the guards moves as they're just too random. There's no progression system like xp or the ability to unlock my own skills. The game hands out new moves, that really didn't help, at set intervals. So combat. There's 3 moves: attack, parry & dodge. The game is a souls-like, but it plays like an ARPG, or maybe the Arkham series. You really need to button mash attack, until an opponent flashes either a parry, dodge, or parry/dodge attack, then you stop mashing as fast as you can, then switch methodical inputs. The bi-polar gameplay style was one I couldn't get a grip with. There's also enviromental objects, but they were never where I needed them. You can kick opponents into objects, but they're never stunned enough. You can wow opponents with acrobatics, but 75% of the time for me, jumping off tables and the like did not trigger the acrobatic wow. Mostly, the only thing that reasonably works is picking up a water pitcher and throwing it right before you attack, which is usually countered by the enemy AI by flashing a dodge from another opponent. I'm very certain that the game reads inputs as enemies would stand around, but as soon as I hit attack, they'd do a dodge attack and hit me. It was very frustrating.The game has, 'exploration,' as in you can find messages throughout. They don't do anything and from what I read, they really don't advance the story or help progress anything. The story itself doesn't provide any motivation. You're the ultimate boss woman and so you're the best. You have to beat up every man you see because you're the best. There's a count that's bad and you have to stop them because you're the best. There's nothing in this storyline that I could even grab onto. I think the game would have been better to ditch the story all together and just have her fight just because. Then tone down the one-liners to be less frequent and maybe shift the downed guards voices; so you know there's no one left standing at the end of an encounter.All in all, I never felt like I had control of this game. I felt like bad RNG and unfair fights prevented me from progression. Nothing in the game motivates you to keep playing and the story is lack luster. I'd say pass on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: A definite 7.5 or even 8 out of ten. Good game and worth the price, but as some players have said, the lock on system definitely needs work. Adalia focuses way too readily and too hard on her current target, and changing it (or even following the current target better) should be worked on. Enemy variety and item variety could also use improvement, if only because the lack of the former results in the game often choosing quantity over quality when it comes to increasing difficulty, which leads to some pretty infuriating fights later on in the (very short) game.Some more TLC to combat and enemy variety, and a few more episodes, would easily push this to a 9 or even a 10. It has plenty of charm and the idea is solid, it's just very obvious this game started out as a pet project and Fireplace wanted it out at a certain time.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really really good proof of concept.The game is very short. Just about somewhere around 2 - 3 hours for a single playthrough if you don't bother with going back and doing the optional challenges that really don't reward you with anything so I didn't bother.The combat is great. It feels responsive and the system all work smoothly. BUT, it get stale and repetitive quite quickly due to the lack of more enemy variety and gameplay additions/alteration. After about the second mission or half way through the third, I'm not quite sure anymore, you've seen everything the game has to offer in it's FOUR total mission. One of which is basically just a tutorial.The art style though... I wish I could have had more of that, no alterations necessary. It is simply downright beautiful in every way and I love the way they handled the LOD system with it making everything in the distance look like a gorgeous painting.The story wasn't anything to rave about, but it did fit stylistically and made me feel like I was playing the pilot of a fun little saturday morning adventure cartoon which was quite pleasant actually. The dynamics between the characters were a little tropy but they put their own little spin on some of them and I enjoyed all of their interactions.In conclusion, if you're looking for something fun to fill an afternoon and enjoy something in the vein of a sort of sekiro-lite, I can wholeheartedly recommend this game. Just maybe get it on sale

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, one of the most barely-recommended games I've played. En Garde is a Spanish-themed light-hearted action game, with a focus on combat and utilization of the environment. Apart from its awseome combat system though, It falls short pretty much on all other aspects of the experience.I will start with the pros of the game: 1. The game oozes the love of the development team.2. The graphics are cute and sometimes even impressive.3. The soundtrack although not too lengthy is fitting and charming.4. The whole dialog script (more on that later) is decently voice-acted.5. A variety of gameplay customization to help all type of players enjoy 6. Offers some extra game modes and secret for some extra (fun?) time.7. The combat feels a-m-a-z-i-n-g.The last point, combat, is basically the whole game. The development team gave all their effort on how the main character feels when moving, attacking, blocking and parrying. The combat system is quite intricate for such a small game. It is quite impressive! In addition, the environmental interaction during combat is very interesting, with a pretty large variety of items and furniture that can be used to the players' advantage. Kudos!On to the cons of the game now:1.Hit-or-miss humor. 2. The platforming sections of the game feel on-rails with no interactivity and mostly no skill involved.3. The story and whole script is just a way to connect the fighting sections together. I started skipping all dialog after the first 20 minutes.4. The game is quite repetitive even though it is pretty short. A no-exploration playthough would take an average player around 4 to 5 hours.5. The game design, is very bad. Most of the fighting sections, which should have been the most interesting since the combat system is amazing, are quite cumbersome and irritating. Most of them felt quite mechanical, meaning that the way the environment was structured gave away the optimal way of dealing with the (too big) group of baddies. At some point, instead of having fun experimenting and playing around with parrying and environmental chaos, I just wished there would be no more combat sections!The irritation the game induced on me really left a sour aftertaste. It is quite a shame since the game is definitely not a cash-grab and something that the development team created on a whim for some quick profit. The love and thought around the game is prevalent throughout the experience. It falls short on game design and structure though.I would recommended only to player that seek intricate and challenging combat-focused games and don't want to give too much thought on any other aspect of a video game.Unfortunately, a 5/10 for me.It goes on sale quite and under deep discounts, so definitely wait for a sale if interested.

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde is such a wonderful little game and I highly recommend it from the get go. The combat is incredibly satisfying and addicting, the tone and sense of humor are really charming, and the sheer amount of dirty fighting going on is a downright biohazard on the ability for competition to reach the heights of this game. This game is the closest a power fantasy can get to the trickster swashbuckler archetype and in doing so it has entranced me so far more to the archetype. Sprinting around ball rooms and barracks kicking barrels and blowing up cannons, creating traps and plans on the fly, somersaulting over your foes' heads and constantly making every grim situation seem like you had it planned from the beginning. This game is like no other, and it left me only wanting for more. Length wise it isn't too long, to finish the game on Medium + Hard and then complete Arena mode up to Legend takes less than 10 hours. But I constantly found myself replaying missions and checkpoints and arenas entirely because I was having so much fun. It takes a lot for a game to give me dopamine these days, En Garde got it injecting into my veins directly and we're not talking just an IV drip. It is short and sweet and while they could've made it longer, I don't think it needed to be. Arena mode is especially wonderful and falls into that roguelike, Balatro-esque delight of creating builds so wacky and powerful that you're grinning the entire time as you ♥♥♥♥ wave after wave up and eventually topple all three bosses at once. As for cons the only I can think of are related to camera bugs at times and occasionally hitting the wrong enemies with your Panache attacks. This usually doesn't cause too many problems but there have been a few moments where something went wrong at a vital time and I got killed for it. At the end of the day though, it's pretty excusable and doesn't inconvenience me. Before I played Arena mode I gave this game an 8/10, after I finished Legend tier, I give it an 8.7/10 and a . It's worth the $20 or any price you could get it for.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a short, simple game, with interesting combat, and filled with charm that makes great use of its swashbuckling adventurous theme.The important thing about the combat is that it's challenging. Far more than the bright colors and breezy tone might suggest. You have to embrace the environment and traps. You're not going to win by standing still and expecting to perfect parry everything. You have to reposition, you have to run away from enemies, you have to kite them around and you have to set traps.Elite enemies have a stamina bar that replenishes if you whiff a parry or dodge, but whenever you're dueling one enemy the others will try to hit you with unparryable attacks. So if it happens to coincide with the elite enemy doing a parryable attack then you have no choice but to dodge and see his stamina go back to full. It can be very frustrating. The strategy here is that you should be using the environment to try and separate enemies so you can fight them one on one, and I'll say that for most of the game that is difficult but doable.However, I'd say the final boss was the low point of the game. In part because, same as the other bosses, it's disappointingly just a regular enemy with ads around it, and since it's the final boss it's a million elite ads. In part because it's a small arena, there are camera issues, there's plenty of single-use traps and halfway through new reinforcements will come in, so if you did too much swashbuckling in the first phase and used too many traps to separate the elite enemies then good luck beating the second phase without any traps left to use.A good ending can redeem a lot and leave you with a positive feeling even for a game that you were frustrated with before. Likewise the opposite is also true, and despite liking most of the game I left on a sour note and not too keen on replaying it just yet.Still, it's a fun game in both its theming and mechanics, and if you don't mind it being short, some jank, and a bit of a challenge, then I'd recommend it. Depending on your regional price I'd say perhaps wait for a better sale and some post launch updates though.Update: The devs have addressed the balancing complaints, especially with regards to the final boss. It's always great to see devs taking in feedback and improving their games further.
