_childDocuments_.review: Very strong game. By the time it ends, it sort of feels more like a proof of concept rather than a fully fledged exploration of what's possible given the mechanics introduced, so I wish I'd have seen more of that.Combat is very tight and it's introduced in such a manner that you're comfortable with the system by the time fights really get tricky. Every mistake feels like it's your own, and there are no annoying WTF moments where it feels punishing. The game could've stood to have even more depth in the combat (directional attacks maybe? feints and flourishes, etc) but after seeing everything the game has to offer, that was most likely beyond the scope of the game.Movement, platforming and exploration feels good. There are often multiple paths you can go about a level which is most definitely illusion of choice but it still does a good job of making you feel like you're making your own way through the city.The writing and voice acting is charming and very well done. Jokes regularly land, and popular tropes are given a nod wherever possible (jokes about trickle-down economy or treasure behind waterfalls come to mind). These are always tasteful and never really seem ham-fisted.The art direction is exceptional and there are clearly certain design decisions that stand out as being wholly unique to the game and unlike anything I've seen before. Many times the art direction makes its way into gameplay with slapstick humor that will surprise you and let you know you can go assuming things (Grab a bucket and throw it, you can be certain it'll stick on somebody's head without having seen it before). Many decisions in the graphics department stand out and really drive the game home as being original and made with love.My only real gripe with the game is that some battles may fall flat if you can't keep up the momentum. There are at least 6 different types of enemies you will encounter routinely, and about half of those need special treatment in a fight. You are s sometimes pitted against 2 or more of these "elites" in rooms where there's not much you can do to split the fight up, and it becomes a drag. That's only like 10-15% of the  gameplay, though. More often, the arenas are sprawling and interesting. If you keep running, you keep finding environmental elements that allow you to get the upper hand.The game is very short (about 3-4 hours, i rushed through it), but it's priced accordingly. Very refreshing to be spending less than $50 on a game that puts forward so many unique takes. If you are a fan of the genre, or if you liked the Arkham/Middle Earth series, you are sure to love En Garde, and it's easily worth every penny even at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde is designed with a specific experience in mind: using your environment to fight your enemies. Groups of foes will shred you if you face them all at once, so separating and stunning them so you can deal with them one on one is essential. This moment to moment gameplay is really fun: running around the arena to outmaneuver the goons and drop barrels on their heads, then swooping in to quickly duel one or two of them, is great every time it happens.The weakest parts of the game were those in which you don't get to do this: a stretch in the final episode where you fight back-to-back bosses in single combat makes the otherwise-quick dueling mechanics feel skimpy.Outside of the combat, the rest of the game is stylish, witty, and well made. Environments are varied and pretty, and dialogue is campy and genuinely funny. The level design between fights does a very clever thing where it leads you down an obvious path to a dead end, which causes you to turn back and look at your environment more closely for opportunities to slip through, which feels like a great simulation of your character naturally puzzling out how to get around obstacles.I played on the highest difficulty and was pleasantly challenged throughout. The "campaign" is a short but sweet four episodes and there's a little arena mode with randomized modifiers that adds legs to the experience. Overall it's got a style all its own and is definitely worth your twenty bucks, even more if it's on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Swashbuckling Girlboss Dressed as a Musketeer. Heck yes."En Garde" is a short but sweet little indie game. You're the female protagonist, and you will lose every fight with all but the weakest enemy. They're stronger and capable of blocking what you do, which makes the entire adventure about using the environment to your advantage. Grab a bag of dust on the table, throw it in your enemy's eye, and then kick him down some stairs; NOW you can fight him. In the first "Pirates of the Caribbean" movie, Will Turner tells Jack Sparrow "I'd beat you in a fair fight!" to which Sparrow responds "That's not much incentive for me to to fight fair then, is it?". That's the core gameplay.Stylistically, the game is outstanding. The music, the art, the cheesy voices, the cartoon villain dialogue, and the theatricality of fights all come together in a love letter from weird theater kids for other weird theater kids. Yahtzee from Zero Punctuation describes the tone as on par with an episode of Disney's Gummi Bears cartoon. Point one, that's fair. Point two, I like the Gummi Bears cartoon.Mechanically, there is a problem with the camera effect. It's a 3rd person Unity camera, which is fine by itself. But the game requires you to constantly be moving and aware of your surroundings. Sometime the camera gets stuck at odd angles on crates or around corners, turning a difficult fight into an impossible one. It's not a deal breaker, but the devs should prioritize a bug fix. Is the game fun, though? Yes. Absolutely. It's a very enjoyable 6-7 hours of story with an assortment of collectibles and a decently entertaining arena fight mode. Is it worth the full price? Eh.... That's a harder question. If you can pick it up on a Steam sale, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine. The group fights are hectic but ultimately doable. The duelist enemies and elite soldiers were a bit of a drag with refilling their guard bar though. I do like the style of the game though, The OST works well, sound design in general is pretty neat. Art style is really colourful and matches the lighthearted swashbuckling fun. But I got through the entire game in 2.5 hours. That's just a bit short at 20 bucks. I got it in a Humble Bundle so I can't complain that much about the price tag. I can see that a lot of work went into this but maybe as the studio gets more efficient the next game can be a more complete instead of a compressed experience.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet game with decent combat mechanics.Though it's a shame just how short it is. If the team behind this ever makes any headway, I hope they'll look back on this and consider fleshing it out a bit more. Wouldn't be too bad to have an expansion, whatever it may be. (The story  a bit limited regarding that; Just your typical robin hood robbing the rich to give to the poor type of beat.)
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Style, soundtrack and voice acting are great, so is the general idea. I also like the humor.However, fighting more than 2 enemies is just not fun. Movement is stiff and combat is clunky and repetitive, sometimes outright unfair. It might and probably should have gotten the fighting system of Batman/Spiderman. Since the combat is the main focus of the game, it results in an overall sub-par experience.Got this in a bundle, otherwise I would have refunded. Hope a possible sequel will be fleshed out more.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A short, fun experience! The story is quite simple, but works well with the style and visuals of the game. The colorful areas, 'putty-like' characters and environments are all very pleasant to look at. Presentation is funny and cliché in a good way. Don't expect a serious or complex story, but do expect silly jokes, funny (well delivered) voice lines and over the top theatrical villains.The game runs great as well, and controller support is excellent, allowing to switch between ps and xbox prompts. I would recommend using a controller, but if you're a kbm enjoyer it's also very possible to play that way.Combat is also very easy to pick up. Enemies and combat skills get introduced gradually. Every enemy type has unique ways to beat them and when you encounter multiple types at the same time it really makes you use the arena and different skills to beat your foes. No parry and dodge spamming here, you are inspired to creatively use items and movement to be successful. The arenas can be a bit cramped and sometimes you will feel swarmed, this inspires you to engage with the entire space. If you're using the entire toolkit the game offers you will be able to style on your enemies, which is really fun. You can temporarily disable some enemies by throwing a bucket on their head, stun them by kicking them against a wall, knock over a vase filled with slippery goop to make your enemies slip and fall, and so much more. Again, you (or at least I) cannot brute force kill enemies by just parrying and dodging. You pretty much have to engage with these mechanics.One thing I'd like to mention is that the camera seems a little too zoomed in for some encounters. Especially later on in the game you will face a lot of different foes at the same time. Being able to see more of them and their attacks would be nice. It can feel a bit unfair to get ganged up on in those instances, but otherwise the game seems perfectly fair.I played on normal and beat the game in about 4 hours and was satifsied with the experience. There's a bit of replayability with the arena and harder difficulties, but I think I'm done with the game for now. Perfect if you're fed up with long games.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game with engaging combat and fun writing and visuals that suffers from a massive difficulty spike near the end. Skill issue? Perhaps, but I genuinely don't know if I'll be able to finish the game on Normal without dropping the skill.Game's still great, albeit a little short, and certainly worth the asking price
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: "Wake up, it's 2003, what are talking about, what open world, what crafting, what RPG elements? A new game just came out, it has no shiny shenanigans you're taking about, just purely fun gameplay and gorgeous art style!"However, it also means that the formula is missing some modern polish to make for a great game instead of just good.The Good:* undiluted oldschool fun;* amazing visuals & overall art direction;* nice music, not amazing, but works pretty well in the setting;* pretty challenging even on Normal difficulty.The Bad:* repetitive fights get old pretty fast;* locations are visually pretty, but also very repetitive, at some point they just blur into one homogeneous backdrop;* considering the good art style and pretty locations, I felt like the game could benefit a lot from more emphasis on exploration, but the levels are very on-rails;* pretty challenging even on Normal difficulty.It's also kinda short, but considering the main weakness of the game is that everything gets old really fast, I'm not sure it's a con. The story is very basic, told through in-game dialogue and static cutscenes, but I didn't feel a short and fun ride like this needed a complex narrative.Solid 7/10, looking forward to more games from these guys.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent gameplay, charming characters, a swashbuckling game thru and thru. Each fight is a tactical puzzle where you are trying to isolate and pick apart the enemy while doing cool stunts to power up your panache bar to do powerful attacks. Mechanically this game is simple, effective, and very well executed in my opinion. At around 6 hours of game play the game doesn't overstay its welcome and some might consider it short but it is definitely quality over quantity in this case.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun!The action is fun, well paced and varied enough to be exciting and a challenge.The writing is both witty, tongue in cheek and entertaining. The comments are so funny, you hang out with the knocked out guards just to hear what they say.The story is simple, but fun and loose.If you want to play some Zorro or a Jackie Chan environmental action movie, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially hesitant to buy En Garde! because of the relatively short length. However, I'm glad that in the end, I got myself to give it a try, because the combat system, however simple and abuseable it can seem on a paper, is so good and satisfying! And after fully completing all the achievements, I can say for sure that it turned out to be one of the best indie releases this year. At least for me.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is all meat and no potatoes. It's short, but it's consistently fun the whole way through. This is honestly one of the best fighting systems I've ever seen. It's all about using the environment to isolate enemies so you can duel them 1-1. It's a lot less about perfect parry timing and a lot more about lining up a kick to knock a guard down the stairs.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En garde! is the biggest surprise of the year. I never even heard of this game until I stumbled on it while browsing steam. Yet it instantly captured my attention and became one of my favorite games of the year.You play as the swashbuckling Adalia de Volador, a duelist in Spain taking on a corrupt, evil count-duke who’s taken over the city. At the heart of en garde! lies its combat system, which is very reminiscent of Soulslikes. En Garde! distinguishes itself in a couple of essential ways though. It’s much more approachable than any soulslike I’ve played. It’s still difficult, don’t get me wrong, especially when you get to episode 3 and beyond, and it’s not afraid to punish you for making silly mistakes. Its combat is much simpler, making it easier to learn but harder to master.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A short but very fulfilling little adventure brimming with character and color! The writing goops on the extra cheese and makes for a very cute toony affair. The combat has a really fun and chaotic swashbuckling vibe, and is set through some very beautiful environments! the style is very eye catching and consistently had me thinking about how pretty it is when looking out onto some new villa or ocean view.My only piece of honest criticism is that i wish there were more! There is some replay value in the challenges and the arena, but i think there is a lot of space for more episodes and new levels later if the developer ever comes back to it! Definitely one of my favorite little adventures ive had in games recently!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Not the most narratively deep experience I've had, nor was it a very long one, but I have to say, there are few games that had me smiling all the way through from start to end. From the quippy dialogue to the over-the-top voice acting, everything about this experience just screams passion.If you see anything you like about this game from the trailer, you won't be disappointed. This game truly knows what it excels at and it doesn't overstay it's welcome. HIGHLY recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This short yet enjoyable game gently introduces players to the parry genre. The art style is stunning, and the map design is impressive. The combat system delivers as intended.If you're looking for a challenge, this might not be the game for you. However, if you prefer a parry game with more relaxed mechanics, this is the perfect choice.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Slapstick comedy, witty dialogue amidst a sea of games with poor marvel-esque comedy writing, and a brilliant protagonist all make En Garde aesthetically appealing in it's own very flamboyant way. Not prioritising style-over-substance, a strong set of core mechanics and cheesy tactics make for enjoyable gameplay and a decent challenge at higher difficulties. Each episode is replayable - important with it's short campaign, and offers arena challenges as well to really test your mettle. The default controller layout may take a little getting used to for die-hard sekiro-like fans.Consider nominating this for game of the year awards!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Quite good, but has a few prominent issues.First of all En Garde! plays by clear rules, which is how I prefer it. Animations are reduced to a visual cue so the player is never left guessing what they're supposed to do. For melee strikes these consist of three easily distinguishable elements: a counter-able attack (parry to punish), a parryable attack (parry to not take damage, but usually part of a longer attack chain) and an unparryable attack (dodge). The first two use the same color palette, but that's totally fine considering the player reacts to them similarly. Lastly there are also area of effect attacks which are communicated as well as a non-top-down 3d game allows for it (which isn't very well, you will often accidentally dodge into these areas).The game incorporates specific rigid-bodies and environmental elements as improvised weapons. Generally these inflict some effect on the target like a stun and fill their "stamina bar". The latter is similar to Sekiro's only rather than allowing for a strong finisher it applies an effect that causes the enemy to take two times the damage. There is plenty of incentive to actually use these makeshift weapons, which in turn gives the player a reason to actually use the arena. It also actively rewards proper playing with speed, which is always desirable.On top of the above you get access to something like a style-meter, which can be spent to perform a special attack. They kind of feel like they're "just there" to be honest and don't mix too well with the remainder of the game. The game also isn't anywhere near difficult enough for them to feel rewarding; instead they feel kinda clunky and slow.The game does have quite a few issues though. Visually it looks pretty good albeit a little generic. The character models are very ugly in my opinion, but fortunately the animations are decent. Shading effects are unsurprising. The writing is kind-of lazy; it's another one of those "quirky self-aware lol xd" scripts, and frankly it's just worn way too thin. The camera does have the occasional tendency to get stuck in close geometry as is the case of almost any third person game. Off-screen attacks become a bit of a problem as the game progresses and more enemies are thrown your way. Especially ranged enemies tend to result in taking poorly communicated damage. The combat rewards defensive play way too much for various reasons; the player is simply too fast and enemies cannot traverse vertical obstacles. Running away has the advantage of being able to use environmental weapons as you go. Dodging has a ridiculous amount of i-frames to the point of literally spamming it making you nigh untouchable. I wish you'd get punished more for constantly running away, but alas.Lastly the game falls for a very classic problem in this genre: having enemies designed in such a way they actively de-incentivize using the regular flow of combat. This isn't a problem inherently as it just forces the player to adapt, but that does mean it needs to be coordinated to actually be sporadic. Unfortunately the game tends to throw a lot of these enemies your way nilly-willy, making the game much slower in the process. In En Garde! these are, once again, enemies that throw a lot of unparryable attacks your way. These can hit you while you parry something else and must be dodged, hence the regular flow is disrupted by them. Some enemies throw nothing BUT these attacks, and they are the lowest priority target due to their inherent tankiness. Just spamming dodge while these exist isn't very fun, and I wish this was coordinated a little better.Overall really decent game. Well worth the pricepoint.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game :( Unfortunately, the combat - which is the whole selling point of the game - is just so clunky. I had to decrease to the easiest difficulty (which I absolutely despise that I had to do) and even then it still felt so messy. Dueling more than one enemy is borderline impossible sometimes - boss fights were absolutely maddening.  En Garde! gave me Sly Cooper vibes with its style and (very minor) exploration, but everything just falls flat or gets bogged down by clunk.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A charming, lighthearted game that doesn't take itself too seriously, and is refreshingly fun in doing so.Pros:1) Simple but fun and satisfying combat mechanics that are easy to pick up, but can be challenging to master.2) Silly, over-the-top comedy that is decidedly slapstick. This one is subjective, but if you don't mind this kind of humour, it's great.3) Short and sweet, not overstaying its welcome. The game does not try to artificially pad itself in any way, allowing for an experience that does not drag.Cons:1) Not a deal-breaker by any means, but i wish the character's mouths had been animated. I understand that this was a budget constraint, but i cannot help but wish this was there since the game looks so pretty.2) No variety in weapons. I would have liked if there were 2 or 3 options of rapiers, allowing for variation in strength/speed. It would have made things interesting and maybe boosted replayability value.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is a solid indie game I can recommend to people, especially if they love parrying stuff lol. If you do consider this game I recommend playing both story and the arena. The Arena mode is pretty fun with it's roguelike elements mixed in and it will also add more play time. Only doing the story is like 4hrs while doing 100% of the game is 15hrs (estimated).My Full Review:
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It's female Zorro minus the mask.  The devs put a lot of heart into its combat system. It's got the playfulness and fun elements in it with the amount of ways you can approach the fight. Despite it being linear and short (4 chapters only), the platforming is really fun to do. Swing ropes and poles, vaulting over obstacles like tables and crates. There are even challenges to complete and secrets to find.  Lastly, there's the Arena Mode. It's where you get to fight waves of enemies, while getting 1 out of 3 random buffs to spice things up.  Mouse and keyboard works just fine for me. All I did was switch the Parry RMB with the Dodge button.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has almost everything:- Great art direction- Amazing gameplay- The different interactions with the environment during combat (I wish more games would do that)- The writing is light-hearted and will put a smile/smirk on your face more than onceOn the bad side:- It is quite short- It doesn't run that great on the steamdeck (would recommend on a laptop/desktop instead)To the devs, keep pushing the concept of interacting with your environment, this is clearly a strong point of your game and it differentiate you from all the others soulslike games. I very much recommend this
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Cute refreshing artstyle and story for a game like this. Very timing based, very low HP and all about parrying and dodging. Mostly reliant on using the environment to your advantage in harder fights instead of straight swordplay. Short but never boring. Makes me feel like I'm good enough to try playing Sekiro again.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game and I hope that they make a sequel. There are secrets hidden in the levels but I am not sure how to find most of them, or what counts as finding them. The combat is pretty addicting. Uncharted-meets-Sekiro is a decent comparison.i suggest that you take a break if you are having trouble beating a boss and your thumb feels strained because it is possible to tear the muscle from using gamepad sticks too rough for too long.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Great tongue-and-cheek dialogue combined with an exciting fighting mechanic. I would love to see a sequel just to have more of the Zaida-Adalia repartée. The one thing about it is that the way the camera angle shifts in situations with multiple opponents sometimes makes me a bit seasick (though there may just be a setting I don't know about).
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Adalia, as well ans the NPCs have a lot of charm, the humor is good and not cringe, the nice art style is accompanied by fitting music. The gameplay is simpler than other your typical souls-like but it is a good thing - there's a focus on reflexes and crowd control in combat, not on a myriad of usable items or a wide range of switchable skills. There are no boring parts and uncovering the conspiracy is lot's of fun.My only complaint would be that the fights with Z presents an unnecessary difficulty spike. Maybe add more environmental challenges, aoe's etc. into the mix, instead of the fast red-to-blue attacks switch.I'm interested in what the next project of this developer will be.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I am conflicted about this game. The positives are impactful–En Garde! is reasonably priced, and it carries a well-developed aesthetic that incorporates not only visuals but also music, writing, and even game mechanics. The distant LOD models take on a colorful, blotted appearance to mimic the faraway details of an oil painting. The score features slick flamenco guitars and bouncy castanets. The Saturday morning cartoon villain sets up straightforward, humorous conflicts. And the fencing-focused combat mechanics do a great job of conveying our heroine Adalia’s effortless heroics. En Garde! is funny, cohesive, and empowering (at least initially). It sells the “swashbuckling adventure” theme convincingly, and for that, I think it deserves a thumbs up.However, the game falls apart halfway through its short runtime. As the number of enemies per encounter increases, you start fighting the controls more than the enemies themselves. One boss (who you have to fight twice) bugs out during a few phases. The secret "Points of Interest" are completely unrewarding to find. And the diversionary platforming segments turn into pace-breaking, clunky frustrations. At one point in Episode 4, I could not physically reach the final platform of a swinging sequence, but falling to my doom teleported me to the next checkpoint anyway. Finally, En Garde! also runs very poorly, despite its linear, small-scope environments.I did not enjoy En Garde! as much as I hoped I would. I had a blast playing its Steam Next Fest demo, but the full game ended up being annoying to complete (and surprisingly difficult). The overall package is still oozing with charm, though, so I think that it’s worth the price if you’re willing to put up with some jank.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game was a lot of fun.I refunded it and I don't think you should buy it.The reason you should skip this game is that the developers have been fairly unresponsive on the forums.  My question was posted in the forums as it's own topic and in the troubleshooting thread and the developers have totally ignored it for over a month.The question was about the sound menu and whether I could enable surround sound or switch to other modes aside from the default.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Action packed, colorful and delightful adventure! The characters are all incrdibly fun and will make you want to see more of the adventures of Adalia de Volador! Terribly fun to replay just like the demo, the arena mode, many challenges and secrets will give you more than enough reasons to replay and have fun with this little gem. The combat is fluid and allows you to be pretty creative which replay plays into the swashbuckling fantasy!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome and hilarious adventure, hiding some really polished fighting mechanics!The game always tries its best to make you feel like you're part of the world. And for me, it worked like a charm! There is an endless stream of verbal comebacks from your character to the enemies, humiliating them in the fanciest way possible. It will make you laugh, more than once.World building is solid, scattering lore points within posters or books, and even secret zones to reward you for exploring.Now, let me get this out of my chest...Fighting. Is. .Dynamic, fast-paced, satisfying and utterly diversified. The arenas all have a set layout, with various environmental hazards to use at your advantage. Over the course of a full playthrough, you find yourself experimenting with every prop laying around, setting up deadly combos with barrels and weapon racks, finishing it off with an explosion with a cauldron landing on someone's head. Due to the unique situations you get yourself into depending on the actions you take during a fight, while the game is fairly short (~3 to 5 hours for your first playthrough), you will find yourself coming back over and over to either explore, try out new fighting strategies, or take down the Arena mode in the higher difficulties for some randomised madness.Overall, it is an unique experience that I'm sure you will not regret trying out. Whether you are interested in experiencing a swashbuckling fantasy story, or would like a challenging action-packed adventure, there's something to for everyone.If you have played the demo and liked it, don't hesitate!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A REALLY charming action game in the vein of the PS2-era. The comedy is great, the combat is quick and encourages creative movement and interactions, and the challenge definitely ramps up as you face more and more crowds. Tons of personality on every level.Short but very sweet. Only downside is I don't super care for revealing the challenges/secrets after I've already done a level. I get there's an argument for letting the player play naturally through the first time, but each level can last over an hour. I'm just not going to take the time to go back and run a level again (atleast not without some kind of other incentive).
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I give En Garde! a GLOWING recommendation. It's genuinely one of the most fun action games I've played in the past 10 years. It's not a combo heavy spectacle fighter in the same vein as DMC or Ninja Gaiden. Combat is less about attacking everyone at once like a one woman army. Instead it's focused on dividing and conquering. Getting surrounded is a mistake. You will die repeatedly and be unable to drop specific enemy types. Enemies attack as a unit and will overwhelm you. When the game says, use your environment, it means it. Kick tables and barrels into enemies, ignite explosives, throw whatever you can grab in the arena, knock enemies down stairs or into weapon racks. Despite how simple the gameplay mechanics are as a whole, the combat is deceptively deep. Experimentation is rewarded greatly. You can knockout enemies very quickly with smart thinking in the moment. Attacking head on is the slowest, most risky approach. The combat is the highlight and I can go on all day about it. There's great enemy variety that aren't just there to fulfill a quota for number of bad guys. The enemy design is great because of their synergy in combat. They will force you to move and constantly parry and try to expose you to a quick easy hit. While you're parrying a normal attack, another enemy is attacking with an unblockable attack. There's no one way to approach these combat encounters.Regarding the presentation, it's a beautiful game full of vibrant colors. The lack of facial animations is a little awkward, but the eccentric personality the voice actors bring more than make up for this. There's a clever effect where textures at a distance are low-res which is typical of games to maintain consistent performance, but instead of being an ugly muddy mess, the textures take on an oil painting type look that's pleasing to the eyes.The campaign is fairly short (only 4 chapters), but it's extremely fun with challenging bosses and varied levels. It doesn't overstay its welcome. The writing is clearly humorous in tone and it's a treat. It's refreshing to play a game that doesn't take itself so seriously for once. Comedic writing is just as "artistic" as any dramatic or philosophical writing. There's an arena mode you fully unlock by the end that is honestly the most fun and challenging part of the game. It puts the combat front and center and tests your skills to the max.En Garde! is one of the top 10 best games I've played this year and I hope there are sequels. (9/10)
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly my game of the year, best day 1 purchase I have ever made. The combat is engaging and a delight to play, with humour that is light and funny without feeling forced. Excellent voice acting and soundtrack make you feel a true part of the world. I understand people's complaints about it being short, because I only wanted more of what I got.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay can feel very spammy and needing to roll for certain attacks is fine but the amount of enemies you fight at once that make you roll means its way easier to just spam roll instead of parrying which is more fun. The special attacks all do similar things with them all being kinda bland. The gameplay in the main campaign and most the arcade mode are to easy mainly because you can use explosives or your environment even against stronger enemies. Even ignoring that though the combat feels one dimensional, you play every encounter the same way.  The map design is really lame and extremely linear. None of the locations stand out as interesting ideas or done in a unique way. The levels also feel like you should have multiple paths or ways to enter, but their are invisible walls and doors you cant open. Replaying levels is pointless as you always play the same in combat and you cant approach which path you take differently.The characters are corny and not in a good way, it has weird dialogue that tried to be funny but i didnt find funny. It Never made me feel attached or interested in any of the characters. The art style is really solid, the character designs are great, and the animations are perfect. But it doesnt make up for the issues the game has. It isnt a bad game but it isnt great either, sifu is similar and is a better game in most ways. I would recommend playing sifu or sekiro over this game instead.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly charming and satisfying swashbuckling adventure that kept me rooted from start to finish. _childDocuments_.review: This a delightful hidden gem! A fun and challenging hack-and-slash with light platforming and extremely light exploration. The combat feels somewhat like a rhythm game, and the environmental "kills" can be quite fun and creative. Also very much enjoyed the humor (not usually hilarious, but always amusing). I played this right after playing a longer, more narratively serious game and this was exactly what I needed!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game has a lot going for it. It is so obvious the love the developers have for this. The vibe is great, movement is rather satisfying, and there are the seeds of a great combat system here. I also think the voice acting is outstanding. I think the game is let down in a few key areas though. On the combat, it's pretty fun, and it encourages experimenting with the environment to help you if you get overwhelmed. The problem is, if you try to run to an intractable object in the arena, sometimes your character will get yanked into an enemy's attack animation, and you'll be unable to move for a bit. I won't knock on the game's length too hard, but I will say there is a massive difficulty spike once you get to the final boss, and I legitimately spent over an hour on it. The lack of character face animations is also rather jarring, especially in cut-scenes, because they're done using static in-engine models as opposed animation. Maybe if this had been replaced with some hand drawn art, like a picture book, they would feel less jarring.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde is a short action adventure game focused on Adalia De Volador – a swashbuckler fighting the evil Duke & causing mischief for the city guards. It’s very well written – it evokes fun and jolly Saturday morning cartoon vibes. The character designs are beautiful & the animation work is outstanding. Graphically it’s a mix of stylized 3D models & oil backgrounds, which really fit the cartoony, wholesome aesthetics. All of it is fully voiced with exaggerated acting. Music is the final touch, full of orchestral sounds & fanfare you’d expect from a swashbuckling adventurous tale! The main meat of the game is the combat – at its core, it revolves around "simple" parrying Batman Arkham style, but the game expands it with the addition of environmental damage & fast movement. You can kick enemies into crates, lanterns & weapon racks; use chandeliers to dispatch a whole group or throw objects at them to stun them - all of it while you’re zooming around using ropes & vaulting over tables. There are bunch of different enemy types that require different strategies. It’s extremely fun and satisfying, but also very accessible thanks to a selection of difficulty options. The main story is split into 4 episodes, each around 40 minutes to 1 hour. There’s also an arena mode and other challenges if you want more content. Each level also has a plenty of secrets to find, so exploration is rewarding. I don’t mind that it’s short, not everything needs to be a 100 hour behemoth these days & it’s a perfect palate cleanser. If you’re looking for something to beat over a weekend or something to play in a quick 40 minute sessions, this one’s for you! It’s just a really beautiful, fun & well-made game. I’d let Adalia snatch my purse for some DLC episodes ;) Oh, and you can pet chickens!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: To make it short: Do not buy this game at the full price. It lasts for maybe 3-5 hours.It is a nice little game. The story is whatever. The graphics were good, audio, too. The gameplay is simple and fine, but a bit repetetive. It has a good standard difficulty. The price for this is far too high, though.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Tight controls, great combat, charming characters, what more do you want. - The story is short and to the point, it never outstays its welcome.- The combat is some of the best I have tried in years.- The campaign is easy but you can try the arena if you want a good challenge. Highly recommend this game, thank you Iron Pineapple
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is such a bright, confident, slick and effervescent experience. It's hard to believe this is the developer's first game! The dialogue is light but amusing and downright funny at times, effortlessly delivered by a cast that sounded like they were having so much fun. I did coo at some of the game's lighting and colour palettes; it's very pretty, reminding me of Sea of Thieves and Dishonored's stylised and evocative visuals.En Garde! is at its best when you're thrown into an arena against all kinds of henchmen and forced to use the environment to your advantage. Chandeliers, cannons, weapon racks, barrels, buckets, lanterns, lutes. The combat, and specifically the parry/dodge system, is simple and easy to understand and the various enemy types that are introduced, with their different attack patterns and styles, constantly mix things up and keep you on your toes. So much of it is improvisational and that's what makes the big fights such a riot. I mean, just watch this and tell me it's not magnificent:I played the game on Hard which really did put up a fight and required me to use every trick I could. I died  on the final episode so don't be fooled by the game's colour and whimsy! I particularly like that the game's episodes are almost standalone, opening the door to possible DLC episodes (fry-take-my-money.jpg). That is to say: I want more.My next stop is the Arena Mode which I expect to be a blast given the strength of the big chaotic sandboxy fights. En garde!Update: yep, the Arena Mode is ace. The enemies get a negative modifier per arena, and you choose a positive. As you progress the modifiers stack and harder difficulties have you tackling more arenas per run. Oh and you only get one life so there are some stakes :) The arenas are pulled randomly from the campaign which is great because they're all really well designed. It's basically En Garde!'s Greatest Hits.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I adored this game, my biggest gripe is there isn't more of it for me to play. I just finished my first playthrough, I found the combat to be a bit gimmicky but fun in a way that encourages experimentation and setting up environmental takedowns. The writing was charming and I enjoyed reading every interactable spot. Overall very worth the 20 bucks. Here's hoping we get a couple of dlc missions or something so i have more of a reason to come back.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: PROS :- Refreshing and original game. I had never controlled a Spanish female musketeer!- The lighting and colors are enchanting, and more than make up for the relatively low-poly 3D. Very pretty game that smells like spring in Spain- The gameplay is top notch, very reactive and nervous- The constant fights, fencing style, are interesting and satisfying, despite being sometimes almost too intense- Everyone talks all the time, reacts to the fights and cracks jokes as you play, which gives a lot of personality and makes the adventure very lively- Almost no cutscenes! Gameplay all the way, yay!- The game looks like a cute toy for children, but it gets HARD pretty quickly. Fortunately, several options are there to tune the difficulty, like automatic parry, and even straight out invincibility if you so desire!CONS :- The game is perfectly linear. Don't expect any kind of exploration, evolution, or any secret to find. For that matter, there's not even an inventory. The only goal is to move forward and beat guards, end of story.- Only ONE save slot! I wanted my wife to try the game, and so did she, but it meant destroying my savegame and starting all over. Now I have to finish the game (or get bored of it) so she can play...- You can't RUN! Sometimes you really want to escape a pressing group of guards, but you just can't run, how frustrating

_childDocuments_.review: En garde is a beautiful game full of charm and wit. The combat feels good and rewarding. You really get to use your environment to the fullest with it. My two biggest complaints are how they handled difficulty and the length of the game. It took me about 4 hours to finish it so it was kinda short, but the game-play itself was very fun. The game also isn't very hard. I played on the hardest difficulty all the way through and only encountered a few snags in the episodes. Their approach to difficulty is lowering your health pool which isn't very fun. All in all the game gets an 8/10 for me and I really hope they add DLC or something.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun! This game looked amazing the first time I saw it, and now that I finally got to play it I can confirm that it really is amazing. The combat mechanics are simple but really rewarding and fun, I especially adore all the different envirtoment interactions that become available in due time. On normal difficulty it's tough but never unfair, it really requires a lot of patience and not succumb to button mashing to get things done. Even if the game has a short runtime, it offers a lot of stuff for players to do afterwards, not only with more difficulty options but also many hidden objects and challenges to do in every level. I really recommend it to every fan of action games. I really hope there's a sequel for this game that can expand the concept even more, there's a ton of potential here

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a neutral option. _childDocuments_.review: En Garde is a short, cute indie game about swashbuckling adventures with a spanish duelist. The game has a cartoony art-style and a very self-conscious kind of humor, which i found very silly and adorable. En Garde is over in just a couple of hours (should take 4-6 at best), so it doesn't overstay it's welcome.  The game has some light platforming sections, with the "meat" of the game consisting of dueling your enemies and spliting bigger groups. The combats happen in "arenas" with a lot of enviromental abilities and interactions, with the sword-fights being a mix of parrying at the right moment and  some fast button mashing.The game has 4 episodes (levels), with the first serving mainly as a tutorial. After the main story is finished, you got some arenas to test your skills. The game also has a lot of secrets and in-level achievements for some replayability. If you want a realistic, serious game, you won't find it here. but if you love over-the top, cute, cartoony swashbuckling adventures, this might just be it for you.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the beginning. Witty, subversive. It nails it's tone very well.But as I got deeper into the game the cracks started to show. Enemies tracking across huge distances to make hits. Taking damage despite being out of range. Enemy AI cheats like moving to blindspots to attack and attacking through each other. I reached a boss who became an exercise in cheap AI behaviour and unfair damage. And I watched as the AI rubber-banded to undermine my successes.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A Swashbuckling action game with some platforming. If you've played the Batman: Arkham series, Sifu, or the older Assassin's Creed games then the combat is somewhat similar to that with some twists. The game heavily uses the environment and intractable objects to help you break enemies guard which then lets you damage them making combat more challenging and varied then the old AC or Batman. If you don't use your kick and/or the interactable environment then fights can be near impossible as enemies come at you nearly overlapping their unblockable attacks to catch your dodges. That said the game itself never felt cheap because you either have enough objects around to stun and break the enemies guard; or you  are fighting a smaller number of enemies that you can handle with dodging, blocking, and attacking. The game itself is rather short but since the core gameplay is solid and you have a rougelite arena mode that gives some replay value.Overall the game is a rather short and simple experience that doesn't overstay it's welcome and provides some fun and challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: Buy on sale. This game is incredibly short. If you pay over $20 you're going to feel a little ripped off.With that said, this game is really really fun! If you are familiar with classic Swashbuckling adventure stories like The Three Musketeers, Zorro, Robin Hood (or for you youngsters, Antonio Banderas Puss n' Boots adaptations) , then you are going to probably find a lot to love here. There's a decent amount of replay value for a game with only 4 stages. (three of which are pretty lengthy),  thanks mostly to the unlockable challenges/secrets and the core combat mechanics. Which are simple and addictive but also kind of complex as you get more used to them. Probably my favorite thing about the mechanics is all of the "Panache" moves you can pull off. Drop a chandelier on some dudes for an insta-kill. Kick barrels, tables, explosives, and all other manner of objects at dudes too. Do a flip over someone for some extra panache. Kick fools off of cliffs. There's dozens of things you can do in combat.Writing is also really fun and clever, with some excellent voice acting all around. The script is genuinely laugh out loud funny at times (especially if you have a familiarity with the swashbuckling genre).Music is straight-up on fire! Their composer 1000% nails the Spanish swashbuckling aesthetic with a mix of frantic flamenco guitars, baroque harpsichords, lush strings and other sounds that all fit perfectly in this fantasy Spanish setting.However, I feel like this game is only 3/4 of the way done. When I saw "Final Chapter" pop up after only a few hours of play, I felt a little defeated and sad. Like this game wraps up, just as it is getting going! And that is a damn shame. They could easily fir another 2-3 stages, and have a much more complete experience. Also Adalia seriously needs new player skins! I read the devs have no interest in DLC or expanding the game, which is also very disappointing to hear. Hopefully they will reconsider, because I could easily sink 20+ hours into this world.

_childDocuments_.review: Get it just to experience this amazing combat system! It can feel overwhelming and confusing but as you master the flow of battle it really clicks. The story mode is short, but really well done. You parry attacks and run around preforming acrobatics and kicking objects around to push the enemies against walls and down stairs, there are a few enemy types that require different strategies and it ends up feeling a little like Sekiro and Doom Eternal had a baby, as you run around managing things, prioritizing enemies, while interacting with attacks by dodging or parrying. I'm sure anyone can agree the gaming landscape could use more, focused and dense games. Even though you finish the story in a few hours, you want to jump right back in or the harder difficulties. There are secrets to find, and special objectives that reward replaying stages. Around halfway through you unlock an "arena". Its a sort of half baked rouge-like mode that puts you in maps from the story with random enemies and modifiers you unlock by beating stages. I don't have too much time with it yet, but the upgrades are pretty surface level, if the moment to moment game play wast phenomenal, this would be a pretty mid mode.Presentation wise, the graphics and sound design are wonderful, that you can tell just by glancing at the photos/trailer on the store page, and luckily it runs well too. The story is lighthearted and funny with memorable characters and lots of spoken dialogue (if i remember right every piece of dialogue is voice acted which is nice to see!)Overall this is another breath of fresh air for the gaming world, a short repayable game that would feel right at home on the PS2 (in the best way possible!) For 20$ its a steal and I recommend anyone who's interested to give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I really really want to like this game. The artstyle and story are cute and fitting, the basic idea is nice and the game as a whole is very charming. It's also short enough and interesting on the first look, that I'd be tempted to 100% it.The normal levels are playable, although the "story" is quite short with four chapters but the arenas and additional achievements are sadly just zero fun. The game is at its best in the opening hour, when there are not a lot of special enemies.Everything from the third chapter on, including arenas and achievements is filled with special enemies that have some different variants but all just end in a gameplay loop where you hit an enemy once and then strafe around for 10 seconds to find another opening. And I don't mean this in the fun "learn the pattern" way, it's just wait until the AI decides to get stuck on something so one enemy is isolated and then hit it.This was bad enough and zapped all the fun out of it for me. Even still worse is the fact that there's an achievement for finishing an arena without getting hit but the modifiers are randomized and their efficiency is all over the place. So you'd mostly re-roll modifiers for 5 minutes before each attemt, which is just plain boring.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Grade! is a fantastic game that hits me with some nostalgia of the 90's/early 2000's (particularly with the opening scenes of Road to El Dorado.) Adalia is an instantly likable character who is voiced wonderfully, the gameplay is a blast to play with while also being a challenge for someone like me who tends to button mash when he can. Using the environment as part of your tool kit is always incredibly fun and thematic. The soundtrack is catchy, really capturing the Spanish atmosphere here. The game oozes charm with its writing as well, not quite breaking the fourth wall, but definitely knocking on it at times, which is definitely the kind of humor I enjoy. What I also really appreciate is that this game is LINEAR. I point that out because in this age of open-world games, where many of them are big, open, and empty, having a set path to go on is a nice change of pace. There's nothing wrong with open-world games, but it's becoming a saturated genre in games. Sometimes I just want an objective and a road to get there with some places to smell the roses along the way. I don't always need a playground with all sorts of things to explore and take me off the main objective. (Yes, I get distracted easily at times.) My only real complaint as of writing this, and it might just be something on my end, is that I've had the game crash on me a few times. I launched the game in both options for Directx and I've had a UE4 fail message that crashed the game. I'm not sure if that's an issue on my end or if it's the game itself, but I wanted to make a note of it. En Grade is a fantastic game that bloomed has from a passion project and I cannot wait to see how the rest of Adalia's goes, and what Fireplace Games has in store for us next. If I'm being honest, I wouldn't mind an edutainment kind of game that helps with learning Spanish. Play the game! It's a fantastic experience that is well worth $20.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde is a lighthearted fencing game with a playful story and a vibrant world to match that spirit.The one-on-one combat is pretty fun, but the lack of depth left me uninterested after just a single playthrough. Most of the encounters aren't one-on-one duels but rather involve multiple enemies attacking you simultaneously, and I'm not really a fan of these gang-style fights. The game encourages you to use your environment to handle these crowd scenarios, which can be quite enjoyable on occasion. However, it often turns into a repetitive pattern of kicking or throwing objects at the enemy mob until you quickly engage in a one-on-one showdown with one of the enemies before the rest recover from their stunned state. The small enemy variety also didn't help in making it more interesting.I believe the developers had solid concepts but fell short of fully realizing their potential. In my view, it's a decent game that offers about 4-5 hours of enjoyment, but not much beyond that.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: “En Garde” is set in Spain and lets you play the role of a hero fighting against a conspiracy planed by the corrupt duke. The environment is beautiful to look at, taking full advantage of the setting of the game. Although a bit deprived of civilians which could have made the town seem a bit livelier, instead you have a lot of cute chickens running around. The world also features some lore drops scattered around and a few hidden locations to encourage exploring. Unfortunately, these hidden locations do not provide any benefits, so it is more for people going for 100%. The combat consists of swings with your rapier, kicks, parries, dodges and a lot of environmental interactions. The combat feels very fluid, with timings for dodges and parries being easy to see, but also the time window for reacting being big. The combat only gets difficult when multiple enemies attack you, which relentlessly attack which makes timing your moves much harder, especially when red moves are getting mixed into normal attacks, which cannot be parried. But the highlight of the combat are definitely the environmental interactions. Throwing chugs, kicking enemies into walls or down some stairs, throwing buckets on people’s heads, explosive barrels, vases and much more make experimenting with the combat mechanics much more enjoyable. Enemy variety is also great, ranging from goons, who can be easily defeated just by spamming attacks, bombardiers, and elite guards, who need the right moves to be defeated.  Another great aspect that they nailed is the humor. If you ever seen the movie “puss in boots” you will immediately recognize this sense of humor again. Lots of quips, sarcasm and jokes makes every encounter just a bit more fun and mixes really well with the gameplay.All in all, although it is rather short (I only needed three hours to finish it) I still enjoyed every single bit of it, making every cent I spent on it worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game's colorful environment and the funny, goofy characters. The charm of the humor, combined with a great soundtrack, adds to the overall experience. What really stood out to me was the attention to detail, especially in the variety of short interactions you have with enemies during combat. These interactions change depending on what’s happening and how you're engaging with your surroundings.The combat system is polished and well thought out. It focuses more on strategy than on reflexes, challenging you to isolate enemies and tackle them in small groups using objects or the environment. The movement is fluid – you can easily somersault over a table, throw an object, or swing at an enemy, all without any awkwardness. Honestly, it's one of the most unique 'dueling' gameplay experiences I've had.The game is divided into episodes, which I liked, but it's pretty short, (3-4 hours). While there are additional challenges you can do, I felt there could have been more content. The quality is definitely there, but more episodes or even a sequel would be welcome. I hope they add bonus episodes !Early on, you face a variety of enemies, each requiring a different approach. However, towards the end, it feels a bit repetitive with just more 'duelists'. Also, enemies often use 'red attacks' (unblockable). I would have liked to see a better balance between parrying and dodging.The frequent red attacks from enemies can make some fights less engaging. When overwhelmed by enemies, you're forced to rely on dodging and using the environment, as direct combat becomes less viable due to them spamming unblockable attacks. While this might be intentional, I would've preferred more opportunities to test my reflexes in direct combat.There are moments when you can get cornered by a horde of enemies and you will just die lmao, which can be a bit frustrating.Cool game! I recommend it. Get it on sale if you have a limited budget.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, cartoony, cheesy and bland - albeit done convincingly, no exploration, no secrets, no update, no puzzles. This game lives and dies on it's combat, and unfortunately it's screwed overall. It gives you lots of combat options and encourages you to use them (mostly fun but some arenas do drag on), and then throws in whiplash-inducing difficulty spikes that chuck all the options out of the window and force endless parry sequences and attack guesstimating in a way that makes Soulslike bosses seem almost tolerable. The fact that cheats are available easily in the menu indicates the devs knew the whole set-up was broken, maybe it should have been fixed instead of having godmode as a toggle crutch.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty awesome.The combat felt fluid and the level design was very satisfying to go through. I would also like to point out the voice acting and scripting for the game being absolutely peak, the humour is great and so is the delivery.Glad the devs end this game before it turns into a ganking hell. Its the perfect length for the games novelty to not wear off. So yeah if your fine with a shorter game than usual get En Garde.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: So I really like this game. Right off the bat, it has a very nice, bright art style and the gameplay is fun with you parrying, dodging, attacking and using the environment to your advantage. It's combat and such are pretty basic with you just basically whittling the enemy's guard down and hitting them a few times to make them fall, but it works. The main focus on combat, however, is the fact that enemies will attack you in two or three pairs sometimes if they can. You can parry one, but not all three! So using your environment like kicking crates, explosive barrels, even kicking enemies down stair cases to create room really helps. There are a few enemy variants, but nothing to really write home about. There are about 4 'bosses' and I use that in quotes because the bosses are kind of like regular enemies just with more health. There is no skill trees or unlockable equipment, but I think that is appropriate for this game, since it is mostly a fun game that isn't meant to be heavy on the whole 'I need X amount of EXP to get my next skill' or 'I can't wait to get my next sword.' What you get is what you get and for this game, I like it. The negatives I have is that it is very short. (At the time of typing this) I beat the story in 2.8 hours on medium difficulty and kind of only died a few times and only on the last boss fight. I will say that the combat does feel like it gets a little stale as you play, not really giving you much in terms of new attacks or anything, just giving you three skills and that's it.All in all, it's a fun game that has some pretty cool things to do, just wish it was longer and there was more to it. I would say this game NEEDS more meat on its bone. There is an arena mode, but that's just a wave mode to fool around in. It's not a terrible game at all and I think this game is perfect for people who just want a fun sword fighting game.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It looks great, sounds great, has a fun attitude, but the combat just isn't there. It's blocky and chunky in all the wrong ways; your character fails to glide between obstacles, enemies, and the environment in situations that all but demand effortless flow. Her movements are clunky while the enemies' are swift.Imagine if you were playing Absolver but the enemies had the agility of Arkham Batman. That's this game.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up loving swashbucklers such as Robin Hood, Zorro and the Three Musketeers, so when I tried the demo for En Garde I knew that I was going to buy it. It was a no brainer for me honestly. En Garde is a swashbuckler's wet dream, oozing with charm, charisma and great aesthetics. It's funny and exciting and when the combat clicks then it's a sandbox of possibilities. But the campaign is only 3hrs long… Yeah. En Garde’s biggest flaw is that it lacks content. I’m always for the “quality over quantity” approach but only 3hrs? Seriously? Sorry, but I can’t recommend it for 19,99€, it’s just too much. I’ve played indie games developed by one person with more content that what we got here. In my opinion, buy it on sale and I hope they plan to add more content. Eventually, I’d love to play a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, charming, silly little game about swashbuckling arena fights. It's colorful and has a great sense of humor, with great dialogue, animations, and fun combat. The main story is only about 2 hours long, but there are plenty of collectibles and optional challenges that afford it some replayability, as well as a true "arena mode" for additional randomized challenges. A really stylish game with a lot of heart. The combat takes a little getting used to since it's not a true "sword dueling" game, and you really need to use your environment to defeat encounters, but once you get the feel for it it's a ton of fun. Definite recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game for what it is, playing the Campaign on hard mode took me about two and a half hours, the gameplay was fun and engaging, and there was only a couple encounters that were frustrating based on enemy aggression/volume on hard mode. Overall though recommend you give the game a try. It's good fun and gives you a lot of flexibility with how to handle situations. The combat is based on the idea of isolating and separating enemies to create as many manageable fights as possible without being overwhelmed, it encourages you to keep moving and create distractions and use the environment to quickly dispatch, and disable enemies to allow you to focus on your target.Give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A swashbuckling soulslike-lite. Refreshingly lean and busywork-less combat and navigation without any items or RPG elements to manage and with healing after every major fight where it makes sense. The setting is great, too. Something different after all the doom n' gloom in other similarly working games. It's often quite funny, too.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A bit of a disappointment...It is repetitive. Same enemies. It is not really funny. Jokes are... not funny.Some moves are. Directly inspired from some old cartoons. That is the strong point of the game.Characters, including the principal one, are really  not interesting.The voice of the main character is kinda boring. Probably since what she says is not really interesting...She is not smart, trying to make smart comments that does not even end to be funny... It definitely lacks of a story writer but unfortunately came with one...Changing map interrupt dialogues. Ok, in fact, considering them, I may consider that become a good point. If only it was intentional.The game was really made to not offend anyone. To the point that I find it intellectually offensive. Such lack of subtlety. It falls flat here.The camera bores me at times. You try to escape or to interact with elements and it moves away.Exploration is a bit poor. Not really engaging.It reminds of Sifu that I did find a bit poor. En Garde makes me think it was not that bad finally.It is not that bad. It is just average or a bit lower than that all along.Buy only if you need to play all that sort of games.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet swashbuckling game where you play as a dashing Spanish woman in the time of galleons and musketeers! I enjoyed this one a lot.The combat is sort of like that of the Batman Arkham games, but with much tighter and snappier systems, and with a big focus on fighting resourcefully using what objects are in your surroundings. The fight mechanics are fun enough on their own but where they really shine is in how the level design supports them with all the extra stuff you can use against enemies. Kickable crates, throwable objects, cannons, bombs, chandeliers to drop and ropes to swing on, stairs enemies can fall down, balconies to kick them over, etc. It all combines with the fatigue and posture/health systems to really make you feel like a roguish swashbuckling hero fighting against unfavorable odds and getting one up on the dastardly villains with quick thinking, reflexes, and clever maneuvering. It provides a decent enough challenge on the default difficulty, as well, which was enough to add to the fun but not enough to become frustrating. In the later fights you'll really have to use every advantage against the enemy to pull out a victory. Boss fights are an extension of the normal mechanics and feel more like fun fight setpieces, but they're pretty good in that sense.In between fights you'll be doing some light platforming and exploration, finding some simple secrets, and going through some story scenes, which are quite charming. The main character Adalia's sudden shift from confident derring-do to bashfulness when interacting with her crush, a cool thief lady, was very cute. Adalia has a lot of banter in fights as well, with even the normal henchman enemies responding in turn, which adds a lot to the cartoony swashbuckling charm. Some of it is actually pretty funny, and the voice acting, for Adalia especially, has a lot of personality in its delivery. The platforming is fairly simple, and reminds me of old PS2 action platformers; the whole game kind of has that vibe, actually, which I mean as a compliment. Its also all very nice looking, there's some really gorgeous lighting and color design at times to compliment its hand-painted textures and stylized characters and environments. The music is exactly how you would expect the soundtrack to Spanish swashbuckling adventure to sound.The game only has 4 levels, plus an arena mode I haven't really touched yet (seems like it has some meat to it though), and I finished it in just under 7 hours. I think this is actually a strength, though, in that it ends up feeling more focused and polished than a longer version of the game would, and the gameplay doesn't really have a chance to get old. I always love to see smaller but incredibly focused games like this get made by accordingly small studios, and I'll certainly be keeping an eye on Fireplace Games to see what they make next.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A swashbuckling simulator about tickling Spaniards to sleep with a rapier. En Garde! is campy fun, but it's also very short, with four missions of ~45 minutes each. The first half is stronger than the second, and the poorly placed checkpoints in the final chapter mix very poorly with the reliance on repetitive boss fights. Chapter 3 ends and Chapter 4 begins with literally the exact same fight, except this time on a bridge--I didn't even enjoy it very much the first time! This is not the only such scenario.The sense of humor is basic but enjoyable for what it is, and the Dark Messiah-esq combat is fun when it's allowed to stretch its legs. The boss fights, though, often have very little to do with kicking and jumping around. In fact a few feel more like complex QTEs than sword fights. Having an enemy's stamina bar reset because I dodged rather than blocked is supremely frustrating, and I found it very hard to get a hang of dodging with the correct timing. But that's also partially my fault, since I insisted on playing with M+K (against recommendation). I don't love En Garde!, and I think $20 is a bit much for its length. But to be honest, I wouldn't have enjoyed anything more; I wasn't sad when it ended. But I don't regret playing it, either. If you're ever in a Three Musketeers kind of mood, I'd definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is it a beautiful game it's just as enjoyable as it is colorful. The mechanics are simple but offer enough options to really give your own flair to it. A true low skill floor with a very high ceiling for masterful impressive looking combat. Don't simple fight and parry with your rapier, but vault enemies to confuse them, kick crates to stun them and even kick them so they fumble down the stairs in a tizzy. You are free to really express your game flow as you like and the game rewards you for it. You do not want to just parry and attack to push your way through, once you find a flow of kicks, throws, dodges and jumps, you begin to fly around the groups of enemies with ease. Our fair Adalia clearly is best at dueling in a 1 on 1, so it's about managing to spread out your enemies and control the entire field with her assortment of actions. And this is all only after completing the tutorial. Please get this game, it deserves it.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a most epic game ever made from epic music to intense fencing action and using anything you can get your hands on to beat your enemies absolute  masterpiece and main character and her charm is also adding another level of humour into this franchise 100 percent a game for those that Love Zoro and Spanish culture and fencing plus enjoy an epic comedy

I'm not going to vote it down because I prefer keyboard n mouse...Graphically, runs fine, the art style is colorful, nice aestheticNo technical issues in the short time I played it, it's just not for me
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

Let us ignore the blatantly homophobic ones and focus on those complaining the combat is too hard and contradictory. Rest assured dear potential player: these people are bad at the game, as like any game with a main focus on combat, it has simple mechanics but with a learning curve. And even if you don't like it, you can turn yourself invincible in the options, because the devs are cool peopleIf you think this might interest you, it will
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: In a year of great games, En Garde! is one of those great games.• Great action combat system• An amazing art style• Music that fits the style of the game• Fun level design• Great voice acting (Thanks for including this Fireplace Games)The game can be hard at times. I'm someone who has beaten Elden Rings twice, the final fight in En Garde! took me over an hour.I also feel a little sorry for the devs. I feel like they chose a bad release date. So many people are going to skip over this game due to the crazy release schedule.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Terrifically fun game, perfectly pleasant and polished to an exceptional sheen. I've never played anything that gave me the feeling of a swashbuckling adventure like The Mummy or Hook quite as well as this, the dynamism of sprinting around environments for better positioning while chucking items at enemies or kicking them downstairs to thin the crowd and tilt the favor of exceptionally executed dueling mechanics in my favor. It's short, sweet, often funny, frequently very pretty, and one of the best pleasant surprises I've played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully stylish game about swashbuckling, not many of those are out there and this one nails it perfectly in my opinion. The combat isn't exactly challenging and it is somewhat simple, but it does allow for fun shenanigans. I'd argue that's the whole point, that it's just fun to mess around with. The story is charming and just long enough to not overstay its welcome. I personally am in love with a game like this, a fun sandbox to mess around in with silly quips that keep you entertained.I do suggest tempering your expectations a little bit, though. The game is short, as I've beaten it in only 2 hours (wouldn't refund it anyway). I've yet to try the arena mode past what the demo offered, but it seemed fun with its gameplay modifiers. With the game being only $20, you get what you pay for here. I also encountered very little in terms of bugs and glitches, which is always a plus.Overall, this game is filled to the brim with love and charm that makes me wanna keep coming back just so I can kick a lackey off a bridge. It's very well polished and has a good gameplay loop. If you like what you're seeing, I'd suggest picking it up and trying it out. It's very modest with its presentation.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely heartwarming game. Colourful and vibrant art design with lighthearted humour. The combat system is satisfying once you meld with it. The flow of the game is similar to a rhythm game in which it becomes second nature to dodge, parry or attack. I don't think every game needs to be a 100 hour venture if the core concept is executed well. However, I do think its slightly short with the potential the game has to offer.

In fact, when I initially heard about the game, I assumed it’d feel like someone took the fluent but pretty simplistic combat systems of games like  and , and built an entire game around them. Faced with a powerful enemy, you can throw a bucket on their head, beat them up until they lose their balance, then kick them into a weapons rack to knock them out.  – but you absolutely need to be willing to experiment with the environment to enjoy the game! If you play En Garde! like any other spectacle fighter and just mash the attack button, you may be in for a very frustrating time.The game currently contains a somewhat .
