_childDocuments_.review: Very good! The combat is extremely slick and feels great. The writing is smart and funny without being annoying, and is supported by fantastic voice acting. I really enjoyed my time with this. There is a pretty steep difficulty curve near the end, but it's a satisfying one to overcome.However the performance is not great, I've seen much better looking games perform significantly better.The full price is also a little high, so I'd get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet game that is pretty much everything you want it to be. Genuinely made me laugh and the combat is a fun mix of simple and easy to get creative and approach in lots of different ways. Just a straightforward swashbuckling adventure that makes you feel like Zorro. The mechanics encourage panache and moves at enjoyable fast paced. Though the plot is simple the characters are likable. The auto targeting is a bit buggy and the game in general could be cleaner and smoother but for the price and the size of the team it is more then good enough.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: You ever wanted to be a Spanish lady with a might sword? Of course you have.This game is just a damn good time, the combat varies from delightfully silly to aggressive and strategic.The only places where this game falls short are:1. The core plot is meh, but I get the sense the game and I were having too much fun being silly to really care. Just don't go in expecting something deep :D2. Honestly, as tight as the combat is, there are times where it feels a little sticky and what I didn't intend ends up happening. I quite consistently struggle to pick up projectiles for throwing at enemies, but I wonder if this is soemthing tied to framerate as I tend to miss more when the framerate is low. Speaking of...3. Steam deck performance, even on the lowest possible setting, can get a little choppyThankfully none of the above issues are really deal breakers, it's still a damn fun time and the arena mode is kinda addictive  NGL :PBravo, Fireplace Games!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Puss in Boots with human characters.Combat is incredibly fluid, I love all the different ways you can use the environment to fight the enemies.The graphics are really nice and the characters are likeable. The game's got a lot of charm to it!Literally my only complaint is what most people complained about when it came to Portal: there's a bit too many loading screens. But they are thankfully really quick. And having short, but optimized levels is always better than having long, laggy ones.10/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful little game! Just about the only criticism I can level against it is that it's short, but I thoroughly enjoyed my time with the roughly 4-hour story and the additional arena mode. The combat feels wonderful and tricky, the game forcing you to split up grouped enemies by giving enemies stronger attacks once they have you surrounded. The array of different buffs enemies have and statuses you can inflict on them means everything requires a different approach, and no arena repeats itself throughout the runtime. If you're a fan of swordfighting games, this is a gem of swashbuckling combat.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is truly impressive, especially when you consider that this game started out as a student project! The visuals, music, and writing is extremely charming and the gameplay does a wonderful job making you feel like a swashbuckling hero in the vein of Antonio Benderas as Zorro (or Puss in Boots). The game is fairly short, but the price is more than fair. The game is also getting new content updates pretty regularly. The devs really gave us something special with "En Garde!" and I cannot wait to see what they go on to do next. 10/10 will swasbuckle again.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely recommend it. It's a very fun game for only 17€, it's not too hard, not too easy. The fights can be challenging, you need to get used to the parry mechanic and everything. I had a very hard time against the bosses and against certain type of guards, but once you understand how to utilize your surroundings, know how to break the ennemy's guard with the right items and know what skills to use, the fights become less frustrating. I wish it had more chapters... I finished the game in 4hours. Hopefully they add some DLC later with new maps, new skills, characters and maybe new modes too, that'd be sick. (maybe I'm dreaming but it's a good dream) It's definitely one of the most fun games I've ever played in a long time. And the graphics are so pretty, everything is so colorful and bright, I love it! The humor is also a nice touch, I had a fun time playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the Zorro game I've been waiting for all my life. A really excellent swashbuckling game. The combat feels weighty and precise, which is no small achievement. The parry window is tight enough to be challenging but generous enough that you rarely feel like you got screwed out of a good parry. Using the environment is mandatory, at least on hard.On hard, the campaign took me three hours. I had played the demo before. It is a short and sweet game, which is how I like them these days. The story is great; it won't make you snort your coffee into your nose but it's charming throughout and the voice acting is solid. There are some technical issues - the camera does not love being in tight spaces and you can get hit a little cheaply when you're in corners. The platforming is functional but not hard or terribly interesting, but it's a small portion of the game meant to give you a breather between combat sections.This game is good. You should buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is basically an endless stream of quick-time events. You wait for a visual hint and press the appropriate button (dodge, parry, attack) while side-/backstepping. I guess that's what most fighting games ultimately are about, but usually there is more variance and the gameplay is smoother and faster. In this game it feels like you go from one location to the next, fight a few enemies in a narrow space with quick-time events, rinse and repeat. Nothing in between. The graphics are colorful and look ok, but there is a strange flickering grain shader I couldn't get rid of, plus for some reason this game stresses my gpu a lot (though the framerate didn't drop below 60 fps).I don't get the massive amount of positive reviews. If you really like fighting games it may be worth checking out, but I found the game very boring after a short while.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: it's a good idea for a game but the combat is a little too janky to actually be fun. enemies often have weirdly good tracking where their attacks will hit you from further than feels natural, you don't have a lot of i-frames on your dodges or during parry, which often leads to you getting hit with no recourse while dealing with something else, a lot of the enemies aren't that fun to fight and despite supposedly being about being clever and using your environment, there aren't a lot of situations where you can actually use the environment to actually defeat the enemies, just stun them so you can keep stabbing them.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shorter game which was honesty a breath of fresh air. It's probably the first game I've completed in a while and of course as everyone else has said it was very colorful and charming. one negative thing I will say is I'm bad at the game so it was a little annoying to skip the dialog every time I would die.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of the one-off games from Gamecube/PS2 era.It's a lot of fun, has some challenging boss fights, and has some silly writing that doesn't take itself seriously. It's also subtly LGBT and written well in that regard. Very cute.It's a short game, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. It doesn't overstay its welcome and has an arena mode if you're looking to continue the duels.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: GAME OF THE YEAR 2023.Do not insult the developers of this game and try to compare it to another game.This game deserves its own category!To the devs: do you know how long I've waited for a game like this to finally exist??? Too long! Thank you for giving me this absolute gem of a game. 11/10. Would play again and again and again.I have no doubts the likes of Zorro and Inigo Montoya would have loved to hung out with Adalia de Volador.This game rewards you greatly for playing stylishly. The more you use your environment, fight stylishly, and avoid smashing the attack button, the more whoop ass you unleash on your enemies!For those who love anime, think of "Sakamoto Desu Ga?" SUPER STYLISH.This video game has the best voice acting and the best one liners i've ever heard out of a video game in a very long time. You will not regret this game.11/10. Masterpiece. This game receives my prestigious "Best of Library" Award. Park this game right next to Skyrim, Borderlands 2, and Baldur's Gate 3 on the top shelf.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: One off the better games that I have played of late. The controls I think are tight and responsive, wish you could pick up everything like pillows saw two and wanted to throw one. I would not be apposed to  a second one maybe some character customization. I Like that its similar to older games no penalty but death to the player and you know where your mistakes are.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished the main game and not even having touched the arena mode yet, I can recommend this game. Charming dialogue and character interactions, good soundtrack, SOLID combat system that will introduce new steps and mechanics as you go with the final battle really being like the final exam, preparing you for the arena mode where you'll likely spend the bulk of your playtime after doing the 3 hour story. Yes it is about 3 hours but it is concise and it doesn't overstay its welcome. I was satisfied having reached the credits and I do not regret my purchase. Check it out if you want some good combat and an upbeat world to do it in.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most charming games released in the last decade! It oozes with character and humor and aesthetic in its depiction of a culture rarely explored yet executed with love. Gameplay is riveting and unique--even challenging at points--with a plethora of styles and options to discover as you swing and dance with your blade across the battlefield to the quips of lackeys and goons falling at your feet. While the adventure of "En Garde!" may be short, its sweetness will have you enthralled and wanting more!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, colorful game with a love of life and good humor. It doesn't take itself too seriously, but it *does* take the gameplay seriously. Very satisfying to nail a combat sequence and has a fair bit of replayability. Not too long, but not every game needs to be - En Garde! respects your time and gives you your money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: well I beat it on hard (Highest Difficulty) in 3 hours in 1 sitting, Way to short of a game for $20, few things i did not like and few things i didPros - Fun Art style , Easy To Run/Play , Arena Mode.Cons - Animation lock (If you parry you can get hit by other enemies while you are stuck in parry animation, Same with picking up objects you get stuck and you can't dodge or parry),To short for the price, Enemies have 2 types of attacks (white Attacks) which you can parry and (Red Attacks) unparryable and at later levels of this short game enemies spam Red attack causing you to spam dodge which is boring, If they had more white attacks would be more fun and felt like a true Duelist parring multiple strikes, Repetitive - you can only kick people and spam the same basic attacks or throw things, no holding down attack no combos/ hit counter, you get 3 Abilities but they feel underwhelming and if you enter a loading screen you lose your whole yellow bar you worked for, not a massive problem but you HAVE to play the female lead, she has a brother they could have added as a playable or for coop but missed opportunity, Little bit of woke stuff in this game if you don't dig that, Feels like it was made for kids.i know I put a lot of cons but I feel the game has a charm, especially if you dig Zoro. good stepping stones for a 2ed game but they really need to push more next time unless they were aiming for a simple PS2 Esk Era game feel.Final Rating - 4/10 ( get this on a massive sale $10 or less)
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: An endlessly charming and inventive take on swashbuckling duels that is well worth the price of admission.The combat hinges on you abusing the terrain and environment to compensate against overwhelming numbers, enemies have no qualms overlapping attacks and covering for their partners openings, some will even behave differently if they aren't your current target. This may take some adjustment but you are not meant to be self sufficient, you are not meant to be capable of beating multiple soldiers head on. You are meant to cause whatever chaos you can to isolate a soldier and buy time for a duel.It has some minor issues, your soft lock will struggle at times when there are multiple enemies or intractable objects nearby, resulting in you swinging and kicking at targets you weren't intending to hit. I can forgive that though since soft lock targeting seems to be impossible to make reliable (even Bayonetta can't escape this issue) and the game is already urging you to avoid group fights.The distances enemy attacks can travel to hit you can feel inconsistent at times, it seems to be if you didn't explicitly start a dodge during the wind up phase of an attack, they will travel as far as they are allowed to. So there are moments where you're running away from a group and someone manages to slide up and take a whack at you.I have some very specific issues with the grenadiers and captains but nothing that makes those enemies a complete chore to deal with.The game is admittedly a bit short but for a product with such high production values relative to the price tag, the length doesn't bother me. The game dishes out it's enemy roster and mechanics in a natural progression, nothing felt underutilised or overdone by the time I hit the credits. Only wrinkle I have on this matter is that because levels are framed as a serialised episodes of a Zorro cartoon, you may not even realise you're in the final episode because of a lack of narrative build up.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes me sad. The visuals are absolutely fantastic. Every location has something different to offer and there's tons of details in the environment. The animations are great, the sound is good. But that's where the list of good things end.The gameplay is some of the most horribly balanced garbage I've ever seen. The basic mechanic of sword fighting is really nice, but the way it is used is frustrating af and as unfair as it could possibly get. Let me explain...There are around 5 types of enemies in the game, each with a fixed set of attacks which you easily learn as you play the game. Individual enemies are pretty fair I would say. But the problem is that you rarely fight just one enemy. And that is where the problems start. You have to face off against hordes of enemies dozens of times. This is clearly by design, as this forces you to use the environment more. But when the game's idea of making something more difficult is to just throw more enemies at you and give the boss more HP, then something has got to be wrong with the core design. Every time you finally manage to make your way through a wave, there is another wave coming in. And usually, you don't get a checkpoint for that. There's 6-wave bosses, with each wave potentially taking several minutes.  If you should die, you have to do it all over again. And because you're "forced to use the environment", the gameplay usually involves just kiting enemies for several minutes and trying to kick something at their face until you break their stance. This quickly becomes a drag. It doesn't help that there's not a lot of enemy variety.One would expect that with good timing, you would get through things easily. But you can't, because there's a mechanic where enemies will help each other and attack you with attacks you can't parry. So if you're surrounded by a group of enemies, you are essentially forced to run away. The "perfect stance" mechanic, where enemies regenerate their HP if you fail to perfectly react to one of their attack, makes this even worse, because you have no chance to beat these types of enemies in a group. Like I mentioned before, the environments look really great, so it's a shame that the "story" was as shallow as it is. There is no suspense, no mystery, no nothing. It feels like an afterthought. And I wish they had put even remotely as much love into it as they put into the environments, because as it is, I started skipping dialogues (which I never do) because I simply didn't care and wanted it to be over with. I have no idea how this game has such good ratings. There are so many issues with it.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Fights in this game are mostly counter-oriented. Basically, you can only attack armoured enemies by throwing stuff at them, kicking them into anything or counter their attacks. They are otherwise immune to your dagger attacks. These types of enemies are very common. Enemies in fights are locked on so if you fight multiple of these armoured soldiers parrying is sometimes not possible. I found myself often rolling on the floor or running away to "align" or scatter these enemies. On top of that, I admittedly did not understand immediately, why the first boss was seemingly invincible. Turned out you must react all the time correctly to what the boss does. If you do not do that once, the boss regenerates one of his three health bars to full. React --> stun, dagger attack, repeat or throw/kick --> stun, dagger attack, repeat. The fighting aspect is around 90%+ of the game. I dislike this system and find it boring. There is no dynamic or freedom on how to approach the situation, no own decision-making given that there is always only one correct choice and it's always a reaction/ counterattack, which strongly limits pro-activity. Sorry but throwing and kicking stuff to stun enemies for a moment is not how I imagine a game about sword fighting. It's more a game of stunning opponents. The basis of the battle system creates a lot of constraints and does not reflect the free-spirited, charming setting of the game.Other ideas are pretty good. I enjoy the theme including the music, the visuals, the parkour-aspect and the playable character. The story and humour are light. The first 30 min. of the game were quite enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a hidden gem. it's short and sweet, straight to the point, the combat is good and the characters are funny. the story wasn't anything in depth but sometimes it's not necessary to have that for a game. all around the game was just filled with jokes while being a badass basically, pretty cool. i got it for $11 and it's a linear, game with souls elements and a little bit of platforming across the areas. the devs did a good job with this one, the art is nice, it runs well and it takes place in a cool area. the enemy variety is nothing crazy, and you will probably catch onto their attack patterns fast if you've played other spectacle fighters and/or souls games. definitely check this one out if you've been thinking about it, worth the money!!!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is super charming.It's a lighthearted swashbuckling sword fighting game with fun combat and genuinely funny dialogue, there's heavy Zorro and Pirates of the Caribbean vibes. Each combat arena is like a big slapstick sandbox, it's all good stuff.I see some reviews comparing it to Dark Souls, it's nothing like Dark Souls.The parrying and dodging mechanics are nice and simple and satisfying to pull off, you simultaneously feel overwhelmed and empowered, that's not an easy thing to pull off but they did it.I really liked it apart from the final boss, it felt like a massive difficulty spike which took me over an hour to beat. If you're having trouble beating the boss, try to ignore the extra mobs who spawn in and just attack the boss, a cutscene will trigger when he's beaten.Overall a very polished and fun game, i'm interested to see what the developers do next.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic swashbuckling adventure. En Garde! Knows exactly what it is and doesn't waste your time showing you what it is capable of. The story is simple and to the point, and full of charm. The tone and characters are excellently funny. The gameplay is extremely engaging. Never have I seen a sword-fighting game with more seamless and creative environmental interaction. More importantly, the way the game encourages you to play it is the most fun version it could be; doing somersaults off tables, kicking barrels into enemies and timing perfect guards. The game is plenty replayable, its levels have little secrets sprinkled throughout and the combat encounters are chaotic, it's just a shame it is pretty short because I would love to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: fun, short game with a silly story that is almost disney-esque. however, the default difficulty is far overtuned and feels more like difficulty for difficulty's sake, which is coming from a player who has beat most soul-likes. set the mode to easy and take off infinite guard bar setting for a far less frustrating experience.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is a really fun, visually stimulating game with witty humour, creativity and light-hearted action at its forefront. The theming alone was enough to get me to play and I am really glad I did! The combat is challenging but in a very soulsy "learn the pattern" way, which is fun and challenges you to get into the rhythm of fencing.It's really sweet that there are accessibility options built into the game, and based on the games swashbuckling themes and aesthetic I think that's really smart - kids would probably want to play this game, but may find the intricacies of parrying quite hard. The only complaints (sort of) that I have are:1) It's pretty short :( And feels like it could be expanded so much more. But the price is fair for what you get!2) SPOILER: I am not a huge fan of fighting the same bosses again for a sort of mega-boss-gauntlet at the end of a game. Some people probably enjoy that but having just defeated Zaida (which was quite a long fight) and then immediately fighting her again was a slog.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Eh.I like the art style. I like the setting. I like the combat to a point. I hate how the art style and setting are totally wasted. I hate that it's only 3 hours long. I hate that the combat is so poorly thrown together at the end. I hate that the game feels like a lot of wasted potential.The game looks great, but it's just repeating assets in small rooms and hallways. The game essentially has four or five small spaces that repeat over and over.Something that really sucks about the level design in this game is the accessibility first approach. What I mean is you'll often finish a combat arena and be in a big room with 5 doors. They all look identical, and nothing in the environment was designed to help guide you to the right one. The solution? A big, giant white arrow literally pointing to the door. You know, you wouldn't need to have a big, giant white arrow literally pointing to the door if you took greater care in how you designed these rooms and hallways.You find little notes around the levels, but nearly all of them are worthless. They don't provide any insight into the region, the time period, the setting, nothing. It's stuff like "Oh look, the recipe for chicken soup!" Why is that even a collectible note? It seems like such an obvious and easy way to engage with players but I guess it didn't really dawn on the developers. They went with the "pointless information of no value" approach. Occasionally it'll pertain to a character or the "story" but getting those means risking getting more "Oh look, the recipe for chicken soup!"The combat is pretty decent, but it really falls apart in the end. I found the game on the normal difficulty to be very easy, but the final boss room has a difficulty spike so egregious I have to assume it's unintentional. The problem is the way enemies will stack their attacks. If you need to counter an attack in this fight, your counter is going to leave you wide open to be hit by one of the other enemies. And you will. So you just dodge. You're going to be dodging over and over and growing increasingly bored and tired while desperately waiting for some minor opening to maybe knock an enemy back. It's a fight of attrition and it's just so unfun and tedious. Any goodwill the game built up was thrown away in this fight and it soured the experience so much it's largely the reason for the negative review. It doesn't feel difficult because they planned for it to be difficult, it feels like it's difficult because you're fighting the game's mechanics. It's just "what if there was a LOT of enemies in the room?" That's it.I will again mention that it's three hours. Just barely long enough to put completing it outside the refund window. I'm not conspiratorial, but if I was, this would be very suspicious. $20 is just too high for this game. It has four levels. Resident Evil 4, Dave The Diver, Cuphead, Chasm, Moonscars, Return of the Obra Dinn, Celeste, and Hyper Light Drifter are all $20. This game's length, depth, and overall quality is not on par with any of those games. I won't even list all the games that are even cheaper that also offer more length, depth, and quality.The story and characters are pretty uninspired and uninteresting, but I guess when the game is only three hours it's hard to create something memorable. Except for all the other short games that did it, I guess.Overall, I'm pretty disappointed and irritated by the game. It doesn't justify its cost whatsoever, and it feels incredibly under cooked. If this had been around 10 hours, with 8 unique levels, with more enemy variety, and with more thoughtful combat, then it would be fantastic. But as it is right now, it feels much more like four demo levels in an otherwise incomplete game, being sold at the same price point as many highly polished and complete games.

_childDocuments_.review: after completing both the story and arena modes I can say that overall the game is really good. the only real complaints I've got is the camera and being able to throw things through walls, but even those things don't take away from the fun. it is a pretty short game but I don't like counting that against it if the game is fun for all the hours I've played it. I'm just hoping that there's more for this game in the future because I do want to play it more. well worth the money

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun and fast-paced game. Levels are supper linear but that is okay so far in my time playing. Making use of the boxed, lanterns and bombs make combat fun.I wish there was some sort of a progression system where you feel her get more powerful. All you get is unlock a skills after each chapter. You only gain the yellow energy for skills by defeating normal mobs. The game really forces your to run around and experiment first before button mashing.Due to the speed of combat performance and stability matter. Currently the game runs more poorly than expected with quite frequent fps drops.Worth checking out still but I would like to see it optimised. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. The story is alittle on short side. I wish there was more missions. This would also help the character & world building. The characters are very vibrant. The soundtrack of this game is amazing. This game is best played on a leisure pacing to fully enjoy the experience. The characters & story are kept simple which is in my opinion fine. I think the game main selling point is it's game-play. The combat in this game is really the best feature about the game. The game mechanics though simple is quite intricate. There is NO annoying stamina system like in other games to slow the game's combat unnecessarily. There is quite abit to learn. If you interested in challenge runs. This game is also really good speed-running as it is a short game. This game has good replay value in both story & arena mode. You can go back and play the story do challenge & secret you missed. Arena mode is really quite the underrated gem. Arena switches things up with the modifier system. This make each arena play-through unique and it is just pure combat fun. I think the price is quite fair considering the high price on newly release titles these days. Not to mention, some of these newly release titles are released in a buggy and sometimes unplayable state. I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly short game with very enjoyable fights (till you want to get no hits arena achievement). Campaign with very simple and self aware story only has 4 episodes and could be gone through in smth like 3 hours. But there is also arena mode which provides a lot more replayability with a bunch of distinctly different arenas from campaign with different mixes of enemies and modifiers. Music is absolutely tailor made for this kind of atmosphere and adding even more fabulousness to it. Graphics is very stylised and also does a very neat trick to both save processing power and add to atmosphere - at distance  (I think it is how this type of paint is called). You see watercolour bridge painting and after going towards it for few seconds it becomes 3d location you go through.Gameplay is fencing with a tiny bit of platforming with very linear path lightly hiding few secret. There are only about 5 moves and 3 skills but with the amount of interactive objects and combinations it becomes quite the spectacle and a bit of a puzzle to use them in order to go through fights. Enemies rarely attack one by one and further you go - more would combine their attacks covering each other, calling for lots of distractions and efforts to divide them, singling out stragglers to finish off before others run you through.Also game is very kid friendly, since you do not kill anyone - you could hear enemies lazily playing dead and bantering with both you and each other.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I slash, I parry, I kick, I riposte, I stab, I kick, I throw vase, I kick, I jab, I kill and kick some more. Most fun I have had in a game for a while, I even enjoyed it more than . I wish there was more content. Please developers I will pay you.   “plays better with a gamepad”, but the keyboard controls work great.Adalia De Volador has a strong sense of justice and has an infamous reputation among the guards. However! Her sword has been stolen by a masked individual, someone called El Vigilante, you cannot leave your trusted sword behind, right?  is short, it has four episodes each with their own self-contained stories but with an overarching narrative regarding the villainous scoundrel, the Count-Duke. I thought “Count-Duke” was a bit too pompous and thought of it as a joke meant to deride an arrogant noble, but no, this was an actual title, used by a real person, who looks suspiciously similar to the character in , attention to detail like that is very commendable.However, the game is rather silly and is aware of it in a way that I find endearing. I did not always love the humour, but it has its moments. What I found myself really loving was the banter and quips during combat, which was a bit surprising, but it's written in a fun way that is hard not to appreciate. It shows off Adalia's bravado, which is quite fitting for a swashbuckler, but it also adds some personality to the city guard.This game is beautiful and colourful, with a nice variety of locations to explore: the streets of an unnamed town, Spanish Villas, gardens and more. No episode is visually quite like the one you played before, but they do thread on some of the same ground, such as streets, or luxury housing.  also fades out objects in the backgrounds in such a way that it is more reminiscent of a painting than a video game. My small complaint would be the size of areas, they are very small, at times a single arena, which can feel limited and tedious, but if it makes the game better optimised then I do not mind, even if it makes the world a tiny bit less immersive.  Characters have all sorts of personality to their design, contrasting colour, panache, it is very stylish and feels era authentic. Same can be said for the enemies, though their designs are more austere which makes it easy to tell when a more dangerous foe appears such as a French Duellist.What really brings all this to life is the animations, and the accompanying sound effects. There is an exaggeration to everything that is captivating, be it from enemies slipping on puddles, to falling down sets of stairs or trying to balance on a ledge, it looks great. That is not even mentioning the confidence of Adalia’s duelling which is just so satisfying to play especially when you get the gratifying effect that signals that you broke someone’s stance. How about they also add a great soundtrack filled with flamenco guitars and tons of diversity to accompany areas, bosses, and the like. It is fantastic and fits extremely well with the game, and really heightens combat encounters even further. Standout tracks would be , , and . If I am being honest, I could have mentioned most song here, since I did like all of them, a lot, glad I own the soundtrack. In  you will mostly be fighting, but there is also some light exploration and platforming, if it is not required to progress you are rewarded with some nuggets of lore, or a secret. Nothing is difficult but these areas of downtime are especially fun when you are rushing through, darting past the few enemies that guard the room, or streets, as they exclaim in surprise, and as you make your way to your goal. However, combat is the name of the game, it is a joy to play, but if you do not want spoilers on the mechanics, then do not read the following section. As you make your way through levels you will encounter enemies, sometimes this will be in an arena, and in other cases they can be avoided. At its core it is simple, you can block most attacks, and you must dodge the rest. This together with the animations and effects is enjoyable on its own, and make for some fun duels, but this game is not about being a fencer. This is about swashbuckling! You rarely fight enemies one-on-one, or even two at the same time, it is often several guards of different types all coming at you at once. What do you do? You fight dirty. As the tutorial hammers home, you should use the environment, kick that box, throw that vase, set off those explosives, divide and conquer. It makes the game somewhat frantic as you run from place to place, kicking tables, vaulting over enemies to take all advantages you can. It is a lot of fun. There is also a healthy number of different enemies, there is a steady progression in their skills with each subsequently introduced foe having one added feature to contend with, but they never abandon an enemy. Even as you fight Duellists you will still encounter them with Elite Soldiers, or Lackeys, so you will need to prioritise and potentially weaken enemies so that their guard does not regenerate. They also have two other enemies that exist outside this formula, one of which has two states which is fun, and the other throws bombs which is even more fun. The bosses were the most enjoyable aspect for me, but unfortunately there are only three of them. I cannot claim that they are complex, but they are very fun to fight with a nice mix of moves, and some adds to spice things up. The only issue I felt that I had was with verticality, or rather the enemies’ reaction to it. They have no idea what to do, they cannot throw rocks, and they cannot drop down (without your help), so if there are stairs they will run all the way around, which is a bit silly and can trivialise some encounters. If you like the combat then you have the arena to play, it is also great, it reuses areas from the campaign but can also mix and match different features and add entirely new configuration of items. Sometimes there is a giant bonfire in a villa, sometimes a square is filled with explosives, that sort of thing. The same can hold true for the enemies, but since it is random, you might get fun fights, and sometimes not so fun fights. Before each area you are also given a debuff, and a choice of three buffs, this generally makes you more and more powerful. I certainly think that this is great, but honestly it can get too easy.  does have accessibility features, which is good, but what I want is the option not to select a buff when playing the arena mode, to make the game more challenging if I want to. On the whole this game plays great and has super enjoyable combat. I wish there was more content, either in the form of more episodes or a sequel, but I got my money’s worth based on the combat alone. The developers have stated that the launch was successful, so I wish them all the best, and am holding out hope for a sequel, a content update, or DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant little game.  You know how there are tactical shooters.  Well this is tactical hack and slash were you have use traps and positioning to ensure that you never have to fight more than one or two foes at a time.  The is very little story with each level being basically unrelated except for the fact that the final level brings all the characters from each level back, but the humor is enough to carry it, with 95% percent of jokes landing.  I got about 4 hours out of the Champaign and am still playing the arena mode (the final arena is hard but I'll keep trying so that I can find out who the secret boss is!).  It does feel like the developers could do more (For example, the bosses could use some improvement, with all except the level 3 boss being beefed up reskins of regular enemies) so I hope they make a sequel or dlc sometime in the future.  Overall great time!

_childDocuments_.review: A female "Zorro"-like adventurer on a noble mission in 17th century Spain with a pinch of humor like what you would expect in "Puss in Boots."We take on the role of Adalia de Volador, a rapier-wielding defender of the oppressed population. While we fight for justice wherever we can against corrupt law enforcers, we also duel with formerly loved interests and our crazy but likeable brother. The story is about our arch-enemy Conde-Duque stealing or embezzling the people's money and putting it all aside on his treasure island. It is our duty as a major troublemaker to stop him. So here, our epic adventure begins."En Garde!" is a fast-paced action-adventure game for PC created by Fireplace Games and released in August 2023. The game features a vibrant, humorous, and stylized world and focuses on fast-paced, cinematic sword fights in which players must outsmart and outmaneuver their opponents through skill, cleverness, and interaction with the environment. Combat and movement are largely fluid, very enjoyable, and intuitive. The parry mechanics are certainly a bit tricky for a newcomer to the genre as the time frame for actions is often very short. But the focus of the game is clearly focused on these duels or how to avoid them. Therefore, it is important to adapt to the different enemy types. Each enemy has its own approach: The Lackey who doesn't block or parry while also being easy to slice up, Soldiers who need to be lured out of cover and exhausted, Elite Soldiers who regenerate their cover, Shieldbearers who must first have their shields removed with environmental mechanics, and Duelists dodge your item attacks but are not actually much stronger than elite guardsmen. Nonetheless, towards the end, in particular, the battles against the Duellists and Elite Soldiers become quite a challenge, especially when there is more than one in the duel or whole flocks of enemies attack you. There are also Grenadiers who throw firebombs at the current position, which can also be helpful, as the enemies are also hit and are therefore more easily thrown off balance for quick attacks. I sometimes let the Grenadiers live for this purpose to help me control the mob. From time to time, defeated opponents lying on the ground comment on their loss, which is sometimes quite funny but often confuses me, as I then think I've forgotten an opponent running around. Using the environment in combat is the key. We throw everything we can get our hands on at our opponents. Buckets blind the enemies and make them stationary, kicking barrels at them knocks them back and surprises them, and lanterns can trigger cannons that blow away everything in front of them with one shot. There is also chili powder that stuns the enemies temporarily so that you can take care of individual enemies, ase podiums and cooking pots that deliver the final knock on the head, weapon stands to bury fighters underneath them when they are kicked against them, and every ledge is an invitation to kick down the careless opponents.The graphic style of the environment and characters is strongly influenced by games like "Sea of Thieves," but you can see that someone has put a lot of work and love into the level designs. The Spanish street sections, palazzos, and locations are truly breathtaking. Beautiful scenarios and level design that leave you wanting more depth. Rooms are filled with a lot of variety, and they would invite you to explore them, but the urge to explore is rarely satisfied as we only run through most of them because there's not much to do here. In addition, we are very often faced with closed doors or one-way corridors that hint at paths but never open them up.Unfortunately, what happens far too often is that you simply wander through large sections of the level without any deeper interaction. Sometimes, entire levels are loaded in which I only fight two enemies and otherwise just run and jump through the level structure. Finding your way is rarely difficult. In addition, guiding wind lines help even the most clueless players not to lose direction. Sometimes, I wish the level design would challenge me a little more. Thrillingly introduced chases are completely without pressure and invite you to wander rather than run. Secret level sections allow insights into cute areas and exploration objects with descriptive texts, but unfortunately, that is all. With this kind of reward, I didn't feel motivated to search the levels in a focused way. The game has some lovely references to popular culture, such as the White Tree of Gondor from Lord of the Rings or some reference to Monkey Island's Insult Sword Fighting. However, these are mostly only found in the texts of the surrounding objects.When we come to a level section transition, we usually open a final door, which often reveals that there is nothing behind it when we swing it open. It’s mostly darkness, but sometimes there really is a dead-end room behind it or a corridor that ends immediately without doors. This seems almost inappropriate in a game that is so in love with detail. After completing a whole level, we are shown alternative objectives, such as eliminating a certain enemy in a specific way or finding a special location, etc. I'm not sure whether these alternative goals will persuade someone to play the level again. Unfortunately, it has a rather low replay value for me. Sometimes, I would have liked a few features that I don't normally enjoy myself, like alternative costumes for our protagonist, timed chases, or other mechanics that make us feel like we're really dealing with something.Dialogues are fully and lovingly voiced in English (with the exception of some item descriptions), which adds to the atmosphere and mood of the whole scenario. In general, the game is short - it took me about 6-7 hours to reach the credits at a relaxed play pace. For the effort that went into the voice acting, gameplay, and level design, that's okay, but not impressive. I think they could have made a lot more out of the unspoiled setting and the characters with a bit more content. There is an arena mode that offers different levels of difficulty and a variety of perks. These perks help you and/or make your opponents stronger. It's quite exciting to test your skills as a duelist against crowds of opponents, but for me, it doesn't offer enough variety for long-term use.The game also offers some family-friendly additional options in the menus, such as invincibility or automatic parrying. I imagine this is quite nice if you want a younger target group to enjoy the game.During my playthrough, I had few to hardly any bugs. Once, I got stuck between two chests and another time; I could stand 2 meters in midair near a cliff. There are also some imperfections, such as very blurred distant structures (at high to ultra settings in the graphics) in the distance, which seems weird.On the start screen, the game makes it clear that it is intended to be played with a controller, and I have to say that it plays great with one. When playing with the keyboard, the game feels very awkward, even if parries are easier to achieve with a mouse.In summary, however, "En Garde" is a well-designed and nicely narrated game that can be finished in just a few sessions. I had fun playing the game and actually felt quite entertained.Story –⭐⭐Graphics – ⭐⭐⭐Sound –⭐⭐⭐Gameplay – ⭐⭐⭐⭐  Fun Meter –⭐⭐⭐VERDICT+ Fresh dynamic combat system+ Environmental Interaction+ Humorous and light-hearted tone+ Intuitive and nice level design+ Excellent visual style and characters- Short game length- Shallow story- Repetitive gameplay- Inconsistent difficulty

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, this game sits in a very werid place in my opinion. The combat is fun but also unfair 30 percent of the time. The worst aspect of this game are unblockable(O attacks) attacks. Now most of these types of games have that mechanic but a lot of the time the O attacks are seen is like 2 nano seconds. They barely give you enough time to dodge. Not to mention that certain enemies(elites) regain their health if you fail to dodge/ block their attacks even dodging a blockable attack will cause it to reset. The games premise is based on dirty fighting by being able to use the furniture, chandliers, coat racks to fight enemies but that whole tactic flys out the window during the Zardia bossfight. Holy hell this boss fight is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. There are no environment attacks because the boss arena is bare. The boss acts like the elite enemy type but more health. However the boss would be simple if you could memorize her attack patterns. BUT, she has like 15 different patterns and if you fail to counter once she regains all of her health. This game can feel more difficult than SEKIRO at times but not because of difficulty but because of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ low times to react to enemy attacks. Oh, and majority of the game is running away searching for another table to kick at a group of enemies because they do the classic thing of putting like 40 enemies in a single room with one useable object.My final critique is the weird accessibility controls despite the game being difficult they give you auto block and god mode. Why would they give you this? Im very confused because the game is supposed to be difficult but they give you things to cheat. So what is the point of completing a hard challenge if you can just open settings and win?I would still recommend this game because can feel really fun. But the Zardia bossfight is easily the worst part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game with a unique theme and a dynamic combat system.The main story istself is only a few hours, but with the different difficulty settings, the secrets, the challenges and the roguelike-ish arena mode, it should make for a package that is worth the asking price.It also made me remember how much I missed Zorro... :)

_childDocuments_.review: Good game!TL;DR: I really enjoyed this game, though it is short. Simple mechanics used well. Great graphics and game design. Levels are very linear. Movement and combat is reminiscent of older Assassin creeds games, and batman arkham city. I played the game on hard, and have finished the story and arenas. At 17hrs I'm starting to be a bit done with it. I got the game on sale. I felt this game proved quite a challenge, especially at first, but once I got into the groove I could see myself improving a lot. I really did feel like a swashbuckler, or one of the three musketeers.The atmostphere and design in this game are great, I really love the art style, it's made to make you feel like you're in an oil painting from the era. The music fits so well.The characters and story are written really well in a light hearted, comedic tone.The mechanics by themselves are quite simple, but when used together makes the for quite challenging and versatile game play.The game is very short though, and I would have loved more levels, with more enemies later down the track. That being said, the levels and character they do have are very well designed.Though most 'arenas' do boil down to a square room.The only other gripe I really have with the game is how linear all the levels are. Having more of a sandbox feel to the level design would have been a nice addition, this may be personal preference though. The game has very minimal bugs, and well polished.I strongly recommend this game, especially if it's on sale. My main complaint is I want more En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun adventure, with exceptional style, with an very good, but unrefined combat system. I played it on the hard difficulty setting, and finished the main campaign of 4 episodes in about 4 hours.The gameplay is very fast, frantic, and chaotic. You use a combination of swift attacks, parries, and dodges, to dispatch hordes of enemies. Throughout this, you can also make use of environmental objects, these come in four forms, objects you pick up and throw, objects you kick at enemies, entities that you activate, and entities that you kick enemies into. Whilst only a small portion of them deal damage directly, they are essential for providing area crowd control, allowing you to then dispatch an enemy or two quickly. You have to take advantage of this, because enemies will otherwise completely swarm you with overlapping patterns that you cannot dodge.Enemies come in a decent amount of variety, and will use different attacks that require different responses. Many enemies need to be dispatched in specific ways, or have statuses such as shields, or "guard" that need to be dealt in precise ways. This leads to having to be creative with how you tackle specific groups, and it works really well.Now onto the bad, there is quite a lot of jank. The game uses auto-targeting, and it often "selects" the wrong target, seeing you swing into a very different position, "waking" enemies up from staggers, or not finishing off 1-hit targets. On top of that, the various physics objects behave very inconsistently in whether you can pass through them, or whether you will get stuck on a silly box that's off-screen. The camera does not help this, by pretty much having no vision of anything that's behind you. Finally, there's the pretty-much-expected jank that comes from the physics based gameplay, but this mostly works in your favor, with enemies getting stuck on things, or being perpetually stunned.Overall, it combines into a very competent combat system, that is a lot of fun to engage with, and whilst it does have its flaws, do not let those discourage you.The combat is broken up by traversal sections, which themselves are sometimes mini-puzzles. During traversal, you do some climbing, swinging, and jumping. These are a good way to temper the pace a bit, and though very easy, break up the game quite well.The images and trailers mostly speak for themselves here. The game generally looks fantastic, with incredible style, and consistent execution.There are a lot of things you can nitpick, texture details is hit or miss, with some objects up-close being very low-resolution, whilst objects much further away are crisp, but most of those do not negatively impact the experience, unless you're really looking for it, and the overall composition, especially in the vistas where you get a long-range painterly style, is great.The general soundscape is competent, the various surfaces you walk on have accurate footsteps, even to the smaller details such as stepping on a few "loose coins" on the floor, and it is mixed nicely. Almost all the major props have accompanying sounds, and it overall presents a nice environment.Music really reinforced the style, and it suits it well.Voice acting is exceptional, a huge shoutout to all the actors, especially the Count-Duke, with the voice overloading from his own insane rants, it's great. The quips in combat are humorous, and it creates a good sense of the buffoons actually engaging you.This was very fun, and it is easy to recommend. The gameplay is fun, the style, both in art and audio, is excellent, and even at only about 4 hours for the main campaign, is worth the asking price.Controller remapping required selecting the entry with the mouse, and then pressing the button on the controller. Without moving the mouse, pressing "A" on the controller would start rebinding the button that the mouse was hovered over, not the one the controller had selected.Even though I tried with my speakers configured to either Dolby Atmos, or 5.1 Surround, the audio menu only ever gave me the option for a stereo mix.The long-distance screen space shadowing techniques used, often cause large surfaces (especially vaulted ceilings) to "brighten up" as you walked under them, and I found this quite distracting when it happened.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: I probably am not the target audience for this game, but here are the reasons why i stopped playing at the Count-Duke(2nd chapter)1.) _childDocuments_.review: Very short game if you just play through the main quest.  I enjoyed it, didn't pay too much attention to the story just ran through fighting.Sword play feels good, the difficulty is okay for a short game, the platforming is intuitive.Only con was the auto camera control worked like 80% of the time. _childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Take this as a neutral review. I like the setting and the music, and to a certain point the gameplay, but at the end of the day, it's really repetitive. There are like 4-5 types of enemies (not counting bosses) and basically three actions: attack, parry, kick. Then it depends what or who you kick, and towards what or where (wall, trap, fire, box, hole, etc.). It helps that the game doesn't last long, but I would advise you to take advantage of the episodic nature of the story. Do one episode at a time. Finish it slowly. Or you'll get fed up quick.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is some of the most pure fun I've had in gaming. The combat is fast, satisfying, and dynamic and using all of the environmental tools to separate and deal with enemies makes each encounter feel like a puzzle solved in real time.The vibrant artstyle and funny quips make for a lighthearted game that was a delight to experience. This game feels like a dramatic evolution of PS-2 era action platformers like Sly Cooper, pulling elements of souls-likes (well more like Sekiro) to really complement things.My only complaint is that the game is little short. I would love a sequel that really delves into these characters and mechanics and gives us more to play with. I would estimate that finding all of the side content would take you around 20 hours, but the main story (with no secrets found) is more like 6 (on the highest difficulty with plenty of retries lol)I am very excited to see what this studio does next.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little gem that brings back nostalgia of games that are simple, straightforward and do not try to bring too many mechanics or systems to the table.The story takes about 5 hours to complete and is filled with humor that would boost your mood.Difficulty ramps up well and it contains collectibles that each give a good giggle.Replay-ability wise, you will unlock an arena that lets you experiment a few mutators (positive and negative).Worth giving it a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: Having played a lot of games with melee combat where you can just parry everything all of the time, this combat system was tricky to get used to. _childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A charming swashbuckling action game with solid controls and great voice acting, En Garde is light-hearted, yet quite challenging. An endearing protagonist and colorful (if certainly not cutting-edge) graphics put this over the top.  It's not very long, with the story mode consisting of 4 episodes that take about an hour each to complete, but there's episode-specific challenges and secrets and an arena mode that add staying power to the game. But for $20 it's an easy recommendation.It's the sort of Indie game that makes me want to look and see what else these guys have made. Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I wish we had a different rating system other than "Yes" or "No." I'd actually put it somewhere in the middle but leaning more toward the "No." Here's why...The game costs $19.99 and is only around 3 hours long. That's a hefty price tag for such a short game. There's really no side-content, the game is extremely linear, and the story is bland, has no character development, and bounces around all over the place. If your game is going to only be 3 hours long... then make sure the story really shines. Sadly... it doesn't.The combat IS some of the best I've played. You parry regular attacks and dodge red, which has been done before in other games, but it's smooth and feels great in this one. Utilize the environment, kick crates to stun enemies, throw objects, and vault over tables. The issue... this game is NOTHING but combat. While that part really shines... it would have been nice to throw in a bit of additional substance. The lack of content outside of combat is just bad and really hurts the experience IMO. No side quests, treasures to find, items to equip/use... you just run from one battle to the next, and that part does eventually get repetitive and old.The music, voice acting, artwork, animations, character design and comical AI is where this game shines, but that will only get a repetitive game lacking of content, story and playtime so far. Overall... the gameplay is missing a lot, and the length of the main story is short, and with such a bland experience, you don't even have a lot of replayability here, either.En Garde was a game I was really looking forward to. The demo was a great time, but you'll eventually realize, the full game is just a longer more drawn out version of it. Do I recommend playing and making your own judgement... sure. You may enjoy it. It's just a big price tag for such a short and lacking experience.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic short action comedy game. The humour, story, combat and platforming are all great.It also has uniquely positional combat. _childDocuments_.review: At the time of this Review I'm currently on the final Chapter Of the game. This is Easily one of the best games I've played in a long time. _childDocuments_.review: I had to refund the game because the camera is bad and the camera controls are lacking.It it a combined 3D platformer and something like a souls-light combat.But when performing 3D platforming in the initial tutorial, I couldn't see where I was going because the camera wouldn't follow from behind my character. One is supposed to run, jump, and grab onto flag poles to cross various gaps, but if the camera doesn't follow behind the character, one can't see which direction to jump in...There was also no control, e.g. R3 (press down on right stick), to auto snap the camera behind your character.Then even though the option says "when you don't manually move your camera, it will auto center behind you as you run", didn't actually work. It would sometimes move to follow my character... but I could run down an entire corridor straight into the camera, and the camera wouldn't move.I tried to up the camera sensitivity settings and constantly manually moving the camera with my right thumb on the right stick, but this just wasn't a plausible game play.I refunded in under 2 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: While it may be a little short, this game burns twice as bright! En Garde manages to integrate conversation between enemies and combat in a way I haven't seen since Drakengard 3! The encouragement you're given to use your environment to fight enemies brings the cartoon aesthetic to your interaction with the world and makes it easy for one to tell whether you have 2 or 10 hours in the game. Even after you finish the story, there is a gamemode that lets you choose from 3 randomly picked difficulty modifiers in a type of horde mode! If you're looking for a cartoony game that let's you feel like a sapphic Puss-in-Boots, then absolutely pick this game up on a sale!

_childDocuments_.review: It is short but sweet. I do think if it was a longer completion time, it would be too repetitive due to the nature of the similar levels and enemies. The amount of enemies you have to face at once can seem a bit BS (The last episode is - the last fight mostly) but I think that was their way to force you to use the environment a lot more. Overall it's a solid 7/10 game, worth the price for a short fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short and sweet little spectacle fighter. There's fun uses of your environment as you fight. The combat itself is pretty tight. It rewards patience more than aggression at times. My main problem with the game is that some enemies have a meter that you must drain by successful dodging or parrying their attacks or attacking them yourself while they block. The main problem with this is that meter will also go back up over time. You can't throw combos or they'll attack between your combos so you just sit in this annoying little take one swing, delay, take one swing, delay, until they attack and you react just to keep the meter from refilling. Those fights aren't particularly difficult, they're just tedious.Another issue I had, albeit rare, was that you can tell whether to parry or dodge based on what color the enemy flashes. Sometimes they would be in some bushes or something and it would be hard to tell whether you should dodge or parry in such a short window. On top of it, it got really annoying when fighting the enemies mentioned above.The game also has some light platforming that while the game mostly takes over itself for swinging and climbing, it still feels solid. En Garde is pretty fun overall. I finished it in just under three hours on my first try. I think if it was much longer that I would have gotten annoyed by some of those tedious fights mentioned above and not enjoyed it as much as I did. It's still worth a play through if you want a quick action game.

_childDocuments_.review: is a nice little campy action game/Beat 'em Up with very light and easy platforming sequences. The story follows Adalia de Volador, the legendary swashbuckler, through several short episodes, which consist of arena-type combat encounters and occasional platforming, the latter being very forgiving. The environment can and should be used against the opponents, and includes stairs, ledges, barrels, explosives, chandelier, and spice bags. The new types of foes are introduced as the story progresses and present later on in various combinations. New abilities as well become available automatically, no upgrades or character customisation are available. There are some optional secrets to discover, but they do not affect the story. There is also an Arena Mode, though I have not yet played it. The keyboard and mouse controls are rebindable and very comfortable. The graphics and visual style are beautiful, the OST is not annoying, and the VA includes strong accents.Recommended on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A relatively short but fun game. The combat is simple but rewarding, though dodging can be a bit jankey at times.I like the way you have to use items around you like buckets or cannons to defeat enemies by stunning / incapacitating stronger ones. Trying to brute force with just your blade is possible, though on highest difficulty you will struggle greatly to do so, especially with the final level's fights which have a few elite enemies at once.The game has a lot of charm, it's fun and the art style and voice lines are fun. There's a few secrets on each level and each level tries to have you replay it to do challenges such as 'defeat 2 duelists with cannons', I didn't really bother with them since I don't find the levels very replayable, but they're there if you want them.There is also an arena mode where you find waves of enemies and progress through the difficulties, each with a boss at the end. However, these bosses and enemies are identical to those found in the story mode, I did not spend much time at all at the arena.I do think the price might be a bit tiny bit too high at £16 or $20 considering it's about 4 hours max of gameplay, but even then I'd say it's worth it if you're looking for a fun game to play for an evening or two.Overall, if you see this game on sale or are willing to pay £15 for 4 hours of a charming, fun game, go for it! It's nice to support new studios like this one, especially ones who are made up of a group of school mates forming a game studio after and make a fun passion project like this.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: A game with little to offer outside of a decent combat system. Unfortunately, the game play lacks some polish in some critical areas:1. Bad camera, its easy for it to get behind walls and enemies to hit you off screen.2. The screen turning grey when you are on your last health bar, while the game trains you too look out for blue or orange lights to know when to parry or dodge. This can make it so you are effectively on your last health point with two health slots left if multiple enemies surround you. 3. Enemy attacks being a bit too magnetic, I have gotten pulled to the ground mid jump so that an enemy attack could land. Enemies lunge very far ahead, which makes the poor camera worse because you can easy get hit from an off screen enemy.The game had a great art direction with decent dialogue. The short campaign was fine overall but was more so just a string of arena's with a throwaway plot. I'd wait for a sale if you are interested in the title.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this one because I'm a huge swordfighting fan (a fencing coach in real life). It's not at all horrible, but not to my taste. The cartoon-style graphics are nice, but very generic, as is the humour. The gameplay is fairly basic - I certainly didn't encounter anything I've not done before in other games. I found the camera controls disorientating (albeit I was playing with mouse and keyboard). Overall it felt to me more like a very polished mobile/switch game than a "proper" PC game.,
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: is a fun, charming indie sword fighting game which, sadly, probably got overshadowed by all the massive games released around the same time. Combat in this game is simple but satisfying, combining swordplay (attacks, parries, and dodges) with opportunities to exploit the environment (such as kicking barrels into enemies to stun them or even kicking the enemies into weapon racks). It's a fun system on its own, but the tone and setting are what really elevate this game.Set in a fantasy Spain, the story has your swashbuckling protagonist Adalia going on wacky adventures presented in episodic fashion as if the game were some kind of lost Saturday morning cartoon. Every chapter has the evil Count Duke plotting some nefarious scheme of the week which she needs to stop. A charming cast of larger-than-life characters (Adalia included) adds a lot of flavor to the story. The environmental combat mechanics definitely lean into the slapstick cartoon vibe, and you'll also frequently hear Adalia exchanging taunts with enemies as you fight them. When you defeat enemies, the game even insists that they aren't dead; they're simply knocked out. The game's cartoony tone ends up being a lot of fun and, overall, manages to avoid overstaying its welcome. it all adds up to a game that is simply a fun, lighthearted experience - and a great palate cleanser in a year of massive, big-budget games. There's nothing in here that will set the world on fire, but I feel  neither needs nor wants to. It's just here to have a good time. If you think you'll vibe with this game's style, I'd really recommend giving it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: En Garde!

_childDocuments_.review: En Garde! is reminiscent of a PS2 action game in the most generous sense. _childDocuments_.review: Okay so maybe I'm showing my age a bit but does anyone else remember watching "The Mask of Zorro" as a kid? Forgive me this weird tangent but I mention it because in that movie there's a wonderful sequence where a new, not yet fully-trained Zorro infiltrates an enemy stronghold while trying to steal a horse and has to fight his way out; completely outnumbered what follows is a sequence of fun swashbuckling action, acrobatics, and wonderful tendency for Zorro to "not play fair" utilising everything around him to his advantage, be it an improvised weapon or a timely kick to wind one of his enemies for a moment, or at one point even a cannon. It is a wonderful scene that's lively, full of fantastic swordplay and a wonderful sense of slapstick humour. Okay long story short En Garde is that sequence but as a game. It's charming, it's funny, and I feel like you can appreciate it pretty much regardless of age.I know mentioning that "kids could really love this game" sounds like a backhanded compliment but I really don't mean it as one; there is some challenge here for those who want it but the tone, the fun sense of slapstick, and the accessibility features for difficulty really do make it something that I think I would have still really liked even if I was 20 years younger, I mention this because back when I used to work in a game store I realised how rare it is to have a really wonderful game that you can recommend that a parent can let their kids play with complete confidence, and unless your child is so absurdly suggestible that they'll play this and think "kicking Timmy down a set of stairs and then throwing a flaming lantern at him is definitely a good idea" I think you'll be fine :)(Well unless you're so scared of anything LGBTQIA+ that you'll boycott the game for having some funny flirtatious banter between 2 women who are very clearly attracted to each other but.... to be honest you can stop reading because I, the person writing this review, is gender-fluid so if you're gonna be that pathetically intolerant then feel free to boycott this steam review as well xD)As far as gameplay goes it's deceptively simple but in practice it's very different from the normal "Arkham" attack and counter systems you may be used to and expecting from it looking at the trailers. It does play like that control-wise but what sets it apart are various mechanics that punish being surrounded and outnumbered but reward using the environment, kicking everything and everyone into anything and anyone and generally manipulating the fights in your favour by doing so. A single enemy is not much of a threat on their own but when enemies compliment each other they become really dangerous, so the environment is mainly used to give yourself the advantage and breathing room to face your opponents individually, and even then it's still fun and useful to mess with them in as many silly ways as possible. The slapstick and tone of kicking a table from underneath someone's feet is always funny but it works because it is actually useful to do; fighting in a way that's playful and fun isn't something you do for the sake of it, you do it because the game makes it always a good option, it's a great system and one that makes the fights have a genuine element of planning, positioning, and thought that goes beyond merely reacting to various counter prompts.It's not a particularly long game (although the arena mode's random buffs/debuffs do give it a bit of fun replay value) but it also stops it from overstaying its welcome, the enemy types are trickled in at a nice pace and overall it's just a smooth experience. Each level plays like an "episode" of a show with their own little stories, no it's not some crazy epic story where you'll cry at the end or anything but it is an excuse to just keep that tone light and fun and it does that job just fine.It's charming and it's hard not to smile while playing it and I honestly hope that if the devs personally feel they aren't fully done with it that we could see even more expansions to it be it new arenas or episodes or whatever just to bulk out the package further but even as is it's a great package. i'd rather be left wanting more of a good thing than tired of it and this is definitely a good thing that I'd happily take more of. It's a lovely, silly, smile-inducing thing; and I just think that's nice :)

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts out strong with a charming art style and combat system that rewards using the environment to manage multiple enemies at once. However even as a short game this game feels like it is lacking in variety, you face the same couple of grunt enemies introduced in the first few levels thought the entire campaign. The new enemies that they do introduce have this odd mechanic in which if you try to parry an attack you should just dodge or dodge an attack you could parry their health refills, which means fighting those enemies end up being about pressing the right button depending on the color that flashes above an enemy as they attack, making combat dull and even more repetitive in a game that is supposed to encourage creative play-styles that make use of the environment. The combat scenes are separated by incredibly simple platforming segments that never introduce anything new after the first level. As if that level of repetitiveness wasn't enough, during the last level you actually face every prior boss again. In conclusion, while fun at first, En Garde quickly turns repetitive and fails to introduce interesting new ideas.

_childDocuments_.review: Wait for a sale.En Garde is absolutely oozing with charm and is a ton of fun to play, but it's incredibly short. It's only 4 levels long - and one of those is the tutorial.In yet another case of everyone else doing FromSoft's formulas better than FromSoft, En Garde is basically Sekiro but 10,000% less frustrating. Mostly this is because the game actually tells you what you need to do to defend yourself: a blue circle means 'parry', a red X is 'dodge', and a white circle is 'either'. You also take a set number of hits to be defeated and don't need to heal (your health refills at the end of an encounter or if you use a special attack move), allowing you to focus on swordplay.The game's premise is mostly that you are almost always greatly outnumbered. You need to make use of your environment by fighting dirty to isolate, stun, or temporarily remove enemies so that you can duel them one at a time. 1-on-1 is very much in your favor, 2-on-1 is an uphill struggle, and any higher is basically impossible. The maps are made with this in mind and leave plenty of tools around for you to work with, and this also requires a very aggressive play style; if you are too defensive, stunned enemies will rejoin the fight eventually.It's a fantastic game only marred by how incredibly short it is, so definitely give it a shot. Even if you're terrible at Sekiro-likes, that's okay, because the game has multiple difficulty levels and some assist modes if you need them. But even on Hard it's still a very fair challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: The goodVibrant and well constructed Spanish inspired environment with fairly easy platform puzzles, some secrets scattered throughout maps, and good music scores.What the game does exceptionally well though, is the combat with fluid movements, environmental and throw-able attacks and push mechanics (via a kick). There are usually many ways you can handle a skirmish including kicking your enemy off a bridge. Combat is always entertaining and never got old, and stayed as the right amount of challenge between chapters, gradually introducing new enemy types as chapters goes on, and you are improving your parry and dodging skills. Boss fights were a treat, each of them felt satisfying to beat.The badThe game is extremely short, there are only 4 chapters and each chapter takes about an hour-ish to breeze through.Characters are one dimensional but somehow that's part of the charm.8.5/10 overall, definitely worth a try at the current price.For those who wants more of the combat delights, there are added arena mode.

I encountered a few glitches and I think there should have been more episodes but damn I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loved this. I honestly might replay episode 3 to fight Zaida again. Great game!
