_childDocuments_.review: This is a faster pace version of heroes of might and magic (HOMM). I think the strategy was dumb down a bit as the battles are more automated. I have the breakdown of different elements below:Heroes / Artifacts - very similar to HOMM. Lots of variety for artifacts, sets, and hero skills you can level up. Unlike HOMM, the skills are in a skill tree and a previous skill must be equal or higher to level up the one you want. This skill tree causes 2 issues, your skills are set (cant choose the skills you want in your tree, but they arent random for the good and bad) and some skills are at the bottom of the tree and or behind skills that are horrible. If the bottom tree skills were the better ones, that would make more sense, but they are almost randomly placed between the different heroes. Skills - they need some major balancing especially the faction related ones. One faction has their 3 magic heroes spawn elementals every spell cast. The might heroes steal units once every 2 days. Considering you can do battle a couple times a day, I would rather have 5 elements spawn every spell cast in every fight than to steal 5 units every 2 days. Another skill gives 25% chance to learn 1 spell on level up, but you automatically get 1 spell and 50% increase to effectiveness if you select pyromancy (fire skill) and it's less random. Bodyguard is a bit out of control too. You get half the difference in power between main army and current hero up to 100 power per skill. Some units can start maxed with bodyguard 5, so just put all units in main army, 1 unit in new hero, and you have a 500 unit army for free that auto revives after every battle. 500 power is more than you can place on the battle field initially. There is also a skill to make the lower level creates change to the highest, so a work into a dragon. At lvl 5 you can be getting 3 dragons per battle! lol Far better than the skill that gives 2.5 dragons per week at lvl 5. Another faction skill gives you ore for winning battles but then lets you trade ore for units and stat increases!!! By level 20 I have 20 points in each stat! Battle - my biggest issue. At half speed it is slow enough to have some strat. If you try to increase during battle the game crashes right now. Fight is real time and you can stage your units on the field before the fight which is great. Spells and hero stats greatly impact the battle. The issue is stupid group selecting of units and poor Ai. I cant tell just 1 unit to run away like a dragon almost dead and even when they do go to where I say they keep trying to turn around and fight. I cant select the exact units I want to move to the exact location I want like air units moving fast and flanking archers... When the battle starts it is semi auto minus you spell casting. Units - each faction and tier has very different units with different stats, abilities, etc. There are counters to each unit. You can select ones that have more synergy with your hero too. They did a great job here minus archers. Archers with "long range" are great and work well even when armies are larger. Each unit needs a certain amount of space between it, so if you have a large melee wall in front of a large group of archers, they can still shoot. If you have regular range or especially short range, your archers could be doing nothing. Now the archer skill can add range, but not all heroes have and some are lower on the skill tree. I can see needing a skill to help short range archers, but normal range, that's lame. Early game this isnt a problem though.  Map - basically copy paste from HOMM with some new structures for upgrading your hero. I like some of the new options. Maybe my biggest issue is the heroes can move so far, especially with hurricane, town portal, and celerity. You can be almost anywhere on a medium map in 1 turn. It's nice for speed, but annoying for base defense especially if you were fighting a human. AI doesnt exploit as much, AI - I dont know how the AI does it, but they will attack me early with multiple heroes with large armies. They have to be "cheating" for resources. I hate how the AI is early game. Late game they arent smart enough to properly upgrade their hero and use skills/spells. Random complaints - outside of battle I cant see my hero's army power or his power cap in battles. When selecting a hero from the tavern I cant see their skill tree. Many heroes get some random lvl of bodyguard when you purchase and I havent figured out why or how. I had a hero start with lvl 5 body guard which was at the bottom of their skill tree and skills before it were both lvl 0. When I looked at his stats before buying it didnt show bodyguard. I have been playing it because too late for a refund and it does bring back my HOMM memories. It gets old / repetative fast especially since there is less strat in battles. It also doesnt have a campaign like HOMM, which I loved, but this is also not a $60 game. Worth $10 if you have time to waste.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★☆☆(Pretty good Heroes of Might and Magic-like game with a retro style)============Review:Hero's Hour is essentially HoMM made for the NES (If you're old enough to know what that is..) with real-time battles.Audiovisually the game is.. well it's retro, it looks and sounds old.I usually don't care much about graphics, I love 2D art and can appreciate finely drawn pixel art, but the art style is too retro even for me.The sounds are also retro but generally do their job just fine. But the music.. well, you know those catchy tunes that stick in your head? It's like that but not in a good way. It's honestly annoying and if this loops in your head.. argh. Yeah, better to listen some other music while you play this.============Now gameplay-wise the game is fine - if you've played HoMM you know how it works. You pick your faction (11 choices) and pick your hero (6 choices per faction).You get a random map generated based on templates and get thrown into the game. You build your town/castle pretty much like in HoMM, though the "techtrees" are somewhat randomized. You buy troops for your hero and explore, fight monsters, conquer mines and level up your hero, gaining new skills based on the hero you picked.The key difference between HoMM and Hero's Hour is that the battles are real-time - the battle pauses when you cast spells, but otherwise it runs in real-time. And honestly it gets really chaotic later when the army sizes get bigger. Sometimes it's hard to tell if you're winning or not, especially since not all of the army fights at the same time. There's a limit which can be adjusted with certain skills to become smaller or larger - and this limit dictates how much "Power" worth of units you can field at the same time. The remaining army joins as "Reinforcements" when your army takes too much damage.The game is not exactly balanced. The factions themselves are not balanced, some are just better than others. But the difference between heroes is even bigger - even inside the same faction some heroes are significantly stronger than others (Every hero has their own skill tree).  But I think it's better this way, it would be honestly boring if it was perfectly balanced.============Overall, I think Hero's Hour is pretty good. It's not like amazing or anything, but if you like HoMM and have tolerance for the retro looks, then you might enjoy the game.If they upped the graphics a notch so that they actually have some detail instead of few pixels here and there, and made less retro sounding music, then the game would be significantly better in my opinion - but that's just my preference.But like this, I think the game is a little overpriced - and you might want to wait for a sale.============Summary:The Good 👍+ Scratches that HoMM itch+ Lots of factions and heroes feel different+ Good random map generatorThe Bad 👎- Too retro look- Annoying music- Too expensive

_childDocuments_.review: This is a mobile game. It's not really something you're going to play when you're sitting at your PC.They say this is like Heroes of Might and Magic but it's not like the versions I played at least. You've got no control over your armies in a battle. The game pretty much just seems to be about running around, picking up items on the ground, and using that to buying better armies for the AI to control. And you need to buy armies, because your hero cannot do ANYTHING at the beginning of the game. Neutral villagers defending a sawmill beat the crap out of him. Random wandering monsters beat the crap out of him. That's not like the classic games, where you were encouraged to explore early on.To me this game reminds me of Desktop Dungeons more than anything. You look carefully and get some resources, then you take on the easiest opponent you can see, then use those gained resources to take on the next easiest opponent you can see and so on. Most of the challenge lies in figuring out what the best order is. And that's alright, but there are lots of games which do that for free and I imagine there are dozens of mobile games nowadays which have this same game loop. You don't need to pay $15 for something like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for a year and was an early purchaser. I stuck with it through it's very laggy and buggy periods and think it's in a reasonably stable and playable state right now. This game is good, very fun and worth playing. I would be writing a raving review about how good this game is if not for the new price. I feel the developer is extremely greedy to be asking this price for this quality of game. Basically yes, the game is fun, you can sink 10+ hours into it, but the gameplay gets kind of stale, and lag can decrease enjoyability. It's an interesting concept mixing some aspects of strategy and RPG, and the factions are all reasonably unique and interesting. This said, there's only 3 factions I've even played (Decaying, Enclave, and Wild) since the other factions seem boring to me.I will say that I'm extremely disappointed to see the developer increasing the cost so much. This is a very basic game and I felt like I got my money's worth at $10 CAD when I purchased during early access. However, at $20, with extra $7 for supporter pack, it really seems to be over-reaching in my mind. If you look at Terraria at $11 CAD, Stardew Valley at $15 CAD, and Vampire Survivor at $3, I just can't justify spending $20 on this.This game really uses a lot of CPU and is not optimised to run without lag on large battles. Also, the game hasn't changed much in the time I've been playing it, yet the price has doubled. I'm hoping some significant changes come that make me change my mind about this title because I really want to LOVE this game since it scratches a lot of itches for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Hero's Hour

_childDocuments_.review: The game has cute pixel graphics and an amazing soundtrack. It oozes personality!All the factions I've played had something unique to them, both in charm and in strategy. As soon as I got bored with a faction, there were another 10 waiting for me, bringing fresh mechanics which changed the gameplay reasonably.I'm not usually into RTS, but I might say that I like the combat better than HoMM3 - it's so satisfying to see units really fill the field in enormous numbers. I always play as a magician, as combat would seem lackluster if all I got was unit bonuses; choosing my spells wisely give me something to do. I wish for more fine tuning in giving unit orders; at least, devs should allow me expand and decrease the selection area, so I'm not forced to make ranged units move into enemies. Also, it would be nice if I could order ranged units to attack somewhere instead of moving (maybe that's possible and I'm missing it?).With standart config I didn't feel the exploration very rewarding - there was always a lot of stuff to do near my base, and resources were rarely scarce. But the game offers some degree of customization and now it's playing much more like HoMM. In my most recent game, I had to set sail searching for a Mercury mine or else be cut off from developing my stronger troops. This is how I like it!There are some bugs around, particularly with the UI, which I use resized (my monitor is small) but this brings some trouble here and here. Some of it was already fixed, so I hope these rough edges will be polished soon. The AI sometimes stomps you even on easy, but after I learned the mechanics of my faction I was able to counter them, and even win a Normal game without much hassle. It might be however quite unforgiving to newcomers to HoMM-like games.I hope this game gets fine tuned and I fervently hope for online PVP. I'd surely push it on my friends so that we can play together :3 the game overall is very charming and fun, in many senses even better than HoMM3.

_childDocuments_.review: The game started off a bit lean, but through the updates it has become one of the most polished, interesting, and fun strategy games I have played. If you are looking for a large-scale strategy battler in the vein of early 2000's classics, but don't want the bloat of modern 4x games, you'll find that in Hero's Hour.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write reviews for games, it's just not something I seek out. I did feel it was worth speaking up in this case though. Hero's Hour is a good game. It's fun and has a ton of potential, but that's the problem. While the game has incredible potential, it's still a long way off from being what it promised to be. And that's fine, these things take time. Games are hard to make, and at times it can be a thankless job, so normally I give the benefit of the doubt to developers that are working hard to polish and improve on what they've made.Releasing a paid DLC for what boils down to a new faction, a few new units and skills, and some maps when the game still doesn't even have a single player campaign or story mode of any kind is more than a little rough. Other people have already mentioned the issues with the Bodyguard skill as well, but the issues are more widespread than just reworking that one skill. The meta of Hero's Hour is almost entirely limited to snowballing. Build your big bad hero with all the power ups and units you can cram into it and overwhelm whatever else is out there. There's very little encouragement to use other heroes for much else beyond scouting and collecting resources.These are all issues that could easily be overlooked for a game that's still more or less in it's infancy, but releasing DLC for a game before the core gameplay is finished is somewhat disingenuous. I have almost 100 hours in this game, I really do enjoy it. It's fun, colorful, and has a good depth of mechanics with each faction having somewhat different play styles. It's a good foundation to build something amazing, and I still hope that's what will happen. But if the developers are establishing that the core game is finished, and any major future changes will be in the form of DLC, it's hard to recommend it to someone else.

_childDocuments_.review: This game suffers from a serious lack of balance and wrong design in certain aspects. Here are the ones that imo make the game totally unplayable and should be fixed asap before any more content updates.1. the spells are too op and lack balance2. the armies consist of single units instead of squads which, in turn, will turn your army into a big blob of 985436827349 different units. to solve this problem the devs should force smaller units, like various foot soldiers, into squads, like a squad of "100 goblins" etc... this way you won't have to deal with your army of 100 dragons being spammed with things like 4 soldiers 2 goblins and 3 flies. it's just stupid.3. the pacing is all over the place. u will have a maxed-out castle before even encountering the other player. at this rate, there's just no point in the whole building and upgrading system. either remove it completely and give everyone maxed-out castles from the very start; or make it much MUCH harder to build new buildings. like, make the price 20x more idk.4. on the same note, you should also make it much harder for the player to build higher-tier units. most of a human nation's army should be consisted of normal foot soldiers, with various other elite units here and there. in this game, it's the exact opposite. Imo the higher-tier units need to be more expensive and "less diverse". you need to make it so that the player actually struggles and puts most of his resources into upgrade/unlocking a unit in a certain orientation and even maybe gets punished by getting soft-locked out of outer archetypes.I usually do not give a damn about a game enough to post this kind of design recommendations in the reviews, but watching a game full of content and with decently active development like this, and seeing it being ruined by such obvious and stupid mistakes just makes me wanna facepalm. hope they fix it. I can see this one actually being a really good game after some proper design changes.

_childDocuments_.review: ⚔️🕰️ Greetings, would-be heroes and armchair generals! Grab your cloak and your sense of humor, because it's time to dive into 'Hero's Hour,' a game that proves managing an army is just as chaotic as herding cats, but way more entertaining.🏰🌪️ Picture yourself as a mighty leader, a strategic genius... only to find out your army has the collective intelligence of a spoon. You'll plan epic battles, strategize like a pro, and then watch in horror (and laughter) as your troops decide that chasing butterflies is more important than following orders.🔮💥 Magic? Oh, it's magical alright. Imagine having the power to cast earth-shattering spells, only to accidentally zap your own troops. 'Friendly fire' takes on a whole new meaning. It's like being a wizard with unlimited power and very limited accuracy.🎭👑 The heroes in this game are as diverse as they are unpredictable. One minute you're the noble knight, champion of the realm; the next, you're the rogue who's lost in the woods because the map was upside down. Each character is a unique blend of 'brave' and 'what were they thinking?'🐉🤣 The monsters you face? They're not just obstacles; they're comedians in disguise. From dragons with attitude problems to goblins who forgot they were supposed to be scary, every encounter is a mix of thrill and giggles. It's like going to a monster comedy club, but you're the punchline.🌟🛠️ Customization is a key part of the game, and it's like playing dress-up with your very own medieval Barbie and Ken, except Barbie is a warrior with a battle-axe, and Ken can cast fireballs. Mix and match your army to create the most bizarrely effective (or hilariously ineffective) fighting force.👏🎉 In conclusion, 'Hero's Hour' is an uproariously fun take on strategy and fantasy. It teaches valuable lessons, like 'don't put the archers in front', 'never trust a goblin with a map', and 'sometimes, the best strategy is just to wing it.'🌟🌟🌟🌟: 4/5 stars for the sheer comedy of errors that is commanding an army in a fantasy world. Who knew that leading a horde could be such a hoot?

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a prototype for Heroes 8. Hero's Hour is a lightweight clone of the Heroes of Might and Magic Series. The objective is to kill all your enemies of the opposing colour(s). Gameplay-wise, mouse and keyboard.Conclusion, do try HH when it's on sale. Feels like a HTML game.1. Elves OvergrowthI liked the idea of converting the mines into a more powerful Overgrown form that produced more materials and had defending units.2. Infernal Gate UpgradingThis is a good design. All the buildings should have something similar. The Infernal Gate has a Sulphur based upgrade. Something like 4-6-10-14-18-22 Sulphur. Each upgrade allows the Infernal Gate to summon more and higher tier demons during combat. This solves the problem of excess resources and provides a choice to the player.  3. Bread and Butter Spell/ActionThe cheap/free spell that is faction specific.This is useful.It gives the player something click-and-cast. When you have reserves and no mana, the battle can drag on for a long time, even with 2x speed.4. Going by Ship/BoatSlightly better than old HOMM2 (You had to be near a useful body of water, build a shipyard, build a ship, waste 1 turn boarding the ship, move across water, waste 1 turn unboarding)1. Resource Class ExplosionCrystal, Sulphur, Mercury, Wood, Ore, Gold. Why 6? From HOMM 5, I think it was just Gold, Wood, Ore, Mana Crystal. Just 4 resources, with Mana Crystal being the special resource. If you don't need sulphur, do you want to waste actions collecting sulphur->going to market and selling the sulphur for gold? Additional steps for no reason.What does Mercury or Sulphur signify?Just use the Crystal as a limited resource for buying Tier 3 units and special buildings. You have to allocate them correctly for optimal play.2. Infirmary ButtonWhy in the world do you need an Infirmary button? It works automatically without any intervention. Like growth3. No Automatic Ship TravelIn HH, you cast a spell to summon ship. Then, board ship and park ship somewhere. Isn't keeping track of the ship(s) a waste of memory?Why can't you make Ship Travel automatic? Let it be a skill, like swimming. Put this skill into the Champion's guild. Once you upgrade to Champion's Guild, all heroes can now learn to swim.No issue with parking your ship and keeping track of an immobile ship. Hero just moves on the water and magically turns into a ship, goes back on land, magically turns back into a Hero.No issues with tiny rivers and trapped lakes. Just swim over them. No issues with learning a spell, opening a book, checking for enough mana, casting the spell, checking if you're within range of water, choosing the correct body of water, choosing the correct tile.Cleaner, simpler, efficient, catchall process.4. Can't GarrisonFor some reason, your hero can't move into the Castle. It has to be near the castle but it can't garrison.5. 1. Mass CombatI'm not sure if I like it or not. On one hand, it's way faster than the old turn-based HOMM model. I like the combat pause to cast spells.On the other hand, I don't think about conserving troops anymore. I just spam summons, knowing that the Infirmary/Hospital will catch any dead troops.2. PotencyPotency's a bit weird. On one hand, I like that there are 2 spells to cast within the same timeframe. On the other hand, I don't like the spellbook doubling with Potent versions of every single spell. If I had N spells, the book would have 2N spells with Potency. The problem is that when you learn many spells, your book overflows and you have to flip through multiple pages.1. Closing the DistanceWaypoint portals. You need to close the distance between 2 castles that are very far apart. If you have just 2 portals that lead to each other's bases, those portals are game-changing. However, if you have a chain of portals that led to each other's bases, it would be similar to capture the point.Think Fast Travel in other games.Town Portal once every 7 days slows the game down.2. CaravansPlease remove this. They take up space. It would be cleaner and easier to just teleport them or increase growth.3. Tiered Growth LocationsCurrently, we have a location that specifically grows a single creature e.g. Medusas only. This will create a class explosion as you have to count race, number of creatures, variants, etc. Instead, just have a tiered growth e.g. Farm for the Human Race. All Tier 1 creatures grow faster.It would be better with Tier-1 choices. You probably don't want to hire other factions.4. Combine Mercenary Hall + Market + Antique ShopInstead of a Workshop/Mercenary Hall/Antique Shop that only show 2 slots and take up 2/3 buttons, combine Mercenary Hall + Antique Shop + Workshop + Market. The concepts are similar, you are BUYING goods, items and mercenaries. So, have 1 Market Button for all the above. That way you can remove 2 button from the right side and you can see everything for combat in one place i.e. Buy Ancient Armour, buy Frost Titan mercenaries, trade for crystals for the Frost Titan mercenary all with 1 button.Since Mercenary Hall + Antique Shop are always higher level than Market, you can always set Market as the base and then upgrade it 2x. Like the Tavern and Champion.5 buttons down to 3. Clean.5. Wonder WinThis is from the Holy Grail quest and Age of Empires. Just create a wonder that will win you the game once it completes. If you start building it, your castle will be shown to all players. Time to win should be around 2 weeks?6. Bigger Tier 3 unitsI felt the Red Dragon/Abomination/Tier-3 Units needed to be 50% bigger graphically. Why? For distinction. The Tier 2 Dwarf Units look the same.6. Remove Infirmary ButtonFrom 5 to 4 buttons. Fantastic. Cleaner UI design. Improves readability.7. Team DeathmatchThe most popular option in most games. Please put players in TEAMS.8. ENDING THE GAMEIf the game drags on forever, it gets very boring. You need a way to end the game.9. Obelisk + Artifact Set JourneyCurrently, the model is touch an Obelisk, touch 5 Obelisk pieces, go to X, dig at X, get 1 or 2 Artifact(s). The first 3 Obelisk pieces are useless and just give you a fuzzy image.Instead, how about an Artifact Journey? No need for complex algorithms.1 Obelisk piece = 1 Artifact Set piece.You touch 1 Obelisk piece, map appears showing you where to dig (no fuzzy image), dig it out, get 1 Artifact piece e.g. the Helmet.Next Obelisk Piece, another new map location, go there dig it out, get another Artifact piece e.g. Off-Hand. Rinse and repeat until all pieces are found.Each additional piece get progressively further from your starting location and you are guaranteed to be able to find the whole set. If another player follows the same path, the Obelisk will tell him who has the item (if it got dug out) and he will see dig holes at the location. If it got sold, Obelisk will tell you it's at the market.No probabilistic issues, you can find the whole set since the Obelisk will tell you who has it or where to find it. Currently, you just can't click on the Obelisk after you find the treasure.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a HOMM3 expert. I played a few hundred hours on easier difficulties and I prefer not to have five heroes roaming about because that gets boring. I was really hoping to find a fun, modern take on the game and it got about 90% of the way there before tripping at the finish line. My primary issue is that the AI is insanely overpowered in ways that do not make sense. On medium difficulty you will come across AI opponents that progress far faster than anything you seemingly can accomplish so its always a losing fight. I've had a couple games on easy where I squeaked out a win but I still found myself going, "How could the AI possibly afford those all those units so quickly" or "How did they get past that gatekeeper in week 2 that is still "impossible" for me on week 4" all the time. I'm going to keep playing and see if my thoughts change but at this point playing against the AI is just a chore. I want to take time building up a city, hero, and army. Not need to be completely perfect on every turn, every build, and unit choice so that I can even attempt to keep up with the AI.Take a look at some of the other reviews and you will see similar issues. Why do I defeat an enemy hero with a ridiculously strong army only for him to come back in like ONE DAY with an equally strong army when mine is far smaller, I only have one of them, and only surviving due to bunkering at home? Where are all these units coming from, where are they getting the resources, and how are they getting them 5x faster than me?Until there is a MAJOR difficulty balance, I'm going to have to say pass on the game. Devs have said they are looking into it but it needs a real overhaul.

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment of this review my playtime isn't much (8.4 hours). So, the game. How good is it? Well, it is quite alright. Its main catch is variety. Variety in factions(I think there is like 10 of them, I didn't really count), variety in skills of heroes, variety of situations you can get yourself into. The crushing defeat to what should've been an "Easy" encounter and surprising victory against "Impossible" odds. Yeah, those are quiet possible. Although, I say that its main catch is variety, many of you will notice its resemblance to Heroes of Might and Magic. Because, while the combat isn't anywhere near similar, the map exploration and base building is almost the same. Hell, even some buildings on the world map look the same as in Heroes IV. But, in functionality they are nowhere near them. The fountain that gave mana to your hero in Heroes? Now it exchanges that mana for permanent elemental units. Of course, it is excluding standard resource buildings like ore mine and lumber mill. City-building is the same as Heroes V. Your city has a level and it rises as you build more structures in that city. Buildings vary from faction to faction, having some generic structures like Market among them, creature dwellings and specialised constructions, like, the faction of Arcane having Spire of Magic that gives your heroes randomized one-use spells that cost 0 mana that switch in-between battles. Not going into specifics, again, variety. Now, before we get to aforementioned battles, we need to speak heroes. As in characters in this game, not game series. Each hero is classified into Warrior or Spellcaster. While it's possible to make your warlord into spellslinging menace it is quite easier to make him into generic headbasher. Each hero at level 1 has 2 skills. One faction-specific and one common. Each hero's skill tree is randomized. Let's say some Jodi has a skill Mysticism on a second row of skills, and Kntrulath has the same skill on fourth row. There is much to say about heroes, but I would like to talk combat now.THE MAIN DIFFERENCE FROM THE HEROES OF MIGHT AND MAGIC. Combat system. It is real time. Thats it... Okay, not really, but if you don't want to read further(and if you don't how the hell did you get to this point in the first place?), then all you have to know is that when you encounter an enemy on the map, you just place your units closer of farther from your enemy and press battle and then it will begin in real time. They will fight and THE FITTEST TO WIN will win. If you want a more detailed explanation then there isn't really one. You place them on your half of the combat screen and then the battle will just start. You don't need to control them much. You have commands like "Defend" which will make them just... stop(DO NOT PRESS "DEFEND" BUTTON), and "Attack" which is a default command at the beginning of combat. You can select some units and "Order" them to move to specific places and as far as unit control goes, that's it. If your hero have spells, he can lob them anywhere on the map. Do read the spells, by the way, if the tooltip says that it will hit "anyone and anything" it will hit ANYONE AND ANYTHING. The only complicated thing in combat is that you often can not place all of your units on the battlefield at once, at least when you have a large and strong army. The game has this ceiling of Unit Power which tells you how much and strong units you can place on the battlefield at one point. If most of them die you can send Reinforcements from the reserve you left at the start.Now, we come(cue Cyberpunk OST) to the real CONs. I spoke about the not-so-intrinsic combat system where you essentially just watch dummies beat other dummies, but it's not really a bad thing. It just means you don't have to be a strategic genius to pull of some impressive things. It is quite satisfying to watch YOUR red dragon go to town and it is terrifying to see the same red dragon go to town, but just against you. I digressed, but I just had to say it. The real bad thing is balance. It is not broken per say, but when I had to against Horde faction I just knew I was in for a ride. THEY CAN UPGRADE THEIR UNITS IN BATTLE. Only in battle of course, but it just means they don't have to waste their time and resources on upgrading buildings. And oh my god is it INFURIATING to see the almost dead Horde army only to see their shamans upgrade and gain another healing ability at which point it just goes to defeat.But, talking about balance in combat and factions isn't really my forte. I main Inferno in Heroes III... But, if I can't speak balance in combat I can speak balance in heroes. Because some of the skills they have range from OP broken to useless. I played Conclave and had this hero that had a FACTION skill that tracked some "beasties" which upon defeating should've dropped some trophies. I encountered those beasties exactly 0 time. But, you guess what? He had a skill that allowed him to recruit red dragons after several battles. Which is... OP. He didn't even had this skill that far in the skill tree. At level 2 I already had it. And by level 8 I had 3 red dragons which is a lot. But going back to useless DO NOT PICK "Oligarchy". It raises health and damage of your army, but decreases amount of units you can place in the battle by a whooping 30%. It is too much. And that decrease scales up with level ups of that skill. I watched as my dragons were picked off one by one, because they didn't have the support of other units. Though, to be perfectly honest, most of the skills are just good not too game breaking or detrimental LIKE OLIGARCHY IS.What about the bugs? I didn't encounter them much, but I wasn't actually looking for them. The game crashes though. Not too often, but it can be quite annoying.What about optimization? And this is the main turnaway of this game. Whether you are on a big world map, or a massive battlefield you WILL see that frame rate drop. Oh my god, I CAN NOT PLAY ON BIG MAPS?! I WANT TO 1v3 ON A BIG MAP BUT I CAN'T BECAUSE MY PC COUGHS METAL DUST WHEN IT TRIES TO PROCESS THOSE MAPS. COME THE ♥♥♥♥ ON. I played CIV 5 on a gigantic map against 7 other civs and I didn't waste 10 minutes of my life watching the turn bar of AI opponents go from left to right. WHICH I DID IN THIS GAME... Okay, I watched youtube while AI did their things, but THAT IS NOT THE POINT. TO THE CONCLUSION WE COME(Cyberpunk). This game is alright. While the balance thing can detriment the positive experience and optimization of this game sucks sus it is still a good game. Maybe my rants above have made a contradiction to a positive review I'm supposedly writing, but the game does not lose its main catch in all of those things. I genuinely excited to see how my army will fair against the HORDE, and genuinely thoughtful of my hero's skill build. I play on small to medium maps, but compensate it with more opponents, who sometimes fight against each other. And it is just so satisfying to see two dumb AIs go at each others throats over a lumber mill. Especially if they were "Impossible" to defeat just a turn ago.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game but with flaws. Hopefully they will be fixed within future updates.Pros:- 11 fractions and every seems unique, with unique units, gameplay and specialization. They're fun to play and provide really nice variety of tactics- Procedurally generated maps, even the same map will be different on the next playthrough, also very good map editor included- Battles are fun to watch and sometimes can get really intense. Beating up 2x stronger army with smart planning and deployment of units gives a lot, really a lot of satisfaction- HoMM nostalgia feeling- Decent soundtrack overall, i like the most Wild city tune, as well as LamentCons:- AI is a blatant cheater. Literally AI feels like having unlimited gold and they gain units from nowhere. Even on Normal and Easy difficulty. It has nothing to do with strategy. It really kills the pleasure when you know you play against silly, but heavily cheating bots. Twice I took over the AI city in the fourth week and guess what? They had EVERYTHING built. How can you hire a powerful army and get enough resources to develop 100% of the city in 4 weeks? Only AI can. This should be fixed, because really playing vs AI is little to no fun- Mediocre pixelart. It's not bad, but i think it could be much better, because the game actually looks worse than HoMM 1 from 1995- No campaign, no story- Poor balance of fractions, spells and heroes- Inaccurate descriptions of unit skills, spells etc.- No online mode, only Hot SeatAfter all i think it's a good game, worth the money. I give it thumb up also to encourage developer to keep working on the game as it has potential. Just fix AI, add Campaign with story, repair balance, get better descriptions and add online mode - it will be a great indie game then, probably the best HoMM successor.

_childDocuments_.review: Name:Hero’s HourVersion:FinalDLC:NoMods:Yes!  On day 3, even!Hours Played:Several-I took a break due to previous concerns now fixedType of Game:HOMM HOMMAGEGraphics:Pixel artMusic:Don’t know...I always turn it offSound:SuitableBeaten:YesMultiplayer:Hot seatCan I play This Drinking?:Yes!Can I play this while Partaking?:Drugs are whack, stay in schoolWas it Fun?:Now that they have worked on the difficulty levels some and it is beatable, yes!Replay Value:Yes!Notes:Fair warning...this is a rewrite of a review I had before.  The reasons that I had for not recommending this game have been removed, and so I am changing my answer.  Of course, I reserve the right to change my mind again in the future.If you’ve played any of the Heroes of Might and Magic games, you’ve played this.  What this does better, however, is the very wide range of groups you can play with, and the autobattler.  You can start as 1 of 12 factions, and have up to 7 opponents, not including neutrals.  You beat other parties, capture locations, acquire resources, and eventually capture the other factions headquarters. You start out in your own corner of the world, with a small force.  You are locked behind a gate to a central location all the other factions are also locked away from.  Building up your forces to get through that gate announces to the world that you are ready for the big times, and now that your opponents don't outnumber you by 4 overpowered armies to one, you have a chance of winning.The autobattler is a nice touch.  Aside from troop placement, you have nothing to do except cast spells, authorizing reinforcements, and plan what to do next.  The combat looks pretty good, and the troop explosion looks just like fireworks.You can also build up your hero with skills, bonuses, and gear, although the gear and some spells are random.  I like to make sure that I have the treasure found before I move to the other locations.I also have to give a shout out to AI programming.  Assuming that the AI doesn’t cheat, it is pretty well written.There was one flaw in the game that made this not worth buying, though, and that was the difficulty.  With patches, this no longer seems to be in effect for the factions I have played as.  Previously, there would be my doom stack (all my units in one stack) facing off against the opponent, who had 4 or more armies, all listed as Impossible in the rating system.  Now, the roles are reversed!I am delighted that the programmers listend to the frequent complaints, and took action.  While not as "pretty" as the HOMM games, I'll be playing this a lot more than I ever did them.

_childDocuments_.review: So for starters, I've never played HOMM, so I will not be comparing the two.Hero's Hour is a fun game where you spawn on a randomly generated map and your goal is to conquer the other players. You do this by building up your town allowing you to summon units, then defeating forts that block your access to neighboring regions or by using boats to avoid the forts. Heros in this game start with two skills: one of two different skills associated to their faction, and one basic skill that any character could have. These skills then go off into trees, where your levels in a skill as well as hero level dictates the max level of skills on the trees. Skill trees can have some very fun and unique playstyles, so its well worth trying a range of characters.I've seen quite a few comments about long games being impossible as well as the fact that the AI are too strong. To sum these comments up, I believe both of these to be completely false (with some notable exceptions). I've almost managed to complete a normal game on every faction, and most games would be completed by week 12-15, being around 3-4 hours per game. Usually, my heroes by the end of the game are between levels 15-20. The game can definitely be extended beyond this if you want to, but you would need to change some of the options on the initial setup to elongate the game. Do note, that the above numbers are from me just casually playing and winning games.Don't get me wrong though. Some AIs are VERY hard to play against. Specifically, I've found that the AI with the starting trait for Mercury Blobs in the Pillar faction often times is impossible to defeat. Mercury Blobs combined with enough time and a Tent can make them able to easily beat every army thrown at them. On top of that, the pillar trait prevents them from dying, so they're a bit strong. If you want to avoid them though, just simply choose all the factions in the game. Its really as simple as that. Tide also has a similar issue for a very different reason: Tide is the only faction that can use boats regardless of if there is docks on a map. This means that they can very easily auto-win "landlocked" maps because they can steal players expansion lands or zerg cities early on in the game, whereas the other players can't due to the lack of docks.I think what it comes down to is that by this point, people expect AI in games to be a pushover, but this games AI can be very disruptive and hard to fight if you don't make sure to pay attention. You need to make sure to have 4-5 armies, with one primary army and the rest  non-primary armies. The primary army focuses on conquest of players while the non-primaries focus on expansion and defending your home territory. Utilization of your Town Portal spells will be ABSOLUTELY necessary to prevent you from getting things nabbed behind your back, which the AI is incredibly adept at doing. I think another issue is that some people don't consider how strong unit econ in this game is. If your hero has skills that give you free units for battles, they are almost 100% necessary for two reasons. One, they alleviate some losses you would normally get during battles. Two, often times, especially later in the game, you can take fights and win flawlessly. This means that the units generated after are basically just free units to extend your army; You want to keep taking easy battles in an attempt to build up a progressively more dominant army.As for the tutorial, I will say that it is lacking in some areas. One thing that I thing needs better explained is how different buildings on the map work in terms of how they work for heroes and how often they can be interact with. To quickly help new players, here are the three different types of interactables:One-Time Interactables: Interactables that can only ever be used once.Weekly Interactables: As the name implies, they can be interacted with by any hero once per week.Per-Hero Interactables: Similar to One-Time, but unlike the above can be used per hero rather than just once. A majority of interactables that change hero stats or give XP are this type of interactable.I hope that these tips help all you guys who decide to try this game. This game is actually really enjoyable if you put the time and effort to learn the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.Yeah it is poorly optimised, it lags a lot, when playing on the bigger maps and the game is about as balanced as Skyrim on steroids.With that said, it is a very fun game, that can learn you much about strategising. _childDocuments_.review: This is Hero's of Might and Magic III-IV: the Arcade Version.  The, "Mom says we have Might and Magic at home" version.Changing the combat to soft RTS is a fun idea that makes the games play much faster, and is actually quite enjoyable -- however, the combat lacks nuance and depth.  With the exception of nesting ranged troops behind melee troops, ordering idle troops into very vague "thrusts" at enemy formations, and knowing when to hide shock troops and flying troops for the right reinforcement tempo, there's very little strategy involved in this game.  Almost every battle turns into one of attrition.  Even the castle sieges are next to pointless without equal defensive troop concentrations, as the walls might as well be made of cardboard. Add into the recipe that the factions themselves are quite unbalanced in terms of unique town and hero abilities, and the game becomes a bit tedious to play.This adds up to a lot of wasted potential that turns what could have been an amazing game into an average afternoon time waster that you'll quickly grow bored of after you learn which factions to avoid playing (and that stacked elite flying units are nigh unstoppable).In the end, I recommend it because its innovative ideas are fun to experience, but only with the disclaimer that this game is not going to be what you think it is.Edit:  Upon further reflection, because of the combat, this game reminds me more of the Kessen series on PS2, but with a Might and Magic skin -- which isn't a bad thing, but again, the faction balance issues keep it from greatness.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating 2/5 stars.Without using exploits and cheesing your way through the game, it is impossible to beat on normal difficulty. If you go at it like you would with the old Heros of Might and Magic games, you will be frustrated.It will take you plenty of games to get used to the mechanics and how each round progresses, but after that, you might even start to enjoy it, especially when you find the bugs and loopholes you can use to exploit the game a little bit, without them, you probably won't win even one round.Which brings me to the actual point, why I cannot recommend the game in its current state: There is no balance in the game. Spellcaster heros and ranged units (besides Mercuries, they are just completely broken) are the strongest units, don't even try starting with a non-caster hero. The devs already moved around some masteries on heros, e.g. it might take a few turns more to unlock the Summon-cheese mode, but without those the game is simply not possible.Last, the most annoying point for me: No matter the size of the map or the number of AIs, every single AI hero (and they get produced in masses) will file into your lands. On easy difficulty you might have a month for exploration, but you can't fully explore a map before you have to start taking out factions, just solely for the reason they get immensly annoying by throwing a hero-army at you every 2 days. They don't seem to fight each other all that much, every single faction is focusing on the player first, which defeats the purpose of having giant maps in the first place. If that could be tweaked, I would be fine with the rest of the game and its difficulty, especially if the player is allowed to cheese his way through the game.But as the devs keep on fixing exploits but don't balance the rest of the game, I can't really recommend it at this current stage.

_childDocuments_.review: I left a video Review on YT for those preferring that: Gameplay: Hero's Hour is a turn based fantasy strategy game, featuring a real-time combat system. It shares a lot of similarity with the popular Heroes Of Might & Magic Franchise, but it does not simply copypasta anything. The gameplay loop is a straightforward world domination with cities to build, landtiles to conquer and heroes to level up and equip with armies and artifacts.New Features:The real-time combat system was a pleasant surprise for me. I would have preferred turn-based combat, but the spellcasting and the unit limits make it a really interesting system which offers a lot of little options to improve your performance around. The Factions and their playstyles are extremely unique and qualify as an own gameplay feature, cause every single faction has a ton of unique strategies on top of an own unit roster and more. Beyond that Hero's Hour plays pretty classic, which isn't necessarily a bad thing - it has meat and potatoes in form of solid and deep content and a really cool combat system.I Liked Most:The depth of the Factions, the sound-artwork and the QoL polish. Everything plays smoothly, works out intuitively and sounds sweet. It's a brilliant example of easy to pick up, yet difficult to master.I Liked Least:Real-Time combat was a bummer, although I started to enjoy the combat a lot over time. Personally I miss some High-res graphics, but the pixel-art style is made with love and a lotta details. I still would've preferred a different art-style, but that's just me personally. And last but not least I missed out on Multiplayer options beyond local hot seat for 2 players. I really hope for some future update/modding effort!Summary or tl;dr:Hero's Hour is a very creative Pixel-Art strategy title inspired by the Heroes Of Might & Magic (HoMM) series. It doesn't copy blindly though, offers a deep and well made Faction set (11 in total, with very unique playstyles) and brings up a unique real-time combat system. The game is very easy to learn and offers a lot of depth to dive into. Fully recommend, lot's of fun, hope it receives a bigger multiplayer implementation!

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game. The music is nice, the factions give you a wide variety of ways to test out how you might wanna battle. The battles are fun and overall, I think this game is pretty fun. That said, there are a few quirks with the game that leave me dissatisfied with my time and money spent.I'll admit, I might not be the best at strategy games like this, but it feels like the enemy AI on normal is relentless. You make a single mistake and you can hardly recover. The enemy AI's armies outmatch you if you have a single slip-up in the game. And even beyond that, what made me write this review is having all too many runs ruined because of this ridiculous mechanic. When the enemy AI goes to attack your city, if they can, they will ALWAYS pick a fight with your weakest hero even if you have 3 or 4 other heroes that can defend the city better. Heroes in this game are like commanders, but more importantly, apply passive buffs to the armies they command and can bring in spells to change how the battle goes. Having a hero you send off to take weak camps or primarily trail off to collect other resources without taking fights can be the sole reason between victory and defeat.This is a massive issue because usually you'll have your first hero hog a large majority of the experience and become powerful. So your other heroes will be fairly behind even with the bodyguard mechanic. The bodyguard mechanic makes it so that new heroes enlisted to help your faction will have better armies based on your strongest army/hero. So it encourages you to try and handle the mass of the land with extra heroes. However, if those weaker heroes die, they will be sent to your city and forced to defend it, even if your strongest hero is sitting in the city. You win the game by going to the enemy city, fighting their defenses, and capturing it. You have to go there. You can't just camp in your city and hope for the best.What really made me write this review is also the fact that when you go to the enemy city to fight them, you have to fight their strongest hero even if there are weaker heroes nearby, giving the illusion that you have an easy fight.Honestly, it feels like the enemy AI is just cheating at that rate. They get to pick better fights than you no matter what. I've lost so many games that I might've been able to win based on this decision alone. It's beyond frustrating.As I mentioned before, this is the normal difficulty of the game. However, playing on easy is an entirely different story. I literally took the main faction's city and didn't realize this until an hour later in my playthrough. Technically you win by taking the city AND clearing out all of the enemy armies. So you either have a boring time taking over the land or play perfectly.I adore this game. I didn't spend 23 hours to uninstall it and remorse over the money I spent on it, but it's just unfair. Until they change the scaling of the enemy AI to not be so overbearing on normal and not force unfair fights, I personally cannot recommend this game to my peers or anyone else.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant to review this at first, because there was some game-breaking glitches still lurking around in the game. Might still be a few - I've had some weird interactions in my games. The worst was my ship during naval combat deciding to leave the battlemap, drowning my entire armies. They seem to have fixed this, among many others, and the new update has greatly improved the many different skills, and by extension all of the dozens of characters.When it comes to the classic feeling of Heroes Of Might and Magic style games, I've seen two directions taken. This was the correct one. The frantic combat is endlessly engaging, and there's a huge variety of playstyles that can be supported. Unlockables and difficult achievements keep the game interesting even once the AI ceases to be a real challenge save on the most oppressive games modes (which still feel beatable, though only just - an excellent balance point to find).In its current state I would heartily recommend it to anyone looking for the game carrying the blood of the aforementioned HoM&M in the current age. It fulfills the lifelong dream of seeing the overstacked army of dragons descend on a hapless stack of mooks many of us have had playing these games, a feature missing in many of the attempts to capture the attention of the lovers of the classic games. I probably still have more than a hundred hours left in this game before I've had a chance to play all the options it gives me. Well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun little HoMM3 inspired game. The overworld gameplay is very similar to classic Heroes of Might and Magic but the auto-battler style combat adds it's own unique twist to it.The battles can be rather enjoyable, as there is some tactics involved in initial positioning, but as the battles get bigger it's way to unwieldy to control normally and so it becomes more a choice of what units to deploy first and use of hero spells and abilities.There are some pretty wild item and ability combinations that can lead to some pretty broken gameplay, but boy is that stuff a lot of fun to use. Balance between the different factions doesn't seem perfect but it does look like the devs are aware and are going to try and improve things later on. Currently though all the factions seem fun and have their own unique mechanics to try out. Faction units as well can have some unique combinations of abilities that make unit choices matter a bit.Mod support is coming and once that hits I expect the community to go crazy is strange and wonderful new factions to try out.

_childDocuments_.review: Hero's Hour is a bit of a mixed bag.You'll either love the fast-paced progression or you'll hate it, and make no mistake, Hero's Hour is very much a rush to the finish line.Most of the game mechanics work well but faction and unit balancing are an ongoing issue. With that said, there has been an update to difficulty and it has made the progression slightly easier on the lower settings. Factions are relatively unique, although, some strategies outperform others by a large margin and heroes follow much the same trend.Game play is very forward oriented, you'll move throughout the map strategically picking fights and collecting resources to produce units and upgrade the town. Strategically being the focus here as a wrong move early on can lead to the AI snowballing to victory. Combat itself is wave VS wave where you as the player watch the battle unfold with little control except for spells and abilities. I must say I really do enjoy the simplicity of it all.On to my gripes. The UI leaves a lot of be desired from the menu, to the text, and even navigation could use work. Performance is spotty in large battles and even more so when a large number of factions are involved. Certain achievements are bugged as well and despite trying to troubleshoot the issues I can't be bothered anymore.Overall, Hero's Hour has provided me quite a bit of fun. It certainly has a number of issues and could have likely used more time in the oven, or better play testing. With that said, I do think it will reach full potential given some more TLC from the developers. Given that patches are rolling out fairly quickly, I do think this is worth a recommendation, perhaps with a 'buyer beware' caveat for those who can't handle the immediate issues or style/pace of progression...

_childDocuments_.review: This game does an amazing job combining strategy, tactics, and role-playing. The individual elements--town building, resource management, hero customization, exploration, and massive real-time battles--seamlessly integrate into a whole experience with ridiculous levels of depth and replayability. Thanks to the many factions and maps, I expect to sink hours and hours into this without getting bored. At the same time, it's quite easy to learn with simple, intuitive controls.There's still room for improvement though:-Once one player wins a major battle, the loser is unlikely to ever catch up, because the winner will always have a bigger army. Would it be possible to add some kind of catch-up mechanic?-The exploration starts to feel predictable after a while. There's always a similar collection of mines, treasures, and troop production. It would be great to add more unexpected, game-altering discoveries on the map.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a fun take on the HoMM formula with numerous improvements:+ combat is real-time with pause, NOT an auto-battler (all the people complaining about being obliterated at higher difficulties obviously treat it as an auto-battler and get wrecked by the AI);+ magic and spells are hugely varied and very powerful with interesting effects (not boring Fireball; Bigger Fireball; Biggest Fireball...);+ huge faction/units/heroes/skills variety, so huge that I have played nearly a 100 hours and still cannot decide which one is my favourite, everything can be made into a winner;+ tons of quality-of-life improvements over the HoMM formula (portal spell for every hero; no need for hero-trains to move units to the frontline...)+ game is still actively supported, new content is added for free regularly and bugs get fixed in a timely manner.Negatives:- no campaign, no story, no lore;- no pre-made maps;- random map generator sometimes bugs out and places a few buildings that cannot be accessed on the map.

_childDocuments_.review: As the other said, this is a HoMM clone. Nice little game when it works.  The game crashes, a lot.  Go to hero inventory, crash. Enter city to build, crash. Pickup random artifact, crash. End of combat, crash. Even the Tutorial crashes. The game crashes so many times during a game, its really really annoying. The next thing is, the game lags, the larger map, the much more lag you will get. It can take up to several minutes before the AI is done moving before its your turn, and this is each turn, so prepare to get a huge cup of coffee ready if you play on bigger maps. Also the AI cheats like crazy. The harder the difficulty, the more it cheats.  You can attack an AI town, destroy all their armies that combined have a lot more units than you could ever possible get. Then the AI next turn pops out with another hero full of units, and another one again and again. Really cheating AI. This game is not done yet, it really needs to work out all the crashes, the bugs and the lags before I would suggest anyone buying this game. So far, stay away for a few patches at least, or you will end up frustrated with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Just play HOMM3/HotA or the new Songs of Conquest.For your money you're getting dumb AI, no campaign(yet), no custom maps(but there might be some online), no multiplayer(except for hotseat). Only a random map generator that puts out the same predictable generic patterns. Ugly graphics, inconsistent sprite work - highly detailed buildings next to tiny 8x8 unit sprites make me want to pull my eyes out, worse than a 20 year old game; and yet with artificial limits on the number of units in battle because the game lags when large armies are fighting. There is some fun to be had, as there's a lot of creative factions with novel ideas to try and exploit, if only against neutral units around the map or up against the massively cheating AI(if you up the difficulty). The game is also in active development, so there's always another "cool" faction to look forward to, but doesn't seem like much work is being done on other aspects of the game right now. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR at the bottomI enjoy the organized chaos of watching a large number of small things fight each other. This game offers almost exclusively that.The rest of it is the strategy layer that determines where you fight and the resources you have to fight with.There's a ingame book that explains every unit, artifact, faction, spell, and more. I have failed to notice a search function but you can click on the relevant tabs.Also you can save/load whenever you want outside of a real time fight. Great way to mess around and find out.The strategy layer is pretty simple: Get more things that help you win such as Heroes, artifacts, units, and the resource nodes that let you get more of them. Heroes each tend to have their own skill tree and while there are overlapping skills, the order in which they get them and their stat progressions are different. Each of the factions feel pretty different with distinct gimmicks. The artifacts can greatly change how you play from giving you skill ranks to giving your entire army healing based on the damage they do in the battle layer. Don't ignore them.Units all have different abilities that define how they fight, with the default being that they walk up to things and swing at them and some of the possibilities include Ranged attacks, aoe ranged attacks, Spellcasting, self detonation, cloning, conferring different classes of immunity like constructs being immune to healing and fear and even just being a map range turret.Resource nodes generate resources and are guarded by neutral enemies. Fighting them will let you see how your initial fighting plan holds up and give you the resources going forward.The actual battle section is automatic with limited intervention. I say limited, but with high enough spellcasting you can summon meteors that one hit random pockets of BOTH sides of a fight or just set everyone on fire. Mind control and turning units into frogs happens too. So much can happen. Your units will run towards the nearest enemy until they can attack them and ranged units will get penalties to melee and try to back off. Theres other nuances but learning how to manipulate the fights and win battles that are above your strength projection is part of the fun. So even if it says a fight is impossible- well there's an achievement for winning anyway. Cheese aggressively at higher difficulties.Speaking of difficulty, there's a lot you can toggle. Resource rates, turning events on and off, determining the amount of cheating the AI can do, enabling different map features and affecting their frequency-Dont like the fog of war? Yeet it.I dont even think it affects achievements.There's no story mode as far as I can tell but there are mods are out there with custom maps and there's atleast 20 different maps already in the game that get really big. You can actually set the opponents you'll face and even decide to split the other factions in a game to being on different teams. By default it's free for all.Achievements unlock heroes. Some achievements are funny, challenging or interestingSome achievements should really be changed. There's ways to cheese them if you really want the hero they unlock. check the steam guides.Dev takes feedback in their discord server.TLDRAllegedly similar to heroes of might and magic but real time. Never played em. I think this is fun. I like throwing large seas of units at eachotherVery customize-able difficultyLots of variety and challenge availableLategame fights and large maps might be a big hit on your framerate. Disabling particles helps a lot.The game is updating and changing quite a bit. I can tell that there have been changes to hero skill trees and I can see more on the horizon.Certain pieces of information are hard to find or even after 150 hours I cant tell where I was supposed to find it. Trial and error and paying attention to what happens on the field will let you notice a difference if you dont know what an artifact does but often the information should reference something found in the lexicon. You may un-ironically be a shadow wizard casting spells. I hope they add more shadow spells.

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches an  specific itch for me. There's a turn-based strategy series out there called , where you play a minor god and fight all the other wannabes to become the one true god. Battles play out without direct player control: you can only queue a set of orders, and most units have memorable quirks (like the ability to convert enemy units, or invisibility). The unit sprites are 2D sprites set against a roughly 3D background.To me, Hero's Hour is that battle-system layered on top of a Heroes of Might and Magic overworld. It's an offering because I can play out those exciting hundred-unit battles with chaotic and unpredictable magic without being overwhelmed by 's finicky resourcing & supply system. I love watching my little units get buffed and do their cute little murders! If (as a little kid) you loved watching ants swarm each other, or loved watching arrows advance on virtual battlefield game-shows, this will scratch your itch as well (I know I'm not the only one!)Each faction also brings to the table different mechanics, enough to differentiate and give an edge (except Pyre--they get 2 different mechanics). Again, this reminds me of : Decay is Late-Age Ermor, Enclave is Middle-Age Ctis, Order represents the various bless-heavy nations, Delirium is R'lyeh, Pillar is T'ien C'hi and so on. Honestly I'd only suggest 3 more 'improvements':

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game on itch.io and buy it on steam as soon as it's published. I must say there are quite few differences from the itch.io game. Some better some worst. Overall it's a great game. But here are some adjustments required for developer to consider.1. Not enough info on anything.Upgrades of the utility buildings are not defined clearly. You just pay and see what it does.Some skill upgrades on heroes are not defined. For example necromancy definition states " After combat...... Each rank also lowers the mana cost per unit" by how much? Is it some percent times rank? or is it 1 mana times rank? Most of the skills descriptions feel like dodged explanations. "Amount depends size of the army, mana used in battle, number of enemies killed, number of owned units died...." Player can have information on their own units but you can't find anything on enemy units before battle. This makes some easy battles lost and hard battles not so hard. After some point difficulty of battles does trick player and it just becomes blindly attacking the opposing sites without any strategy. EDIT: This was my bad there is a lexicon in the pause menu. Also there is a way to access lexicon without pausing. However I'm not going to delete this part since finding lexicon is hard. There can be an easy way to find it. 2. Reinforcement deployment.It's complicated as hell. You can't just add 2 or 3 units from lets say 100 unit stack. It adds a different flavor into the battle but it is impossible to control what to add to your initial combat army. There is a button for filling up the remaining power. But most of the times it just complicate things even more.Also on the same topic you can call your reinforcement army to battle but in which order or which units are not controlled by the player. It feels like some random dudes on the bench are joining to the battle when you are about to die. So they come to fight to die as well. There is a bar for reinforcements to arrive but if I can't make the decision on who to call it feels pretty much meaningless.Solution: Before the battle player should divide the army however they like. Taking 30 units from 200 stack shouldn't be hard. Just select the stack and give an option to player for division. Next, player should be informed on how much reinforcement armies they have. And lastly player make the decision on their reinforcement armies. First reinforcements should include these units seconds should include these units ... Don't get me wrong. I'm saying this again. This game is a great game. It just needs some quality of life updates. Overall it's somewhere in between Heroes and M&M 3 and Heroes and M&M 4. Heroes doesn't feel overwhelmingly powerful. Real time combat is definitely better than turn based. Spawning all the units on the battlefield makes you feel the chaos element in the battles.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, lots of depth, wonderful style. Can be challenging or relaxing at your choice and has many cool things you can do and a ton of variety to it. Its creative, love the pixel art, and generally love the mechanics. Turn based tactical play where you focus on building an army, managing resources, exploring, and somewhat tactical combat just really hit the spot. While there are a few things that are a bit strong / weak and there is some minimal variance to how you approach each run I do not think that's a bad thing, for example things like the Devour skill or free summons being kind of a tier above everything else, and the whole focusing on a single hero is generally the best way to play. But there is always going to be an optimal way to play, and it just so happens I quite like focusing on one dude and summons so it certainly suits me. Particularly for single player that kind of balance is not to important, its fun to find broken and optimal strategies, and you can always chose to try a different approach if you want a challenge to. So overall the game gets a thumbs up, and I find my self coming back for another game despite thinking I am done with it on the regular. That being said, I am rather disappointed at the lack of campaign or pvp online or otherwise. Lacking both these features is a pretty huge turn off, and it seems to be a rather intentional choice. With one or both of those the game could quickly turn  into something amazing. But as of now it just kind of falls a bit flat. A bunch of different maps, but none of them are really that different, offer any story, or new challenge. It just mostly boils down to can you find a broken build, pray you don't get assaulted either to early, or by more than one thing at a time. And even if you are only attacked by one thing at a time after you have had time to prepare, you have to just hope you get attacked from an angle you are close enough to defend. You cant realistically spread your forces out as all but the most hyper focused hero will get easily overwhelmed, and you pretty much just cant beat the AI in speed / numbers. I have beat it on the hardest difficulties and the largest maps as well, so its not a matter of "get gud" either, these are just some core issues. Very close to being an amazing game, and I could not justifiably give it a thumbs down, but it desperately needs at least one of, if not all of: Campaign, PvP, or a little more balance in how things get to go on the offensive (whether that's you getting attacked early, or trying to rush your opponent down.)

_childDocuments_.review: Update: I'm changing my rating to recommended. As janky as the game is, it is actually pretty addictive and can be a ton of fun. It's not a very polished experience, but it definitely has that "just one more turn" appeal and I really started liking the chaos and a bit of randomness of the real time battles.----I'm really torn about this one. After playing the tutorial, I felt like I should finally give Heroes 3 a go and I didn't regret. Coming back to Hero's Hour after Heroes 3 (which is obviously a huge inspiration) doesn't really work in Hero's Hour's favor. There are a few problems I have with the game so far, which make me doubt whether I'll be able to put significantly more time into it.The first and probably the biggest issue is the UI and the graphics. It can look charming in the videos or static screenshots, but I feel very disoriented by it during the gameplay. Not to mention the whole pixelart shtick is so overused. Also purely from a visual standpoint, the user interface doesn't mix well together with the units' and world's artwork in my opinion.Secondly - compared to Heroes 3, it feels a bit too complicated. Where Heroes 3 is nicely streamlined and you can just casually pick it up and play it, Hero's Hour leaves me confused.The third one is a minor one, but I would really like to have some campaign exploring the world, and not have the whole game really on procedural generation.On the other hand I kind of like the idea of combat being realtime, it reminds me of a game I played as a kid and really enjoyed - Legion.I like the rest of the ideas the game has to offer, but I don't feel like I would recommend anyone to buy this game unless being in a deep deep sale, because the first two issues I mentioned make the game too confusing and unpleasant for me to play, despite the rest of the enticing ideas.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely gives reviews, but I like to give this one.This  game is great. Lots of units, buildings, items, tons of spells, different ways to win your fight. At the start of the game, especially if your are playing on challanging or higher difficulty, it is advised to be as efficient and fast as possible. If your hero is level 10 and your enemy is 16 already, you may get steamrolled very early. So it's very important to get your economy running, build up your army and most importantly get your hero to a good level. And the game mechanics are really good balanced at the start of the game. You have a constant feeling of progression, get more options to choose from (spells, units, equipment, buildings) and at some point you battle the enemy for land/mines. In mid-game, depending on your choices, the game gets either hard or easy, but rarely something in between. And in late game, you will very likely steamroll the enemy yourself. The enemy heros aren't that much of a threat, but the AI is really good at controlling like 5 heroes and at targeting your different cities. So the AI kinda forces you to also play multiple heroes, because your main hero will never be able to protect all cities at once. And as long as the enemy has a city, his heroes will keep reviving when you have defeated them, which certainly will drag the game out (especially on huge maps)Abotu the battles: Yes, for most fights the you can go full-auto. But when the fights are moderate, hard or even near impossible, the spell system makes a BIG difference in my opinion. Use low-mana-cost Hex to turn ranged enemy units into frogs? Summon units behind enemy lines to ambush them and bring the enemies ranged units into close combat? Reduce stats of enemy elite units? This game has SO many spells to choose from and is the most fun part for me. And then there is also positioning of your units. You can give commands and tell your ranged units to move further away or to move behind your more tanky units. This can make a big difference at the start of the game, where every single unit counts.So: Great game, really lots of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun autobattling take in Heroes of Might and Magic, it will be instantly recognizable to anyone who has played that series in the past.  The game has a suprisingly good amount of replayability, with over a dozen different factions and with different heroes within those factions with different skill trees, divided between melee, ranged and mage heroes.  You can also unlock additional heroes per faction by doing in game achievements, which gives you additional play options as well as giving you incentive to go after achievements.  Games are not that long ranging from less than 1 to several hours depending on difficulty, map size and number of factions.  The game does tend to lag a bit once battles get huge, with hundreds of units all doing animations and spell effects going off, but it's not too bad.  I got it as part of a bundle so it was a great deal for me but it's on sale pretty frequently and worth that price as well.
