_childDocuments_.review: If Heroes and Might and Magic 2 was taken to 11, it would be this game.The Heroes of Might and Magic series (specifically, from 1-3) is legendary, so much so that they’re still some of the highest-sold games on Good Old Games in history (led by III).  I remember buying HOMM III in 1999/2000 and played the entire game between my last year of high school and first year of college.  While I’m not a fan of having to build up characters only to lose them in subsequent scenarios, the ability to retain a hero between scenarios of a campaign kept it from being too heart-breaking of feeling like I lost progress.  But the games themselves are a ton of fun and are the core mechanics of many turn-based strategy games, especially my favorite of all-time, King’s Bounty (essentially, HOMM without the scenario-to-scenario loss of experience-based progress).  This game went back to the roots of those game mechanics—so much so that the graphics are closer to 1 and 2 than 3—and created so many enemies, races, and game types that it’s quite astounding how varied the gameplay styles can be.  The major difference is the switch from turn-based combat to real-time battles that you control loosely mainly with spells and initial troop placement (as well as some minimal commands).The Positives:-This game is a labor of love.  One person playing around with the HOMM formula and creating dozens and dozens of varied playable characters, races, enemies, items, etc.  It is so wild.  This is Minecraft-level creativity at work.-The graphics are amazingly modern and classic—fully pixelated 90s-style graphics but with high-definition and then thousands of little troops acting on the screen at the same time (it gets wild when you have two maxed-out armies fighting).  It is so much fun to take in all of the beautiful colors and graphics along with the animations and battles.  It’s truly outstanding.-The gameplay strategies are wild.  I started out with one race where I was able to combine a strategy of getting tons of undead troops and increasing my stats by sacrificing troops.  You can create insanely high-powered characters that way.  Other times, you can build up massive armies and increase their abilities.  With another strategy, you can get the right spells and take out huge chunks of enemies or empower your team to take out more than they should.  You really have to do your best—in fact, you can often only defeat a few groups of enemies for the first week before you have enough troops, abilities, spells, etc. to take out anyone else.  You also have extra heroes that primarily serve as go-fers for a while, but you need 2-3 heroes who can fight if you want to be able to hold off from multiple attackers in weeks 3-4+.-The combat is fast, furious, and fun.  This is the big innovation for this game: you can have thousands of troops fighting on the screen at the same time, and many of the spells and combat tactics have to be strategically/tactfully triggered to maximize kills and minimize losses.  And when you have thousands of enemies on the screen, it might be a little slow and unwieldy, but it is cool.-The scenarios are cool.  You can vary the number of enemies, the size of the map, the abundance of resources, etc., and a variety of other elements of the game.  Many of those options help with the achievements, if that’s your thing, and so it’s cool to, say, jack up the number of artifacts (or get an artifact store) to collect them all (because there are many).-The games are pretty fun.  While at higher difficulty levels you have to play a certain way for about a week or so before the enemy swoops in and tries to kill you, at regular difficulty it can be fun to try different tactics and combine exploration, resource gathering, fighting some map enemies, etc.  You have to balance how far your best hero goes and balance it out, but as you get better you can afford to have a couple of backup heroes get decent enough to defend.The Negatives:-No campaign.  The creator made it pretty clear that not only was this an Early Access game that was effectively kind of a hobby for him (he built the game in a year and was planning on moving on to build another one until this one skyrocketed in popularity and people wanted more), and so he focused the game on creating your own scenarios and playing one-off games for fun.  The larger scenarios are sprawling and difficult to navigate (e.g., if you get too far from your towns, enemies will swoop in and you’ll be too far to defend and have to retreat).  It might change, but at the time I played, it was just the scenario-based play.-Strategies that might feel like “cheesing” the game.  The ability to sacrifice troops for ability points, which you can do in every battle, can give you insanely high stats.  It’s so much fun (because you earn it through sacrifice), but if you combine a couple of strategies, you can really be strong.  But it does balance out in the fact that only one hero can be really good if you want to dominate.  And so large games, even with an overpowered hero, can still be difficult because you’re fighting massive competing armies.-Loooooong games (if that’s a negative for you).  For the larger maps with many competing armies, it can take a long time for just one game.  That’s your choice, though, so it’s not so much of a negative of the game as much as it is your choice to do so.  So you can see that I’m grasping at straws to find negatives, but that might be a minus for you and so just stick with smaller maps if you don’t want it to get too long.-Some of the same issues as the HOMM series.  It would’ve been interesting if the game would’ve innovated in how the gameplay worked where maybe you could develop a few heroes or have more troops, but it’s possible that a player could’ve quickly gamed it where they’d have a mega-army with that kind of troop growth and gameplay.  I don’t know.  It’s so tough that I can’t criticize it but will mention that it’s a trade-off that the game makes similarly to the HOMM series.-It felt like the low-level troops quickly become completely useless after week 2.  I always like the idea of balance where an army of smaller enemies could fight decently and hold their own against higher levels, but an army of small troops will get slaughtered by the high-level troops—even if you have the high attack and defense scores.  Again, not an issue per se, but it dials down the strategy to more of “get a ranged unit, a tank unit, and a fun damage or crowd-control unit to win” approach.As you can see, this is a fantastic game that is one of the best of the genre in years and one might argue borderline perfects the HOMM II model.  It’s hard to criticize the game since most of it is more of a trade-off or pro/con situation involved with the genre or the game it’s the spiritual successor of.  If you love HOMM, you’ll love this game.  It is an astounding achievement for one person to do for fun.  Bravo for that amazing accomplishment.  Play this game if you love the genre, the art style, or just want to try a great game.  It’s worth it.  I 100%ed this game because it was so fun, and I recommend that anyone who enjoys PC gaming at least try a couple of scenarios.  It sucks that there’s no campaign with a story and you have to make up your own, but otherwise it’s as good as you can get for this style of game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun. Charming graphics, fun gameplay loop. Overall, I recommend it. But there are issues you should be aware of before you buy. This game has some rough edges. First, I'll give you a couple tips if you're a complete noob. Firstly, this is not really an autobattler. If you don't ever control your troops at all, you'll lose a lot more often. Magic is extremely OP, get as many spells for your hero as possible. Pay attention to where your enemy's reinforcements spawn, and put long lasting AOE (area of effect) spells on that location.(spells like meteor rain, siege rain, etc). Whenever possible, use aforementioned AOE spells to disrupt your enemy's ranged units. Position your big beefy guys and melee troops in front of your ranged troops before the battle to maximize their effectiveness. If you have a fast group of units, it's always a good idea to position them away from your main army so you can flank the enemy ranged troops. Most ranged troops cannot attack at melee range or their damage is greatly reduced, so the faster you can get troops in their face the better. Last tip for battles is a tactic called "hammer and anvil." Summoning spells are good for this tactic. If you summon troops behind your enemy's front line and then smash into the enemy with your own troops from the other side, the enemy will be stuck fighting in two directions and you'll have the advantage. Very effective tactic. Rough Edges:-The UI doesn't scale particularly well. The minimap gets in the way. Either it's too small to read anything on it, or it's too huge and takes up too much of the screen-Game needs a "turn off mouse scrolling" menu option. In battles when you're trying to move troops around from reserves or cast spells and you move your cursor down, the camera also starts scrolling down. It's incredibly irritating. It sort of works to hold W to keep the camera still while you click stuff on the bottom action bars, but it's not a great fix.-The game doesn't control super smoothly, it's clunky and too easy to misclick, and in battles the "drip" feature bugs out frequently when you're trying to move guys to or from reserves. -The AI cheats (as in it gets more resources than you), so you need to be aware of that if you want to win. -In larger games, waiting for AI turns gets extremely tedious if there are 3+ AIs. The game also seems to slow down a ton, so I suspect it has optimization issues despite its simple graphics. -This game is not well balanced, but I don't consider that a bad thing. It lets you do some bonkers strategies that are 2000% unfairly overpowered, but I think that adds to the game's charm.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for March 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before April 4th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A fast-paced version of Heroes of Might and Magic.  In Hero’s Hour, players take a champion who belongs to one of 12 races and fight for supremacy against other characters, whether human or computer controlled.  This is based on Heroes of Might and Magic and turn-based strategy, but in Hero’s Hour, the combat is real-time, with units not requiring micromanagement.  Players can try to order units or cast magic, but this is more about the hero and unit management than focused on individual combat. At the same time, taking away the deliberate combat does lose something special in Heroes of Might and Magic style, and units all feel like they chugged a few pixie sticks before jumping into battle. There’s sadly no campaign that was the best part of Heroes of Might and Magic, instead you play through randomized maps that you set up.  The game promises a faster game for hot-seat fans, but I still imagine this game will take quite a long time to complete.Pick this up if you like Heroes of Might and Magic or King’s Bounty.  Realize the game is more fast-paced in battles as you’ve seen, but that can also be a benefit.  However, this is a slow methodical game outside of the combat, so players will ultimately have to be dealing with how best to use their units and resources.  This also has a decent learning curve that will take time before players fully understand the choices in the game. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: It's an alright game, kind of like an auto battler version of the old HOMM games. But it does have some issues that'd I'd like to see fixed.- Many different factions, thus allowing different ways to play.- Lots of different units, that have different abilities.- Retro graphics mostly looks nice, but some sprites seem much higher quality then others, which can look a bit odd and inconsistent.- Music is ok, sounds like HOMM music. However, it can get a bit boring after a while, so maybe add some more sound tracks.- Bad/Cheating AI. This is the biggest issue the game has. I will say that the cheating/braindead AI needs a rework, they're far too stupid and cheat way too much, like we're talking Creative Assembly levels of cheating AI here. AI Summoning armies out of thin air and getting free resources. Just make a competent AI and you won't have to resort to giving it cheats. Like if it really must cheat only give it those cheats on the max difficulty.- Bugs. There's some bugs in the game. I have had a couple of crashes. So Hopefully that continues to get ironed out.- Frame Rate has a meltdown sometimes. Hopefully some more performance optimisation can be done to improve this. I did see it got better in a recent update, but I think there's probably still room for improvement.- Some balance issues. Nothing too crazy, but some factions seem straight up better then others. I have played them all a few games each to gauge how they play.- Releasing a DLC when the base game is missing content is not smart. I read that there was meant to be a campaign in the base game, but it's not there? So I'm not sure what happened with that. The dev should probably finish the base game before releasing a DLC.Now, should you buy the game? Well that depends. I'd say if you played the old Heroes of Might & Magic games, yes. Buy it. It's worth it for the nostalgia alone, even if the game is a bit rough around the edges and suffers from dumb AI.As for those who have not played the old heroes games, I'll leave it up to you to make your own decision. _childDocuments_.review: I am not good at traditional 4X strategy games, so a strategy game along these lines is easier for me to understand.  I would say this is more like a 4X-Lite or 4X-Mini instead, because of a few things such as the basic concepts of battles; battles are for the most part automatically played on their own with some occasional clicking by the player in order to do things such as using spells or retreat, for example.  Afterwards the claimed bases must be defended from potential future attacks from the enemy by maintaining a large and diverse army at that base.  There is some resource management, but it is basically just for the home base and that does not need to be continually monitored and modified as the game progresses; building up the home base unlocks stronger forces and abilities, which in turn allows stronger fights to be won.It is a relatively simpler concept and because it involves less micro-management than a traditional 4X game, it is more along the lines of a game that can be played casually for short breaks during the day.  This is not to say that there is little content to the game--There already seems to be a diverse variety of classes, troops, abilities, and items in this game, and the randomization allows the game to be a little different each time.  I will admit that I am not entirely good at this game yet so i still have some difficulty from time to time; now if this was a traditional 4X game I probably would give up out of frustration and not give it another try, but I keep coming back to this game.  Apparently the developers will be adding more content, so we will see how the game changes and evolves as time goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. The art is nostalgic and astounding, the generated maps look great, the diversity of factions is so unique, the strategy is simple despite the high learning curve, and the gameplay is just overall satisfying.HOW TO WORK AROUND THE REALLY HARD DIFFICULTY:1.) Be aggressive really early. It is tempting to turtle your army and wait till you can overwhelm the stations without losses, but doing so makes you fall behind in resources rediculously. It is better to claim mines and such ASAP so that you can accumulate wealth enough to pull ahead. It is better to loose an army and gain consistant income, rather than wait 7 turns for you to take that income to save a measley 25 units2.) Challenge ratings are a lie. There are challenges above army heads that say "easy, moderate, challenging, hard, near impossible, or Impossible". I have beat an impossible difficulty before, because the calculation doesn't account for body guards or your hero's (militia leader ) power/magic capability, which can easily flip overwhelming armies on their heads3.) Tactics matter. Part of how you win(in skirmishes), is scanning the army's specific enemy stats and skills. I was able to win a near impossible round WITHOUT a hero simply by using advantagous enemy placement. (i can go into great detail with this, but basic principles. Units are stronger bunched up, keep the units that regen each battle on the front lines, organizing so you surround the enemy force, ect.)4.) your hero is a god. Heros are the units that lead the entire force, and for some reason, the forces get BUFFED BASED ON THE HERO'S STATS. The more battles you do, the more exp the hero gets. PLAN which hero you want depending on your playstyle. Get a skill-upgrade order to make them the most powerful.5.) Know your faction. Every faction has something overpowered about them, you just have to figure out what it is. They each seem to have a unique way of generating excess gold, besides spamming gold mines of course. They each have niche units that you need to understand so you can use them with the best advantage. 6.) PLAN your build order in your city. It looks very linear seeing as how cities have pre-set buildings. But KNOWING what to get first in less turns can get you the most financial success, and the biggest armies early on

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:  It's literally 'Heroes of Might and Magic' (HoMaM) but with auto-battle-ish combatCons:  Each battle has a limit to the amount of 'army power' that you can put on the battlefield. This means that you'll never be able to crush the enemy and also means that you'll constantly have your army chipped away at after each battle. This limitation makes the game more punishing and also dramatically extends the TTC (time to completion) of every map. I remember having played all the HoMaM games growing up, that often I'd spend 60hours+ playing on a single map and that was WITHOUT this 'army power limitation' that this game has. I wish that the limit was either completely removed or a simpler 'total units limitation' was implemented instead, because the current iteration of the 'army power limit' literally only serves to punish the player and to dramatically slow the TTC. If something isn't broken, don't fix it... and there was nothing wrong with the way that HoMaM did 'army power' or overall unit growth. When I started a new game, I had 14 'Impossible' power battles around my starting position... this should NOT be like this. It should be like in HoMaM, where all the battles close to the player's starting position are either 'easy, average or challenging'. Having that many 'Impossible' power battles in the starting position means the game is designed wrong, or there's something broken in the map RNG. The game has a huge amount of missing tool-tips. There were easily 5 times when I said to myself "why isn't there a tool-tip being displayed here?" You have no choice with regard to choosing your starting heroes OR what skills / bonuses they have No fps options No borderless fullscreen mode Can't change resolution size when selecting fullscreen mode No colorblind accessibility optionsIn summation: It's literally HoMaM, but the army limitation in this game makes the game constantly punishing and slows down the TTC. If the 'army limitation' was removed, then I'd recommend this game with no problem... but with it in the game, plus all the other issues highlighted above, it's simply NOT a game that I'd recommend you buy over a game like HoMaM4,5,6 or King's Bounty: Armored Princess / Crossworlds... in fact, I'm pretty sure that you could get ALL those games for around $18 if you get them on sale. So I just can't recommend this game, since it's not better than HoMaM5 which is 15years old and much cheaper.Here's my first hour or so of the game: For more reviews, visit my curator page: For my full recommended list of games:

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great and, more importantly, sorely needed game - it carries the banner (literally and metaphorically) of Heroes of Might and Magic incredibly well. However, just like HOMM it's somewhat of an inscrutable mess especially with moderate to complex interactions.E.g. I'm posting this review after getting just trounced by AI (Google wthe AI and make your own decision), not because I was playing poorly but because a city of mine was about to be attacked and I had no idea how my two heroes, whose combined armies could definitely handle the attack, was going to work on defense if I put them both in the city.The result - poor. It force-chose my initial hero and I think what was her army, but then also let me reinforce with the army of the other... or something like that? I honestly don't even know because the weird UI makes these things difficult. Long story short with this particular story: it was a mess and the order-of-operations completely screwed me as my main hero who could cast Resurrect lvl 3 *six times* was relegated to cleanup duty, and by that time she only had a handful of units so resurrect was useless.However, it was still fun! And honestly more accessible than your standard HOMM fare. Don't get me wrong, I loved HOMM (and turn-based games in general) but it had a high bar to entry and also took way more time than it needed to. The "auto battle" nature of this one makes battles just more streamlined; and the auto-resolve is super nice.Ultimately I recommend this for HOMM fans as it's a worthy successor, though you're going to spend a good few hours figuring out how everything works and, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, would a handful of QoL polish go a long way. But if I can forgive its flaws you likely can too, jut know you're getting a side of jank.Also, it seems to bug out on my Steam Deck (OLED) for some reason? E.g. clicking in certain menus for landmarks, like those where you can hire units, skips the day forward for some reason. Honestly still haven't figured out exactly what's going on because I can't replicate it on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review. In this episode I check out a new Turn Based Strategy game with Heroes Hour by one person development team Benjamin Hauer. This game takes place in a Fantasy universe with a variety of diverse races that are all trying to build their own empire.The game features city building and exploration, hero and army management and of course, fast paced combat. While i did enjoy this game, i think that it does have some balance issues in the latest update. Please note: All opinions in this video are my own. Game was provided by the developer for review purposes================================================Hero's Hour - First Impressions: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Bitchute: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Twitch: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Odysee: Twitter: Facebook: Email Enquiries: Heroes Hour on Steam: ================================================Hero's Hour is an accessible, yet-deep and content-rich Strategy Roleplaying Game. Take control of your hero, explore the world, build up your town, fight fast-paced battles, level up your hero and amass an army large enough to take out the opponents - before they take you out.Turn Based + Real TimeWhile exploring the overworld and developing your town and army are both turn-based, giving you time to think and plan out your next moves, in battles your units will do the best to fight for themselves in real time - all hundreds of them. Cast spells and give attack orders to swing the tide of battle - or just sit back and watch as your might unfolds.Procedural GenerationHero's Hour brings impactful procedural generation to the strategy game formula, ensuring that every time you play, there will be new areas to explore and strange buildings to enhance your hero or army. Seek out obelisks to start you on small procedural quests that send you around the world. You won't even be able to use the same build order each time you play the same faction.Features11 factions with special mechanics, strengths and weaknesses22 hero classes, with a special skill each50 common hero skills177 units (and 99 upgraded units)80 unique unit abilities166 artifacts83 spells (+18 spells unlocked via skills)Dozens of impactful map buildingsLocal "hotseat" multiplayerCo-op with other players or even with the AIBeing on the faster side compared to other turn based strategy games, you may even be able to finish the hotseat games that you start!

_childDocuments_.review: Shameless hommage to HoMM. =)Borderline copypasta in places, but with enough of its own to be interesting. The battles are quite different and probably more fun on a small scale.On a large scale, however, they can become extremely tedious for a couple of reasons:1. The combat is "real-time", but game seems pretty badly optimised, so even on a powerful machine, it can be sluggish. Overworld turn times are also very slow.2. Armies have a command limit, but no unit limit, meaning that they're reinforced periodically over the course of a battle. Where this gets to be an unbelievable drag is when a huge enemy army attacks a town. The default town command limit is minute and towns can't flee or surrender, so the player is forced to sit through an absurdly long combat, manually agreeing to reinforce, potentially hundreds of times, before their garrison is depleted. This is the case even with the minimum garrison for a fully upgraded town.In my view towns should have a very high command limit or none at all and be able to surrender. There are a quite a lot of these fairly annoying QoL shortcomings, such as the abysmal inventory system and the lack of a scroll feature on the town portal spell.I still recommend the game, which is mostly enjoyable, even though it's quite incredible that a developer could leave such un-fun features unaddressed.

_childDocuments_.review: Hero’s Hour shows how compelling and fun the Heroes of Might & Magic formula can be when a developer gets the core mechanics right. It takes a little time to get used to the real-time battles and the limited direct control, but the formula works well and delivers interesting choices and solid challenges. There’s a lot of variety when it comes to both maps and setup options, while the AI knows how to play to win. The only thing I feel is missing is a core campaign that uses the mechanics and the factions. Even without it, players who love the genre will spend a lot of time exploring the variety on offer and finding the best strategic approach for each side. Hero’s Hour might seem derivative at first, but it is a joy to play.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:Its a very interesting/cool/relaxed game if you play with random heros and don't take what happens too seriously. Fun game, but so little balance that its only good for short term play.In Detail:You probably see a lot of reviews of cheating AI's that kill you week two, or are not a threat at all. The fact is. It isn't a AI issue here but a hero balance one.Some amplify their unit of choices effectiveness by 60x while freely generating that same unit infinitely, AND getting extra movement so they can fight more battles and get absurd 3x level advantages. Others like, make a spell 30% more effective with no mana pool.So its not a matter of the AI cheating or not, but that random hero either cripples you or gives you a free win....Ok casual lunch hour game, but nothing to take seriously or buy at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting evolution/different take on HoMM-like turn-based strategy series :)Turn-based battles from HoMM that often turned into repetitive slogs switched to fast-paced autobattler, where positioning is often more important than raw numbers.+ decent tiles (map moreso than units, I wish units were a tad bit more detailed and distinguishable on the battlefield)+ charming animations (little things like floating pickups on water or airborne gargoyles dropping enemies to their deaths) + variety of castles, units and spells+ fast pace - it would beat any HoMM title for quick multiplayer sessions if not...- lack of online multiplayer (very bad for a title that seems made for multiplayer skirmishes in mind)- no single player campaign- no story and lore of any sort, even in the form of item descriptions- AI could get a little more polish, in the 2 hours I played it never retreated once and wiped full armies on walls several times. It should be able to retreat as even in 26 year-old HoMM2 the AI can do it. It also seems to make sub-par decisions like rushing the towns while ignoring nearby threats (but I have not tested higher difficulty settings, maybe it plays a bit smarter on those)7/10, would recommend for any fans of the genre, tho for 5-7 euros less than it currently costs or maybe as part of a bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: Hero’s Hour offers grand strategy in a bite sized package, providing enough mechanics and considerations to be deep and interesting, but not overwhelming. The games are relatively short and the many factions, wide variety of procedurally generated maps, and loads of options makes for high replayability.In Hero’s Hour, you select a faction and balance income, building, and warfare on a randomly generated map. In the early game, you build your town, conquer neutral resource gathering settlements in your starting area, level up your heroes, and build an army. In the late game, you use your economy to pump out units, ferry them from your base to your main army, and conquer the other factions in the game. HH could be considered an “autobattler,” meaning the battles play out mostly on their own. But the player can cast spells and direct troop movement in a broad sense, the interaction keeps them from feeling stale and hands off. The game’s length is relatively short. It goes without saying that the more Ais you put in a game and the bigger the map, the longer the game, but games on smaller maps with a few AI’s typically last 2-3 hours. In my 7.5 hours so far I have won twice on normal, once on easy, and have lost a game on normal. The game can be challenging! I would recommend Hero’s Hour for someone who wants a satisfying grand strategy experience without putting 15-20+ hours into a single game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a massive reboot and refresh on the tired Heroes of Might and Magic (HoMM) formula.Some Examples:1) In HoMM there was one artifact on every map, unfairly placed, by the time you got it on a bigger map the benefits generally didn't have any meaning because someone was already too powerful--in Hero's Hour there's basically one in every zone that's much easier to find, slightly less powerful but also buried with lots of resources.2) Character progression is guided by clear trees that don't restrict you as much in how you develop your character.3) You can hold many more (infinite?) "stacks" of units and not just 6 or 7.4) You get stuck less often behind "monster locks" where you can't proceed for a week or two while you backbuild your forces.5) Everything feels more balanced and well thought out mechanically in the initial zone development for every race.The battles are the biggest and clearest overhaul. Before in HoMM it was abstract -- kind of like chess-piece spreadsheets with HP slithering across the map in turn. Now it's actual little units being rendered in a live, real-time combat where you can tangibly see the performance of individual units against one another. There's a little challenge mode that does an excellent job of teaching you the majority of the monster mechanics and how to leverage certain units' advantages against one another.The retro-pixel design is probably the only place where you "lose fidelity" but it actually works to the game's benefit. It makes it super easy for modders to add new races and the way all the units are rendered and animated on the battlefield it's probably worth it in terms of saved frames, less stress on you computer, and ability to fudge scale. Moreover there's plenty of juice to the graphics so that even though they're byte-sized characters, they're still quite entertaining to watch.The battle mechanics overhaul brought with it a total change in how this game manages magic spells. The magic is still powerful but feels far less overpowered, barring a couple exceptions. There are some magic mechanics and some abilities that aren't balanced well in the mid-to-late game as they let the armies of certain factions essentially absorb all the enemies while other factions' armies at best can only avoid losses. But the developer is constantly patching and balancing so I have no doubt this will be massaged as time goes on.One other change that would be virtually free but have a huge benefit would be with the hero design mechanics. Each faction is pretty much locked to six heroes and the tree of each hero is fixed. That means if you know what you're doing you can min-max beat your opponent, which I guess is good for competitive play, but seems rather rigid for the "I just want to have fun" crowd as randomness would yield greater replayability. I would propose each of the fixed skill trees get turned into a subclass, and whichever hero gets whichever subclass could be randomized (while still matching warrior portraits to the might subclasses and mage portraits to the magic subclasses for aesthetic purposes). By doing it this way the game could add an infinite variety of heroes (in the form of new portraits) without actually losing any of its actual gameplay mechanics. That's just an idea though, the current design makes sense from a simplicity standpoint.All in all it's a super streamlined and refined game experience. Nothing to really say other than great job and fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hero's Hour is a spiritual successor to the old school strategy game hero's of might and magic. Hero's Hour nearly captures the greatness of its legendary forefather. But comes short in a few areas, and finishes strongly in others. To start out, the game and its ideas and systems are fantastic. The talent tree enabling multiple styles of play and character identity is really good. The factions are in abundance and have different play styles. The maps are large. there are lots of different maps to choose from. You can even randomize the layout of maps to keep things fresh. The game is clearly made with love and defined intent on the behalf of the developer. This is all good. However, the game has shortcomings that will not only turn away new players, but perpetually frustrate current and dedicated players. Lets begin with the AI: The AI is terrible. Plain and simple. And I don't just mean in terms of stupidity, it also cheats. Yes, the AI cheats. The AI will spawn in units when there are none to purchase. Making the game unfairly hard and frustrating. This aspect of the AI inhibits thoughtful strategy. There are times where I find myself debating whether or not to siege a city, only to remember that the AI can amass additional units out of thin air, making me worried and hesitant when I otherwise shouldn't be. On top of that, the AI in combat can be buggy as well. There have been a number of times where I have watched a unit or a squad of units stand still and do nothing, or wander aimlessly. And no, they were not under any kind of spell. If there is one thing that needs immediate and drastic improvements, its the AI. Another issue I have is the purpose of neutral cities and hero's. They seem to only exist to further the players experience bar. They're often to strong to fight early and will wander the map aimlessly. They pretty much do nothing. They need to have more impact than simply being a means to an end. Returning to the AI problems: The AI will make incredibly stupid decisions. There will be times where an AI with a massive army doesn't take a siege it would win; or a hero battle it would win. I have noticed on the portal heavy maps that the AI has a tendency to run in and out of the portal for seemingly no reason. Once again, the AI needs a rework. To finish this long winded review, I want to say that this game has been incredibly enjoyable, in spite of its flaws. It brings back a very fond and nostalgic feeling of being a kid and playing the original hero's of might and magic games. The game is made with love, and very much cares about doing a HOMM successor justice. All in all, the game at its core just needs refinements. The systems in place, the factions, the AI, the maps, all are good in their intention, (and some in execution) but all require refinement. Once this game becomes refined, I firmly believe it will be an all time great game, and the best successor to the HOMM franchise. I hope the devs continue to work on this massively potential filled project.

_childDocuments_.review: Hero’s Hour is a pixel based, procedurally generated turn based strategy that has very strong Heroes of Might and Magic vibes but with real time combat. For its asking price it fun to play if you like the formula and offers plenty of replayability and challenge though battles seem un-optimised when you start getting 1000+ figures fighting each other. I’d recommend picking it up when on sale.There is none, every battle is procedurally generated. You have to dig through the games wiki to actually get any info about where the races live, what units actually are or why they are fighting.Gameplay while simple is fairly engaging, with a heavy focus on hero and resource management and also map exploration. There are so many customisable options for any playthrough, and a large selection of playable races (each with 6 heroes with their own skill tress) that you are spoilt for choice. You can edit the difficultly, team members, resources, randomise skill trees, the types of buildings and NPC as well of the rate of encounters to name a few (there’s 3 pages of options).The premise is simple, but you can easily back yourself into a corner if your resource management isn’t great. Towns control what units you can build, provide a base gold income and other features (depending on race selected). You can only build or upgrade 1 building a day, and can only recruit a set amount of units each week (which resets at the beginning of each week). Buildings can be upgraded (which can produce better units, more gold or grant other abilities), and towns can teach Heroes magic spells that can be used in combat.Heroes (and their armies) travel the map, liberate mines (which all produce a different type of resource when captured), visit neutral buildings (that grant bonuses, artefacts or additional units) and fight NPCs and opposing armies for artefacts, resources and experience.  Heroes gain XP from every battle (even if they are killed and the army destroyed) and gain new skills upon every level increase, which gives them additional abilities both inside and outside of combat. If they die, they return to the closest town, so it can be worthwhile throwing heroes at fights constantly so they get XP (and better skills). Each Hero has its own inventory where they can equip artefacts (which grant bonuses to skills or stats) and its own spellbook, which can be used in combat. Additional Heroes can be purchased (and i didn’t find a limit to how many Heroes you can hire). Interestingly many of the Heroes you hire are of different races, and you can use this to convert towns to that race.Combat is real time (which is where this differs from HOMM or Age of Wonders), and you have very little control of the units on the screen. Units can be roughly split into close combat, ranged, or casters and will generally rush as a mob and start pummelling each other. You can kind of direct the army by putting a focus point (which they try to fight towards but generally ignore) or flee. Your biggest contribution is actually casting magic spells (via your hero) and depending on what the Hero knows can totally turn the tide of a battle.Skirmish mode is a challenge mode where you have set amount of gold to spend purchasing an army, pre-selected units you can select from and set enemies to defeat. It’s a straight battle, and removes all of the other gameplay elements.Everything is pixel based (like the 8 bit style). That said, everything is clear, the UI is clean and not overwhelmed with useless information. I didn’t find any areas where I couldn’t see what was on the ground, and the game is fairly helpful when plotting hero movements (it shows if a move will lead to an encounter of not). Combat is wildly chaotic, with mass mobs of units smashing into each other. There isn’t a lot of graphic options (like hardly any at all), but you can increase the UI scale if required. That said, when battles have a large amount of units the game slows right down.I can only remember one music track from the game though there must have been more. Honestly you’re not likely to be focusing on it, it just plays in the background while you do your thing. There isn’t any vocals, and there are few sound effects.Only local co-op is supportedInterestingly many of the games achievements can be gotten with 0 effort (a 0 turn victory is entirely possible with tweaking some of the settings), while others are purely down to RNG luck like collecting artefacts. You will likely be spending most of your time working on a few achievements hoping for the random item to spawn if you are going for 100%.For more reviews please visit

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by the abysmal graphics! If you're a veteran of Heroes 3 (or *gasp* Heroes 4!) Then this game is for you.It brings many improvements to the tried and true formula, and while combat is less involved there's still plenty to do. The upside of the simplified combat is it speeds up the game quite a bit, so you don't need a whole day to finish a game like back in the day.
_childDocuments_.name: Hero's Hour

_childDocuments_.review: First few hours I didn't really see anything special about this game. But the depth is actually amazing. the builds you can go for are varied and wild. The AI is terminator level threatening.If you loved Heroes of Might and Magic, this is a way better imagining of it in my opinion (I could only play H&M&M for a couple hours before i got sick of it). I like the auto-battles vs the hex based slow combat of H&M&M. It is an autobattler so you don't directly control your units for the most part; but you can still set them up at the start and give them SOME on the fly commands (like a cavalry flank).In battle the best contribution you make as the Hero is the precise injections of spells into the melee. Will you summon Air elementals in front of your melee too soak hits? or are they better suited raiding the enemy archer line? maybe you prefer artillery summons behind your already formidable knights. Maybe whats best is just to call down some comets to scatter your foes.
_childDocuments_.name: Hero's Hour

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, this game is enjoyable and has tons of repeatability. But, in my experience at least, there is a huge balance issue when playing against the AI. This balancing issue is compounded by the fact that it is very difficult to "meld" unit abilities and strengths when the battlefield dissolves into a brawl very quickly. Maybe I'm just mad cause bad, but I really think that having more control over units in the battler would make the asymmetric aspect of the game much more engaging. It would allow the player to not only build armies around unit abilities but also fight battles based off an armies strengths and weaknesses.
_childDocuments_.name: Hero's Hour

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10Good arcade style total war game with random scenarios lasting from 30 minutes to several hours. Has some skirmish modes where you can experiment to find just the right counters in a one off battle. Could use a story mode to introduce you to the different factions and their play styles.The gameplay loop can get a bit repetitive and usually just becomes who can mass the bigger force when playing vs. AI. The only exception to this I found was flame spirits. Holy Moley can those demolish an enemy.The game also had a few crashes, which weren't the end of the world since there is a save at the start of every turn. But the interruption can break your concentration/immersion.The music also abruptly changes quite a lot which sucks because it has some groovy music but too jarring of a change from one tune to another (city -> world map & end of turn music transitions in specific).

_childDocuments_.review: HOMM3 meets Circle Empires.I've played HOMM3, Kings Bounty and many other similar titles for thousands of hours and this game is hard to put down. It's really addictive and really fun.Hero's Hour removes many of the limitations and balance issues that existed in HOMM3.More akin to real armies, your heroes can have as many different stacks of as many units as you like and battles are controlled by how many units you can have on the field at any one time, and when these units are depleted, you deploy backup reserves. This may seem limiting, but it isn't because everyone else has the same limitation.Heroes Hour encourages you to develop more than one hero by not only respawning mobs, but also respawning artefacts and resources so that it makes it easier to build other heroes.This is further encouraged by the limitation of OP spells like Town Portal only working once per week and the non-existence of Dimension Door. HOMM3 basically encouraged you to ignore non-magic factions, build one mega hero with Expert Air Magic and Expert Earth Magic where you would simply keep building towns and upgrading your mage guild until you got TP and DD, and then you would win the game. Kings Bounty also suffered from encouraging OP magic builds, and from what I've played so far, it seems like this problem doesn't exist in Heroes Hour where magic vs. strength seems to be much better balanced.You'll have enough resources to build your town and recruit all of your creatures every week, unlike in HOMM3 where you couldn't build your town and support the recruiting of all of your units with the town + 1 mine for each resource once your town was built.I really like the live RTS style battle idea, but it is very poorly implemented in this game. If I had more control like I do in a standard RTS of how I deploy my units and how I control them on the battlefield, this would be much better. This was something I found really good in Circle Empires, and if they did something similar in Heroes Hour, it would feel much better.The way to access the spell book is really badly designed and flipping pages often doesn't work! I should be able to open the spell book with a key press and have a spell book appear the same way it does in HOMM3 or Kings Bounty. It would pause the combat while I select my spell, and then I would cast my spell in the area I wanted to cast it in.The game gets incredibly laggy during big battles. It's a Pixelated game and this shouldn't happen at all!! All in all though, even with the issues that game has that can be improved upon, the fun far outweighs the frustrations and I'm losing sleep because I can't stop playing!! I'm always doing just one more week or doing one more battle and I can't stop!

_childDocuments_.review: September 2024:  After the last "MAJOR" update - If you've read any of my previous reviews then you'll know what I mean when I say that I still use the same strategy to absolutely dominate all other races/heroes.  There's no real way to tune the AI so that they behave intelligently as a real friend would, AFAIK just cheats which isn't fun or challenging, just unfair, which isn't the same.  And I'm absolutely sure that the strategies & tactics I'm using aren't really that strong in the grand scheme of things.PvP multiplayer support would fix this, but currently it only supports shared screen PvP :/  No bueno.If this gets online PvP multiplayer, it will be a hit!  If not, it's probably not worth your money.The "big" update didn't seem to do much other than shift some things around in the skill trees while removing a ton of options available while replacing the tree with a set of 8 categories to level up, each with 4 sub-skills, some of which may or may not be leveled up (depending on how high of level your hero becomes before game-end), and change stats on a bunch of stuff.I'm a huge critic of "the squeaky wheel gets the code" approach to development, in that dev shops or publishers will reactively make game-changing meta updates to try and appease certain audience segments without just focusing on what makes it fun, which, if you're a hard core fan of the 4x genre going back to HoMM... then you'll already know what's missing and not get bogged down like they did trying to balance things before PvP is even fully released.  I get the feeling this is yet another victim of the aforementioned reactive approach to development and game design. It was honestly great before, albeit a bit unbalanced, but the point is that for Hero's Hour -> a lot of work went into the recent updates.  Work which didn't add much benefit in the end.  Especially when you consider there are features not yet built into the game, and everyone wants and needs them much more.  To top things off once finally implemented those features (e.g. pvp online multiplayer support) will cause them to go back and rework those skill trees/categories, etc. all over again when the audience grows massively and the interests & incentives change.it's honestly a bit disappointing and frustrating tbh, this entire game.  mainly because it has so much potential, and yet suffers the same fate as almost all other games released nowdaysOld reviews:july 2024: got bored of decimating the computer with the same strategies over and over, but not convinced that's a problem with balancing just that the AI seem to follow a predetermined set of very predictable, procedural instructions which a friend would not.  if they ever add the ability to play online with/against friends im sure id revisit it again.other thoughts:this isn't a complaint so much as it is an observation: i really like the casual style combat, but i also miss the HoMM turn based style, it gave each type of military unit much more emphasis, some didn't feel like military units at all but people in your army because of how well those were tied together.  Lastly it's not only with how and when you'd place and direct each and every unit and its actions in your combat screen, but how it sparked the imagination in what all of those characters were fighting for and meant to each other a bit more.  I don't think HH inspires in this same way as HoMM games did.  so if you're into medieval fantasy not just for the gameplay...  i think hero's hour does explore the boundaries of what 4x can be and offer, and that is worth checking out, but don't break the bank over it if you're looking for any kind of immersion, this is more of a toy than a life altering experience/adventure which we all know those games can be. loli like that they've added some rain/weather events (only seen rain so far).just yeah dude have to be honest i'm giving it the thumbs down because again i've grown bored with it, and, to my surprise very quickly.  when you consider the price: ehh im not sure whats fair any more for these games, i just know i got bored much faster than homm for about $10 less than what i paid for any of those games originally so the price/value ratio is much lower for HH, for now.retried it: gave it a thumbs up july 2024:I'm playing a lot lately and if I can get remote play to work through steam ill leave it thumbs up, but the below still remains true tbh.  I steam roll all AI with OP skills.first take:It's fun, cute graphics.  Again, just don't see the point unless you're brand new to this genre, but even then you're still stuck with all the same b.s. that comes with games these days: excessive rng, lack of polish, lots of issues.sigh

_childDocuments_.name: Hero's Hour

_childDocuments_.review: A simplified Total War game that's generally fun, but repetitive. There are a lot of races to choose from, each race have their own tech tree, heroes, units, and features. It is quite feature-rich and fairly enjoyable game, where you can use various strategies such as a mage build, or powerful heroes, or economic dominance, etc.The control is intuitive, and how you position your troops does affect the battle outcome.It was fun to fight a tough battle and win, especially when defending castle.However, once your get past early game, even on Hardcore+ difficulty, everything kind of fall apart. The AI is not smart. It will attack if your castle or Heroes is weak, but also sending all their heroes all the way from one corner to the opposite corner to capture a single building and go home, even if I have captured all their building around the AI castle. There are some super exploitative builds that make your Hero overpower. Pretty easy to do if your map happens to have those building, or a hero with certain skills. It's not inherently bad as AI can have the same skills. You need some luck for AI to exploit it, but oh god, the game broke if AI do exploit it.I played a round that deliberately avoiding those exploit to have some challenge, and somehow at about week 10, one of enemy weakest unit have 20k hp, 3k damage, single-shot all of my unit. My Hero, with 60k army power, lose to the enemy 8k army power, to one single type of unit. So I did a long run, dragging the game all the way to week 80 (turn 500+), and I realize there's no way to play without exploitative build. At some point enemy will trigger an exploit making unit that has crazy HP, or crazy damage, or both. There's no option, you have to exploit.Unless you are running the most powerful CPU, it will easily drop to just single-digit fps at mid game. Once you open up most of the map, there are so many particles on the map that kind of lag the game, going to 30fps for me.In battles with thousands of units, you can get to 1fps territory easily. The battle speed is tied to fps, you will start having 10min, 30mins, to hours long battle at mid to late games. At week 80, most battle take up to 30min at least, you just stare there, or play other game during the battle.The first issue is massive army, like thousands of unit on screen tanking your fps. Then, it is almost certain at some point enemy will trigger exploit and you have to do the same. If you exploit HP and Damage, you don't need to do anything, you can win with the weakest troops. If you go with spell boosting magic, you can have skill 1 shot enemy, or summon so many unit that guarantee victories, like summoning hundreds of phoenix costing 50 mana out of 4k mana.If you try to win by army size, you will lose for sure. I have lose 90k army power, 20+k units, to enemy 8k army with those overpower unit.It's just not a fun experience at mid and late game.I used to recommend the game, but with expansion now making it a $25 game, I can't recommend a game that basically force you to finish fast, or exploit the game, and have horrible performance optimization, at full price.Consider purchasing it only if it is on sales.
_childDocuments_.name: Hero's Hour

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially a copy of the mechanics from Heroes of Might & Magic III, but with pixel graphics and much needed improvements. It also changes the battles into a real-time battle instead of turn based one, which is a fun change.However I think the sieges came out a little lackluster. I used to rely on them a lot in HoM&M3, but now walls and the archers on top of them seem to have little impact in the fight. Walls are knocked over with ease, and only hold off the enemy for a brief moment, while the archers seem to be too few.

_childDocuments_.review: A fast turn-based strategy RPG with real-time combat. name: COTTON REBOOT!
detailed_description: Cotton Reboot! is a completely remastered version of Cotton.Fantastic Night Dreams, the originator of the witchy shooting game released 30 years ago, with new features and the latest visual design. The game also features 3 game modes. X68000 original mode faithfully emulates Sharp’s personal computer from the 1993 version. Arrange mode features 16:9 screens, redesigned graphics and characters. Time attack mode the player competes for scores online within a limited time.(2 minute and 5 minute mode can be selected) Cotton reboot!　Ver 1.01 update patch is now available. 1. controller button notation 　Xbox controllers and other controllers (general Xinput-compatible controllers and DirectX-compatible controllers) 　When connected, the button notations have been modified to conform to the Xbox controller specifications. 　PS4 controller is still used when connected to a PS4 controller. 　If a PS4 controller is not connected, the buttons will be displayed as Xbox buttons. 2. Addition of the game exit menu 　Added to the main menu. 3. Screen mode change menu added 　An item has been added to the config to allow selection of full screen mode or windowed mode. 　If you change the mode and save the configuration, the next time you start up the system, the screen mode will be the one selected at the time of saving. 4. speed adjustment for monitors with a refresh rate of 60 Hz or higher 　Changed speed management to be independent of refresh rate when in window mode. _childDocuments_.review: Sloppy port with no resolution adjustments except window and fullscreen. It's locked to 1280x720 in fullscreen and unfortunatly it's "true" fullscreen not fullscreen window which makes it blurry on anything larger than native resolution and can also cause issues with other games running in the background. You can make it tolerable by going to cotton_reboot.exe and opening up properties going to compatibility then to "change high DPI settings"  and checking the box for "override high DPI scaling behavior for:" and setting it to "system". The game will then render the window 2560x1440 with integer scaling (no blurriness)
_childDocuments_.name: COTTON REBOOT!

_childDocuments_.review: I am actually in shock. I just paid $45 AUD for this, on a 30% SALE! The regular price is $65!Why am I in shock? To put it bluntly, "Garbage in Garbage out".There was ZERO effort put into this port, yet they are charging top dollar. When you put a garbage amount of effort your resulting product is garbage.It's actually insulting. It's actually rude.Sure, Cotton is fun to play, but when the switch version is better at 1080P, that says all you need to know.On a 1440P monitor:In windowed mode it is stuck at 720P,  i.e. a small box on the screen. However, this is the only way for the game to look sharp but is far too small on a 15" laptop to be played in any real capacity. So, full screen it is.In full screen mode: it is stuck at 720P. I could accept that for the X68000 emulated port, but not for a rebuilt recoded game with the remastered version.It looks BLURRY! It looks terrible! It looks better on switch!I mean games in 2021/2022 should have adjustable window size with adaptive resolution. That simple.To explain to you just how lazy the developers were, there is not even a full screen or windowed option, you have to use alt enter. There is no exit button, you have to use Alt F4!The only good thing I can say about the port itself is that the controller worked straight away and there were no crashes in the 18 minutes I played it.If this was $10, I'd probably still be disappointed but would accept it.But no way do I accept charging this level of money and having done no work whatsoever on the port.I mean this should be native 4K, native 1440P, and native 1080P. It's inexcusable in 2022.The sheer laziness on display here is astounding. It reminds me of Commodore Amiga days back in the 80's and 90's, when most developers would release AAA priced games that they put zero effort into.It is still at version 1.0.0 - so they haven't listened to anyone who has complained about it, and had I searched the web first, I wouldn't have bought this turkey.BEEP and Rocket Engine, you should be ASHAMED of yourselves. I know you don't care, but hopefully more people will speak up and shame you for charging this kind of money for something you would have likely coded overnight.Buy the switch version if you have a switch. I left mine sealed as a collector's item, but I opened it just now as I wanted to experience the better version of the game. (who would think those words would ever be written about a SWITCH game)? LOL.Oh and HECK yes I got this PC version refunded. Was a no brainer.Do not waste your time unless you literally have an old 720P screen or a PC handheld with a 720P screen. Seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap, after that recent patch, it fixed all of my issues with the PC port of Cotton Reboot. Other than no keyboard icons or a distinct resolution selection, this is now possibly the best way to play this game aside from maybe price. Still maybe get it on sale if you're not a huge shmup and/or Cotton nut like I am. I changed my review to a Recommended, like I said I would if they fixed the game. And they really did. My old review will be kept at the bottom for posterity.Review of prepatch version:As a massive Cotton fan, this game is absolutely awesome (have the Switch SE with the teacup since launch day, even, and that's where most of my playtime is), but I can't really recommend this PC port unless it's on sale and/or it's your only option. It's unacceptably barebones for a 2021 PC port of a 2021 game.720p lock, PlayStation controller icons (and some Switch, like on the Ranking screen) even when using a keyboard, and fullscreen/windowed only in terms of graphics options. That you can only change via Alt+Enter. While this isn't a game that really needs graphics options per se, multiple resolutions are the norm now, and it's disappointing to see when the other versions of the game run at 1080p. It runs perfect on my end, at least, and it loads a lot faster than it does on Switch (one of the main reasons I'm keeping this version, honestly). Even if the game itself is great and is worth playing, $45 is steep for this, especially for the PC porting job at hand here. It's also slightly cheaper on PS4(5) and Switch if you have those options, and I'd recommend picking it up on one of those if you have either option.The game is great but it really pains me to not recommend this version. If it's your only way to play this game, sure, go ahead, but wait for a sale. Or if you have the option, get it on console instead. I'll edit the review if they ever fix the most glaring issues this port has, but I doubt they'll ever fix it.

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of shmups but am by no means good at them, so this review is from the perspective of an amateur who is trying to get through the game using as few lives as possible, but not cranking up the difficulty or setting a 1CC clear as the goal.Cotton Reboot is both a port and a remaster of the first game in the Cotton shmup series. It contains two modes. The first mode in this release is a faithful port of the X68000 release of the original arcade game. The X68000 version was a graphically updated and arranged version of the arcade game, and is widely considered to be the best way to play the original Cotton. The second mode in Cotton Reboot is the arrange mode, which has newly updated graphics and soundtrack, and sports new enemy arrangements, bullet patterns, magic attacks, and scoring mechanics. While I am glad the 90s version is included, I think the arrange mode is the star of the show here with more interesting gameplay mechanics and much prettier presentation.The game contains options which make it enjoyable for a wide range of skill levels, including adjustable difficulty, adjustible number of lives, and unlimited continues for people who just want to clear the game. For the dedicated shmup enthusiast, there are online leaderboards. After clearing the game, you unlock three additional characters to play as. There is also a time attack mode where the goal is to rack up as many points as you can in a given time limit, played in a basic stage with no stage hazards and infinite lives. Cotton Reboot is incredibly responsive to play, has an amusing and whimsical story, and a graphical style which appealingly mixes cutesy characters and enemies with an otherwise gothic and spooky Halloween atmosphere.While some of the criticisms people are leveling at the game are fair (such as not supporting borderless windowed mode), the complaints are hardly deal-breakers. This is a sprite based game with artwork designed for a 720p resolution. Yes the game should have supported a convenient borderless windowed mode with arbitrary scaling to your preferred resolution. But even if that feature was there, this would still be a 2d game rather than a 3d game, and the art which was drawn with a 720p resolution in mind could only be upscaled to higher resolutions rather than re-rendered at that native resolution. Complaining about the 720p internal resolution in a 2d game like Cotton Reboot is like complaining about NES games rendering at 240p rather than 4k, i.e. a fools errand.The only genuine technical complaint I have is an audio issue I encountered. When I streamed the game from my PC to my Steam Deck, when the game loaded it would correctly direct sound to the default audio device (the Steam Streaming Speakers outputting audio to the Steam Deck). But when the game reached the title screen it switched audio output to my PC's speakers. I'm not sure what the root cause is, but I presume it's a bug that is re-initializing the audio device used by the game when it reaches the title screen, but it is incorrectly selecting the first enumerated device in all the audio devices Windows has available, instead of correctly selecting the default audio device specified in Windows. There is no option in game to select an audio device manually, so I had to force the application to use the Steam Streaming Speakers via Windows and then restart the game to get this the audio to stream properly. It would be nice if this bug was fixed but given the game hasn't seen a patch in over a year I'm not going to hold my breath. At the same time I also don't think this is a big enough issue to give the game a negative review over.Ignoring those couple of small technical complaints, both of which can both be worked around, I think the game is deserving of recommendation. It seems like there are many reviews on Steam that malign this release for reasons other than the game itself. Whether the complaints be the 720p resolution, issues that are outside of the developers' control like Steam Deck compatibility, or completely external factors like the price. Make no mistake. Cotton Reboot is a fun time, a timeless shmup, and if you can catch it on sale great value for the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game with colorful graphics, good controls and excellent music.I have played this in the past using emulators but decided to buy it now on Steam to support the devs since I liked the game and having it easy and ready to play on Steam is much more convenient than setting up emulators. These type of games are just pick up and play for a quick run for a few minutes.I'd recommend. It is very good but only when it's on sale like 75% off. The PC port is the simplest thing you can imagine with no options and it runs at 720p, but that's really not that bad for a simple game like this. My take here is that one arcade run can be completed in about 40min, so it's really short, which is common for these shoot em ups, but they really put a very high price on this one for what it really offers.Game itself is great and really fun to play. Good to see a good remake of Cotton available in current hardware, but being really short and with a bare bones PC port it should only be purchased on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: COTTON REBOOT!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the Cotton franchise, it always delivers classic cute 'em up action. I was a little skeptical about this remake at first but took a dive on the Steam Summer Sale. The new art style is fantastic and suits the game very well. The gameplay is very satisfying, I've completed the story multiple times and have been glued to time-attack going for high scores. The voice acting is bubbly and full of life, there are 4 playable characters to choose from, the difficulty strikes a nice balance of not too easy but also not over the top hard. I have been having a blast, I thought I would like this game but I LOVE it.

_childDocuments_.review:
Japan's favorite shooter mascot finally gets a worldwide release as a beautiful HD game with stunning graphics and remixed soundtracks. 

This is the original "Cute em' up", and will test your skills as well as tug on the heartstrings as Cotton and her friends are finally back in the ultimate celebration of one of Japan's most beloved gaming mascots. Choose between the HD Reboot mode or go legit with the X68000 original mode with pixel perfect graphics from the iconic Japanese home computer.

name: Moonstone Island
detailed_description: Wishlist an upcoming card battler! About the Game Moonstone Island is a creature-collecting life-sim set in an open world with 100 islands to explore. Make friends, brew potions, collect Spirits, and test your strength in card-based encounters to complete your Alchemy training! Spend time on islands in the sky! Following your village's tradition, you must move to an island in the sky to complete your Alchemy training. Armed with a team of nature spirits, magical potions, and the support of your new friends, you'll explore ancient temples, dangerous dungeons, and hostile biomes to uncover the dark secret of Moonstone Island. Befriend NPCs, become a member of the community, go on dates, fall in love, and marry the villager of your dreams! Build a new home on any of the 100 islands in your procedurally generated world Grow crops and flowers to brew potions and tame spirits. Cultivate ingredients to cook your fave dishes for fun and stat bonuses! Customize and decorate your home to make it uniquely yours with over 300 decorations Travel by balloon, broom, and glider through unique biomes to reach the outer edges of the world to uncover the secrets of your floating home in the sky Tame and befriend wild spirits to fight alongside you - Over 70 Spirits to tame! Discover and explore dungeons to earn upgrades, collect loot and uncover secrets - Or take on the INFINIDUNGEON for neverending battles and rewards! Optimize your character with unique skills and upgrades Craft dozens of items and vehicles to prepare for the treacherous wilderness Since we launched on September 20, 2023 we’ve been working hard to add more functionality and fun to the game, including: Cooking! 41 new cards! Over 50 new and free decorative items! Marriage! Infinidungeon! More QoL improvements than we can count! + More updates coming over 2024 and 2025 – we’re not stopping yet!

_childDocuments_.review: If you have ever enjoyed Minecraft, Stardew Valley, or Pokemon, (or all three!) this game is going to be a real treat for you. It is cozy, funny, and gives you the freedom to play and explore however you like. I definitely recommend giving it a try! The game is still receiving regular updates, and it generates a new map for you anytime you start a new save, so there's always more to explore!
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: My feelings on this game are mixed - leaning towards negative at the moment.... however, I don't want to be entirely unfair since there are some decent things here... so I'm not giving it a Thumbs Down.The environments are nice. The Spirits and Combat System are nice. Farming seems very simple so far, but I have yet to really dive into it. The big negative here is how..... one-dimensional.... all the townsfolk seem. You don't really "talk" to them... you just hit buttons with percentage chances of giving you points towards Friendship.... beyond that, they only really say anything if you initially meet them or they have a quest for you. I feel like the developers focused too much on that pseudo liberal "diversity" of appearance and not enough on diversity of personality and depth and character - what's actually important in a person. And honestly... on that... the characters more or less look all the same... or at least enough that I don't really think any of them are more interesting or special than another. I couldn't care less about any of the NPCs, but if I had to pick one, it'd be the Blacksmith because at least SHE kinda seemed interesting in the one unique thing she said when I talked to her.Anyway... I like the monsters and that there's a lot of them and dungeons to find, and the occasional secret hole with ore and treasure is pretty nice too. I like the concept of jumping from island to island and being able to build on any of them (though I feel like trying to build on any island but the one the town is on is hardly worthwhile and more of a time sink than anything else. There's plenty of space for likely anything you could ever do north of the town.The combat system is pretty simple - pick cards to use, draw cards, try to strategically use the cards, upgrade them, or get new ones from leveling up your spirits or the occasional shrine you'll come around.All in all, I give this a 5/10 - 5 points off solely for the dreadfully boring NPCs.... it's that big a deal for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much personality and charm. If you like things like stardew valley or monster collecting games, this is for you. It also has a splash of deck building and customization of that. I didn't even play the seasonal updates and things of that sort, but I still managed to enjoy it for almost 60 hours.

One thing i like about the game is the fishing mini-game, I probably spend 30 hours of my total 68 hour on fishing. Not planning on playing anytime soon unless there's a major change.

_childDocuments_.review: Some people are complaining about neutral language in this game, but it isn't by far the worse part.You can't pick your character name. You can't customize your appearance. You can't walk using keyboard's arrows. A lot of basic stuff, like how to toggle auto run mode isn't explained in the game.   The Devs are just too lazy to implement this basic features, but the game was released like a full game, with a full price.  But they were smart enough to disguise all this problems with neutral pronouns, so the poorly designed main character won't be the players focus, and woke people will think the game is good. You, average player, will have no choice to deactivate neutral language. I don't identify myself as a non-binary person. And the game and devs don't respect it. So the game keeps calling me using non-binary pronouns.Also, the translation to Brazilian Portuguese has a lot of mistakes.And the game needs a bit more optimization. My PC runs No Man's Sky smoothly, but Moonstone Island freezes sometimes. What?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun cross between Stardew Valley, Pokemon, and a deck builder game. With the developers fixing bugs, gradually adding more things to it periodically and events taking place to further improve the game I would highly recommend it. It is a great way to spend your down time, and especially easy to pick up and play for a few minutes or so during a journey on Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: Have been looking forward to the launch of this game since I'd first seen it at the Wholesome Direct this year and checked out the demo (which I'd played 3-4 times lol) so I'm very glad to finally have the full game here to get lost in.  Beautiful pixel art and fantastic artstyle all around, lovely cast of characters with lgbtq representation (Which i LOVE), farming sim aspects are great, socializing/dating sim bits are a good time, but the exploration and combat are the bread and butter to me, was worried at first with the card based combat since I suck at card game style things, but this game takes that concept and makes it simple enough to grasp and have fun with!  All in all I would HIGHLY recommend this game. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT AT 130+ hours: I still love this game so much. Many of the things I found needed improvement have already been implemented. And I love that! It really shows how much they care and listen to the community. More updates are in the works, and I will continue to add edits as the game grows and I sink more and more hours into this game. Big thank you to the devs for listening and making such a wonderful game. I look forward to playing more.---Original Thumbs Up Review Below---I have played 57 hours so far, and will likely sink another 57 into this beautiful and charming game. It is a wholesome experience with cute spirits and diverse and delightful villagers. This game has easily become one of my favourite games.However the game is not without flaws.I would love to see some form of events or festivals implemented, as after a certain point there really isn't very much to do in game. It is repetitive, which can be really nice to a degree, but a bit more to look forward to each season would be amazing (maybe even some seasonal event spirits with a limited time to catch). I'd also love the ability to put down decor outside. As well as to have trees and rocks regrow on your main island, as I cut all mine down not realising there is no way to get them back. Also when a mine is completed it would be nice to have the hole poof away as it no longer serves a function and my first mine is in the walkway to my home and I fall down it a lot.With that being said, the game is still very new, there is a ton of room for growth, and I deeply look forward to seeing what they add in the future. Hands down a must own game. Highly recommend the DLC for the super cute house too!
