_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but sadly I really don't. This game attempts to be way too many things at once, and it doesn't really succeed at most of them. It's a _unique_ fusion of Harvest-Moon-style farming and slice-of-life activity, Pokemon-style collect-them-all monster-taming, Card-based combat with adventure-style exploration. However, it doesn't really hit mark on any of the genres it tries to cover.As a lifelong fan of Harvest Moon, Pokemon, and general pixel-art and indy games -- I really had high hopes for it; but ultimately, I don't find this game to be *fun*.To give credit where it's due, it's got a number of nice and novel features:* Nice pixel-art graphics * Cute enemies with funny names.* A different style of dating mechanism which sets it apart from most Harvest Moon-clones. The dialog on dates is rather in-depth, though most of the general game lacks decent dialog.* An outside-the-box concept. It's refreshing, even if it didn't really land well.The bad:* The game feels like it lacks polish for most things.* For a large chunk of the game, I had no idea who lived in which house. If you attempt to enter a room and you aren't friends, it doesn't even tell you whose house it is.* Several graphical glitches in places (most basic example: Alchemy table doesn't remove icons until you move your cursor after picking up items)* Movement is clunky all around. I can't jump down cliffs, but I can hop on my broom for 1 tile, rotate 90 degrees, and that's fine? Swimming feels weird too, especially with up water-fall swimming* The relationship between characters in the town is not very well fleshed out. It's not really clear how anyone interacts with others -- if anyone is friends with each other or not. * A lot of the in-game mechanics are not particularly intuitive. You can figure it out over time, but most games that don't provide much prompts at least make it intuitive to understand. This is not one of them.* There is no real reward for becoming friends with the townfolk. Like, you can enter the room -- but it doesn't unlock new dialog, doesn't let you learn more about them; you can't even interact with anything in their rooms.* Repetitive dungeons: Dungeons all feel the same, are not really all that intricate, and it literally has the same boss at the end of every dungeon. They couldn't even spring for a pallet-swap, it's just the same boss every time -- just with different stats and minions. To be fair, there are season-dungeons (spring, summer, etc) with semi-unique bosses, but that's about it.* Similar to above, caves are super repetitive.* Loot is always effectively the same from chests, with the only real incentive being crafting recipes.* Horrible RNG. Like, really bad. Allegedly 90% chance of success for things that will fail more often than 90%. Whatever underlying RNG mechanism used here does not have a proper normal distribution. * Deck combat is repetitive. Ultimately it's not even all that fun IMO. Enemies often target THE SAME CREATURES EVERY TIME for no real reason.* The music is lackluster. A good game should have a good soundtrack to compliment it, but most of the music is repetitive if not downright annoying. Most music doesn't really fit the ambiance of the locations or moments. Combat music doesn't really sound like combat, if that makes any sense. As someone who listens to indy game music all the time during my day job, a good soundtrack makes a huge difference.* Money is weird; one of the easiest and immediate forms of income seems to be from selling ores, so there is almost zero incentive to actually have a farm at all. There's a whole lot more, but I'll stop here.Honestly, this feels like it should be an alpha early-access game, *not a full release title*.Plenty of people apparently like this, so I guess I'm the outlier. My guess is that this just hits the trendy marks for people right now given the LGBTQ inclusivity, lots of puns, an incomprehensibly diversified cast of characters, inclusion of gender pronouns, etc. Basically hits all the trendy notes, thus doesn't actually need to be fun or a good game for people to go nuts over it -- as seems to be the modern way of gaming these days.Given the DLCs that provide functionless pixel-art items that can be crafted, this feels more like a low-effort money-grab that was manufactured

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game which unfortunately suffers from poor pacing. Imagine combining Stardew Valley, with creature collecting (spirits in this game) and card battling - that's essentially what you get with this game. It's good fun at first, but once you get past the first season the games pacing crawls and there's not much to motivate you to keep going.From my playthrough I stopped just short of the winter season. I had finished all the dungeons and my main team was just under level 30. I couldn't really make much progress to the final spirit types because they were all lvl 50+ and I didn't want to grind battles to be able to progress. I also ran out of islands to explore and things to craft. Seeing the winter season would be cool - but I suspect I'll be done with it after the first day.Balance is completely out of whack. Poison types are ridiculously overpowered. Normally in games being inflicted with a poison status does a fixed amount of damage. In this game you can stack poison to do more damage. Burn also has a similar mechanic where you can stack burn damage. However the difference between burn and poison is each turn poison decreases by 1 stack whereas burn stacks are halved. They both do the same damage - meaning 20 stacks of poison decreases to 19 next turn, 20 stacks of burn decreases to 10 next turn. Why would you ever use burn? Also poison damage completely ignores the armour mechanic, whereas all other types have to deal with it reducing their damage. And finally if a spirit is weak to poison it decreases their armour meaning poison damage not only ignores the armour mechanic for damage but interacts with it for combat control. There's no reason to use any other type in the game - other than for fun. Realising this mechanic might be why my playthrough stalled so early.

_childDocuments_.review: I can confirm what has already been said by others, this game is what you would get if stardew valley and pokemon had a child. It is noticeably more polished than stardew and has a number of quality of life features that demonstrate a lot of love and attention poured into development. While the combat system isn't the most intricate I've ever seen, it has more than enough variety to allow a number of different builds, so I would say it does its role perfectly well. The pacing also seems perfect for a farming simulator. I'm not sure if it has a lot of replayability, but it's totally worth your money

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to like this game, and don't get me wrong, it's a perfectly passable way to spend time, but ultimately, I've been forcing myself to even play it after the 10 hour mark. The creature levelling system is in need of a serious upgrade since they get such little EXP from battles. The ONLY way I've been able to get stronger spirits is just by continually catching higher levels and replacing the old ones, so don't get attached to your starters if you want to get ahead.Not only that, but it felt frustrating to me that it's so difficult to pinpoint which islands have the right level spirits to properly train. One island has lvl 15, and then the one directly beside it has 40+??? I was flying around aimlessly for hours and getting no where.Honestly, it has so much potential, and the spirit designs are amazing, and the soundtrack is amazing, and maybe they'll do some tweaks in future updates to make things a little more fluid, but for now I gotta take a break because I really feel like I've gotten everything out of it that I could at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Stardew elements like farming, mining, potion crafting without the complexity, there's maybe 4-5 stations to craft things vs other games that can have 20+ stations. Relationships and dating with NPCs - cute little storylines for the chars (not lifeless like other games). By far my favorite parts are map exploration to uncover floating islands of different biomes which contain "spirits" (little creatures) that you can tame by feeding forageables or banish via battle - battling is done with card decks that you are able to build along with rng elements - reminds me a bit of doing a draft game of lorcana/magic but very simple rules. Each card/spirit has a type such as Psychic, Poison, Electric - there are strengths and weaknesses and each type has a different playstyle allowing for a lot of playstyles and combos as well. I haven't stuck with a cozy sim like this for this long in a while, a true gem and fresh take on the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Stardew Valley + Slay the Spire + Pokemon. A very ambitious mixture of my three favorite genres, and it turned out... pretty good. The default-unity-lookin assets are a bit lackluster, and I will echo the very common complaint that there is no tangible objective. In just 4 hours I found myself constantly not knowing where to go next since the game doesn't give you much to go with. For a role-playing game, you don't really play much of a role in this world either. The worldbuilding feels rushed and incomplete. Farming just feels like a waste of time and has no soul behind it. There's a lot of good in this game, though. The battle mechanics are pretty fun: familiar deckbuilder and jrpg aspects mashed into a pretty satisfying experience. The monster designs are nothing special, but just very solid. And despite not having a definite objective, there is still a lot to do. I'm having fun with this game so far, despite the issues.

_childDocuments_.review: ok, I've owned this game for 4 days and already have more than 24 hours of game time, I think it is obvious that I've found my new game obsession it's been in my wishlist for a long time and I hate myself for delaying the purchase for so long - this game is awesome! - at first I didn't like that the character is not customiseable, but it makes sence in a really immersive way - you are the child of your parents, and you look like them, and you are wearing the alchemist uniform, not some random hoodie, I love it (I've read dev's explanation on no customisation later and the need to choice between detailed animated character and more appearance options is understandable, the team is small) - the whole cosy old-facioned ghibly-like atmospthere is tickling my nostalgia - nausicaa was my favourite anime and still is, and now I get to fly the glider! - potion system is really neat and cooking is there too, recent update notes said something about juice, but I'm not that far in game yet - I am terrible in decorating my houses, but the options are super cute, and THERE ARE WALLS PARTITIONS AND CUSTOM WALLPAPERS!!!!! it might be the only game in which I will actually try to make my house look nice instead of pure functionality - this is a small detail, but I like that mines are non renewable, and after you exaust them, the only option for more stone and metals is importing from other off-map towns thru the shop - it is nice realistic touch, and againlike the music fading out in mines it reminds that we are on floating islands, not on top of dwarf-magical-time-locked infinitely respawning mines - the fact that most of games in this genre need time and money investment to regrow trees (the naturally renewable resource) but the mines (with naturally finite resources) come back intact every day is something I didn't know bothered me untill I got here - you are an ALCHEMIST, not a farmer!!!! - you can still farm - there is even a greenhouse - but it is not mandatory!! all the plants are in the world, harvestable; some youtuber (that I sadly can't remember) said it right - this genre is better suited with "new in town" sim tag, not a "farm" sim tag because this "starting out in as a strager from zero in a new place you've never been before" is what is common between all this gamessome more details: - graphics is really pretty, especially as you notice small details, like in character animations or background, or weather and wind particles - music is nice, and I also like that we have times with no music - it allows to hear the ambient and get immersed even more (tho maybe an option to customise music frequency might be a good idea - the ost hits my nostalgia buttons) - the battles are easy enough to get into even if you didn't ever play this kind of fighting and at the same time combos, types and strategies are interesting enough that I can see me optimising my team for a very long time - I love the fishing game, it is unique and immersive enough that it still feels like fishing and not just some random minigame for the sake of minigame - I appreciate that we can have all the skills unlocked if we play long enough (and refreshing the skill tree to make choices anew is accessible enough) - and resetting your favourite spirits is there too! - the story is paced to be done in the first year, but you don't have to rush, nothing is missable (except one of secret achievements afaik) - I love that we can settle everywhere we want or even be nomadic - a bunch of important blueprints is linked to npcs, but through quests, not relationships, which means I get to be a mysterious hermit that occasionally flyes into the town and helps people, but otherwise is nowhere to be seen and still get all the cool stuff - there are frequent updated with free stuff! and I've yet to bump into any noticeable bugs, aside from slight lag when my dumb antivirus decides to launch a scanning session while I'm playing, hogging my PC resources (and my PC is old office one, not gaming one lol) - the community is small, but helpful and friendly - there is a lot of content on youtube to watch inbetween gaming sessions lol - many spirits are crossovers and I think it is cute (even I don't recognise most of them, I think this kind of unteractions between games is something that makes gaming field more friendly and cosy place at whole) - I love that almost all keybinds are customiseable (the exception is ESC button T_T and I have to use mouse every time to back from menus because my hands are smol and the ESC is far away from all other buttons T_T) on DLCs, as recently most game forums I've been to got a surge of anty DLC people - all DLCs in this game is for decoration purposes, no gameplay features or achievements are locked behind DLCs - my favourite DLC scheme, because unlike gameplay DLCs there is no missing out on some exclusive useful stuff, you get all the useful stuff in basegame and yes, I've bought all dlcs after playing for 5 hours and realising that I'm here for loooong time, and already had more joy than I've had playing any game this year! P.S. don't sell moonstones for quick cash untill you've build everything you need, money is easier to find that moonstones (but moonstones are renewable in many different ways too) you go, devs! much respect and love from this one

_childDocuments_.review: Moonstone Island is the perfect blend of cozy and exciting, a wonderful mix of gameplay elements and story tropes from all sorts of classic video games, like Stardew Valley, Pokemon, and Animal Crossing. It's a blend I didn't know I needed until I took a break from watering my crops to go do battle with Spirits (and collect them all!). The map is very large, full of secrets to discover, and traveling around the map is fun in itself as you consider travel modes, wind resistance, and warp points. Flying around unexplored areas to find mystery islands was some of the most fun I've had in a cozy game, ever! And the Spirits are so well-designed and thought through, from their punny naming conventions to their element-related visual designs. The most impressive part of this game is how extensive it is for being less than a year old! It's jam-packed with colourful content and provides dozens of hours of entertainment, whether you're in it to grow the best crops, or clear all the dungeons with the help of your trusty Spirit companion, or make the most friends in town. Or, you could do my favourite pastime, and try to figure out what shape each island is meant to represent (I see you, Australia-shaped island with a treasure chest in Exmouth...). To reiterate, this game is less than a year old, and already has several content DLCs released, so it is of course not really complaining when I say, however, that customization options were a bit limited and therefore disappointing. The main character, for example, is non-customizable, which is understandable as there are CGs featuring them, and yet I didn't connect as much as I could've to the main character because I simply didn't care for their lack of distinctive appearance (though the floppy hat is iconic I won't lie). Even simply picking a gender option would have gone a long way, which I was surprised was not already available since this game has a wonderful cast of gender-diverse and well-written NPCs. There are also relatively few home decoration options currently available in game (though I know this will change with upcoming DLCs), making it rather difficult to make effective use of the incredibly large space allocated to the player's home- one of the largest, if not THE largest I've ever seen in any sim game ever. Lastly, I was surprised by the relatively small amount of NPCs in the game, a fact that, again, might change in the future. I can only for now when I say that I was a little disappointed at how flat and un-lively Moonstone Island seemed to be. There are no elders, no children, no families, only bachelor/ettes of varying adult ages. The NPC schedules are fairly predictable and don't have much variation, getting old quickly. The socialization system is also fairly innovative, but simply having the option to "chat, joke, flirt" without associated dialogue doesn't do much to actually build attachments to the NPCs. You only get an inner glimpse at their lives/personalities/backstories if you take them out on dates, which is a little awkward when you're trying to roleplay an exclusive relationship with a specific NPC. That being said, Moonstone Island is a beautiful, rich, and extremely well-conceptualized game, full of things to do and discoveries to make. At the time of this review, it is about to be 6 months old (as of launch date), which is an extremely short amount of time since release to be making up definitive opinions about the game. Still, despite the narrow spectrum of options in a few places, overall it is an expansive and engaging game that is easy to get sucked into and throw dozens of hours into without ever getting bored. I definitely recommend this game to any who enjoy the life sim/cozy/farming genre of games; Moonstone Island has had a beautiful launch, and has the potential to grow further and become a hallmark of the genre in due time!

_childDocuments_.review: Moonstone Island does a great job of making every part of its many available tasks interconnected, but not requiring you to progress in all of them at once. Nothing in the game is too complicated, which means easy flow from one task to another. It's a great game for the casual achievement hunter: None of the achievements are particularly hard, you just have to actually make them your goals as you play.This is a very "boring" game. I can't play for too long at once. I get sick of what's going on in the moment, but I'll come back the next day or even a few hours later excited to play again. I consider this a very good thing. I have enough games I can play for hours on end, and as someone with ADHD that's not really a good thing; I can lose multiple days just playing some games. A game that naturally makes a stopping point for you just by burning out of the simple tasks is great, especially when those tasks become satisfying again when I return.I will emphasize: This game is VERY simple. It's diverse in that simplicity, but it could definitely be critizised as completely missing what's engaging about each of its mechanics. If you play Stardew to optimize and expand, if you play card fighters for the strategy, if you play dungeon crawlers for their interesting puzzles, if you play exploration games for their unique enviornments... you won't get that here. But if you play these games for, or feel like you might be interested in, turning your brain off and just playing, Moonstone Island does that really well.Also, side note, I really like the slight alteration to relationship gain from genre standard. It feels a lot better than just "make sure you say hi" even though it's technically that but more button presses.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: This game isn't worth spending your money on as it is right now. Wait a while to give devs time to update and patch bugs before purchasing.I want to be really clear that I have enjoyed this game immensely when I have been able to play it. I like to concept, I like the art. It does feel a little limited or not fully fleshed out, but it's fun nonetheless.My problem with the game is with the continuous bugs that I have dealt with since purchasing on launch day. I am super understanding that bugs are going to happen upon first launch and I think for the most part, the devs have been pretty good about hearing and fixing problems.However, now for the second time, I have encountered a glitch that caused me to lose a significant amount of progress. I had to completely restart the game the first time, no save file at all despite the fact that the game autosaves every night in game. Now, after the first patch, I lost the ability to play the game completely and when I was able to play it again, days later, I had lost roughly 15 realtime hours of gameplay, despite diligently manually saving every in-game day.At this point, after 26 hours of gameplay, the game has saved maybe 5 hours of it? I'm heartbroken, as I really enjoy this game and had fully intended to finish it. I really didn't expect to lose significant progress a second time, and I am awaiting a response from the support team before I decide whether to pursue a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great casual game, that masterfully blends several of my favorite genres, including creature collecting, deck building, and farming/building. If you're looking for a game that presents daunting challenges (and the dopamine rush that comes with overcoming them), this game will not scratch that itch. But if you're looking for a relaxing, go-at-you-own-pace breather from those types of games, Moonstone Island has got you covered.There's definitely room for tweaks and improvements, but the price point is fair for what the game is, and it could really become something spectacular if it receives future content additions.I'd rate the game a solid 8/10 in its current state, and I do recommend picking it up if it sounds like the type of game you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game if you like farming sims and collecting games. The farming aspect is pretty secondary to the battling and collection aspects, but it's there. You also have the Stardew-style ability to interact with the villagers, though it's kind of limited (but still enjoyable). You can spend a lot of time exploring all the islands and then return home to decorate (or not, if that's not your thing). I like the deck-based battles.If you like games where you can get into a comfortable groove, with repetition, this one is a good choice. It has a very relaxing and open gameplay style. I wish there were more sidequests than there currently are, because I feel like having those to focus on would give you more to do in the game.I do want to stress that they're pushing out content updates all the time, and each update delivers a significant improvement. I got the game when it came out, and it's only gotten better and better since then. I've added the DLCs and are pleased with both (though the game would be fine without). I feel like there's a lot of promise here and that I'll keep coming back to this game as they deliver further updates and events. I really do like that it hasn't been a static release.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first and likely one of the only times I'll write a review because of how much I enjoy a game. I've been looking forward to Moonstone for over a year and it immediately fulfilled the gaming 'drought' I've personally experienced within recent years. It beats triple-A titles by a longshot - you can feel the love that's gone into it. You have Stardew-esque farming plus tons of housing/decoration options which makes it feel very customizable. I normally stray from both card and turn based games but the combat has been so refreshing and fun (plus adorable sprites reminiscent of Pokemon!) and finally the dungeons in this game were a huge surprise. There are also temples and caves, and they remind me of handheld era Legend of Zelda adventuring. I am constantly playing for hours at a time and I still feel like I've barely touched the surface. For only ~$20 CAD this was the best use of money in awhile!

_childDocuments_.review: A mixed review for me I think....but I am quite enjoying this game! It's definitely got some sort of cozy vibes to it; it's chill, the graphics are adorable, the music is decent, and it's a mix of Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, Littlewood, Studio Ghibli and Pokemon all in one. I also love the idea of your little spirits following you around , and you being able to fly around anywhere on your broom! The controls/navigation are pretty easy to use once you get the hang of them and memorize which key/control does what . The turn-base card fighting game is pretty awesome, I could imagine it as a standalone game as well; it's so much fun! As for interacting with the other characters on the island, it's sometimes hard/risky to tell which option is best to talk to them with, as some responses lower the relationship level, others raise it up; I guess it depends on the current mood of the character. You also craft/mine in the game as well, and as far as mining goes....you're lucky if you are able to find a hidden cave somewhere on whatever islands; I find that part tedious and slightly frustrating because I'm chopping/smashing left, right n' center, trying to find another randomly-spawned hidden cave to mine in , and just none found - and you can't even mine in the caves you've already done because if you're like me, you've emptied that cave completely out. Regarding the fishing, easy peasy, and I'm glad it's not like Stardew Valley's green bar one; you just drag the circle around and try to keep it on the fish, and voila! You can also sell things and make money. I find it easier to make money by selling fish, than selling the other random stuff, especially if you catch a gold-starred fish because they sell at a better price than silver and bronze (obviously). The only things  that I wish this game had are:Other than that, a good release that I was looking forward to, I'm so glad I was able to purchase it, and it's definitely a nice game to just chill out to and get mentally lost in. I'm looking forward to new possible changes being made to this game in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: It's such a good idea on paper, and the execution is really solid GB Advance Pokémon Valley, but it's just so dry. The procedural map makes everything feel really bland and pointless, you fly from one island to another and sometimes things are just massively out of your level range with no real warning or way to get out and the grinding for resources is really just bottle-neck'd around moonstone for everything. If you can look past the total lack of haptic feedback and cool animations then maybe you'll like it, it's got lots of horny bisexuals for you to romance but there just isn't much game here. I got it on sale and it's £11 I sorely regret.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game but overall, it feels half-baked. The devs are clearly working hard to address concerns with the game, but where one problem is solved another appears. I played at launch and stopped, then tried to give it another chance and all the sudden there was an abundance of lag and glitching. Interacting with NPCs is like talking to cardboard boxes; it feels like Moonstone has no life to it. This is reflected in the main storyline and quests, where it feels like there's no incentive to these actions other than the game just telling you it's what you're supposed to do. It's really unfortunate because there's so much potential in terms of the world and characters but are doing the bare minimum. The game has many different facets and none of them are executed particularly well. Farming is tedious and slow to get into because you have to collect seeds before they're sold at the store, and there's no real incentive to level up tools. Fishing feels like it was just randomly thrown in because it's expected of 'cozy games' like this one. The spirits designs are cool but battling feels unrewarding and the dungeons feel like they lack life and innovation. Decorating is fun, but some items are locked behind purchasing DLC, which feels a bit unfair given the game itself needs more work. So on and so forth.Maybe if some major adjustments are made to the game I'll give it another try, but as it stands I would not recommend this game to anyone which is why I have to give it a thumbs down despite some great aspects, like the concept, visuals and music.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I never knew just how bad I needed in my game life!!! -PROS-It is a perfect blend of cozy, wholesome adventure along with some fantastic RPG. For those who love to decorate, you are in for a treat, loads of craft-able decor items, shop items and housing upgrades. Exploration is a huge bonus in this game, with 100 islands to explore, collect resources, treasure maps, dungeons and catch spirits. Making money seems to be straight forward, especially with some "sell items" that specifically state "for sale only" no more hoarding useless things in fear of not knowing to sell them. That is a game feature I wish all games had. This game also has a clear story line that is not only cozy but super fun.The beginning tutorial is fantastic, clear and easy to follow and learnAuto-save and a back up manual save along with 9 save slots for multiple play throughOpening any menu will PAUSE the game, such a FANTASTIC feature and  much appreciated.You have the options to truly play your way with loads of difficulty levels, from how easy, normal or hard your battles are, to how often spirits spawn. Truly a game mechanic that some tend to overlook, but this game DID IT PERFECTLY.While some complain on the time speed, I have never found an issue with the length of my days, I am able to accomplish everything in my day. Its no less time than any other farming sim out there.-CONS-NPCS while date-able, are a little dull. The chat mechanic in game is an interesting one with it being based off of a percentage. However, I wish when we did talk to them they actually talked back. The only information we ever get is on a date and even then its usually one or two sentences.Fishing mini game is IMO only good if on keyboard, I have tried multiple times with my controller and I can NOT catch a fish using my controller. Which is a huge disappointment for me since i love playing with controller.Speaking of controllers, some mapping and buttons will only recognize as xbox, even though when I use my playstation controller it all works, except in battles when it tells me to use Y instead of triangle. That can be a bit confusing if you don't remember the xbox layout.  DEVS, If you are going to have controller support make sure the button descriptions match that controller you are playing with.All that being said, I absolutely LOVE this game, It is easily my favorite game. I wish other games that released were as fun and mesmerizing as this one. We have had such let downs lately in releases (cough cough some fairy like farming games) that this one knocked it out the park.Would I recommend? I will say this, while I love this game, my opinion is not always like others, but for me with weighing both pros and cons and price point I would say yes. It really is a great game, the devs truly have a special love for it, you can see that in their discord and the game. I do not think anyone would truly be disappointed in trying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is only barely a not-recommended for me, and since it gets regular updates I'm hoping that this changes over time. Mechanically, this game is phenomenal! The farming, fishing, crafting, exploring, etc. all work with no issues and feel good to do. It's fun! As far as the depth of the game though, that's where it falls flat and why I don't recommend it. The characters are all incredibly interesting when you first meet them, and then your experiences with them are really limited. The town itself feels static, as nothing really changes over time or happens there. It feels a little like if you played the entire game without ever stopping to talk to somebody in town, your playthrough would only be marginally different from somebody who talked to everyone every day. I found that this meant I had to be really self-motivated when making goals in this game, because even for all the quest log updates I got, I never felt like I was connecting with the town and people and doing things because of that connection. I was just grinding through the game because I wanted to play it, and that motivation became difficult to sustain. Your character itself strikes a weird balance between not having any pre-set personality, but also not being customizable in any way I've found. So, they're not a blank slate because you're meant to be able to fill yourself into their shoes, they're a blank slate that somebody else has lovingly and intricately designed, which really exacerbates the fact that they're a blank slate. Why do I visually have so much personality if there is never a single point in the game where I express any personality? I never felt very connected to my character for these reasons, too.The spirits are exciting and the elemental islands are cool as you discover each new one, but that hits a wall pretty quickly as you realize there are 100 islands but only around 10 templates for islands. So once you've seen your first poison type island, you've seen them all. That took some of the excitement out of exploring for me and was the point at which I decided to write this review. I enjoyed what this game had to offer as far as actually playing went, but the story that's present and the worldbuilding that's there is a weird mix of built up enough that you can't fully make it your own but also empty enough that you may struggle to get invested. And again, this game is receiving regular updates, so I hope this does change over time! The foundation for this game is 100% there, but beyond that I found it fell short.

_childDocuments_.review: got this right away after the sponsored drawfee stream and omg its so good!!! im a big stardew valley fan and it really scratches that itch while also having so much unique content that its super exciting to play. the card based combat and monster collecting aspect is v fun and while the combat feels v chill and not too challenging, its enjoyable and engaging so far. the npcs are all very sweet and i want to get to know all of them. the only problems ive had with the game arent too big--theres a weird thing that happens when trying to give a gift or sell items, where a menu will pop up asking how many of the item (if you have multiple stacked) that you want to give, but the game will already have given one of the items on the original click. nothing else is affected when selling items but when giving a gift the whole game freezes when this menu pops up :|  (i think the solution for now is to make sure the item you want to gift is not stacked in your inventory, and then that menu wont pop up)other than that its v fun and charming! would recommend to ppl who like stardew but with pokemon-like aspects :D

_childDocuments_.review: Life/farming sim + spirit (monster) catching/fighting game. A nameless protagonist ventures forth on their broom to complete their alchemy training, but ends up crashing on Moonstone Island, which is conveniently a great place to set up camp. With nothing but a few seeds from their parents and their starting spirit they obtained on their home island, they hone their skills to become a great alchemist … hopefully.    • No character customization. As far as I can tell, the protagonist has no name or gender. However, from how the “end of the day image” looks, they seem rather feminine. So, take that as you will.     • Gameplay involves: flying between islands to explore them, foraging, mining, farming, fishing, dungeon clearing, spirit catching/battling, crafting, cooking, socializing/gifting, and collecting.    • Spirit battles: 3 of the character’s spirits work together to battle 1 to 3 other spirits. Their action cards are all together in a deck and randomly drawn. There are 3 actions per turn, but any of the 3 spirits can use them up. Using items also counts as an action.    • Flying: balloon (very slow), broom (not so slow), and glider (faster). Balloons can travel indefinitely (stamina permitted), while brooms eventually lose their charge and the character can fall … but they magically teleport back to where they started. The glider is definitely best, as it is fastest and can go on indefinitely (stamina permitted), but it takes a while to get the blueprint for it.    • There is a moonstone on every island. Moonstones are the most valuable resource in the game. They also have a  to respawn . (So, why isn’t the game called Moonstone Island?)    • Islands have mines and sometimes dungeons to clear. One mine per island (with a few exceptions). (However, there is a spirit that allows for two mines per island if they’re following the character.)    • Mines are randomly discovered by breaking big rocks on the surface and a big hole appears.    • Despite the story saying an alchemist’s training is done in a year, the player does not actually have to finish the game within a game year. They can take however long they want. There’s no need to rush. In fact, an achievement requires more than one game year.    • Difficulty settings for: Spirit spawn rate. Spirit battles. Day length. Fishing minigame. (These settings can be changed at any time.)    • Running out of stamina/health results in the player’s character passing out and waking up the next day (usually in their home) later than they usually wake up. This also happens if the character stays active past 2 AM.     • The player’s character can fast travel back to the main island via Warp Whistle, which is given freely by a mysterious statue on the main island. Also, interacting with the statue daily yields random loot of varying quality.     • 11 romanceable characters: 3 enbies, 4 men, & 4 women (this was determined by pronouns). You can date more than one person at a time without penalty, but you can only marry one person.     • The home is a tent in the beginning, but the player can begin expanding and decorating immediately and it all carries over to when an actual house is built. There are several different types of homes (more with DLC).     • There is only one missable achievement. It’s for clearing 3 dungeons in one day. You can’t get that if you clear all the dungeons in the game, because there’s no way to reset them. You’d have to start another playthrough.    • My PS5 (DualSense) controller worked  perfectly for the game. (See complaints.)    • I’m always skeptical of Pokémon-like games, because that’s a hard act to follow, but this game is actually fun. The spirit designs could be better, but it isn’t like they’re terrible. I like how the spirits work as a team rather than individually in battle. There are items to get new cards, improve cards, or remove cards to improve the spirits’ decks too, which is definitely needed.     • Portable spirit storage. Eventually, you’ll get a blueprint for a spirit storage, which allows you to switch out spirits on the go. It can’t be placed within the town though, which is silly, but I get it.    • Sidequests for pairing spirits with NPCs. Some request specific spirits, while others will let you choose for them. Once the spirit is given to the NPC, that spirit will follow them around henceforth.     • It was a little anxiety-inducing at first, but it became fun to seek out new islands. You just pick a direction and fly. Sometimes you find really interesting, cool stuff. Filling out the map is satisfying.    • Throughout the game, you can find treasure maps on islands and it’s fun to match them up with islands you’ve already encountered or ones that you’ve yet to discover.     • You can take chests once they’re emptied in mines and dungeons. So, you never have to make one yourself.    • Fish are a great source of stamina replenishment. Usually fish are only good for cooking ingredients or selling for money in other games.    • NPCs actually give decent rewards for sidequests. It’s usually either a valuable blueprint for crafting, a useful item that makes a game mechanic easier, or a decent chunk of money.     • Lots of rooms to be obtained with home upgrades and plenty of décor to choose from (more décor with DLC). The favorite rooms I made were my witchy attic and potions room.     • Great diversity with NPCs, both gender and racial.     • Random crashes that seem to have no trigger. Sometimes, I would not be doing anything but looking at a menu or inventory for a moment. Another time, I left the game idling for literally less than a minute, went back, and it had crashed. Another time, I had just won a spirit battle. (Thankfully, you can save anytime, and I did .)    • A few weird controller issues. Sometimes the game won’t acknowledge that there is a controller even though Steam does. Restarting the game fixes it. Another weird issue is sometimes the game will randomly stop acknowledging button presses and I’ll have to use the mouse to get it to start working again.     • Putting down wallpaper or flooring is a bit of a hassle, because you have to move furniture to place it. That means chests too, and you can’t move a chest if it has stuff in it.     • An achievement for marrying a specific character. I never understand why devs do this. That ruins the fun of the romance element in a sim game of this type. The dev is forcing the player to choose. So, to avoid a second playthrough, one has to give them the moonstone bracelet to fully romance them, then the moonstone ring to marry this character, then reload their save to marry their actual chosen character. It’s just so unnecessary.     • Achievements for playing the game poorly. I always hate this. I guess they’re supposed to be funny, but if I’m actually doing well in a game, I don’t want to purposely do poorly to get achievements.    • NPCs lack character development. The social elements of the game are definitely a weak point in terms of writing and execution. Waldo aka “Magic Man” is the most interesting and that’s because he has to do with the “main objective” of the game. But you don’t even get to know him that well either and I romanced him for the achievement (mentioned previously).     • I am disappointed that you cannot get a cat even though one is featured in the “End of the Day” image. I definitely recommend the game for those who are fan of both genres.

_childDocuments_.review: First four or so hours were fun. You get into the groove of exploring the islands, crafting, and meeting new spirits. The graphics and music are delightful. Then the problems start to become apparent, and they range from minor annoyances to things that make you want to give up entirely.The villagers being boring and restricted to talk/joke/flirt didn't bother me, because I never read villager dialogue anyways. However, I can understand this would be a negative for someone into building character relationships. The story also didn't bother me that much. Compare it to many of the Harvest Moon entries. You have one goal, like save the Harvest Goddess. Then the game sets you free to explore, build relationships, and make money. To me, Moonstone does the same, except the days become insanely boring, you have no motivation to build relationships, and the methods of making money don't really matter/are too tedious. I found combat/spirit taming to be the focus of this game, whether it was intentional or not. Relationships, crafting, and story all become somewhat irrelevant or unimportant. This game isn't Stardew Valley and does not compete on the same level in terms of those aspects.So, combat. I was having a blast. Then my team hit around level 15, and it became an issue of where to pick fights. Most islands near Moonstone have Earth spirits that are way too low level to for meaningful XP gain. Further out, most islands are Electric with enemies that are too high level. Then I found one Fire island and decided to grind there. However, unless you're stocked up on lilypads that take several days to grow, you're probably only going to be able to grind 2-3 fights a day. Maybe get 1 level a day if you're lucky. This game NEEDS more healing items OR other ways to heal spirits in between battles other than lilypads and spirits with passive healing (if you even want them on your roster). So if you have no lilypads, don't have a passive healer on your team... gotta go to bed. And that matters heavily in a game where time is paramount.Another thing is the absurd unfairness of type weaknesses. I regretted picking Ankylo. I should've listened to the people who said Capacibee was OP. If you get to an island with poison with him or any other earth type - consider them dead. Maybe unless you are significantly higher level than them. The enemies will relentlessly attack them. It's not a fair fight. In Pokemon, for example, you wouldn't be screwed just because your opponent has a move that is super effective against you. You still have a chance, especially if you're higher or same level. Enemies in this game tend to bash the type that's weak to them, then essentially two or three shot them with or without the effect of bash. What's even better is poison (and I assume other abilities like burn) damage does even MORE damage when you're bashed. And it doesn't seem to have a cap of how many turns it can last. I've seen poison that'll last for 11 turns. So you better have a way to clear it (AKA a randomly given potion from a chest). If you don't, kiss that spirit goodbye for the day. He'll come back with 1 HP.Do I let Ankylo keep dying, and then the rest of my team? Do I fly back to Moonstone and hope that Zed is still open? Or did I put that spirit in my barn? Do I give up on that island and spend the rest of the day chopping trees? So you MUST choose your team wisely depending on the island. That would be fine with me if there was an easier, quicker way to access all spirits AND if there were more healing items in the game. Why not have Zed open 24/7? Like how Pokemon has 24/7 Pokecenters with computers to access your boxes? Why can't I have a menu that shows me what spirits (AND their stats and decks) are in the science center, which ones are in the barn, and which ones are in my medallion, WITHOUT physically going there? From what I can see, you can only view the HP and experience bar of your medallion team from the menu. Why do we have to use an item to go into a room to feed them, view stats, and so on? I am not a fan of the medallion, as it just slows down the gameplay.Looking past the obvious flaws with the villagers, the story, and things like farming... this game definitely needs an overhaul when it comes to combat. I agree with the review that said you will either have landslide victories or landslide losses. The only in between for me was having my whole team wipe except for my high armor, high HP Sandcrashle. Additionally, the ability to see all spirits in your possession from a menu needs to be added. More and better healing items need to be added. Being able to see enemy level from the map would be nice as well. Like if I were to scroll over an island on the map, and it said, "Average level: 20" or "Enemy level: 17-20." Then I'd know where to grind, then I'd know how to pick my team in the morning. Otherwise, it's a no from me.

_childDocuments_.review: If Stardew Valley and Pokemon had a baby, that would be  - although a lot of people prefer to compare it to Slay the Spire rather than Pokemon. The game is an adorable pixel-art farming sim / life sim, in which you adventure in the wild to engage in pet battles and collect spirits instead of fighting off enemies.As a life sim,  has all the mechanics that you would expect from the genre. You plant seeds, tend to them and harvest them for consumables to be used in pet battles or sell them to the general shop in town. You can also mine and chop trees, whose resulting resources allow you to craft building stations and furniture items or upgrade your items and home. The little town has plenty of interesting characters that you can build your friendships with, or even romantically pursue. The universe of  offers 100 uniquely-generated floating mini-islands for you to explore at your own pace and a nice cozy story, closely guided through quests, with a good mix of easily reachable objectives and long-term goals.As a creature collector,  provides a really entertaining experience through its card-based pet battles, where the decks of your active pets are put together. This allows you to combine these cards for fun combos, as long as the cards drawn are suitable for that. The designs of the 70 spirits that you can tame are full of creativity, one more adorable than the other. Also very cute is that your pet team follows you around like little ducklings when you move on the map, although sometimes they tend to get in your way, especially when farming; however, there’s an option to make them stop following you. The pets that you don’t bring into battle can be stored either in a barn or in a research center, the difference between these two being that the latter does not require any maintenance on your part. The pets stored in your barn need to be fed constantly and in return, they drop items required for quest completion, for crafting or which can be sold for some extra income.Each of these two aspects of the gameplay has its own strengths and weaknesses. For instance, the crafting part is very straightforward, requiring only a couple of steps even for more complex items. The tools don’t have that annoying durability mechanic that requires you to always craft a new one every few days. The plants require daily watering (aside from rainy days), but the watering can doesn’t ever need to be filled and besides, you can just craft sprinklers to water your plants automatically. There are plenty of basic resources to gather (although trees and grass don’t automatically respawn) and the mines that you can open on each island are rich in minerals, chests that drop blueprints, and spirits to tame. On the other hand, a lot of the items required for progression (such as the barn or essential flying items) are gated behind the acquisition of Moonstones. Up until close to the endgame where you get a blueprint to mass-produce them, likely for transitioning into a sandbox kind of gameplay, these are extremely rare: each island contains only one per season, and very few bosses or chests drop any. Due to their scarcity, the progression is extremely slow, and exploring as many islands as possible quickly becomes your main goal. This in turn requires you to be able to fly greater distances (to reach further islands) and to be equipped to fight any enemies that you might find there.In regards to the deckbuilding aspect, you get to expand your deck by one random card (chosen out of three possible ones that the game offers) every time you level your pet. Upgrading or removing a card is possible, however you will need special tokens for that, which are also quite rare (you can find one every few islands). Thus, while the battles are really fun, the deckbuilding mechanic is rather restrictive, as you don’t have full flexibility in customizing your deck.  also offers 30 rather lengthy, yet very exciting dungeons, where you get to solve little puzzles, uncover chests and fight higher-level spirits.Like pretty much any other game belonging to the genre,  is quite addictive. There’s always something to do or explore, and your stamina bar allows you to perform enough activities to keep you hooked throughout the entire in-game day. The game keeps things really fresh by throwing this mix of mechanics at you, which offers endless possibilities. However, keep in mind that the farming aspect is not the main focus of . Instead, it’s used only as a support system for the pet battles, which is the actual essence of the gameplay.Note: I played this game on a different account, hence the low playtime here.

_childDocuments_.review: An honest review!I heard about this game from a friend and from Twitter, so I instantly added Moonstone Island to my wishlist and excitedly waited for its release. Initially, I wasn't sure what to expect when I first started the game.If you're an avid fan of both Pokemon and Stardew Valley, then I think you'd really find this game enjoyable as it has similar features of farming materials and collecting/battling spirits. I am someone who finds grinding/farming enjoyable and the simple and understandable mechanics allow for hours of farming as a form of stress relief. I also really like the turn-based gameplay when you battle with spirits and find this feature very enjoyable. Despite the fact that there are a couple of bugs here and there, it doesn't affect your gameplay whatsoever. I think one thing that this game does lack is a plot/storyline. I would like to know more about the alchemist we play as and even the lore/background story of Moonstone Island and its residents. Although we can go on dates with a resident of our choice (which is a great feature), I would still like to know more about the story behind Moonstone Island.Nevertheless, there were a few things that I had expected in this game but weren't a feature. Unlike Pokemon/Stardew Valley, there's no character customization of our alchemist nor can we name ourselves. I'm not sure if we already have a name, but if there is one then please correct me on that. We also can't name the spirits we collect. There are also no seasonal events/festivals that you could participate in. It makes me feel a little disconnected from Moonstone Island and its residents.One thing that I do dislike in the game is the inability to move buildings unless you have to wait and craft for another one. This process usually requires moonstones and moonstones take some time to collect and farm for them as they are a rare resource. Overall, Moonstone Island is a fun, enjoyable game for everyone and has huge potential for improvement. I even bought the DLC for additional furniture as I love gathering materials and decorating our home. I love playing this game, especially after a long day of work. So, I can't wait to see this game develop further and flourish.

The farming is fun and doesn't feel grindy, the island discovery system has me hooked on exploration, and the art is beautiful pixel perfection. There isn't anything to dislike about the game that I can find, and I'm already worried about how I'll get work done in the next few weeks with this beckoning me to my SteamDeck. A+++++ great job and kudos to the developers!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: A little rough around the edges at times, but it's clear to me that the developers are committed to improving the game and adding content so I'm here for it. Oft described in reviews I've seen as a mixture of Stardew Valley and Pokemon, which sounds accurate, but don't expect for the smorgasbord of content that SV has - not yet at least. My main issue with the game as-is is that there isn't much incentive to keep spirits around in your barn, I'd like to be able to put those lazy spirits to work around the ranch!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest and say I tried to love this game. I really did. It has a nice design, and I can tell the amount of love and effort put into this game. This being said, there are too many issues that prevent me from actually having a good time. I have too many gripes about this game to keep playing. I straight up cupped my face in my hands after it crashed again. I don't want to hate this game, but for those who want to buy this game, here's a few struggles I've had while playing this game, in hopes you have second thoughts. Everything takes way longer and is a lot more complicated than it needs to be. Taming monsters is fun and all, but you can only carry along 3 monsters at a time. Not only that, if you want more monsters, you need to create a barn to hold those monsters. Even if you have a barn, you can't hold anymore more monsters if you don't have a feeder in your barn or your team is full. I went into the first boss fight and found a shiny monster, but wasn't able to keep it because my team was full and I didn't have a barn because you don't unlock it until around halfway to the end of the first month. You can't rearrange or get rid of another monster in your team or barn if you find a shiny, meaning you completely miss out on it forever, even if you end up taming it. Not only that, you need to reach a certain requirement to unlock the barn in the first, aside from beating the first dungeon. This gatekeeps a lot of content and monsters you might need to progress. I didn't even craft the barn until there were only a few days left in the first month.Not only that, everything is too expensive, especially early on in the game. There's a material called Moonstone, which is required for multiple upgrades for tools, transportation, and buildings. This being said, Moonstone can only be found ONCE per ISLAND. Secret underground dungeon chests have a chance to drop them, but nothing is guaranteed. There's a way to increase the chance of chests dropping them, but it's still a 5-10% increase. The worst part about moonstone is that not only is it extremely rare, but sometimes recipes require moonstone bars, which you need 3 moonstones in order to make it, making crafting increasingly expensive. Next is the monster problem and combat problem. Everything is out to get you, no matter what, monsters can and will chase you. The only way to prevent monsters from chasing you is to unlock a skill through progression, without knowing how long you will take to level up that skill, let alone knowing you had it. I didn't even know skills existed until the skill tree popped up out of nowhere when I went to bed. The only way to see your skill tree normally is to craft a mirror using moonstone.Also, monsters in combat will absolutely destroy you if you don't have a proper team, which sucks if you want to level up. In battle, there are several things you need to focus on. Your health and your shield, and the enemies' health and shield. The shield is depleted using certain skills, which both you and the opposing have. While it seems fair, sometimes your fights can become unwinnable. When shields are depleted, the damage dealt is increased to 1.5x the original, with also stunning a monster for that turn. This being said, when you are stunned, and you're dying, you can't use items on that monster, at all. This means you can lose a monster sometimes to a crowd of monsters ganging on one of your guys. While I can understand that strategy also goes into play, fights can just seem unfair, especially against boss monsters. Right before my game crashed like I said earlier, I was fighting a local boss monster that sometimes show up. In this fight, they had a regen skill that they kept spamming that restored them to full health each turn, regardless of how many times I broke their shield or did damage, meaning unless I ran, I wasn't able to get out of the battle. Unfortunately, even though I defeated the other monsters on the field, my weaker monsters that I wanted to level up wouldn't get any experience, which means no level-up. There are ways to level up using crops, but those crops only give you around 100 exp, whereas monsters will need 1000s depending on the level.Of course, there's plenty more frustrations, but that's enough about the combat and monsters.The NPCs are alright. Nothing crazy, or even worthwhile. They're kind of just like cardboard. They have some personality, but I feel like this game is just a dating sim farming game rather than vice-versa. Not even the main character you play feels fleshed out. You can't customize or even name your character, to the point I'm not even sure anyone on the island you land on actually knows your name. It just feels shallow. For my one comparison I'm doing to Stardew Valley, one of the big reasons I liked the game so much was because not everyone was romanceable. People had lives and families, hobbies and interests. In Moonstone Island, everyone just walks around and owns a store for you to shop at. They're just convenient and pretty store clerks rather than people. Finally, the game's performance. The performance and handling of this game is iffy, to say the least. I always feel like there's input lag, and the game sometimes chugs out of nowhere. I know my laptop doesn't perform the best while running games, but it has run well enough to play cute little pixel art games like this one. The main issue is that every time I load areas, I fear for my game because it might crash again. I've played whole entire productive days where I need to do it all over again because it crashed. There's a manual save function, but I shouldn't have to save every time I load an area. So that's about it. I don't want to hate on the game nor discourage the people who like it. There are just too many problems for me to keep playing. I know that this game is new and is still being worked on, so I have hopes for it in the future, but if you're at all worried about finding a cute little farming sim right now, I'd honestly just save the money or buy Stardew Valley instead.

It's so fun trying to collect all the spirits and learning different combos of cards to play in the battles, and power ups that work best. Their Discord is a great community too!! _childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited to try it out and I was a bit sad that I had to refund it but the game is just not it. For me I got it to play it only on steam deck, but it was lagging every few seconds when entering the town or leaving.While it is nice to have so much freedom, it feels like a mix of genres but all of them are not well thought through and so it makes the game feel really slow, repetitive and boring very fast.The card battles are as well scripted, at least some of them, because no matter how hard I tried I had to win this battle and I'm not really into scripted battles. I didn't even get to the point to brew anything, worse than this is basically potion permit.I would give this game a neutral, because you really have freedom, but since I have to decide I don't recommend it because it is just not well thought through, very repetitive and boring in the beginning and sadly the lags on steam deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: So let me start by saying, if you're going into this hoping to dig into the "Creature Collecting" aspect, you might be a little disappointed. However for me, it turned out to be a positive, and here's why. This game makes you work to even start building up you collecting of creatures. You must build a barn, and then stables, which is indeed time consuming, heck, you pretty much stuck with a the first three creatures you catch for the first few hours. However, for me it felt extremely fun to build up you home base and get the space for more creatures, but thats exactly it. If you just want some straight up creature collector, this might not be the game for you. Though the combat is fun, even if it currently feels a bit easy. And the fact that creatures get the chance to learn three random abilities (some only that creature can learn) may be a plus or bonus to some people.Meanwhile the game feels pretty polished. The only issues ive had is a gripe about the kinda weird stuttery movement of your character, and my biggest complaint being what i think is an annoying audio bug. When ever i  enter a building and come back out, the music just goes off, and sometimes could stay off for multiple in game days. Then sometimes it just stops for no reason, which sucks because this games soundtrack is pretty decent.All in all, get this game if you like games like Ooblets or slime rancher. You'll be putting more time into your base(s) than probably the creature collecting.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly addicting, great graphics, and very fun game play loop.  If you like collecting creatures, easy to approach card battling, and fishing mini games this is for you. Also you can romance the Magic Man, 10/10. The developers are hilarious and dedicated, constantly updating the game.  It really took me by surprise how hooked I've been.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: I was absolutely enamored with Moonstone Island the second I saw it in the 2022 Wholesome Games Direct and was ecstatic when it finally came out! The art style, premise, and diverse set of characters (with so many using they/them or combination pronouns!!!) are all right up my alley and so so wonderful.The island exploration is really fun and it's so cool to go fly to the other islands and explore secrets & dungeons & such. The card turn-based fighting style is actually easy to understand and really fun! Usually card type game mechanics tend to not be my fave because I find it hard to understand the rules a lot of times, but I'm very grateful to the devs for making it so easy to learn! I really enjoy the different fishing mechanic as a video game fishing enthusiast. Once you get the hang of it, it's so much fun. And oh my gosh, the creatures are all so super adorable that I just want to collect them all hehe.I still have so much to do and explore with this game, but I definitely recommend it if you (like me) are a fan of pixel art, cute farming sims mixed with creature collecting, romancing characters (but be prepared to not know who to romance because they're all GORGEOUS), exploring open worlds, & all of the comfy cozy vibes!
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: I quite like this game. There's a lot of fun to be had with the combat and exploration. The monster collecting is also great and there's a good sense of progression. However, I do wish some of the mechanics had a bit more depth to them. I want monsters to feel more distinct and environments to feel more threatening. I want more incentive to level my monsters up and more endgame content to explore. I also wish that some of the skills felt a bit more useful. Despite all that, this is still a great game (with a great dev team) that I am excited to see more of.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I was hooked immediately. It gives me warm fuzzy stardew vibes with a twist of Pokemon and other nostalgic game references. I think there are a few things id love to see for this game, like being able to use the Decorative furniture in our homes and little things like that, Expanding on relationships beyond a few dates, etc but it definitely scratches that itch that SO few games like this do.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE ITIt's like a mixture of Pokémon and Stardew Valley but has so many improved aspects with adorable character sprite, cool spirit designs (the names are a little corny though), a more interesting way to build relationships, caves, dungeons with puzzles, and plenty land on the map to explore. _childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: I played through all of it on release, and while I love the 2 genres that it pulls from, it ends up feeling flawed in too many places to ever recommend. Many basic UX tasks are still cumbersome and buggy. Atmosphere is the biggest win, but most of the characters, farming+ systems, and card mechanics just feel too unpolished or janky.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game. Stardew + Pokemon. Very entertaining, but could definitely use a quality of life update. It doesn't have the same depth as Stardew in crafting, farming, relationships, or hidden content. But it is a fun game.The following is more of my plea to the developer to update a few things. Its a great game, don't let the rant below keep you from the game.1. The XP gained from combat seems entirely too low. It would take hours of grinding to level up, and it seems like the only viable way to level up is to spam XP flowers.2. It gets really old, really quick to feed 30 spirits by hand every. single. day. But the auto feeder is so damn expensive considering you need those moonstone ingots for everything that is worthwhile.3. Given how boring it is to constantly feed your spirits, it seems very harsh that they will all just run away if you stop for a few days. Stop producing? Sure. But all 30 spirits just migrate to Taco Bell, never to return?4. The controls on the PC feel like they were developed for a controller only. Even after 20 hours of game play, I often cant remember when I need to hit space, click E, or click the mouse. I recommend clicking and E only.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's quite literally everything I've ever wanted in a game. Farming sim, creature collecting, and romancable characters?!?! It's perfect. On par with Stardew Valley even. The reason I am giving it a bad review is because I am three hours into this game. It has crashed three times. This game is not hard to run. My laptop has 32 gbs of RAM. It runs Cyberpunk like a dream. The problem is definitely not on my end. I love this game. I love the concept. I am not loving having to restart every other day because the game wants to throw up a blank white page. No error message. Just unresponsive. Please fix this.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: So this is one of those I wish there was a middling option, but all in all I did enjoy.As far as light relaxing games go, this is a pleasant experience.  Its got fun deck-builder mechanics; enjoyable exploration; and nice light tone.  But man oh man do I wish there was more depth to everything.  Combat boils down to 'smash armour then attack constantly' with other abilities never really feeling to scale.  Townsfolk relationships never develop unless you explicitly date them; but even then, though well written, fall apart mechanically.  Marriage (bonding) doesn't do anything, nor does having a high relationship with people, and the biggest sin there was a character I dated coming at to me as Polyamourous, then getting upset if you date someone else.It is an enjoyable game, and is worth a try; but I really hope it gets more time and attention and love to become something truly special.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: The first year can really be a grind with a fun game play loop, once your into your 2nd or so month in year 2 you'll feel like you've done it all and that's when the game will become stale.For example now that I am in year 2 I have a moonstone farm in my basement that currently generates 72 moonstones per day, Gold has become useless once you have gotten all the recipes and tools, taming seems pointless now that I have captured all 66 monsters. I've maxed out the amount of dates I can have with the person I chose so the dialogue with them is non existent.I love the game but it needs more content.

But with Moonstone Island I couldn't wait to finish everything! I'm still doing some of the side quests like the Mythical Fish one. I'm super bummed to have finished honestly I wish there was more!!
