_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: If you're hesitating to buy the game because of negative reviews, just know that most of the complaints I saw when deciding whether to purchase have been resolved. Bugs get fixed, features get added. So if there's a specific issue you're worried about, check the patch / update notes because there's a good chance that it's no longer relevant. This is one of the reasons I purchased this game, and I have not regretted it. Seriously, there were a few minor things I didn't like about the game, and they were added / fixed / improved in the most recent patch,As far as game-play goes, this has everything I loved about playing Pokemon, and more. There's so many cute spirits to collect, and they can walk behind you, which I adore. The combat is turn-based and uses cards. NPC relationships I'm not sure about, since that's not an aspect of games I gravitate towards. But I can tell you if you're like me and don't want to talk to NPCs that much, you can just spend days hopping from island to island, taming and battling spirits. When you make some progress, you can use a glider and it's super fun and relaxing.The farming is not a huge part of the game - at least not compared to farming sims so if that's what you're mainly looking for, you're going to be disappointed. But if you're into collecting cute creatures, exploring, dungeon diving, and battling, I think this game is worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: As others have mentioned - this game is a mixture of Stardew Valley and Pokemon.  It has all the basic life sim type of activities - farming, crafting, foraging, mining, fishing, relationships - plus the collect them all Pokemon style spirits.  I'm going to lose so many hours in this game.  And there is an owl spirit that I must find.  Top priority.  Great little indie game.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: If you like cosy farming sims like Stardew Valley; a chance to explore a mythical realm and collect pets like Pokemom; a world layout like Zelda; or a combat card game like Hearthstone... this game is for you. Even if you only like one of these, you should definitely check it out. If you want to take your time or speedrun and give yourself a challenge both are possible. There's a surprising amount of grinding you can do in this game. Overall versatile with a good story line and interesting, diverse NPCs you can meet along the way... Did I mention there's a sexy "magic man" with no face or memories that randomly pops up everywhere in a Baba Yaga house and saves you from danger??? yeah.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a wonderful mix of a few of my favorite games, like Pokemon, Stardew Valley, and Sun Haven. The story is building up well so far, and the mechanics of the game go smoothly. The music is rather mellow, even in boss battles, as far as I've heard, and makes the game play quite relaxing even in combat. I like the spirits and their designs, my favorite guy so far is Dusty. The card battles aren't a new thing, but it feels very immersive and has some unique changes. I will highly recommend this to my family and friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: i have been really enjoying moonstone island!! pros:art style & character design huge map to explore upgrade and decorate your home cons:card based battles can take a lot of time/ feel tedious not a ton of direction for the main story line moonstones are pretty hard to find, and you need a ton of them, one for each auto feed spot in your barn, and 9 for tool upgrades, 9 for crafting large items.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels shallow and the replayability is next to nil unless you enjoy decorating a little housing/farm area that ultimately doesn't matter or filling it with hundreds of spirits that ultimately don't matter or grinding their levels up which also doesn't really matter once you get through your first year and beat the main storyline.The relationships in game are...nice...but they feel like window dressing and are equally as shallow compared to other games like Stardew Valley or Coral Island.The first year in game is a grindy panicky rush and then there's just.....nothing else to really shoot for beyond the cosmetic stuff that I mentioned previously.It's good for a single play through but that's about it.The devs do seem to be updating the game at a pace that tracks for a smaller studio but even the DLC packs feel somewhat lacking and like they're just delaying stuff until the game gets released on Switch next year.I wound up seeing/catching all the spirits in game in my first year, maxed out my talent trees, bought all the housing/farm upgrades, and dipped into the relationship stuff a bit but it all....didn't really feel very filling or satisfying at all.It wasn't boring and it wasn't terrible, it was just bland and more of the same like a number of other games that have tried to emulate Stardew Valley over the years.....the magic just isn't there.Speaking of which, the community is what ruined this game for me and what left a bad taste in my mouth.I've witnessed the devs and their moderators actively discriminating against neurodivergent and disabled types in their discord repeatedly and have seen them treating those folks rather badly, all whilst high fiving each other, and encouraging other similar bad behaviors.Which is ironic seeing as how one of the characters in game basically is neurodivergent/disabled...but I guess that's all window dressing too.It reminds me of the same way the Arcane Waters community was acting before that game and community nose dived.If you can look past that stuff and you're down for a quick farming fix before better games with more funding and better developers update or come out with their new games, then sure this game is for you.And if you can't...then you're not missing much and you can just relegate this game to the "I'm going to watch this on twitch only instead of spending my own time and money on it" category.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend checking this game out, especially if you are a fan of cozy games. If you are not a card game fan, you do not have to focus on this aspect heavily but it is a primary component of the game. The inbuilt pixel art designer and decoration are well done and enjoyable to do. Also enjoyable on the resource gathering axis.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, this is exactly what I was looking for in a game that has a significant farming sim aspect to it.﻿When I tried playing other farming sims, like Stardew Valley, the issue I had was that I didn't feel enough incentive to keep progressing. I like the farming sim aspect, but I needed something other than  farming & romancing the cast in order to keep me going.﻿I'm glad the main/side quests & creature-collecting in Moonstone Island have kept me hooked. I'm able to fully enjoy the farming sim aspect while having things to look forward to in the game.﻿As for the creature (spirit) battling, I suggest you see this as a deck-builder rather than traditional creature-collector battling, otherwise you might end up with massive deck sizes that are unwieldy.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: Has potential but isn't as fun as it could be still seems like a very big work in progress everything seems too simplified and basic and it takes too much time out of your day to do things Negatives-Farming is too slow and tedious-Tool upgrades don't really feel like you upgraded it-Doesn't have any tents or campfires to sleep at for the night when you explore other islands so you gotta pass out or teleport and walk back home-Growing crops take long -Difficulty of monsters goes up too fast so you can't really train your monsters like that-No character customization-Takes too long to do anything even if you extend the day -Characters don't feel like they got personalities like that-Not much options for increasing stamina-Dungeons aren't as well made-Not much of a story to itPositives-Card fighting is pretty fun for a bit-Cute design for whole game and monsters are well designed -Creative Decor
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game if you like deck builders like Slay the Spire, farming games like Stardew Valley (though the farming is very quickly and easily made automated by sprinklers) and enjoy exploring to see a lot of different creatures. I'm pretty surprised I've kept with it for more than 30 hours, despite loving harvest-moon style farming games, I usually drop off after the first few hours - they often feel very tedious and unrewarding. Moonstone Island makes the crops useful and interesting to discover and grow as they can buff your creatures in combat, be used for making concoctions (combining two plants in whatever way you want for more stats,) and be used for cooking.I also am not a fan of traditional Pokemon rpg mechanics, the deck building aspect is a lot more engaging to me. Building your team and combining different types and decks of creatures gives a lot of room for experimenting.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: As someone with severe anxiety, I feel the developers were a little misleading in stating this game as a "cozy" game. Having to worry about stamina when flying between islands, fires, lightning, running into monsters everywhere (but the main island) just put me on edge most of the time. The 20 hours I have in it is mostly because by the time I realized it wasn't that cozy, it was already too late to refund... so I TRIED giving it another shot so I didn't feel like I waste my money.Either way, some people might view this as cozy, if compared to other RPGs, but if you compare them to ones like Coral Island... it's definitely not cozy. What a sad day. Hell, even Coromon is more cozy than this. It's not the worst game, but it's misleading in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend if you enjoy other cozy games and deck building!Pros:1. The NPCs are fun2. The storyline is cute3. The vibes are INTENSELY cozy and comforting4. Everyone on the island is queer af. Cons1. Leveling up is a grind, it's much faster/easier to just go to a higher level area and catch new spirits, as once you're past low levels you get almost no XP. That's fine, but its also not as fun as levelling up a "buddy" who sticks with you throughout the game. 2. The egg hatch chances suck. I completely almost all other parts of the game, but after hatching almost 20 eggs waiting for the ONE egg exclusive hatch and not getting it, I'm calling it quits, which sucks as I had planned on doing 100%. Very discouraging. Otherwise, overall had a ton of fun, but if you're a completionist it can be quite frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, love all the aspect of the game. Except for the dungeon, it's boring to see a same looking boss in every dungeon, and they're weak too (including the last boss). I could beat a bunch of lv.60 spirits with only lv.20s. There are a lot of overpowered cards and the level cap didn't affect much after your spirits reach lvl.20.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very aesthetically pleasing game. The pixel graphics are very nice to look at, and the creature designs are very cute. The card battler system feels novice friendly.This game makes a valiant attempt at bringing together creature collection, battling, life simulation, and farming and crafting which means there's always something to do and focus on every in-game day. I think the in-game days are a good enough length that I can make a choice to focus on one or two aspects every day. There's lots of variety.What I do worry about is the lack of unity in the different mechanics. There's farming, there's creature battling, there's a social aspect of the game, but it really does feel a little disjointed at times and I would love for the dev to bring these aspects closer together.A lot of the mechanics really do feel like they're there just to be there, and I wonder how necessary they were to be included in favour of deepening out other aspects of the game. The social/romance system in particular feels that way to me. I'm not opposed to romanceable NPCs as I enjoy that aspect in other games like Stardew Valley, but here it just feels like it lacks depth so far and I don't see the point of it even existing in its current state.I did have fun with this game, and I will keep having fun with this game mostly in the exploration and creature battling sense. It is certainly not a bad game, and it gets points for its great artstyle from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Moonstone Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. It's an amazing blend of a farming sim like stardew valley and Pokemon. As of writing this I just beat the earth temple and it was a lot of fun. It's a very rewarding game. You can do anything you want, when you want to. There are consequences to loosing a battle or running out of stamina, but they're not massive. _childDocuments_.review: Moonstone Island is like stumbling upon a hidden treasure chest in the gaming world. Picture this: you step onto the island and are suddenly whisked away into a magical realm. The visuals? Absolutely breathtaking. The gameplay? It’s not just a bunch of pixels; it’s a canvas painted with intricate details and vibrant colors. You’ll find yourself exploring every nook and cranny—even beyond your home, wondering how something so beautiful can exist.And then there are the villagers. Oh, the villagers! They’re like a quirky bunch of friends you meet at a cozy café. Each one has their own story, and their own background. You’ll chat with them, maybe even share a laugh or two. And who knows? Maybe you’ll find yourself falling for one of them (wink, wink).Now, let’s talk battles. Turn-based, deckbuilding—sounds fancy, right? But it’s more than that. It’s strategy, it’s adrenaline, it’s that rush when you play that perfect card combo. As you explore the island, you’ll collect these powerful cards and creatures, all ready to kick some foe butt.Moonstone Island isn’t just a game; it’s an experience. The kind that sticks with you, long after you’ve put down the controller.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend? Not at this juncture. I'd say I dont really have any new criticisms as opposed to anyone else's. Initially, I had opted not to play it due to complete lack of character customization. For a game that boasts diversity I thought it was odd that the player character is supposed to be a set thing, but the game was on sale for release, so I thought I would get past it and try it anyway because it's an indie game and I like to support indie game makers.My complaint is perhaps that it doesn't know what it's trying to me. I don't care for the "cozy" genre in general, or what people are trying to make it out to be which is an oversaturation of farming simulators that feel like someone looked at Stardew and said "I can make this but better". I feel like they seldom are. But this one is perhaps one of the few where I wonder why farming was included at all? There doesn't seem to be much point to it in the beginning of the game, where the only seeds that you have at your disposal is forageables, and by the time your crops have grown you'll have quite enough of those in your inventory from exploration alone, so no real need to grow them. Especially *especially* because they sell for very little. I got though about one crop and surmised that there was no point to it.Also, I know fishing minigames have always been divisive in farming sims, especially Stardew where it can be difficult in the beginning, but to not have any sort of game mechanic for it whatsoever just felt odd to me. I dont understand why it would be included aside from being yet another waste of stamina without much benefit.Another thing I dont undestand the inclusion of is the romance system. This is another big deal breaker for me, because the thing I get most from these sorts of games are the NPC interactions, and here there really are none to be had. Others will mention, but the NPC daily interactions are limited to a blurb of dialogue, usually a line, and then 3 RNG choices of random success: Talk, Joke, Flirt. That was extremely disappointing to me, I'd daresay it turned me off. Because essentially it doesn't seem like it matters what you know about a character, which will be very little, so long as your random chance pans out. And it seldom does. It turned me off of speaking to NPCs if I'm honest, and I wasn't much interested in them to start.The main focus is the monster hunting which is. Fine. Better reviews than mine have mentioned the issues with the lack of platforming to traverse the terrain that monsters can scale easily and pin you in. You're only allowed three until you build a barn and building a barn requires moonstone which, if you're not careful about examining the ingredients needed for every item, you might end up using and then needing in a different state for a different level of item (guess who did that one!).Also, I'm sorry, that wheel to switch through your tools is so inconvenient. It's a small issue that felt like a big one, where the tedium is really felt the longer you have to use it. Often times I skipped resource gathering altogether simply because I didn't feel like hitting Q and switching my tools back and forth a million timesHonestly, this is one time that I wish the "do/do not recommend" was more than a simple yes or no. I don't hate the game, it was fun enough, but the cons that I had keep me from having any real desire to play more, I probably won't come back to it while it's in this state because I personally didn't enjoy it. I guess you could say that I don't recommend it, because I think it could be better. I don't think saying that it's made by a small team is enough when it feels like there were so many corners cut on unnecessary things that didn't feel like they needed to be added, at least until they were a little more substantial. I wish if this was a game about monsters, it had been a game about monsters and done it really well, than be a game about monsters and also All This Other Stuff and nothing really got much time and attention otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game but it feels like the devs took everything besides the combat and exploration from Stardew Valley and then they forgot at the last minute that they actually have to make it their own game.1) Farming feels like a chore and a hassle because you have to be within one tile of the plot to plant a seed/water/hoe and because the tiles are so small, it feels like a constant battle of being on top of the tile or too far away from the tile.2) The key binding options are far too limited for the amount of popups in this game. The controls feel clunky and overwhelming because sometimes there is 3 different buttons that do the same thing and you cant rebind half of them to your play style.3) This goes hand in hand with the last one. They basically tried to copy Stardew Valley and yet somehow managed to make the functionality so. much. worse. For example, when you put stuff in the sell bin, you cannot add items by the stack automatically. With every item you need to choose the amount and confirm. This sounds silly but when you're trying to sell large stacks of multiple times, it can become an absolute chore.4) The battle game play feels a little unbalanced. I feel like I can have an equal amount of card type and yet every battle my first hand is all attack cards and then I wont get a single skill card to remove the opponents armor until my 3rd or 4th and now suddenly I have all skill cards and no attack cards. This would be fine every once and awhile but it's beginning to feel like every single battle. This is especially annoying when it's 3 higher level spirits you're battling at once because now, not only have I lost but I've now wasted a whole day.

_childDocuments_.review: With about 50 hours on record, I can definitively say that this game is a decent game, but has too many problems. Let me go over some of the extremely bad bugs I experienced in the first week of playing this game.- The game crashed. Not just once, not just twice, but I counted a total of 19 crashes. No, my computer is not bad. Sometimes when screen transitioning it will just crash and you'll loose all your progress if you don't religiously save.- I lost all my inventory on multiple occasions. This is a massive problem as all I could do was reload or sacrifice everything I had.- The walking house generally doesn't always work to stay on its path. It will just go off the side of the map sometimes.- A notification appeared in the greenhouse saying the plants wouldn't grow in season, despite being seasonless.- You could duplicate all spirits by just taming the main one and running, including rare ones.It's a real big shame. These will probably get patched over time, yes, but what isn't as fixable is the gameplay.- Of the different types of spirits, the balancing severely favors certain types. Not only that, some can deal 1 million damage on turn one, while others barely survive a single hit.- Experience gain is ABYSMAL. Your options are to plant crops and spam them to increase experience or just tame new spirits. You can't reasonably level anything.- The relationships aren't really to the level of Stardew Valley, and it feels that way when you become serious with someone. It ends up feeling pretty hollow, and talking to someone feels like a task.- The dungeons are extremely bland. They all look fairly similar, and there are several that are just "Banish all the spirits to win!"To be honest, my opinion leads to be a roughly 7/10 game. Not a bad thing, but because of the bugs really, really making me waste a total of 5+ hours of real life time due to crashes and inventory losses, it's hard to reccomend it in its current state. The developers just needed a bit more Q&A, and the game could've easily hit the 8-9/10 range. If this game gets good updates in the future, I will switch to reccomending and adjust my review, but currently it's not the best game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent so many hours in this game now that it's difficult to describe what I love when there's !! It feels like a perfect amalgamation of the games I played growing up, like Pokémon, and Harvest Moon, and even Kingdom Hearts: Chain of Memories with its card system. It's a perfect game to , similar to Stardew Valley; but with , the pace is very much in your control. I've fallen in love with all of the townspeople!! While some games have characters that feel very separated from one another, the characters in this game have their own friendships and silly commentary on each other. The characters feel like just as you slowly fall in love with them, they slowly fall in love with you too, making . I found at the beginning of the game that it was slow to get friendship points, but that very quickly changes with unlockable friendship boosters and gift giving. And I love Magic Man.  In general, a lot of the game can feel slow to start, similar to other games in its genre. But if you're used to farming sims, dungeon games, and creature collecting, you know that a little hard work at the beginning makes the game much smoother down the line. With the use of the skill tree and completing quest lines, things like experience, exploration of the map, and the efficiency of the game mechanics (like crafting) slowly become more doable. As far as decoration goes, I'm so happy with how many items you're able to craft or buy to decorate your house. If you enjoy interior design aspects of games, . With a system similar to crafting clothes in the Animal Crossing system, you can also make (or copy/paste from other people's patterns) custom wallpaper and flooring which allows for so much customization of your space. I've even decked out my greenhouse with a few items. The only short coming with the custom flooring/wallpaper mechanic is that on Steam Deck, I haven't found a way to copy/paste other's patterns into it. This also means that when you reset the loom, you have to remake your old pattern since you can't copy/paste your own, either. But on PC, this is a non-issue! Additionally, your house is a pocket dimension so you can place your house on other islands or have multiple on the same! I have my "main" house which is very garden-y, and another that is a bit fancier, for example. I can use both and have access to the same interior!The spirits in the game are . If you've ever grinded to get a "rare" creature in a game, you're not missing out on that mechanic in this one!Overall, it can be a bit "slower" but rewards your work in multiple factions of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Moonstone Island has made me come to realise I am a sucker for games of this genre. I don't typically write serious reviews as most of mine are nonsensical, but this time I feel different. The game itself is like a mix of Stardew Valley and Pokemon, and this is strongly reflected in both gameplay and music, and I love it. The sprite work is colourful and eye catching and the game itself plays well. However, the game does have its flaws (I will mention these in the Cons section), but these flaws don't inherently take away from the fun of the game, not to a significant extent that is.Here are a list of some of my Pros and Cons with the game, as far as my experience goes:PROS:- The characters are charming, each with their own personalities, likes and dislikes, needless to say there will be at least ONE character you will strive to like.- There's always something to do! Farming, mining, fishing, interacting with villagers, exploring new islands, upgrading your house... The game has a ton on offer to keep you occupied.- Music is pleasant and likeable. As mentioned, if you have played Pokemon you'll understand what I mean when I say it will remind you of the games!- While the combat isn't overly complex and fairly simple, It's a change of pace for those looking to distance away from other tasks such as farming in order to focus more on spirits. However, I would recommend enabling fast mode during combat as it can get slow and boring pretty quickly without this feature enabled.CONS:- My biggest gripe is the BUGS. While there aren't many, there are only a handful that have slight affected my experience while playing. One bug in particular completely prevents the menu from being opened, whether this be the pause menu, tool wheel or crafting menu. The only fix for this is to enter a loading zone (house, dungeon, mine or encounter a spirit). The bug occurs when you open and close the menu too fast (as far as I'm aware). Not sure if this has happened for anyone else, but I've read articles and I don't believe I'm the only one who has experienced this issue.- Adding on to above, occasionally the game will soft lock as a result of this bug. If you try to open the menu in the bugged state, (sometimes) it will open but not display the menu. This can result in the player not being able to close the menu, resulting in a softlock.- Another bug I ran into was a soft lock while picking a card during combat, while this only happened ONCE, it may have been due to me selecting a card too fast? I wouldn't worry too much about this one.Ultimately, Moonstone Island is a GOOD game. Don't let the minor bugs deter you from the game itself. As far as my experience goes, if you like Stardew Valley, you'll have a fun time with this game. The game offers plenty to do, mind you I only have 9 hours on the game and I still have WAY more to uncover and explore. For a small Dev team they've definitely created something with tons of potential, I am excited to see what becomes of this game in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game in its current state. The ideas are very good, but the execution leaves a LOT to be desired.Pros:-Cozy, tranquil vibes, even though you are restricted by resources/time you can still take it easy-Interesting concepts and ideas, mixing monster-collecting, deckbuilding card battler and farming sim (think Pokémon, Slay the Spire and Stardew Valley)-Exploration is fairly fun at first and crafting is promising but doesn't go very far at the moment-Cutesy pixel-art graphics and pleasant-enough background musicCons: (this is where things derail)-BUGS. The game is a buggy mess. Even though its a full-release, it has game-breaking bugs. Freezes that require a full Alt+F4 happen FREQUENTLY, and are even worse on Steam Deck, it's been known for months and not fixed yet. Shopkeepers taking your gold and resources and not giving what you bought in return. Upgrades that disappear from the shop list making them permanently unattainable. One type of potion gives you the bottles back after using, and the other type doesn't. The list goes on. Honestly, it feels like the game is actually in some state of Early Access due to the amount of problems. And about that...-Limited systems. Remember when I said it feels like an Early Access? There are few-ish crafting stations, and each one (with the exception of the Decoration Station, which is mechanically "useless") only has a handful of useful recipes. It kinda feels like they started each thing and dropped it halfway through. The main character is an alchemist, but the game only allows you to break about 20 different "potions", and half of them (elemental resistance) become completely useless (you get equipment to nullify the damage) less than halfway into the game. In fact, by the time you get ACCESS to the cauldron required to make those potions, you'll probably already have one of the equips that nullify said damage. And even with the cauldron, you still need to RNG unlock the potion recipe! You can also mix two ingredients into a "concoction", which is done in a different crafter and are simply a mash-up of two foods into a new super-food with the stat bonuses of both. The main crafting station (Moonstone Enchanter) only has a similarly limited number of useful things to craft, same goes for the anvil (only makes the talismans that nullify damage, mentioned above, two-thirds of which become irrelevant because you can just make the most advanced one right off the bat and the first two are laughably bad anyway). All in all, there's the constant feeling like they had these really cool ideas, started to implement and then gave up and left the crafting system half-done. What actually IS there works well and looks good, but there isn't much there.-Limited combat. There's 80 total "spirits" (the monsters you tame). That's not a bad enough number, but compared to Pokémon's starting 150 it feels a little short. Specially considering that some elements have more spirits than others. Ice? Only three. Earth? A good solid dozen. Not only that, but each spirit's "cards" aren't actually unique to them. There's a pool of "neutral" cards that any spirit can get, and there's a pool for each element from each all spirits of that element draw. So two different Water spirits will have access to the SAME cards. The only effective difference between spirits of the same element is that each spirit has an unique "Passive" ability, which is useless in many cases (extra light radius at night? That's just brilliant! I'll take the one that does extra damage instead...)-Poor balancing. The way difficulty escalates as you move between islands is very disconcerting and the game does a poor job of telling you how to overcome that. The difficulty ramps up the farther away you go from the central island, but the jumps in difficulty can be really hard to overcome, specially if you happen to be at elemental disadvantage. Not only that, but heals are limited, so you're very limited in how much you can grind for EXP per day before you run out of items. Not only that, but you also get pitiful amounts of EXP when fighting spirits of the same level. You NEED to buff your spirits up with concoctions/food in order to boost their stats, so that they can punch up at enemies above their level in order to make decent EXP. At that point, you could just search and tame the same set of spirits, but at a higher level island, replacing your team with another of higher level. Might be just my opinion here, but that feels kinda dumb. Am I supposed to level up my team? If so, why is it so hard to level them and so easy to tame a new, updated one? Am I supposed to tame a new one at each level bracket? If so, why do monsters get EXP (there's even food that gives EXP) in the first place?-Janky controls. The targeting and use of tools feels very clunky. At first it doesn't bother you as much as you're getting used to stuff. But once you have a plantation with dozens and dozens of crops and you need to water them all and the aiming reticle is all over the place, it gets annoying FAST. Combat controls are a little bad but not terrible once you get used to them. Overall, it feels "Not horrible, but noticeably unpolished". You also stumble on some strange design choices, such as: You can get upgraded flying tools (Balloon > Broom > Glider), but once you upgrade to a better tool, the old one stays in your tool list forever even though you're never going to use it again. You're still forced (*eye roll*) to use the Broom in dungeons, but you'll never use the Balloon again and it will stay forever in your tool list. Not only that, but tools are put away separately from your inventory, in your "Tool Wheel". The kicker? You can't switch tools with a button press, you gotta bring up your Wheel and select it each time. The second kicker? The Wheel only fits 8 tools, and you use more than that, so sometimes you have to bring up the Wheel and manually change your selection (*EYE ROLL*) on the fly just to use it once, and then switch back. -Limited content. NPCs? Two-dimensional. There's very little dialog compared to other games of this genre. Everyone has very simplistic personalities, not many lines and not much in the way of events or interactions. Only 80 spirits, which all share common card pools based on their elements. Some elements have almost no spirits. There aren't many NPCs to begin with. There's a bloat of different crops, but the vast majority are completely useless and obsolete even in the season when they're introduced (because there's another crop that does the same, but better, and unlocks at the same time). Few crafting options, few buildings (your house, your barn and your greenhouse. That's it. And the greenhouse is pretty small), few cards, there's plenty of basic dungeons, but they tend to be a little short and simplistic. There's four major "season temples", but the "temples" are a joke. Each is just three rooms, the first with a new tool (more useless tool bloat, yay!) and each with a boss fight. That's it.I could keep going, but at this point you get the picture. It's a sad waste of potential.I really want to love this game, and I did at first. It has all the right ideas, but I just can't recommend it in its current state. Either wait for a BIG sale, or wait until they fix at least some of these issues before grabbing it. There are other, better farm sims and monster-collection games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Moonstone Island scratched my (very desperate) Stardew itch, despite its focus surprisingly being on exploration and combat.Let's lay down the core of the game real quick: it's like Stardew Valley if you add creature collecting like Pokemon with Slay the Spire combat. Very interesting combo, I know, but they actually work splendidly together even though all these parts aren't very integrated together. I'll go through each main element of the game on their own to better review them.A big criticism with this game seems to be the lack of a character creator, which is valid. The default main character is androgynous and ridiculously adorable imo, but I understand wanting to play as yourself, not a premade character. The NPCs don't have nearly as much depth as in Stardew or some other games, but they're definitely not characterless. You can definitely love or hate characters, but you won't be spending as much time with them as you will in Stardew. Their routines are also pretty shallow, which I know is a nitpick, but it still takes away from them. As far as the farming goes, it's honestly really shallow and de-emphasized. I think the devs just wanted to make a Stardew-like game so they added farming which ended up being overshadowed by the rest of the stuff they added, which I think is perfectly fine tbh.I was NOT expecting to like the Pokemon aspect of this game this much, considering I don't even like Pokemon, but here we are. The designs for each of the spirits (the creatures) are honestly stellar! The creativity, diversity, and cuteness of them all is honestly really impressive, and honestly the sleeper highlight of this game. The fact that they can also all follow you around too is so cute and awesome and I love it. The actual combat you do with these silly guys is… straight up Slay the Spire. It's fun.This game actually has a surprising amount of exploration, and it's actually really fun. You fly between sky islands with differing biomes and hazards, looking for more resources, dungeons, or temples, and it's just good ol fun. I tend not to enjoy exploration in games very much, but you're always rewarded in this game for it, even if it's as much as a stepping stone to a further island. The progression of it is just really satisfying to me.Now, for my nitpicks. The game generally always has this air of unpolished, whether that be the balancing of prices or accessibility of a certain resource, pixel art scaling inconsistencies, weird UI animations, inconsistent menu controls, etc. It's never game-breaking or anything, not even close, and when it comes to balancing it's at least always in your favor, but it does just make it feel like an early access game when it… isn't. Honestly most of these are so minor that there's almost no chance you notice them, but it mattered a slight bit to me, so I included it.All this being said, I do genuinely love this game. Even though it has some rough edges, it's super fun, so I don't really care. It's addictive in that special way only some games like Stardew Valley have capitalized on for me. I do, genuinely, at the end of the day, recommend this game, a ton.Moonstone Island is… out of this world 🌙(I'll arrange my own execution for that one, dw)Objective - 7/10;Subjective - 9/10;

_childDocuments_.review: While the whole concept and the art style is well done, with awesome game-play loop and mechanic, the control and UX design of the whole game is just sooooo bad that I cannot recommend the game at this stage.First of all, why the heck does the UI not support keyboard navigation? Out of all kinds of game, I would never expect 2D farming sim to not have that supported. Worse still, you also can't play the game only via mouse. You have to use keyboard to move around, no click and go there style of control. Both of this already turned it into a hard-to-control game that is not intuitive at all.Second, the interaction keybind and the whole 'tool' slot and that tool wheel selection mechanic is just so bad that I wonder if they have actually play-tested the game. One example is, somehow, they messed up the scrolling so bad that it often only move 1 slot to the left or right no matter how much you scrolled. Then, there's that tool wheel. Below is an example on what you need to do JUST to swap to a different tool:1. See that 'q'? Yeah. You have to hold it for a while, so the tool wheel pops up.2. Oh are you expecting to just keep holding the 'q', and drag your mouse to the direction of the tool you wanna select? Nope. You have to release the 'q'. The wheel doesn't disappear btw. (Yea it aren't a so called control wheel but more of a dumb inventory UI)3. Then, you have to click the slot of the tool you want to select. Oh but be careful not to scroll! Cause apparently those aren't tool slots, but instead kinda a 'quick access' binding slots. If you scroll, it instead just change the tool those slots bind to.Who designed such a control system like this?! It would be miles better just placing all the tools on the hot bar instead! Remember this is just an example of one of the weird decision they made regarding controls. There's a lot more issues like that which I can't fully list here.Next issue, a farming / collector sim like this should have focus on the character building of the villagers and the 'Spirits'. However, I am greatly disappointed when I clicked the 'chat...' button and it just pop up some hearts instead. They didn't even bother to write dialog for that! Come on!Same happens to most of the 'expected' interactions, like you can't talk to your 'spirits', and such. Basically, all npcs only really have story dialogs and 1 to 2 lines of dialogs for when you start an interaction. That's it.The whole game has really cool gameplay concepts, with wonderful art styles. I can see that there may be deep lore of the world too. However, the first impressions of the game just leave me with such a bad taste that I just don't enjoy playing the game, even tho the concepts sounds like a fun game. The terribly designed controls combined with lack of polishes for the npcs just make me feel like I am playing those simple story rpg game, with extra farming mechanics in it.I would have to say I am greatly disappointed, and I hope that the developers would spend a few more months focused on polishing the player experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: Early impressions (will update this after finishing the game):So far the game is really quite good. Character movement with a controller is a bit clunkier than I'd have liked, but that's a nitpick. Combat is fun and not too difficult. The slight RNG of the deck building adds a layer of tactics to each battle, as you're forced to deal with enemies with the tools you're given. Understanding deck building and how to make good use of different cards is fundamental to having a good time. My advice is to not stack your deck with all attack cards, but instead to rely on upgrading a few good attack cards while always keeping a good stock of bash cards to break shields. By breaking shields, you essentially get a free turn, which means another free hand draw to get the cards you want. Really, it's quite a good system. Good stuff!The farm sim aspect is there. I haven't really bothered much with it to be honest, as I find the monster taming to be more interesting. That said, I've yet to actually figure out how to tame monsters. I always seem to be too low level to tame them when I try. Oh well, my bee starter has been soloing the entire game easily so far, so I'm sure I'll figure it out eventually.The NPCs are fun. Their designs are nice. I like them all really. Haven't gotten very far into the whole romancing thing yet, but I'm looking forward to it.There is a lot in this game that isn't really explained to you. You sort of have to figure stuff out on your own which can be fun. Personally I think it's intuitive enough. Reminds me of SNES-era games where half the fun was just figuring out effective ways to use the game systems to your advantage.I recommend this game. It's charming, looks good, has great music. I can't really comment on how good it is as a whole package, but for the few hours I've had with it so far, I'm very pleased.

_childDocuments_.review: i really, really love this game. i bought this game with caution from a friend that it wasn't too fleshed out, so i came in with reduced expectations. however, i found myself really liking this game - i love the art style, the pokemon-y nature of the battles, and the exploration (especially the dungeons). the game isnt perfect - theres definetly things that need to be fleshed out, for example the fishing mechanic, which feels like it was just put there out of obligance to the cosy game genre, and the social mechanic, which is pretty lackluster - you click a button and the game rolls a dice on wether the interaction was successful or not, and the dates are pretty short. the characters arent as deeply developed as you might come to expect from a game like stardew valley, but a few characters do shine (i have the biggest crush on ferra). additionally, all the characters have given pronouns, and there are a few characters who use they/them, which is not at all a marker on the games quality, but it is appreciated to see representation. where i feel this game really shines is in the battles, exploring dungeons, and collecting spirits. its a mainly simple game that allows you to relax - its less a 'lean in' game, and more of a lean back, at least for me. tldr: if you loved pokemon and you love cosy games, you'll probably like this one. however, a few areas defintely need to be more fleshed out, for example the fishing and social mechanics. the art style is very pretty and overall meshes for a cosy, relaxing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So overall the game seems to have a fairly casual aspect.Generally enjoyable, it's not something you can shut off for but at the same time you don't need to be too focused. Gameplay is smooth and the loop is clear.Major aspects:Farming: Useful for growing crops you don't want to explore forCrops/Forageables: Better for consumption/crafting than saleFishing: Better for SaleExploring: Probably the best aspect currently, good variety of locations with added reasons to revisit islandsCombat: Pretty good, not a fan of card combats but this one is alrightPets: Nice pets, don't like how one of the main needs is locked away behind a mildly obtrusive questHousing: Easy to get new decorationsMost early game questions/tutorials are hidden in the villager quests which is a bit annoying but mildly reasonable as well. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT: This is my final review AFTER the recent patches. Fortunately, it's become a better game since release, but you could enjoy the same elements this game has elsewhere and be satisfied more there than here.---I was one of the people who were invested in this game. The game-play shown pre-release had elements mirroring life/farming sim-games, monster taming, etc looked awesome. The snippets leading up to the game's release had a lot of promise because it had a solid foundation for an early build until I found out it was actually the end-product. There are a few positives, but there are too many negatives that I can't recommend this to anyone, especially my own friends, when they could spend the time and money elsewhere and I know they wouldn't stick to one aspect like I did.1.	Art - Gorgeous. From your character, the environment, & to the townspeople sprites, it looks fantastic. 2.	Music - Fairly good. There weren't any specific tracks that made me stop just to appreciate it, but each track fit whatever it was meant to portray.3.	Price - matches the quality of the game. This game is definitely $20 USD worth of quality. If it were priced any higher, there would have been more issues.4.	Combat - The combat is MUCH more fleshed out than the other aspects. It starts off as a slow paced deck-builder that ramps into combo setups or synergies that makes it fun. The combat is what made me genuinely stick to the game for so long.1.	Combat (again) - Since this IS a deck-builder, I expected more unique cards for the spirits, but there weren't any. The cards each spirit comes with conforms to their element which is fine, but it does dampen the combat aspect.2.	Spirits - since I already talked about the elements above, let's get into the spirits. They gave each spirit something unique in the form of their own passive traits. Some augment tool use, some give boons during combat. The reason this is a neutral instead of being a positive is because most of these traits are HOT garbage. Unless you like the design of the spirit, there's no reason to use them because their trait has no value and there's no unique card in their deck.1.	Dungeons - the dungeons you encounter in the game are lackluster after your first three. Most of them just have time consuming puzzles that serve no real purpose while some are a freebie. One jarring thing is that they all have the same interior design. You'll be in the middle of a poison swamp, thundering storm, or volcanic wasteland but then step into ruins with simple green grass. It breaks the immersion.2.	Upgrade progression - Beginning ore is easy to come across to the point where it loses value. The real ore you need, the moonstone, is more elusive as there's one moonstone per island and if that island also has a dungeon, there's two, rarely three. In recent patches, they made it so the moonstone per island refreshes every season, so it helps lessen the trouble. However, you still need three ores to make 1 bar. You'll need over 108, possibly 156 (60+ spirit feeders, at least axe & hammer tool upgrades, extra tent), if you want to have all the quality of life improvements for the mid-to-late-game. The progression from copper to moonstone doesn't scale well. Pre-patch, I've clocked in just over 100 hours, but I've only managed to scrape together ~99 moonstones (26 islands, 24 dungeons that had upwards of 2-3 moonstones each and treasure maps). Bonus: There's a passive skill you can get to add a small chance of getting a moonstone from opening any new treasure chest. If you don't want to deal with searching, you can save-scum it and it takes under 2 min/chest.1.	Skill trees - The game has different skills with their corresponding skill trees that augment your gameplay. For example, there's foraging, archaeology, farming, etc. At first, the customization seems really cool; it introduced quality of life changes that helped you with your day, but you can't get them all. You can only choose certain boons over the other and you're locked out of the other boons permanently. There's NO resetting the upgrades and frankly, it sucks! If you chose perks that helped with early game, they become completely useless late-game and if you chose perks that helped with late-game, you won't get much value from them in early through mid-game. Not to mention, some perks are just so niche that it feels like an absolute waste of space. It felt like they were trying to copy how some other famous games like Stardew Valley split skill progression, but failed to make their perks universally valuable.2.	Controls & UI - Horribly optimized. For a game releasing in modern times, the controls have no quality of life. Ex: when placing fertilizer down, your character has to stop moving, register you putting the fertilizer down, perform the animation, then register that the plot is fertilized before you can move onto the next crop PER PLOT. You can't hold the fertilizer and spread it while running like you can do in nearly every other farming game. For inventory management, you can't move stacks of items with a few simple clicks or inputs, but instead you either click-and-drag or hold down right click to rapidly deposit items one-by-one. Similar concept with seeds. You have to buy seeds one-by-one with no rapid purchases. You could button mash, but why?3.	Farming/NPC's - Very bare-bones. The farming is pointless as the money you make isn't valuable. Nothing in the game is expensive enough to make you save and most of the crops you use are for buffing stats of your spirits. The community of the main island are sadly not very interesting. So much time is spent exploring that it's hard to remember they exist at times outside of when you want money. The only unique events are through dates that you must initiate, otherwise events will not happen which feels robotic. Most interactions are a few lines then you choose chat/joke/flirt to raise relationship points. It feels incredibly shallow despite the diverse cast. Usually sim-games have good community aspects, but I can barely remember their names even after all my hours because you do other things most of the time.4.	Time/Travel speed - the time per day is too fast. By the time you finish checking on crops then feeding your spirits, you've lost more than half your day. Then it takes a while to travel to another island and you have to speedrun w/e you were going to do before returning home. Every day ultimately pressures you into trying to rush and it burns you out once you're in the third season.All in all, this game is fun in the first 20 hours or til Fall, and even then others saw flaws like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of this game (and it's the first one to compel me to write a review, if that means anything), it's relaxing enough for me to be able to chill out while playing it but has enough substance to make sure I'm not completely bored (which can be the case with some... overly cozy games). _childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential. All the basics are here, but it desperately needs to be tinkered with.1. User Interface is poor. I often missed with my tools unless I was positioned perfectly. I could be standing right over moonstones and still have to click 4 or 5 times to pick one up. It was annoying to have to open the tool interface to swap between tools. 2. Tools tools tools. Too many tools, some like the boomerang were used ONCE and then never again. The upgrades are easy to get, but completely unsatisfying to use. I leveled up to moonstone (highest) level quite quickly but other than speeding up my use of the tools it wasn't particularly useful (since stamina is SO easy to acquire and plentiful).3. Money and Crops. Spirit barns and resource collection are effortless, I never needed to grow crops to sell for profit or really struggled to make profit at any point in this game. Since gold was so easy to acquire and there wasn't much it was needed for it makes a significant portion of game mechanics (growing/harvesting/selling) completely meaningless. The ability to create a sizable amount of sprinklers during the first week of play took away a lot of the "grind" that makes some of these games so appealing and satisfying. 4. Spirits. I LOVE the battles, but... there's not much to them. I leveled up one of my spirits 37 levels in one "day" by planting about 150 of a single XP crop that regrew every 4 days. I then just cycled through the rest of the month to get to the temple boss battles so I could finish the game. A boss I beat in 2 turns because my psychic spirit had cards to gain energy and keep pulling cards to make a never ending unbeatable hand. It felt like cheating.5. Speaking of seasons, what's the point of them aside from dragging out the gameplay? There's no story, there's no festivals, there's no special events, there's nothing except a new batch of crops with new stats to collect. With only 11 NPCs you don't really need to talk with anyone, not that there's much for them to say either.All in all, so much potential! So little to do. So many things that need to be tweaked to elevate the experience. I feel like it's incomplete as is. I played it to completion on the main storyline (didn't take the 130 hours it says I did lol, I just tend to keep games minimized in the background when not actively playing). _childDocuments_.review: I've put 15 hours in, and will likely still play the game some more, but I'm not sure I'd recommend it as it is currently. I was really into it after the first 5 hours, but then it just... dies out on you and I found myself a lot more aimless. All the parts of a great game are here, it just needs more time in the oven and some change in direction. This is one of those games that, yeah, it technically playable, but feels like it's lacking polish and more content. The good: - It's cozy and looks great- Lots to explore- The card battling system is interesting and I felt I could customize in ways I wanted.- The spirits are varied and cute- Quick and easy tutorial before you jump right into the game- The NPCs that exist are interesting and I found one I wanted to date. The bad:- The controls need work. Why I have to hold Q to bring up a wheel menu that I then need to scroll through is beyond me. Let me hold Q and see all my items in a list that I can pick. I don't need the wheel unless there is some weird way to quickly select from it, which I don't think there is.- There is not quick key to get to the quest screen- The map needs more detail- To complete each temple you have to bring specific items. You won't know what items you need until you get there and to progress you'll need to leave and come back unless you're lucky enough to just be holding things. I was not. Tell me upfront or don't lock progression behind items. Flying back and forth is not fun. - It feels a little slow. Sprinting wasn't explained to me, but I found out about it online. Why it isn't the default I don't know. Battles are also a little slower than I'd like. Even with fast mode on. - Needing moonstones for everything is a pain. They are plentiful, but everything good requires them and I don't want to spend days hunting for just them. Remove the requirements from stuff and use gold instead, which I have way too much of. - Having to craft charms is more annoying than cute. The high leveled monsters are enough to keep me away, don't add artificial stamina draining that I need to waste an inventory slot to prevent. - The flower/farming system is strange. I'm not sure I like that they're all over the place. It takes away the point of farming and I found I didn't want to sell them because they all had uses. Potions need to be sold somewhere and the plants need to be more farming focused. Anyway, I think I'll come back to this game in a year or so since they're still doing updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying it so far.  Only bug I've encountered is giving a gift and not seeing the text response from the person.Summary:  Reminds me of a mix of Zelda/Harvest Moon/Coramon.  Randomly generated islands with main island.  Random mini caves to explore.  The only thing I *wish* I could do is have my spirits reduced in size so I didn't have this giant house following me around (Edit: You can actually do this in the medallian and ask them not to follow you.)The health/stamina system is novel. Instead of an hp bar, you're solely focused on a stamina bar. This makes for interesting issues. If you're using a lot of stam in a dungeon, you don't have a separate bar to work with as you go around.  Need to stock up a bit more.I would probably give this an 9/10.  It's solid in the sense that each mechanic is enjoyable. I will re-edit later as I go through the story as to whether it has the same replayability as something like pokemon/harvest moon.Edit: I'm loving the deck building. "Talisman" can change the cards by adding/upgrading/removing from a spirit. It's a really cool idea that gives you control over how a deck plays. I can see a lot of possibilities with it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks pretty darn good. It kind of reminds me of the GBA Legend of Zelda titles but with greater detail. The art for the characters is also great. The game took obvious inspiration from Studio Ghibli and it adds a ton to the game for me. I could see it not being you're cup of tea, but it's an easy 5/5 for me.The game's music is gorgeous. It really fits the game and it never gets in the way of the experience. Great soundtrack, particularly the battle themes <3. They should really make it so that the menu theme's volume can be adjusted separately from in-game (it's always at base loudness when you boot, it's never hurt my ears, but it's a little bothersome).The deckbuilding battles are fun to play and even funner to build. You have 3 energy to spend on a given turn, and you spend them on a deck comprised of all 3 of your creatures moves shuffled together. You can add cards to Spirits decks, upgrade them, or delete them with runes. It's not particularly balanced (looking at you Psychic Spirits) and you can do some crazy broken stuff, but it is absolutely fun. Unfortunately all of the creatures of the same element are effectively interchangeable (they learn all the same moves, their stats are the same, and they will always share 1 specific weakness). This means that when you deckbuild, you do so with Spirit types and not necessarily with creatures themselves (with the exception being their abilities). While this is still loads of fun, something like a signature card for each creature could go a long way for making each of them feel more unique in battle. I love that some of them have abilities that effect the social/exploration/farming side of the game. Armbot's "Long Arms" ability allowing me to pick up items in the overworld from a longer range is a great example and such a neat idea. Unfortunately I couldn't keep him in my party without throwing my combat strategy wildly off balance, so I only brought him out occasionally. I would like a reserve system that would allow spirits to follow you for effects while also keeping them out of your combat. There also isn't anything you can do with your creatures outside of having them follow you, feeding/brushing them in the barn, or battling with them, which is fine ig, but anyone looking to interact with their creatures any more because its a farming sim will be disappointed.I like the people on the island, I really do. They have their quirky personalities, their likes and dislikes, you get it. But the town itself doesn't really feel quite alive. Maybe it's because Moonstone Island doesn't really have much of culture. There aren't any events or festivals to partake in, no games to play, or anything else fun to do with them besides dates. It's all very insulated. I was shocked when I realized that the New Years fireworks event was the only one in the game and it's not much of one. The dates are quite good, and a highlight of this part of the game. Strangely, while you can "enter a relationship" with someone by giving them a moonstone ring this doesn't actually change anything about your relationship except allow you date them at their house and to sleep in their bed. While I understand the implications of such an act, particularly after an exciting date, I can't help but feel the game is missing something really obvious here. After exhausting all the dates and being in a relationship with them for a while I was expecting something to change. Unique text boxes to appear or perhaps marriage? While I wasn't excited for this part of the game in particular I am still a bit disappointed by its limits. The game, it's main conflict, and by extension the town, kind of stop existing past the first year (no new newsletters, events, or quests) which is a bit of a shame. The game has an excellent setup to add rich content to the later years over time, and I hope to see such additions in future updates.Exploration is fun, particularly at the start when you don't know what everything is or what to expect. Each island is based on a Spirit's element and will only have the matching creatures, fish, and that element's seasonal plants. The fruits of the fields are plentiful and goofily themed. Hot air balloons, pinwheel flowers, and lightning bolt shaped plants abound. These are all great to find and collect. The very act of flying from one island to another, when I don't know what to expect, is a joy. Finding statues that teleport you to other islands or rune gates to upgrade your Spirits are also fun treats. Lightning islands make it harder to traverse them they taking a bit of your stamina while you're on them, Fire island make it harder to traverse them they taking a bit of your stamina while you're on them, and Dark islands make it harder to traverse them they taking a bit of your stamina while you're on them. Yeah, it's a bit generic in that aspect. There is little else different between two islands of the same element outside of what I've mentioned besides layout. They have put a ton of effort into making each island feel distinct (as the layouts are all 'handmade' as it were), it will still suffer a bit from a lack of variety by the end of the game.Each island has a random chance of harboring a dungeon, which are Legend of Zelda like mini-trials that offer a variety of hidden loot and enemies to challenge you. These puzzles are fun, but repeat similar elements, losing a lot of their appeal after the 10th dungeon or so, despite their lovingly crafted layouts <3. You don't need to complete more than 10-15 or the games 50 dungeons, but I went for the achievements on this one. The game's Seasonal Temples are, in my opinion, the most enjoyable parts of the game and something I always looked forward to. They function similarly to how pokemon's gyms do, with a bit of legend of zelda items mixed in there. The 4 items you receive from doing the 4 temples are all very useful and interesting and the bosses are an absolute blast. I was worried that I would overlevel and overpower all of the bosses, and while I did still do that a bit, because the bosses are all gimick battles, I still feel like I got the interesting and engaging experience the developers intended me to. It doesn't hurt that the boss battle theme is amazing. An incredible, iconic feature of this game for me.The game has farming. It works like it has always worked since the very first harvest moon game back in 1996. Here it is easily automated, so If you don't particularly like this aspect of the game you don't need engage with it. But if you are into this stuff the game gives you the tools to have a blast, make a huge farm, and some huge income. I enjoyed it, even if I didn't go quite as wild with it as some will. The same is true for customization. If you like the idea of making furniture and decorations for your house, this game has got it and you will get some good mileage out of it. You can even customize Moonstone island itself! You can't remove much there, but you can add! It's a bit of a bummer that you cannot customize your character in any way (maybe in a future update? devs? <3).

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game, it is simple but very entertaining, a wide variety of floating islands from different biomes will appear in your world, you will have to craft a tool to be able to fly from island to island, card combat is fun if you are interested in that, at the same time when you level up your creatures you must choose more cards to add to your combat deck (currently there are 80 different creatures), the game has a function similar to a skill tree, which you can acquire with points that will be given to you after doing some time the activities (mining, exploring, capturing creatures or talking to NPCs), the only problem it has is that it lags a little in certain places but it quickly fixes. i recommend it

_childDocuments_.review: i want to like this game and was very excited to try it out but at the moment i can't recommend it. there is a huuge potential in this game though and i'm looking forward to see how it changes in the future.there is stuff to do, technically, but all of it feels a bit pointless (there is a thin bigger plot and quests) or weirdly grindy. i'm at a point where i kind of have stuff to do and islands to explore but i can't go too far because my monsters levels aren't high enough and they level up slowly against monsters of their own level (also because the fighting can get slow because of rng). you don't have any way to level them without battling and i'm not looking forward to finding a new monster to add to my group since i'll have to grind them up to others level. usually in these sorts of game you can have monsters in reserve that get exp when you battle difficult monsters your higher levels can handle but in this game all three are on the field and i'm pretty sure your monster doesn't get exp if they faint mid-battle.the pixel look is lovely but i dislike the character art and not being able to customize your character is a huge miss - you can't even talk, you have no personality, but yet you're stuck on this look. i don't particularly like the npcs either and there are no old people or kids in this town.also, the beginning of this game feels.. awful? it's very rng - you need to destroy rocks and hope you find a cave under. then you have to travel to different islands to find moonstones - but wait! you can only do that when it's dark out. and the clock is ticking. and there is only one moonstone per island. which you won't know until your dad sends you a mail (or you don't realise it before your dad sends you a mail). and on top of that you can only have three monsters and if you want a new one you have to release one of them before you try to catch a new one. and when you finally, finally get the barn you have to craft specific spots for each monster or they don't have a place to stay. then you have to put food for them (awkwardly, since you have to navigate between monsters and the controls are sometimes wonky). and then you realise it's pointless to even keep them because they don't seem to get levels in the barn so you can't use them in combat anyway.overall - i hope one day i can change this review to positive but at the moment i don't see myself playing this game very much.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could do a 50/50 type thing. I do enjoy this game to a point but there are a lot of things that people who either enjoy farming sims or monster taming games missing that make this a not really recommend for me. I got to fall of year 1 and was hoping some of my issues were 'oh it's meant to just take time and relax' but often times I found myself getting to frustrated at points to fully relax. To be clear, I think the game has enough in it that makes it worth the price. I think it could just use some polishing or ungating certain things.And if you get this game, go into it thinking it's a monster taming game first with farming elements. I thought the opposite and that might be why I'm having such an issue with it. I misunderstood what the game was trying to sell to me, and it might just be my fault to misinterpreting the makers themselves or the online reviewers who gave me that impression.First, before I talk about the problems, I do want to say, I do like this game. It's charming. The spirits are cute. The concept is cute. The art and music is great! However, I find myself not fully relaxing or just chilling out while playing, like with other farming sims or monster tamers, because I feel I have to manage so many of the below stuff.I'll try not to ramble too much and break down some points that I think make this a harder sell:1. The battles are fun enough, and the monsters are cute. I enjoy collecting them. But it honestly feels a bit like a chore. Not to mention, picking the earth starter really hurts you. For reference ( and I believe it might be like this on every world if not I was just unlucky ) The first temple boss is earth. The second is water. If you start with the earth you can only get earth or water spirits because the other elements are gated behind higher levels and you need to skill up to be able to tame them. Or get lucky and get an egg drop from their battle. But that's on the opposite path of the 'exp while walking' which became necessary for me because I didn't want to waste too much in game hours grinding up by battling ( which becomes harder to do at a certain point ). I haven't touched half of the spirits I get because I don't want to bother leveling them up, even if I'm at a type disadvantage, which I had to basically disown my starter because other earth spirits had better cards to start than him and I needed other elements. I don't mind grinding in games, that's when I get some shows watched or listen to a book, but it felt like more of a chore in this game and knowing I have bosses to face makes me feel mentally exhausted in a game I just want to relax with. And maybe I'm just bad at the game, that's 100% a possibility, I could not be using all the plants and potions to my advantage but I just wanted to turn my brain off and relax with this game. And I guess on the flip side of exp walking, you could level the 'tame higher level spirits' path and then go tame a really high level one. Maybe I should just focus on doing that instead.2. Which brings me to 2. Some of the skills require you to plan. You want the max amount of stamina you can get? Don't touch any trees until you get the skill that bumps that up. Want a large amount of chest? Enter as few dungeons as you can before getting the bump the treasure chest appearance up. I'm used to some skills being really great and having to acquire skills you don't really want to continue down the skill tree. But some lock other skills and I'm also used to that system as well but...I dunno, the skills in this game seem really strange? Half of them seem to become useless after a certain point or the percentages are so low in comparison to the other skill that it doesn't even seem worth it. And in a game where it seems the main focus is on crafting and decorations ( the crafting giving you potions for battle and exploring ) with everything else just sort of helping with that.3. Resources are...Hard to come by. You can plant stuff all day, and I love the greenhouse for that. But the islands are becoming ugly and barren because you cut down trees and...That's it. You can use that precious wood to make decorative trees but when you need wood to upgrade all the buildings, build all the stalls for spirits, and make ash for potions you can't really afford to use it for decoration. You can plant everything under the sun, except trees. And some moonstones come back to an island every season, why can't a handful of trees come back on every island every season? I don't want more spirits because I don't want to waste wood on crafting the stalls. It should be the most common resource and it feels like the most precious there is since so many things need it. And spirits all have the same drop when they are the same element. No unique furs or scales or things like that. You have an electric one, it drops a spark. I guess on one hand more resource management might be a nightmare but between that and the slowly dwindling trees I just don't care about having more than a couple of any elemental spirit. 4. The NPCs are cute but...There are only a handful. So if you're not a super fan of any of them...That's it. They are the only ones there. They have quests where they request spirits and it's cute seeing them in town with the spirits they request but it's a little annoying you have to remove someone from your team, put the spirit in your team, go talk to the person and hand it over, and then you'll need to remember to go back and get your original spirit from the barn. It's a bit tedious. The reward is...Usually a free item from their shop? It's a unique idea but I'd rather be able to have a tangible reward because honestly I didn't even realize most of them even did that.A lot of these issues might just be my own. I set certain expectations and that's on me. In all honesty, the wood thing is the biggest deal breaker for me and why it's more of a negative. Honestly if that and a few other things are tweaked then it'd be a solid game. I wouldn't mind the battling and grinding up skills and stuff. But stressing out about what to craft on top of trying to grind up spirits for bosses just makes it not a really super cozy game for me. Which is okay, I still enjoy. I can tell a lot of love went into this game. And if they are continuing to work on it, that's great. I may end up changing my tune. Until then, this is just a warning to anyone in the same mindset as me.
