_childDocuments_.review: Suikoden 2 is my favorite piece of media of all time. Period. I never saw any other media that was capable of conveying the challenges of friends going separate ways due life choices. How responsabilities conflicts with your emotions and push you to do things you dont want to for a greater good. I only have 1 tattoo in my body: the Bright Shield Rune merged with The Black Sword Rune - so that tells a lot about my personal connection with this game. With that said... i will trace a few parallels of this 2 games in this analysis.Eiyuden Chronicles is the closest thing we ever got to Suikoden 2. Story is compeling, but I feel that we lack an overwhelming  BBEG like Luca Blight was in S2. Characters are really good. And to an extend, they even have a better characther design than S2. There were a few companions that I never bothered to level up in S2. In this game, almost every singe character I get is worth it.  I still need to finish the game (i am playing in my other account) , but so far I really liked the story. The conflict between a league of nations and an overwhelming empire is the perfect template to a good story. Clearly the author wanted to SUBTLY trace parallels about real life politics, and this is really good. Is done in a non-patronizing/padering way : The way a proper storytelling should be.However we have to address the elephant in the room... localization really dropped the ball. It tarnish the experience a bit, as much as it hurts for me to say it. Clearly there is a conflict between what the author wanted to portray, and what the translator wrote. Some companions might have a really out-of-characther/inconsistent behavior during a dialogue - just for you to find out later that this was the translator going out of his way to insert a joke or his political view (even when the character it self had a completely different behavior). It is super inconsistent too. A kind character could have 99% of his lines being polite, but out of nowhere he drops sudden accusatory remark or a stupid name calling - only for you to find out that this is not the original script.Eiyuden Chronicles did not deserved this. You can see this is a passion project, made by people that genuinely care not about their fans, but also MAKING A GOOD FREAKING GAME AND A MEMORABLE STORY. And to see such a beautiful project being corrupted here and there by the vanity of an INDIVIDUAL is really disheartening. It feels like finally going to Egypt and fulfilling your dream to see the pyramids... and noticing that some moron decided to graffiti a political message  on it. . It certainly dont ruin the experience : it 's still the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pyramids. But surely does tarnish it.Music-wise, i have mixed feelings. S2 had REALLY great tunes,  considering the limitations they had back then. EC is a bit of a hit or miss. Some boss battles have great songs, some areas have boring songs. I also was not quite fond of the "gimmick" option during some battles. It kinda drives away the strategy aspect of a battle, and it feels like it is just another minigame. However, I can see people enjoying this... just not much for me. Thankfully, it is not included in all boss battles, and it leaves a lot of room for the classical turn based experience.Pixelart mixed with 3d backgrounds is simply amazing. It feels like the perfect mix of retro game and modern game. Gameplay wise, I am super happy. Boss Battles looks reaaaaaaly good, probably the best looking battles in classic JRPG. Castle management is back and kicking, with all the updated features I would LOVE to have in S2. Cooking mini-game is back, Duels are back. This is freaking awesome. I feel like going back to the early 2000's, in the best way possible. I loved the racing and the "beyblade" mini-game too. The only thing I didn't quite like were the War mode. I prefered the S2 War mode, which felt more like a Turn-based combat/strategy. This is more like a real-time thing. However I can totally understand that a lot of people might prefer this one better.Eiyuden Chronicles is a dream game for me, and really deserves attention to ANYONE that likes JRPG. I would love if in a near future, they release an updated localization, exactly how the authors intended. If they did, i feel this game could be as good as S2. As it is, EC is a memorable experience, far better than everything I played in the genre in the last 10 years.Give it a chance, politics aside. And lets hope we go back to simpler times were people were less vain.Rest in Peace Yoshitaka Murayama. The most under rated name in the industry.

_childDocuments_.review: Excluding my bias as a backer and fan of the dev teams original games, I came at this game very critically. It had a lot to live up to and I think its more than exceeded that. It has the nostalgic feel of a PS1 era peak game with the beauty of modernized sprite work and backgrounds. The characters are amazingly voice acted so that they all feel rich in your interactions with them, even though for some very brief. I'd go as far as to say the formula of this type of game was even improved as each recruit gives some small boon so you just want to find them all moreso than feel obligated to find them all. If I am to nitpick over anything its the recruitment bug of 1 character which I believe a patch is coming for soon but the community has made sure is solveable for PC gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: I am only 4 hours in and already this is bringing me back to days long past. Days when I would grind away hours playing Suikoden, seeking out every single hero and mini game and figuring out ideal party compositions. But more than that? It feels both nostalgic and refreshing. The spritework, the battle gimmicks, the sheer personalities of the characters. All of it would not have been out of place in a new Suikoden Game, yet Rabbit and Bear bring us something all their own. The biggest draw is the Voice Acting. Something Konami tried to do with the later Suikoden games, the VAs in both languages do a brilliant job.Do you need to have played the Suikoden series to appreciate this game? Not at all! If you enjoy Turn based RPGs, open worlds, and the very real possibility of missing playable characters because you didn't backtrack or explore every last micrometer of the map, then you will enjoy this game! Should you? Honestly, if you have the ability to, yes. But only because there are a lot of nods and love letters to Suikoden found in here. Final Thoughts: EXPLORE EVERYTHING! TALK TO EVERYONE! BACK TRACK! Never think you are done with a village just cause you did a bit of story.  And enjoy the blood, sweat and tears Rabbit and Bear poured into this brilliant world and story.

_childDocuments_.review: This game hits on so many nostalgic feelings for me, and I absolutely love it. I've been looking forward to it for a very long time now, and would absolutely recommend it! There are so many amazing characters, and so many of them are available to join for combat which makes mixing and matching so fun. Town building has been a blast. Cooking battles are far and away my favorite mini game - I LOVE it, even though I literally did omelet > fried egg > coconut water to succeed every single time haha. It's just fun to me. The sprites are so cute in the cooking battles, and the sprite work in general is amazing throughout the game. It's truly been such a refreshing and enjoyable game to play. The music is great too. Some concerns/feedback - some of this may seem critical or nitpicky, but I am writing it out of pure passion for this game. I am hoping very much to see a sequel that takes this series to the next level because it's like we're right on the brink of something truly exceptional.Story: Truthfully, the depth of the story is just not there yet. It's like they were right on the edge, but every time they got close, they stepped back to be cautious.Nowa is very likable, and I absolutely love his design & personality, but the story doesn't really make him special in any way that makes it believable for him to suddenly go on a very important mission on his first day in the Watch, or to suddenly become the leader of the alliance 6 months later.I understand that they may have wanted to veer away from the "True Rune" route because this is not supposed to be a direct duplicate of Suikoden, but I just wanted SOMETHING more - some reason to believe that Nowa was meant to be the leader of this group rather than just because Perry said so and manipulated the situation to make it happen. Even he questions it in the game, and while it's cute that everyone gives him a pep talk...he's kind of right. There is no real reason for him to have been appointed leader.The same goes for Nowa's relationship with Seign. They met once and spent some time together on a single mission. There were some really great moments between them, but the foundation wasn't in place to drive an emotional impact. Even the bridge duel - it was so beautiful, the music was great...but these characters barely spent any time together, so I just didn't believe it or feel the emotional impact even though I really, really WANTED to believe it. I love both characters, but I just don't buy that they're best buddies - sorry. I'd believe they like and respect each other after going on a mission together, but that would be the extent of it, and the game built it up like it's way more.In regards to the villain - he doesn't feel very villainous. Maybe I am biased and thinking back to Luca Blight too much and setting the standard too high. I just want to see what makes him evil rather than simply being told by characters that he is power hungry, or that he did certain things. Is that his only motivation, power? The lab quest was the only time I felt like we were on the brink of understanding the Dux and his intentions more, but that fell short because even there he didn't really DO anything on screen for us to see. The game shied away right before letting us see how evil he really is.I feel like so many scenes that could have been emotionally impactful were pulled back like that - for example, Nowa's town burning down, except everyone lives and you can basically walk right back into town 5 minutes later and everything is rebuilt, your room is exactly how you left it...it just killed any potential feelings that I could have had about the town burning. In the labs, everything just stopped short - we hear about these horrible events with the villagers but we never see them or get to feel the impacts firsthand. Every time a town is taken over, we can basically carry on and go back in right away with no one acting any differently, everyone is perfectly fine and carrying on like nothing ever happened. I was literally recruiting characters in towns that I should not have even been able to enter. It broke all of the immersion. Marissa's hometown was another example - when we're run out, they act like it's been destroyed and it's this big moment, but we save everyone. Nothing is destroyed, and the game had already taught us by that point that every single town will be fully in tact when we go back, so I didn't even think twice during that scene or feel any sort of impact about leaving because nothing was lost, it was just a temporary retreat basically. Melridge...I want to like him, even now. I adore his design, I think his back story is fine, and his personality - all of that is fine. I just feel like he should have been more clever. As far as tacticians go, he just didn't seem very good at his job or very believable in his role. Any time we're turning the tides or making it out somehow, it doesn't seem like it has much to do with his planning. He didn't get his moment to shine, really. In fact, some moments did the exact opposite because we basically just did what we wanted regardless of what his opinion was. In regards to Rune Lenses - I want to know more about these. The game never gave much of a distinction between a lens and a primal lens, or why I should even care about this aspect of the plot even though it is clearly supposed to be major. Maybe if I knew more, I'd care about why it matters for the Dux to have the one we found at the start - but instead we find it and hear very little/nothing else about it? Why should I care? This has been a pretty glaring opportunity with the plot that could have resolved so many other points.  We need more lore on this topic. Other misc feedback:War battles are very bad. They need to update this mode to allow unit customization, and to make each turn faster. Duels - I wish the choices mattered more? You can basically just hit attack every time and win, regardless. Combat is way too slow in general - auto & even fleeing/allowing to flee has such a long delayRunes - I feel like this system was clunky and overly complicated, and also that it didn't matter what you equipped anyway because offensive magic was not that strong compared to just doing attacks or SP attacks.Some of the EN voice acting is horrible to the point where I did not use some of my favorite characters until I switched over to JP because it was just made me cringe.Beigoma...what a hot mess. The button mash mechanic never worked for me, which I assume is a bug, so I had to rely on RNG for the later part of the recruitment questline. I hate that it's 2 out of 3, and yet we have to do the 3rd anyway even when we already won 2. I wish there was some version of chinchirorin in this game.I think fishing could have been a bit more interesting. Rising's was significantly better, but Suikoden 5 also had a fun mode from what I recallMusic - great overall, but in some areas/scenes, it doesn't seem to be playing? I feel like we should always have music going, especially with how good the music is --I think that sums up the bulk of my feedback. Again, I adore this game and want the best for the series. I think feedback is critical in making the series a success, hence the detailed comments here. Suikoden 2 is probably my favorite game of all time story-wise, so I am admittedly biased here. It's impossible NOT to make some comparisons though, and clearly some of that was deliberate with the plot choices. I think that's a good thing - like we're being teased with possibilities. I hope that we get more from this game, and that it becomes a fully fleshed out series that's not afraid to go a bit deeper with its plot/lore/etc. The foundations are perfect, and there's so much to love already. Looking forward to seeing what comes next!

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing.  Do I recommend the game?  ONLY IF - Let me emphasize a bit better for those that can't read properly.You're like... wha?That's all the outrage is.There are people who hate any sort of humor; any sort of innuendo; any sort of "anime" in their games.  They want the characters to be faceless, generic, no-personality hacks.  Which makes those same people get tired of the game in 10 hours and never touch it again.  Because said games aren't memorable. The humor is benign.  It's childish.  It's a throwback to a past era - which is what they promised you.  But in many cases, the outrage is misrepresenting quotes.If you encountered Bigfoot out in the woods, you MIGHT ask, "is that a he or a she?"In the modern era...you'd get canceled for even asking such a question.  But what I just shared?  That's what's triggering the outrage you see.  Misrepresentation of benign localization.  There are no crass remarks, no sexualization, hardly no fanservice, etc.  It's Rated E and it shows.  But it also clearly appeals to the widest (non-triggered) audience.  Most under 18 won't care.  So if you're a parent, it's a fine game for your kid.That said: you care - or SHOULD care - about the game.  And that's why I'm here.   Now that you understand where the faux outrage is coming from...here's my thoughts on the GAME.✅ This is a fallacy from a lot of people who don't like the game.  They expected Suikoden 6 or whatever.  It's INSPIRED by Suikoden.  It's not Suikoden.  Just like Blackjack isn't Poker simply because they both use cards with suites.  It's nowhere close to Suikoden though.  Maybe 4, but that's it and that's a stretch.✅ Yes, you need to hit save points by traveling back to town (from the overworld. Dungeons have quite a few save spheres spread out).  Yes, there is fast travel but it has to be unlocked; until then you're footing it.  Yes, there's a bit of backtracking.  Yes, there are annoying quests.  All hearkening back to the foregone era.  They told you what you were going to get.✅ I share this because if it bothers you, SKIP THE GAME.  Because there's a lot.  In fact, you'll have points where you walk 10 steps to another cutscene.  It's that bad.❌ Yep - just like Suikoden 3.  Absolutely.  You won't remember 99% of the characters here.  You'll barely remember the story.✅ I remember the first time I played Lost Odyssey and was impressed at a unique approach to battle.  That wore off quickly.  This battle setup isn't bad.  But it's repetitive and the "newness" wears off quickly.  Just like Octopath Traveler, in fact.  There's strategy and techniques and gimmicks and all that, but don't go in expecting some Dark Souls experience or even challenge.❌ It's strange.  In dungeons and buildings and whatnot with all sorts of ambient occlusion and shadows, I can get 120fps solid.  The moment I walk outside?  Fritters up and down between 58-ish and 90, then every so often will stabilize at 60.  I suspect what's happening is a lack of VSync (there's no setting for it) and my GPU is doing whatever it wants.  At some point I'll play with it.  There's also some microstuttering that's more annoying than anything.✅ I can't say there's any memorable music, but it's great sounding at least.  It flows nicely with the game experience.❌ More of a nitpick, there are times you'll enter town and hit a cutscene to hire a character, then the game wants you to follow them wherever and end up in a quest.  It sounds logical, but when you think about how many characters are in the game?  It's clearly padding for the sake of it.It also suffers from the "Dragon Quest IX" disease ("go kill three wolves!!!..., ah, but wait.  You must use this tactic that fails 99% of the time, oh and you have go at night.  Good luck!" BS)❌ Yes, I know, you get a larger bag eventually.  But there was no reason to have a constraint in the first place.  Even still, it's made worse by the fact that nothing in chests is worth keeping really; so your ADD about opening every chest results in a 3-second pause while the game tells you that your bag is full. It's annoying.❌ By which I mean, there are areas that look like you can go and you can't; invisible wall syndrome.  The map is compartmentalized and broken up into (annoying) sections instead of contiguous.  To be fair, Suikoden had the same thing going on (especially 2), but they weren't this small.  The graphical detail is also nothing to write home about - this might have been mitigated with 2D-HD (maybe).Overall, I think it's worth the price being asked.  There's enough here for enjoyment - but again:

_childDocuments_.review: To the racists: Yes, there are black characters in Eiyuden. As there were in Suikoden. Suck it up, or don't. There are also lycans, a bag and a whole host of other, weirder things. There are racists in the game too, but they're kinda the bad guys, as they were in Suikoden (Falena for Falenans). You probably won't like it.For the normal people: It's definitely Suikoden's spiritual successor. If you've played those games, you will be on familiar territory. Thus far, all the things I was once amazed to find and explore the first time I picked up a Suikoden, I'm happy to find once again in this.I will say, thus far the one thing I feel I sort of "lack" is a sense of... threat? But I also reckon I have much more left to experience. However, when I played Suikoden 5 (most freshly in my mind), I remember feeling a little bit worried for many characters. A sense of looming, possible danger (reinforced when one of my decisions got a character I quite liked killed). Thus far, I feel nothing like that in Eiyuden.Oh, and Lian is annoying as all hell, but that's just par for the course. I hated Nanami and Lyon as well, so I always expect there'll be a manic pixie glued to the main character for me to hate until I can get her offed or benched permanently.As for negatives... some animations and graphics look a bit odd? I dunno how else to put it. And then some things, like the pop-ups when fishing and some interface stuff feels sluggish and slow and not snappy/responsive. That alongside repetitive and shouty voicelines make some side-activities (like fishing) kinda annoying. And one time the game froze on me, a few minutes after a boss-fight, before I'd been able to get to a save point. The autosave triggers pretty darn rarely, so I ended up having to kill the game and re-do the boss.Anyways, I'm loving the game, as a fan of Suikoden. Make of that what you will.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start off by saying that this game is masterfully and lovingly made. I've been a longtime fan of the Suikoden series and this is the first game since Suikoden 2 to check the boxes like this one does. I tip my hat at the Rabbit Bear Studio and 505 Games for getting this absolute gem out there. As an indie game dev, I'm in awe at all they were able to accomplish in such a relatively short time. You should all be proud of your work, it's truly beautiful.Ok, now for the long winded review. I'm breaking it up into categories since the game systems are so deep, a general overview wouldn't do them justice.Sprite art 10+/10: Can you get better than this? No, I think this may be the ceiling. The sprite characters are hands down the absolute best I've ever seen. I often found myself just staring at them for prolonged periods of time when they would join to just try to take in their sheer beauty. They are skillfully crafted and there's an astounding amount of them. Not only are there highly detailed gorgeous sprites for every recruitable character, but for so many more characters throughout the game, probably hundreds! If that wasn't mind boggling enough, all the recruitable characters are redone as chibi's for the plays! An overwhelming amount of effort and work went into making that happen and it's superb. The facesets that go along with the sprites are equally beautiful. They're so expressive and well drawn. Each character showcases their personality so well just from one snapshot.Maps 10/10: The maps are very well done and beautiful and the camera work done to traverse them is fantastic. The world is expansive and no corners were cut when it came to the locations. My only complaint would be that it’s a little bit difficult to see and/or navigate at times. Music 10/10: The music is beautifully and lovingly done. I was so happy to see the names in the credits of all the people who played the instruments to make that happen. It would have been cheaper and probably quicker to make digital music and it would have been good enough no doubt, but the personal touch of having it played from an actual orchestra is very very very cool. I especially liked the music toward the end of the game. Also the music for the battle against the countess was absolutely epic!Voice Acting (English) 10/10: I thought the voice acting was very well done. What an undertaking, to voice all those lines in Japanese and English and to have every VA also voice every line for every play. It was pretty cool to hear the emotion from the VA's for the three main hero's as they took down Dux.Story 10/10: I expected a wonderful story from Muruyama, RIP :'( , and he delivered it. The way the stage is set and the pace that it unfolds is artful. The story takes the time to introduce and justify why this ragtag bunch of heroes come together under the umbrella of an unassuming young man. By the time the foundation is in place, you're able to remain immersed as the events that lead up to your resistance don't feel forced, but organic. It's not hard to become invested in the fate of the people that rally to the cause and to want to liberate them from the unfair situation they find themselves in. Once the action starts, the pace of the story provides consistent and necessary pressure to impel you to continue. At no time did I feel like there was a lack of direction or purpose. Every stage had meaning and it created a drive that makes you want to keep going. It's been quite a few years since a JRPG has gotten me to continue to play happily for nearly 100 hours.Characters 9.5/10: The characters are beautifully written. Many of them have deep and moving backstories that help invest you in the overarching goal even more. They become the faces behind the analytics of war. They turn the numbers into Mothers, Fathers, Brothers and Sisters. People with aspirations and dreams, people that contribute to the world of Eiyuden in their own wonderful ways. I was a little surprised that the crew you start with seem to have a black hole in place of a backstory. I totally understand not fleshing out every character though. 100 hours is plenty long. That being said Lian was so irritating I found myself wishing she would jump off a bridge or join a circus or something... And finally why with the Poobee stuff? In my opinion, it only detracted. The game would have been better without it.Character Stats 10/10: I'm a sucker for story and don't usually get too wrapped up in character stats or stat building, but this game must have my number because I found myself swapping party members, runes and gear constantly to try out new combinations and I really enjoyed it! The mystery room is a really nice touch. Being able to quickly level up a character you would like to try out is so awesome. You really have to work for it if you want those hard hitting devastating skills, it's not just handed to you. I suppose my only complaint would be not providing interesting skills when you suddenly find yourself with a blue clad party (not going to spoil it). In that part the the boss fights were unfortunately a bit of a slog when all you can do is heal and deal death by a thousand tiny cuts.Base Building 10/10: The base building mechanic is fun and interesting. I love that in order to get your end game gear and weapons you have to build up your own town. You don't even have to spend a ton of time looking for resources since the mission guild could conceivably gather them all for you while you're playing the story line. It plays so well into the story too, you start with ruins essentially, but over time become a beautiful town, with the power and resources to strike back at your enemy.War battles 10/10: I haven't always enjoyed Suikodens world battles, in fact I usually didn't. But these are a different animal. The whole system is intuitive and fun. Watching the tiny little characters battle it out while reading their comments is a lot of fun. It made me sweat a time or two, but man was that final battle SOOO satisfying.Side View Battles 10/10: The beauty in this battle system is a bit of a slow burn, but it's so worth it in the end. It can be a little rough to get by even on normal mode for the first portion of the game. But that makes sense! You're weak and just starting off. That being said, even then it never feels unfair. The progression builds beautifully, until at the end you feel like the most powerful group in the region, which is great since you are! It's a lot of fun and also manages to play into the story. The way the dialog, characters, base building and character progression are weaved into the story is the stuff of pure genius. I'm floored by the level of skill in this game. Skill that can't be properly savored or understood until you look back at the whole experience.  Continued in the comments...

_childDocuments_.review: 33 hours in, lets talk about Eiyuden Chronicle. I almost never leave a review, but, I LOVED Suikoden for so long and this game was incredibly nostalgic, but obviously the game has issues.. I wish to give my input.The good of the game is how well fleshed out the world feels, the design, sound and sprites for the characters are all beautifully done. It is crazy how well it works together, at least in my opinion, because it does feel like something old sprinkled into something new, while still retaining a heavily classic feel. The story is fun, characters are fairy nice and even the characters that feel like nobodies will give input if they are in your party from time to time. The game is challenging on normal without feeling too hard or too easy, not too much feels like grind honestly. I spent almost ZERO time grinding and the only time I did a bit of grinding was when you unlock Hero rush, or whatever it was called and was shocked when my 54 Lvl something characters jumped to 61 in one fight. I will also say SOME of the complaints about the game are a tad trivial such as Backpack space being limited and the battles feeling slow. In a world where we are always trying to move on to the next thing, there is NOTHING wrong with slowing down to simply enjoy a game.Now what about the bad? Some of the bad things have been said multiple times. Like how the localization is bad, even though I don't think it is THAT big a dang issue, some of the game breaking bugs that have been relatively fixed and such.. Yet, the bad stuff I actually had a problem with are both fairly known, but, maybe not that known.Anyone who has played will tell you the War scenarios are ever so bland and feel neglected compared to the battles in the Suikoden games. From a story telling aspect, it isn't too bad, but gameplay it could have been cut out and nothing would have been missed if it was strictly just story.Character Stats are insanely weird and makes some characters with an aesthetic you like kind of useless. Got a frontline character who is essentially a mage warrior, but his physical base stats are stupidly low, so is his defense and even his magic ability of weaker than dang near everyone else. It is crazy to make a character who is suppose to be a frontline fighter, but excels at magic as well, have no strength or defense and has no way to deal normal attacks from backline.. LOTS of characters have this issue and right now,Rune slots are rather useless for anything outside of trying to buff your favorite characters to be somewhat useful and that almost never works. Its also frustrating when you've used the same two characters from the start of the game due to their good strength and defense can never seem to be beat by anyone else. Iugo has been one of my top frontliners since the beginning, it is crazy and he only has four rune slots, thats how oddly balanced the stats and slots are in this game.My last gripe and my saddest one. Hero combos are useless late game. Most have high SP cost to be even semi useful, some require characters that have abysmal stats and just generally never out perform damage the individual characters can do on their own. They are flashy, cute cause it lets some of the characters express their connections with others, but overall a let down.I, however, would still recommend this game. It is fun, it is literally just a new age Suikoden that is still kind of stuck in the past in a semi-bad way, but does scratch that itch for a game that really makes you remember when good turn-based jrpg's WERE good and had so much love and character breathed into it.I truly hope Rabbit and Bear Studios takes a lot of the feedback and delivers and even greater sequel. This game is BOOMING with potential and still needs some work, but it is FAR from bad. Remember, we should enjoy games because we enjoy them, not because they need to be the biggest, baddest, GPU/CPU demanding triple A hogs that some like to praise. Heck, I even enjoyed Forspoken and my only REAL problem was the last few hours of the game, her late growth and bland ending just really ruined the experience.Also never let big time reviewers or names tell you a game is bad. Just judge it for yourself, so even if you don't like my review, that is fine. Maybe give the game a shot and see if you agree, comment, lets talk about it! And if anyone DOES read this, thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Long time Suikoden fan here.  I came out of J-RPG retirement for this game b/c I always felt we, the Suikodenians, never truly got a good follow up after II. The Pros: -The game looks great, the sprites are great.-The voice acting is actually done well.-The combat is quick, just like it was in the first 2 Suikodens even though they devs didn't allow for characters and enemies to execute their actions simultaneously whenever it doesn't conflict with other actions (just a minor complaint in an otherwise fast combat system)The Cons:-The main character is bland and doesn't have a compelling story to make you really invest in his mission-The story its pretty generic and some of the characters are to similar to some from Suikoden II.-The fact that that game shows you maps for whatever dungeon you're in is bad.  The dungeons have less of an exploratory feel b/c you can see all the paths in an area before you even explore it.  -All the choppy breaks for very trivial dialogue also makes everything a slog.  Every time you move the story along or reach something critical, the screen goes black, then loads the exact same location with all the characters present to then start dialogue.  This is needlessly tedious.  Why not have the characters walk out of the main characters avatar like most J-RPG's do of old?In short the game just feels a bit unpolished and I feel that they just got it "good enough" and pushed it out the door.  Its not a bad game, but its not great and I don't recomend it. This was made abundantly clear when at one point in the game, the main protagonist has to fight a duel with another character.  This actually wasn't a bad thing, except during the fight, both characters get knocked off the bridge and continue the fight on the river bank below away from their respective parties.  At this point, I thought that my remaining party would then start a boss battle with the previousely alluded to tank boss while the duel still goes on below.  This would have been surprising and amazing as it would have taken my Suikoden expectations and then flipped them on my head for what would have been an memorable scene/fight.  Instead, the duel just continues on the bank below the bridge and the protagonist loses the fight.  Immediatly, the screen goes black.  Would I then have the remaining members of my party fight a boss and then come to the characters rescue?  Nope, both the protagonist and his foe just magically appear on the bridge above with the main character near death but not dead to only be saved in the nick of time by the remaining troops from the good guys.  Another instance of this is in the begining of the game and you're just given a "hey, just go recruit some people" mission and you just wonder around aimlessly.  This wouldn't be so bad if this exploration paid off but most of the areas are partially closed off so you can go to them but don't really know you need to until you've already explored them a bit.  Just fluff and not as cleanly put together as the older suikoden games.

_childDocuments_.review: Great JRPG, had a blast with it. Very nice soundtrack, visuals, combat and characters. The story is fine. I've always looked at the Suikoden games but never played any, but from all I've watched of them this game feels like a solid spiritual successor.The only gripes I have with the game are some bugs and one system and a bit of a wonky localization (just a translation would've been much nicer, but what's there now is ok). The cooking mini-game has food categories (appetizer, main course and desert) but none of them seem to count towards what they are and the way they're rated just seems random. Another bug that was pretty annoying was that certain cut scenes where dialogue happens automatically, the pacing was entirely messed up. There was one singing sequence that should've taken probably like a minute or so but took around 15 minutes because it didn't progress. There was one after a duel early on in the game and another one that was really bad was at the end of the game in the beginning of the end credits. It took at least 20 minutes in total for it to progress past that sequence before moving into the rest of the credits (which worked fine). Last bug I want to point out is the dialogue UI jumping around Very excessively when a character is surprised or otherwise excited. It stops after a few seconds, but this should honestly not happen at all. It's awful. Lastly, one design choice I really didn't like was the duel system. There are only a few of them in the game, I get what they're going for with it but it's just really not fun. I'd much rather just have a cut scene instead at current.If the bugs get fixed I'd rate the game at a solid 8 out of 10. Story could have a bit more to it for some extra oomph but it's fine, translation could be better and that duel system could either not be there or maybe get an attempt to improving it if/when the game gets a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very pleased with this game. The amount of care and content is quite impressive, and it kept me engaged and entertained the whole way through. It isn't quite the classic that Suikoden was for me, but it definitely scratched the itch and kept me engaged the whole time. :) Recruiting all of the characters was fun, and even , my least favorite mini-game, had a corny enough side plot with it that I enjoyed it, and it also didn't take long. The combat is only okay, as it doesn't feel like anything except basic attack damage and skills scales properly off stats. Magic ended up being basically only for healing, barring a couple of top tier spells that were spammed at the beginning of boss fights.Progression is well balanced, with good catch-up mechanics for characters who are falling behind. Money for upgrading characters is plentiful.My favorite part, and what left the most impact for me, were the cinematic duels. The mechanics weren't exactly clear, but I really enjoyed the experience of them regardless. They are extremely cinematic, well choreographed, and made me excited for every time the break gauge is filled up, so I could see what visual spectacle was coming up next.The story is pretty good as well. Not revolutionary, but a nice political drama story. If I was ranking this against the Suikoden games, I'd rank them as follows:Suikoden IISuikodenSuikoden VEiyudenSuikoden IVSuikoden IIIIt can definitely stand with them, though it definitely hasn't left the mark that my favorites did. As for the localization... It's fine. It's even really good in some places, though it can be pretty funky sometimes. It's definitely not game ruining, though I'm a pretty chill guy. If you're a Japanese purist, it might bother you.There were also a few bugs, but the devs are patching most of them, and also, I remember playing Suikoden II. For all the wonderful memories I have of that, it had a huge number of bugs and exploits, and things that just didn't work as intended. The minor bugs I encountered were nostalgic for me, if anything, but, of course, I would rather there not have been any. For a small studio's first game (even if some of the team is very experienced), I think it worked out really well. They don't have the resources of Konami behind them anymore, after all. The money they raised on Kickstarter isn't actually that much compared to the cost of developing a game.TL;DR Very good game. Lots of love and care. Not a 'forever classic', but definitely worth the time and money. (Full disclosure, I was a Kickstarter backer.)

_childDocuments_.review: The game introduces some great ideas, clearly inspired by Suikoden. However, its execution falls short.The minigames are bland, and the cooking competition recipes often feel pointless due to inconsistent judging scores. The beigoma minigames are tedious, requiring tiresome searches for NPCs to duel, and are not enjoyable. While the racing game has potential, it needs improvements to make it faster and more engaging. The war battles are disappointing, feeling like prolonged cutscenes with poor pacing rather than engaging fights.Party order often gets randomly rearranged after cutscenes, and the difficulty spikes from easy mobs to overly challenging boss fights are jarring. The auto-save feature is unreliable, inventory limitations are frustrating, and the interface for gearing characters is clunky. The warehouse sorting system needs enhancement; adding options to sort by item type and name would make finding items easier. The expansive open areas waste graphic data, highlighting inefficient design choices.Overall, the gameplay mechanics offer a modernized JRPG experience with unique features. However, the story falls short, lacking excitement, thought-provoking political issues, and deep character backstories. Despite being marketed as a high-level successor of modern 2D-3D JRPGs, it does not meet expectations. Additionally, the translation of the English language script in the Eiyuden Chronicle is inconsistent.Despite these issues, the game is enjoyable in many ways. It's a diamond in the rough; if that appeals to you, it’s worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I still think the game is sloppy and could use improvements but a lot of it can be overlooked. I'm enjoying the base advancement mechanics as well as exploring and finding new characters. Combat did not open up as I expected it to so if you're looking for challenging combat, look elsewhere. To my knowledge, none of my issues stated below have been fixed.--------------ORIGINALThe game is just sloppy and rushed compared to similar products of equal or lower value. Examples of sloppy:- XP Gain boost item does not work- Inconsistent language conventions "deal x damage to all enemies" and "applies x damage to all enemy". Just weird. - There is a cutscene early on where a character joins your party and is also in the cutscene. The character appears in two different positions in the cutscene because of this. It can be avoided if you don't have her in your party.Some other things that are missing QOL items:- No battle speed changes- Slow menus (super slow navigating)- No smart menues, it should remember which screen I was on so I don't have to tab back over to the desired screen. Wouldnt be as big of a deal if it wasn't such a slog doing it. - There's an animation when using consumables outside of battle and again, just a slog.- Not enough auto battle options (but I just came from Unicorn Overlord so I might be spoiled)- Can only change runes at towns (no reason for this, it's tedious to make me go back to a town for this IMO)- No saving anywhere, only at save points (again, just wasting time / progress) Some of these systems seem like fluff that is added to give artificial difficulty but it's really just added tedium. _childDocuments_.review: I'll start off with this: as a Suikoden fan since 2003, Eiyuden is like a pipe dream come true. I'll make sure to review the game without any kind of bias. The game definitely has its flaws, everything does. If you're putting off the game due to the recent surge of "woke" translation in this game, especially if you're a Suikoden fan, you're missing a lot.For a game that is trying to appeal to Suikoden fans, this game succeeds rather amazingly, there are moments where it made me think "Wow, this is really nostalgic!" especially with the beautifully crafted dynamic sprite-works.I've read that some people are a bit put-off by the 2.5D style, but I think Rabbit and Bear Studio managed to merge the 3D world with 2D sprites quite seamlessly. The characters blend perfectly with the world for the most part.The game has a lot of beautifully arranged music, but this game suffers from reusing music, making it feel generic, boring, and it sort of breaking the otherwise beautiful map designs. It takes away its uniqueness because of that.The system and transitions...are eyebrows-raising more often than not. If you're trying to switch tabs from "Items" tab to "Equipment", you'll have to deal with some slow transitions and micro loading times that is 100% annoying...or if you want to get to Status tab, you have to cycle through many other tabs before you can get to it. Don't get me started on attack button during battle. The X button needs to be more responsive...Despite what people say about the English localization, other than a few cringe and eye-rolling dialogues here and there, I think they are doing a decent job at conveying the message of the game, save for some parts where they omitted or changed the personality of the characters.Having an exact translation could be quite awkward, and honestly the westernization of the game scripts reads nicely for me. Sure, there are some out-of-place, modern lingo being put in the game, but it's not game breaking at all. Some of them managed to get a chuckle out of me.Also, the part where a character replied to our main character saying, "We beat him" with "Are you sure it's a him?" doesn't feel woke at all. To me, it's more like "It's a giant rock, I don't think it's a him or her." It's only a quip, or a badly written joke at most, and that's not even the bad part of this whole localization issue, yet people made that the reason they wouldn't even touch the game.The actual issue is actually how inconsistent the translation team translates some of the action tooltip for the game, people need to focus on that instead--even so, that kind of inconsistencies reminds me of Suikoden's translation. Like I said previously, "Wow, this is really nostalgic!"---Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes is 100% a love letter to Suikoden fans, but this isn't saying is a good or bad thing as a love letter can be either well or badly written.There are many things to fix and take note of if they want the game to flourish, but considering this is Rabbit & Bear Studio's first time ever producing/developing a game, most of these bad reviews listed for the game are understandable. Ultimately, despite the bugs, inconsistencies, and many other problems, I give Eiyuden a "Recommend." Don't skip on this game.★★★★★★★★☆☆ 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a true return to form for the (definitely not) Suikoden series. Been having a blast playing--story is engaging, characters are delightful, combat flows like butter. And the music and spritework is just absolutely gorgeous. It could definitely use a few QoL improvements here or there for menus and mechanics, but nothing that really ruins the experience imo.I will say though that there are some creative decisions that come from a more 90s game design philosophy that might take some adjusting to in comparison to other modern RPGs (save point system, limited inventory size, etc.). And there's a few minigames that can be a little tedious to deal with (Beigoma and Shi'arcraft Racing), but that might be more up to individual taste.I would take any negative reviews online with a grain of salt though, not because there aren't things to critique but a lot of the negative views are in bad faith. Either pushing their "Anti-Woke" agenda (I'm so sorry a **Japanese** game has characters of color in it) or because they have a seriously misunderstanding of what makes a good translation (1:1 translations are always terrible, a good translation needs to keep the *meaning* and *intent* intact not the literal words. If you translate "Red Herring" into Spanish literally as "Arenque Rojo" the audience isn't going to know what you mean because its an *ENGLISH* idiom. Idiom, puns, honorifics, etc. there's so much that does not translate well and will have to be conveyed by altering the dialogue--sometimes drastically. That's just how language works, I'm sorry)

_childDocuments_.review: I've been thoroughly enjoying it so far.  I'm something like 180 hours in (completionist, just can't help myself) and all in all, it scratches that retro-styled JRPG itch very nicely.  It feels like a pretty decent successor to the PS1-era Suikoden games as well.The localization does suffer mildly here and there. There's the occasional joke that doesn't land well, and a bit of less-than-stellar voice acting, but I can easily forgive those things given the budget dedicated to a game with so many individual characters that need unique voice acting. I wanted to come back and touch on this review again now that I've finished the game.  With over 100 hours on it, given I'm working on getting the 'all achievements' achievement, I feel I have a far better feel for the game now than when I originally reviewed.The game's script picks up a fair bit around the start of the second act, and a lot of my favorite moments are from that point onwards.  The story itself seems to lose a bit of steam right at the end, it almost feels like they realized how long the game was and figured they needed to wrap it up, but they hadn't sorted out a particularly graceful way of doing so.The minigames are also, by and far, the weakest part of the game.  Even the best of the bunch, the card game, makes you play way, WAY too much of it for the trophy given how shallow it is.  Even if you manage to make every round of it take only three minutes, it's going to amount to 6 full hours of a game that has very, very little real strategy and no need to change strategy between rounds, since what your opponent does has little to no bearing on what you do.It's pretty clear the game suffered from some pretty serious bloat thanks to obligations from the Kickstarter they decided to put as stretch goals.  I was telling somebody that, were I to rate the game on a 1-10 scale, I'd probably put it at 7/10.  But if they actually stripped out all the minigames and the poorly implemented war mode, I'd actually kick it up to an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is superb. Don't take anything negative in this review as me ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the game, I criticize it because I care and wish the game the best. The pace isn't to bad, first playthrough will take reasonably long, the game usually have you gather allies, advance the plot, gather more allies, and so on, but the game is actually just 3-4 hours long if you skip all cutscene and ally gathering section(try doing NG+ with allies carried over, the story is actually really short). I don't feel mad about it, I enjoyed the story for what it is, and the ally gathering section lets me do whatever I want, it's almost an open world free roam.Early on, the game is **very** heavy on interruptions. You will walk 3 steps, trigger a cutscene, fight, only to walk another 3 steps, trigger another cutscene, then fight again. This will happen SO. DAMN. MUCH. that it gets annoying pretty fast. I'm glad most people don't turn away just because of this, because later on it gets much better and I actually get to enjoy the story/gameplay mix.I've seen reviews about how the translation is not faithful, but as far as I can see, the story does not derail from the original plot. Yes, some character personalities changed a bit, but that'll always be a localization thing--If you speak two very different languages, you'll know. Some tropes simply do not exist in other languages, and some sentences simply do not translate at all Lian, for example, upon meeting Nowa, immediately forces him to call her senpai while addressing him with -kun while joining the watch before him by like, 2 days, not really learning a single damn thing during that period, actually is younger than him, AND met him 5 minutes ago, there's no equivalent for this behavior in English(you don't have suffixes, and you don't usually call someone "senior"), they had to sub that with something, and so we got "kiddo". May or may not be the best choice, but I understand the logic behind the translation. I'm not bothered at all by those minor things, I focus on the plot, and the plot stays true to the source material afaik. The story keeps me engaged, a lot of the characters are not two dimensional, with a lot of unsolved hooks for future expansions or games. The music is so damn good. The combat system is deep enough to satisfy a veteran, although I wished more information is shown to us(particularly, how enchantments work and elemental compatibility of each character). And the minigames...the minigames...sucked. Probably unintentionally, but the cooking and beigoma minigame is just bad as it is right nowBeigoma because bad balancing--the drop rates of beigomas are too low without boosters. When you get your first beigoma, that's going to be your only beigoma for a really long time. By the time you have decent beigomas, you'll aready be pretty far into the story, and would have to backtrack to early area to continue the beigoma quest.Cooking because of a major bug. Just feed everyone eggs.

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this game for JRPG fans, but it is a very mixed recommendation.In regard to the story, it's not emotionally gripping. There's fun moments of drama or comedy that I can reflect on fondly, but overall the story disappointed me. There's a huge mystery about the Primal Lenses that never has a revelation to inspire awe. One is fed with blood and used like a battery of magic power, but never do we learn its nature, origin, or any shocking reveal. The pacing of events always feel too slow or too fast. For example, it was hours of searching, fighting, and politics to recruit one city. Then the next city is happy to join after just winning one race. The story is the weakest part of this game.Regarding gameplay, I enjoyed the runebarrow dungeons and playing with my favorite character choices.  The dungeons have wonderful underground designs with puzzles and mazes.  The colorful cast of characters was fun to meet. I enjoyed every minigame of Eggfoot races, Theater plays, Card games, and Beigoma duels. One great feature I love for combat is Hero Mode in which the player makes a team to fight scaled up waves of enemies, and after every floor of enemies the player is forced to replace at least one character in the party for added challenge. The only negative note I have about the combat is that about maybe 1/3rd of characters are so weak that they were not fun to use in battle. The music is great. I loved every track and how it was used.Regarding the controversy about the English translation, I have tested some parts by playing and replaying in both Japanese and English. There do exist moments where the English text does not match because a joke or insult was added or adapted. It's a matter of personal taste whether these are positive or negative, so I will say that my personal satisfaction with the English translation is about 80%. The added joke of a golem's gender wasn't funny to me. The added joke of embarrassing Nowa in his home town was funny to me. It's a mixed bag in that way.For fans of Suikoden if you want the feeling of a new Suikoden game it's here. but it's not everything promised or dreamed.

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT A GAME!! Wow! Hundred Heroes is an echo of a era long gone. A simplistic JRPG without all the "Fluff" of modern JRPGs... Being in the spirit of the early 2000's JRPG Series "Suikoden". It plays very much like that series but in 2.5D. Reminded me of 1 and 2 over the latter 3...Positives:- No "JRPG" Harem/relationship Fluff- No need for endless grinding or oversized Dungeons with repeating tiles- Diverse cast of 120 characters, most of which are combat usable- A steady difficulty curve that can be over taken with the midgame "Endless" Dungeon mechanic- Basically Suikoden 6 in nature, stays very close to the Formula of games- Various mini-games that can reward some useful items for combat- Amazing graphics in 2.5D- Very rewarding Character bonus for getting 119 Characters. (can be a bit OP if you max level them)- Ending Credits ties all the loose ends up and feels good to see the characters "Life After"Negitives:- Many characters are useless in battle (Like the spiritual titles had it)- Intresting characters get out classed by the "Lens" System not giving them many options to boost- There is a section in the story that the Text does show it is just "Coding language"- Mini- game Companions questline is so difficult by the time you get them they are way underleveled- No modern takes or positive shifts- Base building late game upgrades need WAY TOO MUCH "Tree Chips"...- Classic formula not really telling you were to get specific items for quests or characters...(can get a charcter way earlier. If you dont sell an item you get one time in a dungeon. Would have saved about an hour of grinding.- No Dueling mini game- Cut out many features of its inspirational material.(Army setup and unit set up)- Shark boats have BAD controls, they slide way too much and randomly jerk to one side- a lot of characters come way too late in the story to be useful, if not for the ENDLESS DungeonIn conclusion, Hundred Heroes is not Suikoden we remember, and is an extreme good entry into the JRPG genre. For its price tag it is well worth it, at the time of this review. As for the DLC, cannot speak to that as it was not released it. But the base game I got 50+ hours out of it and there is plenty of time left in it to get the remaining achievement.4.5/5 Is my Rating.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like 90's era turn-based RPGs and especially the Suikoden series, play this.6 character parties, over 100 characters to recruit (thus the name of the game), and plenty of optional side content. That said, this is a love letter to RPGs of that era. You find some quality of life features from more modern RPGs missing here. You can only change your party setup and some character setups at  certain locations, and substitutions can only be made there.Most cut scenes have voice acting in both Japanese and English, and many other text languages are available.There is experience scaling to allow characters you have not used much to catch up quickly, so no need to worry about characters falling too far behind. Within a few battles they'll be up to speed.In conclusion, if you're an RPG fan, I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up with the old Suikoden games, I was really looking forward to this game. And from what I did play of this game, it truly felt like a successor to the old games. With the familiar battle system, rune system, recruiting new members etc. A lot of the old ingredients that made the Suikoden stand out from the many JRPG games are there, and i have enjoyed the game so far on that level. But my problem with the game as it is right now, is the English translation. I personally prefer Japanese voice and English subtitles over an English Dub in games, and normally that have been working just fine for me. But in this game the translations deviates too much from the original Japanese lines, to the point where it is too obvious to ignore. The vibes a character gives and what is written in their text-box is often a clear miss match. I understand that localization is more then just 1 to 1 translation, and they have to adapt. But here it is too far off from the original to be called a good, or even a decent localization. It's a shame they gave the job to translators that don't respect the original work, and I truly believe there is a good game in there. But it's hard to enjoy a story rich game, when the story is tainted by a bad translation.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a Backer for Eiyuden Chronicle and I've been patiently waiting for this game ever since the news came out. This was everything i could want from the Spiritual Successor of what i think is the best JRPG i've ever played in my life. All of the jank from old RPGs, the mini games, the frustrating character recruitment, and its story, all of them was a wonderful callback to Suikoden and was a deep love letter to the franchise. It could be my rose colored glasses telling me that Suikoden 2, with all its old 90s quirks at full display, was better. But despite that inherent bias, i am happy to say i loved this game, I highly recommend this game, and allow yourself to enjoy Murayama-sensei's final gift to the Suikoden community, who waited with bated breath for this masterpiece. There is an inside joke in the community that Suikoden 1 was the stepping stone to create Murayama-sensei's ultimate masterpiece, Suikoden 2, the objectively better game. Despite his death, I hope that Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes 1, will be a wonderful stepping stone for the Rabbit and Bear team to make an Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes 2, and 3, and 4, and 5, until forever. Rest in Peace Murayama-sensei. your game was wonderful and perfect to me.

_childDocuments_.review: As a backer, I got early access to this game and therefore won't be mentioning bugs as I'll give them time to work on them and also, none of them are gamebreaking. Just a bit frustrating. Starting with the negatives, so with that said, let me start with the elephant in the room - the localisation. It's not great. But it's not some "woke" dumpster fire, it's nothing that deep, it just feels like a poor and dated attempt at humour that, frankly, doesn't land very well. Sometimes it takes away from the story, as an otherwise strong or dark moment is interrupted with a joke that doesn't exist in the original script, or in some cases the vibes of a character are different. But it's not some catastrophically, objectively game ruining woke nonsense as some reviews elsewhere make it out to be. It's just... not great, and the story would definitely have benefited from a different approach there. As well as the localisation, there's definitely some more objective problems with the game functionally - some of the menu's are a bit laggy, and some of the systems aren't very well explained and I feel I only understand them since I have a long history with JRPGs, and the Suikoden series in general. I can see how they would be frustrating to a complete newcomer, similar to some of the older mechanics implemented. Although a welcome addition in my opinion they run the risk of definitely feeling a bit dated or frustrating to newer players, or even to other longer time ones. And finally, the war battles feel NEEDLESSLY long. I understand they are different games but they feel much longer yet somehow less exciting than those of the Suikoden series. But honestly, these are all things I've been able to look past (although the localisation has been a struggle to ignore at some parts, gotta be honest) because the overall product has been so thoroughly and genuinely enjoyable. I am a hardcore fan of Suikoden 2 and the Suikoden series in general, but rather than making me biased towards the game, it gave me higher standards for what I expected from the team, and they definitely delivered.The game is beautiful, the music has been gorgeous, I thoroughly enjoy most of the characters, and I find the minigames and side activities to be really fun. I'm 43 hours in at the time of writing this and feel as though I've only just scratched the surface of the story with all the time I've spent doing side content because it really does just feel fun.From what I've seen so far of the story though, despite a slower start and when it's not being interrupted by questionable localisation/translation choices, it's a very solid story that I've enjoyed going through so far.The base building systems are really enjoyable, the areas and dungeons have been fun and at some points definitely challenging, and overall there has been a significant step up in difficulty from the Suikoden series which is entirely welcomed. In general, this experience has been a pretty significantly positive one. It's delivered nostalgia in a modern package, in a way that doesn't feel stale, dated, or overdone. It really has delivered almost exactly what I expected from the team behind it, and has been by far and away enjoyable enough to look past any of the negatives and continue to thoroughly enjoy the time spent.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was great for me, overall i like it.1. Story 10/10 : Its give Suikoden 2 vibe, its a bit less dark than the Suikoden 2, but not too different.2. Character 10/10 : Most of the character was good, all of them have their own loveable quirk. Based for my own opinion, Nowa, Seign, and Lian felt like Riou, Jowy, and Nanami relationship. 3. Translation 5/10 : Its because lots of adding some new word/sentence or translated it into a completely different word. But its not as bad as what people keep complaining about, and while i personally didn't approve it, hence why i only gave 5/10, but i could understand why the translator did it. Most of time i only hear what they say instead of reading the translation, so its not a big deal for me.The biggest example was how Lian teased Nowa a lot in translation, which people falsely claimed that its not happen in JP voice. In fact, it does happen in JP voice too, it just in JP voice, she teased Nowa with her voice tone. Most of time she talk to Nowa, she use a voice tone to talk against someone below her/far younger that her, but its in friendly fun way, not as an insult. As it was a voice tone, a mere translation text won't be able convey it, so the translator add some new teasing. People should know that this is not only text to text translation, it got Seiyuu voice too. Check their voice tone too instead of directly translating it. The translation didn't change the character personality nor the story.4. Gameplay 10/10: The same old turn base RPG like Suikoden, Combo attack, Rune Magic, etc. The additional battle gameplay with gimmick was interesting too. It seems no  after playing till the end, looks like at least  was missable, making it easier for me to play with my own pace. But even if its got missable character like Suikoden, i wouldn't mind too much. You guys gave a NG+ in here after all. Its not like i need to start from 0 again if i missed something. Also the townbuilding. Unlike Suikoden which the castle automatically get bigger after you recruited more character, this one need to getting materials and upgrade it manually, it make me feel more involved in the town building.5. Mini-games 10/10 : -Fishing minigame make me feel like i playing fishing in Rune Factory game, the setup are similar. -For the Beigoma, , kind of wish there is an option to upgrade / increase Beigoma level. -The Card game, It was more fun than what i thought when i see it in the trailer. Not hard to do either once you get use to the game.- Eggfoot racing : Raising and breeding those Eggfoot for the race was fun, kind of wish the Eggfoot parent won't disappear when we breed them, but i guess that would make the minigame became too easy. Also, i think it would be more nice if there is additional dialogue for a specific character combination.- Cooking : Same like the old Suikoden 2 Cooking mini game, it was fun to play and see the judges reaction for some of the food, but its very hard to get good score for all of the judges.6. Graphic 10/10 : The character design, map, town, etc game Suikoden vibe. It is a nice good looking graphics.There is only 1 thing i don't like. That we cannot give the castle name manually. _childDocuments_.review: I have loved all of the Suikoden games, and there is a lot here to love. I will probably drag myself through the rest of it because I love recruiting allies and base building. The game is pretty, the voice acting is (usually) great, bosses present more challenging combat experiences, and I like many of the characters. I don't think this game is worth full price though, and here is why:  - Text speed adjustment option: there is none, and text speed is incredibly slow.- Button press to complete text: right now when I press Enter while watching a long, slow text bubble fill up, the whole bubble closes and I have to start over.- Saving on the world map: even for those opposed to newer RPG innovations, this is arguably an extremely old one that seems to be missing. At any rate, I haven't found a way to do it.- Saving anywhere: yes, many of you like the old school feel of having a consequence to dying be that you need to replay the last three hours of a game... I'm in my 30's... going into my late 30's... and don't have as long to live. lol It isn't interesting to me to replay a bunch of stuff and the only consequence is my real world time and frustration.- Sprinting: there is only one speed to move in this game, and it is slow. There are dash shoes that let you move faster and have become a mandatory item in my party... but they take up a precious accessory slot. Dash shoes speed should be thee 'normal' speed. - Battle speed: Suikoden games always have a grind. Some people love it, some people appreciate it more at 1000x speed in an emulator. Just give us the option.- UI design: In battle having the menu on the left and the character info on the right is a poor visual design. I keep going into the Rune Lens menu because I never have any idea how many SP I have... I keep forgetting to look to the right to assess who has what prior to playing their turn. The relevant information player's need is split from where their focus is.They could at least put the character's MP/SP on the left with the command options. A similar thing occurs in rune shops, where there is a large attractive looking set of rune slots on the right but actually you navigate using a very dull, small menu on the left. So you want to follow the selection on the right, only to see that this moves the cursor to a seemingly random rune slot. Just pick one or the other! - Battle select order: since character action order can change, why can't we input commands for any characters in the order we want instead of one by one? Realizing you want to change previous actions because you realized someone else down the order can do something is a pain. It only serves to waste time. Let us select which character we want to issue commands to in whichever order we want.- Cut scene pause: so far I haven't found a way to do this. People sometimes get phone calls, need to use the restroom, or want to get a drink/snack. We should be able to pause a scene. This is also a pretty old innovation so I don't know why it wouldn't be included here.- Random encounter rates: though there are items for it they take up a precious accessory slot when in use and precious inventory slots when not in use. - Conversation auto-continuation: This should only apply in voiced scenes, and the gap should be shorter... like how a conversation would be. Instead it also applies in town when we are reading, rather than having lines read to us.- Chest contents: you have to discard something to open a chest if your inventory is full. You should be able to check what is in the chest before throwing something away... old games also had this and it makes sense. You open a box, see what is inside, then decide if you want to make room for it.-Quit to title: it is 2024 and we have to go to the title to go to another menu to quit a game.- Lazy animations: some characters have running animations, but I don't think most of them do. I think that because of the weird, sped up walking animations used in several cut scenes. There is also a time when a place is burned down. In suikoden 3, you see the ruined village in the distance and can't go to it... a shortcut but it looks burned. In this game you can go to it right away and it looks fine and a character says not to go in... even after they re-built the only consequence is that the outside of homes looks a little crispy. Again in suikoden 3 the population relocated while repairs were underway and became refugees...- Writing: I won't say that the translation is bad but the writing leaves a lot to be desired. At first I thought they were trying to conserve on curse words for ratings or to appeal to younger audiences, but some of the line are just written badly or poorly characterize the person speaking them.- Combat: it seems layered and complex, but is actually extremely dull. There are really very few battles where your choices are relevant if you are appropriately leveled. Mostly you'll be on auto-battle. Magic isn't good until late game (I'm not there yet) but suffers from having limited resources. Every other ability recharges as you fight... you only ever lose MP- Mini-games: Beigoma is garbage and it locks three (?) characters behind it. The card game is better in my opinion. Haven't gotten to the others yet, but I hear they are also terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: For a huge fan of Suikoden like myself, immersing in Eiyuden Chronicles : Hundred Heroes was akin to meeting an old buddy I hadn’t seen in ages. Suikoden itself is already more than just a game to me; it is part of the foundation of my journey as a gamer, having Suikoden 2 as my first JRPG. Understandably, I was beyond excited when Rabbit & Bear Studios announced this spiritual successor.However, my anticipation was met by the onset of tragedy. Earlier this year, the passing of Yoshitaka Murayama was a bittersweet moment for the gaming community at large, especially for those who esteemed his body of work on Suikoden. Despite the sorrow, the hype surrounding Eiyuden Chronicles did not diminish.So, what about the game itself? If you stayed waiting for confirmation of how much Eiyuden Chronicles is like Suikoden, consider this a perfectly looking mirror with another name. The classic turn-based combat known from the ancient traditions of JRPGs, today, experimenting with old mechanics and bringing new power, embodies them in familiar forms. Nostalgia awaits around every corner – all points work to reflect Suikoden’s charm.The big ensemble cast – the game has more than 100 characters with backgrounds of unusual heights. The comics feel more detailed and fulfilling, plunging into storms of unwritten backstories. Wilderness promotes excitement and exploration, down to the last anomaly, while the story in progress already includes a return in depth from past experiences.Nevertheless, not everything is so rosy in the midst of nostalgia and fun. Some slips in localization break the immersion from time to time, and, though such trifles are not critical, they are hardly invisible to experienced players JRPG fans accustomed to quality handling of localizations.Such lags do not shake the overall picture: so my rating – 8/10 – may be considered quite accurate personally. The previous development of the project is beyond reach, but it was a delicate attempt to create another homage to the idol. On the other hand, my experience was shadowed by the disappointment of some gatekeepers in the community including the shipping issues experienced by the Kickstarter backers.Overall, I’m having a great time with Eiyuden Chronicles. It’s both a throwback and a perfect fresh start in terms of adaptation, an event that thrilled fans of the genre. Here’s wishing for even more amazing trips to this wonderful world.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Steam Curator I must say: Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes will make you smile from beginning to end if you're a passionate Suikoden fan that understands that the two supports one another, rather than fight each other for the spot. Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes is a miracle of a game that many wouldn't even hope to have in 2024. Its roots are very traditional and therefore are scattered in the overall project, for the better or worse. It is undeniabale that the Suikoden series serve as a major inspiration for this game, but while the two are very similar to one another, they are also very distinct. While the duo of main protagonists look a lot like the duo of Suikoden 2 and have similar ideals, their dynamic is completely different from the very start and are completely thrown off when a third protagonist gets thrown in the mix, and that's where the game designs its base lines, putting the whole project on a different take of the Suikoden series while still tapping in when needed.Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes features a fantastic turn-based 6 party members combat system with over 100+ characters to recruit and use in all the various sub systems that the game have to offer. The player will find themselves doing all bunch of different stuff with all different characters, ranging from serious tone like tactical war to really silly stuff like playing some kind of beyblade game. While the game is all but perfect and could use more attention to detail, the ground is really stable and it makes me enthusiast for the future. Lots of bugfix and quality of life additions are needed, and some balance changes like making Hard Mode harder and Normal Mode easier, but other than that, Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes has so much to offer that the player will feel immediately thrown in the world when playing. About translation issues, it's not that big of a deal than most people make it, and most importantly is that R&B is aware because ultimately it's their choice. If R&B feels like the translation is fine, then that's their choice, and it means that everything translated is very well conveyed for worldwide to experience the story of Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes. 100+ recruitable heroes to feel represented by, 6 party members battles, Headquarter system with various sub systems attached to it, lots of mini games, tactical wars, duels...  Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes offers so much that you can find in many other games but NEVER together in one. If I only stop to think that incoming patches will make the whole experience even better...I'm already waiting for a Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes 2, basically!

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up a copy on Steam so I can have it for Steam Deck eventually and to support the company, but I've got around 50+ hours on the PS4 copy that I received as a backer. Writing a quick review here for those curious about whether or not this game is for them. - If you are a long-time Suikoden fan, then this game definitely scratches that itch and feels like the Suikoden VI that we never got. - If you like turn-based JRPGs generally, then you will enjoy this. There's a lot of personality and charm to the game and its core systems and minigames. - If you like games with base building, then you're in for a treat.Suikoden and its creator, Yoshitaka Murayama, are two of the big reasons why I work in game development today. I always hoped to work with, or at least, meet Mr. Murayama, and I was deeply saddened that he recently passed away far too young. Rabbit & Bear Studio have indicated that they'd like to keep the world of Eiyuden Chronicle, his last gaming gift to us, going, and I hope they can. With that in mind, if you fall into any of the categories I listed above, then this game is well-worth supporting now. You'll have a good time with it, and it'll help us get us sequels that keep Muryama's spirit alive. If you are looking to buy the game, it's worth noting that there's a Metroidvania prequel called Eiyuden Chronicle Rising that is worth picking up as well. The game's a fun appetizer, introduces you to the setting and a number of characters you'll see in Hundred Heroes, and there's a save import feature that unlocks unique Rising items in Hundred Heroes for you. Have fun, all, and best of luck to the team at Rabbit & Bear!
