(optional) with boss rush mode., this game have a lot of mini games., Classic Suiko gameplay with some new additions. I like the rune customization although it took me awhile to understand. is quite informational, including displaying what a rune can do, which character got unite attacks together., game filled with several light scenes that can make me laugh., grinding is easy, and I am able to equip characters and setup their gears easily, including raising weapon levels. that includes a full drop list in library really helps (please do items collection and descriptions too in the next game) now have unlockables. is just awesome with the all the VAs and stuffs. Watching various cast play different roles is just great. is light and probably more geared torward younger audiences, story is not heavy like suiko 3... Suiko 2 and 1 is best in terms of story, Storywise, this game story telling is in between Suiko 3 and 5. I would give it a 7 for story. need to be improved. XD (the only exception where I quite enjoyed the VAs is in the theater mode)Please Devs improve this in the next game, Suiko 1 and 2 is a good example... (I like experiencing their story through in game event than being told in a simple text from investigation etc). Flik's Story in Suiko Series is a good example of character backstory. _childDocuments_.review: As a hardcore Suikoden fan, this is an easy thumbs up. It's absolutely nowhere near the high point of the old series, but it's perfectly serviceable and hits the right spots for nostalgia to kick in. But there's been very few points where I'd recommend it to anyone else.  It's lows are REALLY bad and it's highs are just pretty good.The plot is generic Suikoden. Evil empire, encouraged to start a resistance army, face off against your friend on the battlefield... y'know... the usual. I actually enjoyed most of the characters and the plot.The dungeon design ranges from mediocre to absolutely dreadful. Mostly, it's a linear path with branches for chests. Mostly, it's more forgettable than bad but the low spots were hard-to-see hidden paths, long stretches of boring nothings, and doors locking behind you preventing you from resupplying...Because this game LOVES to lock the metaphorical door behind you.. and I repeatedly found myself unable to switch party, buy supplies, free-roam, etc until I beat the rock wall that is the next boss/several bosses. After a few soft-lock risks, I found myself afraid to move forward until I was over-leveled and overstocked. This severely hurt the experience.The combat system is deeper than it looks at first glance, and more importantly deeper than the useless tutorials teach you. It has a massive focus on initiative timing, multiple MECHANICALLY different damage types, unique defenses/dodges per characters, load of options, etc. There is alot here to love here... BUT...Balance is non-existent.  Some characters are amazing, some are useless, most hero combos are inferior to basic attacks, and I've found magic to be entirely worthless. One of the first bosses in the game took me 45 minutes due to an insane life pool, yet nothing has come close to that since. It's been a roller coaster of difficulty spikes. It NEEDS some balance patches.This leads to the best/worst part of the game... bosses. Nearly every boss has a gimmick.  Sometimes it's a literally battle "gimmick" such as having a random chance to hit the boss with a powerful attack or avoiding powerful attacks by hiding. Sometimes it's a non-labeled "gimmick" such as the boss countering certain attacks or having an ultra-attack every X activation. Learn the gimmick and you'll win the fight. The problem is that too many gimmick fights make me feel like I'm exploiting the mechanics more than playing the game. Guess what... having the characters in the front blocking to avoid triggering the combo just isn't fun... neither is a party-wipe sleep spell before you can buy defenses for it.This is made worse by many specific battle mechanics that end up feeling more tedious than challenging. Whether its enemies with "Intelligent targeting" that will all target one single hero repeatedly or being unable to revive since enemies will 100% of the time target a revived hero before they can heal... I found myself abusing the systems rather than playing the game. (For example, stocking up on revives to guarantee a wasted enemy action each turn)Recruiting is fairer than the past games and easier to find heroes. On the other hand it's now a series of fetch quests which has lead to me spending hours grinding for rare drops for each of the different characters. I can understand if it's one or two characters.... but I've had to catch the rare fish, find multiple rare artifacts, find the rare lumbers/irons/bones, etc.  It's reaching a point where things are just tedious. (I've probably spent 4 hours of my game so far trying to recruit 3 specific heroes due to trash my RNG) All of my complaints are made worse by bugs in the recruiting, random battle rates, balance jank and potentially other hidden stuff. I've had a few crashes, I've had a few areas where things seemed to get locked, etc. I do feel that this review is far too negative compared to my actual feelings... but these are the emotions that are standing out. I do like this game alot and that's why I'm giving it a thumbs up even now. But they still have work to do to make this anything close to a great game. (And I do have faith that they'll put in that work)

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be succinct: This game is a design abomination which wishes it were Suikoden 1/2 while being worse than Suikoden 2 in every single way. The plot is poorly-paced and inferior to Suikoden 2, the characters are (somehow) more one-dimensional than Suikoden 2, half the main cast is formed from "expies" of Suikoden 2 and the story is on a Saturday-morning-cartoon level and involves a crazy amount of hand-waving details. Most of the characters have no concept of personal boundaries and not-Nanami is one of the most frustratingly written and disagreeable characters I have had the misfortune of seeing in a video game.Your hero is presented as a "meddling do-gooder", which in effect means you advance the plot by randomly helping every flavour-of-the-week generic Tom, ♥♥♥♥ and Harry you run across regardless of your actual duties or priorities (let's be real,  you don't have any because the writing is godawful) and much of the content is shoved into the game not because it has a reason to exist, but because "it was there in Suikoden 1-3 and kickstarter backers are hungry for nostalgia". To make matters worse, game balance in this JRPG is an afterthought. The MP system is amazingly badly thought out, spells are overcosted and the main way of restoring MP is through items which don't stack well and clutter your inventory while barely being enough to restore half the cost of a single spell in lategame. To make things worse, any spell which does damage is more or less useless because you would probably achieve better damage results from attacking or using skills. There are just so many things wrong with this battle system that it's difficult to enumerate them, such as the vast majority of enemies blithely ignoring your front line and attacking your back row, party member stats being badly balanced to the point where some characters are nigh-unusable, and the amazingly limited customisation which comes from having only one interesting accessory slot - but the crux of the matter is that I just don't find battles fun nor interesting at all.To its benefit, the music is quite good and the character art is competent, but that doesn't make up for everything else. If you've never played Suikoden 1 or 2 before, I highly suggest you wait for the remaster of that to be released on Steam and avoid this egregious abomination.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugs. Lots of bugs. The Kickstarter promised backers beta testing, but all they really got was a game demo instead. This game could have used actual beta testing to work out all of the horrible bugs. There are currently 200+ bugs listed by players on the official Discord that could have been fixed before release had there been an actual beta. Yetee Productions handled the Kickstarter rewards distribution. That decision has resulted in a massive mismanagement ranging from people getting the game days and even weeks after launch to nearly all of the extras people paid for not even having a date for when they will receive them. Switch physical users had to be sent digital codes because they have no idea when their physical copies will actually be sent. Steam physical backers got a slip of paper in a box with a code. Many Playstation backers got their physical copies over 1 week before everyone else. The entire thing was just a mess, just like Rising was.So, how is the game? Localisation is weird at times, but didn't throw me completely off. Voice Acting is a little cringe at times as well, but again that didn't throw me off. My biggest complaint is that it didn't try to be different at all. It's a re-skin of Suikoden 2. That's it. Just a poorly disguised re-skin of a great JRPG from the PS1 era. I mean an almost perfect re-skin too, right down to the inept teleporter girl and the annoying sister to the protagonist. The game is decent because it literally copies a good game in every aspect. No attempt was made to come up with new characters or new stories. Just copy and paste with the names changed.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'd give this game about a 7/10No, it's not going to live up to best of the Suikoden franchise (Suikoden 2), but it's certainly as good or better than some of the lesser entries (Suikoden IV). If you are a fan of those games, or old JRPGs in general, you'll probably find this one worth your time. It gives a really good taste of what a modern Suikoden .The story is good, though sometimes a bit unmemorable, and there are a lot of likable characters. The voice acting is fantastic (seriously, kudos to the voice actors) even though the dialogue itself often goes on a little longer than it needs to. The artwork is beautiful, and the battle mechanics are what you would expect, with some quality of life improvements over the games of old (such as a configurable auto battle system for when you're just fighting through trash mobs). So, sure, maybe not game of the year material, but I'd definitely buy and play a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: The developers of Eiyuden Chronicle had an unenviable task before them; threading the needle of being faithful to the memory of a game series that never had a chance to modernize and creating a modern enjoyable experience that didn't feel dated or out of the times. Whether or not you think they succeeded is honestly more subjective than most game opinions people might have nowadays.Brought to you by a number of the original Suikoden devs, Eiyuden Chronicle seeks to bring a new iteration of that unique series to people; a jRPG known for it's numerous (100 in this case) recruitable characters, political sweeping storylines and base-building aspects. A style of game that honestly few games have brushed with since then, maybe borrowing some aspect here or there but rarely tried for a full throated attempt. So, did they succeed? I think so. While I have yet to finish, unless something goes drastically wrong in the last handful of hours. I have enjoyed my time immensely with this game. There have been stumbles along the way, issues or bugs and things that didn't quite work for me, but nothing that ever removed the fun I was having or feeling I was getting that was scratching a long forgotten itch I had for a style of game we don't quite get in modern times.I repeat that I don't envy the developer's task. People clamored and paid money on Kickstarter for a spiritual successor to Suikoden. And people's nostalgia gives them fond feelings and soft criticism that with time has sanded off all the edges and pushed down the more unflattering memories. But if you update too much and stray too far, try to do modern takes on long held memories, people will revolt en masse and claim "no, THAT, we wanted THAT." Just, y'know. The idealized one, not the one that actually existed.There are design philosophies in the game that just aren't modern any more, like walking five feet to a cut-scene and then five feet to another. Maybe dashing and faster movement is an accessory or character ability.  People might complain about "not respecting their time" But the entire time through, it hit that sweet spot for me. These were the types of games I played and they modernized it enough that while not the most updated and efficient for the modern gamer philosophy, gave me a feeling I have not experienced in a lot of years. The combat and dungeons are almost certainly better and harder than either has ever been in the Suikoden series, that's for sure. The above-mentioned fondness sure warms up a game series that was never particularly hard or well balanced. People will complain that so few characters get development or have associated quests or long chains of events, expecting them to be like modern CRPG or Persona social links. I beg you to go back and play any Suikoden and see just how many characters get any sort of shine or even have a reason to join a literal rebel army. And ask you how much development time would it take to actually give the majority any of that? I'd give anything for a team of 300 to write hours upon hours of dialogue and storylines for 50 characters at least but realistically that is not what Suikoden ever was or what it ever could be. People have every right to complain about bugs, but on the other hand, oh my god have you ever played a Suikoden game?! People complain about being anime as heck or have weird tone, but again oh my god have you ever played a Suikoden game? They did voice acting for every single 100 recruitable character and almost every cutscene. Not all of them will hit right but it's downright impressive how much quality VA and writing there is (ignore localization whining, it's the usual suspects). The combat is fun and actually challenged me. I found much more than a handful of characters I liked to swap around and play with. Building the castle was extremely satisfying, as were all the mini-games I could engage with (or not). Visually it has a great aesthetic with a variety of environments and designs, if not the tightest graphics which I don't much care about. And while the plot wasn't quite as heavy or crunchy as I was expecting, which was a bit of a let down since they were going for a different tone for this game, I still enjoyed it. Also, making the MC voiced and have a personality was a 10/10 decision.Other can argue the minutiae of merits and you can get your collection of more in depth opinions on combat or bugs or whatever. Maybe in time I'll not feel the same as I do now. But for someone who played through 2 great but flawed, 2 okay and 1 miserable Suikoden games, this game met and exceeded what I was looking for. A jRPG that feels old, but doesn't FEEL old, you get me? I can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this and the story seemed interesting along with the townbuilding aspect but:The idea of having 100 characters seems great until you realize most of them are actively annoying, especially the women. It doesn't help that they say the same thing every time they do their skills.  Carrie got booted out of my party as soon as possible due to her "Made you look" voice line.  But she still says two lines, one before and one after, every single time you fast travel. Every. Single. Time.  And you'll be using it a lot.  Mellore repeats "Magic Missile" twice every battle.  Even the non-battle characters are annoying.  B'baba repeats the same line each time you confirm you want her to scry.Gameplay is also dreadfully slow.  Opening up the menu and switching pages feels slow.  Combat feels slow, especially when a support character ability procs (the hot spring one takes so long).  Battle plan doesn't work as expected often, e.g. magic use when magic skills are not listed in priority actions.  Auto battle never uses heroic combos.  None of the stats are explained nor have I found a way to figure out how to use the elements or damage types as there's no info about the enemies available during battle.UI generally is unpleasant, e.g. fast travel to the main base requires opening up the map, changing to the world map, and going to the second page of that.  Put it on the first page.Limited item storage makes using the rune system painful.  Gotta know what you want to put on as well as character compatibility to know what to pull out of storage.Drop rates are awful especially when several characters require grinding out items to recruit them.Fishing is boring, but required for recruiting.  I don't want to play the top game, but it's required for recruiting.  I don't want to play the card game, but it's required for recruiting.  And recruiting is required for town building. So I stopped ~20 hours in.  Just wasn't looking forward to finding the next annoying character that I'd leave at my base forever.  The plot had one interesting character in Seign but he can't carry the whole game.

That's it. The world map looked pretty boring and unexciting to me but what I really disliked were the fights:  It feels like the gameplay has already been seen in countless other JRPGs and is super dull and repetitive. There are constantly random battles that surprise you in the middle of walking from one town to another (or in some dungeon marked maps which you'd like to explore), you can't see the opponents, too. It may be that this has always been the case in this series, but I find  just exhausting and annoying in the long run. In addition, you can't save everywhere and have to go through the hassle of looking for save points, which is doubly annoying.As for the characters.. some of them were interesting and to be honest, that is and was my main point in playing. I think the idea to recruit an army of people you can interact with quite funny even though I doubt that all the characters are worth my time or have much to say. Since I have only played with Nowa I coulnd't convince myself to keep playing, I just couldn't connect with him. Okay-ish Jrpg with little new ideas and great music. Graphics are fine, but nothing I haven't seen somewhere else. Only buy it if you are absolutely into typical genre like j-rpgs or the series itself, I'd say. Otherwhise, there are better rpgs to play!

_childDocuments_.review: The game delivers on exactly what it promised at conception: a spiritual successor to the Suikoden series, very much in the style of a modernized Suikoden I and II, and everything that implies. If you liked those games, you'll like this one. They really succeeded in capturing the way you remember those games in your head, through the nostalgia-lens (pun intended!).It adheres pretty hard to the classic JRPG style, arguably to a fault sometimes, but succeeds at giving me the feelings I had when playing these games 20+ years ago. The characters are fun, the story is good (if possibly a bit standard), the voice-acting in both English and Japanese is well-done, and the game-play and combat are both a lot of fun.There are some descriptions that are a bit vague and could stand to go into more detail, and there's a few bugs at release that need to be fixed, but nothing gamebreaking that can't be avoided or worked around for now, and I've seen the bugs acknowledged and that they're working on a fix, so I have faith they'll be rectified soon.You might see people complaining about the localization (and which seems to be hyper-focused on one specific line from Mio), but personally I feel it was well-done. The localization feels natural and captures the feeling of the game, presenting it how it would likely have been written had it been done in English by a native speaker in the first place while still getting across all of the information and characterization, which I feel should be the goal. The particular offending line is, in my opinion, at worst a joke that didn't land and not the start of an overall theme of "Did you just assume my gender!?" like people seem to be implying. The game isn't politicized, it just deals with it's own internal narrative political struggles.All in all, I'm so glad I backed this 4 years ago, they delivered everything they promised and everything I wanted, and I'm very happy with it!

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicles is on the surface a Suikoden 2 tribute, yet the game didn’t captivate me enough to keep on playing.  I loved Suikoden 1 and 2, as well as “Alliance Alive”, so I was looking forward to playing this game.The game itself looks beautiful overall, some people hate the artstyle, but i really love the 2D-3D combination, just like Live-a-Live remake or Chantelise. The Overworld feels great and vivid, and the zones are like dungeons even if they are linear, they have a lot of details that make them feel great. This unfortunately doesn't apply to the first city, where the npcs go by predetermined paths, repeating the same words and no way to interact with them, making the city feel empty. I would have preferred if they were static or with little movement like in the starting zone. And the blur effects in certain environments look awful.The combat looks great, but lacks the dynamism of the characters like in previous Suikoden games, now every character waits for his turn, instead of attacking everyone almost at the same time as different enemies. Outside of that, the animations are great and the camera movements make up for the dynamism.Autobattle it’s great, it not only makes the character attack any enemy like the other games, it makes them use abilities and items to heal HP or revive teammates. Combat planning it's just either basic attacks, abilities or items, the only unit that can use magic at first has severe limitations on healing magic, and protection buff, you can only use her abilities 2 or 3 times before running out of MP. Unison attacks don't really do a lot of damage compared to abilities and you could dispatch monsters in one turn anyways.Many basics QOL in moderns rpgs feels like they were excluded, like saving anywhere (still got multiple save states), infinite inventory space, skippable events, random encounters, battle speed modifier, difficulty change in mid game, and the difficulty itself being artificial since it only inflates numbers rather than giving the enemies new abilities or being numerous. Which is weird, because the “Alliance Alive” fixed those issues on the 3DS. Besides, the multiple short loading screens and being unable to rebind keys, lack of dialogue logs are annoying.UI looks lovely and vivid, but menu and battle navigation feel completely opposite of overworld navigation. On one hand, overworld it’s smooth and responsive, a little slow even if Nowa is running, but still feels great. Menus feel stiff, once you select something you feel a small but stand out  holdback on navigation that stops you a little. Character portraits on the menu look good, and I’m glad the game added you a section on the menu to revisit the pop-up tutorials.Music it’s alright, but nothing special either. I didn’t feel like the battle themes pumped me out like in previous games, nor an upbeat cheerful theme like rock rockland.Those are small complaints that I could accept and say “yeah, a little annoying details, but still a good game” However my biggest problem it’s related to the story and characters.Story: It feels like they didn’t try at all  to find a way to hook you in the story at first, it feels rushed and discontinuous on the events, doesn’t set a serious tone or something that interest you at first and yet instead to keeping on with the continuity, they jump on ASAP to the next chapter. The story itself begins with Nowa, an almost identical copy of Riou, a goodie 2 shoes that joins in the mercenaries for… no reason? Or at least it’s one of his responses, waiting to know the world sounds better, yet it doesn't feel like a proper way to introduce your main character. We also got introduced to 5 other characters in the process, 2 of them being familiar faces since they are obviously Jowy and Nanami. 3 mercenaries, 2 nobles from the empire and Nowa are on a mission to retrieve a “primal lens” (don’t know the english name, I was playing in spanish) from some ruins that will eventually be useful for the empire. However, they don’t even explain how those lenses work or why they are so important despite the emphasis in this part. After retrieving the lenses, the game jumps 6 months in the future, where you are ascended as an interim captain with the mercs.Characters: Like I said, Nowa as a protagonist doesn’t really have a motive in the beginning, making you feel uninterested in his adventure, and neither does feel like he has a real involvement in the story. Compare this to McDohl, the son of a general from the empire that is on a quest to prove himself as an prideful soldier as his father, but is then persecuted by his former nation as the new bearer the “soul eater rune”. Or Riou, a recruit from the Highland empire who survives an ambush from his former comrades, since his squad got killed in order to create a hoax to stop a ceasefire between nations and have a reason to invade Jowston, and gets captured by mercenaries working for said nation. Every one of these situations in less than 2 hours in their respective games.Even side characters feel annoyed and unnatural in the way they talk, not Nanami specially got me on my nerves and just wanted to skip every one of her phrases or remove her from my party. And none of them it’s really interesting since you don’t really know them at all and they don’t make an effort to be interesting at the moment, Mio being just a Baiken cosplayer and Garr just a blunt head kobold captain. On Suikoden 1 we have your 3 retainers and your best friend, each one with different personalities that clash with each other, but they will give their lives for you because they see you as a friend, not as a master. On Suikoden 2, we have Jowy, your best friend who survives the Highland army ambush alongside you and promises you that both of you will go back home with Nanami, and shortly after, Viktor and Flik, 2 of the main characters from the past game.And let’s address the elephant in the room. Yes, the localization it’s bad. Makes you wonder if the localizers saw the Forspoken script and thought it was the peak of english literature and decided to use the same type of behavior in the characters but more sanitized to make it pegi 12. And that’s why I decided to play it in my native language (Spanish) to see if there was something different, but to my surprise, the Spanish dialogue has the same expressions as the English one. Which it’s disappointing. Why does english have to be localized from the japanese, yet spanish from english it’s a literal translation? Why not do a literal translation in the first place from Japanese to english? So not only is the script disrespectful as it butcher up the original script, but we also have to use the same butchered script for other languages too.However, despite that, even if the localization team didn’t participate in the script, the game still gives a bad impression of what they are trying to be, a spiritual successor of the Suikoden series. Because the characters don't feel interesting from the beginning. You had 18 years since Suikoden V, and 7 years since the Alliance Alive to review their stories and characters and what made them memorable since the beginning, and this game didn’t feel like it ignited that flame in me of waiting for the hero to continue on his journey.And I know, this review may sound harsh and nitpicky, but this game is carrying the legacy of 2 great games that are well known for their story and characters. I didn’t want a magnum opus of a game, but a game that at least combines mostly the small things that make other Suikoden games great (story, music, characters, combat, and all since the beginning of the game). Something that I feel failed to deliver this game.I might probably still play this game on game pass later on, however, I don’t feel this game holds up the title as a Suikoden successor.

_childDocuments_.review: A tribute to nostalgia. A game worth buying, but also could have seen more polish.The game, while enjoyable, stubs its own toe by having too much at times; The age old quantity over quality dilemma.  This feeling is amplified when you experience parts where you wanted more of that, and instead see other elements that felt unnecessary, or rushed into the final package.—The overall story is fine for what it is.  Though at times it felt as if it wanted to come off as a story about 3 main characters…when it never truly lends itself to that.I am fine with it being a story revolving around just a primary character, or the ambitious story telling Suikoden 3 did where you trade off between multiple characters.It felt odd at times that the game tried to pull a Suikoden 3 aspect of storytelling, but it felt forced.  Elements that felt unfinished or unnecessary at times.You end up more teased with their other supposed main characters then getting anything memorable; because the bulk of the game still follows 1 main character.—The combat is serviceable.  Clearly they changed the rune system from Suikoden into MP points.  So similar to those games, you’d horde that resource for tough fights or namely boss fights.  Was not a fan of the equip-able rune-lens system however, as it ended up feeling quite restrictive with how little flexibility many of your characters ended up having.  You’d rarely ever be able to change off their default skills for other options due to how they set it up.  The stats of your characters also was a pet-peeve, how some of the characters I wanted in my party due to their look/theme/personality I ended up holding off, because they would be severely gimped in comparison to others.  Presumably characters had different stats scaling at later levels, but you spend the grand majority of the game without the means to get them to those levels…so once more, I was not a fan of having to shelve characters because they felt too hindered compared to others.The team combos sadly felt underwhelming.  In my experimenting, it felt as though you lost out on damage from doing them; there were some expectations, like the AoE base ones. It's understandable they do less, but to more foes.  So for many of them, the only reason to use it was for watching a cutscene.  Just didn’t make any sense why they would go this route.  A number of methods could have been done to fix this, even if it meant buffing them up and limiting them to once per combat or something of the like.—The game had a lot of mini games.  Yet few felt enjoyable.  They should have removed half of them if it meant more time spent to improve upon the ones kept.—While it was a small part of the game, the tribute to the dueling system from Suikoden felt great in its later fights.  Well, the gameplay of it was simple, but for a visual treat it was quite enjoyable watching the [break] sequences play out.    —The main story battlefield events were underwhelming from a gameplay aspect.The story they told during the fight was fine, when narratively you had the odds against you, or how your strategist would come up with twists throughout the fights.But experiencing it through the gameplay was disheartening.  Was always on a small grid where you were forced to start all your troops in 1 spot, just marching forward.—Ultimately I feel my review comes off far more critical of the game.  Yet I still want it to succeed so that we can inspire other game developers to make these traditional RPG games.  They are tougher to pull off, and I'm not sure they appeal to the majority of gamers, yet I hope they never die off.

_childDocuments_.review: So, still playing after 20 hours. I'm a big Suikoden fan. I completed Suikoden 1,2,3 and 5. I've played Suikoden 4, Suikoden Tactics, and Suikoden Tierkries on the Nintendo DS. So I've played good Suikoden games, and bad ones. Visual elements and sounds are good. I turned off the voiceovers, because it took me out of nostalgia mode, but I think they are competently done, both ENG and JP. Just not what I want in a nostalgia kick. The mechanics of combat are good. I am playing on Hard mode, because I like the extra challenge. As such, I've had some tricky boss fights. Resource management is a strategic challenge in the game, because save points don't heal you. You routinely need to drop off unused items at storage, to have enough healing items to get through a dungeon and beat a boss. Strategy mode is mostly scripted, so as long as you maintain positioning, it's not tough. Duels are good, the first one is scripted to be very challenging, the rest are more straight forward. Base building is great, you gather resources and people, and gradually build your castle town. I will update this with my completed opinion about the story elements but here's some basic thoughts. I get why, for voiceover reasons, but I'd like to name Nowa, if I wanted. The MC doesn't have a starting strong connection to anyone except an adventuring sister and a farming aunt. I'd like to see a flash back of them together or something, to better illustrate Nowa's connection to his home town. Secondly, I do think a bit more time is needed to make Seign and Nowa friends, besides one dungeon crawl. Another outing, some letters sent, something to make the growing friendship feel more natural. Aside from that, I think we're good. I've seen some complaints about the translation quality. I feel like some reviewers don't remember the 90's and our weird translation goofs. Working Designs was the best of the time, and they certainly took liberties that would be frowned on today. Japanese voiceovers don't match the text, but that's pretty much standard for long RPG games. As a whole, I think the translation is quite satisfactory.There's also some people who feel targeted by the use of the word CHUD? To be specifc, when a delusional chunibyo mage, that the MC considers crazy, calls another muscley mage CHUD. If you want to take that singular incident to feel politically attacked, knock yourself out. Is it a direct translation, no. Few games are. But it's not garbage either. I mean, the whole of the game is to preserve the status quo of the League, not overthrow an existing empire, or abolish egregious taxation. In that light, Eiyuden Chronicles is far more moderate than Suikoden 1 was.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: I backed this game during the first week it went live on Kickstarter, so I am heavily invested in it's success. I am also a HUGE Suikoden fan.Let's get this out of the way, the English localization is absolute garbage, and the people who worked on that localization should never be trusted with another IP set in a fantasy world ever again. I set my expectations for the localization low, but I still found myself being disappointed by how many liberties the localizers took (there are times when the JP audio will say one thing, and the English text will say another).Pros:- The game genuinely feels like a spiritual successor to the Suikoden franchise, especially GS2.- The 2.5D art style is endearing and very reminiscent of GS1 and 2.- The music is great.- The Japanese voice acting is fairly good.- Lots of mini-games to do, should you get tired of collecting characters or progressing through the storyCons:- The English localization is so bad that it ruins immersion and takes you out of the experience- The cooking mini-game's scoring system is weird, even after the recent patch to fix it.- The boat racing mini-game is so bad that they just let you progress through the story if you fail enough times. The person whom designed the controls for this mini-game should never be trusted with designing vehicle controls ever again.- Both duels and skirmishes are basically on rails. Choosing to play defensively is useless and will often times make you lose, so mindlessly pressing on with attacks is the only real way to go.- You can feel the outdated design of the game right away. From not being able to save anywhere to having to juggle bag space, it can get pretty annoying if you've already gotten used to the modern QOL improvements that have become industry standard in recent times.I recommend this game for die-hard Suikoden fans, and only die-hard Suikoden fans.Side note: My original backer copy was for the Switch, but because it's basically unplayable on that console I asked 505 to send me a Steam code instead. It took them a week to get back to me, and by the time they'd given me the code, I had already bought the game here on Steam and was progressing through Hishan.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to give this a fair shake because it takes time to get into the meat of a long JRPG. 40 hours in and I've given up. Every aspect about this game feels so boilerplate. It functions, which is great. The battle system isn't too easy or too hard, but its also not that deep. Like with the characters its quantity over quality. I get the conventions of a genki boy protagonist, the other side of the coin friend/rival, and "the girl". I played this game exclusively because I thought marisa was cute and i love old jrpgsThis game constantly teasing me with having her around and then switching back to the milquetoast twins. I did not expect any of these characters to be too deep since there are so many of them, but I was hoping for a character I can point and clap at bc I love their concept so much. I didn't even get that. What I got were watered down recolored versions of roy mustang, riza hawkeye, rei ayanami, etcI ultimately threw in the towel waiting for any of the three protagonists to do anything interesting. Yes, they have their plot points but they all feel like ticking their "JRPG trope" box. The low encounter rate is nice since the dungeons are so large, but with all the environments being this large and empty it makes the towns irritating to get through. The music gets stuck in your head but its neither good nor bad. just repetitive.I wouldn't recommend this game if you're looking to experience something resembling your classic late 90s early 2000's JRPGs. It looks that way on the outside but inside it's just standard mediocre plot and generic world building. It's an inch deep and a mile wide.edit: for some reason it says 5 hours on record but i put 40 hours into this.

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes (2024) represents a Japanese role-playing game (JRPG), developed by the company Rabbit and Bear Studios and published by the company 505 Games.++ Meet the members of my dream team, straight from the mental asylum. Mighty Mellore, a delusional sorceress in a sailor moon costume with late-stage OCD for justice one liners. Youngling Yusuke, the misunderstood gangster with his hands glued to his pants and the tendency to kick his enemies into a bloody pulp. Fierce Franscesca, a stereotypical tsundere character with a split personality. And yes, I can fix her! Crazy Carrie, the petite blond who is one teleportation away from summoning a demonic creature from the immaterium or falling victim to the infamous turning-the-inside-out incident. Muscle mage Maureus, a beefcake with a severe concussion trauma believing muscle points (MP) are the most crucial metric for determining how much magical power a caster can draw from. Punisher Prunella, the last survivor of a dwarven commando unit likes to clean her massive bazooka, that I call Fatman, at the campfire while telling stories about past war crimes.+ You will be buried under an avalanche of 71 playable characters, who you can assemble into a team of six to fight a power-hungry empire that threatens to annex your worthless fishing village. But you will abandon your main quest soon enough, because of the countless distractions in form of customizing your castle, cooking, fishing, playing cards, spinning tops, and starting a breeding program for pseudo-chocobos. And for the ambitious among us, enter a neverending dungeon with overpowered mobs to reach your final form. Then steamroll the rest of the campaign.o The supposed challenge of the cooking mini-game confuses me. I simply served the unwashed masses fried eggs, omelets and apple cider soda every time, and effortlessly rose to the status of culinary godhood.- Some scripted sequences have a massive delay before they continue, e.g. the first duel on the bridge, or the song with the shi’arc. It required the patience of a saint to sit through those lags.-- Dear developers, where is my option to double or even triple the speed during combat sections? Just look at The Last Remnant (2009) for such a quality-of-life feature. Heresy, I hear you scream as you try to suppress your tears and clutch your little game codex. But, to quote my arch-enemy and grand illusionist Todd Howard: it just works.To roam the realm of Allraan with the farmer-turned-warlord-protagonist Nowa and my bizarre team of MIN/MAX characters, provoking encounters and hoarding ridiculous amounts of money and resources for the end game weaponry of mutually agreed mass destruction, constitutes my only purpose in this game.Recommended for JRPG freaks eager to refill their nostalgia meter.Estimated time for 100% completion: +150 hoursSingleplayer achievements: 56Multiplayer achievements: none

_childDocuments_.review: A very traditional JRPG - perhaps too traditional for modern taste. The biggest flaw of the game is its slow pacing throughout the game - from visual presentation to gameplay. For instance, navigating through the menu would have those unnecessary pauses; the combat animations are very slow, without ways to speed up; the gameplay features are unlocked very slowly. Other aspect of the game doesn't make up for the slow pacing, so not recommended for those without the patience.[Visuals] The game uses a mixture of pixel art sprites and 3D scenes. But both graphical style and quality are mediocore. The 3D graphical quality looks outdated and the style doesn't work well with the pixel arts. Would look better if just stick to pixel art for both sprites and scenes. The performance optimization is okay but could be better for this level of graphics.[Story] Still early into the game (10+ hrs). But so far the story feels very conventional. It is rather similar to some other JRPGs in recent memory.[Characters] The main character is way too stereotypical and bland- the kind of good-hearted, hot-blooded boy you would see in old school JRPGs. The recruitable characters in comparison are more interesting with very distinct personalities - so meeting and recruiting new characters to your party can be quite fun - which is the main feature of the game.[Gameplay] The game features traditional turn-based combat. But I find even among turn-based games the combat is way too linear - the skills don't have much difference and players tactical choices have very little impact to the flow of the combat. Outside the combat, the town building and character recruitment aspect can be fun. There is also minigames like large scale battles but it's way too slow.

_childDocuments_.review: I am very disappointed I waited 1.5 years for this game for it to come out and be very, very, very mediocre.  This game does nothing new nor exciting for the genre.  The combat leaves so much to be desired that it just becomes stale and disconnecting very fast.  Magic is also so underwhelming and relies on so much resources that you're just better off just sticking with physical characters to make exploration last.  It's also sad that out of the 120 characters, only a dozen or so of them are truly viable for combat while the others just aren't usable because of their pathetically comparatively low or unbalanced stats.  And the story?  Super tropey and dumbly predictable.  It's very safe to say that it's nothing you haven't experienced before.All in all, I was hoping for an absolute epic of a tale.  At least that's what the trailer made me feel I was going to experience.  Instead, I was given a very standard cast of characters with the most traditional of 'evil empire vs other nations' story that does nothing to keep me absorbed and intrigued enough to keep me going.  It's a very standard and very introductory JRPG to those who have never ventured into the genre but for those of us who consider ourselves veterans of it, we may have to settle for simply sensing the smallest bit of nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  truly is the spiritual successor to . It has a lot of passion, however, it also has many hiccups and shortcomings that prevents it from being a true masterpiece, but I loved the overall experience.✅ The soundtrack, art direction and the blend of 2D and 3D is amazing. I really like this trend  spearheaded.✅ Character designs are pretty good and distinct from each other.✅ Combat is reminiscent of  where you fight with six party members.✅ Large scale Boss Battles feature 3D model monsters. Those fights have multiple phases, as well "gimmicks" where players interact with other elements to fight the bosses, such as hiding behind debris to avoid a powerful attack or activate objects to deal environmental damage.✅ Certain boss fights will take places as Duel Battles, where you have to attack and counter the enemy to fill up a gauge. They tend to be pretty cinematic and take place during key points in the story.✅ Some dungeons have pretty cool puzzle mechanics.✅ After a certain point in the story you can unlock a castle and start building a village around it. A quite satisfying activity as you gather materials and recruit non-combat allies to take care of different services.✅ There are tons of side activities and mini-games.✅ The endgame is pretty fun once you unlock the Hero Trial Mode, which is a gauntlet of battles where you have to swap between party members ever three fights. It rewards players who build the entire roster.❌ Performance-wise this game tanks for no reason. It's not a graphics intensive game, yet my GPU was reaching +85C during boss battles. I've played  on high settings and it barely breaks beyond 77C (and that game is an unoptimized mess). I think this is something related to the Unity engine because I've played other recent Unity games that had the same issue. INB4 someone says "It's your rig.", my PC has pretty good airflow and I clean it regularly.❌ The game launched with a lot of bugs, including some that can permanently soft-lock your save file. A lot of those have been patched, but it's quite concerning.❌ The main story itself is not long nor complex, in fact it is even a bit too light-hearted (at first). Some characters are way too silly at times and downright annoying. It tries to be like  but lacks the depth and maturity.❌ There is just so much slowdown in this game. I don't even mean performance wise. Some of the stuff includes:❌ Combat has a lot of issues:❌ You can't save the game on the world map. This was a deliberate design choice but honestly it makes no sense.❌ The English localization is a very, very mixed bag. They changed a lot of dialogues that can completely change the context of what characters originally said in Japanese. I really don't get these changes because most of them aren't even censorship.❌ Still on the subject of localization, the English voice acting is either decent or downright awful. Many voices don't match the characters, and I've even seen a old female villager NPC with a male kid's voice. Some of the voice acting legit remind me of the early 2000's voice acting in games.✅ However, this silliness is actually really funny for the Theater Mode as the characters are acting in the game, so the polarizing voice acting ends up amusing in this this case.❌ Some towns are way too large with nothing to do on them. You can enter certain houses that are empty, not even a treasure chest. I never understood the point of that in JRPGs.❌ New recruits don't join at your average party level. So if you missed a character in the early game and recruited them later, have fun playing with a level 6 character on your level 20 party.✅ However, EXP scaling is really good, so you can actually get +20 levels on a single battle with a low level character if enemies give a lot of EXP.❌ Boss battles tend to be damage sponges and take a bit too long. I understand this since you have six party members, but they drag for so long.❌ The War Mode is incredibly bland. I understand them trying to portray large scale wars, but the whole system feels so poorly implemented and it's simply not fun. I would've preferred if it took place in the a battlefield like map with normal battle gauntlets culminating in a boss battle.❌ The first  promised these really cool cinematic-like boss battles, yet there is nothing like it aside from the final boss fight. I've read that some people experienced motion sickness in the early alpha stages so that's why they toned it down, which makes sense. But I still hoped it had some cool moments of dynamic camera when attacking bosses with your party members.I know I went really REALLY hard on the criticism, but it's only because I care so much for this series and what it represents for the legacy of . Maybe the game still needed more time in the oven. I wouldn't have minded waiting another year for it to release.I really wish this game took some notes from , because the dev team from that game truly improved on every aspect of the original title and added a plethora of quality-of-life improvements that are fitting for modern formats and forgoing the stuff that was outdated. I feel this game latches too hard on the classic JRPG tropes that don't really work anymore.  did that too and many of the issues were somewhat remedied in the sequel.However, ultimately,  still is a great tribute and spiritual successor to , but it lacks the charm and refinement the original games had while being too afraid to take risks. This is definitely a huge step forward to bringing back the  series in a new form, but I do hope the team improves the formula in the upcoming sequel they already announced.I still recommend this game to all JRPG enthusiasts, and especially to fans of the . A real shame Yoshitaka Murayama, the creator of  and the man behind , passed away before the game launched.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I would like to clarify that I was not a fan of suikoden series since PS1 days. I found suikoden series a bit too much and complicated for me back in those days. So no idea how the game had been. I wasn't expecting too much nor this game would clicked with me. I am glad I was wrong. This game remind me of NiNoKuNi2 quite frankly since that is probably one of the latest jrpg I played with kingdom management. So far 38 hours in and honestly I am not even halfway of the story from according to walk-through I am using and also according to eiyuden chronicle HH wiki. I am only at I think around 36-38% of story.Wanna know what I had been doing these times in the game?!!! To my surprise recruiting heroes lol ... ... ... I felt like it is so much sastifying and rewarding the recruitment of heroes are. Just like in NinoKuni 2 but this game have more depth to it.  The whole 38 hours All I had been doing and am still doing is literally grinding resources and recruiting heroes up to the story I am at. I dunno whether it is worth doing it this way or not but it is fun as heck for me. The combat system and the character progression system is simple enough to get a hang of and nothing out of ordinary. If you are doing as much grinding as I am, the bosses so far felt like a mob with big HP pool. I hate grinding too much and yet I am having fun at grinding in this game. The only system that is worth pointing out is the nostalgic system of the runes. Kinda like the materia in FFVII and FFVII remake but not exactly the same. People do say it is the classic suikoden system but I dunno since this game would be my first game to the franchise. All the other things are pretty generic for a jrpg after had played tons of them. Nothing new and yet still refreshing. This game is gonna be my time sink before the ERDTREE EXPANSION comes out. Give this game a go seriously you wont be disappointed at least. Its fun. minigames are also engaging. The bayblade one especially.

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle gave me one of the most unique experiences I have ever had with JRPGs. It brought back things I experienced when I played games from the PS1 as a kid, being items and recipes. The trade outpost mechanic is also really interesting when I played Tradewinds with my first PC.Seign Kesling is my favorite characters, from his personality to his moveset to his physical design. Everything about this game was an emotional rollercoaster. Each character you have to recruit has their own story, and the overall message in the game is that there is someone or something that is worth protecting and that your beliefs are worth standing up for. Stand up for what's right even if there is no one behind you.Duels - AMAZING, weird mechanic but the first time I've ever seen it. When Nowa faces Seign, it felt like a battle of ideals, and it's really cool that there are two endings. Runes are also a significant mechanic as well, made the customization very fun. I like the armor and weapon mechanics - upgrade what you have and buy new physical armor.Every boss fight is fair, the game itself does a great job of leveling your characters at a fair pace. They make the Dux Aldric guy a really despicable villain. Throughout the game, just when you think you have a moment of victory, something takes you down. That's war and luck. What a fitting end to make the last boss battle a duel with Brave Flags theme remasteredThere is no swearing in this game, which is fine. I still didn't expect to see a kid get his arm chopped off, and then we recruit him with "Armed and Ready" as his title.Worst mechanics: Sand Shiarc timed racing. Also, I don't like Wars. Once you get used to it, they're cool, but let's talk about the shiarc racing. If you're using a Playstation controller, you're screwed because the analog controls are inverted. It doesn't feel good to play this mode. You have to resort to using the d-pad to move. Overall, to recruit one unit and to also proceed the story, you have to do 2 races, and it's really frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe I'm not far enough in to where this game gets good, but it feels very lacking to me which is in terms of combat. The first characters you get in a game should really be filling different roles to engage you on team building, all these guys do is about 40-60 damage each every turn pretty much across the board. Maybe the game has a slow start but between combat all feeling very meh and the Nerthus fight being the most miserable experience I've had to endure in a while I just can't really recommend this one unless you're a die hard JRPG fan. Feel like there's better options on the market that start off a lot stronger than this like Octopath and Unicorn Overlord.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game that could use a tune up.  Huge fan of the Suikoden series that inspired this game and, I don't really get the feel of Suikoden when I play it.  Sorta feels like Wild Arms and Secret of Mana with an anime theme.Other than some of the dungeons feeling way too big, biggest grip is the combat system.  Seems like your always in a life or death situation when you enter combat every 12 or 15 seconds.  I think only Beyond the Beyond is worse for random encounters.  Once in, you are going to be in that fight for at least 30 seconds too long dealing with enemies that give you no real experience anymore, but they will eat away at your potions and such.  This only applies to enemies that are at, or near, your current level, because otherwise, you're letting them go.I do appreciate them "making consumables great again", but it's fairly annoying when your backliners, hell, some of your frontliners too, get targeted and lose half their HP in a two part attack!  And yes, the other part kills them.  No problem!  I'll raise them from the dead!  And they're killed immediately because the enemies choose random targets at THEIR turn, not at the start of the overall turn.  Stat growth in this game for most people is abysmal at best for most people.  I'm around level 37 with most of my people and the highest HP is 263 for a frontliner, which isn't bad but certainly not great.  My healer has only 123 at level 36.  I know they're not supposed to be able to tank everything, but that feels a little low just like the whole stat system in general.  Even with stat runes attached to them, they would only be 5% better so, not much of a difference.  Of course, I'm probably not that far into it which would make all of this crying for nothing.Naturally, magic is mostly useless in the early part of the game except for healing which is good, but your healer is almost always the last person to take action....I don't think I'm terribly far into the story despite my hours played, 21 at the time, but the story seems OK for a political intriguer.  Lots of "quirky" female characters that border on the absurd which isn't all that bad considering the sorta nonsensical-ness of most characters.  Don't know where I'm really goin with that but it is odd....They need to figure out a way to speed this game up!  It takes forever to walk anywhere, killing regular monsters in battle can sometimes take FIVE ROUNDS OF AUTOMATED COMBAT!!!!!  With, of course, dozens of potions being used.  Also, getting out of combat back to the map needs to be sped up.  You could add to the sped up list: fishing!  "You caught a rando fish".  Yay I caught a fish.  "Oh and, uh, you obtained a fish".  Thankfully, they cleared that up  with a double notifier of what happened.  Who knows what you'll drag out of the water with your fishing pole at a fishing hole!?  Seriously, no one needs TWO notifications for the same thing.  "Obtained rando fish" is all we needed.Overall, the game is good and I want them to put out more games like this to try and capture the magic of the tragically dead Suikoden series.  RIP mister Prime.  Never again shall we here of your adventures.....  "Insert Le Sad Face"....

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Eiyuden Chronicle might be worth your money, but only if you’re desperate for another Suikoden game. Everyone else should save your money, and play it on Xbox Game Pass instead. EC gets more right than it does wrong, but it keeps one foot firmly planted in the past, and not always for the better.My qualifications: I’ve played through Suikoden 1&2 multiple times, doing almost everything worth doing in each. I supported this game’s kick starter as a “slacker backer”, pre-ordering a game for the first time EVER because I believed in this game and the people who made it. EC is clearly a passion project Rabbit and Bear Studios didn’t have to make. Sadly, series creator Yoshitaka Murayama passed away before he could see EC’s release, but is this truly his magnum opus, or does EC fail to surpass the heights of SK2? IMO, both are true.You should only buy this game if you want to do everything in SK2 all over again, and I quite literally mean EVERYTHING. This begs the question: if EC offers little to nothing new, why not just play SK2 instead? EC tries to differentiate itself mainly through new difficulty options, since one of the greatest weaknesses of SK in hindsight was that its extremely easy. While some of these work, others don’t.No Items in Battle and No Escape from Battles specifically are the wrong approach. Group healing and revival items are rendered worthless, since basic healing does the job for less money outside of battle. Even on the highest difficulty you’ll be auto-resolving battles in no time, and the leveling system is very forgiving so under-leveled characters can catch up quick. This too is rendered pointless. Rather than force players to fight every battle, the game should’ve given us a reason to fight them by making them truly challenging. Hitting “Auto” and opening the menu to pop healing afterwards doesn’t require skill, it’s just plain tedious. Fortunately, the game allows you to tailor which options you want, and which you don’t.Finally, I’d like to talk about EC as a game to play remotely. I can’t be the only one who was excited to boot this up in Steam Link and play anywhere. I even bought a cheap android handheld with the task in mind under the mistaken belief the Developers had remote gamers in mind. Sadly, the Switch version is reportedly the worst version of all. This version offers barely any resolution options, and makes no considerations for users on smaller screens. As a guy with perfect vision, I was squinting to read text on my handheld. If you have any kind of visual impairment, this game is a hard pass on everything but the largest screens.Overall, the game is slightly above average, and gets a lukewarm thumbs up from me. SK 1&2 were amazing RPGs in their time after all, but we have some serious quality of life issues that make EC fall short of what it could be, being more of a mimic than a true successor.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface: I never grew up with Suikoden, the series this is a spiritual successor of. If anything is a standard carryover from that series, I wouldn't know.TL;DR: The combat won't blow you away and mechanics and other such things are rarely explained well enough in-game but the story is definitely worth playing the game for, in my opinion.Anyway, it's really solid in a lot of aspects. Stuff like the music and the story is great and the battles, while not the most engaging a lot of the time, is still good enough to keep me interested all the way through. There's a lot of side content like a card game, notBeyblade, two types of racing minigames, and a theatre but most of it felt, to me, more like an afterthought than something they planned on adding from the get go.  The Beyblades are easily the worst among these. You can choose where to start during the start but that never seemed to matter, and the Beyblades have elements and stats that  didn't seem to matter if you just made sure to use the same "rarity" as your opponent.  The theatre was great though because all the characters you recruit have voice acting for most of it (I noticed one or two didn't, for some reason) so you can make some really funny setups in that. But the meat of it all: the combat. I must say that it felt really basic. Practically none of the physical characters I actually used could equip the skills I kept finding so I had to make do with basic attacks for most of them and the magic felt very underwhelming, enough so to make me only use the water spells for the entire game as that's where you will find the party heal that doesn't scale with the magic stat and instead just does 40% on everyone.  I played on the harder difficulty and never felt I had to actively engage in the rune equip system, nor did I ever level grind as I despise doing it.There were a handful of times where I felt explanations from the game were lacking. I actually read tutorials but take the Beyblades for example: 5 stats, they probably do stuff, but what? The game never says more than "keep in mind the stats".  Or take the secondary battle mode you do a couple times throughout the story. Apparently if you addign someone to only have cavalry, they will have more movement. Only reason I knew that? The boss of the second-to-last one does that against you. So be prepared to look some stuff up as the game surely won't tell you, even though it has a help section in the menu.

_childDocuments_.review: Close to the end of the game. I have few good things to say about the game and too many bad things.I have changed my opinion on the translation somewhat. Still maybe a C+ or B- as a grade.Music is forgettable. The only tracks i somewhat like are the ones from Michiko Naruke. Motoi Sakuraba music, while not grading to my ears is just so generic, like i have heard it a thousand times already. C or C+Making the minigames mandatory for the best ending would have been okay, if they at least were fun. This is not the case. It does not really matter that the cooking game was bugged in the beginnig, even without bugs there were a) too many of them; b) it was just slow and not engaging.For the card game, i confess, this is just my personal bias, i loath any kind of card game in my rpgs. So even worse if i have to engage in it to unlock characters.The beyblade one, for me, suffers from a lack of explaination and even then you can only really start later in the game, when you have found more pieces and can overpower your foes.Fishing you cannot even really call it a mini game (not even some music for it)The whole minigame stuff i would summarize as "Too ambitious", so it feels they just halfassed it to clear their goals. Grade would be an EStory is also really generic. It does do its job, but does not excel at it. There are often lacks of consequences (Villages is "burned", you come back 5 minutes later, the village looks like it never happened). You cannot compare it to the carnage Luca Blight did to all those pigs. Those writers ruined an antagonist with Kotomine Kireis japanese voice actor, shame on them. B- at best, probably more a flat CBattle system. Slow, lack of real customization, magic and unity attacks are broken to the point of being completely useless. No real challenging battles. And if you remember that one trailer 3 years ago where you saw the battle against the Kraken. Just look on youtube for the actual gameplay of that battle and compare...Flat DCharacter Design and Sprites, are one of the only things in this game, i really like. Now if only these characters had better writing and actual personalities, most of them are sadly just one character trope type of people. _childDocuments_.review: Die-Hard Suikoden 2 fan here and I would not recommend this game if you are hoping this would match or "succeed" it.  However, it is an ok rpg game if that is what you're looking for.  The story is very shallow, the combat system is boring, and the characters are not memorable. In fact, it felt like they tried too hard to squeeze in the 3rd protagonist, when it would have been just fine or better if they focused on two main protagonists.  There isn't really much else to say.  I spent 85+ hours on the game trying to complete as many of the side quests and mini-games as I could before eventually just wanting to get it over with.  I made sure to get all 120 characters to unlock the best ending.  Got through all the cooking game and 95% of the beigoma.  Unlocked 99% of the castle nodes (had only 3 nodes left), cleared all of the proving grounds on both normal and endless modes, and got most of the playable characters to level 90+.   I would say that this is more of a shell of Suikoden 2 that's without a soul.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give it a 9.5 out of 10 while I have not finished the game just yet.Speaking from a person who has played most of the Suikoden series, this series has exceeded my expectations. It does JRPG well, but it also chooses to make the JRPG experience more of a challenge. Gone are the days in turn-based games where your characters can heal constantly to the point that most of the battles, even boss battles, are a bore. You can fully heal after the battle, but for an initiate, fully healing in battle, especially boss battles, are a challenge without being difficult. MP can be an issue when it comes to playing the game as one isn't able to get MP items to heal up before each battle (it's rarer than getting healing herbs) so that might make characters who focuses more on magic damage to be on the wayside.That being said, auto-battle is possible for easier monsters. It uses a priority system on what you want each of your 6 characters to choose to do when in auto-battleThe story itself is charming. As I said, I haven't finish the game, but for the characters themselves, some are funny, and some of intriguing.

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up playing the Suikoden games, I had a lot of hope for Eiyuden Chronicles to live up to it's mantle of "spiritual successor". Like many people, games in the past 10 years that I have looked forward to have often fallen flat and I've found myself not getting my hopes up anymore. However, Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes has completely blown me away, and really revitalized both my optimism for releasing games, and for gaming in general. The game is beyond any of my expectations. The story is superb, the character's stories, personalities and content is gripping and emotional (though some of their English voice acting is a little cheesy, I'll admit), and the game is packed with so many collectibles, mini-games, resource gathering, and just enough classic "JRPG grinding" to not be overbearing while remaining true to the genre.With over 300+ games in my account, I can honestly say this game is among my very top favorites. I have binged an UNHEALTHY amount of time into this title within the three days I've played it, and I can't remember what the sun looks or feels like, but I find myself nearing the end of the game and DREADING not having more to play. I can only hope that developers take note and follow the example this game has set in staying true to a genre, reviving classics, and publishing a FINISHED product. Cheers!

Maybe it was the limited Kickstarter funding but this game just feels like a hollow shell of Suikoden 2. Environments are bland and empty, there is very little reward for exploration, voice lines and cut scenes in boss fights repeat to the point of exhaustion. There are very few battle music tracks, the writing is childish and most of the characters are one dimensional. Most of the 100 characters you recruit I simply don't want to put in my party.There is no innovation here for the genre, no attempt at improvement, everything is copy pasted from better games., The combat has little depth, can't be sped up and there isn't much leeway when it comes to building out your characters. The inventory limit of 30 is also a head scratcher.  I was hyped for this game, but after 4 years of waiting all I feel is disappointed. Sometimes you just can't beat the originals. RIP.Update: After putting in more time I can say that the game gets better around the 20 hour mark, but the issues I mentioned earlier still persist. When you are 40 hours in and most of your battles still consist of spamming the attack command, you have really screwed up the combat system.Here is an idea, have a more in depth combat system, have bosses that require multiple 6 person parties to battle. Innovate at least a little. It saddens me that some talented artists spent years working on all these impressive sprites only to be let down by stagnant, boring game mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game after almost 90 hours of playing.And I can say that THIS IS ONE OF THE BEST GAMES OF MY LIFE.The Final Duel at the end really gave me goosebumps, even though the final boss was pretty easy.The story is not as deep and dramatic as the previous Suikoden series (especially 1,2 and 5) and is quite short, but the story of this game is quite warm and just as cool and amazing as the previous suikoden.Battle system I really like, colorful, full of action and cool animation.Mini games are the best! I really like the cooking battle that takes the Suikoden 2 system, and the theater is really fun! I can't imagine how complicated it is to create different dialogs and VOs from 120 characters just for dialogs and roles in the theater. 5 thumbs up for the developer!The music is very beautiful and comfortable to listen to repeatedly, the world is also very beautiful and the classic impression is so pronounced, making me want to explore every side to find treasures or characters.In conclusion, this game is very worthy of the title of JRPG of the year with a score of 9.8/10 from me.Thank you for awakening my childhood soul through this game, I'm really nostalgic for this game, and it's an unforgettable experience to be able to finish this game blindly like back then when we didn't know walkthroughs on the internet.I hope Eiyuden Chronicle will have a sequel, and I will always support your work.Once again, thank you for making such a beautiful game! _childDocuments_.review: This game really could have used more time in the oven. I tried to complete this game since I backed it on Kickstarter...but I just had to put it down right at the end. The main component of this game is tracking down every recruitable hero and never actually use them and just leave them in your town like the pokemon-people they are. This is thankfully the most fun part of the game. Most heroes don't take much effort to recruit so you can get a serotonin boost pretty easily. Some recruits will unlock extra dungeons and features, which is where the mechanic really shines.The story is pretty decent. No big surprises or anything. It felt like a couple of moments were just thrown in there so they could add a few more recruits to the roster. Combat is not fantastic. There is customizability with runes, but most battles up until the end can be easily won with auto. Auto also makes battles go 5 times faster which is super helpful getting through trash mobs.The polish just didn't seem to be here on this game. Dialogue boxes appear before and after fast travel, which can be annoying, mechanics aren't always properly explained, hero hints show up before they can actually be recruited, the mini games don't require much skill but can still be a pain.I have never played a suikoden game. That might be where I'm seeing this game a little differently.  I backed it because I'd heard good things about suikoden, the team was filled with passionate veterans and I was ready for a great new rpg. Unfortunately I got a premium mobile game that didn't really feel all that great. Would love to come back later to play if issues get fixed and the dlc is amazing, but for now I can't recommend this unless you've played all the jrpgs and are desperate for a new one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mess of a game. There's a lot to do, and a lot that resembles Suikoden on surface level, but that's it: it's only a scratch deep. Beyond the initial resemblance, this game fails to reach any of the standards of Suikoden, which is rough, because its connection to the legendary game series is honestly its biggest strength.Voice-Acting Quality is rough. Boss mechanics initially seem interesting but ultimately end up basically being coin flips or hastily slapped together mechanics, fittingly named 'gimmicks', than any sort of engaging means of gameplay. The story is forgettable, most of the game is designed to be played on auto-battle, even on normal difficulty, and what little genuine innovation there is in the form of some of the non-battle mechanics is frustratingly drowned by vague or non-existent information, necessary in order to engage in them properly. I can't count how many times I went through excessive tutorials, reading every line, only to find out that the one bit of information that  already apparent was, for some reason, left out.Chase all that with the fact that the map design doesn't facilitate ease of travel, nor does it seem like that gets much easier over time, and you have a boring, uninspired slogfest of half-baked gameplay that is riding on the coattails of a much beloved, unfortunately very dead game series.RIP Suikoden. We miss you.

_childDocuments_.review: Spiritual successor to the Suikoden series.I love this game but it has it's issues. The character stats are all over the place making some characters completely unusable which is a real shame. Magic minus healing a few buff is completely useless until end game with the vast majority of your damage coming from basic attacks (even for the "magic users") The mini games are mostly based on pure luck and don't offer much of a reward other than a distraction from the main story.Despite all that there is a lot to love. Vast majority of the characters, personality and design are fantastic.Graphics are nice and the music is amazing. Really takes me to being a kid loving JRPGs.Overall I'd give it a solid 7/10. _childDocuments_.review: As a long-time enthusiast of the Suikoden series, I approached this title with a mix of anticipation and high expectations. The game itself is not without merit, boasting solid foundations that could have heralded a solid game. However, the experience is marred by character designs that miss the mark, dialogue that often feels unnecessary, and voice performances that detract rather than enhance. Beautiful sprites/graphics, but poor Level Design (lots of empty corridors and too much back and forth in some of the dungeons). I can't bring myself to recommend this game to anyone outside of those who appreciated the Suikoden serie.Despite these shortcomings, I find myself content with the purchase, supporting the studio with a hopeful eye towards future improvements. I give this game a score of 6/10.I look forward to a sequel that delivers a more refined narrative, improved combat mechanics, and a more polished realization of the game's ambitious features. The potential for greatness is there, and with more mature storytelling and thoughtful execution, the next installment could reach the heights this game aspired to.
