_childDocuments_.review: A good RPG. Unfortunately not a great one. It feels a bit amateur around the edges and lacking some polish in areas. It's more a vision than an actual game. Menus are a pain to go through and unresponsive, combats have a weird delay at the end of the end screen to pop for no good reason, there's a bunch of very questionable design decisions like an equippable accessory to run faster that you feel forced to always have equipped otherwise you waste time on slowly running (the maps are really big compared to most other RPGs so you do want to run fast), the MP vs SP balance feels totally off and casting spells overall feels like a bad idea in almost every situation imaginable.I'm having fun so far with it, and I will edit my review if my view on the game changes drastically but it's a bit unfortunate to see seniors of the industries making such an aggressively average RPG. Artistically it's very inspired: the visual, sounds and lore is quite solid (though audio mixing in english is pretty bad). But then the gameplay feels like it wasn't thought out through at all.As for the alleged bad localisation honestly nerds you really need to go out and touch grass. The localisation isn't remotely bad. Some lines in some instances feel a bit weird: Mio mentionning to Nowa that the golem/boss they just defeated might not be a "him" is often mentioned and while I did found it very weirdly placed because Mio is up to this point very quiet and never teases anyone I didn't minded it too much. In some sense I feel that the english localisation is very "human" if that makes sense. Characters don't feel as much as archetypes as they often do, sometimes they say some weird or cringey stuff but it feels more because the characters are like that rather than the script being cringe. Lian got me annoyed at first but the more you see her interacting with different characters the more she gets charming in the end.Anyway, go touch grass, for real.

They did something that Suikoden had, and made it better.Battle animations are nice. Lots of screen-movement for sure (Maybe too much). And the Environment actions are a fun addition.Items from Bag instead of from equip slots in Battle. Medicines used to basically be after-battle recovery for me, and this opens up options for meI could get gear off of characters who left my party temporarily.Everyone can get runes. There are passive runes that boost stats rather than activate magic or skills.Auto Battle can have priority settings to pre-set what characters do.Party requirements are fluid with the attendant slots, so I have mostly full freedom of my members from the moment i start recruiting. And apparently I can still "recruit" them if I want to have the feeling of getting them again.PostGame Content. Listen, We don't treat Suikoden IV like it exists kay. And this content was challenging and fun.Mock Battles: Yes. War Battles Gameplay. Great Idea! More of this please.New Game+ Carry Over Optional Character Recruitment, but also maintains ability to do the sidwquests to recruit them again if I want.Card Game was a really good minigame.Mock Battles is amazing concept. If I had this in Suikoden 3,4,5, I would be so happy. Biscuit — 05/12/2024 11:55 PMWhat's different?Runes that were like skills now require SP to use em. But they don't seem to have negative effects like you get stunned.You build out your castle. It's nice to see that progress, but it's kinda inconvenient too. When I recruit the item shop owner, I would normally get item shop, but now I have to also build the actual shop too. I'm conflicted on how I feel.Difficulty Modifiers. I played Hard Mode, but the other modifiers don't seem fun to play. I just played Hard because I assumed that other mode would be too easy. And I made the right choice.What feels the same? (And that's fine)Battles have same general feel, but there are differences.Blacksmith/Weapon strengthening is same.What's worse? Attendant slots are a step down from Suikoden V reserve slots. Can't freely swap characters during nor outside battle. Can't have multiple supports.Duels suck. It's a glorified cutscene. I want gameplay.Magic Runes. Healing via Runes sucks. The high cost to use magic leads me to not use it unless against a boss. This mainly due to lack of renewable MP healing items. I either had to trek it back to an Inn or go without.Mass Gearing through storage is more annoying. When I've got gear in inventory or storage, I can't compare it to my whole list of characters to see if anyone benefits. I have to check each individual to check if it's an improvement. When buying gear, I don't have this problem. If it wasn't super rare gear, i just sold it and re-bought it to have this easy visual of who improves or not.Main Story War Battles suck. It's a glorified cutscene. I want gameplay. Suikoden 2 War battles sucked, and this reminds me a lot of it. It was a nice attempt to have a minigame of mock battles, but all they showed me was that the war battles are not that good. I liked the thought of the mock battles though.Locking character recruitment behind minigame grind. And not just a minigame, but multiple minigames. Forcing players to grind the minigame to enjoy the full character list is not a good idea. Make players win once. Maybe 3 times. Put equipment or items behind the grind. 35 Card Games minimum to recruit? 20 cooking battles? ## Beigoma Battles? I've played every minigame in every title, and even though I ENJOYED these games, locking characters behind them have made me dislike them. (Cept the card game, that ♥♥♥♥ is awesome)Unite attacks. They require SP and would be a random guess as to it's effectiveness. Single target Unite attacks universally sucked. Multiple target ones can somewhat be better. There is almost never a reason I used a Unite Attack. My game gripes?Minimap should let me see the entire dungeon. If it has multiple areas, let me see it. I've been through them. Shouldn't be difficult to have that in. Seems overlooked.Resting at the Inn only heals your current party? Why? Because Suikoden had that? Just heal everybody. Swapping back in a character only to remember they had injuries makes me take another trip to the inn. It was bad then and bad now.No dialogue text options? I hate it when dialogue slowly reveals itself. I want the full sentence available, and am surprised that isn't an option. Most games have this sorta thing.The translation was uhh.... passable..... It got the job done. Let's hope for better next time. I'm not a big fan of localization putting in a bunch of stuff that didn't exist. I understand the Japanese jokes, and I understand places where they fill in some English jokes. But if it's too noticeable, then it's not good.Story overall seems lacking. No real suspense, story twists. Villian was boring. I basically knew nothing about Aldric Dux other than he wants Rune Powers. Half the time I was playing the game, I forgot the who the Dux really is other than "bad guy".Split story chapter. Suikoden 3 had this where you basically got forced with party members for the whole chapter. It sucked then, it sucks now. Let me have that freedom to choose at least SOME members. What was the point of the Attendant slots if I can't even use em for this part. There's a large opportunity here to get the player to use different members here by restricting who is available, but instead restricted basically all characters from being available.Random things:Castle Shops. Have these people ever heard of windows? Lanterns everywhere. Darkness envelops them.Why would the Castle Lvl 1 have an option to build Hot Springs, but you can't recruit the character to build it until you level up the castle more? Why have it available then?Water Runeshards. How does a Runeshard Tier1 Water heal the same amount as lowest tier medicine, but cost 5 times more, and only fit half the amount of bag space.

_childDocuments_.review: [Review written after completing the game - 80 Hours of play time]If you have been following the development of this game and hoped for a spiritual successor to Suikoden, I can confidently say this game fulfills those hopes.  Eiyuden captures the original tone, characters, exploration and world building of the Suikoden games.  With many references to the original games (and a number of other JRPGs/anime).  I would say Eiyuden is closest to Suikoden 1 in tone, world design and progression.  But with plenty of events and characters being obvious nods to Suikoden II and III as well.  It is a love letter to all the Suikoden games written and created by Murayama.If you are not familiar with the original Suikoden games, then you're in for something very unique.  I won't go into too much detail as not to spoil the experience.  But basically, Suikoden is one of the most anime styled games you'll ever play.  Even more than other JRPGs.  The closest comparison I can make is series like Chrono, Utawarerumono or Valkyria Chronicles.  But despite the use of common anime tropes and cliches on the surface, Suikoden is still something that stands out as unique.  The experience of Suikoden is not to just play through the story.  It's about exploring and living within the world.  Collecting a huge cast of colorful characters with their own quirks and mannerisms.  And so much stuff to do outside of the main story, you can spend the majority of the game time on side quests.  In short, Suikoden is about world building.  And everything I just described about Suikoden also applies to Eiyuden.With all that said, I do need to address the elephant in the room.  Yes, like a lot of other reviews are saying, the localization in this game is lackluster.  It's not because of any "woke" stuff like some people are complaining about.  I've played the whole game and haven't seen a single "woke" thing in it.  The problem is they took massive liberties with the English translation.  Going far beyond flipping sentence structure or translating a joke.  Many lines of dialogue are just flat out altered.  Sometimes so bad that they're actually saying the total opposite of what the original Japanese meant.  Other times, full of embellishment, with bloated dialogue that changes both the tone of the scene and the personality of the character talking.  This is most obvious with the character Lian, the character so many English players have grown to hate.  But having played the game with Japanese voices on, I can say her lines of dialogue in the original Japanese are nothing like the English translation.  She's a completely different character.  And this happens to varying degrees with other characters in the game.Of course this is nothing new.  Sadly, many Japanese games get this treatment in western localization.  Stuff like Fire Emblem and Dragon Quest are even worse.  But even though other series have been more excessive in their alterations, that still doesn't excuse the localization for this game.  I have to call it out.  If for no other reason than I hope the developers will read this review and not repeat it in any potential sequel.Outside the localization, there are some gameplay and pacing issues.  Some of which have already been addressed with patches and others that the developers have promised to fix down the road.  So if you're reading this review long after the games launch, I would assume most of the issues have been addressed.  I'll also say that I didn't run into anything game breaking when playing the game myself.With that unpleasantness out of the way, would I recommend this game?  Heck yeah I would!  Even if you have never played a Suikoden game in your life, but you're a fan of JRPGs, I really think this game would appeal to you.  Or if you love RPGs that focus on exploration and world building.  Or if you love anime.  And if you end up liking this game, I'd recommend playing Suikoden as well.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid start spoiled by a horribly drawn-out endgame. Overall not a terribly unique game in the sea of great JRPGs we have access to, but I would still recommend it to anyone looking specifically for a Suikoden-like. - 55 hours - Fantastic. 10/10. - Good - Overall very good, though the script is often lacking. - Decent JRPG story. Nothing gamechanging, and does drag quite a lot. - Basic JRPG, doesn't add anything to the genre. - Easy. Rarely do you ever have to worry about element/type advantage in combat. Money starts pouring in after a few chapters and you can buy an infinite stock of the highest tier healing items. - Mixed bag, pulled down primarily by a severe lack of user input or skill required. Card game is incredibly easy but at least there's user input. Spinning top minigame is terrible in every way. Racing minigame is at least cute, but takes too long to resolve. War minigame takes  and doesn't require any skill.The first 10 hours of my playthrough were . The game has all the classic charm of a Suikoden-like: you recruit the people, you get the town/castle, you upgrade the buildings, etc. The plot started out interesting enough to keep engaged, though it is your basic "bad guy empire" story.The next 20 hours of the playthrough were . Recruit more and more unique NPCs, upgrade more and more facilities at the base, unlock more and more areas as the story progresses. A decent loop of plot->explore->upgrade->plot that kept me engaged.The final 25 hours of the playthrough were . Aside from a few comedic interactions between some of the more lovable recruited NPCs, the final half of my playthrough felt both rushed and drawn out. There's a 50/50 chance that each next plot point will either thrust you into a 2 hour block of dialog (maybe broken up with a war minigame, which is just dialog with animations) or a dungeon that takes 2 hours to complete because it's a series of long, long,  hallways with a thousand random encounters.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that I have been waiting to come out since it was announced that they were making it. As a huge fan of Suikoden I been looking for a RPG that would scratch that itch and even though this game is basic, it defiantly did scratch that itch. For those of you who just want a quick answer, yes I would recommend buying this game and for the rest of you please enjoy my detailed review. Graphics/Environment: 7/10The game does look good with a classic RPG vibe. It is a 3D world and characters are 2D sprites. You have an over world where you travel on a big map to towns or dungeons and then there is the town or dungeon itself when you enter it. The over world makes the world feel vast and large which I like because it makes the world feel more real instead of having everything piled up on top of each other. The bad part is it is big so until you unlock fast travel, which is a little deeper in the game than I would have liked, it means going anywhere for any reason will take time. Once you unlock fast travel it is the classic once you been there once, you can go there again.  Even on the PC the graphics are not perfect. You still have pop in and the occasional texture issue. They are all small issues and just need a bit of polish on the dev side to take care of. I did like the light and water effects and the rune magic looks good as well. The way some things walk/move is a bit weird, especially the way some monster that walk to you in combat, but I got a laugh out of it more than anything. Sound: 8/10Not really to much to say here. Everything sounds good and is synced well. All of the sound effects are solid. The reason it has such a high score is the voice acting. It is top notch and never do I feel like they phoned it in. The music is just OK. It gets the job done and there is a lot of it but there is only one or two songs that are a really good and stick out. Story: 6/10 I hate to say it but the story is just OK. Without giving away any spoilers, the game really does not invoke any emotion into the player. The game plays it very safe in that regard. The villains are all lacking something and even the insults are lacking. To give you an example one of the villains wears a mask so the person in your party calls them mask as an insult which is not much of an insult. The villains have no edge to them is the best way I can describe them. They do very little to make you hate them. One of them does something that should have made you hate him about a quarter of the way into the game but the game itself doesn't follow through with it. I know that sounds weird but if you play the game and get to that point, you will know exactly what I mean. The only thing that evokes any emotion is the ending and even that is not as good as it should have been or could have been. The story is lacking but it was good enough to keep me play until the end. Combat:9/10Best part of the game is the combat system. It is a classic turn based RPG and you can use normal physical attacks, magic that cost MP, special attacks that use SP, items that can heal and later use magic attacks and finally gimmicks. In some boss battles you will have gimmicks. If a boss has this it will be under normal attack and it allows you to use the environment in some way to get an advantage. Like using rubble to dodge a super attack and take no damage or using a crane to drop a bolder on the boss for big damage. Some bosses don't have any gimmicks but the ones that do are all different and they all help you in some way to beat a boss. There is also a gimmick in random encounters but those are just to open treasure chests. The other cool thing is some characters have different things they can do for the defend slot. Most just defend but some charge to make their next attack more powerful, others evade so they have a higher chance of dodging an attack, others have magic shields that stay up until they are attacked and so on. The battles give you lots of options especially once you recruit most of the people. Another thing they did really well for combat is controller rumble. It happens rarely so when it does happen, you know it is for something important.Final Score 7/10The game is solid, fun and defiantly worth while. Like I said earlier, if you are a fan of Suikoden then this is a must play. With over 100 people to recruit into your army, you always have someone new to look for and to rotate in and out of your squad. The only other complaint I have is the mini game Beigoma. It is basically Beyblade and the game forces you to play it a lot if you want to recruit everyone. The reason I did not deduct for this mini game is because some people like it and if you are one of them then playing it a bunch is no issue. I did not like it at all and don't want to “let it spin” ever again but odds are I will if I decide to tackle new game plus. This game does have multiple endings and you will more than likely have to play through more than once to get all the endings and Achievements if you are the type of person that goes for that. The good part is that does add to its replay ability especially on a game where one play through can easily be over 70 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Going to review this as someone who has never played the Suikoden series. I saw their Kickstarter campaign and waited years to play this.It is most definitely a love letter to JRPG fans. The tropes, the characters, the grind. If you're an avid fan of classic JRPGs, you'll feel right at home and the typical pain points for most people such as a one dimensional story of good versus evil won't really bother you.Things I liked:- Coming from Octopath Traveler, I really loved how they combined the 2D sprites with 3D elements. I'm not saying it's out of this world, but what I am saying I found myself admiring the scenery and combat sequences a lot, especially during the duels.- Classic JRPG music and motifs. I found myself dozing off in Hishahn (Eiyuden's Japanese themed city) because of the visuals and music.- There are so many side activities and easter eggs. The card game was surprisingly fun with its own booster packs for you to collect cards. Anyone who has listened to Yu-Gi-Oh! in Japanese will love the voice acting. The beigona (their version of Beyblade) was interesting, but outside of the obvious anime references, it fell a little short for me. Of course there's a racing mini-game here and while the gimmick is fun, I can't really say I enjoyed it because I lagged badly. I love games that allow you build a base camp or town that grows over time as the story develops and you can do that here, too! There's even a little shokugeki action.- Combat is ENJOYABLE and there is a lot of depth. With 120 recruitable characters and different battle mechanics, you can really customize your dream team. With the attendant feature, you don't even have to keep the main character in the main party. There's also army combat, which is basically a chessboard auto-battler. It was enjoyable, but I think it'll turn off a lot of players.Things I disliked:- With so many recruitable characters, gear management is atrocious. No way to sort through them easily. Leveling their weapons to max is painful, but I guess I shoulda been doing it as I played.- The lens and runes system really felt lackluster, imho. Some characters are limited by how many runes they can use and I would've the ability to expand that with an expensive or hard-to-get item. Also again with so many recruitable characters, the rune management system is ATROCIOUS, too.- Maybe I missed it, maybe it's not there, but I expected there to be secret bosses or hidden items because it's a love letter to JRPG fans. There were a couple, but not enough to warrant exploration.- You have 120 recruitable characters. You have 6 in the main party, 1 for support, and 3 for attendants. After you upgrade everything, you can send a max of 3 teams of 5 to go gather materials. Why are there not more options for idle characters to participate? Surely, they can go fish? Do guard duty? Maybe station them at certain stations for bonuses or discounts? Just seems like a giant waste. I don't know if it's a $50 tag to be honest, but it offers enough of a novelty experience that I enjoyed it and don't regret it buying it. I feel like with how many things this game can do, the modding scene could have a payday with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was drawn in to this game's Kickstarter with the promise of delivering a solid Suikoden-esque JRPG that i've been looking for so long, and as it turns out, that premise alone is a big problem, even though the man himself was on board the project (RIP Murayama-san) we were perhaps blind by the fact that perhaps a promise alone is not enough and is perhaps especially true when it comes to KS projects, often times, the promise won't match the end product, and it was so the case for so many projects that i've backed on KS, but this one is especially painful to process ... I wanna start by saying that Suikoden is very close and dear to my heart, as it is a title that i grew up with, literally, i played the second game first and then the first when i was perhaps 9 years old, i couldn't understand about 3/4 of the dialogues so i ended up mostly playing it for the gameplay alone, which, for an RPG at the time was pretty novel to me, growing up i often times came back to it and as i did, bit by bit with the help of my brother and friends, i started understanding the dialogue and the story more, when i finally put the pieces together and experienced the true ending of S2, i realized then that the game was special to me and that is why, i believe, is a big problem, it is difficult for me to accept and find  a suitable match to S2, not just for me but for a studio to recreate something similar, or at least, reminiscent, maybe i'm being unfair and perhaps that was never the intent to recreate a spiritual successor of S2, but the similarities or at least, the formula, it's very OG Suikoden, but alas, the end result is not good : The gameplay itself is very much alike Suikoden, with a few elements that are novel to Eiyuden for example the SP points, on paper having a resource for mostly physical tech sounds pretty good, but it goes out of the window if we consider that this game is horribly unbalanced, the balance issue in this game is so painful that severely tests your nevers, ill give you an example, you start the game with Mio, Mio likes to fight head on however ... Mio hits like a wet noodle, while MC does 60 damage, Mio does 30 and doesn't do much else, her HPs are low, her defenses are low as well and doesn't have ANY techniques (SP skills) or at least not until a few levels, as you start recruiting more Heroes you come across similar cases, meet Ivy, she's a small girl with two giant metal arms, you'd expect she'd hit like a truck but ... again, Francesca, my healer-mage hits for 100, Ivy hits for ... 50, and she's slow as heck, has a terrible Rune for magick and a technique that lets her deal 60 damage instead of 50 at 50% chance to miss, many such cases, speaking of Magic, about 1/3 of the cast of heroes are spellcasters and magic in this game sucks for a number of reasons : 1) spells are costly and the mana is a resource unlike HP, harder to replenish2) there are a few exceptions, but most of the low level offensive spells are practically useless for damage alone because they tend to do very low damage in contrast with the expenditure of MP3) when someone is a "Mage" that usually means that they are slow and more fragile which translates to having said Mage dying a horrible death, that adds up at a cost of both turns and items, so in the end if almost anyone any support runes or offensive spells (mostly dark or fire) , might as well integrate 6 fighters into your party and you'll be fine. 4) magic in this game is not that exciting, for support Water is king, the higher rarity Water rune is less efficent but is still useful, the rest aren't that good, Earth is worthless, Wind is not good and Light is a mixbag, for Offense either Fire or Dark, Dark is kinda busted because of sleep, and fire is ... well, Fire, solid overall, so there isn't much variety, there's no summoning spells, there's a few wacky spells like the teleportation spells, but you can't mix up runes like in Suikoden 2. And finally, going back to the techniques, very few of those actually stand up from the crowd, SP is mostly a resource that you stuck in conjunction with the passive that adds damage % x SP points, which is very telling. The story .... eh ... the story, i don't wanna go into too much details, but, in my opinion the pegi 12 did this game more harm than good, infact, Suikoden was a ruthless game, not on par with Vandal Hearts but, very close, in contrast Eiyuden plays it safe, way too safe, the end result is kinda bland, once you reach a certain point during the story, it goes downhill because there's no tension and hardly and stakes on the line, because it is hard to care for anyone really when MC is a glorified 'Yes Man' , the MC is literally drawn into the story because he likes to "meddle", Seign on the other hand was very well written, his story goes into a full arc and he's much more of a protagonist than Nowa or Marisa, Marisa hardly matters infact.as a final note, it really pains me to give this game a thumbs down, given how much i love the work of Murayama-san, part of me kinda feels bad that he passed away before the game's release, but on the other hand, i don't think we shouldn't be able to criticize this game because of the man's passing, other than that, the translation is terrible, but personally, there's more glaring issues than the zoomer terminology used in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: I’ve spent *a lot* more time with this game. Most games play their entire hand at the start. Refreshingly, like the days of old, this is a game you need to commit to before you get to enjoy it. I’d even argue the first 15 hours are a slog, especially if you’re exploring the systems. However it means the game gets so much better with every hour beyond that. The game hides QoL behind gameplay features which you unlock in the mid-game. Upgrading your castle feels so important because of it, unlocking new rooms and shops almost feels like a skill/progression tree.Not to mention the sheer variety and volume in recruitable allies (my advice? Play with a guide for the first 15 hours, or at least until you unlock the diviner who is like a vague in-game wiki). The combat options also open up with allies, and an appreciated amount of unique runes and combos. So yes, the combat isn’t all an auto slog the entire time. It’s even kind of fun to grind again, with so many ways to get gold, and a generous exp share formula for weak allies.This game is almost twice as fun now that I’m further in. It could even be my RPG of the year if it keeps up the momentum it has earned. The castle has so many layers to the upgrade, anything but superficial or shallow like so many modern day games.-Initial review:This isn’t “Suikoden but for the modern day” - it’s just Suikoden, dated flaws and all. So expect some pretty awful QoL and combat balancing, as well as very obscure questing and exploration.The first few hours are a slog and I’m sure many people will refund during it. However, the game picks up once you get to your first real dungeon: the abandoned mine, after a recruitment run in the first open map area.In my opinion, it definitely isn’t up to current standards of what a game should offer and how polished it is, but that never stopped us loving the game it’s openly based on. So if you can look past that and temper your expectations, then you’ll get a lot of comfy nostalgic feelings playing this game.You’ll resort to using ‘auto’ in most random encounters as even on hard, every enemy dies in two basic attacks. However the boss fights are when the game really shines and the combat system can be appreciated.Been keeping myself from getting spoiled on all the recruitable characters, but even of the ones I’ve met so far, they’re a fantastic bunch of likeable, quirky and eclectic teammates with some stellar voice work to tie it all together.This is a very tentative recommendation, in fact I almost came close to not recommending it just to prevent disappointment, but thankfully most reviewers agree on the game’s shortcomings.Current score is a 5 out of 10, but we’ll see how feel by the end of the game where I’ll update my review.

Rune slots are a mess (70% of the cast are bottlenecked by inability to use higher level runes or lacking any kind of variety in the kind they can equip) with maybe 15% or less having any signature abilities to set them apart which is not helped by the sub par damage on combo/hero attacks. Difficulty doesn't exist even on hard things are just spongy and the strategies (if you want to call rinse repeat attacking and healing strategy) remain exactly the same. The writing is particularly dull. Having spent over 70 hours playing I can remember only a few lines Nowa said in the entire game that got a chuckle out of me while most of it is mashworthy and consists of them discussing or flashing back to something that happened moments ago because none of the characters have any other fleshed out connection that what we see the vast majority of the time. Add an easily missable character, a handful of poorly fleshed out and fairly unfun minigames, and I can tell you that while this game is modeled after Suikoden the closest it gets other than the coat of paint is in mimicking some of the things Suikoden got wrong. Dragon's Dogma 2 was the biggest let down of the year by far but this was a slow agonizing burn, because with all that it is this should be better.

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes is the perfect successor not only to Suikoden, but to everything the JRPG fan loves from ages past. This is a game I have waited so long to witness and explore and in the 12 hours I've put in so far, it's been everything I hoped for.Eiyden Chronicle has brought the world of Allraan to life through some beautiful 2D and 3D art styles that are strong reminders of the classics brought into the new age. The addition of brilliant voice acting brings the characters and personalities to life allowing for a deeper connection to those around you and narrative.The mix of play style between turn based team combat, the grid based War system and duelling all keep you on your toes for resolving conflicts, even the boss battles throw in Gimmicks to stop the battles feeling like nothing but a button mash. The War system has always been something I enjoyed from Suikoden, letting your characters take the lead into an all out battle with your army rather than the simple turned based fight.One of my favourite aspects of Suikoden was having a player base to look after and a home for your recruits, I won't spoil the details, but for me it always made the narrative so much stronger in building up bonds with your characters and really helped show they were more than just fighters for your party.Overall, as a huge fan of the classic JRPG games. I can say that this will go down as one of the classics itself for both those who grew up with games like Suikoden and Vandal Hearts to those who are stepping in for the first time. This might be a successor, but it's leaving it's own mark on the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: While I generally enjoyed Eiyuden Chronicle, there are some minor and major caveats. Some are bugs which kill the immersion, especially in the late game. Others are baked into the games essence.However, there are certain aspects which the game nails. First of all, is the artstyle. Incredibly, it mixes 3 different style into one game: pixel art, cell shaded and 3D. Next, are the characters. Most of them are endeering and can offer valuable insights.The sound is also very good.Some middle-good things.The combat feels satisfying and lackluster at the same time, especially in the early and end. This goes even further because of how certain characters are balanced in combat. As some do not have any reason to be in any party, except for making the game harder.The story can also be pretty hit or miss. For most of the part, it is fine. Political intrigues, spies, strategy and betrayal are on the daily order. However, There are some aspects which are completely undercooked. For once, Marisa doesn't feel like a supposed main character. This is most likely due to how late she is introduced. Additionally, there is a double standard in the very last scene unaddressed. Additionally, there are some loose ends, which feel especially unrewarding. The epilogue does say something about that, but it is nearly not enough.The bad things:The minigames. All optional minigames are shallow and badly designed. The cardgame is monotone, beyblade has no explanation and the cooking game suffers massively from bugs. The racing games, both birbegg and ship, are fine.There are some issues with the translation at certain points. The epilogue has some massive grammar errors, but that can be overlooked, also fixable. But the cooking game makes zero sense. When the judge wants something sweet, I would guess that a Lollipop would be nice for them. But it is possible that it can be connected with the current bug in that minigame, as apparently every dish counts as if it where the appetizer.In the end, Eiyouden Chronicle is a very old school JRPG. For the most part, it is nice to have a modern version of that. But some Quality of Life things should be considered to be added as some things don't really impact the game experience in a positive light.

_childDocuments_.review: There's so much to love here for JRPG lovers in general but especially fans of Suikoden 1&2. In fact, there's a lot that it does better than Suikoden, particularly quality of life changes suited for the modern era, such as having a reserves section of the party to store mandatory party members that are typically unused. The game also takes inspiration from Octopath Traveler in its art direction and some aspects of the gameplay, such as the SP system.Don't let the reviews about localization fool you, Eiyuden Chronicle has fantastic voice acting and the writing is spot-on. Localizations are not supposed to be a direct translation of the source material, instead adapting the material to fit the cultural norms of where the game is being played. In that regard, there are no complaints. Furthermore, there's just so many lines that are voice-acted that you could probably play the main story without the dialogue text boxes and follow the entire thing. It's incredibly impressive and lets you focus on the beautiful animations and expressive art rather than splitting your attention by reading.The story of political intrigue and the horrors of war found in Suikoden can also be found here. Some of the depictions of evil are toned down some (Luca Blight remains unparalleled), but there are many shocking and heartwrenching moments regardless. I never felt like it wasn't going as far as it should in providing a captivating narrative.I strongly recommend playing it through to the end, even if you don't go for completion like I did, since stuff like Beigoma and the cooking battles can become tedious. The card battler is actually pretty fun, though underdeveloped; I wish the attention on the card battler and Beigoma were switched, but alas.Very excited for the upcoming DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE EDIT: 9/2024-  I put the game down for a few months to allow for QoL updates.  Happy to report that the steam deck is no longer giving me long load screens and its basically instant now. It looks like they optimized the sound and loading issues.  Also you can turn off the blur/bloom effect in the UI. ------------------------Ive played hundreds of RPGs from the SNES/PS1 Era- This game was made for my generation.Pros:  Great Story, Classic Suikoden Feel, Controls good, Beautiful Art and music. Voice acting.  I waited years for another Suikoden 1 & 2 type game to come out and I finally got it.   Its a great game.  Buy it!  Ill play it through the end, but I'm going to list more cons because I want the devs to see its not hard to fix and I'm sure a lot of other people will mention some of these Cons:  Loading Times on Steam Deck for Combat,  ( Fixable) - Choppy character animations don't match rest of game's polish. Examples:  Nowas running animation on the loading screen has more animation frames than in game movement, it just looks choppy when running across the map.  I get the 2d/3d theme but it feels like there could be a little more fluid. The screen BLUR or Bloom effect when im 5 feet away from a shopkeeper and i cant see him unless I move within 2 feet of him when the entire screen is just the guys front counter.  Let me see where I'm going please, that effect is WAY overused, please let us turn it off.  It gives me a headache. ( Edit you can turn it off) Inventory management needs a little rework ( UI)  There needs to be a better system to equip/optimize multiple people and the storage limitations and manual storing of items makes me feel like I'm playing Diablo 4 again.  Why are there limitations on how many stacks of a herb i can carry?   if its a difficulty thing then just turn it on for hard modes, most of us are playing for the story and convenience.  In the beginning of the game constant story-line interruptions break up the flow of the game especially with random battles. ( Partly fixable for handlheld users if you optimize loading it wont be so bad) Example:  Take 5 steps, cut-scene, then combat, then ( loading screen for 3 seconds if you are on steam deck and 7 seconds for switch) then loading screen to next zone, then cut-scene after 5 steps again, then loading time, then combat, then loading time, then... All while I'm like " JUST GET ME TO A SAVE POINT PLEASE" Why are there save points?  Let us save anywhere in town or outside and put save points on each floor or make a quick-save for steam deck users. Its 2024, we can have the best of both worlds if you add this.If you can tolerate those annoyances which are mostly patch-able if the devs care what I have to say then get it.     Game runs flawless on a full gaming PC but the handhelds need some serious help with asset loading.   Also they shoehorned the English dub with way too much dialog, kind of like my review :)  PS: Lian makes me cringe every time she talks lol but that's character design and they nailed it. All of these comments are out of love and respect for the dev team, Im happy with the way it is, but everyone is a critic and your biggest fans are your biggest critics as well.  I didn't get a chance to join the kickstarter or be a beta tester, I wish I had the chance and time I'm sure there's gotta be people out there with the same viewpoints as me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more than just a spiritual successor to the famed Suikoden series of games, it is able to stand on its own while hitting all the notes of Suikoden, and with good reason! I have avoided spoilers but it features over 100 recruitable characters, each so far has fun and interesting personalities and fun moments. So far it features about 3 different mini games, A spinning top battle game, card game and culinary battle mini game. Unsure if there is more, this review is written at about 17 hours of game play.If you enjoyed the Suikoden series even in passing this game will be for you, combat isnt fact paced. It handles exactly like Suikoden right down to the combo attacks, My only gripe so far would be that the Lens system for magic misses some of the charm and awe that the runes had from Suikoden but thats a shallow gripe based on the aesthetic of the Lens vs the Runes that I loved so dearly. If you pine for an ps1 era rpg this will certainly scratch that itch, The story is solid, combat is interesting and many bosses WILL put you on your arse if you dont take them seriously. Music is good but not great, I havent heard any really memorable tunes yet that stick with me  but again only 17 hours in. I leave this review with one last note! There is a fishing minigame :P Its not bad, Just cast the rod and press A when a fish bites and bam, you catch it. No epic fish battles like Breath of fire 2 or Stardew valley! _childDocuments_.review: I wrote too much below so tl;dr: Worth buying on sale. The city building is good, combat is nothing more than core JRPG combat with some bosses having battle gimmicks (unique actions you can take instead of attacking), there are some bad systems but most of them are just mid (plain, generic, shallow and/or unoriginal).Context: This game's subreddit randomly showed up to me one day and the gimmick of having over 100 recruitable characters was appealing enough to hook me in. I don't really play JRPGs outside of the monster collector subgenre, but have played a few indie JRPGs this year. I didn't participate in the theatre minigame, the egg race minigame and the boss rush mode.This is one of those times I wish there was a 'Maybe' recommendation option. The game is fine, a 6 or maybe 7 our of 10 experience. If the 120 recruitable heroes gimmick is appealling to you, buy it on sale.The Good:The city building coupled with the recruitment of heroes feels great. Watching the city grow was one of the best parts of the game.The battle gimmicks are nice, probably the highlight of combat. Even then having moved onto other JRPGs even this feels boring.The Bad:The Duel system. I figured it out during the first fight, pick Attack or Counter based on what is said before the round starts. However - and maybe this is unique to the English localization - it feels impossible to decipher which to pick half the time. You either trial and error it until you map out the correct options, or jsut look up a guide. It's a shame this system sucks so much because the duel scenes are really awesome.Beigoma. A minigame that relies on you getting rare drops from certain enemies to even begin playing. It's insane that the starter beigoma cannot beat anyone. Additionally it boils down to an unexplained rock paper scissors system + bigger number wins. Finally, you can usually tell within the first second if you'll win or lose, even then you cannot surrender and all 3 rounds have to play out in a best of 3, so often you'll be up two rounds but still ahve to waste time on a meaningless third round.The CCG minigame is Marvel Snap without any interesting cards. Fundamentally good but like everything else in this game it is very shallow.The difficulty. Played on hard mode, it was a little hard at the beginning thanks to how much mana spells cost early, but later there is no difficulty. There are a couple bosses with AoE chance to sleep attacks that can be annoying.The Mid:Everything else. But I'll just talk about heroes, runes and combat.The heroes, obviously, mostly have one note personalities. You can't expect anything else from a game with 120 heroes, however I was hoping that each character would at least be a little unique in combat. However half of the heroes have 0 unique gameplay abilities and those who do just have "AoE attack" or "Single target big damage attack", the most mechanically complex character is probably the main character, who boild down to having a mult hit attack that's terrible against armored enemies and a blunt damage attack that is good at armored enemies. This lack of unique gameplay mechanics + the complete lack of balancing means you're just better of using the best characters in each role, with a few exceptions.The above issue is mostly due to runes, there isn't a single cool rune in the game. Everyone is +stats, passives (conditional +stats), skills (an attack that costs SP and has a generic additional effect) and spells (3 abilities that cost mana. Can deal damage with a generic additional effect, buff, debuff or heal, some AoE, some single target). That's it.The combat is insanely boring, it's the same combat we've seen in JRPGs for decades, there is nothing new. Attack, then big attack when you have the SP, Healers heal when they need to, defend when a big attack is coming and use the gimmick at the right time. The gimmicks are the only thing that isn't the core of JRPG combat and the only sometimes show up. There are other issues too, buffs feel useless, buffing your party's magic defense is a situational ability normally, but in this game you're better off just healing the damage. Hero comboes are also mostly useless, only the AoE ones seem to be worth using for mobbing.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand the negative feedback from some players. Asking for a game based on an old JRPG style will naturally result in gameplay that involves classic elements, such as early struggles with inventory management and long "back-and-forth" travels. The story itself revolves around resistance and the typical rags-to-riches grind. The game will be quite punishing to new players in the beginning, to give a sense of progression as you upgrade your inventory and travel methods. . The developers and the author chose not to change this approach because they aimed to recapture the essence of the Suikoden series, which they successfully did.While the game perfectly satisfied my JRPG and Suikoden cravings, they made it easier, and the story feels lighter.The villains in this game lack the same level of violence, which reduces the satisfaction of defeating them. In the Suikoden series, you often saw gory scenes, like important characters getting stabbed during cutscenes, fueling your desire to defeat the villain. Eiyuden fails to capture that intensity.Remember in Suikoden how some characters could only be recruited during specific events and interactions? You had to trigger these events before progressing the story, or the characters would become inaccessible for a while. I want that kind of anxiety of having to use ALOT of saving slots for each chapters. Eiyuden doesn't follow this approach.One thing that annoys me about this game is how you can still travel to towns that have been captured by the enemy. In Suikoden, you couldn't enter towns that were under enemy control, which was important for the story's sense of revolution. It made you feel the pressure from the opposing side and added to the planning of character recruitment. Eiyuden misses this element, which detracts from the overall experience.Overall, This satisfy my craving as it captures the essence of suikoden. ALSO, FYI. They will be adding DLC for side stories of the characters, which I think is very good!

_childDocuments_.review: One word sums up my experience with this game.Disappointing.Positives :- Looks great (blends old school and new quite well)- Good music- GREAT Japanese voice acting- Very humorous at the start of the adventure (first 10 or so hours) that slowly fades away but still occasionally made me laugh- Recruiting 120 characters was a great challenge and I found it to be enjoyable Negatives:- The story and the characters and the overall feel of the game. It was a huge let down. - The 120 characters are fun to acquire - but not to actually play. The overwhelming majority of them are totally useless. I used the same 10 characters or so for 99% of the game. I even spent time building up EVERYONE and yeah - most of them suck.- A lot of systems and mini games are not fully fleshed out. They end up being cumbersome.- Almost NO quality of life features. I wanted a fast forward/skip button SO BAD. Some aspects were painfully slow.- Lots of useless dialog. Childish and pointless the majority of the time. I eventually stopped caring what the cast had the say. That's never a good sign in an RPG.- Strange disconnects with the story.- Poor inventory system. - Illusion of a great battle system and options - seems good at first until you get deeper into it. The magic system was quite lame.TL/DRI appreciate the ambition and goals they had in mind when they set out to make this but the end result wasn't up to par. Buy it on sale if you're itching for Suikoden of old.6 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game more than I actually like it...There's just enough going right that I'm interested in finishing it out, but there's just some things wrong that I find irritating.  For example, during the recruitment of an early character, the guards you are speaking to suddenly have completely different voices and accents.  The translation of the game itself is also questionable-to-bad, particularly with some of your earlier companions. There's also glaring animation issues.  For some characters as they walk, particularly walking in the Y-direction (up/down), they will kick their legs out at an angle as if they are all bow-legged.  It's extremely jarring.  The kangaroo hops are also very janky, especially if they stop moving mid-hop.  Then there's the battle camera...  The way the camera shifts around in battle is a bit maddening.  In Octopath Traveler, it happens on big events (full Boost attacks, etc).  For Eiyuden Chronicles, it'll move around when you go through the process of selecting each hero's actions.  And that takes time... which slows down the already antiquated, slow-pace of this battle system.  This is a recurring theme, where a lot of the menu changes seem kinda slow.All in all... it's fine.  The game isn't a masterpiece, but I'm not putting on some rose-tinted glasses thinking Suikoden I and II are perfect either.  If released today, they would be equally clunky.  But that's all it is.  Just fine.  Not spectacular.

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicles is the return of the Suikoden team after many years. I was really looking forward to this game and I'm not disappointed. Everything I knew and loved about the Suikoden series is here and accounted for. The many recruitable characters, the castle building, the many minigames, the exaggerated unite attacks. Since minute one, everything was clicking in all the right ways and I couldn't have been happier. There are some snags that I have with how the game was handled. I was under the impression that we would've had three separate characters kinda like Suikoden 3, instead the game is entirely mainly focused on Nowa as the main character, which itself isn't bad, but that also means that Seign and especially Marisa kinda got the short end of the stick in terms of character moments. Overall it doesn't reach the same memorable heights of Suikoden 2 but it still a really enjoyable ride full of character. In terms of music the game is a bit lacking but visually is beautiful. the mix of 2D sprites and 3D enviroments is done really well and character like Lian have a lot of vitality and expression in their animation she's probably the best of the whole roster, the 1 on 1 duels are the best moments in the entire game, the direction and energy is absolutely great. In terms of gameplay nothing really has changed all that much, it's turn based battles, every action has its own speed, you can autobattle of pick singular actions and some combination of characters have some combo attacks that are great for singular damage or crowd control. The Unite attacks are tied to SP point which regenrate every turn, making them a bit harder to spam compared to the old Suikoden games. The runes have got the most expansion, every character has 3 to 8 rune slots each which get unlocked the more you level them up and each slot has a certain level and type of rune that you can assign. Sounds complicated to explain but it's really streamlined and allows you to have a lot of flexibility in how you wanna build your characters. The game is not that difficult in normal mode, but in hard mode you can have a lot of fun messing around with them. I am happy that this game is here honestly, it was a lot of fun and while the story didn't reach the same heights as Suikoden 2 for me, I had exactly what I wanted from this and I hope this is the start for the future where they can dare a little more.

_childDocuments_.review: A fine spiritual successor to Suikoden 2 that does not fall below expectations. I hope many Suikoden fans share a similar view.The story is well-written. I find it quite interesting, above average. However, it contains excessively predictable plots, fewer dramatic events, and fewer surprisingly cunning tactics. The link with the prequel, Rising, turned out to be fine. It gives a feeling just like when Suikoden 1 continued its journey in Suikoden 2.The graphics are a well-done combination of 2D pixel art and 3D-empowered objects, especially the world map and towns. While retaining the old-school style of visuals, it also allows players with older models of PCs to enjoy the game without spending extra money on hardware upgrades.The gameplay is fairly enjoyable, which means there are not many differences from the archetype. Despite this, the duel scenes and the warfare battles are deemed praiseworthy. While the duel scenes turn out to be more exciting cinematic shows than thrilling fights, the warfare battles offer unsophisticated tactical war play but can produce excitement through a Total War-like environment and characters' dialogues while engaging in combat.The effort of the voice actors is highly commendable. Despite the large scale of characters, most dialogues are amazingly fully voiced, which, as a consequence, greatly raises the quality of the RPG game.The vast diversity and quantity of mini-games offered in the game are hard to go unmentioned. In fact, there are so many of them available that only true hardcore players would willingly put in the time and effort to finish them all. However, the good thing is that normal players are only required to partially participate in mini-games as a requirement for story completion. The rest are considered optional. My favorites are the Theatre and Card Game.The Theatre mini-game, however, is the most commendable one. As the player should have learned the personality and characteristics of each character from the dialogues and events, it is quite fun to assign them roles that are deemed to suit them well and expect to produce good results. The most thrilling part is that all theatre-performable characters have their own lines in every show and every dialogue, with varying levels of acting proficiency, and they are all voiced! In my experience, this is the most amazing aspect of this game.Obviously, the English language used in the game is still sesquipedalian. The developer's English translator overused synonyms in the townsfolk conversations, which ruined the natural flow of spoken language and resulted in bizarre dialogue. This issue persists from the Rising prequel, which could indicate that the same translators continued their work on this game as well.Several BGMs (Background Music tracks) are well-composed and memorable, especially those with chorus, which effectively add emotional value to the story.As a backer, I am impressed and satisfied with this Kickstarter project so far. In comparison with the most-acclaimed Suikoden 2, even though several core elements may still be considered inferior to the magnum opus, the game surprisingly surpasses its inspiring masterpiece in many aspects. Thanks to the great effort of all the developer teams. Even as a humble backer, I am proud to participate in the birth of this emerging great franchise, and I look forward to supporting any interesting projects in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: When I found out this had a kickstarter, I was absolutely thrilled and excited.  I played all the Suikoden's in my teens and really loved them all even after the Suikoden 3 was critically not well accepted.  I still enjoyed them.  Suikoden 1 and 2 are my favorite games of all time even ahead of FF7 and 10.  I have to say, this game was a MASSIVE LET DOWN.  The Suikoden stories were so rich with character development and storyline and everything had a place.  You had to definitely do some RNG stuff like gambling so you could upgrade your weapons and buy armor, but it felt purposeful.  The one on one duels were set for pivotal moments and the field battle took some strategy and really some forethought.  Even the culinary battles had a little more to reason than what we experienced in Eiyuden Chronicle.This game just missed on everything important.  Story line; character development and a general sense of purpose.  It's got no soul I think is the best way to put it.  It WANTS to be Suikoden, but it just added all those components and just hoped it worked.  Not a great sign for the sequel they want to do UNLESS they spend the time to actually develop a cohesive storyline and give a damn about the characters.  I personally did not give a single ♥♥♥♥ about a single character and that's 50 hours commitment to get this knocked out.  The beigoma game is a slow and repetitive and mostly RNG.  The card game is fun so props to that.  The army fights were a joke and rarely did you have any actual control of what was happening unlike previous suikodens.  The duels were just there...no reason sense of purpose.All in all, just a massive disappointment.  They missed what made Suikoden so good.  On the plus side, the maps were STUNNING to look at; A+++ on visuals.  The map design were needlessly huge for no reason for it to serve literally 0 purpose...just forces you to run more to get into more random fights.  Also, what's with the unnecessary talking for carrie on EVERY SINGLE TELEPORT.

_childDocuments_.review: It has been nearly 4 years since I first heard the news that there would be a spiritual successor to my favorite RPG game: Suikoden. Although it is unfair to compare the two games instead of reviewing Eiyuden on its own, I find it impossible to do so because of their connection. Besides, the fact it is a spiritual successor is what instantly sold me to buying it in the first place.  Eiyuden Chronicles attempts to stay faithful to many mechanics within Suikoden. You can recruit over a hundred characters with unique attack styles to help build your army and base. There are field battles, party battles, solo battles, and, thankfully, a teleporter which I have always appreciated. The graphics are stunning and a vast improvement with beautifully crafted sprites. The mechanics are decent, but I was not a fan of how everything  (runes, equipment, and potions) shared a single bag instead of having a categorized system to quickly scour for whatever inventory you are looking for. The organization could see improvement, but otherwise, it was decent after all was said and done. Unfortunately, I do have some critiques over the delivery of the story in some areas. Don't get me wrong, Eiyuden is great, but the story does play it safe and sometimes I'd even argue  safe. There is no other way to adequately describe the difference than by explaining this simple formula that all stories generally will follow. Some stories are advanced through their plot, and then the characters react to move the story forward. This is the formula followed in the Eiyuden Chronicles. Other stories are driven by character motivations, moving the plot forward. This is the formula followed in Suikoden 1&2. Every time we met a new character, especially a prominent one in Suikoden, we learned about those characters and their background stories intimately in various ways. We drew connections and cared about them, and those who could be considered a minor character were appropriately given just enough time to make them exciting. Plot was driven forward by the characters in almost every way possible.In Eiyuden Chronicles, most of the character motivations are told to the players and rarely dive further than the initial meeting. If it did elaborate, we only learned about the actual reasons behind their motivation at the last possible moment and only because the character finally exclaims them. There was opportunity, for example, for Nowa to have a huge reason behind his motivation, but they removed those high stakes and made any loss that would have drove him oddly minimal when, in reality, there are always heartbreaks and significant losses in war. Keeping it "safe" ensured emotions were kept safe as well. Marisa, as another example, is a guardian who loves her home because she never felt like she belonged anywhere else, but that is all we really get to know. We do not get a deep dive into how and why that might even be. Even a simple technique of having her accomplish mundane, but precious tasks among her neighbors could have easily drew a stronger bond and an understanding of that deep raw emotion. Instead, the plot moves forward rather quickly, forcing the story to tell us about that connection instead of building and showing us. Suikoden, on the other hand, had so many deep dives into nearly every character that each was memorable in its own way! They were not afraid of raising the stakes! Prominent characters could die way more readily, and they were so much a part of the story I cried tears when I came to them. Consequences were nerfed. It no longer mattered if you failed a task you allegedly only had one shot to do. In Suikoden, for example, the side quest was over if you failed a cooking contest. It made it feel like the stakes were significant. Sure, I saved my game before attempting to face off against another cook, but it still gave the illusion it mattered. Even more notable was that you were never barred from a single city - even if the imperial army took it over. In Suikoden 2, for example, if the Highland army took over a village or town, you could not enter the place, and the Highland army would chase you out. It is something I would expect if I were a prominent general from an enemy army. Instead, I could continue going to any city I liked and do whatever I wanted, as if there weren't soldiers who would recognize me or ask me questions. It was disconnecting to be overly aware of that detail. It kept pulling me away from the story and reminded me how it is a story. Regardless, I do support this game with a high recommendation. The sprites are AMAZING and notwithstanding the negative observations, there are so many good things that make this game awesome! The battle systems are good, and while I have several critiques about the story, it still carries pretty well. I just don't want to explain them too much and reveal too many spoilers, but there are attempts at some painful moments - not as nearly as I would have liked and would have expected, but there are some. There are also some significant side quests that were appropriate in tone and execution and were as you'd expect. Eiyuden is a story that carries well for a WIDE audience, but if you are expecting more stakes as an adult who understands the cruel truth of war then you might find it lackluster. Still, for what it is, Eiyuden IS a  and it will touch those subjects as best it can as  as it does.  FYI: Markus is the best character in the Eiyuden Chronicles. I vote he becomes a main character in the next game. I also vote Francesca becomes his wife. That would be an interesting combo. Rest in Peace, Yoshitaka Murayama. Thank you so much for your stories.

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratches all my brain itches: immersive, epic story; a huge cast of characters to recruit, level, and get to know; a setting with just enough hinted at off the edges of the map that I want to know more; turn-based combat; retro pixel graphics; quality writing, both for dialogue and plot; great soundtrack.It's like it was made for me. I previously played this to the end on Switch, but am replaying now on Steam since I am a sucker for achievements in games like this, and Nintendo doesn't do those. There are some gripes, like how a few of the minigames were implemented, and that there are many of the 120 recruitable characters who really don't have any depth or expansion beyond when you meet and/or recruit them. I wish there was more mass combat, for example, and that the controls in the sandsail races weren't so janky. But by and large, this the best JRPG to come out in years. I can't wait for the sequel.

It is very apparent the story and localization plays it safe to not offend anyone... I wanted to love this game, even put in over 100 hours to get the full experience. The Good1 - Graphics2 - Variety of Mini-Games3 - Mystery Dungeon Content4 - Over-world, Towns, and Dungeons. Eiyuden is more Final Fantasy than Final Fantasy XVI 5 - Speaking of Final Fantasy-XVI. Unlike FF-XVI, Eiyuden has status effects, buffs, weaknesses, and immunities bringing more depth to combat.(The game needs a re-balance, hopefully through an update.)6 - Unite Attacks! - Need I say more. 7 - Runes, they were better in Suikoden. Just like everything else(Besides graphics)The Bad1 - Story - Very bland and forgettable. It's just a cliche political war story with no  turmoil, or      consequences. Town was taken over by the enemy? Sweet! Nothing stops you      from going right back. The enemy's Army let's you do what you want, no questions asked.      Seriously. You can go back to any town you want throughout the game. Only exception      being Yaarnan when taken over by the zombies.     In the Suikoden games, you were blocked off from the territories that get taken over. It felt      really exciting to be able to reach those areas toward the end of the games. A sense of      achievement for the hard work you did. Very rewarding and fulfilling. You lose that in      Eiyuden. You never get a sense of accomplishment. Your just done and on with the next      thing. It is like that with the story and characters. Nothing really matters in Eiyuden.2 - NO TRUE RUNE equivalent driving the story. Your just a farm boy who joins the local      military to "Help". Every Suikoden game's protagonist had a connection with a TRUE      RUNE of some kind; Making him UNIQUE. Nowa is just a "meddler" with nothing unique      going on.      REALLY disappointed with how the game ended. The Primal Lense just vanishes?      Nowa should have acquired it. Missed opportunity if you ask me. 3 - Character and World Development - Suikoden used some of the quest lines to flesh out      characters throughout the game, and did a great job.      Eiyuden just streamlines them into your entourage and tells you up front who they are      and what they do right off the bat... Leaving no mystery or mysticism. Mini-Game recruits      were the exception. The only way to get to know a lot of the characters is by reading B'      Baba's notes yourself. 4 - The localization: Dastard>Changed To>Bastard - What was that thing? >Changed To> Are      you sure it was a he? ----- Some of it is just really weird and bizarre; Luckily the community      is fixing it....5 - Quality of the Mini-Games - Some of them are pretty decent. Some of pretty bad like cooking. Suikoden II did it way better.6 - Army War Battles - I liked these in the previous Suikoden games. In Eiyuden they are      scripted battles; Kind of equivalent to Auto-Battle in normal battles. Not fun or engaging.7 - The Music - It wasn't terrible but nothing stood out. Exception being the theme to the Siegn      vs Nowa duel. Part of this is probably from the music being muffled when the voice actors      talk. Even with the VA off, the music still gets muffled. I wish I could recommend this game. Been waiting 18 years for a game like Suikoden I/II/III/IV/V (Suikoden V 2006) But honestly your time is better being spent on any of the old Suikoden games. BEST TO WORST in my opinion SII > SV > SI > SIII > SIV > SIV Tactics > Woven Web > Tierkies > Eiyuden: HH > Eiyuden: Rising

Its fine if it wasn't such a chore & long as I dont find beigoma or the cooking mini game enjoyable- Localisation (Not the best, but IMO i'm fine with it)- Balance/Difficulty spikes as with 2-3 attacks per turn can just one-shot characters (Kinda offset by leveling up, or I have skill issues. The Mystery Room overleveled me which makes things too easy in the endgame)- Inventory Management problem- Runes/Spell can only be changed via Npcs in town- Random Encounters especially for farming certain drops (I'm not a big fan of this) - Carrie's Dialog every fast teleport (Gets annoying real quick)- War mode (I like the Concept but not much control)- Not much story attachment/development to characters which i get as it is a huge cast anyway- Backtracking to refill consumables... (Multiple Boss slogfest .........)- A little bit clunky (Eg; Menu Transitions, Scene transition, Battle transition)Honestly, Kinda of an average experience.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the $50 for 66 hours so far. If you like classic JRPG's and enjoy a classic kinda figure it out yourself character collecting game with some grind, this is the right game for you. If you want something deeper and more personal with a detailed lore/history and in-depth tutorials, its probably not the game for you.Is it a perfect game? No. Is it enjoyable? Heck yes. Does it remind me of the Suikoden series? Heck yeah!!!! Is a carbon copy? No. Did the devs make mistakes? You bet. Do I regret my purchase/support? No.Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes has its pros and cons like every other game. Below, I will review some pros and cons and some comparisons with the Suikoden series.Story/Characters:Pros-Very similar Suikoden vibes.-I like the diverse cast of characters in terms of how they look and different races/tribes of people. Thats always been something the Suikoden game excelled at so it was reminiscent of it. And yes there is a LGBT+ character in this game and its not that deep.-The story makes subtle references to other places that you do not see at the end of the game. Such as a University known for education and its observatory. Even some characters are from this university or has been there in this game. This was similar to Suikoden I and II where they referenced other places and then introduced them later in the series.-There are lots of heroes to collect and I believe there's about 120 characters.-There are lots of minigames to play. My favorite is probably the card game. There is a beyblade-esque game too.-Has a killer/catchy theme song that is mostly in Japanese but then goes "hundred heroes" which was awesome.-They definitely acknowledged the backers that helped make this game and I thought it was cute seeing people on reddit say they found themselves in-game.Cons:-The story could have been written and told better. Everything was there for a reason. They did not focus on building the characters relationships with one another. Lets just say even the game itself had some scenes where you see a black screen and it just says 6 months later...a few weeks later...etc.-They tried to copy the bond/rivalry of Suikoden II between Riou and Jowy but failed with Nowa and Seign. This made their duel anticlimatic because they knew each other for a day before war split them which as a reader/gamer, you did not feel the emotions they were suppose to feel. -Localization could have improved but I understood what was going on just fine. The dialogue from certain characters was questionable. I found a lot of very annoying characters, mostly hyperactive/loud/obnoxious female characters but I think that's a JRPG trying to make them cute thing which I personally don't like. -They skip over a lot of important lore or things that could have expanded the world. I'm not sure if this is due to them wanting to expand it later, but they missed a big opportunity here and this is probably why a lot of negative reviews says it feels rushed. They focused on the storyline and that was it.-There are parts in the game where they just tell you to literally go find characters to recruit which doesn't flow well and seems forced.-They released the game with a bug that caused you to be unable to recruit a character but they fixed it within the week of its release.Battle/Turn-based GameplayPros: They improved on the rune system in my opinion. Adding rune slots beyond the 3 from Suikoden's head/left/right arm was such a great improvement. This provided an opportunity to make some characters fit what you want them to do while still giving characters some uniqueness with exclusive runes and restrictions. -Most characters will have at least one level 3 magic rune and a few stat enhancement or skill runes. Some even have an anything you want rune slot. One special character even has all of their runes at level 4 as anything you want. -Removing rune charges for MP was also the best thing they could have done and having MP restore items and rune shards. This allowed you to kinda tinker characters stats and in this case you can adjust their MP should you want. -The auto battle system works well for lazy people if you know how to set it up properly and pay attention to your characters speed/sp/mana management.-Characters will learn and open up new rune slots as they level up. Some exclusive runes are learned this way instead of being found which Suikoden didn't offer and locked behind rune charges.Cons: -The instructions on battles can be confusing but once you know the basic, its actually quite fun. -A lot of people will struggle with how SP is generated and the game does a poor job of explaining it. Basically SP is randomly generated based on the luck stat. Not all character will use SP or have the ability to do so. If you have high luck, you have more chance of gaining 1 or multiple SP after each round. -Stats of some characters can be very random and unappealing such as a mage that has higher strength than a warrior or a mage with less MP than a warrior. The consistency seems a bit random and I'm not sure who worked on these numbers. Personally, it didn't get in the way of the overall enjoyment.-They removed the dojo's/skill enhancer/grades which I really loved in Suikoden III/V. This means that many characters can hit multiple attack counts, but it doesn't seem to make any difference in terms of hit counts/overall damage. In fact, multiple hit counts are pointless and does not offer any incentive.-The hero combos cost too many SP from each character and the damage is not worth the turn or SP cost.-There are no range physical skills that are good which makes rangers inferior. Its a mage/warrior kind of game. There's like 3 useful tanks, but tanking and covering is all rng and luck based.DuelingPros: The cutscenes during the duels throughout the games are pretty cool and fun to watch.Cons: The combat itself is not enjoyable because it forces you to select certain options to continue with the animation so you can't just attack them to the end or use your special whenever. In previous Suikoden games you could do whatever you want and it made a big difference.Warfare/Strategic BattlesPros: You see (what I believe to be) random backers and their names being killed in battle lol. Besides that there aren't really any pros.Cons: I found the war battles so boring and useless. You can't really edit your team. You select and move them and have little to no control otherwise besides some 1 use skill that can't be improved upon. Your characters stats doesn't matter so you can't just obliterate everything and can still die from something stupid. I'm not sure how this is calculated but this is the worse part of the game. I wish they stuck to Suikoden III and how you can still influence the map yet still choose what you want to do.So yes, I wrote a lot, but I also enjoyed the game for what it is. Did it exceed my expectations? No. Was I happy with my purchase? Yes. Because I supported a game and it delivered a game that brought joy and memories. Can it improve? Absolutely. I hope people give it the chance to because there is so much to this game and I hope the dev's will listen and improve on these things.

_childDocuments_.review: This is suikoden, but much worse.  The scenery looks beautiful in some cases, and the 3d ish aspects are a nice touch, but it is incredibly inconsistent. The great news is that its fixable, but if they thought this was in any way acceptable i wouldn't expect them to do anything. maybe a mod community would help.  The other issue is that there is a jarring amount of time and pausing in between characters talking.  It makes it completely unenjoyable.  This is not a love letter to jrpgs.  Its a horror story in what not to do.The battle is a suikoden clone, but somehow less entertaining.  They added some wrinkles but it doesn't do much for me.  Ultimately it does not feel like a game, it feels like a chore leveling and exploring in this lifeless, empty world.I got this for $35.  It isn't worth it even if it is free in its current state.
