_childDocuments_.review: *This review is based on having played the closed beta and 20 hours of the full released game*It's hard not to constantly compare Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes to the beloved Suikoden series (1 and 2 in particular). I've been a fan of the games for as long as I can remember and am one many who've waited for a sequel to Suikoden. Although we never got it, we have be fortunate enough to experience Eiyuden Chronicle. - The visuals are truly stunning. Eiyuden manages to combine tradition with modern and does it effortlessly with gorgeous, colorful backgrounds, mixing 2D sprites with 3D elements. - The music has been both soothing and epic when it calls for it, creating a sense of adventure.- My first War battle had me nervous, haha, but I quite liked what they've done with it and can imagine just how epic it would be as things progress with the story and you control more units in a larger scale.- The voice acting has been a mix for me - there are some I REALLY love, and others.... could either use some work or perhaps have a mute button for, lol. But overall they've done a fantastic job with the variety of ethnicity in the characters and their voices.- Eiyuden has outdone it with the Castle and the amount of things you can do with it. I can certainly see this giving players hours and hours of gameplay just trying to improve and build on it. Not to mention the sheer number of side things that can keep you occupied (fishing, farming, guild/hunting/missions, card game, collecting all the cards, etc.) A huge highlight for me for sure.Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes is truly a love letter from Murayama-sensei and team to all of us Suikoden fans.Message received ❤

_childDocuments_.review: I can only imagine what this game could have been if it truly had been made with input from the fans/backers. A real beta with feedback from the players instead of a demo would have made this an instant classic. Instead of an evolution it's just a collection of the worst 90's game mechanics with a season pass.Things I liked:1. Characters so far, are all unique and interesting.2. World map looks nice.3. Art looks great.4. I like how the row combat works. Ranged can hit anything, but melee can't target the back since the row is protected.Things I dislike and feedback:1. Translation in some parts ruins some of the characters that I have encountered so far. Please be mindful of outsourcing your life's work to groups that deviate from source materials. *Back up, folks! I'll handle this one. Rub-adub-dub, open, ya schlub! This was in one my first encounters in the demo and it really took me out of the game. 2. Garr and Lian VA so far don't really match what I would imagine from them as characters. The Japanese Voices are superior for these two. However, the English Mio is good so far. I am normally not that particular for dubs, but this very noticeable. 3. Moving cameraThe camera should move some during battle, but it's jarring zooming in on each participant on their turn only to select a generic fight option for most situations. Maybe change the zooming to happen after inputting all the commands so we can watch the end result?4. When the menu appears there is a 4 second delay to just fight which is the most used command since it requires no mp it would make sense that it would be pre-selected.5. Blurry environments, I get that sometimes the in game character can't see something due to visibility, but it goes a bit far causing blurring of environments.6. E for everyone rating. Very odd to see a game about heroes, warfare, and villains try to adopt this family friendly approach. I hope they lean into the serious elements in future installments. 7. Somehow the hero Nowa can do melee attacks from the back row while other melee characters cannot. I get that he's a hero, but consistency is the key.8. Boss battles depend too much on gimmick's, which started off fun but evolved into a chore. After all of the dungeon grinding I did, it seems strange that a gimmick matters more than levels or gear etc.8. Rune-lenses, I found a ton of them but equipping them is a nightmare since most characters are very limited early on. With inventory slots at 30, I would have really preferred finding them later in the game so that I could actually utilize them. Right now they're in storage unused.9. Magic is very cool, but I was unable to use it for 6 game hours due to rest spots being so far away. I didn't want to go into a boss fight with no mp so I just use herbs for everything. 10. Inn saving shouldn't be a thing. Saving anywhere would make this a much more portable experience. With all the dungeon grinding it would be awesome to just save and come back if you can't clear the dungeon because you have things to do.11. First duel is lumped together with the first battle making players redo the tedious parts to try the duel again. Players should be able to save after each milestone so the game doesn't become a chore to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome old-school RPG.First of all, this game does have a lot of flaws, mostly due to some "retro" game design choices and lack of budget:* very slow start (mainly due to lack of fast travel until 10~15 hours into the game)* sluggish menus due to fade out animation being too long (loading time is not a problem on PC)* un-intuitive/retro UI design e.g. can't sort characters/inventory, base mission/gathering lack real time timer, cant save in overworld, can't view character skills when modifying party ... and a lot more designs you would expect from a 90s game* character back stories are all text based, which is a real disappointment because some of them would have been awesome to watch a scene for* some weird design choices such as spell mp cost and hero combo being weakHowever, it still deserves a big thumb up for its fun elements:* Character recruitment - the game does live up to its name-sake with 120 characters to recruit, and each of them comes with varies personality and powers that can be added to your party* Base building - it's satisfying to see your castle grow* Mini games - some of them are cheesy and nostalgic (e.g. cooking and bayblade) and some are hilarious (theatre)* RPG elements - character growth and customization are very satisfying when your build and grow your characters to one-shot an entire screen* Art and music - classic and epicSide note, there are some controversies reguarding this game that needs to be cleared up* translations are not perfect, but it doesn't bother me at all. Only a grammar police would complain* there are no technical issues in PC version after latest patch (load time are insignificant, no game breaking bugs and no crashes at all)* there are no "wokeness". Let's just say the game has female characters come in all shape and sizes

_childDocuments_.review: is a spiritual successor to one of my favorite RPG series of all time, . As such, it has a lot of expectations behind it and for the most part it played it safe with some very obvious homages to the  games. This is a bit of a double edged sword, however. While they borrow some great tropes and story beats, I can’t help but feel like I’m just pointing at the game going “hey remember that from !?” and the constant comparisons sort of damper the game as its own thing. Especially because Eiyuden makes a lot of questionable decisions so when comparing it to , it doesn’t always come out on top. That said, reality is there won’t ever be an actual  sequel so this is the best we’ll get and it’s still a very enjoyable story and game worth playing for any fan of the original series.I honestly found the very start a bit slow. But after about an hour when it opens up and lets you start recruiting characters, I started to love the game. From then on, it only got better as political events that shape the world and story occur and so on. Like the  series, the story revolves around a political conflict in which you play as an underdog faction of ragtag heroes that slowly builds up power over time through many recruits. Not all recruits are fighters either and some are cooks, librarians, etc and help manage your town. I think it’s neat to show the importance of everyone working together to keep the faction going and not just the generals fighting the wars (although certainly they get most of the screentime).  Unfortunately, I do have to say while I enjoyed the overall story and the primary antagonist, it really falls short of the  plots. It largely boils down to a severe lack of stakes. I never really felt in danger. Towns may get taken over and yet you can still just walk right in and recruit people. A town may get burned down and still there a few days later. Where are the actual consequences of the ongoing war?Characters and side stories varied. Some had barely any story before joining while others had involved side quests. Overall, I think they’re cool and fun and the variety was nice.I don’t really care about voice acting but the game has it. I thought it was OK. I’m impatient and tend to read faster than they speak so it means nothing to me. I did like the music and the overall presentation of towns, characters, etc. It’s really fun to see so many stray cats roaming the towns too.A majority of my frustrations with the game resides here. I enjoyed my time with it, but could not help but constantly feel there are a ton of Quality of Life (QoL) issues throughout the game that actively pissed me off. Only for some enjoyable moment to make me forgive the game again. Then get pissed off by something else again. I was constantly going back and forth.I get that the game is purposely invoking old-school RPGs but that should never come at the cost of being an active detriment to enjoying the game. First, the game is a turn based battle system with a return to the 6-character party. I love that. I also like that you can shove story-required characters into the reserves and ignore them. What was frustrating is the changes to the battle system. First- the overall speed just feels so slow. In , everyone would attack at once and the combat felt extremely snappy. In Eiyuden, it just feels so slow! Secondly, the beloved unite system seems horribly balanced or bugged where you’re better off just using two individual attacks than combined attacks most of the time. The combined attacks just do terrible damage and are not worth it. This sucks, half of the appeal of the unite system was to try out interesting combinations to pull off big damage as well as observe the fun animations. Thirdly – magic is strangely balanced. Early on, MP is difficult to recover outside of Inns and magic as a whole seemed underwhelming outside of healing. In the late game, magic finally takes off and is great to use (at least for the extremely OP Momo lol). I really miss the unique magic system of the  series which had limited casts at each level. This allowed you to still use magic on trash mobs while conserving the big spells for bosses. With the MP system, mages are more likely to just spam normal attacks for all trash encounters in order to save everything for the big bosses. Just feels way less magical. Also no double beat rune????For other QoL issues - inventory management is rough early game, lack of bulk selection for selling/appraising/weapon sharpening, etc. Just so many weird little choices.Also hope you aren’t a completionist. The grind for that is painful (and still ongoing for me). Beyblade minigame was painful and everyone hates it. Ship racing game terrible controls.  Card game is actually fun but not “win 120 times” fun. The theatre is actually a wonderful side feature and I love it.Duels and war systems were a major let down and each felt more like interactive cutscenes.No issues.Operating System: Windows 10Processor (CPU): Intel Core i5-3570K CPU @3.40GHzGraphics Card (GPU): NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070Memory (RAM) 16 GBIf you’re into headquarters building with recruiting tons of characters, you’ll probably enjoy this. There is also an interesting political storyline that’s more complicated than the typical “good vs evil” story of many turn based RPGs. It’s a great game, but definitely temper your expectations in comparison to the series it was based on. Keep in mind also that the game intentionally brings old school vibes and this means a return to save points and a useless auto-save that only works when you go to the world map (prepare to lose hours of progress if you rely only on the auto save). I promise though, it is a good time and a fun game if you’re able to look past the flaws and focus on the character collection and story.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm  really mixed on this one,  like a lot of people came into this looking for a modern Suikoden. While the core mechanics early on are great, it's got some really annoying issues. One of those games where Steam could really use a middling option. While I'm not far into the game so far, the gameplay is great, a classic turn based JRPG, levelling up, exploring dungeons, and even early on free access to multiple little towns and dungeons. The difficulty is pretty good, while never strained I do find myself prioritising targets and bosses actually force me to use caution. (Although early on, even with a full roster the team dynamic is a bit shallow while they're introducing more mechanics) The art is great, animation is great. But frequently it seems inconsistent with itself. Turning off depth of field helps a lot as a small circle of focus seems to hang on the screen which can be jarring as shading and details seem to flicker into place suddenly. Textures on 3d objects seem to have a wild disparity, some have detailed 'normal' maps whereas towns can often look flat and like a simple 2d texture was slapped on. The sprite work and animation is great but it feels like 3d was used to expedite a lot of the asset creation. Monsters, bosses and locations feel very rushed compared to the character sprites. It's a bit strange as I feel like if the quality of the 3d assets was consistent among itself, even if some of the clearly more cared for textures were simpler. It would be far less noticeable. There's a lot of nitpicking to be had here but overall the sprite work impresses, but I'd highly recommend turning off depth of field. The music is pretty good, no complaints but so far no stand out tracks. I'm not far in as of writing. But overall the music is pretty good, even if it does suffer the JRPG curse of having a very repetitive battle theme that wears itself out. The real problem I can't recommend it though. The translation. There's a lot of annoying hammy dialogue that would make a trashy anime blush, and while I do expect some of that from a JRPG (I just finished FF8 again, so I can handle trash dialogue) this really goes into a realm of being obstructive. Everyone talks as if they're a 35 year old Discord mod imitating a 9 year old. As much as this just seems like an insult, I have no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clue who or what anything is. Character breaks to make little gender comments, they set up the world to have 2 factions at peace but heading for a war early on, but it's hard to keep track of who is with what faction, because half of the characters are wasting words spouting out cringe, it's like watching someone write for Borderlands but carried away fellating themselves before they actually deliver the expository part of the line. At first when I heard about the localisation complaints I assumed it was a bandwagoning mob. However, there's no sense of character in anyone, and the plot feels second to hearing one of the many "spunky teen hyper fun" girls say something silly. Like being trapped in a room full of myspace comments. Compounding this issue is the voice-overs. Although impressive there's a large roster of voices that needed to be performed, the quality is wildly all over the place. I had to turn the volume of voices down entirely, leaving me coldly reading the crowded writing to save me from eating my own head in frustration. While a couple of characters are voiced with some kind of professional restraint, like Nowa, Seign and Hilde, every other character (and there's a decent amount even in a short space of time) make me want to finger ♥♥♥♥ my own ears. From the first line of dialogue, I had to sigh, as the first person you meet has that cringey false deep voice that seems plucked from a fan fiction read along, before you realise every character you meet is a "oh so whimsical anime" character, over-acted poorly. It's pretty grim. It does feel like a lot of the voice talent was plucked from some cheap anime fan club. From goofy accents, to cringe inducing  repetitive screeches to half of the male cast sounding like a 15 year old putting on a "gruff" voice, it seems to have every voice acting sin in a short space of time. If 505 really wanted to make money, they'd put the volume slider for the voices behind a paywall. It's like the voice director was greatly inspired by stories of the CIA torturing prisoners with bad music and decided to pay homage to that with the medium of VO.Overall, although I think the whole DEI discourse around this game is a bit overblown, the localisation really does cause a big issue with following a plot driven game genre. Especially as this was tauted as a spiritual sequel to the sadly long dormant Suikoden series, which despite having it's own share of bad tropes and bad dialogue at times, still didn't plague the story or game as a whole. It's a shame, as the game itself does have some quality mechanics I'm still keen on getting into, although I am definitely going to be slow plodding through the plot to get there.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite JRPGs is Suikoden 2. This review is me comparing it to that.This is a game that feels like it was made during that era of JRPGs. It ticks all the boxes. Tedious random encounters, not being able to save anywhere, archaic minimal hint based objectives.I played through multiple 60+ hour jrpgs (FF7R2, Unicorn Overlord) this year and this is by far my favorite out of all of them. Compared to Suikoden 2 though, the game Eiyuden is heavily based on.This game just can't hold a candle to the PS1 classic.The story feels like they played it safe, It's more heroic than S2's Dark Grim Crisis-filled story, While there's nothing wrong with something more lighthearted. I really wanted something that made me feel the same way as Luca Blight did in S2. This doesn't make the story bad though, just more predictable and cliche.The character recruitments are one of the strongest points of Eiyuden. Suikoden 2 also has all the mundane very forgettable recruitments but I think that's just part of the charm. There's always a character for someone in this game.The combat is awesome. A lot of people say the enemies are very spongy but if you experiment with some characters some of them turn out to be insanely good, to the point where some of them can 3-4 turn bosses by themselves. So ofcourse people are gonna struggle if they keep using the character that shines later and hits for 85 per attack instead of the character that comes out of the box doing 300 per turn. So I made sure to experiment with character combinations and that made the game much more deep for me, despite it being really simple.Overall, If Suikoden 2 is a 10/10 for me. This game is an 8. I highly recommend it. There's nothing like this right now and with S2 Remaster in the horizon. There's no better time to enjoy this love letter to the franchise. RIP Yoshitaka Muruyama, And thanks R&B, 505 games for this fun and amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10.The opening to the game is quite slow, it feels like something is missing, and then the drop happens.Like with previous works from the now late writer, Murayama, this game taps to a pre-established beat.It is hard for me to not compare it to the old Suikoden games, as will be the case with many I am sure, however it did something unexpected for me.  It has reestablished my love of this genre.  Things that were done in the past were repeated in this game, but the designers also ramped it all up to 11 and left me with my jaw dropped in surprise and excitement.It has been such a very long time since I experienced a sense of sheer 'squee' from a game.  They always try so hard to make you feel sad, or angry, but this one like previous of its creators handiwork leaves me instilled with a grand sense of wonder and joy.Though the narrative is about war, it doesn't focus on the negatives and the brutality that other games would, and instead it feels almost like a journey that you would experience from playing something like dungeons and dragons for example:  Your characters are mostly fresh to the world (as are you when you start the game for the first time), and from there you start to explore your surroundings, learn the way of the world, and find your place in it to defend and protect what is important to you/the characters.There are some parts that feel a bit too drawn out, I'll give it that, but at the same time the end result is worth the lengths you have to go.  Whether it be uncovering something astonishing, or a big plot point that you hadn't expected so soon!(Sorry trying not to spoil it for others! You'll see when you get there!)The lighting is a bit intense in places, or design choices (such as putting blue shapes on a blue background) aren't the best, however the aesthetics, the soundscape, the music, the story, the animations, the copious amounts of cats, the overall ambience and feel of every part of the game you can tell the creators put their souls into them to make something to the very best of their abilities.Some may say some of the system choices may seem dated by today's standards, however I honestly don't think they are.The bag for example forces you to engage with your inventory.  You can't just be a hoarder and expect to pick every little thing up.  You need to be wise and choose things appropriately - that or you can just walk back, inventory dump, and then return for the rest of the chests if it's that important to you to open them.For what it is worth, this game has ticked every single box I had hoped it would, and then some!I will sing this games praises for years to come, because to me, it is a fun and enjoyable game that has done what it promised it would: It took me on an adventure, fed me nostalgia, and showed me a new story that I never would have been able to dream of.I truly wish there to be a second of this games title some time in the future, and though it won't be the same without Murayama who's stories shaped my childhood all the way through to my adulthood, the rest of the amazing people he worked with for a very long time are more than skilled enough to continue on the legacy he helped create.Very much looking forward to the studio's future endeavours! Thank you for all your hard work and for giving a good smile, Rabbit & Bear Studios!Best of luck to you!

And its not the localization that bothers me - I'm actually not sure why so many people whine about it.  I mean its nothing to write home about, but its not that bad.For me, I generally play jrpgs for the battles.  And I think this is what's buggin me.  For one, there are some weird balacing issues in the game.  For example, more than once I'll just mow down every enemy left and right only to get to the boss who's somehow a giant pain in the ass - hard mode seems to give the bosses tons of hp and the battle more or less ends up being how many potions I brought with me.  Literally every game I've ever played with intense boss difficult spikes like that just turn me off.  And the way the experience works, you won't be able to level up or really go buy some better armor, its just - well, the boss is gonna hit me like this, in this really static pattern, so I better just buy a bunch of potions, yawn.And, speaking of buying potions - you get very little mp and everything costs a lot of mp.  So maybe I'll get a small handful of magic heals if i don't use magic to attack at all and then I'll once again, have to dive into my pile of items (which you are limited in how many you can carry, mind you).  You basically can't use magic, or maybe this is the one jrpg that eludes me as to how I'm supposed to use magic in battles.  "0h great, i casted a magic attack on a regular enemy, now i have 3 heals left and have to use potions on the boss or run my butt out of the dungeon and go buy some more"If you don't turn off magic use in the auto battle settings, you'll basically burn 100% of your magic on the first couple groups of enemies.  If you do turn it off, you might get lucky enough to heal a couple times or attack a couple times on a boss.  Tons of fun - you can't even experiment cause you're just always out of mp.there's an sp system that recharges as you fight - but its kinda boring.  Most characters have one or two moves (maybe they get more, but i'm 30 hours in and most characters have one or two moves).  When you only have one move, the pattern is always like: regular attacks until you have sp, use the move, rinse and repeat (and use potions since you don't have any mp ever).  There's just no room to really do anything at all.  Blame it on hard mode?  maybe, or maybe its just kinda boring after a while.the 'war battles' are just, what's the point??  like i played all the suikoden games - the wars were super fun, you felt like you had some agency and got to do some stuff.  In this game, it feels like you're just wasting 20 minutes until the game decides to move on with the script.  Like you don't have to win, you don't have to survive, you just play a couple rounds of this slow battle with little to no strategy, and then you have to watch some more cut scenes.  like why?  why not just watch the cut scene since playing the battle has no point and you can't really lose.i got to the part where I had my base and could collect characters.  I started to enjoy it but that's mixed with some story on rails segments with the other main character (the red guy is the freeform one moving about the world and collecting characters and the blue guy has some stuff where you're locked into a specific place and dungeons and whatever).  basically, i did some plot event with the red guy and then the game was like "okay now you should play the blue guy and catch up the story" - but when it put me as the blue guy, i'm just stuck in this dungeon without enough resources and a low level where i don't get any xp from the monsters or very much money, so I think I've spent a few hours grinding enemies in a dungeon to just,  like "kill a few guys, get money, spend 10 minutes running back to the only town i have access too, load up on potions, run 10 minutes back in, rinse repeat".  I mean its just total ugh - my heroes are clearly under powered for this area i'm stuck in, but i can't get xp and i can't level them up in the over world where the red guy is and yea - this isn't a challenge so much as its just GRIND.  It wouldn't be so bad if I could use magic or if the inn's weren't 3~ battles worth of money (the inns will be like 1800 gold or whatever and you'll get <1000 per fight).  So its just, GRIND GRIND GRIND GRIND where I get no xp, no money, and have to constantly run back and forth to slowly inch my resources up enough to beat the boss of the dungeon.  Is this hard, or is it just annoying.I wanted to like this game, I really did.  But the balancing issues are all over the place and you never know if its gonna be pointlessly easy or just some ridiculous grind for no reason.ugh, and this drives me crazy, but there's HELLA lag when flipping through the menus.  You go to the menu screen and you have to use the shoulder buttons to get to the equipment or items or whatever, and it like, takes FOREVER.  its just a dumb menu, just GO to the next page, right now, don't make me wait, just GO.anyways, I think i'm giving up on this one, or maybe i'll try again if they update it and address the balancing issues.  But  yea, just not feeling it.  they say this is a game for jrpg fans, but I feel like they missed what's good in the classic jrpgs that inspired this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle is a spiritual successor to a game series I love: Suikoden. If you like Suikoden, you'll probably like Eiyuden Chronicle. That might not be helpful comparison because Suikoden never quite caught on like other RPGs of its era, so its understandable if you've never played those games or maybe even heard of them. But the short version of this review is that. If you like Suikoden, you'll probably like Eiyuden Chronicle.So now for the longer version. I feel very conflicted about Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes. On the one hand, it's so much like Suikoden that my nostalgia for those games is doing a lot of heavy lifting to help me look past the game's flaws. On the other, I recognize newcomers to this game probably are going to be put off by a lot of stuff. Eiyuden Chronicle is a turn-based RPG where you recruit over 100 heroes, build up a castle base, and follow the story of these heroes as they fight against a powerful enemy. I'll start with the things I really like about this game.The world, story, and characters for Eiyuden Chronicle are all stand outs in this genre for me. I played the prequel game, Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising, and thought that game was fine. Nothing particularly special but it established an interesting world. I felt this way about Suikoden and I feel the same about Eiyuden Chronicle in that it feels like the world should be incoherent but isn't. The developers have thrown a lot of things they think are fun or interesting into this world that somehow work together. For example, many of the characters are anthropomorphic animals but there are also elves and dwarfs. Even though it seems like this should create some inconsistencies in theme or tone, it just makes the world seem bigger and more interesting because it has all these different thing in it.The story isn't anything particularly special in its broad strokes; it's mostly a story of good triumphing over evil and an underdog winning when the odds are against them. But the moments within the story are strong and unique. With so many recruitable characters, not every character will get a strong arc but it's fun to follow the ones that do as their relationships grow and change. There are some weird and interesting twists that keep things interesting. It also sets the story on a grand scale which contributes to the world feeling big and complicated.The character recruiting and base building aspects are probably what was most unique about Suikoden when it first came out and in the decades since I haven't seen many games duplicate that success. And here Eiyuden Chronicle shines too. Even when a character isn't super deep, they will always have a cool design or contribute something to the base, so you'll want to seek them out and you'll get excited when you enter a town and you see that sweet, sweet unique sprite standing there waiting to be recruited. The rhythm of the game usually goes: complete a main story mission, recruit a bunch of characters. And that's a great rhythm. Plus all the characters are voice-acted which is wild to me for a game of this scale. And even more impressively, the voice acting and writing is great, with maybe one or two characters that might rub you the wrong way. A pretty good ratio considering how many there are in the game.The turn-based combat is also a highlight for me, although it is missing some of the quality of life tweaks that older-style RPGs like Eiyuden Chronicle benefit from. Battles can sometimes go a little slow or drag but there are items and options for avoiding fights if they're getting too frustrating. Because you can have up to 6 characters in your party, plus a support character, there's a lot of room for experimentation. The battle animations are fun and flashy and the hero combo system, where different groups of heroes can team up for an attack are a lot of fun to test out, while you're trying to build a team that synergizes well. You can customize a character's armor and accessories, upgrade their weapon power, and modify their runes which give active benefits like new spells and passive benefits like increased stats.If you can focus on those areas, you'll probably have a good amount of fun with Eiyuden Chronicle, especially if you like RPGs. Unfortunately, to recruit all the characters and get the best ending, you have to do Eiyuden Chronicle's minigames, which are the least interesting parts of this game. There are a lot of minigames in Eiyuden Chronicle and I'm sorry to say I didn't really enjoy any of them. We're living in a golden age of minigames where some games have minigames that eclipse the main game or go on to be spun off as their own standalone games. So it's hard to look at Eiyuden Chronicle's fishing mingame where you wait for an exclamation mark to appear above your character's head and then press the button and feel any kind of excitement. That fishing minigame is something video games had mastered years and years ago and even with nostalgia, it just isn't compelling (although the fish are very weird and silly which I appreciated). Of all the minigames, beigoma (it's like battle tops) was my least favorite (with cooking coming in a close second) and the theater was the best. With the theater, you put on a play where you cast your characters in different roles and somehow it's all voice acted which is an incredible achievement. The insult to injury here is that there isn't usually a big benefit to doing any of these minigames, especially considering the time you have to put into them, so once you've tried them, you probably won't go back. This is where Eiyuden Chronicle is too close to its inspirations. It adds things that it doesn't really need that slow things down in an unfortunate way. My best advice would be to do only what you have to with the minigames and then leave them behind for the much better parts of this game.So that's the long review. They don't make games like Eiyuden Chronicle anymore, for better and for worse. I think people who enjoy RPGs, especially turn-based RPGs, will enjoy this one if they stick mostly to the main story, character recruiting, and base upgrades. Despite some gripes, I don't regret playing this game at all and enjoyed it from start to finish. I'll be overjoyed if we get another Eiyuden Chronicle because it feels like the start of something incredibly cool and unique, picking up right where Suikoden left off.

_childDocuments_.review: *Update: Review amended to reflect failure by developer to deliver promised Season Pass DLC on time.*Overall: While it won't set the world on fire Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes is a competently made game from a veteran team at a reasonable price point. Even if you aren't a fan of the Suikoden series from which it derives its a solid traditional JRPG in its own right that will entertain you for its forty plus hour run time if you can get past its flaws. A definite buy even at full price, especially the Digital Deluxe Edition which gives you both the soundtrack and a season pass for just three dollars additional.Pros:[+] Combat: It might be turned-based but its extremely busy. You have six characters to play with at a time, each of whom will have four to six runes slots, plus combat gimmicks, initiative positions, formations, teamwork attacks and support characters. Regardless of how you play you'll have plenty to do and customize once the game hits its stride at around Level 10-14.[+] Presentation: While its not Cyberpunk 2077, the game is beautiful; The use of 3-D backgrounds and forced perspective coupled with very expressive and highly detailed 2-D sprites gives the game storybook feel, as if it were playing out on a pop-up diorama.[+] Music: Both Naruke and Sakurabe are industry veterans with impressive resumes (Dark Souls, Tales of Destiny, Wild Arms, etc) and they deliver a solid soundtrack that is a joy to listen to. Getting the soundtrack as part of the Digital Deluxe edition was a real treat though unfortunately it isn't the Complete Soundtrack, only covering the first third of the game.[+] Size: Setting aside the plot and the titular hundred heroes, there is a lot to do in the game; Exploration, base-management, a half-dozen minigames and collectibles.Neutral:[~] Traditional JRPG: Eiyuden Chronicle is definitely done in the vein of the JRPGs of the 80 and 90s. Meaning it does not have many of the conveniences that modern players have gotten used to; There's no hand holding when it comes to the mechanics or missable content, points of no return/lock-in pop up out of nowhere, resources are always tight, no fast travel, healing is sparse, fights can be unforgiving, dungeons can be really long and save points can be few and far between (Heck you can't even save on the World Map!).Cons:[-] Localization: Even a cursory glance at the Steam forums will tell you this is a massive issue for a lot of “players,” many of whom have sworn that they won't buy the game unless Rabbit and Bear redoes the entire thing to be faithful to the original Japanese text but really its just another overblown manifestation of the culture wars sweeping the industry. While there are indeed some Americanisms, like Mio's infamous gender joke or Lian's use of the word “chud”, it does not really appreciably its characters or its story. All told its more akin to Tidus' Macarena joke in Final Fantasy X than the completely unhinged ADV dub of Ghosts at School. Of greater concern are mistranslations that actually impact the game, whether causing needless ambiguity in the game's mechanics or UI and, in at least one occassion, providing outright wrong information (Reyna's recruitment condition). [-] Dubbing: Clearly this aspect of the game was remotely done and was impacted by its slim budget because while voice acting for the main characters voices are passable, the side character VA's performances are uneven. Some VA's just can't act or at least did not receive any direction from the studio (like Francesca) while others' have been subjected to atrocious sound-mixing (example Cassandra), resulting in delivery that is off-key, garbled or overly loud.[-] Underdeveloped Mechanics: While as mentioned there is a lot to do, its pretty shallow. Many of the mini-games are mechanically simple (heck fishing is just hitting a button when an exclamation point shows up) and some of the new systems added like castle-building are ultimately just pointless fetch quests used to pad out the game. Of special note is the War-system which is a definitive step back from Suikoden II and V, both of which gave you the ability to customize unit rosters and unit types while fighting on a large game board with Advanced Wars style special abilities. In contrast the current iteration has more or less degenerated into a scripted shoving match.[-] Technical Issues: The game has quite a few, mostly borne out of having adapt to simultaneous console releases. Though most have been patched, several still remain to be addressed like ghost inputs on joyticks for controllers, non-rebindable keys on MKB and noticeably slow menu speeds.[-] Bad UI Communication: This game has a lot of mechanics. Unfortunately many of them are either hidden from the UI or unexplained in the Help menu (they don't even tell you what the character's stats do!). For example, the game doesn't tell you that all characters have affinities for the six spell elements in the game but nowhere does it appear on the individual characters' sheets. So might end up giving a favorite mage a bad element and they end up underperforming for seemingly no reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Following the legacy of a series that had decades of work poured into nearly a dozen games and spinoffs is no easy task.  This game seeks to fill a void left behind by a long running fantasy world that has been abandoned by its owners.At the start of playing Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes I enjoyed playing a game of spot the comparisons.  The tropes, story beats, character archetypes, every similarity between it and the early Suikoden games I could.  There are plenty to be found, and as I played I was wondering if the game would actually stand on its own.By the end of the game, I feel like I've come to appreciate the world more as its own.  I'm spending less time focusing on the similarities between the series whose legacy has come to a sad end, and more thinking of the legacy that might be started.I really hope in another decade we can looking at the Eiyuden Chronicle series as one that grows just as vast and intriguing as its predecessor was.  That what we've delved into so far is just a small piece of a bigger world ready to expand wherever the imagination can take it.If you want a game that has a bevy of the qualities the early Suikoden games offered, I wholeheartedly recommend this for you, and I truly hope Rabbit & Bear Studios continues to explore the world they've introduced us to in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: First, the good points:The music is great, there's full voice-acting, and the character sprites are on-point. Grinding experience for low-level party members is very easy and the 'Support' option exists to place aside characters who are forced in your party but whom you may not wish to use. There's a little icon in the minimap which guides you to where you're supposed to go next, which is pretty handy.However:- The full voice-acting is a double-edged sword. The dialogue is very clunky- I find that many long conversations and monologues could have been shortened significantly while conveying the same amount of information. What's worse is the need to keep repeating the same voice clips over and over again; Whether it be the fortune teller saying her magic words over and over, people in battle saying their battle cries repeatedly, and worst of all the teleporter who feels the need to pat herself on the back before and after every teleportation. You'll be hearing Carrie a LOT, and it is NOT pleasant.Yes you can turn off the voices, but it's a shame to do it when the effort was put into recording it at all. The script just needed an editor and some restraint. - Speaking of, one of the earliest bosses is a poorly designed shell-game, and every time you miss, or even make an attempt, you have to listen to Mellore and Nowa repeat the same dialogue. It gets very old very quickly.- Dungeons can be very long slogs involving a LOT of backtracking. Worse, if there's a treasure chest in a boss room, after you beat the boss, they kick you out of the dungeon so you need to trek all the way back to the end of the dungeon to get it. - Many of the characters are annoying one-note archetypes who were already portrayed much better in the Suikoden games Eiyuden is homaging/parodying. There are times when they'll have conversations alluding to long histories or interesting incidents in the past, but these are not a substitute for actual character development that we should be seeing in-game. - The Minigames are long, tedious affairs. The cooking minigame seems glitched to where it appears the RNG decides if you win or lose to where you need to reload until the game gives you the win. The beyblade parody feels tonally out of place and requires WAY too much investment of time and effort. Worst of all, you NEED to play all the way through both minigame questlines to recruit every character. - The army AND the duel battles are not intuitive. The explanations are poor, and I ended up blindly clicking through until winning/losing. I've been through six war battles thus far and still have no idea how they work. Luckily it seems like they're just glorified cutscenes and it doesn't much matter WHAT you do- something will interrupt the battle and you'll win or lose to move the plot along.- The plotline is flimsy at best, character motivations seem arbitrary. Inklings of good ideas exist, but were done far better in Suikoden 2.- YOU DON'T GET TO NAME YOUR OWN CASTLE. YOU HAVE TO PICK FROM (Presumably kickstarter backer) PRE-GEN OPTIONS. ONE OF THE QUINTESSENTIAL PERKS OF A SUIKODEN STYLE GAME.  - Speaking of Kickstarter backers, they seem to want to wedge evidence of those rewards into every aspect of the game- random NPC sprites, animals, gravestones, soldiers in the obnoxious info feed during war battles, all of these and more are crammed full of what I assume to be backer names which is VERY distracting.- Also, speaking of the castle, instead of just gaining castle features like shops and services for free upon recruiting the character, you ALSO need to farm resources and dither around with a Skill Tree style menu to build those same additions. The sidequest to GET the characters is often enough without having to grind, although some may enjoy it. - What purpose is there in having a front and back row if any enemy can just jump over the tanks to reach your mages and healers?- Perhaps some Unite attacks could render Suikoden broken here and there, but being forced to wait and bank SP to execute them while the enemy can spam powerful AOE is not fun.- Who in the name of God thought Pastole was a good idea for a character? Unless you have a VERY nuanced and permissive sense of humor, he would be offensive to EVERYone.- While the animation of the character sprites are very well animated, the enemies generally look like they were made for cheap app games like Hero Wars or Mutants: Genetic Gladiators, and the bosses that are fully rendered in 3D animation just look out of place. Render them with the same art style as the heroes, or at least render all enemies the same way. I'm starting to get close to the end of the game (112/120 recruited) and, while I appreciate the work that went into this game, I'm disappointed by the final product. It is, as mentioned, a hollow imitation of Suikoden 2.(Whatever insults or constructive criticisms I could hurl at this game, there's probably no greater condemnation than the fact that I fell asleep playing it.  )In fact, the most (and only) real fun I've had with it is when the Developer Build somehow got turned on and I got to mess around with the Debug mode for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: - Combat- Music- Characters- Story- Visuals- Duels- Base- Minigames- Voice Over- War Battles- Localization- Background Image for Towns and Outdoor Dungeons.- Party/Item Management Menu- Some Missing QoL features Combat is fantastic. Always have loved the 6 team parties, the front/back row set up, hero combos*, and rune system. Playing on hard, and not grinding levels, has led to having some difficult boss fights that require using all the combat mechanics except hero combos.  Yes, random encounters will devolve into using auto-combat. But outside of souls-like games, I have never had "difficult" random encounters or trash mobs. Some of the rare random encounters will act like mini-bosses and auto will not be good enough unless you are overlevelled. *Only complaint is hero combos do not seem worth it unless they heal or buff. Damage on them seems bugged. The music is top notch. They do a great job at using it with the main story. The only thing I want from the music, is even more of it! Not really music but the only thing I would critique in the sound category is that they could have used some more ambient/background noise in places. Like tavern sounds, city bustle, nature noises, applause, or sounds of cheers.  The characters are great. Very distinct, anime-like personalities. I struggle with deciding who to use in my party cause I like so many of them. There are even characters that I thought I was going to not like off first impression and then came to really like them. Whether that is from story moments or use in combat. As someone who loved Suikoden series, I can already see some of these optional side characters continuing their stories in any hopeful sequel.  The main story is very solid and interesting. Having trouble on what to say without spoilers. I highly enjoyed it. Looking forward to learning more of the world in a hopeful sequel. Love all the nods to the Suikoden series and there are quite a bit. My main critique about the story would be its pacing. A lot of events just happen back to back it feels. Some events are stated to happen in incredibly fast amounts of time early on. I felt like this could be handled better with more hints at what your enemies, allies, or strategist is up to.   The characters, enemies, and animations are fantastic. I have always thought the Suikoden 2D visuals were some of the best. These are just more defined and beautifully animated for the modern era. The 3D dungeons and towns are good but clearly give a feel of older generation; probably a limitation of developing for Switch too. Have surprisingly caught myself though finding a blend of the superb 2D characters and the 3D world still giving me multiple eye catching moments. Main critique: The background image in towns/outdoor dungeons. Duels return from Suikoden and are just as fun. The story moments and animations are great. Do wish they used them more for recruiting too. Base building system is solid, fun progression. More interaction with building up the place compared to Suikoden games. You can quickly build passive resource generation early on that will take care of the vast majority of your needs. Only thing I would change is that I wish our base was one of the Runebarrows. Would have made it more aesthetically distinct.  Minigames have been enjoyable. The Theatre is by far the best with you being able to slot any recruitable character into roles with vast majority of it fully voiced. Hot spring is typical Suikoden. Card game is really solid. Beigoma is not for me but was able to enjoy its side-story. Eggracing is decent enough for what it is. Really enjoy the cooking side-story but sadly the cooking mini-game has been outright bugged since release. Easy to win but not working properly. Main issue: All the games could use more polish/QoL. Most of the voice over work is great. Japanese voice over will have some notable credits for anime fans. English voice over is also good for the most part. Had many favorites. I enjoy the use of different accents to bring characters to life. With that said, there are also english ones that feel like they are not so good or the voice doesn't fit the character.  War battles are alright. I preferred the more Fire Emblem-lite system from Suikoden 2. These ones play out more like a incredibly basic version of Total War fights, but turn based instead of real-time.  Has some clear issues in places but overall negativity blown way out of proportion. From what I have seen though is that the main story itself is the same. Outside of 1 character personality that seems heavily changed throughout, it is just certain random moments with some characters will seem super off and out of nowhere. A lot of the G-PG insults come from the game itself going for a E10 rating, which just takes you out of the moment when these adults are using 5-10yr old language. Most people would not blink at the dialogue if it was using insults age appropriate to the character.  In towns and outdoor dungeons the background image uses 3D terrain models with very little texture or detail. The low detailed background only works when you do your best to hide or ignore it. But you will sometimes get these outdoor pan out shots, and the background becomes apparent to you. Worst is probably if you go to the top of your castle for the scenic view, and it just green and brown shapes with no detail.  The general menu you will be opening and using the most, for party and item management, is very clunky to use. Takes a good while to get somewhat used to it. Still always catch myself fumbling through it. Will say that I feel that the menus for stores, mini-games, and other home base stuff is mostly done well. Warehouse could use a sort option. There are some other QoL things I find a little frustrating the game lacks but might get updated. This is my list of things as of May 9th 2024:  1. Game  a Help page that details what each stat does. Power, Magic, Phys Def, and Magic Def are obvious. But what exactly does Skill, Speed, and Luck affect? Nothing in-game tells you at all. As well as character elemental affinity added to their status page so people know what magic they have bonuses or negatives with.2. Game could really benefit from a side-quest log for recruitment. Sometimes you might forget what someone wanted and its annoying that you have to google and hope for no spoilers or go all the way to them just to be reminded. 3. All mini-games could desperately benefit from a pass of polish. Nothing wrong with the games themselves. Things like winning 2/3 beigoma ends the match instead of having to play a 3rd pointless round. Speeding up the animation placement of cards or switching of turns in the card game to make matches go by at a better pace. Fix joystick controls for shi'ark racing. Or cooking not bugged. 4. Epilogue slides need to be slowed down. Hard to read. Overall, I love the game. Been waiting for this for so long. I am happy to have the spirit of the Suikoden franchise return. A franchise that was so dear to my heart growing up. Eiyuden is a world that has felt instantly familiar to me. I greatly enjoyed it. Hope there will be a sequel. Cheers Rabbit & Bear!

_childDocuments_.review: I was so hiped about the game and now I see just a bunch of good ideas and rushed to the end. Which seems to be kind of the fault of Konami as well, because they tried to torp this game, since they saw the money it made with their backers. But there are also so many issues and I really hope they fix the most and improve the game.I would say the most important one is the localization for English and the translation from English to other languages. Because this is nowadays a thing that nearly every game studio is doing and it lowers the quality of the game. Especially, when you got a rich language like Japanese and others. This loca is so low quality, that I sometimes think the conversations are retarded and even inappropriate. On one hand this game is for kids, but on the other hand they put some sexual content in, when it is not the time and the place for it. Sure, Suikoden had some hints here and there, but not like this and not that blunt in your face. For example: You are on an important mission and everyone repeats this to you, one guy is like "I don't like girls, but this woman here *rawr*". Even the content before was not sexual at all.And this is just one thing and I ask myself if this is game doesn't even take itself serious, why should I?Kids got the voice of a grown man, women got the voice of men, men got the voice of women. This is just  here and there, but you won't miss it.And I still got the feeling the main character is retarded. I hope this is not the case in the japanese version, because this is just. WHY?! Why would anybody give him the authority of an army? He can be tricked and/or manipulated easily. But that's not a problem at all, because the plot said so. And he wants to help people, so they will join your ranks, because you are a nice guy. You know what? In Suikoden I and II, the main character had to suffer and overcome these issues. (sure these games had also issues, but nothing like this one) This guy is the friendly dude and he will help you and you will join him. Because he is just at the right time at the right place.Marisa and the guardians feel more like a filler. If they would have been cut out, I think the story would have been better. Nowa trying to stop the empire from outside and Seign from inside. But nah.And to add some postive stuff, I like Carrie (The teleporting lady) and Francesca (the healer with an anger issue).Game breaking bugs are still in the game, you can lose 2-3h of gameplay, just because of a random crash and this one is random, because it can happen when you are switching to the loading screen. The loading screen appears on every location, when you enter the world, map, house, etc. The cooking contest was one of the most funniest part of Suikoden 2. It is back, but in really bad. Resources are added to the world and can't really be used for cooking. Which was possible in Suikoden 2, but not in this game. It looks to me like this feature wasn't finished before the release. They already addressed the issue with the contest score and that they will fix it. But my issue lies within the depth of this mini-game and I think it is pathetic to call it even a mini-game. To explain a bit better, in Suikoden 2, there was a cooking contest game where you had to choose the dishes for the categories and also the ingredients to "improve" the dish. For example, if you would take a main course for an appetizer, you would lose points. In Eiyuden, it doesn't matter! You can have the appetizer as dessert and if this is the favorite dish for one person "TADA", you get the high score. On top of that, why I think this is incomplete, You can catch different fish and get different ingredienst like sugar, pepper, etc. But it will be only shown as "fish" and "food".Recrutable characters won't show up as they should (already addressed by the devs, but still in the game).What the game is teaching you, is sometimes not the thing you need to do. And this is something for the gamedesigners to fix, asap. What I mean by that: Fishing will be shown on different spots and different locations at the same thing. But not, when you want the recruit one special character. This is a totally different location, no hint, nothing. And on top of that so small, when you blink, you will miss it.Also, the game is withholding important informations in the tutorials. Things you should know will be presented later, with different characters who can teach you.When you enter the skirmish battle, you can't leave till you won/lost it. This is so annyoing.The Beigoma mini-game doesn't finish after 2 rounds won/lost. YOU HAVE TO PLAY THE 3rd ROUND!The castle, good idea, but the implementation is clumsy at best. Sometimes you need a special character to get further. Even this got nothing to do with the related area. Why should I build a theater when I want to upgrade my guild? This needs to be reworked properly.I could go on and on with this one and I really hope they will fix these issues, because it is getting super annoying. You just can't ignore the issues they got, because it is happening all the time. I really want this game to be good, but in this state right now. If you know japanese, maybe you got a better experience than the ones who go through the english conversations. <.<Btw. Before I forget about it. The music is really good! (fishing needs some sound btw. not only the "plop" and the animated catching)

_childDocuments_.review: As a spiritual successor to Suikoden, this game succeeds , and is everything that I could have hoped for as a huge fan of the earlier entries.It's everything Suikoden was, just . Recruiting heroes, but  of them. 1-on-1 duels, but  spectacular. Headquarters, but  expanded. War battles, but  ... better.Murayamas writing is . The interplay between characters is great, and the political machinations of all parties are sublime.No matter which way the wind blows, everyone always acts appropriately and in a believeable manner. Nobody is made stupid just to progress the plot in the direction it needs to go.I truly appreciate that the antagonist is strong both in body  in mind. An intimidating presence throughout, whose machinations are always impressive, without taking anything for granted and underestimating his opponents.I was  engaged in the story the entire way through, and enjoyed it wholeheartedly,  the end. The only thing I didn't like as much was how there's one scene that is practically a 1:1 copy of a scene from Suikoden.The sprites by Kawano are amazing. I was shocked how good they looked when I first saw them. Some obviously look better than others, but most of the designs are really interesting in some way.I also found most attacks really appealing, and most spells and special attacks look really cool. While the 3D itself isn't anything to write home about, the way they blend 2D sprites into a 3D world looks really nice. It looks really interesting.I  the system they made for upgrading your HQ. Previously, you would just recruit a proprietor, and they would add a service to your HQ. When you've recruited enough heroes, your HQ would upgrade automatically.Now, recruiting the hero is only the first step. You now also need enough resource to build their establishment, and then you can even . The HQ still upgrades, but now that is itself an upgrade, and when you do that, you unlock  upgrades to go for. Very exciting stuff.Even better yet, you can even customize some aspects of your HQ too. The options might be a bit lacking (maybe it's just because I didn't really like any of the options), but it's better to have a choice rather than not.My favourite war system in Suikoden is the one in Suikoden 3, where you build squads out of your recruited heroes, and then have them fight opposing squads using the regular combat system (but automated). I did think that Suikoden 2 had the better presentation and more control over where you move the squads. So my hope was that Eiyuden would have a mixture of both these systems. Which is basically exactly what we got.The squad building from Suikoden 3 has been simplified, and the overview is much less visually appealing compared to Suikoden 2, but overall I am very happy with how it turned out. What I don't like about them though is how each battle is  scripted, so while the story plays out in a nice way, there's almost no way to make an impact one way or another.Another thing I  enjoyed is how most bosses have a gimmick mechanic. They add another layer to the boss fights, and you have to put extra throught into your actions, which made them more interesting than just a somewhat harder normal enemy. Not all gimmicks are significant, and some seem to just be there "for the sake of it". That said, I still wish that  boss had some sort of gimmick.All of this being said, the game  has a whole lot of flaws as well. There are a number of bugs that softlock you out of progressing, and all platforms suffer from crashes.The worst problem, by far, is how it  likes wasting your time. It takes like 5-10 seconds to appraise an item, and you can only do them one by one. So better be ready to spam confirm for several minutes if your inventory is full of them.Whenever you hatch or retire an eggleg, there's a bunch of pointless splash screens that just stay there for a few seconds, but they are not skippable. The card game is also unnecessarily slow, the AI takes its turn slower than I do, instead of being instant (or at least letting us skip the RP).Similarly, the war game also makes you watch a bunch of mini soldiers hit each other for  too long, before it moves on to do the exact same thing . It's cool the first couple of times, not so much the 100th time. The fact that the Eggleg race makes you watch the entire race makes more sense, but it still consumes  of time due to just how many races you have to run to do them all.Finally, there's been a lot of discussion about the localization not respecting the source material which is,  true.While most of the changes are "inoffensive", the sheer amount of  changes is staggering. Whenever I would listen to the Japanese, I would almost always catch some pointless change, and  were  of these changes for the better.There's even a couple of memes in there, and you don't even need to know Japanese at all to catch those, many others only need basic knowledge.However, I've seen the claim that the English version is "disgusting" (or similar) but as much as I hate localization, I can't really agree with that judgement either. It's definitively far from a good localization, but it's still ... passable, and the game itself is good enough that I think it would be a real shame to miss out on it.Obviously, this is still very disappointing, but I also expect nothing less from the industry today.I think the phrase  is a perfect description of this game. While its currently suffering from quite a few issues, it is still an incredible game with an amazing story at its core.I've got no doubts that the bugs, and other issues, will eventually be fixed, but the shoddy localization will forever remain a blemish.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not been updating my review recently but as far as I am aware no major patches have released since I finished the game.The game is good overall, it is indeed what Suikoden fans were waiting save a few shortcomings BUT you need to know this game isn't actually finished! Not in the sense that the story isn't complete but in the sense that entire game mechanics and systems range from unpolished to completely broken.THE BEST RECOMMENDATION I CAN GIVE YOU RIGHT NOW IS WAIT FOR A FEW PATCHES. I'm fairly certain I am going to change my recommendation into a positive one if the fix the biggest issues, all things that shouldn't have gotten past QA and should be easily solved by the devs in a reasonable timeframe. _____________________________________________Here's a concise list:- The scaling for all low level magic in the game is broken. They DO NOT do more damage depending on the character's magic attack attribute.- The scaling for all team combos in the game is broken, apparently whatever damage the combo is supposed to do is reduced (divided by the number of characters participating). Therefore some combos hitting all the enemies are still somewhat viable for random encounters but any other is a net damage loss.- Currently one character is easily and permanently bug-gable out of recruitment (one was fixed, one more remains).- Text speed cannot be changed and it's slow (this makes the next point egregiously bad).- On non-voiced dialogues tapping A/X on the controller skips any dialogue bubble entirely even if it's not finished yet! (in any other game your first input would fill the text and finish the sentence, allowing some time or waiting for a second input before skipping). - Battles and menus have weird wait times in which you're locked out of inputs, it adds up quickly in a game with un-skippable random encounters and constant menu navigation.- The english localization is not great. Some use of puerile jargon, obscure wordplay, weird made up words that don't fit the game can be off-putting at times, especially in the beginning but it's not a disaster like people say.- The way the camera follows you is inconsistent and often completely off, at times negating all vision while at times zooming out to no end. Weird and it takes you out of the experience.- Any configuration of the battle plan for auto-battle that would take priority actions into account is broken. THE ONE THING you want to do when engaging with it, choosing priorities while avoiding MP consumption, is THE ONE THING you cannot even try to do because there is no option for that.- The screen-shake cannot be turned off and the main character's first skill, which he will use in almost every battle, has the most obnoxious case of excessive and unnecessary screen-shake in the history of the genre. If you have photosensitive epilepsy but are usually ok with this kind of game, beware of this one.- The Eggfoot racing minigame is the most evil timesink scam I've ever seen in a videogame on top of being one of the most boring. It's an insult to gamers and their time.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, just finished 100% this game, and my verdict is: yes, but.    It is a gorgeous homage to PS1 era JRPGs, obviously the Suikoden series in particular. Is it as good as Suikoden 1 or 2? In my opinion, probably not, though in many ways it comes close. The visuals and music are great, the voice acting is impressive, if a little uneven, and the gameplay definitely feels like something straight out of the era. And that last one is part of one of my "but"s with this game. When trying to capture the feel of a classic game, one must remember that some of the changes to the genre that have happened over the decades since were for the better. I won't go into specifics here, but just know that it is a bit clunky in places that, while making it authentic, end up feeling a bit grating compared to a more modern game... which, this actually is.The story is decent, again very much in the vein of the series they were trying to emulate/spiritually succeed. And just like the Suikoden games, the main conceit of having such a huge cast is neat in concept, but in reality it means the majority of the characters are going to be lackluster either in battle, in story, or in both. As someone who values story and character development as the highest points of an RPG, this has always been a problem for me since the first Suikoden game, though not such a horrible one that it ruins the game by any means: one simply has to go into it knowing what to expect.    There is a very steep difficulty jump halfway through the game that I found rather jarring. Things went from rather standard JRPG fare to "you're gonna have to carry LOTS of healing items and use them after every single battle, and if you are unlucky and one of your weaker characters gets targeted more than once in a round they WILL go down". Maybe difficulty is the wrong word, because it is not necessarily difficult if you adapt accordingly, it just feels weird because it jumps so drastically, and honestly can become a bit tedious. That said, the boss battles are pretty fun throughout, especially the ones with fun gimmicks.    My personal biggest gripe, which I know not everyone will share, is the minigames. Too many, and of much more relevance, most of them take a LONG time to complete, wearing out any welcome they might have had long before you earn your ultimate reward. The ship racing game has HORRIBLE controls, but thankfully is the quickest to complete if you can manage to get past them. The top battling game and the cooking battles are the only ones you need to put time into if you don't care about achievements because you need to complete or nearly complete them to recruit a couple of  characters. And while the over-the-top yet totally straight-faced way they handle them is a bit hilarious, the mini-games themselves are... not fun. The card game is actually not bad, I actually enjoyed playing it a bit. Which quickly got ground out of me as I had to win 121 matches to get the achievement. Seriously, who thought that many was a good idea?! It was Blitz Ball all over again: a decent idea that WAY overstayed its welcome! And finally the eggfoot races. F*** the eggfoot races. Boring. Long. Crappy rewards. If it wasn't for the achievement I wouldn't have touched it.    Anyway. tl;dr: It is a fun game and a very faithful and loving tribute to the Suikoden game series, but a few questionable design choices and a mind-numbing batch of mini-games keep it from greatness. If you are a fan of old-school JRPGs, especially Suikoden, and either don't care about achievements or don't mind awful mini-games as much as I do then definitely give it a whirl. If nothing else you will get your money's worth in the course of completing it as it took me almost 120 hours to snag that final achievement.P.S. Special shoutout to the theater segment. It is goofy, the rewards are decent but definitely skippable, and you only need to get an S rating in one of them to get the achievement, but I found myself intentionally creating the worst possible casting just for the laughs. They didn't have to fully voice all of these little plays, but I am so glad that they did.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a kickstarter backer right when that first teaser dropped. Awesome sprite work. Fluid animations and battles. Great OST. However, from what I've seen in the first few hours of play though is a far cry from what I was anticipating. The entire progression of the game seems to be designed either unintentionally or deliberately to waste your time:- Trivial overworld fights that don't self-resolve: If the fight gives me the option to "let the monsters go", why do we bother with entering the battle at all?- Tedious backtracking: I met a character while leaving the city who directed me to a eastern gulch to fight a boss for her recruitment. In a town in the opposite direction, a character demands you prove yourself by slaying three generic mobs in that same zone.  Couldn't the fact that I had the initial character be proof enough? That's two visits to the same zone, two crossings of the same map,  over fifteen worthless encounters, a bunch of loading screens and a new party member who's got a really lame look and personality. I don't doubt this type of thing will be happening frequently in the future.-Uninspired dungeons: When encounters are random, I want to spend less time in dungeons, not more. But nearly every fork in the path leads to a chest that you feel compelled to grab, which just opens you up to more random encounters. No optional bosses, no shortcuts, no real secrets.- Auto battles: This is more of a personal gripe, but I firmly believe that a game that gives the option to speed up or allow auto battles is self-reporting that it's battle system and progression is bad. At least a game like Bravely Second doubled down on grinding by allowing chained encounters and action queues as well as giving the option to disable fights.I only played the opening of Suikoden 2 on an emulator, but at least that game had a nice dramatic hook in the opening moments. I'm really not appreciating this slow windup when the pacing issues are front and center. I can't in good conscience recommend this JRPG over the hundred others that got it right.EDIT: Apparently there is a journal and map, just not in the main item menu. Whoops.

_childDocuments_.review: While it's got some unpolished edges as to be expected of a kickstarted game this big, it still really captures that beautiful spirit of Suikoden and other PS1 JRPGs of that era. The sprite work is gorgeous and you can really tell a lot of love and passion went into this game. My only real crticisms are:-The main unpolished issue of the game is the constant loading screens, something most JRPGs don't really suffer from nowadays (heck suikoden 2 definitely didn't have them for their battles so the fact this game does is surprising) the loading is fast enough to be an almost non issue tho (like half a second to a second at most), it's just surprising that it's there at all.-The localization quality isn't quite the best as I expect nowadays from games, mainly in side stuff/throwaway lines, but it's not bad either cus other scenes will be super well written and performed, just very hit and miss unfortunately. -English VA can be wildly hit or miss as well, my guess is some weren't given great direction or context for their lines.-The difficulty is very very easy, even on Hard mode. _childDocuments_.review: Haven't gotten as far in the game as most of the reviews, but what I've played has been pretty fun. I don't think I've met a character yet that I've disliked, and I think I've found around 30 of them so far. There are definitely some characters that are better in battle than others, but I don't think there's any that can't find some sort of niche. It's easy to get comfortable with a given team, and I don't think this game means to do that. The rune system is pretty interesting, but I'm not sure how long it'll last. Every team I've been on has a Water rune somewhere in it, and some of the non-magic, non-locked runes don't seem like they're doing much. My biggest gripe with the game is the controls. Everything feels intuitive, and I believe this game was built with game controllers in mind. However, it's got the tiniest dead zone recognition. After I finish moving a joystick, there's a decent chance your lead character will just move off in a seemingly random direction until you flick the joystick just right to get it to stop dead center. I haven't had this issue with other games I play on controller. Hopefully they add a bit more support for controller dead zones in a future update.Overall it's good. Nice cast of characters and some of that old-school JRPG charm (whether you love or hate it). Can't universally recommend it, but if it sounds like it's up your alley then go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: So, after hearing all the complaining about this game and having opted to give it a fair shake, here's my two cents:- It's a solid retro JRPG and many of its downsides are the result of it being too faithful to old school game design/mechanics. It's valid if those choices annoy you, but as far as I know the game was always meant to be like this. Hell, comparing it to real old school stuff I've recently played like, say, Shining Force, this game is positively modern in every way.- IMO it looks good and the characters are fun enough even if tropey. It manages to feel consistent with the prequel even if that one was a Metroidvania-ish adventure game and this one is a turn-based RPG.- The whole tantrum in some circles about woke dialogue and terrible localization is kind of  ridiculous. That throwaway line about being sure if a golem is a he in context seemed to me more like " a golem is an it" kind of thing rather than some gender identity thing like people are trying to make it seem in order to complain. And even if for some reason it was a gender identity thing that made zero sense in context, it was a single line of dialogue and the other characters don't even react to it. I haven't run into any more of this really unbearable wokeism being shoved down my throat for roughly 10+ hours I've played it. If the game has one vaguely "woke" line of dialogue per 10 hours, I'd say flipping out because of the politics they inserted into it makes you look like a crybaby.- The complaints about a slow pace and simplistic and not terribly engaging story are fair. I just played Rise of the Third Power, a much humbler indie game,  and it does a much better job of portraying different factions engaging in political scheming while some try to prevent an all out war from breaking out. That game keeps the pace going by pushing the main story and having the side quests be little detours you can do while progressing it without going out of your way that much, while this one often feels like you're mostly doing side quests that don't really matter and that feel like run of the mill filler. All in all, it's an okay game. Not as good as some of its defenders claim, but nowhere as bad as its detractors also claim.
