_childDocuments_.review: A fun and simple platformer with action gameplay. In this game, you spend most of the time going back and forth between town and dungeon as more areas open up with some of them being just optional area for extra loots and for quests.The biggest concern most people fuzz over is the quest design and how most of it is just a short and simple fetch quest. While you may not be going on a grand adventure for a 3-parter that will take 5 hours to complete, the quest design is fitting for what the game is about. Most of your quest givers are just plain and boring villagers that want their slight inconvenience dealth with. That premise might sound boring for a quest but seeing the town becoming livelier and seeing each npc actually have their own agenda to deal with is a nice change. Even most of the generic looking npcs do have their own name and their own development when you accept these short quests that involves them over and over. So short and plain they may be, these quests and the dialogue and development provide really make you feel like you aren't just another adventurer in town anymore and is actually the new friendly neighbor who just moved in.So while not a grand game to write a lot about, it certainly does what it needs to serve as the appetizer for the mainline game.

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle Rising is not a bad game. But sadly, it's even more not a good game.Game has lots of quests. However, all of those are toned down to simple fetch quests. Main quests, side quests, talking/hunting/gathering - all quests end up as fetch quest.From the point above, game has lots of dialogues. However, it's way too many dialogues. At one point I've stopped reading side quest dialogues, then the same happened with the main quest dialogues. I've got the overall idea of what's happening but details and talking are so dragged out that it's annoyingly boring to go through.From the point above, game has lots of characters. Three are playable as your party (switching between them freely within dungeons), some primary characters and many many secondary characters. However, while they seem to have different backgrounds and personalities, they are already forgotten. Especially the non-essential ones.Village feels dead. You improve shops and facilities, you complete secondary quests and after a short cutscene you have a feeling that the village grew. More background characters appear, it becomes lively visually. But there is no player interaction between player and characters unless it's part of yet another tedious quest. You can't talk to merchants and get a changing commentary about how their business is growing, you can't talk to village residents and see how their attitude changes. Nothing, unless there's a "!" above their head.Game also has no challenge. It's too easy. You end up killing everything with one hit or one combo except for the bosses. But even those are not hard enough to make your party faint or make you grind a bit for a level or two.There are rings that are meant to boost your stats, temporary boosts from potions and other means. Yet for the first playthrough you hardly need even healing potions.After you complete the game, there is an option to load pre-final state and change game difficulty to Hard. Makes enemies stronger for a couple of dungeons, then you breeze through the rest of the side quests and all the bosses on Hard difficulty just as you've done before on Normal., Eiyuden Chronicle Rising could be a great game but it underperforms in so many ways that the end result is mediocre at best. I enjoyed the first 3-5 hours, then got bored but decided to finish the title anyways (15h total for Normal difficulty with all the upgrades and side quests available, +2h after that to 100% the game on Hard with new side quests and new upgrades).P.S. I still have some hopes left for the next title as Eiyuden Chronicle Rising seem to be a prologue of some sorts.

_childDocuments_.review: Basic premise/StoryFrom developer studio, Natsume Atari and Rabbit & Bear Studios and directed by Hirohisa Ota. Eiyuden Chronicle Rising is set in the same world as Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes. A prequel where you play a very small cast of characters, participate in town-upgrading elements and unravel what secrets the town has. Unique GameplayIn the beginning, you can only control one character. CJ. is a young budding scavenger who is looking to get rich by finding treasure. She’ll have to help out the townspeople before qualifying to get a license to travel deeper into the surrounding areas nearby. But along the way, she won’t be alone. The gameplay is pretty simple. You can jump and attack with upgrades to the combat as you gather materials from the environment and enemies to acquire the necessary materials to buy upgrades. Thereby improving your combat repertoire. Sooner or later more companions will join you on your adventure. Making the gameplay fresh in some way. Final thoughts/RuminationsDid not experience any bugs or crashes during my playthrough. Honestly, the game is good. Just don’t expect a lot from it. The main cast of characters sold me on their interactions and i'm looking forward to seeing these characters again in Hundred Heroes. However, I did have some gripes on the main game as a whole. First, the enemy types. Pretty good in the first couple of hours. But once I got around the five and ten-hour mark I could already guess what enemy I would face again. Just a different variation. Granted there was one new type of enemy once I traveled to a new biome. But the game recycled the same enemy type with little variation to differentiate. I think the game could’ve benefitted from different enemy races instead of going back to reusing the same old base model. Second, a pretty simple combat system. You could technically change characters during combat and perform link attacks along with a unique ability for each character. However, the main combat formula becomes stale as you go through the game. You’ll hit the same three buttons continuously again and again. Didn’t bother me a great deal, but I think readers should know about this if they’re expecting great combat gameplay. Third, Music could use some more tracks when venturing off into different zones. You will go back to old areas to unlock new paths once you progress further into the main story. But this coupled with the repetitive combat and seeing the same enemy types can dull your experience quickly. Fourth sidequests need to be trimmed. Less on the go kill ‘x’, gather ‘x’ type, meet person ‘a’ then go back to person ‘b’ then repeat until done can quickly become a chore. If you want real sidequests, inject some flavorful side quests. Head into a zone to kill a unique monster type. Meeting NPC, who has a relationship with one of our playable characters. Detective sidequests, puzzles, escort with telling lore in the background, and more I could list which would elevate the game far more.  Thankfully the main story can do wonders to alleviate the main tedium. And the town upgrades you can do while on the road to complete a sidequest are a nice way to pass time for a small distraction and rest from the main story. Now for the good parts. The environments and graphical style for the game are eye-candy and I constantly found myself walking through the world seeing the new biomes and would be giddy when a new part of the town is unlocked for you to tread through. Seeing new shops, and new NPCs and upgrading them as you progress through the story is a treat.Likewise, there are plenty of shops around to upgrade your weapons, armor, special abilities, consumables, accessories, and a bunch more to sink your teeth into. I would usually after finishing some sidequests peruse through the shops to see if I could upgrade my characters further and honestly didn’t have problems scrounging up materials I attained from enemies and the environment. The main strength I feel is the characters. While you control CJ you do have more companions who join you and learn more about them. Their personality, habits, quirks, and more is such a delight I couldn’t stop playing through the main story to see what more I could learn. In addition to these characters, you will also meet a colorful cast of NPCs within the game which I cannot wait to see again in the future. There were countless times I chuckled and rose an eyebrow at scenes that would pop up. By the time the end credits rolled. I couldn’t believe how fast time flew by. Despite some gripes I have with the game overall I still recommend Eiyuden Chronicle Rising for the simple fact of making me become much more invested for Hundred Heroes to release. There were surprises in store in this hidden gem. And I adore the main cast and greatly look forward to seeing them once more in the future.Total Times Beaten: 1 Score: 7.5/10 Date Finished: 5/21/22Date Reviewed: 5/21/22Hours Played: 12

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game, I can finally put an end to my misery… Sadly, I don't recommend this game. Don't get me wrong, I am psyched up about Eiyuden chronicles Hundred Heroes as I am a big-time fan of the Suikoden franchise that inspire the game.But then Eiyuden chronicles: Rising is a spin off, and a poorly executed one. I’ll be brief:First of all the game feels like a mobile game (graphic and gameplay wise..).Then there is the writing… Oh boy that’s bad, the story is virtually nonexistent, the characters are generic.Comes after that the game’s length: I finished it with 100% achievements in 23H, that’s Okish for the price, but then 90% of the game is.. SIDEQUESTS. Yup, didn’t count them all but >150 of them, all more boring fetching in the 5 dungeons of the game, and a LOT of backtracking...(Oh, and did I mention the writing ? because the sidequests don’t really bring substance to the world, I ended up skipping dialogues of the lase 30 or so…).Next, the game is surprisingly easy, only one difficulty mode (you unlock “hard” mode after the end of the game, and its still quite easy, as your party is already leveled up..)For the good parts… The lore of the game seems fine (even if underdeveloped in this game, but then again, a spin off); even if its not really detailed in this game, it keeps my hopes up for Hundred Heroes. And... that's it for the good part..!In conclusion, I just think the game was targeted for children (writing / difficulty / gameplay), that would be an amazing game for them (for a first approach of the RPG genre). You could always buy the game to support the devs for a quality Hundred Heroes release (recommending a buy on sale).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually much of a platformer guy, but this was pretty fun. It's a small setting with a bunch of short, relatively easy quests in the style of a mobile game. _childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is a packed package, not full. It offers many great things: gorgeous graphic, mesmerizing soundtrack, lovable characters and interesting story with good localization.        However, I can see people having issue with the gameplay. There's not much of customization with no flashy moves or special combo/mechanic. The game works in a very old-school way with just attack, jump and switch characters. It can be a bit clunky at first since the game was designed to be played in a very specific way. Later on, you can unlock more mechanics though they won't change the core combat much. The whole game is a big fetch-quest and town building aspect is just not that significant.         That being said, there are many QoL features that help ease up the repetitive game loop (quick access to fast travel, many save points, useful mini map, quick loading screen, etc.). I really like the writing and characters of the game (which are pretty much the main points of Suikodens anyway). The game is easy to understand and requires not  thinking so it can be very relaxing. Just don't expect a "Suikoden" game and you might find it surprisingly enjoyable.Edit: It also runs great on Steam Deck!

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be called "Prekoden ." I'm one of those people waiting for a new Suikoden and this scratches all the itches. It's a compelling side-scrolling RPG. I know this can be daunting for some - but the density of activities takes quite a sting out of it. There are some metroidvania exploration elements. And the quirky characters make every quest fun and often funny.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed both the main game and this companion game (got it for $7), because Suikoden was a severely underrated JRPG franchise, and I want a true Suikoden spiritual successor. Needless to say, I have a personal interest in seeing this franchise take off. On that note, my personal perspective is to treat this game as a companion piece whose main purposes are to lay out the foundations of the lore, provide extra context to the main game and to the backstories of this game's main characters who will be playable in the main game, and to help tide Suikoden fans over. In my opinion, the game did well with its gorgeous artwork and intriguing lore, and I am stoked for the main game.However, as a standalone game from the perspective of new players who are unfamiliar with Suikoden, this game can be overly linear, can be very restrictive in the early parts, can be incredibly easy if you do all sidequests as you get them, lacks sidequest variety, and basically amounts to just an OK game overall. It can also use several quality of life improvements, like larger fonts, per page scrolling like when managing inventory, as well as some gameplay balancing.It is also worth noting that this game had no patches (from launch till time of writing), and I already finished the game 100% without glaring bugs/issues. That alone is already commendable in an age of gaming where it is almost never worth buying games at launch prices due to issues or DLC/edition shenanigans. What is more impressive is that I played this exclusively on Linux via Proton.In conclusion, if you have a vested interest in seeing a worthy Suikoden spiritual successor take off (after all these years) and/or you want to reward developers who actually ship products that work without showstopping issues on day one, then go and buy the game. If not, then maybe wait for a good sale price.

_childDocuments_.review: If CJ could only break the fourth wall, she would undeniably see and seek the little gem that is this game. The artstyle - especially the backgrounds - is gorgeous. The music fits each situation very well and the action combat is very smooth and just feels good. The game itself is a grind - both for leveling up as well as for the many many many sidequests you'll do in order to unlock more levels. But even though you'll run through the same old forest many times in order to finally get enough wood, it never feels boring. Some quests are really unnecessary fetch quests (talk to X, now to Y, now to Z and then back to X), but thanks to fast travel this is a non-issue. The story itself was pretty good. Even though, what I read from other comments, this is "just" a prequel for Hundred Heroes. Some characters are presented as more important than they actually are, which felt a little weird in the end. Maybe this was also just a teaser for the main game.All in all pretty good game which I can wholeheartly recommend to anyone not afraid of a little grind. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed feelings about this one: It's a perfectly fine game, and I used it as a time killer, but it also comes across as rushed and repetitive. Moreover, it felt like the designers followed a checklist of what RPGs need, but the presentation ended up being awkward. CJ just felt generic, Garoo's plotline was alluded to a couple times then hastily resolved at the end, while Isha is the only one that got a decent amount of love as a character. As for gameplay progression, it's annoyingly linear for a Metroidvania. CJ's boilerplate declaration that we should not explore beyond the plot boundaries is lazy writing, and the side quests (all 160 of them) are about the quality of most 2004 World of Warcraft quests. Many are just "go one screen over and talk to someone".This is a gaiden game, though, and it's cheap...so much of this is to be expected. The first main series game is slated for release in a few months. Hopefully that one will be beefier all around.

_childDocuments_.review: In a steam binary approach to reviews ive chosen negative one, but my general impressions from the game are more of a "mediocre".This game is a 2d side-scroller/ beat em up/ hack and slash/arcade game with little RPG elements on top. Your main protagonist and 2 unlockable companions travel through various locations filled with monsters to kill,plants to harvest,ores to mine and treasures to loot. The combat is real time beat em up,only 1 button required to fight with one character and occasionally push your teammates buttons for combo attacks. Levels feature very little platforming action. Between battles you can visit local village and do some quests,resupply and upgrade your gear.All in all,i had a little fun while playing this, but the game of such quality is ABSOLUTELY not worth the full price,see details below.PROS:+decent visual style+somewhat coherent plot (for these kind of games)+a lot of things to upgrade: gear, potions,trinkets,shops,etcCONS:- very few different biomes to explore, all are very typical jungle/cave/magma/frost levels- garbage "side-quest" system.This game has 160 "side-quests" of the MOST ANNOYING and degrading kind - fetch this,get that from another corner of the map, mine X ores, gather Y plants, rinse and repeat. What really pissed me off was a number of quests (!) where you literally just need to talk to another NPC...ONE SCREEN AWAY from quest giver. Also you need to traverse previously visited levels again and again, artificially prolonging the game and "boosting" the amount of content by doing those mindless tasks. Some of the quest objectives at least are marked on the mini-map,but MOST of them - not, so you have to travel ALL the chambers of a dungeon yet again and again to find the blasted quest-mob or chest with quest loot.Such lazy and uninspired quest design doesnt belong to 2022.- not enough content to justify its price. It took me 17h to 100% this game with all achievements- very few types of enemies/bosses.This game features about 10 different mobs, which are then reskined throught the entirety of the game: yellow slime, dark blue slime, light blue slime, red slime, purple slime...you got the idea. Yet another lazy design feature, like in some unpopular MMO.Only 5 unique bosses, each is a joke to beat.- laughable level of difficulty. Player can choose either normal or simple mode,after beating the game you unlock "hard" mode. But even on hard difficulty mobs and bosses are complete joke, they are mindless meatbags for you to slaughter. If you use dmg potion and upgrade your gear regularly (not much else to do anyway) you can kill most of the bosses in 2-3 hits.- music is very repetitive and lack variety, gets stale very fast. I turned it off after first 2h of gameplay.TL:DRVery mediocre game at best, i think its intended for children no older than 12. You can grab this on sale if you have nothing else to do. If you watched the nice trailer and gameplay sample vids and decided to buy it for full price - boy,you are gonna regret it, just like me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the Suikoden series since I got the first game. Unfortunately it's owned by Konami and barring any ports in their insatiable quest for money... the series won't be revived anytime soon. Enter Eiyuden Chronicles, a kickstarter game that aims to be the spiritual successor to the Suikoden series. Stoked and hopeful? Yes. So much so that I bought EC: Rising, no questions asked. Just waited a bit till the bugfixes and whatnot had been done so I could give it a proper go. Unfortunately, I have to hope that EC: R is not an indicator for how the main game will be.TLDR: Many issues, caveat emptor if you don't want fetchquests.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of back and forth fetch quests but the side scrolling action combat is the star of this game and is done extremely well and makes the game a lot of fun. The fast travel system is a must and turns what could be a chore into something trivial so you can focus on the important aspects of this game. The story is cheesy in spots but overall is well done with a comedic tone at times and kept me interested. I think this is a good primer to the world of Eiyuden Chronicle in preparation for Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: While not having anything really impressive, this is a decent game without any major problem. Here's some minor .(I played this game in another language, some words may be a bit off but probably doesn't affect understanding. )Excluding the town, there's only 5 areas in this game, with roughly 10 sections in each. However, given the price, I personally think this is acceptable. In some specific locations, waves of enemies spawn. If the player's actions cause several enemies to attack in a specific interval. This is impossible to dodge and enemy "combo" may lock the player to death. Anyway, this is not too common. This design is not really a problem, but can be annoying when the player needs to farm specific materials. This game doesn't force the player to upgrade gears. However, due to some hard-to-dodge attacks mentioned above,stats are way too important in this game. This game has some accessories to increase the chance of getting rarer ores, but there's no such accessory for woods. It's very annoying to gather top rarity woods for side quests. This is probably the biggest complaint i have on this game. The low drop rate of high rarity woods made me use the trader for the first time, this is all the meaning I found on the trader. The exchanges the trader offers are insanely expensive. Here's some  I can think of.The increase in stats from foods are permanent. This gives players the motivation to do late/end game farming. Not sure if there's any, but I didn't find anything missable. Side quests will not disappear on pushing the main story. I played it on Steam Deck OLED and didn't find/trigger any bug. Overall, a game that matches my expectation. Nothing extraordinary, but no major problem.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good. It's OK. It's aggressively fine. By which I mean that it is mechanically solid enough to be enjoyable (at least as long as you don't play too long in one session). It's baby's first metroidvania. A very solid one but also very basic.That's not to say that the game is not enjoyable, but it's just fine. Unfortunately, the greatest compliment I can give the game is that there is nothing really wrong with. There are some petty annoyances: the loot spawns after the enemy's death animation has ended, so you can blaze through a wave of enemies only to have to do a little walk of shame to go pick up the items they dropped, and the aim on the one ranged attack we get could be better (or at all extant), but those will only start to get annoying if you play for too long. The story is also fine and at a few points even threatens to get interesting - how many games can you name where you get to play as a tsundere kangaroo? - but if you decide to do all the sidequests, it gets diluted enough to qualify as homeopathic. I've played a few games where I wished that I could give them a 'mixed' rating because they had equal amounts of very good and very bad points, but this is the first game to which I would have given that rating because it leaves about as much of an impression as an unseasoned cracker. It's plain, but I can't rate it as bad because there is really nothing wrong with it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't for everyone, but I absolutely loved it.The story isn't anything too special, but it's fine. The world is pretty standard for a jrpg setting. The side scrolling action reminds me of something like Muramasa, but with a bit less depth. The game's core loop is a bit repetitive, so I understand if this doesn't really work for a lot of people.But the three protagonists are pretty fun. I loved watching the little town grow from a bunch of shacks into a thriving town. Even though most of the quests involved fetching stuff from the dungeons and coming back, or just talking to NPCs, I liked that they were fairly bite sized. This was a great game to complete a couple quests before bed, or during breaks and it was ideal for the steam deck. Overall, I found it to be a fairly cozy, enjoyable game and I'm definitely interested to check out Hundred Heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale and it was worth it. The 2d sprites on 3d background look good imo and the gameplay wasn't super deep but enough to keep me going to the end. I will say I wish some of the combat felt a little bit more fluid. There were times when I felt like trying to switch characters there was a delay in the attacks coming out even with me spamming the button. Not to say the game is hard though, I cruised through it only having about 2-3 spots that required me to use potions. There is a lot of side quests and most of it is filler fetch quest type stuff requiring a lot of going back to revisit the same areas. They are mostly optional but some are used to upgrade shops to upgrade your gear. Luckily most are pretty quick to take care of but beware if that's not your cup of tea.Overall the game is a solid 8/10 for me and I'll be keeping an eye on their next game. Took me about 15 hrs to beat doing the majority of the quests. There are definitely flaws here but they didn't detract from the overall experience too much for me. If you're still not sure you can always wait for another sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect much coming in (I got it on sale for about three dollars), but this game is surprisingly fun.  It comes off as a bit simplistic at first, but once you're past the introductory phase it picks up pretty quick.  The combat is slick and feels great once you get the hang of it.  The side quests are nothing special, but they're satisfying to complete and it's got a decent storyline to keep things moving.  I think where it really shines is in its level design- the environments are absolutely beautiful, and lovingly crafted.  There's a ton of detail and none of it ever really feels recycled, and as a result the exploration element is a ton of fun.  The music's pretty good too, which is a nice bonus.  The cutscenes tend to drag a bit, but that's not a huge deal.  The only thing this game is really lacking is challenge.  It's pretty easy to get through without a whole lot of effort.  But even then, it still manages to be fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a lot. Beating the main story and doing all of the sidequests while reading all the dialogue took around 15 hours, so it's on the shorter side but it's very well done. For story game aspects: the dialogue is interesting and engaging, the character development is great. Lots of humor and lots of surprises. It's been rare that I've seen developers put so much care and effort into a story, rather than the usual bland dialogue and cliche themes. The gameplay was enjoyable for me: it wasn't challenging but you got to jump around and do fun combos while exploring interesting areas. The music and sound effects are incredible. The leveling system and gear system are fine: nothing extraordinary but well done enough. You don't need to put a lot of effort into min-maxing anything to get through the story and enjoy the game. One of the surprising things about this game is that when I looked through the achievements, 25% of players had completed the whole story, and that's pretty rare for a steam game to have. I would definitely recommend this to people who enjoy action-story type JRPGs, without needing too much of a challenge in terms of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a complicated relationship with this title. The game is pretty deceptive, because it's not as bad as most people think when taking a quick glance. While the "mobile game animations" look  dated (especially for a 2022 title), the game is actually surprisingly fun. Combat feels lackluster at first, but as you unlock new skills it gets pretty enjoyable.+ Gorgeous graphics, especially the backgrounds. The character sprites look very good too (until they start moving).+ Combat is simple but satisfying, and gains a bit of depth as you unlock new skills.+ While exploration is pretty straightforward, it somehow reminds me of .+ Slowly building the village and unlocking new features is pretty neat and has a lot of that  energy they're going for.+ Pretty good soundtrack.- Character animations have this very "mobile game" feel to them, with "puppet" animation.- The story is pretty basic, even after the supposed "big reveal". No huge stakes, little to non-existent character development.- Lots of backtracking. Although the game has fast travel, it doesn't make it less annoying.- Overly repetitive gameplay loop: get a fetching quest, farm monsters, give items to NPC, proceed to the next.- The whole village building system, while cool, feels like something you'd see in a mobile game. Very barebones.- Money is extremely scarce even if you farm it.- Constant pauses in the gameplay to announce that you started / finished a quest, with fading screens and slow transitions. Again, this feels very "mobile game" stuff.- No Bestiary where you can see monster drops.- Foreground sometimes prevents you from seeing enemies.- Damage numbers are a bit too big (especially when you land critical hits) and clutter the screen.- There is a post-game section while you can continue to do quests and upgrade your gear after beating the final boss (which just brings you back to before the point of no return) but it's honestly very boring._________________________________________________Overall, I think that while this game is nothing groundbreaking or remarkable, it does well in creating some kind of world-building for the actual , by showing characters that will be playable in the game and establishing the overall tone we can expect from . Either way, this is a fun game, despite its many flaws.If you're excited for the actual Eiyuden Chronicle and want to support the devs, this game is for you. Otherwise I can't really recommend. I did have fun and it made me curious to see more of this world and its characters.

_childDocuments_.review: This being a side game, I went into it not really expecting too much. It certainly did what I wanted it to do, get me excited for Hundred Heroes next year. The gameplay is what really kept me around. I am not usually a fan of metroidvania games, but this one just did it for me more so than most do. It has that old school charm mixed with the new school polish. While a story is there, I wouldn't call it anything special. It does enough to give you a background of the world (Or at least the small part of it you play in) and a couple of the main characters, which was all I really wanted. A main issue that stuck out for me was the side quests, Good God, I am going to go ballistic if I ever see a stamp again in my life. It's all fetch quests, that slowly progress you towards completing a "stamp page". All this stamp page does is give you some small rewards after completing each tier, and holy there is a lot of them. The other thing I would note is, this game has no real weapon or armour loot. It is all tied to farming the same resources you did for the side quests, and then using them to level up the gear you have. Some upgrades to your armour and weapons do give you new abilities when obtained, which is nice, but there are a total of 4 of these for each character, so you get them fast. Last main gripe, the jump animation is not it chief. It feels very jittery, and once you get the dash/immunity for CJ you can basically break the animation to fly through enemies and never take damage again. If this was intended, that's fine, if not please fix it for the main game. Overall, I think this game being only 20 dollars (At least for me in Canada) really works to it's advantage. Were it much more than this I am not sure I would have felt my purchase justified. Regardless though, this game will certainly bring me back for Hundred Heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like that this is easy to pick up and put down, the fetch quests may be fetchy but they are often thematically linked to the lore and often by inhabitants of the town who you then find out more about. The dialogue reads very nice, in particular, personalities come across well. I am no platformer or action gamer, and my reflexes and eyes aren't the best anymore so I'm quite chuffed to be able to handle this in simple. It'll tide me over well until Eiyuden Chronicle releases. Hats off to the Natsume team and the localisers! Love the backgrounds and portraits of the charas. Especially that they change for the main ones, depending on emotion. I wish they were bigger though. And an option to increase font size would be nice. Also Currently my achievements no longer sync with Steam altho I get them inside the game just fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid, cute little game.Pretty handholdy at the start, but once you finally have all the combat options unlocked, the battle system is pretty fun for a short game, even if the difficulty never gets truly challenging. (Hopefully they add a hard mode later on.) The combat is a lot less generic than I thought it'd be going in. It's sort of a Trine-like fight system, but better than in that series.Sidequests are a bit repetitive, but that's kind of the point, and it never got truly egregious to me. The vast majority of the time I already had the resources the questgivers wanted, and I just marched down the street, upgrading their shops. You're not required to do them if you don't want to anyway.Visuals are fantastic. I wouldn't say it's "high fidelity", but almost everything is appropriately detailed for the distance from the camera, and post processing is used masterfully. Screenshots or online video compression cannot do it justice compared to running it natively on your monitor. Calling it pleasing to the eye would be an understatement.I didn't expect a huge track variety with a budget title, but what's there is good imo. Composed quite well, with an adequate amount of layers for each track's feel. The melodies aren't quite as front and center in all the tracks, or sometimes they trade the main melody off between different instruments, and imo that seems to lead to most complaints about them not being "memorable".Charm, charm, charm. This thing oozes charm, and that's probably what elevates it more than anything. It's a great intro to the Eiyuden world, and the main characters get enough banter and fleshing out in the short runtime to make me look forward to the main game.If you're not interested or don't want to be interested in Suikoden or Eiyuden, it might be a hard sell. But I think it's well worth a base $15 price point. If you're that skeptical, I'm sure it will go on sale in the leadup to Eiyuden Hundred Heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: I like Suikoden and I like Metroidvanias. For whatever reason I assumed I wouldn't like this. I find it's combat system to be very weak but it's RPG and story elements are just strong enough to pull it back in the other direction. I see this as a $15 prequel set to hype up the Hundred Heroes Release. As far as that goes, it does succeed in doing that. I am very excited for the main event. Beware though, more than half of your time is grinding and if you max your weapons and armor you will be basically invincible. The 100% crit accessory you get after beating the main story also serves to trivialize the concept of a Hard Mode. As a demo I liked this game but I wouldn't have spent full price. $15 was an appropriate price point and kinda makes me feel like the $50 price tag on the full release took all of that into account. This game was a funding round that allowed them to continue with the full game they intended to make. Prudent financial play.Anyway, enjoy this for what it is and get ready for the real game, Eiyuden Chronicle Hundred Heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for around 3 hours on my friend's PC and I just want to share my thought about why I bought the game myself.READ BEFORE BUYING.I am an oldtime gamer, been playing since even before Suikoden 1. This game is by no means a great game, but it gives me that little bit nostalgia feeling. I didn't have very high hope for this game, because we all know that this is just a companion game for next year Eiyuuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes.The battle is clunky, I thought it would be like Dust: An Elysian Tail, but I was wrong. There is no flashy moves or mechanic about the battle, this game is just like an old time SNES game recreated with current technology, hit-hit-jump-dodge, rinse and repeat. Even after you got the 2nd and 3rd character, it's still basically the same except that you can use combo by pressing different buttons (X, Y, B). It's too stiff for an ARPG game, for example jump feature, you can't set the jumping power by pressing shorter or longer, if you press jump, then you will be in the air for a set amount of time without animation cancelling.The main gameplay itself is just a big fetch quests, from the start to finish. There's also very few customization for your characters. You can get new weapons, gain levels, create some accessories, that's all. The art is good, I quite like it, but I am sure art style is very subjective, so is the music, which pales in comparison to the old Suikoden games.I don't want to advise any of you to buying or not buying this game, I just want you guys to know, if you set your expectation high, you will be quite disappointed, especially if you're young gamer who doesn't have that spiritual connection with Suikoden series. There are many far far superior 2D ARPG titles worth your money.I will not continue playing this game, even if the price is cheap, I'll just wait for the main title next year.TL;DRBelow expectation, sub-par gameplay and mechanic, giant fetch quests. Some nostalgia feeling, but not enough to warrant a playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is okay if you're bored.The first two hours are an incredible slog.I regret not skipping all sidequest scenes that don't involve characters that show up in the main story, and there are A LOT of them. Walk 1 screen to deliver grandma a sandwich over and over.The combat design in relation to player power creep is insane.You start with a 2 ground attack combo and a single air attack.7 hours in I have a 4 ground attack combo and a 2 air attack combo, a double jump, an air dash, and directional (up or down) attacks. This should be the bare minimum that you start the game with. Instead I had to farm materials and money to be able to do all that. The combat is just not interesting at all before you have most of that stuff. You need to farm materials to do all of that on the other 2 characters you get as well.Seems like extending play time got in the way of interesting or satisfying design. Instead of slowly unlocking more abilities to make the combat more interesting I feel like not playing.

_childDocuments_.review: 26 hours to 100% it.  From what I read, that is more than a lot of people took but I was having fun. _childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is a prelude to Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes that releases on 4/23/24. This game is a prequel and gives a little bit of insight to what we can expect out of Hundred Heroes. If you have ever played the Suikoden series, these games are being made by the same creators and crew as those who worked on Suikoden many years ago. Rising is an ARPG that introduces us to the world, some characters and gives a bit of information regarding the plot setup of Hundred Heroes. Hundred Heroes will be a more traditional RPG true to the spirit and soul of the now dead Suikoden series. At first I wasn't sure I would like Rising as the animation of the characters reminded me of cheap mobile games, but as I played this game and gave it a chance I grew to love the game and the characters. If this is the level of writing and story that we have to look forward to with Hundred Heroes, then I would say it's a safe bet that those of us that loved Suikoden will be eating good with the next game. I went into this teaser game with low expectations, and came out pleasantly surprised with how much I enjoyed the experience of the whole game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Short and pretty easy game which makes it an enjoyable pasttime; gets quite grindy post-game especially if you're going for all sidequests/achievements.You go into a dungeon, and run/jump freely. Enemies are around, and you can attack them (or not) as you want. Sometimes they ambush you, and you have to beat them all to proceed.As you beat them, you get exp and can level up, which raises your stats. They can also drop items, which can be used for crafting at shops or for completing sidequests.There are minibosses (and bosses) here and there, which respawn alongside regular enemies.There are 3 characters - Twin axe user who has dodging and speedy movement; Big sword user with block/parry capability; Magic user with different spell effects based on elements. The game lets you swap between them with a button press, and lets you link their attacks together to do high damage combos.Equipment for each character:Their weapon (which can be crafted/upgraded via 2 shops) - upgrades give extra attack benefits (like upping your crit rate) alongside increased attack power.Their armor (also 2 shops) - upgrades give extra movement benefits (such as a double jump) alongside boosted defense.2 accessories  (which can be crafted/bought by 1 shop but can also be a reward from sidequests) - has various effects from strength up to higher item drop chance.2 runes (same as accessories) - adds elemental attack/defense to characters, based on slot.In both dungeon and town/hub areas, you unlock fast travel, so even when you have to backtrack, it doesn't feel terribly slow to move around.There's fishing! Cast your line, then press the buttons in the order shown on your screen.Ore/Wood gathering also exists but that's more of a "hit the tree, get wood" type of deal.It's 31 quests long. Should take around 10 hours to do; closer to 15 if you're doing all the sidequests alongside. There is backtracking and some forced sidequests to teach you about certain mechanics, but all-in-all, it's a fairly light and easy romp.Some grammatical/punctuation errors here and there but it's alright.Beating it unlocks a Hard difficulty but it's a generic "give enemy higher numbers/levels" difficulty.160 SIDEQUESTS ().There is a Stamp system. Do a quest, get a stamp. If you get enough stamps, you can get special items at one of the shops.While some of the sidequests feel like they're padding the game (such as "talk to this other npc 2 screens over"), a fair amount of them have benefits, such as upgrading shops so they sell you more/better items. Some of the quests give you items you can't even buy at the time it unlocks.And you learn more about the characters that live in the town.Many of the quests ask you to gather items, which chances are good you already have if you've been fighting/mining everything your way.You can take multiple quests.The game marks where you have to get quest item(s) if it's the currently-active quest on the top-right of the screen, but you can go into the menu and change the active quest.The problem for me, when it comes to sidequests, is the post-game.The last dozen-or-so sidequests can't be done before defeating the final boss; fine. However, doing those unlocks EVEN MORE SIDEQUESTS. If you thought the last ones were padding, the new ones are especially so - a lot of them are "do this exact sidequest you did previously" with the sidequest name referring to the previous one. My assumption (aside from trying to get you to play the game more) is they're giving you more quests to get more money/exp/items - but I feel I could just go back into the dungeons and get those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is ... fine? I mean, is playable, I have played worse, but definitely cannot recommend it over better action platformers.Graphics for all the backgrounds are insanely good and eye catching; but character models have a rather lanky movement, as if their arms and torso were actually separate sprites, which makes the game looks flash game quality. Enemies are the same, with wolves' death animation being basically just flipping the sprite belly up. Music is good, not particularly memorable except maybe for the two town songs. yet by the time you reach the ending it will start shining due to it's absense.Story also is serviceable, but with the caveat that it links to a yet unreleased game, so at some point it'll just start throwing names and places you have no idea about, but will be relevant for that future game. It comes without saying that the ending is open ended as a result of that as well, just as you'd expect. The main party characters are better than the story, though. CJ is pretty shonen protagonist level of basic, but Garoo and Isha have more depth to them that makes them entertaining.The gameplay is original, but simple, and is held back by a major flaw that makes it too easy. You have a jump button, a designated attack button for each character which also serves as their tag in button, and a button for defense. CJ is the fast attacker with great maneuverability; Garoo is slow with relatively low DPS, but has a defense move that basically lets you play Sekiro and laugh at basically most attacks; and Isha tags in, fires her stuff, and immediately tags out since she'll be useless for like 3 seconds afterwards. Tagging in during an attack lets you chain your attacks for better results. You're not invulnerable on this, and a knockback can prematurely end the move, but that rarely happens as a result of how SLOW the gameplay is. Everything is way too telegraphed or has too much windup, making the game mind numbingly easy. It also doesn't help that enemies barely scratch you (unless you neglect armor upgrades, but some of them have mobility options attached to them so ignoring them makes the game an even slower drag) until you unlock hard mode at the end game.The game loop is terrible, and by far the lowest point of the game. You have 5 areas to explore aside of the main city hub (two of the areas are intertwined together, but whatever), and about 140-150 side quests to do. Those sidequests, which take over about 90% of the total gameplay, are all the likes of "go gather x amount of items", "kill that thing and give me back my stuff", or "go talk to a couple NPC's that are like a screen away". They're all very easy to do, specially since you can track were to go, and are basically to pad the gameplay to ridiculous levels. Supposedly the side quests are there to flesh out the town and it's inhabitants, but all the NPCs are one-note. To add to the tedium, every single result from clearing a quest is given on a separate window and taking even more time as you close them all, making the whole experience something like this:QUEST COMPLETEYou got moneyYou got itemYou got exp.Level up (you)LEVEL UP (a shop)The shop now has new stuff.(fade to black)(returns from fade to black)NEW QUESTGo do this thin now.Tutorial for new shop.Ok, now you can play again.Again, the game does work and can be fun, is not a complete waste to play it, but is hard to recomment purchasing it if there're other action platformers or metroidvania games you'd wish to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I really feel bad thumbs downing this, but I'm not really comfortable recommending it and so I feel the "Very positive" average oversells the game and will hurt people going in. At it's best, this game is "okay"... at worst its "Not bad".One thing I like, unlike alot of the reviews here, is the overall flow of the game. It's made up of 160 bite-sized quests that last 3-5 minutes each. As you play these quests you're collected resources which you'll use to upgrade your town and your gear. You'll rerun the same few maps repeatedly but you'll unlock elements that open up new passages and occasionally the bosses will level up. It's not deep, but its the sort of thing I'd play on PSP while waiting for the bus. While functional, the combat and movement in general is feels clunky and weighted especially until you've upgraded into late game. I think they wanted to create the feeling of growth but ultimately my "Speedy" character had a 2 hit combo... that's not speedy. Combine this with a characters switching as you attack and automatically This is all made worst by the elemental design and status effects. THEY ALL RESTRICT ACTIONS! Basic attacks can stun lock you, petrify freezes movement, ice freezes all action and the damage of time effects prevent you from switching characters. If that's not bad enough... every enemy in a zone can hit you with status effects! This removal of control just adds to the feeling of slow clunky combat.Yet, despite these frustrations the game is mind-numbingly easy so it doesn't really get frustrating. You level up at a good pace, you collect loads of resources and when you finally unlock up the freedom around half-ways through it flows well. You even unlock a hard mode in post game which really would have been nice to have while I actually was playing the game.Overall, I don't regret my purchase or my time spent here. But the fun doesn't really start until the mid to late game when they stop holding your hand. And even then... there's better options.

_childDocuments_.review: All of my play time with this game has been on the Steam Deck. It worked out of the box, using the current default proton version (7.0-2), with only a 5-second delay when launching the game, and played flawlessly. I set the frame cap to 30fps and get about 3.5 to 4 hours of play from of a full charge.As for the game itself, I was pleasantly surprised. The music is nice, I like the script and graphics, and the gameplay is fun so far. The 1.4 hours I played was in one sitting, as it was easy to get carried away doing the quests and things. I was also surprised to see that quite a few of the early characters I've come across in the town/village so far have Indian names! Isha, Priya, Ganesh, Shiva, Rajiv, Sarita, Mannan, etc.I had received the code for this game after backing EC on Kickstarter, and I'm glad I paid extra for it. I may update this review when I've played it some more (which I'm about to do now).

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising plays, at its best, like a mediocre flash game. The combat animations are very choppy and unsatisfying. The game is constantly flashing the words "Level Up" on the screen for everything from establishing a business to adding skills to gear, because the developer thinks that seeing those words makes the player feel accomplished and could find no other way to produce a similar feeling. The dungeon design is very bland, and the gameplay loop essentially has the player repeatedly entering the same few dungeons, fighting the same enemies, not random or scaled up or anything, to grab one key item and then returning to town, then repeating this again and again for hours.From the moment I gained control of my character, I was scratching my head trying to figure out how on earth this game has an 85% positive rating on Steam. I tried to find some reviews from users/publications online anywhere else, and found that the game appears to have a pretty niche following. I'm a sucker for early 00's Newgrounds flash games and I love metroidvanias/2.5D action games, but apparently in order to really enjoy Rising I'd have to also like the super cringey dialog, the (so far) shallow plot and uninteresting world, and the sequel that hasn't been released yet but is marketed as the first game while Rising, released first, is the spinoff. And even if I was invested in the bigger project, and even if I spoke out loud exclusively in memes and cheezburger language, I'd still argue that the sheer number of weird word choices and grammatical errors in the localization are jarring and detract from the experience. I understand the use of words like "prob'ly" because it intentionally adds tone to how a character speaks, and I am willing to overlook a handful of typos throughout an entire game, especially when it's made by a smaller developer. The frequent, consistent misuse of grammar in a way that doesn't add to atmosphere shows that the people who did localization simply didn't know what they were doing. And I'm only 3 hours in as of this writing. i've got a lot of boring dialog to decipher yet.In summary, Rising has decent, if clunky, gameplay, but overall feels like it would rather waste your time to keep you in your chair longer instead of giving you an engaging experience that could do the same. If it was a free browser game, it'd be tough to recommend. If it comes for free in a bundle with the second game, it might be worth playing if you love the world and want more lore, can't say yet. But on its own I don't think it's worth spending 5 USD, let alone whatever they're charging when you're looking.

_childDocuments_.review: Would recommend on sale.It's a very odd game to review because a lot of it feels super clunky, dated and frustrating but at the same time the cast of characters (at least in english translation) is very charming. CJ is a very fun main character and the main 3 playable characters all get really interesting by the end of the game.You can get through most of the main content fairly quickly.It's the kind of game I would buy and play if you are bored on a day off and are looking into diving into a different world. Or if you are interested in Eiyuden Chronicle as a whole and don't mind the very odd combat/platforming of this game and the overwhelming amount of fetch quests.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game for it's price, and it's a good proof of concept for Hundred Heroes.Gameplay reminds me of old school action JRPGs like Ys, or Odin Sphere. The combat is a bit clunky compared to more recent action RPG sidescrollers, but it's good enough and really opens up after about 1-2 hours. The structure is a bit repetitive. Most of the game you're doing sidequests for the towns people, but it's not really a big deal and most quests take 5 minutes max to complete. Often times I already have what the villagers need just by exploring on my own.Where the game really shines is it's presentation and characters. The game is beautiful. Reminds me of a mix between Suikoden 2 and Octopath Traveller, where you have 2D character sprites on a full 3D environment with shaders and lighting. The spritework especially is really reminiscent of Suikoden 2. The environments, animations and art is all fantastic and a really good taste of whats to come in Hundred Heroes.The small details also really help with the games repetitive nature. You might see minor NPCs you completed quests for having lunch at the tavern you helped build, or townspeople just having a good time in the background. The town also gets more and more developed the more sidequests you do, so it at least gives you incentive to do as much as possible.The character writing and dialogue is very well done and feels like a more refined version of the Suikoden character formula. Seeing everyone's interactions, talking with people and slowly learning about the world and the situation of the village makes the constant fetch quests more tolerable. CJ is also a fantastic protagonist and reminds me a lot of Estelle from Trails in the Sky.Overall, get this game if you want a cheap but fun character centered action RPG, or if you're planning on playing Hundred Heroes next year (apparently, elements from Rising will carry over into HH, but we don't know what exactly that will be yet). Either way, this is a good taste of what's to come for hundred heroes. If the outsourced side game was this good, we're in for a real treat next year.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not take long to master and is something to keep you engaged. The game could use tweaks to the combat to make it more difficult from a earlier part in the story but still keeps you wanting to get all the achievements.

The gameplay itself is decent, but way too easy.Still, for the price you can get some entertainment and support the development of the spiritual successor to Suikoen.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: To some of you this will be good news, and to others it won't: I'm terrible at action RPGs, and it took me 28 hours of gameplay to clear the game, complete all achievements, and beat the hard mode versions of the bosses. (Hard mode is unlocked after beating the game once; all it does is raise enemy levels, as far as I can tell.)For me this was a blessing, because I was worried I wouldn't be able to make it through this game to get the lore and character introductions before the main Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes game came out. But I do realize that for the more hardcore/genre-savvy, this may be a letdown. However, the game is a different genre than the main game will be, and that leads into my main point for the review: you're going to be happier with this game if you accept it for what it is. And what it *is* is an introduction to the universe and the characters for those eager for the main game of the franchise.Approaching with that mindset, I would give this game a 7 of 10 overall. It was shortish, it was charming, the story is an interesting introduction to the world (stick around after the credits for bonus lead-in to the main game!), and the graphics were gorgeous but thwarted by somewhat janky animation in places. The music is so-so. The character interactions and banter were amusing, and the game is very well localized. The combat was fun but it took a while to unlock all three characters, and to upgrade their weapons and armor enough that the more fun aspects of it unlocked, making it a bit of a slow start. There is a lot of backtracking to explore the same zones multiple times, which wasn't an issue for me as an oldschool gamer; I'm used to metroidvanias requiring multiple explorations of a zone, and it was a good way to pass time while I listened to Youtube in the background.The satisfaction of spending three nights playing this was more than worth the $7 I paid for it as a Kickstarter backer, and I also bought a copy for my spouse at the full $15. If you're on the fence about it but looking forward to the more traditional JRPG Eiyuden Chronicle game, you could always wait and see if this goes on sale. It's worth the money and time as an introduction to the world, but may not be of interest to those that don't have an interest in moving on to the main game later.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that's supposed to introduce us to the series's world, it did its job. Gameplay was average at best, but the environments were amazing with the 2.5D graphics. The story was pretty simple but interesting enough to make me curious about the upcoming main game. Can't wait for Hundred Heroes and I hope CJ, Garoo, and Isha are going to be playable there as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: A game of entirely 'fetch quest style quests'. And it is awesome. The little town you come to after being on your own is amazing. It faces a problem and you're here to help and solve it.The Game is simple and easy, and its beautiful to look at an fun to play. I cannot wait to continue my journey in the world of Aalraan!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst the game does have beautiful 2D+3D scenery, it falls short on it's story & writing. Side quests felt like a chore as it is largely fetching resources or lost items. _childDocuments_.review: I backed the main game way back in 2020Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising has a basic story nothing mind-blowing but it does the job.Side quests are mostly fetch quests,some can be pretty funThe combat system gets more complex with each upgrade.You need to go around and get materials,it can be grindy but is not that bad.I would give it a 7/10 is a decent game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Was excited for Hundred Hero's and wasn't expecting much from Rising as it was meant to be a game to go along with it. However it ended up being a fantastic game with great artwork expected from the team behind Suikoden. The gameplay is all side scrolling with fluid combat and very little issues. Interesting dungeons in the sense that you can only progress further in them as you get items to deal with blockages, so that only 3-4 dungeons keep you coming back to them. around 160-180 side quests on top of the main story that just by dungeon diving you can complete them pretty quickly. Highly recommend this game to drop a nice 20 some hours into.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- The Attacks are fun to perform,- Lots to do (but a lot of busy work in between)- Metroidvania style maps are always fun to explore.Cons:- This feels like MMO busywork on a Single Player game.- The story is lacking at least so far (13 hours in)- Character design clash with everything else (I know its an art style, I didn't like it, now or on PS1).Conclusion:I bought this game thinking it would be a nice way to get into this franchise considering the next BIG Rpg is coming in next year. Sadly considering how much work they did on the story, it just made me unWishlist their next release. 13 hours in, One single town, I've delivered letters, messages, surveyed, interviewed all of the villagers, the rewards aren't good enough. If you measure your enjoyment with Playtime vs Price, this game is a good example as to why that's a wrong measurement.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: If you love side-scrolling Metroidvania's like Castlevania, Bloodstained, and/or Dust: An Elysian Tale you'll love this game.This is probably gonna go down as one of my favorite side-scrolling exploration games.It has a massive variety of quests and treasure and enemies in the game, and the game has a handful of unique but easy to master mechanics that make the game fun and fills it with diversity and excitement.I really love the characters and the world, and it has such a diverse variety of characters from Humans, Elves, and Beastfolk inhabiting the world.Plus the Lore of the world being built upon the ruins of highly advanced civilizations is pretty interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: The Characters have personality, the twists & turns in the story is real, the Combat feels good but doesn't demand of you to be a Hack & Slash god, & the graphics are gorgeous! (Minor nitpick: It feels weird for CJ's Sprite while she's running around to erroneously show her wearing Knee-high Boots when her canon Boots are actually only ankle high.) Good humor in parts of the game, & a surprisingly good try at making Fed Ex Quests galore not boring.I look forward to seeing how all my efforts in this game will transfer into the Full Game "Eiyuden Chronicles: Hundred Heroes"!P.S. The Tunes are gorgeous as well...
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent, fast paced action game.  Bought it without knowing so much about it, because I felt the gameplay and the art style looked really good.  After playing through it, and understanding more about the entire story, I'm looking forward to the JRPG that is coming up.  I realize the gameplay likely won't be the same, but I really liked the writing for the characters and the story within this.I will say, that overall, the game felt a bit easy.  Understandably, a lot of that I believe is because I was grinding a bit more than I realized with getting materials.  It made it very easy to obtain the upgrades as required for the heroes, and eventually it really was only the bosses that provided a challenge at times.  Finishing the first time does unlock a hard mode, but you resume just before the final act, with other things to do.  This leads to your characters still being fairly overpowered for the end content.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: What is otherwise a fun game gets ruined in the mid game.You start unlocking abilities that let you break the shiny rocks a few hours in. However these rocks are not marked on the map. Meaning a completion-ist like me is left re-exploring the map every time you get one of these upgrades. It is not fun to re-explore the same area 15 times(for side quests and then upgrades). I'd like to know where the rock is and go to it and explore the new area. Its not that bad when you get the first one! However it becomes tedious in the mid game when I've seen nearly 10 of them and have to remember where they all are on the map.Also so many useless boring quests. Talk to X for X. It becomes so boring. This is like 50% of the quests. The Dialogue is way too long and happens much too often. I found myself skipping 95% of cutscenes. I can still track the story. The dialogue doesn't have substance. I would be more than happy to listen to it but they'll talk for minutes for a quest to talk to X for X. This is just boring and doesn't make the characters feel like they have any weight.Mobility upgrades are mostly meaningless. Other than double jump. Towards the mid game enemies stop being tough and they just start spamming them. Quests are not rewarding. The stamp book rewards are literally garbage until you do nearly all of them. Accessories are so menial that I feel like its just meh.Some quests will not tell you even a general map they are on which is frustrating. The game is fun but is just inflated with boring quests, terrible dialogue and cutscenes, and anti-fun exploration mechanics.I would recommend it if they just added a better minimap. The other things are whatever. I can skip dialogue. I can skip quests.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: if you are a fan of classic ps1 JRPGs like suikoden 1 & 2 then you are in for a treat this was actually created by Yoshitaka Murayama the creator of the Suikoden video game series by Konami Murayama had directed Suikoden and Suikoden II during his time at Konami but left the company in 2002 shortly before the release of Suikoden III this was added due to the kick starter reaching one of its goals i just finished the main game and now I'm digging into this i cant wait to see more of this fascinating world
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Played for 4 hours and I'm enjoying my time with Eiyuden Chronicle Rising so far.I would recommend this game for fans of action JRPG with a side of Harvest Moon. The combat, character design, art direction, and story are exactly what I want in a metroidvania gameplay style. It's very welcoming to new players in this genre, but for hardcore players this might be too easy for you.(Even though there is a hard mode after you beat the game).The only negative thing about the game and many games struggle with this is providing side quests that are a bit more engaging to the player. Some of the side quests are great, but sometimes the classic fetch mission is a bit bland. I do like how you can build up your town and farm your way for the best weapons and gear, however, adding the stamp function introduces a more charming way when completing quests. You develop a sense of careness to the people who live there as you bring in more new adventures.Overall, I would give this game 9/10. It's not perfect, but definitely I'll have a fun time fighting more bosses and exploring new areas. I believe for the price of the game, you are getting a great valve, even when a Steam sale happens. I'm excited to see where the team takes Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes in 2023.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: From the people who brought you Suikoden 1,2,3 Comes a new story about three unlikely friends and heroes. Join CJ as she looks for the biggest treasure ever, and collect some stamps along the way. I have to say, the game surprised me in so many positive ways. The sidequests were the biggest part of the game but it was never too tedious to do them. The combat is simple but with some intricate mechanics that makes it a dopamine rush every time you nail a combo. Gear will improve not only your stats but sometimes also give you new abilities to make traversing the world a little easier. It's definitely one of those games you want to 100% (Though I haven't done it yet cus I ran out of time for 100 Heroes that came out around the time I started playing the game. But I will definitely revisit to finish the rest of the achievements!) The story is fun and charming, with some colorful personalities to top of the interesting designs. This is, NOT a turnbased RPG, however it is still an RPG in it's core. You prep gear, buy and craft items, learn new abilities as the story progresses and so, many, sidequests! There's a tonne of sidequests and the game will motivate you to do them. Difficulty wise it's not super difficult, !!!SPOILERS!!! If you want a challenge wait with doing most of the sidequests til post campaign as everything gets harder. !!!SPOILERS OVER!!! All in all a good classic vibe to enjoy. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: It's a neat little action/platforming game with some RPG and Metroidvania elements that has plot/backstory relevance for the main game (EC), as well as a few minor unlockables for same if you carry the save file over. It looks and sounds nice, it plays well with the ability to swap among the three characters at will and link their attacks together (shades of Trine, here). It also has some post-game content; reaching that point also unlocks Hard Mode and lets you enable it immediately, bringing some welcome challenge back to the game if you're been over-leveling your characters.My only real gripes are that the (optional) sidequests are repetitive and that the menu system is a bit rough – e.g. Characters cannot swap Accessories and elemental Runes with one another; you have to manually remove the old one from the first character if you want to give that piece of gear to someone else. Note that the dev team for this game is apparently NOT the same as the one that made the main game.That being said, the game itself is fun and well-written, and definitely worth giving a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Entirely not exactly what I expected but was glad I tried it out on Xbox Game Pass.It's weird to have characters be One-Button-andys.By that I mean, I hit ONE button to swap to them and they only do ONE attack.Heavy Attack (Y) = Slow AttackerLight Attack (X) = Fast AttackerUh, Other Attack (B) = Magic Attacker.The start of the game becomes really annoying as you can't do much. Dashing, Blocking, teleporting are all something you get a bit later and upgrade equally later. It feels very limiting and brings down the overall enjoyment of the game.There is a focus on Linked Attacks instead of giving meaningful combo attacks and different abilities.While Linked Attacks are awesome to look at and perform, it's hardly a solution for more customization of characters.The game is true to the banner art in which you get 3 characters and that's it.If you don't like their attacks or abilties, tough luck.The highlight of the game is how easily you can grind improvements for you characters and not the boss fights.The bosses of the game are complete jokes and often even if they hit you several times they won't be able to kill you unless you're under-geared for the fight.Speaking of improvements, Cooking food require crafting items but once you craft it ONE time, you can just buy it from then on. This system is also done for Shop items. However, food items grant permanent bonuses to your stats.You can literally increase your attack and Defense until you can steamroll every enemy in the game. This includes having all the Weapon, Armour and Lens upgrades. All of which are insanely effective at making the game easier to deal with.Beating the game on Normal mode unlocks Hard Mode.While you might think all enemies would be 40+ or scaled to your level, you can still find fairly easy enemies until you start reaching towards the end of the game. You can switch between Normal and Hard whenever you want once unlocked. And Hard doesn't seem to grant bonus items or better drops, which seems to be a missed opportunity. It's just a bit more game to enjoy so you can finish getting achievements.Overall, I enjoyed my time with this and for the price, I cannot go wrong.I'd say it would be around 8-10 hours of gameplay without 100% everything.A solid 6 outta 10 experience (Not entirely sure how it got 8 to 9's). While there are better indie games out there for around this price, I enjoyed my time and will move onto EC:HH.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Side quest simulator.Cute visuals with some good music. The combat, which starts out really simple, gets progressively more fun as you obtain more characters to chain combos and upgrade gear to unlock newer mechanics for each character. Items in shops need to be crafted first before being sellable.Story doesn't really pick up until about the last third of the game, the rest of the game is filled with fetch quests. After completing your stamp cards in the post game, all the side quests repeat (All 160 of them... with some slight dialogue changes... at least they are not needed for achievements). Hard mode can only be unlocked after beating the game which is a shame since the game is really easy.Fun game, sets up some lore/characters for the next game: Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I gave it a thumbs up because the game was cheap.It's not a bad game but it just get grindy and repetitive.The story isn't bad but i feel like watching an episode of One Piece with all the filler.The side quests come down to go here talk to this NPC, or grab this item from the dungeon... not a lot of variation.I played and finished this game because it's a sort of prologue to 100 heroes which i was eager to play.The game looks beautiful so no argument there.All in all i had a good time, not bad, not great, just good.The game is cheap or if you can get it at an discount even better!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: ---{Graphics}---☐ Masterpiece☑ Beautiful☐ Good☐ Decent☐ Will do☐ Bad☐ Awful☐ Paint.exe---{Gameplay}---☐ Try not to get addicted☐ Very good☐ Good☑ Nothing special☐ Ehh☐ Bad☐ Just don’t---{Audio}---☐ Eargasm☑ Very good☐ Good☐ Decent☐ Not too bad☐ Bad☐ Earrape---{Audience}---☑ Kids☑ Teens☑ Adults---{PC Requirements}---☐ Check if you can run paint☐ Potato☑ Everyone☐ Minimum☐ Decent☐ Fast☐ Rich boi☐ Ask NASA if they have a spare computer---{Difficulty}---☐ Facerolling is enough☑ Easy☐ Significant brain usage☐ Not so easy☐ Difficult☐ Dark Souls☐ Easy to learn / Hard to master---{Story}---☐ Lovely☐ Good☑ Average/nothing special☐ Bad☐ Doesn’t have☐ Story illogical, cryptic or unintelligible☐ Particularly funny☐ Particularly sad---{Game Time}---☐ >100 hours☐ 100 - 50 hours☑ 50 - 10 hours☐ 10 - 1 hour☐ Endless/game has no final objective---{Bugs}---☑ Never noticed any☐ Minor/few bugs, that do not bother the gaming experience☐ Can get annoying☐ Ruining the game☐ The game itself is a big terrarium for bugs☐ Bad AI botsFirst of all, I bought this game as a long-time Suikoden fan. Since I definitely want to play Eiyuden Chronicles: Hundred Heroes, I thought I should definitely complete this prequel first. However, my expectations for the game were not particularly high after seeing images and gameplay.In the end, I was pleasantly surprised by the game overall. Not by the gameplay, which is rather dull, to be honest. The game flows smoothly, and the controls and movement in the world are enjoyable. It's more about the complete lack of difficulty that doesn't impress in this aspect.The standout features of the game are undoubtedly the world-building and the characters. Initially presented as stereotypes, not only the main characters but also some supporting ones develop into strong personalities. However, genuine emotions are not yet fully conveyed in the relatively shallow storytelling; those expecting a sad love story will be disappointed. Nevertheless, the game still has a few small surprises that hint at the potential of Hundred Heroes.In my opinion, both the graphics and music are excellent. The 2.5D graphics are solid and look absolutely beautiful, managing to evoke nostalgic memories. The music is atmospheric, although after a while, the soundtrack in the same town feels a bit repetitive, mainly due to spending about half of the time there.I took around 17.3 hours for a full playthrough with all achievements, reading every dialogue and exploring all secrets.In conclusion, Eiyuden Chronicles: Rising is certainly an enjoyable and entertaining game that I can recommend for its price, especially to fans of the Suikoden series. It definitely got me excited for its successor!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm exactly 2 hours in, the refund time limit.The game has a few different areas. The first area is the forest.
