Each time you go, it's exactly the same.  They keep you going back by adding tedious little changes, for example, the second time you go to the forest you have to gather wood; the third time you have to kill the boss; the fourth time you have to go gather stone; the fourth time you have to find an NPC's lost quest item, etc. etc.It is pretty monotonous and linear. Side quests are kind of meaningless (help a guy collect mushrooms, help a girl get a wolf pelt.) You end up completing the quests inadvertently by just playing as you normally would. Being linear, there are no choices, just a story line that you experience as you play through the game.In terms of challenge, I was surprised by how hard the first boss hit, but dodging all the attacks is very easy. 2 hours in and I'm about to fight the second boss of the game.The rarity system in the game is 1 star to 5 stars. You start with 1 star weapons. Then you upgrade to a set of 2 star weapons. There are no choices, you are forced to upgrade and there is only one option. I presume that after I kill the quarry boss, I will be forced to upgrade to the 3* weapons and there will be no options to choose from.The combat system is pretty straight forward. You are limited in your abilities. Game gives you double jump and slowly unlocks more combos in your chain of attacks as you upgrade weapons. idk... meh.I think there are better games out there for $15.That being said, the game is pretty.*update*. second boss was really easy and slow and simple and not challenging. kind of disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short, your enjoyment of this game hinges on two things:1. Wanting to learn about some characters and world of the upcoming Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes (a Suikoden clone).2. Wanting a super-casual and cheerful, time-killing RPG.I found this game by accident after seeing cover artwork that reminded me of a PS1 favorite: Suikoden. Oddly enough, this game is a teaser for a Suikoden clone by original Suikoden devs! I saw multiple reviews saying it was repetitive, but for the sale price of $3 and my need for a relaxing game in the evenings, it fit the bill.I don't regret my (sale) purchase for a niche need and it served its marketing purpose of getting me interested in the upcoming game. However, . You really do go to the same five or so areas over and over again, the main character is too agile not to use all the time, and doing side content lets you faceroll everything, negating the need for potions, runes, food, and secondary characters' equipment.+Bright, colorful and beautiful artwork+Combat generally fluid and enjoyable+Some minor metroidvania elements+Map and quest logs are decent+UI shows when enemies are strong/weak to your attacks+Destructible enemy shields were nice+Characters likable, albeit a bit cliche'+Some humor+Lots of fast travel+Autosave, frequent save points, multiple slots+Experienced zero bugs, crashes or even typos+Switch between 3 characters at will+Trader NPC helps swap some older materials for new+Clearly marked (temporary) point of no return+Can keep playing after beating the game+Long play time (20+ hours?) for completionists~Does not play in any way like a Suikoden game~Very easy: making runes, food, and potions near-useless~Very upbeat. Game rarely dwells on "heavy" stuff.~Very linear with little exploration or secrets~Segmented character model movement always looks weird~Music is either really nice or maddeningly repetitious~Post-game content is seriously grindy with no added story-Very very repetitious. Seriously. Same areas over and over.-CJ ridiculously good. Almost no reason to bother with the other two.-Meat of story and character development held til last 5% of game-Hard mode only unlocked after beating game-Bronze is not an ore-Recipes sometimes require materials you won't get until much much later

_childDocuments_.review: Shockingly, despite being fan, I'm putting this on 'do not recommend'. The reason being precisely that I'm a fan. It's a metroidvania-esque 'extra' that introduces you to some characters who will feature in the main Eiyuden Chronicle game, offering you just a taste of the world you'll be immersed in in the future. There are limited maps and all the side quests are basically iterations of fetch quests (over 160 of them to be precise) and the combat isn't particularly challenging without self-imposed restrictions. Buy it if you're interested in dipping a toe in the EIyuden lore, otherwise if you're looking for a stand-alone game, this probably isn't for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. I had fun, as it reminded me of older, simpler, more confined stories from the NES and SNES years. It's lighthearted, imaginative, and has a fairly well thought out world that, I'm assuming, we're going to be seeing me of in the future.I will make some notes for the developers though, on the chance they might see this. Some criticisms and possible fixes. There will be spoilers, so reader beware.1. The endless fetch quests got exceedingly tedious. Not because they are, in themselves, bad, but you stuffed the game to the gills with them. I understand that with a 2-D Platformer, there's only so much you can do without programming in new engines, but there is a reason why the SNES and NES games were shorter. They didn't shove THIS MUCH inane, tasteless tasks in to pad out the game.Possible fixes. Cut down the quests that have nothing to do with progression. There is no reason these adventurers trying to save people and gain treasure would stop to help kids find playmates, or a child find a parent less than a screen transition away. Add more puzzle quests, maybe more Menhir-style puzzles to break up the monotony. Or more incentive to do Fishing, or more in depth Trapping. Something to think about for the main game.2. The dismount of this game is terrible. I do like that there wasn't a token "Dad's actually ok" ending, but there was nothing to really sink your teeth into at the end. Random bandits appear despite not having any way to get there, a new named character shows up that we only just heard his name maybe 10 minutes ago and he's just HERE now and gone. And the final boss was visually interesting, but slow, weak, and lacking any sense of threat that you've been building up. I mean, we never even found out what this power hungry narcissist's NAME was, or why he wanted this power. Was he really just a "Am Evil Want Power" character? Because you went into backstories with so many other characters, and hinted at some with lesser ones, but the final boss get's that kind of treatment?Fixes. It doesn't have to be much. Some of the recordings could have been that this Mage had been kicked out of other places, and is now obsessed with furthering his research to prove the other lands are weak. Maybe he was kicked out for being too extreme, even for the Empire. Maybe he was an agent sent out by some faction in the world and he was researching for a greater cause. Just SOMETHING to motivate him into gaining power.3. The CONSTANT "Completed Quest!" "New Quest!" "GO HERE NOW!" notifications! They don't need to be so many and so in your face! When you accomplish something, the first thing on your mind shouldn't be "I'm got enough time to check my Youtube feed while this song and dance goes wastes my time." Main story quests can get that treatment. "Go to the bar and eat" should not.Fixes. You want to highlight big events, not every event. Make the player feel like they accomplished something big. Just have the quest tracker flash a nice little sunburst when it changes to the next task.Edit: I decided to go back into the game to finish the Black Task card missions, just to see what was there for the completion bonus...And there was nothing but MORE inane tasks. But not just more, but the SAME EXACT tasks I had just done. No fanfare. No final goal or party. Just more inane busywork. Come on people! When you put pepper on something, do you unscrew the cap!? Do yourselves a favor and hire a QA team. Some group of people to tell you "No. That's enough." You NEED it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has its ups and downs. For the most part I would say this game deserves a solid B-. It doesn't do anything particularly bad, nor does it do anything particularly amazing. The story is really unimportant, and doesn't feel important till the last 7 or so main quests. The gameplay is fun but its more or less a hack and slash 2D side scroller with a combo system. The fighting does get pretty old after 12hours but weapon upgrades that allow for longer combo strains keep the gameplay some what fresh till the end. Side quests in this game are all more or less just fetch quest with no real reason other than to pad the game and make it feel longer than it should be. You could honestly completely skip all side quests if not for the fact that completing your stamp quest gave you an extra combo link for every page you finish. Every side quest really just felt like some flat chested girls bra filled to the brim with tissues. This games length would honestly be cut in half if I didn't spend so much time completing side quest for one or two extra combo links. The bosses in this game are all for the most part nothing different than most enemies, other than the fact that they have large health bars. The soundtrack isn't anything to right home about. The art and graphics is definitely the one thing to take away from this game and even then its not really anything special. Octopath and Triangle strategy both have the same if not better art design as this game. So in conclusion, just wait for a sale. If not on sale this game isn't worth the 15$ price tag. It feels like a cheap indie game for 5$.

The town building is a major grab for me in any game I play and EC:R does a good job at it. The art style gives me that nice retro feeling from old PS1 titles but does a fantastic job at modernizing it and making the backgrounds look beautiful. The combat is all right but the real shining star is the tag team attacks that are so fluid and very satisfying to do.However, I can not recommend this game to the average person. While the game has a very short and simple story, it is filled with fetch quests and grinding that remind me too much of old school RPG's. If you enjoy those types of games then this will be right up your alley. After finishing this and doing everything the game had to offer, I really wish I had just done the main quests and moved on. _childDocuments_.review: I thought about this review for a couple days now. I thought if I'd be okay with recommending it even at the low price point of $15, but I just can't do it. I believe I could only recommend this game if it were a remaster of an older game so I could put it in the context of the era it released in; however, it's not and I expect a bit more in these games now. The one thing that I do really like about this title is the backgrounds. They all look amazing. Whoever did that work did a great job.Other than that, I can't recommend it because it's just so average. Nearly everything about it is average. You can get a better action RPG experience elsewhere and you should seek that out. The side quests are all fetch quests or "go talk to someone for a hot second," and typically most of these encounters aren't really that interesting and usually only involve one or two very short encounters. However, you'll want to do them for the monetary rewards and the other progression system () you're introduced to early in the game. There's just not a lot of variety or excitement here.One thing I did enjoy were those -esque puzzles you'll eventually run into, but even then, you only do them 3 or 4 times at most. The system of  I figured I'd enjoy more, but it wasn't seamless. I felt like having the ability to switch those out with L1/R1 would have been more enjoyable rather than taking me out of the action to make changes.The combat feels pretty good, but it's also very easy. Before I bought the game, I was wondering why players on the community hub were telling the developer to release the hard mode from the beginning and I agree. That should be a choice. You'll have no problem fighting most enemies in this game on what I'm presuming is the easy/normal mode by default.For $15 you'll enjoy some of the ride, but I found myself not wanting to continue the side-quests as they weren't engaging. Also, the ending was INCREDIBLY . The credits just came out of nowhere like mid-scene. Very strange.You very much get what you pay for here. If you have no other side scrolling action RPG to play, then I guess try it out -- it is cheap, but I’d rather you just play something with more meat.

_childDocuments_.review: As an immense fan of Suikoden 1 and 2, this supposed prequel to the spiritual successor of those games (Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes) piqued my interest. Unfortunately, after having logged six hours into it, I can only describe my feeling with it to be intense loathing.This game is nothing like Suikoden 1 and 2. There's no political intrigue. There's no morally ambiguous wars that pit complex characters in ethically troubling situations. There's no charming, interesting characters that have complex motivations. It's an absolute paint-by-numbers JRPG that does nothing to harken back to the games it was supposedly inspired by.The gameplay is just the most basic Metroidvania. And your entire time with the game will be spent doing fetch quests. It is fetch quest after fetch quest after fetch quest. Everything comes back to you collecting stamps from people, which you get by doing tasks for them. And they all invariably involve you going from A to B to collect this to deliver to that person. It's mind numbing.What kind of game is it? I am entirely unsure. It doesn't really seem to have an identity. It is so hopelessly generic that I find myself at a complete loss as to why it was necessary to even be made. I have nothing positive to say about the story, characters, or gameplay. It's all so damn forgettable.Both Suikoden 1 and Suikoden 2, especially 2, had my rapt attention within the first hour. The only reason I even put six hours into it was out of respect for those games and the hope that maybe it would get interesting. It never does.If this was supposed to get me hyped for the main game, it did the exact opposite.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely do NOT recommend Eiyuden Chronicles: Rising, please go do anything else with the spared 10 hours. Sincerely from someone who completed the game. It does NOT respect your time.Gameplay:Playing the game feels like playing a Megaman level, getting a fourth of the way and running back. Dozens of Cutscenes. Repeat that about five times. Then you fight the Boss. Then do that about eh, five times again. Just... why?! Let me complete Levels and do content AND THEN you can rail me with cutscenes. I just want to go and have a good time fighting and looting. At about 4hrs in (Volcano) you finally start to play through an entire stage without being interrupted every 2 seconds, however it swiftly ends and you resume the cutscene saga with the realization you've been conned into playing a Movie disguised as a Game.Tutorials the GAME:This game is extremely hand-holding and doesn't want to let you go... EVER. At 2.5 hours in the game I was still doing tutorials which unlock more aspects of the game. This would be fine if it was needed, like so complicated that the tutorials are required but this is basic stuff. Like a Blacksmith and Armorsmith to upgrade... well, I MEAN GEE I WONDER WHAT THEY UPGRADE. Inn, Tavern, Accessory, Apothecary, so on and so forth. I understand you don't want to dump twenty different shops on the player all at once however the game feels like it took a every single Shop an RPG normally has and divided them into two/three individual ones.RPG 'Elements':This has 2 Accessory Slots and 2 Rune Slots. The Accessory slots are basic things like ATK/CRIT/PDEF/MDEF or Lifeskill (Hunting/Fishing/EXP/Drops). The Rune Slots are for Offensive/Defensive Element selections. Got that all? Okay okay. I never EVER in the entire game used the Defensive Rune Slot. The Offensive Rune Slot you are forced to use to progress or I would've never used that either (destroys Elemental Barricades). I forgot the Accessory Slots even existed until I had to change my Offensive Rune, so not game changers. Then there's Weapon/Armor upgrades which just flat upgrades your default gear +1/2/3/etc. Then there's Levels, not sure the Max Level but I beat the game without getting to it or maxing the Weapon/Equipment. Both are pointless grinds.Lifeskills:You one-tap a tree or ore and you get stuff. You see a trap spot, you place a trap and MAYBE get something when you leave the Dungeon. Fishing you press whatever button combo you need to catch the Fish. It's nothing exciting, none of it is well done. The Lumber/Ore part is just mindless sprint back and forth while smacking enemies and you'll generally be set. I only used the Traps for Side Quests and never really bothered otherwise, Fishing was the same. Do not expect it to be like Fishing in other series, there's no catalogue or anything. It's just there to get the basic Fish Ingredient.aRPG Combat aka LINK ATTACK:Combat's got the depth of a puddle. Essentially you have an attack button and a 'special' button depending on the character. You then have ANOTHER button (gasp!) which swaps your character and does an attack. This new character you now control has an attack button and THEIR 'special' button. If you hit an Enemy with the first character attack button, then the second character attack button (X, Y) then it starts a chain link you practically can't mess up: X, Y, X, Y until it's dead. It's a little overwhelming when you unlock the dreaded B button (/s). Link Attacks are limited initially starting at a 2-Combo then slowly growing to 3, 4, 5-hit combos.The Link-effect will just warp your character wherever and do a slowdown-time effect. I wish the Link Attack didn't have the slowdown as it's the main way you'll be fighting and gets annoying fairly quickly. You can't control what you're even aiming at because it's the last unit hit which means you'll be wombo combo'ing a very already dead enemy when there's plenty of alive things around. There's no i-frames after being hit so getting staggered in a mob of enemies is common. Enemies inflict damage if you get too close to them. I think you can imagine what it's like to use the Link Attack, and randomly teleport into an enemy and flop on the ground like a fish. More importantly there's status effects in the game. If you get hit by the status effects it disables the ability to swap between characters which means you can't do Link Attacks until it ends. This is absolutely INSANE to me as a design decision. You literally can't play the game if you get hit by a status effect. There's a Boss towards the end of the game who's only mechanic is to prevent you from Link Attacking because he can dodge out of the combo which is SO weird that the entire game is based around this concept and there's multiple mechanics trying to prevent the use of it. The Devs need to make up their mind on how they want people to play the game. I'd love if this was more of a Marvel v Capcom-like asthetic where you have a single character you can do combos and the other two characters can just give assists. This is a watered down version of something that could've been great.Stages:The dungeons are all generically element themed. Woods = Earth, Cave = Lightning, Mountain = Ice, Volcano = Fire. Having what amounts to 5 stages isn't great to go back to over and over the entire game since you'll be farming those stages for Side Quests or Equipment.Bosses:Bosses are ALSO generic surprise, surprise. The Woods Boss needs to be waited out to reveal a Weakpoint, while the Quarry Boss needs to have a projectile reflected to break it's guard. The Mountain and Volcano Bosses can just be attacked until they die, you CAN down the Volcano Boss similar to the Quarry Boss by deflecting projectiles with Garoo but it's optional. The Final Boss is exactly like the Woods Boss, wait for him to do his stuff and then his Weakpoint comes out for you to kill. None of the Bosses are hard, they have 2-3 moves total and hardly have mechanics.Quests:There's 160+ generic Side Quests to do (Collect X or Talk to X). You're forced into doing them to unlock upgrades for your gear and even the Main Quest turns into Side Quest material where you run around gathering Eggs. I quit the game at 160 Quests and it unlocks what I presume are repeat Quests that you can farm for rewards if you're enough of a masochist to continue grinding for no particular reason. What do you get for completing the 160? You break the game by having Unlimited Link Attacks which makes Combat even more of a joke.Difficulty:The game is absurdly easy. Once you complete the game it soft-resets your save to before the Final Boss where it unlocks 'Hard Mode', which is just a level increase for all the Bosses/Mobs. At THIS point that there's a noticeable difficulty spike, because suddenly you're fighting a LV70 Bandit at probably ~LV30-40 which means they'll just straight delete a character if you get hit. However I can't say the same for the Bosses. These random Mobs and Side Quest Mobs can be a menace, but the Bosses are all at LV55 and aren't NEARLY as difficult as the Bandits I mentioned. Which I keep saying 'Difficult', it's still not. It's like the Bethesda Difficulty slider just slid to Enemies doing more damage.Horrible QoL:[STAMP ANIMATION][QUEST COMPLETE][LEVEL UP][EXP +750][GOLD +1000][CUTSCENE][NEW STOCK]I can't understand why a typical Quest Window was divided into five separate windows. Please just combine all the information I listed above into a concise SINGLE window. ONE. SINGULAR.Can only track ONE Side Quest at a time, despite the 160+ Side Quests.  Which means you'll spend your time going into the Menu, Quests, and scrolling to see what other Quests are in the same region. The Map should be showing where my Quests are at all times AND you should be able to track MORE THAN ONE at a time.There's a Notification Board to show Available Quests but you can't accept Quests from that Board.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game with easy to understand mechanics. I 100% completed the game at 40 hours - although for some reason my Steam page says I haven't gotten the hidden achievement for maxing all my weapons, even though all my weapons and armour are maxed, but oh well.This is my first side-scroll type game, as I've never been that keen on this time but I was really surprised at how much I enjoyed it. A nice little classic JRPG storyline and only 3 playable charas keeps things streamlined, so you don't need to waste hours building and choosing from dozens of charas in the roster. However, do be aware that there are a loooooot of side quests and fetch quests - 160 in total. And while many need to be done in earlier parts of the game to raise your level and rep, the side quests after the end of the main story are purely optional.

_childDocuments_.review: For the price, this is a nice game. It's simple, the UI can be a bit sticky and clunky in places, and about half of the game is story cutscenes and running around town to find errands and sidequests, but I feel like I got my money's worth. The best part is that, despite being a supplement story for Hundred Heroes, this game's story only takes about 10-15 hours, depending on how much you get sidetracked on errands. I enjoyed getting invested in New Neveah and everyone living there, and now I'm looking forward to finding them in Hundred Heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's Trine & Maplestory mixed together as a rather casual but still fun JRPG.One thing that stood out to me was.. this was one of the few RPGs I've actually COMPLETED in years, and that's due in no small part to its very gentle difficulty and pleasant introduction. This game breaks no new ground, but is still rewarding as you slowly build up New Neveah from a hovel with nary a shop to a bustling town. It's a charming little JRPG, one that doesn't overstay its welcome, so while the game is 'simple' it never feels like a grind. The story is straightforward, but it helps to keep the action going rather than add gameplay hours for the sake of it, and I consider that a plus. For its price it's well worth trying it out!

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Rising: A Charming Adventure in Town BuildingRating: 4.5/5"Eiyuden Rising" is a delightful action RPG that brilliantly combines town-building elements with engaging quest-driven gameplay. Set in the enchanting world of New Neveah, players embark on an epic journey to rebuild and enhance their town, creating a vibrant community from the ground up.Story and SettingThe story begins with your character arriving in New Neveah, a town in dire need of restoration. The narrative is rich with lore, and each of the dozens of inhabitants adds a unique touch to the unfolding story. The game's writing is superb, offering a mix of heartfelt moments, humorous interactions, and intriguing mysteries that keep players invested in the town's revival.Gameplay and MechanicsThe gameplay is a blend of classic RPG elements and town-building mechanics. Players collect raw materials through exploration and combat, which are essential for upgrading buildings and crafting new items. The town of New Neveah evolves with each upgrade, visually reflecting your progress and growing more vibrant with every improvement.The quest system is robust, featuring a wide variety of missions given by the town's inhabitants. These quests range from gathering specific materials to battling formidable foes, ensuring that gameplay remains fresh and exciting. The inhabitants themselves are wonderfully designed, each with their own backstory and personality, making the quests feel meaningful and rewarding.Visuals and SoundVisually, "Eiyuden Rising" is a treat. The art style is colorful and detailed, with a charming aesthetic that brings the world of New Neveah to life. The character designs are distinctive and memorable, contributing to the overall appeal of the game. The soundtrack complements the visual experience perfectly, with melodic tunes that enhance the atmosphere and immerse players in the game's world.Pros and ConsPros:    Engaging Town-Building Mechanics: Collecting materials and completing quests to rebuild New Neveah is highly satisfying.    Rich Story and Characters: The narrative is compelling, and the diverse cast of characters adds depth to the game.    Beautiful Visuals and Soundtrack: The game's art and music create an enchanting atmosphere.Cons:    Repetitive Combat: While enjoyable, combat can become repetitive over time, especially for players focused on town-building.    Resource Grinding: Some players might find the need to gather resources tedious, particularly in later stages of the game.Conclusion"Eiyuden Rising" is a charming and captivating game that successfully combines town-building and RPG elements. The joy of seeing New Neveah flourish under your guidance, coupled with the engaging quests and delightful characters, makes this game a standout experience. Despite minor drawbacks like repetitive combat, the overall package is highly enjoyable and offers countless hours of rewarding gameplay.If you enjoy town-building games with a rich narrative and engaging characters, "Eiyuden Rising" is definitely worth your time. Dive into the world of New Neveah and experience the magic of rebuilding a community from the ground up

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is a metroidvania like action RPG that serves as a prequel of sorts to Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundre Heroes.The game features CJ, kicked out of home at the age of 15, she is on her quest to retrieve an artifact, greater than the one her father found, as a family rites of passage before she can return home. Along the way she meets Garoo and Isha and they join up to stop the Evil Sorcerer™s evil plans.The game features a classical JRPG feature such as town building, which lets you progressively unlock new vendors allowing item purchases and upgrade of weapons and armor. This is handled via the quest system, where the vendors of New Neveah, will frequently offer simple quests in order to unlock their additional inventory.The game also has a small selection of dungeons, broken up in to segments of scenes, with fast travel options available which you unlock as you move deeper, and with monsters resetting when you leave the dungeons to return to the town. There's also a classical and simple cooking crafting vendor, that lets you eat what you cook, for small stat ups and health regain.As far as core gameplay, the game is fairly relaxed in its approach, letting you essentially button smash your way to victory throughout the game, and despite a limited inventory for components and health potions, you'll rarely need the potions, and inventory space is increased to the point where it no longer matters.The combat is fairly simple, you start out with just CJ, but are quickly joined by Garoo and later Isha, letting you play as either of the three characters, by simple key press, but they can also combine their attacks for devastating combos. Upgrading weapons and armors allows for additional attacks or movement options.The game doesn't really feel like it manages to balance all the various upgrades, between weapons, which have two separate upgrade options, armors, foods and the somewhat pointless accessories that are only active on the current character in control. The later a bewildering design because there are the usual assortment of accessories which increases drop rates and what not, but they are only active on the current active character, which constantly changes due to the games linked combo system.Then there's the inane repetitiveness of the side quests, or the quests in general, as the majority of them are simple fetch quests, or farm quests, or as mindboggling as running courier between two NPCs within 30 steps of each other. You can collect stamps throughout the game for additional rewards, one stamp for each quest, but there's more than 160 quests, which is far too many that just serves as filler in the end and drags the games overall presentation down in the gutter.The story isn't anything to write home about either, what little there is. It's stepped in cliches and the silliness of the NPCs quickly drowns out any interest you may have for the overall story.If the game hadn't been so mind numbingly grindy, it might have had some redeeming value.

_childDocuments_.review: Light-hearted metroidvanina kind of game that involves simple RPG elements and town-building   + The story is easy to understand and does it's objective of introducing/setting up the characters and the elements that will be used for the next game+ Combat is above average fun and simple but felt clunky in a way that it feels cheap+ RPG element-wise, the customization suffers a lot from early to mid game with the inclusion of drop rate increasing accessories sharing slots with combat related accessories. This is a old jrpg design element that doesn't really improve combat but downright affect customization (sometimes it affects gameplay too if such things as dash boots or equivalent accessory is present in a game)+ In terms of difficulty, the game is casual and lacks harder challenges or difficulty options on the get-go+ The environment is very gorgeous. The 2.5D style is well-crafted.+ The map is easy to navigate even with its simple map design and mini-map but lacks depth of exploration compared to popular others of the same genre+ There are a number of side content, while it is very satisfying to see the town grew from your actions, a lot of the other side content felt like it is only there to bloat the content+ Graphical Fidelity (FPS, Detail and Resolution), the game runs well without any performance and graphical issues (RTX 4070 Laptop), The blending of the environment while the player is exploring or battling is vibrant and pristine.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I've sunk over three hours into this mind-numbing snoozefest that plays like a very mid Newgrounds flash game from 2012.But so help me God, I'm going to keep going because the colorful presentation, likeably one-dimensional characters, and mindlessly satisfying gameplay are just what I need right now.Recommended for depressed insomniacs with low standards.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill game designed to suit people not good at action games. Writing is of great quality with lots of humorous dialogues. Sub-quests may get a little repetitive if aiming for 100% achievements. I only wish lore-related information are more evenly spread out rather than concentrated towards the end.Oh and graphics is amazingly beautiful especially when converted to HDR. I'm using RTX HDR.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun! Not very difficult but the gameplay/story has a fun flow to it & the combat feels pretty unique with how it handles 1 character per button & their mechanics/gimmicks you switch to on the fly.I wasn't expecting this to be a Metroidvania style game but I like them so that wasn't a negative for me at all. I think I am nearing the end but for the $15 I paid I've already gotten my value from this, I definitely recommend the game even without considering any of the other games in the series, nor it's "sequel" that just released recently (hundred heroes).If you are interested & like side scrolling Metroidvania with fairly unique action Combat with a fun story, give this a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: neat "little" 2-D hack'n slashyou basicaly play 3 characters, each kinda assigned to 1 button (PS4-pad like square, triangle circle). each character has it's little special gimmicks, like one got a dash (also in the air), one can parry, one can float/short range teleport, each having their own combat approach: quick melee-combos, large slow sword slashes or magic (ranged). each can be linked (depening on the stage of your re-building of the village) which basicaly means you can combo enemies via changing your attack-button during an attack and thus call in the other party-members to attack.there's some light jump'n run stuff (nothing difficult, even when it comes to hidden treasure), light (!) metroid-vania elements: during the game you encounter enemies/areas linked an element (lighting, fire, ice, earth) and also way-blocking-pillars linked to an element; once you get the right elemental "lens-setup" you can smash these pillars and proceed. nothing complicated and you can count these blocks with both of your hands. the gameplay loop is basicaly you beeing in town, which expands during the course of the plot and depending on how much you engage with the side-quest/re-building efforts. here you take on main- and sidequest, upgrade your gear or buy consumables, etc. then you venture out into either the Quarry, the Forest or the so called Runebarrows which lead to a snowy and lava region aswell. it's like dungeon-devling in the most literal sense. enemies drop materials, etc. and there's materials like trees for wood to be found in each "dungeon". side- and mainquest, gear upgrades, new buff-food all needs specific materials which can you farm/hunt for. it's a very uncomplicated, easy to digest gameplay loop. each solved main- and subquest has a high chance to net you an ingame stamp for your collection (kinda an ingame running gag), unlock enough stamps to get more linking-combo-attacks and see the village improve/rebuild.now on it's own nothing here is very special or intricate, but it's the general vibe, the visual design, the absolute fantastic and upbeat OST and the very enjoable writing (short lines, to the point, often pretty tonugue and cheek humor; again: easy to digest), the lovable characters and the general ubeat vibe that makes it quite entertaining. the OST especialy carries a lot here: beeing it the humming beat in the Quarry, the somber, almost nostalgic tunes in the snow or the low-key-techno-beats in some Burrows places, this OST rocks in it's production (quality) and it's deliverance. goes to show you how important music can be.as sorta special side-note the games serves as a pre-quel to the now released "real" game, a jrpg-callback to the Suikoden series of old. some stuff gets unlocked depending on how much you progressed in Rising, but even more important and after having now finished Rising and played quite a bit of the main game: Rising is a perfect pre-quel introduction to 100 Heroes. you learn about the lore and the world, the terminology and a lot of characters you are actualy gonna meet back in 100 Heroes again. those 10 to 25 spend on Rising are imho realy worth it if you plan on playing 100 Heroes, less for the unlockable boni in the game, but more for enjoyment of the world- and lore design.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This is my second play through. I played this in a different platform. It's a very fun fast paced game and despite being a "beat em up" side scroll platform you'd be surprised on how rich the story is. I fell in love with the characters and the town and it gives a very nostalgic vibe when you see your base "grow" as you progress through the game. It's very newbie friendly and if you played its predecessor, nostalgia is going to hit you really hard. I suggest to buy it at full price. It's a short game where I unlocked everything and it's pretty straight forward without the round about BS that other games do (unless of course you like those kind of things). If you can buy it on sale, even better. Plus, devs say that it has cross content feature that can probably alter the next game's story (minor) like the name of weapons and the food that you'll create in the game.Try it out. You will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game that respects your time and doesn't burden you with quests that require searching all over the internet through forums, half-assed trolly outdated guides with unanswered questions. You won't need to have your browser opened with a guide and get bored with it before finishing it . There's no game breaking bugs that leave you trapped where you can't complete or miss any achievements. 10/10 for an ethical development team that doesn't scam you and force you into an eternal grindy hellhole of hideous boredom. It's a perfect sidescroller.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Its a nice little game. It invents nothing new trys to intruduce you to the world of Eiyuden Chronicle I like the art i like the presentation but to be fair i am a big fan of Suikoden 1&2,What i did not like the game i was repetitive, sidequests were almost all boring fetch and talk. the game was to easy.R.I.P Yoshitaka Murayama you gave me many good hours of fun with your Games thx for that to you and your team.it took me 23hours to do anything so its on the shorter side.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the unique hack and slash where all of your parties can participate in single combat, instead of building and focusing one character as main DPS and the other just an addition figurine or support.The learning pattern is quite simple and straightforward, no tedious gameplay, no boss is too hard, no grinding is required. The side quest might seem repetitive but it's completely unnecessary to do. You can just straight main stories all the way with ease.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Its a neat little metroidvania/arpg type game. A good way to prepare yourself for Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes. The game isnt complicated and I would even say its easy. LOTS of side quest to a point where its kind of a joke but theres a lot of stuff to unlock in stores. Basically you need to rebuild a village, so youll need to help the villagers and upgrade the towns stores.The story is aright and the gameplay is fine although I felt like the game overstay its welcome a little bit. It does drag on especially if you want to 100%. I bought it on sale for 5$ and I dont regret my decision, I had a fun time.Some feature from you save file will transfer to Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes when it releases. Stuff like how you name your weapons, food and maybe more (no onw knows for sure at the time of writing this review)
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it to tide me over until Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes, but ended up overwhelmingly enjoying it just on its own merits.  Fun game play loop, heart warming story, rewarding town building/progression system, I legitimately would have loved this game even if it didn't have the Eiyuden Chronicle label.  The fact it does tie in to the HH game with stuff that will carry over has just makes it extra special.Its worth noting there is a decent amount of backtracking, particularly if you want to get "everything", this is kind a metroidvania in that respect, so if your the type who hates that, I could see that being a negative.  I also kind of wish it had voice acting, there's a decent amount of dialogue in the game and from what I understand the main characters will have voice acting in Hundred Heroes, so there's already actors for the roles, but that's more of a QoL request then a real gripe.  Lastly, it might be slightly on the easier side, but I do feel like the game does a good job of giving you control over the difficulty with how much you choose to grind/quest/equip/min-max your team, I'm just a completionist so I'm doing everything, and if you do everything you'll inevitably end up a little on the strong side once you do progress the story.Final Thoughts: If there's ever an Eiyuden Chrronicle: Rising 2, I'd buy it, this game is so good its crazy to me this is the "side" project to the main Hundred Heroes game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Solid, simple action RPG. Purchased on sale and it was totally worth the price. 100% the game, it wasn't very complicated, and hard mode wasn't exactly that hard. Overall I had a fun time, the combat felt pretty snappy and opened up a little better once a few weapons/armor is unlocked. Probably not for everyone since it is a bit grindy, but I picked it up in anticipation for 100 heroes and I have had fun with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up on sale, but would buy at full price ($15 USD as of this review). Side quests are a little repetitive, but a nice break from the story. Loved the combat, especially as you level up your weapons and gain new abilities. Story is fun, characters are charming. Looking forward to the next game in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like fetch quests? If you can answer yes to that question, you'll like this game. It's odd in the sense that main quest isn't really the heart of the game. The side quests are. It's a side-scrolling action jrpg. Imagine a simplified Astlibra Revision. Pretty simple combat that isn't very difficult. You get a quest to fetch something from a dungeon, you get it, you come back. Repeat. While this sounds tedious, it's actually a blast. Every quest gives you something. Maybe you get a better shop, maybe you just get to know the residents a little better as you do more quests. As you quest, you gather a lot of items that you sell or use for the many, many upgrades. Good music, great 2.5D art style, likeable characters. Not afraid to make fun of RPG tropes, or even itself. I don't know why I didn't hear about this one sooner.tldr: Side quests make dopamine go brrr 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This kind of game isn't usually my cup of tea, but with the hype building for the release of the Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes game later this month, I figured I'd 100% the game and keep the save file in the hopes that the developers of the game keep the old Suikoden feature of using a save file to enhance the next game of the series. No idea if that's how it'll pan out, so I guess I'll find out.Back to this game though, this was an unexpectedly good game considering it's not what I usually play. There's a simplified version of the controls which helped me out MASSIVELY into continuing this game. Lots of lore buildup for the next game, and a lot of quests. There's a hard mode that can get turned on once you beat the game and you can basically just run quest repeats over and over again if that's your thing.Once you've reached a certain point, you're basically unstoppable and it feels real nice to be that overpowered after not being that for so long. Especially against the wolf-types.Story is great and only really touches in that local area where the game takes place with light influences to other regions which I think is perfect for this game ahead of Hundred Heroes.I'm not sure that I would have played this if it wasn't for the Eiyuden Chronicle team having made such strong callbacks to Suikoden, but this this series, I definitely don't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games I wish Steam had a neutral rating for.The combat, story, and art are all satisfying. I think the only category that pulls ahead of them is the characters. They were well-crafted and Garoo in particular you knew for a fact the gears were turning in his head even when he was silent.Where the game falls apart is that side-quests are the primary means of actual progression. Awarding a total sum of xp and currency far in excess you will get elsewhere that you will  to upgrade your gear (a lot). And most of them are "go back into the dungeon for the umpteenth time to mine ore or kill enemies" . I’ve put thousands of hours into grindy games before. I don't think I could stomach 40 of this. Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes is releasing at the end of April. I will be rethinking purchasing it if reviews roll in that it's as grindy as this.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts out slow, and I mean painfully slow. The main character is an immature, tomboy who has set out to prove herself to her family by finding treasure. However you actually end up spending the vast majority of your going back and forth from the same forest to the town running errands. Over time, you see your efforts pay off and the town grows to provide useful shops and of course, more quests. After awhile you gain a travelling companion, and then another (purposely avoiding spoilers here), and eventually you start getting hints at the characters individual stories, though at 14 hours in, I still have no idea what the main story is. I will admit, the only reason I purchased this game was because as a longtime Suikoden fan, I've been hyped for Eiyuden Chronicle Hundred Heroes and was under the impression that the story in this game ties into that. That said, the game has grown on me since I started playing.Exploration is gated by completing certain objectives and/or obtaining certain items. You return to the same place many times, opening up new areas each time. The combat reminds me of the Ys games, although simpler, which is just fine, because there are plenty of overly complicated action rpg's out there already. Each character has a basic attack, which can be charged into a more powerful attack by holding down the button. Combos consist of switching characters mid-fight to chain your attacks, and each character has their own strengths and weaknesses.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Its like a Monster Hunter-lite in metroidvania style. Play it as an ARPG - ignore and skip the filler story & conversations which run very slow. If you want a game for story - skip this. If you want a fun game to smash monsters, level up, develop your town, have simple but enjoyable boss fights - this is good.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I actually wasn't too captivated by it at first but returned to play it more so I can upload it to Hundred Heroes for bonus content.It became a lot more fun once I unlocked more combat skills/passives from upgrading armor/weapons and getting link-attacks. The game encouraging us to combo-juggle dead enemies for more exp is a nice touch, the poor things just get beat the crap out of. The game's entertaining and interesting enough that I went and did all the achievements even though I didn't need to.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Easy pick up and play, with a battle system that's simple yet fun. Many will complain that the gameplay is extremely repeated and quests are dull, but to me it was enough to satiate my hunger for what's to come. Ultimately playing this becoz its the precursor to the coming game, and wanted to show my support to the developers and get familiar with the world/ characters. Looking forward to the proper game in April!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 Nice to see a modern release of something in the spirit of Odin Sphere. Each explore-able area has nice unique graphic sets and the town building concept is well executed. The art quality throughout the game is of a high standard. Bosses are pretty well designed and I found those fights to be some of the best in the game. The quest exploration does get a bit grindy at times which is a shortcoming. There is also a lot of dialog which can feel like its slowing the pace down too much (but you can fast skip it if you choose). Definitely worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: represents the prequel to the incoming main game . Now, if someone already knows the well-known saga of  then is familiar with this kind of fantasy worlds where humans can interact with anthropomorphic animals (or "furries" if you prefer). The plot is focused on 3 characters who will reappear in the main game, the "Honorable Scavenger" CJ, the blue-haired magician Isha and the "Beastman" ex-mercenary Garoo. This trio will explore the territory of New Nevaeh and nearby Runebarrows. Maybe it won't take much to complete it, as a matter of fact getting all the achievements is rather simple. I think the strong point of the game is mainly to restore the town to its original splendor, a well-designed feature, together with the introduction of several characters who will appear even in the other game (for example the magical girl Mellore). If I should find something that might not be very appreciated is backtracking: it can be a little boring being obligated to go back in the zone you already explored just to get some resources for the subquests, still, in some cases that's necessary to update stores and get better products. Farming isn't that heavy, considering that you can always move when fighting, so this can make the game an , we may say.  is basically a story in which you can find both serious and comical elements (like the frequent quarrels between CJs and Garoo, with Isha trying to be the voice of reason), and that's something important for a not very lasting game like this. So, what I can say? If you really wanna know more about the world of EC and be prepared to main game, you have absolutely to play this game, it will be definitely worth it! =)
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game to help support the Eiyuden Chronicle devs and really I didn't have high hopes for this game being any fun. I thought it was just going to be a quick lil play through with some background story for the main game. I was pleasantly surprised with how much I enjoyed building the town up and getting to know the townsfolk. The stamp system is addictive and the combat isn't as janky as I thought it would be. Platforming is serviceable and after playing this I am even more hyped for the main game later this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who completed the game pretty much 100% as well as all achievements my verdict is...It's fine. It's enjoyable, but nothing groundbreaking.The game is just easy to play. It's methodical. You can play with the sound off if you want to. The combat isn't particularly challenging or require an inordinate amount of focus. The quests eventually wear on you and you might start skipping the dialogue on some of the side quests by the end of it. The game makes it easy to locate, pick up, and track quests so it's easy to just cross things off the list. It also makes it relatively accessible to upgrade things, from tools to weapon to armor, as well as customizing your accessories and utilizing potions and elements.It's fun. It's a good time killer. It's worth grabbing on sale. The dialogue and main narrative are fine. Some of the characters are a bit more annoying than others. The animation is pleasant to look at.Yeah. It's fine. If you need a pretty simple game or break from some more complex ones out there this is a fine detour. For the price on sale (I got it on $7.50) it was worth the money for the time I got out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Despite the fact that my stats say I played this for only a couple of hours, I played it on my Steam Deck offline and that time is for some reason not reflected, which seems to be an issue with any game in general.Since I want to play the upcoming Eiyuden Chronicles: Hundred Heroes RPG and I read this is a prequel and the characters from this game will appear on the next one, plus it's more of an action game Metrodivania-style, I decided to try it.I liked it for what it is. It's like a non-stressful alternative to the recent trend in punishing Metroidvanias inspired by Dark Souls, since it's pretty easy in comparison. The main complaint I've seen is that it's just a bunch of fetch quests, but it's not that different from any Metroidvania, only here you backtrack to deliver some resources or supplies instead of just because you finally got the item or ability that lets you open up some dead end. Plus, most of the time I found I'd already farmed what I needed for many  quests just by exploring and doing the main missions and the few times I had to actually go and farm specific stuff weren't that big of a deal thanks to the fast travel points in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle Rising is a pretty fun action JRPG overall. While the story is simple, you get drawn into it very quickly and the simple but fun gameplay will really keep you hooked for the ride. The game also offers a lot of replay value even if many side quest are shallow. The musical score is generally great and the ambiance overall just makes you want to stick around all the time. The characters are funny and very likable. I often laugh at the dialogs, especially with the banter betwen CJ and Garoo. So overall, a simple game but that is very much worth it even at full price. If you like action JRPG, youll likely like this one. I was pleasantly surprised and it made me look forward for Eiyude hundred heroes.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Despite it's cover art it's not "super anime" like it implies. I would even argue that after 4 hours it is close to being a cozy game. The graphics are beautiful and the combat is pretty easy. Some might complain about that but cozy gamers should check this one out. I've been having a very good, chill time. I admit there's probably no replayability though. Note for the creators: pretty icky that you made CJ really attractive and then told the viewer she's 16.  Why not avoid sexualizing an underage girl?
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game, took me 13ish hours to hit credits. Did all the side quests that were available throughout my play thru and max'd out everything I could. Honestly it was fun. I usually struggle to finish games because of retention issues but this game was perfect for me if I'm honest. Simple and rewarding. The characters were fun and varied. I recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most fun Dungeon Crawlers / Metroidvania / Platformers I played.Characters even the NPC have so much personality are so colourful and full of charm that kinda makes u wanna do their sidequests.Story / narrative is pretty interesting that keeps you engaged with how they show world grows as u progress.Locations look nice both visually and thematically.definitely worth ur money if u are planning to give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts out feeling slow and a bit clunky, but it's similar to a metroidvania in that it becomes more enjoyable to play as you unlock different moves and special attacks/combos. The controls are nice and responsive, combat is fun and mostly easy but a few bosses and wave encounters were somewhat challenging. The story and characters are charming enough, not a lot of dramatic weight to it but I guess it's acceptable as a light prequel to the main Eiyuden game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is an alright game, not bad and not great. I would grade it around 7.3/10. Recommend to get this only on Discount.It has good art, ok OST, simple short story. Gameplay is slightly better only after you upgrade character weapons etc.One major thing that annoys me is too many fetch quest, might as well change the title to Eiyuden hundred fetch quest.I get this game to support Yoshitaka Murayama, but I heard he only works on Rising as supervisor. Hopefully its RPG version would be great since I heard he personally directs and produces it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I'd never heard of this one before and picked it to play basically at random after getting it in a bundle.  I ended up really liking it, it's got a cute style with fun characters that I ended up getting pretty attached to.  The plot is fairly basic but serves to keep things moving along.  The combat is fairly simple but feels really good especially as you power up over the course of the game and increase your combo limits.  It felt too easy at the start but ramped up a bit to a nice challenge without being too hard.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Simpler Dragon's Crown/Odin Sphere that lacks some QoL features (like scrolling page of items with shoulder buttons, indication where you can finish active quest on map, etc.).It takes a while to unlock core gameplay stuff. It feels too careful to not intimidate a new player and blocks extraneous exploration so you'll progress like the game wants you to. It's good so far, like 6-7/10. It's a simple, easy enough game. Worth its price when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, the movesets and combos open up as you play the early game. about 15-20 minutes in, depending on how fast you quest. before that might feel a bit sluggish in combat until you get your first team mate. Otherwise, the combat becomes really fun. the characters are very well written, the dialogue is good. lots of quests to do, a town to improve and a lot of leveling up of characters and gear. LOVE THE GRAPHICS and the SOUND!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: First off, if you are looking for a casual or easy game, then I recommend this game.The game mechanics start off as so limited that it's restrictive, but you gain more abilities and tricks as you progress the game and upgrade your gear or the town faculties. The battles aren't too hard, but there will definitely be moments were you trip up in a good way. And as long as you make sure to upgrade your gear and keep potions, you won't have to worry about getting a game over.The main story is pretty simple, but it's still nice and written well enough.I also recommend this game if you aren't really that interest in the Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes game like me. A game with over a hundred playable characters is too much for someone like me, so I won't be playing it when it comes out.But Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is a pretty decent game that can stand alone from the series without needing the knowledge of the Hundred Heroes. So if you don't care if Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is supposed to be the spin-off/prequel, then this game is alright with you.Now, the game does have some issues that I want the developers to keep in mind if they ever make another game like this.1. Side QuestsIt's good that the side quests aren't too hard to complete because of factors like the Trading Post and the accessories to boost item drops.The problem is that you have too many side quests that aren't fleshed off enough. Side Quests are stories that can just as good as the main story. You need to focus on making good quests over making many quests. Remove any unnecessary or boring quests, and focus on improving the more interesting quests.You even have opportunities to flesh the side quests out by using the side quests that you already have: the relationship between Avan and Priya, Bertrand's dream of knighthood and his past with killing someone's brother, the relationship between Rene and the songstress Jeanne (along with Jeanne's fan Olivier), Mellore's relationship with the townspeople and her insecurities of not being helpful enough, Iugo's past, the story behind the scamming Emerson, the weird relationship between the gamblers Keke and Bianca, the story of Asmee and her monster friend, Viti could have a running joke set of quests of her diary being stolen, the story of Ranbir's building up the town's defense, and survivor Bhuv's relationship with Isha's dad.Here's an example:-One series of quests could be about Avan and his feelings for Priya. The first quest is when Avan scared off Priya's cat, showing the two kids dislike for each other. The second quest is when Avan's mother asked you to fetch Avan in order to make him apologize to Priya for scaring Priya's cat, with mix success. The third quest is when Avan asked you to get a fish for Priya's cat as an apology, with CJ realizing Avan has a crush on Priya and then she teased Avan at the end of the quest. The fourth quest is when Avan desperately asks you for help because Priya had gone missing. You found out that Priya had gone to the forest entrance to pick some herbs because Avan's mother had gotten sick, but Priya hadn't returned. Avan found out about this before you, and chased after Priya into the forest. When you finally enter the forest, you found out that Priya got captured by the bandits. The bandits threatened the girl's life if you don't surrender all you belongings, but Avan arrives to tackle the bandits and drag Priya to safety. This allows you to safely attack and defeat the bandits. After the incident, you return the children to the town and scold both of them for going into the forest despite the danger. But Avan argues back by saying that he could never abandon Priya because he cares about her, earning Priya a blush. CJ then makes sure to properly explain that, whether it is helping out someone or saving them, they should be asking help from a grownup since they are too young and too weak to defend themselves or anyone else. But CJ added that she is impressed with how Avan saved Priya. So she told both children to stay out of trouble and to get stronger so they can protect who is most important to them.2. Named NPCsA major problem I have is remembering all the NPCs.One of the reason for this is because you added too many NPCs due to adding too many quests. So cutting down the number of unnecessary quests with one-time NPCs is a good idea.For example, if you remove all the unnecessary fishing/hunting/mining contest quests, you would be removing a lot of one-time NPCs.I also recommend having more quests that use the same NPCs instead of new NPCs (especially if that NPC is only going to appear once or twice). As long as you use these quests to flesh out the reoccurring NPCs, the quests will work.3. Town DevelopmentThe visible improvement of the town is limited to just the improvement of facilities and the increasing crowd. You could do more to improve it in small or big ways.For example, Ranbir is improving the town's defense. Completing his quests will improve things like turning wooden fences into stone walls, creating an armory for weapon storage, increasing the number of local guards, and changing his clothes into a suit of armor. Here are some minor examples too: You could help the stargazer Thara build a small shack for her stargazing. You could help the songstress Jeanne create a stage or form a band. You could assist Iugo in creating a headquarters for the guards. You could help Awamuri finally sober up, giving him a standing sober sprite. You could repair Kimaya's brooch and have her sprite visibly wearing it upon finishing her quest.4. HurstwineHurstwine, despite being an important character due to being the leader of the bandits and being a representative of the Imperials, only got a few screentime in the end of the game. Someone important like him should have been shown off more.Have the party overhear the bandits talk about Hurstwine. Have Hurstwine appear at the bandit camp that you discovered and have him talk to Garoo during that cutscene. Have Hurstwine be a reoccurring boss that the party clashes throughout the main story. Maybe even some quests where you fight him whenever the group clashes with the bandits. There were ways for Hurstwine to be more fleshed out instead of appearing at the last moment.These are the main critiques I have. I hope you understand where you got wrong and learn from them to make a better game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty... decent. I can't give it a glowing recommendation but it's not like the game's a bad experience. The game itself is pretty short, took me 14 hours in-game time and 15 and a half hours Steam time to hit the post-game while going out of my way to do every available side quest. The gameplay and strategy is pretty light, combat's easy, barely any equipment to manage, and progression is very linear. The story felt a bit weird at first, but it picks up a bit once you have the full party and the last few missions tie everything together pretty nicely. The one thing you have to watch out for are sidequests. There's a lot of them, and they can feel very grindy. The first part of the game is literally just doing sidequests until you get enough stamps and that turned me off from the game for a while. It gets a bit better once the game doesn't force you to do sidequests to progress, but they're all "Talk to this person, go to this marked location on a map, get a thing or beat something up, and come back." Sometimes you have to grind for resources in an area and those are even more tedious. That said, ignore sidequests at your peril. Sidequests build up the town facilities, get you resources you need to upgrade your gear, and your link attacks get better the more cards you fill out. You'll need every Link Attack boost you can get to beat some of these bosses.Overall, I think this game did well in what it set out to do. It's supposed to be a teaser for Hundred Heroes, and it succeeded in making me care about my party members and some of the supporting cast. By itself it's a pretty mindless/grindy beat-em-up RPG, but in the context of what's (hopefully) to come it's pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Great action adventure game with lots of little details.What stuck out to me was that you could actually see the town gradually grow from some rubble to a bustling village, and that there was not a single background-only NPC. Every NPC you see has some quest or interaction at some point. It not just some sprite running pass you, it's whats-his-name who is a master trapper, and has a son whom he regularly eats at the tavern with.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: A fun platformer (albeit with a bit of a grind) with good pacing and a story that is nice enough to add humor and give good explanations, with some good quality of life for maps and fast travel. It also has some town-building elements, but the pacing is nice as well. It's possible to get all achievements and 100% it in a single playthrough, and took about 33 hours give or take. It'll also lead into some kind of bonus when Eiyuden Chronicles: Hundred Heroes comes out, so if you're interested in that game, it's probably worth playing even if 'metroidvania-lite' style games aren't up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: A solid B+/A- type of game. Simple gameplay mechanics and not many segments felt like a drag. The writing was enjoyable and the characters are memorable enough to care about their motivations. Relatively short if you cut out all the side quests. But backtracking to re-grind the dungeons satisfied my pack-rat hoarder instincts, not to mention the pacing of the game is pretty solid from the story to the gameplay.Pick it up on sale and enjoy a couple weekends with the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed the game more than I thought.  It was addicting with a loop that made you want to do one more quest.  It had a layout map like a metroidvania style game but almost a single corridor with one offshoot room.  Nothing hidden or secrets to find.  The game was very easy, linear, and short.  This doesn't really sell it, I know, but it was relaxing to play and again had an addictive loop.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep it succinct:1. This game in a vacuum, I would not recommend people to play, unless it is your first RPG, or the characters seem interesting to you, or if you are quite young. It is just too shallow on its own.2. This game as the first entry into a series leading into Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes (launching in ~7 months after this review) is perfectly _fine_. 3. Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes in a vacuum looks to just be an objectively better (although slightly different) game, and one I am looking forward to playing.My overall recommendation:If this game looks interesting to you, wait for Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes to release and play that instead. If you end up loving Hundred Heroes and want a tiny bit more character development on some of the recurring characters, come back and play Rising.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was neutral review, but is this good or not:pros: if you like simple sidescrolling hack&slash rpg, this could scratch your itch nicely, from platforming perspective dungeons are nicely constructed neutral: but game has relatively low level of challenge in it, partly thanks to how rpg levelling oomphs you up to oneshotting slayer machine quite easily, still it can be quite fun and relaxing due that.negative: repeating dungeons 3rd, 4th maybe even 5th time due quests can get bit boringon price: if you enjoy relaxing rpg hack&slash where you can just slay away, full price is low enough to justify pricingif you just want this on prequel filled for hundred heroes, and like platformers but want challenge in them, maybe wait for sale to drop to 50% - 75%)
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game is a victim of expectations set by its title's reputation (and the reputation of its spiritual predecessor), as well as comparison to games with a similar pattern of gameplay. If you go in expecting the sprawling RPG epic that Hundred Heroes is promising to be, or the tight combat and challenge that a lot of side-scrolling action RPG/metroidvanias carry, you will be disappointed.That being said, I still found it an enjoyable way to spend time. It was a nice break from the more complex games I had been playing. It had fun characters, a good main story, a lot of side-quests and collectibles to keep the gameplay loop flowing. Most importantly, it left me wanting to know more about the setting, which is clearly its purpose in the larger picture of what Eiyuden Chronicles will be.Ultimately, while it wasn't the best game I ever played, it was worth the price of admission. Pick it up on sale and spend a weekend playing through it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: listen, i really enjoyed this game: the story isnt nothing special, the gameplay is simple but effective, but holy actual ♥♥♥♥, the sidequest design can actually eat its own ass. its just sidequests so its not massively impactive on the main experience, but it feels like your intended to complete most if not all of them: and i love passive grinding in RPG's, or running around doing sidequests for hours, but this is a whole new level... the sidequests have no good little plots or relevant ones to the main story, with i would say 50% of them being literally "billy bob want meal"(walk/warp to tavern, talk to lady, go back to bob) "k, thanks!" (upgrade to tavern now unlocked.)and the rest being "get 10 bear pelts for me".its genuinely MMO level quests and i skipped all the plots after the first 15. of like, 130 or so. and i read all the text in every JRPG i play. if this sidequest system due to its innate intertwine with the main quest actually lead to some story or alternate ending or something- i wouldnt know, because holy F, i finished the game and still had 50+ to go and said, nah bro, im good, ill save myself 10 hours.its sad because, some of the sidequests i skimmed though were kinda funny. but 50-75% of them should have been cut out of the game, because they are time-wasting bullshittery with no interesting action that lead nowhere other than an experience bubble, that i never needed in the first place. maybe relevant in the post-game hard mode where you can refight the bosses? but why the hell would i grind to beat bosses i have already beaten in a game i have already finished.if you buy this game, the story is good and combat is fun: ignore the sidequests unless, maybe, you need them for upgrades for your characters equipment. ignore everything else, and half the stores for that matter too- any shop that sells accessories or potions (unless you are really bad at the combat system) are a waste of money spent upgrading your damage/defense instead.

_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: For a preview/introduction for Eiyuden Chronicle as a whole, this game is solid enough to bring interest for Hundred Heroes. The story is barebones for the most part, but for the reason mentioned before, it's not necessarily a bad thing. For a metroidvania game, it's pretty decent with unique gameplay variety and a lot dungeon of exploration. Admittedly, some side quest can be boring, but you have to do them to get resources and level up properly because defeating enemies do not give exp nor money.Doing the post-game content in hard mode does extend the game quite lot thanks to the enormous list of side quest and unless you're doing a completionist run, you can skip at least 20% of them and focus on getting achievements instead. And as a side note, the game looks and sounds gorgeous. For the most part, it leaned towards a "chill" atmosphere more than anything. Though in bosses in does has its moments. Overall, a pretty decent game with noting much to write home about, to be frank, especially since it's mostly serves as an introduction to Hundred Heroes. If you're interested in that game and want to experience a taste of it, then go buy this game first. You can also transfer save data between the two, but I'm not sure of the details.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a solid 8.2 for me. Not too picky, not that easy. Overall it's nice.
