_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fantastic game a great story line, crisp and snappy controls that felt awesome in hand (played with a Xbox controller) and a grind that didn't really ever get boring (town improvements).  Can't wait for 100 heroes and I highly recommend this game if you like any of the latest side-scrolling epics that have come out in the last 5 years.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is a 2D sidescrolling beat-'em-up that's also a prelude to Eiyuden Chronicle Hundred Heroes (which will be a JRPG).It's a very easy game to get into, even for someone like me who doesn't play this genre much. The controls are easy to learn and it can be satisfying to chain attacks. It's not very deep, but it's more than serviceable.The larger gameplay loop also includes a series of quests that you need to accomplish to rebuild the town of New Nevaeh. These usually only involve either talking to townspeople or farming resources at the dungeon. It works okay but can quickly feels formulaic and repetitive. It might've been more interesting to include other types of quests, such as time challenge, damage threshold, figuring out the ingredients to a recipe, etc.The story is pretty short and not particularly memorable, but the characters are oozing with charm. CJ is a cheerful scavenger who's a tad quixotic; Garoo is the gruff voice-of-reason with a hidden tender side; and Isha is the rapacious but responsible acting mayor who's struggling with her past.It's a delectable if not too filling appetizer to the world of Eiyuden Chronicle.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game with a nice story. Gameplay is good, a bit on the very easy side. It's more of a casual, relaxing game, not something to challenge your skills. The quests can get a bit tedious and repetitive, but the fast travel system helps a lot. The fact that the progression is tied to how dedicated you are to help the people in town is nice. Overall, I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: this is by no means the most complex or challenging metroidvania i've ever played, but given it's a lead in to a new series and sold at a reasonable price for what you get it's a must try. my favorite part was watching your actions directly change the town the story was based in. the story was well written and the characters were enjoyable. Give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: The best way to describe Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is "solid".While the game's fun and all, and kept me engaged, it does not transcend into "very good" or "great.There's some interesting developments in the last couple of hours, fantastic localization, fun gameplay flow/combat, lots of character and charm, and even hits some emotional beats quite well, but it feels like an appetizer—a particularly good one, that makes you salivate for the main dish, but an appetizer nevertheless.Well worth the money and time, interested in what comes next and whatever else this team has done.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: it's not the deepest or most technically complex game, but sometimes you want to play something cute and simple. if you're seeking a challenge, look elsewhere, as the gameplay is fluff. narrative-wise, it bodes well for EC:HH's place as a spiritual successor to Suikoden; it has the same mix of silliness, light heroic fantasy, and the hint of a much larger, vastly more complex world that I loved in the Suikoden series. pre-release marketing discussed the game as something to hold fans over until EC:HH's release, and in that this game fails utterly. by giving us this hint of the world to come, it only made the wait harder.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little sidegame before the big JRPG blowout of Eiyuden Chronicles: Hundred Heroes. Most of the sidequests are your standard material delivery tasks and you can definitely tell that this game was made on a budget. That being said, the combat is simple while still being decently fun and the backgrounds of the various dungeons look great. Most importantly, the writing is solid enough to get you to care about the party and the various citizens of the town. If you want some worldbuilding before Hundred Heroes drops and you can get this on sale I'd say its definitely worth it, this game managed to get me excited for the main event.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an easy game that will probably take 10-12 hours of your time. That being said, the combat is engaging and mechanics are not very convoluted. _childDocuments_.review: There was some aspects of this game I enjoyed, but it was way too tedious for me to even finish it. I'm hoping they can fix some of these issues in the upcoming Eiyuden game because I still have a lot of hope for this game series.The good: 2d rpg combat is dope. The combat system of switching characters is a little janky but still pretty cool overall. The story as far as I got was pretty much get the village to trust you and the wizard girl's dad is missing, but the story was not the game's focus. I think it was more about the interaction between characters, which was done well overall. There was a good variety of characters and the dialogue was relatively witty and quite funny. The bad: This game turns everything fun into a CHORE!!! There's like 200 sidequests in the game and you have to the sidequests to progress the main story. This wouldn't be as much of a problem if the quests were actually fun, but 90% of the boil down to glorified fetch quests, "Go get me x of y yada yada..." It made the game a slog and kind of feels like it was used to pad out game length. If you like mindless collection games, then maybe this will be the best game you've ever played. Otherwise, this is a bundle of great ideas and characters slogged down by about 199 too many fetch quests. Wishing the developer luck on their next game.

_childDocuments_.review: easily has one of the worst stories of any game to be released after 2003imagine yourself playing a jrpg where you do laundry for townsfolk most of the time. that was the majority of my gameplay. i had dirty clothing in my hamper all day. i don't know why i spent so much time doing thisall in all, this game sucks. it's really poorly designed. but the combat is fun and it's cheap. and i have too much nostalgia for castlevania. so i give it a pass.

I have high hopes that the sequel game they're about to release will be an improvement on an already fun game and I can't wait for it to come out!

_childDocuments_.review: Support the devs if you are nostalgic for Suikoden!The game is fine. Not great, not horrible. Basic game play, basic story. Nice to chill out to, since it is pretty easy. _childDocuments_.review: After getting 100% completion I must say that this game is quite goodGraphics 9/10 - love the mixture of pixel art and 3d graphics, although I must say that it's kinda weird that some characters didn't got portraits, even though they got not a small role in the plot  and the characters movement were a bit meh (but at least from looking at the Hundred Heroes trailer, the next game already fixes that)Gameplay 5/10 - it was most of the times okey but nothing ground-breaking. After about 4 hours of playing the gameplay became a bit stale and repeatablePlot and characters 7/10 - Main story was pretty good but the main characters where a bit too bland for my taste and from time to time they didn't feel really consistent  and honestly, I somewhat really cared for side characters. Side-quests 8,5/10 - I love the fact how detailed the sub-stories were. The fact that I still remember some side-characters from them and what relationships they had with each others is already a really good plus for the game, but I also must say that there are just too much of side quests (about 190), where you don't really do much. Most of them are just "bring me x" or "talk to y", those kind of side-quests ain't bad but doing those thing almost 200 times is "a bit" much.So yeah, a pretty good 7/10 game, worth play a day or two

_childDocuments_.review: Works and looks great on Steam Deck!Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is a sidescrolling action RPG with beautiful 2.5D graphics, flashy battle animations/effects and a lot to do, such as exploring, crafting, quests. _childDocuments_.review: This is an underrated gem - it's more polished that a most games with much bigger teams and budgets. It has exactly the PS1 era Suikoden charm I was hoping for. _childDocuments_.review: Game is fine. 7/10. Doesn't do anything different then your typical beat em up rpg. Game is a bit clunky until you get your main character's 4 hit combo, made her feel way to slow in attacking which almost made me put it down altogether. In game time took about 21ish hours to 100 percent. Biggest demerit is that while watching videos and playing this game it kept crashing on me. Based on Steam play time it seems like I had to redo around 3 hrs on gameplay. Another downside is that there is no voice acting at all in the game which isnt necessarily needed but IS the reason I was watching youtube while playing which led to crashes. Lastly in-game music was fine except there was one part that made me keep thinking that my cat was meowing which was strange. _childDocuments_.review: With a short storyline, foreshadowed clues and story background, limited places, characters, and items, this game indeed serves as a prologue to the main game of the series, Hundred Heroes.As an action RPG, the action movement is considered fairly playable with the introduction of the unique Chain Link Attack. However, overall, the action gameplay is quite easy to play, perhaps too easy, and not very challenging or complicated.The game contains good character designs, and we can look forward to seeing hundreds more of them in the next game.The town rebuilding feature, magical rune mechanism, and item and upgrade availability are mediocre for a spiritual successor of the Suikoden series.Obviously, the English language used in the game is sesquipedalian. The developer's English translator overused synonyms in the townsfolk conversations, which ruined the natural flow of spoken language and resulted in bizarre dialogue. For your information, a good translator's work can be found in Suikoden V, where all language levels between royalty, nobility, commoners, and low-class folk are well utilised and differentiated.As one of the backers, I am looking forward to seeing the greater work in Hundred Heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: First off think everyone who plays will agree Shiva is a ♥♥♥♥.but after that honestly I really enjoyed the game from start to finish.controls are fairly tight and combat and movement was really good after a little bit at first to get used to using multiple characters at once for both combo combat and traversing certain places in the world.main story is fun and overall the side quests were a good variety of fetch quests and honestly never really felt like I had to go out of my way until the very end to just collect a couple materials i fell short on.if you do the side quests during the main story you will get both really useful items for progression and greatly speeds up your material collection as its always on the way to a quest

Combat starts way too simple but gets better over time,although still very repetitive. There are some cool boss battles, but they are buried under 160 stupid fetch quests that are unrewarding and boring. And you will have to do them if you want money to upgrade your gear. _childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those games that I can recommend to casual or people who never played games before. The game has a very appealing visual presentation. HD 2.5D looks really good. Combat and doing link attack feels satisfying. Story is nothing ground breaking but the characters are charismatic enough, The story also became interesting at the later half to set up for the following sequel. Even though quest are tedious, but the writing made it interesting enough to make you care about the side characters that made the town alive.One personal detail I love about this game is the progression of the town building and such. The more you do quests, the livelier the town become with many people walking all over compared to when you started the game. Also, the more you explore the dungeon, the more people will appear and also explore the dungeon in the background. It truly makes you feel that it's alive and you're not adventuring alone.The game is overral fun, had that JRPG feeling, But all of the game mechanic aren't complex and perhaps too simple (i.e. fishing), The quest cycle maybe tedious and endgame rather repetitive and grindy. Also, for a metroidvania, levels are simple and in some case linear, which is why I recommend it to casuals and people who don't play video games.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I'll recommend with a warning, there is a repetitive feeling that comes too early in the game. It's fun , its cute, its beautiful. But game world is too small and quest are kinda boring. Youll get back over and over to the same town, grab quest, fetch the materials needed for said quest not too far away in the same areas again and again, bring em back, rinse /repeat. Also some 'texts' are too childish even for 'general audience', and made me goes blehhhh even if im used to childish Jrpgs stories. But I gotta say that I love the art, their take on 2.5D style is really great. Controls/fighting are perfect and im usually quite the whiner when it comes to platform games. I cant wait for hundred heroes, and Im still hyped even though I hope itll be better written than this 'prequel'.

_childDocuments_.review: Couldn't get myself to push past the first 20 mins.   Spent more time using the skip button on cut screens than playing the game.   The dialogue was way to drawn out to continue reading it.    The final straw was after 15 mins with mostly skipped content.  I spent 30 seconds fighting and found my quest. _childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I do like the game, but not enough to recommend it to others. Here's my breakdown:Pros   The art style is very nice   The music is nice   The town-building is enjoyable and satisfying   Characters. There is a wide array of characters to interact with that all feel unique and help flesh out the world.Cons   Combat is lackluster and clunky. Most of the combat is just mashing the attack button. The block mechanic I found very difficult to time. This is my biggest con. I found myself not enjoying combat due to either being way to easy or frustrating beyond belief. I never had a middle ground.   While the game is a city-builder, you dont (at least until the point I have played so far) get to pick which buildings you build or where they go. It's a very linear progression with little choice from you as the player.   Keybinds. I know this is a small thing cause you can just change them but the default keybinds are weird. And it made things that should be simple like the fishing mini-game extremely difficult because it uses keys you dont often know off the top of your head.   Story. I mean, it's there. It's just not that memorable.Overall I am liking the game and plan to play it all the way through, but I wouldn't recommend this to most of my friends unless they were very specifically wanting to play it for the chill vibes and aesthetic and not the combat or other mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Art style is wonderful, gameplay is simple to grasp and characters have... character. If you have a steam deck, it's perfect for a handheld session.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, this is an interesting thing. It's very grindy and you keep doing tons of fetchquests, with only a few distinct areas, yet it never felt that bad all. The quests are short enough, even if they have you fetch rare meterials, there's a good fast travel system -- unfortunately, they don't always tell you where to find things, so keep Google on shortdial.The game is easy enough, which is something I like. Only the first boss was a minor problem; following that, I was probably overlevelled far enough to trivialize them. Almost the same applied to hard mode (whch unlocks after completing the game), except that I didn't even get to the final boss in that mode (well, might have if I had used potions, but seeing the amount of damage I took from the first enemy...)Still, there are two control schemes named "normal" and "simple". Both are... annoying. In "normal" you have to pull off precise timing to trigger some special combo thing; in "simplified" it happens automatically, but characters keep switching and teleporting around like crazy as well which creates a lot of confusion during larger battles. Or it can be annoying when you switch to the ranged char because you want to clear out some enemies blocking a pit that you want to jump over, but then the character switches and teleports over the pit, falling down...Still, seeing these combo links trigger quite a lot, I left it on "simple" anyway. There are no bottomless pits anyway, you just have to walk a bit and try again.The characters and story aren't half bad, although there isn't much of that. As I said, there's a lot of fetchquests, which are used to develop the town. While their marketing likes to stress that this is a prequel to some other game, which I haven't played, it can certainly stand on its own. Yes, a mysterious "empire" makes an appearance eventually, but their role is obvious enough so I don't need to know any intricate details about them.I didn't use most of the town facilities, though -- Í only actually used the blacksmith/weapon/armor shops, the tool shop, and the rune lense shop -- but I did them all anyway. So, it was an alternation between progressing the story, and doing the fetchquests for the town, which generally appaar in large batches as the story progresses. For me, it worked out wwell enough. I even spent some extra time to upgrade my kit to max, even if meant fetching some more materials and money.The game looks great, I really liked some of the background tracks (my favorite is probably the Runebarrows one)... but, there's 0 voice acting.There is one annoying detail when going through the world, though -- you have be "careful" to not leave item drops behind. Most of the time you'll just pick them up automatically during the battle, but it can happen that you're too far away for that to happen... there's really no good reason for this design choice, and it prevents you from just running through an area full-speed that you've already seen countless times anyway.

_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: A thrilling tale about an overworked carpenter rebuilding an entire town on his own.Jokes aside, since I managed to get to the end I qill tentatively give it a thumbs up instead of down. I'd prefer a sideways. Combat starts off being incredibly dull with combos being locked behind progression. The 1-2 hits allowed at the outset eventually evolve into a combat system that's reasonably fun to execute. The plot and story is generic and forgettable, as are the characters, though not particularly bad in and of itself.There is what I would describe as an unwelcome level of backtracking and grind in this game and it just so happened that I was in a mood that could tolerate it. I have dropped better titles (Hollow Knight) for less in the past. In any case, I enjoyed my time with Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising but am content to not pursue post-game content nor ever revisit the game in the future. Having said that, I wouldn't be averse to a sequel if improvements are made.Pros:+ Eventually decent combat.+ Looks pretty.+ Some of the jokes are funny.Cons:- Lots of backtracking and grind.- Targeting issues with ranged class.- Largely forgettable plot and cast.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: What we've got here is a coming of age / rite of passage adventure about a young girl out on a treasure hunt. She has no choice but to accept the task of filling out a town's 'stamp card' by completing good deeds in order to get a license granting her access to areas with the treasures she seeks. Through her good deeds she invertedly helps rebuild the town in the process and makes new friends.While the main story is decent, the game as a whole starts off slowly and tediously. This sets the precedent for all side-quests being filler in how they pad out the game with banal tasks - everything from finding a cat and collecting laundry to gathering wood and stone. It does become a chore and I wish it'd feel less vanilla than it does, because side-quests are the game's greatest weakness, yet you spend most of your time doing them.What makes these especially tiresome is that the game doesn't like to move you as part of the story or quest to progress it. You always have to leg it back to where you're asking someone to go, even letting someone know that the person they are looking for is on their way back to them... this creates unnecessary double backing. Allowing the player to use dungeon movement abilities (Dash, etc.) in town to break up the monotony would be a nice feature.Despite being side-quests, certain shops require theirs to be completed else you won't get access to higher level gear.This is how abilities are handled, not found nor gained by defeating bosses, they are instead granted from upgrading weapons and armour.Combat, especially once you get a full party (and play in "normal" control mode) is pretty fun. Each button corresponds to a different character attacking, so you get some flashy striker-like abilities calling in various party members to string together powerful combo attacks.What about the characters? CJ personifies every side-quest completing player that does it purely for the gratification of a clear quest log (stamp card), hilarious even if annoying.Garoo is hands down an awesomely written character, great backstory, values and attitude, the fact he's a roo with a big ass sword just makes him that much better. Him saying "Why are you doing this for stamps?!" got me good.Visually it looks great. Where Octopath Traveller focused more on HD-2D inspired by the SNES era, Eiyuden kicks it up a notch with even more detailed 2D sprites akin to the PSX era JRPGs and vibrant 3D backgrounds. Combined it looks amazing.Audio wise, your traditional typical JRPG music is here. Not so memorable unfortunately, albeit catchy, mostly, with background homely tunes on repeat.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I hesitated on buying this because I'm looking forward to the "main" Eiyuden Chronicle game, and I didn't want to risk what is obviously a low-budget tie-in coloring my perception of it... and I should have continued hesitating, because even at $3 I can't really recommend this.  I'm 3 hours in and don't think I can be bothered to keep playing it.The best part of the game is undoubtedly the graphics.  The backgrounds look nice and have a lot of detail, and there's never any confusion about what's in the background and what's in the foreground, which is often a problem for 2D games that use 3D backgrounds.  The art is nice and the sprites look good, although the animation for the sprites is a bit stiff.  The user interface is nice and clean; it does a good job of presenting important information but also suiting the style of the game.That's about where my praise ends.  The writing is juvenile to the point of making me worried about what Eiyuden Chronicle is going to be like.  It reads like it was written by a teenager who has no idea how personal interactions or societies in general work; all of the dialogue is vapid and is constantly trying to be clever but isn't.  The characters are shallow and there's no real hook to the story.  Maybe this is just filler content because they didn't want to spoil anything for the main game.Combat feels stiff and slow.  Your character doesn't feel particularly responsive and doesn't have a lot of movement options.  That might be fine if this was a game that had challenging combat that required deliberate planning and movement, but it's too easy for that; you can just button mash your way through fights and you'll be fine.  It seems like you gradually unlock more movement options later in the game, and maybe those make it better, but the game shouldn't just be outright stiff for several hours right at the beginning.The game is also very, very hand-holdy.  It always tells you explicitly what you should do next, and what you should do is usually just a few screens to the right, after which you have to walk a few screens back to the left and talk to an NPC again.  Exploration is minimal and there's nothing interesting to discover.  It feels like this was designed to be somebody's first 2D platformer, but it lacks the interesting level design or enemies of even early Mario or Mega Man games.At this point I'm going to just put the game down, walk away, and hope that this isn't indicative of what's coming in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: An small snack to tide us over for Not-Suikoden-But-The-Only-Suikoden this year, Rising is what it is: a window onto this new world's storylines, an introduction to some of the characters, and a self-contained plot, via people not working on Rising.Its got Suikoden but in a slow lane feel; I wont deny it feels like part of both it and Trails where the Venn diagram overlaps in that regard, and is snappy. _childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest this review is very subjective due to my love to the dev team that also made Suikoden I and II, the game that made my childhood so memorable. Now after completing the game 2 times and get 100% achievements, this is my review:I always like this kind of game, adventure RPG or JRPG with pixelate graph that make you feel like the 100% complete achievement is in your grasp. Because most or should i say all of pixel game will give you true hint for a hidden items, shortcut, and secret area that are somehow hidden but also obvious enough to be seen. So it gives less stress for perfectionist player like me who want to explore and find every item in the game, HAHA.Other than that, i love the gameplay and the combat system. The link system is just interesting, and i see a lot of references in this game, for example every quest was designed with mini stories to make it less boring for it is a little bit repetitive, just like the witcher series.The graph is side-view with only 2D direction, but they brilliantly made it more complex by adding top and down map so in terms of control its still 4 direction movement with left-right-top-down.The fishing mini game is fun, the accessories in this game was made to help in a SIGNIFICANT ways. Unlike other RPG that we usually see where accessories is kind a *duh*, or just simply for special effect for your attack.The stories have a very strong background and this whole game are just a glimpse for their next true Suikoden Successor Eiyuden Chronicles 100 heroes. There are some key characters that appeared as cameo other than the main character, and this game seems want to gives you a grasp of the basic concept of managing you castle in Suikoden version.Worth the price because the graph for pixel art is very stunning. The scoring are not so memorable, i hope the 100 heroes can have a better backsound music, but overall the game is a kill!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, really fun game. There’s something about how certain games start off with simple combat mechanics that steadily builds upon itself as you progress that’s really addicting  to me. The story is okay I guess, but there’s not much you can expect from a game that was practically made to be a prologue, not even a prequel, to the real big project, which is Eiyuden 100 Heroes. Now, of course there’s one MAJOR aspect to consider that is undoubtedly either a hit-or-miss with players, and that is the amount of fetch quests you will have to do throughout the game. It starts to get really crazy towards the end of the game, and thankfully I beat the game before it got too bad for me to handle. Lots of backtracking and “talk to [X] NPC]” side quests. However, the game does have ways to give the player a sense of constant linear progression by completing the quests, even if the rewards are crap. Often times the quests aren’t very clear on where you actually need to go to complete them.However, despite the glaring flaws, I did end up really enjoying the game. It’s charming in its simplicity.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good action-RPG for what it costs.  The character swapping setup allows for a lot of neat variety in combat - like softening up an enemy with CJ to finish them off with one meaty swipe of Garoo's sword, or sniping an enemy with magic to let a melee character combo teleport past their defenses.  The game makes you intimately familiar with the little town that you're fighting for, and gives an interesting glimpse into a wider world that will hopefully be expanded upon in Hundred Heroes.  Every quest you complete unlocks new items or upgrades or combat skills, so there's a steady sense of progression and improvement that you can really feel.My biggest complaint is that the game re-uses and abuses it's handful of locations over and over again for the dozens of sidequests.  If you're a completionist, expect to run through each dungeon dozens of times to grind materials for crafting or pick up every NPC's lost macguffin.  The story is likewise padded for time by making excuses why the party needs to go back and find a new key for the latest door, which usually just drops in their lap later when the plot is ready to go forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: +++ Fun, unique combat mechanics.+++ Crisp and clear graphics.+++ Good character pacing and progression.--- Large portion of busy-work sidequests.--- Egregious enemy palette swapping.This budget-priced title can keep one occupied for roughly 30 hours of casual, not-too-difficult gameplay.  The shining star is definitely the character hot-swap mechanic to perform combo attacks.  But otherwise?  A whole lot of expository groundwork is laid out and then nothing is done with it.  While it's a recommendable title for its accessible core mechanics, it's one that'll mostly stand as an easy way to kill time between two more major titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Great artwork, story and setting had a definite charm. The core gameplay was super easy for me, a veteran platformer gamer, a minor disappointment. A bunch of the side quest were fetch quests, running around the town talking to people. A good fetch quest at least puts some sort of challenge between you and beating it but so many quests were literally just running around a town talking to people, often with fairly mundane stories attached to them, like go fetch me a sandwich, which would be forgivable if they added some sort of gameplay challenge, but i just spent 30 minutes straight running around town talking to people. It's a 15 hour game where at least 3 hours will be spent just doing this.Overall I did enjoy it, but I wouldn't call this a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an new take on the old style of JRPG (like Suikoden) it's also a prelude to Eiyuden Chronicles: Hundred Heroes that will be releasing next year (as of the time of this review) but back to this game you help build up a village that has been suffering from suspicious circumstances ever sense the acting mayor reopened the mines for adventures far and wide to explore, you play as three different characters each with unique fighting style of their own no character feels the same even secondary characters have their own uniqueness the story is interesting every turn feels like something new and unexpected is waiting for you to discover.The graphics take on the two point five art style the world really does feel alive around you and the developers clearly know what they are doing the many different areas come alive with the NPC's or monsters while the different colors can be vibrant and lively or dark and dim to fit the mood of where the player is at. _childDocuments_.review: 10 hours in and though I would give my impressions, Great graphics, especially the backgrounds. good characterizations with me breaking out into smiles multiple times as they intereacted with each other and the NPCs. I was worried there would be lots of grinding but so far I have not felt like i am just going through levels to get the one item. The one issue I would bring up is that the combat is slightly clunky as it is difficult to switch between targets during a combat chain but all in all if this is what is basically a side project for the main game is like I cannot wait for the 100 heroes to come outall in all i give this game an 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neat game with a nice story.  I really like how the crafting and upgrades work.  I do not like how much grindy farming is required between side quests and material gathering for said upgrades.  However, the action battle elements worked really well and I enjoyed how elemental stats matter (using runes to change weaknesses, attacks, etc).Worth it on sale, or if you one day find yourself invested in the next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10? (average/good)Its a good game mostly what you would expect.The Wow: Combat feels good. Plenty of varied enemies. nice character designs. Great art design in general.The ugh:Too much back tracking while traversing the dungeons. Especially those long dead ends.    -Make use of CJ "dash" "jump" "dash" to get around faster.Most of the quests are grind for x on repeat.why does every game need an annoying fishing mechanic?
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Playtime: 18H (3 Hour Postgame)Synopsis:A side story from main game, set in the town of New Nevaeh, a remote region of where the main game will be set. It is a poor rural town that mines ore. A few months before the start of the game, there was an earthquake, which lead to the discovery of some ruins nearby. It became lively, and many people who wanted to get rich appeared.CJ,  a young girl from a family who generation after generation has made their living as scavengers (ruin hunters). She came to the town to fulfill the "Coming of Age Ceremony" that has been passed down in her family.Plus:+A decent Metoridvania game +Sneakpeek some character that will be appear in maingame+Tight Control+Town vibe change by completing sidequest+Short and Compact sidegame+You can name the weapons of main party and "specialty item" that can be transferred(?) to the main game Min:-80% Sidequest is fetch quest-Post game is kinda grindfest, especially item requirement for max upgrade-Some accessories is useless-Hard Difficulty just makin enemy harder to hit and damage increasedMixed:=Postgame=Elemental Lenses only give some minor buff =You can brute forces the Boss in hard difficulty because all of them have same pattern, only damage increased..Very short and compact side game..i hope the quality is much better in main game..
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Story:Many foreshadowing for the upcoming Eiyuden Hundred Heroes and there are reference to places or characters that didn't get explained ever. In this game, your main task is to collecting stamps (read: building the town) by helping townspeople with generic kill or fetch quest while also uncovering the mystery in it.Gameplay:2D platformer with simple button, only button mash to combo your way to victory. While in town there is base building feature to improve combat stats or buying item. Up to 3 playable characters can be controlled with unique move set and unlocked by progressing the story.Probably recommended if you are also planning to play the main game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: The critiques of the game you see are valid. Almost every side quest given by townsfolk are just fetch quests, and the difficulty of the game is very low until post-game (and even with the "hard" difficulty on, fights are still quite easy).But, if you can get past that, Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising has some good writing and the fighting mechanics are actually pretty good. While we all wait for Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes to be released, this was a great little way to get introduced to some of the world. With doing every side quest along the way, I beat the main story in about 19 hours, then got 100% achievements with a couple more hours put in. If you skip side quests, you could finish even quicker (though you won't unlock long combos). So maybe add this one to your wishlist and get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I played this entire game through on the Steam Deck (more on that at the end), and while I know this sort of game is not for everyone, the idea of a dungeon grind town building (kinda) game, is pretty up my alley. Graphics where nice, story was shallow but fine, didn’t hate the characters. No voice acting what so ever which is a bit odd in a modern game. Kinda felt like a mobile game to be honest (and I played it as such). The music was hit and miss, some songs where pretty nice, but ALL of the songs are too short and loop too often, so with the lack of voice acting, I found myself quickly muting the game often, as some of the songs get quite old.Gameplay was not bad, controls felt mostly good, although only when you start unlocking movement upgrades. That first hour sucks. Combat makes up most of the actual meat of the game, and once you unlock Link attacks it feels pretty good. There are some moments that feel like BS and like the dev intentionally designed an enemy to piss you off by having just enough reach to hit you (Thunder/Frost jellies), and any of the fights against two wolves (which there are several…) tend to get frustrating as they can stun lock you (preventing you from switching characters). Those gripes aside however, combat feels fast and fluid, but never too difficult.The ”town building” is mostly about upgrade, and you have no real say or control over how things get upgraded. I do wish there was more visual distinct upgrades for the buildings as you played, so it really felt like the town grew. A note about the ending (Then some Steam Deck stuff the spoilers):As mentioned, I played the entire game on Steam Deck, game ran great, had no issues with controls, though I did find the text/font a touch small for my liking. To get a bit of extra battery life, I lowered the refresh rate to 45Hz, and the framerate cap to match (45 FPS). I also enabled Half Rate Shading, which had no impact on the visuals for this game (but also only saved like .3w of power), and I enabled TDP Limit, and found 8-9W was the sweet spot where I did not see any dips below 45 FPS, while getting 3.5-4.5 Hours of battery life.Great game on Deck!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: very worth it for the price. it's side scrolling with some beautiful scenery, not too beautiful like eg: ori, but really nice. the combat is simple action with some combos, you also get abilities like dash, block, etc, that adds to the mechanic. story is nothing great, more slice of life than adventure maybe, they are quite engaging tho sometimes the dialog can be.. uh,.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: A short Game which takes you about 15 - 20 Hours for 100 % the Main Story itself could be completed in 8 - 10 Hours. While I'm waiting it was nice to already learn something about the World we are going to explorer in Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes. Seeing the release Trailer that droped some days Ago I already interacted with some of the possible Heroes you can recruit and I'm hyped to see where their journeys are going to go.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this if you plan on picking up "Hundred Heroes"It's a great introduction to the world, some of it's characters, and an idea of whats to come in the main game.Gameplay wise: I found myself loving the side scrolling action. It scratched a nostalgia itch i didn't know i had. However, even as a casual player, this is super easy/casual. Like, i didn't use a health potion until the final boss, on hard. I'm at around 29 hours, and 100% the game. That doesn't really ever happen to me ha Most will probably get that done sooner as you can fast travel to any section of the town at will (excluding dungeons) and i didnt mind manually running around most of the time.Side quests do tend to be repetitive fetch quests, and A LOT of back and fourth. I do appreciate that completing them  (not sure if REALLY a spoiler, it's minor. buuuut just in case) and not just "extra lore, xp, and items" This is where the fast travel at will within the town is nice. The music isn't bad. There's a few that are catchy and stand out, others are a bit generic. I did like how Personally, for $15, i really enjoyed this. Looking forward to the main game!For those who played, what did you name your weapons?Mine are:1- Storm Axe2- Dragon Slayer (sorry, i just had to)3- Astra Galaxy
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 sprite workfighting platforming and puzzles are average, nothing special or too difficultthe 3D environment can be a bit jarring alongside the more traditional jrpg sprite art but it does have its own charm and i was able to get used to it.Many of the characters have very memorable scenes and personalities though some of them could use a bit more. overall though they do a pretty decent job of expressing the characters if you are willing to read. though some characters personalities do shine through on their sprite work. devs could try to find more varied ways to express characters personalities. This game seems to be kinda like a very light metroidvania over a more traditional rpg. but the quest system runs more like running errand like side quests in a traditional rpg than a more natural metroidvania exploration system. the quests can get a bit old and samey.overall the game is alright nothing to write home about. neat little side project. but the devs working on the main game do seem to be taking feedback into account and that game looks to be a different style so i look forward to what this upcoming franchise has to offer in the future, especially if it can scratch that itch that the series it is trying to be a spiritual successor to itched so long ago.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like side quests? Do you like getting stamps for side quest completion on your town loyalty card? Do you like trading in ten stamps for crafting materials that you can use to complete more side quests? Do you like one of your party members complaining that the main character will run off to do any crazy side quest for just a stamp? Then this is the game for you!In all seriousness, though, this game got it right. You get to watch the town grow as you help its increasingly quirky cast of residents, and the quest dialog is a delight. There's a notice board that will tell you were to collect any quests you don't already have, a quest log you can pull up at any time to check the quests you do have, and location-specific quest objectives will be marked on the map for your active quest. You can fast-travel between any two rooms outside of dungeons and there are ample fast-travel points within dungeons.100% completion took me about 27 hours and should give me some sort of bonus in Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes when that comes out. It's a good, fun introduction to the world and its conflicts, but it's worth the price even if you're not planning on playing Hundred Heroes.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game for a fair price. The combat is fun and there is room for creativity and building. Nice exploration. The quests are more like fetch something inside some map. The characters are really fun, well developed and the history is also good. I don't think there is too much appealing for replay, unless you want all achivs.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: enjoying this cute little title despite its handholding at the start and a stop and go structure, there's always some plot reason to pull you back to town. _childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every second I played of this game! <3 I wanted to wait for my review after I completed the story and I can definitely say that this is my Game of the Year! ^^ The story is such a nice story, it's exactly like the anime stories that I grew up with and it's the type of story from Dragon Quest that made me fall in love with the series <3. It doesn't do anything particular special or different but it's just a lovely story to play through. Perfect for adults and children, especially since the main characters(aside from Garoo) are teenagers. The combat is not difficult, I was apprehensive about how much I would enjoy this at first because I am not good with action based combat. However the combat is very simple and easy to use ^^. You have the three characters on X, Y and B, Jump on A, dodge/parry/teleport on RT. Super simple and easy. I recommend this game to everyone who loves anime storytelling. It is a *very* anime story, but that is why it's so charming ^^. I love all the characters just like how I do with Dragon Quest games, the writers are fantastic just like Yujii Hori. I was most excited for Eiyuden Chronicle Hundred Heroes, and after completing this now I don't think I could be even more excited XD! Ah Hundred Heroes can't come out fast enough! <3

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in anticipation for 100 heroes.I have played 100's of games over the years and have enjoyed the vast majority of them.This game however literally made me fall asleep on 2 occasions! Constant fetch quests going back and forth to the same areas constantly.Save your money and time for the main game.The art style and graphics are ok but i can't pick anymore positives.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I am a supporter of the Kickstarter project, and from my experience so far, I am sorry to leave a not so positive review at least for the moment.I am an old fan of the Genso Suikoden franchise, probably my all time favorite, so when crowdfunding was announced, I didn't think twice about supporting it. Unfortunately, the distribution and communication management in particular was not respected and does not bode well. Above all things, I was able to play Rising with a reasonable delay, while the non-backers started and completed it even before I received my backer code. I'm afraid for what will happen with the main title given this messy confusion, but I guess we'll see.Anyway, Rising is a nice prequel to introduce us to the world that we will hopefully get to know completely next year. The graphic/art style and colors are very beautiful, as the environment, the animations for combat and such maybe a little less, but can be improved for Hundred Heroes in any case, like the rather light dialogues and weak characters development. However, do not expect a classic JRPG here, a mistake made by many between Rising and HH, since this is instead a not so long companion game, kinda action RPG, town building and with lots, A TON of fetch quests, and with that, very repetitive.Honestly, I paid for my copy at backer price, so half of the public one, and if you can wait for a discount, just do it. Last but not least, I played it on Steam Deck and runs perfectly.The general premises are good, is not a bad game itself, but it can be better for sure, I want to trust the team, and I expect a more professional management too. With much respect for Murayama & Co., can't wait to see more of it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, story line was great. It was immersive enough for me to continue wanting to clear the achievements after clearing the normal mode and heading into the hard mode. Though the hard mode was kind of tough if I did not managed to enhance the equipments to an ok state. Overall, I would recommend this game to people who loves JRPG and I cant wait for the next release of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: EC/R is a great RPG in 2.5d format. It which follows the story of a young agile adventurer as she shares exploration and combat with a tank and a mage. Fighting is real-time, one at a time, with a sort of tag-in capability so characters can follow-up to each other's attacks.  What stands out from it being a simple level crawl is a spirit of delight and wonder. Two virtues that can often be sacrificed for difficulty.  As you discover and grow the town where you reside slowly grows as well. Rather than erupting quick jump points. Thankfully, the plot manages to sidestep RPG tropes in lieu of novel ones. Granted there can be back tracking as well as re-spawning monsters, but it doesn't tire the game play.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is... mediocre. A simple thumbs up and thumbs down feels too binary. When I'm actually playing the action part of the game, I enjoy it, but it feels like I'm interrupted every few minutes for conversation, and getting my rewards requires running in circles through the town.  Seeing the town grow and upgrade as you progress is very cool, but you need to gather materials, upgrade buildings, gather more materials to craft gear, and also have enough money on hand, and all the while every character's asking you things and telling you about their personal life, and the writing's just not interesting enough to justify all the talking to everyone.  A few of them are interesting, but a lot of them are just "I'm cooler than you because I can catch the biggest fish. Prove me wrong by catching a bigger fish," and even the main quest frequently stops for you to collect lumber and mine stone.And the thing is, I like collecting lumber and mining stone. That's actually the fun part of the game: running through dungeons, murdering everything, and gathering materials. But then I need to talk to like six people about nothing before I can finally turn that lumber and stone into anything useful.What this game really needed was longer dungeons, less dialogue for sidequests (there's a bulletin board, but you can't take quests from it, it just tells you where to find the person to talk to), and for the primary gear upgrade to have come from quest completion rather than having to complete the quest to upgrade the shop and then buy the gear after.If you get this game, I strongly advise you use the Skip feature to ignore any conversation that isn't the main quest.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I hear there was a kerfuffle with the release of this game but having played through it I have faith the main game will deliver when it comes out. Was a fan of the music, combat, dialogue, and the town and world building (having played the Suikoden games before these last two really scratch that itch). It also reminds me of the Ys series if that has any value, mainly because of the characters and action/exploration aspects. The only downside I think worth mentioning is that the optional quests would be virtually unplayable if not for the fast travel (they'd really test your patience), but there's some fun to be had from optimising quest routes. Overall, definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: So after 100% the game I'm left with a solid feeling on this game but I want more from the world in general. I picked this up due to its connection to the coming Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes and I'm pleasantly surprised.I usually do a big breakdown but the game is fairly short and simple with an enjoyable achievement hunt. Overall its a good game but it isn't groundbreaking either. If you're looking for the next Castlevania or Hollow Knight, this isn't it chief.While enjoyable it does have it's issues, controls can be a little slow or unresponsive, the overall size of the world is small meaning you backtrack a lot, movement speed in town feels tedious after running around constantly, the enemies are 'varied' in the most generic sense (meaning each area has a copy of each creature just of a different element, not to mention most of the quests are just your typical fetch quests.But for $15 it's a really solid game and quite fun. Not to mention it's got 50 achievements that aren't too hard to accomplish, meaning you achievement hunters could get a new ribbon in a little under 30-35 hours.Can't way for Hundred Heroes!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: If Eiyuden Chronicle was already on your radar, this is a no-brainer. Excellent characterization for a half dozen characters who are, by all indications, completely ancillary to the core plotline of the main game (releasing next year, with benefits for transferring clear data from this game into it).If it wasn't, this game is still worth your time if you want a well-written story with a surprising depth of character development for a side scrolling action game. The combat is initially underwhelming, but you are introduced early on to the mechanisms for unlocking greater complexity, and I feel the gating intervals for said complexity increases are only a hair too long to be considered ideal. (For reference, Death Stranding is my gold standard for mechanical progression curves)Building out the town is satisfying and only mildly grindy, with solid rewards for each stage of development. I enjoy gathering materials for character upgrades as a concept, and this game is extremely willing to meet me where I live on that score; every item that drops from enemies or gathering nodes is used to either unlock or purchase gear upgrades (which are split between straight stat increases and mechanical enhancements) or unlock new meals at the tavern, which can then be purchased for money, and which provide a small but permanent boost to various stats. Overall a deeply charming game, and far more than the simple cash-in on a highly anticipated title that I worried it might turn out to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: A very lovely game that's easy to get into and fun to collect all the little easter eggs.There's just enough hints at the inspiration for this series to satiate this old fan. Beyond the main plot you'll find the many, many, NPC's that you come to get to know and run errands for end up expanding both the lore and the world (and your stats). Plus, if you like Metroidvania type games, this one is a good addition to that genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and well fleshed out for a mobile game port! Story is pretty decent, dialogue is fantastic, combat starts out quite slow but picks up as you level up. Took me about 20-ish hours to get all the achievements. I got this game for free for backing the kickstarter for the main game, Eiyuden Chronicles: Hundred Heroes. I'm very excited and have high hopes for Hundred Heroes when it eventually releases!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Just for the sake of transparency, I supported the kickstarter for Eiyuden Chronicles and got this game for half price. Having said that, I still believe this game is very fun for a certain type of person. If you enjoy collecting a bunch of resources for various side Quests using semi-clunky combat controls, then this is the game for you. Plain and simple. The graphics are beautiful and the sound is decent, but if you don't enjoy non-button mashing combat (making it a little slow at the beginning of the game until you get better upgrades) to collect resources, then you won't like this game. If you do, you will.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: It's not gonna blow you away but it does have enough of the classic Suikoden charm to be worth the price tag and playtime. Still holding my breath on hundred heroes but this helps take the edge off that anticipation. I griped and first but it grows one you fast and doesn't overstay it's welcome. Do I recommend it? Yuss!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is a magical little town building metroidvania with heavy JRPG influences.If you're a fan of games where you build up a town or settling from nothing, this game will resonate with you.  I found the graphics very aesthetically pleasing, the music incredibly satisfying and relaxing, and the character design to at least be on par with the quality I would have expected from the original few Suikoden games (which Eiyuden Chronicle draws heavily upon for inspiration).Add all of these great qualities to the low asking price, and this is an easy recommend.The only downsides I can think of is that the game is very easy, and can be overly simple until you recruit your teammates.  In addition, you will be doing a lot of fetch quests to complete optional content.Other than that, really no complaints.  Excellent game.  Buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Let me first say this, I do plan on playing Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes and I have been a huge Suikoden fan.If you are a fan of that series and feel apprehension towards whether or not it will feel the same, I think this game will assuage your doubts. Character wise, it feels similar to the way the Suikoden characters were written in the past. The world and implied politics also feel as if they haven't skipped a beat since Suikoden 3.Gameplay is fairly simplistic. It is a fairly standard 2D action adventure game with not a lot of variance. It took me around 17 hours to get full achievements for the game and was a fairly easy game for someone who doesn't usually play this kind of game. It's also very easy to break the game by just raising CJ's crit as crits interrupt most enemy attacks and animations. The three characters do play differently but also are each only one attack (plus a charge attack) assigned to a single button each.The music for the game is good, nothing groundbreaking, but well made and atmospheric for the locations.Overall, it's a fine game that I would definitely recommend for two possible reasons. Either you want the story and to have the prelude to Hundred Heroes, or you are an achievement hunter. I think everything is solid for the game at the price and worth if if you have the interest for Hundred Heroes.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: If you're excited for Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes, I think this is a decent little appetizer for the real thing. There's a lot of jank--the animations could use some work, the quests are mostly fetch quests, there are no difficulty options, things take much longer than they need to--but at the same time, I lost myself doing the fetch quests and upgrading the town. It kind of gave me the gameplay loop I wanted.My biggest criticism is that the game suffers from Tiny Text, as in, all the text is hard to read. I'm not sure what settings they playtested under, but sitting on a couch with the game displayed on a 50 inch TV, I still thought the text was too small. I hope the main game includes accessibility options.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is maybe the most "fine" game I've ever played. It's not exceptional in really any way, but there's a certain charm to how the combat, animation, and music work together that makes it an enjoyable experience. The whole game essentially boils down to doing fetch quests and running through the same half dozen or so dungeons over and over, but the length is short enough and the combat is entertaining enough that it doesn't overstay its welcome.Definitely accomplished its goal of making me more interested in the world of Eiyuden Chronicle, and I'm looking forward to the main game more now than I was previously. But just don't go into this one expecting anything you haven't already played before.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot more to this as a side game than I was expecting! The visuals are beautiful and the gameplay is fun.Despite the quests feeling like Errand Simulator, there's something about the way they're handled that doesn't make them feel tedious at all, but rather, engaging. Maybe it's because there are great elements included in the game that alleviate some of the usual RPG tedium, like being able to jump to sections of town or to key markers in dungeons.I really like how fleshed out the town and all the services are, and given that I've already spent several hours on this game I'm pleasantly surprised that it really is a game on its own instead of something you need the main game to enjoy or understand.Really looking forward to Hundred Heroes after this!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: For the price and the offert, it is a great game.I like the system gameplay and you will get entretainment with the achievements.The storyline is regular , the soundtrack is decent, the graphics are well made.the only bad part the game is kinda easy... still a good start for the next year game Eiyuden Chronicles saga.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly great game! Not only is the story fun and engaging, the cast of characters are colorful and endearing. There's also a great balance between the more serious moments and the lighthearted and humorous ones. The game play is also well crafted. Admittedly, it took some getting used to for me. Once I got the hang of it, it creates a fun game loop whenever completing missions and side quests.The art style and animation are also very on-point. Renders and portraits have a very classic feel to them and the animation and pixel work is surprisingly fluid.A great game overall, 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Been enjoying it quite a bit. Don't mind the excessive amount of side quests since you get a counter that you can always see and you know that you won't miss any of them if you check the bulletin board often enough. Does its job in hyping you up for the main game and setting some groundwork for the lore even if the story-line itself here is a bit simplistic (so far). Note that the two games will be different in gameplay, however.

_childDocuments_.review: Real cool, Very short game than all Suikoden games I have played. Price was reasonable. Wish had more Rune power and more characters. Graphic is 5 star. Story is 5 star. _childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: All-around this is a very good, but simple, action/platformer/RPG with crafting elements.  It's simple in its design but the gameplay is very tight and satisfying, and the expansive list of quests and crafting options adds to the game's length in a positive way and even grants it some Metroidvania elements (in a sense) as some upgrades you build for your gear unlock new abilities that grant access to previously inaccessible areas.  On top of that, the game is beautiful, with great spritework and gorgeous 2.5 environments.  This is one of the best JRPGs in years.  My only really strong complaints are a) it is not very difficult, even on hard mode, a lot of enemies are palette swaps with a few ability tweaks, and c) the campaign is quite short for an RPG, but for the price point, it's definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: As an old school Suikoden Fan. This scratches the itch I've had. The combat is different but the characters and the story telling feels like I've stepped back in time. The game overall is straight forward and pretty easy if your willing to grind. Recommended to those who can't wait for the main game like me.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: In general, game is good. Very good, If you are excited about the main Eiyuden Chronicles game.Everything is rewarding. Combat is fluent and fun. Writing is pleasant, although sometimes there is a bit too much dialog. Characters are likable with a surprising amount of personality and backstory for a spin-off game. There is a lot to do, however most side quests are fetch quests with backtracking into previously visited locations to get more items. It didn't bother me for the most part, because I liked the gameplay and quests were usually fast to finish. Town building is just a reward for side quests, but it's fun to see it getting rebuilt thanks to your actions. Music is ok. Graphic style is surprisingly good.I backed this on Kickstarter, and I'm not disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this companion game a lot. Suikoden is my favourite game; so I may be looking through rose tinted glasses and enjoying this more just by knowing who created it. I enjoyed every moment of playing though. Keeping in mind that it is a different style of gameplay than Hundred Heroes will be it was a great introduction to the characters, story, and atmosphere/setting. While not one of my favourite types of gameplay I still found it enjoyable.This game is very side quest heavy, but also self-aware of that. Personally I enjoy lots of side quests and didn't mind. I could see some being disappointed by that though. I think for the price it's well worth it and a great taste for certain aspects of Hundred Heroes.I would definitely recommend getting this game. Even if it's not your usual cup of tea; if you want something to hold you over a bit while waiting for Hundred Heroes, or want to support the team behind it; then I think you will get your moneys worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Loved every minute of the story so far I think it's amazing. Its giving me the suikoden vibes I've been missing. Combat felt a little clunky for me using keyboard controls however, steam's control function works really well and I found it much better played with a controller. Can't wait for the next game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great, yet simpe Prequel to the upcoming Game of 100 Heroes.The Conversations are sometimes hilarious, yet informative.Generally I had a great time playing this and you probably will enjoy the Envoirment and Music. And its not as short as some other games ;'DFor all Fans of Classic JRPG and specifically Suikoden, this is for yo!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is a great but simple action RPG set in the same world as the much anticipated Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes.Gameplay is quite fun but repetitive. Gather materials by slaying monsters, upgrade shops and gear, all while completing quests for more materials, gold and experience. I ran into no bugs and the visuals as well as the story are alright. Especially at a very cheap price point. I was able to pick it up on the backer store for ~$7. Wait for a small sale and Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising is well worth the purchase!
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game was pretty enjoyable for $15. The graphics are well done, the characters have personality, the writing is acceptable, and the combat was smooth albeit simple. Now for what most of the contention is about: the grinding and the fetch quests. I didn't really mind that much but I can definitely see how it would rub a lot of people the wrong way. It got a little tedious towards the end trying to fill up all the stamps and upgrade your characters all the way.But, for $15 bucks, it's worth it especially if it provides some setup for the actual full JRPG thats coming out later.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so I just completed this game at about 26 hours. This is with doing every side quest available throughout the entirety of the game, and maxxing out everything I could. So with that in mind my review will be a bit extensive but well researched. PremiseFirst off, this game is a stretch goal from a kickstarter of another game: Considering that, this is actually really well put together. It's essentially the tale of a treasure hunter looking for hidden secrets in a mysterious dungeon called the "Barrows". You make friends along the way, as with any RPG, and it comes with your typical "the power of friendship" style story with all of it's themes and moral complexity (or lack thereof.) Graphics:They're interesting, in a world of extremely stylish 2D highly detailed sprite games out there, a genre I'm increasingly coming to like, this game sits pretty well up there visually. The 2D/3D mix is pretty well done, and much of the background scenery is really quite visually pleasing. It covers a range of biomes and does each of them pretty well. The sprites are really quite good. There's a lot of detail there, but of course the monsters are largely pallet swaps throughout the game to fit the overall theme of the biome you're currently in. (Think Green Slime, Fire Slime, Ice Slime, and so on.) Not the first game to do this, won't be the last. Nevertheless the primary characters are well done and stand out without being World of Warcraft pauldrons level of over the top about it. Even the non primary characters were diverse enough that you don't really see any duplicates. It's a nice touch when I've seen some lazier work out there.Story: Run of the mill mild fantasy with a story that doesn't really push any boundaries or do anything different from the typical tropes you'd find in a JRPG. The side quest stories are laughable in terms of actual storytelling quality or breadth/depth, but I imagine given the fact there's like 140 of them, and again, it's a kickstarter stretch goal game, I'd say they did quantity over quality with the story aspects on the side quests.Credit where credit is due, it does feel satisfying reaching a milestone in side quests and watching the town grow and improve. (Gave me big Suikoden 1 Castle vibes) so there is that. I will say that I do hope there's at least some good references in the primary game, or that we at least learned some good world building information/seeing characters again that will make certain elements in the main game seem more interesting. Gameplay/Animation:It's pretty fun, the devs were generous with fast travel, and while the side quests are numerous, few of them actually take more than a few minutes to complete. The movement is pretty wonky, and the people criticizing the "puppet style" movement are spot on. It is janky, though I think the combat doesn't suffer for it. To me it's purely an aesthetic thing. The combat is pretty fun. You can customize it to a point with different elemental attacks and what have you, though you will be utilizing one character far more than the rest. The combos are alright, easy to pull off and they have a sleep through it mode that even does the very easily timed combos. The ability animations are okay, mostly forgettable, though I do like that they made different animations based on every element used. I would say though grinding wise you really don't have to do much to beat this game, as it's very easy if you do even the bare minimum. Going out of your way to do all the quests and get all the upgrades makes everything a cake walk. Other than that I believe they should have done more to even out the playing field when it came to movement abilities. You're easily only going to use one character to move around the map, honestly some people might not even pull out the other characters unless they have to for taking down character specific obstacles or during combo links. Though the game is so easy on the normal difficulty you can even use these non optimized side characters without relying on anyone else and easily slap bosses. I beat the last two bosses with one of the two side characters never using combos or other character attacks and didn't even have to worry about it. Overall:I think it's a pretty fun game. The gameplay loop isn't punishing but it's very easy by the end of it. It does let you reload to just before the last boss to finish up getting the rest of the achievements, and all of the achievements can be gotten in a single playthrough. There's also some stuff you can get before you're supposed to utilizing some of the janky movement abilities and swapping characters that's kind of fun to do, as well. Bonus points for a fishing mini game, too.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game. Solid recommendation 7/10.This little journey has really won me over.Even though the story is short, or the game by itself is simple, it has quite a depth in its lore. I feel like its strong side is the character interactions, between the main parts and also with the NPCs. Most of the time it cracked out of me a chuckle or two, so it was nice.The soundtrack is soothing, is not the big deal, but it does its job. And at least for me, they don't get annoying in any point. There are even a few tunes that I like.Graphics are gorgeous, love the 3D background with the 2D models. Again, although elementary, they are lovely.On the gameplay part, you have a bit of items customization, which is awesome and adds to the adventure. The combat by its own, although satisfying, can get repetitive. Which brings me to my only negative, a bit nick picky, that the game is mostly linear. Still, nothing game breaking experience.So, yeah, I can't wait to see where the story will take us in Eiyuden Chronicles: Hundred Heroes. Which, for what I've seen, it looks like to be the main game, they're focusing on. There are more heros, better animations, it appears to be a more extensive game. I, for once I'm pritty exited to play it.In summary, this was I pritty great view on the universe of this games. It's worth, both the money and time.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun prequel to the upcoming RPG from the developers of Suikoden.  Eiyuden Chronicles Rising is a side-scrolling hack-n-slash that is beautifully created, but can get very repetitive at times.  While the upcoming game plans on having 100+ party members, this game attempts to shove 100+ side quests in a 12 hour game.  Gameplay wise it is fun dungeon crawling, but backtracking for mats to improve armor can get tiresome for someone not invested in the grind.  The world itself is the best part of the game, with some absolutely gorgeous backgrounds/foregrounds.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a challenge, you're not going to get one here. If you're looking to get a peek at some things we might see in Hundred Heroes, I'd say it's worth a consideration. Also I played with a controller and have no idea how the game feels on keyboard. Below is just everything else I have to say.Short, simple, and overall I enjoyed it. I'm only finding out about Hundred Heroes now, and while the story of this game was serviceable, I'd say it definitely served its purpose as a prequel and set some foundation for the world we'll be getting into in the next game. Which is something I can really appreciate.The combat here is just like the overall difficulty of the game: easy. Three face buttons to attack/swap to their respective character, the fourth one to jump, and R2/RT to activate your active character's unique action. For me, the most satisfying part of the combat is landing a full link-attack combo. Equipment wise, the only things you can really change are accessories and what elements you assign to your attacks and defenses. Nice and simple, hard to mess up.The town-upgrading is directly linked to performing doing side quests, and there are at least 160 quests in total. Most side quests are just fast-traveling around town and talking with NPCs, sometimes going areas to gather stuff and kill specific mobs, or just handing over the materials you happened to collect along the way. While I enjoyed seeing the town visually improve, the fact it is so intertwined with the side quests and not just its own thing is a little disappointing. As questing in this game is easily the weakest link.
_childDocuments_.name: Eiyuden Chronicle: Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this because there is no middling option.It is tedious, repeating quests, errand running madness, revisits to old areas along with some janky animations, It is definetly not Suikodens spiritual successor for those who think so. But this is simply a light Metroidvania style game that spin offs on the true spiritual successor that is Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes. But it got a cozy feeling, a charm to it and a bunch of characters that will drop by  in the proper JRPG. The story is not WOW nor the most mature but there is grim elements like in Suikoden and the world is  slowly being shown and built up for the release of the main game. It would be a hard time recommending it for non fans or those of no interest in what  Eiyuden will aim to be, a spiritual sequel to Suikoden. I would say it is way to easy for proper Metroidvania fans! This is a very easy game and  the easy mode makes it almost play itself at times.  I give it a 6/10 for trying and the rather low price. But there is nothing here that will be a revolution of the metroidvania genre nor will it probably do much to sell us Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes. But for those who seek a short but cozy game about building up a village struck by an earthquake, unravel a mystery and treasure hunt with new found friends...well then it is probably something to try out.  DO NOTICE: This is not a JRPG like Suikoden, this is not Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes but a spin off  type of game that acts as a sort of prequel. The main game will be vastly different and more classical JRPG than this sidescrolling action-rpg  metroidvania-like game.
