_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun for a bit but gets old fast. I can't recommend it to anyone unless you can get a lot out of incredibly repetitive content. You need 332,777 Karma for all characters, 139,700 Karma for the books, and another 6,000 Karma for the locks and a few thousand more for the extras. Each loops gives on average 2,500 Karma if it completes and takes around 20-25 minutes to complete a loop when factoring in lobbies and load times. This means you're looking at about 71 hours to get everything. Further more 277,777 of that Karma is relegated to 2 characters and a book so that's 41 hours relegated to grinding out those. Meaning after 30 hours you will probably have all the affordable characters and done all their challenges and will just be grinding the rest out. That would probably be fine as the game is supposedly designed to be played casually and not to just 100% it. However, there are 250ish stages and you do 4 stages a loop. Given you would need about 191 successful loops to unlock everything you would in theory see each level 3 times. In actually you play the same 5-10 levels over and over again. See stages require specific characters to trigger and the player base likes to play the same handful of characters so you don't see a majority of the the stages. This is because of the character challenge system which encourages you to play a character until you get a loop that let's you finish it's challenges and ditch it forever but more on that later. You also need a lot of players to see stages which is cool if you play with randoms but the game prevents you from pairing with friends+randoms because the devs are scared of griefing. So if you want to have a casual experience with your friends and it's not easy to organize all of them to play with you at the same time then guess you're playing the same levels forever.The game advertises itself on having 50 characters, there are not. The game has 40 animals plus the blob and the squirrel that you can get from a card. Even if you count the Sherpa that is still only 43. The thing is is they want characters to be unlocked via the Karmapass system which requires the player base to earn an incredibly large amount of Karma. Basically it's a sneaky way to artificially extend the game's life by promising new content over a player led amount of time. Except it's not new content, it's content that is advertised as being in the game. To make matters worse, characters aren't even that unique, the first two characters released on the Karma pass are just the same as other characters but now they are bigger/heavier.  The characters in game also have this issue but at least a lot of them accomplish the same task in an somewhat different way.The animal abilities are also rarely used. Some levels do a good job an actively make use of player abilities, some even combine player abilities together for their puzzles, but the vast majority of levels that spawn are complete-able without any abilities. The game seems to have no system built in to prioritize the interesting levels over the blob levels so it's just a roll of the dice whether or not you get something neat. This also hampers the character goal system. Each character has 2 challenges plus finishing a run to do in order to obtain a shining star. These challenges kinda relate to the character most of the time but it's just dumb luck whether or not you can actually complete them. You can go 10+ loops and never see the object your character needs to even start their challenge, let alone the number of objects needed. This would also be fine if the challenges saved progress between loops but they don't. Need to break 40 blocks and you got a stage with only 38, guess you'll have to try again and hope you get a stage with more blocks or two stages in your 4 loop run. Of course the random nature of the challenges seems to be the point, the devs don't want you running out of content too soon so rather than make completing the challenges fun they instead make it tedious as hell. The gameplay loop is just a giant Skinner box. This also has the added effect of just encouraging players to one and done characters so you can move on to the next character. Inevitably players find the characters than earn the most Karma on average and only play those.All in all the game gets old fast and to fix this issue the devs use grinding Karma to artificially lengthen things. And you can tell the Karma grind is all players care about, those are the only cards people pick if available. Once the grind is over this game will die. The entire game is always online, you can only play the totem mode with an offline connection. You can't even access the hub without being online. See the devs know this game will die when the grind ends which is why they spend most of their efforts preventing anyone from subverting the grind. You're Karma count is stored on their servers so no save editing and if someone in your game was cheating they can just null whatever Karma you earned in the game. Of course players cheating in Karma in the middle of a game that is then sent out to everyone could definitely be a problem for people who don't want to cheat, this wouldn't be a problem in the first place if they just let people who don't want to put up with their grind the ability to just cheat their save file. Instead they spend more time on their anti cheat system and more cheaters show up in my games.Some things that could make the game last longer without an artificial grind would be more levels with the ability to actually show up and possibly a level editor allowing the community to actually keep the game alive rather than it being artificial. But I have doubts that will happens, the last patch the devs decided to nerf the Karma gain on characters so the grind takes even longer. What a joy. The player base for this game is already very small and I do not foresee it expanding much meaning this game will be dead by the end of next year unless a major overhaul, in not only the game but dev team's mentality, happens.On a side note, there is still no cursor lock in game making it annoying if you play with Keyboard/Mouse. This has been reported since the Beta and is still not fixed.Update 3/4/23: Game is no longer being worked on including bug fixes and what not, all content from the pass is in the game now which is just a bunch of characters that did the same thing as others and other meaningless rewards but adds about 100k more Karma required if you want everything. The addition of the snail improves the grind which is why I have everything unlocked in a shorter time than estimated but don't expect to accomplish the same thing as me with the player pool lower than ever. There are 47 characters, a base form and the sherpa which if you are being generous could count as 4 characters bringing the total to it's advertised 50+. The crocodile in the trailers isn't in the game which is apparently a joke I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game a lot when it came out. It was a really cute idea, and played pretty well. Some of the character balance was off, and some character challenges were unreasonable, but it was still a solid game with a fun gimmick. It pains me to vote down, but I just cannot recommend this game in its current state. For those who don't know, this is an online co-op platformer where you work together with other people to get past obstacles using each other's character abilities. You get different levels depending on which characters are in the current game, and you get rewarded for helping others. However, due to the online nature of this game, I always knew it had a limited shelf life. Whether it was from server shutdown, or lack of a playerbase, the game could not last forever. And right now, the latter is the issue. As of writing this, SteamDB says this game has ZERO current players. Which means it is literally impossible to play unless you get a handful of friends together. I played a lot of this game when it came out, so I've gotten good mileage out of it, but getting the rest of the achievements is impossible for me now unless I specifically boost for them. I'm not sure if there's anyway to fix this. The devs seem adamant about not playing solo. I'm not sure if playing with bots or whatnot would even be fun. But right now, the game is simply unplayable, and that makes me very sad.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a delightful teamwork game. I love the concept and it makes you feel good. It feels good to wait for someone who will be trapped behind a door if you leave, it feels good to use your unique ability to help everyone reach a tough ledge, and it feels good that (mostly) others will do the same for you. That's the problem though.The game has unfortunately gotten worse since launch. The devs made obvious choices to reward teamwork and encourage that sort of play and I think they did a great job with that aspect. Unfortunately, despite it all, a lot of players just feel the need to blast through every level without ever turning back. They nab all the secrets, never save you and never wait. Like, you snooze you lose I guess, but I just don't really understand that style of play in this game? As long as you have a partner who wants to zip through as well, you can get right to the end in almost every level. I'm not sure what the criteria for completing a level is, 50% of a team at the end or something? Almost every time I play now I feel like I get to the end with this poor small group of stragglers that don't get the chance to solve any puzzles or feel special at all.It's still a fun game and I do recommend it. I've definitely had several remarkable moments; saving others just before they turn into a ghost, exploring with a partner and finding a secret that everyone missed, or saving the day by being the only one that can perform the task at hand to solve a puzzle. It's a bummer though, it feels like there are too many experienced players now that are only pushing for unlocks. Those remarkable moments don't happen as much anymore and so it doesn't feel as fun as it did. Kudos to the devs though, it's a charming game and gives you a lot of satisfaction on a deeper level than just playing the game well and succeeding.

_childDocuments_.review: There’s a corgi in this game so this was an instabuy. :)What's cozier than an online co-op game that rewards you for helping your teammates? It's simple and wholesome. I was hooked immediately. This was a magical experience, and a game hasn’t made me feel that sort of happy in such a long time. I absolutely just loved the sentiment behind this game! A game built around wholesomeness and helping people out is just a beautiful thing. I also really love that the creators admitted this was partially a social experiment and I fully respect it. It's a pretty fun cooperative platfomer game. It’s a purely coop (local or online) game where you’re completing a 2D Platforming level with some puzzles in it. Your only means of communication is whatever noise your randomly assigned animal makes, and each animal has a different Platforming ability to aid in your course. The way it gets everyone cooperating and working towards the same goal with nothing but these off pitch honks is just delightful. It really has made me feel so happy to see strangers work together. I especially liked the beautiful community with kind people always willing to work together. It's really lovely to see that it's one of those games where the toxicity in multiplayer just isn't a thing. I think with the price tag and all the good about it, I'll be worth picking up for anyone that’s even remotely interested.Finally, there are elephants. And penguins. It’s always game of the year if cute elephants or penguins make an appearance.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Karma Zoo is a Game about being nice to Strangers online is the best way I can describe it, and it's perfect at that, every core game mechanic encourages you to be nice to people.That alone is a big selling point in my opinion, but if that isn't enough: it's a cozy online coop plattformer where you collect karma (a currency) to unlock new characters. Each character has its own abilities and levels that are designed around it, there are lot of fun ideas in the levels and while it can be a bit rough communicating with strangers with just emotes, it's usually fun and works out. Give the demo a try and if it's fun, the full game is only like 10 bucks. Have fun collecting Karma!

_childDocuments_.review: [Edit as of 2/7/2024] If you are living within the US (I personally am US West)  The servers have dwindled down to maybe 3-5 players during evening hours  and peak player hours are early in the morning local time. [End of Edit for 2/7/2024]I really like this game, but I cannot recommend it at the current state it is in without some fundamental changes made to how the game functions and interacts with the players.While Karmazoo is exactly what you get on the box, a character based platformer in which you play as a different animal which different abilities in a cooperative setting in order to reach the end while helping each other and collecting fruit. The overall goal being completing 4 levels and reaching the end to feed the karma tree and be rewarded in Karma (in game currency) based on how the group did. Rinse repeat. Different characters are unlocked via the karma. Each character has objectives to master them and unlock their linked Sherpa. However, the pricing on characters range from what could be achieved in a normal round, to almost 40 hours worth of grinding and hoping you average over 1.5k karma to obtain 100k for a single unlock. This is where the problems start, the grind is probably one of the worst I have seen especially after the nerfing of earning karma from characters that were designed around earning large amounts of karma. There is no incentive to play other characters beyond completing the challenges unless that character earns more karma for the group, in which case you will see more of that character. Because of this, it makes the same characters show up in queue, which as the levels generate based upon character abilities, the maps tend to be the same variation queue rather than any maps that require specific abilities. Continuing this on with the fact that you are not able to queue with friends and randoms, in addition to the quantity of players also makes the level choices vary, the levels repeat relatively quickly. There are no incentives for experimenting with different character combinations, and there is no way to change characters once you have entered a lobby. This means that if there are 3 fires, 2 spiders, and 2 wolves, you have to completely leave to change a character and pray that you might enter the same lobby. There is also no in game chat, which while a benefit to remove both the language barrier for crossplay and toxic/foul language, it makes communicating game mechanics very hard. This is especially so when one character is needed to complete an objective to progress. There is a lack of emotes for concepts such as "here/come here" "yes/O" "no/X" "exit" "fruit/karma juice." There is no way to communicate these concepts to other players, especially if you are trying to get them to stand in a specific spot, telling them not to leave as there are still fruit to collect, or to leave if the rest of the group had separated for fruit to leave the exit (or if they are softlocked, and you need to leave in order to progress, which has happened twice to me personally.) This is paired with the ways to communicate are also hidden, meaning that new players might not even have what more experienced players are using in order to communicate basic concepts of "let's go" or "stop."It's frustrating as the game is really fun and a great game to chill play with friends. However, some of these flaws make the longevity of the game seem to be artificially extended through partial character releases through community objectives, but not actually expanding player's interest through creating catered experiences to mix things up. This game is basically dying and the devs are not doing anything about it. Don't waste your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I promise not to leave you behind.I should probably tack on a bit of actual review instead of just trying to be cute with it. KarmaZoo's entire theme is selfless cooperation, and this endearing platformer uses all kinds of clever mechanics to reinforce that. Helping others is encouraged at just about every moment-to-moment instant of play, providing rewarding incentives even to players who might be just into it for themselves. Players are given ways to encourage their teammates and express appreciation for their help, from simple emoji-based communications to cute little dances and activities, up to providing players actual point-based rewards (which are, if you complete the run, shared with everyone, so using these even benefits the user). Everywhere it was possible, the developers found ways to make working as a team feel rewarding and fun. It's rare in my experience to end a run without finding another player or two who end up feeling like your best friends for a little while. There are tools to vote out troublemakers, so there's a last-resort option for bad actors, but while I admit I haven't played the game extensively, I've yet to see them needed.If I had to voice one disappointment, it would be the inability to play with friends in public games. I understand this was done for a reason. You wouldn't want to let griefers consolidate power in a game to make themselves immune to being voted out (or able to exploit the vote system), for example. But if you want to play with your personal friends, it will need to be with just them. That sad necessity aside, it's a nice bite-sized little mood booster that's chin-deep in charm.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been beta testing KarmaZoo over the past few months and have accumulated over 50 hours of playtime in the limited time sessions we have. And I can say for sure, KarmaZoo is AMAZING. It’s the type of game to take a new spin on the multiplayer formula, it’s all about co-operation! This game is perfect for playing with friends, and works really well when playing with strangers. It doesnt have any greedy micro transactions nor dlc (so far) and i don think it ever will. KarmaZoo has so many fun characters, fun gameplay mechanics and level design and tons more epic things. I love how satisfying the progression is and the amazing community. The core game has a fun gameplay loop and the endgame is amazing, it will take you probably over 100 hours of playtime to complete it. Characters have abilities that are unique to most characters and these abilities are incredibly fun to use, most of these abilities are about helping each other, for example: boosting another player up, giving someone a speed boost, making a web for others to climb on. It’s all amazing and fun, there are some characters with abilities that mostly benefit themselves but those are fun to play too! The difficulty can range anywhere from easy and simple, to intense and fast as you’re rushing to complete a level right before the timer runs out, as for the level variety there are tons of different levels with different variation so it’s always fresh. If you enjoy multiplayer co-op games, this game is for you and even if you don’t it has a PVPmode that is also amazing! Totem is one of the most fun minigame modes I’ve played in a while and I absolutely recommend it for a party night. Although the one downside is while you can play it online, so far you can’t match with randoms, but then you can always join the discord and hop in a lobby code to play a few! The music is great, and the art style is very cute! Overall I really enjoyed my time with karmazoo and will definitely be playing it for a long time, I hope you can consider karmazoo to play and maybe even give to your friends, for it’s incredibly cheap price :3! SEE YOU IN THE LOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOP!  P.S: Buy the spider character, (I am the spider marketer)

When you're actually in a game with an assortment of different player abilities, it's super fun. But the actual fun game is wrapped in a bunch of un-fun stuff. I hope there's still will to iterate more here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game a has a great core concept and a good gameplay execution, but has some awful design decisions.+ Great fun coop gameplay that encourages sticking together and helping eachother.+ A lot of different characters.+ Super cute animations!! The songbird will for example put on a cap and sing into a microphone and do a mic drop.+ A lot of secrets in the lobby.+ Levels will change depending on who's in the lobby, you won't get an incompletable level.- Each character has their own 3 missions they need to complete. These need to be completed in one loop. some of these missions are literally impossible; For example you might need acid to complete a mission and acid is not in the level rotation. Another problem also is these missions are designed around being selfish. A few characters will for example have "collect 50 fruit". This is not the whole team, so if you have a quick raptor on your team they will unintentionally be griefing you. Why they didnt make the missions team based is absolutely absurd and is why I almost don't recommend it.- The lobby system. You can not choose which lobby you join. You do not know if there are multiple lobbies up and you do not know how many people are online. This means you will join multiplayer, the game will put you in a solo lobby, then you might exit this lobby right away and rejoin multiplayer and get put in a 5/10 lobby. Or you might not. You won't know. Awful. Awful.- There's no way to switch animal in the lobby, you have to leave.These two issues are such bizarre design decisions. It's like the devs wanted the game to be "plug and play" with the online, but didn't realize that their version of plug and play actually makes it less likely to have a game actually be played.

_childDocuments_.review: This is best-designed fun co-op puzzle platformer I've played. If you're like me and you don't enjoy the competitive/combat-focus aspect of every other online multiplayer game, then this is a breath of fresh air.The devs have come up with simple but brilliant mechanics to solve issues that make other games incentive uncooperative play. This game instead makes you want to work together, get rewarded for it, and get endangered when you don't.For example, the halo system. Think of it as a personal-space bubble around your character. If your bubble doesn't overlap someone else's, then you are in danger of dying in seconds. This solves the problem of one person breaking off from the pack, which you probably encountered before if you've played a multiplayer platformer.For more info on their approach to solving these issues, watch their devlog.

_childDocuments_.review: This multiplayer platformer is based around getting rewarded for cooperation. You are a shape-shifting blob that can take the form of animals and use their powers to traverse the levels in a big group as going too far ahead of the pack means you will be killed by the toxic air and have to sit the round out. By acting altruistically (opening doors and keeping stragglers from dying), you will be rewarded with karma, the currency to unlock all the animal forms and other goodies. The game is pretty simple and really doesn't take a ton of skill. It's more of a pleasant time-waster than anything to while some lazy hours away in an enjoyably mindless fashion. I got this as part of a Humble Bundle, and while I had no problem finding matches and even was able to play with a full house of ten players several times, once this surge of new players brought in by the bundle is over, who knows active this game will be. It doesn't look like it has a single player mode, just an online and couch co-op mode. Honestly, I think the matches are better off with maybe 5 to 8 players than a full room. I noticed that we earned more Karma bonuses at the end of the rounds in this player range than going in with a full team. Probably because it's a bit easier to coordinate when you don't have everyone either trying to do the same thing or just running around like a headless chicken. There is no voice or text chat just a few emotes to try to herd the stragglers, but while that does make communication difficult, that also means the other players can't curse you out.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's definitely worth it for the price they're asking. It's not perfect, you will definitely start seeing repeat stages pretty quickly, and you currently can't do loops (the main co-op game mode) locally or alone which is pretty bad for preservation. The ability to invite friends to public lobbies is also currently missing, and I hope is addressed soon in an update.But if you get friends to play this game with you online, I definitely think it's worth it. A fun and cute little co-operative platformer.Edit: Unfortunately going to have to change the review to negative. Back when I originally posted the review, I genuinely would've recommended it due to how cheap it was for the amount of enjoyment you could get from it. Sadly, the game did not seem to sell very well. The servers are simply too empty for the game to properly function anymore. A game about playing online with random people doesn't work without people. I simply cannot recommend anyone to buy this game anymore.Many things went wrong. The game received practically no updates, aside from some bug fixes. There was never a reason to return to the game. The biggest mistake though, from what I can see, was simply the lack of marketing. I barely saw Devolver Digital mention this game. I never saw YouTubers play and promote the game. I probably heard it mentioned in a video once, and even that was a passing mention.It doesn't help that the game came out so close to another similarly priced online game, Lethal Company, which was a phenomenon and got everyone's attention.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have one other friend you want to play with, you can't simply party up together and hop into online with randoms. This is a dealbreaker for me. Either bring 9 friends to a private lobby or none at all. Please correct me if I'm mistaken.Also there is local/splitscreen but you can't take your local partners into online mode with randoms.There is no incentive for players to pick the exciting or fun bonus cards; the ones that potentially result in more hearts/less grind will always win. This results in extremely repetitive matches.Certain classes are linchpins, once their particular job is loaded into the procedural generation, if that player fails to perform their task the whole lobby is cursed. Mousewheels have no alternative activation method, for example.Players can railroad the entire group into leaving before all collectibles are gathered just by hopping into the portal prematurely.Player hub is obtuse by design and doesn't explain well what you're spending your karma/efforts on. Also no refunds.Skilled player POV: Waiting at the portal wondering, Why can't these kids get coordinated!!? New player POV: Ghostly panda slaps you repeatedly for being last in line while you're constantly white-knuckle racing against the dying light of your aura, also feeling bad because someone has decided to be your personal chaperone and will also not be seeing much of the map because of you.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: I can't even begin describe how awesome this game is.Beautiful pixel art animations, wholesome gameplay, and the kindest community of any game I've ever played! Please feel free to stop by the game's discord to get to know the community. You'll start to recognize some familiar faces after enough encounters with people, and they grow into some beautiful friendships. If you have an ounce of interest in these types of games, I highly recommend you give it a try. I'm looking forward to seeing you all in the loooooooooooooooooooooooop!
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: Game starts simple enough but the more you progress the more diverse your gameplay becomes. A wide range of characters to pick with special abilities leads to a lot of unique interactions with other people. I played what feels like hundreds of loops, yet all of them felt different. Even if you get the same level twice, the way you progress will be unique based on your team composition and your knowledge of this level. The game has overall calm and cheerful atmosphere, and while it can get intense, it never got really stressful. They managed to balance difficulty, even when having newbies and long time players in the same lobby. If you are new, you won't be put in a hard position and you'll have a chance to slowly learn, while seasoned players will still be challenged. I don't think I have ever seen such fluid difficulty.Careful with this game though, it's very easy to get addicted. I played all weekends non-stop, only had breaks for food and sleep. And I won't be done with this game any time soon. Everything just feels so satisfying to do.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! Low stress, addictive, and scratches a cooperative (with randos) itch I've had for a long time. It's fun being able to constantly switch things up by picking a new form and there's a lot to unlock (and some secrets to find too ;)). There's also global goals that'll unlock more in the future, and I'm very excited to see what new forms we get.The only criticisms I have is that sometimes you just don't get a stage your form is any use in. I crave being a helpful little guy so it can be a little boring if I'm not doing much for the team. There's also the constellations that require you to do specific actions that require getting stages that use your form, too. The other criticism is a very specific one. This game is very chill and friendly and it's hard to feel like you're "failing" or that your team is upset with you. However a few of the final maps are significantly more stressful than others i.e the map with the large hamster-powered platform and lightbulbs below it that the spider(s) have to reach, especially when you're the hamster or you only have one spider. I think if more form powers were useful/the platform was faster/players only respawned on the moving platform it'd be less so.Small gripes aside this game is easily worth what they're charging, especially with its current sale. If any part of it looks like it might appeal to you, get it! It's so much fun.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great relaxing game for the most part. The art style and general conceit is great working as a team to gain hearts and beat levels. Most the of the different avatars have their own individual powers and that keeps things fresh but once you get to end game most player will probably be the high earning which kind of hurts stage selection since stages are chosen based off avatars chosen. If you aren't going for all the avatar or books you shouldn't have a problem with the grind and enjoy yourself without worries of optimal avatar choice. Overall i would say it's an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: KarmaZoo might just be one of the cutest games I have played all year. I mean, you can literally shoot hearts at your teammates to spread love and I can’t say I’ve played another game that quite reaches that level.At its core, KarmaZoo is a game about cooperative puzzle platforming. You’ll run into situations where you need one player to unlock a door for another player to pass, or where you need one player to sing to activate a platform for another player to stand on. It’s not a really difficult formula to understand and doesn’t really get too complex, which may be an issue for some, but I feel like the devs did a great job making it just complex enough to draw in players that may not be familiar with the genre while still being engaging for those more experienced.Levels are divided into “loops” which are kinda reminiscent of a roguelike run. The levels are handcrafted and selected from a pool of over 300 according to what characters are selected. After completing a level, players vote on a card to activate for the next, and this was a kinda fun feature in itself because you can do interesting stuff like force everyone to play the same character in the next level or one of my group’s favorites - a card that activates a saxophone to play with the background music. These were fun to play with even if they don’t always change the gameplay.Characters range from your simple blobs, to owls that can glide, to lions that can sing in all directions, to literal flower pots that can create platforms from their flowers. There are 50 such to unlock, so there’s a lot of replayability in that regard and given that you can play with up to 10 people, I can only imagine how insane some combinations would be. That said, I was a bit disappointed to see that some of those characters had identical or very similar abilities to others instead of truly being unique.Playing through loops and trying out different character combinations was fun, activating the dumbest level effects was also fun, and the game even has a competitive mode called Totem that can be played online or locally and that was a ton of fun too. That mode has a bunch of different level types, like races or eating challenges and it was really cool to see how the devs could take simple concepts like that and craft a ton of levels that all feel different from each other and try new things.My only real concern with the game is its longevity. This is not a game that can be played solo. Like, it straight up just does not work. Trying to join a loop or creating your own spits you into a lobby with a message stating that two players are required to continue. This is not surprising, given that the gameplay would actually just be impossible to complete as a solo, but it is very important to note as once this game loses its playerbase, it will be extremely difficult to play. I would give KarmaZoo a light recommendation. It’s a fun little co-op puzzler that is great to play if you have a group of friends ready to give it a shot. It has a ton of characters to unlock, level types to work through, and the competitive Totem mode is a lot of fun too. That said, if you do not have a group to play with, you’ll be at the mercy of the online playerbase which I honestly cannot see lasting that long, so that is definitely something to keep in mind.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: The core concept of the game is interesting, but several things hold it back from being a consistent fun experience:1) No co-op with friends. Since the game is designed for 10 player lobbies the only way you can play with friends is in a private game. This is great if you have a large quantity of friends to play with, but if I want to share this fun little experience with my partner, and experience random people helping each other I can't.2) Challenge system. Each character you unlock has a challenge to complete and, while this works sometimes depending on the character and it's challenge, these challenges are session specific where if you don't complete them before the end of the final level they reset. This turns the game from cooperative into competitive as you race to grab things before other players and getting frustrated when they beat you. Unlock 5 doors with a key in a session, but what if the game doesn't generate 5 keys? What if there are only 5 keys and, out of the 10 players, you need to grab each one otherwise the challenge fails? This is a fundamental design flaw and really changes the tone of the game, unfortunately.3) Loop/level repetitiveness. Since the levels aren't randomly generated in any way this kind of game works well only if there's an extremely large variation of levels. Unfortunately I was seeing repeats straight away. Maybe a level editor for players to create or some randomisation in the future would fix this issue, but for now it's only a matter of time before it becomes a speed run as players get used to levels.It's a shame because I feel like this game does something really unique and it's nice to be working together, but it's these 3 points that hold the game back for me.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: In their DevBlog, the developers said they tried to make a game that encourages teamwork and eliminates toxicity. In some cases they succeeded. There are a lot of very helpful and patient players in KarmaZoo. But people are people and so of course there are a few bad apples who spoil the fun for others. Unfortunately, I now see this in more matches than I would like.Some mechanics in the game also contribute to this. For example, the annoying challenges that you have to complete within a single match and that bring an unpleasant PvP touch to the game.Also that only three votes are needed to completely remove a person from the game. Honestly, in my nearly 100 hours, I've only met two people who tried to intentionally manipulate the game. I met a lot more players who kicked others for apparently no reason. Even the fact that a single person can end the level sometimes interferes with the goals of those who would like to collect everything within the level. The game appeals to different target groups, but does not help them to reach any kind of agreement.Having to go to an external website to see the progress of the KarmaPass is also an inconvenient solution. It would be more player-friendly to be able to see this directly in the game.KarmaZoo really conveys positivity, the gameplay is fun and the majority of the players are helpful and friendly. I understand that the development team is very small and not everything can or should be changed, especially not immediately. But unfortunately for me the negative aspects now outweigh the positive ones. The last few times I started KarmaZoo with a bad feeling because far too often people get kicked out if they're just new to the game or aren't that talented. This doesn't correspond to what I understand by co-op. With all due respect, it's a waste of my time, I'd rather play something that's GUARANTEED to give me a good experience instead of just hoping for it.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: I would die for this game. This is everything I love about games. It makes me feel good in my tummy. Good platforming, lovely animations, a bunch of features in it that serve no other purpose but for bein a silly billy. Run around with your little buddies and pals and friends and get the fruit yay! Everyone should try this game. What speaks to its quality is how fun it is solo. Many games arent as fun playing with randos online. But this makes it so lovely. I LOVE those goofy unspoken communications we do in games, like crounching (n!) at each other. Take that idea and water it until its a big fruitful tree to climb and jump on, and you have this game!
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and chill little co-op game that keeps you wanting to go for "just one more round". The gameplay is simple but efficient. Unlocking a new character and discovering their abilities is always fun.I do wish there was a "hard mode" (maybe with better rewards as an incentive), as it truly is on the easy side... but either way it is addictive and well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: Played the beta and then bought the full game (on sale) this is the only other game I've bought so close to it being released (the other is battlebit, also on sale) here's my completely honest review of it so far, love the concept and the execution, gotta lower it by 1 star and put it at 9/10 because even though there's a 10 player limit I only got one other player in my first game but they were super kind (even though I couldn't talk to them or back to them because I didn't have emotes) they stuck by me throughout my entire first game and it was great and incredibly enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: KarmaZoo is a very wholesome 10 player co-op puzzle platformer with roguelike elements all about working together as different characters that each possesses a unique ability that can help your team solve puzzles to get through each level with the common goal of reaching the end of a 5 stage loop to grow the karma tree for all players to receive karma hearts which could then be spent on new characters. Its a pretty fun and addicting loop, choose a character, spawn in with other random characters and work together to get through the level before the time runs out which will end the run. You can also collect fruits throughout each level which dictates the quality of special cards your team then gets to vote on one at the end of a level, they can give everyone extra karma hearts, extra level time, team power boosts, and other fun stuff to keep things interesting and every run unique. Besides the main roguelike loop, there's also a mini game mode to compete with friends which can give you a nice little break from grinding karma hearts. It has a really sick 2D pixel art style with vibrant colors, cute characters, nice music, and whimsically fun gameplay. Its a beautiful gem of game where it rewards you for working together and helping others no matter how big or how small, I recommend it with all my karma hearts.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty calm and fun co-op game. There's plenty of charm with all the animations the forms have and the music is nice to vibe to. It does a good job encouraging teamwork with random people. Can get a little repetitive as stages the game picks are random so you're bound to get repeats but overall the game is worth the price.Would be neat if there's an option for a stage select for private lobbies. Being able to pick stages specifically designed for the forms you and friends are could be fun instead of praying for RNG that you get stages your forms are actually useful in.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game with a great base, but it feels a little bit simplistic. In bigger lobby it's a little bit hectic and not everyone feels useful witht the character they pickecked. The maps are clever, there are some brutal ones, but they're mostly easy, which is a shame, because the harder maps bring cooperation into the game and actually relying on your teammate. Nevertheless, it's a game worth getting.

_childDocuments_.review: 10 hours in - 3.5/4 starsYou play 5 level “loops”  cooperatively with strangers. The brief runs is nice given you can’t pause it. Biggest drawbacks for me is that1) remote play together doesn’t get you the “main campaign” sort of levels. The multiplayer competition available through local play is still fun though. 2) the available characters often have at least one repeat in skill (with one or two clearly superior choice in implementation per group) so the number of characters I’m looking forward to playing is maybe half. 3) Completing the goals for a character can either be quite simple (all three goals done in one run) or so deeply dependent on the levels that I seemingly can’t complete it at all- looking at you, mouse, played 7 “loops” and didn’t get a single breakable block to walk on. Or the ones where you need to collect so much fruit or be the one to unlock a certain number of doors (which the other users don’t know/care you are trying to make those goals or are even competing to do them themselves) but also doesn’t track between “loops.” Unclear if there is more story to play beyond the three goals per character as  I’m only ten hours in, but it’s a fairly enjoyable game for me. It has some annoyances. I lost connectivity during a loop once (not on my end - did a Speedtest of 400 down and 200 up) - but it was just the once, although it required a reboot of the whole game to remedy. Have still been playing and will probably continue. Remains to be seen if I’ll finish it. It has quite a few “yet to be released” character slots that we’ll see how that impacts the ability to finish the story as is.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: To start, I am a little worried on longevity since it'll basically be dead if no players are on but that's a future problem overall.Past that, games great. It's adorable, charming and wholesome as heck. Each character has their own unique abilities from squirells to frogs to elephants. You start as a little blob that can stick to walls but can unlock a bunch new animals and abilities Theres no voice chat but you can 'sing' in a direction to activate things and prompt people to do stuff (I think there's emojis too but I haven't found them yet)I've only played a tiny bit but it was silly, wacky and again very wholesome. I really liked the emphasis on teamwork, and being rewarded for say sacrificing yourself to get a platform moving or to be a meat shield vs spikes. Things may change so if they do I'll update my review but it's cheap as heck (10 bucks), is cute and has a bunch of content. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a co-op platformer with some really interesting mechanics. The game play itself is simplistic which is great because you don't have to rely on much communication. You still are required to work together though as you work your way through each stage. It's essentially a roguelike where you play through 5 levels per run so you can pick up and play shorter sessions if you'd like. The tricky thing is that since it does require cooperation with other players, you'll have to be able to play with others. These indie games often have very small communities so you'll be limited to when you can play unless you can organize a group. However, when you do get a few people, it's really fun! I'd still recommend picking it up even if you try to play at prime time hours, you should still be able to find enough people to have some fun with.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: This game didn't get enough traction, and it's unfortunately not worth getting. Getting into a match seems to be almost impossible at this point. I really enjoyed what I played of it and wish I played more while there was still an active player-base. KarmaZoo is super easy-going with the largest challenge being coordination with strangers. Sometimes it doesn't work out, but most of the time it does and I have tons of fun with it. There's lots of unlockables to keep me engaged and that also effect the levels you play through. It makes almost every run unique in some ways and the game never asks too much to further your meta-progression, so unless you're unlucky you won't be asked to play the same animal too many times over to finish the challenges. There's crossplay too, so even though it hasn't totally taken off here on Steam, it seems like I rarely have too big of an issue finding matches. I'd highly recommend this game, it's cheap, fulfilling, and original as heck. I love KarmaZoo! It's probably my top new indie game released this year, and there's been a lot of steals on great new releases so that's saying a lot for me.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: I really really loved this game!! I enjoyed playing it so much! I put in a lot of hours to 100% the achievements and enjoyed playing with friends. The puzzles were engaging. The bigger the lobby, the more challenging the puzzles. The helpfulness and sending kisses to complete missions were cute and inspiring. Great game for different ages. Sadly, the lobbies became sparse. Fewer people are playing. Of the very few remaining, there are some who are glitching through walls and puzzles, making the game tedious and losing the cooperative fun. I sincerely wish the game could continue to be supported with new and challenging puzzles, more story, and newer animals with different abilities added. However, if I read correctly, I don't think the devs are adding anything more. T_T
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun puzzle game that adapts the level you plan on based on the form you and your co-op partners choose. Each form has a special ability to help the team out in some way shape or form. There are tons of things to unlock in this game. I see comments about low player count, and sure I suppose there is, but I have never had a problem getting at least 5 people in a lobby which is enough to play the game just fine. As of the writing of this review, it's been a blast. I do fear that eventually the game will go silent if player base lowers though. You cannot play solo.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: An ambitious game. I really enjoyed playing it and the only reason I stopped after only 2 hours is that there isn't a big enough playerbase to quickly fill a decently sized lobby. The main game loop, while not super-challenging, is very fun as the game somehow managed to make cooperating with up to 10 totally random strangers work amazingly well! The story didn't seem like anything complicated but it's presented in an interesting way. Also there are many many characters that you can play as that keep the game fresh and interesting. The only problem lies in it's strength. The game is the most fun when you play with many random straners (I don't think it will be as fun playing with friends, although there is a totally different mode for that, featuring many mini-games that I didn't try), so the playerbase getting smaller means that you get a sub-par experience.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few multiplayer online games where you can actually collaborate with random strangers to achieve a common goal without having to deal with any toxicity and people do help each other (although that's mostly because the game mechanics kinda force you to), it's also really fun and adorable... and I think this might count as a game inspired by religion, yet it does it without being preachy which is pretty remarkable.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit I was skeptical at first. A game where you work together with other players? Yeah right! But I say this game handles this beautifully. Working together is a blast and there's so so much content. The levels change based on your group size and characters which allows so many combinations to happen. Even if you get the same level it's still a blast. Not only that but each character has their own unique ability to liven up the game. I'm personally very excited to play more of this.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: I played this in beta, and I'm so glad it's finally out! This game is a lot of fun! If you like simultaneously being nice to strangers and also screaming at them, you'll love this game. You start out as a blob, and then eventually, after being a nice little blob, you'll get enough hearts to blossom in to a beautiful whale (or whatever your heart desires.) _childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: KarmaZoo puts cooperation back into co-op.It's a simple puzzle platformer with emphasis on cooperation. Online with 9 strangers or co-op with friends. Two game modes. Variety of unlockable characters with different skils to help your team. Masterfully done visual style and music. Speaking of style, I usually get stuck for up to a minute on the mode selection screen just for the way it's tastefully presented (try switching modes back and forth, you'll see what I mean).KarmaZoo is my pick for Steam Awards 2023 in three categories: Most Innovative Gameplay, Best Soundtrack, Sit Back and Relax.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I've been recommending this game to all of my friends. I'd solidly give this a 9/10! Such a nice idea. One thing I'd recommend adding the whole thing about the community working towards an update. I love this game! Another thing I'd mention would be the fact it takes a second to get all 10 players. But this will be fixed after more people buy this game. I also do have to say the game easy at times, a little too easy. Especially with 10 players. You just run through and crowd the screen. But, me saying that it's too easy might still dissuade people from buying the game. I should add that sometimes you do lose, especially in the levels with electricity. I do have to add one thing, I'm disappointed in this game. After some research, I discovered that you can't actually play couch co op. Which is the main part of the game. You have to play with utter strangers all the time on a co op game. The developers could have even added local couch co op, but no. Also, I wish Totem were online, as I want to play it but none of my friends have it. One last thing, I wish they ported to the versions before Xbox Series S and X/ PS 5, my friends who only have those want to play the game but can't. All in all, I highly recommend this game, and I can't wait to see the community grow!
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: KaramaZoo is an extremely innovative take on co-op gameplay. With team sizes allowing up to 10 friends or random players this team focused game makes it fun to complete goals and find various secrets without making it feel forced. Progression feels the same way but as a player you want to play more and unlock the various other characters which could impact how your team completes a level. Even if you don’t have friends who play this game I highly recommend it just to play with new people towards a common goal.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: Not going to lie, the elevator pitch of a ten player co-op 2D puzzle platformer...uh...well, made me go, "I've done this song and dance before....pass". Being the one trying to catch up with everyone else in a co-op game while all the challenges had been solved is a frustrating experience. But, surprisingly, this couldn't be further from the case in this game. While there are some frustrations, overall it has been a super charming experience that I keep going back to. The best way I can describe this is a politeness simulator where you get to play as a variety of adorable animals and other objects. And the levels themselves appear to be generated when you load into them to require the skills of the characters that are brought into them. So, whoever you play as, you are always a necessary component of the team. Be it for tasks that anyone can do (such as holding a door open for everyone) or something only your unique skills can solve. And, at least in my experience, everyone seems to understand this. As, every time I've missed a jump or misunderstood the challenge, people have gone back for me. Whether it's just to keep my protection bubble from popping or to provide a shortcut for me past a solved puzzle. And, considering the limited means of communication, it's charming to see how everyone seems to have developed a means conveying information is a fairly effective manner. I do have a few complaints, but they're fairly minor. The puzzles can sometimes be vague in what they're expecting from you. Though, since the level timer is pretty lenient, that's generally not a problem. The player feels like it's fairly low at certain times of day, though again. It's not a huge deal since the stages are generated based on skills present and capabilities of the party...regardless if it's three people or ten. And, one that I understand, but still find frustrating is that it's not possible to form a partial party and queue up. I know that it sucks to be the one random tagging along with a nearly full stack. But, I feel like you could compromise and...say, allow parties of two to queue up, but have an additional requirement of requiring at least four people to start. Still, all in all, this has been an unexpectedly charming and wonderful experience that has brought quite a lot of joy. What a fantastic game~
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: The concept is a simple, but effective, multiplayer puzzle game.  You pick a form and its unique ability, and group with up to 10 other players, all trying to get through a series of platforming levels.  These levels can't be traversed alone, and you would literally die trying, but they're selected and generated such that cooperation with whatever team you have will get you through.  Some abilities might make specific points easier, but none are impossible so long as you're working together.As it stands, the tutorial could be a little more robust; while it clearly covers the basic mechanics and controls, a handful of puzzle elements will only show up while you're on a loop.  They're pretty intuitive, but it made my first loop feel a bit awkward, testing the waters and observing newer players without getting in the way.All in all, this game does an excellent job presenting teamwork-focused puzzles, and a structure that maintains it as the core element of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually tend to enjoy coop games with random matchmaking, I stick to solo or multiplayer with friends. This is one of the few games that immediately got me hooked because it just works so brilliantly right off the bat. It's like Meadow, but as a puzzle platformer. Immediately fell in love.The game throws you into a set of puzzle platform levels that appear to be auto-generated based on the amount of players and what shapes they brought to the table, catering to the abilities you have available. It has a satisfying progression system (helping in any way shape or form rewards 'karma', karma unlocks more shape shifts). There is no direct communication and only very rudimentary means to emote, but somehow it doesn't result in total chaos. It just intuitively works, somehow, overthrowing all of my preconceived notions about random matchmaking multiplayer. FULLY recommended even if you don't have friends for coop.
_childDocuments_.name: KarmaZoo

_childDocuments_.review: 100% YES,Chill multiplayer game where you just help each other to the end via sacrifice and abilities.Reminds me of journey but more structured around the multiplayer.Only thing I'd change is some of the character missions, some can be harder or easier depending on the lobby size and will take multiple attempts. The game is already a bit of a grind fest but this is where you feel it the most.We need emotes n cards :)

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute delight! Platforming around a map with a group of strangers seems like it would be a nightmare, but the game mechanics and levels facilitate working together and sticking together. Charming characters to play as, delightful soundtrack, and really gorgeous art make for a very enjoyable experience!

_childDocuments_.review: KarmaZoo, a unique game with a unique cooperative playstyle. A game you can enjoy at home or outdoors. A game that you can play with your friends, your family as well as strangers you may encounter in The Loop! KarmaZoo is a game that teaches the value of altruism and that helping others is it's own reward! With many varieties of characters to choose from, each level adjusts according to the characters players use, so whether you enjoy using an old favourite, or if you love a different experience every time, you'll always have a special role to play, whichever character you choose! You will find yourself platforming, collecting fruits and helping each other along the way, sharing and generating that sweet Karma. At the end of The Loop, you will find that love multiplies, and with that earned Karma, you can unlock and possess more characters as you play! Additionally, there exists the Karma Pass, which progresses as players all around the world collect Karma! The Karma Pass is contributed upon globally, and together, as Karma is being amassed all over the world, we can unlock new characters and new benefits as we go!Not a fan of cooperating? That's okay! There is also Totem Mode! Totem Mode is a mode that you can enjoy with the people around you in Couch Mode. Or you can also host your own lobby in Totem Mode. When in a lobby, you can share the secret code provided with other people and friends online to join you! In Totem Mode, you and up to 10 players will be competing against each other in a variety of different frantic and fast-paced minigames! You'll be using different characters suited for different minigames, you could be in a team or going solo, so be ready for anything!In KarmaZoo, you'll learn to communicate with players in ways you've never imagined. There is no voice chat or texting in this game, so you'll have to rely on emotes and your characters' voices to communicate with other players!KarmaZoo is game for everyone that can be enjoyed all around the world, supports multiple languages, is crossplay between all sorts of platforms and consoles, so there's something everyone, and you'll never miss out on anything, however you choose to play!So what are you waiting for? Buy KarmaZoo now, join us in The Loop and share the love with every blob you encounter! 🤍🤍🤍

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.For the record, this is technically a co-op-only multiplayer precision/puzzle platformer, but it is both adorable in its visuals and ruthless in its intent of having players stick together and do their tasks (especially when you're outright required to use one of the unique skills of a certain player) to progress in its time-restricted stages. Communication is minimal through pop-up baloons and basic directions and emotions only. Bad actors and "AFK farmers" can be quickly dealt with by vote-kicking and you can even tell the game to avoid matching up with any player for the duration of the next seven days counting from that moment.But, it is nonetheless amazing the variety of animals and their special interactions they've pulled up, and at this point in time we're not even seeing all of the unlockables since they're being rewarded for completion milestones on total progress of the entire playerbase. My only gripes? Some people just seem refusant to learn from observing others, others don't care about minimal objectives for the bonus stage effects, and yet another portion refuses to even attempt to collect the high bonus karma boxes in the stages. Also there's the problem of timezones conditioning the players you can match up with in the lobbies; as someone playing in Europe, it's easiest to get players at night, but you may run into the problem of having only 6 out of 10 spots in your game lobby at certain hours at best.But hey! We welcome more people into the Zoo. And it's sure to be a good time if you like platformers!

_childDocuments_.review: KarmaZoo is yet another of literally thousands of console ported 2D retro platformers infesting Steam and lowering the average quality of all video games everywhere.KarmaZoo is a handheld (Nintendo Switch)/console game that's also been put on Steam as a bit of an afterthought, as it's very much designed for the handheld/console gaming audience.This is obviously no AAA game, more of a B-, the Devolver brand gives this an air of popularity it otherwise wouldn't have (I think the industry needs to understand 2D retro pixel platformers have saturated the shallow end of the Steam shovelware section).  The idea behind this yet-another-bloody-2D-retro-pixel-platformer is you guide a group of animals through puzzle platformer levels, but the big difference is that other players can join you and help out. There's that co-op focus to the game, so you need to co-ordinate with your friends to play this... I guess that's easier for the developer than making a compelling single player experience.  Creating content is hard!  Why bother?Like I always say, if the only thing that makes a game fun is your friends, that just proves it's fun to spend time with your friends, and doesn't say much for the game at all.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.To make matters worse, while lazy, low quality pixel "art" has been used, making the game look bad, many elements of the game aren't done with pixelcrap... which accomplishes a couple of things.  First, it shows the developers perhaps could have done better and they knew it, so that's a major screwup.Secondly, it destroys any hopes the developer had of creating a "retro aesthetic" as their excuse for the lazy pixelart compromise... It looks completely inauthentic from a retro gaming perspective.  Visually, this is a hamfisted mess, a dogs breakfast of bad visuals, and this kind of laziness and poor quality should never be foisted on gamers.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.PC gamers will be insulted by the demand from the developer that a console peasant children's toy controller should be used, despite this being on PC.  Developers should try to be aware which platform they're developing for, and must never, under any circumstances dictate to gamers how their games are to be experienced.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?KarmaZoo has the almost scam-like price of around $10 USD, it's not worth it given the defects and shortcomings with the product, especially considering the sheer number of completely free, much higher quality games on Steam.For comparison, the $10 asking price for this game could get you games like "Torchlight 2", "X-Com: Enemy Unknown" or "Portal 2".  No pixelcrap is worth $10. If developers want to get paid the same kind of money as real game developers who know how to do graphics properly, they need to learn how to do graphics properly.

_childDocuments_.review: KarmaZoo is a multiplayer roguelike game where you among other players (up to 10) try to complete four random stages under a given timelimit. During each map there's also active one "event-card" which players vote to choose. These cards range from every player having boosted jump to soundtrack changing to kazoo nightmare back from 2010 South-Africa FIFA World Cup.Upon completing co-operative objectives and stages player gains karma hearts that can be used to unlock new characters that have special ability like frog having triple jump instead of double jump to spider that's able to make ropes down from spiderweb. These unlockable characters bring a good variety for each run though I wished unlocking some more hidden ones like  or  wouldn't cost between 10 to 100 thousand karma hearts as right now you on approximate gain 2000 karma hearts per run so unlocking something like alien is not really worth the time investment. What also becomes apparent after 10 to 15 hours of playing is that lack of level variate starts to show. While I understand how hard it must be to create levels in a world where one crucial character like  whom can only spin a wheel leaves the run all of a sudden I'd still wished we could have more different levels or have more challenging maps available for more experienced players and that way gain faster more karma hearts.Despite shortcomings in level variety after 10 to 15 hours of playing KarmaZoo is still one of the best (but not The Best imo) game's to release in 2023. If you loved PICOPARK's concept KarmaZoo is a great pick on it's asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, relaxed and casual fun that gets the good bits of co-op very well.However one thing that is souring my experience greatly is the random element of completing challenges for each creature you play as.I've spent probably around ~20+ attempts trying to get a Crystal Lock opened on my owl, and out of those I've gotten it once where it then promptly disconnected me so I couldn't complete the run. The other two times I was unable to do it because the puzzle demanded a faster character. The moment I swapped to another character I immediately got a Crystal Lock by pure chance, so it all just feels very infuriating. You're just hoping to first of all get it and then even getting to the three at times, and then you actually are competing with others to get these map-specific objectives. It is greatly at odds with the concept of co-op that I have to rush away from the team just to have a shot at getting them.I still recommend it though because it's unique, but I will update this review if am simply left without the ability to progress due to this RNG continues.

_childDocuments_.review: - - -Original release reviewSurprisingly fun game that brings back to mind worldwide, have-whatever-fun-you-want cooperative games like Noby Noby Boy. While you're unable to play with a single friend in a random online session (which the option would be greatly appreciated!), the game does let you create private lobbies so multiple friends can join in and play at the same time.It's a cozy time that anyone who just wants non-communicative fun can jump right into.- - -4/6/2024 Review change from Positive to NegativeIt's both rare and difficult for me to give a game a second look-over while my thoughts on it also sour. I think the developers of the game just repeatedly failed to address the issues of the community in ways that mattered while also failing to garner wide enough success to sustain the bleeding game population.Since the game depends on having a population to work off of and you can't invite friends into public lobbies, finding a full match nowadays is just simply improbable. I can't convince that many friends to buy a copy of this game to play just to fill a lobby unfortunately, which is one of the bigger reasons why I've come back to change my review. There should have been more focus from the start on including your friends because I personally feel that this is the first of the big 3 points that killed this game.The second sticking point for why this game failed in my eyes was a lack of taking the community's issues seriously and making changes to the game to remove those issues. I will list two examples of this: A good portion of challenges for characters were so blatantly selfish that it promoted acting mean otherwise you wouldn't be able to finish them. This directly contrasted against the developer's intended positive interaction philosophy, and it was never addressed in a way that soothed the community. There were multiple ways to solve this, two of which immediately come to mind:1. Making these challenges not take one singular loop to finish.2. Changing the challenges so that you don't have to be the one to physically pick these objects up.The other example is that the developers went great lengths to nerf groups efficiently farming karma earlier into the game's life. Flames generating karma only once? They used to generate karma per torch lit. People were having fun getting into coordinated squads to get the karmapass counter up. The developers nerfing these types of strategies had a visible impact on how people felt playing the game to farm karma.Finally, I believe the third reason why this game burned was because... there just wasn't substantial content developed for it post-release. There needed to be more levels, additional gimmicks added in, and a push to generate just... more in general. Maybe that's just a sign of the times. Without more reason to keep playing beyond just collecting karma, people will eventually move on to something that artificially draws their attention more, with more battle passes and multiple developer teams stressfully, constantly, developing content for their game. It's a shame that people moved on from this game so fast because the concept felt worth exploring in ways that were more substantial. ...I think it's okay to move on while looking back and saying you had a good time, but that the game is no longer worth purchasing due to the myriad issues you'll face just trying to get into a loop at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a simple, but charming cooperative platformer that is built off of the idea of being kind and respectful. With many games today seeming to build a somewhat toxic/negative community, it's great to see something like this. In terms of the gameplay, the game is simple to understand but also very dynamic. Since it features a massive amount of characters with unique abilities that can be unlocked as you play the game, you open up more ways to play, the more you play. An unfortunate side-effect of this is when you join a room and wish that you had chosen a different character since someone else might be able to perform the same task as you (break glass blocks, provide a platform, etc.) The game does allow you to "shapeshift" into the default blob character in order to still fit through small spaces, but I do wish that you could pick one small + one large character to bring two abilities to the table. The levels themselves are fun. Some feel quite simple, while others can be very challenging. The puzzles in a lot of these levels are often repeated, but the layout of them can vary their difficulty significantly. For example, a common puzzle involves arcing electricity between players to reach light-bulbs which when all lit, will allow everyone to progress. There have been some instances where my "team" has not been able to cooperate well enough and caused time to run out. With that being said, I do still wish their was a bit more variety in terms of puzzles. However it is cool that certain levels may only appear when certain characters are available. A level with a lot of breakable blocks may only appear if there is a character that can break said blocks, for instance.When you complete a loop, it feels quite rewarding. It doesn't take long to get enough Karma Hearts to unlock a decent amount of stuff, and you get rewarded more depending on how helpful you are. So as long as you are making sure that everyone is getting through every door, you shouldn't be worried about unlocking stuff fairly regularly. I do feel as if the progression of the game outside of characters feels non-existant. This is not the case, as there are goals for each character that supposedly affect progression, but I never feel like they do anything. Maybe I just haven't done enough yet. Lastly, a small personal gripe. I do wish that it required a few more players for the ending of a level before it would start a countdown to move on. Often times players are hunting down the remaining fruit in a level (which is used for potential bonuses), and are never given enough time to be able to do so. This is especially the case during the end of a loop as it only requires one player to end the level instantly. The last level does not have fruit, but can still have extra Karma Heart bonuses. After all that is said, I do really enjoy this game. It is a nice game to turn on for awhile when you just want to chill out and play a rather stress-free game. 7/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Problably one of the most creative games of this year. If you want to cooperate with others to get the goal, this is what this game is about. Each character has a unique ablility and you can use that to help each other and complete the stage.It's very interesting that all simple attitudes made to help each other are rewarded with "karma" (points in game).I was expecting that several people would not cooperate or get in the way of achieving the goal, but almost in all matches players knew how to deal with puzzles (and help each other) and try to get as many points as possible. And if a person get in the way you can just kick him out :)

_childDocuments_.review: Karmazoo, with its adorable characters and innovative gameplay, presents a fantastic concept for an online multiplayer experience. The game's charm lies in its ability to bring players together in a vibrant and whimsical world, fostering a sense of community and collaboration. However, like any online multiplayer game, it's not without its challenges.One aspect that stands out is the unfortunate presence of a few players who let their egos overshadow the cooperative spirit of the game. It's disheartening to see individuals attempting to dominate the gameplay, dictating the pace for everyone else and discouraging exploration and enjoyment. In a game like Karmazoo, where the joy lies in discovering the delightful surprises the world has to offer, these ego-driven players disrupt the intended experience.The developers have crafted a world meant for exploration and shared enjoyment, and it's dismaying when some players lose sight of this vision. Karmazoo encourages a sense of togetherness and mutual discovery, and the game's longevity is undoubtedly tied to players embracing this cooperative spirit.Despite the occasional encounters with such players, Karmazoo still manages to shine through. The game's potential is vast, and with time, it is likely that the community will self-regulate, fostering an environment where players can truly relish the enchanting experience of Karmazoo without the interference of overbearing personalities.In conclusion, Karmazoo is a delightful game with a captivating concept for online play. Its charm and potential for shared enjoyment make it a standout title in the genre. While the presence of some ego-driven players can temporarily disrupt the cooperative harmony, the game's foundation is strong enough to withstand these challenges. With continued updates and an active community, Karmazoo has the potential to evolve into a truly magical and inclusive online gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: My pick for 2023 Steam Awards Innovative Gameplay award.A 2D coop platformer with teamwork baked into the core of its design. Jump onto spikes to leave strategic tombstones for your mates, work together to solve puzzles and unlock gates, and stay close so your halo doesn't fade away.The roster of characters is adorable, with enough overlap and distinction between abilities to make them all feel unique. Playing a specific character increases the chances of seeing levels designed for that character's abilities, and being the required character on a level you understand is an incredible feeling.
