_childDocuments_.review: I think the idea of Nuclear Blaze is more compelling than the actual gameplay. To me it feels like the myriad difficulty settings and relatively short length are an attempt to compensate for core mechanics which just aren't very fun to play with. However, the short length of the base games can allow you to beat the game and still get a refund from steam even if you die quite a bit -- so that's one positive aspect.The checkpoint system is very odd, the player can respawn in the middle of a level but every door leading to the checkpoint is closed again instead of having the checkpoint save the world-state. Coupling that with instant death means making mistakes is rather frustrating.The game is from one of the devs of Dead Cells but I find the movement and controls to be significantly worse. Climbing down ladders has a weird delay due to a conflict with other control bindings and the game doesn't have the same "jump down from a ledge" system as Dead Cells. It also feels like the game would just be better without power-ups -- they're just there because... it's a game and games have power-ups? I really don't know.Anyway, I died quite a bit and still beat the game in under 2 hours. I haven't decided if I'll actually refund the game yet but it's quite tempting. Nuclear Blaze is probably best for kids that want to be firefighters. Just turn on all the assists and let them run through it. Even then a child may only get limited enjoyment from the game because it is very short.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw a short snippet of the trailer I knew I need to get this game because I always wanted a game where you play as a fire fighter. So I had high hopes for this one. But my expectations were surpassed. This is a fantastic game. It nails the feeling of a firefighter, to strategically put out the flames, burst into room by kicking in doors, the backdraft, the debris that falls down, collapsing ceilings. But be careful, the fire spreads if you are not quick enough.I completed the game in 2.5 hours so it's not a long game, but I prefer a very well made game where I enjoy every moment to a game that claims to have 50 hours of gameplay and half of it is boring. After you completed the game a harder mode unlocks where the level design gets changed so you can play through the game with a different set up apparently. I haven't played that one yet but there is replayability beyond the let's try it on hard mode. I also like that there is not a time limit on the levels. So it's not that if you don't put out the fire in 3 minutes it's game over. If you take longer, the flames will spread and you need to put out the fire in places you already extinguished it before, but thats it. So it's definitely intense but there is no frustrating timer ticking down. Oh, and when you finally put out the fire in a level, it's so satisfying that the room changes from a hot red color palette to a calm blue one.Fantastic is also the difficulty setting. You can choose to ad armor so you don't have a 1 hit kill or increase the water tank but that then decreases the difficulty setting. So you can freely adapt individual options to have a gameplay that is challenging but also satisfying for your custom needs. Very clever!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty short over all. Hold my beer mode does double he length and makes evel level more challenging but was enjoyable never the less. final boss was very annoying until i realized you can stay on the ladders under the jets of fire and easily hit the boss and all their.....balls.... *ahem* over all I'm happy with this buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: If you asked me what I would rate this before getting to level 14, I would have given this a 10/10. A great short to fill your evening for an hour or two.After reaching level 14 different issues start to show up that make the game frustrating and unfun. These include somewhat random deaths (something that kills you one run won't kill you in a second run) and when paired with minimal or no check points this results in a cycle of replaying the same section over and over and getting killed by random things. This issue would be completely eliminated with more check points (level 14 is most guilty of this and may also be the case for further levels I have yet to reach).I do think it is rather telling that there is a noticeable drop off in players that have achieved the latest achievements prior to level 14 (each achievement having a drop off of around a few percent) and the achievement immediately after level 14 that has a drop off of around 15%. This drop off would indicate players putting the game down during this period of the game, potentially due to this increase in frustration. (Edit: corrected 10% to 15%)Another issue I've noticed is that collected secrets are NOT recorded when collected when replaying a level. If the game does record it then there is no indication of it on the level select screen.Overall I do think the game is good and well designed, however it does have elements to it that make it frustrating and not fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Such a short and amazing 2d platformer! Great game!(+) The pixel art is absolutely gorgeous!(+) Gameplay is very simple but engaging, I enjoyed it a lot.(+) Extra content is great (Hold my beer mode!)(-) Due to 1 hit death, some sections can be quite bothersome as the checkpoints in the later stages are scarce.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet platformer about a fire fighter fighting fires. The game is very short but containing a fire and trying to find all the secrets was fun throughout. I could easily see this being expanded into something longer with more upgrades to find, but what is here is just a nice fun way to spend a couple hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on sale for 3.99€. Was it worth it? Yes, it was. Let me start with the negative. From what I have heard, this game started out as a Game Jam entry. I don't know exactly what they changed between that version and the one you can buy here, but they could have polished it up a bit more. The sound design is oddly disjointed, with stock sounds that don't work well together. I understand that you just take whatever fits for the jam, but later on they should have taken the time to find sounds that fit together. The escalation of the game is jarring. I don't want to spoil anything, but let's just say you get a twist that I don't think is necessary. I also put this down to the game's game jam roots. It was probably easier to change it up than to explore the core gameplay loop more deeply.Now for the positives, because I liked the game overall (at 60% off). The core gameplay is fun. At first it seems like all you have to do is aim water at fire, simple. Later, especially on the hard difficulty (hold my beer), you have to be strategic. Simply following the fire as it burns in a circle will never get you to your goal. Personally, I didn't use any of the accessibility features and didn't find the game too hard, but it's nice that they added them. The checkpoint system is fair most of the time. The game is short and sweet, knows when to end and doesn't overstay its welcome.If they ever make a Nuclear Blaze 2, or if someone else picks up the concept, I would hope for two things. 1) Lose the twist. A game about firefighting can be fun on its own.2) Explore the core gameplay more deeply. There are different types of fire retardants for different fires, a variety of protective gear, smoke can play a role, etc.It took me 6 hours to finish the game in normal and hard mode. I didn't find every secret area but I had enough fun with the game and I'm done.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Nuclear Blaze is a pretty fun indie 2D platformer as a firefighter investigating a secret lab. The music is really good, although there's not enough of it. The mechanics work and it was fun trying to solve some minor puzzles as you put out fires to reach the next area. The game can be completed in about 2 hours and I enjoyed the whole 2 hours.Now the frustrating part is after you complete the game, you can unlock "Hold My Beer" mode which is basically hard mode with some new paths you have to take. I was enjoying it at first but after you get about a quarter of the way through the game, it becomes too difficult due to poor game mechanics. You have to be incredibly precise in all of your movements, jumps, dodges, etc as you race to put out the first completely before it spreads. Even one missed jump, missed dodge, misstep will lead you to failure and have to restart the room. I don't normally mind challenging platforming but the jumping, climbing, and dodging doesn't feel precise enough for this kind of difficulty. I enjoyed the first run, I wanted to do the second, but I gave up on the second just because I thought the game mechanics weren't good enough for the difficulty presented. I still enjoyed the base game however, and would recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR really fun, great difficulty control from HMB mode to kids mode, good graphics, good music, good story, repayable.Phobias wasps, fire, claustrophobia(maybe).AMAZING game! Seriously transported back to the days of finding a new game on Nitrome except where Nitrome did one thing per game and didnt really branch out Nuclear Blaze is not so one note. Nuclear Blaze fully expands on it core mechanics and in some places exceeds the expectation. I do love the placement of the axe and it makes me want to replay immediately and then there the HMB mode!The graphics are cohesive tho once or twice i did find myself growling "wtf I couldnt see that." Pixel art typically gets labeled "retro" but I dont feel that label applies to this game. I cant be certain if its a limited pallet or not. I suspect not but the art feels deliberate, intentional, and well thought out in the same way a good 8 or 16 bit game was.The music is good and the change between fighting and done is very nice. I didnt notice it too much but it was always complimentary and I never felt like i wanted to be listening to something else.I have a habit of either breaking a game (in a bad way) or getting distracted to the point where I lose the thread and I lose interest or I have zero idea where I'm supposed to go.         I didnt get lost once in this game.          I can not overstate that. Ive gotten lost playing celeste...Difficulty wise this game is for all skill levels. With the ability to change behaviors of flames, give your self armour, AND the kids mode this game is most certainly a game for anyone. I played with a controller and its very will layed out.The game without giving anything away is very "SCP". While this game is for anyone its probably not for everyone. Some of the areas feel claustrophobic, there are large wasp enemies, and some of the areas feel for lack of a better descriptor are kinda creepy and on top of all of that the obvious one this game does deal with large amounts of fire.Though this game is short I'm writing this after finishing the game and looked into kids mode totaling in 2.2 hours this game feels "complete". Now I say "complete" because I could totally see a handful of games done in this setting. Perhaps a puzzle game as some one fleeing, a Metroidvania as a continuation of this story, or a resource manager where you are over a special division of fire fighters. HOWEVER, its not NEEDED. This game is complete and I cant think of anything that would make it better without ADDING anything.I cant wait to see what this studio does next!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet platformer. Just the right size to explore its concept, before it overstays its welcome.Can be a bit difficult in sections where it's one mistake = death, but it gives you options to tone down difficulty if needed (I didn't do it). It also has game+ mode after you beat it, which I haven't played so far, not sure if I will.Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: I still can't believe I enjoyed this as much as I did given the fact that I hadn't even heard of it before I saw it in the Fanatical bundle it was part of.A really refreshing game. The fire mechanic was very interesting and in the hold my beer difficulty it forces you to think how you will tackle extinguishing the blaze otherwise you'll run around in circles trying to extinguish the flames until you die.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Quite short, but fun game. The pixelart and gameplay are both very good and the small story has some interesting elements.I encountered some issues though were a checkpoint spawned the character to die immediately again and it took some button mashing to break free from the death loop.Recommended on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a few genuinely fun parts, beautiful fire effects and a nice sense of humor (yes there is a "this is fine" reference), but falls short with level design that just isn't interesting most of the time. The "hold my beer" NG+ mode is an improvement that adds some much needed dynamism to the game, but it's not worth slogging through the first playthrough for. The checkpoint system is also kinda buggy; sometimes I get kicked further into a level when I die, other times I get keys removed from my inventory, or have to redo scripted events that already happened. It really adds to the tedium.My biggest issue however is that the game feels generally choppy and unresponsive, despite showing me a constant 60 FPS. After checking the forums and some gameplay videos, I know I'm not the only one with this problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: First review ever here and its for a 3-4hr game...that I loved. It could have been 3X longer but in a world of sprawling rpgs and metroidvanias, this little bite sized nugget of pixe-lated goodness is a fun time. Colorful, great surf style music, cool sound effects, I was addicted 100%. Great on steam deck and PC, cloud saves work. Going to try the new game+ mode soon to play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Damn good. Simplistic concept and not too hard to program, but the design is absolutely key. Good environments, level design, and sound. I'd say holdmybeer mode is about as rough as a good Anjanath fight in Monster Hunter. Only gripe is that sometimes its hard to notice when fire is about to start below you and thereby gib you when you drop.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: The respawn system is a little odd, and the controls somewhat slippery, but they're both consistent at least.  Fun gameplay, challenging levels, multiple ways to scale the difficulty, and a story that is very intriguing with a lot of fun jokes worked in along the way.  I completed it in about 5-6hrs, so plenty worth it even at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Celeste, but you're a fireman!Honestly, it's pretty great. There's a lot of originality, thought and care that went into this. The mechanics are easy to pick up, and solving the "puzzles" of dousing fires is a lot of fun, and challenging. Plus there's a difficulty slider for even super young kids to play.My only critique is that it's very short. Even going through and 100%ing the game, I was left wanting a bit more.That stated, it's worth it. Especially for the $10 price tag. Maybe wait for a sale or you're strapped, but if you want a fun platformer, check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little puzzle platformer. The controls have a really nice chunky feel. As a fan of Dead Cells, it’s easy to see the shared DNA. It’s very satisfying exploring and putting fires out. It feels great to clear an area and get the calm colours on screen. The way that fires spread keeps the tension high until it’s released with that satisfying feeling.I have to give a huge shout out to Kids Mode. This is a very simple and friendly mode for very little kids to live out their firefighter fantasies. My boy is currently obsessed with fire trucks and fire fighters, and so I tried it with him for his first gaming experience. It was a huge hit, he was laughing with delight as he put out fires, and he hasn’t stopped talking about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Very short and very polished, Games like this should be played more. The premise is you play as a fire fighter and deal with fire to an epic scale, it's a "puzzle" game where you have to methodically deal with the fire or else you'll be overrun and perish. The kids mode is cute, The "Puzzles" themselves are mostly well thought out. ultimately it took me one 4 hour session which is fine to me but some may consider short so I would I advise buying on sale. 0 regrets buying
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty cool tiny little game that has one specific concept that it executes decently enough. Good sound, excellent pixel art and a fun fire fighting conceit but the artificial difficulty borne from simply denying you vital tools like "shoot water while on a ladder" doesn't really make for much of a difficulty curve. It's fine. It's over in a couple of hours and has some unwelcome faff but it was apparently made by a dad for his kid who loved firefighters so I'm not putting it down any more than this. It's cheap and short.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game - great atmosphere, and difficult to put down once started.  ...which makes it such a shame it's so darned short!  Given the dev's decent open-source level editor  I'm surprised there isn't an editor available - with that, and Workshop support, I'm sure we'd see many custom campaigns which would really extend its longevity.  There is a second play-through mode to unlock which makes changes to the campaign, but after that, that's your lot.For Steam Deckers: it plays , but does have slow down in sections.  The only section where this became an issue for me was the last boss.  I played under OpenGL as DirectX crashed.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Nuclear Blaze is a puzzler where you fight fires and feel like a badass while doing it. From a design perspective, it's impressive what was able to be accomplished by simply focusing on the dangers of firefighting, and incorporating the SCP universe for elements of fantasy. Expect tight puzzle design that encourages you to work against the clock, though there are nice break segments in between where new hazards get introduced and the plot thickens.I managed to beat the new Hold My Beer mode, and recommend it for anybody interested in a second go as it introduces new elements and routes to the game. However, there are also generous difficulty settings to make things easier if one would like, including a whole mode tailored to kids!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. 100% in under six hours. I especially like how the game tells you where the missing collectibles are.If I have to mention a downside, it would be the difficulty. I felt it was a bit too much on the frustrating/annoying side, with 1 hit KO. For the Hold My Beer mode I ended up changing difficulty options. It's really easy to kill yourself and end up repeating stuff a lot.The kid mode was super cute. I wish more games would let end a game by just having me rescue cats for five minutes as a little treat.Would buy a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever played, so much fun! Music, gameplay, graphics, all 5 stars! The only problem is that it was too short for me! I finished the game in a couple of hours, then it took me an extra couple of hours to finish the "hold my beer" mode which I expected to be harder than it actually was. I really hope that the dev is working on a sequel for this game!! I want so much more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Hold my beer mode is a great idea weighed down by ridiculous fire spreading that ruins it for me. Can't believe they charge $15 for this game on consoles lol, I paid 7 and while I enjoyed it it was BARELY worth itReminds me of the art style and clever level design of Carrion. Very satisfying and fun for the price (I got it on sale) although very short. I find it quite replayable tho
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: It is such a treat when I find a short game like Nuclear Blaze, one which can be finished over the course of an evening. The fire extinguishing game-play is novel yet based on familiar platforming conventions so there is a negligible learning curve. It was a delight from front to back, and didn't have enough time for me to get tired of any part of it. I highly recommend it. Other “evening long” games I have enjoyed include A Short Hike (highly recommend) Fossil Echo, Far: Lone Sails, and “The Looker.”
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Standard Mode:An excellent little game about firefighting! The standard campaign is very neat, with a lot of levels and little secrets. Some can be accessed from the get-go, while others need you to finish the game once. The firefighting mechanics are satisfying to use, and in the later levels, you need to be fast if you don't want the fire to spread everywhere. The default difficulty settings are kind of punishing, as you die with one hit, but it also makes you meticulous and efficient about what you are doing, making the game more enjoyable for me. You can change this and other difficulty settings if this or other stuff is frustrating; games are for having fun. The aesthetic is excellent; the pixel art, music, and overall game style create a cool space to navigate and move on. Also, its story and setting get a lot of obvious inspiration from , which adds a bonus to me because I love that universe. The opportunity to explore one of the  in this style and gameplay, with a lot of care about its lore, made it a good experience for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun puzzle platforming adventure! The visual style is awesome! It's like if Celeste was a firefighter. The game has good balance of difficulty (for me) and provides a special difficult mode which doesn't just makes existing aspects of the game harder, but also alters the layout of the levels. This is very cool. It also has a fair bit of humor.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Found some cats and fixed some security breaches resulting in fires. 10/10Don't expect a full blown epic adventure over several days. It's avery short game and has a moderate amount of replayability. Everything that's there is very tight and atmospheric. Really well made. If you're in for a bite sized action puzzle-ish game with lots of references  and some pretty funny easter eggs then go for it.Playtime for a seasoned 2D gamer ~ 1 - 2 hours on first run.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: A fireman game with some story, nice and easy but here and there some challenging gameplay. It is fun! The first playthrough ist like a "get to know" to the game, while the "hold my beer" runthrough is the more advanced. Same mechanics, but more difficulty. And in my opinion the difficulty is really well managed. Right in the middle. You will need some more tries, you will need some strategy, but everything is doable.Also how the cat collectives are handled is nice. You know in which levels you missed and can just get back to seek for the hidden path. No guides needed on my side. Due to the shortness of the levels it is good to find. So must a game be! And the happy cats you rescue are sooo cute.Also the child mode is a great idea. I have no kids to let them try it out, but I found it good and think it would be fun for them.So Pros:- Cool mechanics and advancing mechanis during the game- short levels, so you can have some quick fun- you are a fireman!Cons:- some situations I wish more checkpoints, because sometimes making one step too far you are instant death and have to do the whole level again. Q.Q- the range of the machine guns could be less, as I see /have difficulties in taking them out as they can shoot farther than iPrice is on point. Game is on point, gametime is on point.Would buy again!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game. Graphics are nice, plays like an old platform game with modern elements. Fighting fire is a joy in this game. Everything just feels right to be a simple yet enjoyable game. Difficulty is just perfect, as in I died enough times to find out how to complete the level yet not enough to get frustrated. Playtime is around 90 to 120 minutes, just what you would expect around this price point. I'd recommend getting this game if you like platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that I'm inclined to describe as 'mostly fun'.  The pitch is great, having you play a firefighter who stumbles across a secret facility while searching for the source of a mysterious forest fire, and for the most part, it's well-executed.  The levels around the middle of the game were my favourite, combining puzzle-like level design that emphasises finding the right sequence with which to approach the problem with timed threats that will explode if left on fire for too long, and of course, the propagating fire.  Fires are satisfying to fight, quickly extinguished by your hose in a way that makes it feel powerful, and the variety of threats, such as falling debris and backdrafts, is just high enough to keep things interesting.Unfortunately, this starts to fall apart in the game's final third.  The levels start to become lengthy and extremely complicated, which couples with near-instantaneous deaths to create a lot of frustration, particularly given that if a tile has just caught fire, it can be extremely difficult to tell that it's actually burning, and thus unsafe to stand on.  The dodge starts to feel less and less safe as well.  It covers a lot of ground, which is a good thing for escaping backdrafts early on, but toward the end it's more likely to just fling you directly into fire that's propagated behind you.  What's worse is that the game introduces highly mobile floating targets that you need to hit for a good few seconds to extinguish, or they'll set other things on fire as they move and pose a serious threat to you, not a bad idea on paper, but when you're trying to deal with them, you will
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Nice indie gem. You are a firefigter in a spooky secret base. You fight fires and rescue cats. Mechanics are solid and fun. Second unlockable difficulty with different route through the levels. Separate game mode for little kids (basically another very simple game). IMO one of the best indies this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun little 2D action/platformer(?) firefighting game from creator of Dead Cells.  It is on the short side (just over 2 hours for normal playthrough) but it does have a New Game Plus mode now and nice accessibility options so you can adjust as you need.  Played on Steam Deck, and while I had to use the OpenGL option (default option crashed on me each time), I still loved every minute of it!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute beautiful pixel art firefighter game from the creator of Dead Cells! Had lots of fun, about 2-4 hours of content. I played it 2 times. After you beat it once, you unlock the "hold my beer" mode. I would highly recommend to play this mode if you want the true ending and a bit more of a challenge. You can adjust the difficulty, and replay any level at anytime if you missed a collectable. I unlocked 100% achievements and really enjoyed doing so. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good little firefighting adventure. Delivers on the premise of battling an out of control blaze in a mysterious setting, with some frantic challenges and appropriate power-ups. Has a lot of levels with frequent checkpoints, and then a whole alternate replay route with more advanced challenges which is pretty cool. Well done. There aren't enough firefighting games and Nuclear Blaze shows why they can be fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Nuclear Blaze looks and feels great to play. The premise is simple and easy to engage with, you are a firefighter doing what you are expected to do, if you ever dreamed of being one as a kid well this is your chance. Difficulty wise, the game is flexible enough, it even has a kid friendly version so it is accessible to pretty much anyone and, if you are up for a more challenging run, you can unlock the Hold My Beer mode after the first run for some spicier firefighting action. Speaking of beer, this a great game to play casually while having one. I Especially suggest this game to cat lovers!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Really good and innovative platformer. The fire spread mechanic made some levels really difficult at the hardest difficulty, which required many tries to figure out how to beat it. Luckily the checkpoints are decently spaced so I never felt I lost to much progress. The accessibility settings are great too, and combined with the Kids mode allows anyone to play, regardless of skill level. Overall a great little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really different take on the action/puzzle dungeon crawler. It's really well done with nice chunky pixel graphics and music that blends into the background well. If had one con for the game, it's the distance between the checkpoints in some levels, but it's not so terrible. The option to bump the difficulty down is always there and user configurable, so that can take the edge off particularly difficult spots. Overall, fun game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic little game that any fan of pixilated 2d indie games will enjoy, and any developer would be proud to make. It's a very simple idea: you put out fires, and it's a lot of fun! The pixel art is superb. The fire animations are dazzling. The atmosphere is just right for a slightly spooky, but fun and cute game. It's short. About 2 hours of play. My only complaint is that there are a few times when the controls don't work as expected. You'll notice this when ladders are close to short cliffs. The power ups are a little bland. One of them is the ability to shot up lol! But still I loved playing this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Nuclear Blaze is an awesome game which expands on its concept quite beautifully, like so:CONCEPT: You're a firefighter, called to put out a large fire.QUESTION: What's the worst place you could possibly be called?  What's the worst place EVER to have a fire?  Like, where it would be catastrophically bad.ANSWER: [REDACTED]All jokes aside, the game is great.  It's a platformer with basically no enemies where your task is to combat a force of nature; having to deal with so many different problems at once feels frenetic and engaging.  I'd almost compare it to Diner Dash, but there's so much more depth here, and, between you and me, I don't really like Diner Dash.  The environments in this game are truly beautifully drawn, with brilliant use of color in the gameplay; the music, like the art, is fantastic, and the game changes the music up enough to avoid feeling repetitive.  (I don't play a lot of games with the sound on; play this one with the sound on, not because it's story-important, but because it's just worth it.)  The lore is fun and interesting, albeit borrowed from somewhere else; I still enjoyed it, especially noticing the game's hidden easter eggs.  I'm definitely going to recommend this game to some friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but this is a tepid recommendation. The game is fun, the premise is novel, and it looks nice, but I have a number of issues. First, the controls just aren't quite good enough. Far too often I'd die after I ended up just a little short or a little further than I wanted to be. Second, the visual language of the game needs work. It's way too easy to step onto a tile with fire because you don't see it there. Especially when the screen turns red it's hard to see where the fire is. Third, the game has interesting ideas but never combines them. There are several mechanics that are used a few times and then discarded. Fourth, the game is a bit short for $10. I generally appreciate shorter games. Too many games run out of ideas but keep going for hours. However, it's hard to justify $10 for this especially given my last point that more could be done with the mechanics the game has. Overall, I did enjoy it, but I can only somewhat recommend it. Maybe wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This is a puzzle(ish) platformer where you are a fireman who must put out fires in a secret military facility.Along the way you will gain new techniques and encounter new perils as you go through the map, things getting gradually more tricky. You'll confront fire, purple fire, electricity, firebombs, switches, pumps and values - you must conquer them all and defeat the final boss to win the day.It's a pretty short experience, one you'll be able to complete in a couple of hours, but it's a good challenge, that does start to ramp up in difficulty towards the end. Fortunately, if you get stuck, you can tune down the difficulty by giving yourself more shields (even immortality if you really like), so you'll be able to see the end of the game regardless of your skill level. I'd play it on the default settings at first though.A short game, but at £7 it's well priced and worth a look I think. I give Nuclear Blaze 8 radioactive burns out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game play, average play time to do everything in one run(hold my beer and all secret cat locations included) I'd say about 3-4 hours but if you missed a few things and had to go back I'd say like 5-6.Overall, I had a lot of fun and the mechanics are great, only comment is that if you die, all gates and doors you unlocked in that level before the checkpoint will have to be done again, so if you turn on some sprinklers, advance to a key card, get that check point and die, you'll spawn in the key card location but will have to go back and turn on the sprinklers again. Not too annoying but could be fixed and is something to take in mind.Besides that, I'm really happy with my purchase, hope to see more games from you in the future
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that's a little difficult to write about. Not because it's bad, or good, or whatever, but because there just isn't much to say. It's fun, sure, but overall it's pretty forgettable. Play, have fun, forget.Let's get one thing straight. The game looks, sounds and plays very well. The graphics in particular are wonderful with all the different colours mixing together in a symphony of flame and steel. The gameplay is unique as well; the only enemy you fight is the ever-spreading flame, and your abilities to fight said flame grow as you progress. The game gets tough towards the end, but you have a lot of options to adjust the difficulty to your liking. Extra hitpoints? Stronger water hose? You want it, you got it. No shame.But here's the thing. There is a story of sorts here, but it just falls so incredibly flat. Narrative design clearly isn't the dev's strongest point. It almost feels like it would've been better if there was no story at all, just your little fireman dude and the flames and the destruction they caused. But let's be honest: you're playing this for the hot fireman action, not the story. So does it hold up?Yeah, it does. Rolling out of danger, spraying that water, activating switches to contain the spread of flames with sprinklers, finding secrets and rescuing cats. It's fun. However, like I said before, it gets tough towards the end, and I had to restart the room many times due to some minor mistake. There aren't many checkpoints; it gets on your nerves rather quickly, if you play on the default difficulty settings (which I did). The final challenge in particular is annoying rather than fun. But overall I did enjoy myself quite a bit playing this, hence the recommendation.There. It's like a hookup from a club: it's pretty, it's fun, it's forgettable. But I'm hoping that this game will at least spread the idea of a firefighter game - I really like the concept. And if there ever is a Nuclear Blaze 2, I'll be sure to pick it up as well. As for you? Yeah, it's pretty cool, go get it. Just don't expect any paradigm shift from this one. Oh, and it's quite short, but there's a "Hold My Beer" mode for extra content after you beat the  main game. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice old-school-themed platformer "puzzle" game. It's not too difficult.The first run is very short though : 2.7 hours, a good chunk of it getting the only boss fight in the game.I've not tried the "Hold my beer" mode yet which will probably take about as much (unless it's insanely difficult)One think that I would have loved to know before playing : there is a "secret" area on every level. I only realized that from level 3 so I've missed (at least) one achievement because of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Very well done and polished game. Although it's rather short, it's very prone to replayability, (new game ++) and it has something that hooks you instantly. Graphics while being pixel art are amazing and controller (or Deck) support is perfect. Has tons of difficulty settings to adapt to anyone.Just a small gem that everyone can and must play
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice fun half-platformer half-shooter (sortof). The main story is the perfect length - about 4 hours long, and then you can spend some time finding the kitties, and then there's the extra New Game mode which is much harder and will take you a while more if you're into that sort of thing. I really enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: A short and fun experience. While the game can be frustrating at times there is a custom difficulty that allows the player to make the game as easy as they want even mid way through so if you get stuck you can make the game easier for that one part (there are no downsides or penalties for using this). There is a new game plus mode that makes the game good for another play-through. It is fun with a lot of Easter eggs to find. I will say that the game is very short. my first play though, getting all the secrets only took about 2 hours. But if you are okay with a short game give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Full written review on Twitter: TLDR- Very short game 2 hrs max but with Hold My Beer adds an extra 2 hrs totally 4+ hrs- The first playthrough is very easy but its perfect for children once you unlock Hold My Beer it gets harder- Very simplistic controls so easy pick up and play- It has Easter egg to find and cats to save- It has multiple ending- Pixel graphics and map design are colourful and look fantastic- There is a kid mode for age 3+
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Very creative game which works very well. Focus is almost entirely on puzzles, though the puzzles require you to work very fast to complete them. Racing to put out fires, and beating them, is very satisfying. Introduces new features at a steady pace, and all the features work together well with each other and with the core gameplay.Cons: This game is very short. The original campaign is about 1.5 hours, but there's a New Game+ mode that's different enough to be worth playing, and secrets in each level, so the total playtime for 100% completion is more like 4 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: basically a perfect version of the Beat It In An Evening indie game ideal, the aesthetic isnt New obviously but its well-considered for this mix of action and horror-adjacent (without ever really crossing over) uncertainty. the central mechanics, the action puzzles and territory capture, are that golden note of making intuitive sense esp in context, while also being a wonderfully unique! honestly i felt the atmosphere was compelling enough that i was a bit let down by the end reveal being played a bit Hokey and Jokey, but the final encounter is still a great climax to a lovely and memorable little excursion
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Nuclear Blaze is an action platformer about fighting fires. However, it is also a puzzle game in which the player has to stop the spread of the fire, by using choke points and activating sprinklers. The game is short, but very challenging, and constantly introduces new hazards and mechanics. To anyone who worries that the challenge would make the game not enjoyable, there is adjustable difficulty, such as allowing the player to take additional hits and have a more powerful hose. Keyboard controls are nice to use, and are rebindable. The one major negative of the game may be the price, as $10 may be too much for a game that can be completed in about 2 hours, but after the “Hold my Beer” update, which introduced NG+ that doubles the game’s playtime, the price is much more reasonable.

BUY IT!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: I brought this quite a while ago and really enjoyed it, I love the atmosphere and graphics and the difficulty is really well balanced aside from a frustrating final boss, having options to change the challenge were great too. The only issue I have is the length, it's really short. I beat the entire game at normal difficulty (except I made the hose a bit stronger near the final boss) in an hour and 45 minutes; while i didn't feel ripped off, I did feel like it ended a bit too early. I almost took a refund of the game since I could but I chose not to as I'm hoping some new content arrives eventually and it might be fun to replay someday.Buy it on sale, unless you have money to spare. I don't think it's not worth the price or anything, but paying £7 for 2 hours of fun is quite steep, for that price you can buy a bunch of much longer/more replayable games that will give you more play time for the same price. I think if it was 1 hour longer and just cost £4 I would be more willing to easily recommend it.I really hope it gets more content added eventually though, as I had a great time with this and would love a second campaign or something with this great art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a 2D platformer that's themed around firefighting. As might be expected from being made by some of the Dead Cells folks, the pixel art, music, and sound design are phenomenal. Absolutely no complaints there, it's top notch. Speaking of top notch, the game is fine tuned and feels fantastic to play. I'm not even a big fan of platformers and I enjoyed the game so much that I went back and played it the second time to rescue all of the kittens. Which is completely uncharacteristic of me. And, with it being about three hours long, it's just the right length to feel satisfying to play, show off all if its strong points, and wrap up without feeling like it's overstaying its welcome. Another thing I appreciate is how with the exception of one kitten, if you don't stumble upon the secret during the level, seeing the vent at the end tells you that you missed it and you can still go back to retrieve it. This is great balance between offering a challenge for secret hunters while not leaving more casual players out in the cold. Something that I definitely have to give the game props on is a whole range of accessibility settings. While the default settings felt fantastic to me, the ability to make the water go further, fires spread faster, have extra water capacity, and dial up or down the overall difficulty...this is fantastic attention to detail. Superb job there. The only complaints that I can think of is on my first playthrough, the final boss took a fair few attempts to clear. And, for one of the kittens, if you miss it while you're in the right part of the level, it's impossible to go back to rescue it when you see the escape vent.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: What an excellent game! I could not stop playing. It managed to make a platformer with very little to no combat, and yet feel like an action game, dangerous and exciting. All with an air of suspense and mystery about the environment.My only nitpick is that to uncover all secrets I have to start over.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! The fire extinguishing is very satisfying, and I like how it gradually adds more mechanics in each level and that you get to save kittens! The art, animation and game feel are great, and I love the options to make the game easier if you choose to use them. The kids mode is super cute too and I loved playing that for a very short session.As someone who doesn't have a lot of time to play games for fun, I appreciated these when I wanted to progress but didn't have time to do levels over and over. Ironically, I started another playthrough when I found out I didn't save all the cats.Highly recommended for a fun, tight and unique platformer. Full disclosure, you'll find me in the special thanks section of the credits even though I didn't work on the game in any capacity (Though the creator has cited my blog and videos as help in making the game's trailer)
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This game brings an entirely fresh experience on the classic 2D platformer genre. Sometimes it plays like a strategy puzzle where you need to decide where to put out the fire first, and sometimes it requires you to pull off some platforming skills and quick reflex to get yourself from being toasted. I also like the mystery in the game world, which takes some inspiration from the SCP Foundation.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: + Interesting gameplay mechanics, good music, good pixel art,+ Pretty challenging in the later levels.+ Kittens!- I was very disappointed with the story. It started out great, but... come on, REALLY? - The game feels too short. I hope they keep adding to it over time like the Terraria and Celeste devs did.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly one of the best Indie games I have ever played. There is not a lot of firefighting games out there, and this game makes me want more of it. I will be honest with you, I haven't really followed the story all that where. To my knowledge, something went wrong, a lot of people are dead. There's fire everywhere, and you need to put it out. You get abilities to help you with your water gear, and it will take some patience putting out the fires as fast as possible. Captain obvious here, but fire spreads. If you don't take it out quickly, it will come back. If i have to complain about something is the fact you can't jump downwards from a ledge, that's usually common in 2D games like these. Another complaint is the movement and feel of the character, it just feels off to me. You get this ability where you can twirl in the air and that really does help with moving faster and dodging fire, and obstacles.  The soundtrack is incredible, and it makes me feel like i'm fighting for my own life. If you are a fan of super Metroid on the super nintendo, you HAVE to get this game. You just have to. That is why I am recommending this game to everyone that wants a frantic but fun 2D platformer like super metroid, and if you're a fan of firefighting games. You are going to have a blast with this. There's nothing really bad I can say about Nuclear Blaze, and the price is so worth it. I think honestly, this should have been a $20 dollar game.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun and challenging. Reminded me a lot of Axiom Verge in trying to uncover the mystery through the story-telling. My one issue is the checkpoints. Some of the later rooms are pretty tough, and having to replay most of that level after only 1 hit was frustrating. Also, the roll is a little too aggressive for some of the late game area's that are tight quarters. Especially when trying to avoid the Loved the rest of the controls and highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun couple hours!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: this is a very fun, if very frustrating game that is far far far too short for its potential.  My full playthrough took around 2 hours, nearly 30 minutes of which was on a single  that just kept getting me.    It really feels like an unfinished thought that i want all of.  New mechanics are even introduced in the last _minutes_ of the game.  Hopefully there will be more levels in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game ever since the LudumDare Game Jam on itch.io, I only found the itch.io version because I was bored one night and was interested in what people had created based on the SCP Universe, it was amazing back then and it's so much better now. I bought the game two days after release and I played through the game non-stop and finished it in about two or so hours. It's a really well-made game, it has a remarkable amount of detail and quality. I also love the Kids Mode feature, it's an amazing feature for kids who love Cats, Firefighters and Firetrucks/Helicopters. Even though I'm not a kid I love lots of Emergency Vehicles with flashing lights.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! While it may run on the short side, every moment is a blast to have. The explosions that occur make the game feel cinematic, and the elements of opening doors leading to back-drafts made me feel like it came directly from said movie. I really loved the inclusion of the supernatural elements that are in the game, assuming you find the secret areas that have them, but I really wished for more length to the game as I'm having such a good time playing it.  I'm taking time to find all the secrets and normally I don't do that in games, as full completion stopped mattering to me a while ago. I really hope to see another game like this from the creator in the future, one that is much longer, but I appreciate all that this little game gives as it's got a lot of heart..
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Cool little platformer, feels a bit related to the Creeper World games in that you are pushing against a tide in place of fighting discrete enemies.I expected it to be more of a metroidvania, but it's definitely a very linear game so far. That works well, just wanted to call it out in case someone else has the same expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Nuclear Blaze is great! Artwork, music and gameplay all just clicked for me. The upgrades you find are used throughout the game which is great. Controls were simple and smooth and did not impede me in any way. The way the fire works is fascinating and leads to some frantic moments of scrambling back and forth utilizing your tools and skills to douse the inferno. I think replayability is pretty good with all the hidden areas to find. I also liked the lore of the game. It gave the game just enough story and flavor to intrigue me. I love the idea of a smokejumper getting mixed up in a paranormal cover-up. Without any of the normal horror trappings (blood, monsters, freaky visuals) this game managed to be decently creepy and I like that. My first playthrough was around 2 hours and I am starting a second to find secret areas. I think that's pretty good value for the $9 I paid for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Nuclear Blaze is a short, but enjoyable experience about a firefighter exploring a mysterious compound in order to eradicate the fires within.  I beat it on standard difficulty (without finding all secrets) in about 1.5 hours, but if you wanted to "get your money's worth", I imagine about 5 hours of fun could be had with difficulty settings and secrets combined.The music, ambiance, graphical style, and simple storyline are what makes this game shine, and those features alone make the game worth experiencing. The level of polish is very satisfying.Gameplay is simple but engaging, and introduces appropriate challenges throughout. As you go, you collect Metroidvania-style upgrades to improve your ability to clear areas, and the game introduces increasingly advanced puzzle-like elements you need to figure out in order to clear an area of all fires.  Once all fires in an area are extinguished, the containment doors to the next area open.  Can you get to the bottom of what's going on here?if the trailers look at all interesting to you, I's recommend playing this game to the end. If you liked the game Control, you might also enjoy this vastly different indie game. (i won't tell you why)
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10. An excellent title. Fast, fun, and adventurous.It leaves you wanting more as a barely 2-hour experience, but it's frankly a perfectly self-contained game in its own right, especially for the cheap price point. What you get is brief, but high-quality.If I had one major gripe with the game, it's how it handles death states. The act of merely touching a wall or floor on fire results in an instant death - which has subsequently lead to a handful of very frustrating deaths where I'd nearly finished a level, but then didn't react to a fire developing underneath my feet in time or made a bad jump and had to start it all over again. But again, it's a short title, so even its worst parts can only frustrate you for so long.If I could make a suggestion though, a heat meter to give you even a little leeway when standing on or around fires would be lovely.I'd love to see this concept developed into a bigger, meatier title - honestly even a sequel or two of comparable size. Not sure where you go thematically after...that, but there's so many more mechanics you could introduce and flesh out with a concept like this. Looking at the toolset and hazards of real-world firefighters leaves a lot of room for more ideas to flourish, especially in a fantasy setting like this. Hell, I wouldn't bat an eye at ripping mechanics straight out of Super Mario Sunshine.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fantastic game, where you play as the world’s toughest firefighter. Game play controls are tight, and the mechanics are straightforward – but it is a fun challenge to play. Pause menu gives you plenty of options to tune difficulty, most of it makes the game easier, but there is an option to make fires spread faster, which makes it much harder. Nice to see more games giving these types of options, opening the experience to everyone. The game also has a ‘kid’ mode which is much easier, and you just go around rescuing cats, which I think is also very cool. Lots of fun SCP Easter eggs, and cats hidden throughout the levels you can hunt for.My only real criticism would be that the game is a bit short (about 2 hours for me), but for the price point and an indie developer it’s definitely worthwhile. Would be cool to see a level editor and some workshop support for custom levels! Definitely looking out for the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely 2D platformer with gorgeous pixel art and atmospheric music. The mechanics and problem solving of firefighting were a complete blast and where I had the most fun playing this game. There is some combat in this game near the end and while I enjoyed each new mechanic as it was added to the game, combat was not nearly as enjoyable as the game's puzzles. The hidden cats were a nice touch and while I did not use it, the adjustable difficulty settings add a degree of accessibility and make me want to replay it on both higher and lower difficulties. This game is on the shorter side- I completed the campaign with 10/12 cats on 70% difficulty (the default) at around 3.5 hours. This said, it is a very tight and lean experience with each section counting. I will be replaying this again in the very near future. Check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: Remember the old Inferno flash games? This is not exactly like it, but it's kinda similar. And it's awesome through and through.Be warned, the game is very short. I got through it in about three hours and I'm pretty sure some speedrunners out there will be done with it in twenty minutes. Speaking of speedruns, the game has a speedrun timer that you can enable in the settings. Anyway it's worth every cent.I also love the Kid Mode. And I'm 25.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: This game was great! Looks great, controls great and the water/fire mechanic is great. There are secrets to find along the way, cats to rescue and power-ups to use. Increasingly level complexity and a nice atmosphere and light story to follow along.This is a really well crafted game and if you're looking for something short and sweet it will be for you. Kid friendly, too (content is all ages, and there are difficulty settings to make the game easier).I'm glad Sébastien (Deepnight) took this game from a game jam game to a full version. It was worth the effort.The game is worth the price due to the quality of execution across the board. It's a satisfying experience for the cost of a fast food meal.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really cool albeit a bit short.It has really awesome pixel graphic ,the music is just on spot and the gameplay is really fun.I managed to  finish it (and 100% in 1 run) in about 4 hourish(with alot of afking so about 2 hours i would say).The big plus for me is that it's developed by deepnight almost solo(maker of alot of awesome games like deadcells and die2nite) and the entire concept is fun.As cons the control schematic is finicky and could use some adjusments and the game maybe a little to short.Worth the price if you want to support a good developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Nuclear Blaze

_childDocuments_.review:
The world is burning.

Well, not exactly, but the whole region is.

As a trained firefighter, you're being air-dropped right in the middle of this hell blaze to investigate and look for survivors. But the unexpected presence of an unknown military facility might somewhat affect your plans.

Nuclear Blaze is a unique 2D firefighting game from the creator of Dead Cells, with all the devastating backdrafts, exploding walls and sprinklers you could expect. Fight your way through a mysterious facility and try to keep the blaze under control.

name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly
detailed_description: In a time where people are isolated from each other, Coffee Talk is a place where we can reconnect over a cup of warm drink. It’s time to revisit your favorite late-night coffee shop and reconnect with your fantasy friends over a warm drink or two. You are a barista, and your customers aren't always humans, listen to their stories and influence their hearts with a warm cup of coffee or two. The game features: Brew Warm Drinks Mix a combination of ingredients, such as tea, ginger, mint, chocolate, coffee and many more. Experiment and uncover secret recipes, change people’s lives by serving drinks that will warm their hearts. Create Latte-Art Masterpieces Show your creativity, draw your own latte-art masterpiece with our in-game fluid simulation to decorate your drinks. Chill Lo-fi Atmosphere Immerse yourself in the relaxing coffee shop atmosphere. It’s raining outside, brew yourself a warm drink, play that lo-fi chillhop beats, and listen to the coffee talk. Urban Fantasy Cappuccinopunk Set in an alternate present-day Seattle where humans, orcs, elves, and other races have been coexisting since the beginning of time. Explore the world through the stories told by your customers one cup at a time. Hangout With a Diverse Cast Meet quirky and interesting characters, such as; Baileys the elf freelance graphic designer, Lua, the succubus bisdev executive, Myrtle the orc game developer, and more. Listen to their stories and influence them with a warm drink or two!

short_description: Dust off your coffee machine and prepare your warmest smile to meet your customers again in the second episode of the much loved coffee brewing and heart-to-heart talking simulator; Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly.

_childDocuments_.review: I had already commented on the first game, how much it made me want to open a night coffee, to warm the hearts or cool the ardors that haunt us, once the sun sets. It’s been three years. I grew up, and the characters too, they also continued their lives, their adventures, and their reflections on love, immortality or even on why sign a contract if it is not advantageous for you despite your passion ? (Aqua, we see you)I loved it. I cried. This game is successful. Plunged me back into the person I was, 3 years ago, I too evolved. I, too, have had my dreams accentuated or realized. And to them too, our fantastic characters, what I say, our friends for a game. The fact that we never see the physical of our character and the extraterrestrial knowledge is fantastic, it represents us, we give it our first name, we can only imagine being him since he has no defined appearance, even less gender. Thank you for growing me up, reminding me that my dreams during lockdown are not just dreams in vain, I can and MUST make them happen. Just because the world won’t wait for me, like Baileys didn’t wait for his family’s approval, just like Aqua didn’t wait for his favorite publisher to question himself, or just like Silver or Neil, didn’t wait for love and learned to discover himself, as the bright person he is. Thanks to TogeProductions, thanks to you, the characters of Coffee Talk, and thanks to the players of the game for allowing an episode 2. Thank you for these emotions, this parenthesis of life, poetic, sometimes angry, sad or crazy insane.We are capable of the best, believe in your dreams and don’t wait until the next day to get started. I wish you the best. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely play games of the same saga one after the other, because I've found that they put me off a bit and I usually end up leaving the second title half finished, or I force myself to complete it. However, when I finished Coffee Talk and received the opportunity to play its sequel, I immersed myself once again, fully and without hesitation, to this fantastic universe so relaxed and jovial. I must say, being a narrative and enjoyable experience, I didn't feel that usual overwhelming feeling, and I'm very glad since both titles have been truly magnificent. Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly, is the second installment of this very special game that has touched many people since its release. It is a title that presents itself as a visual novel with simulation elements, putting us in the role of Barista (the main character whom we can name, and whom I will refer to as him for simplicity), owner of a very peculiar coffee shop that only operates at night, and which is frequented by creatures and people of all kinds. I will try not to repeat myself too much with respect to my previous review (from Coffee Talk 1), The  follows the same pattern as in the first installment, being told as a set of stories that involve the various characters who visit the Coffee Talk café. On this occasion, we’ll be able to glimpse a little more about characters that previously did not have so much prominence, such as Jorji, the neighborhood policeman and proud father, who escapes from time to time to have a hot drink between his nightly patrol days. This gentleman will follow the trail of acts of vandalism against cars, and little by little will be involved in a couple of somewhat paranormal events that will make for a strange case.On the other hand, new and curious individuals will make an appearance in our establishment, such as Lucas, a ‘satire’ influencer who focuses on trends, or Riona, a ‘banshee’ whose dream is to become an opera soprano. This particular duo is quite prevalent in the 'story', and among the new characters they are certainly my two favorites. Lucas is very charismatic, but has moments that filled me with tenderness, and Riona is somewhat shy and pessimistic, but will open up with us little by little. Among other new characters, there is also Neil's (an alien from the first game) sister who has come in search of her brother and to learn more about our race.Other of our dear old customers will also have their moments, such as Lua and Bailey, the couple that against all odds has finally reached the path of planning their wedding; or Hyde, the vampire model who is already a bit bored with his job and is looking to broaden his horizons. These and many more stories are woven thanks to the atmosphere of our coffee shop, a special corner where people can feel at home, and we as Barista will be in charge of welcoming them and giving them warmth. We'll also be able to unveil some secrets and uncertainties that we were left with in the first installment, such as the origin of the Barista himself, which kept me in suspense on more than one occasion. It is, as in the first installment, a story full of interesting, comical and emotional situations, a tangle of very nice tales and that although they are set in fantasy, they feel very real. A narrative that captivated me yet again.The  does not change much with respect to the previous title, we can continue reading and interacting with our customers by preparing them drinks in an enjoyable mini-game. However, we’ll have some variety that will keep things interesting, since we’ll have a new mechanic where we'll be presented with objects, whether by their owners' own will or not, and we'll have to return them or pass them on to those who need them. This must be done at the time of serving the drink, and on more than one occasion I have lost the opportunity to serve the coffee with the corresponding item next to it; I recommend not to follow my steps, and pay attention! Otherwise it will happen to you as it did to me, that at the end of the game I was told the following: "you may have completed the story, but you have not appreciated all its nuances".Another thing that stands out a lot this time is the new repertoire of ingredients that we'll have at our disposal when creating new mixtures. In particular, we'll have hibiscus and anchan tea, spices that provide a very colorful aspect to the drinks we can prepare. Hibiscus gives a very lively reddish tinge, and anchan, on the other hand, creates a bluish coloration that conveys tranquility, and these details will be important when it comes to fulfilling orders; after all, these two herbs will be very popular among our clientele, so it is worth taking note of the drinks we create with these ingredients.A detail that I didn't mention in my previous review, more out of absent-mindedness than anything else, is that depending on whether or not we get the drinks we are asked for, will be how the 'stories' of the characters end, in a good or bad ending, so to speak. It is something that curiously did not give me "problems" in the first game, but that is much more noticeable in this second installment, as it has more variety with respect to the arcs of each of them. Customers play more with your memory, asking you for drinks like "the one you served me that day", and sometimes... they even reference requests from the first installment, so evil!In addition to coffee and recipes, we'll have a new function in our app "Tomodachil", in which we'll be able to see the 'stories' of our customers and leave them a 'like' if we want; it’s a simple detail I appreciate it, as it is entertaining to see what kind of interactions there are between the characters in this social network. Just as in real life, they disappear the next day, so you have to be attentive in case you don't want to miss one of them. Apart from that, we still have the recipe book, the music player app and the diary, although Freya no longer writes in it. It is not that there is a great revolution in gameplay, but I have been entertained as I was entertained in the first game, and that's what I find most important.The  are just like the previous one, a detailed and very beautiful pixel style. Some of the characters will have new aspects, such as hairstyles or clothing, and the environment is still that cozy coffee shop we are used to. I remember mentioning that I regretted not being able to glimpse those creatures passing by on the sidewalk, through the shop windows, and I am grateful that this time we could meet Lucas and Riona, these two new races and individuals who have a phenomenal style. The  returns with a vengeance, boasting delightful songs of various rhythms; I noticed the occasional livelier one, such as a very fierce piano tune, but they still don't leave out the melodies that convey tranquility and relaxation. There is little I can say about this section, since I would be repeating myself too much in respect to my previous review, but I want to make it clear that it is still an excellent soundtrack.In , Coffee Talk 2 ~ Hibiscus & Butterfly  is a second episode that, with a stronger than strong story, once again brings us all kinds of emotions between conversations and endearing characters. The strong point has always been its storytelling and the interactions between its clientele, and it's beautiful to be able to see the relationships that have formed between the characters that started as cafe acquaintances, to the point of calling each other family; and these moments touched me to the core. The gameplay did not lose its touch and added some other entertaining mechanics, and the audiovisual aspect maintains the impeccability of the first title. Totally recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wonderful, just as good as the first one, if not better in terms of writing. Having the foundation of the first game to use as a stepping stone really helped elevate the writing and expansion of returning characters. Here is my review after my first play-through of the game. I normally review games looking at both negatives (the bad) and the positives (the goods) and honestly I only have one negative about this game and it has nothing to do with game play. It is the title.I have seen many wonder if this is a dlc to the first game rather than a stand alone game due to how they titled it. The "episode 2" part needs to go. Just Coffee Talk 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly" would have been better. The episode part just throws people off. And on the other end there's really so much positive to say about the game. The writing in this one is outstanding. The artwork, even though in the style of the first, looks just as wonderful if not better too! I love making drinks and guessing the drink combo's that the character orders. Also like the first game you input your name at the start of the game and the characters throughout the game refer to you by your name. A nice little touch to keep you immersed. You never see yourself in the game, it is always from your perspective. However this game had a few comments about our character that made it very interesting about who WE are. In the second game you can influence the story more than the first game. By doing certain actions, like getting their drinks wrong or right, or forgetting to give them certain items,  you will have some different outcomes in how the story progresses for good or bad for some of the characters. You may even stop seeing customers if you mess up their drinks too often! Or if you give them the right drink or the right item you will see extra story content for some of the customers.  I had no crashes and the game supports widescreen. All you really need is your mouse to play. There is some light comedy, some heartfelt moments and some serious undertones to some of the characters' stories. A great game told through the stories of your customers as you, the ever present, caring barista listens on. A hug of appreciation for Mohammad Fahmi (may he rest in peace) and his entire team for forging ahead to bring the world of Coffee Talk to the fans again. It was well worth the wait and I think he would be so proud of the final game and the entire team.  I recommend both games, and honestly encourage everyone to start with playing the first one. For those who are returning to the world of Coffee Talk, enjoy your adventure! ☕

_childDocuments_.review: UNMARKED SPOILERS FOR COFFEE TALK 1If there was a 'neutral' option I'd pick that. I played the first Coffee Talk because I wanted an experience like va11halla. The game ultimately disappointed me quite a bit but I could see the potential in it and I was looking forward to giving this one a try. The mechanics and story beats between the two games are largely very similar. This one has a few more drinks and the ability to give items to patrons. Honestly I strongly recommend playing this game with a guide. Replaying days to get drink orders correct is a pain in the ass due to the fast-forward feature not actually fast-forwarding through character animations and the like, and the expanded menu and choices mean little in terms of branching plot content. The good options are objectively more interesting and satisfying than the bad ones (at least from what I experienced).The story and character selection has somewhat improved as well. I found Freya from the first game to be fairly obnoxious due to her constant meta conversations about stories and narratives. Glad to say that she's pretty much gone. The new characters aren't the best and some of the storylines are utter bores, but at least there's nobody in the cast I hate. In my review of coffee talk 1 I expressed my disdain for Lua and Baileys' story and the very forced allegory to racism and inter-cultural marriage. A lot of people mistook this as me hating the game's 'SJW agenda' or something but I have no problem with games tackling contemporary political issues. The reason it was such a bad storyline is because it failed to be interesting within the context of its own world. See, coffee talk has this problem where it gets so caught up in allegories and dialogue that it seems to forget that it is supposed to be a game in its own world. Succubi and elves have no obvious cultural differences. Any historical context simply isn't mentioned. The language they use to talk about their conflict far too strongly resembles the language of our world despite Bailey and Lua literally being different species. I know this isn't Coffee Talk 1 but this tangent applies to the alien storyline in Coffee Talk 2. Between the talk about being accepted, changing your appearance and pronouns to better fit with who you are, and coming out to the person you're dating. Silver (previously Neil) is a somewhat obvious allegory for gender identity issues. However when the allegory is this intentional, it starts becoming a little weird that your stand-in for a trans person is literally an alien being pursued by the men-in-black because... well actually they never give us a good reason why. It's like this story was written as an allegory first and a story in the world of coffee talk second. However this story comes across as extra bizarre because Silver and the other alien spend a lot of time teaching you about the nature of their species. If you remember the reveal from the first game, you literally are one of these aliens. Why are they telling you all this? Coffee Talk really has a tendency to use most of its dialogue for the benefit of the player while sacrificing more organic conversation. Gala and Hyde remind you explicitly of their long lifespans multiple times. Why? Your player character has talked to them a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of times. This should be common knowledge. It's like if you asked a Chinese bloke what he had for lunch and he told you "I had a delicious bowl of white rice, the staple crop of us Chinese, which I ate with chopsticks, the cutlery of choice for many Chinese folk." It's bizarre and immersion-breaking. Even Jorji's storyline about the mysterious spooky vandalism cases has shades of this. Some of the conversations very quickly stop feeling like conversations and start feeling like a Wikipedia page written in casual speech. Although I just spent several paragraphs ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the game, it's not all bad. The newer sprite work is subtly but noticeably an improvement. The first game's art was fine, but some sprites looked more like low-res paintings than active uses of pixel art. Coffee Talk 2's sprites lean a lot more into the pixel art aesthetics. In some places such as the sprites of the drinks, and pictures on the social media app, the improvements are a lot more obvious. A lot of the casual conversations in this game unrelated to the main plot threads have very strong character building. Lua and Hyde specifically get fleshed out a lot in this game, and are much better for it. Rachel was one of the stronger characters from the 1st game and although she only shows up here and there, she's still a lot of fun in this one. The new characters do manage to have their share of interesting moments as well. In spite of everything, I do think this is an improvement over Coffee Talk 1. If you liked the first one, I am certain you will like this one. But I still think it is too flawed to earnestly recommend.
