_childDocuments_.review: I first found Coffee Talk episode 1 on itch.io, and after playing it, episode 2 was an instantaneous buy! I dearly love the characters, and while episode 2 is able to stand on its own if you haven't played the first game, you're doing yourself a major disservice! Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly builds beautifully on what made the first game great, and brings in a cast of characters new and old with interweaving storylines.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED this game, I played the first one as well and thought this built upon the world and characters in a really enjoyable, thoughtful way. Unlike the first game, this one introduces routes with a perfect, bad, and good end. I don't typically enjoy bad endings and just want a happy ending so I didn't explore the alternate routes, but it's still just as enjoyable as the first game. The music is awesome, there's an odd twist at the end of the perfect ending just like the first game and I think you're meant to replay it to get more insight on what's going on there, but I might take a break before doing that. All in all, great game and if I muster up enough heartlessness I might go and see what the bad endings are. TLDR: PLAY THE GAME I LOVE IT
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I try to like visual novels, they often fall flat for me. Coffee Talk though, I LIKED the character, their interaction with each other and making coffee. While playing this sequel, I also noticed that I LIKED the lack of "routes" as well. A lot of visual novels and otome games forces you to play all the routes, the good and bad ending, etc. one way or another, either by hiding extras or secret endings behind a wall of "complete all routes" or steam achievements. I noticed with this game that one of the (many) reasons I liked Coffee Talk 1 was the LACK of routes. Yes, there was an extra scene, but you didn't need to go back and play the WHOLE game to access, just replay 3 specific day that the game hints at and voila. In Coffee Talk 2, they didn't do that. And I hated it. Like I said, I LIKE the characters of Coffee Talk, they are like friends or acquaintances that you quietly listen to them talk and enjoy being in their presence. And the fact that I had to force them to a "bad end" was...hard. I wanted to see them "happy", period. I didn't need to see them "unhappy" and it made the last bit of game an annoyance. Just like how in otome games, I don't necessary like all the love interest, but am forced to play other's route just to see the secret ending, this felt like that.Anyways, the only reason I'm giving it a thumbs up is, like I said, I loved the first game, I liked the characters and I was happy to see their "happy" ending. But Coffee Talk 2 pales in comparison to its predecessor.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: The game retains its signature art style, a charming mix of pixel art and soothing color palettes, perfect for creating that late-night café ambiance. The new additions of the hibiscus and butterfly pea ingredients give you even more creative freedom to craft drinks for your customers. This slight gameplay enhancement adds an extra layer of depth without overwhelming the relaxing nature of the game.One of the most enjoyable aspects is how the characters feel even more fleshed out. Each customer comes with their own unique problems, and it's fascinating to see their stories unfold over time. The dialogue feels authentic, capturing the warmth and sincerity of casual, late-night conversations. The mix of mundane and supernatural elements works incredibly well, making every character and their personal struggles relatable, whether they're an elf, an orc, or a human.The soundtrack deserves special mention, as it sets the perfect mood for unwinding after a long day. The lo-fi beats create a calm, immersive environment, which pairs well with the storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: Pains me to say this, but just simply not as good as the first game. The Lua/Bailey relationship tension plot gets reused, aqua and myrtle are totally shafted, and most of the new characters just aren't as charming or interesting either. They also ditched my favorite character Freya, which ordinarily could've worked great for focusing on the other characters more, but the story just didn't hold up this time without a sidekick to bounce stuff off of.However, I did enjoy the story with Jorgi a lot. I also loved them locking in with having Silver be a trans allegory, and Riona was a lovely new addition, even if I didn't care for her story line with Rachel and Lucas.The hinting at deeper lore between Silver and the Barista continues, albeit with very little new information actually given. That was kind of disappointing, especially considering a third game is far from confirmed. Maybe if it were more subtle I'd be okay with it, but the lack of payoff burns a bit, especially when the rest of the story didn't hold up compared to the first one. At least the resolution with the cat was heartwarming and sweet (RIP Fahmi).
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Coffee Talk 1 and VA-11 HALL-A so trying this game was a no brainer. After playing it I think I like just as it much as the original CT. The stories pick different beats from the original game, the new characters are interesting, and the secret reward for 100% made me absolutely bawl once I learned the story behind it. If you're looking for an amazing visual novel then this is  what you need. Just make sure you've played CT1 or much won't make sense. Also once again Andrew Jeremy with the absolutely divine soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Coffee Talk (and I did), then this is more of the same, with a few little twists for good measure. I'm glad I replayed Coffee Talk as a refresher before launching in to Hibiscus & Butterfly, and would recommend against playing this one without playing the first, as there is an assumed knowledge of the characters.As a bit of a nitpick, I didn't like the new music's record crackle sound effect, I found it off-putting compared to the versions used in the first game's OST. However with plenty of music on offer, this was a minor quibble. On the other hand, I appreciated how the game lets you know when you have and have not seen everything it has to offer - very handy.Overall I had a thoroughly enjoyable time playing through this game. If you like cosy narratives, then Coffee Talk 1 and 2 have you covered.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: My friend gifted me this game for my birthday as they knew I've been wanting to play it for a while now!I've only got to Day 6 when i making this review, but it's already so good!! The character design, the music and the story has been incredible!I definitely recommend to people who are looking for a game that is calming, but has that *tea* drama you are wanting in day to day life!
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent sequel to an excellent Visual Novel. It shares the same issue as the first game, in that you don't get an index of specialty drink recipes to choose from but rather must experiment with limited tries. Compare this to VA-11 HALL-A's index of drinks, and using the info there and stuff you have to pay attention to in the dialogue to tell the observant player exactly what drink to make.That said, this sole issue is again easily bypassed by using a guide. _childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: [Recommend playing with headphones for the full coffee shop atmosphere] What an incredible game and sequel to 'Coffee Talk', the continuation for some characters' storylines to be further developed and evolved to include the new characters has been done very well.The music really creates the environment of actually sitting in a coffee shop along with the sound effects too, of chairs scraping or coffee machine beeping-the attention to detail has been thought through very well. And artwork is amazing again and just really goes well with the theme of the game.It is slightly tedious to re-play through the game multiple times to unlock all the different endings but its definitely worth finishing the game to view all the different artworks in the gallery. _childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: The first Coffee Talk had a special place in my heart as it was my introduction to this genre of games. I had some high expectations and man did it deliver. It's very reminiscent of the original but also fills you with a sense of nostalgia seeing these characters grow beyond their story in the first game. The absence of a certain original character is definitely felt, but it's understandable why they weren't included and I think it was a very respectable decision. Overall, Hibiscus and Butterfly was carefully made with love to exceed all expectations of the original's fans. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: Cried multiple times, during this and part one. I don't remember the last time any game has made me feel this. I came into this expecting another shallow cutesy simulator without any soul and found depth so vast was I spent the last four days drowning in it to the point of finding it hard to break myself away from the screen. _childDocuments_.review: To call this a lifechanging game would be an understatement. _childDocuments_.review: Coffee talk 2 is quite a nice follow up to the first game, introducing new characters and new problems for our previous characters. The game is quite a basic sequel nothing crazy to change up the game but I felt that sometimes the game could have actually used more, such as dialogue options to get more out of each character instead of the more or less binary option of "give them the drink they asked for, or don't." Just a bit more player choice in the game would have been nice to appeal to the whole interactive part of the game. But it does make up for it with pleasant stories that are quite low stakes but quite enjoyable. The game also continues a trend from the first game being a very well handled dealing of racism. Multiple characters in the story will deal with racist stereotypes being flung at them, but I won't get too deep into that stuff as I'm not the person to talk about it, all I can say is it handles these themes with tact and care. Much better than what I'd directly compare it to being bright, which the less said the better.Anyway it's a simple story with simple graphics, simple gameplay, and simple music. But the culmination is absolutely a relaxed vibe that is terribly enjoyable. I won't blow this game out of the water because it's just a barista simulator that takes place in a modern fantasy setting and I feel like it handles it's setting and world very well and uses it effectively to tell good stories.I do have two little complaints they aren't that huge and definitely don't serve as a deal breaker. The first is that at the end of the game it suggests playing through it again to "see things from other perspectives" which considering that the achievements state very binary bad, normal and good endings for each story felt a bit silly considering I got everyone's happy ending. The other is that I personally have a hard time picking out any one song, they feel at least to me to blend together and not stand out. I'd struggle to differentiate any of the songs, but maybe that's just me.Anyway good game worth it for the nice vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

For example there's this prompt of warm and very sweet drink. So I make coffee-cinnamon-honey. Very warm and max sweetness. But apparently it's not the right answer. the answer is any warm base with two stack of honey. So I made tea-honey-honey, equal warm to coffee-cinnamon-honey, but one point less sweeter. But that is the correct answer. There's a lot of cases like that, it make the drinking game more frustrating. I'd say still recommended but the first game is way better,

_childDocuments_.review: I had to stop in the middle of playing to type this review since I want to let others know just how much this game means to me. _childDocuments_.review: Title: "Coffee Talk 2: A Brew of Social Awareness"Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3/5)Step back into the comforting world of Coffee Talk 2, where the aroma of coffee mingles with thoughtful discussions on modern society. However, it's worth noting that the game's dedication to addressing contemporary issues, often described as having a heightened "social awareness," continues to prominently shape its narrative. This approach, though laudable, may impact the experience for those seeking a more lighthearted escape.Similar to its predecessor, Coffee Talk 2 subtly delves into societal reflections, exploring diverse perspectives on contemporary themes. While the intention to foster inclusivity is appreciated, some players might find the delivery to be more overt than they anticipate, potentially affecting their enjoyment.It's important to emphasize that this critique does not diminish the importance of the themes explored in the game but rather raises awareness of the potential divergence between player expectations and the narrative focus. For those seeking a more carefree or straightforward gaming experience, the continuous emphasis on societal reflections might feel more pronounced than desired.Additionally, the absence of romantic opportunities for the player character remains a consistent feature. In a landscape where some games offer romantic relationships as part of the player's journey, Coffee Talk 2 chooses to maintain a different approach, potentially leaving some players wishing for a more inclusive stance on character relationships.In conclusion, Coffee Talk 2 retains its commitment to addressing contemporary issues in a more subtle manner, yet this may still be perceived as overt by some players. The three-star rating reflects the game's potential to polarize audiences based on individual preferences regarding the integration of socially reflective themes. Whether you appreciate the continued exploration of societal perspectives or find it somewhat intrusive will depend on your personal gaming expectations. So, whether you're seeking a thought-provoking experience or a more carefree atmosphere, Coffee Talk 2 offers a brew that may not suit everyone's taste.

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk 2 Review: A Warm and Soothing Cup of StorytellingCoffee Talk 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly is a heartwarming and relaxing visual novel that serves as a delightful sequel to the original Coffee Talk. Set in a fictional Seattle-inspired city during the early 2000s, the game follows a new barista named Isla as she interacts with a cast of charming and eccentric characters, brewing them drinks that subtly influence their lives.A Familiar Yet Fresh ExperienceCoffee Talk 2 retains the core elements that made the original so endearing, including its soothing soundtrack, lo-fi aesthetic, and emphasis on character-driven storytelling. The game's pixelated art style is beautifully rendered, capturing the cozy atmosphere of the café and the vibrant personalities of its patrons.One of the most notable improvements in Coffee Talk 2 is the expanded social media feature, Tomodachill. Players can now actively engage with the characters by liking their posts, commenting on their updates, and even sending them messages. These interactions provide deeper insights into their lives and personalities, adding another layer of connection to the game's narrative.Brewing Stories with Your CoffeeThe heart of Coffee Talk 2 lies in its interwoven stories, each character's narrative unfolding as you serve them their preferred beverages. The game's branching dialogue allows players to personalize their interactions, influencing the course of each character's story and potentially altering their relationships with one another.The stories in Coffee Talk 2 are a mix of lighthearted and heartwarming, with a touch of melancholy that adds depth and relatability to the characters. These narratives explore themes of love, loss, identity, and the pursuit of dreams, resonating with players on a personal level.A Soothing Escape from the EverydayCoffee Talk 2 is a welcome respite from the stresses of everyday life. The game's gentle pace, soothing soundtrack, and focus on positive interactions create a tranquil atmosphere that invites players to relax and unwind. The café itself serves as a sanctuary, a place where characters can escape their troubles and seek solace in the company of others.A Must-Play for Fans of Relaxing GamesCoffee Talk 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly is a charming and heartwarming sequel that perfectly captures the essence of the original game while introducing new elements that enhance the experience. With its soothing atmosphere, engaging characters, and heartwarming stories, Coffee Talk 2 is a must-play for fans of relaxing games and anyone seeking a moment of tranquility amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life.Overall Rating: 4.5 out of 5 stars

_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually leave reviews for games as they aren't really my thing to do. But I feel as if I'm compelled to do this. Starting from Coffee Talk 1 and moving over to 2 I was on a Coffee Talk high, in a lack of better terms. This game made me feel like I knew these characters for years, and its safe to say that these characters grew on me. Everyday that would pass I would be eagerly awaiting their return back, let be it from them ordering their drink and/or them simply wanting to chat, I was their for them. From Myrtle and Aqua's gaming adventure to Baileys and Lua's marriage plans to even Silver and Amanda's earth gathering quest (Lord I love those two). I am there for it all and boy am I grateful for them allowing me to be apart of their world. To anyone who reads this, I implore you to play this game. _childDocuments_.review: Hibiscus and Butterfly introduce more characters to the mix but leaves Freya out of the picture. She only appears for a very brief moment at the last day. Some of the dialogue turn a bit philosophical and each character talk about their own struggles in life, from work-related stuff to a story about a haunted tree and relationship drama. There are different endings as well and you're inspired to be a "good" as well as a "bad" barista ^^ I've only gotten the good ending but there are achievements tied to giving bad customer service to the regulars and new ones. New to the game is Banshee Riona and Satyr Lucas. Both of them aspire to be successful artists. Not gonna spoil but their stories are really interesting.. Didn't really care about Lucas much, he's a social media influencer and his goal is essentially to start a podcast featuring underrepresented artists and minorities to shine some light on their talents. I don't really care about social media, YouTube, and that kind of stuff so I skipped past Lucas dialogue's a lot cause I just didn't care about him nor did I feel engaged in his story. He's a bit naive but there is growth so that's good.I felt a bit salty that Freya was largely absent from the game because I really related to all her struggles from the first game. But objectively, this game is just as cosy as the previous one and the drinks are much more colorful an beautiful too. A recommend if you enjoyed the previous game for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: Storywise this game feels less cohesive than its predecessor because the central character that connects everyone together in the previous game, Freya, is absent for almost the entire game. The four or five story arcs have almost no connections.Just like the first game, there are no dialogue choices. Instead, as the barista you brew the correct/incorrect drinks to influence the story. The brewing puzzles basically involve figuring out what the customers want based on the obvious or vague descriptions. However, it doesn't have puzzles like that one puzzle in the first game where you have to go against Freya's wish to get espresso when she is extremely burned out to get the good ending. Here the good endings are obtained by brewing drinks the customers request, and the bad endings obtained by brewing the wrong drinks. I think it is one step back.There is a new mechanic that lets you give certain items to certain customers, but I don't think it has that much impact on the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I sincerely believe that this game is a gift to mankind.How many of us were blessed by the presence of the original iteration throughout the pandemic? I cannot be the only one soothed by its wistful soundtrack and heartwarming storyline as I was isolated inside. Even though I am no longer confined to these four walls, I still find myself comforted by the familiar sights, sounds, and citizens inhabiting our classic coffee shop – and thankfully, this sequel has provided an experience that not only lives up to the original's hype, but surpasses it in every instance.As a fellow writer, I want to give a massive KUDOS to the developers who honored the legacy of the last game's cast. These were not simple cameos (beyond Freya), nor were their problems lackluster in comparison to their original crises. Instead, their newfound woes expand upon who we helped them to become in the original game and provide justified, compassion-eliciting obstacles for them to overcome. With our help, of course.That's not to say that the new characters are anything to scoff at. Lucas and Riona are the exact type of characters that steal my heart, and their dynamic – both with the Barista and with one another – comprised the game's foremost charm. Lucas, in particular, had such a spark in each line of dialogue that I could practically hear his lines being voiced. And let us not forsake Amanda: a character who expounds on Neil/Silver's racial lore whilst remaining closer to her home than to our homeworld. The way each of their stories intertwine with one another and with the rest of the cast is masterfully done, and what we learn about this world's lore always has me chomping at the bit for more information.If I were to dock the game any points, they would be for a lack of true innovation. This game is comprised of plenty more of the same quality characters, songs, storylines, and settings that you loved from the original. But as for anything truly new? There's not much to see here. Achievements have been expanded, as have alternate routes, though some are admittedly more confusing to accrue. We have a simple system to hand over items along with drinks, which did provide for more routes and reactions. However, there's little to nothing else I can think of that truly freshened the formula – something I'm willing to overlook for such a lovingly-written sequel, but which would undoubtedly start creating a feeling of stagnation should this series get the third game it deserves.In addition, my biggest gripe about the original game – the inexplicably frustrating Latte Art mechanic – has received absolutely zero changes that I can find. This shocked me, as I found my confusion to be a pretty universal reaction and couldn't believe the devs chose to preserve a mechanic that was widely panned without even an assistance feature for the artistically-challenged.Even those gripes contribute little to harming my opinion of this title. In fact, they are so unbelievably minor that they should not keep any player from purchasing and playing this from start to finish. This game is special. It is a gentle hug to the heart, a reminder of what is beautiful in a broken world and how we can still find goodness in ourselves and in others despite sleazy business practices, professional rejections, professional disenchantment, and yes...even ghosts. Anyone seeking solace from a stormy world – both literally and metaphorically – should look no further for refuge than the bean-scented seats of Coffee Talk.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished, in total around 7.5 hours. Not done all the endings, just the first playthough. The characters from the first return and continue to develop, and I think they're done excellently. Jorji is excellently characterized, and Gala is currently my new steam avatar. Maybe Myrtle & Aqua needed one more arc. In contrast I find myself wanting a bit more from the new ones, though that may just be because I've had a whole first game to get attached to the original cast. However, I'm overall satisfied.The game is obviously political, the whole concept is. I think occasionally the writing is a tad 'on the nose' whenever it's clearly talking about our world. It's not wrong or bad necessarily, I was just occasionally jarred too hard out of the game and back to reality.The new drinks were interesting, and I even brewed some of them IRL. The Hibiscus w/ milk ones were surprisingly tricky (milk curdles if not careful), but was delicious!The sound track was fantastic as usual, excellent job Andrew Jeremy.Overall, if you enjoyed the first you will definitely enjoy the second. Great work. I'll play the next game you guys release.

I wasn't much help, considering I either forgot to give them or just thought said characters didn't fit the item.My point is, this game really involves the player on a different level. Playing a bartender, but instead of serving alcohol, you serve coffee.I'm so curious about the character's lives and stories they have to tell. And the character we play!The only thing I really wish this game had was a bit more game play besides making coffee/tea. I understand that's the general gist of this game, but maybe the further along we go, maybe the player could have an option to choose their responses to the characters?All in all, I like this game. It's a really enjoyable and cozy experience. I'll be waiting for episode 3, that's for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely sequel to the original, with a longer story line and more characters in addition to the regulars you've come to know and love. The music is nice and chill, the variety of arcs has greatly increased, and the drawer system adds to the player's responsibility within the narrative, which is really nice.There are a few things that sort of make the experience a bit less immersive or polished as it should be. None of the customers finish their drinks, when customers move seats there isn't any sound or animation, and there are a few spelling errors scattered around the dialogue that grab my attention. A nice patch addressing some of these issues could fix these right up, though. Also, for a world based in 2023, the themes of social media are a bit... old? I didn't necessarily feel anything new being addressed with that topic, but that might just be me.Overall, I enjoyed this game, and would recommend it to anyone who liked the first one or something similar like VA-11 Hall-A. Chill beats, warm drinks, and a bright and lively cast of characters, as always.

Cannot recommend this game enough to anyone who likes chill vibes and great characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really put into words how much Toge Productions and its games has continously exceed my expectations. And this sequel is totally a deserving and heartwarming sequel to the first game. The characters had all grown and we get to dive deeper on their new emerging problems as they enter a new stage of their life. Meeting them again in this game feels like meeting an old friend whom you haven't talked in so long, and yet you still share the old memories of those years gone by (gosh, I sound like Hyde, don't I...). But yeah it's nice to continue their story while meeting new curious characters as well.I personally love that in this game and the previous game, Toge doesn't shy away from discussing heavy but important topics, especially for us youngsters looking to find our way to navigate the world. Some of the conversations between the characters do got me thinking and definitely there is a lesson learned there somewhere. But that aside, it's what you would expect the sequel of a chill and heartwarming story would be. And not gonna lie, I almost always have a smile in my face while playing this game, and even if I'm not smiling, there is always something I feel inside, which shows how good the storytelling on this game is as you easily get emotionally and physically (sometimes mentally) invested in the game. It's as if you are following the journey of the characters as if you are really part of the story, which is the appeal of this game from the first sequel as well. So I can't thank you everyone at Toge (including the late Mr. Fahmi) for bringing us such an amazing story and game to experience. Although I can't speak for everyone, so I would recommend everyone to try and see for themselves and hopefully it would leave a lasting mark on everyone too, as it already leave quite a remarkable memories for me personally. So cheers!! And I can't wait to see what story Toge will bring to us next!
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk Episode 2: Hibiscus & Butterfly

_childDocuments_.review: Hello, someone who 100% completed the first game here! I am a huge fan of Coffee Talk, so you bet I got excited to play the sequel the moment it released. I can honestly say this game is a great sequel overall, and expands on the first game when it needs to. Some things are a little different, such as new drink combos, characters, etc. but overall it keeps the formula of the first game and what made it enjoyable, which I say as a massive compliment!The only other thing I will add is that it's best to come into this game expecting a continuation of the first game (which is to be expected when it says "Episode 2" lol). Because the game is very much the same format, it does feel like we play right where we left off, so you NEED to play the first game in order to understand what's going on in this one. I still have yet to get all of achievements so I do not know all of this games secrets yet, but I can't wait till I do.

_childDocuments_.review: If you ignore customization, you will struggle to run out of coins to use on the arcade cabinets. You start with 500, and arcade cabinets eat these up as credits like real machines do, but there's no microtransaction BS going on. Thankfully. Console titles don't need them, and are all accessed from a different machine.You get coins for completing challenges, which is hard not to do as they progress by simply playing the games.(every so often a character will show up in the arcade by completing them as well.)Each locked game just requires you to play another game twice. (Simply launching it doesn't count. Quickest way is to just start a game and run out your lives.)Pac-In-Time is japanese, but has subtitles that appear below the game itself during cutscenes. Beyond that, You get what you pay for. I did have to force V-sync in my gpu options to eliminate screen tearing, as the in-game v-sync option wasn't cutting it.  I'd say it's worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: PAC-MAN MUSEUM+

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually Steam review, but I'm contributing one for this just because every Pac-Man fan needs to know: this is the most love the series has seen in over a decade.If you want Pac-Man to stay relevant, this game needs to do well. Frankly, it deserves to. The ports are well-done and polished, and there's some amazing never-before-released and long-time-coming games bundled in here that longtime fans would appreciate finally being able to play again. The bar wasn't very high for this game - it just had to do the games justice while functioning as a package without any ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and thankfully, it does. The inclusion of both versions of Pac-Man Arrangement, the OG Championship Edition, and Pac N' Roll are especially noteworthy. It's a good game and a labor of love. Simple as that. If you like the yellow eating disorder boi, this game's a must-own. Now remake the Pac-Man World Trilogy, dammit!
_childDocuments_.name: PAC-MAN MUSEUM+

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of classic arcade games, and/or PAC-MAN in particular, the new compilation PAC-MAN MUSEUM+ is well worth checking out, even if you owned the (rather lackluster) previous PAC-MAN MUSEUM compilation.It has a total of 14 games, well presented and emulated, and with plenty of extras to keep you busy (unlockables, achievements, online leaderboards for each game, ...), for an affordable price.Everything about it shows that the team that handled this release placed some heartfelt care on the overall package, from the (highly customizable) virtual arcade setup, a collecting element with virtual figures that you can get on the in-game "gotcha capsule" machines, an extensive jukebox (that features tracks from all games, and various PAC-MAN media, including Ken Ishii's Join the PAC, the Official Theme Song for PAC-MAN's 40th Anniversary), and that care even extends to the compilation's production credits, that are lovingly presented as a release timeline of the various featured games.As a result, it's no surprise that, at the moment, this compilation has 100% of positive reviews on Steam. Great stuff.As for the included games, despite the apparently "limited" formula of the series, there's actually some variation and some great games included.Personally, I always had a soft spot for Pac-Mania, which allows the character to jump over the enemies.And of the "new" games included (compared to the previous compilation), I admit I was somewhat unfamiliar with the "arcade version" of Pac-Man Arrangement, and it's a lot of fun. I can see that I'll be spending some time with this one, since it features appealing and colorful pixel art, catchy tunes, and fast and fun gameplay.This compilation has turned out to be far better than my expectations for it, and if you have any interest in the series, this one is well worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: PAC-MAN MUSEUM+

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty sad negative review, but I don't feel this collection is worth recommending in its current state.There's an odd amount of input lag for the games, which makes the reflex reliant original Pac-Man come off as sluggish. You might try to fight the input lag, but it'll just result in you losing your rhythm. Pac-Man at its best puts you in a flow state, but the lag just pulls you out of it.On paper this is a very good package, 14 Pac-Man games for $20, but most aren't the best versions. For a compilation title, that's insulting. Why are English titles slapped on top of Japanese text for a game that had an English translation? Where's the game setting modifiers? There's just enough minor flaws to make me scratch my head in disbelief. Pac-Man has been around for 43 years as of this review, but despite this being the newest port of the arcade classic, it's not as good as owning an original cabinet. At this point there's no excuse.Maybe input lag isn't a big deal for you, and additional game settings don't make sense--that's alright. What's compiled here gives you a great overview of the pill gobbler's career as a game icon. While it's a shame Ms. Pac-Man and some other Pac-Man titles weren't included in this collection, (Why was Pac-Man Championship Edition 2 omitted?) there's enough here to justify the price tag. Hell, 14 games for $20 is a little over a dollar per game. Just a shame there's input lag.
_childDocuments_.name: PAC-MAN MUSEUM+

_childDocuments_.review: Good but flawed collection. First, I'll go over the collection as a whole, then I'll give my thoughts on each game.The emulation is fine I guess, I'm annoyed that the games aren't scaled with nearest neighbor, which means that pixels are blurry instead of sharp. That can also cause shimmer, most noticable on text. Pac-Mania is very blurry for whatever reason, almost like it has a bilinear filter over it. There are also missions for each game, but instead of being used for interesting ways to play (for example, beat a maze while leaving the power pellets for last) it's all "kill X amount of ghosts", "Beat X levels without getting a game over", etc. They're extremly easy at best and awfully grindy at worst. There's also noticable input delay, I was able to adjust quickly, but I know those couple frames could be a deal breaker for some. There's also the elephant in the room, there's no Ms. Pac-Man. That's because of copyright reasons. What's really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ is that Ms. Pac-Man was also cut out from the games that had her, replacing her with Pac-Mom, who looks like a bootleg character.-Pac-Man (1980)Classic Pac-Man, not much to say about it. An absolute classic-Super Pac-Man (1982)Imagine Pac-Man, but there aren't any dots, you have to collect all fruit, and you have to collect keys to open doors. You can also turn giant to run over ghosts, it's fun but repetitive.-Pac & Pal (1983)Flip over cards to open doors to unlock fruit. There's also Miru, the titular pal, who can't hurt you but will collect fruit which you can grab from her before she returns to the ghost only zone. I find this game pretty frustrating because of her.-Pac-Land (1984)A 2D platformer predating Super Mario Bros, the controls are pretty ♥♥♥♥ but aside from that I think it's pretty fun.-Pac-Mania (1987)Imagine Pac-Man, but in Cavalier perspective (Cavalier is like isometric but not quite), and you can jump over ghosts. Starts out slow, and not that interesting.-Pac-Attack (1993)Tetris but with trominos instead of tetrominos, and some blocks are replaced with ghosts, and every once in a while a pac-man will replace one of them and will eat every ghost until it gets stuck and dies. Pretty decent.-Pac-In-Time (1995)This game blows, it's a reskin of an unrelated 2D platformer, and it's extremly frustrating. The only decent thing is the worms-like rope swinging, but it gets very frustrating with the awful physics.-Pac-Man Arrangement (Arcade) (1996)One of my favorites, basically Pac-Man 2. Features some interesting stage gimmicks but I wish there were more of them. Also, they used the japanese rom so the new 5th ghost isn't named "Kinky" like in the normal english version, lame.-Pac-Man Arrangement (Console) (2005)Partially a remake of the arcade version, partially a new game because of the new gimmicks and bosses. Slower and less fun than the arcade version.-Pac-Man Championship Edition (2007)Not to be confused with the far superior Championship Edition DX+, a faster version of the original pac-man where collecting all dots on the left or right side of the map spawns a fruit that spawns a new half of the level in its place. Doesn't feature the ghost chain following you, that was only in DX+-Pac Motos (2007)A reskin of the arcade game Motos, featuring pac-man characters and power ups. Not that fun but useful for grinding the awful collect 7650 coins and play 765 rounds achievements. -Pac'n Roll Remix (2007)A remaster of the DS game Pac'n Roll, replaces the last world with a new one, is missing some bonus content and doesn't have any story. Pretty decent.-Pac-Man Battle Royale (2011)A PVP version of Pac-Man. Pretty fun, but they should have included multiplayer, without it it's pretty lame.-Pac-Man 256You can really tell this was a mobile game, because everything costs way too many coins which you probably would have paid for in the mobile version. It's a never ending game of Pac-Man where you constantly have to run away from the 256 glitch. Pretty fun, but the extremly grindy missions (seriously, max out 10 powerups? it costs 4080 coins to fully power up ONE) make me never want to touch this game again.Overall, decent collection but if you have a voice in your head that screams at you if you don't 100% complete a game then don't get this because it's a grindfest.

_childDocuments_.review: A revamped version of Museum, with more games and a customizable arcade room. The Pac is truly back, taking the World series look over Ghostly Adventures.You start with a set amount of coins, and there are no microtransactions whatsoever. You spend coins at the arcade machines (like the real thing), and at the Gashapon machine for a chance at additional figures. Coins are earned simply by playing games and clearing missions, so you never truly run out of them. Think of this as a method adopted from the Pinball Hall of Fame series of games.There are a wide variety of games available, with Pac-Man Arrangement, Pac-Attack, Championship Edition, and Super Pac-Man among my favorites. Controls on them are mostly good, save for Pac-Attack's finicky rotation system (likely due to SNES limitations). Other games, like Pac 'N Roll, are best used with a controller.If we ever get paid DLC for additional titles, I'm hoping to see 1998 Pac-Attack set in outer space. That was a missed opportunity on Museum, given the PS1 Anthology port there.Better to get during a sale, but if anyone missed out on the original Museum, this compilation is much, much better.

_childDocuments_.review: (TLDR: Great selection of games, but marred by poor emulation and lack of options.)Well this is surprising. This game suddenly came out on Steam a day earlier than the expected release date. This might have to do with releasing in Japan's time, but whatever.The game itself is just another collection of Pac-Man titles ranging from the original up to the PSP era. But what makes this one unique from other collections is that the "museum" is a virtual arcade which can be customized by the player. While I really do like this idea, it really wasn't executed the best.The game itself runs off one type of in-game currency, which is used to play the arcade titles and purchase stuff for the arcade. And while you do start with a lot, It feels kind of unnecessary since everything is rather cheap. And there's not much stuff to buy anyways, aside from gambling your life away on a gacha machine that's just kinda there. Most of the content is only obtainable through playing the games and completing challenges anyways, But I feel like the currency shouldn't be required for playing the games and only for the unlockables. Speaking of the games...I really like the selection. Not only do you get the obvious classics, but some newer titles from the Wii and PSP era are now included, including games from Namco Museum Remix. Lesser-known titles are also included such as Pac & Pal and even Pac-In-Time. And the Arcade Pac-Man Arrangement finally gets a re-release after a very long time. It's a really good set of titles. But a lot of it is nearly ruined by several other factors.The emulation for most of these games are NOT GOOD. While the games perform perfectly fine, all the arcade games have no integer pixel scaling, and some have an ugly filter. This results in tons of shimmering and/or a blurry picture depending on the game. The sound emulation is not so good either. Most sound effects and some music sound rather off, even in the original 1980 classic. However the more modern titles and console games seem to have much better visual and audible emulation, albeit with the near lack of any upscaled textures. Hell it gets downright lazy too. The original Championship Edition is just stretched to fit on the screen and Pac-In-Time is in Japanese in all regions and subtitles are just thrown in there. And if you're playing on a controller, there is very noticeable input lag.I should mention that ALL references to Ms. Pac-Man are completely eradicated. All the way to the point where any game featuring her is either removed or redesigned to "Pac-Mom." The reasons for why this is are best explained elsewhere.To make things worse, not only do the arcade titles lack good audio and visuals, there are almost no visual settings whatsoever and a complete absense in DIP switch settings. This is inexcusable. And even though they're just simple maze games, being able to make the game easier/harder would be much appreciated for the more casual or hardcore audience respectively.And not only that, half the games need to be unlocked. And to unlock one, you have to play through a specific game completely until you get a game over. Twice. So unless you're intentionally getting game overs to speed things up, some games like Pac-In-Time will takes tons of "time" in order to unlock the next game.After all of this, I'd be safe to say that Pac-Man Museum+ was likely rushed to release. But do I recommend this game? Just barely. If you're only here to play the games and just have fun, I'd say go for it. But if you're somebody who really cares about the quality of the games. Hell no. But hey, at least this is a big improvement from what was given back in 2014.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Pac-Man Superfan, a Pac-Fan if you will, I've played damn near every game in this compilation, in and out of it, probably at least 3,000 times combined, and that's not hyperbole. I'll cut to the chase and say that this is a great compilation with some shortcomings, some of which or weirder and more confusing than others. This will be a long read so if you want something short, there's a TL:DR at the end.So let's start with the positives, which there are many of so I'll try to keep this first part brief, but probably fail. Most important among these is the games all run really well. They've pretty much had emulation down pat since the mid-2000s with Namco Museum 50th Anniversary with only very few notable errors since that game's release. I'm happy to report this game doesn't have any real errors. I have heard that some people have experienced input lag on some releases of the game, but from my experience, the PC version works pretty perfectly. The presentation is honestly the best it has been in ANY Namco Museum adjacent title since 50th Anniversary. Whether it exceeds the quality set by the PS1's literal history museums is up to personal preference IMHO. The customizable arcade is genuinely way more fun to screw around with than I ever thought it'd be and though I do wish there was an option for borderless games during emulation, the arcade borders especially are so cool, as they're recreations of the cabinet art, that i'd never even bother turning them off. I'd say more but I don't need to. It does exactly what it needs to do, and more to be a really great Pac-CollectionSo basically, the games look, feel, and sound pretty damn good in terms of emulation quality, which are the most important aspects by an overwhelming margin, but I do have some nitpicks as a long time Namco Museum/Pac-Man fan. The biggest one being that you can't change game settings like Lives, Extra Live requirements, etc. I suspect this is due to leaderboards but that hasn't stopped so many other past releases from just disabling those whenever you changed settings. Also, though I love the arcade, they give you way too many decor options for how damn tiny the arcade is. It's a 16x10 space, which doesn't sound small, and maybe I'm just bad at space management, but even then only 10 spaces long on the top and bottom is limiting. Also I know that they had to cut off the game list somewhere, but they really included Pac-In-Time over Pac-Man Plus? Over Pac-Man Vs.? Hell even Pac-Man 2? I mean it when I say that I feel Pac-In-Time is not only the worst game in the collection by a long shot, but it's the only truly bad one. Even the other choices some may not like, I feel there are many others who will. And my last nitpick is how you play these games: The Tokens. Now in concept I love this idea. It's a very cute idea that makes the experience really feel just that little bit more authentic. That said, they only truly exist for the Gashapon machine and nothing else. Tokens otherwise are your credits for the Arcade Games only, and 1 Token = 1 Credit. Thankfully if you're a gacha nut, there are console and mobile games in this collection that are free to play and you earn tokens by playing games! That said, some games make earning tokens so damn easy that if you don't care about the Gacha mechanic, or the arcade at all really, that you will never come CLOSE to running out. If you do need a good way to earn more fast, literally playing a couple levels in Pac-Motos and like 10 Minutes of Pac-Man 256 work really well for me. While it's good to have quick and reliable ways to earn these things, when it takes 10 minutes to earn enough for over 20 plays of an arcade game, it feels worthless to include them.Speaking of the games, I'll go over them and review them with 1-2 sentences each and a number out of 7 rating. Keep in mind these are my personal rankings.Arcade Games:Pac-Man (7/7)It's Pac-Man.Super Pac-Man (6/7)Despite being my favorite Pac-Man game ever, I do concede that the Key gameplay is a little too subject to Trial and Error than I'd like and the Super Speed can be hard to control. The bonus stages are very fun to master though.Pac & Pal (5/7)Similar to Super Pac-Man but with some less traditional ideas, including a stun beam replacing Power Pellets. When you get good with the new mechanics, High-Scores are very fun and challenging to go for, but it takes quite a bit of practice.Pac-Land (5/7)A fun platformer with weird controls that aren't explained in game. Though fun when you get the hang of it!Pac-Mania (6/7)The early levels are pretty slow, but when you get farther in, the chaos ramps up exponentially, which I personally love. The new jumping feature enables that super frantic gameplay that also allows for huge points from ghost chains!Pac-Man Arrangement (Arcade) (7/7)It's Pac-Man again, but with really fun gimmicks. Since the game is progression based with an ending, trying to stay alive to keep a higher score is way more fun than in any other game here.Pac-Man Battle Royale (5/7)Now IF you can get friends in the same room to play, this is a 7/7. However I gotta dock points for not having online multiplayer. Use Remote Play for this one, otherwise only bother for the achievements or for a quick mild thrill.Free Play games:Pac-Attack (5/7)It's a Tetris like game, but much harder to get a handle on. The amazing Puzzle Mode saves this from being a 4/7 for me.Pac-In-Time (2/7)The puzzle solving is kinda cool, but everything else blows so much. ONLY play if you want the achievements.Pac-Man Arrangement (Console) (6/7)Not as good as the Arcade version, but it does have plenty of legit pros when opposed to it so give this one a play too!Pac-Man Championship Edition (6/7)If you enjoy this game, buy DX and/or 2 as well. Every Championship Edition game is fast paced, addicting, and so much damn fun. Only a 6/7 because DX exists.Pac-Motos (4/7)Not a bad game, but pretty samey. Better than the original Motos Arcade game imo though.Pac & Roll Remix (5/7)Nothing super special, but good fun here. This is a remake of the DS version that's been simplified on all fronts. I've played both and I'd recommend the DS version over this one, but it's still a fine way to play a fine game. Don't come in expecting anything mind blowing though.Pac-Man 256 (6/7)This game is extremely addicting, though VERY tedious to complete. I only gave it a 6/7 instead of a 5/7 due to the fun and addictive factors.Overall, though there are some shortcomings, including the lack of options in all senses, the useless tokens, and one I didn't mention: the complete lack of extra content outside of the Jukebox item, this is still one of the best collections they've ever put out, especially in recent years! There are a couple of games I'd recommend over this, like the PS1 Namco Museum Lineage, Virtual Arcade, and Namco Museum Megamix, this is still a great collection, especially for $20. Though obviously, your mileage will vary solely on if you like Pac-Man games and would buy 14 of them in a collection with nothing else, which is something I'd do many times over.TL:DR: Very great collection with some minor, though baffling inclusions and omissions on all fronts for both. easily worth the $20 as long as you are a Pac-Fan

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so, here comes Pac-Man (aww ♥♥♥♥) Museum+, the latest compilation re-release for our yellow disco ball. Time for the biggest Pac-Man nerd on the planet to tell you how it shapes up. Buckle up.Let's start with the good:+You get 14 titles for $20 USD, incredible value+Range of games is quite wide, anything from the classics to some real obscure sequels and spinoffs+Rarer titles include some real gems like XBLA Championship Edition and Namco Classics Col. Arrangement+Leaderboard support for the above mentioned+There's some enjoyment to be had doing up your own personal arcade, collecting figures and listening to musicHowever...-Some games are baffling choices, 3rd party ones like Pac-In-Time, or 256, a 2015 mobile game in an arcade compilation?-Subjectively I think the mid-2000s games like n' Roll and Motos are mediocre but YMMV-No DIP switches or difficulty tweaking. Want extra lives for practice? Too bad.-Multiplayer doesn't exist. No online functions or remote play, nor do local inputs work, ruins games like Battle Royale or Arrangement co-op-Arcade customization is lackluster, props are ugly and many unlocks are just duplicates-Related, no multiplayer hosting or visiting arcades, missed opportunity IMO-Game progression is laughable and unrewarding, missions are often tedious and flat, with poor rewards-Token system and achievements are pointless grinding with no payoff, and the all Mastery grand prize is -No Ms. Pac-Man. I know it's for legal reasons, lawyers ruin everything, but it still hurts. Enjoy the ugly redesign-Worst of all, no extras. Compare this to other Namco "Museum" games or SNK 40th and you'll be disappointedIn summary, the games are worth playing and there's variety, but I still think this is a lukewarm compilation re-release. Definitely played far better arcade compilations not just from Namco but also from other arcade tycoons. The features advertised range from missing to underdeveloped and Museum+ falls shy of the Namco Museum games put out before it. For $20 USD, you could definitely get your worth of this compilation, but it's not gonna be the nostalgia trip you hoped for.I would recommend this game IF you really want a Pac-Man sampler platter for your own curiosity. However, as a seasoned Pac-Man veteran, I won't pretend it outdoes the other innumerable Pac ports and compilations. Definitely go for this if you're interested, but playing other versions or using MAME is also valid IMO. And hey, at least it's better than the previous Pac-Man Museum.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's a review of the complete package of games, from worst to best based on my experience with them:Pac-Motos: the best feature about this one is that it's short. Indeed, the bouncing ball mechanic for squarely confined levels is quite imprecise for most, even if they don't last longer than 30 seconds, every enemy is a ball and it doesn’t help that the bosses are pretty dull. Worst of all, the last boss has 2 phases, and the second one you’ll need to be lucky since depending on where you position yourself you may die instantly or fall through the floor. But hey, at least it serves as a coin hoarder if you're willing to beat 1-1 over and over again.Pac-Man Arrangement (Console version): It’s very slow compared to the arcade version with uglier 3D graphics despite it coming out years later. It also has some of the worst hitboxes and the last boss had a glitch so I had to give up a life in order to beat it. The only good aspect I can mention about it is the soundtrack which changes with each world.Pac-in-Time: This might be the most disappointing one considering how long I had waited to play it again. The soundtrack is great, the presentation is ok for the time it came out and there's an actual story here. The problem is the rest as the controls are way too bouncy for what the precise level design demands, especially on the latter half of the levels, there’s way too many one hit kill obstacles, bad enemy placement and elusive mechanics that unless you know beforehand, they might get you stuck (such as rope pulling and hammer shockwave). At least the rope is still fun to use.Super Pac-Man: A weird twist on the Pac-Man formula by locking different parts of the maze with keys and adding super pellets. In theory it's creative, but the only maze there is doesn't make it justice. There are way too many sharp turns to be made for how fast the game gets later in order to avoid the ghosts. Plus, the mentioned pellets randomly give you super speed, making Pac-Man very difficult to control. Fortunately, the coffee break cutscenes were amusing and the rest stages were a nice bonus.Pac-Man Battle Royale: A very simple multiplayer arcade battle game that is hindered by the fact that you can only play it against the computer. With 2 to 4 players in an actual arcade this would probably be a lot more enjoyable. Otherwise, it’s pretty simplistic and repetitive.Pac-Land: The idea of having a Pac-Man 2D platformer with varying levels, power ups and trips is certainly here, at least in a better fashion than Pac-Man 2. Nonetheless, the controls are severely outdated. For instance, there’s the hovering mechanic for which I had to repeatedly tap right or left in order to get across an obstacle and for it to work I had to pull out my keyboard despite playing the rest with the joystick fine enough. There's certainly a reason why most games have a dedicated button to run nowadays. Either way, the main tune is pretty catchy and looking up on YouTube what I missed in the later levels I would gladly put this one forward as a strong candidate for a possible remake in the future.Pac'n Roll Remix: Much like in Pac Motos, Pac-Man is a ball and it rolls around, but the levels are longer a square grid rather they have proper obstacles and different power ups to traverse them. The textures and background looks very clean, the tracks have a good rhythm to them (I’m quite fond of the fire world one) and up until the third boss I had no complaints about the controls. From that point onwards however, they can become too loose and you'll be much more prone to fall off the stage. But with enough patience, it’s very doable.Pac & Pal: This one takes off from where Super Pac-Man left off and with a more forgiving map it introduces the ghost pal that steals the fruit and power ups you have to collect but also helps you complete the level. This can either be a blessing or a curse, depending on how you approach it. In my case, once I figured out the way it moved towards the ghosts’ spawn point, I made sure to follow it accordingly in case it had a power up or leave if it was just another fruit. It's much appreciated that there's also a safe zone in the middle of the map, even if I wasn't able to get to it all the time due to how the maze is laid out.Pac-Attack: I was certainly not expecting Pac-Man to be crossed with Tetris and working even, but I’m happy it does. While the presentation is old, the controls are stiff especially compared to modern Tetris and there's no restart button, the core idea of thinking where to position the ghosts and then dropping a Pac-Man to fill out the board is clever. In fact, there is a dedicated puzzle mode with 100 varying levels to go across than add their own twist to it. Add it to the list of candidates that need to be remastered now.Pac-Man Championship Edition: The most frenetic one here in terms of how you can achieve flow state if you can get a good enough chain reaction of eating power pellets and ghosts to get lives. You see, not only does it level up the formula by having the fruit serve as the way to get more dots and pellets, it also doesn't pause whenever you lose a life, and you have to last through timer in order to beat each level, a feat that will make you think fast and not drop many lives too quickly. I'm keen on checking out later the sequels it spawned since this one was too easy to get all the records.Pac-Man: It's basically the game that started it all, so there's not much to say about it that hasn't been said before. Well, maybe except for the fact that if you're going for all the missions and aren’t that good (like myself) you might wanna look up how the ghosts move, the way they interact with specific parts of the maze and general patterns and tips that with enough practice let you begin each level confidently, leaving small room for error. That was a huge help in my case and a great satisfaction to get right.Pac-Mania: Classic Pac-Man set up in an isometric and smooth 3D view with the addition of the jump and bounce mechanic. This might be this high up mainly because of how tight the controls are and the way the simple jump mechanic can make you change the way you approach ghosts. The songs also have a good repertoire of instruments and despite not having that many levels, the worlds leave their mark and are no laughing matter in terms of difficulty.Pac-Man 256: A great idea that came from a bug in the original game. Why not create an endless maze where the glitch follows you? Not only is this fresh, it has the biggest catalog of power ups from the collection, not to mention the skins which make it very replayable. It even has a multiplayer mode that I wasn't able to delve into unfortunately. That being said, Its major downside is the sheer lack of music. Fortunately, this can be easily fixed if you take it as a podcast game. I certainly had to do it with how many hours it took me to get 10 power ups to level 8.Pac-Man Arrangement (Arcade version): The most fun I might have had with Pac-Man mazes ever. The pixelart is on point, having that feel of the great era of arcades, the power ups are pretty wacky in their use, the mazes are distinct and go through nicely and most importantly, the final boss… doesn't suck. Not to mention the music, sound effects and length of it all wrap it up to be the definitive version of Pac-Man arcade (at least, out of this collection).Finally, regarding the game itself now, it does have a lot of achievements that you will need to grind out (just take a look at my playtime) though it compiles a good variety of games from the franchise history. As a result, I recommend it just for checking them out at the very least. Maybe one day we'll get the World games in one as well. In the meantime, if you’re struggling with the decoration achievements, be sure to check the vending machine every day as that's the only way to get new ones (unless you time travel, of course).

_childDocuments_.review: I was highly anticipating the release of PAC-MAN MUSEUM+ since its initial announcement in November 2021, and I'm happy with the game as a whole. While Ms. Pac-Man is (understandably) absent, every other game that HAD to be here is featured here. The inclusion of PAC-MAN ARRANGEMENT's arcade version is most certainly the most exciting addition here to me and it plays great. However, some of the earlier games do have input lag issues. I never had any obvious issues with PAC-MANIA or PAC & PAL but sometimes it would take a millisecond too long to register a turn with SUPER PAC-MAN and PAC-MAN. I assume Namco is aware of this at this point because it is the number one complaint I am seeing related to this game.The coin system, which you use to play all games that were originally released in Arcades, is, admittedly, dumb. You get coins depending on how you do while play any game, which makes it basically impossible to lose coins if you don't buy any customization stuff, which begs the question of why you even need coins for the first place. You can also use coins to buy things to customize your arcade, a very noble idea which I hope future Namco Museums and game compilations take note of, albeit more fleshed out. I believe the coin system would be better if it was only used for buying stuff for your arcade. I do hope this game does get DLC in some form. The original PAC-MAN MUSEUM in 2014 featured Ms. Pac-Man as DLC, and I hope they can come to an agreement with AtGames or whoever to make that happen with Plus as it is admittedly a very, very glaring omission. Another, not so glaring omission (although still weird it isn't here) is PAC-MAN WORLD, which, to a degree I understand why it wasn't included. It isn't super big in Japan and most people only played the sequel, which is a PS2 game and harder to emulate. However, I think if they are going to put absolute garbage in this collection like PAC-IN-TIME, I think putting the first PAC MAN WORLD in as DLC wouldn't hurt. Also, if you're gonna go out of your way to, again, put absolute garbage in this collection like PAC-IN-TIME, PAC-MAN 2: The New Adventures should have also been added due to it's similarly bad status and the game's box art. Go in all the way or don't at all, Namco. You shouldn't cower in the face of infamy.At the end of the day however, Ms. Pac-Man or not the game is $20 and it has both PAC-MAN CE and the arcade version of PAC-MAN ARRANGEMENT. It's probably the best deal for a game collection I've seen in a long time. If you want Namco to care about PAC-MAN again this is the best game to show them that this little guy has an audience.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a definitive collection of over a dozen classic Pac-Man arcade era games and then some, your time has come. Following in the spirit of the original Namco Museum games that came out well over two decades ago, we've finally gotten a "Museum" title worthy of it's ancestors. To be more concise, this iteration feels more like a reboot than anything, but a reboot done well. This game, instead of being a barebones outing with a menu and some arcade selections like the 2014 version that preceded this release, allows you to control Pac-Man (reminiscent of controlling him in the Pac-Man World series) inside a small arcade hub world - fully furnished and customizable with statues, Gashapon figures, wallpapers, music and of course, arcade machines. In addition, you get in-game missions to increase replay value and that's on top of the Steam achievements which you're also getting here.This game makes the arcade layout more immersive by implementing a system where tokens are used in and earned by playing the machines. A couple of tokens (5 for a Gashapon capsule, for example) will buy you cosmetic items and one token will give you access to play a credit on an arcade machine. Don't worry though, you start with 500 of them so you'll find that running out of these would be a very difficult scenario to find yourself in, especially since you'll be earning them just by playing the game anyway. The console games are played without tokens as well, so they're not used for everything. Thankfully, there are no in-game purchases or micro-transactions to be found here and that is a very good thing. All currency is strictly earned by playing the game - keeping it fun, as it should be.Also, a message for Steam Deck users: I tested this game on my device and, while it is not yet Deck verified, I can confirm that it runs flawlessly on it at the time of posting this review.On a separate note, I would like to mention that I prefer to play these kinds of games with a controller, and while playing using this layout I noticed that when using analog sticks, some games (specifically ones like the original Pac-Man and Arrangement, for example) are sometimes not very responsive turning corners. I tested with three sticks, namely - Steam Deck, Xbox Series X/S and Switch Pro controllers, all of which exhibited the same issue.  upon switching to the D-Pad on all of them the games controlled silky smooth. In the end, I'd say it's really not an issue as everything functions as intended otherwise. _childDocuments_.review: It plays well and includes original Pac-Man CE, Pac-Man Arrangement (Both versions), Pac-Man 256 (Also on Steam as a separate product but sorry Pac-Bros you're probably gonna be double dipping on that one. No discounts.), Pac-Man Battle Royale, and Pac-And-Roll. There's also a lot of complete garbage games (Imagine playing Pac-Mania for more than 10 minutes) but it's still an excellent collection of some of the absolute highest points of Pac-Man's history that would require several different emulators otherwise to jerry-rig if you wanted them all otherwise. Pac-Man is still relevant today not because of Namco's careful stewardship of the brand (Pffft) but because the original game was solid and works really well, and the games on tap here offer you a wide array of good (And terrible) extensions of it. This package does the franchise justice and, if you have a taste for retro arcade games but have only a passing familiarity with Pac-Man, this is a great way to pick it up. For seasoned Pac-Man fans, this is a collection of a bunch of games we FINALLY have easy access to.But no Ms. Pac-Man sadly.Brief per game reviews:Pac-Man: The OG. Needs no introPac n Pal: A cute take on the original Pac-Man with less dot eating and more maze runningPac-Land: Utterly horrific.Pac-Mania: A completely soporific take on the OG. Only worthwhile for the unlocking the rocking Genesis style midi music for the in-game jukebox and curing insomnia. World 2 is one of the best themes you can turn on in the in-game jukebox if you want to avoid a thousand different terrible waka-waka remixes.Pac Attack: There are people nostalgic for and porting/emulating Cleopatra's Revenge competitively. I only say that because block falling puzzlers of all sorts that you've never heard of can have a niche crowd, but one does not exist for this turd and one never ever will.Pac in Time: Reminds me of the era of the Home Improvement SNES game with terrible greased platformer physics. Intolerable unless you are a kid growing up with this crap.Pac n Roll: There's a reason you've never played this time-wasting Monkey Ball wannabe. The art is really nice though.Pac Motos: A Kirby style minigame with the great Pac n Roll assets so it's decent fun as an add-on to this collection.Pac Man Battle Royale: This is really only worthwhile playing with friends and probably still only worthwhile if all your friends are drunk and cooling down from playing heavier games at Dave and Busters but you're gonna have to play this crap solo if you want unlocks.Pac Man Arrangement: A extremely good effort at making Pac-Man into a traditional game while still keeping the core of Pac-Man. The arcade version is definitely nicer to look at; the console version has been given a nauseating face-lift meant to appeal to some manager's imagined version of pill-popping kids.Pac Man Championship Edition: From the XBLA era, so it's glowy dark and neon, but it is one of the finest iterations of the OG Pac-Man formula refined for really satisfying score chasing.Pac Man 256: I have reviewed this on Steam as well but the main point is this may be a mobile game endless runner with Pac-Man flavoring but it is TRULY excellent at capturing what makes Pac-Man good in that context designed by actual gamers who make actual games, here with the mobile grind removed of course. Don't sleep on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Nearly twenty years ago, I had this fun little Gameboy game called Pac-Man Collection. It was a bundle of four different Pac-Man games that allowed someone like myself - who didn’t get to really experience the arcade era - a chance to get into the Pac-Man series proper. Now here we are in 2022 with an exponentially better version of that game.Basically, this is a collection of a bunch of different Pac-Man games with this cool “arcade” customization feature thrown on top of it. As you play more games, you unlock tokens which you can use to play other games as well as roll in a gashapon machine to unlock statues that you can then use to deck out your arcade.Each game has a bunch of different “missions” to complete and these too unlock more cosmetic things to place, whether that be flags, figures, benches, tables, or even new wallpapers. Overall, the whole arcade customization thing is kinda basic, but it’s a fun enough distraction and definitely a better alternative than just a menu listing the different games you can play.That Gameboy game I mentioned earlier? It has just four Pac-Man games. This collection? It has fourteen, including everything from the original 1980 arcade game to lesser-known ones like the 2005 DS game Pac 'n Roll or the 1995 SNES game Pac-In-Time. Most of the games take up the traditional Pac-Man style gameplay, but those two examples, along with others, offer up a bit more variety - mostly in the way of platforming.Not to say that they are all good though - I wasn’t really a fan of Pac-In-Time and Pac-Man Battle Royale is pretty much the worst thing ever if you don’t have others to play it with. It’s mostly balanced out though - a bit of good, a bit of bad, a lot of just okay. My personal favorite was probably Championship Edition.That said, the collection is missing a few key Pac-Man games I would have liked to see. The major one of course being Ms. Pac-Man, although that is likely because the game was not developed by Namco directly. But then you’re missing stuff like Championship Edition 2, which is very surprising seeing as how the first one is included and Championship Edition 2 is perhaps the most definitive Pac-Man experience yet and would have likely been my favorite game in the pack if it were included.There are others of course - the Pac-Man World series definitely deserves its own collection - but overall, it’s a solid collection and covers a lot of Pac-Man’s history. In fact, it is by far the most definitive collection of Pac-Man games yet and I would have no trouble calling it the best.The collection plays well, runs just fine, looks great at 4k, and has just enough customization to make it more than just another collection of Pac-Man games. That and it even works right out of the box on the Steam Deck - where I had fun jumping from game to game.So yes, PAC-MAN MUSEUM+ a pretty easy recommendation to make, not just for Pac-Man fans, but for fans of retro gaming in general. It’s got a fun batch of games to play through, some nice bonus features by way of leaderboards and arcade customization, and I am honestly struggling to find anything negative to say here - it’s just an all-around solid release and a great way to get into one of the medium’s most important series.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: You get what you paid for. The collection itself is great, and I love the overall presentation of the games compared to the original Pac-Man museum. I specifically bought the game for the arcade version of Pac-Man arrangement, Pan n' Pal, and the Pac-Man remix Wii games (Pac n' Roll and Pac-Motos). These titles are very hard to come across these days if you do not use emulation, and to have them all together in one collection is really REALLY nice to finally have after waiting so long for something like this. I'm very pleased with the game, but I am writing this review specifically to list some things I did not like.* Missions are a complete joke. If you are in any way SOMEWHAT good at Pac-Man, you will have absolutely no problem finishing the missions. The only one I had trouble with in the entire game so far was getting to board 15 in Pac n' Pal. I really really wished that the missions were going to be at least somewhat challenging when I heard about them, but they're not. I feel like most people who would go out of their way to spend 20$ on a collection like this are true fans of the series, and the true fans are pretty damn good at most of the games. I don't feel like i'm the only one who would have liked it a lot more if they had missions that took a lot of effort to accomplish. For example, most of the arcade ports have 50,000 as the highest score to get to which....really isn't high at all. Pac-Mania's highest is 100,000, but in that game you can easily reach 100k by the end of board three if you know what you're doing. I would have loved to see missions like: Score 500,000 in original Pac-Man or something like: Complete Pac-Man arrangement (Arcade Version) without using any continues.* There are a few games missing in here that I would've liked to see. If they were going to bring over two of the games from Namco Museum remix on the Wii, I don't see why they couldn't have brought all of them since the ones we got are pretty much straight ports. I was honestly very shocked when I found out that Pac-Man Plus wasn't going to be added to the list as well. I felt like that was pretty much a guarantee with how much the game has been popping up in other arcade ports recently* The audio sound effects for some of the ports is kind of...not so good. The two games where it stuck out to me the most were Pac n' Pal with some of the point counters, and the sounds for the specials being pretty loud too. Pac-Man Arrangement (Console Version) also had some pretty poor audio especially the sound Pac-Man makes when they eat dots. Don't get me wrong though, some changes in different games I actually really really like. The sounds in the original Pac-Man are different but I really don't mind them. The sound Pac-Man makes when they eat a ghost now is extremely satisfying compared to the original sounds, and the complete music overhaul in Pac-Man arrangement (Arcade Version) was a really nice welcome.* I personally do not like Pac-Attack that much..didn't really plan on playing it other than for the missions (thank god these ones were easy at least), but why did they have to use the snes version!! I would've loved to see the more updated version, but they gave us the one we see everywhere else instead. Overall though, I really enjoy this collection. The things I listed above are very minor gripes, and didn't steer me away from the game really at all (those missions though cmon man). If you're debating about getting it..if you really do like the Pac-Man series, or haven't played a handful of the more obscure ones pick it up. If neither of those apply to you, wait for it to go on sale. Hopefully this game does super well so Namco finally gives us a damn Pac-Man World collection
