_childDocuments_.review: I can give this one a weak recommendation if you spot it with a decent discount. A bonus if you have a healthy attitude and can appreciate checking something interesting out without being compelled to absolutely finish it to the end.What this game absolutely nails is the aesthetic and art style. Sound and animation also deserve a nod of respect. Where the game falls short is in being just generally kinda boring and repetitive as you go on.Darkest Dungeon is the obvious comparison and this game doesn't quite reach the same level of intricate and layered mechanics. While there are distinct classes, it doesn't feel like they complement each other all that well. The skill sets are also often a problem. You get new characters with some skills unlocked, but so far there is no obvious way to swap them. A random set can make some picks feel entirely useless.There are no dungeons to explore, and no provisioning to invest into. You can swap your squad after ever battle, save the game and hit the next set of enemies. No particular strategy needed. You can mostly take the enemies out in the order they came. No lasting penalties or perks.If a character dies in combat, they're out. But you can also hire a new one right away. A random skill set can pose a bit of a challenge though. The selection of hires does not refresh automatically. You just pay to refresh the offers, which kinda discourages you from exploring too much.There's the big new mechanic of organising a circus event, and I guess there's some complexity in that, but it also gets repetitive. It ends up being a bit of a side-gig where you park some of your roster between fights.UI navigation can bit just a bit clunky. Inconsistent button placements. Having to hit a back button with mouse when you could have right-clicked out into the previous menu. You get used to it, but it's not the smoothest.Some of the items you can equip are more of a curse than anything else. Each character has two item slots. One of the items I got gives a 20% discount on levelling up skills. Absolutely useless in combat, but because resources are limited, you now have to make sure you swap the item around your entire roster when levelling up between fights. Who thought that was a great idea?Finally, a personal problem I have with the design. Characters use the Precision stat to calculate the odds of hitting an enemy, when it obviously meant to be Accuracy. Preposterous!

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to tell yet if it's going to have the same replay-ability of Darkest dungeon, but it's very fun and scratches that itch. There are so many different systems at play that it's a bit dizzying to get your head around all of it, but the tutorials do a good job of letting you know what to look out for.  The difficulty as of only a few missions seems to be substantially easier, but I have a feeling that is going to change, as I'm still in the "tutorial" section I believe.If you're interested in something with a similar style to DD I would recommend it as of now, but this is coming only an hour in, if the gp loop or story falls off, I'll updateOK after several more hours I can say this is darkest dungeon lite? or as others have said Iratus (I have not played that) You can save and reload which makes being ill prepared for a boss fight able to be cheesed if you want to, and if a persons devotion drops to 0 (akin to sanity in DD) instead of the person having a meltdown/heart attack, they just flee the battle and are available again after if you get their devotion up.It's fun, the loop is what you expect from this style of game, some of the "heros" you get seem to be fairly bad compared to others.  I've yet to find a situation that couldn't use at least 1 strongman if not 2, if you get their precision up they just do truckloads of damage compared to anything else I've seen thus far (just unlocked ventriloquist)Anyways if you're expecting a exact copy of DD you might be disappointed, if you're looking for that gameplay style with more of a story and less of a challenge with a lot of bells and whistles added in, I would recommend checking it out.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game is overlooked. Maybe it's because of the steampunk circus concept? I wouldn't call this game "great" but i do think it's worth playing. It's a bit of a slow-burner though so it requires a bit of patience to get going. I'm only on the 3rd map, level 4 circus, and it feels like there's still a lot to unlock. I'd rather have a game that's slow to pick up instead of one that's quick to become bored with.The graphics are pleasant, using fully animated 3D models for the characters. Each character within a class has a set of randomized parts, skill set, and performance capabilities. So although all characters in a class will feel similar, they'll all be a little different in some way.The combat doesn't feel RNG-heavy at all. I feel like i can find a strategy the works and rely on it to keep working in the same conditions. While there is a diverse set of classes to make teams from, i do find myself having a usual lineup with a usual strategy. It's not good to do that though because some characters can't do anything in certain weather conditions and i got caught a couple times using the fire breather in the fog (she can't attack at all in foggy weather).One thing i don't like is planning the circus performances because it feels like i need to take notes to make sure i hire the right characters for them, and i really don't like taking notes for games. I still think it's a neat idea though. There's also a story to this game but i actually don't care much about the story as i'm more interested in the gameplay.For the record, i've never played Darkest Dungeon or Iratus so i had no expectations coming into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: You are probably here to scratch that Darkest Dungeon / Iratus itch. To be honest, this game might or might not be enjoyable for you. Why? It looks great, it plays great, it has everything you probably wanted from a DD inspired game.While this game offers plethora of "classes" that are gradually unlocked throughout the game, their skillsets and interaction is extremely limited to a point they make no sense in lot of cases. I won't go into details like some of the others reviews go, but be warned. There is no fun in selecting your team. There are no fun combat interactions unless you take a great joy in using the same skill over and over. And that is a real shame, because it would take just a little more work for the devs to give some of the combos thought and the game would be almost perfect.Still, the game was mildly enjoyable for me. What kept me going was unlocking new classes. But unlike DD or Iratus, I will never touch it again.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the concept of this game, and the similarities with Darkest Dungeon. It has a lot going for it, but honestly I cannot recommend it.I may be doing something wrong, but the biggest fault is that the progression path only allows you to travel one way, meaning fights cannot be farmed for EXP. This means that by the time you get to the level "boss" if you lose you are locked into a cycle of failure. This pretty much dooms your whole run if you are not prepared for it. Once you are at this stage all you can do is fight the boss, or "hire" a new team. If your team is not good enough then thats all folks.If the progression was reworked it would be recommendable, but until this is tinkered with I cannot recommend other to buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is gorgeous in almost every aspect. There are so many unique backgrounds for each fight, it's impossible to get bored with the scenery. It's easy to see why it's compared to Darkest Dungeon in almost every review. They've pulled almost every mechanic from DD and added their own on top.To address what other reviews are saying; YOU DO NOT NEED TO GRIND FOR EXP.Your party members cannot outlevel your circus and the level cap is 10. The exp requirement is so high you would be grinding for hours just for half a level. Level means nothing in this game and it's more beneficial most of the time to not level your (side) characters, like at all, ever. Due to the most bizarre resource system I've ever encountered in a game. I finished my Normal run with levels 8, 9, 9, 8. You don't need to stress over it that much.DD tells you that your heroes will die and not to get attached to them. CE tells you to get attached and pushes this by making your heroes expensive to invest in. However, in CE, your performers consume food. How do you acquire food? You have an RNG chance of gaining food after each fight. That's it. It's fully possible to softlock yourself out of progress because you got unlucky, hired too many characters or levelled up too quickly. Not being able to backtrack saves you from running out of food before you even get out of the first district so it's really not a problem.Never trust the game if it says you have a 97% chance to hit.Get the train to level 7 as your first priority, ignore upgrading everything else.District 5 has a massive difficulty spike and eases off again in District 6.You can get extra food from the club fights.Pay attention to the weather.The Bobbery Alarm will go off, just kill the bobbies instead of restarting the fight over and over, you will not end the fight quicker than the alarm will trigger in many situations.I adore this game and would like to see any potential sequel reduce the micromanagement just a little.

_childDocuments_.review: - The story is pretty cool, albeit a little predictable.- The art style is amazing and the graphics are really pretty.- The game is incredibly unbalanced:1. A lot of classes are beyond useless.2. Keeping high devotion is incredibly easy. Just wait till there is only one opponent left and use heals and devotion-boosting skills.3. The AI is dumb. It seems to randomly use skills. It sometimes gets it right though...4. When the AI "gets it right", it has the ability to two-shot your squishies.- The circus-managing aspect is original but becomes tedious pretty quickly. The fact you can't save "line-ups" for your shows is not excusable. The resource management is pretty unbalanced too. I need tools. I have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of other resources but never have enough tools.- Some descriptions of skills or powers are not clear at all. I'm not stuck. I could easily continue but the fact that the options for good parties are so limited made the game tedious after a while.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice aesthetic and good voice acting/art direction are not enough to let me overlook embarrassing writing, a messy jumble of hodgepodge mechanics that don't belong in the same game, an overly fussy UI, a stale and samey gameplay "loop", and weightless, mediocre combat. _childDocuments_.review: Great game that combines the best of Darkest Dungeons and a game like Iratus, a notable unique take on the 4 on 4 party rpg combat of Roguelites. This game has a lot to give, a great soundtrack, unique management elements not seen elsewhere and a fully voiced story (so rare for roguelites). The only issue is that the game is *far* too slow at giving you new characters. So many are unlocked just hours and hours after slog and slog for the campaign. The campaign is fun, don't be mistaken, but the fun in these games is finding a unique team comp with characters you don't like or haven't used. The game meanders handing out characters so long that you'll always have 2 of the 5/6 starting classes available at the train cart at any one time. Asides that, great game. Worth the money for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: Electrique is truly something special. Like strongly pointing to landing in my Top 10 this year kind of special.The visuals are simply arresting with a unique style and sense of place. It can look busy on the surface but the language is parsing a lot of info to the player in an intelligent manner, all with convenient mouse-over info pop-ups.You can just tell there was a lot of thought & TLC put into it. Like how the tutorial is spread over the initial hours of gameplay, not throwing everything at you all at once, but rather getting the player comfortable with the myriad of systems a bit at a time. Unlocking & introducing new concepts only after the previous have been test-driven for a bit. Plus there's a fully fleshed out Codex explaining all the nuances that you can access anytime in-game complete with cool "Fallout Valut-Boy"-like animations on each page. Even that little magnifying glass on top-left opens a full infographic explaining unique concepts of whatever screen your currently on.There's just so much going on between circus management...upgrading facilities, recruiting & upgrading performers (15 unique classes!). Setting up daily circus acts and synergizing performers for better payouts. The board game-like map progression where you cruise nodes in divergent paths to main quest goal markers. The way time of day & weather affects the battle system kinda like Divinity: OS. The VN cutscenes between battles with legit great voice acting and character art. All that and I haven't even unlocked all the circus facilities yet, lol.I've read some criticisms like that story is flat or circus event planning can feel grindy. So it's not like GOAT(!!!) or anything. But man, as a $20 package it feels fresh af and dense with content. I think the setting goes a long way as well. I punched up Darkest Dungeon for a quick moment just to compare/contrast my thoughts. And while there's not doubt DD is masterclass in this tactics subgenre, it was so freakin' bleak & dour, the whole vibe just felt nihilistic & depressing. In contrast Electrique is like a Skittles color explosion while oddly still having a bit of bite with that Victorian London steampunk thing. Feels kinda Burtonesque, kinda We Happy Few. A more welcome balance of grim & fantastical was my quick takeaway.Man, what a hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: While the fighting part of the game may feel really familiar for anyone who played Darkest Dungeon and similar projects, this game by its setting, new mechanics, and story-given gameplay can outstand that label of a Darkest Dungeon clone. A pretty solid game so far, will definitely recommend giving it a try to all fans of the Darkest Dungeon style of gameplay. Prepared a short video review about the game if anyone is interested:

_childDocuments_.review: The negatives from other reviewers are correct.  Be advised, the developers have NOT play tested this game on hard mode.  Resource management on hard mode is a joke.  You can do half of a district run and not get a single needed material to craft even the most basic items.  This could be resolved with some sort of tent or store in town.  They have a tent to look at what you have, this should have some sort of trading option but it doesn't.15 classes in game and half are useless.  There is no concept of a front tank line with a soft back line.   The game is able to hit any position at any time and harder than you can.  The only mechanic in game to counter this fact is that you can employ healers while the game AI doesn't heal much.  You also do get ultimates.  So the battles become their damage versus your healers.  Many defense skills don't even apply to 75% of the stuff they throw at you.  On my second playthrough I just stopped upgrading half the skills each class had because I knew they were worthless.This is also another one of those games that pre rolls hits before you even use the skill.  Try it.  Make an attack, reload the fight, make the attack again, repeat.  You'll hit forever.Another serious flaw is the circus show arrow system.  I just dismissed everyone who had a colored arrow and only recruited classes that had the multicolor star.  It cost some extra money but I could play any class anywhere I wanted in the shows.Another serious flaw is the rage system.  When the computer has one remaining enemy, it goes into automatic rage and gets a damage increase.  With certain classes this can lead to one shot kills.  You can execute a fight flawlessly down to their last man and then bamb, he deletes your players one by one.  Saw a 295 damage per hit enemy Strongman one time.  So now you have to split DPS against the last two enemies so you can one shot the raged enemy in the end.  It's stuff like this which is why put a "restart fight" button in the game.Which is the next problem.  The mechanics are sooo all over the place and unpredictable that they can't implement a Darkest Dungeon run through system.  You basically just keep restarting fights until RNG lands in your favor.This game is too easy in normal mode, not mechanically viable in hard mode due to lack of play testing.  The game is beautiful and themed expertly with a semi decent story but you'll speed through this only to end up at gameplay that has issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: What the hell went wrong?  The Darkest Dungeon-type gameplay and the semi-clever circus management should have been a shoo-in for a great game.  The steampunk aesthetic is really well done and I enjoyed meeting and/or recruiting new performers (or battle machine in the case of the Robot Bear).  The first few hours are captivating and I have many more than that sunk into this.And yet, I can't recommend it because I'm struggling to finish it.  IT IS SO TEDIOUS!  Managing the character bars just isn't fun and the enemies ramp up to being damage sponges that do far more to you than you do to them.  I'm having to hold off on buying upgrades because the RNG resource allotment is so bizarrely random; you can get hundreds of one resource and less than a dozen of another due to bad rolls.  Leveling up punishes you in a way that doesn't encourage smart resource management but hoarding said resources in case you fail to get replenishment, sometime for a whole zone.Fun in the beginning and maybe in small doses thereafter.  No replay value that I find and not a lot of compelling story to go on.  BTW, the villain miracle escape is really old and tired after the third success.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a terrible game, its good a nice style and a sort of humour to it and if you're absolutely fiending for a Darkest Dungeon style fix then this might serve as a sort of methadone, but ultimately it just got kind of boring. A good metaphor for the game is the shows it asks you to set. Before every battle you have to fill out a circus show to earn money, fame, experience and crafting items. Constantly repeating the same show loses rewards and the auto fill option for performers little more than random. You can't set certain performers as defaults for certain shows, and so every single battle you have to stop and go through a quite dull puzzle of fitting performers into the show, every time, its not a tricky puzzle, its not fun or rewarding, its just there. Which is the problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: Much like a real Circus, the game is all style with little substance.On the plus side, the visuals are gorgeous.  If you're just looking to play a pretty-looking game with vaguely Darkest Dungeon style mechanics, then this is your game.  That alone kept me happy enough to finish the game, so I wish steam had a 'neutral' review option instead of yes or no.What pushes me down to no is that pretty much everything else about the game isn't well thought out.  The circus shows are mostly just busy work, the ability to swap out your whole party in between battles breaks a lot of the challenge from the original Darkest Dungeon design philosophy, many of the skills are poorly designed, and many of the characters aren't worth using as a result.Of that list, I'm going to pick on skills the most, since those are the biggest part of gameplay.  You have things like a 30% self-buff to damage that lasts for one round, with the obvious problem that it is worse than just attacking for two rounds in a row.  You have also have things like "attacks enemies that move" which sound good, but are broken by the implementation because it only takes effect when the enemy moves voluntarily.  Skills from other party members that force enemy movement don't count, so you can't set up a combo.  As a result, the most effective way to play is to just pick whatever characters do the most damage (either physical damage or devotion damage, though you  shouldn't focus on devotion damage because it doesn't work on bosses) and use those skills exclusively.  This was enough to easily carry me through the whole game on normal difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Darkest Dungeon-like rogue-lite, but with Steampunk theme to it. You play Amy, a reporter whose mother died in a mysterious fire, maybe started or caused by your Uncle who owns and runs a circus. You go to meet him, covering a story, and when the lights turn on for his new attraction, it starts the madness. For some reason, Amy owns a lion she takes with her, but neither Amy nor Lion dirty their hands attacking the mobs.From there you will fight the folk suffering from the madness in turn-based combat, using the various skills your different circus employees have. You can have up to four characters in a team and you will fight up to four enemies per round. Of the four positions in the combat arena, certain skills can only be performed in certain places, with their effects also having restrictions on which of the enemy positions they can reach, depending again on the skill.There is also a base camp, the circus, where different areas will open up as you progress, allowing you to create shows (for money, experience & fame), recruit new people, heal and go on expeditions.There's clearly a lot of inspiration from Darkest Dungeon here, but this one stands up well with its Steampunk theme, having it's own flavour on the concept. If you like the art style and this genre of game, it's worth a look.I give this one 8 cowardly lions out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate leaving a negative review for this game because it has the skeleton of a decent game. But there are way too many elements that drag it down.1) The game draws immense inspiration from Darkest Dungeon, but fails at the things that DD did well. Whereas the pacing of DD was quick sporadic fights with downtime to recover and plan the next excursion, in this game the loop goes: Figure out who to put in a show --> Stuff people into various buildings for bonuses --> Put together a random team with the remainder --> Fight one battle --> REPEATIt's extremely poorly paced and tedious, with none of the exciting team comp building elements that DD had. Worse, there's no way to save team comps so you're building that all from scratch, every single time.2) This might seem petty, but the game is overall ugly. The cartoonish art direction was intentional and meant to match the circus motif but all you're looking at is amorphous, formless blobs for every character design. Compare this to Darkest Dungeon or Iratus where the designs had an element of coolness or badassery. Every class is an eyesore in this game.3) There's no real strategy or team synergy. Unlike DD or Iratus there aren't a lot of abilities or item combos that create unique synergies that allow you to overcome harder fights. You really just have 4 independent chars that more or less just operate independently. Makes combats very dull by the midway point.A real shame for fans of the genre as there aren't too many yet.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR;  I had fun playing and writing about my experience.Ladies and Gentleman, Children of all ages.  I entreat you to join me upon my journey into the circus game you didn't know you needed.  To see the concepts of darkest dungeon applied to the mystical, applied to the fantastic, applied to the circus.  The Circus Elictrique.The StoryIn the world of Circus Electrique, you shall  enjoin a journalist of years gone by in her struggle to obtain something worht reporting on.  Though dreading the thought, she knows her uncle shall provide a great source of news... though perhaps not in the way she expects.  Nuggets of lore surrounding an uprising of strange steam powered enemies will force her to team up with circus folk in order to solve the deeper mysteries going on in England.  The story is passable, and at times engaging, and I rate it two and a half fire breathers out of three.  If you want to know why theirs half missing, ask the  illusionist.The Game playThey say imitation is the sincerest form of flattery, and if so, this game is in love with Darkest Dungeon.  A lighter take with some game play improvements, turning sanity into a currency of effectiveness called "Devotion" You'll see much the same game play as you would in its much darker dungeons.  Adding more to do in town, such as throwing a circus performance to increase your crafting items, money and Devotion and an ever developing mystery in a linear story event.  With characters such as Fire Breathers, Clowns, Tinkerer's and more, this Circus Electrique feels less daunting to pick up as a party management dungeon crawler than other games of this style. While the enemies often feel monotonous, unique boss fights exist serve to break up your usual fighting style and will force you to rethink your unit placement and combat strategies. With a unique feel, okay city management and engaging boss fights,  I rate this a Full three solid Circus acts out of four.Overall the game takes you down the path of darkest dungeon while giving you story, lore, boss battles and unique unit abilities that will keep you pushing through battle after battle as you manage your circus and troupe in the one, the only, CIRCUS ELECTRIQUE!!! ;)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AMAZING!  The circus sim mechanics are alot of fun and once you hit a certain point the combat becomes brutal (gamewise - its depicted in a fun goofy manner) and strategic.  **Pros** - Fun characters, great combat system, good voice acting, if you are nostalgic for Darkest Dungeon you will like this game, and if DD thematically was too gritty for you, you may find this game more fun.  Loony Toons meets Darkest Dungeon.  **Cons** It seems to be possible to get into "checkmate" if you don't save often.  In DD if all your good characters got killed you can start leveing up again and still have your buildings/progress etc.  This game can put you in a situation where the only battle ahead requires high level characters but you have no money and no high level characters left.  So I would manual save often (in addition to the autosave) so that if you wind up in checkmate you can go back to the last game state where you had a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically it's darkest dungeon set in steampunk london, you build up your circus to upgrade performers and gather materials if you've played darkest dungeon you'll pick it up pretty quick.It's a very linear game, you move through the a district map 1 fight at a time there is no exploration just set up a performance before you go then fight, no looking through the districts for secrets just a event then a fight.The combat is where it ruins it for me it really feels like there isn't any point where moving an enemy into a different position actually does anything, they still do the same abilities just in a different space making some abilities on the characters you run with useless or ruins your set up. The devotion mechanic doesn't work in boss battles either I got the first boss down to 0% and he didn't flee. There doesn't seem to be much in the way of enemy balance either getting spammed by the same debuff attacks so you can't even hit anything or getting a couple of guys who can taunt and get healed its just not fun at all, if you want to flee you wait til your next turn by that time some of your people are dead.Spoiler/rant for second boss battleI've stopped playing since I got stuck on the Thane fight. There is no real way for me to hit it's backline with major single target attacks with the characters you unlock at this point it's just a bunch of blanket attacks that don't do a lot of damage or attacks that are only effective in the first and second position it then spams it's heal ability negating all the damage you did that round. _childDocuments_.review: Circus Electrique (CE) is a clone of Darkest Dungeon, but the setting is a circus in Victorian London with Steampunk embellishments. Many of CE's mechanics are straight out of Darkest Dungeon, however they are tweaked somewhat with effects, status, and state of mind working similar in some ways, but some with more complexity. The labels are all changed; for example, “Devotion” is the analog of Darkest Dungeon's “Stress”. The circus setting adds an odd twist, as a portion of the player's available characters will be required to put on a daily show, while four others are out exploring the streets of London. The idea behind this is that the shows bring in money and components, and the explorers go out on the street maze and fight.The are some settings and options in CE, but none of them are very important (except the ability to turn down the music). CE was designed for a console so there are oddball options like limiting the frame rate to 30 FPS. There is a Controls menu item, however none of the controls can be changed other than "Invert Coin Flick Controls". The hotkeys and control layouts can be viewed, but not changed. It doesn't matter much because the game can be played with the mouse alone and the interface design is pretty solid in this regard. The game features a tutorial built into the start of a campaign that presents a bewildering amount of information in a fairly short period of time. Fortunately, there is a "Codex" that is easily accessible with detailed descriptions for all of the game's mechanics, skills, status effects, consumables, crafting, activities, etc.CE has a backstory that is voiced with static paper doll actors, it's easy to skip past all of it. It doesn't really add much to the game, but sort of gives a reason for the craziness occurring on the London streets. There are two main activities in CE, setting up the daily circus shows and sending a party out on the streets to explore and fight. Yes, this is a somewhat surreal scenario; a circus is putting on daily shows with patrons paying to see acts to finance the performers going out and clearing the streets of London of bad guys. As strange as it is, it does add a way for four performers to gain experience fighting, while three or four others gain experience putting on shows. Choosing who is going to fight vs work a show becomes a complex problem, and perfect balance is hard to achieve. Often, creating a good show will leave the party without the ideal mix or worse, positioning problems.The same kinds of cutthroat RNG fighting mechanics and cheesy tactics that exist in Darkest Dungeon are found in CE. For example, frequently at the end of a fight, the player will need to make passing moves on the last enemy over and over so that a healer can heal the whole party. This is due to the fact that health is persistent. Back at the circus, there is a healing area called the "sleeping cart", but as with Darkest Dungeon, a character in healing is unavailable for the next day and limited spots are available. The biggest difference between Darkest Dungeon and CE is that the party only does one fight, and then goes back to the circus instead of clearing a whole maze at once. The "dungeons" in this case are street districts and they are part of a progressive campaign that are unlocked one by one. Each of the circus performer types come with a randomized skill set and there are synergies between characters. There are even non-combat synergies for the shows. Leveling a character allows the upgrade of skills and the circus act capability as separate items. Characters lost to combat are easily replaced, via a daily train, however sometimes upgraded characters are painful to lose. There are crafted items for party consumable use and gadget items for individuals as well. CE has some bugs, it occasionally crashed with an Unreal Engine 4 message, and a few damage mechanics involving enemy position changes feel like an exploit. Overall, Circus Electrique is a competent and perhaps more forgiving Darkest Dungeon clone, but with a light-hearted atmosphere and a bit of added complexity.

_childDocuments_.review: After having beaten the game once and abandoning two more runs, I'm confident in saying that the complaints of other reviews are absolutely justified. The game starts out really, really strong. At first glance, everything looks fantastic, sounds fantastic, plays fantastic. For about 10 - 20 hours, depending on your patience and RNG tolerance, it stays that way. Some specific points:After a while, however, you begin to notice the flaws:The absurd, story-bound unlock system and inability to grind resources in midgame is just so frustrating that it negates all the fun in the end. Apparently, RNG mercy is also a very limited resources. After one successful run, I got stuck twice halfway through because I simply couldn't upgrade any of my buildings - despite being conservative with the crucial resources. I really hope these major flaws will be addressed somehow. Maybe a new building that generates food/tools or lets you trade one resource for another could be a solution for the resource issue. Revamping the Training mode could also help - as it is, it grants no XP to level characters, only gives random minimal amounts of resources, and all fights are the same (against 1 - 4 identical dummies). Maybe allow the player to pick enemies that were already encountered instead of the dummies, set conditions, make it  training where team combos can be tested, and increase the rewards depending on the selected enemies. A 'roguelike/freeplay mode' with a random starter team of 4 classes (or some 'balanced' combo) and the rest to unlock for a resource cost in any order you like; story nodes on the map replaced with fights and events, or just randomly generated maps - that would be the dream. Such a mode would also justify the price. 20 EUR for a campaign of ~30 hours, and hardly any replay value - is a bit much. In its current state, I can't recommend the game - although I hope I can at some point in the future. It's only been 2 weeks since release, so maybe some of the problems will be addressed in an update. There is a ton of potential here. It's just not fully realized (yet).EDIT: Changed my verdict to a careful 'Recommended' because the major frustration (not enough resources resulting in a midgame softlock) has been addressed in the latest patch. There is now a Trade button that lets you purchase resources. It is not a perfect solution, and my other points still stand (especially my desire for a non-campaign freeplay mode), but it's enough to tip the scales.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is good. The game play loop is decent, the design and artwork is cool. I love the setting. The major problems I have encountered is the pacing of the game. Story seems pretty good, but wish they found a better way to tell it instead of speech bubbles you have to click through after each fight. Its pacing is really too slow. At the time of this review I had about 2.5 hours of playtime on it, and my circus is only level 2, and no where near leveling up (250/1,200xp). That's way too slow, way too much of a grind. It has lootboxes that you unlock periodically. They are free, but it makes it feel like a mobile game. And possibly the biggest let down I have experience is that despite the fact you have to plan shows, you never ever get to watch them. I'd say its worth it to buy it on a decent sale, maybe 40% off of the original price, but definitely not for full price. I would love to see more titles with this sort of setting, but this game play does not do the theme justice.

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much going on in this game, and none of it feels like it matters.Each unit gets six attacks, but only two (maybe three) ever get used. There is space for over a dozen units in the tent, but you only need to worry about focusing on six of them (team of four plus two alternates). Circus performances are a puzzle with 6-9 distinct variables, but the player can get the exact same reward paying attention to only 2-3 of the variables as they can trying to optimize them all. There’s a map, but no real differences between the available paths.But, the most disappointing thing about this game is how little uniqueness each unit has. Half the time I couldn’t remember which clown or escape artist I had decided to bring with me on an expedition, and 100% of the time it didn’t really matter.They stole so much from Darkest Dungeon, but the real tragedy is that they didn’t have the wisdom to use what they stole properly.

_childDocuments_.review: I started a run on The hardest difficulty and found it too easy. After 100 battles im in the end of the 4th district. I assume there are 5 based on story progression. I am now bored. I dont know if i want to play another 10+ hours to win this one. it has become a chore. The story is transparent but the graphics are nice. Resources exist but were literally never an issue even on hardest mode. ( I assume the devs thought people would max roster size right away but that's the worst thing you can do).Tips for beating the game:To win these kinds of games, Lamp Lighters, DD, Etc. on hardest mode you have to just determine win comps, juggle eqm before battles, cheese resource generation.Keep your roster lean no more than ~10 and by the time you are in district 4 you will have over 700 meat easily.People cry about the Devotion "Mana" cost of abilities and enemies tanking your devotion but it's easy to counter. you put the right trinkets on the right people and have to juggle them before battles. You save a support enemy as the last opponent and cheese heal and devotion up before leaving.If its raining or night you need to prioritize quickly ending a battle. You wont win if you don't use items, its better to conservatively heal units since many any of them can be 3 shot. And if they are squishy they will die to an unlucky 1 shot. This makes taunt Invaluable and HP up trinkets a necessity.On hardest mode healing is critical in a party at a minimum 2 clowns or 1 fakir are needed. Get 3  units to be your circus farmers, ideally * type that can link together in a chain this will allow you to 8-9 star 2 different shows and you can alternate (occasionally a 3rd show is needed at reduced value)Use items, Use Items to boost shows,Use Items to heal in battles (cola and bandages are all you will need).Squishy will be 1 shot so you need to give them + HP trinkets. Don't get max roster because units cost resources and only ~10 will provide value at any moment. Don't waste money on level ups let them die and replace them (or use trinket to reduce level up costs on legendary units)you can change districts at any time by going back to London map,... so when you hit level 8s out of the blue you will def be under leveled and NEED to go backwards and level farm. Spinning wheel game resolves 2 to the left of when you click it.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me go ahead and say that I don't think Circus Electrique is a bad game. Honestly I think it has its merits and can be fun, especially when it comes to micro-management and the art-style. (Maybe also the story but I didn't play that far) I think its issue comes to light when it inevitably gets compared to Darkest Dungeon given it's combat, permadeath and similar mechanics when it comes to management and combat. It's a double edged sword that sadly led to me refunding it. I can certainly see myself trying this game again in the future, but I think for the time being I'd rather play Darkest Dungeon (Sorry Zen Studios). To those who want to play this game, I am fully aware that I am recommending it to you, and more power to you! If anything, if you don't want to play Darkest Dungeon because you think it's too challenging, or maybe you don't like the art-style or themes, I recommend giving this game a try and then if you liked it, look at Darkest Dungeon to see if you want a different taste of team-building, RPG combat that is also a Rougelike.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR in case you don't want to watch the video:1. If you've played Darkest Dungeon, the combat is similar, but NOT the same at all. The way the status effects and positions stack and synergise with each other really makes the combat much more challenging, and to some extent, confusing at first.2. Art & sound design are top notch, and the game has some really great voice acting!3. Positions are the name of the game - it can make or break your party combination!4. Speaking of party combination, there are a ton of classes and abilities, both passive and active! Not to mention, special party wide abilities unlock based on how amazing your combinations are!5. The base and resource management aspects are simple, but juggling the combat and setting up good shows, whilst at the same time giving your circus performers enough time to rest and recover, is what makes this game tense and fun at the same time.6. The negative comments on the inability to backtrack is valid - however this speaks more to the difficult roguelike aspect of Circus Electrique. It IS possible to overcome a failed boss fight by putting on more shows and upgrading your train to recruit high level fighters, or by simply saving your game regularly. Despite that, it is fair to say adding an optional backtracking option shouldn't be too difficult, and would definitely make things less abrasive.I would highly recommend fans of turn based games to give this a try, especially at its current, reasonable price!

_childDocuments_.review: London, 1899. Young Amelia visits her uncle who is the master of the Circus Electrique, just when the city is suddenly invaded by the “Vicious”, ordinary citizens turned into crazy bandits who brutally kill everyone on the streets. Amelia, who is also a journalist, chooses to investigate this mysterious phenomenon while secretly trying to uncover the truth behind the death of her mother, who once worked at the same circus. To do so, she gets herself the manager role, controlling the Circus finances, performers and events. London might be in turmoil, but people still go to the Circus and while the shows go on, Amelia and a group of performers explore and battle through the city investigating different mysteries. This is, essentially, the narrative premise, which unfortunately becomes quite predictable later on. Most of the conversations happen in the form of a visual novel, going through screens of characters and dialogues that are fully voiced. The character design looks good enough and the game greatly replicates an alternative Victorian setting using film grain, steampunk elements and vintage effects for the menu screen and user interface. Graphics are nice as well, but during combat the steampunk magic tends to be ruined by low quality 3D models with sluggish and unpolished animations. Now the prologue could feel rather overwhelming, as you move through a tutorial that is full of info, from the character descriptions to the turn-based combat and circus management. There is a lot to learn, especially if you are not used to this genre, but the tutorial guides you through all the fundamentals and gives you a codex to check whenever you feel the need. The gameplay features an interesting mix of different mechanics: on one side there is the Circus management, where you need to control your resources, hire new performers and put on epic shows to become more famous and increase your funds; on the other side you have the exploration, in which you navigate through the city map, investigate different events and fight against the Vicious gang. Starting with the circus gameplay mechanics, you begin with few resources and a pre-selected team of performers which will help organize the first shows. When preparing a new show, it’s important to select members who have better affinity with each other, as this will increase the public satisfaction and reward you with more money, experience and gifts. As you upgrade the Circus, different kinds of shows will become available, and it’s recommended to swap them each day so people won’t get annoyed watching the same ones. You can also find some other buildings that can be upgraded, mainly a train where you can hire new performers, a dormitory where you can heal the injured performers, and an artisan where you can craft new items to use in battle or when preparing a show. After many successful shows your Circus will eventually level up, unlocking new buildings and better upgrades. The circus management directly affects your power and skills in combat, so it’s really an important and fun aspect of the gameplay.Speaking about the exploration part, before moving through the city you need to build a team of max four fighters. You explore the districts by choosing different roads which lead you to the same objective (the final boss of the area). Each road has different types of events in it, maybe a conversation with your uncle, a treasure chest, a mini-game or a random situation that requires you to make a choice, but more often it’s going to be a combat encounter. Your performers have different stats, attacks and passive abilities depending on their level and their class (clown, firebreather, illusionist etc.). Combat is turn-based and you can place your fighters on different rows, altering their order as well trying to alter the one of your enemies using attacks that inflict different penalties. Characters also have a devotion bar, which is essentially their level of trust. The devotion can also be affected by some attacks and if it’s too low then the character (yours or the enemies’) will flee from combat. Battles also include day/night and weather conditions that can increase the effectiveness of some attacks and nullify some others, like when using electrical or fire attacks under heavy rain. Combat at night is more painful as there is an “alert” bar that fills after each attack and notifies the police after reaching its max, so the best strategy here is to aim at enemies’ devotion or select the most powerful attacks to finish the battle quickly, otherwise backups will arrive and it will be harder to win. Combat is probably the best part of the game, as it shows enough variety with enemies’ classes and challenging boss fights, allowing for different strategies. The only problem I found is that you can only move forward through the city roads, meaning if you are stuck on a battle and you don’t have enough skilled performers, there isn’t much you can do. You can’t go backwards, take a different road and complete other fights to gain experience and level up your team. That’s why I recommend saving often, at least once after two in-game days to be sure you never find yourself in this position.Circus Electrique is a good-looking variation of the  formula, less punitive, more linear and with not much replayability. The story, although showing an interesting premise, becomes flat and predictable after a while, leaving you with only the pleasure of managing your own circus, discovering the districts of London and engaging in challenging fights.

_childDocuments_.review: Listen to the negative reviews.There's a lot that's decent here, but the game wears thin in the fourth district and a *lot* of critical flaws start to show.Broadly, Circus Electrique is Darkest Dungeon, but in a linear narrative form. It's also got heavy worker placement elements, since you're running a circus.Now, Darkest Dungeon does a lot to cushion you from randomness. The deathblow system, clear communication about how mechanics work, no recruitment cost, no roster maintenance cost. You can softlock yourself, but it's hard.Here, though? You need a bunch of high level characters to do performances to generate resources, but you actually don't want that at all. Characters cost meat to keep around and scrap to upgrade, and both are unreliable to get. In fact, nearly all of it comes from random drops as far as I can tell. You might get it from circus acts! But the acts don't tell you if you do. And you get a universal currency, cash, that you can convert into meat or scrap, but it's expensive and you have to manually click for each conversion for some reason.But the early districts are super easy. So it's very likely you'll do what I did which is replay one of them to level up a bit more, get screwed on meat drops, and have to dismiss half your roster to try and get costs under control.But the game wants you to have a big roster stuffed full, so as soon as you dismiss units you don't have enough to do circus shows at your level, and you have to go for easier shows that yield less, and congratulations the tail spin has started.Also of note, a lot of the units in this game suck. As in, they don't have a plan. They don't have any self synergy. They don't function. And you can't swap their skills out. You're stuck with whatever random garbage they have by default.Fire Eaters are good, Clowns are good, Strongmen are good. That's three classes out of maybe ten that are useable. Everything else has crap like "50% chance to move a single target to a random spot, lose 10% sanity" for five out of six moves, and then "10 damage to any target, lose 3% sanity" for its sixth move. The circus acts want these other classes, and they want them levelled up, but again: you don't.I think 90% of my problems with this game would evaporate if units didn't have a constant meat upkeep, and easy mode cures that, but the gameplay is already a little tedious and making fights easier would just make that worse. Plus, fights are kind of flat. The most effective strategy is just Do Damage To Man, and buffing and synergizing is just wasting your actions.That all said, there's an okay game buried in amongst the jank. With some polish and reworks, it could be really good, and I think it's still fine if you play trying to aggressively conserve meat. I wouldn't recommend it at full price unless you're really thirsting for Darkest-Dungeon-likes, but it's a fine pickup on sale.Edit: The linearity of the game *really* hurts it. As does the inexplicable decision to put meat, which you need regularly to maintain your lineup, exclusively behind random loot drops from fights. This makes it *very* likely you'll play this thing like a normal dungeonlike and softlock yourself twelve hours in. Also, in a game where the most powerful skills are just dealing damage, damage scaling on enemies is a bit cracked. In DD, you can log a couple hundred hours before you lose a character for reasons outside of your control (back-to-back envenomating spider crits.) In Circus, that's just normal high level play. There's also no stunlock protection, and later enemies have AoE full party stuns, so you can just... spend a full round never getting to act and losing 2+ characters as a normal game experience. It's doody, is what I'm saying. I'm wiping my save and starting from a new file, and we'll see if the game is more possible when you've already played a bunch of it.2nd Edit: Seven hours into save file #2 and I've caught up to my first save. By only raising the skills I know I'll use (at most 50% of a character's kit, usually 20%) and avoiding upgrading the sleeping facilities and keeping my roster limited to just the folks I need for combat or performances I'm... still only a couple rng rolls away from total starvation on normal difficulty. Also the class balance sucks waaaay worse than I thought. The ideal team comp is just four Strongmen. Two in the back to aoe, two in the front to burst down targets that taunt. You probably want to give them +precision gear, and you need to make sure they randomly generate with the boomerang skill, but otherwise they outperform every other class. They can handle the bonkers damage from late game attacks, they can eliminate an enemy team in two rounds, the only thing they don't work in is a gauntlet of fights and then you just take one fakir with points in only their healing skill. Some other classes can perform a bit better in very niche circumstances (like fireeaters at night), but even that's debatable. What a shame.3rd Edit: Multiple choice events come with icons under each choice to help you figure out what they might give you. For example, an exp symbol and an item symbol mean the event does not give you exp or items but instead costs you half your meat and money. Another way to describe this is "pull from a hat, and one of the items in the hat is reloading your last save."4th Edit: Redid the multiple choice, picked an option I'd picked before, got a pile of bonus meat instead. This is bad! If the multiple choice events are not just random in what the symbols mean, but random in what the individual choices output, and sometimes they can *cost* you meat, and meat is scarce and running out can brick your save, the game's just deciding on its own whether you're going to be able to complete the campaign. Nah. I like the aesthetic, and effort clearly went into the writing and worldbuilding, but we're in thumbs down country now boys.5th Edit: Acrobats and cannoneers are useable! Not better than strongmen, but most of their skills are functional. Also you're apparently supposed to be using as many rare unique characters as possible, since they have lower food costs and scaling and their own unique passives, but you kind of have to gatcha for them, and only after you've unlocked them via random event, and once you do have them they can still get randomly deleted from full health by two enemies acting before they do. If you get very lucky, you can find the trinket that reduces food cost and stick it on characters in your back row, but it's also purely a random drop. Sensing a theme? Spin the wheel, win a disappointment.6th Edit: Nah. Late game damage scaling (on normal) is bonkers. You start a battle, your acrobat takes one action, two enemies act, your acrobat is dead. And everything is spongey as hell. Even if the enemies spread out their attacks (they don't), you're still wailing on the same dude for a whole turn. And that dude drops a taunt + dodge up + regen on his turn, and his healer friend brings him back to full health on his turn, and you could theoretically bring a debuffer to try and counteract this but your debuffer acts once, two enemies act, your debuffer is dead. Twenty two hours is more than enough to say I gave this thing a fair shake. It's a nice aesthetic wrapped around a badly communicated tedious slog.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun Darkest Dungeon in steampunk London.  You have 15 classes of characters that you need to juggle between circus shows and fighting against various steampunk enemies while you explore various districts in London. Every 1-3 days, you can have a circus show, depending on the complexity of the event. At the same time you have to explore the map. Each district is a series of distinct paths leading to a final boss fight. Win that an unlock a new district. Once a path is selected you cannot go back. One in-game day finishes when you win a fight on the map. With various recourses that you can get by winning fights or finding them on the map, you can unlock some special fights, hidden paths or reopen completed districts, allowing you to choose the other available paths. You need to keep a varied selection of characters as it's possible to get stuck on a fight, if you focused too much on one type of squad. Characters have health and devotion. If they are not in fights, circus shows or other special buildings, then they will loose devotion and eventually leave your circus. You cannot just keep characters around if you don't use them. Overall it's a good game, especially if you are in the mood for a less stressful and more easy to pick up Darkest Dungeon. Worth the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: A strategist's dream come true.  Balancing skills for fighting with skills for performing,  and choosing who will go out each day.  Sometimes you need you best fighter to pull off a particularly challenging performer.  Which items will you spend your resources on,  which tents will you make use of (is the benefit worth the cost).  Lots of meaningful choices to make. Playing on Hard mode,  I'm finding that resources are plentiful,  yet you still need to make strategic choices.  You can't just upgrade everything the instant you level up.  You need to make choices.  Similar with the performers.  I like this one better than darkest dungeon and other popular titles in the genre.  The ability to save (plus autosaves) can be a boon for folks who might be tempted to rage quit after loosing their best characters.

_childDocuments_.review: A flawed but overall fun experience.It removes a good chunk of the randomness of Darkest Dungeon style combat (easy access to healing/taunt effects) but replaces it with frustrating minigames on the map. Understandable that they are of the appropriate flavour however, it gets old fast especially when you're a completionist like me and who genuinely enjoyed most of the game.Lategame also gets quite tiresome, either from 1 dimensional bosses that will one shot your squishier performers or easy access to broken combinations (healing is a blessing in this game). The other thing which bothered me was how similar the builds were, even amongst the unique performers it was often just the same strong effect but with one or two different attacks which felt a bit boring to be honest.Overall, if any of this sounds interesting then pick this game up on sale, otherwise I can't honestly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This could be a great game. It's a decent value for 20 bucks. It plays very much like Darkest Dungeon but has enough of its own thing going on in the way of aesthetics, story and twists on mechanics to be different. If you are done with Darkest Dungeon and aren't sold on DD2 because of its departure from the original formula, this might be for you. There is a lot of shine on the finished product and some cool concepts to dig into here. It takes until the end of the first act to really start to pick up steam, so you won't be able to properly evaluate the game and still be able to return it if you don't like it, so check out a few videos before you do. It is story driven, so there is a samey vibe every time you restart a run. I hope the devs come back to this hidden gem to release a proper dlc, but I somehow doubt that is in the cards. I haven't encountered any bugs and it runs well on my potato...so again, for 20 bucks, it is a worthwhile venture if you like roguelike DD clone style gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Nice first impression, strong aesthetic, but ultimately a poor imitation of Darkest Dungeon with severely lacking balance in both the combat and base-building aspects. Maybe try Iratus instead, if you're done with Darkest Dungeon but still want that particular itch scratched? It honestly does a better job of living up to their shared inspiration.Full Review: In a sense, this game is remarkably on-brand for its circus/carnival theme. When you first start, you'll be wowed by the gorgeous presentation, the strong aesthetics and the intriguing setting. Mixing up the by-now classic 'Steampunk Victorian' setting, you find yourself leading an  Circus, fighting against a clockwork-and-steam based menace throughout London's fog-shrouded streets. Balance putting on grand shows in the Circus proper for money and crafting-materials with pursuing an answer to the current crisis, fighting and engaging in various minigames as you explore each borough!Sure, the basic gameplay is lifted wholesale from Darkest Dungeon - gather resources through position-based side-on turn-based RPG battles, then use them to build up your base, allowing you to strengthen your team in various ways as you dive in for the next fight. But instead of Lovecraftian horror and dour adventurers who seem ready to crack at the drop of a hat, you've got quirky circus-performers, a lighter tone, and the ability to save and load your game as you please! Not necessarily a bad shift. Certainly, a fresh take on that style of RPG, considering that Iratus: Lord of the Dead is similarly dark and gothic.But, alas... if you linger overlong in the carnival, you'll start to peer past the painted facades, and realize that the machines chugging along behind them are held together with chewing-gum and string. Sure, it's got everything Darkest Dungeon has, it all just works a bit  somehow. The 'Devotion' system that replaced Sanity feels vestigial and bolted-on, failing to provide the same impact. Your 'performers' all have randomized skills and abilities rather than you being able to configure them as you please, which - along with entirely too many enemies throughout the game possessing Taunts or repositioning attacks - makes the combat fairly janky, denying you the ability to make a well-tuned, carefully thought-out team like you might in Darkest Dungeon.And as for the base-upgrading... you know how in Darkest Dungeon, the various dungeons had different drop-rates for various upgrade-resources? And how your limited inventory meant that you often had to choose whether to bring home Heirlooms for building-upgrades, or instead focusing on gold and gemstones that could be used to upgrade your team? Yeah, you can't do that in this game. The rewards you get from battles and treasure-chests are seemingly randomized, and the various boroughs of London are explored in a strict order as you follow the plot. If you're short on one resource or another, well, too bad! Nothing you can do except pray. Well, that, or  it, of course. Using money. Which is another resource that you'll soon find yourself running out of.In general, you just seem to be in a constant state of not having enough  - unlocking new upgrades for your Circus only to find that you can't afford to actually buy them, leveling up performers only to find that you can't afford to upgrade their skills, and if you finally DO get some of the circus-buildings properly upgrades... you'll find that you can't actually afford to USE them. The difficulty-settings, meanwhile, ONLY affect the combat-gameplay, which is pretty easy if, as previously mentioned, ... doing nothing for the resource-management aspect. For an extra bit of frustration, the only thing you reliably CAN control is the crafting-materials you receive, because of COURSE this game has a crafting-system, every game has to have one of those these days, by law. You mostly get those from circus-performances, and you can thus choose to put on the performance that'll net you the stuff you need. Except that virtually everything you can craft ALSO requires one or more of the 'basic' resources that you're always running out of, turning the whole crafting-system into just one more thing you generally can't afford to use.Perhaps the most annoying bit of imbalance, though, is the 'beds'. You have limited slots for your performers. VERY limited, and very slow and expensive to increase. Everything else in the game screams for you to build up a large and diverse 'stable'. Performers are, as previously mentioned,  - so you'll never see everything a given class has to offer without hiring two or three specimens. They also have separate stat-blocks for combat and circus-performances - someone who's awesome in combat may have a fairly useless performance, while someone with a vital performance-skill could be quite useless in a fight. Different circus-shows - which, as previously mentioned, are needed in order to get different crafting-materials - also require different performers. And then there are the 'Legendary' performers you can unlock and add to your collection. Except you don't have room for them. At all. Ever. Instead, the arrival of a new class will usually force you to fire an existing performer in order to make room, trying to decide whose departure will screw up your show-plans and battle-party the least. In Darkest Dungeon, the fact that your 'heroes' could permanently die, necessitating replacements fresh off the stagecoach, as well as being able to profit by hiring a fresh batch, sending them under-equipped into a dungeon to gather loot, and then kicking them out afterwards instead of spending money to help them recover... that was was all part of its dark tone. You were desperately trying to keep your seasoned troops alive, while simultaneously being forced to recognize that they were all expendable pawns. It , there. In this game, with its vastly different atmosphere? The fact that you're often forced to callously discard the people who've fought by your side and protected you up to this point, in order to make room for the new and better models, is just incongruous and at odds with the tone. Oh, and of course, whatever precious resources you spent upgrading those discarded performers are forever lost too. Grand.That's Circus Electrique - like any carnie-game, it'll blind you with a flashy presentation while hiding broken mechanisms behind a brightly-painted front. It is not without its virtues, true - the artistic and aesthetic side is genuinely amazing, and the plot's not too shabby either - but the gameplay is just poorly balanced throughout, which is enough to turn the thumbs down for me. I haven't even gotten into how some performers are just flat-out useless while others are overpowered, or the way you can (with the right resources) re-explore old areas in order to try different paths and find missing collectibles... only to find that nothing's been scaled up to your current level, making prizes and XP-gains alike underwhelming at best, and turning the unavoidable battles into a dull, pointless slog. Consider this a pointed lesson on how important it is to get the details right, not just the broad strokes or first impressions, then go play Darkest Dungeon instead - or, if you can derive no more entertainment from that masterpiece despite its vast and active modding-scene, check out Iratus: Lord of the Dead, which did a much better job of stealing its fundamental gameplay-loop.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming Darkest Dungeon-lite that wholly commits to its aesthetic. The range of appearance and animation of the (somewhat exaggerated, in cartoon-fashion) carnival heroes is worth the ticket price, and the combat is enjoyable, if somewhat less consistent than Darkest, with the taunts and traps of later derivatives more central, and characters greatly ranging in efficacy (though the design is so fun, it is worth it to try to make parties with all of them, regardless - though maybe less so on Hardmode).Circus management is much more involved than other DD genre pieces; I suspect one of the only ways to get into "failstate" is to over-invest in infrastructure, but given that you can save at any "day," it is pretty easy to backtrack. Setting up performances is the main draw here. I would've liked to see more in the resolution, but for a indie game, the newspaper clippings are still a pretty good compromise.Stress (called "Devotion" in this game) management is made a little too easy by relying on a couple of the character classes; I would've preferred an emphasis on "benching" via circus performances as stress-relief, but early versions of Darkest Dungeon had this as well (defensive Jester setup), so hardly a new problem.Highly recommended if colourful carnival characters and a Tesla-Victorian setting appeals, or if you want a positional dungeon crawler with more mercy than Darkest Dungeon or more heart than Iratus.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot. Honestly sometimes I feel like they made it just for me. So, if, like me, the phrase "Electricpunk Darkest Dungeon style circus game" excites you then regardless of the rough edges in place you will enjoy this game.It plays a lot like Darkest Dungeon but does enough of its own stuff to separate it from that game. It's story is fun and the characters are surprisingly enjoyable with unexpectedly good voice work from the main cast. The exploration and circus management side are fun but its the combat and wonderful variety of classes (all circus performers of course!) that really sell it.My main gripe is that the final two areas see a really large jump in difficulty compared to the rest and, at that point, grinding is basically mandatory. If you don't mind the grind you'll love it. If you are on the fence give it a try! I want to see more from the developer and the creativity of this title deserves to be supported.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: So after 10 hours and reaching the very end of the 3rd district I just don't think I can recommend this game. I don't regret buying it because it a cool idea from an indie company that just was not well executed. My biggest issue is the game is just boring. The circus gimmick quickly becomes a chore rather than something fun due to the annoying meet this number requirements. The amount of performers you are allowed to have at any one time is WAY too low especially because almost none of the class are actually helpful for combat in ANY way. I played for 10 hours and used the same 4 classes because the other classes I unlocked were WAY too weak to even begin to compete with the absurd enemy damage. Combine this with unlocking classes at a snails pace and the game just does not feel good to play. The game wants to be like Darkest Dungeon but fails to capture the meaningful class dynamics seen in that game. Along with this the way the exploration is done is poor and requires the use of an item to fully explore. This is a major issue in a game like because if you are wiped on a boss battle and do not want to safe scum then you have 0 way of grinding a new team up and have soft locked yourself. I have seen a few reviews talking about the difficulty and while playing on normal I have never lost a performer let alone a battle, HOWEVER, I have also been using pretty much the same party comp for my whole play time with the occasional swapping of a single character so it would not surprise me that if you attempted to try different party comps and spread the xp around to classes that do not perform well in combat that the difficulty would quickly spike to the point of frustration. All in all while I would love to recommend this game because I love the idea and love turn based RPGs the issues with the game play and lack of class balance make it simply an unfun experience. So no while the game has a very cool theme and is in a genre of games I ADORE, if you were my homie (which you are) and asked me if you should buy it I would unfortunately say no.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Steampunk-flavored art and story line. Wonderful voice acting. Easy to play mechanic. This is a game that anyone of about any age could get into and play easy, even if the game itself isn't.  I'm not done yet only because I've been rationing this out like a sweet candy. This game - this company - understands Steampunk so well that as someone who loves the aesthetic, I can't help but love this thing and hope they are moved to make more games of the same high quality and playability.  Thanks guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: Good game based on the Darkest Dungeon formula. Surprisingly decent story with more voice acting than you would expect. I enjoyed the setting in a not often explored timeframe.There are some balancing issues with some character archetypes not feeling as useful as others, but the combat overall works.Worth a play if you want to support indie developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: As of this review, I am 4/5 of the way through my first playthrough. The resource system needs to be less RNG-dependent, but other than that, I think this game is brilliant.You have to approach most fights very strategically - meaning you will likely be reloading a lot after seeing a fight with a suboptimal team on the field. While that feels "cheaty" or monotonous in some games, here it feels like it was the intended (and fun) way to approach the game.  Are enemy stiltboxers buffing themselves to extreme levels and then one shotting your team members? Then bring the illusionist and start stealing all those buffs so your performers can one shot. Is a human cannoballer charging up and blasting herself into your back line? Then bring a escape artist and start chaining her down when she tries.I am growing addicted to this game and dont really want the campaign to come to an end.8/10 overall as it stands now - will be 9/10 if they can fix the resource RNG somehow.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: This is a mixed review.  Game is pretty good.  Nice theme.  Unlike other games this one expects you to never loose.  If someone dies you have to reload or just be behind.  No way to really grind up.  Game plays okay till Ch 5 then you just have to  reload about 30+ times hoping to get lucky.  If you like these kind of game like I do you will think this is almost a good game.  Maybe they'll patch it and fix some of the balance issues, or add new modes to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: I love the aesthetic and character animations are very playful, cute and sometimes silly it really does make me smile with its steam punk Bioshock vibe the score is enjoyable and its easy to pick up and play the story is interesting and fairly comedic mini games are different which is nice to see. I really enjoy this for the same reasons as i enjoyed Darkest Dungeon the combat is pretty much identical it keeps the same risk of loosing characters and employing new ones to replace them as well as the item finds during exploration levelling up both your characters and home but it does it in a much more light-hearted way. Circus Electrique feels like you are making your way towards something with high moral but still has a sinister overtone rather than the impending doom and damnation lording over you in DD.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this game kinda suffers from having too much and also not enough happening at the same time. There are a ton of combat mechanics off the top that are much less clear and direct than Darkest Dungeon (the clear inspiration for the combat/base section) but the rate at which new things are unlocked and that you can bring in new people made me fee like I was still in the tutorial by the end of the 2nd map. It has a lot of chaff that could be trimmed and a lot more hand holding than it really needs. The maps are very linear as well.Conceptually it's a fun game and the art is nice but it just doesn't scratch the DD itch that I was hoping for and I'm not likely to finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with a cool theme and art work. Love the filter to make it look old too, adds some charm. Way less excited about some of the classes than I would have liked. Clearly there are great ones, good ones for certain situations, and many which just suck all the time. But overall I like the story and the game play in this. Setting up nightly circus is cool and giving your crew tasks around the circus grounds while you go out and fight is a nice way to make your whole team useful, something I wish more games with big rosters did. Worth the $20 for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great concept and a combination of gameplay mechanics I have adored in the past, but it didn't quite come together for me. I'm recommending it because I think it's good, I guess it's just a worse version of that first Darkest Dungeon though. I think just the details are off a bit and it could get that final polish I'm looking for in time. Having said all that and even with the intent to come back I will say at 7 hours I was looking at something else.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: Very good alternative to Darkest Dungeon gameplay with neat twists and tweaks the formula. Good voice acting with a decent story. Good sound and VFX as well as clean so you can play on a steam deck well. Long on the tutorial aspect to get you introduced to the world and how the systems work but it ramps up later in the game satisfyingly.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very fun game, but there is one big issue for me: The shell game becomes increasingly unfair and difficult, and if your eyes aren't up to snap for one reason or the other, you can forget the 100% districts. I always will hate shellgames, and given that some achievement-related content is hidden behind it makes me very sad. Otherwise I absolutely love it and have no nitpicks.
_childDocuments_.name: Circus Electrique

_childDocuments_.review:
When everyday Londoners mysteriously turn into vicious killers, only the circus' lineup of Strongmen, Fire Blowers, Clowns and other performers possess the unique talents necessary to save the city. 

Circus Electrique is part story-driven RPG, part tactics, part circus management, and completely enthralling - all with a steampunk twist. 

Through tactical turn-based battles, these unlikely heroes face Bobbies, British Sailors gone bad, aggressive Posh Girls, and other Victorian-era archetypes stand in their way - not to mention the occasional menacing Mime or Robobear. 

The game's innovative Devotion morale system affects characters' performance not only in battles, but also for actual circus shows, dutifully managed between heroic jaunts through six sprawling districts.
