_childDocuments_.review: It's kind of interesting that you play as a police squad solving cases, but it's just SUCH a generic JRPG outside of that. There are some genuinely great options (like automatically skipping the title screen and loading your newest save) but I couldn't convince myself to give more time to it. It keeps you from getting overleveled, so it can make every boss fight frustrating because you're barely capable of winning.If you want a JRPG to play, I don't recommend it even on sale. There has to be a better choice for you. And I really wanted to like it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: This is the definition of a very slow burn. I would say 80% of the game is the side content and 20% is the actual story. It also doesn't pick up until near the end. Anyone who tells you this is a good starting point is steering you in the wrong direction. That 20% story content is literally a sequel to the previous trilogy. Names, terms and characters appear you don't even know about that you are supposed to.The game also has some annoying achievements that are just not fun or worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: I dont do much reviews after 09232 games i bought on steam, but this game is a boring buzz kill. Prolong quest is a zzz n roaming around the city confusing location quest  for 6 hours is too much for me.  Bought this because i have played the newer Trail of Heroes n good review.  This is a hard no for me for $39, sadly steam only let me refund after 2hours I used 6.  Deleting game n moving on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that i have played every single Trails game released in the west to date. The Sky series was one of the best games i ever played in my life and i cherish those games. Then i played CS and liked them until the end of CS2 when things got kinda stupid with the whole "Lol, they didn't REALLY die!" bullcrap. I pushed myself through CS3 and CS4 because i was invested in the story and the characters, even if i hated just how formulaic the storytelling and game structure had become. The ending of CS4 left a VERY bad taste in my mouth, even with the good ending where Rean doesn't die at the end because none of the antagonists learned from their mistakes or even suffered any consequences for their actions. CS4 had turned into a soup opera.Fast forward to this game. Now i know that it's not a problem for a lot if not most people, but there is no English dub for this game. There was English dub for all the other games but this one gets the shaft for some reason. I realize that it's a personal thing but without understanding what they are saying, i actually found their Japanese voice lines very irritating. I had been hearing that this is "The best one in the entire series." But i'm already starting to see some of the same problematic writing in this games story. Couple this with some baffling design choices for some things and the no English dub and knowing where the story ends up ultimately at the end of CS and i just can't enjoy this game anymore.TLDR:People, just because a game is in the same series of some other games you enjoyed, don't assume it'll be for you. Do your research before you spend way too much money on it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write a review, and when I do, I only write the ones I like, but this one is really the opposite. I couldnt stand the first hour of the game, this game has the most filler & rubbish & boring dialogue you can imagine (maybe there are others that are worst, but since I dont play any game, this was my worst one so far, seriously), so I just closed the game and requested a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Japanese rpgs have a serious issue with just flat out disrespecting your time. Gets to the point that i dread finding new areas because every npc in the place is going to trap me in some conversation that feel like its written by two people who have never engaged another human being. Just heaps and heaps of useless dialogue that adds nothing and goes nowhere. if your not going to localize it well, just make less of it.  Then you get an objective with no context of where your supposed to go, not even like a general heading. Just makes you feel like they enjoy wasting your time. All of the controls feel like they were mapped by someone whose never used a keyboard too. another layer of ♥♥♥♥ this.Also there seems to be a not very subtle inferiority complex from the devs towards western culture. for example, one of your party members is a 14 year old girl who during her introduction informs you shes been sent to you on special assignment from the Epstein corporation. Like you could have named it anything lol. kind of neat insight to what a POC must feel like when your group just gets a blatant shot taken at you. just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bizarre.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't like other entries in Legend of Heroes, this one isn't going to change your mind. It's mindlessly dull, uninteresting story, uninteresting characters. I think these games can be good, but they have such terrible pacing it becomes too much of a chore trying to find anything decent about them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Overpriced port of psp games that already had english fan translation 2 years ago. By buying this port you support publisher that actively hurts western fanbase by taking down fan translations of current Trails games. If you really want to play Trails from Zero and support Falcom you should get japanese version of the game for much cheaper and install fan patch with almost the same translation as this version.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review for both Zero and Azure and I got to say they did a fantastic job following up from the previous games. The Crossbell arc in this series has such amazing world-building despite Crossbell being so small compared to Liberl. Every new day in these games you have support quests added to your list of things to do, but there is also so much extra dialogue to be found with characters around the country. And the characters are so interesting and enjoyable, easily one of my favorite casts in an RPG.The story is great with this game taking place roughly a year after the Liberl arc. It has tons of call backs and references to the previous games, however you can enjoy these games fascinating story without the previous games. These two games also have such amazing settings for some of the chapters that make the world feel alive.The combat is mostly the same with slight tweaks, mostly to the magic. Nothing really to complicated as its not to difficult, but in Azure you will need to utilize everything you have as its endgame can be brutal. Another thing that caught my attention as well is the music. The soundtrack for both games are amazing with great battle themes, groovy or calming area themes as well as emotional songs too. A negative might be that in Azure at least a lot of songs are from the previous games which makes Azure soundtrack fairly small, but the songs they do have are some of the best, especially the boss themes.Nevertheless this duology was very enjoyable. I still suggest playing the Trails in the Sky games first, but you can play this one as more of a taste of what this series offers. Plus this game works great on Steamdeck and requires no tinkering.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. Truly amazing. This first entry in the Crossbell duology doesn't have to hide at all behind its liberlian predecessors. I fell in love with all the characters of the Sky trilogy, but getting accustomed to this new cast happened in basically no time. Doesn't mean you won't see any known faces around ;)Crossbell is a small country, and when I crossed basically the whole map by chapter 1, I was worried that the game would run out of locations for its long playtime. But worry not, there are still more than enough locations left to explore for Trails to Azure ;)If you didn't play the Sky trilogy, you can technically start with this game, as it is a new story arc with only a few links and unspoilery callbacks to the predecessor. However, these few links will hit much harder if you know the previous story. And the Sky games are truly awesome as well, so GO PLAY THEM ALREADY!
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: The forth game of the Legend of Heroes Series, an absolutely great game with the introduction of a new arc. I really liked the new cast and the rest of the characters in this game. Moreover, I really like the different approach of building the story and characters. although it was not 100% similar the sky's storytelling but it shined on just like the previous games. I was not fond of the new battle UI, but it was nice change and i got adapted to it eventually. There is a lot of quality of life features that were not in sky arc, and made the game more smooth and enjoyable to play. I do not recommend starting with this game as the entry game for the Legend of Heroes series, because most of the build up that happened in the prior games is clearly on an effect when you go through the story of this game. Really great game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: I sometimes hear that the Crossbell arc is the worst arc of the series. While it might not be exactly as grand, absolutely DO NOT sleep on these games if you loved FC/SC/3rd and want more! I went from 3rd to Cold Steel but this was a mistake; Crossbell DOES fill in some stuff from the previous games. Not required to enjoy CS, but it will deepen the plot and give more backstory.The layered story and world-building are very similar to the Trails trilogy, and even though Zero has a slightly slow start, after a while I totally fell in love again with the characters and world. It still runs on the FC engine, which mean the graphics are less "modern" but are still overflowing with charm. The soundtrack has a few more "not-as-memorable" tracks than usual, but also has some true bangers.After finishing Zero, I didn't feel like I played something inferior or skip-worthy; to me this was a full-fledged part of the Legend of Heroes series!Man, I love Falcom so much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely one of the best games jrpgs I've bad the pleasure of playing! For anyone interested in getting into the trails series, I recommend staring with the sky trilogy. You could technically start with zero, but there will be some spoilers and some references that won't make sense without having gone through the sky games.I played FC and SC on normal and sky 3rd on hard. I decided to go with nightmare for zero and it was a very enjoyable experience. If you have a solid understanding of how the trails games function, than you shouldn't have too much trouble with this game. The only difficult parts were a couple fights early on, some of the black chests, and one of the side quests was rather challenging (even though the party felt that fight in particular was easy lol). Between all of the sky games and zero, I think I would say zero is second only to SC. I'm a few hours into Azure, and so far it's looking very promising.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the Trails In The Sky trilogy, this was a lovely sequel to jump into. A new location (huge city) with a new cast and a bunch of NPC's to meet. At the same time, there's a lot of connective tissue tying back to the older games and even some cameos. Love that I didn't have to resort to a 3rd party mod to implement Japanese voices this time. Lots of graphical improvements while still maintaining the lovable chibi animation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: The Trails series: 10/10 masterpieceThis is the fourth installment in the winding The Legend of the Heroes: Trails (Kiseki) series. This series is one massive story that began in 2004, is still published in 2024, is planned to go on for decades longer, and is still growing in popularity.This begins the Crossbell arc - a new country, several new characters, and an extension of the story and worldbuilding from the Trails in the Sky arc.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the 4th installment of the TLoH series. It was a good game if we compare it to the first 3 games.It was nice seeing new characters and seeing old characters in a different story. It was a different experience as the game is in the POV of police officers instead of bracers. We still have Estelle and Joshua in the game as they are one of the main characters. But it was interesting to play from Lloyd's perspective.STORY 8/10 - Quite similliar to the other games but the twists had me suprised.MUSIC 6/10 - Didn't strike any interest while playing like the FC and SC did.COMBAT 10/10 - Definite improvements into the combat, even the orbal system was changed.GAME 8/10 - I did enjoy playing it but one thing that I didn't like was the absence of Haze system that was in the first 3 games. This means you either have to dodge enemies or fight or try to flee every time.I would recommend this game to everybody that wants to play a good rpg
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: The Kiseki games has been known for its great world building, writing, twists and characters. The brilliant story of Trails From Zero is focused on the state of Crossbell, and honing in on a smaller cast of characters, Falcom delivers a fantastic and engrossing adventure to uncover the mysteries and secretive scandals of this nation.The music is an excellent additive that complements most of the iconic moments that this game has to offer. Inevitable Struggle being my favorite one.Regarding the gameplay, this is the natural evolution that Trails in the Sky introduces. This is no surprise since its a direct sequel from the previews Kiseki games in the world of Zemuria. Altough a great starting point for newcomers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: In case you don't know you should start this franchise with Trail in the Sky.Coming from trail in the Sky, Zero is a fantastic new arc:+ Great story+ Stellar Cast+ Lots of fan service with returning characters and all+ Rewarding combat system (if you plan Hard or above)+ Lots of Quality of life options- easiest game in the series to this point- still no access to the menu inside combats9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Going through the Trails series and next on the list is Trails from Zero. The game does start a bit slow, but the new cast of the SSS have such a great dynamic that even the slow bits were enjoyable to hear them comment on. It was also nice to see some plot threads from the Sky games get wrapped up in this one so despite being a new arc, it's probably not the BEST starting place despite what NISA might say. Combat is what you'd expect from this series by now with little tweaks here and there. But overall a good start to the Crossbell duology. I've heard the real meat is in Azure so I can't wait to get started!
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Really great from start to end. I liked the slow start leading to an intense ending that presented questions to be answered in the next games. The SSS grew on me, and I loved how, despite their limited experience, they persevered through adversities and showed their resolve till the end. Randy is funny and a nice bro.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Ngl I was a bit turned off from the game by the lack of English VA. However, after turning the voices down and playing more of the story it's actually a pretty solid game. Combat flows really nicely, characters are unique and likable, music is varied enough to not be grating. If you look past the simpler graphics its a nice entry to series as a whole. Can't wait to play more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Trails from Zero is the start of the Crossbell arc, this means that it can technically be started without playing previous games but most fans, including me, will tell you to start with trails in the sky. There is a plot point prominent in this game that was more of a wrap up of a prominent character arc from the Liberl arc so you should understand that story first at least. If you liked the earlier trails games, you will love this one. Crossbell is the fan-favorite arc for a reason and this game is VERY solid. My biggest problem with this game is that crafts still kinda suck by the end of the game despite trails in the sky the third fixing the problem. The localization barrier of this game being overcome was fantastic and I cannot stress enough that this game and arc are really good and if you like this game you HAVE to play Azure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Watching  dealing with some loose threads from the Sky trilogy made me feel like I was playing as the side character but, on the other hand, at least I have some idea of how the Liberlian soldiers must feel, watching a bunch of way-too-young bracers running around like they own the place.Btw, this is the best PC port I've seen in a long time. Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Obligatory positive Trails series review. I think my internal hype for this game while playing through Sky 3rd raised my expectations a little too high, because honestly I think Sky FC was a much stronger beginning to a story arc. That said, Zero was still exceptional, and this game still more than delivered. So far, compared to Liberl, Crossbell absolutely nails the pacing, whereas I felt Liberl dragged in places (namely the beginning of SC). Zero is a rollercoaster of ups and downs the whole way through and the ending is nothing less than immensely satisfying. Absolutely play this game if you liked the Sky trilogy. Randy Orlando my beloved
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: ok, so I've played through the trails in the sky series, and a couple of the cold steel back in the ps3. and this one, trails from zero, has been the best in the series so far. just started in the sequel as well, it's just a gift that keeps on giving.though, for the best experience, I highly recommend you play all the other games before.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Trails To Zero - 7.5 - A new area, Crossbell, with a whole bunch of new characters after the Trails In The Sky series. This one wasn't as charming as the first two Trails In The Sky but it still offers a great amount of moments with some excellent characters. While I feel the main plot could have been more intriguing, and the side quest were blah, the art design, battles, and characters all were really solid.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Once again another very good start for a new arc in the series. I think this game does a lot better in terms of getting the story rolling and up off the ground into the sky in terms of events, character building, and pace, but suffers just a little from how easy it is overall. Outside of that this game was great and i would put it above Sky FC and below Sky SC, very VERY good game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: It's Kiseki. Of course it's really good. It has a brutally slow start though, especially compared to Sky but when it gets good it gets real good. Oh, and play Sky 1-3 before these. Some of the most powerful scenes in the game don't hit nearly as hard without seeing what happened for yourself. You can do these after Cold Steel and before Reverie but don't. Also the PSN port is trash, this version got a lot of love and care put into it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. Especially if you've played the previous games, or plan to play the next. Worth it to install the extra portraits mod, and to patch in the exclusive quests from the Vita version of the game. It takes a couple of minutes, and how can you not grant Shan Shan a portrait? That seems obvious to meNot as much voice acting as in FC, SC and 3rd. That was a bummer. Yes, it's still a lot more than Cold steel. I'm on Cold steel 2 now and there's like no voice acting. Some characters are even quiet in the middle of major cutscenes. It's a mess. Pretty clear that the re-releases of the older games are of higher quality production. Oh well. This is not supposed to be about Cold Steel. But just know that these older games have something that the others don't.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: One of the Best JRPGs of all time which builds up for the best JRPG of all time. A game so good it got a full fan localization, which was used in part for the creation of this game's script, though having played both I think I prefer this translation overall. Have experienced a couple bugs, like non attack arts not showing up in my menu at times, but that's my only real complaint. The port overall was done excellently.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Played it offline on my Steam Deck so it says I only played it for a few minutes despite the fact that I finished it.I really liked it. Since it´s set in Crossbell and its environs the map, and the amount of locations you visit, is much smaller than in the previous trilogy but it was cool to see this place that was often mentioned but never seen in the previous games.Much to my surprise, even though the main cast are all new characters and instead of being adventurers (named bracers in this world) they're actually cops, it's not as unrelated to the previous story as I expected it to be. Set a few months after Trails in the Sky the Third, many of the events and their aftermath are mentioned and several characters are brought up in conversattion or actually show up as side characters.As for the game itself, if you liked the earlier games you'll probably like this one. It's basically a version with better graphics and updated mechanics, but retaining the tone and charm of the originals. To me, Trails in the Sky FC and SC felt like a single game split in half, and Trails in the Sky III felt like a DLC they padded to make a full game, so this one is the first that actually felt like a true sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: I've played CS 1- 3 and Sky 1&2, skipping 3. This has been my favorite start to a new arc so far. The locale feels extremely fleshed out compared to the others and it was fun seeing returning characters in such small increments vs other games where they rely a bit heavier on these returning characters. Also loved seeing a happy ending for you know who !
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: This is the fourth game in the Legend of Heroes series but the first game in the Second (Crossbell) Arc.  This game takes the formula of the first three games and continues it's great story writing, characters and turned-based combat.  Once again the PC port is very good, supporting ultrawide monitors and really well done M/K controls as well.A lot of people say that you can start here if this is your first Trails game.  I would for the most part agree, as it introducing entirely new characters, events and places.  There will however, be several scenes that will simply not hit nearly as hard if you have not played the first Arc.Voice acting is added for most of the important scenes as well, although it only supports Japanese voice overs.  It's still adds a lot to the presentation and is much appreciated.The Legend of Heroes Trials... series of games is quickly becoming one of my favorite JRPG series ever.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10The Crossbell arc, considered by many among the best, however, falls short of that ideal due to outdated mechanics, a repeat of the first arc of Sky, and many mechanics that started here (and would be further criticized in Cold Steel) 8/10Most of the time it's really good, and there are some amazingly intense moments when the music just ramps everything up to 11. Additionally, it was a nice surprise to find voice acting in these game, it certainly helped give it a different vibe. 7/10It certainly works, though it’s nothing to brag about. The sprites look good, the effects are solid, and some of the animated scenes are good. 7/10 You can FF, but not completely skip scenes. Meaning that if you want to replay it, you are still stuck seeing the same scenes again and again. There are hidden bonding points for the characters, with no information about them, and you would have to use a guide or just pray for good luck to obtain the ending with each character.Besides that, the gameplay remains practically the same as Sky series with virtually no changes; If you, which is most likely the case, play this game after playing the Cold Steel series, there are a lot of instances where you will miss the QoL mechanics.  8/10The story starts really slow, getting to know the SSS as they delve into Crossbell, its politics, and daily life. Unfortunately, it's too similar to Sky. While Sky was more about the struggle of the day-to-day by normal people, and here we have a struggle of the people vs the politics, it still feels too similar. Near the end of Chapter 3, things ramp-up, and the game turns interesting again. Even if a lot of things like  or the team's, almost sadistic desire, to save the criminals even after everything they have done. The good thing is that the tight and small cast gets to shine more. With each chapter having one member be the focus (except Randy, poor guy). On the downside, here we see the MC inadvertently turn everyone he touches into part of his harem. Which really sucks, and does detract, a bit, from the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! I thought Trails in the Sky the Third made me feel some things, boy am I right, it sure did, BUT this game made me feel way more things. I felt some happy things, sad things, and everything in between. I'm being vague cause may either you know how freaking stellar these games are, or you're missing out, and nothing I can say will do it justice. If you're considering buying this game, and are somehow reading this review, do it, love it, and hopefully you'll play the rest of the games, cause what a ride, I am stoked.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Simply, this game is....wonderful.I started this title right after finishing the Trails the 3rd, which if you check my reviews, you will notice I found very underwhelming! However, Trails from Zero is somehow bringing all the freshness from Trails in the Sky FC, while also progressing it's themes! _childDocuments_.review: I was initially hesitant to buy the game at first, having purchased the Japanese copy a few years ago with the Geofront translation. However, when I heard about the localization efforts for the western world, I decided to buy it again. Despite the game being expensive, especially where I am, it is worth the full price. I usually follow a trade of 1 dollar - 1 hour, and I have exceeded it with this game.This is the fourth installment of the Legend of Heroes franchise, and I highly recommend playing the following games in order:Trail in the Sky FC,Trail in the Sky SC,Trial in the Sky the 3rd.I absolutely love this game. The Crossbell saga is probably my favourite arc of all the Legend of Heroes series. The characters are fantastic, and the four main characters have taken me through a roller coaster of emotions. I teared up on a few scenes and got hyped as ♥♥♥♥ at the coolest ♥♥♥♥. I appreciate how the side quests are relatively small in comparison to the story. However, some of the side quests hold significance towards the future of the story or the past. It's the first time I've enjoyed doing a side quest in a long time. I highly recommend doing as many as you can, or at least the important ones.The game still has the best music of any Legend of Heroes game. The battle, rescue, boss, etc., themes of this game were so exhilarating. I have the soundtrack in one of my playlists to this day.I loved the gameplay. While many people got sick and tired of the gameplay from the Liberal arc/trial in the Sky games, I did not mind it at all. One of the key things that was nice began with the creativity in S crafts. It was a nice touch-up and introduction to this game. I enjoyed the quartz system as usual in these games and especially enjoyed the orbal arts/range it introduced again. However, one word of advice:DON'T PLAY IN NIGHTMARE MODE ON YOUR FIRST PLAY THROUGH!!!!!!!!!!!I nearly broke my controller just getting constantly one-shotted while trying to 100% complete the game. It is unfair, the scaling is ridiculous, and you should only tackle it if you know what kind of art, game play, and 'barrier' is required to 'overcome' each battle.Other notable things include the collectables, which are reasonable, not too much, which isn't too great, but Trails to Azure is going to have a lot, so I'm not sad about it. The Western Port is fantastic, despite being a PS Vita kind of game; it outshines a lot of JRPG to this day.Overall, I highly recommend this game, even though it's not the greatest entry to the Legend of Heroes series. It's honestly a fairly great shout, and you can always go back through the games to get an understanding of the rich lore and additional main characters and side characters that will appear later on. I have been a fan of the series for nearly six years now, and it is one of the best JRPG stories I have ever played. It is worth every dollar, and the more recognition this game gets, the faster and better we can get localization for future games. Anyway, I'll see you over in the next game:THE LEGEND OF HEROES: TRAILS TO AZURE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Its very good.While I've been generally positive about the previous Trails games, they were typically a mix between good and bad aspects that averaged out on the positive side. Zero manages to break from the crowd with its consistent level of quality across all the entire experience. I think this is the first Trails game I can recommend without any hesitation (though I would still advise playing the Sky games first thanks to the context they offer).Combat and gameplay, while still largely the same as previous games, has enough improvements that it feels noticeably better. Balance to enemy health and damage numbers make the fights much more engaging and limited the number of encounters that felt tedious or boring to get through. Meanwhile changes to how orbments and arts are composed gave a much greater variety and complexity to the builds which was further emphasized by the smaller cast of main characters encouraging depth and complexity unlike the huge ensembles of prior titles.As for the story, I'm largely positive. Crossbell feels much more cohesive, more believable, and more interesting than anything Liberl offered. And while its hard to judge much of the content here since a lot of it seems to be setup for the sequel, I think Zero did a pretty good job of giving us the backdrop for its events while still showing meaningful progress in the world rather than leaving the resolution of events entirely to the next game to wrap up.Considering how much of this game is supposed to be setting the stage for Azure, I'm very excited to play it. And while Azure's quality doesn't directly influence whether Zero is a good game or not it does mean I'm willing to overlook some of its weaker points since many of them seem to be planting the seeds for future plot points to take advantage of.So overall, I really liked Zero. Even after spending nearly 200 hours playing the previous three Trails games this still managed to feel fresh and engaging. Definitely worth giving it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: This is currently my 4th game in my Trails/Kiseki journey, having played Trails in the Sky FC/SC/3rd prior to this recently (started in early 2023), and I am constantly blown away by the cast of characters we are introduced to with each game. If I had to compare the first chapter of the Liberl story Arc (Sky FC) vs the Crossbell story Arcs (Zero), I think Crossbell takes the W, mainly because I think it picks up faster than Sky FC personally, and we are immediately introduced to the 4 main characters we stick with for the entire game, with different personalities that mesh together well (I absolutely loved the SSS banter throughout the game). I think the QoL additions played a great role too.Regardless of this being the 4th game in the Trails series, I think this is a fine game to start with if you are looking to get into the Trails/Kiseki series, because it is the first chapter of the Crossbell story arc. HOWEVER, I think it is important to keep in mind (especially for those that love connecting story plot points and point of interests) that certain stories and plot points that were introduced in the Liberl story arc continue on and/or conclude in this game, because timeline wise this game begins approximately 3 months after the events of Sky the 3rd. Additionally, there are a bunch of cameo characters and locations we are introduced to in this game that were previously in Trails in the Sky or mentioned. I think for those who are mainly getting into this for the world building, these 2 points notably bring more impact to certain events that happen over the course of the game.If you are playing this game having recently finished the Trails in the Sky trilogy, Trails from Zero gameplay wise functions very similar to the older games but with more QoL. You will still find a lot of dialogue that changes frequently during the course of the events that happen, the good old chest phrases (the mention of grass clipping had me chuckle), completing side missions within a timeframe, and a similar quartz/arts system.QoL additions include voiced dialogue in Japanese Only, (although Sky has an EVO version with voiced lines not available on Steam by default), a toggle/hold option for “High Speed” mode with various speed options for BOTH the over world and battle, and a turbo mode for speeding through scenes.If I had to give my personal take, I would say play the Trails in the Sky games first, but as I said above, Trails from Zero is a fine game to start with. Getting into the Trails/Kiseki series is definitely an investment, having a lot of dialogue and a lot of world building, so it is definitely not for everyone. As for me, it has been a worthwhile investment seeing the world building and experiencing the stories on this continent called Zemuria.

_childDocuments_.review: The fourth entry in what is currently of 9 localized games, and soon to be 10 during summer 2023, with an 11th entry currently only in Japanese (although there are English patches for that version to get around that). If you haven't heard of this series, I advise you double back and play the Trails in the Sky trilogy first, and then return for this game.Trails from Zero takes the things that made Trails in the Sky great, adds more to it, changes very little - mostly for the better - and gives a feeling of both familiarity and a new sense of narrative direction in another story set in the region of Zemuria. Coming off of Trails in the Sky the 3rd, the story at the time had a lot of characters and moving pieces that we hadn't seen yet, on top of the already plethora of cast featured in the Liberl arc. From Zero takes place in Crossbell, a region that sits between Erebonian Empire and the Republic of Calvard, two regions we hear about often in The Sky trilogy but not unlike the context in this game. From Zero brings you into Crossbell as a foreigner and quickly familiarizes you with why this City-State is neutral territory that sits on a very thin line fro\m falling out into chaos. The story this time has the same feeling In the Sky FC had where it was a world unfamiliar to us that the characters knew and I believe again they did a good job to make things seem both new and fresh but also like something that's been around for years and I'm someone foreign visiting to learn about this country. Gameplay has been improved with having voiced dialogue (only in Japanese voices) cutscenes that make up a good majority of the game, even faster turbo settings (up to 6x on the field), many modern day settings for a PC port, and as usual great performance for the steam deck out of the box. The biggest gameplay addition is on the field characters can swing with their weapons to attack and stun monsters on the field. If you attack a monster from behind, it puts them in a stunned state and if you engage it allows you begin battle with critical turns on every player and allowing you to act for 2 turns on each player before the enemy can move. This makes farming/grinding significantly easier to do in this game.Another addition is team based attacks, a new icon added on the turn bar is the team attack icon, which has the 4 players dog pile a group of enemies within an area for free damage - think of the move Chain 3 from in the Sky but now it can be used for anybody as long as it lands on any of the player characters.There's more besides these surface level changes but I don't want to spoil them all. I was greatly pleased that this game left me with such a strong impression and continues to convince me that investing into this series' long-running narrative was worth both the money and the time. The only cons I have for this game are similar to what were in the first two games, many cutscenes, many points of traveling around for slow building story, and a very slow buildup for having action feel less basic when you unlock newer orbments.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is another excellent game in the Trails series. The story starts a bit slow (as in many Trails games) but is never boring and quickly accelerates into a more action-packed climax. The characters are endearing and interesting. The game play itself is highly strategic and on higher difficulties requires both in combat tactical prowess and strategically foresight in setting up the different characters' abilities. Fortunately though, any character can have their abilities and equipment changed at any time, there are no permanent choices.I would advise having played the Trails in the Sky series before starting this one. If you couldn't get through it because of Trails in the Sky 1 having a very very slow start (I don't blame you if that's the case), then at least watch a summary video. There are characters from that series that make a return as major supporting characters and it's nice if you have some investment or at least some knowledge of their role in the series. However, the game is absolutely still worth playing if you can't be bothered.Overall 7.5/10, a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Secret auctions, Mishyland, car chases, and drugs... lots of drugs. Not the fun kind of drugs either, the kind that turn you into demons.Welcome to Trails to Zero and the start of the Crossbell story arch. This game takes place after the Trails in the Sky The 3rd. You play as Lloyd Bannings and the Crossbell Special Support Section. If you have played any of the Trails in the Sky series, you will be very familiar with format. You run around and discover the world. You do side quests. You beat up monsters and bad guys, and you save the day. Along the way you meet a lot of cool characters. As usual there are plenty of story twists and turns.For maximum effect you should play Trails in the Sky 1,2, and 3 because there are some major characters from those games that show up in this game (and the next), as well as references to events that have happened in those games.Having played Trails of Cold Steel before these games feels bad because these games set up Trails of Cold Steel. So kind of bizarre they didn't translate these games before dropping before now.I did most of the quests, utilizing turbo mode, and clocked in around 50 hours. Which is actually pretty short for a Legend of Heros game. Most of the games in the series range from 60-100 hours.Anyways, fantastic game. One of the best in the series. High recommend. Lets Go!

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic entry in the series. I've you've enjoyed the Sky trilogy (which I really recommend you play before this game) then I'm almost certain you'll love this one as well. The power of the Trails series for me really is in its world building, its "living world" (where NPCs continuously reflect the changes in the story and seem to live their own lives) and the fact that all the games share the same universe, which allows the writing to escape the confines of a single game and really deliver a setting that exceeds the scale of basically all other games I've played. As a side note, this version of the game is also a great port with tons of useful features such as customizable controller icons for basically all controllers you could wish for (Xbox, Dualshock, Nintendo, Steam Deck and even Stadia), a high-speed mode with a configurable speedup factor for battles and overworld sections and optionally showing the BGM information when the current track changes. It also works perfectly on Linux for me, having encountered no issues on my Steam Deck and my Desktop.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome, folks, to Crossbell! Quick note: If you're new to the Trails series, stop reading this review and go play the Trails in the Sky trilogy - you'll be missing quite a bit of context for this game if you don't!Trails from Zero is the fourth game in the Trails series and the first game in the series's second story arc, commonly known as the "Crossbell duology." Set just months after the events of Trails in the Sky the 3rd, Zero is set in the city-state of Crossbell, a bustling hub of trade and finance which has quickly become one of the most modernized countries on the Zemurian continent. Unlike Liberl, with its rugged landscape and limited technology, Crossbell more closely resembles our world in the 1980s-1990s, with cars, buses, flip phones, and the newly-developed "orbal network," which is basically the Internet. Coming in from Sky, this change was a bit jarring at first, but I eventually came to enjoy it as a sign of Zemuria's economic and technological diversity, much like our world - if Liberl is Switzerland, then Crossbell is Hong Kong!Zero's gameplay loop is similar to Sky FC and SC: You and your fellow  officers run around the state performing odd jobs like fetch quests and monster exterminations, earning  Detective Points and advancing the larger story as you go. Aside from the new setting, there are some nice differences between Zero and Sky FC:+ You get a full party of four right off the bat, unlike Sky FC where party size fluctuates regularly. While I appreciated the parts of Sky with only Estelle and Joshua, it's nice to actually have a full party to work with for most of the game.+ Because of Zero's smaller setting and cast, you are exposed to the greater story elements sooner and much more directly than in Sky FC. The result is better pacing and more exposure for the supporting cast, both of which Sky FC struggled with.+ You get more gameplay options to work with: Overworld attacks on enemies, Team Rushes, Combo Crafts, weapons upgrades, etc.As for the story, it's got some good political and criminal intrigue, mostly the latter since your main villain is  The later half of the story took some unexpected turns that, in a way, felt recycled from Sky SC, but it works all the same, Overall, a worthy entry into the Trails series and a precursor to some great things to come (I say as someone currently playing Azure)!Misc. good and bad:+ Stat buffs/nerfs are much easier to keep track of than in Sky+ Fast travel thanks to the bus system+ Trap chests are specially marked+ NPC arcs and chest quotes are still here- No English voice acting- Recipes became harder to obtain, much more so than necessary- Weakest villains of the series so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Trails from Zero is the fourth game in the massive Trails series, and was originally released for the PSP over a decade ago. The game suffers from minor pacing issues at times, but the payoff is well worth it. This is the beginning of the two-game Crossbell arc, so it can serve as a starting point for new players. If you've already played the Cold Steel games (or even just the first), you may know some of the events that occur in this game already and it can dampen your emotional response; however, one thing that cannot be adjusted is experiencing the events through the perspectives of Crossbell natives.The storytelling in this game is barely short of master craft, and you owe it to yourself as an RPG fan to dive into this game. The gameplay is typical to your other Trails games, and Durante and team have heavily enhanced this port to modernize it as much as playable. Not going to lie, the chibi character models did take some time to grow on me, but they certainly did. The SSS is likely my favorite cast from any of the Trails games, and I say this as a veteran fan of the series.So, what are you waiting for? If you don't have this in your library yet - overcome the barrier and purchase it! Once you get rolling in this game, you will be hooked. So, help LLOYDO-SAN and his comrades figure out the mysterious events going on inside Crossbell!9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since Trails in the Sky 1, I have a soft spot for The Legend of Heroes series. The games are long, some would say too long. There's a lot of dialogue, a lot of lore; a lot of reading in general. If that is something that turns you off, it will negatively affect your enjoyment of this game. There is a skip button to circumvent this, (hold down circle on a playstation controller), but you'll lose most of what makes these games so charming: its world and characters.These games make you feel like you're stepping into an established living world. It constantly changes, every time you do something in the game, you'll find the reactions and dialogue of NPCs changing. The NPCs live their own lives, all have their own little storylines and events, which go from superficial to quite deep, you really get invested in them, it makes you care. There are also loads of hidden events and other easter eggs.If you do choose to play this game, I strongly recommend you look up a walkthrough so as not to miss anything. If you do not, you're going to lose out on a lot of content, which would be a shame.The story is amazing, if you like RPGs, play this series. It has combat that is easy to learn, hard to master. The graphical fidelity isn't off the charts, however, the game has a distinct art style which makes the game enjoyable to look at.If you like JRPGs, and could stand to lose 50 hours or so, try out the Legend of Heroes series. All the games build on each other, the events and characters from one game are referenced and often important in others. This does not mean that you need to have played the previous games, but it will make the game feel much richer. Even as a standalone series, I can still heartily recommend Trails from Zero and Trails to Azure.10/10 will play again.

_childDocuments_.review: This entry into the "Trails" series is a major departure from previous entries, but does so exceedingly well. I highly recommend this game. As opposed to other "Trails" games, this chapter in the series has a small cast - this allows for more in-depth character development and pushes for a tight-knit group. The SSS characters are painfully aware of their limitations, limited by bureaucracy (and all the red tape it entails), and are fighting an ever-uphill battle against injustice. The SSS scratches an itch the other entries can't, since they're an official government division as opposed to the Bracer Guild in "Trails in the Sky," or the Thors military school vibe of "Trails of Cold Steel," and have different social dynamics as pros and cons as a result.The game play is nearly identical to the "Sky" series - turn-based with different perks to acting on specific turns - and expands on the tried-and-true formula with different additions, like Team Rush actions (basically a mob attack), S-Break paired attacks, and new actions like double attack to exploit. Keep in mind that this game originally debuted on the PSP, which had no right thumbstick, so the game employs a camera-on-rails instead of a freely-rotating camera like the other series and takes a little getting used to. The camera-on-rails is tactfully done, and actually highlights some cinematic elements, like panning upward to see an entire tower, etc.The graphics upgrade for the PC port is awesome, with support for ultra-wide screen resolutions (though some of the borders of maps simply aren't programmed that far out), and lots of QOL upgrades like turbo mode (I keep mine maxed for battle and overworld) and FPS options.

_childDocuments_.review: As the fourth entry of the Trails saga and the first of two games that specifically tackle the region of Crossbell, fans of the series will still feel right at home with many aspects of Trails from Zero.Visually, the environments and characters have been touched up for this version but maintain the charming 3D environments, expressive 2D dialogue portraits and sprites. Another large story awaits players with an overwhelming amount of dialogue that often adjusts after each major plot point. One difference from most of the games in this series is the main cast is surprisingly small and they're often together. Each character will get a chance to develop at their own pace without someone overshadowing them (for the most part), a refreshing change of pace. Turn-based grid battles return but have a few tweaks in its mechanics. The soundtrack sets the mood and is among the best Falcom has produced. There are many game systems that were introduced or reworked starting with Zero that have greatly influenced the design of future entries in the series. Some examples include field attacks, chaining encounters, battle evaluation, item exchange shop, cooking dish types, and bonding points.If you've played the Trails in the Sky trilogy and wished for more of that, this is as close as you're going to get. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. I'm so glad I decided to embark on my Trails journey back in June 2022. _childDocuments_.review: A story driven game, full of characters and lore, which will keep you guessing the secrets of this world. The game plays in a turn base fashion, with customization regarding spells and stats.Be warned that the game is heavy in text and will need lots of reading. _childDocuments_.review: It's a Trails game, so that means turn based combat, Trails style, universe and all that (whether you think that's good or bad is up to you, I personally think it's great.)  This game is on an older engine (think Sky rather than Cold Steel), and is balanced a lot more like Sky rather than Cold Steel.Most of the game is rather small scale.  It's all in the city of Crossbell and the surrounding areas.  You're a small new police unit that's made almost as a publicity stunt, and you spend most of the game doing smaller jobs and trying to get respect.  No Ouroboros (except refereed to on the fringes a bit) no grand schemes to end the world, it's regular every day type jobs.Now it's in the same universe as Sky and Cold steel (set at the exact same time as Cold Steel I), and has a lot of tie ins to those games, especially the Sky Trilogy.  Renne's here, with Estelle and Joshua looking for her, but they're off to the side, they are by no means the main focus.A lot of the game is on the slower side, but towards the end all those little jobs you've been doing start to tie together and the plot really kicks in.  This is when the game really starts to get good, what you play to reach.  Don't get me wrong, the early game isn't bad, but it's scale is smaller than the end of Cold Steel got me used to.  It's all set up for what comes at the end though.  It's very much worth it too.It's a very solid game and I'm really looking forward to its sequel out in March.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Crossbell get's over the barrier! Firstly, Thank you to all the mod teams from the Flame Edit, to Geofront for all of your hard work and dedication and time. Making this incredible project succeed! And NISA for publishing them.Trails from Zero takes place canonically after Trails in the Sky 1-3. However the Sky Trilogy isn't required to play Zero and Azure. It definitely helps with character nuance, from the prior games. +World Building is top notch. From character interactions, to multiple events, and culture of Crossbell and how it interacts with the surrounding nations.+Characters, and side characters. Our team at the Special Support Section, are fantastic. They each build on each others strengths and weaknesses, They have backstories that get fleshed out between Zero and Azure. +Music - Absolute banger of a soundtrack, Japanese voice over is fantastic! +Sprites and art style- character portraits and japanese voice over portray emotions very well. Sprites look very high definition.+Mini games! BlackJack, Roulette, Poker, and Fishing!Trails from Zero adds to the Trails franchise. If you're a veteran you know what to expect. If you're just coming into the series. You can expect a slow burn to start, but ramps up pretty quick! Great characters, and very formulaic story progression. A grand JRPG experience, And the best is still to come next year.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've been thinking about diving into the Trails series, this may be a good starting point. There are several Trails sagas and there is a chronological order to them, with Trails from Zero being the start to the second saga. Most fans would recommend you begin with the first saga, Trails in the Sky, as there are parts of Zero that will spoil Sky. Personally, I found Sky to be a bit hard to get into. The Trails games are a slow burn, and while Zero is no exception, Sky was at times more of a slog through traffic than an adventure. I recommend starting with Zero for that reason (or try Sky and if it doesn't click, come back to Zero). Zero features a memorable cast of characters both playable and non. This series is known for immense world building and an intense focus on character development- Zero's adventure primarily takes place in a small state called Crossbell and by the end of the game you will feel as if the writers would be disappointed if you didn't express some sort of faux-patriotism for their imaginary underdog nation. In most JRPGs protagonists are faced with increasingly ridiculous foes, often escalating from bandit leaders at the start to deities by the end. Now, imagine a game that's focused almost entirely on the protagonists opening call to adventure, dealing with local challenges that are small in scale. The first 15-20% of your average JRPG. That's basically Zero. Sounds bad, but hold on. Zero IS the first in its duology, but beyond that the payoffs in this story are that much more satisfying. The "zoomed in" gradual build-up of tension persists throughout the plot as the game directs your focus mostly towards character development. It makes every cutscene worth your attention...something I can't honestly often say with this genre. Though the game originally released a decade ago, the remastered visuals look great to me. Like a fancy PSX era game. And the music is incredible, go listen to that battle theme on YouTube for a good example. You'll be hearing it a lot if you play this game, and it never gets old. Zero plays like a pretty typical turn-based JRPG. It's inoffensive and thanks to the game's "turbo mode," which speeds up EVERYTHING by like 3x, with the exception of boss fights, most battles are over in less than 20 seconds. You can see the enemies on the map and avoid most encounters too. So there's the longest review I've written for a game on Steam. What can I say, I liked this game a lot. I've played through 3 other games in the Trails series, and so far Zero is my favorite. It took me a while to get into Trails, but I'd consider myself a fan now. The series is slow and the developers play it safe with battle and exploration. But what Trails games lack in intensity they more than make up for with heart. If you're willing to invest the time and appreciate a more intimate story focused on characters and places (instead of battles and action sequences), give this series a try. Zero's not a bad place to start. If you can't tolerate sprite graphics, consider Trails of Cold Steel - just know it's a bit of a rough start and will spoil significant parts of Sky and Zero.

_childDocuments_.review: Forewarn: I have already played this game twice (fan translate).If you liked the predecessors (Trails in the sky) of this game, you will love this chapter of The Legend of Heroes Saga as well.Trails of Zero (and Azure, hopefully soon) is far closer in style to the Sky series rather than Cold steel.The game delivers a captivating story of a fresh young detective/police/pseudo-bracer trying to be a positive driving force in safeguarding the identity of the rich but highly unstable and disputed city-state of Crossbell. Again, the game continues the tradition of the saga in strong world building, good story telling, and fun RPG battle system with some added improvements and twists.Some advice when playing: -  Play with a guide (non-spoiler of course). This game retained its predecessor's nasty habit of missable contents and quests that are only available in short time frames and are sometimes hidden in obscure way ... Extremely frustrating for completionists.-  This game is hard, and should be played on normal or easy for first comers:If you choose hard mode, the word 'hard' is taken literally. You will find yourself dipping hard in your resources even before you reach the dungeon bosses.  Grind becomes unavoidable.If you choose Nightmare mode without proper knowledge of the game mechanics, you will make yourself hate yourself and the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Trails game, another positive review.Most people consider the Crossbell arc to be the best story arc of the Trails franchise (so far). Most people are correct. The Crossbell arc combines the excellent writing and storytelling of the Sky arc with (some) of the gameplay improvements of the later Cold Steel arc. Zero is absolutely excellent as far as a "game that introduces a new area and new characters" is concerned and is in my opinion stronger than Sky FC / CS1 / CS3 in that regard. If you already have played some of the games in the Trails series, there's no reason not to play this. If you haven't, you should probably play the Trails in the Sky trilogy first, but it's not entirely necessary... Zero is a viable entry point to the series.As for this specific version, the PC port by PH3 is, to the surprise of absolutely nobody, excellent. You get high framerate support (up to 144), ultrawide resolution, AI upscaled textures, and loads of other quality of life features and improvements that make this version of Trails from Zero undoubtedly the best there is.The localization work isn't quite as good as the porting work, but it's still competent. There are a few typos here and there, and I actually stumbled upon three of four messages that were still in Japanese, but considering the massive, massive scope of the game, it's not bad.The fact that all the voices are only in Japanese is kind of annoying though. I understand why this is the case... This game is a fairly low budget localization expected to only sell to a small number of hardcore fans, so they couldn't justify the expense of dubbing the entire game. I get it, but it's still unfortunate.In any case, this is an exceptional port of a mostly well localized, exceptional game. Buy it. Play it.

The characters in this particular game snap harder than most LoH games too.  They feel more real and developed than the kids you get in Trails in the Sky or Cold Steel.  I am very excited to see how their story plays out.The soundtrack bangs like most Falcom games.  You won't be disappointed there.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted a game to take things slow, focus on world building and lore, have low stakes, and have a small core team that they try to flesh out through that? This is that game. It is very different from the Sky and Cold Steel arc, and goes all in on taking its time to set things up. It is basically a cop drama, and you are going around doing a case, and questioning people. And these can often takes 15-20 minutes, sometimes even happening back to back. The cut scenes are long, they are meaty, and it goes to great lengths to build up people and organizations and what they do in the city. Does taking huge chunks of game time just talking to people with no fights in sight, while building its story sound interesting? This is for you. Don't feel bad if you bounce off it because it is thick it dialogue, this is not for everyone. You will go long stretches without a fight or a new dungeon. Does it pick up? Yes. But thats after the halfway point when it really does enter another gear and more important story and setting events happen. Its a slow burn of a game till then, made more obvious when the prologue is several hours long, they really should have just called it chapter 1 if it was gonna be that long.Don't worry about playing this first in the series or not. This game is very stand alone and Crossbell is the main focus. You will see things from other points in the series, but you will be completely find jumping in here. The characters care about Crossbell, its people and its problems. The other places are a distant problem, and the focus is taking care of smaller local threats.Combat is fine. Better than Sky at this point, but missing some features that Cold Steel has that make it better. I liked it, You are actually building spells with the amount and type of quartz you use, make sure you read the detective manual to learn the combinations for good spells, its all there.But once again, for most the game it will live and die on if you can sit through the long dialogue and like the small cast. I liked it, but I can recognize that its not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not exaggerate when I say that Trails from Zero is not only one of the best JRPGs I've played but also one of the best games period. Even I was playing the Trails in the Sky games back in 2020 and absolutely enthralled with the setting, characters, story, and world building, I had heard from longtime members of the community that Trails from Zero (and Azure) were the absolute height of Trails, and it had me very excited but also skeptical. I absolutely loved the Sky games (Second Chapter and the Third in particular) and I just really didn't know how the series could only get better as it directs its narrative towards the small city state of Crossbell and the Special Support Section. And finally playing Trails from Zero (with the hard and passionate work of the Geofront), I was absolutely blown away by Zero, but not in ways I would have originally thought. Falcom really outdid themselves with this game, the setting in particular. Saying that Crossbell City is one of my favorite settings in any video game is no understatement. The city itself is so well realized and developed with the game's narrative that I would consider it almost emblematic of everything that makes Zero as a game work. That makes Zero as a TRAILS game work. You will almost all of your time in the city, and while that may seem boring to some, the way the people and the city itself are fleshed out, it really makes you care about the going ons, the people living their daily lives, the new and developing technology, and the intense struggles for political power that go on behind the scenes. Moving on to the characters and the main cast in particular, they are great. I love the dynamic of the SSS, and the four of them will be your main party for most of your journey. This is a bit of a departure from Sky where you'll have a good handful of companions outside of Joshua and Estelle who join you in your journey, and VERY different from the upwards of 10+ members of Class VII and their allies in the Cold Steel games. But I gotta say, less is more. By focusing on the four in the SSS and how they grow with one another, it really makes me care about each and everyone of them and I feel they are well developed (especially by the end of the arc's conclusion in Azure). I could honestly say a lot more of this game. I could honestly ramble on because I love it that much. Crossbell is the height of the Trails series in my opinion. And while BEST experienced, with Sky in mind, I still think there's a lot to enjoy even if you haven't played a Trails game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my top 3 "The Legend of Heroes" games. Like the others said it's strongly recommended to play the first Trilogy, Trails in the Sky, before this one.Took me 80 hours on Nightmare, with a lot a retries the first 15 hours and on some bosses after. NG+ was a breeze for the rest of the achievements (30 hours or so) except the "100 hours" one.Score : 8.5/10-Good story overall, each chapters got a different case and all come together on the finale one, also it's the best chapter in the game-The main 4 characters got very different personalities but they go well together as a team. The bond between these 4 are one of the strongest i saw in this series.-Lots of interrestings NPCs to talk to. They all have different dialogues between chapters.-Most of the subquests are interresting and add some background to the universe or the characters.-Solid combat system it's the same as the Trails in the Sky series but with the new C-Crafts.-Bangers songs as always with Falcom.-Very good port, constant 144fps, with some graphics options available. The textures got reworked/upscaled aswell.-The speed features in and outside of combat. A must have in any JRPGs nowadays.-Too much dialogues during some parts. Some scenes last for +20mins.-No dungeons maps.-A ton of missables, without a guide you will miss DP/items/quartz etc...-The extra content in NG+, which is a dungeon, should have been integrated on NG.-NG+ carry over system (based on achievements you did during all your playthroughs) and some missing features like chests % and DP/quests carring over.- Not that important if you're not hunting for achievements but they didnt touch the 100 hours achievement in this version, it counts the IG time on one savefile, not steam so it doesnt count the time spent in the hours of cutscenes and all the reload you can do. With the "speed animations" feature the time spent in game doesnt go faster; so you will most likekly have to keep the game opened for some hours (40 for me) if you want this achievement.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my 2nd favorite Trails game (only behind Azure, the direct sequel and my 2nd favorite game of all time behind Persona 4 Golden.) For context I played both games with the Geofront patch before they came to Steam.It has my favorite cast of characters; Lloyd is my favorite main character in any game I've played, Tio is one of my favorite characters in anything period, every character has an insane amount of personal growth (as is tradition for a Trails game)If you played through Cold Steel before playing these games, a lot of staple mechanics in those games started in these two. Field attacks and battle advantages? Cooking with characters? Master Quartz (in Azure)? To an extent even character bonding, all started in Zero and Azure. These are also the last two game that use the (arguably) more fun line-based Arts system compared to the ones just tied to the quartz itself in Cold Steel.Outside of the game itself, the team that worked on the game did a great job adding so many extra features and even things I didn't think were possible. Graphical improvements, native controller recognition, message log, BGM information, even an option to make encounters only trigger if your leader hits the enemy so your giant snake trail doesn't proc an enemy advantage while running away, and of course, the chest messages.Overall, these two games are some of my favorites of all time, and I'd gladly recommend this series to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Zero focuses exclusively on Crossbell, instead of having you explore most of a country like the other Trails games, and the trade-off is that there's less actual places in exchange for probably the most attentively curated setting in the series. In particular, the game loves to explore how Crossbell has experienced both a mix of prosperity and loss of culture from the proxy war attempts of the two political powers the state is sandwiched inbetween.   The Orbment system from Sky returns, and combat has taken a snappier, fast paced approach where you want your party to deal with enemies pretty quick, in line with the feeling of being a police unit. The only issues I take with the tweaks going on from 3rd are the reworked Advantage system requiring you to hit enemies, and escaping battles being a dice roll (which stuck moving forward). Sky's 100% flee chance was ahead of the curve in terms of QoL, needing an item/quartz to do that feels redundant.   The actual port changes are pretty handy. There's a handful of hiccups here and there where some Japanese wasn't scrubbed away, but it's nothing outrageous. Having a speed up button for an older JRPG is always nice. A few bugs and softlocky scenarios in the original game are patched out. Not having an English dub is understandable even if it's a letdown, but the Japanese dub is still good. _childDocuments_.review: I fondly remember starting with Trails of Cold Steel 1 during the pandemic in 2020. Had a lot of extra time on my hands and fell in love with the Legend of Heroes franchise. To any considering, I'd say some of the key points to consider:- This is a time commitment. It isn't meant to be rushed and you will gain little from it if you are just trying to speed through.- Compared to the other two arcs, this one has just as good if not better of an overall story and the characters bonds will grow to matter in the future arcs as well, it rewards the effort you put in to getting to know your team.- It's a visual novel, more or less. You will read a LOT of dialogue, but it is very endearing and pulls you in if you can enjoy that type of format. The stories are intricate and keep you going and make you feel involved in the plot. There's also just enough combat mixed in at times to keep you thinking about your current build of the team.All in all, Trails from Zero is the most recent release, but it sits right in the middle of both of the other localized arcs. I'd highly recommend it as a starting point as it retains the nostalgic character sprite model of gameplay, but also has a nice modernized polish to it for newer fans. While Zero has it's own contained story, know that it will tie in HEAVILY with Trails to Azure which releases next year and will be an even greater experience to enjoy if you end up loving this title. To fans who have played the fan translation or PSP ports, this is my second full time playing through and I am enjoying it as if it was the first, the turbo option allows you to run through any parts you don't want to pay attention to, while you can also leave it off and coast through if you care to. Multiple options for veteran fans and newcomers alike!

_childDocuments_.review: POSTED: SEPTEMBER 27The Legend of Heroes: Trails from Zero is the best set-up game in the entire Trails series. No cliffhanger endings, a perfectly good story on all its own, yet with deep connections to Azure that are impossible to see within your first playthrough, and unsolved leads that make you wonder just what is going to happen to Crossbell.Starting with the setting, the City of Crossbell is the absolute greatest setting in all of media. Situated between and always being fought over by the two major powers of the Zemurian continent, the Erebonian Empire and the Calvard Republic, the Autonomous State of Crossbell is in one of the absolute worst scenarios for a country to be in. The political situation is essentially just damn near a proxy war between Erebonia and Calvard, which drastically screws over the citizens, with a majority of the tax revenue just going to either side. Despite this, however, the citizens still enjoy much prosperity due to Crossbell City being, essentially, the trade capital of Zemuria. Countless mira flows in and out of the city, all governed by the watchful eye of the International Bank of Crossbell (which, despite its name, has many branch offices in other countries). Department stores, high rises, and other such features of a prosperous city dominate the streets and skyline. But it is all a veil drawn over the eyes of tourists and citizens, for Crossbell has a much seedier underbelly.Nearly everyone in the government is corrupt and allies with one of the two major powers. Anyone who tries to make a change for the benefit of Crossbell is immediately tossed out. Not only this, but ties run deep with the Crossbell mafia, Revache. They pay off politicians in order to get away scot-free with all of their crimes. Yet nothing can be done about it, as those politicians are backed by the powerful benefactors of Erebonia and Calvard. It seems as though Crossbell's fate is to be stuck within an endless cycle of no progress.This is where the Special Support Section comes in. This newly established unit essentially seeks to emulate the Bracer Guild, which is much more popular than the Crossbell Police Department due to them actually being able to protect citizens, and having the A-rank bracer Arios MacLaine. Because they emulate the Bracer Guild, they can gain popularity with the citizens, and under the lax eye of chief Sergei Lou, they are essentially free to do what they think is best. With the backing of the citizens, the CPD will be hesitant to axe the unit. But this all comes with time, and Zero shows us how the Special Support Section rises to fame.Back to the Crossbell City itself, the city is littered with at least two hundred unique NPCs whose dialogue makes them feel as though they really are a live person living within the city, and not some generic no-name spouting either slightly plot-relevant lines or completely irrelevant nonsense. You will not forget these NPCs.As for the gameplay itself, it builds upon everything established in Trails in the Sky and makes it even better.All in all, the Crossbell duology is the best piece of media I have ever consumed, and you will absolutely love it to pieces. Just make sure you play the Trails in the Sky trilogy first.
