_childDocuments_.review: Trail to Azure is a great conclusion to the Crossbell arc of Legend of Heroes.+ Stellar story and writing. The best in the franchise and obligates any existing other RPGs. It's not even close.+ Great cast with a lot of returning characters from Trail in the Sky and even a few from Cold Steel+ The build options are way larger than Trail to Zero+ Very challenging on Hard (1st playthrough)- The last area / dungeon is way way too long. Trail in the sky has the same issue- The last boss is trash. Cheap trash with the meanest gimmick I've ever seen. - Still no access to the menu inside combats. 9/10 (10/10 for the story alone)
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: A satisfying continuation of the game before it. Trails to Azure picks up right where Trails from Zero left off and delivers an even better narrative full of memorable characters in a carefully crafted world. Highly recommended for any JRPG fan who enjoys a good story, a lovable cast, a fantastic soundtrack, and just the right amount of challenging battles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: After making my way through Sky and Zero, naturally it's time for the fan favorite Azure. With all they hype going into it I was excited to see why this was people's favorite Trails game. Unfortunately...the first few chapters in particular did not make a strong case for this game, as it's mostly just playing set up. I was even getting burnt out trying to make my way through...until we hit chapter 4. Suddenly the plot kicks in full force and the game becomes WAY more engaging...and I can tell this is the part people remember from this game. I do think the final chapter dragged on a little too long though. During my play through it took me about a week from start to finish, which I'd say lasted around 10-12 hours total playtime.Overall thoughts? Yeah, fun game. It's definitely not a good starting point for this series, but if you can make it here...you're in for the long haul.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game for the first time. It is by far the best arc in all of Trails so far for me. I've completed Sky, Crossbell, and 3/4 of CS. If you play any of the Trails games, play the Crossbell arc, you will not regret it. Playing this after 3/4 of CS really makes you realize how much better the story telling was.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: This game was incredible. Even though I kind of wanted to rush it, I kind of couldn't. The story was compelling, the side quests fun and funny, the battles meaningful, and I really really wanted to end it today, but one of the best and most thought out endgames in a game like this I've ever seen said, "Hey girl, be patient, the story is what matters most."And whatever the JRPG makers are on when they make final bosses etc, wow. It's a turn based RPG, and i'm sweating, and pacing, and cursing, and getting really into it. Whew!Satisfying and well worth it. I'm so glad they translated Zero and Azure. I have played Cold Steel 1 and it was kind of hard to follow, but playing these now, I can tell there is a lot more that will make sense to me when I play it.Have fun!
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: Great storytelling all the way. It starts off slow, showing the daily lives of the SSS after Zero, and gradually ramps up as the stakes get higher towards the end. More lore and character backgrounds are explained, with answers to the questions presented in Zero addressed. There are great references to the events of Cold Steel I & II. I got goosebumps in many scenes of the game. Wazy has now become one of my favorite characters in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the best Trails games. 100 hours in and just finished the ending. I talked to every NPC in this game and in every step of the way.The crossbell dual series and Trails of Azure especially is well-paced narrative and game. The characters are going to be someone who you will truly love. Even the NPCs, I have known by heart. They have swayed my emotions and made me happy for them consequently. The callout from the Sky Series & some parallel things with TOCS has been awesome too.Crossbell is also one of the best and most developed game cities you will ever see. The plot, everyone, and seeing each unfold has been a game experience that I will carry throughout. I can see how others in the fandom recognize this as one of the best Trails arc.You must play this game. Whichever order you want, but I really really recommend to play this masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: Trails to Azure is possibly one of the best JRPGs I have ever played, I say this as someone who grew up on JRPGs and has played A LOT of them. Obviously please play at least Trails From Zero first, but otherwise, you HAVE to give this one a shot. The characters are fantastic, the OST is top-tier, and the story is so engaging, all in one of the best-built worlds ever known. This is one of the few games that I will ever give a 10/10 to. If I have to criticize this game, the only small issue is that the final chapter is just a little too long and crafts still fall off hard by the end of the game (except for Lloyd cheese on a couple of bosses.) I cannot stress enough how much I love this game and anyone who has ever liked a JRPG should absolutely try this series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: A nice step up from Zero. Azure is basically the second half of a two parter, and so with that a lot of crazy ♥♥♥♥ happens (Especially chapter 4) leaving us a much better paced game for the most part than zero. I like this group of characters, Especially Lloyd, KeA, Ellie, and Randy. However, most of the side cast didn't do much for me. They're not bad per say, just not all that interesting. I also feel the side quest in both zero and Azure were lacking something. And that chapter 5 dungeon, final one, draggggged. Now the bad out of the way I really enjoyed the story beats here. Some real nice twist and turns, and once again some villains view points are very understandable of why they did what they did. Love the interactions, especially anything with KeA. The combat is the best in the 2D games by far, making for some really great battles and challenges. Only one or two bosses I felt required you being cheap to win but for the most part the combat stayed fun for all 32 hours to beat. I thought the graphics and animations were smooth for 2D and obviously the series evolved and more budget was brought on which was nice to see. And this closed up pretty well, with some great character beats on top of the main plot.This and Cold Steel 3 are tied for great experiences despite some flaws. Where's Trails in the Sky FC/SC remain my favorite, Azure comes out a very solid game that is stronger than it's first. A 8/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: I only got into Trails after many many people and review sites recommended it. Now, it was like 6 or 7 years ago at this point, but I don't have a lot of free time for video games. These games have been incredible for me. I have played the Sky trilogy, Cold Steel I and II and now Zero and I'm working on Azure. It's taken me this long because, again, I'm playing like under an hour a week on them. The story is absolutely fabulous. The characters are endearing, and I don't think I'll ever forget them.A lot of people say the Crossbell arc is their favorite, and I definitely see why. I think Sky will likely always be my favorite because those games literally got me back into gaming. I hadn't been into anything in a while but finally decided to give Sky I a try all that time ago and I found myself falling in love with the world, characters, and music. I love these games. Yes, I recommend, obviously. Azure is amazing, with huge plot twists, fantastic music, fun moments throughout, and more. I recommend above any other JRPG series out there. These are the best games.Bestelle.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Played it offline on my Steam Deck, so it says I've only played it a couple of hours despite the fact that I'm currently in the final chapter.Much like Trails in the Sky SC and The Third feel not so much as actual sequels to the original but as parts of the same very long game, this one does the same for Trails From Zero and expands upon the story told in its predecessor and follows all those events and their many repercussions. If you liked the first one, you'll like this one too because it's basically the same but better, adding a few extra locations on top of revisiting all the places you saw in the first game, adding a few new mechanics like Master Quartz and the ability to better fast travel from any checkpoint by using the newly assigned SSS car, and an expanded main cast by way of having two new recruits in the team, even if they're both someone you already know from TFZ. New villains pop up, old villains return, and some familiar faces from the previous games show up. This series has been consistently great.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing the series since Trails in the Sky, and after a disappointing 3rd entry in that series it was nice to see them pare this storyline down to two entries.  Gameplay is fairly simple dungeon exploration with tactical combat.  I played through more as a relaxing distraction rather than getting really invested in the story, but the story is quite good if that's what you're looking for.  If you're curious about this, I would recommend checking out the first Trails in the Sky and going from there.  You can skip the 3rd and go right to Trails from Zero, and then have the option to do the Cold Steel series.  Glad to see this get an English translation all these years later.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

From the story, setting, characters, gameplay, music, etc. I can safely say that right now, this is my number 1 favorite game of all times. That only flaw that holds the game back for me that I mentioned earlier is . _childDocuments_.review: Azure is very different to the other "payoff" entries in the Trails series (Sky SC, Cold Steel II, Cold Steel IV) in that it's a bit of a slow burner at the start and takes a while to set up. Think of the other arcs as hills in terms of stakes, where the first entries start of shallow and then the stakes shoot right up in the second game.The Crossbell arc is more like a "rolling hill" structure. A slow first game with an intense final quarter, a slightly slow second game with an intense second half. The reasoning behind this is probably the fact that Zero, unlike Sky FC, CSI and CSIII ends on a happy note, with all the issues cleared up and the SSS all smiling and waving at the camera, rather than an emotional cliffhanger like the other first-in-the-arc entries.Admittedly, I prefer the other arcs' structure of putting all the excitement into the second game, and I prefer Sky SC as a result, but that doesn't stop this from being an outstanding game.It's Trails. It has all the wonder you'd expect. And the unique thing about Crossbell is that the NPC story arcs are even longer and more detailed than in any other city. Some even go through struggles, seem to find success, then even relapse before improving again. That's a difficult story to tell for a MAIN character. Imagine the effort Falcom are willing to go for these NPCs, just to make this city feel truly alive. (Some things never change though. Looking at you, Haas!)As for the story, when it picks up, it REALLY picks up. Given the small setting, when Crossbell is in danger, it really feels as though the whole world is in danger as this is the world you've grown so used to. The way the changes affect the SSS (the old AND new members) and, of course, the supernatural elements and great powers that remind you of the true stakes of the Trails series.This game also ends on a twist. One hell of a twist. Some might be conflicted on it, but most agree how insane it is, and not something I've seen in any other game.As of where I am at CSIV, this is my 2nd favourite Trails game after Sky SC.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: Near unanimously agreed to be the best game in this already phenomenal series and the best RPG I've ever played. It'd be more efficient to list the things I dislike, because I love everything else:Chapter 1 is slow, but enough mystery is set up to make you want to keep playing.It relies a bit too much on magic cryptid septium vein plot writing in some side parts, but it's not NEARLY as bad as Cold Steel 2-4.The finale drags on and is a little too big of a tone shift from what came before.The combat is still slow, while the arts&crafts system is alright and improved from Sky, it's not on the level of the shard system from Daybreak or press turn from SMT/PersonaThey cut the "If this ain't a bruh moment then I don't know what is" line from the original Geofront translation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: I've been highly addicted to the serie since Trails in the Sky FC and so far this has been the most complete, the longest and the best entry overall : the lovable cast of characters and the intricate political story which totally skyrockets during the game blew me away.I'm not particularly fond of the bonding point system, but it makes the game more immersive and it's nice that every optional event, side quest and hidden quest contribute to the main story and worldbuilding.I'm not sure wether or not it has stolen Trails in The Sky SC's place in my heart but it surely rivals it...The ending makes me want to know what happens next but not sure if it's worth playing 4 long Cold Steel games which I fear to be disappointing...
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this review short:If you played and enjoyed Trails from Zero then you very likely will also enjoy Trails to Azure. I bought both games at full price and consider them worth the money. As was the case with Trails from Zero this port was done by PH3 and the improvements they made to the game make it as close to a definitive version of Azure as you can get.If you didn't play Trails from Zero then you shouldn't play this game. Technically it does have a backstory feature in the main menu that explains the events of the first game however it isn't a proper replacement for playing Zero as a lot of smaller details are left out. Though I can see it being useful if you played Zero a long time ago.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: Great ending to the Crossbell saga and intro for the Cold Steel series. All questions answered you had in Trails to Zero, and there are too many plot twists and turns to even start with. Overall, lived up to the hype I've heard about it, and might've even preceded it. The story after ending raises some questions, but I think those will be answered in Cold Steel 2. So just keep playing, everyone! This is a series that deserves every minute of your time, trust me.P.S.: When I saw those developer chest messages at the near end, made me almost shed a tear. They are all so passionate, it feels great to be a part of this series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: At time of writing, ignore the playtime. I played through the whole game on a different platform.You can't really play this game without play Zero since it's a direct sequel. It helps even more if you play Sky FC/SC to give you more background on some of the characters, but not necessarily like Zero is.Game play wise, it's basically the same as Zero, and very similar to the Sky games. I like that you get a bit more time with some of the other characters to play with, which adds a little bit of more strategizing based on what abilities they have.I still think this story is not quite as good as Sky since there's the whole bonding thing where the character you bond with the most is not set. While I understand that it adds an additional mechanic to the game and more variety to dialogue, I don't think the writing is ever as strong. The relationships don't feel as well developed. Nevertheless, overall, I do like this story and the characters.If you plan to play the newer Cold Steel games, I highly recommend finishing this before playing Cold Steel 3.

_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: This is my game of the year.  Trails from Zero was a 7/10 to me...I really didn't expect this arc to become my favourite of the Trails series but the game completely won me over.   This is a game that's greater than the sum of its parts because of how wonderful the storytelling comes together.  This is a 9.5/10 in terms of video game stories that rivals the absolute best I've played in my 40 years.  The actual moment to moment game play on the other hand is like a 6/10.  The pacing in this arc is brutal for my tastes as so much of your time is spend travelling from location to location having short conversations and then repeating again and again.  You probably have more combat in the final dungeon than you do in the entire prologue and first two chapters of the game combined.  Its just not a good balance at all for my preference.  Other Trails games have questionable balance between story/combat but this one takes it to another level and I felt it.  Still...the way things come together makes this stuff totally worth it.  These two games are highly recommended almost entirely because of how Azure brings things together in such a satisfying and clever way.  While it does not have my favourite cast in the series...this is Trails storytelling and drama at its finest.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: Trails to Azure is the epic conclusion of the Crossbell duology in the Trails series; and looking at the five games I played from them provided me the most satisfaction. A lot of story arcs get resolved, the world changes and of course there are quite a lot of battles, little story bits. And they are necessary, as the game basically retraces the locations of its predecessor, Trails from Zero, with only a few new ones added.The result is close to being more of the same as the previous entries, there is no great innovation in the gameplay, but everything is put together masterfully, but this is balanced out by the increased challenge (let's forget the few truly rage-inducing bosses here :) ) and the interesting characters and world.So, to finalize, this is a great JRPG (with all of its mandatory elements), and almost makes the entire series up to this point worth playing for (but please, play the earlier games before starting, it expects you to know about the world).
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: A great send-off for the Crosbell arc, full of twists and turns and heart-felt moments but I feel that the ending was way too stretched out and bloated for what it was worth. Last several hours were dungeons that just kept coming. There could've been some other way to deal with the branching storylines but they chose this one. I found the first game to be more solid and cohesive, all though much smaller in scale too. This game is everything you would want from the series and I would recommend playing these games from the beginning to fully understand the plot and to know all the characters. In my eyes this would be the worst part to begin your journey. Played on Steam deck, worked wonderfully.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly abrupt and underwhelming ending asides, Azure is a very respectable successor to the already incredible Zero. The stakes are higher, the player gets more freedom on what they can do and the characterization and world building the Trails game has been known for is still very solid.I do think this is the turning point where the writing can get more cringy with how Lloyd becomes an even more obvious harem master and the very unpleasant character that's Shirley, but still not to a point it becomes insufferable.A shame after this we got the horrible saga that was the Erebonia arc and completely sent the narrative down the drain, I'll rather act as if the anticlimatic ending we got here is where the series died than whatever nonsense Falcom came up with afterwards.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: I have played many JRPGs over the years: Final Fantasy 1 through 12, Breath of Fire 1 through 4, and so, so many more, but the Crossbell Arc of The Legend of Heroes is the best I've experienced by a wide margin.The characters are deep, the music exquisite, the worldbuilding rich, and the attention to detail unsurpassed.I have played Trails to Azure more than once, not all through steam, and one of my playthroughs was on Steamdeck without an internet connection so that playtime isn't reflected.I recommend playing through the Trails in the Sky arc first; it is also excellent, and the same overarching story continues in Crossbell!PS Don't forget to double-tap those chests!

_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay has been slightly refined from the previous entry Trails from Zero, some of the ridiculously OP crafts have received a nerf such as Ellie's broken craft point healing combo, to make the overall combat more balanced. Magic ends up being better in this game than crafts are, putting this more in line with the Sky trilogy. They basically made all out attacks obscenely rare which can make normal monster encounters more annoying, but the feature is still there. There is a new combat mode called Burst added at 'climatic' end of chapter fights but it's hardly anything to write home about and is more of a gimmick than anything, but it is interesting nonetheless. They also added a new feature to orbments called master quartz, basically including a class system into the game without relegating people to roles based solely on how their slots are allocated or their stats. It's an interesting change that makes team building more versatile and fun.Story and character wise, this is obviously the meat of the main plot of Crossbell. Trails from Zero was more of an introduction to the team, along with a 'first case' for them to solve. I will say that this is a true sequel to Trails from Zero, rather than a literal game cut in 2 pieces like Trails in the Sky was with it's absolutely dreadful cliffhanger at the end of the first game with little to no interesting events taking place until second chapter. I appreciate this change, as it allows both games to be able to stand on their own, as an introduction to the team that first game still had interesting stakes and a compelling villain. This game's two new additions to the party are Noel and Wazy, but I must say they hardly feel like part of the gang. You spent that entire first game with Llyod, Tio, Randy, and Elie and these two characters joining the group after playing such a minor role in the first game just doesn't sell it for me and they still feel like they're tagging along, but the character writing is still good. I must say this has been one of the finest JRPG stories I've read. It's very well written and has amazing payoffs with a thrilling antagonist and final act (especially compared to Trails in the Sky). I saw people hating on the ending to this game, but I think it's great. Fantastic story.If I had to break it down: the story is great, the gameplay additions have been welcome, but the two new characters in the main party don't necessarily feel vital to the main story. So far it's a fantastic 9/10 and it get's my hearty recommendation. This is not only the best Trails game by a landslide, but it's also a staggeringly good JRPG.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: I have played Trails To Zero and Trails To Azure multiple times and still find something new every playthrough. The characters and storyline are fun and engaging. My suggestion would be to play Zero first and then Azure as they complete the Crossbell story arc. They are both part of a much larger story starting from 3 Trails in the Sky, the 2 aforementioned Crossbell, Cold Steel I-IV, and now Reverie. It's a time sync, but I'm retired so, eh.

_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails to Azure

_childDocuments_.review: I love this arc - and it is essential for  the Erebonian arc. This game has no equals in its genre. The storytelling, the attenton to even minor npcs - please finish the entire series with the same quality, with the same heart and love for writing and for characters you created. The series is very positive and life affirming and impactful, gameplay very engaging and there are so many fun little things to discover when interacting with just about any npc. I love this world, the characters, the themes, the way the story develops - it's quality writing.And the Azure tree is one of my most favourite final dungeouns - it's fun, it has trials meaningful for characters. I also love how bonds work in this game, with special unique skills learned for each character. And the master quartz  - I prefer the orbment system in this game more than any other part. But each Trails game brings something unique to the table and the storytelling up to Reverie has been keepiing me engaged and involved in all characters and looking forward meeting them again. I can't stress it it enough. The characters make this game on top of the way story takes its time to develop. It's magnificent. _childDocuments_.review: I am so glad I got into this series in 2023, because after this game I can absolutely say this is one of the best JRPGs I’ve ever played, AND this has so far been the best entry I’ve played in the Kiseki series, having previously played Trails in the Sky FC/SC/3rd and Trails from Zero (I have been tackling the series in JP release order).This is by no means a perfect game, I have certainly come across a few gripes (insane surprise attacks, cool as they were, and bonus missable DP behind long scenes) as well as recurring ones from the previous entries (again, missables… personally, I hate em), but Trails to Azure really nails A LOT of the points I enjoy in a JRPG. So far, Trails in the Sky the 3rd and Sky SC have been my favourite out of the entries I’ve played so far, with some of the best soundtracks and satisfying finishes to a story and arc I’ve experienced in a game, but Trails to Azure has managed to surpass all of that by taking it further beyond. Like Trails from Zero, the quality of life is great. You’ll find the same quality of life options in Trails to Azure, such as 30-144FPS, Soundtrack titles, options for High Speed modes and the like.About the points it nailed, Trails to Azure really popped off. I thought Sky SC had the best final boss music in the series so far, until Azure. I thought Sky the 3rd had some of the best overall music (especially the battle tracks, hello 'Fighting Right On' and 'Dreamy And Boisterous Holy Land'), until Azure (now 'Conflicting Passions' and 'Unfathomed Force' is my best friend). I also thought both SC and the 3rd had great, satisfying finales; now I can put Azure on that boat as well. The gameplay still pushes out the system you may be familiar with from previous entries, and that continues to evolve with the world building. In particular, Azure introduces Master Quartz which allows you to focus on a particular build style, which I particularly liked. The foreshadowing as we reach the conclusion of an arc and prepare to go toward a new arc is something I loved in the Liberl Arc, and was satisfying in Azure. The main characters, major characters, support characters, and cameos, I LOVE them. Not much else to say to that!I would like to give a huge shoutout to the previous game Trails from Zero, which with Azure makes up the Crossbell duology, because if it wasn’t for that game exploring each individual main character’s growth and experiences, the events and barriers they faced, and the meaning behind Zero, Trails to Azure truly wouldn’t have shined as much as it does. The narrative shot up to the stars as each chapter from the beginning to the end had me on edge and wanting more. Oh and thank God for the break chapters, truly. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, it was everything I expected and more for the second Crossbell game. Plot, characters, writing, world, gameplay all improve and flow seamlessly from Trails from Zero. Props to the Geofront team for putting in the translation work as well.Only complaint I have is that the final boss is rather annoying instead of difficult. But playing on Nightmare mode first go turned out to be a fair challenge. Building Lloyd as an evasion tank made the game a lot more manageable, though.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good final game in the duology of Crossbell, i can see why it's highly praised by a lot of players. The story is very slow for the first 3 chapters but the 4th and the finale are worth it. The main drawback for me was the combat which is very unbalanced, crafts start strong but get weaker the game goes on and the arts are the opposite. There are a lot of "one shots" bosses move from nowhere in the last chapters, you need to experience it once and have a game over to know there is one,  making the overall felling of the combat not that great in the last 20-30ish hours. That make having a 100% physical evasion tank, Tio S craft "Zero Field" and casters a must have for the endgame.It took me 70h to finish the game on Hard with all sides contents available in the first playthrough and most of the achievements. 15h for the second one on NG+ nightmare, skipping all dialogues and rushing the main story, with the new NG+ content and the rest of the achievements.The last 15hrs with the game open doing nothing for the "100hrs played" achievement which is ridiculous to do with the speed function added in this version.Overall score : 8/10Pros :-Very good OST as usual from Falcom, special mention for the last boss fight music one the best in the series.-The story start slow but finish very strong in the last 2 chapters. It's a good conclusion of the duology and the events from the previous game.-Very good mains and secondaries characters. The 4 mains characters are one the best in the series imo. If you love to talk to NPCs there are a lot of that in this game, like the previous one.-Very good quality port and english translation. The japanese VA is nice.Cons :-Lot a of reuse places and monsters from the previous game.-A lot of missables (items, quests... and some of them are well hidden). A guide is mandatory if you want to 100% like all the games in the series.-Slow build up story for the first 3 chapters. There are some important parts storywise in these but its just a setup for the 4th and the last chapter.  A bit sad that there is not really an epilogue too.-Combat is not well balanced. Bosses on the finale chapter are very physical resistant and magic become a must have. Furthermore, going melee is very punishing if you dont have an evade tank and casting arts is just safer and do a lot more damage than spaming crafts.-"One shot" moves on some bosse on the last two chapters. You need to get hit by it a least once to make it somehow predictable for the "retried" combat. Tio S craft "zero" field is a must have in endgame and make her mandatory in a party. Same stuff with the evasion tank.-The last dungeon is a bit too long and the finale fights last way too much even with the speed up animations.

_childDocuments_.review: My entry into the Trails series was Cold Steel. And I LOVED it. I thought it was the bees knees in every way, shape and form. So I was pretty confused to see that many people had a lukewarm response to it.I went back and started from the beginning with Trails in the Sky, and after finishing Trails to Azure, I kinda get it. The bar was set ridiculously high by the Liberl and Crossbell arcs.Trails games are a masterclass in storytelling and world building, and Trails to Zero & Azure are peak Trails in this regard. Both games do an incredible job of letting you get comfortable with the day-to-day goings on in Crossbell, and then BOOM everything gets turned upside down. Then, just when you think things have peaked, the stakes get raised again.So if you're looking for a memorable, slow burn rpg with an incredible story, then look no further. You don't necessarily HAVE to play Trails in the Sky before this series, but the payoff is a hundred times more impactful if you have and I would highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: From Zero to Azure, it has been an amazing journey full of great moments, emotional roller-coasters, memorable characters, and of course, superb soundtracks. If you like JRPGs, then the Crossbell duology (Trails From Zero and this game) are games that, in my opinion, are very worth your time. While the Trails Series is filled with great games, I would say that this duology is the one that has my favorite cast and story out of all that I've played so far (namely, Sky Trilogy and Cold Steel 1+2).The story starts right into action with our Protagonist Lloyd in pursuit of the remnant of Zero's main antagonist group, and it does not get any less exciting from there. Following that, Lloyd and his team, the SSS, are faced with political reform as a result of the aftermath of Zero's event. While all of that was happening, the two major neighboring superpowers were setting their sights on Crossbell for its highly geostrategic position and also as the center of trade on their continent. As both countries begin making their moves, a conspiracy that is trying to make use of all players at the table and the current political situation begin showing its true form. It's now up to Lloyd and his friends to unravel this conspiracy and seize the truth.Building upon the foundations laid by Zero, the story in Azure expands the scope to international politics, giving a look at many countries that exist in the world of Trails as well as some key individuals from said countries. These world-building adds more complex layer to the setting while also showing how large the scale of the world actually is. The world-building also complements the story they are trying to tell perfectly, as it gives a sense of scale in regards to how Crossbell stands and its position in the world of Trails.Next is about the cast of characters. Also building on the foundation set by Zero, some characters are explored more in Azure, giving them more backstories to flesh them out. On the other hand, characters who already had their arc finished in Zero did not have much focus. Between Main, Supporting, Antagonist, and even NPC characters, this game has no shortage of intriguing cast of characters which will make your journey an eventful one. The character development in Azure is a huge improvement over Zero, and some character arcs are simply amazing, with my favorites being Lloyd, the ever-lovable cheesy shonen protagonist, Randy, the best bro, and Rixia, the best girl.The gameplay also has many upgrades over Zero. The first is that the difficulty has improved. There are barely any moments in Zero where I feel that the difficulty is, well, difficult, despite playing on Hard in the first playthrough. I don't even use OP builds, and I barely use any Combo Crafts at all. In Azure however, I feel that the difficulty is just right, with some battles pushing me to the limit, making me use more items, Combo Crafts (which, in a twist of fate, became one of my favorite mechanics), and the new mechanic, Burst. Second is the addition of the Master Quartz system, which increases the gimmicks you could play with as well as creating more possibilities for various different builds. Third, fast travel to locations outside of the city is now possible by car.Last but not least, I would like to express my gratitude to the Geofront Translation Team, NISA, and other people involved who made it possible for me to experience this amazing game in English. Reading all the chest messages in the final dungeon made me realize all the effort that has gone into translating and localizing this wonderful game, and it makes me appreciate the journey much more.

_childDocuments_.review: Trails to Azure is an awesome sequel to Trails from Zero. I was surprised how much better this game is when compared to the first one. Let's explore the ups and downs of the game (+, +/-, -, ?):+The biggest improvement here is Lloyd. He felt very flat, and kinda boring, in the first game, but here, I can finally see why people love Lloyd. What a great journey!+The game looks and sounds fantastic, like all The Legend of Heroes -games.+The story is a fantastic collection of deep politics, personal struggles and conspiracies. ♥♥♥♥ gets really real and very shocking at times. There are so many great scenes here, and I was invested at all times.  Crossbell, the reveal of how , the Trade Conference, the end of ... Damn, I almost wanna play this again already!+That Intermission was awesome, for various reasons...many, many reasons...+More playable characters! Yes! The best thing about the new additions to the team is that no one feels useless. You can play any combo you want.+I don't know what happened here, but Tio is a killer in battle!+! Yesss!+The dungeon design is almost perfect here. I usually hate long dungeons, but here everything works perfectly. Well, maybe not the .+/-The final chapter feels like it never ends, but it's not painful or anything.*+/-Most bosses are surprisingly easy and pose almost no threat. The threat comes in mobs, like with .+/-So, do we see more of  in the new game or not? _childDocuments_.review: This game is a direct sequel from Trails from Zero. In order to fully comprehend the story of this game please play that first.+Same amazing 2D art-style that has charm and character. Probably the last Trails game that will be in 2D.+The story is amazing with lots of plot twists and even more mysteries.+I love trails music, so it's still amazing.+From my experience Trails is always known for its world-building and excellent characters.+The optimization carried on to the sequel. The customization you can have fits any preference.+Once again the voice acting is only in Japanese, it still adds a lot to the experience.+-Minigames! Some of them are bad and some of them are good. The achievement for the  minigame is a nightmare. Getting 4000 points in that minigame is no joke and I highly recommend you don't even try unless you like torturing yourself. If you played Trails of Cold Steel 3 you will be familiar with . Yes it's in this game and I still have a love hate relationship with it (maybe because i'm bad at it okay).+-The combat system is starting to transition in to more of a trails of cold steel type system, giving additional orbment slots for more customization. My only gripe about the combat is that very specific builds are required to beat certain bosses. Unless you are a perfectionist and want all the Detective Points first play-through like me it probably will not bother you. I had to redo these fights over and over because I wanted to win and get the points.+-More hidden objectives, quests, decisions, and quests (some of them are evil to find). There is optional areas and bosses on new game+ which makes my 100% scan achievement impossible on my first play-through (I'm still going to replay it later anyways).-They fixed the random Japanese text that was in Zero. Some of the Japanese voice lines are still too short and obviously not the literal translation. Minor flaws and gripes but this side of it was majorly improved in Azure compared to Zero.-The opening movie STILL doesn't play for this game too, I just want to see the opening when I start it up...-There are a few scenes that don't make any sense but I believe the overall story makes up for it. The story is still amazing! Which for me is expected in a trails game. This game definitely has some bigger flaws in some of the story points compared to Zero, but the overall story is spectacular and really enjoyable to uncover. A lot of bugs I complained about were fixed and really couldn't be happier. There are some fundamental issues with the combat system but you can still enjoy the game without doing the recommended strategies. The minigame mentioned above was an absolute nightmare to get the achievement in. I played on hard mode again which felt good until said boss fights above (but they were still do-able). _childDocuments_.review: Hard for me to review this without spoiling most of the game...Without spoilers, the short of it: - The music is pretty here and there for me, either half the soundtrack was on par or better than From Zero, or i found it easy to forget. As expected, plenty of songs from From Zero return in this game. - More mechanics have been added to battle, which means the difficulty has also been upped. But I can say overall, it's a welcome addition and doesn't feel bloated or artificial. People playing on higher difficulties will be utilizing the newer mechanics.- This game is very much a Falcom of Falcon games. It's longer than In the'Sky Second Chapter, which is a feat because that game was also pretty meaty on its story. Well worth the investment however. - The port is also good, as usual, reliable performance on the steam deck without any tweaking, and on my higher end PC i didn't have any issues playing this game at 144fps at 1440p, save for a few moments the game would skip a frame or two because its faster than how it was originally designed. The story in this one is insanely detailed, down to the very beginning of From Zero even, it ties together events; concludes character arcs; and has some wild revelations that made me understand why people considered this game to be the pinnacle of the Trails franchise and their favorite game overall. The pacing is slightly better, for a trails game, its still slow overall but the slow sections aren't as bad as the previous 4 games and when the game reaches its second to last chapter things hit the ground on rockets. The very last chapter lasts a couple hours too... with exploration and sidequests on top of finishing the story, final chapter took me about 20 hours. that's kind of insane. The one thing I personally wasn't a fan of, and its more of a trope i never liked, was KeA's entire character. Its revealed why she's been important this whole time and adds a ton of continuity to why everyone makes her to be such a big deal. And while I'm not a fan of children being made into important story elements that everybody wants to care about, the reason felt like something they pulled out of their butts but it was conceivable I guess. I would've replaced her with a talking Church Artifact and just do something with that. Crossbell was an arc that started off insanely slow (From Zero didn't get interesting until Chapter 3 looking back) and then finished out stronger than ever. I'm not sure if I can say this tops the Liberl arc, but its pretty close in its own right.

_childDocuments_.review: As JRPG, its so good it's ridiculous. As with most Trails games, the start is quite slow as they slowly reintroduce characters to you and recap on some of the main points from Zero. The devs also spend some time building the political situation as you do side quests.Like a lot of long JRPGs, there's a lot of missables that you need to be very meticulous or just use a guide. I recommend Neoseeker's guide that hides spoilers.The more of this series you play, the better the series is. Can't wait for Reverie! Azure is probably the crown jewel of the Trails series. Highly recommend every JRPG fan to play the series. _childDocuments_.review: This is the conclusion of the Crossbell SSS arc and is the sequel to Trails from Zero. The game sets up the events of the Trails of Cold Steel series. If I remember correctly many of the events of this game are happening at the same time as Trails of Cold Steel 1. So if you've already played Trail of Cold Steel 1, some of these events will seem very familiar to you.Overall there is really nothing new here if you played any of the previous games in the series. The game follows the same format as the previous games.I would highly recommend playing Trials from Zero before playing this one because you would be missing out on much important backstory.I feel this game shares some of the pitfalls when I think of Trails in the Sky 2. Basically the game takes place in the exact same part of the world and really feels a bit like you've been there, done that before. So the game is not really as fresh as the previous one. However there are still many twists and turns that still make it really interesting. Playtime coming in at ~59 hours while running in turbo mode. This is ~9 hours longer than the previous game but the final chapter is quite long. A bit too long and repetitive in my opinion. After the final boss falls the game raps up at light speed, and it just feels like I wanted more of an epilogue.I would rank this game as good but not great. Not the worst game in the series but not the best. However it is important for setting up future games.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I got into Trails, I've heard nothing but good things about Trails to Azure. Many fans consider it to be the height of the series (so far) in terms of writing. So, naturally, I was especially curious to see how this one would pan out. And the end result: Pretty good! Not my favorite Trails game - that honor goes to Sky SC - but it comes in a strong second place, well ahead of the other games that come before it. That all said, let's go to the bullet points!The Praise:+ A memorable, colorful, well-written cast of characters. Crossbell arc's small roster (relative to Sky and Cold Steel) means more time for character moments, and we get lots of them! Everyone from the SSS to the villains gets their time to shine. Some are done better than others, but no one is written badly, by any means.+ A wild plot full of twists. There were many instances where I had to stop playing just to process something that had just happened - and I mean that in a good way. Not even Sky SC had this many, "OMG WTF" moments. But putting the twists aside, the general plot and the series of events Azure follows flow extremely well. The build up to and execution of the major events are organic and feel satisfying to play through.+ New features and additions, most notably the addition of Master Quartz and Burst, allow for a gameplay experience that is markedly different from all past Trails games, even Zero.+ Killer soundtrack, as expected from the likes of Falcom.Neutral Observations:* The general design the second half of the game is reminiscent of Sky SC, story-wise. It's understandable why Falcom might try to repeat that game's formula, given how successful it was. IMO, it works well for the most part, but it's just not the same. * There are a number of boss battles where you're "supposed" to lose, meaning that even if you somehow win, the boss will basically just get back up and be like, "Nah nvm lol." From a narrative standpoint, it makes sense, because the main protags are a ragtag group of underdogs fighting supremely powerful opponents. From a gameplay standpoint, though, this can turn people off for obvious reasons. You do get extra DP for beating these "impossible" boss fights, though, so it's not completely meaningless either way. ||There's actually one such fight where you won't progress, win or lose, unless you get the boss down to at least 50% health.|| Criticisms:- Trails to Azure takes place at the same time as Trails of Cold Steel I and II, and the events of those games are somewhat interconnected with those of Azure. The issue? You get spoilers for both games. Falcom's writers aren't stupid, so I'm sure the details you learn here are relatively trivial, but it does detract a bit from the excitement of moving on to Cold Steel arc.- The late-game writing feels too... safe. Azure's dramatic parts like to stop short of killing off characters, which stops them from having the weight they should have. I'm not saying the game should have killed off more people just because, but there were moments where death would have made more sense and gotten me more emotionally invested. Overall, a great game and a fitting, climactic turning point for the whole series. On to Cold Steel!

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent sequel to Trails from Zero. This game really builds on the characters and plot from its predecessor, and I would highly advice against playing this game without having played Trails from Zero first. Trails from Zero is a good game so it's worth playing in its own right.This game builds upon the gameplay mechanics that Trails from Zero had, allowing greater strategic though. Mostly. This game falls off a bit though when you realize there is exactly one strategy that is needed for the vast majority of the game's hardest boss fights. If you play the game on a difficulty higher than normal, get ready to specialize in arts because many bosses have absurd amounts of physical armor. From a story perspective, we get to further explore many characters' past that was touched upon in the previous game. There were some extremely touching moments in this game and I don't think you'll regret playing it. This is a 7.5/10 game, held back some by the somewhat rigid tactics that high level combat requires to not have a miserable time. Without that it'd probably be 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A great end to the Crossbell arc. A great RPG with a ton of content, more freedom, a few needed combat improvements, and a good job with the world building. Before anything else, I want to talk about the common question of "Can I play this without playing any other games?" The game has a section that recaps the story from Trails From Zero, and it does an adequate job of catching you up on characters and the setting. But ask yourself, are you actually gonna read that stuff? You will miss the minutia of things that happened with a quick overview of things, but if you are jumping in cold and not even gonna bother with that stuff then you will be lost. The story pretty much immediately follows up Zero, and while you do get a bit of catch up in game, it is strictly trying to get that out of the way to deal with the new stuff. You could jump in if you don't mind being lost, but a lot of the story leans on knowing the characters and relationships from Zero.The main story here is dealing with bigger issues than just Crossbell. While Trails to Zero dealt with internal threats and problems, Azure deals with the external issues and problems from the outside coming in. It is a good way to increase the stakes, and does a good job of making you feel like Crossbell is in over their heads with the issues they face on a larger scale. If you liked the more grounded villains and stories of Zero, this one takes it to the fantastical and really gives you threats that are way bigger than a group of cops should handle.  One of the great things about the story is the decision to cash in all the story and character elements for a few big moments.  There is a good chunk of the game where you are still walking around and solving things in Crossbell, talking to people, doing small things to really get to know the towns people. By the time those things happen you are familiar with all the characters and locations, and then the big gut punches happen and you see just some rough spots for the town you have been helping. For the sake of not spoiling things, It did a good job of making me care for the place when the bad times came.Gameplay is somewhat improved here, not that it was bad in Zero. The game introduces Master Quartz, if you played Cold Steel you are already familiar, but these just give a special boost and a special skill when you max it out late in the game. My only complaint is it takes forever to level them, which is reasonable considering the skills you learn when they are maxed out. A good addition. If you did well in Zero you wont have problems here.You also pick up more characters than the base group that Zero had. They are good additions, that make sense in the story, and its a welcomed change. Its nice to have an extended cast that bounce off each other in a good way. Other than that, I do have a few personal gripes with the game. Did you like pom pom party? No? To bad, its back, and you are even required to play it once during a story section. You can lose and just move on, but I just personally did not love that moment. I do wish some of the more helpful orbs were available earlier like detection.  If you don't like the "have x amount of elements on your enigma to cast a certain spell" the Master Quartz help a little, but it is a pain to still deal with that when you get a new orb that just can't fit in with the current build. Most of these things are fixed in future installments, so this stuff really doesn't bother me. This is an easy recommend, that fills in a lot of holes in the rest of the series, and is just in general a good game. I enjoyed it from start to end.

_childDocuments_.review: Another excellent adventure in the legend of heroes series of video games. A lot of people will tell you that these games are dull boring and take a long time to get started. Each game in the series starts of with a ton of story exposition so you can get to know the characters the world and what the current issue is with in. Naturally this is going to take time to really build up with something good and the climax in every game is always worth sitting through all of that. These games are known to be a huge time sink and if you haven't played it from trails in the sky 1 and onward i highly suggest you do. Each series of games takes place with in the same world but different sections of said world.So in one series you are playing in liberal while another your playing in erobonia then another your playing crossbell ( this set of games )  then cavelard. Each set of games will be known as these arcs in the over all plot so it's best to play in order.  You can certainly get away with watching a synopisis to catch up with the series but it's much more rewarding to see how it all goes down rather then it getting explained to you in plot points. Just know that you will be putting in 1000+ hours to play catch up but is it worth it? In my general opinion yes.

_childDocuments_.review: While I received this particular copy for free, I played this previously using the Geofront fan-translation. I also purchased the collector's edition of this game for Switch, so if that reduces the bias in any way, then hey, neat.Alright one last disclaimer, this game is a direct sequel to Trails From Zero. However, it is also the 5th game in the Trails series (which started with Trails in the Sky 1-3). Characters from the Sky games do appear in this and influence the plot, so if you want to get the most out of this game, you'll want to experience the others. It's daunting but worth it imo. The other games are also amazing, so giving those a glowing recommendation.Anyways, going to go ahead and say it. This is my favorite RPG of all time. For a while, Golden Sun 2 held that position, but this game is just incredible. Now this is not to say this game is perfect, no game is, and I want to hype responsibly lol. But this was not only a satisfying conclusion to the Crossbell arc, but is just one of the best gaming experiences of my life. Let's get into why.Trails' combat has always been one of my favorite aspects of the games, and this is where they refined the system to it's best. There are features from CS that were created in this game that works excellently in tandem with the mechanics of Zero. There is so much freedom of customization, and with new game+ I am actually wanting to do some runs where I get to really mess with party loadouts from the get-go.As for the story, it hits the ground running early on, and slows down as is usual for Trails, but the story is easily the most intense of the series so far. With lots of twists, turns, and clever setup for the Cold Steel arc after this. It also feels like the most full experience, as the Cold Steel arc hit similar beats, but this game manages to pack it all into a single game and it just makes an epic experience by the end.The characters are all very likeable, if only very anime. If you hate anime, I feel this series in general probably isn't for you, but as far as anime-styled characters go, I like pretty much everyone. Some characters do some stuff that makes people cringe which is fair though, I'll just leave it at them being touchey.The music in this game is incredible as always from Trails, with the final boss theme of this game being my favorite song of all time. I listen to it multiple times a week, and I first played this 2 years ago, send help.I will also note NIS did a really good job localizing this behemoth of a game alongside the Geofront team. I noticed maybe like 4 typos, and considering how much text is in this game, that's impressive.If I had to pick any major negatives:  This game does require you to play it more than once to see everything it has to offer. You can easily YouTube some scenes, but it is worth mentioning. I did the math and if you want every single combo Craft upgrade you'll have to replay the game 5 times, BUT that is not needed to get every achievement, so you're fine with one playthrough. The most you'll miss out on is a few optional monster fights.Get this game, just play Zero first.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Trails game. If you're familiar with the series then you know what to expect, and I'll simply say that Azure earns its reputation as one of the best entries in the series. If you're new here, allow me to introduce you. The Trails series is at this point 9 games long, (with more coming). Their DNA is about 2 parts Persona, 1 part Grandia, 1 part Gundam. So expect to spend most of your time fighting battles, talking to NPCs or watching cutscenes. The combat is fun, the music is good, the art style is charming if very low res, but what sets Trails apart from the competition is the writing. Even casual banter tends to be surprisingly witty, and even though the series loves to turn up the cheese factor, it still knows how to get serious when it wants to. Azure in particular deals with questions of independence, nationalism and WMDs. This is definitely not the place to start the series (go play Trails in the Sky), but it's a great game.

name: The Legend of Nayuta: Boundless Trails
detailed_description: * Previous owners of the original Japanese release of The Legend of Nayuta: Boundless Trails on Steam can download the English update for free. Nayuta has always dreamed of exploring beyond the horizon of his island home. After a fateful encounter with a fairy by the name of Noi, he and his friends find themselves whisked away on an adventure through multiple worlds in order to stop an evil plot that has been set in motion. About Nayuta spends his days gazing up at the stars above his island home and wondering what lies beyond the horizon. Though people claim the sea they live on is flat and finite, Nayuta knows there must be more out there, just waiting to be discovered. Occasionally, ruins and stars will fall from the sky over Nayuta's home, offering what seem to be glimpses of other worlds. While exploring one such ruin, he and his friends save a small, fairy-like girl by the name of Noi. She tells Nayuta that something very important has been stolen from her and asks for his help in retrieving it. It's with this that Nayuta's journey begins—one which will take him far beyond the confines of his island to experience new worlds and extraordinary discoveries! Key Features Worlds Beyond Home: Experience all the wondrous phenomena The Legend of Nayuta has to offer with HD visuals, high quality music, 60fps, and new illustrations added for this Western release! Skills for Every Season: Enter the fray with real-time action gameplay and environment-based puzzles that are affected by the current season. Utilize season-based magic and powerful weapon skills to take down your foes, and unlock new techniques based on your performance. An Ocean of Adventure: Dive into a different kind of Trails game! Experience a light, whimsical story rooted in fantasy and discovery with a variety of colorful locations and characters, plus tons of extra quest content.

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Nayuta: Boundless Trails follows the title character, Nayuta, a curious young man fascinated by the stars and the world's possibilities that he and others cannot perceive. Contrary to popular opinion, Nayuta believes their planet is not flat and is obsessed with learning more. In addition, his parents life ambition was to reach "Lost Heaven" beyond the horizon, but they failed and died, which piqued Nayuta's curiosity even more. Ruins and crystals are also falling from the sky from time to time, and some believe they are from other worlds. Thus begins a journey in Lost Heaven about the seemingly infinite possibilities and the quest that lies beyond the horizon.Nayuta's gameplay is more akin to the Ys than the Trails series. As you travel Lost Heaven, you'll encounter action fighting and platforming. Each location features stages where you fight monsters, collect items, finish optional quests and advance to temples where boss encounters occur. Combat blends Nayuta's sword powers with Noi's magical moves. As you progress, you have access to more of each. Clearing stages while clearing specific conditions, for example, earns you stars, and as you earn more stars, you can acquire new sword moves for Nayuta. He can also alter the seasons, unlocking seasonal variants of previous levels, providing even more replayability and star collecting. The seasonal stages change up the landscapes, platforms, and enemy variety enough that it never gets boring. The platforming portion of the stages, on the other hand, felt a little hazy at times. These stages are presented in 2.5D, and there were numerous occasions when I had to jump onto moving platforms only to misjudge my distance and receive fall damage. It also doesn't help that the camera is fixed. While I prefer turn-based combat like the mainstream Trails games, the action combat system in Legend of Nayuta is solid and simple to learn. Fighting, jumping, and dashing your way through the relatively short parts is incredibly exciting, and it's worth looking for secret treasure chests and goodies thanks to the accurate controls and solid gameplay. In battle, though, Nayuta is merely a slasher. You can do a rapid sword combination, a dodge roll, and a double jump. You slash at an opponent, and if your combo isn't enough to kill him, you avoid his vengeance. This is simple at first, but the game quickly introduces foes that demand tactical thinking. It could be due to ranged attacks or resistances to all but a few tactics. When you come into groups of enemies that combine several of these features, things become tough, but in a good way.What keeps me playing is the characters, art style and quests. The companions are wholesome, and the environment is lovely thanks to Remnant Isle's warm feelings and the mysterious Lost Heaven. The story is significantly more clear than in previous Trails games, yet it has enough mystery to keep me playing. Especially since there are some probable connections to gnaw on if you've played prior Trails games. There are additional side missions in each of the chapters, but for the most part they are only incidental, but they are still a nice way to pass the time. Nayuta is an engaging, lively main character, and Remnant Island is an appealing backdrop, but the broader plot is somewhat tedious, relying on tired and generally expected genre clichés. Despite plenty of well-written dialogue and a few story twists to keep things interesting, it all falls a little bit flat. Overly serious antagonists, a squeaky mascot companion, and the appearance of a mystery female with amnesia are a recipe for disaster in any RPG.The multi-phase boss fights are also another highlight. These critical fights have their own quirks, phases and while it may take a few tries to find a good approach, there is a lot of uniqueness on display, especially since this was initially a PSP title. One could even say that Nayuta is one of Falcom's more experimental works in terms of gameplay, which often works to the game's benefit. Still, the title feels a little unjust at times. Off-screen invisible enemy attacks can be annoying, especially when they knock you off a platform and reset your progress. Overall, these are minor difficulties, but the aggravation can mount when attempting to conquer a level for certain rewards. However, if there is one area where Nayuta excels, it is in the presentation. This is a fantastic remaster of an already fantastic PSP edition. The graphical style, with its wide spectrum of vivid colors and stunningly pretty lighting effects, really comes into its own with the higher resolution, while running at a faultless 60 frames per second. The only two issues I've discovered is that I can select 144fps/hz with my resolution, but it never goes above 60 fps. The second issue is that numerous dubbed lines are missing, and I believe they could have done a better job voicing more lines.The Legend of Nayuta: Boundless Trails is an entertaining action role-playing game that takes elements of the larger series on which it is based and creates something unique. The gameplay from minute to minute is engaging, albeit with some minor platforming frustrations here and there. Even if the story is simple and politically not as captivating as the main Trails games, the heartfelt characters, secrets and side quests help enrich the world.

_childDocuments_.review: There's 3 different perspectives that I think it makes sense to break this up into. From someone who has played only a Trails game before, from someone who has played only a Ys game before, and from someone who has done neither. If you want to see the short TLDR, just skip to the bottom.For anyone who has never played a Falcom game before:This game is very much more than meets the eye in many ways. Combat is simple but very addicting and the music is basically as great as you could possibly expect from any RPG game of this style lol, its phenomenal. The story is solid, good at parts, extremely simple at others, but it works and I think it's definitely worth seeing (even if it is not life-changing). You do not need to play the other Trails games at all to enjoy, and it makes hardly any references to the main series. However, please do keep in mind that this game can get VERY grindy if you try to 100% each level, as there a lot of levels in this game (no spoilers, but take my word for it). To be honest, I don't recommend doing it, as it will likely burn you out from enjoying the rest of the good stuff in the game. Overall though, yeah absolutely recommend this game. If you're looking to start getting into Ys or Falcom, its a good starting game. If you're looking to get into the trails series specifically, I think you're much better off starting with Trails in the Sky FC or Trails of Cold Steel 1 and 2 (then circling back to Sky FC, you wont regret it if you liked those games). Nayuta is just far too different to really call it representative of the other Trails game experiences.For those who have played Ys:This is very similar to other older Ys games post Ys VI (so like Ys Origin, Ys III). If you like the gameplay loop of those games, you'll like this without a doubt. Its got that action RPG that flows fantastic with the music just like you'd expect from those Ys games. Story is about on par with those games as well, so solid but not super impactful. Upgrading armor, loot, etc is very similar to those games, and the addition of Noi gives you the magic powers you sometimes get in these games. Nayuta is also very similar in grind to something like Ys Origin in some ways, except the story is linear and not recursive/repeating like it is in that game. All that being said, if you're looking to get into Trails from Ys, this game isn't the game that really gives an entry into those games. Its just too different in almost every way. If you just want more Ys goodness though, go wild, you'll enjoy it.For Trails fans:Fun game, but its absolutely not the same kind of experience you would get from the other 10 Trails games that have been localized as of this writing. Not only that, and I dont mean this to be condescending, but anyone who has played those games know how wild the plot can get. This game definitely does not hit that (incredibly high) story standard, but its still alright. It's not relevant to any of the plot lines going on in Trails however (it mentions some things in "The Empire" and its extremely vague). Frankly, even if it becomes relevant at some point via ret-con in a future game, I just dont see it being something that is a must-play entry to know whats going on.Nayuta has the great music you can expect from the Sky or Crossbell games though, and like I said in the other sections I very much think the game is worth playing. Just don't go trying to hold off on playing any other entries in the series to play this first like its mandated, it absolutely isn't. Play it as a fun, less-ambitious action RPG with the Falcom incredible music you know, and you wont be disappointed.OVERALL: Nayuta Boundless Trails is a solid game! I enjoyed my time with it overall, despite the couple quirks it has (none of which have to do with the port, which is excellent). I don't recommend 100% completing every level and quest the game has to offer unless you're a hardcore completionist willing to also play new game +, as the grind will disenchant you from the rest of the experience. The story does have a few unexpected turns here and there, so if you can look past the very simplistic dialogue there's some cool parts for sure. Other than that, definitely a fun game worth its asking price!

_childDocuments_.review: The Legend of Nayuta: Boundless trails was truly a surprise of a treat to play, it had a mix of the more classic YS style of visuals in some regards with the models mixed with the more recent ones in terms of gameplay, between the story and the gameplay it has that Falcom quality and it literally brings joy to my heart that I got to play this, for an action game it has a lot and is a decent length at that, you're in for a fun time if ya play and even more content opens up on NG+ so it's well worth a second round at that dood.Okay on to the meat of the review as I usually do, so the game focuses on the adventures of a young man named Nayuta on summer holiday/vacation back at his home town with his best friend Cygna who open up a handyman business, from there things get crazy and escalate in some real fun ways and it just keeps going I'll say that much dood!The game starts off basic, you have a four hit combo, a jump and a dodge but as the game goes on it expands on that heavily, you have a choice between one handed or two handed weapons too at that, the only benefits being the heavy weapon is stronger but much slower and the one handed is faster, both work well enough though dood.You have two things to do in the game, first off you can do sidequests for the handyman business, this nets you various things that you will really want and then of course there will be stages to play, they are your typical affair but you also have stars for each stage, these both work as markers of completion for items, gems and stage mission and for collecting enough you can trigger an event somewhere (as to not spoil lol) that will let you learn more skills so it's insanely worth it! They can be a hassle here and there but what's a reward without the challenge dood!!The games not super hard and has enough mechanics that if you use them well you'll do great, the music is outstanding, in fact some of Falcoms in house teams best work in my eyes (and ears) it made the levels and game itself a real extra good time and it really was for sure, even equipment changes on Nayuta for some great visual differences and the game looks great with the better textures, which are off by default mind you so feel free to make sure to turn that on when ya start dood. (Honestly I appreciate that, not everyone has a crazy powerful rig that can start a game at max settings without crashing, my first laptop suffered hard back in the day x.x)So yeah all in all the games stellar, it's not like the most amazing modern day visual spectacular that a lot of games are but the heart and gameplay are easily there and it still looks great despite that for it's style, what's more although Falcom stated otherwise there are many things I feel could easily connect to this game and the legend of heroes series so have fun with that if you're as big a fan of the series as I and many others are connecting all these things that are apparently not connected dood! _childDocuments_.review: This is a good game from Falcom and a good option if you want something different than the mainline Trails games or Ys to play in between. It's a nice change of pace while still keeping the usual Falcom vibes. Even if you're not into Falcom games, Nayuta is a good spin off game totally unrelated to the Trails series.The story is short and can be beaten in about 16 to 18 hours without rushing anything and the concepts are relatively simple without much complexity. This game doesn't try even one bit to connect to mainline Trails games and doesn't even tease the player about it being related in some way, despite the main protagonist surname being Herschel (same as Towa), but that has happened in Tokyo Xanadu too. All relations and connections are completely up to the player and the community to build theories about the game's world and I will discuss some elements later on this review in spoiler tagged lines.The concepts about climate change and changing the seasons to change the stages in the same location was very interesting and definitely added some replayability to the game. I liked how the game was designed around a 2D and 3D camera hybrid platforming with hack n' slash gameplay that reminds a lot of these old platforming games from the PS2 and PSP era, which are kinda rare these days. It feels almost like a simpler version of Ys Seven combat mixed with a little bit of Trails aesthetics. Combat and progression are all very simple, but fun. I recommend playing this slowly as a side game.The PC Port is also excellent, made by the legendary Durante. Since it's an old PSP game running on modern hardware, no one should have performance issues. I played this perfectly on my hardware without any issues, and I must say I was impressed by the remastered assets. Text looks very clear, the new 2D assets and artwork are high resolution and the 3D textures in HQ actually look really good, definitely way better than running from an emulator.There aren't really any negatives I can think of but there are two things that bothered me during the playthrough. The first is the protagonist Nayuta himself which is very childish and doesn't have a strong and concrete reason behind him to do whatever he is doing and defying the enemies and the People of Mythos. It's basically surfing over protagonists power and the power of friendship thing lolThe second is how the story progresses. It has some development as you go, but it's basically do the same thing 4 times in different regions and then do the same thing 4 times again in another different region.It would've been better if the story had more complexity and the progression had more varied things, but it's completely fine as a side game and limited by the old hardware it was originally made.It's a good game and recommended as a side game, especially if you are a Falcom fan. The price is right for what it delivers.Now, the real reason why one would play Nayuta is to try to find if there are any connections to the mainline Trails games, and there are definitely some stuff that we can make theories and here's some stuff I've been thinking (spoilers up to Kuro no Kiseki II):

_childDocuments_.review: So, I knew going into this that this was one of my favorite games of all time. I've played through the PSP version to 100% completion about a half dozen times, I was a minor contributor to the fan translation of the game on that system (just contributed character and place names, really), and I was fully glad to do another 2 playthroughs to get all the achievements again.Now, I'm not blind to the flaws of this game. The highest difficulty (that you unlock after beating the game once) is honestly just not fun for about 30% of the fights in the game. Gear Hold is frequently infuriating, causing jumps to fail after releasing with obnoxious frequency. A couple of the bosses in the game are... not great (looking at you, Armadaries).That being said, taken as a complete package? This game is absolutely worth the money. There's a load of incredibly fun stages to play through, and most of the bosses are quite enjoyable to fight. The combat and movement feels good most of the time, magic is varied and interesting, the world is compact but interesting, and the story, while not groundbreaking, is still pretty fun. Also, this being a Falcom game, the soundtrack absolutely slays.Even better, the game actually gets more fun to play as you go. As you unlock new abilities, your moveset really opens up. Gear Drive, in particular, is a joy to use both to cruise around stages and bully enemies. But the progression doesn't end at the end of the game. New game+ adds a handful of quests to the first 5 chapters of the game, an additional tier of equipment, and most importantly, unlockables that really enhance the game, using points gained from achievements.These unlockables are huge. The biggest ones are an additional season for each of the first four areas, for a total of 12 new stages. You'll also be able to increase both Nayuta's level cap, as well as the magic level cap. Perhaps best of all is decreasing the craft gauge cost for your Gear moves, eventually making them free. Being able to Gear Shield for free, or Gear Buster at will, or Gear Drive through an entire stage? All feel amazing.This game is definitely worth your time, attention, and money, even at full price. The port is solid, with only a couple of minor translation errors I noticed. Plays great on Steam Deck too. If you love action games, particularly ones by Falcom, this is a must play.
