_childDocuments_.review: After playing this for 200 hours!? I gotta say it's hard not to suggest the game XD but seriously, Trails into Reverie was a hecking blast, it took all the mechanics the games had up to this point and ramped them up to fun levels, in fact fixing certain issues they had in cold steel IV while also improving on existing mechanics allowing you to build what I will frankly refer to as literal Gods you can play as, to top it off there are like 50-51 characters in the game which is awesome as heck, how and why? Yeah not gonna spoil that, all I can say in the short here is the game is stellar with an interesting story to it and of course has the lovable characters we've all come to know dood.Okay still there? Cool time for the long part of the review! So to start I will go with the one glaring thing that may bother people, especially considering how the prior games worked and that's how linear it is in this instalment but it works for what they are going with here and frankly is a nice change of pace considering the games are usually both vast and yet typically set in the exact same places with a few additions throughout each series of games and has a little something (which is really a big something) that makes up for that as time goes on, basically it all works out in the end and feels right dood.Gameplay is the usual affair as CSIV but as I mentioned they fixed a few things, I'll say this much, they made things like orders and burst attacks much more viable and that was by adding a whole new, amazingly great mechanic on top that really ups the strategy of the game, in fact late game with the right combinations it frankly breaks the game turning most fights into a breeze at pretty much no cost and it feels great dood.Mini games! How can I not mention them, the glorious glorious mini ga-*vomits* sorry I couldn't keep that up, now granted like before it's got the same mini games but with a liiittle more to it as they usually do but they've added a bunch too, some are honestly pretty fun! Others maybe a little less so but if you're a mini game enthusiast then holy heck you'll be right at home unlike me! And do note none of these are bad exactly, even if I have my personal gripes about them, I just wanna play the actual game and not feel forced into playing for really reaaaally good rewards dood.Another thing they have improved is the master quartz, besides having more than there are even characters to choose from, they now go all the way to level 15!! Allowing you to make the effects on them stronger than ever and varying your strategies even further!! There are even new Quartz and accessories that will again make your characters just feel cheaty XD but in a fun way dood!The game has a heck load of costumes to it too, sadly not every character has them which is a darn shame but makes sense considering the insane roster and a butt load of accessories (the visual kind not equipment) for every character too dood.Overall the game does so much right, so soooo much right, some things I can't even mention because it becomes borderline spoiler if not right out spoiler, although I know that the best aspect of it is something that they can't really take into the next game sadly unless they did then well...dang I'm excited to get to it! Either way though there's so much content and stuff you can do along with copious amounts of lore and a maaaassive reveal once you get through it all, it's just a fun time dood.Thank you for reading and hopefully you all enjoy this game as much as I did if you get it dood! ^-^7

_childDocuments_.review: Hajimari no Kiseki is the perfect conclusion to the greatest saga in fiction. To describe it I would say Hajimari is much like that perfect, light, fluffy dessert following an incredibly grand meal, that warm cup of coffee accompanying a quiet and peaceful morning, that beautiful cascade of twilight colors in the afternoon sky you witness following a fulfilling day. It's that seemingly fleeting but perfect moment where you stop, take everything in and wish so sincerely, "I want this moment to last forever." Genuinely, this game takes everything that makes this series what it is and puts it together into one grand farewell that leaves you melancholic but prepared for the next stage in this wondrous story. Hajimari no Kiseki is a love letter to its fans and the series itself, living up to its title of "festival game" and sincerely celebrating this long beautiful journey in a way that is unforgettable. Falcom continues to deliver an incredibly charming and emotional experience by taking Rean, Lloyd and C's stories and weaving together a brilliant narrative of conquering oneself and coming to terms with your past. It is the ultimate exploration of regret, acceptance and moving onward. It is the ultimate application of the infamous trope of "facing oneself" which fully brings to closure many characters stories. I would even go so far as to say the Sen saga would be incomplete without this masterfully crafted adventure. This does not even begin to touch upon the perfected game play, the incredibly fun time sink of the mini rogue-like post game Infinity Corridor and the myriad other additional game play additions that will keep you returning to this game. Every single decision between the various episodes, mini games, costumes, absolutely crazy equipment, boss rush and so much more is designed to give you a sandbox to explore as much of what was introduced within the last nine games. To say I have spent hundreds if not thousands of hours within this particular game alone would be an understatement. It is hard to think of fault for any aspect of this particular experience simply because each feature, story moment, character is crafted with so much love and adoration you can't help but go, "I love this series."And.. I often regard Hajimari no Kiseki as my "favorite Kiseki game" and will continue to do so. This is NOT to say the previous nine games mean anything less to me. Often times, I find many assume this very notion. This is false. However, it is to say that this game embodies such a pure and simple theme, one that I believe is best represented by the credits theme, "Kiseki's Journey". This game brings to life the idea of "our journey to this point and our journey beyond". Playing this game when it released in 2020 struck me incredibly hard. My journey began almost seven years prior to Hajimari's release and through that time I watched my favorite characters laugh, cry, smile and experience, love, joy, sorrow, despair, hope, sadness, grief, death, anguish, regret, relief, pure happiness and be brought to the very depths of despair and learn to conquer their demons. And their very journey was mirrored by my own. While fictional worlds, characters and events will remain just that...fictional, I grew up alongside these characters. And I have grown attached to them in a way that I believe only those who have experienced this series much like me will understand. It has been.. a very long journey. And every event, every character arc, every OST, every moment in Hajimari no Kiseki is delivered with some form of finality that can only make me recall all those hard days, those sad days, those lonely days but also those happy days, those grateful days, those beautiful days. It really was a journey to that point in my life when I first played this game and now when I revisit Hajimari while writing this review. I can pinpoint the exact moments I went through some monumental moment in my own life's journey by relating to this franchise's release dates, my own playthroughs or even moments with the few friends I've made through this franchise. This series is fundamental to a core part of who I am today. To them, to me, to this game and this series, thank you for this journey. It has been an incredibly long one but one that I will never forget. I am incredibly grateful that the entire cast was able to come to terms with their journey's as we all look forward to their, and our own, journey beyond. This game truly brings to conclusion the greatest saga in fiction and I look ever forward to continue growing alongside this cast, world and characters I love. To Sora no Kiseki, to Zero no Kiseki, to Ao no Kiseki, to Sen no Kiseki-thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to give a little background on this, I have already played all games up to Kuro no Kiseki II. I play these games in Japanese on console at launch and then replay them on PC when the English version releases, usually 3 years later.I think if anyone has reached this far into the franchise, there's no need for a review talking about why you should play the series or how the game works. It's core mechanics is pretty much the same as CS4.Trails into Reverie is a game that could only be possible due to everything the series has been building up to now. 10 games on the line with interconnected stories across almost 20 years. Trails into Reverie brings everyone, since the first game, marking a turning point for the series. A final chapter, a departure from Western Zemuria before we go to Calvard and begin a new arc and move to a new era for the series.This game requires the player to have played all games up to it and all the knowledge and attachment to the characters in order to fully enjoy Reverie. It brings a closure to Rean and Lloyd stories while also adding a new story line of a character named C.This game actually acts more like a last chance to revisit Erebonia and Crossbell and play with your favorite characters rather than actually setting the ground into Calvard territory (we don't go to Calvard in this game). And everyone is in the game, more than 50 characters to play.The story in this game is on the shorter side (takes around 50 hours to beat) but it was well paced without padding. It feels more like a spin-off story in Crossbell.Reverie is actually a new story that feels contained within itself, it begins and ends within itself. Trails into Reverie did not bring any answers of the various questions and mysteries raised in the end of CS4 and did not bring us into Calvard territory but it does give 3 episodes that explain a little bit about what's next for Calvard regarding some of the characters and 1 episode that teases a little bit about Ouroboros Final Plan and Grandmaster.Reverie is really a "last chance" game to reuse all assets of the previous games before diving into a new era of the series. At least for now when finishing the game, maybe it will pay off in the future Kuro games when the consequences of what happened here starts to appear in the future (I already know the answer, just teasing and keeping spoiler free for readers lol)Despite not bringing much answers about the previous game or foreshadowing the next one, it was really great to play with the 3 protagonists and change between them and the story was interesting.As for the Reverie corridor, it is pretty much an enhanced version of what we got in CS2 and where the padding content is, with a lot of enemies, trials, minigames, etc... It has a arcade feel to it, where you can choose anyone you want and defeat a bunch of enemies to reach higher floors and unlock stuff. I will be honest that I'm not a big fan of these corridors in Trails games because they feel very repetitive without adding much significant progress to the lore. Thankfully the distribution between when each floor is unlocked and the main story progression is good.The insane amount of characters available to play can be hard to manage. It's good that everyone is in the game and you can play with your favorites, but managing equipment and quartz for everyone is hell and XP is not shared between them, so I recommend just picking up a few characters including the main ones from the main story and invest in them.Zero issues with the PC Port. It ran perfectly at 1440p on a RTX 2060 Super. Thanks to the legendary Durante for the PC port.Soundtrack in this game is good but still quite weak and forgettable overall compared to what Falcom used to deliver in the past. A few tracks are excellent, but the soundtrack as whole is average.Trails into Reverie is a good game, by reaching this far into the franchise I think playing it is an obvious choice. However it is not one of my favorites of the franchise since it not bring a lot of answers raised in CS4 and barely showed anything about Calvard or Ouroboros. Also not a big fan of the Corridor structure and character bloat.The story is like a spin-off standalone (for now), but it is interesting with good pacing and the gameplay is very fun and polished.I'd put Reverie right into the middle of the series rank (for now). Not one of the top games but definitely not on the bottom. This game, like Sky the 3rd, may get better over time, as we learn more about the series lore and discover that many things that appear in this game actually may have connections to the events in future games.

_childDocuments_.review: Trails Into Reverie truly is the neat little bow to wrap up both the Crossbell and Cold Steel sagas into one majestic and emotional conclusion. But it is one to be opened once all the previous trails have been traversed, something that shouldn't be a problem for most veteran players that have undertaken this odyssey. THE GOOD:The gameplay has been perfected, with over 40 playable characters and a nearly limitless amount of possible broken builds to overcome the barriers in your way. The music is still a banger like always, with geniuses like Mitsuo Singa and Yukihiro Jindo on the team. And the story, which spans across 3 routes, is masterfully executed. Trails into Reverie truly is the greatest entry thus far when taking everything I've said into account.THE BAD:Unfortunately, I can't end this review without mentioning the several technical screw-ups which fall into NIS America. From the LE preorders having all those delivery issues, the numerous bugs at release (which have been patched for the most part), and the many many typos, item and/or craft description errors, and downright wrong names in certain dialogues (which haven't been patched as of the time I'm writing this review, and I doubt they will.) The Quality Assurance truly left more to be desired, and I hope they can reflect and improve for the Kuro release so this doesn't happen again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game ties all the lose ends left in the Erebonia and Crossbell arcs. The story is the epilogue revolving around the aftermath of both arcs and puts them together for heartfelt send of for characters we connected with over MANY games. It also serves as a mini prologue for the Kuro series, introducing characters that are playable in said games. If you are left with more questions after finishing the previous games then playing this game gives you all the answers desired. THE GOOD:- Combat has an added mechanic that adds more strategic freedom to the player as well as giving a previous mechanic the attention needed to be worth using often. The system has been refined since the first game into a highly polished experience, any more additions would tip the balance into unnecessary bloat. - Playable characters are not temporary like they were in previous games, they do swap out in the main story but are still viable for play in other ways. This makes team building and character optimisation very fun if you enjoy theory crafting.- End game is a first for the series (i think) and is done fairly well for players who want to either watch background story or grind for the best items in the game. Both add a decent amount of time to the unusually short story.- Cut scenes are slightly improved in terms of camera movement and animation but watching combat scenes instead of playing through them at times was enjoyable.- Nightmare difficulty has more tactically interesting bosses than CS4 did. I am glad they also added a tougher mode for New game+ because Min Maxed characters are very powerful and the added difficulty makes enemies especially bosses deadly.THE BAD:- Pacing in this game is HORRIBLE. It still suffers from the low starts and high ends pacing this franchise repeats for nearly every game. However since there are 3 routes in this game players must endure this pacing trend for 3x longer which made me restless at the start where 80% of the dialogue feels like filler before a short combat section. Even when the story starts to pick up, the completion of one route means starting another route and going through the same pattern.- Plot in this game strays away from the high fantasy lore the previous games tend to build to. This caught me by surprise and was on the fence if this new direction (being so relatable to our reality) make this world more interesting or not. From the little i have seen from the kuro series, orbal technology is a main presence in the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't made much progress but as a hardcore Legend of Heroes fan, no way I going to leave a negative review unless game is unplayable. I recommend waiting a short while and keep eye out for any patch notes if they come our way before picking this game up and also, you want to get the most out of this game, suggest playing through Zero, Azure, all cold steels at the least but most enjoyment comes from playing Trails in Sky saga first, then zero/azure, then finishing it off with all the cold steel games before tackling this.  Also doing this gives this game time to get bug fixes and hopefully they come out soon or the review scores going to plummet.I'm keeping positive review for now, but it will be changed if they don't fix anything after some time has passed.  I have faith in the devs and I got a feeling the localization team was overwhelmed by deadlines since legend of hero games are known for having ton of text to read.  For that reason, I be happy to give them time to work on patches and not complain any further for now.Review will be updated at a later time.First Review Update:  Good news, they were quick to fix the largest bug in the game that broke link attacks and since they done it so quickly, I am excited and hopeful for upcoming fixes from the smaller issues and fortunately are aware and responsive to players. _childDocuments_.review: The finale to Librel, Crossbell and Erebonia Saga. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this was so long. I’m left defeated after knowing that I caught up to every English version of the games so far. ♥♥♥♥ got me tearing a bit in some scenes…. (Big Spoilers Warning)This is the tenth installment of the Legend of Heroes, and I recommend for those who want to enter this game to follow the story in order: This is the finale so it makes sense to do so.Trail in the Sky FC,Trail in the Sky SC,Trail in the Sky the 3rd,Trails from Zero,Trails to Azure,Trails of Cold Steel 1,Trails of Cold Steel 2,Trails of Cold Steel 3,Trails of Cold Steel 4.There is one thing you need to know from Trail of Cold Steel 4. And that is reading the three and nine book series. This is the backstory of both Swin and Nadia which would rarely be explained in the game (Kinda stupid)The story takes on 3 main protagonists. Lloyd, Rean and the mysterious C. The story begins on Crossbell Independence Day. Until it is interrupted by Rufus Albarea, who broke out of prison to revolt against independence. The SSS loses the fight and are forced to reclaim their land again.  Rean's story will connect with Lloyds except it begins with the investigation into the disappearance of Olivert and Scherazard. As they deal with the mysterious C message of capturing them. C story is centred around a doll named Lapis, who becomes a driving force in the story. Alongside new characters like Swin and Nadia, two escaped assassins from an organization called Garden. In their attempt to uncover the overall truth. This game follows the purpose of who you are, what you are doing this for and goals that ain’t really needed to explain. The antagonists were pretty lacklustre in my opinion but what made the game positive for me was that C is an amazing protagonist in my eyes. C and Lapis has been my favourite duo interaction since Lloyd and Kea and Rean and Altina. The plot twist in this game is something else, some amazing, some really random. But I enjoyed it. C is just Lelouch with friends lmao and I love it.Camera angles, cinematic and cut scenes are so much better in this game. Their new engine was used here and it really shows, it was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. There was dialogue with some goated camera angles that I could greatly appreciate and the action scenes were saucy af. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ splendid work on this game, it caught me off guard and it was sick af. They also played around with CG animation which is a new delight to the series. I am looking forward to the future of Legend of Heroes.The character roster is even bigger in this game. Like 51 characters to play through (There are so many characters and some very unexpected ones too) and the orbment got a massive upgrade. There is some strong af quartz this time and sub master quartz restrictions are lesser in this game which is great. The one thing I want to talk about is the united front. A new mechanic that is really really broken. I don’t wanna go too much into it except at delay with that and status ailment about to be a field day. Evasion builds are even broken in this game which is funny and master quartz combos are broken when they are stacked.When I said “Bring back the old mechanic” from my TOCS 4 review. I didn’t mean, let’s bring it back and break the game. They do some real ♥♥♥♥ lol. Everything is back. Brave orders, burst, etc. And the introduction of tag-along, reverie, etc. But too much info and it is a spoiler lol.There is a new difficulty called Abyss mode which was designed to be soul punishing. Enemies have like 4 times your average speed and they hit for one shot the majority of the time. It gets easier later on, the beginning is so brutal, fights took a long time to end out. ♥♥♥♥ was cool and fun though lol. 10 / 10 recommendation. Extra RP point requirements in battles are still there except less prominent so thank you Falcom.Music is lacking as usual. TOCS 4 had better music, this game didn’t have much great music until the end. The battle theme is so boring, I wish they brought back the spark from older games and just went ham on it. The music is a big part of the game and to see it end the three main sagas off with lacklustre music is disappointing. I am looking towards the next games to be even better on this aspect of the game cause I miss it a lot. Despite that I did like two tracksSpecifically Entrusting Kindred to the Future. That track was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good during the scenes, it got me hyped, sad and feeling all types of motivation emotions.There isn’t much side-quest, except it’s substituted with the Reverie Corridor. It’s like Phantasma from trail in the sky 3rd but the sub story is lacking a bit. Master mission is your way of earning rewards and rp. You can play mini-games like pom party, vantage master, (vr mode beach event………..) etc. You unlock characters while just like Phantasma, you can see the behind the scenes of certain characters and what happened between TOCS 4 and Trails into Reverie. You go through floors and dungeons to uncover the truth. The daydream event are really fun and nice to watch though (Some of them are spoilers for the next game: Post game content) I do recommend doing post game content as well Collectables are the same. Get the fishing, get the books, get the recipes, etc. The standard stuff, there isn’t any gifting system in this game which is pretty sad. And there is no bonding system in this game so you are pretty much in it for the story with growth of specific characters.I recommend this game to end the saga off. It isn’t in my top 5 favourite trails games so far but it did give me a bit of satisfaction. I am more sad that the saga has ended and we have to say goodbye to Rean, Lloyd and C for now. I am at the end of the road. But I still got the next game to play. I have begun my new journey over in Calvard where we will find our next protagonist of the series. And finally exploring the highly anticipated region after so long of knowledge and lore. I will see you all over in the next upcoming Legend of Heroes game:THE LEGEND OF HEROES: TRAILS TO DAYBREAKKKKK!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Another excellent entry in the long running franchise the legend of heroes. before anyone asks. YES PLAY THESE GAMES IN THE PROPER ORDER. Regardless of what area the games take place in you'd be missing out on a lot of lore character and world building if you don't. It is a commitment so strap in for a wild ride.Now for the game play if you've played them all up to this point then eveything is pretty much the same accept now you are armed with the arcus 2 ! With this upgrade you now have the option for full on team attacks up to 8 characters at once yes i said 8.... back to that in a bit Additionally you have a cool new options allowing you to group attack with a regular attack arts attacks or you can heal your self as long as  you have charges gem filled up. These either fill up over time while you are walking on the field or every turn you take. I like this as it adds another layer of strategy on an already good battle system. You can still link up with other characters providing them with back up support abilities which trigger at random that hasn't changed. It's been awhile since i played cold steel 4 but the timeline also remains largely the same you got the turn order on one side of the screen and your hp / ep status on the other.  It's critical to pay attention to the time line because the battle buffs and debuffs are back. If an enemy is in line to get a buff status you can either impede it or use a s.craft move to give it to your self or out right cancle it.there is  a TON of playable characters in this game every character from all the past games is basically playable as either an attacker or a supporter given you plenty of options to mix and match a grand total of at least 40 characters where ready to me by the end. You can have up to 8 in battle 4 attacking and 4 ready to sub in.

_childDocuments_.review: A fitting bookend to the whole franchise up to this point. This one involves most characters from the Sky, Crossbell and Cold Steel arcs, while introducing a few new characters and ideas that are presumably intended to set up the next story arc. To me, the whole Reverie Garden/Corridor and the Daydreams made this game feel like Trails in the Sky the Third Part 2, which is not a bad thing because they add conrtext and further develop characters and their relationships, and you get to see and play as many of the extended cast from the whole franchise like in Sky 3.I did enjoy the way the three simultaneous story paths weave into each other, and when the real identity of the new C who leads the team from the third path was revealed I was sincerely surprised because I did not expect him to be that character at all. My only complaint is that, after all that has happened in the Crossbell and Cold Steel arcs, having to yet again fight off an occupying force refusing to let Crossbell live in peace made me as a player feel kind of like Juna says she feels. Just leave this freaking place alone, already. Now, on to Daybreak.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t know why I took so long to write something about this game, maybe I just wanted to let it fully sink in, but I think it is finally time to buckle up and get the job done.No spoilers as always haha.Trails into Reverie is a game with a lot to live up to, it's a game that was revered as something special in this series since the time of its original japanese release, and did it manage to? In my opinion, yes, above and beyond. This game was a return to form for the series in a lot of ways and really rekindled my love and enthusiasm for the series.Tying up a lot of loose ends from both Crossbell and Cold Steel (much like how the 3rd was for Sky) while serving as a bridge to the Calvard arc, Reverie stands strong as the 10th entry in the series.The route system is something I was really interested in and it delivered, it’s a great way to handle a game with such a massive cast while giving the characters natural reasons and motives for being where they are, also allowing for some of the best and most engaging pace I’ve seen in the series.While the core gameplay is very much the same as Cold Steel, what makes this game shine is the amount of options and characters you have to mess around, the Corridor is a playground of endless possibilities where you can spend hours upon hours just trying builds, reading side stories or playing minigames.On a technical side, besides some bugs from release that are now fixed, Durante’s port is great as always.This game was a really special experience, it’s everything I could have wanted from the final chapter of the first half of the series and a send off to both Crossbell and Erebonia, it was a labor of love and it shows in every aspect. The Trails series have been with me thought some of the best and worst times of my life now, it has been almost 3 years since I played FC for the first time, the ride had some of the biggest highs I’ve ever experienced in my life, but also quite a few lows, but even so I can confidently say that this is my favorite series in anything, and I will forever treasure the wonderful experience I had with this series.Personal feelings aside, the bottom line is that this is a great game haha, one that is definitely worth your time.Thank you Falcom for creating this series, thank you xseed for pioneering the series in the west, thank you Geofront for all the effort in making it whole and thank you NISA for carrying the torch.See you all beyond the reverie.

The mysteries are intriguing and all 3 protagonists get very satisfying conclusions to their character arcs. The new characters introduced are also incredibly likeable. (And be sure to read the in-universe book , accessible from the Backstory page on the main menu before getting into the game itself. Trust me, it'll pay off.)Sidequests are kept to a minimum, with the game feeling a lot like Sky the 3rd in both progression and content. Whether this is a positive or a negative will depend on the person, but as for me, it's made the game feel a lot more focused and the story's pacing is excellent.But for real, if you're a Trails fan, chances are Reverie will not disappoint. I personally consider it to be the 4th best game in the series (in other words it's amazing) and it made me excited for the series' future after Cold Steel 4 left a bad taste in my mouth. It's not without its hiccups (Lloyd Act 1 and how the postgame is structured come to mind), but it's overall a fantastic addition to the series, and I can't wait for Kuro's official announcement (even though the NISA store page is already up.)

Besides the main story, there is a HUGE GAMEPLAY AREA that is revealed quite early but not fully accessible until the end of the story. THE REVERIE CORRIDOR. _childDocuments_.review: This is basically part V of the Erebonia arc of Trails.  Or part III of Crossbell.  It serves as both, to wrap up events in that parts of Zemuria and in post game has a few things to serve as a preview of the Calvard arc.  So how is it?The game play is the final evolution of the Cold Steel formula, familiar, but more of everything.  More master quartz, more characters, more options for what to do with them, and more ways to break the game with brutally overpowered characters, which frankly, is good.  These (with a few exceptions) are not new characters and certainly none are kids just starting out.  By now these characters are seasoned pros, monsters in their own right, so it's only fair that if you put in some work you make them act the part.  On the other hand, this does mean the difficulty isn't huge.  Granted you can set it high with nightmare or the new Abyss difficulty, but even then, you can break the game and beat those with the right setups.Enjoy it while you can, Calvard goes to all new sorts of setups, no more master quartz, no more  Arcus, so if you like the system, make the most of its swan song.  If you don't, well, like I said, Daybreak goes in new directions with its shard system.It's also your last chance to spend time with most of the characters.  Some will appear in Calvard, but most are just a mention, so for a lot of the characters you've known for hundreds of hours, this is the last time they'll star in a game like this.  And if you haven't spent hundreds of hours with them, why are you here?  Trails is a terrible franchise to play out of order.  Don't do it.  Pick an arc and play from the start of it (or from the start of all of them, Trails in the Sky).The story's told in three parallel tracks, Rean, Lloyd and someone named C.  It's not bad, a little over the top and a few moments that need some suspension of disbelief, but it works.  I don't know that it's the peak of Falcom games, but I enjoyed it.  Certainly it did the job, kept me interested and helped bring the story of the characters to a close (at least for now, since a few games from now, who knows who will show up again.)There's a lot to do, especially post game if you want to max all the characters, which takes some dedication, but is doable (you can just run the characters you love setup how you want and have 4 along for the ride who don't fight, just leech xp.)  So if you really go for everything your playtime will get up there.  I maxed all the characters on a normal difficulty run and came in at 179 hours to do it all, though if you just want to win you can easily do it in about half that.I really did enjoy the game, and despite a few over the top moments in the story, I enjoyed every minute of it.  By now it's a world and characters I know quite well, and one last chance to see and spend time with them all was great.  But if you're looking at this, you know the franchise, this doesn't break the mold, if you love it, go play it.  If you don't love the Trails formula, this won't be the game to change your mind.  So really, you know what's here, you should know you either love Falcom games or you don't.  So get to it already.

_childDocuments_.review: BEFORE REVIEWING:No, you cannot start with Reverie. Let's just get that out of the way. Now, to fully enjoy Trails you have to start at Trails in the Sky FC/Trails in the Sky. As this game is a capstone for both the Erebonia arc and the Crossbell arc. So please, go and play from the very beginning of the series to properly enjoy this game and what it has to offer. Also this review is primarily targeted at the main story, not the extra in-game content you're able to do nor is it a review for the novel/short story that comes with the Deluxe Edition of the game.Review:This game was a lot of fun, it was a pretty great way to end both of the Erebonian arcs and the Crossbellan arcs. I know a portion of the community doesn't like the Cold Steel/Erebonian arc, but personally it's one of my favorites and Rean is definitely my favorite MC even if it's just by a tiny bit (All the MCs for each arc are just great). The fact that Trails into Reverie splits the game's story into three different paths you can follow and keeps them all sync up with each other is a really interesting approach. It lets you see multiple sides of the same story. The Reverie Corridor is honestly a lot of fun as well, and it adds so much replayability to the game. You can compare this game to being similar to Trails in the Sky the 3rd, but the majority of it adds a fresh twist onto the concepts from that game.Now, for the specifics of each part of the game. The story itself is really interesting and like previously stated is split up into three different "Trails". These "trails" are Rean, Lloyd, and the enigmatic "C", each with their own perspective of the events that happen in the main story. These events initially start out pretty separate from each other, however, over time they start to merge into one, with interactions between each MC's part being scattered throughout. The general story was great and had a lot of twists that I genuinely didn't expect to happen. They were also all particularly well done, with no one twist or no one aspect of the story being unwanted to me. This is especially true as you start to uncover the truth behind what is happening in the story and going over concepts that are pretty new to the series overall. As you would expect with any trails game, the emotional aspect of the story is on par with previous entries, making you experience a wide range of emotions while playing. Main story aside, there are also mini side stories you can go through in the Reverie Corridor as well that expand on certain groups of characters during the events of Trails into Reverie. Think of this like the doors from Trails in the Sky the 3rd, but without needing specific characters to view them. Gameplay wise, it's pretty much the same as you would expect coming from Cold Steel. The gameplay in battle is a lot of fun, very fluid, and has a lot more aspects that you would expect this late into the series. Although, they added a new aspect to combat which is personally a lot of fun to use. That system being the United Front system. You can either use it to heal, attack with regular attacks, or attack with arts. This has saved me quite a bit of work when it comes to healing or defeating enemies as it either makes quick work of mobs with a large group or gives you a good amount of healing when you need it. Of course, this changes as you start to enhance this system within the Reverie Corridor. Overall, the new battle system that was introduced in Cold Steel 3 & 4 continues to be very satisfying to play with.Regarding the characters themselves, they continue to expand upon previously introduced characters from the Crossbell and Erebonia arc and showcase new characters that have been brought into the series via C's group. The previously established characters continue being the great characters you know and love, with the mini stories I mentioned before giving more background into the daily lives of your favorite Erebonians and Crossbellans. However, when it comes to C's group, I am a bit more mixed on. I love Lapis and Nadia, they're a lot of fun personality wise and their backstories are pretty interesting. Both of them are also very fun to play as well, especially Lapis. C is a good character, with the end of the story definitely making me like him a bit more than I originally did. However, when it comes to Swin, I just genuinely do not like him. He's just kind of bland and isn't really a great character period. Sure, his skills are pretty interesting, but he's easily replaced by any of the other established characters or even characters that are in his group. He's probably one of the main reasons why I didn't enjoy the C side as much as I did someone like Rean's side. Not saying that C's side was awful, it was still pretty good, but it just didn't feel as good as playing through Rean's story or Lloyd's story (though I am biased towards Rean because of him being my favorite MC). Though I am also sad that the romance option from CS4 didn't have much of an impact on Rean's side, with the exception of a few moments. I would have loved to seen some really adorable moments between Rean and Towa.In terms of artstyle/animations/music, this game SLAPS SO HARD. The great artstyle from Cold Steel 3 and 4 is carried over into Reverie, with a lot of characters even getting new art to go along with this game. It's super high quality, even if I put the game up to 4k resolution. Then you have the animations, OH BOY THE ANIMATIONS. I don't know how, but the animations for this game are AMAZING. Everything is SO FLUID AND SMOOTH, I LOVE IT. CS4's animations were good, but Reverie's animations were just a whole different level of amazing for any game in the trails series so far. You can tell that Falcom put a lot of love into making each of them really high quality. To go along with the amazingly high quality animations, Falcom does it again and brings an absolute BANGER of an OST to this game. There was no song in this whole entire game (hell even the whole series) that wasn't a banger or that I didn't like. All the boss battle themes were spot on, and the emotional scene music was just right as well. This game's music is definitely something you will come back to just to jam out to.Overall, I would recommend this game at full or discounted price (like pretty much any other trails game I've reviewed so far, and probably will review in the future). The story adds a lot to and finishes off the Crossbell and Erebonia arcs of the overall trails narrative, just like how Trails in the Sky the 3rd finished off the narrative for Liberl's arc. The gameplay is satisfying as you'd expect this late into the series, the story is pretty great overall and explore some interesting new topics that the series hasn't gone over yet, and the characters are just as lovable as you'd expect (except you Swin, you can go sit in the corner). My only gripe would be that there wasn't enough Towa. Please Falcom give more Towa, she's such an amazing character and is probably my favorite character in any story I've went through. Additional note:Towa Herschel is best.

_childDocuments_.review: Review after 100% completion and 100% achievementsA wonderful experience and a great RPG.  But perhaps more importantly, it is an excellent conclusion to the previous Trails games while acting as a beginning for the next ones.  My second favorite of the ten Trails games.  It can be what you want it to be in so many ways and it does a lot of things right.It has a TON of optional content.  You'll see people who played around as much as I did who completed it and people who played less than a third of the amount I played who completed the main story.  Those are very different experiences.  The difficulty levels range from nearly complete cakewalk to actually challenging for veteran players in some parts.  There is English and Japanese voice acting, by a huge number of actors.  The controls are very customizable.  It is very player friendly overall.The main story starts as three storylines that later converge.  This is done exceptionally well.  At certain points, you'll have to pick another route to play for a bit.  This is so you're experiencing the same calendar dates for all routes around the same play time.  Sometimes the routes interact with each other in cool ways.  My favorite of the routes was C's route.  It takes a very philosophical approach to a lot of topics and was very interesting.  Rean's route is an interesting continuation of Trails of Cold Steel 4.If that were it, though, I wouldn't have liked the game nearly as much.  The optional content is what takes it to a very high level for me.  There is an extensive postgame section.  I actually liked the SSS-focused postgame story significantly more than Lloyd's route in the main game.  But the real treasure for me in the optional content are the so-called Daydreams.  These are short stories that generally continue or conclude smaller stories from earlier in the series.  There are a few that are more humorous than serious.  And there are some that kick off storylines that will be important going forward.  Almost all of them revolve around a small set of characters.  And many of them pack a great deal of emotional power for long-time fans of the series.  I loved a lot of the Daydreams.I also really liked the hilarious Magical Girl Alisa stories.  The enjoyable Vantage Masters makes a return, even including a part with a funny storyline at the end (Dojo).  There's also banana boat racing, watermelon splitting, fishing, mechanized/piloted action combat, Pom Pom Party, trivia, and more.  The optional dungeons are some of my favorite in the series - interesting challenges, interesting effects (like battles that have to be fought by people not in the active party), mini-missions with small goals to keep them interesting, special scenes with certain groups of characters, etc.  There are optional boss fights where you're forced to use certain characters.  There is really a TON of optional content.Most of the English voice acting was fantastic.  It is such a huge cast now that it is really impressive how many actors give great performances.  Lots of returning favorites.  And among the newcomers I especially loved the voices for Renne and Lapis.  I could listen to both of them all day.  The music is very well done and never got old.  I was a bit disappointed that there wasn't a standout vocal song this time.There were a few areas where the experience could have been better.  Lloyd's route in the main game is essentially "Crossbell is in trouble. Again."  It did not offer me what the other routes did, though it got better in the post-game content.  It felt like the game could have used another editing pass or more detail-oriented playtesters.  There are a bunch of lines or descriptions that are obviously incorrect.  It isn't a localization issue, it just seems like things that fans of the series and native English speakers would notice as being wrong.  The camera is a bit wonky, sometimes changing position on its own without any player input.  It was always quick to fix, but still annoying.The biggest negative was something that doesn't seem to affect all players, but definitely affected me.  During a scene transition (going to a new location, leaving a minigame, etc.), the loading process can hang.  The game continues running and sometimes the music continues, but nothing else ever happens.  The only choice is to close and re-open the game and load a recent save.  And sometimes this happened to me in places where there was no opportunity to create a manual save and the autosaves didn't work.  That was pretty frustrating.  It probably happened at least a dozen times during my playthrough.And on a slightly more humorous note, my complaints were that Kevin was present but never on-screen and we didn't progress much in the overarching storylines.Also, apparently I am Team Student Council by the very end.  I would never have expected that.

_childDocuments_.review: The best way to describe this game is Trails in the Sky: the 3rd done better. This game is brimming with content from the 3 concurrent main stories to the dungeon crawling Reverie Corridor, along with every mini-game and most mechanics from the rest of the series. It's a pleasant family reunion of characters and places from this nearly 20 year old series and I couldn't be happier with it. The only real critique I can muster is that with so much content there is bound to be some low points and occasionally I did notice some plot lines being retreads of the past games, which is a shame because the newest cast and their story is far and away the crown jewel of this game so far. Overall a solid addition to the franchise and a must play for anyone that loves the series!Edit: Finished the Series at almost 100 hours, game is one of the most content-rich Trails games to date. My feelings are roughly the same as they were when I originally made the review, with the addition that some side characters could have used more love and attention.

_childDocuments_.review: With Reverie ends the first half of the whole Trails series and in my opinion, it did a great job closing a lot of the remaining character arcs. When I started Reverie, my expectations for the story and characters were high since I had heard a lot of good things about them and well... I'm glad to say that they didn't disappoint in that aspect. In fact, from all the 3 routes C's route was the most fun because of the new 3 characters. What Reverie really shines at though is the Reverie Corridor which is kind of like a randomly generated dungeon where you can farm, fight bosses, recruit characters, watch episodes like in sky 3rd and play mini-games. I don’t want to say that much about the story to avoid spoilers but I will say that it does get somewhat ridiculous in its plot which... can vary from pretty cool to kind of stupid imo. Another problem that doesn't only effect Reverie but somewhat the entire series so far is Falcom, for some reason, rarely wants to go through with character deaths. By that, I mean letting one of the heroes or any important characters (that are NOT villains) be killed or stay dead. This problem already reached its peak in CS4 where they thought of all kinds of excuses for why character x didnt actually die or later gets revived and gets away with a little scar. I find it very unfortunate since the stakes could be so much higher if Falcom actually tried to commit to the deaths (or at least stopped with the fake outs). The soundtrack overall was ight with a few really good bangers.Overall despite me being a little negative towards the end of the review I still loved this game a lot. Aside from the few annoyances I had everything else ranged from good to peak so yeah I'm giving it a 9/10

In a world where most new pc games release completely broken and unoptimized, trails into reverie puts every so called "AAA" publisher to shame. You'd think having access to a way bigger budget would allow for better PC conversions right? Wrong, it's always the opposite as the PC platform is heavily disregarded by most publishers and developpers nowadays. _childDocuments_.review: Short Opinion:If you are true Kiseki fan(As I am, beaten everything from sora to hajimari at this point) and have anything even remotely resembling the brain - perhaps it would be worthwhile to consider skipping this game. It is a spit to fan's face as i see it, truly the pinnacle of bad writing, char developement and crisis of ideas. Just watch last three daydreams that connect this game to Kuro no Kiseki and go straight to it.Long opinion(SPOILER ALERT):You absolutely shouldn't introduce god-like enemies in the plot until you really know what you are doing. Many jrpgs suffer from that trope, but nevertheless. What you ABSOLUTELY ABSOLUTELY shouldn't do is putting pieces of previous games onto skeleton based on that kinda rotten plot and make MOST of the game consist of it, aiming to induce nostalgia or the same feelings these sequence of events made in the past.Unfortunately, I'm not joking - uut of three roots presented in the game only one is remotely interesting and mostly due to characters presented. Rean's root Is repeating itself from cold steel, and he is going through the same damned arc of having faith in those around him and problems with his head. But what they've done to Lloyd is even more disgusting - the overall plot at large and Lloyd root specifically is just a reskin for Azure no Kiseki + a bit of Sora the 3rd, but worse in every way possible. Nothing like down-to-earth history of a deeply broken man, wanting to suffer forever and eventually regaining humanity, nothing like star door 15, nothing like a complex story with political intrigue and rotten to the botton system in which crossbell was during Zero/Ao. Nothing remotely like this. All you get are standard "Let's belive in our frieds and ourselves", stries you already have seen in previous games and tonns of cheap fanservise that in most cases looks like a genuine spit in my face.Not every time - it was really heartwarming to see ol' folks from doentown district all around Crosbell as well as characters interactions with each other, but when they introduce damned Hospel from 2nd Sora only for one fight just to break it down and don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about the this that can possibly change ALL warfare in the world, cause now it doesn't require Aureole to work... It isn't fanservice, it's a piece of ♥♥♥♥ noone asked about, which rips you out of the immersion and comletely destroys the logic of the world. And unfortunately that's not the most hilarious moment of the game, throughout which you will destroy tanks by hand in a cutscene and beat the crap out of 7 divine knights merged together... also by hand. Just a quick reminder - at the end of CS1 you destroy basic panzer soldat by hand, but then another one with higher rank apperas and... it cast art and physic immunity on itself against you, but i guess it's a somewhat lost ancestral technology. The list of inconsiistencies goes on and on and on...The main conflict is awful as well - we literally have a machine that can forge literally everything including copying artifacts and predict the future as our enemy, albeit it doesn't and gets nerfed every time plot needs it. I was rather upset at the ending of Sora SC, when Weissman suddenly dot dumb, but still our "heroes" couldn't say nothing more reasonable than "what a monster", setting aside that his plan REALLY could get the things right, but this game... it's broken from the very beginning to the very end. After all nothing really have changed if the plot didn't happen. Yeah, we wouldn't had been introduced to Swin and Nadia, also the Rufus wouldn't have "died" in the end, but that's mostly it. When you really think about it, it is nothing more than a filler even though A LOT happens in a real world compared to Sora 3rd.In terms of game mechanics it is a step forward, of cource, mostly in QoL features. It feels just right as it should while playing and that's the most positive i really can say about this one.Overall the mocking patchwork of previous games on top of a rotten plot with almighty, but constantly nerfed for absolutely no objective reason villain totally killed this game for me. There vere several moments that i really enjoyed, but all of them were as far from the main plot-called thig as possible. Definetely the worst kiseki game so far, and not by the slightest, the difference is incomparable. I can now say with utmost certainty that i really hate this one and wouldn't recommend it to anyone except you can turn you brain off for the most part, but if so you can go to any third-rate jrpg packed with date sim and probably this will be even better experience that i had, seeing my belover series literally raped in front of my eyes for literally no reason. If i didn't know Kuro no kiseki is way better, there would be a great chance i dropped the whole series after this.

_childDocuments_.review: Trails' second of three "intermission" games has a burden not only to painting a path onwards to the back third of the series, but also digging out of the corner they painted themselves in with the previous few games.Gone are endless rescue missions, harem scarem, fleeing villians, and needless bloat of the last 4 games. Main game is 45 hours, 3 paths, and in general books thru the story and character beats they wanna tell. It's a refreshing change of pace to have mistakes fixed and sludgy storytelling clarified, and having the fluff being fun and shoved off the end to the largely voluntary dungeon crawler.Now, its 7th, so that means there were problems. One is that the 3 paths are not equal, with C's route being an excellent emotional ride concerning pentience and belonging, Rean's being a pretty good yet procrastinated mopping up of Erebonia's and his threads, and Lloyd's...oh boy Lloyd's. Yall've seen how good Zero and Azure was right? How much sense of place Crossbell has, the ever-increasing tension and intricacy of its plot, and its vast cast of lovable and interesting characters right?Yeah, that doesn't exist in his route. Most of their personalities are sucked out, plot beats are recycled wholesale, and the city feels like a theme park more than Mishelam could ever be. Here's also where all the skeevy and anti-LGBTQ stuff ended up too.Music's better than its predecessor tho!And this ties into BG3 above, in that this was another series some don't give the earlier games of its maker much of a look before it went cinematic, but with Reverie, they actually choreographed scenes out and had all character movement look good for the first time. Seriously, this is actually quality now.Looking forward to the series continuing to shed its recent bad habits with Daybreak after playing this.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to say it but I think I'm done with the Trails franchise. I didn't like the direction Cold Steel arc took in general but there was a lot there that was still great.  Cold Steel 3 is one of my favourite entries in the entire franchise.  While Cold Steel 4 was a poor game...it at least wrapped things up so the story could scale things back a bit and get a little less bonkers.   Or so I hoped.Did that happen though?  Not even close.  To say this game doubled down is an understatement.  It quadrupled down on the stuff I didn't like.  This no longer felt like a world of great characters and a great setting with a sprinkle of mystery.  It felt like watching Star Wars Episode 9 where stuff is just happening because it was written that way.  The prologue and the first act of this game is AWESOME!  9/10 stuff...had a real chance to be my favourite entry in the franchise.  After that the game loses me completely and just digs a deeper and deeper and deeper whole to the point where I actively disliked this games story.   I know that the Calvard arc will start slow and build from there and I suspect I'll love that part of it...but its going to catch up to what this game setup quickly and almost certainly surpass it and I want no part of that.  Some people like the over the top stuff in anime or the kind of thing you might get in the last 20 minutes of a Final Fantasy game where the story goes nuts...that's the worst part of those games for me.  4/10.  Do not recommend. Game play wise I have very few complaints.  Character bloat made menus annoying but the actual combat was arguably the most fun its been in the franchise.  If for some reason you play this game primarily for the combat then Reverie is well worth it for that.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE July 14 2023I got to a Mishy boss and the game completely froze - and that whole segment was extremely tedious.  I refuse to do it again - Rain Code has my attention now anyway.I can't recommend the game now that I've had a chance to really dig in.  It's not that it's bad.  It's that it's clear they wanted to make a mobile game but figured they would put it on console.  The story isn't that good, there's very little town exploration and the characters are slapped into teams with no real rhyme or reason.  Some of the minigames also are unskippable; normally this isn't an issue, but they're just horrible VR experiences rather than something that's actually interesting to do.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Figured out the graphics issue - Borderless is essentially broken/useless.  Requires Fullscreen to set the proper refresh rate for the monitor, then rates are between 80-100 on the highest settings.  Still feels unoptimized, but I can live with this.- Music is pretty good, though nothing really beats Cold Steel III (so far).- It seems like they at least tried to have more voice acting (Cold Steel III and Cold Steel IV were pathetic in this regard).  Again, not quite far yet to say for sure; Cold Steel III in particular started strong and then fell off for the second half.- I don't know what it is but Lloyd's segment so far is extremely dull.  It's strange; it's like they purposely copied the feel from Azure and Zero, but that doesn't translate well at all to 3D.  It's hard to explain.  Like if you look at Cold Steel 1, the first part is meeting everyone; so you expect it to be a bit slower because these are people you haven't met, but with Reverie, it's dog slow yet isn't trying to introduce you really to anyone; it assumes you know who they are, which means it feels slow.  It's really hard to describe.- Are these controls different than IV?  I'm having a difficult time with the buttons and I don't know why.  It took me forever to figure out how to get speedup going; and I'm thinking I have to customize this back to what I'm used to maybe.If you can get this on a STEEP discount - I'd say no more than $30 - sure, it's worth that. _childDocuments_.review: Yeah, I gotta say this is just a cheap cash grab with a strange little story that was forced together to combine the earlier Trails games into one "finale".  At least half the game is just designed to be seemingly endless grinding getting ready for the "next" stage of the story.  Character management is insane, you have 30 characters that all need to be leveled up and all need to be equiped by the end, it is a logistical nightmare since they all share the same inventory and money as well.  Which goes back to the endless grinding already being built into the game as a requirement, but you also just need to keep going back with different characters to level them up and get resources to upgrade their gear.  If it wasn't for all the grinding, which has been probably 3/4 of my game time, the remaining 1/4 is actual gameplay and story, and the story is completely dilluted by the fact you have SO many characters that there isn't time to actually have much of a story at all.  The whole game takes place over just a couple of days.  It really should be just DLC for the last Trails game, without all the required grinding, at a fraction of the cost.  I am just over 150 hours into the game with over 100 of that just grinding away, I've made it to the "finale", but I just don't have enough interest to keep grinding because it just told me the finale requires everyone to be "battle ready", so I've abandoned the game as it's just not worth finishing!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this review with I generally love JRPG's and I understand that I hopped into a series that's at the end of it's run. I am sure people who have played all of these games will love this... maybe like honestly if you ignore the glitching I think pokemon violet and scarlet might have better animation.I bought it because I saw a review saying it was a great new entry point to a "Beloved" series. It is not. I should have probably turned the game off and asked for a refund when the game started with a 20 minute cutscene that introduced (generous because it mostly just flashed their faces and a name) with some incredibly mediocre animation. After 20 minutes of cool stuff I didn't get to do, I got my next hint this game wasn't for me. For throwing you head long into a story, without any effort to grab you if you don't know what happened in the last episode, has one of the most obnoxiously over explanatory tutorials I have dealt with every 5 minutes minimum through out the prologue there would be paragraphs of explanation about basic game mechanics. As you progress through the incredibly linear prologue chapter initially fighting deeply mundane jrpg battles suddenly you are confronted with your first miniboss, it's a nice step up but not so difficult it feels unmanageable. some more badly animated cutscenes and boring combats and you make it to the final battle. Only to be confronted with yet another incredibly long, schmaltzy and boring cutscene that achieves NOTHING for the story, because for all the yapping you still have to fight them! The final boss of the prologue is a ridiculous step up from the rest of the combats you've faced. After two hits 1 team member was dead and the rest were on deaths door. It would have been interesting I guess if it had felt like I was supposed to be progressing, improving my characters, learning combat through actually doing it and not reading walls of text. Unfortunately, and I really mean this because I think it's a huge problem you start at level 98, if your fight every battle in the tutorial you won't level up, you don't get any new gear, nothing changes. Just all of a sudden you're confronted with an enemy that can do 50% of your healers health with one of it's AoE attacks, so better hope it isn't going again right after that. Then you finally make it through the prologue thinking you're finally going to get into the meat of the game only for more boring, poorly animated cutscenes and worse yet a text wrap up of the cutscenes you just watched. Then after this terrible intro, you realize you're 3 hrs into a game you hate so you can't request a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: This game should be thought of as a prestige campaign, much to the likes of a DnD prestige campaign. The original campaign was CS 1 to 4; this is the coda campaign. Being a prestige campaign, that means the player can pull out all the stops in designing the most broken character build and fight against the "back of the codex" monsters that were intimidating in earlier games. Additionally, the scope of the campaign can be the most ambitious. Rean and friends have already had their standard 'hero's journey'; this game features the phase of storytelling after the hero's journey. That means the story stakes are even larger than the previous game (which itself was continental in size) and the archvillain has to be even more overwhelming than the previous archvillain. The archvillain and the scope of the conflict is much more metaphysical than in the previous games, which can be a detraction because the previous games were more grounded relative to this one. And the grounded quality gave gravitas. But again, all this ambitious stuff comes with the territory. The main thrust of this game is surprisingly not the story but instead the gameplay. Indeed, this game features the very best gameplay in the entire CS series. And the addition of a "speedup" option makes battles lightning fast. Because I know every single characters' stats, crafts, and arts like the back of my hand having played the previous 4 CS games, I very much can lull myself into an auto mode and let my fingers fly around the keyboard and execute umpteen battles within moments. Battles very much play like a slot machine, which is designed to reward you constantly with visual and audible stimuli (and not coins) in order to keep you hooked perpetually. That is what this gameplay is like. The inclusion of more than 50 playable characters would seem bloated to the uninitiated; however, since I've played all 10 games prior to this, I believe it or not know quite well each and every playable character and character mentioned in dialogues. Only once in my entire playthrough did I stop to wonder who this or that person was. And maybe I jogged my memory; I don't recall; he was such a tertiary character from whichever entry. Thus, it is surprisingly easy to keep track of all 50 playable characters because the previous 10 games were my warmup to this one. And leveling each character is a breeze, even when some are 20 levels behind: simply tag the undeveloped characters with the powerful ones, and within 5 battles the undeveloped characters will gain about 99,000 experience and jump several levels in one go. There is a convincing air of mystery to the story by the beginning. We don't even glimpse the main villain until about 30 hours into the storyline, let alone duel with the main villain even further down. The bloated cast mainly backfires during the main storyline; there are simply too many cooks in the kitchen. The best characters remain the central protagonists Rean, Lloyd, C, and Lapis and friends, and C and Lapis have a the best dynamic. Thus, their scenes and interactions are always the best. But Rean's pals whom I've gotten to know over 500 previous hours of gameplay are relegated to side comments. In order to include them all in group dialogue scenes, fan favorite characters like Fie, Laura, and Alisa simply have generic comments which anyone else could have said. For example, Emma Milstein is stuck always talking about mana, the higher elements being present in some area, or identifying some magic spell being used. Wow; how predictable. Yes, it makes sense to assign that dialogue to her; but, does she not have anything else or personal to say? And in order to keep Rean's and Lloyd's posse open for all Trails Shipping fans, each lady has generic compliments to them, and nothing is personalized or deeper than surface level. This is disappointing because I for example shipped Rean and Laura over the four previous games (with Fie as a very close second), and all Laura says to Rean is "we should train more!" Gee... real dense stuff there, Laura. The game's answer to the bloated cast number is the inclusion of 'daydreams', much like the star doors in the Sky the Third game. Sky the Third's cast was much tighter (16 versus 55), and the star door scenes were brilliant writing sequences; many of those scenes I remember vividly how many years afterwards. In the daydreams, two characters typically are featured at a time interacting, which means the scope is much more personal. And the game's writing retains its brilliance in these moments. Scenes where the story zooms in on two are by far the best: C and Lapis, Swin and Nadia, Rean and Lloyd together. Estelle anywhere makes a good scene great; after 10 games, her character retains the exact charm she had from FC. That's staying power!There is a lot of narrative convenience in this game; and once again, given the bloated cast and the 'prestige campaign' quality of this game, I think much of this comes with the territory. Mostly, lampshading the plot conveniences simply jars my attention out of the game; that is the main detraction. For example, Renne very early on on C's chapter joins Nadia and Swin. And to fans, this makes absolute sense: the three are childhood assassins, and it is natural Renne would join them. However, she herself never describes her past to the Nadia and Swin, which makes it unclear to the two of them why she tagged along. Indeed, Swin asks at one point, "why is she with us?". Hmm... that plot convenience could easily have been ironed out had the writers included a 5 minute scene with Renne describing who she once was and why she identifies with the Miserable Sinners. A missed opportunity. There was a needless disconnect between what the player knows about Renne's past and what the characters themselves knew. It simply distracted me. In all, the plot itself gets an A minus. It is still very coherent, tightly paced, and organized. The three routes was a novel approach to linear storytelling. When one storyline got too slow paced, I could change perspectives on the fly. And the main campaign was simply too short. It was a great concept, but by the time I had gotten deep into the weeds, well, here's the final boss battle. This contrasts previous entries, which often completed upwards of 120 hours. The 50 hour mark was the real start to the story. And by this 50 hour mark, I was in the final dungeon. Since I have marathon-long expectations of this series, I simply wasn't expecting a 50-hour campaign length. That's not a detraction looking back; it was short and sweet. Compared to other storylines that have A average or A plus writing, this story gets an A minus. Still better than most any other game story I've played, so I'm quite happy with it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the tenth game in a long-running series, and I'm quite pleased with it!The gameplay's still the same Trails gameplay I know and love. I played on Nightmare mode, so other people's mileage may vary. While I thought that the earlygame was a considerable step up in difficulty from CS3 and 4, the difficulty curve flatlines pretty hard as you gain access to stronger options. For example, I noticed that earlier bosses had enough speed to shake off the break status more often than in CS3 and 4, until I got access to speed boosting and delay reducing brave orders to mend things. Rixia's Buzhihuo was my brave order of choice whenever possible because it's BOTH a speed boost and delay reduction! Instead of the usual abundance of sidequests, this game has the True Reverie Corridor for optional content. This weird dimensional space serves as a place to level up your characters and try out team comps that aren't normally possible in the main story. It's a decent time. You also unlock minigames, characters exclusive to the TRC, as well as these Daydreams that tell stories of what the cast have been up to between the events of CS4 and Reverie. The actual dungeon portion of the TRC doesn't fully open up until after you beat the main story, which I believe makes it the first time a Trails game has had postgame content!Speaking of the main story... it's hard to describe in full detail how I feel about it without going into major spoilers, but I'll do my best here. In short, I liked it! I thought it was faster paced than the Cold Steel games. Slow doesn't necessarily mean bad, but it did feel like some of Cold Steel games dragged on a bit too long. I think what helps Reverie's pacing is the three routes that take place simultaneously. I liked being able to switch between the three of them and seeing the mystery unfold in each one. And what a mystery it is!Lloyd's route is probably the weakest because of how it feels like a retread of Trails to Azure, so sometimes I was sitting there thinking 'I feel like we've been here before, have we been here before?'. While it can be disappointing to some, it still has its emotional bits. One particular moment in Act 4 between Lloyd and Randy almost brought a tear to my eye, partly because of the voice acting. Rean's route was pretty good. It had probably some of the most insane moments in the game (in a good way!) and I thought Rean's arc throughout was a suitable epilogue to everything he's been through. It all comes to a head in the Finale when he confronts his self-doubts and self-sacrificing habits once and for all. Good on him!Given who the new C is, tensions between him and a few returning characters in his route were a bit lower than I'd hoped, but his story and development were very fascinating! C's route also stars the new batch of main characters, and I liked all four of them, my favourite being Nadia. Good game overall! In a tier list, I'd probably rank Reverie above all four Cold Steel games, but I'm unsure how it stacks up compared to the older games. Either way, I'm looking forward to seeing how the story unfolds in the next Trails entry.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost didn't play this because Cold Steel 4 left me feeling so burnt out on the series (I wanted to say cold lol).  Don't make the same mistake I did.  Trails into Reverie does it's best to rectify some of the narrative issues that plagued the back end of CS3 and most of CS4 and while it is a somewhat mixed bag, I found it to be a lot more enjoyable following the three converging storylines.The combat is the best it's ever been with a handful of small additions, and managing character equipment and quartz is thankfully easier than previous entries (a godsend when by the end you have 50+ characters).  This also makes the game quite a bit easier than the rest, so I would recommend Nightmare mode for fresh plays instead of waiting for new game plus.The reverie corridor makes a big return from CS2 with a lot more thought and care behind it.  This is where the majority of the side content plays out as well as acting as a hub for all your characters.  While there are a decent number of minigames, trials and 'daydreams' to take part in (similar to the doors from Trails in the Sky 3), they did completely strip the social building elements from previous CS entries. I felt like those were never that well fleshed out to begin with so they were not missed.Overall I was very pleased.  Trails into Reverie marks a great way to cap off everything that went on in the Crossbell and Cold Steel saga and shouldn't be ignored, even if you were less than enthused with the ridiculous length and ludicrous story elements from earlier games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely fantastic, but you know, it isnt for everyone.First and foremost, if you just knew this series by finding this game on steam store, know that to fully experience this game you should play another 9 games. Yeah, the three "Trails in the Sky", two "Trails from Zero/to Azure" and four "Trails of cold steel".This series is my absolute favorite, and I highly recommend you play them all. Yeah, you can skip them and read the events (the game has a kind of library where you can find a short summary of what happened till now) but im strongly against it, since you are missing a lot of good content, easter eggs and hype.If you are here after playing these games and are a fan of the series, needless to say you are buying this lul. _childDocuments_.review: Trails into Reverie is the 10th installment in the Trails series.Playing "Trails to Azure" (Part 6) before Reverie is highly recommended.Story (without spoilers):Cried, Laughed and had some WTF moments 10/10It isn't a full conclusion otherwise there wouldn't be more sequels coming.Gameplay:The gameplay isn't the best in this series (6/10).It's more like a dungeoncrawler and similar to Trails in the Sky 3rd.The ingame stuff is sometimes overwhelming so sell what you don't need.At certain points the story forces you to switch main character which sometimes is annoying.Character switching can also be fun, so I'm just leaving it at an equal standing.Summary:It's worth the money. 30 hours on story mode (very easy without a lot of side content) is not bad.Some contents from prequels would be nice, but then the content could be too much.PS: Some new characters are adorable (not you Gilbert) and I hope to see them again.PPS: Gilbert was introduced in Trails in the Sky and is a running gag, for those who aren't familiar with the series.
