_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Trails fans, buy this it's peak Trails. Everyone else play the other games then experience peak Trails.If you've been playing Trails this far, you know what to expect. If you have never played a Trails game, DO NOT start here. Probably the worst one to start lol. At minimum play Trails of Cold Steel 1 through 4, strongly recommended to add Trails to Zero and Azure. You can also play the Sky trilogy which comes before both Cold Steel and Zero/Azure, but lets be honest: mechanically those games have not aged well and i am a snob when it comes to graphics and those haven't fared much better either (flame me). This is a game for the diehard Trails fans, you get an absolute absurd number of playable characters from virtually every Trails game, an area that serves as a sandbox and playground to experiment with builds, characters and lots of lore implications for the future. The perspective switch with the three protagonists was neat and kept things interesting, sometimes showing different perspectives from two or even all three routes. As always Falcom Sound Team puts out banger OSTs, final dungeon theme is honestly the best "final dungeon" they've done. Runs great on my RTX 3070 with maxed settings, though fans got loud. There were some bugs when it launched like most characters not having their linked abilities or funny stuff like english Laura speaking Japanese when she casts arts (but who is using Laura for arts anyways? lol) but that's all been fixed now. Honestly, the biggest critique of this game is ironically a strength: the cast. There's like over two dozen if not close to three dozen playable characters. It's a lot. A lot of people to gear, a lot of people to level and a lot of mira to spend on them. My own minor critique is getting Platinum in this game is a pain, seriously do EVERY master mission? Have you seen what they want? EVERY character to level 250, do a ♥♥♥♥ ton of forging and crafting, ALL the minigames....I platinumed CS4 and I thought that was a lot lol. Also still malding that I missed ONE chest without a guide, I hate this achievement lol.Just buy the game. I usually wait for sales but Trails games are my one exception, they are always worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: If you haven't played at least the entire Cold Steel Saga, I can't recommend this game.This game is essentially a capstone to both the Crossbell and Erebonia games, so 6 titles in total. I don't want to go into detail too much but if you played the series up to this point, this game will be an absolute treat for you. If you haven't you will be utterly lost.So don't get this if you plan to start Trails, but absolutely do get it if you are already invested in the series and played the previous games!That said, there's almost too much content in this game. It's just crazy how much there is of everything, no matter if its main story, side stories or minigames.
_childDocuments_.name: The Legend of Heroes: Trails into Reverie

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful way to close off my current run through the Trails Series. It was nice to see a refocus on the Crossbell characters and wrap up the conclusion to the Arc that started with Trails from Zero.The game is a combination of the dungeon crawling aspect from Trails in the Sky 3rd (Reverie Corridor) and Main story progression. Minigames and side stories are explored in Reverie, while the Main story is divided into three routes. I found all the protagonists fun to follow. The way the game is broken up may feel a bit off in terms of pacing, though, depending on how much grinding and dungeon exploring you want to do. Reverie allows you to get stronger to the point where Nightmare felt pretty easy from mid game up until the final boss, which was a challenge.Otherwise, more gameplay options, a lot of playable characters, and a nice wholesome story that explores many characters and wraps up nicely. Looking forward to playing through the Calvard Arc, once all is said and done.

_childDocuments_.review: The culmination of 20+ years of good story telling paving the way to the next arc in the world of Zemuria.A games which very enjoyment bares heavy weight on previous stories told. As in having played and enjoy the previous 9 games in the series.It's story is multifaceted and bares many references and plots to the overaching plots of each of the 3 arcs that came before.I can recommend this game as a "Trails fan" who have enjoyed previous titles. But i could imagine someone picking this as their "first trails" Would be in absolute confusion of all subplots and references around and. Would probably have a hard time making head and tail about reamifications of the stories plot or sub-plots.This game is by all means a love letter trails fans who enjoys this series such as i.it even features some unlockable sub-stories that give just a genuine good feeling to watch and play.This game has touched me emotionally and made me sit on the edge of my seat in anticipation mutliple times and is by far one of my favorite j-rpg titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Does it has the best Trails graphics so far? YesDoes it have great story, musics, and characters? YesIs the battle mechanics better than Cold Steel 4? YesDoes the gatcha system somehow added positive nuance to the game? Weirdly yesDoes it contains a lot of easter eggs and nostalgia for Trails fans? Definitely yesBut Does this game actually important? I would say notYes I am a Trails fan, but if you think deeply, this game forcefully open the satisfactory ending you have in the cold steel IV, milk that story, and then close it again (still in a good way). I would rather Falcom to add a small DLC to close some open ends to Cold steel IV base game then go straight to the next arc. Nevertheless, this is a great game to Trails fans, but I hope Falcom do not prolong the story anymore than it need to be. Please let the series ends before the story becomes stale.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Trails into Reverie concludes both the Cold Steel and Crossbell sagas, and it does a damn well job of it. I was very disappointed in Cold Steel IV, but Reverie was a fantastic ride all the way through. It's a 'Sky the 3rd'ish formula this time around while also having a route system where you follow three protagonists. It's a pretty neat and welcome Visual Novel-esque style of storytelling, kept me interested in what will happen next. The bulk of my gameplay went into the True Reverie Corridor, essentially a training ground similar to the likes of Mementos in Persona 5 Royal but with a whole load of extra content such as Daydreams (similar to the Doors from Sky the 3rd), mini-games, trials, and more.I started my Trails journey with Rean and Class VII, so admittedly it's going to be hard to let them go until they inevitably return as the series draws towards the end. I've come to love and adore  every character () this series has introduced thus far, and I'm very excited to see how past and future characters will play their roles in Trails through Daybreak.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe this game is one of the better Trails gameThis game is meant to be somewhat of a filler arc between Cold Steel 4 to the next Trails series, don’t connect/set up much for the next series but close some plot points while introducing a new character. Believe this has the best gameplay but the story at least for me feels a bit off in many places, it didn’t ruin the experience but it did make me question it a lot in a bad way.The system is a copy of the whole game of Trail of the Sky 3rd, another pocket dimension where it is a dungeon crawler but WITH THE WHOLE CAST (that u have at the time of the story). It's pretty good, the dungeon is randomized, the loot is randomized and there is a good pool of enemies to fight.Another part of it is all the side content it has, basically where all the side content in the game is in general as the game has only 1 side quest. It has all the mini-games + more with its own twist and small story and daydream, the same system from Sky where you can watch cutscenes of random events that happen with the cast, they are enjoyable. The Corridor also has all the shop needed to keep all the characters geared for the act as well as random misc accessories to customize your characters looksOverall it is a good addition to the however the only downside I have with it is the plot of it. It was introduced that all the protags have a weird mirror that brings them there to train for the up coming danger, but that is all of the story it gets (unless there more posts beating the game but if that is the case that would be bad IMO, I haven’t done the post-game content as of writing this review). Unlike Sky 3rd it at least has a story driving the whole pocket dimension plot where at the end of each dungeon it gives more info of why it exists or just more story for Kevin but the Corridor is so disconnected from the story that even when it mentions the main plot it just gets pushed aside and forgotten.I try to keep the routes short so I won’t say too many spoilers but just give my feelings for each part.Wish the prologue didn’t exist, SSS is my favorite cast but I feel like the writer put themself in a position to not like this route as much as I want to, it starts with liberating Crossbell again from this small rebel post-CS4, just for Crossbell to be taken over by a new threat ALL IN THE FIRST HOUR of the game marking it the 3rd time the plot of “we must liberate Crossbell” happens. The topic is so overused that it makes the overall route feel like you reliving the last arc of Azure as it feels like it follows the same beat but with CS plots and characters spread around. If u never play Azure then you won’t notice it or feel burnout by this topic but from someone who has played it, I hate they went this route for telling Lloyd's pathRean’s route feels like a whole bunch of random goose chasing for the first 2 acts and a whole ??? for act 3. I don’t think it is a bad route, there is not much to hate about it but there also isn’t much to love about it, one thing I would mention now is the game gives Rean another major story about his power which is a bummer for me as I felt like the whole Rean curse/power arc was nicely closed in the CS4 but was reopen for this gameI 100% would say C’s route is the best in the game as it feels like there were all the new ideas lie, a new and enjoyable cast, their involvement in the main story is huge and they the only route that feels like the character are more connected to each other then the rest as cast as the main 4 characters stay in the party throughout the game instead of swap around like the other two routes did. They also have the best-written story in the game imo.Won’t say anything that happens but I will give how I feel about it. After beating the game I was disappointed about who the main villains were and their involvement in the story and kinda of made me feel like it was missing something, doesn’t help that the reasoning too was a bit cliche seeing they wrote better reasoning for the villains in their past games-Music: Might be my Favorite OST in the Cold Steel Series-New combat system: The United system is a great addition to the game, not too OP but not too weak to not used, feels pretty balanced in its uses and the added XP bottles help bring character you don’t use for the Corridor up to spec without having to do the extra farming in battlesWould recommend this game

_childDocuments_.review: I have been enamored with the Trails series ever since I played Trails in the Sky a few years ago, and I went on to binge the entire series back to back finishing with Trails of Cold Steel IV. This series is very near and dear to me. While not technically, mechanically, or graphically impressive, the masterful world building has created an absolutely enthralling world for the numerous characters and narrative threads to exist in. The lifeblood of the Trails series are the characters, and their impact on the world and each other as the story progresses. Falcom does not deviate from these core strengths in Trails into Reverie. This game serves as a massive epilogue for the entire series thus far, but primarily for Trails from Zero/to Azure and Trails of Cold Steel I through IV.I wholeheartedly recommend this series and this game, but with one massive caveat specifically aimed at people who have not played a Legend of Heroes game before.Imagine this scenario for a moment. You just saw an amazing film, and you're talking to your friend about it. They say it sounds interesting and plan to watch it tonight. The next day they come back to you and say they  didn't like it because they had no idea what was going on, weren't attached to any of the characters, and weren't invested in the plot. When you ask them about a particular plot point, they have no idea what you're talking about, because it turns out they fast forwarded to the last fifteen minutes of the film and only watched that. Bewildered at this silliness, you tell them they have to watch the entire film. This is  an entry point into the series by any stretch of the imagination, so without any doubt whatsoever I do not recommend you buy this game if you are unfamiliar with the series.If you've only played Trails of Cold Steel I-IV, you will likely get some enjoyment from this title, though you will find yourself occasionally lost and not knowing what's going on.If you've only played Trails of Cold Steel I-IV and Trails from Zero/Trails to Azure, you will enjoy this game but will still miss a few references to past Trails games and certain events and characters won't have as much of an impact on you. If you are one of these people I highly recommend you play through Trails in the Sky FC, SC, and 3rd or at the very least watch a story recap (though I highly recommend playing them).If you've played every Trails game before this, then you probably already know you're buying this game and don't need my recommendation, but you will greatly enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a celebration/send-off to this era of Trails, it does a great job. As a stand alone story? Not so much, but I never expected much to be coherent given this is mostly an asset flip jrpg. The appeal imo is just getting to play as most of your favorite Trails characters across 3 different arcs, with a few welcome additions. It's more like Trails in the Sky the 3rd than anything else, but since I knew what I was getting into, it was good. Grinding and equipment management is more of a pain than ever given the bloated cast though, but you can mitigate it somewhat by only focusing on your favorites. This game is pretty easy though, since it still falls into the same pitfall Cold Steel 3 and 4 had of "if you break an enemy they never get another turn" which can get super tiring especially coupled with equipment grinding. The pre rendered cutscenes are a highlight as well, even if there are only a few.

_childDocuments_.review: Before you buy :The engine port is very good like the previous game but there are a ton of mistranslations in equipment/quartz/MQs and missions objectives in the Reverie Corridor, Plus some questionable choices of words in few sentences during the main story. As of today it's still not fixed.Took me approx 150h to do all the content in one playthrough on nightmare (Main story + post game and achievements) and griding for the 1500 victories done in Very easy (it was a bit painful not gonna lie).The goods :-The game with the best gameplay in the series, a ton of characters to play and more new MQs/quartz/equipment than ever.-The daydreams are a nice addition, there was something like that in Trails in the Sky TC, where you mostly watch a slice a life of secondary characters before the main story of this game. Some characters have some epilogues too which is cool. It's very enjoyable and make them more "humans" and it make a nice break during the gameplay and the main story parts. I hope Falcom will keep putting them in future games.-The true reverie corridor, the random dungeons are ok but the grinding and all the side activities are fun. The RNG/gacha drops are fine and not frustrating because you can craft everything if you're unlucky.-Finally we have an postgame after the main chapters with a nice extra story and the possibility to push your party to the max. The mini team missions with the "skits" from the "Tales of" series are enjoyable extras.-Three differents teams to progress through the stories. The 3rd route with the new character is the most enjoyable for me.-Solid OSTs as always.The bads :-Mediocre translation for some items and quartz, it didn't do what it's written, do the complete opposite or with an incomplete description. Furthermore, during some dialogues there are some "internet slang" and "Gen Z" words here and there, come on NISA...-The worst main story in the series in my opinion, a lot of deja-vu from previous games and some characters are just here for the nostalgia/fans and doesnt contribute much to the story. Lloyd route was the worst where nothing really happen.-Some characters are lacking in the craft department, for example only 2 crafts for Estelle and Joshua. 3 crafts for each characters should be the bare minimum. A bit sad that's it's missing some characters from Liberl.-Arts is way too strong endgame compared to crafts, specially on high difficulty (still better balanced than azure).

_childDocuments_.review: The Trails series is incredible. Having played since the start of Trails in the Sky, I've sunk many hours into this series already, so I'm here until the end truly captivated by the world that it's constantly expanding upon.This game doesn't really miss, but what I was very happy about, was how much I was able to play as the older characters (e.g. the Trails in the Sky gang), which we've only gotten a taste of since Trails in the Sky the 3rd.New players will have a hard time jumping into this game without knowledge of prior games, and while ordinarily I'd suggest starting at Trails in the Sky (since it is my favourite arc by far), it is a bit dated now & much easier to start with Trails of Cold Steel / Trails from Zero[+ to Azure] (which both play out at roughly the same time in the timeline). Even Trails from Zero is fairly outdated at this point, but there are a lot of important links back to the Crossbell arc.It is very much a classic turn-based JRPG.There is a LOT of worldbuilding; the Trails series has an insane amount of text-based dialogue in these games (most of the main story in this game is voice acted though!), which continually builds upon and references its past games.Graphically it's getting a little better over time. It doesn't really feel like a modern game per se, but the visuals are there. It has decent enough models and such, but exploring the world usually doesn't give you any real "wow" moments. Its story is definitely more of the Trails forte.I love these games. The only gripe I have is that it takes them so long for the english release to come out, so I've started to really consider learning JP to play the original game. They do such a great job with cleaning up & improving settings and such in the english version though.Favourite character has always been Estelle, so the fact that I can play as her again is incredible (even though one of her skill ranges seemed bugged for some reason, but oh well, it didn't really affect much).

If you're interested in this (very long) series, go check out  (first game chronologically) or  (first game in the third arc, and arguably more user-friendly since it wasn't made in the PSP era). _childDocuments_.review: So I've finally caught up with english Trails releases. This game is not standalone. If you have no prior knowledge of Trails you'd have to start at one of a few points. But aside from that, Reverie definitely serves as a very fitting conclusion to most plot points up to this point in the series. I don't get the massive hate for CS IV but definitely this ending serves as a much more fulfilling one with the 3 main characters getting the screentime they deserve.First place to start for newcomers is definitely Sky first chapter. It's the oldest game so the pacing might be slow, I did drop the game for a while but I picked it back up after a while of playing Cold Steel 1. This game serves as the chronological first game in Zemuria, while not essential to the other starting points it does build up the world and I do recommend this just for Second and Third chapters and their much better story.Secondly you could start at Trails to Zero or Trails of Cold Steel. This is part of the split in timelines for the franchise. Eventually if you'd get to Cold Steel 3 the timelines will merge again so having prior knowledge of both is pretty good to understanding the larger story context. But if you'd like to skip those...Cold Steel 3 can also serve as a starting point but you'd need to be filled in on all the lore points up to that point. It is the middle of the Cold Steel arc being 3/4th games, but it does tell its own story and is still playable but I don't recommend this one. Reverie is not suitable as a starting point, it serves as a sort of epilogue game alike Sky 3rd, mostly finishing the storyline their respective arcs seek to tell.

_childDocuments_.review: Reverie is a sort of epilogue to the Crosbell (Zero/Azure) and Cold Steel arcs. It's probably the worst possible starting point for the Trails series, and if you're playing this game you should have ideally played at least the games for those two arcs.The gameplay and narrative intent are both closest to the 3rd Sky game as there is a large slowly expanding dungeon area where you can eventually use all 50+ playable characters. However, that's only half the game since the other half is handled through three intertwining story paths where you play as different groups. I absolutely loved the blend of both of these styles since it permits a nonlinear storytelling of past, present, and future events. It also lets you see POVs of events and stories from characters that you never would have had the chance to with the flow of a linear story.Overall, it provides satisfying closure to two arcs spanning 6 games while introducing new characters and extending the threads of what's coming next. Onwards east towards Daybreak/Kuro!Side note: Trails continues its tradition of having the in-game stories from books turn out to be about actual characters / people from the past or present. As such, I recommend reading through at least the main collectible book series in Cold Steel IV before playing, if you haven't already, for an even better experience.

I thought it was less bloated than Sen no Kiseki 2-4.This is absolutely the wrong place to start this story. If you haven't experienced anything in this franchise yet, go check out Trails in the Sky and get ready for The Feels.

_childDocuments_.review: ***This is more of a short endorsement of the franchise as a whole, but Reverie is awesome!***I was looking for something to get into after running through the Xeno games over the course of the first half of the year. Trails is what kept coming up as the go-to recommendation. And funnily enough, it seems like I got into it at just the right time - with the completed localization for Zero and Azure dropping just as I needed them to. So I was able to play through all 10 localized trails games in one marathon. That probably sounds like a daunting task, and let me just say that it definitely was! But boy was it worth it. This series does world-building and character arcs in a way too few do. So much so, that by the time I rolled credits on Reverie, the end screen and music playing over it gave me a sense of catharsis that I've rarely felt in any medium. I know this entry is by no means the end of the franchise, but it's a great stopgap before the next era. If you love story rich RPG's, you'll love Trails. If you love Trails, you'll love Reverie.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a conclusion to all the previous games to lead you to the new future stories that the franchise has for players.Read the book 3&9 it's very relevant for this game and upcoming titles. It's painfully long but needed.It's with a tear that I say "goodbye" to those characters that we played with for many years.It was a fun ride, a roller coaster of emotions. Worth at least 75h of gameplay, so you are spending good money on a good time.Don't expect a revolution from the game itself. The graphic remains the same, the UI is improved for easier sorting. Still could be better but it's a welcomed improvement.It introduced a new type of gameplay, you will be playing from 3 different perspective "at the same time" to progress through the whole story.I do find it sad you are not able to explore Erebonia post-game and you cannot have more "bonding stories" which was a fun bonus honestly. I wished that you had more story on the world itself like previous title then just being happy with having only the plot. No side mission, no side quest or whatever that add some more life to the world.It's a very tunnel type of game, not much freedom. Play it in a specific way if not, you will suffer a bit from remorse for missing out on some items.Plot and story wise it's a bit silly honestly. But that has been the fun, flaws and frustration of that franchise since the beginning. If you are new to that, you will be upset. But for old veteran, the classic plot armor, lack of consistency on certain story mechanics, the dragging and teasing of Ouroboros master plan is getting old (game cover).The usual lack of casualties makes the tension and stakes very low. I am not asking a "akame ga kill" plot but more like a valkyria chronicles "death" to rise the stake and increase the tension of the plot. Instead of giving a slap on a criminal and letting him go to repeat his crime later on.The lack of punishment and consequences for the antagonist render the morality and conclusion a bit weird.The fact teleportation is a easy way for the antagonist to escape all the time from his crimes while the protagonist need long chant and preparation to even teleport. The usual victory but defeat gameplay mechanics is a bit old. Since you don't really feel strong with such style of gameplay.Those have been recurring issues from games to games.As always, I am sad this game like the futures ones still are not being released at the same time and with the english version being available day one with the Japanese version. As now, I can just wait with impatience the new title get localized.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend every game in the Trails series. The greatest strengths in these games for me is the huge cast of characters where each gets a great moment.  They do not all get equal treatment, but for me, generally they give the most concentration to those characters that resonate broadly.In addition, they do a fantastic job populating the world with interesting details and conversations to help provide insight into how NPCs live. In so many ways, despite not having sprawling open world maps, this series manages to feel more lived in than so many open worlds.  You can see in the small conversations between people over the course of the many games how their lives are transformed by the events of the series, and how they experience those events differently without knowledge of all that your characters know. I also find the spirit of the small kingdoms and their desire to be free from oppressive large states a great element from an old-school American perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: 1) A good story to conclude the "Erebonian" and "Crossbell" arcs (although the overall story for this particular game felt like "spin-off" story that was designed just so to give closure for multiple main characters from previous games more than anything else).2) This game has SO MANY boss battles (even surpasses "Cold Steel 4" when counting all monster/human boss battles in the game) with plenty of good boss themes, which is what I look forward to the most in these turn-based JRPGs.3) Music in general in this game is very good, although I would say the normal/boss battle music didn't stand out as much as previous games in the series (the bar was already very high from previous games, so it's no surprise that attempting to top those off would be a difficult task in general).4) Newly added characters who are making their debut in this game turned out to be quite interesting and made me wish that they had their own dedicated game that explores their past, leading up to the events in this game.1) The  Some characters sound very loud, while others sound very quiet. It was very annoying for me to keep changing the volume over and over throughout this game depending how loud different characters were during conversations in or outside battles (the in-game settings didn't help very much). The developers could have definitely made a better job in "voice optimization/normalization" for all character voiceovers for a more pleasant game experience overall.2) Too many  where clothes/accessories/weapons clip directly through the characters' physical bodies (which can be "immersion-breaking" at times), which is something I haven't really seen/noticed in prior games, so it is kinda disappointing to see the developers put in less effort in polishing/addressing these things before releasing the game.3) As stated above, the overall story for this game felt like a "spin-off" story (it's NOT, but it did feel that way at times) as the "main threat/villain" for this game felt "disconnected" to previous games and more like a "last minute fabricated villain" just for the sole purpose of "giving closure" to some characters and setting the stage for what's next in the "Trails" franchise (this story, or more so "the villain" of this game, doesn't feel "as integral" to the plot of the overall series and so this story feels that it can be "skipped/ignored" when evaluating its significance compared to previous games, similar to "Trails in the Sky the 3rd" which had a "self-contained/side" story plot that can be overall skipped, in my opinion).4) While there were many "mini games" in this game, none of them stood out to me, in fact, I found some of them to be  to deal with and while I could've skipped them for the most part, the rewards that you gain from completing them the first time are SO worth it that makes them feel "mandatory" to complete at least once before moving on from them (wish the "Blade II" card game was back in this game, but sadly it wasn't). All in all, this was another good great "Trails" game and I have thoroughly enjoyed my time with it and I simply can't wait for what Nihon Falcom has in store for us next in the "Trails" franchise! :D(Note: I only rated games from "Trails of Cold Steel 1" onward because it felt  IMO as those games are more comparable from a  point of view than the prior "Trails in the Sky" trilogy and "Trails from Zero/to Azure" duology games)

_childDocuments_.review: Another great entry in the Trails series, Reverie manages the transition between arcs immeasurably better than Sky 3 did. If you're new to the series, welcome! Please start with Trails in the Sky. For veterans, why are you even reading this?Reverie has a surprising number of mistakes in menus, and the plot feels a bit rushed. Some central concepts are barely explained. At the same time, it delivers some wonderful character moments and sets the scene for the upcoming Calvard arc. It doesn't focus on the old characters very much, as they've already had their time in the sun. It is also the easiest Trails game mechanically, so a veteran could probably comfortably play on Hard difficulty. It's a good time, as expected.Finally, please play the post-game sequence. There's more plot there, and you wouldn't want to miss it. This is a slapdash review by any standard, but you know what you're in for at this point in the series. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Another excellent entry into the Trails franchise, if personally not at the absolute top of my list. An A- entry into an A+ series is still nothing to scoff at though.However, as every other review you've seen of this game says, don't start with this one - it's the tenth game in a continuous running story that assumes you've played and finished every game that came before. More over, it acts as an epilogue to most of the major plot threads from all of those games. Beginning with Reverie is like starting a TV show halfway through the final season. Getting into Trails is absolutely worth the time, but this is unquestionably the worst starting point. Go pick up Trails in the Sky, Trails of Cold Steel, or the upcoming Trails through Daybreak for much better entry points.Story acts as a solid capstone and sendoff to the previous arcs, even if some of it feels like a bit of an emotional and narrative retread of parts previous games (especially Cold Steel IV). Even so, I frequently found myself grinning from ear to ear at just how much I love these characters and this world. Some people understandably dislike having such a huge roster of characters (over fifty that are playable, and dozens more named NPCs of various importance with backstories that you'll be familiar with from all of the previous games), but I never found myself any more frustrated with the "everyone chimes in with a line or two in every cutscene" storytelling style that has become synonymous with Trails than I was in previous entries.Gameplay is definitely the most fun so far, with tons of post-game team building content that just begs you to optimize the hours away looking for that perfect setup. Reminds me of what Persona 5 attempted to do with Mementos, except dramatically quicker and more engaging. Master and Sub Quartz are a really excellent RPG system that actualize Final Fantasy VII's Materia system into modern sensibilities, and Reverie's implementation of the system is head and shoulders above previous entries. Brave Orders are still generally entertaining and serve as a great way to add functional gameplay elements to characterization of the cast, and the new United Front system feels suitably "power of friendship" for a game that at its heart is about how much the player appreciates a cast of characters developed over a decade and a half.Ultimately, if you're at the point in this series where it begins to make any sense to pick up Reverie, then you don't need a review. Buy it and continue onward into what has probably become one of your favorite franchises.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy Aidios!(Please play the other Trails first)TL;DR:- Gameplay: The formula started way back in Sky FC refined to perfection. If you know what you are doing, this game is a breeze. If not, a true challenge. Especially in Nightmare.- Graphics: They do the job. Very well, too. And that's the point.- Music: Falcom Sound Team. They need no introduction. OST is perfect, ok?- Replayability: In spades. And you'll want to replay it again, both for the challenge and to just bask in the...- STORY: The capstone to the big tales started in Sky FC, Zero and Cold Steel I. All comes together here. So DO NOT play this game first, go play the others and work from there. The impact of this conclusion and new beginning is all the better that way.Well worth the many, many hours invested. Quality gaming indeed.Le Rant:What an epilogue! Because this beast of a game is the actual epilogue of the first half of the Zemurian saga. I kid you not, play the others first. They are all here at Steam.And you have to play them. I've been following the series for 13 years, playing each and every game as fast as I could get them. I've taken my time with them, true, but seriously:You won't find another JRPG series like this one (or the Ys series). From the smooth gameplay that can make the game a breeze if you mastered its quirks or a challenge if you didn't, to its gorgeous, far-reaching story that even to this day has me loving every GD minute of it. Now on my third run. All 10 games. Back. To. Back.All those known faces, all those stories in West Zemuria that finally find closure here. And the endings, both the main story and the after story... I can't stress it enough, but if you've played all the other Trails before this one, you'll love to this final, wild encore.And with Falcom's JDK music to boot! Which, as anyone knows, it's beautiful and fits this epilogue like a glove.If you are a fan, you don't need this review. If you are starting: please, please play the others first!Support Falcom so they can continue making these amazing stories that keep growing and growing, wilder and wilder. You won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Trails game, another positive review.As usual, a warning first for potential new players: Trails into Reverie effectively acts as a continuation of both the Crossbell story arc (Trails from Zero / Trails to Azure) and the Erebonia story arc (Trails of Cold Steel I to IV). This means that you cannot play this game without having played those six games before, otherwise it will make very little sense.Now, obviously, I assume that anyone who spent 500 hours playing through those 6 games is obviously going to want to know what happens next, particularly on the Crossbell side which had a few unresolved plot threads. Well, this is it, so buy it. Well, by the time I post this review, I assume that most of you already did. Good!For those who haven't yet:In terms of structure, this game is effectively a combination of a traditional Trails game and Trails in the Sky the 3rd. It contains the equivalent of a complete "standard" Trails game, but it also has a ton of Trails in the Sky the 3rd-type content. It makes for a refreshing change of pace since it's been so long since a Trails game has deviated from the normal structure.As usual. the PC port from PH3 games is fantastic, the localization from NISA is fine, and the game overall is excellent. I mean, it's a Trails game, and by now Trails has clearly established itself as a quality series. This is no different. Buy it. Play it. Then wait for Trails Through Daybreak.

_childDocuments_.review: After finally finishing the main story I think it is safe to say that this was a good conclusion to both Erebonia and Crossbell's arcs.  It was nice to finally see the closure of the bid for independence back from Azure as well as finally say goodbye to Erebonia with this 5th and final installment before jumping to Calvard.  In terms of story, Lloyd's route felt nice to see although maybe a little uninspired and Rean's just got a little messy all around. C's route however was a wonderful perspective shift that I think also works wonderfully as an appetizer for what will come in Kuro (I did play these two out of order). Gameplay feels like it is in fact at it's peak of what it can be, it's clear that there's little room to grow as this compared to CS4 had very minor differences and it was very easy to build momentum to steamroll anything that came at you.  Anyone would tell you that this is not a game to start with so if you are looking to get into the trails series, I absolutely do not recommend this one specifically as your start, pick any of the first games in a saga and go from there.  As a long time fan however, I would absolutely recommend. As a side note, in terms on technical issues, as of the time of me writing this, many of the issues seem to have been resolved as the game ran smoothly for me the entire time, however there are still some very obvious translation errors that will hopefully be fixed at some point, as long as it doesn't slow down Kuro's (Daybreak's) release.

Cant's wait for the next arc and the next title in the Trails series: Trails Through Daybreak!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, and a good end to the Saga. While not my favorite in the series, it is easily top 3.After beating Cold Steel 4 I really did feel there was not much else to do with these characters. And while most of the story revolves around the problems in Crossbell, the story keeps it fresh by having the mysteries of why things happened being the more important part of the story. Eventually Crossbell just became another problem to solve, while the mysteries of what were happening is what pushed me forward to finish the story.The gameplay is largely unchanged from Cold Steel 4, with only United Front and tagalong being good quality of life additions. United Front gives you a field wide heal or attack while putting the assault gauge to good use. Tagalong gives you better options with Brave Orders by letting you use the Order of certain characters who are not on the team. Good additions to the game overall.The game has introduces a 3 route system and it is completely fine.  Don't worry about when you need to change routes. The game will just tell you when to change routes, but you can change routes whenever you want for the most part until the game forces you to change.Reverie also has an absolute monster of a playable roster. While this makes equipment management a complete hassle early on, it is amazing to have certain characters just show up and join the team that you never had a chance to really use extensively before. The Reverie Corridor introduces a randomized dungeon that you can just have fun with and really put the huge cast to good use by making a dream team to tackle it. Its also a great way to power up everyone in the game, and I really felt overpowered after each trip. I do feel like the game has a balance problem, with the limited gear early on and huge boss hp pools, making the early game a slog. However, once you get through the Corridor dungeon a few times the game becomes a breeze.The game thankfully removes side quests and bonding events. This was the first time when I wasn't really worried about missing much and could just leisurely play the game without worrying about missing a hidden quest. Romance is out the window here for the mot part. You can thankfully pick anyone you want for Rean's romance at the start of his route, but the romance was only brought up twice in the main story. The game is really laser focused on presenting the story.The game also tones down the overuse of nicknames and titles, and the dialogue is generally better here. There are still some cringy moments, and people gasping and the general use of ellipsis, but its much less and no one is constantly interrupted by people saying their name after every other sentence. The characters and story is given time to breath here. Unfortunately, the story is really focused on Rean, Lloyd, and Cs group. Most of the side characters barely have any dialogue after showing up, and some characters just come and go without contributing much.  Don't expect much from the cast. However, I was really happy how they managed to give Rean an appropriate end. It started with me not sure if I wanted another game with him after Cold Steel 4, to ending with closure and a perfect end for him.One thing I really wish you could do is revisit areas from different chapters. A lot of the early game for Rean is areas where he never returns to. Didn't get everything from his first chapter? well, your gonna have to comeback in new game+ because he never returns. Also, the game still has a few noticeable bugs. The amount of times a daydream or minigame just crashed due to someone having a costume on is wild, the worst being never able to finish the magical girl mini game until no one has an costumes equipped. Even the ending crashed because someone had a costume, finished it when I just removed them all.I also have to mention the final dungeon. By far the most bare bones final dungeon of any in the series, with you able to run to the end of the dungeon with only a easy required fight before the final boss. Largely a forgettable dungeon. However, this is by far the funnest final boss in the series, and also the absolute longest. That fight is really, really long. But it is also obvious they tried really hard to make it fun and varied.Finally, I really like the use of Daydreams, which are stories mainly for specific characters to shine. I do dislike that when they involve combat its with a fixed team, with fixed gear, bu they weren't to hard. It is lame when you only have the basic spells to sling at boss fights with huge hp though. But I do like that some are just anime episodes to just sit and enjoy.Overall a great game, and my favorite just to play in the series. A few things really keep it from being my top of the series, but it is a game that I really enjoyed, and a story worth telling.

_childDocuments_.review: To think I started my Trails journey randomly finding CS1 at Gamestop needing a game to play for my Vita to then wind up buying 2 on release, purchasing a PS4 to play CS3 and 4 respectively at launch and then binging now Reverie and I was not disappointed at all. Trails continues to do what trails does best in having a bunch of amazing payoff moments with very lovable characters all the way through. The wonderful new cast of C and others has been so refreshing and even though people give the music allot of flak, there are certified bangers in here, looking at you Elegant Prowess. Combat continues to be fun for me as Ive hit insane numbers with the new mechanic added to this game, if anything I just wish we had access to even more playable characters but I digress. For people starting, if you want to have some fun,  you can always do abyss on the first playthrough :)I've convinced multiple friends to start Trails during my wait for Reverie originally and to see said friends, now playing through and finishing this game makes me proud and justifies this game / series as a favorite franchise of all time. The story will only continue to get crazier into Kuro. We are a decently small niche all things considered so I do my best to rope in whoever I can for it. Here's hoping early 2024 for Kuro!

The story overwhelms the game play which usually I would be against it but, the story is good so all is forgiven even the fact that i fell asleep while watching some stories because its too long.I started on Hard difficulty but it didn't last long until I switched to Normal. _childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the Trails series, I am very pleased with Trails into Reverie. The game has everything I was hoping for. _childDocuments_.review: So, this game takes place after the events of Trails of Cold Steel 4. Crossbell is about to finally declare it’s independence, but a new threat is rising and it’s up to our heroes to save the day again!If you are familiar with the series, there is not a whole lot new here. The game takes place in and around the Crossbell area. Unlike the other games there are 3 distinct paths that you must play, and you must swap between the 3 different paths to progress. 1 path is Rean Schwarzer and mostly Thors students and alums, another path is based around Lloyd Bannings and the SSS, and the last is made up of some old and new faces but focuses on the character named “C” (it’s a surprise!).  There are 3 new playable characters that all appear in the 3rd path mentioned above. Swin and Nadia who are some types of assassins and a lovable new character called Lapis. I would rank Lapis as SSS+ tier, Nadia as A tier and Swin as F tier, I just sort of find him Forgettable.Overall, this game has an insane number of playable characters. I didn’t count but it’s probably around 40 or so. Almost every playable character from every game is here, minus a few from Trails in the Sky series. This is both a blessing and a curse. It’s fun to run some old comps and mix them up but honestly it also just feels daunting. Luckily the game makes it relatively easy to swap out characters by granting you potions you can use to give any character XP. When the end game rolls around you can really field anyone you want. The number of XP potions is not enough to upgrade everyone in the roster, but you should be able to put together a sizable team with plenty of options.The game is also not really that grindy as far as JRPGs go. There is a place called the Reverie Corridor that opens partway through the game where you can run dungeons. It’s like the old schoolhouse in Trails of Cold Steel 1. You also find gems that unlock other things like side stories, minigames, and gear. It feels rather rewarding overall. You only must go through the first 4 stratums to complete the main story and you can grind the rest after completing the main story if you want.The main story has good pacing, and the story moves along in typical Legend of Heros fashion. The game feels really streamlined. It would probably take you around 60-65 hours to play through the main story, and I never felt bored.After the main story there is still a good 20ish hours of game play, if you want it. You can grind the rest of the Reverie Corridor and unlock more characters, side stories, and mini games. This is not really required; there is a mini story baked into the rest of Reverie Corridor but it’s nothing special and probably will not have any real impact on future games.Considering the number of characters and locations in the game you should be warned that this is not a great first entry into the series. It would be like picking up a long running show like Stargate SG-1 in season 6. You can totally play the game without knowing all the backstory and characters. However, to really appreciate the game it is required to play ALL THE PREVIOUS GAMES. That is a lot to ask. There are 9 previous games that stretch 60-100 hours EACH. Trails of Cold Steel 1-4 feel basically required. Following that up the Crossbell arc games, Trails from Zero and Trails to Azure, are also highly recommended. The Trails in the Sky 1-3 are the least important, but also there are many characters from those games in this game so very much recommended.  If I have any real disappointment, there are some old favorites like Scherazard and Princess Kloe that hail back from Trials in the Sky. They make minor appearances but are not playable. I guess I just find it odd considering they have models and voice acting but not playable.This game was fantastic, from the characters to the story to the pacing. The port is well done and I didn’t have any issues. I would rank it as one of the best games in the entire series. In short it gets a very high recommendation!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Good game overall, but more of the same made it feel like an expensive DLC for Cold Steel IV rather than its own game. But the story and dialogue is fairly massive from a text perspective so that probably pushed it into being its own thing. Has some translation/in-game-explanation issues. Certain parts of the game felt underdeveloped or over-expansive to me.Caveat: this game is 10th in an overarching series and an epilogue to two sub-series, so not the best place to start but ... you do you. I only played the Cold Steel sub-series and used the internet to figure out the relevant info from the other two sub-series. But there's some minor rewards for having save files from the 2 Crossbell arc games as well.I enjoyed the game but not as much as prior entries. In many ways, I feel this game feels like a full game priced major DLC for Cold Steel IV. It has a enjoyable story that benefits from being able to bounce around between three concurring protagonists. Good stuff! The game's events happen over the span of about a week in game, so I needed to suspend my disbelief that the protagonists solve everything so efficiently, but the characters are largely elite to begin with, so it's not completely preposterous. And with a lot of personal bias, I was more interested in Rean's route, and the newer playable characters in "C"'s route, over Lloyd's route. The SSS and Crossbell characters aren't my faves and the weave some hefty chunks of Class VII into their route but I'm just not as engaged when playing that route.The combat style is polished and satisfying but at this point you've probably been casting the same arts and crafts for a few games now and I ended up fast forwarding through most combats. There's a reverie dungeon that, before concluding the main story, is somewhat interesting but somewhat repetitive by the time you reach the third strata.Overall, I enjoyed the game there's a few spots that detracted from walking away from a good feeling upon completion.1. When the player chooses to make the attack into the final dungeon of the Finale chapter, there's a significant amount of going-ons involving the supporting cast. This going-ons are somewhat lengthy and rendered with the game's normal graphics. It really should have been an animated cut scene. It definitely feels like Nihon Falcom was aiming for epic but it kind of falls flat. It just doesn't feel like it captures the scale of what they are trying to show you, at all. For me, this dropped my vibe and made my interest dip somewhat.2. There's a ton of typos. I most noticed it in the Combat Orders. Good luck finding an order that does what it's text says it will do; it'll do something like what the order says it does but not what the order actually says. This is usually just percentages being wrong but there were some other ones. Also If the game properly explained how to set tagalongs once they were available I missed it. I figured it out but it was a couple of hours after they became available.3. The reverie corridor! A place for all your people to come together and bond. It has a bunch of time-sinking content that opens after the main story ends. I like some of it, but it kind of drags and IDK if I'd bother doing it at all a second time. There's a bit of foreshadowing that happens in here, but I bet there's a social media content creator that has/will make a video showing/telling the foreshadowing you need to know going into the next game.?. It's not a criticism of this game, but it takes too damn long for the games in the Trails series to get an official English translation.But I did have fun with it, mostly.

A good continuation and closure to the Crossbell Independence storyline. But on the other, the post-game stuff left me feeling a little drained in the end. _childDocuments_.review: There are many thing I would like to say about this game, and the series as a whole.Trails into Reverie is essentially the last 3 chapters of a 50 chapter book. Its sole purpose is to conclude the two main story arcs from the previous games; with a nod to the original. That being said, if you have not played the previous games, I cannot recommend playing this. The heart and warmth and depth that are so key to the Legend of Heroes series is not present in this game. However, that is to be expected, as that level of love and care that took many games worth to establish cannot be replicated in a single title. Legend of Heroes is a fantastic series, and you owe it to yourself to start it from the beginning, or at the very least start at the Trails of Cold Steel. In my first few hours into the game, i felt it was rushed, empty, lacking features from previous games, and it took me a while to realize the expectations I had were misplaced. This was meant to be a finale, not an entire new Legend of Heroes storyline.So I will repeat myself, if you have not played the previous games, do not play this, or you wont enjoy yourself.However, to the returning fans, heed what I said previously, do not go into Trails of Reverie with the same expectations I had, it accomplishes what it sets out to do, and thats it; nothing more, nothing less.I will advise, however, you play on hard or higher, ESPECIALLY if you are carrying over save data from previous games. I made the mistake of playing on normal, carrying over data, and the game was laughably easy.To the Legend of Heroes team: thank you, for years of tears, shivers down the spine, laughter, and enjoyment, and I cannot wait to see what the future holds.

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best parts of the Trails/ Legends of Heroes series is that it takes its time to tell the story, delving into the motivations of many characters  - and not just heroes. It also probes deeper questions, inclding what it means to live and what it means to be human as well as the nature of time and  possibility.  This jrpg tops any other jrpg out there in terms of storytelling, gameplay features, art, heart and execution. The final part is reminiscent of Trails 3rd, but gives a lot more freedom in  going into the reverie. I loved Phantasma and I think Reverie delivers and ties many emotional loose ends. At the same time, it continues stories that will still take their time to grow in Kuro, pretty sure. like Renne. The storytelling is very moving and satisfying, with a positive and inspiring message that is very important to me.  Thank you for the story, Falcom, writers, Nis, Xseed, translators... for Olivert, Schera, Lloyd, Rean, Estelle, Joshua, Randy, Mireille, Kevin, Ries, Jusis, and so many other npcs  whose fates are tied, who have formed so many strong bonds and relationships. I love pretty much all of them.  and ...the unexpected hidden playable character in Reverie. I did not expect that.  Gives amazing depth to the character. Well-done!  Also note: post-game make sure to try talking to characters in the reverie corridor as different characters -you can control who walks around the garden then, and some conversations are worthwhile. Try Jusis and the secret character, for instance. I love Oliver and Schera one. THe side stories in the reverie are also fantastic. It's trulyl a game worth EVERY penny. This is the best jrpg ever and that's it! Play it all, from the start/ It's a journey worthwhile unlike many otherx out there, playing Reverie only made me want to go back and replay the entire series so far, to again experience how they all got to this point, how thye grew.... _childDocuments_.review: Before saying anything else, it is important to make clear that this game is pretty much "Trails of Cold Steel V". Even though it doesn't share the series name and that the Erebonian Story ended on Trails of Cold Steel IV, this one picks right after the end of it and the game will act as if you played it. In no point during gameplay it will explain who those characters are or what happened before.DO NOT START THE TRAILS SERIES FROM THIS ONE.With that in mind, if you played the Trails of Cold Steel series and liked it, you will like this one too. The gameplay loop is pretty much the same, with the tradicional balance between fighting areas and exploration/npc interaction areas (even though it seems to be pending more to interactions, with smaller enemy areas - this is fixed by the return of the Reverie Corridor from Cold Steel II - A randomly generated area filled with enemies for you to grind against). The graphics are improved just enough to look like a new game, but mantain the traditional cartoony feel. The textures are still lacking and ambients and debris are quite blocky and both feel dated, but they do their job.The Port seems good, the game runs well, with not many glitches or bugs (I only experienced 1 major bug during a boss fight that forced me to close and reopen the game, but that didn't happen the second time - As in any RPG, the advice I give is: Save before any major event, just to be sure)So, TLDR - If you enjoyed the Trails of Cold Steel Series, you will enjoy this one, if you haven't, there is nothing different here to change your mind.If you played the Trails from/to Azure, I recomend this game as it brings Lloyd and the party back to the forefront and closes the story on Crossbell (but you need to play the Cold Steel series or dive veeery deep into the wikis to understand it).And If you have been playing since Trails in the Sky and picked every single one since...I really don't know why you are reading this, we both know you are going to pick it.

_childDocuments_.review: You've probably heard of the technical issues. There is no excusing them, especially given how long we waited for this game to be localized. However, if you're playing on Normal mode, the lack of link attacks for certain characters will not impede your progress. You'll still be able to enjoy this really awesome game and experience the story - so if you're holding back while waiting for a patch, just know that unless you're trying to challenge yourself you can probably handle things. Anyway, as for the actual game itself: It rules! As a big fan of Skies 3, I think this one captures what that game was going for very well. I have a long way to go, I'm sure, but it has been a great ride so far. Make sure to play all the minigames and do all the daydreams - they include some top tier content.

_childDocuments_.review: You probably already know whether you want to play this, but as someone who was really disappointed with Trails of Cold Steel 4 I'll note that I enjoyed Reverie more than any of the Cold Steel games. You should definitely play Zero and Azure first if you haven't already though, not just because they're great games but because Reverie very much expects you to have played them - the Crossbell characters and setting are far more prominent than they were in Cold Steel 3 & 4 and parts of the story are a direct follow-up to Azure.Sadly it has to be said that there are a _lot_ of gameplay-related translation errors, things like ability/item descriptions and mission descriptions (e.g. Laura's self-buff craft which grants completely different buffs than the description says it does). Most of the localization is pretty well done but parts of it were obviously rushed (or just not edited) - the NPC dialogue in the final chapter has typos and grammatical errors galore, plus several instances of characters referring to a location using a different name translation than what the main story dialogue uses. There's also one lategame instance of the "Helmord" soldat being mistranslated as "Hell Mode", which is funny but obviously a mistake.The translation errors weren't a dealbreaker for me but they did occasionally take me out of the experience; I really hope they clean it up before moving on and then do better with the next game in the series, because Cold Steel 3 & 4 didn't have this many obvious mistakes (at least after CS4's translation got patched).

_childDocuments_.review: After ten games, so far, completely  and ported in an official manner, I of course have my favorite games and moments, but I have to say that Trails Into Reverie here is much more than I was expecting and, believe me, I had high expectations, but this game surpasses all of them, big time.I knew this was going to be the actual end of both Crossbell and Erebonia’s sagas, but Nihon Falcom went above and beyond all possible expectations, honestly, if there’s such a thing as being too satisfied…that’d be me right now, after playing this game, including all the post-game content of course.Let’s take a small detour from the review itself to talk about  and, at this point, this is the part that surprised me the least, because the game has , as it is tradition with the ports produced by PH3.On my  and  this game performs quite similarly as Cold Steel III and IV, so I basically played the whole game at Max Settings, 1620p DLDSR downsampled resolution to 1080p native, with fullscreen MSAA 4x too, and very much stable and locked 60 FPS, at all times, not a single drop in like 100 hours of playtime.It is possible to play at 1440p and locked 120 FPS, reducing the amount of MSAA to 2x, but I prefer the maximum image quality possible and 60 FPS, for a game like this.This game I also feel it looks slightly better than both Cold Steel III and IV, it’s not a huge difference but, considering it is the last entry using the old engine…it serves as a good send off for it and I think it looks pretty decent all things considered, especially with the extra PC specific settings that we’re used to get in these excellent ports by Durante and his team.Having the  available within the game itself, instead of a Launcher, is a great QoL addition too.Continuing with the regular aspect of the review, well I won’t get into spoilers but it’s obvious that they went all out with the , but the good type, the one that’s done , aimed at fans of the series as a whole, making it so worth it if you played the previous arcs.This was strongly solidified for me when I started doing the  episodes and, let me be honest here, Trails in the Sky the 3rd is a favorite of mine, not just for what it represents, an obvious connection point between Liberl and both the Crossbell and Erebonian arcs, but also because of the Door System it had.With Reverie here, the Daydreams felt pretty much like those Doors, they are all really great, I enjoyed them so much, and of course they even added a couple of special ones teasing the “future” in the series, or more almost like the present at this point, hopefully soon for all of us waiting for the official Kuro No Kiseki English Localization and Voice Over announcement (I sincerely cannot wait to meet and learn about the new cast and their actors).Speaking of  and their actors…simply bravo, all of them, incredible performances all around, going from the main protagonists in their respective series to all the supporting characters, they are all great and this is something NIS America seems to improve with every new entry, and I hope they continue to do so with the Kuro games.I feel I’ve spent so many hundred hours listening to these English actors by now (nothing against their Japanese counterparts, I know many of them from lots of other games and projects too, they’re fantastic), but to me having played all of these games (where available) with both voice languages, made me appreciate how good of a job the English Direction team did when choosing actors.It is not so much about sounding exactly like the Japanese actor per se, but how they convey the personality of their respective character, and I believe they all did an excellent job.This is also greatly enhanced by the obvious fact that Falcom upped the quality of their , and no doubt Reverie has some of the most well animated scenes in the series so far, and I am well aware this continues, and improves, in the upcoming games, so I'm thankful for that, because it does adds so much to these already amazing characters and their actors' performances.I personally loved the three Routes in the game, almost equally, there's a ton of character development in them, but I have to say that the "Imprerial Picnicking Squad" takes the cake, they were so fun and engaging, being "new" characters, the writing was incredible.Lastly, as it couldn’t be any other way, the  in this game is also fantastic, especially the new tracks, some of the new combat theme songs are quite catchy and I can’t get them out of my head honestly, they’ll be there for a while I feel.Having one last chance to listen to a certain track for the final post-game boss was also quite hype, couldn’t have been any other track, it was the correct one : )All of the new added small  changes too, compared to Cold Steel IV felt quite welcome as well, and I really love the Reverie Corridor system, since to me the Trails series is, currently, one of the best Turn Based JRPG series out there, so having a chance to battle enemies to my heart’s content feels great, while also being rewarding at the same time.I’m really looking forward to the future of the series, now that we’ve crossed that half point.

_childDocuments_.review: In our review, we won’t give you any story spoilers for this or any of the other Trails games. We’ll only give you a basic premise of the first few hours of this title’s plot.Trails into the Reverie is an amazing conclusion and epilogue to both the Erebonia and Crossbell arcs in the Trails series (or Kiseki as it’s named in Japan). It’s a very fun turn-based JRPG with many customization options for making distinct character builds, many difficulty options, many collectibles and many quality of life improvements making the gameplay the most fun it’s ever been. This is the 10th entry in the Trails franchise and in all honesty this wouldn’t be the best place to start if you’re new to this game series. The plot of this game follows from Trails of Cold Steel 4, which follows from 1-3 of course, and it also follows from Trails to Zero and Trails to Azure. It follows from Trails in the Sky 1 to 3 as well, though the other arcs are extremely important to complete. So in a way, this game actually concludes two arcs rather than just one making it even more important to play the older games. While I used to suggest you could play the earlier Cold Steel games without playing the other games, this game really feels like the “Avengers” of the Trails games, with an all-star cast of characters solving a new conflict in Crossbell.In this game you actually have three parties of characters, meaning you have three protagonists. You can switch between these groups after the prologue at almost any time barring certain exceptions. Some dungeons later in the game actually require multiple parties to explore at once to trigger switches for the other party, which is not something I seen in JRPGs too frequently and is certainly welcome (Infinite Undiscovery is one rare game that did this a while ago with great dungeon designs).It’s really fun and novel because you can do whoever’s story you’re interested in first, and if you even feel like just changing your mind you can just switch whenever and not lose progress. At first I was overwhelmed with all of the equipment and quartz I had to manage for all of the characters, but I got used to it quickly and even though there are three parties of characters you get used to them quickly.You play as Rean, Lloyd, and the mysterious character “C” who I won’t spoil of course. The former two are the protagonists of the Cold Steel and Trails to Zero/Azure arcs, respectively. If you’ve played those games (and I won’t spoil them of course) you’d probably be wondering where the plot would go from there because those arcs seemed to conclude rather nicely. But this game starts off with Lloyd in Crossbell, and managed to introduce a new conflict well without making it feel forced.I was also a bit tired because I thought there would be character bloat with the addition of a new protagonist “C” and his new party of members. But surprisingly, C along with their group ended up being my favorite characters in this game! I can’t elaborate more on this without giving spoilers and the C reveal is the main reveal of this game, but they have really great character development and their attitude and how they approach problems is very different than Rean or LLoyd, who are both very plain “straight shooter” kind of characters.I genuinely wouldn’t have minded if the entire game was centered around C and his party, that’s how interesting he was as a character! The routes definitely don’t have the same quality, but most of them are generally well-made without being too repetitive. Whereas Cold Steel 4 had a rushed ending, Trails into Reverie actually helps flesh it out and fix the ending of Cold Steel 4, retroactively fixing rushed plot points.There are numerous callbacks to older characters from the series as well and this game ends up being an opportunity to showcase combinations of characters you don’t get to see interact. All of the Trails games have NPCs that tell you about the world and current events, and you can talk to them after every plot event for completely new dialogue, resulting in hundreds of pages’ worth of extra dialogue and world-building if you choose to pursue it.I’m not too crazy for that, I generally talk to all NPCs in a new area before and after a big plot event and that’s about it, but I noticed this Trails game did one thing different: it has a lot more important NPCs such as old playable characters or old major supporting characters from the older games which is a very great attention to detail.The art style is very charming, and with every new title released the graphics improve more and more. There’s no 2D sprites or clunky models anymore, the characters all have really great designs and models. The cities genuinely feel like large bustling cities, while the rural towns and villages manage to capture a beautiful rustic feel.The soundtrack manages to capture the moods of the areas and many tracks in this title are from older titles, but re-made with modern technology such as in many of the districts of Crossbell or St. Ursula Medical College. There aren’t too many criticisms I have regarding this game. A small issue is that this is a shorter game compared to most mainline Trails games. Usually Trails games have very long main story modes and when you do sidequests you’d end up with an 80+ hour playthrough. This game’s main story isn’t so long though, taking us about 30-45 hours to complete. There is a lack of major story sidequests like all other Trails games (but you do get character episodes to compensate). I was also disappointed by the lack of Divine Knight battles, which was basically fighting in giant magical mechs in all the previous Cold Steel games. It is a little odd seeing Crossbell facing another dire situation, considering how many back-to-back hardships the country has had in the past few games.But although the main story of this game is shorter, this game makes up for it with the “True Reverie Corridor”. It’s tricky to summarize what the TRC is briefly, but it’s basically a non-canon area you can warp to anytime during the game. Plotwise, everybody loses their memories temporarily while in the TRC. You can use all your party members, or basically any playable character from the older titles, to explore randomly generated floors to get treasures and you can grind and buy new equipment as well as complete missions for rewards.If you care about story, there are memories in the TRC which are sorted into episodes that explore certain supporting characters in-depth. There are post-game bosses as well. Trails into Reverie does an excellent job of placing the player into a beautifully crafted world filled with well-developed characters, intricate storytelling, and addicting gameplay. Trails into Reverie improves upon the older titles on a technical level, and all of the returning locations from older games feel visually distinct and character models have are more detailed than ever. Having three protagonists was ambitious, but it worked out well and the new cast of characters in C’s route are extremely interesting, with distinct personalities, motivations and backstories. The turn-based gameplay is fun, but also accessible and if you want to break the game you can. There’s a lot of customization through equipment and quartz which changes the spells your characters can use or you can grind levels to gain stats. The soundtrack features both new original tracks as well as re-made tracks from older games and they really manage to capture the emotional moments in the game. This isn’t a perfect game, as some of the routes do drag on for a bit too long and it is true that the game does recycle certain areas in a bad way such as the highways you always see, but generally it’s not too egregious. Just be certain to play the other games first, as this game really feels like a conclusion, or even an epilogue to the old Trails games.

name: Age of Wonders 4
detailed_description: Expansion Pass 2 About the Game Rule a fantasy realm of your own design in Age of Wonders 4 ! Explore new magical realms in Age of Wonders’ signature blend of 4X strategy and turn-based tactical combat. Control a faction that grows and changes as you expand your empire with each turn. Triumph Studios’ award-winning strategy series has emerged into a new age, evolving the game’s iconic empire building, role-playing, and warfare to the next level. A new storytelling event system and hugely customizable empires provide an endlessly replayable experience, where each game adds a new chapter to your ever-growing saga. Powerful Wizard Kings have returned to the realms to reign as gods among mortals. Claim and master the Tomes of Magic to evolve your people, and prepare for an epic battle that will determine the ages to come. Craft your followers by combining bodily forms, societal traits and arcane powers. Build anything from a clan of cannibal halflings to mystic moon elves, or recreate your favorite fantasy tropes Seek powerful tomes of magic to enchant your armies and evolve your people! See your people physically change as they morph into angelic beings or scions of chaos to face their enemies. Seek glory through brutal domination, cunning alliances, or ultimate arcane knowledge, and write your legacy into the very fabric of the realm itself! Every choice opens up new possibilities and tactical advantages; deep, multilayered strategy allows you to try new tactics or explore new powers at every turn Tactical turn-based battles bring your armies to life, showcasing their power in an environment shaped by your decisions. From skirmishes with roaming monsters to vast sieges with dozens of units on each side, with the addition of a morale system and more features, every battle brings a fresh challenge Tremendous variety in empires, units, and environments keep the game endlessly replayable. Age of Wonders is more moddable and open-ended than ever in the series’ history Explore a new realm with each game - or create your own! Challenge new variations and combinations of locations and features, from frozen wastelands ruled by ice queens to desolated ruins where dragons roam A new event system provides unexpected levels of storytelling for 4X games. See your decisions shape the world around you, from growing cities and roaming armies to world-warping magic effects Guide your empire to greatness - but the story doesn’t end with your victory or defeat! Ascend your rulers to an in-game pantheon and unlock ways to further customize your experience. Encounter your own creations as potential rivals or allies in subsequent games, and experience the next chapter in your own story!

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5 As of the Dragon Dawn DLC, my opinion:PROS: High level of sandbox, returning playable leaders from AoW2, rebalancing and reinvention of old series mechanics, as well as a whole host of new gameplay mechanics that are both unique and fun. Mixing and matching race traits adds a lot of customization and replayability, and mixing and matching those traits with cultures and tomes allow for some really cool and rewarding gamplay combos.CONS: Overall unit balance issues, strategic AI is a cheating bastard as always, minimalist story (and no flavor text on units or spells!), and they mostly did away with the "empire" meta-game mode of AoW3 and Planetfall. The Pantheon is still there as some kind of overarching progression, but the rewards are mostly just leader cosmetics--that's mostly my personal preference anyway, if they kept "empire" in two titles and ditched it in a third, it must not have been popular enough to keep around.
