_childDocuments_.review: Where to begin with this game. We went in with what I would say were reasonable expectations. However, even with these taken into account, i feel the game has failed on too many accounts. Far, far too many accounts.For a start, its bad.Like, really bad.For a $50 game, one would expect that it has been play-tested by a human being, or at least a willing one. Has anyone actually managed to finish this game. Are they ok? Do they need help? Help from a guide that is. Because you need one. Even the online walked throughs (plural) we were forced to watch got lost.Without a doubt, the puzzles are the worst, and most prominent part of the game. They don't connect, they're nonlinear and at times the game will just tell you that you should know where to look. You don't. There's little to no guidance, you're aimlessly wandering around for a new area to open, desperately hoping for some sweet relief from the suffering, soulless, joyless, monotony of the the puzzle gameplay. Don't even get me started on the planets. And why do you just have to take random pictures of things unprompted? Is there an indication? I didn't see it. And another thing, why can't we just open doors by clicking them. Why must we slide the mouse halfway across the living room to get anywhere in the game. My wrist will never be the same. Don't even get me started on the drawers. Quick question, why the on earth is there an inventory item limit, in a puzzle-based horror game? How does walking back to an item-storage-safe elevate the gameplay experience in any notable metric? All it seems to do is elevate my blood pressure?But the horror on the other hand, or the one scene that I saw before refunding the game and writing this review, was excellent. Some of the best horror I've seen, and I've seen a fair bit. It's honestly tragic that it's buried beneath the weight of all the randomly generated safe codes. Perhaps I'm, being too harsh, there's a lot of love and passion put in by the devs, and they should be proud. Just in future, please stick to the horror, limit the puzzles by a good 1000 - 2000 percent.

_childDocuments_.review: I had the privilege of being able to play it a few days before the official release.I must say that for me, it is the horror game of the year.Graphics: 10/10The graphics department is incredible, everything looks very realistic, and is taken care of to the extreme. There are no objects that pass through walls, and there is none in the scene that are not taken care of in extreme detail. It shows that nothing was done in a hurry, and I think that one of the points that makes each element have maximum detail, is that there are no purchased asset packages and everything you see in the game was created and worked by themselves. That adds a lot of points when it comes to differentiating itself from generic games, with generic assets.Sound: 10/10This section is the one that plays the most important role in the game in order to make it a true horror game.It's a delight to notice the different layers of sound that the game offers. The 3D sound makes the immersive element sublime, and it features a random sound system that makes the atmosphere of the game always haunting, providing a sensation of extreme suspense.Gameplay: 10/10Totally enjoyable, with unique mechanics, achieving its very own identity. It perfectly mixes the use of the camera as a main element both to advance in the story and solve puzzles, as well as to serve as a defense weapon.It combines psychological horrror and survival horror in a perfect manner.Another point in favor in the gameplay section is that it has collectibles that you can obtain throughout the game, and it features an achievement system that (for fans of playing through a game 100%) is very satisfying, and allows one to replay the game to get them all.As a last point in this section, regarding replayability, the game implements a system that when played again, all the puzzles, scares and others, change, making the experience of playing the game a bit different each time.Story 10/10What is a good horror game without a good story behind it?In this case, the game has a highly profound story, where the player dives into other rich sub-stories.These are not separated by chapters, which is appreciated, but they progressively converge and merge with the main storyline in an exceptional way.And a special mention to the voice actors who actually ACT and not just narrate like in other games.MADiSON 10/10I believe that this horror game doesn't come as a successor of any other, and in fact, it has truly managed to find its own identity, and I firmly believe that it will establish itself as a horror classic.

_childDocuments_.review: -Short and heavily padded. There's not much there, and what is there is... okay, I guess.The game starts out promising, with a good atmosphere and an ambiguous premise that leaves lots of unanswered questions, though the game ends up mostly playing everything straight.Most of your time won't be spent engaging with the story or horror set pieces (some of which are admittedly pretty good) but instead juggling items between your safe and an extremely limited inventory that seems to only exist to increase how often you have to backtrack to that safe and solving some rudimentary (but occasionally tedious) puzzles. Sometimes you'll die and have to spend time redoing puzzles and rejuggling your inventory to regain lost progress.None of these things are cardinal sins, or even necessarily all that bad on their own, but even with all that extra the game is only a few hours long. I don't want to harp on run time too much, games aren't just about length, but... this game has five mazes in it. Five. Plus the aforementioned tedious inventory system. Multiple 'chased by a monster while trying to solve a puzzle' sections where I died an embarrassingly large number of times... and for all of that the game couldn't break three hours. My 4.7 hours of total playtime is playing it through twice. That just feels really bad for the game's price point.When you actually are engaging with the game's content, it's a little hit or miss. The set pieces are decent, the atmosphere can be spooky... but the story never really feels like it takes off and the main monster is a bit silly looking. It just never felt like it did enough, to the point where I almost thought I got a false ending the first time around and the game was meant to open up to more content.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one for me, because I do think Madison does quite a few things good, but it does an equal number of things very poorly. Speaking from my experience with the game, it runs very poorly. I'm well above the recommended specs, yet I encountered constant crashes, freezes, and stutters. Usually while some big story thing was happening, so I wouldn't even get the full picture because it was like watching a stop motion film at times. It would also crash right after transitioning out of an area, which was just constantly annoying. There's also the matter of having little to no direction. It works for some games, because most of the time, you'll find something that tells you where you need to go and it'll be in your inventory when you need to read it. This game is literally just walking around taking pictures of EVERYTHING until something clicks and works. There's no rhyme or reason for it, and it slows down the game significantly. I can't tell you how many times I would backtrack all the way across the house just to realize I went the wrong way, then I have to very slowly walk all the back. Graphically speaking, when it wasn't crashing, freezing, or stuttering, it looked great. The enemies are well designed and each invoked their own sense of dread, though I fail to see how one of the enemies had any bearing on the story, and I'm sure we all know which one I'm talking about. I just wish we had been able to see more of them. The rooms in the house are equally well designed, giving off a vibe that something horrible that you don't know about yet happened in that house. The other locations are nice too, but some definitely aren't as memorable and some are quite tedious to get through. The puzzles are mediocre at best. They are very tedious and leave little to no clue on how you're supposed to go about completing them, which is fine, as some things you can figure out by yourself, but there were some puzzles I just gave up on and looked at a guide on how to finish them, because they are so unclear. Overall, I don't think this game is really worth the $35 price tag. Maybe if it were $20-$25, I could see it, but this game clearly was only trying to capitalize on the trends at the time with constant jump scares and somewhat creepy atmosphere. If you're interested, get it on sale and save yourself some money, because you won't come back to play it again after you finish it once.

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the better horror games I've played, and it is rated pretty highly if you do some online research for the "best/scariest" horror. I ended up buying it for the Halloween sale price, so my perspective is paying about half price of it's usual retail cost. That being said, the game does have some "holes" if you want to focus on the negative. I definitely see some valid complaints in other reviews, and I noticed some of the same things, but I didn't really mind because the game was great in most ways.                                                                                  Puzzles:               I think the worst part of the game, and the complaint I agree with the most is the puzzle design. First, there are several aspects of the puzzles that are simply not solvable until you progress further into the story, get more information, or get an item you need. Yet they are fully available for you to attempt to solve them in the meantime. You could easily waste hours trying to figure out something that is right in front of you, but is simply not possible to solve because of the way this works. I think that's why the play through time is estimated at 8-12 hours. Not that it's a short game, but if you spend upwards of 10-12 hours on this game, you were definitely stuck on puzzles for quite some time. I realized about half way through that I preferred playing with a written guide, that would give me a hint if I got stuck, but wouldn't spoil the game like a video walk-through would.               My second complaint about the puzzles is just how flat out difficult they are at times. I understand every game has it's varying levels of difficulty, and the puzzles didn't ruin the game for me overall. However I always prefer a game that I can just open up, play start to finish without any aid, and get my horror fix. The best example of this I can think of this being done correctly is "Infliction" which had a nice level of challenging, yet not so difficult that you can't figure it out on your own in a timely manner. Madison is more along the lines of PT, which felt like it was virtually impossible to beat without looking things up.                                                                                       Sound:          The sound design is good, except for the random noises that seem to not be associated with any in game event or object. For example, quite often you will hear a door slam, creak, or other noises that has no merit whatsoever on the game play, but is only there for the atmosphere. This lead me to check several doors that were in vicinity of the sound, until I realized it was just random. It didn't bother me once I found out this was the case, but I can see how some players could find that annoying.                                                                                        Jumpscare:             The jump scares were great for 80% of the game, visually, sound wise, and the timing of them. However there were 2-3 small parts of the game, in which you are pretty much repeatedly jump scared, to the point where you knew they were coming. That puts you in a place of being annoyed by the loud sound, and defeats the purpose of actually being unexpected.                                                                                          Story:No complaints about the story or voice acting, I thought that this was one of the games strong suits.                                                                                         Visuals:Not much to say, you can see the trailer video and the screenshots, the game has really good graphics and atmosphere.Overall recommend it if you are willing to look past the flaws that are few and far between.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't justify this game for the 34.99 price tag. However if you catch it on sale, it may be worth it. It took me 8ish hours to 100% the game, could of took me far less but I wasn't interested in rushing my first play through. The game itself is revolved around a cursed camera and the effects it has had on the main character "Luca" and his family. The story starts off well but in my opinion losses steam about half way through. There are only two portions of this game where you can be harmed or die, other portions are puzzles with clues laid around the house etc. The puzzles are generally mild, and if played on normal difficulty the photos and clues are marked by Polaroids lying around. To me the ambiance of the house was over done, creepy sounds like crashes, thing being moved, tapping etc are just way to frequent and thus takes out the horror element. There are a few decent timed jump scares although not from the monster entity, which the name of the monster just took out what little immersion I had left by the ending. Overall I give MADiSON a 5/10  graphics are nice, movement is smooth, but the dwindling story and fumbling the ambiance of the environment are just things I cant get past and the price is just soooo high for what this is. It is possible to speed run this game in under 1.5 hours, there's even achievements to take less than 40 pictures and beat the game in 2.5 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: A Haunting Masterpiece That Redefines HorrorRating: ★★★★★From the eerie echoes of the past to the heart-stopping moments of the present, MADiSON delivers an unparalleled psychological horror experience that both terrifies and captivates. Every element of this game—from its chilling soundtrack and meticulously crafted atmosphere to the ingenious puzzles and compelling storyline—is designed to keep you on the edge of your seat.The game's use of a Polaroid camera to interact with the environment is not only unique but adds an intense, unsettling layer to the gameplay. This mechanic ingeniously blends the narrative and the gameplay, making you feel like you're truly part of this terrifying world. Each snapshot not only progresses the story but also brings new fears to life, making you dread what might develop next.The graphics are visually stunning, with environments so detailed and lifelike that you can almost feel the chill of the ghostly corridors and smell the mustiness of long-abandoned rooms. Coupled with the game’s exceptional sound design, you’re in for an immersive experience that few horror games can match.Voice acting and character development are top-notch, adding depth to a story that is as engaging as it is horrifying. The lore is deep, full of dark secrets waiting to be uncovered, making each playthrough as thrilling as the last.MADiSON is not just a game; it's a work of art that pushes the boundaries of the horror genre. It's a psychological journey that haunts you long after you've put down the controller. For anyone who claims to be a fan of horror, MADiSON is an absolute must-play. It’s a terrifyingly beautiful game that will leave you begging for more yet fearful of what lies ahead.Highly recommended for those who think they’ve seen everything horror has to offer. Prepare to be proven wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for the perceptive, poor game for those who get distracted easily. My rating is reflective of certain aspects of the metagame, not necessarily for the game as a whole.As far as a horror game goes, fantastic; definitely top-of-the-shelf material. It keeps a consistent atmosphere throughout, keeping you guessing if another emaciated figure is around the corner waiting to tear your face off. The story, while par for the course, is derivative in how it's told through the eyes of the victim and through context clues laid out along your journey- not necessarily for that reason alone, but rather how it's executed. I choose to be slightly vague here so as not to ruin others' experiences. The scares are great, loud, and well executed. While at times I found myself irritated at the constant scares (it wasn't necessarily the games fault, but rather mine (maybe), more on that later), I often found myself taken aback by how the game mechanics weaved perfectly with the executions of each moment- again remaining vague to not ruin anything.But the puzzles... therein lies my biggest problem with this game.I'm not entirely sure, but I found this game tedious to try and solve my way through. I feel as though the average playtime of this game bloats up about 2 hours with how unhelpful the game is at conveying any scrap or crumb of how to move forward and leaves you to it to wander around the same house aimlessly until you find the one thing you missed 1 hour earlier that then sets you into motion once more. Keep in mind that this case could be entirely individual, I could just be a tunnel-visioned individual, but I feel justified in this gripe given that several of the achievements for this game is completing sections within certain time frames. I don't know, just a thought.I don't think this game is for me. It may be that I prefer a more railroad-style horror game that leads me to where I need to go with each puzzle being in a more isolated environment, but who's to say? _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's a puzzle game in a haunted house setting. 6/10Only giving a thumbs up for this because the house and environments are well made and designed, the story in general is serious and spooky, and also because of the last 20 minutes of the story which is really true horror.BUT, 95% of the 6hs experience is ruined by the puzzles which deviate your focus from the setting, and just 30mins into the game when you realize that there is no threat, you don't have to be careful about anything because the only things that happen are jumpscares around the corners while you're moving from place to place to solve puzzles. That's it.Also VERY frustating to realize that the ongoing looping sounds you hear (doors opening and closing, objets being dropped or dragged on the floor, etc) are just that, background sounds on loop that represent actions that are not really happening in-game. There was only two instances I recall of actually seeing a chair dropping back on the floor in front of me, and a cabinet being dragged violently in a hallway, but I'm sure those were scripted story events and not random. The whole experience would be so much better (and different) if there were events like this randomly happening (it's a haunted house ffs) instead of looping background sounds that are just fillers and not even really happening.The final sequence of the game it is really what the game should have been about the whole time. You have to escape from the demon, which is a great horror character btw (in the likes of The Babadook), but sadly he's not given the deserved attention throughout the experience appearing only as jumpscares that since the beginning you understand that don't change anything in your game because all you have to do is solve puzzles, get this from here and use there, match colors, match shapes, add, substract numbers...very very boring.I expected so much more from this. It is a well made and written game, but what ruined it for me is that since the beginning it's a puzzle game in a haunted house setting with jumpscares in between.

_childDocuments_.review: Madison is a great walking simulator. The challenge lies in how cryptic this game can be. The puzzles became quite straightforward once I grasped the actual goal for each respective puzzle.Now, for some hot takes I have:The main criticism I have about this game is that, for almost the entire game, the jump scares posed absolutely no threat to the player. There are only two parts of the game where enemies can potentially kill you, and deaths are relatively forgiving in terms of loss of progress. Compare this to 'Visage,' where in every chapter, once you reach a certain point, you are constantly in danger if your character's sanity is low enough.I can't stress this enough, but if your walking simulator lacks enemies or any kind of threat that can kill you, then what's the point of calling it a horror game? This is precisely why I loathed Layers of Fear.The strong aspects of this game are the graphics, audio, atmosphere, tension (up until the realisation that there are hardly any enemies that can kill you for most of the game), and the puzzles. The story excels in the themes it delves into, and the voice acting in all the tape recordings is not only convincing but also deeply disturbing.The tension created by the audio soundscape consistently keeps you on edge, always anticipating a jump scare just around the corner. And that anticipation, wondering what might lurk around the next corner or what could suddenly appear at any second, is far more terrifying than any of the jump scares the game provides. After a while, the jump scares in the game start to feel overly predictable, especially Despite the lack of enemies capable of killing you, all the positive aspects in which this game excels outweigh this single gripe I have. I still consider it a good horror experience, and I genuinely hope to see more from this developer. We need more well-executed psychological horrors in the vein of 'Visage' and 'P.T.,' with attention to detail, thought, and a proper audio soundscape, all of which 'Madison' excels at

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep it short:+ great graphics, good pacing, mostly clear objectives, only two chase sequences (doesn't get old too quick, spaced out), succeeded where PT and Visage failed, great story, good scares (had to actually stop playing for little breaks because of anxiety), camera is a cool mechanic (can review photos which was awesome for puzzles and memorizing codes and whatnot)- maybe too reliant on jumpscares as opposed to suspense building, can easily get lost or not know what to do for stretches of time (mostly clear doesn't equal always clear), way too f*****g dark in some sections, can cheese whole chase sequences without much effort, not long enough imo, played too hard into demonology without having a fulfilling ending or lore behind Blue Knees, Grandma (Eli), Dad, Mom, etc. overall, although lacking in story and lore, and perhaps a bit too short (beat it first try in under 6 hours), everything else is horror perfection. There was never a moment I genuinely felt safe or not being followed. Wish it did less jumpscares (let's move on from these tropes please devs), but I am happy for the price I paid, which was agreeable given the game feeling well-built without any bugs or glitches except 1 where my fps dropped from 144 to 96 for maybe 3 seconds. _childDocuments_.review: If you like games like Visage and PT demo this is the game for you.  I picked this game up for £22 and have already enjoyed over three hours of game play.  I've read there's about 6/8 hours of story in total but I will be going through it multiple times to collect all the extras and spot things I missed in the first play through and of course to extend the life of the game. The sound effects and background noises are so creepy and make you feel uneasy all the time.  You have the feeling of always looking over your shoulder expecting things to come for you.  For such a small development team this game is very impressive.  Graphically it's great and the lighting and shadows add to the atmosphere, but the sounds make it.  I've been impressed by a lot of the little details around the game with some great bits of text and writing on the walls adding more to the depth of the story.  The game really does a great job of creating the feeling of dread and consistently leaving you wondering what's coming next.  Also the puzzles are pretty nice, not to hard, but they also don't just hold your hand through it and encourages a bit of thinking too.Time to change my kegs....

_childDocuments_.review: Currently sitting in my own piss as I write this:I was impressed by the work that had to have gone behind the art to making this game. BLOODIOUS GAMES did an amazing job capturing the horror of sitting in front of your PC or console trying to contemplate pausing the game or continuing through knowing your heart rate will rise with your blood pressure.The graphics were up to par with date creating a unique style where I would say has a common ground with something similar of P.T (Silent Hill) if you can remember that demo that was never fully finished. More of a grain feeling yet still solid texture throughout the game. It gave off a vibe that would keep your hairs erect the entire time. The mechanics were not difficult to control and there were not many buttons that you had to control to manage through the game. Pretty straight forward and honestly, couldn't see it working out well if there was a lot of buttons and unsettling nerves racing through your body. No one would be able to finish the game.The sound was very particular and was always used at the right times. The great effect used was the filler sounds that kept yourself on edge and wondering whether that was something you needed to look behind you. The score was discomforting in the best way possible. I won't spoil some of the sounds and music that were used to bring the suspense of horror to the mix. Well done on this.Voice acting was great and a lot of emotion was put into the voices. This can make or break a good game if the voices are not willing to give it their all. These actors showed up and gave a good performance to keep us in the game the entire time.The story flowed well and the mystery was kept under wraps until it was the right time to feed the information you needed to stay along the path. I didn't find the story to be clunky or all over the place. It went down the line A.B.C.  I streamed this and had help from other players. My duration of game time was 7 hours but some of the people that helped me told me it took them almost three days. Saying this. The hints were very far and few. I'm not saying this is a Con. They expect you to pay to the littlest detail in the game. This can get somewhat frustrating at times but I believe they made it in hopes that people would find that the puzzles are meant to be difficult. If you are willing to brave through the frightful story of a scared boy escaping demonic possession through difficult puzzles and horrific sounds. Then this game will be just right for you. Now excuse me why I go change. 8/10-Luke

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I do recommend playing this game.In my opinion, as a horror game enthusiast, Madison did well on relaying its story. The progression of the story was good and it didn't leave me waiting too long for revelations. In terms of the game's fear factor. The jump scares are not cheap and are really placed at a time where they would really get you when you least expect it. Some interactions with the enemies may be repetitive but they are manageable and don't last too long which makes up for its repetitiveness.However, Madison immerses its players mostly in puzzle solving rather than placing them in constant fear. This can be one of the downsides of the game which pulls back its "fun/horror" factor. Some may become frustrated of the puzzles, but some may enjoy them. It depends on the person though. Overall, I would rate this game a 7.5/10, with only the puzzle parts as the main concern. Oh and I also recommend getting this game on sale (I think it should cost less but yeah the developers still earn their hardwork).BONUS RATING:This game is a bit similar to visage so let me compare both of them as reference for those who have played visage. VISAGE (9/10):-is consistent in immersing the players in constant fear in terms of atmosphere and not jump scares. There will always be a sense of danger wherever you are.-jump scares are well timed and are not repetitive.-the players are only given puzzles that are not too hard to solve.-stories are well narrated and are well told to the player which helps the player understand more about the game's context. The endings are tricky and are fun to interpret.MADISON (7.5/10):-is not consistent in immersing the players in constant fear in terms of atmosphere. Some areas feel scary, some areas feel safe. The game is a bit-reliant on jump scares.-jump scares are well timed but some are repetitive-some players may or may not have fun with solving the puzzles as some are too tedious-stories are well narrated and are well told to the player which helps the player understand more about the game's context. The ending is cryptic, dark, and open ended. It is fun to interpret.

_childDocuments_.review: Madison is a brilliantly paced and written horror game. There’s some shortcomings here and there, sure. And the plot starts to crack a bit if you scrutinize it too heavily. But it has a real arc and cadence to the storytelling, which gives it a lot of credibility as a narrative. There’s some clever foreshadowing and symbolism going on too, sort of building a picture in your subconscious as you go along. Even though the rest of the story is very cryptic and light on details. The devil is in the details here. So what starts out as a somewhat grounded murder-mystery, escalates into something between a haunted house and a fever dream. All told through the viewpoint of an unreliable narrator who’s as scared and confused as you are. In the end, it’s this sinister puzzle box of a game, terrorizing you, making you question what’s around every corner. It never reveals its hand -- keeping you guessing as to how it’s all put together. The fact that the game’s got that edge on you as a player is great. Sure, it goes a little overboard on the ambience and sound effects at times. But overall? Highly recommended if you enjoy good, focused horror experiences.

The father was great, for exemple, Madison as well  and some other recordings were pretty good, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I was face palming every time Luca (the main character was talking). He is constantly sobing and commenting on what he's discovering. He felt unsufferable.My other lower point would be more about the scary parts : some audio feedbacks are generated randomly and honestly, as first, it felt great. I was constantly looking behind me. But at some point, I felt like it was always the same kind of noise. It changes while you go through, let's say, 70% of the game, where new feedbacks and events are coming, but yeah, that, and the fact that the horror mainly remains on jumpscares.I feel like there's a big inspiration of Visage (even some feedbacks looks based on the same noises) but it lacks the oppression and the idea beauty of diverse moments.However it still is a great game but I feel like considering those points and the short lenght of it, it's still a bit expensive. _childDocuments_.review: Its an atmospheric puzzle horror game and does its job well and doesn't try too hard. The story is unique and while not deep it provides enough interesting content for what you expect of a puzzle and exploration orientated game. Its not a deep survival horror as for the most part on rails and you are more or less guided to the next experience; however, the benefit is not getting lost and confused over nonsense convoluted puzzles and physical mazes that would otherwise be frustrating on top of an already tense atmosphere. I played through blind on hard, which offers fewer hints, and would recommend doing so as even without the additional hints getting lost was difficult and I would believe additional hints and hud would remove from the existing atmosphere.I'd call this horror-light but its enjoyable in that sense. Its not trying too hard, its pacing is good, and the atmosphere ramps up appropriately as the game progresses. For its price, the length of the game, the types of challenges faced, I feel justified in what I paid and what I got out of it.

I also had screen tearing when trying to look around too fast. This same issue is also a fault of opening doors/drawers/etc. too slowly. _childDocuments_.review: Since I stopped playing video games quite a while ago and recently got back into it, I thought it's time to play a game of my favorite genre - Psychological Horror.I have now finished the game and I'm ready to write my review. This title caught my eye by scrolling through the steam store. And after looking at the trailer and screenshots I decided to give it a try. And man I have to say - I am not disappointed. This title holds it's promise! You get an eerie, blood-curdling, and hair-raising atmosphere though the whole gameplay which makes it feel very intense. The soundtrack and sound effects are very well made and fit the events and horrifyng storyline. Speaking about the storyline - The plot is very catchy and makes you want to continue playing just for the sake of finding out what happens next. The few characters all have their own petrifying past and stories which makes you feel "greatly involved" in the events happening. The puzzles and riddles aren't easy, but that's how it's supposed to be!The jumpscares often come unexpected and will definitely get your adrenaline pumping! All in all I have to say purchasing this title was a great decision and got me once again hooked to the genre. I am well aware that the price of this game is not cheap, but it will undoubtedly get you a high quality experience!My rating would result in a solid 8/10 - Can recommend to anyone interested in the genre!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, but it does contain a few issues here and there. Pro:Atmosphere is great, the visuals are appealing and well designed.Sound and Music is well done and adds well to the already unsettling atmosphere.Story is quite interesting and the puzzles are (mostly) crafty and "challenging".Game Length is okay, around 8hrs, but it depends on your own speed.Con:The voice actor is a whiny ♥♥♥♥♥ and honestly does not fit the mood and or scenario too many times. Him being whiny makes sense for the most part, but hes whiny all the time in every scenario. Even when hes talking about normal things that are not unsettling at all he sounds like hes almost crying, because theres a chair in a photograph or similar.This becomes a bit annoying after a while, but not annyoing enough to break the enjoyment of the game, so not a dealbreaker.The game relies almost entirely on cheap jump scares, yea they work, they scare/shock you, but its cheap and its quick and it does not really build up tension in the atmosphere it just makes you aware youre gonna be scared for 3 seconds and then  just continue on your way.A lot of puzzles` solutions are not really logical. You cant find a connection or a clue or make an educated guess based on logic because alot of the solutions are just randomly doing stuff that makes no sense or has no connection to anything like randomly photographing the same thing 10 times and only after having it done the 10th time something happens and you get feedback that you apparently did something that helped you progress. Or you make pictures of something that seems logical but you did it 5 seconds too early but the game does not tell you at all or gives you any kind of feedback so naturally you would think ok that was not the solution and do something else only to find out you did the right thing its just that the game enabled that solutions only a few seconds after you already tried it. Quite annyoning.All in all the game is not worth 35 bucks imo. 25-28 EUR would be a fair price for this game.Currently I would suggest to get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. I rarely say games are a must play, but this is a MUST PLAY. Puzzles weren't easy for me, but not impossible to figure out. I dislike puzzles that are too easy or too difficult. Haven't been genuinely scared from movies or games until now. The feeling of random jump scares was amazing. Great plot. Well done for an especially small team. If Bloodious Games were to collaborate on a Resident Evil or Bioshock game, it would be the #1 game ever made. Incredible ambience. Definitely play in the dark with headphones on. Very unique game. Will definitely be purchasing any games they create in the future and would have gladly paid $59.99 for this game even being as short as it was. It took me about 11 hours to complete. If I was more intelligent, maybe less time.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent a Lot of time debating writing thisI will recommend this game because I believe in supporting the developersHaving followed the development of this game for about 3 years, playing several demos that I really enjoyed, I was overall disappointed as an experienced horror gamer, I think if this was among the first 'larger' horror games I played I would've shaken in my boots so I don't feel it's fair to the developers to give this a thumbs down and I do genuinely want to see more. This is a game to pick up on sale, I don't feel it's price tag is justified for the experiencePositives;Jumpscares were well doneAtmosphere was goodPuzzles were complex yet made senseGame was BEAUTIFUL to look atBut Ultimately some of these points comes into a negativeNegatives;Jumpscares were incredibly repetitive to the point where I eventually would just say jumpscare every few minutes and I would receive a jumpscareAtmosphere was repetitive it was the same over and over again so eventually you just get numb to itPuzzles broke the game if you started one before completing anotherSpoilers Below + bugs + rant;I experienced a game breaking bug from putting the key you find in the first 10 minutes (towards the end the game leads you to where you will find the key hidden in a cabinet, I found it right away because I always open everything which I feel is common for most gamers) I put the key where it belongs, about 30 minutes later I was solving a puzzle BUT the puzzle would NOT complete because I had put the key in so I started overI experienced a game breaking bug caused by putting a picture on a wall where it goes (because I had not solved the puzzle to find the last picture that puzzle would not complete because I was expected to start the 'picture puzzle' after finding all pictures)These were basically the only bugs I experienced, but they caused me to restart which was horribly frustrating and I think gave me a negative outlook on the rest of the game, being overly cautious as to NOT do something out of order. The autosave most likely would've brought be back to before the bug but I did not remember if it had saved prior to the bug or after so I restarted both times, I am upset about these because these should've been caught during play testst. If I am presented  with multiple things, I should not be expected to do things in the exact way the developers have determined. Because of these bugs, I almost put the game down at 50% and did not come back, friends told me they wanted to see the rest of it so I pursued after a few weeks to cool down from the frustration.The Part in the sewer where you are establishing a connection, the game disables your ability to take out the camera unless you are in the 'connection spot' I assumed taking out the camera was a bug as it had been disabled in this section. You then hit me with a REALLY good jumpscare. You did this 3 more times in that sequence. Better execution would've been the first one and the last one, or nothing until the last one, because the last one was HUGE. When in comes to jumpscares, more does not = better and it numbs your player to the effort you've put in, because that last one would've thrown me out of my chair if I wasn't expecting it.There's another 'wet' sequence with lighter, this was BEAUTIFUL, the only part where the atmosphere truly changed, sound was ON POINT, the lighting was perfect. Super tense. Then you hit a 10/10 jumpscare of the thing walking in front of you, then you did this 2 more times to finish with a HUGE one, once again, less is more.The church, really well done, puzzle was great once I understood what I was doing, no fault to the game I was stupid. Then you hit me with a jumpscare, really well done, then you repeat it again and again and I die (I guess I was supposed to run away) but that pushes me into the next sequence regardless so dying = progress. In the next sequence I am expected to run away from the exact same thing that caused me to make progress 2 minutes prior, if I had run away the first time, this would make sense, I got an achievement for dying so I figured I had done the intended path. So I tried again, and died. Tried again, this time trying to take a picture, and died. I tried the picture approach again because maybe I didn't do it right, died. Then slowly walked backwards to realize I can walk away from it, so I died and ran away to make progress.walking around the house and receiving the same jumpscare over and over is just draining and numbs your playerThen you later introduce this underlying lore to the game towards the end, neat. Then you make me stand there and play an obnoxiously loud song multiple times and receive deathscare or eyeball/take a picture to make thing leave me alone. This is probably the part I complained the most, because the loud music was just... loud. It pulls the player out of the experience because it just assaults your ears, I normally play games close to max volume or set volume in the beginning, then I cut stream volume to half, so if it's a little too loud on my side, fine, but even chat was saying it's way too loud, and they are 50% of what I was hearing. I am rewarded for successfully completing this sequence with a deathscare jumpscare, the same one you gave me throughout the sequence for failure... I guess just in case someone manages to do it perfectly you still want them to see it, but I failed 2-3 times so it just goes back to being repetitive (this one I can kinda give a pass to because I understand you want the player to see it if they did everything perfectly and did not receive it)The ending was spoiled by steam, achievement pops up prior to completion so you know exactly what the next step is and where it endsMy main negative is the repetitiveness of the jumpscares, take out 70% of the redundant ones and you have a significantly scarier experience. They were REALLY good scares, ruined by getting them over and over and over. There was one with a doorway to a bathroom you walk by, it made me nervous to walk anywhere near that doorway for the rest of the game because it was so good and NEVER repeated, that one was REALLY good and you didn't repeat it, which made it perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of horror light puzzle games this is and very solid one that stands out from the rest with it's great sound and well thought out photo mechanic. You never really get stuck but they are not mind numbing  either and take a little work and are the highlight of the game. The story while standard is masterfully told and the presentation raises the experience. it's also brutal and gory as a warning for anyone who that's a turn off. My only real complaints was there was an item in a really hard to see spot that was way too easy to miss () this was a massive annoyance. and the chase sequences were a little too obtuse and unforgiving. You can get killed without enough understanding why and it can get a little frustrating but it never puts you too far back so not a huge deal.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a good game and worth the wait. I enjoyed the demo and I'm glad that the full game delivered and wasn't a few hour experience, the demo itself sold me on paying full price for the game. It's very much a play and complete once because of where objects are and the scripted moments. I played through once on the hardest difficulty to take away the extra prompts and it took about 6 hours in total.The puzzles are "you need a yellow key card for the yellow door". If you find everything to pickup or come back to on your first walk through a room the game will be shorter, you'll experience more jump scare frequency but if you miss things your sense of dread will diminish as it can often be quite predictable especially when you realise , that's not to say that the jump scares didn't get me for the most part though. Some of the puzzles I was trying to put too much thought into them when in reality they were as simple as they first appeared to be, given the nature of the puzzles overall I don't think that there were too many. Solving them is much like a maze that at first is hard to navigate but you learn pretty quickly. I worked out early on that the:  which I felt could have been better as you really don't want people working out a core part of the game so early on if you're trying to scare folk.The story is dark though but could use a little more story telling as some of it's voice and some of it is in journals to read and it's getting a little old in horror games having to read the story like a book, the ending is something I wasn't expecting. Enemies: In terms of replayability, I don't know what you expect from a horror game - it is what it is, its the experience no matter how long it takes to complete. It's much like any single player game, any movie - if you enjoyed it, you'd watch or play it again, if it was in the middle you might in a year or more and if you didn't really like it you'd shelf it or show it to someone who'd never played before but good to have in the library as good horror games are few and far between.Would I replay this game? Yes if a few changes above were made and it was put into VR otherwise no as I'd know exactly what was coming and it just wouldn't be the same as the first time. If they intended on bringing out a prequel or DLC I'd probably replay it again though however I wouldn't buy anything more unless the following issue was addressed and fixed.The worst and most game breaking thing: is the that games FPS is fine running high but the refresh rate is hard locked to 50hz, no matter how many FPS you get the game only sends out 50, or that's how I understand whats happening. From what I read on this its to do with the settings used for mobile games through the development program used that is automatically set to 50hz, which is something that devs forget to "turn off". There is no fix to this consumer side but you can alleviate it by forcing your computer to run at a custom resolution with 50hz and locking to 50FPS, if you don't have any preset options. I run a capture card on a separate machine I was unable to do this and another suggestion suggested running it at multiples of 50, I had the option for 100hz which I used, it sucked at first but after a while I got used to it though I never forgot it was there.With the above issue this games a 5/10 and if you can overlook it or it gets fixed, it's a solid 8/10. I can't put this as my top three horror games until that's fixed but fix it, and it gets there or very close as had I played it without the janky stutteryness I'd have probably enjoyed it a whole lot more.

_childDocuments_.review: Since I first found the trailer for this game, I was really excited. It seemed like a clone of Visage. And, although a clone of a pre-existing game doesn't sound great, it's actually a positive factor because of how much I loved Visage. Regardless, this game is different & unique, but keeps similar aspects that make Visage so pressure-inducing.There is no combat in the game, and you CAN die at points, but it is not overly annoying and does not require you to run & hide all the time like games such as Outlast or Amnesia.The graphics really seal the deal for me. I love realistic horror games, as it makes things so much creepier. Walking through a hallway is something that at certain points of the game I find myself questioning if I really want to, even though I know I have to in order to proceed. If the game can make me too unsure of walking forward, you know it does well by making the player fear the unknown.I feel the game took heavy inspiration from (obviously) Visage, as well as an old favourite Half-Life 2 mod called 'Nightmare House' and it's sequel, 'Nightmare House 2'. In fact, the voice actor for a few characters in NH2 actually voices a character in this game, and I feel that was definitely done on purpose. Kudos for that.General pros and cons:Pros:- Great graphics- No bugs (at least I never encountered any)- Enough achievements that it makes you want to try and get them all- Not overly difficult but not too easy- Fun puzzle-solving, with a fair amount of hints to help you out if necessary- Great atmosphere- Randomized codes / combos for certain puzzles (each playthrough will have different combos)- Certain tasks can be done in different orders (the game is linear but not EVERY step is required to be done in a certain order)Cons:- Not THAT long (but it's still a solid length, don't get me wrong)- Classic Amnesia physics doors (this is subjective, but I hate the click & drag doors with the softened sensitivity, it's hard to explain, but sometimes the doors [depending on where they are grabbed from] have reversed controls, as in I can pull a door towards me to open it by moving my mouse down and the door moves forward and closes)- Relatively heavy character head-bob / wobble (after an hour or so you get very used to it and can ignore it, but it would still maybe be nice to have an option for it to either be on or off or at least be able to adjust how extreme it is. If you stand still, it's like a sniper scope in COD when you run out of breath from holding it)- In general, there's limited options (There is only 2 audio options, 1 slider and 1 to mute your character from speaking the lines so you only read the subtitles, etc.)- (DEBATABLE) Price [The price for me is no issue, and I don't regret buying it at said price, but for some, for a first-time game from a new company, it can maybe scare a few away. However, the team that made this game appears to be incredibly small and they did an absolute amazing job, so I am more than happy to give them all the money for this game, as I want them to make moreOverall, the game is fun, always keeps you on your feet / the edge of your seat, looks and feels great, runs great, has an intriguing story that I actually cared to follow and remember details about, and definitely made me yell and jump on a multitude of occasions. Props to Bloodious Games; I look forward to seeing what else you will create, as I will likely be buying it.9/107/14/2022 edit: As of 7/12/2022, the developers have added an 'accessibility' tab in the options, allowing users to customize intensity of the head bob, arm sway & camera shakes, as well the ability to turn on a 'reduced camera motion' option and customize the UI AIM transparency. This knocks off 2 of my 5 previously listed cons, and the other 3 are debatable or extremely subjective anyhow. Loving to see that this game is being treated well already. Great work guys!

_childDocuments_.review: I had anticipated this game for months, and I can honestly say it exceeded if not met every single one of those expectations. This game can be likened to other titles such as Visage, Layers of Fear, and even a more recent title like FOBIA: St Difna Hotel which takes references from Resi/Silent Hill/Outlast/etc. In many ways I think this game is more terrifying then Visage personally, and where Visage failed in balance, MADiSONs exceeds in its ability to make the puzzles just the appropriate amount of confusing yet rewarding once you actually solved them. The jump scares and atmosphere of the game are done so well, and truly stray away from the cliche and atypical types of cheap scares that often kill a lot of horror games. The developers truly understood the importance of ambiance and scenery and how it can really enhance the scary nature of the game. While the price tag may seem a little steep, I wholeheartedly think its worth it. I got a decent 7 and a half hours of gameplay, mostly because some of the puzzles did truly stump me at times and required a good amount of effort to solve. Honestly, hats off the the developers. If they can produce something at this quality with essentially just a team of two, I can't wait to see what they can accomplish in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be brief: At it's best it's a pretty spooky game. The house is beautifully designed, the sound design is great, the story is pretty interesting and I would say if you liked PT and Visage, you'd probably really like this.BUT.A few problems really bring this from being a decent little game to being a frustrating one.I played on hard mode, this includes no clues or visual hints. I thought the hints and stuff would trivialise things but I wish I had played on normal with the hints because some of the times you have to use the camera to reveal things or progress the game are pretty un-intuitive. What happens when you don't realise you were supposed to take a picture of something is you spend an hour wandering around the house wondering what you missed, only to start taking pictures of everything in the hope that you manage to find the thing you missed. If you do play, play on normal, the hints showing you where you need to use a camera are probably not that out of place but wandering about wondering what you missed is definitely immersion breaking.The jumpscares. As I said the game is pretty spooky, but what really diminishes the spookiness of the game is how often the developers throw a thing at you out of thin air for half a second. The spooky tense atmosphere they build up just gets ruined when they have a monster shout "BOO" at you, and it happens WAY too often. At one point in the game it's happening every minute while you're moving around the house just trying to figure out a puzzle. I wasn't scared, I just took my headphones off because I was annoyed and the sudden loud sounds hurt my ears. I figured out they use the view frustrum to flash you the monster so if you just look at the ground while moving around you don't get jump scared (the monster can't hurt you anyway so you're in no danger lol). Some of the monsters can kill you so you can't do this for all of them but if you get to this section and get annoyed just look at the ceiling or something.  But yeah, they do a good job of building up a spooky atmosphere but they're determined to demolish it on a regular basis through the overusage of cheap jump scares. If you like being jump scared then you'll like this game but if you prefer variety in how the developers scare you then you won't find it here because 95 percent of the scares in this game are a thing blink daggering in and shouting boo at you. The sound design I mentioned was good, and it is. But they overuse random environmental noises like creaks and movements and stuff. It's supposed to unnerve you by making you think there's something in the house with you but it happens so often that you just stop paying attention to it and it loses it's effect pretty quickly.Overall my feelings on the game are mixed. I'm gonna recommend it because there's no neutral option but I pretty easily could have gone negative. Pick up on a sale, or get it now if you're really desperate for more stuff like Visage. It's still worth playing, just understand the caveats.Side note: As of when I played the game had some technical issues which were kind of annoying. The game has like some aggressive mouse smoothing meaning your camera usually trails behind where you're trying to look which if this were a shooter or something it would make the game unplayable, as is it just feels like bad mouse lag. In addition the framerate despite saying the game is running at 144fps, actually looks like it's running at 60. If I had to guess there's some kind of fps cap or something. It's not that big a deal given the nature of the game but it would be nice if the game ran at your monitors refresh rate.

name: Ereban: Shadow Legacy
detailed_description: Ereban: Shadow Legacy is a fast-paced stealth platformer game where you become Ayana, the last descendant of a forgotten race. Harness mystical shadow powers, high-tech gadgets and avoid or kill to uncover the truth about your past and the key to saving a dying, morally grey universe. What will your legacy be? Experience an unprecedented combination of stealth and shadows with the Shadow Merge ability. Dive into shadows and move freely through them to climb walls, reach inaccessible places, attack from cover or advance unseen. Absorb echoes to learn more lethal and non-lethal shadow powers, craft high-tech gadgets, and combine all this with your agility to infiltrate Helios lines and investigate what they are hiding. Avoid or kill. Spare or consume. The decision is yours: how far are you willing to go to uncover the truth? Approach each level with your own style of play. Use your powers to move like a ghost or strike as a deadly shadow in this sci-fi universe where actions go beyond good and evil. Discover the ruins of lifeless cities, infiltrate sci-fi facilities carved into ancient temples and forge alliances to unravel the mystery of who you are and what happened to your people.

_childDocuments_.review: Ereban: Shadow Legacy is a great, replayable dark sci-fi stealth game I recommend if you really enjoy stealth of both the non-lethal and lethal variety. Although it will feel a little easy for very passionate stealth fanatics, this also makes it a great introduction or a way back into the genre for any player, and it's very comfy to play if you've just been missing fun games that you need to stay undetected in. The game's signature mechanic, Shadow Merge feels unique in the stealth space, speeding up gameplay quite a lot, and you can easily imagine inspirations from Splatoon and Aragami as you sink into shadows and flow around, invisible and incorporeal. Ereban features no combat, so unless you can react quickly with an item or skill, it's best to have a fast, safe way to escape to high ground if you're detected and chased, since enemies run faster than you, and they will always catch up to you unless you're tricky. So, being detected usually means you're about to lose and reload a checkpoint. This is a game for lovers of pure stealth.Ereban really shines and is at its best when it comes to level design and guard-layouts, with each mission feeling pretty distinct from the rest, and its guards all being rewarding and fun to sneak through. My first non-lethal playthrough took me about twelve hours. I played for another twelve after, doing a second (lethal) run, as well as replaying missions from Chapter Select to test out what my unlocked skills and gadgets feel like on earlier parts of the game.Our player-character is Ayana. She is Ereban, a species which apart from her has vanished from the universe. Ereban are a race attuned to the shadows, meaning they can wield, merge with and control them. Other than Shadow Merge and its sub-skills, you can evolve your skill tree in two different directions during the story, Lethal or Non-Lethal, and they're both pretty fun, though I did enjoy Non-Lethal more.Depending on how bloodthirsty you are, it does affect how a certain character reacts to you and the kind of ending you can get, which is another fun reason to replay the game so you can see a different outcome. Movement feels great most of the time. Ayana's animations, speed and responsiveness are all what I want in a character moving through this kind of world. Controlling her doesn't feel irritating or get in the way, and the distances of her kit all feel intuitive. Jumping, Shadowmerge, your amount of Merge Stamina, this kind of polish and tuning is tough to get right, and I think they did well here.Some linear platforming sections feel like something straight out of a Prince of Persia game, since Shadow Merge when used on vertical surfaces is functionally a wallrun that you can do in any direction, ejecting off the wall to a nearby platform when you like.Throughout the entire game, I found myself enjoying reading the environments and learning to spot available shadows more and more. Seeing the shadows being cast by objects is something you'll noticeably feel yourself getting better and faster at, which is a cool feeling, and the path the devs seem to suggest you take isn't always one you're forced to use. I had fun with Ereban, and if you're a starving stealth game fan, you might like it too.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to be honest—I didn't enjoy it. It lacked the creativity and uniqueness of similar titles like Aragami or Dishonored (despite being heavily influenced by them). The story fell short, and the characters weren't engaging, the gadgets/powers aren't that fun to use and the world is just barren. Aragami was $20 when it was first released and it offered around 10 hours of gameplay, including main quests and side content, with excellent replayability. In contrast, Ereban, priced at $25, too me less than 5 hours of gameplay for completion and finding most of the collectibles and upgrades, and I don't see a point of replaying it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so mixed on this game that I felt the need to have a substantial conversation with a friend about whether to ultimately recommend it or not. While I finally landed on not recommending it,  does have some redeeming qualities.The general concept of the game is great. While there are obviously other stealth games that make heavy use of staying in the shadows, I've never played another that allowed the player to "merge" with them or to use the moving nature of shadows to reach otherwise inaccessible places, such as higher floors or the other side of substantial gaps in the floor.I also generally liked the game's world, and enjoyed figuring out its history. Who were the Ereban and how did they get these powers? What makes the rebels feel that Helios (the prominent energy company in the game) is dishonest? Are the Ereban somehow complicit in what has occurred? I dutifully read each lore piece I located to try and find these answers. And although the game looks very "Unity engine," I liked the environmental and character designs as well.But unfortunately, every attempt of the game to move beyond simple enemy avoidance/assassination and shadow traversal fell flat for me. Outside of the "Sonar" skill, the others were either not useful or difficult to use. There are multiple skills that I never figured out how to use, like one that supposedly could help me get away when grabbed by one of the game's robotic enemies. It's odd that skills like this are on a radial menu alongside the Sonar skill, which really should be its own separate button on the controller/keyboard (considering how often it is used in games of this style). Unlocking new skills requires finding collectibles in the game's expansive levels, which unfortuntately contain a ton of similar-looking structures and terrain. To make matters worse, there's no map to help the player find out where they've been already.Most of the time I simply surveyed an area for a shadowy, less-populated route to an objective, and did simple assassinations on any enemies in my way. If I was discovered, I was killed 95% of the time and had to start the section over. Enemies shine lights on Ayana (the game's protagonist) to pull her out of the shadows and they can run faster than her as well. Even so, I didn't get discovered overmuch and didn't find the game particularly difficult.If the only issues were the combat and the skill trees, the traversal might've been enough fun to carry the experience. But unfortunately, there were issues here as well. First off, there are multiple times that Ayana will need to jump horizontally out of a vertical surface in which she's shadow-merged. While the game helpfully provides a different surface texture to pinpoint where you'll need to jump from, it also automatically changes the camera and disorients the player. I missed many of these jumps in the game for this reason, restarting from a recent checkpoint each time when I fell into whatever pit was beneath me. To make matters worse, you'll sometimes need to activate a shadow ability to carry you the last few feet during some of these jumps. There's a specific window of time where you can activate the ability, all the more difficult to nail when the game is swinging the camera around like a lunatic.Secondly, just running and jumping forward (not even when you're shadow-merged!) is challenging as well. Ayana has a strange sense of momentum and the camera can make it difficult to tell if your feet are actually on the beam or pole you're attempting to land on. I've linked a screenshot here to the most difficult section of the game for me, in terms of how many times I died attempting to complete it:While I'm always glad to see a new player in the stealth space,  just didn't do enough to make itself a contender. If you're interested in third-person stealth and haven't played them already, I'd recommend either modern  game ( or ), Rocksteady's  series, or Monolith's  series. If you're looking for something similarly mid-tier, you could also try either of Lince Works'  titles.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Aragami I bought the game immediately after seeing the trailer as it's very clearly inspired by it, and conceptually the main ability to merge with the shadows seemed really neat. Unfortunately it's not what I was looking for.The levels are large and open but don't have the challenge to make every choice feel meaningful. Often I'd find there are multiple routes to get to the same place, but then neither route would have any enemies that could see you or any unique challenge to them. Maybe I'm just too used to stealth games, but I managed to get pacifist and ghost in every level pretty easily and I didn't even use most special abilities, just blind a few times.I think there's almost something here, but what I'd want is more enemies in every level, enemies being able to see further, enemies detecting you faster if they spot me, something to stop you from just going high ground to avoid sight everywhere, and better guard routes that force you to keep moving in certain sections. Also just less empty space- I think some of the puzzles were neat, but less running through empty areas with no enemies would be good.Right now I think I can't really recommend this game, but if you want and easier stealth game with a unique mechanic this may be what you're looking for. This is the dev teams first game though as far as I'm aware, and I do see a lot of potential here, I hope in the future to see them take another crack at games main mechanic with some tighter level design and smarter enemy ai.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I found the game enjoyable, maybe 7/10. I think as long as you don't go in expecting AAA quality similar to something like Dishonored then you'll have a good time.The core gameplay is solid. Pathing through the shadows to either avoid or backstab enemies is simple but effective. There are some additional powers and gadgets, although I rarely found myself using them outside of the scan ability that showed all nearby enemies (and collectibles after leveling it up). The story is nothing memorable: not particularly interesting but not offensively bad. It does its job to string together the levels and objectives.There's probably two main criticisms with the game: difficulty and length.As I mentioned, I played the game almost entirely using the basic "travel through the shadows" power. There were no areas of the game that were difficult enough that I ever felt like the more advanced powers were necessary or really even worth using. I think some more difficult encounters would help make the advanced powers and gadgets more relevant, rather than everything being either "wait for path to open" (non-lethal) or "wait for enemy to be alone" (lethal).The length of the game also isn't that long; it only takes a few hours to beat. Most of my gameplay time has come from replaying the levels to do collectibles, medals, S ranks, and other achievements. If you enjoy stuff like that then I think the game offers a fair amount of play time for the price. If you're only interested in a single playthrough then it will probably feel too short at full price.All in all I think it's a fine game as long as you keep your expectations in check.

_childDocuments_.review: I am typing this review pretty much fresh after i finished my first playthrough of the game. I also recieved this game for free but i will most likely give it to someone as a gift so more ppl can experience this as well as to support the developers as i believe they do deserve it.As it is my very first review i am simply gonna pour all my thoughts into here and attempt to make sense.Graphics : I think graphics are very strong side of this game, Areas are vibrant and well thought out, i never had a situation where zone was looking bland even industrial areas were lookign amazing, lighting was working perfectly with open as well as closed areas, Art direction that was take with this game is interesting as it reminds me a bit of Borderlands, but better, more detailed and less Randy Pitchfork. One thing that got mentioned to me on streams is that main charachter looks like Raziel from Legacy of Kain series and when i look deeper into it i dare to say there probably was an inspiration.Gameplay : I enjoyed the gameplay of the game, it definetly had some lows which i will mention in a sec, but first lets start with stronger sides. I rarely if ever see utilization of shaded areas or shadows s form of offence, defence and transportation at all when in video games and i pretty much welcome it. Powers and abilities, that you unlock and upgrade as game progresses, are fun and not of them are useless. For my first run i have unlocked whole left side of the tree, and i think only ability from that that should be by defult without unlock is one that allows you to free yourself from SYMs hold right before it executes it attacks. Gadgets are pretty alright, i consider sonar to be probably the best item in game that is 100% worth upgradign to last rank, mines are neat and can be used as traps or for "what if" scenario happens, a tip, do not go above level 2 in them rank 3 seems to be obsolete, I did not managed to use decoys, but i believe there are useful, the most useless item in game in my opinion is the visor, sonar that is not even fully upgraded does the same job if not even better. Enemy AI seems to be inspired by Metal Gear Solid 1 with sound detection addition. By that i mean is that when it comes to sight they function by detecting objects that come to their cone of vision while also hearing loud footsteps players can make right behind them. I also noticed that AI can be pretty much cheesed by simply climbing an elevation, or moving to areas in which they cannot get access to. I also find it weird that SYMs responsible for resurecting others, once they find one down, or you go into alert, they immidietly know where every downed enemy is Other than that i think gameplay itself is pretty enjoyable and is deffinetly a good starter for ppl that never played stealth games.Story : Sadly story of the game feels like a mixed bag. The back story of Ayana and her people that we discover as we absorb echoes is interesting and i think there should be more of that lore as it is really nicely made, Charachters and their developmement as game goes is, odd. I find it difficult to feel any connection to that other charachters in the game. By that i mean, each charachter have a purpose that they fulfil but they just lack that OOMPH for me to care about them. Premise of the game is pretty solid, you simply are a being that tries to find about your past and your ppl as you forgot it due to an accident.Sound & Music : I think sounds are very nicely balanced and not obnoxious, music if pretty good in matter of fact i will buy soundtrack when its going to be released, i enjoyed sneaking music the most, yup that is pretty much all i can say. Maybe i will add the fact that voice acting is pretty damn solid and it definetly compensates for lack of any facial animations, it simply does a good job, kudos to voice actorsOther Thoughts : I am a sucker for references which this game has a lot, i have found Metal Gear Series "bandana in a box" referenced in a note, Mass Effect "Throw it out the airlock" and robot speakin their emotion just liek Elcors did, referenced as you try to find key item to progress in main objective, i think there even was a Splinter Cell reference but i am not 100% sure, there was even a sneaky Bioshock refrence with "Would you kindly" but it would be fair to assume that i overreact Other than that i think this game is inspired by Metal Gear Solid, Hitman and i think to a point Nier series. I was kinda afraid that game itself would be crashy or poorly optimised, i must say with eyes full of joy that this game is very well optimised, i mean for 98% of the whole run game was running like a dream with almost consistent 60FPS and there was no crashes or game breaking bugs, only one actual bug that i noticed is that music stopped playing out of nowere, but resetign the game fixed it so it is not that big of a problem. This game even have an NG+ which i will always welcome tho i do not think its needed, this is where implementation of different profiles works perfectly well for ppl who simply want to start a clean file or for ppl who simply want to max out all the skills and gadgets. I have also enjoyed the fact that i could disable visual help at any point via options menu that way no person can complain about "omg purple paint bla bla bla"Final Words : It one hell of an impressive peice of work for a first game ever released by Baby Robot Games and it is worth the price tag of 25-30$. So grab it, hold it, love it is a solid and i think perfectly justified 7/10. Thank you and sorry for subjecting readers for reading my wall of text :)

_childDocuments_.review: Full review at .Another one of those titles that stands as an argument for the sorely lacking "sideways thumb".A very inconsistent game. I ultimately decided not to recommend because I think it's a bit on the pricier side for how bland it truly is. Ereban: Shadow Legacy is one of those games designed entirely around its one gimmick - and everything else seems to suffer for it. The first few levels are, for all intents and purposes, a boilerplate stealth game from 15 years ago (and not a good one; just a barely passable attempt). The platforming feels weightless, the enemies pose no threat whatsoever, AI is non-existent, the maps feel confused in being overly large but offering no meaningful interaction. There is no doubt a lot of passion went into this project and you could purchase it for that alone. It has a terrible yet somewhat endearing story that likes to pretend it's much more profound than it really is, underlined with equally awful dialogue produced by someone that watched a Marvel movie too many. The game looks pretty good in its own incoherent way. The gimmick is nice, when it decides to actually work.Unfortunately it's all just really bland gameplay wise. An okay-ish commercial debut title.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing is rough.  That's not to say the story is bad, just the dialogue and voice direction is rough.  The world and events surrounding it is cool and interesting.  Gameplay is solid.  Uncompromising stealth gameplay where the best response to getting caught is to run, with very few exceptions.  Feels like what Aragami 2 should have been, and it rocks.  Again, writing is hit or miss but once you get used to it, it's fine.  Kind of reminds me of how edgy jak 2 and 3 were with an oddball sense of humour thrown in at inappropriate times.Solid 7/10, oldschool mgs and splintercell fans will enjoy this if they can get over the writing and setting.

_childDocuments_.review: Ereban is a neat stealth game with some mild platforming elements. The story is interesting, but also somewhat confusing.There is one thing that has to be said: From a gameplay perspective, the game really favors you to take a pacifist approach, i.e. it is way easier to simply evade the enemies rather than defeating them, since you only have a back-stab and a drop attack and you only have very limited ways to hide the bodies of defeated enemies. So if you expect an action-focused game, then you are probably going to be disappointed.I recommend buying and playing Ereban it if you 1) ike stealth games, 2) are fine with pacifist runs and 3) are fine with the sci-fi-fantasy setting.
