_childDocuments_.review: The mixed reviews had me a bit worried at first, but playing the game quickly eveporated those worries. From the very first opening shot after you've pressed play and the whole intro sequence that followed i was hooked. The game immediately intrigued me with it's wordless storytelling, impressive visuals and masterfull sound design. The game deserves more recognition for the piece of art that it is, but sadly the poor launch plagued with technical issues and the comparisons to playdead's INSIDE burried this in the depths of steam. Don't miss out on this! The issues have been mostly resolved, and other than a few little quirks here and there the game is quite the experience! The game is still worth experiencing so while it may not be worth full price, but on a discount or in a bundle with planet of lana (another amazing title) this is very worthwhile.The setting of an invasion is masterfully done here. All the things happening at the start and the repercussions thereoff shown later in the game are very believable. The world is in disarray and humanity is scraping by. You see people hiding, running and fighting but it feels hopeless... We're outmatched and there's no chance of coming out of this situation. This creates a feeling of despair that sticks throughout the whole game. Luckily there's some hope as well, things like your loyal four-feeter that appears throughout the game and some others i won't spoil. The whole narrative from start to finish is quite something. The beginning especially starts of very strong but tapers off towards the middle before going full force at the finale. While it wasn't as profound or vague as some of its contemporaries, it's still memorable enough by the end.What's also memorable are the gorgeous visuals that really look as good as INSIDE did many times. While the backgrounds aren't on the same level of dystopian storytelling as that game, they're still a treat to look at. The lighting, the textures, the composition of the levels, it just clicks. This is as close you'll get to that INSIDE fix untill playdead finally brings their next title to the public. In any case the visuals made me take many a screenshot, some of which deserve to be framed in an art gallery. It truly is a work of art in that regard, and the studio should be proud of what they've accomplished here.The audio is also of the same quality. Music is sparringly used but to great effect, and the opening theme especially is a masterpiece. The rest of the sound effects are also amazing, the whistle of the wind, the footsteps of your character or the crumbling of rocks near cliffs. It's very immersive but the real star of the show are the off-worldish sounds that the aliens make. From giant searchlights to smaller creatures to the suprise at the end, the audio just blew me away. I'd recommend playing this game with a stereo for the best experience. Immerse yourself in this world and let it take you away.While visuals, audio and storytelling are all masterfully done, the gameplay is a bit varied. There's a nice variety of puzzles, and i really enjoyed some of them but they were at times a bit too simple for my liking. Luckily this makes it so the pacing never suffers but this isn't like INSIDE where every puzzle is enjoyable and different. There's also some light issues with the controls from time to time. Things like getting stuck on a piece of geometry, or not quite being in the right spot to interact with something. Luckily everything is clearly communicated/signposted so you won't be puzzled yourself as to what to do next.Lastly there's performance and bugs. The game ran well most of the time but i sometimes had some significant stutters or framedrops that lasted for up to a minute. This was mostly when reloading checkpoints or chapters but on a technical side it's just not there yet. I also encountered some minor bugs but nothing major that blocked progress. The game is often held up to the standards of INSIDE because the games share a developer but that's a high bar to meet. Artistically it surely does in it's audiovisual presentation, but on a gameplay and technical level it's overshadowed. That isn't to say this game isn't worth experiencing, it's almost worth the asking price but not quite. On a sale it's an easy steal, and it's a must play for all cinematic platformer enthusiasts!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll try to be fair and technical here. Somerville is not a good game. but I recommend playing it:there's the obvious: the art production is of the highest quality. the compositions, colors, visual storytelling in the environment, the style, the music, the shaders. all are masterclasses in game art. these can be partial reasons to go through the game if you don't mind paying for it.I played it because I was really curious about the reviews, and part of me didn't want to accept that a partially ex-playdead team can deliver something "bad".to summarize though, the issue is a lack of a clear game direction. in detail: Somerville has some very good 'potential' mechanics, which it introduces and then kind of doesn't know what to do with them. it creates expectations and doesn't meet them. I think the disappointment would've been less if the game sold itself as a walking sim, but the game mechanics evoke contradictory feelings in terms of interactions, both in terms of the presence of puzzles, and emotional expressions.there's a reason why people compare this to inside. yes, playdead is the shared link, but let's not forget, Inside was also a silent game, in which the story was also purely told by the environment and the gameplay. the puzzles were playful yet somehow aligned with the narrative at all time, walking from left to right never felt too much or too long, every scene and puzzle was crafted with intent and care, and the end was a revelation to behold. so yeah, would I recommend this bad game? yes, if you are like me. you like to enjoy amazing art and sound work with great camera work, and you want to see this as a lesson of 'what not to do when making a game'. (but otherwise please don't buy it, haha)

With great mechanics and puzzles, it gives moments of stress, sadness and fear just like the other games. You do get some connections to the character, but I did get a Fallout 4 vibe from the story. In the way I HAVE to find my family, because they ARE my family. For me this doesn't give me a great emotional connection to them because there were not enough buildup beforehand. I did not have the same drive in the beginning as with Limbo or Inside, but it did get a lot better the more I played.All in all an ish good story with great mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this review before finishing the game because I am simply angry about the poor comments. So...To enjoy this game, you should be someone who can switch off and enjoy. There is nothing here that you need to accomplish faster than other gamers. This is not about competition or showing off how cleverly you can act. It's about being able to decide when to take a break and whether you want to be an interactive part of a small story.Regarding the poor reviews about the controls: Yes, they are slow and different from other games - but intentionally, because those who complain would otherwise simply rush through the game without noticing anything of the beautiful environment. Limits are set here, but in a way that allows the player to take their time to admire the wonderfully designed world and soak up the atmosphere.Regarding the puzzles: FINALLY, a developer has incorporated puzzles without destroying immersion. They are wonderfully integrated, and there are no boxes randomly lying around to push onto a button. Those looking for that should look elsewhere.All I can say is that anyone who appreciates nice animations, stylish design, and loving effects should play this game. Actually, I would describe it as a must-have because I can't think of any game that comes close.And yes, I also love INSIDE, but this one hit my taste and nerves more.Thank you for the great game, dear Jumpship team.PS I have been following your blog with posts for many years and am really glad that such a great game has come out of it! I am now immensely looking forward to continuing playing, it's a highlight for me, and I enjoy every scene.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was quite put off by the mixed reviews about this game. In the end I still decided to play it and have a few things to say about it.Although the game has a nice look to it some of the animations are quite sloppy and don't really look natural. There's also a not inconsiderable amount of clipping through walls. The character is hard to control in some places and difficulties with interacting arose quite often. The riddles were incomprehensible in some parts and straight out dumb in some others although I would say there's also a ton of creative and fun riddles to solve too.Nevertheless, this game has some up parts aswell. What stands out the most for me is the camera movement which gives the game a very special character. There were parts of the game that were so special because of the camera that I would recommend people to play it just because of it. The sound design is also very impressive and gives the game a great atmosphere. The beautiful sceneries make up for a lot of the game's flaws too.All in all I was hoping for a game in the vain of Inside. It's definitely not perfect the way Inside is but I liked it especially because it's trying to be something on its own and I'd say it succeeds as that while still bringing back some familiar feelings.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: 25% off normal price. Recommended game for your library!Definitely a unique sci-fi puzzle side scroller.Also longer than normal cinematic pieces, and no dialog.Could do with indicating the player/current character can now move(cinematic piece is over)Also the ability to run instead of only auto, and limiting the player from walking into a locations that you don't know where the current character is, or prevent walking into a direction that is not logical for the current solution.Over all entertaining, and an interesting game.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game, while not as good as Limbo, Inside or the Little Nightmares games this is still top notch. I really liked the strange science fiction vibe but I was not a fan of the multiple endings. I kind of wish the devs just picked a solid ending and went with it.I definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Although it has nice atmosphere and setting i can't really recommend it.Game is really weid, puzzles are very basic, and movement is really clunky to the point you get stuck and have to restart from checkpoint.Very short (not really downside for me but some might have issues with that) and story is....erm....yeah.On the other hand visuals and audio are pretty good, I enjoyed that part of the game very much but that's about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cool game. very visually enticing, with an interesting story and an overall gameplay design that favors the player's engagement with the narrative over any type of problem solving challenges or demands for technical mastery. Somerville is a nice change if you are needing a break from punishingly difficult, 100+ hour games. The bugs are not as game-breaking as some would have you believe, but there are aspects of this game that could use a little polish. I hope this developer keeps making games, because while I don't think this is their magnum opus, there is definitely something there.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of potential, some great visuals and environments.Felt like a slog to get through, could probably be half as long or a third shorter. The main puzzle solving mechanic is alright but the puzzles often only have on thing you can do so solving them isn't really a puzzle most times. A lot of the game ends up just being press forward until you need to interact with something, then maybe use your power when it's available.Would love to see something similar done better though.The pieces of info you need for the ending are also so obscure and confusing even once it's fully explained.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Very good experience. i dont think this deserves the mixed ratings its getting and I hope Im helping to bump this into the positive where it belongs. its very well done and succeeds in creating the dark existential atmosphere it set out to create. This cant be lumped in with Inside and limbo because it tells its own story and does it well. Great job Devs
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of Limbo and Inside will find this game interesting. It's again a puzzle-focused gameplay loop, but this time with some added extraterrestrial effects! The puzzles here do seem to be a bit more straightforward compared to the other two games. Somerville is a much more cinematic, atmospheric, and emotional experience than the other two games, but I do wish there was a chance to give us more of the story. There are five different endings so there is some replayability, but I'd probably just load up the last couple chapters to check out the other endings rather than go through the whole game again. Mostly enjoyed the experience, definitely worth checking out if you were a fan of Limbo and Inside!
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: One of those must-play games that come out once every few years. Brilliant artistic vision and very enticing sci-fi world. Unfortunately, feels like it was released one year too early as it lacks that final polish. Controls are not the best. Gameplay is a bit lacking - but it was expected, it's more of an interactive experience than a typical game. There's some cool optional spoiler stuff that's very difficult to fully figure out, which I appreciated a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves a better review. It certainly has some flaws especially regarding the endings clues which are really too cryptic / well hidden in the game and minor collision issues aside, the overall execution, the art direction, the 'mise-en-scène' and the music give a very good narrative video game.Puzzles are fairly simple, allowing you to focus on the story and the overall scenery.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: 6.8/10I'd *lightly* recommend this game at a cheaper price than it's currently offering. The story, while minimalist, offers up some intriguing mysteries to reflect on, and the puzzles are decently engaging even if they never make you think too much. It's definitely a game that is more about atmosphere. I feel the game is also the right length, as you don't want a game like this with limited mechanics to go on for too long.Unfortunately, there remains a lot of stuttering even for someone like me running a 3080 and 5 GHz CPU. That's unacceptable.If you haven't yet played the Little Nightmares games or INSIDE, absolutely play those first. They have superior puzzle design and better atmosphere for better performance. If, like me, you played those games to death and badly wanted something similar, this game is fine. I'd say just wait for a greater discount first - at least 50% off.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great, short, little game. It's a spiritual successor to Inside and Limbo, but from what I saw with a cursory search the only people working on it in common was a producer who co founded Playdead. So don't expect it to be too too similar.It definitely has it's own take on this style of gameplay.I have to say it's disappointing to see this is mixed. I thought it was incredibly solid. There were a sparse few mechanics but they were explored well and in depth enough that I was satisfied ending the game after 6 hours or so (we really took our time playing through as well).I had some screen tearing throughout the game but it wasn't anything so bad that it ruined the game for me, certainly.If you enjoy a short form story oriented game your should give this a shot. It's short and simple and sweet and cheap. Pick it up
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting game.  Setting Limbo and Inside aside, it stands up fairly well.  There a couple of difficult puzzles here, but a lot of them are unnecessarily forecast with visual indicators.  The ending feels uncannily like Mass Effect 3's, leaving me confused and disappointed.  Ultimately the game's art direction and atmosphere win my recommendation, Georgi Simeonov's touch is seen strongest about 2/3s in and I think helped sell the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: With the help of Playdead's co-founder Dino Patti, Somerville follows the footsteps of Limbo and Inside with beautiful environments and design paired with a story that's open to many theories and possibilities. This game definitely left me speechless but wanting more. I recommend going for the multiple endings for the full experience and story. Aside from some slight stutters, I felt there was nothing wrong with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Somerville was the only new game I was looking forward to in 2022 (there were others but they were delayed into 2023). I held off at the release due to confusing messaging in Steam initially indicating keyboard and mouse was not supported (keyboard & mouse was added at launch, however) and some so-so reviews indicating some less-than-stellar game play issues and decided to wait until a few patches came out before I made the purchase. I am glad I waited.The story is compelling and the artwork is utterly fantastic. I never found myself in the situation where I needed to find help on the internet to solve the puzzles, but at the same time they were not so easy to solve that I didn't have multiple head-scratching moments. The environment provided some clues as to how to solve puzzles, and also some warnings, so I highly recommend new players pay attention to everything.There is no dialogue, almost no UI and no text prompts. The length of the game is a bit short and I feel as though there should be more to the story. In my honest opinion Jumpship has a golden opportunity for DLC here; it would be a shame if they consider this project finished and moved on to something else without adding more content.This game is not entirely bug free. There was a puzzle mid-game where I died and then half of the puzzle was automatically solved because my character was physically past a certain checkpoint at death. The puzzle in particular was annoying so even though I'm sure that's not what the developers intended, I consider it a "feature" bug and it did not break the game.I would love to know more about certain characters in this game, and more backstory lore, but I'm not sure how such a thing could be added to the game itself.Overall I recommend this game, although the full price may be a bit high for people who prefer lengthy games.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Inside, and Mosaic, then you'll enjoy this title! Scifi adventure with good music, and some puzzling. I adore how this game looks, and the story it tells. My playtime is not a true runtime, as I looped back to complete achievements and probably let it sit "paused" while I made a coffee.It didn't outstay its welcome, and had a few impactful moments that I'll remember. Great start, Jumpship!
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Somerville is a homage to all cinematic games, from Another World to Inside all well represented here, but with a incredible camera handling that pushed the whole genre to another level. It really makes you feel deeply imerse and wishing more from the next Jumpship games. Even with the glitches (which is very common on another games from the same genre) I feel just like a 8 years old kid wacthing Spielberg masterpieces again!Well done, Dino!
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful game. For the most part you're tasked with simply solving puzzles and moving from place to place without much explanation of what's going on. It's not until the last quarter of the game that things begin to come together. But it feels a little too stretched. It's an interesting game with some slightly funky mechanics. But an enjoyable experience nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: CONS:- BUGS: Because Somerville has the visuals of INSIDE, people expect the same perfection in terms of edge case animations, edge case interactions, polish, lack of bugs etc. If the visuals were different (check Little Nightmares) the unfavourable comparison wouldn't have been so obvious.- PUZZLES:But that's irrelevant. People also wouldn't have been that impressed by the bugs if the puzzles were more interesting. But they're not.- INTERACTIVITY:Because of the above, the interactivity is also very limited. Let's forget INSIDE - the first 15 minutes of Little Nightmares have more interesting puzzles / interactions than all of Somerville.PROS:- THE HIDDEN CORE IDEA:The idea behind the game is amazing actually. The aliens and the materials they use are so otherworldly that our inability to fully understand them with our puny brains makes the relationship between us and them similar to that of our cats and dogs to us. The aliens are not trying to  It is up to you to actually figure out that  and prove that you are worthy of respect as an intelligent being, even if not very intelligent.Unfortunately, this amazing idea is not enough to carry the whole game.  Here, the greatest idea is actually hidden only for the smartest players to figure out, and the rest is just visuals without good puzzles or interactions to support them (I'm sorry, I find the liquify / solidify matter puzzles very bland). If I have to paraphrase one movie, "Liquefying matter is like fire, and solidifying matter is like ice, and when fire and ice meet, you end up with lukewarm water."- THE CINEMATIC DECISIONS:Unlike other players, I like that the protagonist chooses his own walking speed and I also like the static cameras. It's a decision that reinforces important emotional points of the game even if it's not very "gamey". There would have been fewer complaints about this if the rest worked better.YES OR NO?Even though Little Nightmares and Inside are better (play them first), I can still recommend Somerville, just because I like this type of games. Somerville reminds me not just of Another World, but also of the 80s Sierra games. We're getting there, rediscovering the action-adventure gameplay of the distant past. Too bad that the modern "walking simulator" influence is stronger. In any case, Somerville made all the right decisions on a macro level but failed to execute them properly on a micro level. It was still worth the experience, at least for me.I am sure the creators are devastated by the bad reviews, but at least they had a chance to make the thing; the creators of Afterlight (another INSIDE wannabe game that had incredible promise) didn't even manage to succeed in their Kickstarter campaign.Thank you for the effort to make beautiful things, Jumpship.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: definitely recommended. i'm slow as hell, and not very good at these kinds of spatial puzzles, but i really enjoyed Limbo and Inside.  different studio, same executive producer.  this is like a variation on the themes of  the game mechanics in those games, with some nice extras, so you don't feel so helpless all the time.  the story introduction and evolution is really well done and equally enjoyable.  not sure i agree with some other reviews that suggest this game won't encourage multiple play-thrus.  i can certainly see myself wanting to play this at least one more time after i've finished it.  if only to see how many of the puzzles i remember.one more thing i might add is that there's this 'transition' from heavy story (when you're first learning the basic mechanics -- and they are very basic) to when you're full-on in the game.  it was jarring for me, and i had to put the controller down for a bit and come back to it.  i realized later that i was actually pretty deeply emotionally engaged with the start of the story and didn't really want the game to kick in when it did.can't say i ever felt that with either Limbo or Inside, mostly (i guess) because you're dropped immediately into the gameplay.  kinda feels like maybe the folks at this studio are operating on multiple levels.code is a bit glitchy in spots, and i did see frame rate drops, but nothing that interfered with my enjoyment of the game.  yes, the controls take some getting used to, but once i stopped fighting them and just moved the character in a more leisurely way, i found the whole experience more enjoyable.  wouldn't mind them tightening up the responsiveness a little, tho.i bought this day one, after having followed it for quite a while.  it was worth the looie.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: THIS REVIEW CONTAINS SPOILERS "Our commitment is to deliver unique experiences that treat people with respect "I find it hard to agree that the player is treated with respect in this unique experience. For 90% of the game the designers have enforced that the character should move at an overly cautious, weary pace. Not only is this annoying in the many situations where you will want to move faster, it is often at odds with the very story they desire to tell. How is there such a huge gap between what the designers seem to think is a good pace and what many feel a gravitation toward?The main character, despite being in seemingly urgent circumstances never seems to want to RUN to save his lives of his WIFE and BABY CHILD, personally, this takes me out of the experience a little. To be fair, maybe my desired pace is not what the designers had in mind, but that is precisely a shortcoming that has made this game worse, what exactly did they have in mind? I think it is a little ridiculous to expect everyone to want to gaze and appreciate your camera angles instead of exercising their agency and appreciating each piece at a speed they feel comfortable, you know, playing a game. The sound design is great, as well as the excruciating effort put into the coordination of set pieces, gigantic vistas, and environmental design. The visual storytelling is obtuse, and the teams desire to walk you through an impressively seamless flowing set disintegrates into multiple flowing dream-like sequences (in the mid way) that beat the horse to death. It actually does this to an extent it becomes confusing what is going on.You really get the sense that there isn't a clear direction to the story, when the end came around it was sudden and I felt I had missed something.While the shader effect used in gameplay sections is quite nice, most of, if not all sequences often boil down to the following :"Ok player, find the piece of the level with some yellow on it indicating it is a handle, then make him walk (not run) over to it and press the A button" "Ok player, time to watch the shader go off now, ok that was fun", "Ok player, time to show us you understand what gravity is, over and over again." "Ok player, press the left trigger""Ok player, press the right trigger"This is not game design to me, this is a long winded, and low effort.What's on offer is a beautiful enough cinematography storybook, yet the pages can only ever turn at a pace that would lull a snail to sleep.Showing some Cube Raptor Aliens stalk the useless Father, meet the survivors of the apocalypse, watch the cyber ninja run and jump around having more fun than you will for these 3 short hours of story telling tour de force, you're in the alien ship now, now you're the most important man on earth saving the world from certain destruction. All ideas you've seen before executed in more depth and dignity. I don't want to be rude, but for $30 it does not at all deliver any kind of lasting memory, and is over in 3 hours.The past achievements of the creators are not lost on me, but with great reputation comes some amount of expectation, pretending this game was coherent would be silly. Hopefully this can be a great learning experience for the studio!Back to the drawing board and can't wait for the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to rate but I guess I'm going with a thumbs up. Like most everyone has pointed out, the controls are subpar and need to be patched or something. It's frustrating but I will say it's not completely game breaking; it is possible to play the game to completion in it's current state. The puzzles are OK, occasionally good but very little of it feels intuitive. I had to consult a walk-through guide a good five or six times because I couldn't figure out what the game wanted me to do. Towards the end of the game the plot meanders all over the place and things become pretty abstract, sort of a Space Odyssey type of ending that's sort of cool but not particularly satisfying lol.So why the thumbs up? All I can say is, Somerville succeeds in being something different. This is a strange story rendered in  very unique, eerie settings. Art direction and soundtrack are where this game excels. But it's nowhere near as compelling as INSIDE or Limbo. It almost feels like a project from the creators of Vane, another very fascinating but quite flawed game. For those of us who like weird games, we look forward to experiencing releases such as Vane or White Shadows or Scorn or even something like Obduction. None of those games are perfect but they  definitely succeed at being off the beaten path when it comes to world building and story lines. If you're that type of gamer, I'd say you should give Somerville a try. But having played it, I don't know that I'd pay full price for it unless or until they patch the controls and some of the character movement, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: The beginning of the game is captivating with great audio and visuals, but the game sadly moves into chore territory. It is a bit of a walking simulator at times with fancy effects going on. Some memorable moments mixed with mundane filler puzzles and plenty of "this doesn't make sense at all" character interactions (I'm not spoiling anything). The end of the game left me with a feeling of "thanks for wasting my time". I really tried appreciating it for what it was but something left me with a bad taste I can't shake. I do think you should give it a shot if you are interested in this but know that it has its flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Eerily beautiful and the perfect game to play after Limbo and Inside but ... once the aliens have you and have left your family behind, the story just drops away into repetitive nonsense and leaves you deeply disappointed. Also ... there's the dog (or rather where's the dog), who seems to have vanished in all the endings I could find. Poor storytelling mars a beautiful idea - shame ...
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I liked this game. However, the narrative doesn't elevate itself to someting like  did. The movement feels clunky, and it has a few technical issues.But on the positive side we have the sound design and puzzles which are simple and clever. I give this game my recommendation, but I would recommend INSIDE even more.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game.It's a little clunky in the movement. Mainly early on due to larger scenes and walk speed. This is less an issue in the back 2/3 of the game I thought. Also the fact that you can move in 3D in the scene, so fwd/back vs just left/right on a plane in a 3D world. But this and some other things are nit picks. After some time with the game it gels and you just play and the issues fade into the background.I really enjoyed the visuals, atmosphere and storytelling, even though the ending and other details are more like "wtf?" than anything solid. But I can roll with that for the overall experience, which I really liked.Sound effects are amazing and I love the lack of any interface (apart from the first room or so) and love the lack of any spoken dialogue. Failing a sequence of dying is never a chore as the checkpoints are liberal and on point and you never lose much progress. Load times are very fast, too. Dying is a non issue, I thought.There are some really good puzzles once you get going. While not up to the level of INSIDE, across the board, the game is enjoyable and I wanted more of it. End of the day the game could have used a couple more months of polish.All in all there are not enough atmospheric cinematic platformers like this game (or Inside or Limbo or way back in the day, Out of this World). I can overlook a little clunk and sit back and soak in the game. If you like cinematic platformers and stroy/puzzle driven games, you will likely enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game, can't say there's a lot of replay value though. I spent a little bit at the end of the game trying to get all of the endings and will likely replay the whole game once more to try and 100% it. I'll probably come back to it every once and a while like I do with Journey. As for bugs, I noticed some animations didn't line up to where the person would actually end up and when your wife picks up your child they will disappear for split second before reappearing. I saw that there was a rare chance to get stuck in the falling animation but, you will probably not encounter this in your playthrough as I didn't in 5ish hours. Most of these will probably be fixed when the planned hotfix comes out later down the line. And if you asking, "Should I buy this?" I'd probably pick it up if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting so long for this release, and yes! It was a great play through. I love the use of SFX and music to set the tone and guide the player through the game, it really allowed me to explore the beautiful environments. As a gamer who first experience Another World and Flashback at their local Sears (electronic department), it was so rewarding to enjoy Somerville in all its glory. Incorporating 3D movement did take me out of story from time to time but got me saying "oh yeah duh". Somerville is shorter than I would have liked and the ending a bit different than expected, but overall, it was worth the wait. Thanks Jumpship for your work and ready to see what you cook up next!
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Got exactly what I was hoping for from this game! Music, visuals, story, all top-notch. Invested in the story throughout, if this is your type of game, you'll have fun! People who have issues with the puzzles need to play their favorite lego game from their childhood lmao. Glad I played this game before looking at the reviews if I'm gonna be honest.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: similar as many have said to Inside and Limbo, though not quite as polished and you likely need some beefier gpu since those came around. : )  Still with my 7? year old system its doing ok. Nifty use of 3d with the side-scrollish animation and perspective shots. If you did *not* like Inside or Limbo, doubtful you will like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game, i completed the game at 100%.The only thing that it's kinda concerning it's that the game gets laggy, even for my PC specs (NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti, 16 GB RAM and AMD Ryzen 3400 with Radeon Vega Graphics which you should more than enough.)But everything else it's just great, in my opinion i really recommend SOMERVILLE, just make sure to have good specs!
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: I understand why people had high expectations for this, but it ain't really a Playdead game, so you have to forgive the game when some jank happens. Overall, I think it was super fun and had interesting puzzles, but the ending was a bit too obscure and the game was a bit short for the $25 price tag. I'd give it an 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: The player animations are pretty lackluster. You clip through stuff regularly, the animations get cancelled often, the interact button doesn't always trigger and sometimes it's quite hard to navigate because of the fixed camera with 3d movements. I thought the game was okay to start with, but the problems listed above caused me much frustration pretty early into the game. Also, the story wasn't very good, but more importantly, the execution of the story wasn't good. It missed those subtle moments that made Inside and Limbo so great in my opinion. It kinda redeemed itself towards the end, because the last chapters were good.If you go into this game with the expectations of Limbo and Inside quality atmosphere, storytelling and animations, you'll be disappointed. But it still showed those quality moments towards the end, it was just a struggle to get there. My advice? Buy it when it goes on sale. 6/10 recommended (just barely).
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Putting aside patchable technical issues, this is a really middling entry into the cinematic puzzle game genre. These are my main criticisms.Technical quality is something that can be easily improved in the future, but a lot of the creative concepts in the game felt flaccid. I pray to god that people writing and illustrating sci-fi stories will soon lose their infatuation with RGB lights, "bad-ass" military concepts and angular geometric greeblecore.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Somerville was a hard one for me. Ever since I discovered it a couple of months ago I was hyped for its release, especially after playing Inside. However, its important to remember that Inside IS NOT Somerville. Although Jumpship was cofounded by a CEO of Playdead, this does not necessarily make the game an immediate step up from Inside. Regardless of all of this, I still enjoyed Somerville but it felt like an unpolished release. Multiple performance issues on PC, shaky/quick camera cuts and pans, difficult interact prompts, and overall strange 2.5d movement led to me being dissatisfied with what I expected the game to be. However, the art style, general game engine physics, sound design, and ending sequences were all huge pros. Small discrepancies in the gaming process was what brought this game downhill, but in general the puzzles, graphics, and story made up for it. Overall I give this game an 8/10 recommendation, something that's a must to pick up if its on sale, or something that is worth getting for full price if some of the minor performance issues are fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: A short story told through astounding and diverse set pieces. Compared to Limbo and Inside, this game tells a more grounded narrative during an apocalyptic/invasive setting. The dark tone of this world is usually contrasted with vivid design elements. Unlike those games, the story immediately introduces the simple goal of the protagonist throughout the journey. Although some characters evoked interest, the resolution of the story felt uncompelling and rushed. As much as I wanted to be invested in this strange world, I was only left confused while wondering my involvement in the story. The physics-based gameplay mechanics can get a bit tedious, but the character's interactive abilities were spectacular to watch. Sadly, Somerville does not utilize the full potential of these tools, where puzzles are often left basic and uninspiring. As much as I wanted this launch to be smooth, there was a couple of game-breaking and minor bugs that halted the game's pace. While Somerville does not live up to the reputation of Inside and Limbo, the game sacrifices gameplay depth for its unique and eye-catching art direction.My rating: 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Do you love Playdead's LIMBO and INSIDE or Tarsier Studio's Little Nightmares series? Do you own a controller? If you answered yes to those, then you are in for a nice treat with Somerville! Although it rather disappointingly fails to reach the heights set by those titles, and the game's clunkiness will likely prevent you from wanting to play through it more than once, which is a real shame, and hopefully a patch or two will change that feeling in the future.It's hard to talk about Somerville without spoiling it, and it certainly is a game best experienced with no knowledge of what to expect. The intro sequence in particular is one of the greatest intros I've ever seen in a videogame, and I was simply blown away by all the eye and ear candy that was going on!This intro quickly introduces you to Somerville's excellent sound design, which remains impressive throughout the game, and a very exciting opening set piece, although that segment probably does end a little bit too soon. As a result, the initial impression of the game as it properly opens up after this seems a little more underwhelming, and the game struggles to reach the intro's height again, even though it's not too long before other interesting elements and set pieces are thrown your way. One of those interesting elements are Somerville's puzzles, which are pretty original in places and will leave you with a 'Oh, that's clever!' impression when you (quickly) figure out what the solution is. Sadly, the game's occasionally broken physics do let some of these puzzles down though, and will sometimes leave you with a 'Glad I don't have to do that again' impression, when the game engine itself gets in the way of you solving that puzzle smoothly. The game has other flaws too, the most obvious of which is the 2.5D movement. Similar to Little Nightmares, your character can move around freely in a 2.5D space, and to be honest, I don't think it's working as well at the moment as it does in Little Nightmares II. Some of the puzzles work great with the 2.5D movement, but when you're simply traversing the landscape, it doesn't feel as fluid. You'll often clip the environment around you, and there are places where you'll feel drawn to explore where there's no visible boundary, only to be hit with an invisible wall. I have also encountered instances of my character being stuck inside the terrain, forcing me to reload the last checkpoint, which thankfully are very generously placed. You have to be ridiculously precise with interacting with objects too. I spent way too much time trying to get my character into a very specific spot to interact with a plug or switch. It does take you out of the experience a little bit, and you will often end up wishing the movement was on a 2D plane like LIMBO and INSIDE, but when the game does something great with it, it's great! But sadly, the clunkiness is enough to drag certain parts of the game down and leave a lasting poor impression.Also, a quick note for you Ultrawide monitor owners out there, I'm playing this with a 21:9 Ultrawide monitor and the game scales pretty nicely to my aspect ratio and resolution, with miniscule black borders on the left and right, not enough to notice in normal gameplay though, and it looks very nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed my playthrough. The world and atmosphere is incredible. The art style is perfect and the character animations are full of emotion, though at times they don't always match the action occurring in the environment. Trying to figure out the story from the little information we get is fun, leading to a fairly satisfying ending.I do take issue with some of the puzzles though. I wouldn't categorise it as a puzzle game, but there are some puzzle sequences. When the puzzles work they feel satisfying, but more often than not its a struggle due to the janky interactions that require you to be in unfairly specific locations to activate. After the first hour I noticed the janky interactions less but maybe this is me just getting used to it

_childDocuments_.review: As a preface to this, I think 90% of the gameplay problems could be solved with UI prompts. If you haven't played Inside, just go play that one if you want it for the gamePros- Gorgeous art style, love it want prints of it around my house and an art bookCons- Basically everything else- I feel no emotional attachment from any of the characters. _childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: There is no way I am giving this a negative review. But there are definitely many problems. The game is full of good ideas and creative puzzles. The visuals and atmosphere are great, I liked the whole trip, even though I feel the ending has been rushed. I think it's hard to make sense of the story. At first our mission is quite concrete. We are basically looking for our family and trying to survive against whatever is invading the earth. Then we end up in some kind of cosmic journey and it feels....random. Things happen. And then it ends abruptly. I am not sure to see how the player is supposed to understand any of this. Inside was cryptic but not that much.Now, the biggest problem is the controls. They suck big time. It's hard to describe, but the character is very unpleasant to move. It's clunky as hell. And I hate how the "rules" change everytime. How many times I kept holding the A button and the character just doesn't want to run. How many times I had to make several attempts for simple actions. How many times I had to play with the physics just to be able to go where I want. It's really messy.Second problem is the lack of polish. The animations for example. When you have to plug a cable, the character doesn't plug it, the physics engine does. So bascially, the character will let go of the cable instead of playing an animation, and the cable will plug itself if its collision box meets the collision box of the target. It's ugly everytime it happens. Same for death scenes animations, I loled so hard because they are just plain bad. The game does a quick job to hide them behind a black game over screen.Third problem is the camera perspective. The camera does a good job in the aesthetic department of the game but just doesn't care about the player comfort. It's just hard to see where to go sometimes and it just doesn't help with the stiff controls.I really feel bad for Jumpship regarding all these negative reviews because this game deserves better than that. But I am still confused as to why Jumpship would risk to destroy a potential success by delivering a game riddled with so many mechanical defects. They should have released it one or two month later just to get rid of all those obvious glitches. But what this game really needed is good controls. I played with a Xbox 360 pad and I couldn't help but think about how slow and sluggish it feels when you move the character.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting on this game to come out since the first trailer, so I was ecstatic when I heard that it finally released. I looked into the publisher, Jumpship, a while ago and saw that Dino Patty- the Playdead CEO who worked on  and - was the co-founder of Jumpship, so I just KNEW this was gonna be a great game. I finished Somerville today and I am so sad to say how disappointed I am. I was hoping this would be another banger like  with almost no dialogue but carrying a deep story that sucks you in, but I watched from the beginning all the way through the end credits and I'm still clueless to the point of this game or the story it was trying to tell. I feel like I got no resolution for all the hours I spent playing. Chris Olsen said himself that this game is "definitely not a puzzle platformer," but it so obviously wants to be one. I love puzzle platformer games, but this just felt like a walking simulator with a couple simple puzzles to solve blockades in your path. Don't get me wrong though- the game was absolutely stunning, and that opening scene was fabulous. I would probably recommend this game, since it was a very unique sci-fi adventure that others might enjoy more than I did. I just got my hopes up for a bussin puzzle platformer and got an "experience" instead. 7/10UPDATE: There's another ending called "Understanding" which is SOO much better and makes me feel better about this game. If you find all the little ball creatures, they tell you (in a sense) how to get all the different endings... or you can just watch the yt video like I did lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a stunning story with amazing visuals, fans of inside, limbo, or the Little Nightmare Series should definitely try this masterpiece. It has stunning camera work, great puzzles, one of the coolest art styles in any game ever, and amazing sound design. The puzzle mechanics are cool and very original and the change of pace and scenery always make every encounter feel fresh and unique. The only thing wrong are some minor bugs but that never inhibited game-play too much for me, the worst bug literally just made me restart an easy puzzle. Definitely recommend to those who like story games(Also post patch update fixed pretty much all the bugs)
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game at $10 or less.The game is a pretty great adventure/puzzle experience.People will compare this game to Limbo and Inside, and they are kind of right to do that. While the gameplay isn't exactly the same, it is similar enough to put them on comparison. Somerville doesn't really feel like as rewarding/satisfying of an experience as the other two, but it is still worth the investment at no more than $10 in my opinion.I really couldn't understand the story, nor did I really care too much to dig in and find out what really happened...The sounds and music are excellent!To beat the dead horse, I believe this game is worth playing, but only if you can pick it up for $10 or less.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute master class of visual storytelling, sound design, and atmosphere. JUMPSHIP has created a very interesting world with beautiful art direction. Although the story and narrative aren't quite as strong as it's spiritual predecessor INSIDE; I think it was very much worth the 6 hours of play it took me, as it was a hell of an experience. The narrative does seem to sort of scramble and not know where it wants to go towards the end, which is in my opinion supported by the fact that the player has multiple choices that affect the outcome of the ending. I wish it was more a tight package in the end like INSIDE was, but still a great game experience nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: To get right to the point, this game has its ups and downs. To be fair, I'm writing this review the day after the game came out, so a part of me really hopes that the issues I bring up will be fixed. The positives: The story, the style, the music, and the sound design of this game are incredible. The minimalist style works very well with both the sci-fy aspects of the game and the natural environments, ex. forests, cities, houses, caves. The character animations are unique and add a ton of personality to the individual characters--for example, the dog's ears will bounce as he runs, the child claps his hands as he is watching television. These little things bring the characters to life and make you care about them all the more. The music and sound design are very notable, the world sounds alive and full, even in silent moments there is a world of sound. The soundtrack is mostly piano and it works perfectly for the mood and the emotional moments of the story. The characters too will make dynamic sounds, as you continue running your character's breath will become more labored, etc. The story is similar to games like Limbo and Inside, giving you little to go off of and letting you just experience the game as it is. Upon my first play-through of the game I was a bit upset when I finished, but after some more work I got the good ending and am very happy. Overall, this game looks and sounds very, very good. Now, the negatives: the controls. The controls in this game are not good. They are clunky and slow and frustrating. There were many times during the game that I was pulled out of the experience because I was having extreme trouble with the controls. The issue is that the game tries to take the profile angle from Inside but have it in a 3D plane, and we get the same issues we had in Little Nightmares 1--characters get stuck in walls, invisible walls block your progress, puzzles relying on perspective are difficult for the wrong reasons, etc. The controls are just not great at all, and while you can definitely push through them, they're a big set back for the game. The game also has a lot of bugs present, characters will flicker and vanish sometimes, objects will suddenly stop existing, the game will stutter, animations won't play properly, etc. Once again, since the game is new, I'm willing to give it some leeway, but the bugs were noticeable and pulled me out of the moment more than once. So, overall, this game is very good. Fans of Limbo and Inside will love it. The controls and the bugs definitely need work, as they really hold the game back, but if/once those are fixed, this game will truly be something special. Until then, it's still definitely worth a play. P.S. There is a happy ending! It's difficult as hell to figure out but trust me, it's worth it. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely did not like this game. Atmosphere? There is almost no such thing. Schizophrenia? Almost yes. Why was there such a mess with INSIDE ideas, why was there so much abstraction added, why such an abstract end that does not agree in any way with a very verified and understandable beginning. Two-thirds of the game you play for fun, then some nonsense begins, as if the authors did not understand how to finish what they started, and the time and money for development ran out. And then, a very short game. Terrible level design, sometimes it is absolutely unclear what and how to do, although you understand that you need to lift and move something as usual, you constantly get up and do not understand what and how to do. This game is when a cool design and the ideas of a skilled artist fall into the hands of an inept level designer. I won't say anything about history, it's in the spirit of "I see it that way." I do not recommend the game, wait for discounts, for once and forget.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Falls short in a lot of areas when compared to Limbo and Inside, and while understanding they are a different studio now, it felt it needed a longer story to it, and a better ending instead of the trippy dream-state nonsense it turned into. The puzzles were way to simple and never had me stumped, only died around 2-3 times, and the overall game is very very short game, easily can finish in under 3 hours. Falls very short towards the end of the game, and leaves a bit of an unpleasant taste, feels like the writers just winged the last fifth of it all, goes from a what seems a depth filled war of the worlds type game to some unexplained deep thought BS.On the plus side, the artwork, graphics and lighting are nothing short of breathtaking, but I'd say it's defs not worth $30, maybe $10-15, or wait for gamepass etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Somerville

_childDocuments_.review: Like others have stated, there is a lot of potential in this game. Great visuals, story seems pretty cool and the sound effects & music are amazing. Sadly, the terrible movement, abundance of invisible walls, weird hitboxes and - most of all - the huge FPS drops ruins the experience. The game is extremely laggy on my computer even though I'm running a machine above the recommendations. I also had to restart a chapter or two due to scripted events getting stuck. It took me 20 minutes to figure this out as there were interactable objects in the area which I thought I should be using somehow. Turns out they were just red herrings, which is quite annoying. I've been waiting for this game for years, thinking it would be blowing my mind like Inside did, and instead it's a disappointment. I think/hope Jumpship can fix it, so I'll be coming back in a few weeks to see if it has been patched. For now, I'm leaving it.

name: Decarnation
detailed_description: Decarnation plunges you into a haunting, dreamlike adventure where reality and fantasy become one. Inspired by some of the most influential surrealist works (Silent Hill, the original tale of Alice in Wonderland, films by David Lynch and Satoshi Kon...), allow yourself to be swept away by an intense and mesmerising story, oscillating between dreams and nightmares. Gloria is a cabaret dancer at the end of her rope. As her career, relationships and self-esteem begin to deteriorate, a mysterious patron makes her an offer she couldn’t possibly refuse. Will this event mark the end of her recent struggles , or the beginning of her descent into hell? Decarnation is a story of survival, where monsters and nightmares weave themselves into the fabric of everyday life. Get ready for a poignant and captivating adventure! With a wide variety of mini-games, Decarnation expertly brings together the classic elements of horror and adventure games, where each challenge requires consideration, responsiveness and coordination. Solve cryptic riddles, confront ominous enemies and explore a bewildering world... Decarnation's Rêve and Cauchemar soundtracks feature contributions from numerous artists, including the renowned composer Akira Yamaoka (Silent Hill) whose works blend horror and the paranormal, breathing life into this nightmarish tale. 'I'm delighted to have been able to take part in the development of Decarnation [...] I've developed a special bond with this game. Numerous references and inspirations from cult horror works have shaped the world of Decarnation - can you spot them all?

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell French people are great at art, because this is a grotesque beauty.I was fortunate enough to playtest Decarnation and now Im allowed to talk about it, great! Its most definitely very unique, every area and dream world you visit has its very own design and is filled to the brim with details. Despite this, the experience is rather narrative driven, with some short puzzles here and there, and other interesting mechanics. Glorias character is very fleshed out and keeps on growing, the rest of the cast is also interesting. I wish to go more in depth but want this to be spoiler free.The major problem I had with the game so far is the aformentioned shortness that puzzles have. Every area is so beautiful and carefully created, but you always last just a few minutes there, gameplay and puzzle sections are done extremely fast, which somewhat ruins the immersion. You cant really take everything in, except you actively do nothing before proceeding.Thank you Shiro Unlimited, for choosing me to be part of this adventure early, and crushing some bugs while at it.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: To be a woman...to experience every woman's fear...Finished this game in a bit over 7 hours. Challenging, atmospheric, terrifying, and heartbreaking. Decarnation tells the story of Gloria and her life as it spirals out of control. I wish I could go in depth but I'd hate to spoil anything. Gloria is written as a multi-dimensional, complicated being with complex feelings. We often float between reality and her dreams, which are full of Junji Ito-style body horror. The artwork is fantastic, music is beautiful, characters are interesting. It's only January and this might be one of my favorite games of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but it kept me entertained for about five hours until I saw the credits rolling, which means I did enjoy it. You get a rather unique game, a conversation-heavy thriller about an unsecure woman in her late twenties meeting the man of her nightmares. I won’t spoil what happened to her, but it was an extremely unpleasant experience. You play the woman during her real life, and you play her in her sleep while she explores her subconsciousness and confronts her psychological demons. Gameplay consists of exploring the environment and some puzzles, mainly of the simple find/use an object variety, and there are a bunch of different but not too taxing action/puzzle mini-games. Gamepad is supported, there are no voice-overs but a few good music tracks. Finished it with only 8/15 cheavos.Mature-themed thriller with simple puzzles and mini-games. The story left me thinking about it long after I finished it.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: + Decarnation oozes style and is very confident in  it's trying to be; its influences are obvious (Silent Hill, Perfect Blue, etc.) but it borrows without feeling boring or derivative. + The game looks great & sound fantastic with beautiful pixel art and a catchy soundtrack.  The game's arguably a perfect length but it's almost disappointing that you don't spend more time in it to better appreciate what's been built here.+ It handles sensitive subject matter with unusual grace and, instead of fumbling or coming off exploitative, I ended up feeling a variety of emotions--sadness, revulsion, pity, hope.- Decarnation is light in the actual "gameplay" department; much of your time will be spent walking between Point A & Point B, reading dialogue, and watching events unfold.  The actual mechanics--the minigames, the puzzle solving, combat, etc.--are fairly limited and may leave the average player wanting more.- Ironic (given its floral symbolism), Decarnation sometimes seems allergic to stopping and "smelling the roses".  The game's environments and set pieces are impressive and painstakingly detailed, but short of stopping to stare at them, the game gives you very little reason to spend time in many of them.  At times it felt like I was jumping between one brief scene after another in a way that was more disjointed than deliberate.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of psychological horror/thrillers like Perfect Blue, Misery, and/or anything by David Lynch, you'll probably love this game. In Decarnation, you play as Gloria, a fading cabaret star who's trying to keep her sanity while trapped by an abhorrent admirer. It's a very character-driven game where we explore Gloria's inner world, and if she's willing to give in to the madness or find a way out. Essentially, it's a story rich game where the story is actually compelling.A few things to keep in mind before purchasing: the game isn't necessarily scary. It's more unnerving/unsettling than flat out terrifying. Someone wanting a horror game that keeps you on edge might not get a lot from this game. It's also worth pointing out that there are significant chunks of the game with no gameplay; the first chapter almost plays like a visual novel, and you will have to be patient when the puzzles and other gameplay mechanics kick in. Anyone not interested in reading swaths of text will probably not like this game. With all that said, I'm glad I picked this up, and if the above concerns don't apply to you, I definitely recommend it. A great story-driven indie title bolstered by incredible art direction and a satisfying character arc.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: A game about finding beauty on the inside. Or maybe about finding beautiful insides? Hard to say for sure. It's tough to decode symbolism while gagging.- Grotesque & surreal atmosphere.- Oppressive, tense narrative.- Excellent use of soundtrack to convey protag's state of mind.- Minigames are mostly a distraction.- More frequent checkpoints would help to prevent rehashing meaty story segments.- Fans of uncanny or Cronenbergian horror- Fans of character dramas with strong stomachs.- Anyone coming home from a bad date or job interview who could use some perspective. Another atmospheric horror game in which you learn all about the protagonist and then immediately wish you didn't. Different cultural lens than Decarnation (Taiwanese/Chinese) and tells a more historically grounded, but by no means less horrifying or surreal, story.Did my review help you make a purchase decision? Maybe I can help you find other games you'd like.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: i for one enjoy good interactive storytelling and don't require fast shooting finger twitching action, but others may be disappointed by the lack of gameplay in this game. this is narrative storytelling occasionally punctuated by mini-games, not a game occasionally punctuated by cutscenes, set your expectations accordingly. as far as the narrative is concerned, i found it to be an excellently told psychological horror thriller story with fantastic art and memorable music. the original tunes from synthpop act fleur et bleue are an absolute treat. DO CHECK CONTENT/TRIGGER WARNINGS before purchasing. this game covers heavy topics. in my opinion it handles them with respect, grace and tact, with nothing gratuitous or glorified, but they are still heavy topics none the less. my only real issue...are the rhythm mini-games. i know this isn't Guitar Hero. i know that you are supposed to fail some of the rhythm sections as a reflection of your lead characters instability. BUT...the inputs often did not make any sense in regards to the music, and the input timing was always off just slightly from the actual tempo. i'm not trying to toot my own horn, but i'm *great* at rhythm games. i am a musician, i started on drums, i am very good at keeping time. when i play rhythm games i watch the upcoming button prompts but i always input them on feel, because i don't need to watch the note land in the circle to know when to hit the beat. the input timing on this game are just slightly off enough that i *had* to watch and hit the note on the visual of it entering the circle. i was not using my ears at all, it was literally easier to take my headphones off because hearing an actual beat was too distracting and i naturally wanted to follow it. if i have to play an AUDIO rhythm game VISUALLY, you messed up. i don't have input lag issues on any other game i have ever played, so i would be shocked if this was an issue with my setup. if this was an intentional design choice for the sake of immersion then i applaud the developers effort even though they chose the most frustrating way to do it. but this doesn't feel intentional, it feels like someone who doesn't even like music programmed the note patterns.that was a LONG rant for such a small part of the game, so if you find the story intriguing don't like it dissuade you. the rhythm games are only a tiny fraction of the game. i just needed to vent that frustration. 4 out of 5, recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I'm granting "Decarnation" a hesitant recommendation for its superb pixel art and genuinely creepy imagery alone. The premise is nice, too: it's essentially a gender swap of Stephen King's "Misery", and I like it. There's a clear and well-intended angle to the story which I appreciate. However, I liked the plot well enough until I didn't. The ending fell flat for me. While I believe that horror genre has enormous therapeutic potential, I don't think it should feel like a poor therapy session. Besides, the thing about therapy is that it should NOT push you towards vague solutions (such as "find your hope!", "find your intuition!" and so on), but rather teach a language of introspection. Instead, "Decarnation" becomes a pretentious motivational coach by the end, beating you over the head with its message. It'll work for some but whoooo boy, it did NOT work for me. One other thing I did not appreciate were all the minigames. I'd prefer a straight up 'walking sim'. I for one don't see anything wrong with some chill exploration, and I don't need it to be occasionally broken up with a bunch of QTEs. So there, these were my frustrations with "Decarnation". I still recommend it. It's a decent game. And besides, it reminded me of an old favorite of mine, "Sanitarium", with its inner mindscapes and not-so-subtle metaphors. And the thing about "Sanitarium" is that its second half sucked even worse. And yet I still remember it after so many years. So... Good luck, "Decarnation".
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game!  The subject matter is pretty sensitive but the writing feels like it was done with care. I think it's easy to fall into just writing "misery for the sake of misery" with horror, but this is not the case at all. The horror elements and art style complimented each other very well. I don't think this game would be the same without the art style for sure. It was beautiful and horrific and I loved every moment of it. Akira Yamaoka's music for this game is great, too!  If you love trauma horror narratives, you have to check it out. There are several puzzles and minigames, which aren't difficult, but the focus is definitely the atmosphere, artstyle, and writing. Can't wait to see the future work of these devs! Their first game knocked it out of the park already!
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you for making this game. It spoke to me in a way that no other game has in a very long time. Beautiful visuals, touching narrative, fleshed out characters, catchy music. This is why I like horror, such a good medium to convey human experiences.Thank you for your hard work, dedications, passion and whatever else kept you going through this production. Loved it from start to end.PS: for those of you who don't like games that don't like narrative centric games ("walking sims") this probably isn't a game for you. If you do like narrative heavy games,  I do recommend it because in it's genre it's one of the best I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I never write reviews, but I thought this time would be different as I was completely disappointed by this game.First off, I thought that the visuals, style, and some of the music was great. I also found the plot to be engaging at first, and it did keep me interested enough to finish the game.Unfortunately, I was underwhelmed by the story and bizarre gameplay choices made. I felt the story lacked subtlety, and the dialogue had too many puns and jokes for its own good.The mini-games, especially the rhythm game, became tedious and repetitive. I felt as though the interactive parts of the game were forced into the game to justify itself as a "game" rather than just a series of cutscenes.There are other issues with the dialogue. At points the game auto-advances dialogue for no apparent reason. I disliked the fact that some dialogue would occur during mini-games or during songs with lyrics which made it difficult to follow along. I really feel as though this could have been a great game, but personally I ended up not enjoying it. Ultimately, I would not recommend this game if you are on the fence about buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have to finish Decarnation to speak highly of it, quite frankly. Its understanding of psychological horror is admirable from the onset; small details quietly but precisely shape an unsettling, macabre aesthetic and narrative, paying homage to both classical and modern art as part of its tumultuous tapestry. As a filmmaker, I've already noted elements of Satoshi Kon's "Perfect Blue" intersecting with parallels of David Lynch's "Mulholland Drive" alongside some obvious reverence for Dario Argento's "Suspiria", Park Chan-wook's "Oldboy", and Stanley Kubrick's "The Shining." Make no mistake, however; Decarnation does not derive its worth from the works it draws from, nor does it falter in weaving a captivating web of its own design. For me the weakest piece of this puzzle is the "combat," although I hesitate to describe it as such. Often you enter an area and get swallowed up by some abomination a number of times before stumbling into the next stage. It doesn't necessarily add much to the experience, and that part of the game is rarely frightening. The implications of the thing, not unlike Silent Hill before it, are far more integral to the game than its interactive confrontations. Even if Akira Yamaoka had no involvement, the score would be top tier; its visuals, while simplistic, have an engaging character; and, significantly, Claudia's story almost immediately and effortlessly communicates both the vulnerability and the strength of women in the face of dire traumas. I would like some improvement for the timing on the dance sequences, but I wouldn't discount it for that alone when they are enjoyable nonetheless. Don't pass this one up, this is something special regardless of its small missteps.

_childDocuments_.review: Decarnation is an excellent pixel art based horror with a dark disturbing story tackling challenging issues. The plot here revolves around our protagonist, a dancer in Paris who is finding herself lost in life she quickly finds herself getting an interesting offer from what appears to be a rich adoring fan an offer that sends her into a nightmare experience that leads to her being tracked in her psych.Gameplay wise most of this game is focused on the story. It's a walking simulator with occasional puzzles and sometimes some light combat/stealth mechanics too. Much of the time is spent reading dialogue and doing simple quicktime events, however the story is so engaging that even if it didn't have these light interactions and puzzles it would still be excellent. What matters here are the visuals and plot which carry the game to amazing heights.Visually this game is astounding , the pixel art is disturbing, gorgeous and creates such horrific, shocking imagery that you'll be lost in the nightmare worlds that the leads psych conjures up as she goes through unimaginable trauma. Sound wise its also great, the soundtrack features some heavyweights of music and gaming contributing fantastic audio. There is no voice acting, but it doesn't need it either. Not much replayability here but the game is a good price for it's 5-6 hour length. Decarnation is a visual, audio and story telling work of art that will leave you gripped and horrified to it's disturbing conclusion.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

While you not find beauty inside you.It’s a great variant to get unusual experience and touch some of problems that still happens in our society. I’d like to say that it’s a negative that we can’t choose on some moments what we want to do. But because of this it surely can be called psychological horror.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game, but I think it markets itself quite wrong and much to it's own detrement.This thing is quite "light" on gameplay. Most of your 5-6 hours you will spend reading text and interacting with each item in a room so the next dialogue triggers. You have a few "dodge the monster"-sequeneces, a few rhythm game sequences and very few unique things like the chess puzzle, which you can see in the screenshots. It's not really an action game, I would even argue it's not really a puzzle game because at almost no point do you have to think about the solution. They really don't "require consideration, responsiveness and coordination", they are not in the least "cryptic" and if you think of "confronting enemies" in any "fight"-sense, you are far off. Without any negative conotation meant: it's far closer to an interactive story/experience. People wouldn't call a Telltale game an action game because it has the odd QTE in it either. But the story Decarnation tells is absolutely fantastic. It's far more grounded in reality than the storepage might make you think, you get a stellar written, very cerebral Psychothriller here that deals incredibly well with a lot of mature topics. This is the kind of writing that keeps you going for "just five more minutes" and before you realize it an hour has passed. The pixelart is also great, especially when it comes to "monster"-design and their animations and it only elevates what is already a very good story. And while, sure, you can say "Oh this-or-that looks kinda Silent Hill-ish", I also don't think the game does itself any favors with that comparison - because the whole thing is more than strong enough to stand on it's own. Not only in terms of writing, but also in terms of the visuals that go along with it. I hope more people give Decarnation a chance, but I also hope the dev updates the store page to more accurately reflect what people are going to get here. I firmly believe there is a market for these kinds of games, but I think these players might not realize this might be for them. On the flipside, I could easily see someone expect something much different from this game and then end up disappointed so much from a gameplay perspective, that they might just abort/refund the game. And I want this to sell more copies, I want more people to experience this.If you don't mind a REALLY dark story, if you don't mind a game that is light on gameplay (and challenge), definitely give it a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: BUY IT, PLAY IT, YOU'LL NEVER FORGET IT.This game was an absolute ride, and I will surely remember it for the rest of my life. It reminded me of OMORI, Perfect Blue and Silent Hill in the strangest ways. The horror is incredibly real and well-written, and the graphics are dead gorgeous.The soundtrack is an absolute blast, and I just literally can't think of anything I DIDN'T like.Some people are saying the game is really short, but it took me nearly 9 hours to clear it just because there was so much gorgeous things to see.The best game I've experienced in the past couple of years. Thank you.
