_childDocuments_.review: . It plays more like a  with long segments during which you won't do anything except for reading the main character's anguishing thoughts and dialogues between her and other characters. You will face a few puzzles (and minigames) as you explore Gloria's quite colourful psyche but they're short and easy to solve.Now, thankfully Decarnation really shines with its narration and how it deals with serious topics. It was very refreshing to see how each artistic and practical decision made by the devs serves a purpose in the narrative, in a genre where games more often than not rely on gore and provocative imagery just for the sake of it. Here, it's filled to the brim with details that you can easily miss if you don't check (and re-check) your environment. The levels are beautifully crafted and evoke a sense of despair and longing for freedom.  you don't get to stay there long enough to take in all the gorgeous yet macabre imagery... And I get that, dreams are but cruel ephemeral illusions of a deeply warped reality. The soundtrack composed by Fleur Bleue and Akira Yamaoka can feel as liberating as it can feel suffocating in the best way possible ; it is the cement that holds together the bundle of joy that is Decarnation.The story wasn't quite what I envisioned it to be but in the end, thanks to these points, I felt invested enough to go through the entire experience. Is the game perfect ? No, but I do think it checks all the conditions to be a very enjoyable, immersive experience if you are willing to give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm genuinely shocked that I don't think I've ever heard anybody talk about this game. _childDocuments_.review: I'm having trouble putting into words everything this game meant to me. Game-play wise it unfolds like a play with mini games, puzzles, and exploration, and it's a beautiful show.Playing this game gives people a chance to experience firsthand a woman's fears and motivations, the expectations laid on her and others of her gender, and the way the male gaze affects them. The story is overflowing with visual metaphors for trauma, compartmentalization, and what the mind is willing to do to itself to survive insurmountable odds, as well as the effort it takes heal.I was chattering about this game nonstop over the three days I played it, and I'm still completely obsessed. The hungry mouths that are held at bay by the safety of spotlights, the half-removed but still utterly upsetting sight of Gloria's likeness being assaulted, the "trash compactor" for the traumas she can't handle being shaped like a woman's mouth adorned in lipstick.And the MECHANICS. The sheer amount of thought put into the programming of this game is thoughtful in a way I've never experienced. So many parts of this game call on the player to follow instinct in ways I didn't realize were possible. Subtle marks on a rug to indicate a necessary movement, using the safety of lights to avoid prowling predators, and the sleep mechanic?? That alone was groundbreaking to me.The game particularly hit close to home for me because the main character, Gloria, bears a strong resemblance to my abusive mother in ego, beauty, and even horoscope. It gave me a chance to look through her eyes, and see Gloria take the journey towards personal growth that my mother never did.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Solid little RPG-maker style horror/thriller. YMMV on the price, personally a 5-8 hour story well told is worth the 12 quid entry fee but others may not agree.The gameplay/puzzles/QTE's vary between between very neatly designed and irritating. Some sections it became almost pixel hunting and could sometimes be immersion breaking, overall was positive though.Story is very well told; as others have said fans of David Lynch et al will probably love this. Chibi art style juxtaposed with the dark subject material works very well.Excellent soundtrack/sound design in general.PSA: the content warning at the start is not to be taken lightly; some parts may hit too close to home for some people. Would not play it on a bad day if you are likely to be affected by any of the subjects listed in the content warning.

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game is more depressing than scary, lol. And super short. I'd normally refund but I feel bad because short games can still be good and the asking price isn't high. However, be aware that it's hella short. My hours played are a bit wonky according to steam but I've pretty sure I'm nearing the end.The game isn't much of a game. It's more of a visual novel with some basic rhythm game elements. In a nutshell, it deals with depression and the sexualization of women. The MC is a cabaret dancer, which is like a high class stripper that doesn't often get completely naked but does remove clothing.The MC is 29 years old, and that alone should probably say a lot lol. Though 30 years is quite young, it's a common 'joke' that woman stop being 'young and beautiful' at that point. The MC is also dating a college kid at the time, which must be at best like 20-22, but the game treats the relationship like she's 60 and the other girl is freshly 18. a 20-22 and a 29 year old in a relationship isn't the end of the world and the Mc calling the other girl a baby is ridiculous.I don't want to spoil much, but basically the MC bemoans the fact that's she aging and that her career is dead-ended by that fact, as beauty is a strong part of it. All the expected things happen right at the start; she's being replaced by younger dancers, her GF leaves her, a sculptor makes a statue of her but when she goes to see it some dude is groping it right in the museum, and all this sends her into a spiraling depression that makes her not pick up all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ red flags of an 'offer' that leaves her kidnapped by some pycho admirerer. You see this coming a mile away and this is all like the first 20 min.From there, you get a pretty looking but rather lackluster and uncreative story of depression and self-loathing while dealing with a psychopath abuser. I was kind of hoping for something like Silent Hill 4 where you're scratching your head as things become increasingly insane and trying to figure out what's going on.Right now, there isn't much mystery... or scariness. It's just really depressing because it hits home pretty hard. All the things that happen to her could happen to anyone and has. Maybe there will be some kind of twist at the end, but unless you feel like playing 'regular everyday life depression simulator' I wouldn't bother with the game.Calling this horror is beyond generous. And trust me, psychological horror can be done an infinite number of ways. Just like at OMORI.Edit: for those asking me about my playtime, I play on both Steam Deck and my PC and that's why it's not updated. Sometimes one doesn't update or the save doesn't automatically go throw, especially if you play games offline like I do at work. Usually if you leave the Steam Deck online long enough it fixes but I don't. It shoudl be fixed now, so please stop asking me about that yeesh.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tricky one to recommend. Decarnation is visually stunning, wears its inspirations on its sleeve, and has a pretty good opening story hook. So if that sells you already, I highly recommend it. But don't go in expecting an actual game, as most of the gameplay is walking around and clicking on things until things change, reading text, and doing very simple rhythm and timing minigames. Along with this are some puzzles to solve, some sequences where you have to run from an creature, and a boss fight towards the end, but those moments were few and far between. There are also some "gameplay" moments where you have to tap A or press a direction to perform an action, such as breathing or thinking, but these moments didn't exactly add a whole lot to the experience. I enjoyed the simplicity of the story and how it allowed for thorough exploration of Gloria's situation. The ending was a bit anticlimactic, and I think the villain should have gotten a bit more details in his backstory, but overall it was a decent experience. There are few tracks used, but I liked them all so it didn't detract anything. I'd say it was about a 6-7/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun game in which you discover the life of Gloria, a young dancer who is loving her life. Without spoiling it I can say that she goes through a ton of strange events and also terrible. It's like at first you're going to have an opinion about why all this is happening, and you're going to interpret it a certain way. You will either hate her or love her at the beginning. Your opinion will change little by little as you discover what is happening. It's very interesting, the story is a bit cliché yeah, but there are twists and events that make it worth playing. Some things might be disturbing for some people so, if you are sensitive you might wanna think twice before playing it. Not really scary, it's psychological horror before all. It took me near 7 hours to finish the game (I did it in two evenings and I still need a couple achievements) so it's not super long. I didn't like the same song playing over and over at the beginning but it shouldn't prevent anyone from having a good time. A fascinating, short experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game to others? Well - yes and no.No because:- Story can drag on and on without much gameplay inbetween- epilogue is incredibly slow/long and forces you to replay at least one minigame- the subject matter is incredibly uncomfortable though trigger warnings are given- puzzles are simple, do not look for a challenge here- if you dislike abstract content/art, this is not for youI do however recommend buying it if:- you wanna experience the horror women go through in a story that treats the subject respectfully (though it's Really being hammered home that women get abused and harassed all the time in one occasion, which annoyed me and I'm afab/fem presenting)- you don't mind slow paced pixel game horror stuff- you wanna enjoy a story centered more on true/human horrors than fictional/supernatural ones- you like atmospheric psychological horror- don't mind a badly timed rhythm game or two lolI cannot support others saying the runtime is very short. It took me 7 hours after all, that's very decent for the price.Overall had a horrible time with this game mentally and I'll be gnawing at this very real scenario/horror situation for a while but I think that's what the devs intended. _childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that I'd expect to see covered by all mainstream horror content creators, its subject matter is beautifully handled, even when it delves into very hard topics that are often mishandled by horror media, like sexual abuse, objectification of women, generational trauma, etc.I'm a big horror fan and I enjoy all its branches, but I specifically like it when artists are able to both spook and hook the audience through a mix of ambiance and story telling, and this game has both in spades. The soundtrack from different artists, one of which is Akira Yamaoka of Silent Hill fame, set up the atmosphere amazingly, as well as its expressive pixel art. You can feel its roots in games like Yume Nikki and Silent Hill of course, but also from David Lynch, Argento and a bunch of others.The story of Gloria is one that grasped me from the opening minutes and I can't stop thinking about it. I admittedly feel bad for buying Decarnation on a deep discount, this game deserves its retail price and more. I hope it reaches more people because we need more experiences like this in gaming.

All around I don't have any complaints about this game. I'd recommend anyone with the maturity to play it, do so.

_childDocuments_.review: is possible (one of) the heaviest game I have ever played, it is “wonderful” in the sense that I was engrossed with it from start to finish and was either uncomfortable or anxious through most of the story. Gloria is a dancer, and she is nearing thirty. As we are introduced to her, she is posing for a sculptor who remarks that it is good that he got to her before it was "too late" then he starts complaining that his first muse has become old. Later she is asked to take a step back from dancing to instead tutor her replacements, as you might expect this is not having the best year of her life.But I am sure things will only be looking up for Gloria in the future, and that nothing worse will happen to her in this psychological horror (adventure) game. starts out with a disclaimer warning its audience about its sensitive themes, I am glad it has that because this is possibly the heaviest and darkest video game I have played. It goes to terrible places and explores many parts of Gloria including things she would rather not confront or acknowledge.This game made me feel a lot of emotions especially since I grew so invested in Gloria and her struggles. I could definitely picture her and every other character as actual people which is one of the reasons it feels so heavy to play. As for gameplay, there is not a lot of it, what we have is well contextualised to Gloria and her backstory. You have a rhythm game because she is a dancer; she is an adult, so she needs to stretch and drown intrusive thoughts, in others words she is very relatable. Another thing it does well, which more unvoiced games should do, is how they play around with the text. The font changes size, the text appears at different speeds which is great at conveying tone, and emotion. Honestly this might be super common but if so, I have missed every game that has done it, either way it is great, and I love it. Most of  takes place in Gloria's dreams and nightmares as she takes what refuge she can in herself. As such there are many surreal visuals from the broken and distorted streets of Paris, manifestation of her captor, and twisted reflections of herself. I love the designs, the areas look cool, and there are some really beautiful scenes though they are rare. The animations are also well made, they seem to have been done with great care and have a nice mix of fluidity, character and emotion. This is all topped off by a killer soundtrack. You can separate it into two categories (which is what the developers have done) one is a more ambient one and is great at building tension, mounting apprehension and making me anxious. A prime example would be the very first chapter, when Gloria visits the museum to see her statue. I was unnerved, and I could tell this early that I would like the game.The second soundtrack is songs Gloria listens or dances to. This one is also very good but obviously has very different connotations, it's a bit more comforting but something comforting can also be corrupted and turned into something dark. I don't speak French and if I did, I might have been able to say something clever about the lyrics, but I got nothing.As stated, there is a rhythm game tied to the dancing and it is not too hard. I like how a lot of things goes on as you play it as it is easy to be distracted while on the stage which I assume was a conscious design choice. There are also some unexpected interruptions that do a great job at reinforcing your impression of Gloria's current state.If you like the songs and the minigame you are later allowed to play each of them uninterrupted and freer of distraction, but that's by the credits, and you will have a lot to experience before you reach that.

_childDocuments_.review: The visual presentation is sublime, and the soundtrack is both haunting and memorable. Though the game is short, it hearkens back to the traditions of classic point-and-click adventure games when a solid narrative mattered more than branching paths. Decarnation provides an experience that can only been told through an interactive medium and will stick with you for a very long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. Very uncomfortable to play through. Contrary to the title art, it's far more psychological horror of being stalked and trapped than it is body horror or grotesque, so be warned. Gameplay is primarily talking/interacting with a few puzzles and minigames thrown in, you should be able to flay through it fully in <5 hours
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Around 6 hours long. Wonderful pixel art, lots of attention to small details which I loved. Story was "OK-ish", but definitely not for everyone. Lots of walking, reading and looking around. Not much gameplay elements outside of small mini-games. One small criticism, before the end was reached, I couldn't stand the main theme song anymore as it felt overused within the course of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: a lovely experience! i've been following this game's development for a long time and im happy to say it didnt disappoint. as someone rather critical of how media decides to portray sensitive topics such as the ones featured in this game, i believe the themes and narrative were handled respectfully. i also feel like i can just feel the love and care put into this. especially when it comes to the art direction, which is just oozing with detail and intention. yes, gameplay is rather simple, but that's to be expected in a narrative-driven game such as this. i enjoyed my time with it so much, i'll probably play it again eventually! what a wonderful little gem :')
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Saw a tweet about this game around the time it came out and put it in my wishlist, and it sat there for over a year. And I've got to say, it was fantastic. I can't help but feel something poignant that I started this game in the day time and the game quickly gets dark and dreary, only for me to finish in the dark with the game being the brightest and most hopeful it could be.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Decarnation is a women's psychological horror about a dancer named Gloria and her fight for survival and control over he life and mind. Inspired by the films of David Lynch and Satoshi Kon, it also explores the way's women are exploited by the art world in pursuit of their aspirations. At times it is incredibly demoralizing and bleak but it is also genuinely moving and uplifting story of self-discovery, acceptance, and empowerment. Totally worth picking up for it's soundtrack and beautiful environmental pixel artwork alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the art, loved the story. The gameplay elements are adequate, but this isn't a game you're playing for the mechanics of it.  There is light puzzle solving but nothing brain busting and they all feel thematically appropriate instead of tacked on.Wish I had a book of just the art from the game.  Highly recommend, worth the price of entry. Enjoyed a lot and hope they make more games (maybe with more nuanced subtext).
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game is stunningly beautiful. The pixel art oozes horror and charm in equal measure, and I can only imagine how much work it took to bring this game to life. From a visual standpoint alone, this game is worth playing.The atmosphere is extremely well done, and the way the narrative weaves between reality, dreams and nightmares is handled well. There are parts where you may be unsure if what Gloria is going through is real, or if its all just a part of a horrible dream. The story, if you're rushing, is about 4-5 hours long. This game is primarily something of a "walking" simulator, where the main point is to experience a story - gameplay involves a bit of exploration and some light puzzle solving with some admittedly janky minigames peppered throughout. Its nothing to write home about, but it serves as a fine vehicle for the narrative, which is what it exists to do.A warning, as well - this story gets dark. While there is a content warning within, the visuals can be quite intense, and the plot takes more than a few dark turns. I was actually quite pleasantly surprised by the way the game handles the topics within - its by no means perfect, but it handles some quite frankly horrific moments in a way that makes them tolerable. Worth playing through for the art alone, in my opinion, but its a nice little thriller/horror experience as well. Feels a bit like an art house horror film, in the best way possible. I would be excited to see what the devs made next!
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: It's...interesting to say the least. It's like playing a horror/drama novel visually (First time I can say that.) It gets you drawn in to the point of interest where "graphics" (What are those to judge) I guess it can be hard to describe as it is a psychological game. It's unique and a mind fk for sure. It is short (9 hours for me without doing the mini games) It's a game worth checking out - 15 bucks I think (I typically drop 1-5 on 9hr games, but this is worth your money) just to support what was put into the story/music/graphics(imagination)
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: In my first iteration of this review, I was about midway finished. All-in-all, the main plot took me 6 hours to go through; the game's short, but absolutely worth the price! I still stand by my thoughts from my original review: the horror, art, and music are wonderful. They're unique in their own way while still somewhat reminding me of classic pixel art horror (see: RPGMaker games).I absolutely suck ass at rhythm games, which you'll be encountering fairly early and consistently though I've been enjoying them nonetheless; the same applies for the other mini-games! They break up story points, but not in a overly-intrusive way (for me, at least). The puzzles were alright and pretty fair, my favorite one being  which felt quite unique from the other puzzles throughout the game.In my first review, I found myself questioning quite a few plot points though I did have them satisfactorily answered by the end. I appreciate that the story doesn't immediately end after the final act  and continues to show a mere glimpse of what Gloria had to deal with following the events of the game. The themes of the story were handled respectfully and wasn't there just to be there. There is optimism and empowerment, in spite of what Gloria experiences, and I think more games that discuss similar themes could learn from that rather than just portraying those themes.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: as i write this, it's close to midnight. i played through all of this game in like, two sittings.the subject matter and themes can be a bit much to handle, but please. it's worth it, so long as gore an body horror aren't too much for you. this game is such an incredible journey. i promise not a single cent you pay for this will be wasted, even at full price. or you could wait for a sale, i don't care. i'm not your mom.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: A silly game about a woman who likes cake and eats too much cake and then doesn't eat cake anymore because she eats too much cake when she eats cake. Oh! There's also a very interesting psychological horror story that is basically a David Lynch movie with a ton of cool, surreal imagery and interesting characters, all wrapped up in a super nice to look at pixel art style. Rad music as well. The funny cake girl is the main focus, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I just played this game in a single sitting by accident because I got sucked into the plot so deeply. It’s beautiful, well written and has fantastic sound design. A little linear, by the looks (I see no indication that there’s more than one ending), but fans of the Silent Hill games will likely enjoy this. The OST bundle is well worth getting too!
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent, brilliant, inspired, artistically unique and with a real depth in terms of psychology and real originality in the use of horror to bring us into the main character's psyche. The gameplay is less important than the story but it very nicely creates a link with the player and puts us even deeper into the mood. A great game (not for all public though).
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning and creative pixel art for both the settings and props, perfect character dialogue. Bob is absolutely chilling and fury-inducing. I understand where the story is literally taking me, but i don't understand what the story was ultimately trying to tell me or leave me with, other than "find your voice" or "keep hope alive". I find the parallel between literal and spiritual captivity to be really exhausted, especially for a female protagonist. This is a great game, but maybe  not one that I'll be reflecting on for years. I'd love to see more from this team, especially if they're willing to hire a different lead writer, to better tell a story from a female protagonist's perspective, or tie the recurring themes together more effectively.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: LOVE THIS GAME. There are some parts that are just absolutely WILD. Obsessed with the soundtrack especially the last song in the game. If you love dark visual novels - get this! The gameplay is mostly puzzles and rhythm so it's easy to move through the story at a good pace. This was definitely a unique experience and I'm so happy I got to play this!
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I was pretty excited to dive into this game based upon a dynamite trailer. I'm a massive Satoshi Kon and Junji Ito fan which the trailer embodied. Overall, I would say that this game leans harder into Satoshi Kon territory with the Junji Ito influences mostly confined to designs. As a result, the game isn't the horror game that I expect, but I was also surprised and immersed by the product I got. The story is linger with me beyond the the game's epliogue. This is more of a piece of interactive story art as opposed to a *game*. Which is both a pro and a con for this. It is laser focused on telling a narrative so the puzzles are mostly kept local  and not brain twisters. However, some of the game elements they chose to go with are repeated and are kind of janky. Specifically for me, the rhythm sections especially in the late game never clicked quite right with needing to repeat it a few times to clear it almost by chance.Overall, I really enjoyed what I experienced. I would love to play more games like this and this is an exceptionally told narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, touching story. Mini-games are truly original and interesting, and the visual style and soundtrack are just awesome.The upsetting thing is the achievements are broken. I finished the game and only received 3 of them for completing Act IV, Act V, and completing the game. I'd like to get them all, but I can't.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever wondered what it feels like to be seen as nothing more than a 'piece of meat,' then Decarnation does a fantastic (and unsettling) job of portraying that. It'll definitely make you feel uncomfortable right from the start till the end. When it comes to the story, it's very well done. However, in terms of gameplay, there isn't much to it, unfortunately. You'll encounter some puzzles here and there, along with quick-time events (QTEs), but nothing major. Additionally, the heart rhythm game lacks clear cues for button presses, which can be frustrating. Moreover, some of the dialogues auto-advance too quickly, not allowing you enough time to read them. Despite these shortcomings, the overall experience is still worthwhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely CAPTIVATING narrative from start to finish. Really well told and you can feel the painstaking love put into the animations. Played this on the Deck via the TV and it was a treat and a half, binged it in a night. Also genuine scares at times too! For those who like a slow creeping burn and/or cosmic horror. A+ more please
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Underwhelming. Gameplay-wise it is quite bad, maybe intentionally as at times it feels they are thematising the mechanics, but surrounding that concept there's too much boredom as there's no cognitive challenge at all. Also, the dialogue and story development lack that subtlety that may have given the thematisation of the mechanics some meaning.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: A really cool and disturbing short horror game, Decarnation managed to keep me totally engaged throughout the whole playthrough simply because it's story was so interesting and it's pixelated art style was so nice looking. It made me care about the well-being and safety of the main protagonist as she struggles through a nightmare situation. Though some of the mini-games are a little annoying and strange, the game is quite forgiving with it's difficulty and everything else about the experience makes up for it in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Found this game a really gorgeous and compelling piece of work, the aesthetics, art direction and atmosphere is incredibly well done with the subtle characteristics of the environments and both inner and inter-character dialogue paints something that feels genuinely human and nuanced when it comes to a surrealist narrative about trauma, collapse, the decomposition and assimilation of the self especially in relation to artists. Alot of its story telling hits hard.The mechanics of the mini games I did find a bit rusty and fair warning I did encounter 2 crashes during my play-through but didn't diminish the integrity of what this game is. Genuinely a really great piece of art I really appreciated encountering.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I have not wrote many reviews or felt I should go out of my way too, But something in this game is truly special. Please forgive if my review is weird as like stated above I rarely write them. Decarnation has made a place in my mind and beside my heart not many games have, The story while dark is truly gripping and shows the mind of the protagonist so well. The beauty in this game is that one the surface it seems simple but has amazing art portraying some grotesque things. I loved the horror style, story and game play immensely.This game is not light on some of it's themes but if you like darker media and are on the fence about this game, I would strongly push you to go ahead and try this. Personally I didn't know if I would like the art and style of this game but it will surprise you and hook you.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: It presents a great, thought-provoking story, that constantly switches between "the real world" and the surrealistic, most-of-the-time disturbing world inside the mind / dreams of the protagonist, Gloria.She is a 30-year-old burlesque dancer living in Paris, in 1990. Dreading that her golden years as a dancer are behind her, she is simultaneously dealing with the pressure from her mother and the break-up with her recent girlfriend, Joy. She ends up in a traumatic, life-or-death situation that pushes her to the limit.One of the great aspects about this story is that is greatly open to debate and interpretation, looking for the meaning of certain symbols and situations. However, some of its plot-twists can be spotted miles away.The best of this title is, without a doubt, its music, with a bunch of melodies created by Akira Yamaoka (among other composers). These end up putting up a great atmosphere and helps us players understand Gloria's several emotions and struggles throughout the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Great psychological horror storytelling. Even when it's on the nose, the writing is sharp enough to make it all work. I was also impressed by the sprites' expressive body language; they lend a welcome theatrical quality to many of the sequences. In terms of gameplay, there could've been more puzzles in between the basic button interactions, as those on-screen prompts get very repetitive. They didn't bog down my enjoyment too much, thankfully, but they prevent the game from being a favorite on par with the likes of Detention for me. One might jump to call this derivative of Satoshi Kon's Perfect Blue, though it stands on its own well, offering different kinds of commentary. And it's truly a complete story. Any other issues are technical--some typos here and there, graphical bugs, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: 2.8 hours in; so far it's really good. I don't normally play games for their story and I don't normally play horror type games but I have been very much enjoying both of those aspects in this game. It does a great job tuning in just the right amount, and it makes it such an easy experience to continue through.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: This game has: nice visuals, cool story premise, cool music.  It also is very decently priced.The game is not perfect however, eventually the story climax falls a bit short in my opinion. During playing I also felt like some aspects of the game were really oddly placed, like the game devs wanted many things out of this project but ended up doing too many of them at once. There "horror" aspect is not really there, except for one puzzle where there was a decent jump scare.Overall I will still recommend this game to people who want a cool story.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Decarnation has cool art design, nice animations and a good (but limited) soundtrack. The story started off quite strong but then I found myself unable to relate with the character's internal conflict and thought the actual gameplay was really boring. I was expecting more actual horror elements and less existentialism, and the pacing of the game felt uneven to me.The game length is also something that bothers me. About 6 hours of active play time unless you want to repeat the same mini games over and over again. For a game that is 15€ at full price I don't think it's quite worth it - 10€ seems more reasonable.Just stumbling upon this game I wasn't entirely sure what to expect but it looked interesting enough to try it. Unfortunately it wasn't something that I personally enjoyed and I can't recommend it based on my personal opinion, but to each their own and maybe this game will grab someone else in a way it couldn't grab me.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: So I just finished the game and WOW what a ride. Some things...without spoiling anything.The story and writing is phenomenal. The setting and art design is amazing. With that being said, I'm glad this isn't so expensive because it is VERY short. From the clips and pictures posted, I expected more gameplay. I expected more silent hill-esque apsects. I expected to be running around a messed up bit-sized town and it only partially delivered on that. First and foremost, if you are going to play this game, better get ready to be reading most of the time. The amount that you are actually controlling your character is minimal, and thats hard for me to get over considering I finished it in 8 hours and I'd say there was 2 hours worth of me actually in control. I wanted to explore this town this world that looks SO rich in detail and lore. I expected the tone that the game begins with to be consistent but it wasn't. The first half of the game very much leans into the eldritch horror. Then part way through thats basically dropped for a thriller genre.It would go from depressing to scary to happy to straight up concerning. All while you really aren't actually doing much at all. You usually just get stuck doing a rhythm game, which some of those were not fun. The heart at the end was so nit picky that even 10th of a second off I'd have to restart.Guess what I was saying was that I expected more HORROR and less psychological thriller. And i definitely didn't expect a poorly executed rhytmh game.With that being said, the story being told is really well written. The characters DO feel like full characters. The art design is really impressive. It was really compelling to play. Maybe because the story is so chaotic at times that you feel you just NEED to know what happens.At the end of the day, I DO recommend you play this game. It really explores some hard to discuss topics. It DOES have some scary moments. But if you are looking for a bit-sized silent hill horror adventure, look elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so happy I went with my gut and jumped on this game! Ended up doing a whole play-through stream of it on YouTube (Sadtiric) if you're curious to check it out! I recommend this to anyone into horror and pixel art. It was beautifully made! I wish I could play it for the first time all over again. The whole story took roughly 6 hours for me, but I also did take my time and look around and interact with everything I could.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: i’m loving it so far! the story is well written, interesting and original, the animations are stunning, the music is so good, i just love everything about this game so far. i would say that it is worth the price and if you like horror, you should definitely give this game a go! i will update my review once i finish the game 👍
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Here is a possible way to format your review for Steam:You play as Gloria, a cabaret dancer who is offered a chance to escape her miserable life, but at what cost? Navigating through puzzles, facing nightmarish creatures within Gloria’s nightmarish reality and trying to keep sane, this game will keep you on your toes with an uneasy overtone.Highly recommended, but not for those who are faint of heart or easily offended as ***Trigger Warning***  It is a game that will shock and disturb you. 9/10 [Decarnation]
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: On one side I would actually rather give a "sideway" thumb than a thumbs up, because though the story is good (good, not great) a lot of what might want to be called puzzles is either bad or annoying or just plain boring. Some of what I say is of course personal taste. I detest rythm puzzles, quick-time-events deserve to be a thing of the past and those stupid jump scenes were just unnecessary.Fortunately those things were mostly few (except the rythm games...those were WAY to often and just the easiest at the end was skippable *facepalm*) so it wasn't bad enough that I would want to give the game a thumbs down.But actually, I would rather have played a visual novel with a great story and without the poorly executed puzzles, than a mix of both were the story got a little bit too little time.But for the pros and the reasons I'm giving it a thumbs up: The pixelart is beautiful, the story is deeper beneath the surface if you care to think about symbolics and context and the music and general soundtrack is great. (even coming from someone who is not to much into french music and language.)In short, it is a nice and beautiful visual novel, that has everything about it's art right but can still learn a bit more about gameplay and puzzles, or maybe rather even concentrate more on story than trying to build tension with the wrong elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game was close to being great, but ended up dropping the ball in way too many places. I love the art style and character design, and the music is nice in places. It definitely has a good hook, with small mysteries put into place, wonder surrealism and great horror. Many parts are very tense and exciting with fun visuals. However, it very quickly comes to a halt. You spend most of the game in one bland area, with most of the rest exploring even more bland areas. Everything is grey and the horror aspect completely disappears. There's no real threat, no chases, hardly any body horror, no time limit or anything to put you at unease. It very quickly goes from a horror game to. well. not a horror game. The story becomes very predictable far too early on. Despite the game being focused on our protagonist, it feels like we learn so little about her. The pacing is painfully sluggish; despite taking five hours to finish it, it felt much longer than that. At some points it's really just a walking simulator with uninteresting dialogue and uninteresting settings. I really really wish I could like this game because it set up a great premise and had a lot of potential, but it just fell far too flat in far too many aspects. I don't hate it, but I don't particularly like it, either.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I bought this game and did beat it in one sitting. None of the riddles are overly difficult. They are easy to solve by pretty much braindead trial and error. The narration part doesn't improve the general cooking in my taste at all. I feel no particular symphathy for the main character despite her troubles. I did beat it in one sitting right after buying it. If you expect exploration content you may end up disapointed, a huge part of it, without spoiling much is happening in one area with some varations over time and progression. I am quite perplexed about where this game wants to go except to just rub up the right way certain kinds of modern society standards that I personnally do not approve. A renowned video game music composer included in the project ? It does not feel different from having to earn your bucks and do whatever comes to get those in my eyes, or ears. I could not say that it was a pain to play this game entirely, but it was by no way a mesmerizing experience either. I like the main artwork, I could have perfectly lived the rest of my life without the experience of this game. I guess it will find its enjoyers. To my concern, I'm neutral about it and think it's an unecessary purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Rating this game is a though choice but at the end I'm gonna recommend it because there is clearly some love and effort put in this game. The main issue here is that the creators seems more artists than game developpers and so Decarnation has the typical issues of this kind of product. The main one is that the scenes repeat themselves a bit too much to lengthen the experience more than it is required. Plus the gameplay is very basic and sometimes somewhat bad (I appreciate yet the effort to vary it and to represent something).Despite this initial limitation, I never really felt annoyed by the game (at least not to the point of leaving it) and the overall psychological themes are subtly and elegantly depicted and/or tackled with. The overall story was a bit predictable but the main character inner journey is as (if not more) important than the story itself so that was not a huge problem. FInally, yes the game do have some "woke" inclination but that's not really pushed and the themes are pretty universal and as I said subtly depicted so that is not a big issue (many times "woke" art is a bit empty like commercial spots but that is not the case here).Overall this was a catching adventure with a real soul, and that alone makes me recommend it provided that you understand that it is not an horror game and that gameplay is very limited.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: All in all a pretty big disappointment if i'm honest. While it has horror themes I really wouldn't call it scary. The story is interesting but very slow with poor pacing. Each of the game's six acts are roughly an hour and that even includes the epilogue which really could have been shortened into a 15 minute wrap up.Pros:Interesting storyExcellent artworkGreat SoundtrackConsPoor pacingExtremely weak gameplay (often you're wandering around a room tapping x to make the story move forward)Not scary or overly memorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Very disappointed with this one. References alot of material I enjoy. Junji Ito, Silent Hill, Mullholland drive, bit of silence of the lambs, Old Boy. All of it fell completely flat, thought it was really pretentious and I play alot of artsy ♥♥♥♥. It was meandering as all hell and the pacing and writing were really awful. The art is fantastic and the ost is alot of fun but the game itself is nowhere to be found. This is a visual novel with some 'gameplay' tacked on, none of it feels correct at all. The rhythm music sections feel bad to play and the whole thing was absurdly long for its story and just didn't land at all. I would argue that chilla brothers do more to coney the themes of the male gaze and stalking in one short hour game than this fails to do in 6 whole hours. People will complain about games and say things like, this is too short, not worth the money. I am a firm believer that things are exactly the length they should be and if it works, I'm happy to have signed on for it. In this case they dragged this things ass to the 6 hours mark and it pained me
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely a heartbreaking, but empowering experience.  Smart writing, and while it tells a horror movie plot that's been over done this exploration of the themes is unique enough an experience it's worth going through.  The graphics and art direction is strong and the music ties it all together.  Definitely a possibility of being a hidden gem and I hope more people find it.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Decarnation is a fantastic narrative indie gem. I'm a sucker for visual novels but this one of WAY OFF the beaten paths. Gloria's story is original and well executed. Pacing and atmosphere are great, inspired by directors such as David Lynch & Satoshi Kon, a feat that is extremely difficult to pull off in the game media. Pixel art is stunning and a visual treat from start to finish, managing to oscillate gracefully between Gloria's daily life and the dark side of her psyche. The depiction of a twisted Paris is wild and intriguing, and overall art direction is top notch. Soundtrack is absolutely delightful too, with a mix of "typically french" electronic music, the legendary composer from Silent Hill and a great voiced title by Fleur & Bleue. ...solid & memorable stories, quality over quantity...games such as Friends of Ringo Ishikawa or Lisa...beautiful and lovingly crafted pixel arts...great soundtracks....horror movies & unusual, weird, and occasionally disturbing themes...moody & slow-paced mysteries...QTE, games with women or games where you don't spend your time shooting people in the face
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Decarnation claims to be a Survival-Horror or Adventure-Horror game, or at least claims to be inspired by those. It is not.I "played" for almost 4 hours and encountered one puzzle and a handful of (silly) Quick Time Events, other then that - nothing.There is nothing to explore, no items to collect and basically no enemies to fight.Decarnation is a visual novel (!) with almost no gameplay, no decisions to be made and barely any tension.Yes, the art style and soundtrack are good, the story seems to be interesting (at least in the first hour), but thats not enough to sell it as a "game", especially not as a Survival-Horror or Adventure-Horror game.If you want to press A about a million times to continue dialogues which mostly seem repetitive and get increasingly annoying while doing a stretching or dance mini game every 30 minutes - this is your game.Ultimately I was too bored to continue and uninstalled Decarnation.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Game is absolutely gorgeous to look at, with very creative visuals, but that's pretty much the only thing I really liked. The rhythm minigame works terribly, the puzzles are simplistic and the dialogues drag.As for the story, I don't like how it seems to portray male sexuality as being instrinsically perverted. Some people may say it criticizes the male gaze. I just find it misandric. Perhaps I'm reading too much into it, but it's what I perceived to be part of the massage of the game, especially considering how unsympathetic and/or abusive the male characters are.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand the great hype behind that game. Yeah the 1st act is good. But after that the game becomes so booring and annoying with it's minigames. I just played the last chapter for the story and I just wanted it to be done. And  that's never a good sign. And the "big" soundtrack everyone talk's about? Yeah when you like frensh pop you may like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Act I, and I have to say I am truly impressed. The attention to detail is insane. Whoever did the pixel art in the gallery of real world art needs a raise for sure.Visually stunning for a pixel game, simple enough, but also thorough enough to keep my attention the entire time. I think I've really found a gem here, and I can't wait to experience the rest of the game.Also, played on Steam Deck, no problems whatsoever with performance and controls. Works flawlessly despite being unverified currently.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Hey guys welcome to a Furby Review ™ today I'm going to be reviewing Decarnation (wow!!)Graphics: easy 10/10 because of the pixel realism. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it was phenomenal. A lot of the areas looked like Blasphemous in the sense of having big nonsense buildings that just felt right. Easily my aesthetic through and through.Story: The story felt a little bit farfetched, I thought it was going to be a lot more fantasy than reality and dealing with your situation but overall it was good for what it was. The whole game kept me thinking about if I was doing the right thing or not and a lot of it would go in directions I wasn't expecting at all. Lots of times where it would build up to something really messed up and just be something completely normal.  9/10Music: Easy 10/10 in most areas, Akira Yamaoka did some of the soundtrack and it was fun to guess which ones he did. Some of the other songs I didn't like so much but I can see how they're catchy, overall 8/10Gameplay: Super simple, just walking and interacting with things. It had a rhythm game section but it was so off tempo that it was almost impossible to play properly unfortunately, I think it was just because of how it was made since they were all like that. Nothing special to write home about, 6/10All in all I feel like this game was pretty good.The only complaint I have is that it feels as though a few of the achievements are currently bugged and impossible to get, shown by the achievement for act 4 having one of the lowest completion rates and yet the achievement for completing the game was fine, same with the hide and seek and rhythm games in the night club.Final score: 0/10 it's FrenchJust kidding, easily an 8/10 for me. I look forward to seeing more from this team in the future!!

_childDocuments_.review: The ultimate bluepill experience. The heroine is unlikable and judgmental of all men, but then again, maybe I can’t blame her when the dev made every male character a vile monster. The narrative laid it on so thick that I can’t imagine there being any sort of revelation at the end, like a “maybe I’m the baddie” type shocker. The men are evil to a comical degree, like, imagine going to a museum and some Average Joe is groping a statue of a nude woman. Or imagine posing for an artist, and instead of your average progressive hipster artist, our heroine just happened to find the only artist on planet earth who will outright tell a woman about the horrors of aging. And our poor heroine has to take this abuse in stride… Pokemon is more believable than this!As soon as I saw the game open with an interracial lesbian kiss, I knew I was going to get tackled by The Message. Whether you’re playing a triple A title made by an international megacorp, or an “indie” (allegedly indie) project, it seems you can’t get away from The Message. You’ve accepted The Message, haven’t you? Don’t you know that being a victim is the ultimate superpower? Don’t you know that man is bad, and woman is good? Don’t you know that straight is bad, and gay is good? Don’t you know that failing to accept The Message can cost you your job? I hope you accept the message, dear gamer… or else!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Beautiful game and story. Highly recommend for a one shot game. When I bought this game, I didn't think much outside of the art looking cool af. _childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: What I was originally expecting to be something akin to David Lynch's Blue Velvet ended up being something so much more visceral than I had ever imagined. This game tells a very haunting psychological horror story that I don't even want to bother explaining for the sake of spoiling it for someone who wishes to play it: needless to say, Decarnation definitely delivered on a cerebral experience that reached right into my chest cavity and tore my heart out, threw it on the ground a few times, picked it up, dusted it off, and then attempted to put it back in its place. Mechanically it dragged in a few places, and sometimes the grueling nature of the story itself made me question how much further I could go, but ultimately I needed to see this journey out to its end, and I'm so glad I did. One of the better pixel adventures I've played in recent past.

_childDocuments_.review: What a short and simple psychological horror game that uses aging for its body horror. Case in point, the first scene of the game starts with the exploitation of the protagonist's body dealing a blow to their well-being. Surprisingly, the narrative holds well given its twist and I do appreciate a sincere ending for this genre. I do disagree with the epilogue though.As for its mechanics and gameplay, it is quite lacking in both puzzles and horror. The puzzles can be unclear in their intent as well as monotonous to some degree where a sprint option would have helped to reduce this friction although I would have this over the monster rooms. Horror is subjective but I did find it weak in terms of its impact but not visuals. Perhaps I needed more scenes of body horror and maybe impact the protagonist during the fantasy sequences like flesh falling off and turning into enemies. For a positive point, I do like seeing more rhythm mini-games and the hide-and-seek mini-game is surprisingly fun. Overall though, this is the only reason why I think the game is brought down despite its small scale.Still, its creativity and effort makes this an short indie gem worthy of attention.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting story. Like most rpgmakers you settle in for a semi-long tale full of emotion, heartbreak, twists and healing. Decarnation has a fun soundtrack, unique visuals and a decent story. It's strengths are in its music, it's lead character, Gloria, and the overall story direction with an uplifting message (once you struggle past the unfortunate scenario). There are no faults other than to say that there are no real standout moments. Its a familiar experience but by the time you wrap credits I think the upbeat outro and positive tones will have you smiling, if not a little confused on what's real and what is not, for the time invested. Would recommend for those looking for a decent story that be as deep as the effort you put in deciphering the underlining journey. _childDocuments_.review: Decarnation is a charming piece of multimedia art unfortunately mired by most of its gameplay elements. Clunky, awkward minigames and a laundry list of bugs shackle a superb OST, lovely spritework, and gripping story from achieving the greatness they aspire to.The Good: As an art piece, Decarnation is a stunningly good first effort by Atelier QDB. This is a game that looks great, sounds great, and is lifted high by a grim horror story that packs the same stomach-churning kinetic energy as a real pageturner thriller novel. The sound design is really excellent and the often upbeat synth-pop tracks scattered about create a sort of dissonance that works wonders to lower the guard of the player for an effective scare or to build an uneasy tension.The art is fantastic, plenty of eye-catching screens throughout. Stylish character designs and fluid little bits of animation feel properly emotive, expressive, and at times even relatable. The plot is mostly well-executed and handles some very sensitive topics with enough grace that I wouldn't be too inclined to recommend most people away from playing it for content reasons, but exceptions should still be made for those with extreme sensitivities. The Bad:Unfortunately as seems to be the case, Decarnation feels like a real first-effort in the gameplay dept. for this studio. I experienced a staggeringly high amount of bugs and glitches in my playthrough, chief among them was a dev option I presumably enabled on accident that permanently watermarked the corners of the screen with the build version and current level screen name, a real bummer as this text was not only distracting but often spoiled the narrative metaphor or upcoming twist of the gameplay and I had to force myself to ignore it.The mini-games were sadly pretty mediocre:- The dancemania rhythm game was horribly off-beat and was a tad overused, I also found that with both a keyboard and controller connected it was impossible to hit clusters of notes, attempts counting as automatic misses.- The 'purple creature' puzzles were so often unengaging and tiresome, either posing no challenge whatsoever or relying entirely on sheer patience. At times the pacing drags and at other times it shifts into overdrive creating a sort of tonal whiplash, the freakiness starts up in what feels like an instant, the player is given little time to step into the shoes of the protagonist before things start going south. The game wraps up similarly quickly and the final few minutes feel unfortunately pretty weak in terms of closure. Overall, Decarnation is a fairly solid entrance for a new indie studio. I'd say it's more of an art experience than a full-blown game and therefore not for everyone, but it's priced where it belongs and a steal if on sale, I'll be looking forward to what comes next from this studio.7/10

Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful game!!! The twists it delivers with Gloria being a (generally) unreliable narrator are outstanding-- you get enough hints for everything make sense, but not enough to where I found it all predictable. The puzzles were easy but in a good way where you still feel a sense of accomplishment after finishing. A few of the jumpscares got to me as well. I found myself getting invested in Gloria (obviously) and other characters (only one of which i regret feeling pity over). The game is very story heavy and you do need to pay attention to a fair bit of the dialogue to progress effectively. I found it hard to concentrate sometimes based on how stunning the art is. The environmental work, the body horror stylization, how Gloria's psyche is shown so perfectly through these hallucinations/lucid dreams... It all had me glued for a 5 hour straight playthrough, I'll tell you that. My two complaints is that I just know I'll never 100% this game because it requires you to jump through some intense game play challenges to get there and I'm a very casual player. Secondly, it's hard to tell what direction the song arrow point to. They're just triangles really. I had to memorize their colors instead, which wasn't the worst but not fun either.Overall, a wonderfully creepy game. I'd like to do a second play through after a while so I can re-experience it through fresh eyes again. A great game for horror enthusiasts who enjoy psychological trauma reflected through body horror-- especially that of a woman lean, where the consequences f the male gaze and entertainment commodification upon the female body is made apparent.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The story of Gloria is harrowing but, in the end, very much an introspective piece.    The visuals, writing, and music all make an engrossing tale that I couldn't put down.    The mini games were very fun too for what they were, and kept me involved enough to complete the game in a single setting.  Don't look anything up and try to go in blind if possible.I definitely think its worth a buy and worth setting aside a day to step into.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. That didn't feel like 1.7 hours... is a cautious recommendation. The directing and visuals are so good that experiencing the game is like watching the start of a top-rated drama or psychological horror movie. It has some very cool hellscape puzzles and is dripping with atmosphere. The writing is very good too (particularly the puzzles and poems), especially considering it was translated into English.However, I found the pacing a little sluggish and the cutscenes--as good as they are--delaying actual gameplay for too long. The puzzles are simple. Despite a few moments of levity, the game is terribly depressing. It covers some  topics, including unrequited love, forced retirement (sort of), abduction, and existential dread. While there is a heavy theme of sexual violence, there (mercifully) isn't any of that in the game. This is all I will say about the content and pacing because critiquing the game too directly would also spoil its best moments.I wasn't in the headspace to finish the game on my own, but I made it to Act 3. I played the last couple of hours vicariously through YouTube let's plays. Other players took about 4 or-so hours to finish the game. I think we are going to see better and better games from this developer. If you're going through a hard time or the subject matter bums you out too much, skip this game. If you enjoy psychological horror games, good stories, strong pixel art, ludo-narrative synchronicity, and compelling characters, at least try the game--it's on sale! Even if you don't make it through, I don't think you'll refund it.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: this game is utterly gorgeous. the pixel art is crisp and expressive, the colors and environment pop and give me a sense of nostalgia for something i have never experienced. the story is so poignant and incredibly relatable. watching Gloria navigate through nightmare dimensions of body horror, gore, and twisted landscapes, juxtaposed with her imprisonment by a madman in reality and her both literal and figurative exploitation by the elements around her - everything is done and treated extremely masterfully. In my opinion, all of these things tie together and make this game a work of art that I can honestly play again and again just for the story.but...like a lot of people are saying, the gameplay mechanics leave much to be desired. the controls come off clunky at times. the minigames can be frustrating. while the puzzles are lovely and there's no hand-holding, they are a bit simple. in terms of the controls, the most immediate thing that comes to mind (without spoiling too much) are the rhythm-game style cutscenes encountered throughout the game while gloria is dancing. it's a little off-center and frustrating to sync up, to the point where i was muting the music entirely to avoid getting thrown off. all in all, wonderful game. incredible, surreal and vivid experience that perfectly captures what it means, sometimes, to be a woman, and it touched me deeply.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: ** no spoilers **It's refreshing having a great story in a game again - not meaning that in a pessimistic tone, but it's quite often that game stories are sticky-taped onto the game, whereas in this case, it IS the game; there are some puzzles/challenges along the way but most/all can be skipped and are there more fro the interaction and "struggle"I would actually preface this game to say that it fits less into the horror category and more into thriller, but the moments are there for its interpretive/artistic purposes - and are welcome, it makes the game look great.I don't really have any downsides to this game - the movement can be a little slow in some occasions where you just need to advance (where a temp run button may help) but that is purely nitpicking.Great Walk-em-up, brilliant story and I hope it gets the success it deserves. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: A very pretty looking and lovely sounding game.What the game really nails are breaks and slow dialogue, rather than allowing you to just fast-forward every piece of dialogue, you have to endure uncomfortable pauses and periods of silence, really setting a captivating mood and taking a bit of control away from you.The game is mostly on rails and the parts where you actually "solve puzzles" can be quite dull or annoying, but that's my only complaint in an otherwise thoroughly enjoyable experience.
