We follow Gloria through her ups and downs and how the will to survive takes the form of hope and intuition. Similar premise to Perfect Blue with some minor twists. Game play was essentially non existent except for some minor puzzles, played more like a visual novel which is fine if you're into that.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: honestly, to call this a "game" would be a bit of a lie. it's an interactive story with some small bits of gameplay. its never bad or a drag, but basically everything that ISNT the gameplay is the reason you should be here. when i read a book that evokes a world of madness, this is what i imagine, whenever you see directors or animations attempt to capture an ounce of insanity or the horror of the soul on a screen, this is the kind of stuff they're aiming for.fantastic from start to end
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really beautiful and a truly complex work in the psychological horror narrative.I'm still processing my playthrough but I enjoyed it heavily and it's something that is a lot of fun to think on and think about it over a cup of coffee.The main character is an aging dancer who might need to step out of the stoplight, a significant life event happens and much of the game is an odyseey through her regressing psyche and it is a fascinating exploration of her character and life.Additionally, the pixel art for this game is amazing. I would say it's up there with Fez and Owlboy in terms of you can kinda disappear into the canvas, but I think this does more with the visual motif than some of the other pixel art games out there. You can really get lost in some of the details and there is a lot of fun emotion they're able to convey with the characters. Finally, tertiary to the story but still important,  the soundtrack is really great. Not only is it a fuggin bop at times, but it is also very poignant to the story beats if you care to look up the lyrics. I loved this game, I'll probably revisit it in a year or so, additionally, I'll probably come through a little earlier and see if I can nab some of the achievements. The real gameplay beats are more of a mini-game compared to the visual novel story, but they are still challenging and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: This game had a really engaging and thought provoking story, and even though the actual events the main character Gloria may grapple with may not be relatable to everyone, the emotions, thoughts and personal grappling she struggles with certainly will be. The overall story is heavy but hopeful, with a lot of twists and turns that I didn't expect.The puzzle elements were mostly good, being a reasonable level of challenging, but that one intuition puzzle I still don't understand but managed to brute force it with enough trying haha. Other than that they were good.The rhythm minigames were unexpected but honestly really fun and visually pleasing. The visuals are absolutely stunning, I took a lot of pictures of the environments as they were so pretty.The music and leitmotifs were also really nice to listen to, I wish I knew more french than I do so I could understand them better but they were beautiful to listen to and complicated the emotional highs and lows of the story wonderfully. Also the credits minigame was a nice touch!Overall:Pros:- Beautiful art + visuals- Engaging, emotionally complex story- Fun minigames - Good puzzles and musicCons:- Some puzzles involve you having to traverse the same area a few times, which works thematically but some may find annoying.- The horror aspect is mostly psychologically based, so this is not a game that will actually give you scares or a thumping heart. But it will give you a grim sense of dread + grapple with helplessness.Great work, devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals and storytelling are great, but the music is the real star of the show here. Excellent title that gets marred a bit by certain minigames that fall flat. I appreciate the music/rhythm parts, especially when they pop up in the most unexpected moments. I got Perfect Blue vibes. Solid 4/5 experience overall for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I loved everything about this. ♥ With around 5 hours of gameplay, you get a beautiful and frightening story line with expressive pixels and puzzles that are more fun than challenging, along the way. Not too much horror, but it is unsettling. It definitely invoked the female rage within me, and had me crying through the end, touching a fragile part in all of us girls. heavy depression TW as the MC is seriously going through it; please play in a safe mindset. TWs hidden for minor spoilers .
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: there was a lot of love put into this game and it shows! the art is beautiful and the writing is really nice, without any stilted or awkward moments like so many other story-heavy games like this. while the themes of the story are very dark, i think the balance with gloria's growth as a character kept it from feeling like a depressing nightmare. i wish there was a little bit more horror, especially toward the end, but i think they told the story they wanted to tell and they did it very well. (also in regards to the story, it's fully linear, so no choice consequences or multiple endings if those are your thing)most of the gameplay mechanics were a lot better than most pixel horror rpgs i've played, keeping me a little more engaged after long cutscenes full of dialogue. the puzzles were not anything to write home about, but i never felt completely lost or like i was totally breezing through what should be a stressful moment. i will say though, the rhythm game was pretty janky and hard to keep up with, which was a little disappointing. but since they're not the point of the game at all, they get a pass :)it is pretty short, so get it on sale if ya can!
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game for everyone.  As other reviews have mentioned it plays more like a visual novel most of the time than a game, but here's the thing, for once in my life that didn't matter so much.  The game is dark, with equal parts gorgeous and horrendous pixel art along with a great soundtrack.  Like a lot of people have pointed out, this game isn't "scary" in the sense that it will jump out at you to scare you, no what this game does is much more insidious, along side the surreal landscape is a story far more real and possible than a lot of us would like to admit.  I play a lot of horror but never have I felt this particular brand of discomfort from a game before and I think that's where it truly shines.  It tells a story of fear, despair, hope, and anguish.   I can already tell that it will be one that won't hit me all up front but will stew in the back of my head for quite some time.  Definitely a game, in my opinion, worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: This was such an amazing experience, from emotions of fear while playing horor game to relating to mental issues of the protagonist, later on joy from it all. Reccoment id so much!! I almost never cry but somehow this made my eyes wet at the end. Might come back to take some inspiration how to be better hooman later on :)
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Such a beautiful presentation for such a somber and harrowing tale. Easy to spend minutes just wandering an area and observing the gorgeous design. More of a narrative experience that expected, but I feel that plays to the strengths of the overall story. Highly recommended if you enjoy a thoughtful and emotional game experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterpiece of storytelling and art work, ther are manny games that market them self as a adult game, but this is truly a brutal adult horror story.And even if the gameplay can be a bit left on the side as you mostly do a lot of walking and talking, it also have a lot of surprising gameplay secsons and even boss fights.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Good mature story-focused game.Art direction and design is great, biggest focal point of it imo. Story is decent as well, personally it was enjoyable because it resonated with me. Puzzles are alright. Only one I really enjoyed, but I don't mind it because it's narrative-focused. Overall it is a fun and short play through.Spoilers:The part where Gloria belittles herself for feeling harassed after the first incident because she's a cabaret dancer that shows a fair amount of skin is very realistic Not to mention her grieving over being 30, or "not being at her peak", being replaced by a younger woman-- is a common thought many women express due to beauty standards in society.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: While some of the gameplay elements are a bit rough (the DDR-esque sections are _close_ to the rhythm, but not quite on the beat), the overall story is incredible, and I found myself continuing so that I could play more and more and more. Definitely not for all people, but it hits such a strong horror chord!
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Is the gameplay bad? Yes. Am I the type of player to whom that matters a lot? No. If you're also that kind of person, and you enjoy narrative games that address disturbing but important themes, this is a must play. It immediately earned a spot in my top 5 story-focused games. When I say the gameplay is bad, what I mean specifically is that it does not feel satisfying to engage with and is sometimes outright annoying/frustrating. There was one puzzle in particular that I had to just look up the solution to because I was not going to mess with it. BUT, I am ok with dealing with things like that when a game's story and theming are so well thought out and focused.A couple particular things I want to mention: - I found this game to be very "tight." That is, it felt to me like every element of it had a purpose, whether that purpose was immediately evident or became so later with more context.- I have rarely seen a pixel art game evoke mood and specific vibes so effectively. It also renders the surreal in such an compelling way. If you liked Omori, you should play Decarnation. - This game is deeply psychological. It depicts the subconscious in the external world and also in the dream world. If you're fascinated by that kind of stuff, play this game now.If you get activated by themes such as female objectification, emotional abuse, and implicit sexual violence, this game will be very upsetting to you and you should avoid it, or else approach with extreme caution. For anyone else, though: this game was extremely emotionally impactful to me, and I could not recommend it more highly.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I absolutely loved this game!! It was the perfect blend of unsettling and introspection. It touches on many sensitive subject matters, but does so with a great deal of nuance and tact that leave the player with a perpetual sense of unease and discomfort. It's not horror in the sense of fear. It more focuses on building a psychological dread and uncertainty through it's unreliable main character and her various shifting mental states. Despite it's many macabre and dark dream sequences, it's the sequences that take place in the real game world that really hit me the hardest. There's a cruel realism to the story that hits just right.With that said, it's definitely a slow burn, and for those looking for something with deep gameplay this may not be a game for you. The gameplay is the weakest part. The minigames aren't anything special and sometime detract from the immediate experience, but they serve the game well enough. This game really is about building a mood and exploring the complex psychological state of it's protagonist. If you enjoy a really deep narrative with gorgeous imagery and a dark mood, this game delivers in spades! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent art and animation. I'm happy to find such polish and detail in a game of this type. The music is very good, too (even the songs that aren't by Akira Yamaoka). I found that the horror lost its edge somewhat as the story progressed, and I couldn't help wishing that the game had ultimately committed a little more to the surrealism. But that said, I enjoyed Decarnation for what it is. (I was hopeless at the rhythm parts, though, which fortunately don't require a good score to proceed.)
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most beautiful pixel-art horror adventures I've ever played with a fire double-soundtrack that lifts the spirit and also sends it diving to the darkest depths. These are very accurate depictions of trauma and probably not the best for the faint of heart, but I will say the resolution is absolutely satisfying.TL;DR - If you're a fan of horror games like: "The Cat Lady" and "Angels of Death" you will find this game very satisfying!I hope to play more wonderful games from this developer!
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Small and good horror / psychilogical game.pluses :- the music- some of the art- the psychological aspect- the overall settingsminuses :- Some small bugs with achievements. but overall nothing too much game breaking.- Some way too obvious plot twist- the ending ? i feel like we don't get enough closure
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a strong emotional journey, light on the gameplay, which is entirely at the service of the story and the atmosphere. The themes are hard and the distresses and joys of the character are excellently conveyed through the art and music. All with a linear hand-crafted storyline. One of my strongest narrative games experiences of recent times.Felicitations à l'équipe!
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: This was an absolutely beautiful game, It screams love from the creators at every pixel. The symbolism throughout the game took my breath away, especially as an art major. I love analyzing and taking apart symbolism or questioning the psyche behind every character. Not every game provides me that chance, but once in a blue moon, we get amazing creations like Decarnation. The art was fantastic, and don't get me started on the smooth animation. Many would brush off horror pixel games as not being scary, but I found myself tense throughout the game. The visuals always managed to surprise me when I least expected it, and the way it was animated was very creative. The variations of puzzles were also fun, refreshing, and got me thinking. The lore spread through the game never felt tiring, and I genuinely was invested in reading every single little thing. I also truly appreciated the symbolism throughout the game of the parts of ourselves and coming to terms with them. Having to fight self hatred, connecting with your inner wise woman, your inner child, facing the parts you hate about yourself and trying to love them, failing and having to get back up again. I cried honestly as I was playing because it was so raw and depicted a lot of my inner struggles as a woman, an artist, and someone struggling with years of depression.  Thank you so much everyone for making this game. It has become my favorite, and I will carry it in my thoughts for a long time. If there would ever be a physical copy, I'd buy it in a heartbeat. I look forward to seeing what you all come up with next! For those questioning if they would get the game, ABSOLUTELY DO!! I already have a copy on Steam AND on my Switch. You wont regret it! Although fair warning, there may be a lot of triggering content so approach with care :)
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: This game's storytelling is amazing! From the start, I was hooked by the writing. I love this game and can't wait to see how it ends! The mini-games make sense and have a solution that can be found with a little hunting. They're correcting the syncing issues with the rhythm game portions too, but none of those have been necessary to get to the ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good short and sweet horror game. Before buying keep in mind that the majority of the game is mostly just watching the plot unfold via cutscenes and simple interactions, with some QTEs and arcade-y segments every now and then. However, the plot is great and kept me glued to the game the whole way through. I wish there was a strong emphasis on puzzle solving, but overall I recommend if you enjoy short horror experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat this one last night. Great little game, about 5 hours (a little under for me). If you like Perfect Blue, it’s a great dive into a lot of those themes. Has some real messed up moments and unpacks a lot of dark issues, but I was pleasantly surprised at some of the resolutions you get in act 6. Gameplay is very simple: a couple Rythm mini games and puzzles and cat and mouse to keep busy between story beats. Solid game
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: The art of this game is very beautiful and it is fun to find all the small details that are included in the environments. I was especially drawn to the grotesque creatures and environments shown in the trailer as well as in the game. HOWEVER: If you want to play this game you have to be aware that it is HEAVILY story based; meaning that there is little actual game play except a few puzzles here and there (not a lot) and some QTEs. You will have to read A LOT as it is really just about the story and the inner turmoil the MC goes through. If that is something of your interest, then I can recommend this game. I personally am not too sure about the actual depth of it all, but that might be on me. If you enjoy visual novels and/or story heavy and focused games, as well as some grotesque visuals you will find a liking in this game. ALSO: the music slaps.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game with beautiful art design & music. I loved the variety of the environments and the high level of detail. It's clear the team spent a lot of time to make visuals feel "liminal" and unsettling.It's not a scary game per se, but there were some quite dark moments and general feel of despair.Story-wise I liked it, but also feel that second part was a bit uneven in terms of the mood. I think it would have benefitted from from longer dream episodes and less "wakeup" interruptions.Game being short (~7 hours) means that we get to know Gloria well but other characters remain somewhat basic.Some of the puzzles were quite annoying or unexpected (didn't know what to do at first), but after some tries I passed them.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games or movies with the themes and atmosphere of the media listed below, then this game is something for youHunting Ground/DementoClock TowerSilent hillPerfect BlueYume NikkiLisaIt is a lot more storydriven and plays more than RPG-Maker Horror game with some little gameplay sections. The artstyle is very beautiful and disturbing at the same time. Please take the warning in the beginning seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: The art of the game is gorgeous! The soundtrack amazing! I'd highly recommend this game if you like a good story.However, I think labeling as a horror game might hurt it. It's not a horror game, it's a walking simulator with some simple minigames and dark visuals. If you're expecting a horror game you're going to be disappointed.It's a extremely focused story game with amazing art. If you're ok with games with barely gameplay (that's fine) and want to enjoy a nice story with great visuals and music, this is your game. If you want a scary game or you don't like walking simulators, maybe you won't be too happy with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game! I was able to finish it in a few hours (it doesn't take 13 hours to beat I just left it on while I went out for 10) But overall it's stunning! I really enjoyed the art style seen throughout, and also the mini games weren't excruciatingly boring and are mostly strategy/puzzle based. The magician sucks though.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so I'm gunna give an honest review because I believe this game deserves it.This game was one of the best surreal adventures I have ever played within the realm of an rpg game. The horror elements were exquisite. What I thought would be an extreme gorefest was actually tastefully done (which imo can be very difficult to do). The story is beautiful and goes through stages of emotions that kept me anxious and engaged. Gloria is a great mc and I love throughout this game how suffocating and desperate you feel.The art is stunning, the music is memorable, and the side characters are captivating. I cannot lift this game up enough and I believe everyone should experience the story for themselves. I hold a very high regard for this pixel horror rpg and I think everyone else may find a lil hidden love for it tooP.s. The magician is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cheater LMAO (someone who spent way too long playing the card game)
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review:
Paris, 1990. Gloria is at the end of her rope. A struggling cabaret dancer dealing with the fraying of her relationships, career, and self-esteem, she takes on a new artistic endeavor sponsored by a mysterious benefactor. Would the generous proposal be Gloria's lucky break, or something worse?

A survival story with layered psychological stakes, Decarnation explores the contrast between battling limitations in the physical realm, and the subconscious landscapes one can't escape.

Decarnation is an emotional, startling story-driven experience that will keep you on your toes until the very end.
_childDocuments_.name: Decarnation

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for a fun, good Gundam Game on Steam for a good long while. After Gundam Evolution shutdown and was sad, but now that Gundam Breaker 4 is out, I've been having a blast. Yes, the game has a lot of little issues here and there. The world/map textures like to render and unrender (that might just be my computer), the animations can be a little jank depending on the Mobile Suit. The character avatar's are a little plain and don't have many (if any) animation. But the number of Mobile Suits and the customizablity makes up for the little downfalls. I can finally put to form some ideas I've been sleeping on for a long time. Ideas I could not build IRL but now I can in game. Other players imaginations are outstanding and sometime scary (spend 5 minutes on the comunity hub and you'll understand). The call backs to the older Gundam Breaker games are a nice touch and make the story mode just that much better (even though its not a great story, it still gets a 7/10 form me). Over all 7.7 out of 10. A good game, with room for improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's main appeal is definitely just the customization and dioramas.The story is simple, predictable, and can give mixed feelings. Not exactly the best of story and writing.The gameplay can get repetitive and boring after a while. Very easy too no matter the difficulty. However it's simple and easy to get into so if you're a casual that plays on-and-off, you'll enjoy this game enough as a solo player. Camera and movement can feel off so it might need some tweaking to feel better.The friendly AI is glaringly stupid and the enemy AI is kind of dumb and slow too no matter the difficulty. Probably intentional that way since it is a multiplayer co-op pve game.Speaking of multiplayer, it doesn't work as well as I thought it would. There's visual desync most of the time and you can't join majority of teams in lobbies for dumb mundane reasons like being in different download regions (not sure exactly but that's what I heard.) It mostly doesn't matter anyway since it's a simple PvE game, but does interfere with the co-op experience with its problems.There's a few things I hope they'll improve on and fix-The online multiplayer side of things (desync, joining teams, finding teams via Multiplayer desk)-The ability to control the joints of the gunpla without the need of poses when creating dioramas-Add battleships to the game-Add more gunpla from the other series and shows-Buff or change how funnel attacks work-Reduce the amount of loading screens-Improve translationsAnything else they should do should be basic sense for a game.Otherwise, I don't recommend this game that much at its current price but it's still worth playing for the customising aspect alone. Wait for a discount until then before buying.This game is more for people who are knowledgeable in Gundam and to people willing to know more about Gundam. _childDocuments_.review: I really wish Steam had a "neutral" response for "Do you recommend this game?" instead of just thumbs up and thumbs down.GB4 is an extremely mid beat-em-up game with extremely detailed character customization.  You create your own custom gunpla by kitbashing together pieces from various different gunpla kits, and the game gives you an impressive degree of freedom in how different parts can come together.  All kits are based of gunpla kits that have been released IRL, and every gundam series up to and including Witch from Mercury is represented.  You can scale pieces to fit your gunpla, apply custom paint jobs, add weathering, and even mount extra "builder's parts" all over the gunpla.  Only HG and SD kits are included, although MG and PG kits show up frequently as boss fights.Actual gameplay is an extremely  grindy beat-em-up with absolutely no finesse or skill.  There are different types of weapons and they all handle differently and have different combos but it doesnt matter because all you really need to do is mash about 3 buttons randomly to faceroll through the entire game.  Arenas are small and empty; this really feels like it could have been a dreamcast game but for the large database of gunpla parts.  Actually I've played plenty of dreamcast games that have larger and more varied environments than this.As for story, it's your standard "single-player game about kids playing an MMO" affair that's been done a million times by a million different games (many of them better than this game) since .hack came out over 20 years ago.  There's nothing from the "core" gundam anime series, not even in the fictional MMO the kids are playing.  The only thing that's based off Gundam is the gunpla kits.In short, this is a game that will really only appeal to you if you're a big fan of gundam, and specifically the gunpla/build-fighters/build-divers segment of the gundam fanbase.  I'm satisified with my purchase and I will continue to play this game because I enjoy putting together gunpla kits IRL, but if I was only a fan of the gundam animes or just a gamer with little exposure to the gundam franchise I'd be bored of it within an hour.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying I have played Gundam Breaker 1,2,3 and A New Gundam Breaker.  The latter I wish I hadn't played, but I was beyond excited to obtain Gundam Breaker 4, as a long time fan of the series.  I bought the game as soon as it launched (I never pre order games since content is no longer exclusive) and jumped right in.  I blasted through the tutorial and first couple of levels with ease, some of my muscle memory from 3 had come back and I settled in for the ride.  After acquiring some parts and making my Gunpla stronger, I was excited to progress into the story.  I know the story of these games is meh at best, but it had some charm to start.  After playing for about an hour, a dread started to settle in, as the mission and gameplay loop became apparent.  Spawn in a small arena, enemies spawn, you defeat them, get teleported to another area, rinse repeat.  Oh no, this is kind of awful.  I started searching for information and asking in groups if the levels ever expanded.  I was told they did, so I got back into it hesitantly.  To my surprise, the levels never really opened up, damn.  This game is essentially Beyblades with model kits.  You have to keep your combo up by continuously attacking for bonuses, but sometimes an enemy can land on a ledge, or your abilities will just  fire off in a random direction despite being locked on and your combo will drop.  The AI is also laughably bad, sometimes you can get stun locked, but most of the time they just sit there and get juggled, while your team mates do...whatever they do in the background.  I don't think I have seen them defeat a single enemy outside of cutscenes.  They don't even make a good distraction for multiple enemy bosses.At the end of some of the missions are giant bosses, these were done well in previous titles, but I feel there was absolutely zero innovation brought in for this game.  You fight a giant version of a Gunpla in an empty arena, making me miss some of the levels from A New Gundam Breaker.  You can completely destroy certain parts of them, usually the legs first, making it so they take 0 damage unless you move up to their head level, and some of them move so much that it becomes a chore.  They do restore those parts at a certain point, gaining a shield that you have to wear  down before you can continue, which I also found to be a little obnoxious.  I learned from a video about a grappling hook, which I immediately sought after, and that can streamline combat a little bit, but it  feels like the grappling hook flips a coin on whether or not it pulls an enemy to you, you to them, or just does nothing.  I highly recommend finding a good axe as well, as it does really good BREAK damage, and makes getting an S score on BREAKS extremely easy.  Overall, my opinion on Gundam Breaker But Bey Blades is, meh.  There is an insane amount of customization, which loses a lot of it's appeal in the mediocre gameplay loop.  Gundam breaker 3 did a lot of things right, and maybe they should have stuck to that.  The missions are short and predictable, your character has almost 0 interaction with the story, funnels are basically useless, but I will probably continue playing and hope for some updates.

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5THIS is the gundam breaker that we've been waiting for since 3, not the travesty that was New Breaker.The game goes back to its roots, so returning players are gonna feel right at home. They even kept the old music from 3, which I wish they would've given a fresh new feel, but its nostalgic.New stuff: COMBO and BREAK based system. The higher your combos and the more parts you break off enemies, you get bonuses in battle like more damage and getting better drops, so maintaining them is high.New modes: Quests, basically side missions that you can do if you're stuck on trying to find a specific part or something new to help get through story. Some are defend the point from enemies, some are a boss rush of Perfect grades.Bounty Hunter lets you fight other player's builds as long as you're connected to the internet otherwise its just the builds you see in story, and -Survival. Fight and survive for as long as you can.Weapons like Epyon's or Qan[T]'s sword options can no longer be spammed and used in place of ordinary melee weapons like before, they all have a short cool down now so you only get one combo off before letting them refresh. (Back in 3, you could use them indefinitely and could make your main weapon obsolete, or have a multitude of melee options). They've also changed and switched what skills are available as EX or OP skills, and gotten rid of quite a few of the old ones like the split beams and ranged slashes, so if you're feeling extra nostalgic and want to recreate your old unit build, it won't be 100% faithful and fight the same.Mastering skills now require you to fully upgrade a part's rarity, after which the part's inherent skills ex/op can be used without it on. For those that are new, that means that if you have a backpack that has skills you really like but don't like the look, if you max its rarity, you can choose to equip its skills regardless of what part you have on.Diorama mode is fun and people have been creating crazy shots. The sky (and the diorama cost) is the limit for creativity. Photo Mode was nerfed, because you can no longer toggle special effects on like your vernier thrusters and can no longer move the back image around, it's static. Instead, that's been moved into Diorama and replaced with plastic bits that are either clear or glow so it feels more like a plastic kit. (Yes, they are two separate modes).

_childDocuments_.review: This game already have plenty of positive feedback so I am giving negative review to address several issue and my criticism with the game:1. There are several small but annoying bugs. One of them being the background music keep looping after several seconds whenever a boss appear or when using awakening ability.2. Field Area is too small. It wouldn't be a problem if we know where the boundaries are, but the invisible wall in this is well... too invisible. Usually, you would notice an invisible wall because most game would give some kind of visual cue when you are near it. But this game doesn't do that or even if it did, it isn't noticeable until you boosted yourself into the wall and found yourself stuck in a corner.3. Ranged weapon got nerfed bad. While I know that the new dual wielding mechanic is mostly focused on close range weapon, you shouldn't really need to force people to use close range weapon all the time. I know this because I also played GB3 on PS Vita and the ranged nerf really shows here. Full Open Attack in this game hits like wet paper.4. Too many parts skill but less variety. Is there really a need to split weapon skill into both left and right arm? It seems tedious and very annoying. The long skill name is already hard to read to begin with but you have to split it up to left and right arm. It makes my eyes hurt just trying to find the skill I want to synthesize into my parts. Also despite the unnecessary Right and Left parts distinction, there is lack of variety among the parts skill. Head, Legs, Chest, all have similar skill with only 1 or 2 skill exclusive to those parts. I also hate it that the only way to modify my EX and OP abilities with skill is only by using the precious weapon skill slot. I know that they are trying to implement some kind of filter function to make it easier to find skills you wanted. But they should have add it in the first place instead of the useless filter function we have right now.5. This is just personal gripe of mine and can be ignored, but in the GB3 when you use Awaken while also using Trance Skill, the BGM will switch to the corresponding BGM of the Anime series the Trance Skill belongs to. For example when using Trans-am while Awaken, the BGM will switch to Trans-am theme like in the anime. I think this is just an easter egg in GB3 but I was disappointed when this wasn't the case anymore in this game.I have other critiques, but the first 4 seems to be something that the game can fix easily in the future so I will leave it at that.Overall, game is better than New Gundam Breaker but feels inferior gameplay and storywise compared to Gundam Breaker 3. Gundam Breaker 3 Break Edition is both cheaper and better than this game, so if you have a PS4 or even PS Vita for the 3 people who still have working Vita in 2024, you would be better buying that than this. The game is not that much different aside from the addition of newer kits that was released since then and the dual wielding mechanics that isn't really ground breaking or even useful.But if you only have PC, then this is the better option compared to New Gundam Breaker.

My only GB experience before this was NGB, which was god awful, so this is completely devoid of the influence of what came before. As a Gundam fan I was really hoping for a story and music alongside some mix and matching of model kit parts. Unfortunately this game presents an extremely shallow, ...man I can't even think of what to say about this story. It's just a lot more childish and elementary school reading level than I expected. Colourful anime characters overreacting to everything, 3 minute dialogue scenes where someone jokes and the others take it seriously until the scene ends. New character introduced and they're absolutely amazing!!!!! But then they join your team and they actually just move from one enemy to another hitting them once or twice, while the enemies mostly just stand in front of you waiting to be hit. Maybe it's my fault for expecting more than that, but I had hoped it wouldn't be so similar to the Build Fighters type of content. I'm just one of those who really wanted a good Gundam game but for me, this isn't it. In conclusion I think yeah, it's a kids game, or a brain-off collection game. I'm seeing people compliment the combat, but the AI isn't even competent enough to require any amount of skill. Can't win? just swap to more powerful parts. The whole game relies on finding new, better parts. I suppose that makes sense, but again I hoped for more. At the very least I hoped by selecting Hardcore difficulty that I would be somewhat challenged, instead it's the same brain dead AI with 20x the health. So overall do I recommend it, no. _childDocuments_.review: So, I'm a pretty casual Gundam fan. I've been watching the mainline series' since I was like four, bought a few Gunpla, and have played all the Dynasty Warriors: Gundam games. I came into this game as my first experience with Breakers, and honestly, if you like building and collecting Gundam, this game is for you.HOWEVER, if you like in-depth buildcrafting and action combat, I'm unfortunately going to recommend you hard pass on this game. I can tolerate it, because for an hour or two after work this game has been great for just shutting my brain off and mashing buttons, but I do also recognize this game's VARIOUS faults when it comes to buildcrafting for combat, and combat itself.Here are just a few major problems with these systems, which I will remind make up at least 50% of the game for most potential buyers:- Substats on just about every piece of customizable gear are TERRIBLY BLOATED, but especially so for weapons. Weapons, for instance, will differentiate weapon-specific buffs (of which there is one for each weapon type) between left and right hands, AND there is a general, less powerful, substat that buffs all weapons that is ALSO differentiated between left and right hand. This is in addition to the 10 or so other unique substats you can find on weapons that buff things like special ability gauge recharges and things like that.- Substats are also TERRIBLY MISTRANSLATED. Many of them will not make sense to the layman, and much of the community surrounding the game has had to rely on one YouTuber, "TheOtherMC", spending hours figuring out exactly what each of them actually do.- If that wasn't enough, there is also a part synthesis system in the game you unlock at about Chapter 3 of the story that allows you to level up parts and rearrange their substats between ones you fuse into the part you're leveling up. HOWEVER, if you wanted to get specific substats on that part for a build you're making, you'll very likely have to sift through HUNDREDS OF PARTS to find the ones with the substats you want, because THERE IS NO OPTION TO SORT BY SUBSTAT and also you'll need dozens of parts with that same substat to level the substat up in addition to the part level...- Combat, generally speaking, is very easy in lower difficulties and really just "annoying difficult" on the highest "NewType" difficulty you unlock after beating the main story. I got roped into a NewType difficulty mission during online play about 3/4's the way through the story missions and not much was different about it other than mini-bosses would attack and guard more frequently and soaked up loads more damage. Even then, though, the mini-bosses really didn't attack much at all, because in lower difficulties they almost never attack you to begin with... Currently, 24% of players achieved all S-Rank scores on their FIRST PLAYTHROUGH OF THE STORY. For me, I literally one-shot the entire story with all S-Ranks.- Combat is also terribly unbalanced in the player's favor, due to access to certain game-breaking abilities--some of which are outright bugged and some of which appear to actually be working as intended. Cloaking abilities, for instance, completely turn off enemy aggro. What this means is that enemies, when you use the Cloaking ability, will stop attacking and literally just stand in place doing nothing for the duration. On top of that, because substat and weapon combinations were CLEARLY not tested, basically at all, you can also spam LITERAL NUKES at enemies with the right setup, which annihilate smaller enemies and basically stunlock giant bosses. Then there's also Gundam Barbatos' bugged large mace which can spam a certain heavy attack that deals well over 100k DPS, in a game where top-end melee attacks usually do about 7-10k per hit depending on what type it is.- This one is probably the most unforgivable for me, though: THE LEVEL AND MISSION DESIGNS ARE ABSOLUTE GARBAGE. Everyone was saying during the Open Network Test that missions really opened up after a certain way through the main story, but that was an outright lie. The level design of this game is a wave-based beat-em-up, where you're tossed into a relatively small arena and need to kill waves of enemies until you're eventually met with mini-bosses or a giant boss. Sometimes you'll be teleported to a different, but altogether absolutely the same, arena to fight more waves. Mission design DOES NOT WAVER from this, basically at all. In a rare few story missions you have to guard an objective while enemies attack it, ala Warframe's Defense mission mode, while in others you'll have the opposite where a Monolith will spawn and you have to defeat waves of enemies that are defending it in order to damage it and beat the mission. Other than these missions, there is a Boss Rush that just takes you through a gauntlet of giant bosses, Survival which is just the same wave-based beat-em-up missions but that goes on for 50 waves, and Bounty Hunts which pit you against other player's custom mobile suits but controlled by AI and upscaled in "difficulty" (read: they have way more HP and attack power than their parts should allow). That is all the mission "variety" this game has to offer, and it's abysmal. There are more problems with combat and buildcrafting that I could go into here, such as the Part Mastery system and how much it sucks, but honestly I feel like what I've said above is probably enough to turn most people looking for a good action combat game featuring Gundam away from this game.TL;DR: DO buy this game if you like customizing Gunpla. DO NOT buy this game if you're looking for a good Gundam action combat game.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this game if you are expecting to have a reliable Multiplayer Co-Op experience. The game's Multiplayer uses the same Networking Code from Gundam Breaker 3 which is notoriously unstable.For example, when I try to play this game with two other friends only two of us end up being able to play missions together cause the 3rd keeps getting a connection error due to the bad code. Myself and the other were able to stay together at least, partly because I'm the session host. But this is all due to the networking code being trash.Another BLATANTLY noticable example of the poor quality of the networking code is what is called Desync. When you and your friends are playing together you'll see your friends attacking seemingly nothing while an enemy that isn't even in front of them or even anywhere near them is being hit by invisible attacks when in reality your friend sees that enemy right in front of them even though to your perspective that same enemy is in front of you.So even if you manage to get into a mission with a friend or two friends, you can 100% expect things to be jank during gameplay.The only thing I can say about this game is the Solo Gameplay is at least spot on and I'll recommend the game at least for the Single Player, but not for the Multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: Conclusion;Bandai is allergic to making good decisions, and us fans flock to the games anyway because we're starved of good gundam games.Pros;-customise gunpla and watch them moveCons;-The story's target demographic seems to be 3-6 year olds. Very painful to get through.-Restricted to 8 custom parts to add on, excluding arms, body, head, legs, weapons.-No transformation support for transformable MS-Non-boss enemies and AI allies spend most of the time just staring, taking no action.-UI/UX was designed heavily for controllers, and keyboard/mouse controls suffer heavily because of it;--Even when trying to rebind keys, for OP skills for example, you are forced to using ctrl + another key to use the OP skills. There is no option to use a single key, or using another key combination. This also means most movement doesnt work while using OP skills.-Decals and most UI Icons have no labels. Want to know what an Icon means? AHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHHAHAHA-Abilities have no explanation in game. They often reference a category represented by an icon. As said above, good luck, because the icons have no labels.-inventory management is maddening; you have cannot filter for specific ability rolls, so you have to look at potentially thousands of parts individually. I have spent more time looking at my inventory trying to sort it, than I have actually using my MS, or even building my MS.--When synthesising parts (using obtained parts as material to upgrade another part), materials must have the the ability toll you want to upgrade, but no way of finding specific abilities, so the more efficient method is to just dump every part as material regardless of whether it has the roll or not. for QoL you can bulk select parts as material. HOWEVER, only materials that will not give you a warning when selecting will be affected by bulk select. ---Any part higher than 3* will give you a warning.---Any part that is composed of more than one part (e.g byarlant custom's arm includes its melee and ranged weapons) will give you a warning.---Any part that is labelled by you or is used in a blueprint will give you a warning.--At end game, most of your parts are 4* or 5*. Some have additional parts integrated. So when youre tying to mass select, you have to individually select and confirm more than half your inventory. And any warning for a part you used in another blueprint (because you have no ability to filter those out) will likely be ignored because almost EVERYTHING HAS A WARNING. There is no option to turn off any warnings.-Dual wielding weapons is always the better option.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanna hear a SECRET? (scroll to the bottom)How to play with friends:     - Own the game     - Set your download region to your mate's region (I.E you're both in 'Ohio')     - Restart Steam     - Launch the game and send friend codes via Profile Card     - Join Multiplayer lobbyRealize that the enemy do not sync up to each other so you end up playing early builds of Skyrim Together where they randomly explode due skooma cancer.For real though this game suffers from the Monster Hunter World Hand holding locking off level up until end of chapter 2, Monster Hunter Gems at chapter 6 (1 act before game's done) & shredding A LOT of small things that add up to a HUGE problem I had when it came to customs.GB3 immediately lets you make & level with your mech upon completing mission 1 it even let's you R&D hidden parts like the Super Fumina through the Powered GM if you know the combination. This game says make a abomination and take a slog through Blight Town while Silver Knights pelt you from the shore. It feels as fun as it sounds because you're doing damage but it is unsatisfying that in a game about making a MECH as the selling point you have to use this aborted fetus when you already have access to the parts you want.Gems or whatever it's called is a complete after thought all they do is increase stats or make parrying easier, yes this game has a parry system but it DOES NOT payoff for the effort. It can also do something called a "shield bash" action that gets unlocked but I have done a lot of button combinations & I did not see anything I still only block or dodge.Alright fighting has moved from set weapons such as 1 sword, 2 swords, 1 greatsword, 1 lance to. 1 weapon fighting (which is completely obsolete if you're a fan), dual wielding & greatsword BUT you can use the other weapon to do a heavy attack and launch opponents in various directions depending on the weapon you used.This means a sword does either a AOE spin or upward swing for air combos while the axe will do a focused downswing that knocks foes away in a 40ish degree arc. Greatswords remain the same using the I studied the blade mindset HOWEVER all weapons are functionally the same & have either only 1 combo move set or 1 other.Swords   - You have the SD/Saber move set which are functionally the same just SD is goofier & both are all rounders.   - Then there's the Katanas which are definitely more accessible & functional here than they were in GB3 same idea all rounded but has access to sword projectiles.   - Axes are still one target weapons & still NTR your lover harder than the Lance will.   - Lances no longer are a jump across the map & hit everyone instead it's now a stabby version of the axe but it wants to be the Twinblade at the same time.   - Twinblades (or Darth Maul) are underwhelming, the idea is you do your best Human Spinner or Human Directional impression but here you cannot do that anymore it's now the I am cavalry fear me as I need to do a few runs through you to pick you up in my twirl blade.   - Greatsword users must own a katana because they remain the same & use the default move set from GB3 unless it is the Demolition Knife which still has it's Unique move set, but it's light attack then hold or press Alt attack to execute the big hitters.   - Whips, still dommy mommy.   - Claws, Fist & Kung Fu are still amazing same idea as the Greatsword.Guns are functionally the same & despite being entry 4 (we do not talk about New) can no longer spawn with a different action/attack this means your dinky beam pistol can no longer fire a laser the size China at Japan nor will it spawn as a machine gun for it's alt action meaning it is BOTH a giant laser & a infinite ammo machine gun that does 13% damage per bullet, that is a lot when you add the extra bullets.But hey you can dual wield but it ends up being like melee you have the gun which does burst damage & the gun you like for various reasons.   - Let's be real we all used the Atomic Bazooka eventually if that is your set up.Lock-on I forgot about lock-on. It tracks enemies you wanna fight in what seems like a list, what this means is that when you enter aggro you will lock onto the enemy who encountered you 1st so say.You wanna knockout the back line there are 6 foes, 4 in front 2 in back.   - You kill the 2 in back but then because you ran past the melee guys who're not any near you nor each other so you end up having to cycle between the guy who is furthest from you & fighting an ally NPC instead of fighting the 1 guy right next to you.   - Instead of it being like GB3 which was a "who is closest to me I am using the Butchers Nails / have gone berserk bruh All vs 1, me you won't."Builder parts are just better especially how you access them but there still isn't enough variety for making other mechs like Mazinger or Combattler for example, Armored Core still does it better somehow especially for the painting, it's good but you can't make custom emblems however you can still plaster them across a big space.Mechs you have access to however is lackluster for launch but they catered to Switch as well so like a awkward family dinner we MUST have a small selection & it will include the Grimoire [Red Berret] & that's it we've seen everyone else already off the top of my head. Master Grade (MG) still does nothing from what I've seen.Storywise it feels like God Eater 2. Which you'd need to play to understand so I'll sum it up as post-apocalyptic humanity on the verge of death O.M.G but our side content is the funny.Here it's "Turn off the game & touch grass, devs will fix enventually ♥♥♥ you, did I mention we're all gamers here lol!.!!!.! >:[ - Also Ai bad."Funny part is that's actually how the campaign goes & they do try to make a stance on Ai. Blending humor into the main experience though only worked because you are diegetically playing a game if it were an Isekai (oh god no) it'd be ♥♥♥♥ & you could be making so many jokes some part of me wishes they went Isekai route but this ok.Better than New. would buy on sale. 6/9 not NICE

_childDocuments_.review: If you look at my previous Gundam game reviews on PC, you'd see I've been hard pressed, and I speak for many Gundam fans, to play a good western release on PC. That has been hard to come by. NBG was a lonely mess. We got an Overwatch clone, and an outdated online MS battler with longer qeue times than a Chick-Fil-A line on a Saturday afternoon.GB4 in short, scratches that itch really well. Doesnt matter if you're a general Gundam fan or a GB specific fan. The customization is well done, the gameplay feels fun, fast and challenging. There so many parts and gunplay (over 200) with the base game alone that you always have something to work towards. People actually inhabit online lobbies (for now, hopefully that remains the case) and the visuals are colorful and vibrant.As far as negatives my only complaint (about 20 or so hours in) is the story like most arcadey, anime themed games is generic and lackluster. The gameplay and combat, as well as the in depth gunpla customization, makes up for the skippable (thank god) cutscenes.In summary, if you're a Gundam fan, UC or AC series, doesnt matter. Buy it. You'll love it. If the price is too steep for you then follow the game, and wishlist it untill a sale. This is Steam after all, it'll be on sale soon.Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm... What to say here... I'm writing this not long after starting my second playthrough. Let me start off by saying GB4 is a good game. There are some improvements compared to 3, namely the ability to set/dual wield melee and long-range weapons in your hands (still not shields, though), much like I do when actually building Gunpla. Game's stable, and maintains the same combat style as GB3. Plus, my freakin' Leo finally released as a kit a few years back, so it's in the game. You can finally pilot SD units, if that's your thing, or even combine standard designs with SD parts for some truly, TRULY horrifying combinations. Now, compared to 3, there are some drawbacks. Gone are the days of funnel-spamming optional parts, rail guns (to an extent), and Big Zam (and equivalent) beams. All of those have moved to the EX-skill slots. Gone, for better AND worse, are the days of moving up to a MG kit. The game holds true to real-life in the fact that kits that haven't been released as Master Grades aren't available as such in game. Rather, the whole necessity surrounding MGs is nixed in favor of individual part scaling and a more traditional leveling system for the parts. As a guy that likes to unlock things, this kinda limits replayability and the necessity for Hardcore/Extreme/Newtype runs outside of just enjoying the gameplay. That said, this also means my Leo was stupid OP, and I could focus on making my best SF Type Leo (based off a kit I built back in the day) possible. The individual stats can still be tweaked with various abilities, which can be as tedious as rewarding. Biggest gripe? Level design. Unlike in 3 where you could actually move around and travel an arena, albeit in limited quantities and save for a few, the stages are literal boxes which different skins. 3's stages weren't big by any means, but you could still, and in some cases, had to, travel around killing things before being transported to the next section of the mission. In 4, when I say "literal boxes," I mean it. Frankly, for a wait of 8 years (not factoring in the other Gundam games that have released since then, nor do we talk about NGB), the level designs outside of the final mission seemed a bit lazy. Story is as campy as usual for the G-Breaker/Build Fighters/Build Divers-type area of Gundam, but hey, we're playing a game, within a game, using simulated plastic model kits. Still decent. Seemed shorter than 3 for the story missions, but 4 DOES introduce a number of side missions with the end of each act, brings back the old Bounty Hunter mode, and introduces a new Survival mode, so there's replayability there. Even if the hunt for new stuff still ends kinda quick, there are also 5 difficulty levels for both Story and Quest missions (Casual, Standard, Hardcore, Extreme, and Newtype, respectively). Doesn't seem like there are a WHOLE lotta new kits added into the game, but there's still a ton, and customization is easier than real-life, but can be as in-depth with stats and internal components as any Mechwarrior/Battletech/Armored Core game out there. As previously stated, this can be tedious, but if you enjoy that, awesome. Sometimes, I sure as hell do. Nothing like making a custom grunt unit kick the proverbial engines off actual Gundams. Literally. All in all, a solid game. There're enough improvements over GB3 to compensate for what we lost, customization is still solid for the most part (excluding the choices around EX/OP-skills), aaaaand I haven't had a SINGLE bug unlike most AAA game titles out there (EA, *cough cough*). If you're a fan of any Gundam series, anime or manga, enjoy building Gunpla, or enjoy mech games in general, I'd recommend it. Pros: -Short missions allowing drop-in for shorter sessions, but plenty of them for extended gametime-Surprisingly short file size compared to what I'm used to lately. -Combat is fluid overall-High levels of customization-References previous games (it IS a true sequel to 3), and done well-Gameplay can be as challenging as you can handle. -New and old game modes beyond the story have been added. -*Note, personal pros: My Leo made the cut, as did certain characters returning from previous iterations. Yay!-Can now link-fire or separate certain optional parts with/from each other, as long as they're the same. Cons:- Story seems a bit short for an $60-100 pricetag- Changes to the EX/OP-skill system leaving utility of certain parts (funnels, beams, etc.) lacking, which can be a detriment to the overall customization choices available. -EXTREMELY simplified (if I'm being totally honest, dumbed-down and lazy) stage designs for each missionNeutral: -Same, G-Breaker/Build Fighters/Divers-style campy story. It's written decently enough that it can be enjoyed by any age range, IF you're a fan of the Gundam in general and previous G-Breaker (numbered) iterations. -Changes to leveling system of parts and the method in which you permanently-unlock new EX/OP-skills, which makes customization simplified, BUT at the cost of rewarding replayability. -Miscellaneous adjustments to OP parts across the board that were both good and sad to see (my favorite missile part from 3 got nerfed, but they added another one that's just sooooo good). Closing comments: I can only hope we actually see some serious DLC added to this installment. GB3's DLC were great, but 4's story left me feeling like we've only scratched the surface of what GB4 can be. Literally, the end of the game even states as such, so BANDAI NAMCO, Crafts and Meister, and hell, even Sunrise (if you know, you know) have no excuse  to drop the ball with additional story content. The base story/game IS finished, unlike a lot of AAA titles (EA again, *cough cough*), but it leaves you craving more. At least, it did for me. Frankly, I'm just glad I didn't have to import a rest-of-Asia release, again. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Veteran of Gundam Breaker 2 and Gundam Breaker 3 on PlayStation.This game is far and above the best mecha game out there as far as customization of gameplay and appearance goes. For a game about 'Gundam', there is an incredible amount of flexibility in terms of part options, placement, and abilities they offer. My current arsenal includes a gundam, a fighter jet, Hatsune Miku, a Unicorn, and a flying saucer, all built with *Gundam parts*.In terms of combat, Gundam Breaker 3 had more unique weapon types and combos, but with the new addition of duel wielding, there are many new playstyles available due to being able to mix and match any 1-handed melee move sets. There is a huge variety of melee and ranged combos, as well as some support-type abilities. As far as balance goes, all playstyles seem to perform similarly with the exception of bugged weapons that do *too much* damage.As a looter shooter/beat 'em up, there is alot of RNG in this game in regards to getting certain parts to drop,  and to get the desired bonus ability stats on those parts. This is alleviated by a couple things,  namely that you can directly buy the Gundam you want from an in-game shop to get the parts,  and that you can combine parts to inherit/move/level up the randomimzed ability stats. Unfortunately, because of the RNG parts and stats, the inventory system can get very cluttered, and the someone what vague stat descriptions,  and lack of specific inventory filters can make it a slog to look for specific gear or stats.Regarding bugs,  they are definitely present, but most of the time do not pull you out of the game or cause severe issues. This game is extremely well optimized (since it has to run on a Nintendo Switch), and as a result I have never experienced lag/buffering/crashes. There are three types of bugs I've experienced: - Animation bugs (where animations from different equipped weapons/parts interact in weird ways) - Audio bugs (in particular, the music sometimes cuts out, or loops the same 5 seconds repeatedly) - Damage bugs (some weapons are extremely overtuned, doing 2-10 times more damage than expected).

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fine game, there plenty of parts to build with even if the gameplay boils down to wave battles. The fact that the netcode is nonexistent when multiplayer is advertised makes it hard to recommend the game at full price. If you've played any of the other Gundam games available on PC then you already know how Bandai is with networking issues. The game manages to desync all wave battles but keeps boss battles perfectly synced. Maybe one day a real company will be in charge of making Gundam games. Until then their multiplayer features will always be bottom tier.If Steam gave a neutral option I'd give it to this game, and I'd recommend the game on sale if you want a decent single player experience. If you're looking to play with a friend, you will be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I played GB3 about 6 years ago. and it's still one of my all time favorite games ever... but this? this shocked me with how much it felt like GB3 (story notwithstanding but I'll touch on that later.) I will be brutally honest and say that when I first heard the news I was distraught because I didn't think after the dumpster fire that was NGB that Bandai could pull off what they have here. I've been seeing alot of bad reviews and I think it all just sounds like whiny BS tbh but thats just me.I'm just glad we got another Gundam game in the west because they seem allergic to that for some reason, money talks though, and if you want more Gundam games the only way to show that is to vote with your wallet, and luckily I'd say this is worth it, it definitely helps that we don't have to import this like we had to with GB3 and G Gen Genesis too.if you want the TL:DR before I go in depth. 8/10 go buy it and have fun, just know that the story is scaled back from GB3.I'll try and make the rest of this short so I'll jump right in.Story: It's passable, the characters are fun but the real stars are the returning GB3 cast members of Misa and Nagitsuji (the name of the GB3 Protag.) and that makes sense because GB3's characters are like insanely good and just outshine the other guys. The villains motivations kinda leave a bad taste in my mouth, I can see what they wanted to do but the way he words it and with his backstory it just kinda feels in poor taste for reasons I won't spoil, luckily that only shows up in the last two missions so you can just ignore it for the most part. I just hope Misa and Nagitsuji finally get together and get married or something, I do miss Will and Dorothy but I get it's better to focus on new characters before we bring back the old homiesGameplay: It's GB3 but without the Funnel and Big Laser spam, which makes me sad because I loved watching Funnel's go out and destroy my enemies but ehh I get why they did it, after about an hour you get used to the EX part changes, The selection of suits is pretty much the same but with way more customization, this is the definitive Gunpla builder simulator in that regard.Performance: I don't feel like this will reflect for most people since I've been blessed enough to have a rig powerful enough to simulate god but the game ran perfect for me, one crash happened randomly I dont really know what caused it, i attacked a little loot gremlin guy and it crashed but other than that it was smooth sailing.Pacing: one of the very few gripes I had with GB3 was that, to me at least, it felt like some missions dragged on forever, and you were seeing the same map 7 times in a row it just got so droll especially when nothing was really happening plot wise. well GB4 handles that much better, idk if it's just cause of the shorter story run time or not having the DLC's to play off the bat like I had with GB3 but the fact they keep changing maps every wave and theres a good amount of them to go through it just felt so refreshing.One small gripe: ok so this is something that only affects me and a few others, but I use an Ultrawide monitor (yeah I'm one of those guys.) and while the game has an option for ultrawide resolutions it doesnt actually have like, IDK the right word for it, an Ultrawide FOV? the camera is way too close is what I'm saying and I just played in windowed mode in a normal resolution. Personally I wouldn't have cared if it was fullscreen "Ultrawide" where its just 1600x900 with big black rectangles on the side but ehh, would've been nice to have actual Ultrawide support. Thats it, it doesnt detract from my score but I figure someone might like to knowagain, if GB3 is a 9.5/10 for me then this is a like 8.6/10. I'll probably update this when the DLC comes out and the Misa and Nagitsuji stuff is updated and we have the "full" MS roster.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like the combat system was bought for $25 from an asset store. Every encounter feels identical. Perma-stun lock enemies proportionally to how many health bars they have. Rinse and repeat. Every now and again, you're greeted with a "boss", if you can call it that. _childDocuments_.review: 5/10 stars... It's really a game for either fans of this particular line of games or just gundam fans. I still think the controls are janky, however they are an improvement over the last game, New Gundam Breaker. To address that failure, they 'went back' to GB3. Funny how NGB seemed to have better graphics and ran better on my machine though..But let's remember that in game design, going backwards is going backwards. And even when people fondly remember the past, like how many long for the good old days of the simplistic Everquest MMO, when you do go back you are dissappointed. Many people stepped up with their own versions of that old game and it just further divided the smaller player based and reminded some why they quit. Here, we get the in story announcement about how the new in world gundam game has advanced thanks to Ai bla bla bla, and it just smacks me in the face reminding me that THIS, GB4, isnt that by a long shot. It's a return to what worked ages ago, something japanese industry seems stuck on. Stick to what's safe. In many instances compaired to runaway american corperations it's actually a good idea, yet it highlights that if you don't move forward at all or only in inches at a time when you can do more, you're failing to make the growth you should. We're all happy to get a new Gundam Breaker, but we're treated to another title with an over simplistic ZzZZzz story meant for kids, weak graphics, no open world elements, lots of grind and meh gameplay. What really sells it is the Gundam Kit Building element. You know it's what we are here for. But I myself personally could have used less of a reminder with how japanese corperations are stagnant and failing in many cases except for a few exceptions (and how Gundam fans keep getting screwed by crap game design and weird corperate choices from Bandai), and welcomed a game meant to please gundam fans and gamers alike which would have drawn new interest and fans for Gundam from other gamer bases and fandoms. It's a missed opportunity, and one that I can say isn't worth 60 bucks. Wait for it to go on sale. It's not that it's BAD, but neither is it GOOD.

_childDocuments_.review: While a little more variety with missions would have been nice, its a fun action-packed time and is enjoyable to build your gunpla.  There are an extensive amount of parts to earn and use and numerous visual customization options to adjust part position, size, color, and more.  If you are willing to spend the time and get creative, you can create designs you wouldn't expect are possible.  Beyond that the combat capabilities of your gunpla can be customized extensively as well with parts that add extra unique abilities and up to 2 ranged weapons and 2 melee weapons.Long term player progression involves grinding your builder level by completing missions which has various unlocks in addition to boosting your stat parameters by increasing part levels rarity through synthesis.  By combining several other parts into another one you can level up and transfer over affixes.  Getting your stat build just how you want it can be a bit of a grind, but may be enjoyable for those that like a grind.As mentioned the game is a bit lacking when it comes to variety, as missions will generally just involve combating a few waves of enemies and sometimes might conclude with a big boss fight.  The game is quite easy too, especially if you are using synthesis to grind your part levels and stats up to their limits.  Hopefully they add some form of content to challenge endgame players.  The in-game currency feels kind of useless as well and desperately needs some kind of sink for players to dump it in.  Lastly, some QOL stuff would be greatly appreciated, such as the ability to disable the constant rarity warnings when im using synthesis.  It's incredibly annoying when you are trying to fuse over a hundred parts into something and you have to manually select each one and answer a prompt.

_childDocuments_.review: Dreadfully basic best describes it. When I saw that the install was only 10GB, I thought "either these guys are optimization and compression geniuses, or this is going to look like a mobile game." Unfortunately, it's the latter. Even on max settings, the game looks - and plays - like a lazy port of a last-gen mobile game. Control scheme choices are weird (why is dash and jump the same key, for example?). AI, both friendly and enemy, is brain-dead. Animations are stiff and movement is jerky and spastic. Voice acting is between cringe and grating. Though, big props for not bowing to the woke PC mob and referring to the player as "he" rather than "she" or "they".Environments aren't much better, they are all tiny arenas with basic-looking scenery. For a $60 PC game, it all looks very low-budget. Come to think of it it probably would look mostly OK on a phone screen, but on a PC monitor it all appears as if it was made by an amateur having his first go at 3D design and texturing.It's probably a great way to spend some time kitbashing the models and posing them for screenshots, but I honestly didn't get that far. After experiencing what fast mecha combat can be in Armored Core 6 (at which I am, admittedly, godawful), I couldn't stand the idea of slogging through the bland combat here to unlock parts.I guess my biggest problem is the price point. $30 would have been fair (I think), and if it ever drops that low I might re-buy it. Maybe they'll patch the AI and combat in general by then. Right now, I can't see how anyone could pay $60, much less $100 for the "ultimate edition". For that money I could 1-2 actual Gunpla kits. For now, refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I will say I have only ever played Gundam Breaker 1 on the PS3 and I liked it a lot, even if I couldn't understand any of the menus or descriptions because it was in Japanese only. This review will e comparing them and not GB2 or GB3. GB4 is a lot better than GB1 in the customization, but it falls flat on level design in my opinion. In GB1 you had stages with multiple descent sized areas you would walk through and fight through and they had optional chest you could break for more parts. In GB4 (Up to chapter 4 so far at least) The stages are pretty small and enemies just spawn in waves near you and once they are all defeated you just teleport to the next area and I have yet to see any of the chest like GB1 had. There is a bounty mode where you can select three enemies frtom a list to fight, If you play online these seem to be other players builds and their parts level do get higher the larger the bounty they have. I am unsure if it is a bug or intentional but offline for me even the ones with 100,000 bounty still only had level 1 parts which lead me to being able to beat them easily and get the bounty achievements and a ton of money with no issue at all.The boss fights against the mobile armors and PG gunpla are extremely fun especially on hardcore difficulty and I think that is the best part of the combat side of the game so far
