_childDocuments_.review: Picture me, sitting around and wanting to play another game that involved mechs/mechas. I already played Armored core 6, have played a bit of Mass Builder and have tried Mechwarrior 5. I saw New Gundam Breaker and SD Gundam Alliance and figured "They look cool but the reviews say otherwise" and skipped them. Then, out of nowhere while browsing steam for a game in the mech/mecha genre, Gundam Breaker 4 pops up and it looks right up my alley so I decided to preorder. At first I thought I was gonna regret my purchase, some people where skeptical about how the game was gonna turn out since New Gundam Breaker crashed and burned pretty hard. I'm here today to say that the game is worth the purchase and here are my reasons.1. The Combat:The combat compared to most games I played in the genre is pretty fast paced. With the amount of maneuverability and weapons that have various combos and stats, the combat feels really fast and exciting. My favorite weapons to experiment with are knuckle weapons, greatswords, whips, bazookas and pistols. The game has 3 mission types: destroy all enemies, destroy priority targets and defend an objective. The game tends to repeat these missions and they may even throw mini bosses and major boss fights into the mix, so it can get a bit repetitive, similar to the previous mainline entries. But the next thing I'm gonna mention will kill the repetitive vibe.2. The story:Most mech/mecha games have a story to follow that more or less is just in the background. Sometimes the story tends to get left behind as you play due to the story not being interesting, being too basic or being straight up bad. This game's story is a bit of an exception. With the game having a fully voiced English cast and the characters being very colorful and animated gives the story more life then most games. There even is a bit of mystery in the game as you play that you and your story related clan need to solve while playing the game in its beta. For some, this story can be okay, but for others it can be a nice breath of fresh air since the previous Gundam Breaker games had still images and no animation, not to mention the voice acting only being in Japanese with English subtitles.And last but most certainly not least, The Customization:If you thought armored core and its customization was in depth, this game rivals that by a large amount. Not only can you pick from 250 real life Gunpla model kits that totals to about 2000 parts (might be more due to dlc and free content) but a majority of these parts are unique with there own Ex skills and Option skills. These parts later in the story can be upgraded, have their skills swapped and get their rarity increased through synthesis, making it so you can keep that custom look that you want for your Gunpla. Not only that, you can also resize parts to better fit your Gunpla, recolor it with presets or individual colors and test out your build to see if its viable for later missions. And lets not forget the the diorama mode. aside from placing Gunpla in scenes that you create, you can also pose them and add effects that make for awesome screenshots and shows off your custom Gunpla design compared to the previous games that didn't have a mode like this.Now I'm also going to take a stab at what people might fear when playing this game that plague other games in the genre or just games in general.Is the game too easy?Short answer: No. Long answer: The game at first is a bit easy. Chapter 1 and 2 are easy due to the game in a story sense treating you like you're still new to the game, so obviously the story starts off a bit easy. But with the added difficulty options and the fact that chapter 3 kicks the difficulty up a notch instantly destroys that easiness the game has. I've gotten my butt kicked a few times in chapter 3 and had to use a couple revives due to the enemies not only getting tougher and doing more damage, but they start becoming evasive and start using more Ex skills along with ganging up on you. Your AI partners, while good, can only do so much. So no, the game isn't too easy.Is the game online only?Short answer: No. Long answer: The game has online capabilities such as coop and bounty mode, but you can not only turn the online mode off, but you can play this game completely offline, no internet connect, no steam servers, nothing. This game has a single player and multiplayer experience that you can enjoy without issue.Does it run on steam deck fine and what about the optimization?From what I've heard, the game runs fine on steam deck and as for this pc port, It's really solid. I'm running on max settings with no lag, frame drops, stutter or graphical oddities. That and the game can be played with a controller or PC controls. The game was also meant to be played on Switch so that could also be why the game runs really well. Not to mention the game also is rather small in download size, 9 gigs for the game and 5 more for save data and dlcs. the game did just release so the game may get more events and content to slap on to the mountain of stuff you can do already.Aside from that, the only thing that is holding the game back a bit is the marketing. Bandi barley gave this game enough marketing before the release aside from a few release trailers and giving out review copies. So unless you are an avid Gundam fan, keep track of games like me via Youtube or online articles and posts or just so happen to watch Nintendo direct, you may not have known about this game. However, that fact it released on PC, PS4, PS5 and Switch opens up opportunities for the game to grow. While I personally recommend the game, It's up to YOU to decide if you want to give this game a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not played Gundam Breaker 3 so I can only compare this to New Gundam Breaker and Gundam Breaker Mobile.TLDR: it's a better action game, it's a worse kitbash preview simulator.Overall, I recommend this game as it is fun but I don't consider it to have too much replayability as the only reason I'd play it again after beating the story would be to make more kitbash previews but with only one slot to work with I'd have to start over from scratch rather than revisit a saved project that I made in advance.The combat is a lot more fun. It's very combo friendly and you can switch up how you're attacking at any given moment between the dual wielding melee and ranged options as well as the abilities. While I don't personally care for the looter stat maxing aspect of it, I'm sure some people enjoy pretending like it's Armored Core.The story is different between every breaker game so take that as you will. Though, the fake MMO plot they're going with sort of contributes to my criticisms below.My main criticisms are with the building. You can swap out all the parts you want and add some extra parts like swords and spikes and whatnot as before. The ability to dual wield individual parts is nice so you could make symmetrical or asymmetrical aesthetics as you want. HOWEVER, YOU CAN ONLY DO THIS ON ONE GUNPLA. I'm not sure how it was in GB3 but the plot being a fake MMO means the gunpla you make doubles as your "avatar" and this means there are no longer any build slots that you can use to create multiple gunpla. If you're an ordinary player that's probably fine but if you like to make multiple builds or split main/farming builds or use these breaker games as a kitbash preview simulator for the real life model projects you want to make like I do then only having one slot to work with is annoying. Additionally, the builder menu is a bit more restricted. You can't select and color/weather every part all at once anymore. This was useful for creating a "primed" gunpla base state that was a good starting point for coloring as well as fully removing or adding all weathering and making the glow effects consistent across the whole gunpla. You can at least select all the paint sections of an individual part to do this but being able to do the whole gunpla at once was better. This game has many more kits to choose from compared to NGB but you can't make use of them on one slot and given the looter aspect of the parts, you will have to manage or sell a bunch of lower rarity/level duplicates to keep it organized and with one slot you're liable to accidentally sell a part you use for your main loadout if you don't have your sorting algorithm in a certain way to make it easy to see the parts to compare. I recommend Alphabetical->Rarity->level to group all the duplicates together and see which is better.On a side note: admittedly I have not checked if there's a lock function to prevent the above problem yet. Also, I haven't played around with the number values too much yet but just going off the default color options, I don't know if this game has good options to create shiny metallic/chrome colors. I can have something sort of shiny but it looks scratched and cloudy. I will update this review after checking these things later.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a return to form for the breaker series. Also the the lock-on appears to refuse to move to another mech sometimes too? Otherwise the game is really good, dozens of ways to make your own Gundam or mecha with dozens of unlockables, with even a "bounty hunter" system, which used to be players gunpla in breaker 3, which now appears to be just randomly put together gunpla and not players own gunpla...? the player gunpla in breaker 3 made it really interesting to play, but now in 4 its just the random ones, it's not quite the same. Generally though i would highly recommend the game to anyone who's a gundam fan or even just a mecha fan. The issues i've listed are things that can be fixed through updates, so they're definitely not deal breakers. FYI i've played every minute of the gameplay for this on my steam deck, performance is perfect, battery life not so much unless you drop to low graphics... max around an hour and half on medium/high settings, on low i was getting closer to 2hrs.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you're a fan of Gundam or past Breaker games, this game is for you. Otherwise, you might struggle to like it.Intro: I've been a long time fan and player of the Breaker series. I've played Gundam Breaker 1,2,3, New, & 4. All on Playstation consoles. This is the first time I've been driven to play a Breaker game on PC. While I was playing Breaker 4 on PS5, I was encountering quite a few performance issues. For transparency, I was playing Gundam Breaker 4 using a physical copy I bought for my PS5 Slim (Disc drive model). Most of the game ran fine. However, near the end of the game the FPS was dropping down to somewhere around 15 frames per second. Yeah. On a PS5. I couldn't stand it and also couldn't justify getting the PS5 Pro at the retail price. So I bought it here on Steam.Review: Playing on PC has been a MUCH Smoother experience than on PS5. My DualSense controller is instantly recognized (via USB) and all the on screen icons show exactly as if I was playing on Playstation. Also, so far, I've ran into ZERO problems with performance (I will be listing my PC's Specs at the bottom of this review). I am deeply enjoying Gundam Breaker 4 on PC. I have only gotten through about 12 missions so far but I can tell this is the platform I will be playing this game on going forward. I already enjoyed this game on PS5, even with it's performance issues. I will warn anyone reading that this game is pretty repetitive. If you're not already a gundam fan or a fan of the previous Breaker games, I would say there is a decent chance you may struggle to enjoy this game.  Final Verdict:I give this game a 9.5/10 as a Gundam fan and as a fan of the Breaker series.However, I give this game a 5.5/10 if you're not already a fan of Gundam or the Breaker series.There isn't much here for people who aren't fans of this series or gundam in general.After you beat the game, there isn't a lot to do other than chase DPS numbers, test out new builds and creation ideas and maybe participate in a Theme'd Gunpla creation event every now and then. _childDocuments_.review: For better and worse this is a mostly upgraded version of Gundam Breaker 3.Gameplay has mostly been improved from previous entries with each mech being able to carry up to 4 weapons (two ranged, two melee), with up to 8 recharging abilities that you must wait until their recharge finishes before using again, 4 that require energy from a gauge that you fill during gameplay (damaging others, being damaged, and potentially over time) that you can fire as often as you want as long as you have the energy, and a single special attack that requires filling a second independent from the previously mentioned gauge. You gain parts that grant you these abilities by going on missions and fighting other mechs that will occasionally drop their parts for your use. For the most part there is no requirement on what you can use so nothing is stopping you from unleashing an eyesore with all the best parts. In between missions you can upgrade your mechs individual parts with straight upgrades and specific tuning.Abilities saw a massive upgrade compared to older titles even if you might find yourself favoring Macross quantities of missiles interrupted by the occasion nuke and/or funnel/drone swarm. After a part has been upgraded enough it built in abilities become available to any mech, allowing you for the most part to use any part you want with little concern of built in abilities. In addition you have 8 slots to add optional parts that might grant you access to certain abilities or just look cool. It does have some annoying visual choices on the part of the developer where if you use an ability from another part that you don't have equipped it will swap out that part temporarily with a wireframe version of the part that has the ability and all of the optional parts will return to the default mounting position when fired (meaning those 8 vulcan guns you put on your shoulders and torso will clip into each other when fired regardless of how far apart they were). It's doesn't really affect gameplay, but it annoys me.Part selection is better than previous titles (except the mobile game) with a wide variety of mechs to choose from. In addition dual wielding of any ranged weapon and most melee weapons is now available and left and right arms now can be chosen independently allowing for greater customization.The level design is a massive step down from previous entries, especially in comparison to Gundam Breaker 3 and New Gundam Breaker. The respectably sized levels have been replaced with a series of tiny themed but mostly empty arenas. Probably my biggest disappointment with the game.Bots are as dumb as they come while still being able to be considered actual bots. Enemy bots rely on being damage sponges and having high damage attacks to be any real threat and can easily be baffled by terrain (probably why level design is so simplistic compared to older titles), and friendly bots are nearly useless with their only use being reviving you if your health is depleted (if ordered to and their AI doesn't get confused/distracted).DLCs are so far, for better or for worse, completely unnecessary. Seemingly most of the mechs being variations of ones you will already have access to via the base game and no gameplay alterations that will put you at a disadvantage without.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's break this down by selling points.1. Gameplay:      The gameplay is fairly decent. As far as beat-em-ups go, it's a pretty average combo heavy system. Not totally remarkable, but far from awful. Not much more to say beyond that, since it's basically the same as any other Gundam Breaker entry. Also, expect to carry your NPC team mates, especially in higher difficulties. You might as well go solo, if you can help it.2. Story:     The story is absolute garbage. I'm sorry, it just is. Most Gundam games are expected to have a lackluster story anyway, especially the Gundam Breaker series altogether, but if you were looking for a compelling story that keeps you interested with good writing and great characters, you will not find that here. Be warned.3. Gunpla Builds:     This is the meat of the game. Having to grind for parts can be tedious, and the game is very luck-based in that regard, but it's not too difficult to find what you're looking for. Putting the pieces together, customizing them as you see fit, and painting them to perfection feels satisfying enough to go through it. The sky's the limit on your options with how many kits there are, and there's more on the way too, or at least at the time of writing this review.Overall, definitely great for a build simulator, passable for a Gundam themed beater, but I can't stress enough how that story writing is easily the worst part of the whole experience. Otherwise, pretty fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Gundam Breaker 4 is for the simple minded who don't value their time. Every Gundam fan who's been thirsting for a new game is currently blinded by their love for the franchise because they keep giving this lackluster, mass-produced product outstanding reviews...I'm here to tell you why you shouldn't listen to the placated masses.The only thing this game has going for it is the good (but not great) combat, the extensive customization and the Gundam license. However, aside from those meager selling points, this game offers nothing beyond an extremely repetitive grind in the same handful of small arenas for dozens upon dozens of hours. You could have the sickest looking Gundam with the greatest moveset around, but it means little if the game systems built around it have no intrigue or variety whatsoever.This game has the same issues as it's predecessors, having changed nothing to remedy the fundamental design flaws. To start off with, there's no mission structure beyond "kill all enemies" in virtually every single mission. Speaking of the missions, they all take place in very small arenas that are nearly all flat, featureless and boring to look at and each enemy wave has you teleport from one to another giving you no reason to explore at all. Finally, the mission will end in a boss fight that has no thoughtful design to speak of. They will simply repeat the same few canned animations over and over again without ever feeling like a real threat all while annoying, childish sound effects drone on and on. Hands down, this is the most repetitive series I have the shame of saying I've sunk many hours into in the past, and I was really hoping that GB4 would fix that. I'm being dead serious when I say it's even more repetitive than most "gotcha games" out there.An easy remedy to these issues could've been rather cheap and quick for the developers to implement, but after four sequels, they have yet to do it. First, they should have given us larger maps with some verticality (for the flying robots) and they should have scattered them with persistent enemies of both the cannon fodder and elite varieties guarding certain areas. Second, they should have added actual mission objectives, simple ones, that would have given us  a reason to traverse these maps. These objectives could have been as simple as capture the flag, king of the hill, zone defense, collectathon, minibosses, traversal challenges, hacking challenges, bomb defuse/plant, time attacks, power-ups, hidden items and many more easy to program examples. They could still have kept the small arenas and enemy spawns as part of the design in between these larger, more interesting maps, but they should've made us travel to them instead of teleport. Lastly, they should have learned a thing or two from all the wonderful examples of boss design we've seen over the years in all these souls-like games that have come out. More threatening and cinematic bosses of both giant and small varieties would've done a lot to enhance the experience with a greater challenge and fun factor while also adding some much needed visual variety to the game. These simple fixes would've made this a AAA game that even people unfamiliar with the Gundam franchise would actually want to play. It would also make the solid combat and incredible customization a lot more compelling for the fans who already love it. Unfortunately, this is not the reality, in fact, it's a major disappointment.That being said, if all you care about is a halfway decent combat system, customizing a Gunpla and posing it in a virtual diorama all while you mindlessly grind away in a soulless, repetitive slog, then by all means, buy this game. However, if you're someone that actually has good taste and you've come to expect more from your games in 2024, then please, save your money and demand we get a much better Gundam game than what's on offer here. As for me, I've played for 119 minutes and I'm requesting a refund. I'm fully aware of what's to come if I dump more of my valuable time into it and I am not for it.

Having played 3 I always wanted a better translated game and/or port and 4 delivers. Not only can you BE SD Gundams in this one, you can combine the parts with HG parts to quite the hilarious effect. You can swap between a more targeted enemy camera and player camera on the fly which helps overcome the limits of both cameras which is always my only issue with these games. It's an odd looking system but works just fine in the heat of battle. Glam is the name of the game with the interchangabilty of the parts, the paints, the poses, the backgrounds and the dioramas. You can even resize and reposition some of the parts. Its wonderful. I could spend all day making new kits and showing them off. While not a replacement for Gundam Evolution, it will scratch the itch. (I MISS YOU EVO)Highly recommend this game. Easily 10/10 as a fan of the breaker series and gundam in general.(Bonus points for it running fine on steam deck)To the reviews stating these are "ps2 graphics": 1. They are far from it, I remember that era. 2. It was made to run on the Switch so you are going to have to make some sacrifices. 3. It plays well enough in the heat of battle you're not going to notice. To the reviews stating it's a button masher:Yes, yes it is. _childDocuments_.review: This game has more potential, but squandered it due to BNE maybe.===========After playing the story, I feel like it's a lot weaker than GB3 <Spoilers GB3 has a dangerous threat that involves the world>. There is only 36 Story missions, compared to GB3 story missions. I wouldn't count the other modes as the purpose for them is to farm parts + GP. GB3 Characters makes an appearance which is fun mention, but the problem is the GB4 characters' personalities feels a bit rush and lack real character where you feel involved with them. If you don't want your AI slacking, click on Wingman's Mobile suit name AFTER you clearing a mission and bring out a mobile suit saved in your blueprints that you made <Pointless imo>! Post-Story about that, there is NONE at launch! WHEN?!DLC and only 5 story missions, what about stories with your characters you made, you can milk them more you know into at least 5 story packs with 30 missions?!========Yes, there is a lot more Gunpla than it was in GB3 launch which is positive in my book which it shows that GB4 cares mostly the customizing and game-play. However, I recommend save some parts you are using so you can evolve them to 5 GOLD Stars if it has EX/OP Abilities. They also improve systems where GB3 lacks, where now Max Rarity Rank you have that EX/OP Ability available to use at ANY Time as long you set it up. Meanwhile, abilities are stack-able when your synthesize them on to your main equips and if you want more slots you need to upgrade their rarity with Evolve items or farm a drop. Dual Weapon system, it's great addition but I feel like there's more potential with it. You can also order your AI companions to help you fight, but I wouldn't give high hopes. There is no reason to grind MG parts right after Story as there is nothing different from HG! :D =======Oh right, COOP you can play with your friends after you make a multiplayer lobby with/out a password. You can play 1:1 in story up to 3 players. You set up a room, then make a mission lobby. Your friends can join by Multiplayer Mission and join via Friends/Clans ONLY in that lobby. They must be in the multiplayer room that you make. SO, what about latency? Well you will encounter mismatch when they FIGHT only, if you see your friends shooting at nothing but the enemies dying left and right, that tells you how much latency mismatching you are getting. HOWEVER, when they don't fight but move around it's 1:1 perfect no latency. :D=======Japanese VA = great. I haven't seen any lackluster tone or dull sense of I'm here for my paycheck. I presume English story is the same. Music is great, however, I wish you can customize your own music for Awakening or more. =======Overall: I don't really recommend this at launch. IF YOU LOVE GUNPLA and try to save yourself from buying real ones, then buy this one at launch. If you are just a GB3 player, you will find some stuff lackluster and would prefer to wait until they refine the game in a year.Time: You can finish this less than 7 hours using the same parts and do it on Easy, if you don't care of making your own personalized Mobile Suit. <This is my own speculation after completing all the missions on Standard.> Score: 6/Misa

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; I'm giving this a no at the current price tag. I had fun for a while but damn was it not worth the money.I was hoping that this game was going to bring back the old feels I used to have with 'Zeonic Front' or 'Encounters in Space' - hell, even the DW Gundam games; alas, it was not to be.First up, if you're here to build custom Gunpla and play around with the diorama and photo modes, you're in for a good time. Sadly, I bought the game to smash giant robots together, have a good time doing it and maybe have a giggle at the storyline; eh, not so much. The story is absolutely banal and generic (even by Gundam standards): almost every single character arc is completed within an average of three missions, the characters are just clones of better written anime and/or Gundam characters, for some reason every interaction is done by the Gunpla - unlike the anime cutscenes with the characters of old - and the story mode took me just over seven hours to get through with it's 30 odd missions (S ranked those suckers every time).Gameplay is good at the best of times, brain numbing on average and a mess at worst. Each mission consists of three stages of three waves of enemies or, if you're unlucky, a PG boss enemy (hope you like fighting the same three Gundams or three mobile armours again and again). Prepare yourself for consistent button mashing until your special attacks open up and then you can mash them instead. The AI is practically non-existent, especially the friendly AI: you will mash buttons to do all the work while they cry and scream about "This is impossible!" or "How did I lose my parts?" ad ifinitum.The presentation is also outrageous for the price demanded: I know they're meant to be Gunpla and plastic representations of the Gundams but oh my do they look like they came from a game generation or two ago. And how come I can't just walk on the ground, instead of being forced to hover around everywhere. Everything just clips into everything consistently, so any immersion is gone almost instantly when playing with your custom MS. At least the customisation is quite cool but it would have been nice to have had some more part separation plus more options. And no, you can't just put stickers everywhere like they said in the trailer.In general, the game feels unfinished and rushed out to me personally. And for the love of whoever, don't get the special editions: you'll unlock everything that's present in the game that comes with them in a few hours of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: (Game clear review at 21.8 hours) (short version)ONLY buy this if you are a fan of previous Gundam Breaker games, or want a near infinite level of mobile suit customization across nearly every mobile suit ever designed.  IF that is why you're buying this game, for that reason and THAT REASON only this game is worth its $60 price tag.  Otherwise, even out of curiosity be ready to refund GB4 before playing 2 hours, or wait for a sale for it to be $30.  In my personal opinion there is a lot left to be desired before GB4 should have been released, and I hope Bandai continues to improve this game, as it currently stands GB4 is still in early access and lacks significant aspects of a truly complete PC game. (long version) (I'm not grammar checking it because TBH its TLDR for even me at this point :) sorry about my bad grammar)I hate myself for doing this but I am going to recommend a game that I don't actually recommend.  Only for the very specific reasons that if you like Gundam building type games that this is a very good game.  This is the first Gundam Breaker that I've played (I played new Gundam Breaker for a tiny bit and quit after the tutorial) I have to agree with every other positive review that there is an IMMENSE amount of customization, I don't think there's any other game on the planet that has this much customization.  If you're buying the game for that fact and that fact alone I fully recommend it otherwise well we'll talk about that.  Why I absolutely don't recommend this game at all for anyone else is because it misses so many marks.  Enough that I can actually prepare a list for them vs the positive reason above which honestly that's it  that's the one.  Why you should not buy this game if you're not going to only buy it for the building.#1: The price; this game is a full AAA priced game with the features of (to be honest) a mobile game. (speaking of which)#2: The game play; essentially the game play is build your mobile suit (it doesn't matter how you build it that will be mentioned later) level up your mobile suit to 5 levels below recommended level or higher, face-roll or push a button non stop, you win! TBH the most fun I had was the first 2 hours of play when I didn't realize I could level up my parts and I was fighting perfect grade suits on chapter 2 with only level 1 gear but the fights took 15-20 minutes and I was screaming inside with how effing long it took.  Then I realized I could level parts up with plastic and the game became face-roll city.#3: The plastic; do you love grinding? Then GB4 is for you! After level 30 get ready to spend hours repetitively pressing x and y to get mediocre amounts of level up materials to eye dropper level up your mobile suit, just like a mobile game! Seriously though, the best way to get plastic to level up is on survival mode, a 50 wave (x3 or 4 waves) event that is just mind numbing at best and infuriatingly dull at worst.#4: The battles; the battles on every level consist of fighting a group of suits (regardless of mission) 3 or 4 times before moving to the next wave  (wave 2) where you do that again to move on to the next wave (wave 3) then you do the same thing again (player boss battles) or fight a perfect grade kiju mobile suit (boss battle) and you clear the level.  Do this 5 or 6 times to clear a chapter.  No seriously if you're reading this that is the LITERAL game.#5: The story; choices are presented but they don't matter, so it's irritating, all I'm going to say is  #6: The jank; omg... Developers just give your team time to develop the $%#@ game, its beyond irritating that I spent $60 on a game where AI is frequently just standing around during a battle, that mouth animation dialog freezes (ESPECIALLY IN END GAME!) this is just jarring and pulls you out of the 'emotional moment' you're trying to establish.  I am a huge supporter of Bandai because they do make good games, more often then not though it seems they are taking the cheap route and just pushing garbage.  The only reason I believe that GB4 is succeeding is because they have such a loyal fan base, if they keep this kind of thing up though they're going to drink the well dry.#7: The endless amount of things that could have been implemented with just 1 more day of development.  There are incalculable amounts of options to customize your mobile suit.  When it comes to player icons it's pathedic, it's so generic and limited that it seems an after thought.  There is no online PVP? Why? I cannot think of other examples but that was one of the things that really killed me, they devoted so much to some things but others it seems that it was put in on the last day and everyone literally had to leave the building regardless of completion at 5 pm and the game was shipped.Did I have fun? Yes, for about 12 hours I honestly had a lot of fun, after that I realized that GB4 is basically a face-roll simulator with mobile game elements.  Would I refund it if I could? No, maybe they'll fix these things, I'm ever hopeful of this.  However, I do doubt it look at Gundam Operation 2 or Gundam Evolution as a reference, I will remain hopeful though.  I'm a model simulator fan, I may pick this back up one day but I don't know for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: "I came, I saw, I built... and then I built some more."Let me be honest, I went into this thinking it was just another mecha game that would bore me faster than a Zaku in quicksand. I mean, how many times can you punch and shoot robots before it gets old, right? WRONG. Oh boy, was I wrong.This game is a Gundam fan’s dream/nightmare. The customization? Endless. I’ve already spent what feels like a lifetime (okay, 2-3 hours each) crafting over 5 custom Gunplas, and I’m still not done. I’m pretty sure I’ll be trapped in the workshop forever. Send help—or just send more plastic parts!The gameplay is so fun that it almost makes me forget the story exists… almost. But yeah, the story? It’s so corny that it might as well come with a side of nachos. But hey, it’s for all ages, so we’ll let that slide. The graphics could use a little polish, but honestly, when you’re busy building the Gundam of your dreams, who cares?Bottom line: Best money I’ve spent in a while.Gameplay: 8/10Graphics: 7/10Cringe-Worthy Story: Priceless

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Most of the quality improvements you were hoping for were not added and they took several steps back in multiple areas compared to GB3. If you liked GB3 you will still probably play this. GB4 isn't horrid, but compared to GB3 as a whole, a game that is almost 10 years old, it is worse and that's why I don't think it deserves a recommendation. I think Bandai cut more than a few corners with it and I feel like you shouldn't support them for intentionally releasing an inferior product, especially with how much of a dumpster fire NGB was.Here are some of the issues or missing quality of life features with GB4, this is not all of them but these are the bigger ones off the top of my head:Most builder parts are broken, missile launchers and parts like that reset to default position and size when you use them, so they are just clipping through hard and looking very awkward, which in a game that's main mechanic is designing what you want and having it work properly, that is kind of a huge screw up. If they can patch that then great, but this never should have been an issue. There also aren't a lot more builder parts than what was in GB3, and I have unlocked everything, so again its like they didn't add much to the base game.GB3 let you master abilities and let you use them with mostly the same visual effect and it was pretty good. GB4, forces a wire mesh version of the mastered part to replace the limb of where it would go to use the effect. Again, in a game where the whole point is designing what you want and using it, this is idiotic. Also most beam weapon options for parts are now ex skills, so now you have considerably less creative options and they are less fun to use without mods because ex skills have their own resource and you go through it quickly.GB4 color palettes in general that you use for Gunpla have a noticeably less range of options, especially for parts that glow like eyes and cameras. for cameras and yes the colors look more washed out and not as bright as GB3, that made it look like how it would in the show.GB4 bullet and beam effects are over saturated while some are a weird mix of over saturated but at the same time washed out. GB3 had them pretty close to they would look like in the show while also making them sound correctly with each series the beam effect is from. GB4, either doesn't do that at all or again, has a washed out sound version of what it should be. Similar issues with overall thruster effects and things like GN particles, or particle effects in general. Again, in a game that is supposed to help you feel immersed with the Gunpla you made, this is another screw up. Also, builder parts like thrusters that would actually work in GB3 and make it seem like your unit has more thrust, do not have any kind of visual effect. They just sit on your Gunpla and do nothing. Some other quality of life things they left out that GB3 did better: Particle effects in GB3 looked correct and for things like GN drives, you were able to change the color of the particles coming out of the drive. The GN barrier had the correct color and texture while GB4 has a very generic over-saturated green barrier. The awakening mode is also this obnoxious over saturated flame effect that ruins the look of your gunpla. GB3 had a lesser color effect and  know flame effect so you could still mostly see your Gunpla for what it is. Also, in GB3 some nice little additions were for example, you were using Super Mode from Shining Gundam and activated awakening, it would turn you into hyper mode. If you were using normal trans am with the Quan T chest and then activated awakening, it would turn trans am into the green Quan-T version and you could teleport dodge around. There were multiple QOA features like that which game GB3 charm and felt like some love was put into it.You also don't actually get cutscenes in GB4 like you did in GB3. GB4 just does very lazy different camera angles and have people do the same annoying 3 or 4 emotes for any kind of expression. The amount of gunpla to build with from the start was not increased very much from GB3, so all those several dozens of units that should have been there from the start are not. Can you come up with more creative creations in GB4 and make dioramas? Yes, but when too much of the game is lacking compared to its predecessor, it doesn't compensate for that.

The only saving factor is the vast number of Gunpla kits & parts... as well as the updated and refined system for building and customizing Gunpla. While the Gunpla building and kit-bashing is fun, the core game feels like it was developed well over a decade ago. I really want to enjoy the experience but there is so much that can't be overlooked, if this game came out in the 2010's it would be an instant classic & a beloved edition to the franchise. But since we are nearly in 2025 at the time of release it is just ridiculous they are charging the insane amount they are for this very dated entry.All of this aside underneath it all is a lot of fun to be had. If you can look beyond the graphics, animation, story & menus, the game allows you a great Gunpla kit-bashing experience. I realize this game had a very small development team, and they were very likely rushed beyond belief to release the game on time, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this needed another year or two in the oven.Do I recommend this game? No, no not really. Do I think it's worth playing if you really like Gundam? Sure, it's not like we have any better options...

_childDocuments_.review: I played the every loving crap out of Gundam Breaker 3 so when I saw this I was extremely excited. My reaction to it though is very mixed. Pros: - Customization: This is easily the best thing about this game. I find it a little harder to make work than GB3 but being relatively new on this game and having not played GB3 in a hot minute, I'm gonna chalk that up to me just not knowing all my options. The amount of Gunpla parts you can use, variety of weapons, freedom to mix colors, and way you can change the textures really makes this shine. There's a goldmine here for making custom suits and with even more Gunpla/Gundams than the last game, this was worth the wait. - Diorama mode: I get this. I personally don't care too much and won't use it but if you're someone who likes to remake iconic scenes, snap pictures of new ideas of fights between gundams, or just have fun seeing all you can do with this, I can imagine this being a good time. I haven't fully explored it but it seems VERY intensive and I can tell a good chunk of work went into making this work (which is both a blessing and a curse. I'll explain the curse part in cons).- Multiplayer: By the time I got to GB3 it was well past its due date. The online community wasn't dead but I don't have any friends who are into Gundam so I never got to play multiplayer. And that's all well and good, but I've tried this and I'm having a good time with it. You can check out other peoples Gunpla they've made, fights can be interesting, and have changed a bit from the multiplayer gamplay I saw from GB3, and SO FAR I haven't encountered much toxicity. Cons:Gameplay: Compared to GB3 I'm finding this... lacking. GB3 handled multiple weapons MUCH better than I'm finding this game does. I don't really care about dual wielding so much. It pales in comparison to being able to switch between MULTIPLE weapons on the fly and use them fully instead of just pushing a button to activate them for a short time. That feature was far more fun than this and the amount of different combos you could use was insane. You could be using the GN Sword 3, switch to beams sabers, switch to your back mace, switch to GN katars, switch to the GN long and short sword, and use them as if they were your primary weapon all in one extended combo. The second I destroy a mobile suit? Use the Infinite Justice's shield to grapple somebody and attack them. It was beautiful and it flowed much better. Additionally, stages are limited to a small arena area. This quickly becomes repetitive and while it's fun now for me, I can already tell I'm not going to be enjoying this later. The small stuff: This doesn't matter as much but it makes a huge difference for me. Being able to use music from the shows associated with the gundams Awaken Abilities (For instance, Trans-Am plus Awakening would play music from Gundam 00 (yes, I'm a huge Gundam 00 fan)) was a game changer in how hyped I felt playing the game. It pulled me in, got me excited, made me feel into the game, and really was a nice touch in GB3. Now? Gone. The Eye glow sound effect for each Gundam when launching? Gone. Little landing effect when hitting the stage to make the launch feel realistic? Gone. GB3 was also more visually impressive somehow and it seemed to have more work put into the small stuff that added up to make the game more immersive. I find myself missing these things and wanting to go back to GB3 to enjoy them which is not a good look for a newer game. I also don't like the new hud. I find myself looking to the bottom left where my old health bar would be while my health bar is now in the upper right. This is something I'll have to get used to but it's still a little irksome.Overall: I do find the game to be... acceptable. New comers who like gundam will love it. Die hard fans who have played the series though will be a bit let down and it's kind of sad. A lot of work went into this game but I don't think it went into it in all the right places. Diorama mode is cool but skipping out on the gameplay stuff to focus on that really hurts. I'm hoping in the future some of this stuff gets implemented but only time will tell.

_childDocuments_.review: Fails to be a successor to Gundam Breaker 3 with:> A boring gameplay loop of the same mission structure over and over again> Heaps of equipment not worth using because they don't do enough damage or have gimmicks not worth using> Missing a lot of gear that used to be in Gundam Breaker 3, making certain suits either not as immersive or terrible to use. e.g. TR-6 Woundwort doesn't have the long-beam rifle claw that it had in previous games> Awful Fusion system. Not only is there too many skills, but several of them are Left-Arm/Right-Arm specific, bloating the drop pool and making optimisation worse. Lack of description for skills makes you wonder what they even do> Terrible enemy AI with no challenge. They either stand around and get stun-locked forever by your weapon combos or they have attacks with high enough damage to randomly oneshot you if you aren't already running +%HP modifiers> Lazily thrown together VN Cutscenes with terrible story writing. Gundam Breaker 3 had proper VN sections to keep you more immersed. Here you have characters only ever showing one at a time on the left side of the screen with the blandest dialogue you can imagine.> Environment detail is a massive downgrade from Gundam Breaker 3. Where in GB3 you could have detailed mountains and lush forests, or interesting lunar environments, in Gundam Breaker 4, all of these look like terrible basic assets plastered on the world like Gundam Battle Operation 2, but even GBO2 had more interesting environment layoutsWouldn't recommend purchasing until they improve the game

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is good. Didn't expect a 3d fighter combat system with grabs and pulls in a Gundam game. After the first couple missions, increase the difficulty and play the missions over to get some challenge, just be prepared for the boss to take a bit longer to clear. You'll unlock better posing and photo options as you level up, along with more parts in the shop. Story is nothing to write about so far, and there's an option to auto skip seen scenes in the menu.Editing this after I beat the game:It's still good, and I'd recommend it, but there could be improvements. Locking systems behind story progression is something I'm on the fence about. Part limits are too low. Playing through each story mission and side mission using the drop rate tickets put me near the limit by the end of the game. This is an issue since you unlock MG pieces after beating it, so you can't buy them all from the shop due to said part limit.  MG pieces are larger with the same textures, though, so I'm not sure why they exist here, when you can already rescale part pieces freely.  The auto targeting system against the giant units doesn't work too well for melee, until you max scale the HG pieces. Found out that it works better aiming with weapons, too. The story itself is fine. Could be better, and is fairly predictable. I am tempted to go read the EULA, since if one of the twists happened IRL, it would go against most games' terms of service.There needs to be better sorting, and selecting options for pieces when upgrading, or selling. Searching through trying to find specific pieces to upgrade or add a skill onto a part is tedious. Doubly so for the ability capsules. Stats themselves aren't also fully explained. What is an "Inherent EX" skill? Does the low health damage buff trigger at full health, if I have the "critical health" skill at 100%? Step vs dodge, and cancel mechanics aren't well explained either.

_childDocuments_.review: The ultimate in robot character creators. There are hundreds of main parts to choose from, as well as hundreds of smaller parts you can tack on. Resize, rotate, recolor, add logos. It ranges from generic protagonist suits to grunt to edgy to weirdos. You will likely find parts you like. If you really like a part, you can keep it the entire game with parts that upgrade level and rarity. Higher rarity means more room to put in substats, and trash parts can be absorbed to steal their substats. Once a part gets highest rarity, you 'master' any special abilities it might have- which lets you steal a skill from an ugly part and put it onto whatever other build you want. Once you hit chapter 5, you start having enough to just focus on aesthetics over powerful parts. Gameplay is a musou game- only 1-3 enemies on the map actually matter at a time. The rest are just filler so you can build meter and combo. There are a vast number of abilities, but sadly the controls are just loose enough that it is hard to do cool combos by stringing moves together. High difficulty modes tend to just have spongey enemies. But it is good when going through the main story on standard difficulty. The story focuses on a fictional MMO that is DEEP into the "we are serious about children's card game" anime genre. They pretend there would be a viable esports scene with sponsor drama. There is some dissonance in 'serious' moments because you are unsure if they mean people actually have physical plastic models they hand craft and put into the video game(?) and they worry about the model being damaged and needing tuning. It seems to be a hold over from older games and anime where things were done in person, before this game went the MMO route.

_childDocuments_.review: So overall I have fun with the Game but coming directly from GB3 to this, has me scratching my head at a few things that dont impact my fun with the game but just feel off. Using Builder-Parts reset their scale and positioning during use, having them suddenly pop into arkward positions and firing from wierd angles (GB3 had that issie at times as well but not with all of them), Shields retain their positioning in both slots leading to back stored shields having jank positioning during use.The addition of SD Parts is nice and well but they feel a bit off in terms of use with HG/MG Kits, but still A for Effort... the new texturing features are really cool though, personally like the addition of glowing surfaces in some of the textures you can apply.In direct comparision to GB3 the mastering of EX Skills is a bit of a downgrade, while GB3's way of having all Skills being usable without having a root for the attack (think Satelite Cannon comming from nothing) its still batter for cehision in your builds than swapping in a holografic torso of another Gunpla Kit for the duration of the EX-Skill being active... locking you out of the other skills/options you have bound to the part being replaced.Talking about Options and EX-Skills, I understand the need for balancing some of them but at times the shuffeling feels a bit random, so comparing it to GB3 once again, all Funnel/Bit type attacks I have unlocked so far are now EX-Skills while in GB3 many of those were Options, even Beam Cannon attacks such as S-Gundams Back Blasters are now EX-Skill bound.Also in terms of customisation GB3 had the ability to customise the GN Emission colour of the drives, meaning you could have a blue GN Drive with Bue Particles, here as far as I can see this is not possible.Bountyhunter is utterly wank, I mean I get wasted in a one shot by level 1 Parts with a leve 20 suit, the Wingman AI seems to be functional at best and Idiotic in the worst situations. I would never want those guys to have my back in a Gundam Story, they cant cover or revive you reliably, I somewhat step down compared to GB3, they were still idiots but at least reliable in a pinch or distraction.If it is possible for the future, I would love to have the ability to change FX-Designs, meaning coloring the Beams and Vernier flames,At times there are some intersting Camera glitches if your start a Wave 3 Boss fight while being in Awakening the camera gets stuck in position, the camera also really dosent like focusing on the Parts of the large MA and PG Bosses, during painting Backparts and Builder Parts it gets zoomed in to much when the Part is one of the large (example Strike Rouge IWSP and MG 00 Raiser with something small like Victory) also the Speech/Curse word filter is really obnoxious and locking us out of customising the Mecha Musume you lot added with the Super Fumina and Mobile Doll isnt going to earn you praise.So at the End the Game is fun, a bit of a down in some areas compared to GB3 and some steps up... while also adding some weird if baffeling decisions down the line...8/10I guessAnd a warning for the future of this, modding hopefully wont get the big corporate Ban-Hammer as for what my guess is we could se some modded in Suits or replacers, so hoping to god that they wont slam that door shut from the get go, Gundam games on PC are really rare, especially once that have the potential to get a big community and hopefully not get wasted.

_childDocuments_.review: Get it on sale. Not sure if it's worth the full $60 but I had a lot of fun. But there's something I need to say that will get lost in the pile of reviews.Many people complaining about how it's not a gritty political story like UC Series or IBO. This is Gundam  This is a whole different series meant for Gunpla fans. You're looking in the wrong place if you want a serious story. In this universe they treat Gundam fights like Beyblade and I'm here for it. The villain is a goofball and is surprisingly based being anti AI. The amount of customization can let you make anything from a beautiful custom Gunpla of your dreams, to an edgy deviantart OC variant of your favorite suit or an absolute monstrosity.Also don't listen to people saying that there aren't difficulty options. THERE IS SELECTABLE DIFFICULTY the UI is just really bad so some people never found itThere is unfortunately some of the worst desync in multiplayer that I've seen in years that makes the game a bit dry. On one person's screen they're doing a DMC style melee combo, on someone else's screen their teammate is having a schizophrenic seizure trying to hit the air. This makes the game far too easy in multiplayer as the enemy pretty much just gets stun locked by 3 people at the same time as everyone is seeing the enemy in a different place.The game often feels like a mobile game in several respects. The UI is often overly complicated, and poorly designed (you can't just click and drag a slider you have to click the slider then click it again and then drag) making navigation a chore. Multiplayer lobbies are particularly frustrating, with a convoluted process for joining friends (There's a reason you get an achievement for successfully connecting). Lastly the graphics are underwhelming for a $60 game. I'm not expecting realistic graphics but the plastic parts could at least resemble plastic more convincingly.Many series are poorly represented IMO. For example, Witch from Mercury only features two mobile suits, which clearly limited the creativity of the developers who often reuse one of these suits to fill out enemy teams. Additionally, there's a surprising absence of sets from both the Build Fighters and Breaker series though I admit I'm biased as I personally hoped for the Barbataurus to be included. Also the selection and acquisition of SD parts is disappointingly sparse, with nearly 80% locked behind a single mission near the game's midpoint, which feels overly restrictive.Ranged weapons often feel underwhelming, dealing poor damage to justify their use in most situations. Melee weapons generally prove far more effective and fun, as they maintain your combo and break meter, allowing for consistent damage. However, relying heavily on melee attacks can become tiresome over multiple missions due to the repetition of spamming attacks.I really hope they learn from this entry and update it or make the next one even better.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to the previous Gundam Breaker 3 it's a letdown and here's why:-It's not as open world when navigating to next enemy wave. I missed the times I could walk around and be free and explore as well as use terrain to my advantage in GB3 and to go to the next area you went to a gate or door and then it take you to the next area seamlessly. GB4 I feel like I'm in a circle and the abrupt teleport into next wave feels like I have no control or that I'm just grinding a tower.-The avatar you walk common area with. If you were gonna make it like Gundam Build Divers why not let us customize our avatars in that way instead of just " Oh your avatar is you gunpla " seems lazy to me. Build Divers had races, clothing, cosplay. Even GB3 had you seem like a pilot and your gunpla was on standby. Wasted potential. The control scheme is AWFUL. i get the thought behind much of the design, but it feels like ass, and they don't have options that would allow it to really shine. some key examples are the melee and ranged mode switch. WHY is it permanently locked to requiring two inputs? every single First and Third person shooter for the past 10 years has gotten this tiny detail down. The lock on controls are the same way too, why can't i just press tab quickly to switch target? why do i have to hold tab and press another key? it's slow, and breaks up the flow, not to mention the camera modes. i want something in between lock on and free cam, but it's so set in stone, i can't lock on while keeping my eyes on the surroundings, it's one or the other, and the lock on is so strong that you are either locked in on a target full send, or you can't ♥♥♥♥♥♥' hit anything2. the graphics look like they let the person who designed the Gundam COD skin crossovers handle the render engine. _childDocuments_.review: If you're entering as a GB3 fan like me, expect to be disappointed by the EX system. In GB3 everything runs on a cool down and you can get it recharged very quickly but in here? It feels like a slog. The EX part break build up is slow. The enemies are boring, small mobs don't even break parts. They're not a threat and even the wave bosses are nothing at all. The worst part is that weapons EX skills now have changed into other part's skills. Skill mastery is worse now as when you're using a mastered skill, you'll override the skill on the current part you'll be using. Eg: You're equipped a G-drive backpack and you'll have the Trans-arm skill. But if you mastered another backpack(transformation) skill, they'll override your backpack and you won't be able to use Trans-arm or their respective other skills like GN cannon or blade finsThe story is so predictable, feels like everything is going by too fast paced and it could have been written better. But if you're a fan of Gundam though, you'll love the diorama system and the AMOUNT OF CUSTOMIZATIONS you can do in the game. They really stepped up their game in letting players customize their mechs as much as they want. THERE'S SO MUCH SO TO DO THERE.But I'm not a diorama person nor really a customizing person so I can't really say how much impact they have to me. I do admit that the customization is really much more this time.I'm more of a "I had lots of fun in GB3's battle system and so felt challenged there and managed to stack funnels upon funnels and missles/Great sword powerhouse or the nuclear missile goes kaboom build" OH AND THE FUNNELS! Funnels in this game.... They're just... I felt so violated to know that builder part funnels aren't OP skills anymore. It's an EX skill that cost 1 for every 2 funnel part you used. You can still stack funnels in this game.... But they're too expensive to fully stack even for a brief moment. The EX bar just builds up too slowly. And their damage and it's attack frequencies has been scaled down A LOT. I really loved GB's combative system since you can really stack almost anything you want. And if it works, it works. Not to say GB3 is perfect in terms of gameplay. But they're what I'm much more familiar with and spent a lot of time with and I'm sad to see that they revamped a lot of stuffs like these that I love. I'll just have to play while getting used to this new system and see how it goes then.At the moment of writing, I have cleared the story of the game in normal mode. 14 hours and I felt like 12 hours of suffering through the story and dialog and is..... Too.... Lack luster I guess? It's just too shallow and felt like it's just enough to be a game but not enough to entice someone to keep reading it. At first I was quite curious about the characters but after you connect some links and the settings they are in, you'll pretty much guessed the whole story already. The moment the villains revealed themselves, I pretty much pressed skip after reading a few dialog boxes since it's quite obvious where it's heading. So, during every cutscenes afterwards is just, read a few boxes, not interesting enough to read, skip.It's not that GB3's story is ground breaking or anything. Their story is also quite as boring as well. But at least it's paced not as quickly as GB4.At the end of the day, I'm just a person who wanted to build the mech that I did in my old PS4's save data and hopefully fulfill that power fantasy that I had in the past, but it didn't really work... So I'll have to play around with it until I get one that works with GB4.Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This is my first Gundam Breaker game. I am someone who loves the shows AND building actual Gunpla.So Gundam Breaker 4 is a third person mission-based beat 'em up where you build your machine from all kinds of different parts from across the entire Gundam franchise. The story is serviceable but nothing to write home about, this is all about the gameplay, and to the teams credit, it feels good to play. With such a wide variety of parts and weapons and add-ons and powers to mix and match, finding a playstyle that is fun and Uniquely You is actually quite enjoyable. I personally settled on a combination of God Gundam and Barbatos Lupus Rex to throw hands all day long without a single ranged attack.With all of this being said though, the game does leave me wanting. It would have been nice for the story to feel more involved, or for the CPU to feel a bit more challenging. Increasing the difficulty just gives them more health and makes them hit harder. I would have also liked to have had the chance to actually fight more weird combination units, which the story could have utilized more often, but alas. The mission types are scarce and pretty samey. I forget the music as soon as it stops playing. This is very much a "you got the basics down but you could do so much more to polish it up." Again, just like. An overworld, a more engaging plot, letting the player be more than a faceless, voiceless spectator DURING the story. It very unfortunately has the vibe of being made with the intent of online multiplayer to carry it, which I am. Not here for. So if that's your jam, this likely won't apply.Overall, yeah, I do recommend it, especially if you're a Gundam fan. Hopefully we'll get more content down the road to beef it up a bit, but I'm not holding my breath.One thumb up.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to NGB it's a massive upgrade.Compared to GB3 it's three steps forward, three steps back. It's got the raw beating heart of 3 which is enough to get my recommend, but none of its style and flair.Getting the cons out of the way, the story presentation has suffered greatly. I started with Gundam Breaker 2 and it left quite an impression on me, so now I'm one of those weirdos who plays GB for the story. Honestly its been downward spiraling with each entry. We are so far removed from GB2's amazing and dynamic Divinidad fight cutscenes that were synced to Silent Trigger. I used to launch GB2 up just to make builds to watch them star in those scenes. Now the animated story cutscenes are often stiffer and more lifeless than the visual novel segments for god's sake. At least the main cast is easy to like, if a bit cliche. Companion AI has degraded. It was never great but I could always count on it to revive me in most situations if I ever went down, can't even rely on them for that now. And then they try to sell the story as if anyone in the cast is remotely near your level.Music's taken a major hit too, not a single theme from the shows is present, not even for bosses or when you use a super-mode. In GB3 if, say, the 00 Gundam appeared as the final boss of a stage it'd play the 00 theme. If you used NT-D while using Awaken, the Unicorn theme would start playing. You could essentially change the BGM at will. None of that is here. Also despite seemingly getting BACK-ON to make a new song for the game, it doesn't even play at the climax! It's only at the end credits... hope the DLC rectifies this, I recall them doing the same in 3.Last big hit is the changes to OP and EX skills, I think we lost far more than we gained changing the system up from GB3-4. One particular stickler is something that ruins the otherwise phenomenal visual customization; using Mastered skills now replaces your parts whenever activated. Tolerable for skills that use built-in weapons, intolerable for super-modes, when in GB3 were I to use a mastered EXAM it'd just give me the aura VFX and turn my gunpla's glow colors red, it was cool. Not here sucker, now your head gets replaced by a holographic Blue Destiny head and ruins the whole look.Now the good stuff. Parts scaling. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, individual parts scaling is a godsend and opens up so much of the visual customization, it almost justifies all the missteps in the game. You've also got new texture options for paints which is nice. Gameplay is much like GB3, albeit with the caveats of the changed EX/OP skill system, and some less interesting enemy AI. Perfect Grade bossfights have more varied and unique movesets. Dual wielding lets you play around more with loadouts, and there's mechanics to make single-wield remain viable, though I'm not sure how well they achieve that. Movement is quick and slick as ever, though you get more fuel than you could ever realistically spend in the tiny arenas."Chaos could be here", he thought. "I've never been in this lobby before... There could be CHAOS anywhere." The cool wind felt good against his gunpla's chest. "I HATE CHAOS!" he thought. ReBreak by BACK-ON reverberated from his iPhone, making it pulsate as the psycoframe circulated through his thick powerful veins and washed away his (merited) fear of spilling spaghetti in front of his clanmates. "With a Lilin, you can ask Aura for anything you want!" he said to himself, out loud.

_childDocuments_.review: Better than New Breaker, doesn't live up to Breaker 3.  It feels like Bandai honestly tried to find a line between correcting the mistakes of New Breaker, living up to Breaker 3, but creating an accessible game for new western fans.  I think that last part is where they went wrong.  The fun part of Breaker 3 was finishing the campaign was just a warm up act.  Inferno gave you better parts, stats, and levels as well as higher abilities.  There's no inferno mode here, not yet and newtype, the highest difficulty thus far, is a cake walk with a properly leveled up MG Gundam, this is before maxing out abilities.  Meaning as of right now, until an update or DLC happens, the post game is a misfire where back in GB3, it was the main event.Back in GB3 option parts could be switched between and could affect gameplay in multiple ways.  Here, option parts are used as rechargeable op skills.  I used to have a blast switching between main and option weapons for my Seven Sword raiser gundam in GB3 and going combo mad.  Not possible in GB4.  There's still a serviceable set of combos and builds, but nerfing option parts and their involvement means gameplay is missing much of its depth.So the post game is a misfire and gameplay is a step back.  Well the good news is a step back from gundam breaker 3 is still a fun time.  The presentation looks amazing, Gunpla have never shined quite so bright as they do here.  Steam Deck performance is excellent.  And an updated roster is very welcome.  Gameplay is still a chaotic good time and carries over from GB3 very well.  Ex skills are still great, configuring your gundams abilities for a specific build is still viable, the combat still holds up and is a good time.  Gundam fans will be well within their element.  I've given the Dub a few minutes of my time, I don't care to give more.  You have to be a pretty intense dub fan to accept the quality of this dollar store voice work.  The new track from back on is passable, But doesn't live up to mirrors.  The story follows up six years from breaker 3 so expect some familiar faces, likely more will show up in the planned DLC.  As it stands, Breaker 4 is good.  Maybe even great.  But it feels like so much is missing from what made Breaker 3 the best gundam title ever.  Inferno mode needs to make a comeback in a bad way.  MG parts only stand out from HG due to base ability levels.  Option parts are nerfed.  I'd say give the game time for the DLC to drop and updates to occur, and maybe the game can fulfil its full potential.

_childDocuments_.review: For the first GB release since NGB globally, I think Crafts & Meister actually hit it right out of the park in not just making a game that feels as good as GB3, but even better. To start, I did see a review that did state that there is a huge lack in mission variety, but that's moreso the GB3 version of the problem rather than the NGB version, so if you felt at home in GB3, you'll feel that things are pretty much as they used to be in this game. You'll primarily be doing 1-2 kinds of missions with a sprinkle of a 3rd mission type, mostly warping between rooms as you beat the ever living hell out of every mobile suit the game has to offer.The story is much more casual than New Gundam Breaker, which attempted to adapt a few Gundam story beats to a school setting, which didn't really work for a huge majority of the story branches apart from the Shion storyline(which is the funniest one). However, in replacing that with a casual MMO setting, I think I actually like this story better than New Gundam Breaker's story. No one really plays Gundam Breaker for its story, but for what it's worth, the casual setting allowed for actually decent worldbuilding! I like that C&M were actually able to capture what it's like to play an MMO for the first time with people you befriend, and apart from the final 2 chapters I could say the story was at least servicable. I'll be talking about spoilers from this point, so I'll put it in brackets so you can skip that part.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[The story of growing in a friend group, with Tao, Lin, Lilin, Sheena, and Mashima to become the best Gunpla battlers in GB4 is what I think was done well enough. Each character does fall into an archetype of Japanese character writing, but the group itself is a good "ragtag team of misfits" that actually ends up working well by the time we reach the final clan battle. However, the story pacing is a bit slow for chapters 1-5, and the cast doesn't build new Gunpla kits until Chapter 6, which personally is a bit late considering Tao scores a mission with a huge part drop rate in Chapter 4. IMO, it would have been better paced if the new Gunpla for the cast were featured in Chapter 5 instead, to show how everyone's been preparing for the final clan battle of the in-story beta. However, Chaos, while his setup as a villain was at least not the worst, did not get enough time with the protag to actually justify how he ends up taking over GB4 at the end of the game. It's a pointless takeover that wasn't really necessary.]---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------As for gameplay, I think this is the best feeling gameplay Crafts & Meister offered with the Gundam Breaker formula. While mobility is similar to Gundam Breaker 3, I love how EX skills and OP parts were bound to the shoulder buttons on the controller to allow for easy access to your build's skills. It's not only quick, but it's actually accessible to those who have to use specialized controllers(If you need to use them for any reason). I also love how the gameplay this time is centered around the building of your custom gunpla. However, the reversion to Gundam Breaker 3's system actually gets rid of the one thing I actually liked about the building that was present in New Gundam Breaker(Which imo had the best building in the entire series up until this game): The customization of your Gunpla's inner frame. New Gundam Breaker actually presented us with the option of making builds to specialize in certain roles in the field that actually work for the gameplay in that game, in which you could have a a build that specializes in breaking, or dealing damage, or zooming around the field to collect all the parts. I think it would have benefited the gameplay to create a similar inner frame system that could fit Gundam Breaker 4's gameplay loop, but in fairness, this is probably just an unnecessary suggestion for a system that really doesn't have a reason to exist in this game. It was just a neat little reference to the existence of the Real Grade kits, which actually do use inner frames!In place of the missing frames, however, GB4 actually heavily expands on GB3's building by allowing us to use 2 different kinds of arms, and dual wielding melee and ranged weapons. This heavily expands the options GB3 players had before, from having dedicated dual wield parts to being able to dual wield anything! Now you can have a pistol paired with a nuke, or twin beam sabers, or even a beam saber with an axe for combos into huge damage!This level of customization is the only real bit of variety for the point I bring up at the beginning of this review: The grind loop. As mentioned earlier, you'll be mainly doing 2 types of missions: Suppression, in which you destroy everything in sight, and Target, in which you destroy all the targets to complete the objective. There are monolith missions that take up all of Chapter 7, and a slot machine one in the Quest category of missions. Quest missions also offer plenty of boss rushes which consist of all the PGs you face in the game. However, even that replay value is stretched thin due to the monotony. Overall though, this game works well as a return to form for the Gundam Breaker series, and despite its shortcomings, it also empowers its players with uninhibited creativity which has been the biggest source of replay value in the Gundam Breaker series. The amazing gameplay only adds to it, and while the grind loop can be monotonous, GB4 utilizes this loop more as a testing grounds for your builds to show off what it can do. Overall, this is a good Gundam Breaker.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunpla shopping simulator.It's anime cheese. That's all you need to know.The music is upbeat anime cheese. The UI is unintuitive. It takes way too many actions, menus and popups for the simplest actions. The graphics look like a mobile game. Heck, I've played mobile games that look better. GN Field is just a glowing bubble without particle effects 🤯. Granted, there are a lot of parts and technologies from different series to cover.Also move categories are completely opaque. Nothing in the game tells you what a "Wild Dance" is but there's a lot of abilities for it. Solvable with Google though.If I rate this as an action game, it'd be pretty mid. The game is easy and button mashy. Don't expect a challenge. You go through a mission with 3 waves, each being a small stage and bust some gunpla up. It's either masses of small gunpla or single big mobile armor gunpla. They give shiny loot at the end to enhance your gunpla parts. That's about it.But I'll rate this as a shopping and customization sandbox game. If you want to spend hours looking at different parts and figuring out how to piece them together for a custom gunpla, this is . They inherit abilities from their respective series too. A GN Drive will give Trans-am, a DRAGOON backpack will launch DRAGOONs and so on. And unlike New Gundam Breaker you can buy dozens of Gunpla boxes instead of farming missions for some part that refuses to drop. Also there's nice photo and diorama options.Honestly I wouldn't recommend this to non-Gundam fans. If it didn't have a bajillion parts across various Gundam series, everything else, from the looter shooter portion to the story frankly aren't worth it.That said, the sheer amount of parts and customization options make this a great sandbox for fans.

_childDocuments_.review: While there is plenty more customization options in Gundam Breaker 4 than there are in Gundam Breaker 3 and Gundam Breaker 4 is leagues improved over New Gundam Breaker,  there are a few features that are absent in Gundam Breaker 4 that I miss: 1) Elemental Damage types on weapons are missing entirely. In Gundam Breaker 3 elements on a weapon could give a player a few more options on what they could focus on, like increased stun, reduced armor, DoT effects and so on. In Gundam Breaker 4 there are Heat and Electric elemental damage types, but they are locked to certain Optional or Extra skills and are few and far between. Corrosive and Frost elements are absent entirely and I have not found them on any part in the game.2) Weapon derive is absent. There is no way other than RNG to get certain weapons in the game. In Gundam Breaker 3, a player was able to obtain near any weapon in the game through derivement with whatever function they wanted (i.e. HE Machinegun, Delayed Burst Bazooka). Not having this feature is annoying, but not gamebreaking.3) Free Movement in Levels. In Gundam Breaker 4 you teleport automatically after each encounter. This can be jarring often times and I prefer Gundam Breaker 3's pseudo dungeons over the teleporting in Gundam Breaker 4.That said I rather enjoy the freedom offered in Gundam Breaker 4 for customizing your Gunpla. Markings, patterns and even enlarged or shrunken parts are on offer here. If that's what you enjoy like me, then go ahead, if not I would highly recommend waiting to see if the full game (DLC included) goes on sale. I think I paid a little too much for what was included in the base game (The story was/is incomplete) and every mission includes cutscenes that must be skipped through. I'd say it's a solid Gunpla simulator (although there are hundreds of kits not present like the HiZack, Marasai, Zock, Zaku I, etc.) that will give you hours of play time, but again I recommend waiting for a full package sale if you are only interested in Gundam and not fully 'invested' (i.e. only a passing interest). That said, I enjoy it and will keep playing it but I do not think it's worth full price. Solid 7/11

Go nuts.Want a Gunpla where its SUPER close-combat focus and have fun simply using different weapons at your disposal? Absolutely.Want to make the most WHACKIEST looking nightmare ever? The worlds your oyster.Because of this, this game is NOT, for Gundam-Series fan. The combat is more akin to the Dynasty-Warrior style where you're hitting 5+ enemies at once, doing air-combos and doing flips and tricks with your gunpla. If you were hoping for slow, dedicated actions and movement, timing and reaction being important, or simply that Gundam-Anime moments, you'll be sorely disappointed. No aiming down sight for that sniper or FPS style gameplay or anything like that. Armored-Core, Mass-Builder, or the Gundam Battle-Operator games will cover that MUCH more than this game will.This, is a game for Gunpla-Fans who wanted to build their dream-gunpla and be able to play it as freely as you customize it.
