_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR of the below. Yes, but pick it up on sale. Mostly if you like to build/customize.This feels like a mobile game. If you played the recently decommissioned mobile breaker title, it's like that but with more customization for skills, no gachas, and no auto-play/AI option. Also, where prior titles gave you an incentive to farm out MG parts, that doesn't really come into play here.The story is a near carbon-copy of the original Build Divers, as far as their time within the actual game is concerned. It's more bland, though.The customization options for detail are really nice, if you are the type to invest hours upon hours into it. Genuinely saying this as a positive. Each piece as a wide variety of material layers, where you can apply your own PBR customizations to them. Being able to also use custom panel line colors is also a nice touch.Alongside that is a diorama option/mode, where you can spend just as many hours creating new scenes to share out.The general gameplay is very monotonous. Missions with monoliths feel like a slap in the face, and battles feel like they're lacking. They brought back the large target fights from the Dynasty Warriors games, but between their ability to repair/replace damaged parts, attacking (and hitting) you while facing the opposite direction and not really giving you anything other than a tough fight, it feels like a swing and a near miss. The targeting system is also kind of atrocious. The manual target cycle they teach you at the start of the game doesn't always work, and seems to ignore some targets. If you unlock the target reticle, let it display an icon on your intended target and attempt to lock again, it may instead lock on to someone behind you at a further distance.There's a sort of coup-de-grace move that you can repetitively use on units while they're on the ground and trying to regain parts you've knocked off. But at some point, this mysteriously disappears once you've progressed far enough in the game, which feels like an artificial lengthening/difficulty increase.One kind of neat thing, is that you can share parts with people in your clan. But, the major caveat is that you can only access that shared list once you've finished the campaign.Drop rates aren't that great, unless you can use a booster and/or maintain combos. But, if you're willing to enhance parts from level 1, you can buy most things in the shop as you progress through the story.The friendly AI will go down frequently, and doesn't seem to keep up with difficulty well at all.Get this if you want to OCD over visual customizations with the occasional pew-pew. But do not expect good gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: hold shift to use OP skill is so aggravating, why can't I just use one key instead of this baked in two keysSept 1, 2024 update:when you open game and load into lobby you have to sit through quite a long unskippable loading animation, super annoying if you launch the game multiple times a day, even one time a day is annoying. Exiting the game from assembly mode you have go through several loading screens to back to menu mode, then you can exit.testing room in assembly lacking a lot of features to test properly, ex. can't set enemy to attack you, can't remove baked in instant cd on op skills, no ui showing keys pressed just what op or ex skill u usedif you have no friends, trying to join multiplayer game is as difficult as it gets. They have a separate lobby system that houses players(20 ish max) that you have to join and in the lobby you have to set up a team to recruit players. Searching for open teams directly is poorly developed, most of the time it will return you the same bugged team that you can't join, effectively blocking you out from using that direct search option. If you search by story or quest mode, 95% of the time you will get no results.  A third option is to search by lobbies which you then go inside and pray the ppl in there aren't afk, then you pray they have a team open that you can join. Trying to join the team this way is also annoying, since you have to find the host, walk up to him and interact with his avatar to join. There is also the option to search open teams in that lobby but you have to know what mission/type that host is hosting to find them. You can't even search by difficulty at all for any of these options. The lobby team system is so convoluted and most of the time if you search by lobbies you'll just get a list of lobbies with 1 or 2 players inside.Way, way, waaaaay too many events and loading screens. Your gunpla blasting off scene before the mission, mini boss appearance which also grabs your camera, boss spawn event which also grabs your camera. A mission has several maps, each map has several waves, and each wave has a mini boss sprinkled with a few trash mobs. Then you have bosses mixed in. When you move between maps, that is a loading screen. If you use your awaken skill, event pans camera in front of your character, if you are in player mode your left dumbfounded because now your staring at your gunpla and not at the enemy that you want to use your awaken on. Multiplayer has auto skip event option, but playing solo doesn't. If other member in multiplayer doesn't skip event, you have to wait it out watching a giant message saying you have to wait, instead of letting you watch the event as well until other members finish or decide to skip.  If you can clear waves fast it becomes a loading screen simulator.You'll have a lot of inventory and skills, so much so that you'll need a filter and search option for all of these. Unfortunately the search function is as bad and convoluted as the multiplayer and some filters don't even work, example filter by no labels in cartridge. UI information is severely lacking in assembly, in order to know what an ex or op skill does you have to equip it then go to ex or op tab to read about it then test it further in the test room. English description of a lot of part abilities is not intuitive, example near death remaining, reaction speed performance, x y z parts lost (yours or enemy?). Trying to find answers in discord and google most of the time will leave you unanswered. The weapon type beginner tips is so bland, might as well say nothing.Using keyboard and mouse is scuffed. Some might not even figure out how to access some extra options with mouse if you don't watch a youtube guide vid. You'll have to use controller to have the better experience for this game. Also the mouse sensitivity config in this game is horrid, I'm guessing it's because of their engine or how they designed the game, but it's as convoluted and equally frustrating to set right, ex. they have separate vertical and horizontal sensitivity scaling, why? it's a mouse just add one sensitivity scaling (and maybe f off with the acceleration?), also they separate scaling for each aiming mode, like lock on, player mode(free aim mode), firing mode(sniping/range mode), lobby mode. I just want to set my mouse sensitivity so I don't feel like a spazztic kid high on logan paul's gatorade or feel like my hands are freezing, it's just that simple, like every other normal third person shooter.keybind config is also scuffed on keyboard, op skills is hard coded to use two keys no matter what.oh yeah, this is a $80 cad game WITHOUT tax added yet. What the hell happened? This could of been a very good game. Did no one from the devs sit down and just play this game for like, i don't know, 2-3 days, you know, like what I just did. I thought they had several play tests before, perfect time to test your multiplayer. And no one said yeah this is definitely not a torture to find a multiplayer lobby? And this is on and near launch days where player count should effectively be at its peak and here I am struggling to find a game without going through hoops.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good.  The Breaker formula is basically a mix of Dynasty Warriors and Monster Hunter drops.  Kill the thing you want parts from.  It's not complicated but it does have some complexity from the vast amount of parts and weapons available.  If a mecha is known for doing something special, it's probably reflected in the game more often than not.  Compared to GB3 it's similar in mechanics with an updated roster for the series that have come out since.  On the downside, though, the bosses are not as good and all the levels have been condensed down to a handful of small, generic arenas.  3 didn't have astounding levels, but it did have some memorable ones, and they were longer to make each mission feel like more than just a handful of arena waves.This is much easier to get ahold of than GB3, though, so hopefully they plan to bring back some more compelling level designs in the next one.I'd say a soft recommend.  It's not their best outing but it does have all the basic mechanics in place.  Maybe it'll get back on its feet and take a step past GB3 in the next sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: After only a few hours and having played GB3 here's what I can tell about the game. It is a way better launch than NGB and I am really happy about that. Knowing that it is the first time we get a proper GB game on PC and seeing how well it is faring for now, I expect to get a new one within a few years.With that said from what I can experience, the gameplay is improved from GB3 allowing new combinations and combos, ranged weapons are way more viable than in GB3 so on that point it is quite good. When it comes to melee the game is tad bit slower than GB3 but still quite fast. Overally the game is pretty well balanced compare to GB3 which was really melee focused. I also feel like builder parts are a bit underpowered for now: we could litterally make ennemy fly with vulcans before.For the stages, they are somewhat repetitive and missions a bit on the short side -about 10 mins to 15 mins- however coming to GB repetitiveness is expected and I much rather prefer short missions than endless stages like in GB3 when in later missions it would 30 mins of unending and painful grinding.Gunpla building has been improved from GB3 which is always pleasant.I still do expect that the DLC will bring new features and suits of course. But I would say that Banco made a good game and that they have all the cards in hand to make it great.Also the game is quite nice visually and is quite light on performance: a good point.

_childDocuments_.review: This is very specific game for very specific tastes.In terms of progression and meta mechanics it's similar to something like Diablo, Nioh or any given only action game like PSO2, Vindictus or Warframe. You're supposed to replay the same content over and over on progressing difficulties to become stronger yourself and progress further, it's basically a loop. It's not endless, but if you like it, it can offer hundreds of hours of gameplay. I've spent over 300 hours in Nioh 2 for example, before doing everything there is to do, it's that deep.In terms of combat it's a mix between dynasty warriors (gundam) and devil may cry. You can juggle enemies, and float in the air yourself while comboing. You can mix and match normal, special (OP) and super (EX) attacks to make lengthy flash combos, while fighting enemies. There are ultimate (burst) attacks to. The longer your combo is, the more bonuses you get, it's more transparent grade system similar to DMC, but instead of letters you're outright told what bonuses you get for better combos.You still get letters for missions though, based on time and amount of parts you've broken off enemies. There isn't SS or SSS though, only S.And finally, at least 50% of your play time, or even more, you're expected to spend in character editor, in this case plastic model editor, where you mix and match parts of your toy robot, paint them, upgrade them, fine-tune and min-max their stats. It's simpler and more accessible system than Nioh 2, but still pretty deep and can change how you approach combos and bosses.However, if you don't like robots, or grinding, or looping gameplay progression, or unrealistic floaty combat with juggles and combos, then you won't like the game.While DLC is just the last chapter of the game cut off and sold separately, I'd recommend to get both it, and the base on sale. Publisher is way too greedy.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the series that has played all the installments, (even the mobile one) Gundam Breaker 4 is not the ideal sequel we all have definitely had in our heads, but its a solid course correction for the series, and judging by the fact that Bandai Namco has put out multiple giveaways of the game through Social Media (Influencers etc.) I think its safe to say the game is selling really well, perhaps securing the future of the franchise for good this timeNow onto the game itself:PRO:Combat - The game's combat flow is a lot more smooth than even GB3, no more shuffling option parts on the D-pad as both EX and Option actions are activated through the face buttons depending on the shoulder button pressed, there is less discrepancy in DPS numbers thanks to your weapons now influencing your EX and Option DamageCustomization - This is the biggest improvement of the game, Part Scaling, Positioning and Rotation, Emissive Coloration, Left and Right Separation for Arms and Weapons, Functional Builder's parts etc, there is a near limitless amount of combination possibilities, you can easily tell someone is creative in designing a Gunpla when you see oneSpecifications - I feel appropriate to put this in the pro section, the requirements are low enough that even Steam Deck would have no problem running it smoothly provided you tune your settings quite a bit, I know people want to be excited for the next Visual Sensation in Video Games but that's not really want you want to look forward to with this gameProgression - This installment is the most generous when it comes to loot and drops, Breaker Boosters (Then Luck Boosters) used to be a paid only item that increases drop rates but can now be earned in-game, parts upgrade is also less tedious as part abilities are more complementary than necessary, Ability cartridge allows for endless build customization because of how much it affects your build despite being all random statsCON:User Interface - This is by far the single most infuriating thing about the game, if you have played GB3 then it would anger you even more, every part of the menus need to have a confirm button, the paint section for example is made more tedious because of this, lots of needless button pressing, more importantly, the design is so disastrous that it confuses me to this point even after 17 hours of playtime, The button icons are ALL OVER THE PLACE, with no sense of cohesion whatsoeverSkill Mastery - A signature feature of GB3 is mastering EX Skills so they can be used regardless of the parts you have assembled for your gunpla, the BIG problem with this game's implementation of it is the presence of the part hologram, that transform your current part into the part which you mastered the Skill from before executing the move, This just reminds me of the Part Swapping Mechanic from New Gundam Breaker, which was one of that game's biggest problems, I hope the developers patch out this visual mechanic but retain the Move and the effects instead, no need to worry about it looking awkward, since they've introduced so many things that can make your Gunpla look AwkwardEmergency Landing - This one is also quite annoying, you probably encountered it in the game one way or another, because of how easy it is the execute, just press jump while in midair, except when you do that, your instinct is to use it to boost to a different direction, typically away from harm, This mechanic was definitely inspired by Gundam Versus, except in that game, verticality is king and so you would find it useful there, but in GB4, AI is not even sophisticated enough to warrant the presence of this mechanic, it has only served to put me in trouble and nothing else, Bamco, Please remove this!AI - I think not much needs to be said here, the premise of the game warrants very little to have an AI more advanced than this, I get it, but in times when we need it to be reliable within reason, it still fails, Oh wellOverall, GB4 is a decent package for a game series about making your own robot, it has glaring flaws that drag the experience down considerably, I understand people not wanting to call this GB4 to signify its following in the footsteps of GB3, which is still in my opinion the better designed game, but like I said in the beginning of this review, this is more of a correction than a straight up sequel, but at least you and I won't have to suffer NGB just to play a Breaker Game

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with Gundam Breaker extends largely to the demo of the first game and Mobile, though i have a decent amount of experience with both Gundam and mech customization games and am an avid Gunpla builder IRL. For what it is, GB4 feels like a very fun beat-em-up with a huge helping of customization and builder expression. It is a bit more limited than kitbashing IRL, but given the limitations of computers, this is entirely understandable and the options presented are more than good enough to simulate modeling. However, I will say quite a few things are... needing improvement. The presentation is rough, with the game refusing to explain certain things like the abilities each part can have and what they actually mean, with no hover over or select for more info option, which makes Synthesizing very difficult and tedious. There's no way to save individual palettes, nor is there a way to select a group of parts without selecting them all, which makes painting a pain. The multiplayer interface does its job, but is awkward to invite people to clans or to start a mission without understanding what you need to do first. You're left to figure out what the various gauges on your HUD mean, and it's entirely possible to proceed without understanding what the HUD is trying to tell you.None of these issues are unfixable; I understand it'll take time to do so, but I believe that prioritizing ease of understanding is important if this game is to last and grow beyond those who are already familiar with Gundam Breaker's entries. I can't speak to those who've dedicated their time to GB3 for a long time, but as for myself this is a game I love despite its flaws, and sincerely wish for its success.TL;DR+Huge customization factor with additional filters to represent modeling techniques which are great+Decently fast beat em up combat with opportunities for various forms of skill expression and difficulty+Faithful recreation of SFX from the various series represented+A game that takes only 10GB and plays well in 2024-Some customization effects seem off (unable to affect the glow colors of GN Drives or certain parts in an enhanced state)-Difficult to parse information presented by the game, especially with abilities-Unintuitive setups to invite people to clans or starting missions-Some weapons lack satisfying damage or audiovisual feedback (i.e. most funnels)Overall, in its current state and as someone who uses the entire 1-10 scale, GB4 is a solid 7/10 - it is competent at what it does, but it absolutely has flaws that are difficult to ignore when it comes to enjoyment.(P.S.: If you identify as female/non-binary, play a drinking game where you take a shot every time you're referred to as he/him in the story.)

_childDocuments_.review: It has its up and its downs. I've been enjoying myself for these past 25 hours, and will probably put more time into it. I like the grind because it doesn't take you 5 or 6 missions to max one part. I've been playing 2-3 missions and have been able to get enough parts to max my pieces rarity and level for most of my suit. I don't mind grind, but too much grind is a turn off, and this has just enough to so that when you're bored with your current suit, you can just make another.  I have three gripes with this game. One, the perfect grade fights are not implemented well. They have a system where you hit specific areas of the perfect grade suit to stun it so you can do more damage to it. The problem is that the tracking system aims for every other part except the part you are trying to hit, which can be really frustrating especially against the last boss. A lot of times you are better off turning off the lock on so you can aim manually where you need to hit these pieces, but switching between lock on and not is an absolute pain. My second gripe is the translation of this game. There are A LOT of skills in this game, and the game doesn't help you understand what certain terms mean, or which skills power affect which weapons. Luckily you can find the answers you need on youtube, but the fact that there isn't a way to look up it in game makes it very time consuming to build a gundam, and you forgot what hypertrance means so you have to online or Barrage. My third gripe is that there are way too many skills in this game. Having to synthesize a part and read through every single piece because you are looking for specific skills will fry your last two brain cells. There is a skill called flinch, which is basically your stun, except you have no idea how to track it because there is no gauge or number to look for in stats, but it is a skill that works. You just can't tell how well. I do not enjoy the skill searching and adding part of this game, I do enjoy the grab a gundam, synthesize a bunch of random pieces up to level 50, pick what skills you want and take it to the field to smash everyone else. The story is, I don't care. I skipped every cutscene cause I truly did not care, I just wanted to hop into the levels and fight, and they did a great job in that aspect. You don't run looking for enemies. They spawn around you continously, and its great cause the only lull you really have are between waves. Getting S rank in all your missions isn't that hard either. Just smash things, really really hard. I almost forgot but this is my last gripe. Your ai teammates are stupid. They will literally just walk around you instead of trying to pick you up when you are down. It really boggles my mind to have the opposing ai bum rush you, and your ai just sit back and take bets on which of your parts will break first. I know it sounds all doom and gloom, but honestly, it's a great game. If you came here to make gundams, and smash things you're looking at the right game. It's not perfect, but it's good, and since they plan on releasing DLC for this game, hopefully they fix some of my complaints on the way.

_childDocuments_.review: OK so to start. I have played Gundam Breaker 3 (GB3), but most of my experiance with GB is with Gundam Breaker Mobile (GBM).I LOVE GB. I loved the shows that came out and made me truly WANT to be a builder, and GBM helped my flesh out some of my ideas with its builder.Now that intro's are out of the way into the meat.EXTENSIVE ability to customize almost EVERY aspect of your Gunpla build      - if you want to be a melee master you can, shooter you bet ya, hybrid absolutely, mixed weapons without          a doubt      - ability to adjust almost any part for size, angle, position, and/or to be "invisible"                                                                                                                the part is equipped but won't be visible      - ability to USE any part: you can still use a weapon even if the arm already has one inherently      - an absolutely mind boggling amount of prefab paint schemes (the weathering and damage filters are                                                                                                               fun)      - after mastering a part the inherent ability (EX/OP) is able to be equipped without the original part Simple to play, difficult to master      - you can basically beat the game without having to do any upgrades and just using reward parts. Making          your Gunpla look like Frankenstein's monster. (which i have 2 variations of :-D)      - the amount of depth to the chase of numbers to "MASTER" a build gives you HOURS (if not more) of          gameplay. Especially when ability chips come into play.The gameplay is fair: without abilities, chips, or enhancements all parts of the same type are equal. The stats of all left arms are exactly the same at max rarity and level . That means the total stats of the part you are using depends on what abilities you add to the part itself.The battle fields are pretty and a bit more detailed than expected.The controls are easy to use and understand. (I don't use mouse and keyboard but the option is there)You can test your gunpla versus other players gunpla which adds a nice calm way to add a "PVP" aspect.the story is lackluster, in the fact it feels reused. it would have been a decent story if there were more multiplayer aspects but the gameplay makes it feel like a single player game, and because it feels like a singleplayer game i feel like there should have been a bit more character development or a way that makes your accomplishments feel more rewarding, rather than just a statement or a fact. Like yes I know I'm the HERO but yall feel like you're to weak to give me a challenge or that you're any kind of a threat. It has SOME music, and  know that there is a disparity between anime music making it into video games but I do wish they would use soundtracks from from the anime's to allow a more "This is Gundam" or "Gunpla is Freedom" feeling. Or give use the ability to use our own music. ok to preface this the battlefields aren't BAD (for some of the missions provided) however i would have loved to see more variety in the structure of the fields.             - all the fields feel more like you're supposed to have a FFA brawl            - the "larger" fields feel like narrow stripes of a road with large rocks on the side            - it seems that the only major change to the different maps are the foliage used so IMO GBM did a much better job in making the EX/OP skills LOOK powerful and                                           exciting                     - the particle effects in particular feel underused ie                      - some/most of the verniers do NOT look like they activate, AND you can't change color or                         intensity                     - and the "hologram" of the part you are using an ability from that replaces your equipped part                         while in use is pretty stupid and ruins the look of you Gunpla while in action. While Technically there IS PVP in the form of battling other ai controlled user Gunpla, it leaves MUCH to be desired. the ai is no different than the regular ai you fight against in the game.                     - GBM actually lets you play WITH other players in specific missions. I'm sure that if a MOBILE                         game could connect other players to fight together im sure that they could have done the                         same with this game and even added true PVP where its a human fighting a human and not a                         human fighting and ai.                       - The major driving point of the game is to "make the best Gunpla" and i feel that it  falls short by not being able to test your own skills against other players so you CAN comunicate using emotes and premade comments with voiceover like "Good Build" or "Gunpla is freedom!". that being said im sad that you literally cant type in chat even if you have a team made. there were so many questions i would ask other players like how they made a build or if they want to do any particular missions.Even the game says in the story that "its a place to socialize" but there is no ability for other players to socialize in game except through "thumbs up". but me being an older gamer also thinks that it is a good thing to keep the trolls and toxic people away from ruining someone else's enjoyment. And there ARE other platforms to use to find other like minded players and still enjoy the game game together. i do not like the fact that you cant START a new build from scratch, and you cant use a "basic build" to start your new build. Like if i wanted to use an Exia build I'd have to select each part individually instead of using  "the box build" selection. This is more of a QOL thing than a pro or con.I  this game as it is and i can see this truly shining in about a year. I would WHOLEHEARTEDLY recommend this game to anyone who enjoy's gundam models, or loves customizing giant robots, or action arena combat.Even my wife enjoys this game and she mostly plays Tetris or a Metroidvania game.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended for some good old mindless fun combat, parts farming, and gunpla building.Now, immediately, for those returning from GB3, you'll feel a bit weirded out by the combat - stages are basically just arenas after arenas, not much at all in the way of moving from point A to point B. You'll recall in 3, after you beat all the enemies, you have to go to the "Move to next area" spot. In here, you're just transported to the next arena, then rinse and repeat.For the newcomer and general gamer, this may mean that the combat may quickly become stale for you, especially if you're looking for something more in-depth like Wukong or Dark Souls. Please dispel those ideas. The repetitive, rather mindless combat system of the Dynasty Warriors games are probably the comparator/example I can give. So just turn off your brain, spam those attack buttons and just enjoy the ride!One thing though about the combat are the skills. for GB3 players, they may find some changes very annoying as I did, like how funnels are now EX skills and not OP skills (Not to mention they suck major ass in GB4), And also the lock on camera will take some time getting used to. I think it's too close to the gundam and position very awkwardly.The real meat of the game is in the customization, or in other words, making your own gundam by mixing and matching the different parts from different gundams and then painting them to your liking. There are a LOT of parts, and the main difference between the parts are just skills that each part have, which you can master anyways later on so that you can equip those skills while using other parts. The parts all scale equally based on their level, and while each part can get different Abilities (Modifiers), you can put these modifiers onto your preferred parts later on, so just go wild on what parts that look best for your designs!One thing that GB3 players will immediately notice is that skill mastery is now tied to the part's rarity instead of actually mastering the skill through use, like how it was in GB3 where you need to use a skill multiple times, fill up it's mastery bar until it's maxed and mastered, and only then can you put it in other parts.In GB4, you instead need to use plastics to increase the part's rarity up to 6 stars, and once it reaches max rarity, even if it's still a level 1 part, you will have mastered the skill associated with the part.Of course, this means some farming, but don't worry, the game is actually quite generous with the materials needed for bumping up the rarity. As of writing, I have enough of those materials to basically master 3 full gundam sets of gundam parts, including weapons, all of which was farmed in just a few short hours.TL;DR You don't have to hard grind using ♥♥♥♥♥♥ unleveled parts to master the skills that you want anymore. Just get some evolution plastics, rank those babies up, and now you've got the skill. MUCH quicker than GB3.HOWEVER, one caveat is that when you use a mastered skill when you don't have the associated part equipped, your Gundam's model will temporarily switch to that mastered skill's original part in the form of a wire hologram for the duration of the skill. Aesthetically, this BLOWS hard. The biggest offender is when using an Install skill that boosts your stats, like Trans Am or Super Mode, your torso will be a lame ass pale blue wire holographic of whatever part had the skill throughout the duration of the Trans Am or Super Mode. It ruins the Gundam's look mid-game and sometimes really just takes you out of the experience, hope this fixed.In summary:Combat can get repetitive very quickly, but its quick, mindless, and overall fun to just mess around in and just relax.Gundam modeling / customization is top notch, and imo you have more freedom in terms of customization without needing to worry much about parts mastering ugly parts for their skills, so an overall improvement.Great game. May or may not be partially biased because I do enjoy gundam and the mecha genre in general, so I wasn't looking for any deep combat systems, but I'd rate the game a solid 8/10. Maybe even an 8.5.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm in the same group of people who have played the previous GB games (besides New GB but forget that game, tried it on a friend's playstation). There is a lot to unpack with this game but it is honestly worth getting. It could use some work though.ProsThe customization is great! Part scaling and variety really helps to make some beastly gunpla especially now that mastering parts give you their options as well as their EX skills. Combat feels great. Going on a rampage with your custom tuned murder machine feels as good as ever thanks to new mechanics like dual wielding weapons and the adjustments made to existing weapons. Awakening now charges faster making it more viable across missions rather then waiting to use it until the last boss of the mission.Many new quality of life features such as the instant (but fortunately optional) recoloring of newly equipped parts. No need to recolor new parts anymore if you don't want to in order to match your custom color scheme.Game runs extremely smooth at a constant framerate with no loss of frames as of currently. I never ran into any slowdown throughout the entire game even when using VFX intense abilities.So much gunpla variety from across the franchise with more to come in the future. I love that they added Bolt Gundam. Still hoping to see Gundam Maxter in the future. Edit: We got Gundam Maxter in the fourth DLC. About time but still happy to see that suitConsAlly and enemy AI is really stupid. Outside of mini and actual bosses, enemies are cannon fodder and allies panic even if the enemy so much as looks in their direction. This gets really annoying if you are down. Do yourself a favor and play with actual players.The story feels meh, it's not bad but 3's was way better. The scenes all feel like the characters have no lives outside the game and may as well all be AI programs. I liked the still images in GB because those at least showed what you and your team were up to and what was going to happen next. Seeing a bunch of gunpla sit around and emote is not a scene. A VN gives more a feeling than this nonsense.Why are 90% of the perfect grade boss fights against the RX-78-2 (OG Gundam) and/or the Unicorn Gundam? Did none of these devs see what GB3 did with the PG boss fights? Those were intense and fun while these feel repetitive and bland. Edit: First dlc mission has a PG Strike Freedom as a boss. That actually felt more intense and what I was hoping for. Shame it took a dlc to do something like that but keep it up Bamco.The effing EX gauge. What was so bad about having EX skills being on cooldowns? It forces you to wait ages to actually use your EX skills and some feel too expensive for how little they do (*cough*AnyfunnelEX*Cough*).No crossplay. Understandable but still a con given that the game is only on four platforms and two of them run on the same system (PSN). Only two of my friends play on pc. Honestly this game feels like a downgrade from GB3 but it's still good overall. Hopefully the DLC shakes things up a bit and the free update is something I am rather eager for. It's worth getting for Gundam fans though for non Gundam fans, I'd wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember sitting down in 2018 with a bunch of friends after we'd all purchased Gundam Breaker 3 for the PS4. We spent  glued to the game, with some of us completely abandoning other games we'd regularly played due to how hooked we were. I remember playing the game for probably 500+ hours, and absolutely loved my time spent with the game, so I was super hyped when a Gundam Breaker along the lines of GB3 was announced. Sadly, Gundam Breaker 4 truly feels like a game which is three steps forward and three steps back from the predecessors it aims to iterate upon.Truly, I enjoy Gundam Breaker 4, but the game just hasn't hooked me the same way as its predecessor due to a myriad of confusing design decisions. Gundam Breaker 4 has managed to take several of the lacking aspects of Gundam Breaker 3 and iterate upon them in meaningful manners, such as the gunpla building and the player combat, but really the core game feels flawed and shallow to the point that I wouldn't so much as call Gundam Breaker 4 a "Gundam Game", but rather I'd call it a "Gundam Experience", and if someone asked me to recommend a Gundam Game to them I'd point to SD Gundam Battle Alliance.- Gunpla Building. Gunpla Building is FANTASTIC in this game, and the scaling features and various other aspects of the Assembly system which have just been improved upon since Gundam Breaker 3 are incredibly refined and well-tuned. It's definitely this games selling point, to the point it feels like some of the other features within the game suffered as a result. Truthfully this is the main selling point of the game, and what's primarily causing me to give the game a recommendation, which I feel is truly befitting of game.- Combat. Allowing the player to use two different melee weapons and two different ranged weapons in every build was a fantastic decision that has opened up all sorts of avenues for combo-design and allows the gameplay to flow much better. Unfortunately, the combat systems in the game feel a bit overdesigned when most of the enemies stand still and just allow you to hit them as if they're punching bags and nothing more.- The Story. It's your standard Gundam Breaker styled story. Person wants to be the best or person wants to do bad thing within game which you then stop. Nothing extraordinary, and it makes sense for this type of game where they want everyone to be their demographic. - Mobile Suit Selection Choices. I don't quite understand some of the inclusions into the game. Variety is the spice of life one might say, but many of the choices and additions are either just reskins, or are variants of mobile suits which aren't considered particularly popular, with the most sought after variants being left out in the rain. There's an unnecessary amount of recolors which have alternate unit designations which clutter the games roster, when there really was no reason to add them when players could've remade them due to the assembly tools given to them.- Playing Fields and their variety. Here's another one of the things they took from Gundam Breaker 3 and changed drastically to the point it just feels sad. Gone are the sprawling playing fields where you'd traverse them with your friends and wander into encounters, as GB4 puts you into a square-shaped arena and constantly drops enemies onto you to fight until you're done and then they teleport you to another square-shaped arena to do it two more times. Worst of all, there's maybe 10 different arenas for the ENTIRE GAME which are just reused over and over to the point it feels almost mind-numbing.- Co-Op Synchronization. Unless you're fighting one of the bosses such as a Perfect Grade or a Perfect Grade Unleashed the game has basically no synchronization and it feels like you're basically playing the game alone still. Enemies will take damage that your friends inflict, but they'll be across the arena hitting or shooting the enemy and it will just magically flinch and then die. - Enemy Difficulty and their AI. This hasn't ever been the main selling point of Gundam Breaker as a franchise, but honestly Gundam Breaker 3 felt like it had better enemies in it. Often times in that game I at least found myself occasionally in frantic situations, whereas whilst GB4 has *serviceable* AI, they're certainly not challenging nor are they smart.- Terrible Online Communication Options. I'd hoped that I could look into making friends with some of the people within this game, hopping from lobby to lobby to meet others and share Gunpla designs and help them do missions, but communicating in this game is basically nonexistent. _Overall Score: 7/10. A Gundam Experience designed with singleplayer in mind with co-op strapped to it as if it were an afterthought. Only really recommended if you're wanting to experience the customization aspect.Worth $59.99? Absolutely not, unless you DESPERATELY want to play something where you can customize your own gunpla which has gameplay which is lacking.

Once you reach end game and your drops are now 4 star and above rarity; the mass select button becomes useless because it only works on 3 star or below. _childDocuments_.review: My first Gundam Breaker game. The battles are very fast paced, and I feel enemies are thrown in a stream towards me.The story itself is very shonen, and it's easy to laugh at the general cliches you get from the type of genre, so it was pretty fun to follow along.Playing the game, the customisation at the start, you won't be married to your parts as you'll rotate them, instead, I feel you create a colour identity for yourself through the paint system, and later settle on a final mecha loadout for yourself by the late game. They have a pretty extensive diorama system, though, I feel only hardcore players who are interested in posing digital models would be interested in this.The parts I didn't like are the presentation, and the UI, as it often confuses me, and I often press the wrong buttons to navigate, even after 10 hours in.Playing co-op, it's a bit difficult to setup a friend group as you need to be set to the same download region on steam for people in other regions to connect to each other, and on top of that, the UI for joining is confusing if you access by the desk, however, you can still interact with the player in your lobby to join their mission. There are sync issues during coop play unfortunately, though, most of the combat is you in your own devices rather than working together too heavily.Overall, I'm having a lot of fun with the game progressing through the ranks and getting more parts to try out.

_childDocuments_.review: Gundam Breaker 4 goes back to the system that works. Build a Mobile Suit, go into a stage, and beat the crap out of enemies.Unlike GB3, where stages were these huge sprawling things where you'd go from enemy to enemy, taking them down one or two at a time and looking for the next trigger point to spawn in more enemies, along with some random bit of story, GB4's levels are much shorter and to the point. You spawn in, get a wave of enemies to take care of, after which more spawn. The action is non-stop, which is great. There's still a story, which is... well, it's a Gundam story, so you know what you're getting. But you don't have to run around the map looking for triggers to get it going. Everything just flows.Customization is better than ever. You can change size, position, angle, wear, and so much more with every part. You can make the MS of your dreams.Multiplayer has you either doing co-op missions, or fighting against other teams. Lots of fun with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Note that I've only played about 15 hours at the time of writing this review.Gundam Breaker 4 is everything I'd hoped it would be. None of the terrible decisions from New Gundam Breaker are present and it really seems like they're trying to redeem themselves after NGB.It plays like Gundam Breaker 3 but better. Smoother gameplay, more in-depth customization and a few changes to the way things worked in terms of skills and abilities compared to GB3. The only major downside I've encountered so far is that the co-op party limit has been decreased from four players in GB3 to three players in GB4.For anyone who loved GB3, this is an absolute must-have.For anyone new to the Gundam Breaker series, this is a fantastic jumping off point.For people unsure about the Gundam franchise in general, the base premise of this game is making your own robot and then using it to blow up other robots. So far at least, I can highly recommend this game to anyone that's either a fan of robots, Gundams or building real-life Gunpla models.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an extremely simple beat em up where you're constantly building and rebuilding cool little mecha toys to fight more mecha toys. Everything works great and is exactly what you're looking for when you look at a game like this.It can feel like mindless mush for a lot of it, in the same way Dynasty Warriors games tend to. It is just fun to put something together and watch it blow up 10 enemies like nothing. Though, from my experience now, the harder difficulty tends to actually put up a fight and I like that there's something to work towards.I highly recommend if you wanna play mecha dress up and play around with a million different weapons. It's kind of like Earth Defense Force in the way you're always getting new weapons that range from Really Cool to Hilariously Terrible.The only MAJOR ISSUES is that the online play is a busted experience. There is desync with enemies, though bosses seem to work fine, and also you have to go to your Download Settings on Steam and make sure everyone is set to the same region or else you can't join each other??? Completely insane, even for a Bandai Namco game. Another thing is that there isn't really a way to chat in this game. There's only preset messages and it doesn't make any sense considering there is a whole chat box in the game that you simply can't use and the game is built around going online to share what you've done, but why bother when you can't even really talk to anyone? It feels like the game is two steps away from being everything I like about Phantasy Star Online or a Monster Hunter, but somebody got cold feet last minute.Even with those Pretty Major Issues it at least Works Well Enough. The desync only really applies to minor enemies and it's not like you're using abilities to assist each other. It's Fine. But for the love of god fix that accidental(?) region locking.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Gunpla, you'll likely appreciate "Gundam Breaker 4" for its deep customization and attention to detail, which are central to the Gunpla building experience. The game offers an expansive selection of Gundam parts from various series, allowing you to mix and match to create your dream mobile suit. The customization is intuitive and extensive, letting you tweak everything from weapons to color schemes, which is perfect for someone who enjoys the creative aspects of building Gunpla.The gameplay mechanics are solid, with fast-paced action that captures the essence of Gundam battles. The variety of missions and the inclusion of both single-player and multiplayer modes give the game good replay value. The multiplayer, in particular, is a highlight, as it allows you to showcase your custom-built Gunpla in competitive or cooperative play.However, the game isn't without its flaws. Some missions can feel repetitive, and the story might not be as engaging as one would hope. Additionally, while the customization is a strong point, the interface can be a bit overwhelming at first due to the sheer number of options available.Overall, "Gundam Breaker 4" is a must-play if you're a Gunpla enthusiast. It captures the joy of building and battling with your creations, making it a worthy addition to your collection.

_childDocuments_.review: Gundam Breaker 4 is not a $100 game.Gundam Breaker 4 is not a $90 game.Gundam Breaker 4 is not a $60 game.Gundam Breaker 4 plays like a mobile game with a $5-$10 price tag and would have been an acceptable product for that asking price.The Good:The visuals are fine. The graphics look dated, but it really is cool to see the vast variety of Gundam and mobile suits fully rendered and animated in an aesthetic that somewhat ties them all together in a coherent way. It's cool to be able to very freely swap out suit parts and weapons and they give you enough tools to adjust and scale what you make enough to have it read on-screen. Unfortunately that's about it for positive things I can say about it.The Bad:This game is BORING. In terms of gameplay, the first several chapters of the story mode consist of a very small handful of mission types which are repeated ad nauseam, boiling down to "destroy enemy mobile suit(s)" within a certain timeframe. The story itself is also a massive nothing burger with zero of the charm or gravity of a typical Gundam story.Paying the least bit of attention to your build makes even the harder difficulty levels extremely easy, and the only element of difficulty comes from putting you up against spongier and spongier enemies as you progress. None of the vast variety of weapons or abilities end up feeling different or impactful due to the fact that enemies will just stand around doing barely anything while you unload your arsenal at them, chipping away and chilling away at their HP bars in gameplay that feels more like WoW combat than a fast-paced mech fighting action game. This is ESPECIALLY egregious in boss fights as the bosses tend to have very little in terms of move sets which are invariably EXTREMELY slow and telegraphed.Despite how different you can make your custom created suits look, they all end up feeling basically identical in terms of gameplay due largely in part to the above. The game's flagship gimmick is extremely undermined by the fact that the gameplay does not at all reinforce it. No matter how you build your suit, gameplay will consist of flying around large mostly empty arenas button-mashing at largely stationary braindead AI opponents hoping your excel spreadsheet of stats happens to be higher than theirs.The Ugly:$60? $90? $100??? Are you kidding me? Armored Core VI came out a year ago at $60 and the gameplay MASSIVELY justified its main gimmick of modular mech building by providing a widely varying and challenging gameplay experience including engaging PVE story missions and boss fights, meaningful mech customization, and high-intensity PVP. Gundam Breakers 4, in a bid to avoid the poorly-implemented PVP from the last installment, just decided not to even try and shipped the game without any PVP included whatsoever. Armored Core VI was also a Bandai-Namco published title; what in god's name happened???The Verdict:This game looks like a pretty okay PS2 game and plays like a free-to-start mobile game. The fact that they're selling a version of this title for $100 is an outright insult and even the biggest Gunpla fan is going to be bored of this title before their playtime hits double digits.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm new to the series, and I've heard universal disdain for the previous title. Therefore, I can't give a comparative review, only standalone critique. I love Gundam. Everything Gundam that isn't SD (I don't dislike it, I'm just more about the war/drama type stuff.) Even though I've only dabbled with a few HG kits, I enjoy Gunpla. What I don't enjoy is typical shounen franchise #22,205, otherwise known as Gunpla anime. No surprise here, just your typical type-casts, "friendship & let's do our best to reach the top!" plot with a tiny dash of cyberpunk element. I haven't beaten the game, but if the only shakeup of the plot hasn't gone anywhere by the third chapter, then I've officially given up any hope that there's gonna be anything redeeming. As you can probably tell by my writing that I'm pushing "old," but hey, the people that make this stuff are even older than me, so it's not like I feel like I'm playing Paw Patrol or anything, just too much of a G-rated story to be mixed with the legacy of the greater Gundam franchise.Now I'll get to the actual game itself. It looks like a PS3 game remastered with 120 fps. Nothing stunning, but nothing horrendous. There's only a few "battlegrounds" that the game reuses, and missions just go through (usually) three stages. Where you're transported to in the next section of a mission has no relevancy, you're just there fighting enemies. Combat is nothing-at-all special, and having come fresh off of Armored Core 6, I find it bland. It keeps a steady pace though, and there's an incentive to taking your hack-n-slash skill seriously, as keeping a combo meter gives you a better chance of high(er) quality parts, meaning higher stats. Other that, there's just defeat fodder, dance with some more-iconic mobile suits/gundams, and long, drawn-out epik showdowns with gargantuan mobile armors ...or even oversized mobile suits! These encounters (for me) range from braindead, to soaking bullet sponges. Additionally, you can equip accessories that either serve as vanity, or actually grant skills such as homing missiles or powerful saber slashes. These can be moved around  and sized to your liking, even if where they operate from makes no sense.I like to talk about muisic in my reviews, but thankfully I can just say it's basically hold music across the board. Even battle music sounds too generic to give me any pump. It's just... there.Characters, voice acting... The characters are typecast, but creatively designed. Of course they just sound like squeaky kids, but the English actors do okay for what kind of characters they're playing. Each character seems to have something holding them down in "real life" but as far as I've been in, you just get bits and pieces; enough to give them some recognition of humans (save for a certain character.) But just like with most other things... uninspiring.But not much of that matters when you have a wonderful cosmetic experience for the game to tout. Many, many kits that can be bought with in-game money as the plot progresses, however they'll be basic Lv1 in stat. If you're just looking to build, there's not much of a grind. If you're in it for making good battle builds, get your straw hat and pitchfork, because anything that gives CONSIDERABLE stat gains comes from top-tier drops. Otherwise you'll probably just be putting Frankenpla together just to keep good battle stats. But thankfully, the game provides hundreds of color schemes belonging to various models, so you don't have to worry about meticulously color-coding to get something that looks like it's all one design. Or you can just go wild and color multiple sections of every part. But the creativity goes far beyond with photograph and diorama modes. Photo itself is nothing special, very bare-bones to most camera modes in modern games. But it's where diorama shines. It's a lot to explain in a review, so all I can say is it's very, very fun once you've gotten the hang of it. Posing, multiple models on screen, gunfiring blasts, etc. You can make some very dramatic scenes if you put the effort into it. There's various landscapes and backdrops, if few. But there's enough to provide a standard Gundam scenario.In conclusion, getting this is a no-brainer if you're simply looking to building the gundams and mobile suits of your wet fever-dreams. If you're in the range of 7-12 years old, you'll probably enjoy the story, otherwise it's not there to be the headliner. If you want engaging mech action, you're better off with AC6, M.A.S.S. Builder (I HIGHLY recommend,) or Daemon Ex Machina, as those are also design-based mech games. also being  If you're looking to enjoy the game all-around, I'd say wait for a sale.My score: 7/10. Note that this is based on the standard edition.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love GB3, you'd love GB4. It doesn't do much to differ from its predecessor, but it doesn't need to be, or else we'd be stuck with New Gundam breaker.For old GB3 player, there are some changes to the previous format, such as:-  I genuinely do not know why this isn't part of the tutorial either, as it is very baffling. You don't even get plastics (for upgrading levels) until the 'feature' is unlocked either. So I would suggest just blazing through the first few tutorial chapters with any gunpla you can find. -  Kinda good because you don't have to spend hours grinding while using some unwanted parts, but well...Honestly the above two options should be part of the tutorial. Better yet, don't lock out features until you get to a certain part of the story progression. Or at the very least, have the player be able to see the option but it's greyed out, just to avoid people thinking that these options weren't there. We were still  traumatized from New Gundam Breaker, and in there having to constantly change parts was the main trauma.- Option no longer have a gauge. It's one time use, and then it will go on cooldown before you can use it again, just like how EX attack worked before. It is not as big of a change as activating Head Vulcan for example will keep it shooting until it ran out anyway.- Healing is no longer an Option, it's an EX action, and now share resource gauge with your ex attack.- EX attack now share the same resource gauge that you can stock up like Musou in the Warriors series or Fighting Games. It can stack 9, maybe more, so you won't be too starved for EX actions. It does make using more powerful EX moves like Trans-Am a bit clunkier, as some only takes 1 of the ex stack, some take 3.- As highlighted, weapons are now left and right based, both ranged and melee. The light and heavy are now based on quick tapping the button or holding it. It is weird at first, but it is quite nice change, as you now essentially carry two weapons so you can switch your playstyle at whim. Some weapons like two-hander and fist can only be equipped two-handed.- Combos and breaking parts actually matter now, as you get buffs and rank from these, so no more spamming mindless things or idling. On one side, keeps the actions rolling and rolling, on the other, keeping that meter topped is kinda annoying.It's honestly a straight upgrade from GB3. Some changes here and there, which ends up streamlining and making things easier (like how you can just choose abilities as well as upgrading at the same time, letting you just mass select everything and then choose the ability you want that way). I honestly don't think there's a downgrade (except the previously mentioned hiding features).If you don't find GB3 fulfilling though, it is unlikely that you'd find GB4 more fulfilling. It doesn't have the story and atmosphere of AC6, it's gameplay is closer to the beat-em-up genre instead of a tactical mech, the weight of everything doesn't make it feel you're controlling a robot as they're very nimble, those sort. And yeah, I come in with huge bias as a huge fan of GB3, and in my opinion, the game truly delivers, and more.

_childDocuments_.review: A PROPER RETURN TO FORM! I got into Gundam Breaker when 3 was released, and was very, VERY disappointed by New Breaker. The swap to a new engine, the cookie cutter story that  somehow made the boilerplate tournament story the prior game had look sophisticated, the unnecessary changes to gameplay made to chase trends, the slapdash quality of it all- it was all enough to make us Gundam fans believe that the series had been killed. Yet, here we are, a decade after 3, and we finally have a PROPER sequel. The part hotswapping that ruined builds, the limited inventory space, the weird gauge management, it's all gone. Instead, this goes back to what worked in 3 and builds on it. Obviously, there is a far larger selection of kits to pick from, but the customization has been taken to another level by allowing us to scale *any* part to our liking, meaning the already infinite potential has been expanded twofold. The frantic, arcadey, hack n' slash joy of the original trilogy is back, meaning that the clunky awkward gameplay of New Breaker is gone. But that's probably enough gushing to convince a veteran player, what if you're coming into this entirely new?The good news is that the game is easy to pick up and play. The combat isn't really deep, but nobody comes to these games for Devil May Cry levels of complexity; it's all about the builds and artistic expression. Build, destroy, build, destroy, ad nauseam, until you get sick of it...and then inevitably come back for more. You'll be hammering away on your controller- because really, why would you try to play an action game like this on a keyboard and mouse- and delighting in the over-the-top combos as you tear through wave after wave of foes. The game has JUST enough mission styles to keep things fresh, even if it just changes HOW you go about tearing up every Mobile Suit that so much as blinks.One thing I would like to simultaneously praise and criticize is this game's online. Hallelujah, I can rip and tear alongside my friends! However, I got connected at least once during a gameplay session. It doesn't help that Bandai Namco *STILL* can't get a grip on easy to use multiplayer menus; having to hop between desks constantly just to have a friend join, or play a level together is trite annoying.  A step up from the nonsense of queuing in Gundam Battle Operation 2 but still tedious. Leave it to this company to over-complicate a process that should be as simple as inviting a friend and then playing a level together. That's literally my only gripe; the lack of X or Y Mobile Suit will be fixed in the inevitable multiple waves of DLC, and (GOD I HOPE) the internet issues will be smoothed out for a launch as global and as important for the Gundam franchise in a game like this. Because we're beyond the era of importing a game from the SEA region just to play it in English, the game comes with tons of language options baked in. It's a good thing the game is so solid and fulfilled its promises of being a true sequel, and not a misguided retool, then...that'd be a much larger audience to disappoint.If you're still reading this and you're a Gundam fan, and you're somehow not convinced yet, just buy the game already. It's worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: As it currently stands, you can beat the entire game in under 10 hours, and unlock every single part in about 20.The rest of the game is centered on grinding, which isn't a dealbreaker for me, but the fact that multiplayer is broken so badly that you can't finish most missions without desync or disconnects is troubling. The old SD gundam MMO from OGPlanet had better netcode....Until that gets fixed, I wouldn't suggest this for 99.9% of players, because the enemy AI is not even remotely a challenge, even on the highest difficulties, so there's not really much outside of showing off your suits in a lobby.Now, if you're into building, there's a decent amount of customization here. It's pretty freeform, though you're not going to be "making your own parts" or anything. Still FAR and away better than MASS BUILDER though, and it's the best gundam breaker to date in terms of sheer number of parts.But for most people? You'll drop $60, play for about 10 hours, and have everything you care about unlocking. Unless you're a pedant who wants to count grinding to level every single different part to maximum as "content", there's....not a lot here after the story mode and quests are completed, and those don't take long at all to beat, and once you've beaten them, you'll be left with the broken multiplayer as your next big "feature" and....yeah, it's very broken. Disconnects, desync issues abound, and outside of shorter missions, the chances of you running into a disconnect is VERY high. _childDocuments_.review: overall i really enjoy this game, it's a good way to kill time, though it can be incredibly formulaic. this is my first gundam breaker game, but i've heard most people prefer 3's gameplay. the missions generally come down to destroying as many mobile suits as you can as quickly as possible, and most missions don't put up much of a challenge, especially in the story. the moment-to-moment action feels very similar to a dynasty warriors gundam / gundam musou game, but with fewer enemies, less complex scenarios and objectives, and slightly more depth to the combos.the real strong point of this game is in the customization, you could easily spend hours at a time creating your perfect custom mobile suit just on an aesthetic level, let alone the time spent fine-tuning its skills and buffs to make an overpowered loadout. the depth and variety of aesthetic customization is nearly perfect, and most of my complaints with it would just be bias that more of my personal favorite obscure mobile suits aren't here (haze'n-thley II-rah when?). if i had to pick a universal negative though, it would be the menus for in-depth color, finish, and decal customization. some of the options are several menus deep, especially when you start color picking new palettes. an option to save your own preset palette would be nice, though i don't see myself using it as much because i like to pick exact color applications. the decal placement tool is really finicky and sometimes completely changes orientation, especially on curved surfaces, so most of the time i left the decals in their default placement. another feature i don't see but would absolutely love is a customization mode that is fully for cosmetic purposes and doesn't require you to currently own a piece to use it as long as you've previously acquired that mobile suit. like a gunpla dress-up with no stats involved.there are a few big negatives, namely the story and the menu UI.the menus for ... really anything are too difficult to navigate and easy to get lost looking for one specific option. some buttons and sliders in the customization seem to work inconsistently and have to be understood through trial-and-error. as i said before, some options are buried behind several sub-menus and it's not always obvious what the point of those sub-menus are. managing your items is a complete nightmare, and the filters and sorting options are obtuse, unhelpful, straight up don't do anything for certain item types, or just don't work intuitively. same goes for abilities and stats themselves. some of them are so obtuse or poorly translated that they've already become notorious ("wild dance" and "hate up" are obvious examples). others seem really redundant or just poorly explained, and there's no in-game glossary to explain what these do ... except that one item type DOES have an explanation screen that tells you what abilities do but still does a poor job at explaining them AND has unweighted randomized debuffs included so you could just get one of these items that has all downsides and no upsides. another frustration is that certain items will pop up with an "are you sure?" prompt when you want to merge them into another item, for high-rarity items, items with a paired part, items that are already saved to one of your mobile suits, or when the item you're merging them with is already max level. so in theory you could click one item and have to click through 4 "are you sure?" messages to do what you want (these prompts default to "no"). all of this combined makes leveling up and improving items incredibly tedious.the story on the other hand is really worth ignoring if you just want to burn through the missions to unlock everything. but if you choose to stick with it, you'll be met with a "quirky" band of misfits:tao: the nerd who is annoyingly pathetic and "someone wrote a gamer character"-corelin: the slightly tsundere girl who is secretly really tragic (they promise)lillin: obviously a robot but they will annoyingly drag out any and all discussion surrounding her as if they didn't let the audience in on this fact the moment she was introducedsheena: would probably be the best character if it weren't for the fact her whole story is about how difficult it is to be rich and important and how being really really rich is actually tragic"mister gunpla": someone using a fake name and avatar who pretends to be good at the game but doesn't really seem that experienced but is revealed to be someone who should be really experienced??mashima: annoying pickup artist "ladies' man" who literally can't open his mouth without saying something creepy or embarrassing, and yet everyone just accepts him and says "oh, you!" when he does his white knight shtick. literally says "m'lady" multiple timesand besides that you have tons of other annoying or bland characters that aren't worth recounting in this review. the plot itself is just "this is a video game. play video game" until the end when it gets worse. i have to also address that they use "AI" in the sense of a true artificial intelligence but conflate it with our current trend of learning algorithms that use the buzzword "AI" ... and in turn basically just feed every misconception about it while being complicit in manufacturing consent. so that's cool.on the more pet peeve-y side of things, they ask you to name your character and make your own custom profile, custom gunpla, etc, but also assume you're male and thus every single line of dialogue referring to you, the player, uses male pronouns and male nicknames. in fact they bring up the gender of characters often enough that it would just be weird and awkward if you're not male and not making a point to embody a male character for the sake of the story. in most games this is avoided by either recording different dialogue for different gender options, using non-gendered terms, or just cleverly writing dialogue that avoids that issue. but this game seems to be making a point of bringing that to the forefront as often as possible.on the other end of annoying writing is the fact that in this game you're very overpowered. you have an infinite wealth of options to break the game wide open. not only that, but you have an ability that basically no one else has in the story (it's your devil trigger). so being the pinnacle of BDE, you expect the story to acknowledge this right? maybe as an indulgence of power fantasy? nah, they just pretend that all of your comically useless teammates are precisely as powerful and valuable to your success as you are. it's to the point that despite you being in every single mission lineup by virtue of you being the player character, they still act like they have to come to a decision to choose you to be on the team for each mission. EVEN FOR THE FINAL MISSION. it's farcical. it doesn't help that the computer-controlled teammates are completely useless and don't even try to put in any work.overall, i'd say if you're already interested then you should go for it. there are ways to get your money's worth, it's probably worth waiting for a sale if you aren't dying for this game though. i'm definitely going to spend a little more time with it but it's very much a "turn your brain off" game, which is what gundam musou was for me too. more importantly i'm going to be spending a lot of time customizing gunpla and hoping that they add more of my favorite mobile suits later on

_childDocuments_.review: 1. People rarely if ever actually host or join a hosted mission, quest. 80% of the playerbase sit, idle, afk in the online lobbies. 2. Customization is the only selling point for this game. The gameplay mechanics itself was not a priority. And it shows. 3. The story is trash, it ignores 45 years worth of source material. It tries way to hard to lean more towards Gundam Build Fighters series the most. Followed by the after thought of G-Gundam. If you are expecting a Gundam game that is somehow linked or tied to the Manga / Anime. I did go through the whole story without skipping. I just don't recommend it.  The depection of each scene goes as follows. "Static busts of the actual character on a small screen next to the dialog box (Only Mouth moves)" "Gunpla's using the limited total of seven Emotes built into the game to show expressions as the story progresses" This is the experience you will have as you progress throughout the story.  Lazy. And Basic. 4. Combat lacks in a lot of fields. Firstly maps are really small. Each mission has 3 phases. You'll bump the edge or corner in each mission at least once or twice each phase.  In each phase, Gunpla spawn, you fight, more spawn, you fight, some gunpla's are treated as a mini boss.  Then you go onto the 2nd phase and repeat. 3rd phase is the same leading into a "Final Boss" of that mission.  Combat is just flat out repetitive and boring. After 60 hours you'll find the game repetitive. 5. Stats, Abilities,  lack flavor text.  There isn't any detailed explanation on what certain abilities and stats do.  Zero information that tells you what "Wild Dance" does.  For example.  The game has it's own description and take on specific abilities and stats. So even if you are used to JRPGs, or MMO's the stats in Gundam Breaker 4 lacks an in depth description.  You have to rely on 3rd party websites such as YT to get a better understanding as to what certain stats and ability effects does. And even when you get an idea it's still a bit confusing.  6. Online is basically dead. Sure at the time of writing you have 1000+ active players according to steam charts. But 80% of them are not actually playing the game. roughly 20% is actually playing the game, as in doing missions.  If you host a mission it'll be a while before someone joins. That's if someone joins. The playerbase is dropping with each passing week and that's normal.  But about 2 weeks after release hardly anyone wants to host or join a mission.  Not making this up.  So if you do get this game. Don't expect a lively active ready to play playerbase.(Overall the game is mostly negative to me.) With all things considering.  The only saving grace it has is the fact that there are over 250 model kits. And you can mix match parts customize colors, and basically cosmetically give your gunpla a makeover. That's literally it.  Gameplay is meh, Online was pretty much dead on sight. Story was the worst I've ever witnessed. Cutscenes are extremely basic and low effort. Using the ingames emote system is a total joke in itself for the game to convey each cutscene.  No I don't recommend it.  Unless if all you care about is Customizing a Gunpla.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to kitbash a gundam from a huge list of possible parts and don't really care about the quality of the rest of the game then I would recommend this game. The gundam "character creator" is really cool honestly. You can make such a huge variety of things, just check out twitter for all sorts of cool stuff. There is also a diorama system where you can pose your creations to make cool scenes. The actual gameplay outside of this unfortunately is just not very good at all.Mission design is the most immediately obvious offender. Of the 36 missions there are 2 minor variations otherwise they all play out the exact same. Load into a map and kill all or most enemies (wave 1), load into the next map and kill all or most enemies (wave 2), load into the last map and kill either a boss wave (1-3 enemies with more health) or a giant gundam. 33/36 missions follow this exact structure. The 3 missions that don't just have more/less waves before the boss wave.As well as story missions there are "quest missions" which as far as I can tell are just the same as story missions but without cutscenes. Bounty missions which are just the 3 enemy boss waves on their own. Survival mode which I didn't play because by the time I unlocked it I just didn't care anymore.Challenge is nonexistent. Enemy AI doesn't seem to do much other than stand around occasionally attacking, blocking or dashing. Enemies with more than one health bar or bosses will attack more often but don't seem to be any more intelligent. Giant bosses present some minor difficulty in that attacking the same part gives diminishing rewards and the targeting system is very awkward but you will never die to them so it just makes them take a bit longer to kill. I enjoyed switching up my gundam design at first but it became obvious that it didn't really matter what I was bringing in There are multiple difficulty settings but all they do is increase the level of enemies. All this does is drag mission length out even more.The story and characters are very generic and not really worth discussing.I would like to believe it's possible to make a game with a character creator this good with good gameplay but this isn't it. I hope we get one in the future.

GB4 is at least second place in the line and coming from New Gundam Breaker, this is still a big step up. After 10 years from GB3, it is a fresh take on the game, however after 60 hours and almost max out achievement, I think ill go back to GB3 on my PS4 for the thrilling combat and more user friendly UI. The biggest let down of this game is the clunkiness of its UI. I am a very strong Gundam fan and it breaks my heart to actually complete the game, max out all the stats in my custom Gunpla 20 hours into the game. I itch for more and maybe in the future they will update the game for more content but I highly doubt it will be free. I paid for full price on this game and more so yes I had high expectation. I was hoping this game was made with pure love from the developers based from their fan that have been keeping GB3 ALIVE.I wish this can be a love letter to the fan. I really do, but in the end, there is a lot of quality control that they actually would look into. All and all it is still an awesome game to play. Easy to get into and fall in love with especially if you never played GB3. For me, after all this, Im still sticking to GB3 as the greatest Gundam Breaker game ever made.
