_childDocuments_.review: I would warn you against purchasing this game because it requires a Microsoft account to play and this includes the offline single player mode. I had been looking at this game for quite some time and finally decided to go ahead and purchase it. I assumed the Microsoft account would be for the online or multiplayer aspects of the game and never imagined that your access to this game is entirely dependent on access to this Microsoft account. I created a character, did the tutorial and a few missions before deciding I would come back to it later. When I came back the next day to play it, I found that my access to the game had been entirely revoked and that Microsoft was claiming I had done something illegal / suspicious and therefore my account had been suspended. Apparently just playing this game is suspicious to them.What was suspicious to me, was that Micorsoft wanted me to give them my cell phone number and in exchange, the ban on my account would be lifted. Let's assume I had done something suspicious or otherwise illegal as they claim, if so, why would simply giving them my cell phone number make whatever it was I had done okay again?While it is possible that this message is some form of generic lock / error that you get -- it's troubling that within 48 hours of purchasing the game, I found my ability to play it ENTIRELY blocked, even the offline single player and due to the wording of the it, it basically gives Microsoft a free pass to suspend your access to this game at any time, for any reason.This means that even though you paid VALVE and Mojang for this game, you do not own it and there is no guarantee you will be able to retain access to it because Mojang has chosen to involve Microsoft as a third party.I contacted Mojang and attempted to talk this out with them but their rep basically refused to assist me at all and was deadset on shifting the blame onto Microsoft to spite the fact that it is their game, and offering support is their responsibility. If you involve a third party in your business and that third party negatively impacts your interactions with your customers, it is absolutely your job to handle that problem, it is not the customer's. Upon my telling the rep that, he responded by blocking my ticket and refusing to respond any further.I attempted to contact Microsoft to obtain more information about this situation as well but found that to be impossible to do so, and rightfully so, it's not their job to deal with this, this isn't their game. Microsoft does own Mojang Studios but that does not make them responsible for handling issues concerning access to the game.After discussing this with VALVE over the course of a few days, VALVE agreed to issue a refund to spite my having played this for longer than 2 hours, so I guess the take-away from all of this is at least VALVE was willing to assume some responsibility for this situation because it certainly didn't look like it was possible to get Mojang to due to their rep's attitude.In the end this was all very disappointing to me because from what I did play, the game seems great and I was likely going to enjoy it but I am not okay with spending money on a game that could be taken away from me by a third party at any time with or without reason and with no way to discuss or appeal it.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay itself is  fun enough if repetitive. I just wanted something simple to play while I listened to podcasts. But I was compelled to leave my first review ever because of the horrendous DRM applied to this game. -you need to login with your microsoft account to play. Which is fine except for that it doesn't seem to always remember your credentials, so you need to relogin often. And it makes it so you can never play truly offline.-say you switch between steam deck and PC. Every time you play on one device, when you finish you need to upload your character, then download it on the other device to play there. Why is this necessary???-on steam deck, I often need to restart the game multiple times to actually get to the game. Sometimes a white rectangle will show instead of the login box. So I restart. Sometimes I can't access the menu to download my previous save, so I need to restart.Plus some gameplay issues:- if you enchant something, you can't enchantment without getting rid of the weapon entirely-IMPORTANT: you can't ever truly pause the game, even in "offline" (but not actually offline, you still need to login) mode. Bring up the menu, you can still get attacked and killed by mobs. Some of the maps I've played can take at least 45 minutes to complete. Very weird choice.After the 5th time dealing with the upload/download thing, I got tired and decided to stop entirely. It can be fun, but not fun enough to deal with that.Microsoft--if you're not going to take advantage of the cloud-save features that dang near every other steam game uses, including indie games with a single developer, don't put it here. I don't know much about game development or steam integration but I have to imagine your employees are capable of figuring it out, clearly this is a weird business decision. Do better or don't use steam.

Unfortunately, the second I started the game on the Squid Coast (the tutorial level); the achievements started to come in, all 104 of them! I was stunned and a bit upset to be perfectly honest.Apparently when you have your Xbox/Microsoft account linked with Steam, this happens because it has crossplay enabled and saves everything you’ve previously done in the game (this is what I’ve heard from a handful of people who described it as a bug that shouldn’t have happened but I haven’t found any further info, so I can’t 100% confirm).Upon further inspection, I was even able to use my old saves/characters. I am all for crossplay but I don’t think saves and  achievements should carry over.I’m still having a great time replaying the game, already sunk a few hours into it and will probably put many more in over the years but as someone who enjoys achievement hunting, this is a shame. _childDocuments_.review: If you want a varied and mature dungeon crawler, I strongly advise against Minecraft Dungeons.As Minecraft, the game really grabbed me at first. The controls are simple and the gameplay is clear. After the first levels of the campaign, in which I searched every corner for secrets as usual, I realized that the game lacked depth for my taste. You don't really have to look for hidden boxes. You stumble over them on the way through repetitive level design and always the same hordes of enemies.The items in the game come with randomly generated perks, which offer at least a touch of variety when looting the different dungeons. However, since the items also result in the entirety of the character development, this is hardly sufficient. Leveling is therefore monotonous and doesn't exactly invite you to play the game again.With the right combination of items you can assign yourself to a certain class, which in multiplayer makes sense here and there from the gameplay, however, it is simply worth equipping the best possible items.The "campaign" itself also leaves a lot to be desired. These wishes are partly fulfilled with the DLCs, but could have been included in the main game.The monotony of the opponents can also be seen in the bosses. I can count them on one hand, so I'm not really impressed.If the flattened gameplay wasn't enough, the controls are also mouse milking. A controller may help, but if you play with a mouse and keyboard, you can expect something. You navigate by clicking through the world, but the pathing is so horrible that the character keeps running in unwanted directions or moving back and forth very quickly on the spot. Positioning yourself to jump onto a platform, for example, is an ordeal in itself, as you can only jump in the direction of travel.If you run under a bridge or a tunnel, the game sees this as pathable terrain and moves the character in a direction unknown to the player.I was too stingy and had to play through the game to sleep with the feeling of having thrown money out of the window. But the longer I played, the more the little things just mentioned got on my nerves. Maybe I'm just too old for a game obviously intended for a younger audience.It just wasn't worth the 40€ to me.- Graphic          8/10- sound             5/10- fun                  3/10- Gameplay       4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Minecraft Dungeons takes the beloved blocky world of Minecraft and combines it with classic dungeon-crawling action, resulting in an accessible and fun adventure for players of all ages. Here are the key points of the game:1. GameplayThe game offers a simplified hack-and-slash experience, with players delving into various dungeons to fight enemies, gather loot, and complete objectives. While it doesn’t have the depth of more complex action RPGs like Diablo, Minecraft Dungeons nails its core mechanics, making it approachable for beginners and casual gamers.Combat is fast-paced, easy to pick up, and satisfying. With a variety of weapons, armor, and artifacts to collect, you can customize your character’s playstyle, whether you prefer ranged attacks, melee combat, or using magic-like abilities.2. Art and VisualsThe game stays true to the Minecraft aesthetic, featuring the same blocky graphics and familiar mobs. The art style is colorful and charming, giving the game a unique, recognizable look, especially when combined with the action-packed environments of dungeons, castles, and lush landscapes.3. Multiplayer and Co-opMinecraft Dungeons shines in co-op mode, supporting up to four players, either locally or online. Teaming up with friends enhances the game’s fun, as you strategize to overcome waves of enemies and challenging bosses together. It’s a great way to bond over a lighthearted yet engaging game.4. ReplayabilityOne of the standout features is the randomly generated dungeons. No two playthroughs are exactly alike, with different layouts and loot drops each time. Additionally, higher difficulty modes provide more challenging gameplay for those looking for a tougher experience and better rewards.5. DownsidesFor seasoned RPG players, the game might feel too simple or repetitive after a while. The lack of a deep skill tree or complex character progression means there’s limited room for advanced strategies. However, this simplicity is also a strength for casual players or families looking for an easy-to-play game.6. Expansions and DLCThe game offers various DLC expansions that add new biomes, levels, and enemies, extending the lifespan of the game and providing fresh content for returning players.ConclusionMinecraft Dungeons is a fun, family-friendly dungeon crawler that keeps things light and easy without sacrificing enjoyment. It’s perfect for casual gamers, Minecraft fans, and those looking to enjoy a co-op experience. While it may not satisfy hardcore RPG fans looking for depth, it offers hours of entertainment in the Minecraft universe.If you're looking for a cooperative adventure with plenty of charm and Minecraft flair, Minecraft Dungeons is worth a try!

_childDocuments_.review: I played Minecraft Dungeons at launch on PC via the MSFT Store. I loved the game then and I love the game now. It is a simple, easier take on the Diablo formula that is fun and refreshing while leaning on the popularity/nostalgia of the Minecraft franchise. Who would have guessed that one of the most popular games of all time that is based around player-driven adventure and narrative would lend itself well to another title that is based in that infinite world of storytelling and adventure? The game is not particularly challenging while providing constant dopamine hits in the form of an ever-steady stream of better and better loot. The game caters to many different playstyles and all around is mechanically sound. The game is graphically impressive for an Xbox Studios title, and the sound design is equally pleasing. I've had many, MANY issues with random crashes and being unable to play with friends, but the game is worth the hassle. I've been informed by child owners that the game is a good gateway for introducing more mechanically complex titles to your little gamers. Either way, I've had fun with this and you likely will too if you like Diablo or Torchlight.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is no longer being updated. HOWEVER, it's still pretty fun.SINGLEPLAYERThe entire game is fun, and scales well to your skills. If one player is significantly further ahead than others, it makes the game boring for them (too easy enemies) and boring for everyone else (too tough enemies and the other players pick them off before you can even get there).INSTEAD, I would recommend that all multiplayer be done via the Tower game instead. Every player starts at the same level, and you work co-op towards getting to the end of the tower. This is the only truly equal, fair, and fun way to do multiplayer on Minecraft Dungeons. It has a few difficulty levels, so this also scales a bit based on player skill level.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming, yet very simple entry in the “Diablo”-like genre. Instead of classes your character build it completely reliant on the equipment you use. So there is no wrong skilling or hard decisions to be made, because everything can be changed with a few mouse clicks. There is also a simple upgrade system for weapons. For every level you gain, you get a gem that can be used to unlock skills in your gear. Gear can be dismantled anytime to regain all spent gems, so there is no wrongdoing here either. While simple, it still offers plenty of possibilities to form a character of your liking. The classic stereotypes like mages, summoners or barbarians can be put together with the right equipment. There are also some nice synergies between some equipment to make it even more efficient.Despite its simplicity and a shallow hit feedback from enemies, I had quite some fun with Minecraft Dungeons. I couldn’t play it for hours without end, but for shorter sessions it is a nice gap filler. I recommend the complete package with all the DLC because it adds a lot of levels and variety to the mix. The game is rather short otherwise, but the open ended leveling process, highly scalable missions and seasons passes - that are not time-gated! - will give plenty of playtime if you are into grinding stuff out. Just don’t expect a complex beast like Path of Exile or Grim Dawn that offers plenty of replayability and more interesting stuff to experiment with.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good approximation of Diablo gameplay, but without the compelling story and immersive aesthetic.The problem with that is that it lays bare the fact that Diablo gameplay, without anything on top of it, is mostly a gambling game. Or, given a long enough time period, a game where you grind a TON until you get the items that you want and maximize your build. There's no skill tree so all you're really doing is repetitively playing levels over and over, and rolling for items.There's an optional randomized mode called the Tower where it plays like a Roguelite (also a highly gamble-centric genre, imo). Enter a floor. Fight monsters. Pick a reward. Move to next floor. Rinse and repeat. Every few floors, you get a merchant or a boss fight. At the end, you get a high-level item that you can give your character for the actual game.If you happen to be okay with that, and you also like and are familiar with the Minecraft universe, the game is also pretty buggy. I kept getting glitched out of a boss arena, or somehow getting trapped between colliders or something and dying. The pathing for the character is also quite buggy. If you're using a mouse and you click on the ground that's just around a small corner, it often (but not always) just runs against a wall or a tiny corner block instead of around it, which is really frustrating in the middle of a dangerous fight.The game is divided into levels rather than one contiguous world. And each level is really long. Progression requires you to finish an entire level in one sitting, which would've been okay on a Switch if you could pause it and pick it up again later. But on PC, it's really rough and tiring. You can leave the level and return to your home base any time you want, but a lot of the progression and rewards require you to finish levels.The base game without the DLC is probably as long as Act 1 in Diablo. So "finishing" it makes you go to the next difficulty level. (similar to finishing Diablo on Normal and then letting you play the game all over again but all the numbers are bigger) Here, it sort of feels like you're playing Act 1, then playing Act 1 again. The second difficulty (called Adventure) has really spiky damage and is not fun at all to play.The DLC is kind of weird and even buggier than the base game.References to the main Minecraft game aside, the sound design isn't particularly great or satisfying. The music also feels odd.The game isn't all bad. It has a lot of good mechanics and contributes accommodating ideas that make the genre more accessible to less hardcore players. It's also a nice visual adaptation of the Minecraft aesthetic.But all the bad parts make me want to not recommend the game. I don't want anyone, certainly not minecraft kids, to psychologically become gambling fiends because they played a pared-down Diablo game with no substance.

_childDocuments_.review: After about 45 minutes with the game, I had enough time to experience the majority of what the game had to offer.Is it a good Diablo-like? Honestly, no. Not many choices to help make your hero unique.Is it an innovative game? No; I think the developers missed an opportunity here. This is a MINECRAFT game; you could have made BUILDING an integrated part of the experience! For example, in order to cross to the next area, you have to make a bridge made of wood. You can have your player do that by CRAFTING an axe, chopping trees in enemy-infested zones and building the bridge! They could have added player-made strongholds where players could place mobs and built forts/castles that other players/friends could invade. Even while a player is offline, another player could download the stronghold and invade it.They could have added a map editor where you could make your own custom levels. Or integrate a Minecraft-like experience where you could customize your camp to your liking. Long story short, there is nothing Minecraft about the game other than the aesthetic.Ah, look at the time. I have spent much of my time talking about what could have been.Now let me tell you why I recommend this title:This is a great game for children who have never played an ARPG dungeon crawler before. I think this game would feel complex to younger audiences as there are some strategies to taking down certain opponents. To an adult over the age of 18, I think there are better titles out there for the same price or less (Diablo 3, Path of Exile, Diablo 2 Ressurected, Warhammer Chaosbane, etc).Why do I still play this game?I got this game to pretty much just rack up gamer points for my Xbox profile through achievements. Once I 100% this game, I'm pretty much deleting it because the experience is not novel enough for me.

_childDocuments_.review: By the time I'm writing this review I just finished the main quest (defeated the Arch-Illager and completed all the secret area missions on mainland)I think the game experience overall is solid but in my opinion it is lacking in some key areas with some very needed polish.The first thing I noticed while playing is the lack of a proper "minimap", in this game, you have two options for looking at the map of your current mission, you can either get a pause menu map or a transparent version which appears centered on the screen. While both of these options are usable, I'm kind of sad that for the 16 hours I spent so far I was focused on this transparent map most of the time, I would have loved a square minimap to toggle in a corner rather than this option, which would have let me look at the game more, taking only occasional glances at the minimap. As for the fullscreen map, please display the level in full, you only get a tad bit more vision over the level than the transparent minimap which makes it completely redundant, the only useful info there is the secret/chest count on the bottom left corner.The second thing I was annoyed about is the enemy balancing, and sometimes the AI, though I think this is due to my poor experience with dungeon crawlers.I found that some enemy types are way harder to defeat (and not in a challenging way, in an annoying way), for instance, the spear and mace enemies on whom you just cannot land any hits sometimes, without getting pounded yourself anyway, I just think their attack delay could use some work, in the meantime they remain my main source of arrow spending (and depletion)About Redstone Golems, something needs to be done for the poor things, it's very hard to land significant damage on their walking phase, because their punch has almost no significant cooldown, you have to wait for them to charge, and even then doing good damage there is difficult, to reliably defeat them I abused a bug in their AI that lets you spam hit them on their walking phase without getting punched (their detection area seems to be faulty close to their center).As a final note on enemies, I think they sometimes suffer from bad placement (thinking about how swarms of armored vindicators were placed ON the landing zone of pistons in the final mission), although this is a very minor issue, you just have to be careful when jumping/traveling to an area you couldn't observe beforehand.I like this game, because I enjoy the gameplay dungeon crawlers provide and Minecraft as a whole, but I am kind of disappointed from the lack of polish, which isn't something I expected coming from Mojang Studios. Minecraft Dungeons still has some way to go before being quite right and I hope it'll be brought there eventually.

_childDocuments_.review: Minecraft Dungeons manages to blend the beloved universe of Minecraft with the thrills of a dungeon crawler, creating a quirky and enjoyable experience for players of all ages.From the outset, the game's hack-and-slash mechanics and loot-collecting antics are easy to grasp. The blocky foes and procedurally generated dungeons keep things interesting, maintaining the iconic Minecraft aesthetic while adding a touch of adventure.What truly sets Minecraft Dungeons apart is its cooperative play. The game transitions from a solo endeavor to a chaotic team effort with friends, where the shared joy of discovering loot or accidentally sabotaging each other adds an extra layer of entertainment. It's a reminder that sometimes, blocky adventures are better when experienced together.While the initial dungeon-crawling excitement is palpable, the game can start feeling a tad repetitive after a while. However, fear not, as the multiplayer aspect significantly alleviates this issue. The camaraderie of cooperative play keeps the experience engaging, even if the core gameplay loop remains somewhat familiar.In the grand scheme of things, Minecraft Dungeons may not redefine the dungeon-crawling genre, but it doesn't need to. It offers a lighthearted and entertaining experience that's perfect for casual gaming sessions with friends. So, grab your blocky gear, team up with pals, and embark on a pixelated adventure – because sometimes, the joy is in the journey, not just the loot.

(The chance of said item being usable being 1%...) For example I spent 20 minutes wandering through the first nether level exploring all the little nooks just to get 2 common weapons from mobs drops(I found NOTHING on the side paths) I immediately trashed. Like wow I really want to go see what garbage I can find on the next mission!- At first combat seems cool with the rolling mechanic but because someone with a dent in their head gave it a cool down combat boils down to 2 things. _childDocuments_.review: First off I'd like to mention that this is not me saying the game is bad. The game is actually really good for what it tries to bring, and I’ve played quite a bit of it before it came to Steam. It's a fun introduction to the dungeon crawler genre, and a fitting introduction if you're a kid but as a parent find the already existing games too violent to play. In that regard, go ahead and play the game, I'd love to give it a positive review from that perspective. I'm however judging it from the fact that it's also advertised as a dungeon crawler player's introduction to Minecraft, judging by the words "inspired by classic dungeon crawlers... and set in the Minecraft universe!", rather than the other way around. So as a whole, this is a neutral review. I like the game from a Minecraft player's perspective, but from a Dungeon Crawler player's perspective it could use some great improvements.I will touch on a few things, nothing related to the lore or spoilers or anything. Just details that I feel is worth mentioning. I will start with the major ones, and then work down to the more minor stuff at the end. Some stuff could be classified as irrelevant to some people, although I feel others might feel otherwise. I'm still mentioning them as it's what I noticed from playing, and it's what I feel should be improved should anything change in the game. There's also other stuff mentioned in other reviews that I haven't encountered so I won't touch on those, but they are also valid aswell.The loot system itself is great, don't get me wrong. I feel they've hit the perfect balance when it comes to the amount of stuff. It's somewhat too few drops coming from Dungeon Crawling, but again, this is an introduction for Minecraft players, so it's fine. What I do feel needs adressing though is that when choosing a mission, you get to choose a difficulty, and by doing so the recommended level goes up. This allows you to play against higher level mobs than your own. This is common in games like Diablo III which has greater rifts where you get way better loot the higher level you go. I expected somewhat of a similar thing in Minecraft Dungeons, but I feel I was mistaken. I'm power level 15, and played against power level 22 mobs, however only one drop out of 16 drops that mission was power level 22. Rest was around my own power level. I feel this isn't very encouraging as you only make it difficult but for no reward. I feel higher difficulty should give a higher reward, but as it stands at the moment, that is not the case.This in itself is a minor detail, but its impact becomes a huge deal if done poorly, which I feel it is. Movement should be dependent on the path I'm trying to take, not the obstacle I'm clicking on. If I click on a floor tile up to the left on my screen, I want my character to move up to the left on my screen. If there happens to be an overhang in the terrain that occludes the path, it doesn't change the direction I want to go, I haven't moved my mouse, and even if I had, I can't even get there to begin with, so stop trying to go there and keep on moving up to the left.This gets even more tilting when you can interact behind things. I made a YouTube video about this where in it I showed how slimes below a bridge could completely ruin your day by being clickable even if they're outside of your reach, and end up stopping your character completely. I was running away from 1 creeper and one tanky hard hitting guy I forgot the name of, running across a bridge, only to have my character stop because there was a slime stuck below a bridge that I couldn't see but now apparently was clicking. I had not moved my mouse, the moving view had put the slime below my cursor, and I was now caught up by the creeper, instantly killing me with the explosion. I'm sure clicking on an enemy should try melee it, but not if it's unreachanble and I'm clicking directly on reachable ground itself, then I should try to move there.I feel the health pot is a heavy time waster. It's 45 seconds last time I checked, and supposedly still is. I feel it should be reduced to 30 seconds, or at least give some form of natural regeneration or sped up cooldown when not being engaged in combat for X amount of seconds. It happens when pushing difficulty that I accidentally miss a roll and get hard hit to 1hp right after a heal and have to retreat, and stand afk for 45 seconds waiting for the heal cooldown to run out. This is a complete waste of time, and an uneccesary design choice. I know shorter cooldown is ruining the challenge, but standing afk for 45 seconds without being chased isn't a challenge, it's a stupid waste of time.The roll has 2 main issues. First how to choose direction, and then the force. There's also the fact that rolling gives you slowness for about a second after using it, but that to me feels like a design choice that should stay, as it's not meant to be played like for example Wolcen where you just roll everywhere to speed up travel time. This is a slow paced Dungeon Crawler, and I honestly respect the slowness after a roll, it's a nice touch.I'm speaking more about how you use it and some flaws with its implementation. Firstly there's the way you choose direction. Literally everything in the game is based on where you aim your mouse cursor. Abilities, movement, TNT block etc. The roll however is based on where your character model is facing, and having the wobbly movement when traversing block corners, this can cause serious damage if you were to roll off a ledge accidentally, or you need to switch direction away from mobs and roll, in which you first need to move mouse away from mobs, click once to turn around, and then roll. You can't just move your mouse and roll. This is also the only feature in the game that I can think of that works from your player model's facing direction.Then there's the way and force of which you roll. While as I've mentioned this is sort of a slow paced game, I do feel not being able to roll through mobs is a bit too far of a restriction. I feel being able to roll through mobs should be a good change, especially if you were to keep the way you currently pick roll direction, as that's currently making this limitation even heavier. There's also the corner funkyness I mentioned, if you roll into a dip, your roll stops, and you sometimes can't roll up a block. It's kind of tedious at times when fighting in areas with lots of bumpy snow layers, having your roll rejected because you were standing in a 2 pixel deep hole of snow layers.I do, yes, I do think this game is well made. I just feel these things come up too often, and being sort of aimed toward actual Dungeon Crawler community a fair bit, I feel these things need to be mentioned, and not just upvoting the game because it has the name "Minecraft" in it which I feel is what a lot of reviews here are about. I do like the game though, but I feel a lot has to be done before I will actively talk about this game with other people as a Dungeon Crawler inspired game, rather than a Minecraft inspired game.

_childDocuments_.review: Newcomer to this game, as of Sept. 17th. TL;DR, I think this game is super fun and I can thank my nephew for getting me into it -- and this game is likely going to branch me into picking up Diablo after so long of just... not.  Also, early-game "pro tip" the Firework artifact is OP as hell when paired with the Ancient Bow weapon, with the Dynamo enchantment (fully stacked to 20) and the Infinity enchantment, while wearing Hunter armor; and it's also stupidly efficient to use the Dynamo skill (fully stacked to 20) + Artifact Synergy on the Soul Knife or Glaive weapons (in tandem with the Fi+AnBo+Dy+In combo just mentioned) against any boss. You'll pump out ridiculous damage. For the deets. A few days ago I saw my nephew playing this on his Switch, just at a glance. Immediately recognized Minecraft. Looked at reviews, they're all from a year ago and say the game is "super easy" and "really short; you can beat it within 4 hours". I ask to borrow the game for my Switch at home, nephew agrees. I really like it, so I buy it on Steam (coincidentally it released today). I discover the Cloud Save function, and it makes my day that I can carry over the progress made on my Switch to my PC, and vice-versa at will. Man, I wish more games that exist on both platforms supported this feature [looking at you, Borderlands].Might be because the DLC or other adjustments since weren't out at the time, but those takes are really incorrect, in my experience.  Now, GRANTED, I do intentionally play 2 levels higher than the recommended for my current gear level, so I do make the game harder at a base level, but even at the recommended level, or even on really low levels where I'm supposed to be overpowered, it can still be difficult. Enemies can, and will, swarm you. If you pick up the Raider Banners, they add negative modifiers that can take even an "Average Difficulty, Level 1" run and make it feel like you on "Average Difficulty, Level 7" (at the trade-off of apparently giving you more and more of a chance to get an additional reward item on mission completion-- and this is not even taking into account the banners on the higher Levels. It can be BRUTAL. In terms on length, as of this review, I'm 9 hours in and not even halfway through the "main story" of taking down the Arch-Illager. Mainly because I'm being a "completionist" about it and getting all the Chests, Secret Missions, Daily Missions, and Ender Eyes-- but also the fact that these dungeon maps are MASSIVE (or so I perceive them to be, as I don't have much experience with dungeon crawlers, like Diablo). An easy, casual run can take maybe 15 minutes or so, while my average run (again, on higher-than-recommended Levels + Banners adding realtime modifiers and harder difficulty) on a dungeon can take up to 45 minutes; and it's not even a guarantee I'll succeed in beating it. Half the time I don't win, and I even take advantage of different item loadouts and cheesing methods mid-combat when I can. And there's still like 6 DLCs worth of content to go through after the main bit across two other "world maps". I can see my hour tally for this game going up to nearly 200 hours, easy. And it's gonna be a blast getting there. I'm currently Level 36.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to play this game a ridiculous amount on my switch, all the way through including the DLCs in both Default and Adventure and after having not played it in a good while, my friend gifted me the steam version to play together. Even after having to adjust to the game again I still love this game. It plays like Diablo but its very different in its execution which I can appreciate. small things like Chests just not being in alternate pathways, dodging slowing you down until your next dodge is recharged, the lock on being sticky dragged the game down for some of my friends. They're just annoyances for me, but they can be turn offs for others.Combat is very enjoyable, there are very few movesets I actually dislike, and all the weapons feel very unique. Artifacts are very powerful and all offer a unique purpose making combat very flexible and fun.Most maps are surprisingly open, with secret paths and entryways in each level, letting people like me who want to explore the entire map get plenty of enjoyment doing so. A certain  does get  open tho, requiring multiple levels of time to explore, you are rewarded for your time however.The game can get difficult if your not running a very powerful build especially on the harder difficulties, but you can get by running something unorthodox. Some things do unfortunately fall off though, like Summons.There are no stats or spells of any kind, your build is entirely based on your equipment. I love this system much more than a stat system, allowing swapping a build easily without making a new character and making theory-crafting a build much easierThis game looks absolutely phenomenal. The post processing is just right, not being over abundant to keep its style intact, but also making the game prettier than Minecraft could ever wish to be. The builds for the stages look amazing too, with diverse sets of blocks and new blocks to make transitions from dirt to stone bricks look prettier than ever. I thought I was crazy being really inspired by some of the structures built in this game, but even my friend has gotten ideas for builds from this game too.All the DLCs are amazing, with Flames of the Nether and Hidden Depths being my absolute favorites. They all add new stages and new Of course, this being a (fairly) modern game, it has a ✨Battle Pass✨, but its one of the best in my opinion. Its a bit of a grind, but the tracks aren't time limited, they can be completed well after the season ends giving you ample time to get it done even if your behind. the premium track is only 4$, far cheaper than most games with a battle pass and includes particle effects for killing mobs, healing and teleporting to other players. It has pets, skins and capes to get too. The base game is kinda pricey for how short it is, being 20$, but the DLC is super cheap for just how much they add. _childDocuments_.review: I am an ARPG fan and a Minecraft fan.  This game ultimately provides an extremely simplified and streamlined approach to the ARPG formula and has a great sense of progression, finding foreign types of weapons and increasing in power frequently enough that you can see your power climb in real time.  You go from dispatching enemies one by one relatively easily, on to slightly more challenging encounters where you may actually get hit, finally on to being absolutely explosive, chaining together tons of kills while avoiding the screen being 50% on fire and it is really satisfying to mash through the enemies, especially with a buddy.With no DLC installed I don't feel like I'm missing out during the base game, I don't feel like I have to spend any money on season passes, and I don't feel like the game is pushing me to do anything that I don't want to do in the game.  The 30 floor roguelite mode is fun, the main campaign stages have frequently varied environments and enemies, and the bonus areas can be relatively interesting or challenging.Playing with a friend locally is as easy as cloning your main character and then hopping in for a few hours, no investment required and the controller operates more or less as well as the keyboard and mouse (just turn the deadzone up on the right stick for more accurate rolling).Super charmed by how well crafted this game is.  Clearly the creators have a love for ARPGs and Minecraft and understand both how to create a product that would engage children without overwhelming them and engage adults with a sense of progression streamlined enough to reward you for playing with new ideas being offered to you as you dispatch wave after wave of monsters.

This is what you play if you want to have a few hours of fun without the existential dread of not having a properly specced out toon. That said, armour and weapons do range from basic to unique, each with different skills attached. You can enchant them further to make them more epic, so there is a light and friendly build-craft system available.The environments are rich, colourful, and massive. The sounds are cute, and the music, as with Minecraft, is excellent. The story itself too, is cute, even though there is not a lot of lore involved in the game, but this is very Minecraft, as it builds upon an imagined lore.I thoroughly enjoy Minecraft Dungeons. 10/10 would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I've already accumulated a decent amount of playtime on the Microsoft-store version and I can safely say that the steam version is better.While the game itself is exactly the same, the reason the steam version is better is because, among other things such as steam-overlay, it allows you to apply game boosters with other programs like MSI or Razer. You can't do that with the MS-store version because Microsoft hides their files in a place you can't (legally) access and neither can most other programs, atleast not without trickery.Enhancing overall performance and smoothness of the game can certainly help with the overall enjoyment for lower-end systems. And although framerate was never an issue for me I can definitely still tell a difference in terms of loading times, it feels great.In case you also played the MS-store version before and wonder if your save file will transfer to this version; the answer is yes. To make absolutely sure you can also just upload your character to the cloud and download it again on the steam version should the transfer not happen automatically.As for game deals I highly recommend purchasing the Ultimate Edition as it offers about 4-5 times the amount of content the base game offers for just double the price.You don't need to be a fan of Minecraft to be able to enjoy this game as they have little in common aside from artstyle and certain item/mob sprites and names. If you like ARPGs I recommend you give this one a shot as it offers a nice amount of character customizability and, hence, playstyles despite not being nearly as flashed out as games like Diablo or Path of Exile.

_childDocuments_.review: Minecraft Dungeons is one of the only hit spinoff games set in the Minecraft universe. It's visually stunning and offers a fresh take on the franchise. While the gameplay is simple and fun, it can get repetitive after a while. The game's lifespan was short, but its extra content is affordable and doesn't pressure you with time-limited content. It would've been cool to have mod support through Steam Workshop to extend the game's life. Even though the Mojang sunsetted Minecraft Dungeons, it's understandable that all good things must come to an end. Hopefully, we'll see a sequel in the future when there is more content in Minecraft. Overall, it's pretty fun for a few hours and it's on game pass so that's a plus.

_childDocuments_.review: Before you say I didn't play the game that much, most of my hours are on the Xbox/MC Launcher version of Dungeons, not on Steam with nearly 200+.I really want to give this a positive review but Mojang really dropped the ball with this game and I can only hope Minecraft Legends doesn't suffer the same fate as Minecraft Dungeons and Earth did via slow burn or abrupt uncontrollable circumstance and not wanting to stick out the storm.The main reason I chose negative is that it took almost 2 years to get basic features like a simple storage system/chest to be added which meant we had to choose what to keep.This compounds with the event/seasonal exclusive weapons/gear you could get (which at the time before they got added to the Tower in that update) were objectively worse in power level so they were just a status symbol to show off to the tiny playerbase that you were there that was useless on the higher tier apocalypse difficulties. Not helping is that one of them being the corrupted pumpkin is still unobtainable because they didn't add artifacts to the tower despite their being in the steam and MC feedback site. Many request for QOL features fell on deaf ears for cutesy corp speak and additions that add little or are cosmetic instead of addressing problems like needless bloat and clutter (such as consolidating the reskinned gear into being a toggle instead of separate items entirely being one example of a missed opportunity).The big elephant in the room is the one they neglected and gave a outright no to when asked to add; modding support or at least Steam workshop support.Half the fun of being on Steam is the workshop and the fact they opted out of allowing you to mod more easily and safely by downloading mods through the workshop which is built in and instead just said no and offered no way speaks volumes to their attitude on modding outside of the Java edition which I'm convinced they only keep around to keep the Java devs employed and quell discourse because I'm sure they'd want Minecoin integration similar to what they did with Legends.Workshop/modding support could have added a infinite content and extended the life of dungeons but instead Mojang opted to release a season pass system for this game, only released 3, then missed not only the winter event, but the games anniversary, didn't say or make a blog post about its birthday, then proceed to boast their player numbers of 25+M players in dungeons despite most of those being gamepass buyers who tried it and NOT concurrent players who return and then cut support/sunsetted the game about a week ago.No goodbye, no fanfare, no final event, no cosmetic crossover/carryover for what you bought in MC Dungeons from the seasons passes/challenges like with Minecraft earth to keep as keepsakes like emotes, capes, or pets, no more events; its finished, over. The bare minimum they're doing now is just having a tower level be procedural generated off of present pre-sets every week while keeping purchase servers up for your cosmetics; that's it.TLDR; If you're thinking of buying this game for long term content or playing with friends, don't bother. The games officially over/discontinued and no more DLC or content is being made/updated. They did quite a poor job of marketing this game as well as their other Minecraft spinoffs or published games such as Minecraft Story mode, Earth, Scrolls(Callers Bane), Cobalt, and now Legends.Don't bother getting this game unless you REALLY like dungeon crawlers and even then there's much better than this game that are actually actively being updated. Legends sadly might follow the same fate as Dungeons if Mojang's actions with their past games are repeated.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the ultimate edition fairly recently. I had played the game previously on Xbox game-pass, and had a decent amount of fun. But now that I've payed the $40 for the included DLCs, I seriously would not recommend this game.The whole point of the game is combat, and leveling up your gear. The game fundamentally fails at this on numerous levels. The gear you obtain is almost immediately outclassed by randomly dropped loot from mobs, so there is no real incentive to upgrade the gear you have. Emeralds are another issue entirely. You spend most of the missions navigating horribly structured levels (I will go into detail later) for your only reward, if any at all, to be a couple emeralds which you can't spend outside of upgrading your gear (Which I've already explained is pointless.)The level design is abhorrent. I often get lost trying to figure out where I'm supposed to be going, and this isn't helped by the fact that the only support the game offers (An almost invisible marker which is frequently covered by the HUD) only works half the time, and will often disappear completely, or as I have mentioned, become covered by the HUD.This game has little to no redeeming qualities. Even the combat, which most dungeon crawlers are known for, feels clunky and unfinished. For the price, I recommend purchasing Diablo, or other established dungeon crawlers. Especially for that disgusting $40 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: What exactly is Minecraft: Dungeons? It's an all-new action-adventure game inspired by classic dungeon crawlers, where you'll constantly discover new weapons and items that will help you defeat a ruthless swarm of new-and-nasty mobs. You'll fight or flee through canyons, swamps and of course mines. You can brave the dungeons alone, or team up with friends. name: XEL
detailed_description: The Save the World Edition contains XEL as well as the official Soundtrack , Artbook and Comic A Lost Friend and is a great way to show appreciation for the developers, while simultaneously supporting a good cause. Assemble Entertainment will donate 10% of the proceeds for every sold Save the World Edition to Sea Watch , in order to help refugees from distress at sea! Uncover XEL’s dark past XEL is a 3D action-adventure set in a sci-fi fantasy setting. Play as Reid, shipwrecked on the strange world of XEL . Without any recollection of her former life, it is up to you to unravel her past and connection to XEL . Ready your sword and shield as you explore the overworld of XEL and dive into imposing dungeons full of unforeseen threats and challenging puzzles . Throughout your journey you will make new friends and foes, find new gadgets as well as being able to jump through time and space. As Reid delves deeper into the mysteries surrounding XEL , she discovers an endless cycle of peril. Will she be able to break free from it and what will it take? An ass-kicking 3D action-adventure through space and time Explore the mysterious world of XEL and uncover its dark past A vibrant overworld and challenging dungeons await to be explored and mastered Help Reid figure out who she is and why she is stranded on this strange place Hack and slash your way through gone-haywire-robot-minions and face the exotic wildlife of XEL Solve time bending puzzles and make use of your arsenal of gadgets Old-school gameplay meets new-school features A classic top-down 3D action-adventure awaits XEL offers a well-crafted combat system with dodging, parrying and gadgets. Upgrade your weapon, shield and gadgets to kick even more ass Unique abilities will let you jump through time to traverse prior inaccessible areas or encounter foes in a weaker state and bend the rules of space The dungeons and puzzles in XEL will put your wits as well as your guts to the test The world of XEL awaits Experience an intriguing sci-fi fantasy tale with a strong emphasis on story-telling, combat and puzzling Meet a memorable cast of characters and engage in witty and charming dialogues Discover time-distorted areas that allow you to take a glimpse behind the curtain that led to the downfall of this strange place Interact with your environment and actively engage with NPCs A timeless soundtrack and visuals XEL offers vibrant visuals, handcrafted by a passionate Indie team as well as a timeless soundtrack composed by Gidon Wolff

_childDocuments_.review: Erf, it's another one of those games that could have been good if the devs had done some basic research on quality of life from other successful games.The player can be obscured by the environment, so you can't see anything at all. Games with this camera angle have had the whole "ghost outlines" through environment down for a while. Also the camera feels really far away, which disconnects you from the action.Vsync is forced on, and while I understand why (due to lots of game engines having issues with physics when you unlock the FPS), it made my game feel a bit stuttery. Unity's in-built Vsync is pretty bad, it's better handled by the graphics driver/monitor.No mouse support in-game, and the default keyboard bindings are awful. Mouse is available in menus, for what it's worth.The opening cutscene is badly compressed so it's full of artefacts. I assume others are, too.The combat is pretty clunky, and not overly enjoyable. The first boss sign posts its attacks pretty well, so you avoid the attack... but no, get hit anyway because the hitbox of the attack is actually way larger than the visuals for it.Most of the voice lines are out of sync with the models moving.The writing is... a bit childish, from what I saw of it. The voice acting is below average. The main protagonist delivers most of her lines alright, but the first other talking character you come across is pretty dyer.Animations are a bit wooden, which I guess is fine for an indie team, but the your character has a fairly clean run cycle, but the first other character you come across doesn't. He also just ran over a broken bridge... like he had the power of flight...It's cute, it's cheap. It's probably worth the price point if you can put up with the jank, but it crashed on me a few times within the first 2 hours so I'll just get a refund instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Xel is an action-adventure jumping you into the role of Reid, a girl with no recollection of her past. Equipped with a sword and a shield, she must hack through murderous robots to ensure the safety of the Xel citizenry. While I enjoyed the puzzle-solving moments, it's plagued with numerous, unforgivable flaws that I can’t recommend it.                           Crashing on a malfunctioning spaceship called Xel, an amnesiac young woman named Reid finds herself trapped in a world teeming with hostile robots and crazed zealots still stuck in their old ways. Searching for her lost past, she teams up with the resident boy scout, Desmond, and aids his village with several tasks, including repairing the ship’s engine to prevent it from blowing up. Along the way, she discovers a new meaning to her life, finding a purpose worth fighting for. The story starts strong with the introduction of Reid and the other supportive characters she meets. A humorous touch is added to the dialogue and playful banters, and sometimes it ekes out a chuckle or two from me, but they are trying too hard to be funny, causing more cringeworthy moments than anything. There is also an air of mystery regarding Reid’s missing past, and a few audio logs allude to who she was before, but the reveal feels very anticlimactic. Overall, the story is mediocre at best, with a few ups and many downs. By the end, I remember begging the game to conclude because of how boring it became.Combat is relatively simple, slicing and dicing your way through recurring foes who will either chase you till the ends of the world or stare at you while you beat them to death. Reid's arsenal consists of a sword and a shield, which can be upgraded with parts you find on your journey. She can dodge, but I find it rather finicky since it practically has zero invincibility frames, making it useless in most cases. It could be that I am dodging too early or too late, but I simply end up absorbing the hit because you can find enough “heart” upgrades that can increase your health. Stamina is also a feature, and it is used whenever you block or dodge, but the impact of it seems negligible, making me wonder why it is implemented in the first place. Reid will discover handy tools that support her during exploration, like the "Stickyhook", which can shoot out a sticky residue strong enough to climb unscalable ledges. It is good for backtracking and unlocking unexplored regions of the map. The "Clobber" and "Burnhilde" act in a similar fashion with the former able to smash any insecure glass minding their own business, and the latter burning through ice barring your way. Gadgets also function as a sub-weapon, such as the "Zap-Trap", which can stun enemies during combat and also short-circuit electronics that can open a door or gate somewhere. I find that they are a creative way to encourage players to sweep the same area for any treasure that might have been missed. In the campaign, Reid will notice that there is a chunk of magical stone lodged in her head, and it grants her the ability to travel through time. She can’t control it willingly, and can only activate it when a broken “Chronal Pillar,” the device used for saving, is in the vicinity. Functionally, it is the driving force behind the various puzzles scattered throughout the world, and I like how it is executed because it showcases inventive solutions for an otherwise simple puzzle. They are entertaining to figure out, and I wouldn’t mind if the core gameplay revolves around this mechanic rather than what we have now. To support her adventures, a strange and probably insane man sells our heroine recipes like “Heart Candies,” and “Tough Gum” that can heal your damaged hearts, or temporarily buff her defense, respectively. They can be cooked in campsites dispersed around the field and requires ingredients to be created. The materials aren't difficult to locate since you can either buy them from a merchant or obtain them from enemies. Unfortunately, there isn’t a hotkey for consumables, and it becomes rather tedious accessing the inventory, then scrolling through the multiple snacks items every single time I just want to chew on gum. I need an active button to press for convenience. The world of Xel is bright and colorful and includes distinct biomes to explore. I find it fascinating that a single space station can have different climates, like “the Bog,” a swampy locale, or a snowy place called the “Glacial Glades.” Each area has its personality and design and is visually appealing. They are also interconnected through shortcuts, which is a nice addition. In terms of technical issues, this is where the majority of my frustration stems from. Although numerous glitches have been patched, I still managed to come across texture glitches that causes me to fall off the world. Floating enemies, the buggy map interface, and non-responsive enemies are irritations I can live with, but the incessant notifications when you pick up an item you've already found all compound into an amalgamation of nonsense that is intrusive and downright aggravating. Another issue I have is the camera because it is zoomed out at a terrible angle, and at times, the environment can obscure your vision, so if an opponent, for example, enters that blind spot, you end up getting hurt or swinging your sword wildly. I wouldn’t even have a problem with it if I can move the camera around for another perspective but that’s not possible yet. Lastly, the keyboard is very awkward to play in, even after changing the defaults around. I find it weird that you can’t map the main attack to the left or right mouse button, but you can still select things with the cursor, making it a bizarre design choice. I highly recommend using a controller if you have it because it is more comfortable. As for performance, there are dips here and there, and the graphical settings are very sparse, but I was constantly hovering around 50-60 fps so that isn’t an issue for me. Finishing at 8 hours, the adventure isn’t too long, even with a decent amount of exploration. After deliberating on it, with its tedious combat, so-so storyline, and all-around buggy nature, I can’t in good conscience recommend it. I truly wanted to love this game because I can see the makings of a good one but it is marred with so many problems.

_childDocuments_.review: As of 2023/3/31 there still are bugs so I would recommend this only on sale or in bundle. I liked the game and gave it a thumbsup despite it. Fingers crossed for patching.Gameplay is fun, the story/characterization is fine, and the deeper plot/theme of the XEL pretty interesting, I felt that gave a lot of depth to the whole game.The exploration is fun, but it does take some getting used to the initial mechanic that you only jump when the game has specific-looking ledges. Much of the boundaries of the game are simple step-ups that visually look jumpable but of course are hard boundaries.First gameplay tip: always save, every single time you are within a 1-minute walk to a save point. Because multiple bugs force you to reload your last save. And rewalking from two zones over... the second time... the third time... pleeeeeease.This is the worst of the gameplay bugs: there are several locations where you unknowingly step "down" into a location that you can't step back up from. Your recourse? Stop the game & reload last save. There are also some locations where you can clip and fall. If it is near a "intentional" fall to death, you lose a heart. If not, you either GAME OVER (and load from last save) or you fall infinitely and have to stop/reload. One of these locations prevents you from getting to a chest area, so that's sad.Another not-funny bug: when I buy the last upgrade (it was zap-trap for me), the Shirl-store doesn't allow me to exit. Not sure if it's a soft-lock or what. But I never could buy the last zap-trap upgrade.But aside from this, the visuals are impressive. When you are walking around, you see depths below and above, and you get a really enjoyable oh wow moment. The last two areas really nail this and are worth playing through the bugs to see. The visuals actually give your eyes something to do while you do those "pre-fast-travel" long walks.Regardless it is a relatively short game, and enjoyable once you know where most of the bugs trigger. I would recommend it at a relatively low price in its current form, and hope the bugs get patched soon.If it matters, I'm playing on a decent game laptop, so I don't think the bugs triggered due to resource constraints.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a ton of potential; the characters are interesting, the story is engaging, if a bit predictable. What truly brings it down is the amount of bugs, especially game-breaking ones. I've clipped through the floor multiple times. Since the autosave doesn't trigger often, this means you'll often lose a ton of progress with each bug. The biggest one, however, happened at the end. After some story, you get transported to an area where you have to break a glass pane to progress. I have the correct tool to break the pane, but it just bounces off. And this is after I restarted my game, the first time I was able to get there the whole screen didn't load. So now I guess I'll never know the ending.Overall, not worth buying yet. _childDocuments_.review: I like the game and I'd wholeheartedly recommend it, but unfortunately I can't due to bugs.That is including a game-braking bug closer to the end when after certain someone reveals his masterplan you end up either stuck in a 2 meter corridor in front of a glass wall which for whatever reason refuse to break or stuck in the exact same place, but instead of a game you see a loading screen. Either one of those break ability to finish the game. I can tolerate quite a lot, but game-breaking bugs almost at the end... that's where I draw the line.Beside that:— encountered location which refuse to load until you jump into it while it's unloaded and when it appears you already plummeting into abyss below;— loading game from pause menu keeps focus on gadgets in the in-game menu despite menu is closed when you load the game, so as soon as you call for either one of your gadgets it'll end up re-assigned to Zap Trap (first gadget on the list);— fell through the floor in quite a few places just by walking and once while talking to an NPC.Not a bug, but another negative would be the fact that the game world feels unnecessarily stretched and empty.Decent even though somewhat repetitive combat (especially bosses — they made one and copied it into multiple places with minor gimmicks), really nice and consistent art-style, decent music, good voice-acting, interesting details about the world revealed through the audio-logs and, while partially predictable, but interesting plot. That's quite enough to make a good adventure game and Tiny Roar got all of that, but seems like they failed at execution. It doesn't matter how good are the ingredients and the dish you serving when you serving it on a dirty broken plate.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Xel. The gameplay is good and the story is alright except for the foul language which felt out of place. But I have now had two playthroughs and both of them have not allowed me to proceed.The first play through was stopped because something I was supposed to select didn't let me select it. Because I had fun with Xel, I waited for a patch in which a fix for this bug was mentioned. It happened and I hoped I could play through the game again.I played through a second time, but after what seems like a close-to-the-end cut scene, the game is stuck showing a loading screen while the character is placed back in the game. _childDocuments_.review: Our protagonist Reid, has crash landed her spaceship on the world of Xel. As you come around, you are greeted by a flying mechanical ball called Chap, who becomes your companion on your journey through the many realms of Xel. Unable to remember your name or your past, you must work with the inhabitants of the planet to try and uncover the secrets contained within. Xel is a 3D action adventure set in a sci-fi environment containing light puzzle elements and hack and slash game play. The story is quite intriguing, if a bit slow to develop, with some nice character development among the main characters, but others are quite trivial and have a lot of meaningless stuff to say. The story doesn’t really start to blossom until the half way point of the game, as Reid uncovers the secrets to her lost memory and how she fits in to the world of Xel, but even though the story wasn’t mind blowing, it served as a nice way of gelling the game play together.Combat mostly fell on the normal to easy side, depending on the number of enemies present and which type of enemy was encountered. There was quite a variety on offer, with some firing projectiles; some having shields; and others needing two kinds of weapons to kill them. You will encounter a few boss fights. Most of them are doable and it will only take a few tries, especially if you have plenty of health boosts in your inventory.The game suggests that there are time related puzzles involved, but it was more of a mechanic than a puzzle. You can use your time stone to bend reality and enter a different time. Here you can either move to a certain position and then go back to reality, or perhaps move a block into position to use in the real world. These “puzzles” are incredibly easy and obvious in the main.You can upgrade the four pieces of equipment you’ll eventually own, but some of the resources needed are very hard to discover and this means you’ll have to choose only one or two items to upgrade. Killing enemies drops common items used to brew health or stamina potions, but to upgrade weaponry you will need things like gold cables or energy cores, which were only available through opening chests or defeating bosses, and were very limited. Each weapon required the same ingredients, so once you had used them on one item it was extremely hard to gather enough for another one. You can buy items in the shop, but they are mostly common items that you don’t need. You won’t be able to buy much to help you upgrade weaponry, and oddly you cannot sell any of your inventory.There are a few different areas to explore, some are available from the beginning and others need specialized equipment or items to progress. The map is absolutely useless in providing you with any kind of directional help. There are no way-points or pointers to your objective, and navigating the map is very difficult with a controller. I gave up trying to use it as a direction tool. It also has no key, so sometimes identifying objects on the map is difficult.I got lost quite a lot in the beginning and you will do a lot of running around, looking for certain areas, except there is no run button, so it’s more like a jog. I hated that there were no fast-tracking methods, until at the end of the game fast tracking suddenly became available. I don’t know if it was always available or somehow, I had unlocked something, but it came far too late in the game. That seemed to be a common theme though, and I don’t think things were explained enough. For example, I had a torrid time trying to use the web slinger. It just wouldn’t work properly and was a huge source of frustration, but later I accidentally discovered that you need to use LT to target before using it. There are no tutorials on how to use equipment so that is why I was misusing it throughout. Level design seemed to be unbalanced, especially with the amount of save stations. In easy levels, there seemed to be plenty of save opportunities, but on harder planes there were hardly any. The worst culprit was the final level where there were no saves at all, and if you got killed you would have to replay about an hour’s gameplay. When the game bugged out on the final boss, I couldn’t be bothered to replay that whole level and just gave up. Also, there are meant to be three save slots but I could only ever access slot one. I could not work out how to use the other two slots.There are so many bugs still present in the game. I got stuck in the environment, I fell through the game world when initiating a time jump, and there are little annoying things like not being able to see what you are doing due to the camera angle and the environment getting in the way of your character. Often, I fought battles I could not see and ran around blindly trying to pick up loot. If you open a chest or collect an extra life, a cut scene is initiated but enemies can still attack you during the cut scene! Every time you pick up an item, a box flashes up telling you what it is which can disturb combat and becomes tiresome very quickly. Xel looks gorgeous and has a nice atmosphere, with its pleasant soundtrack and professional sounding voice acting, but there are too many frustrating moments for it to be enjoyable at the moment.There are a few characters to meet. One even helps you in combat in the latter half of the game, and there is a shopkeeper and weapons expert who can upgrade your gear.Reid uses a sword and a shield in combat. The sword can be upgraded which adds a short-range teleport dash apparently. Again, I was never showed how to use this and never did. You are also meant to be able to parry, but was never shown how. The shield can block any projectiles.There are four pieces of equipment to acquire. An electronic device that can stimulate doors to open, or can temporarily freeze enemies, and yourself, who can then be attacked.A web slinging device that can stun enemies briefly, or can launch you over large gaps if there are some anchor points available to use.A flame throwing device that melts ice and burns enemies on contact.An experimental prototype weapon designed to emit a powerful sound wave, disturbing certain enemies so that they can be attacked. It also smashes glass.

_childDocuments_.review: Xel could be ( If it's patched ) a really nice game. Unfortunately this game suffers from a large number of rather bad game design decisions.To be fair Xel is a decent little game with nice 3D Art.Nonetheless.  Here's my list of poor design decision in Xel: - No Mouse Support during gameplay. Instead of being able to attack with LMB, you have to attack with the I Key. And you cannot rebind this in Settings. - You can't Jump manually. The game Jumps for you at specific Jump locations. This is such an awful design decision imo, because it means that you can get stuck in locations ( rivers or small gaps ) where you can't easily get out except by wandering around looking for a ramp. Also it takes pretty much all the fun out of jumping. - A crafting system that really doesn't add much to the gameplay. - Lack of enemy variety. In Level 1 of the game there are only 2 enemy types, Robot and Turret. That's it. - A large city hub that takes ages to explore, but has little of interest to do, except talk to NPCs and craft.- A large amount of game mechanics, UI Design, Sound Effects are ripped straight out of Zelda: BOTW. Xel could have been a really awesome game.  There are so many cool things about it. Nice artstyle. Cool Level Design. Good Voice Acting and Script. But all the poor gameplay designs make it a chore to play and a bit boring. Really no Key Binding options. Fine if the game is in Early Access and Devs plan to add it later but it's in full release.Sorry. Better luck next time.

_childDocuments_.review: Tough game to like. Definitely not worth its price or your time, but I'll let you know the pros and cons...Pros:+ Good quality character models with decent animations and decent voice work+ Soundtrack is great. I'm happy I have the soundtrack separate to this game.+ Nice premise for a kid-friendly adventure story.Cons:- Characters often have very broken animations and often you'll see some pretty derpy stuff when an NPC attacks another NPC.- Easy to get lost. Difficult to find your way around the game world. Sometimes, however, you just get stuck in an area due to...- Many frequent glitches/bugs. There was a bug in my initial playthrough of the very first level where a door didn't open when it should have. I wandered around aimlessly trying to find where I was supposed to go for quite a while before eventually just restarting the game and lo and behold, the door opened.- Boss battles are winnable but not because of skill or being able to figure out a clever puzzle. There's nothing to figure out. You just have to hit them and minimize damage to yourself as much as possible and make sure you have full hp before the battle. It's tedious and not fun.- The story is not told in an exciting way. Dialogue is mostly filler content and adds little substance to the game's story. A hour in, I felt like I was barely scratching the surface of the story and I just couldn't invest myself into it because the game was so monotonous, so boring.- The camera is static and overhead except in cutscenes, and no effort was given to make important objects or even the player visible behind walls.Overall, I'm just stratching my head over why this game was released in its current state. It needed way more time in the oven.

_childDocuments_.review: is a classic top-down 3D action-adventure set in a sci-fi fantasy setting. Explore  as Reid, who has no recollection of her former life, but it is up to  to help her recall her past memories and connection to this "world". Fight countless enemies and bosses, and solve challenging puzzles. Find new tools to use to help you on your journey, upgrade your weapons and jump through time and space. 	So, I was extremely excited about this game. The first 5 hours were extremely enjoyable, with very few bugs/glitches (in my experience). I know a lot of people are complaining about bugs/glitches but I also am aware that the developers are working tirelessly on releasing hotfixes and updates for us players. The bugs I experienced were minor, e.g., Desmond disappeared in the beginning after a death and never respawned until I met up with him in the Wilds. Progressing through the game and going towards late game, I encountered more screen freezing and a couple of instances where I actually fell through the world. But like I said, nothing too horrible. I simply reloaded my save and all was fine.  	Some of the animations were a little derpy, I encountered many NPCs that were sliding along on the floor or just were spazzing out while standing in place. This didn't affect my experience in the game or make me enjoy the game any less but this is just a weird thing that I noticed. In terms of the dialogue, anytime you speak to anyone, sometimes the dialogue gets cut off and the NPC doesn't finish speaking its sentence-- this kind of irritated me as I enjoy hearing the characters talk in full and listening to the voice acting. Sometimes it resulted in me missing full sentences and missing out on a bit of lore. In some instances, you will have dialogue options and you can choose things to ask a character. But, if you're using a controller, you cannot press up on the d-pad as it will open your inventory. If you choose the dialogue options with your analog stick, Reid will walk around and away from the character she is speaking to. This isn't horrible but it was a little weird on the controls side of things.   	Anyway, onto some features that I feel should have been implemented into the game already or should be in the future.	Throughout playing , I kept wanting to zoom in on my player and see more or look at an item more closely but was unable to. I feel like this feature should be patched in a QOL patch. Another feature that I feel should've been implemented is a pannable camera. There were a lot of times that Reid was behind a wall or a rock and I couldn't see her and had trouble getting out of an area if I was stuck. I would love an option to turn the camera and see where I'm going. I found myself also getting frustrated with the saving feature. I'm unsure (please correct me if I'm wrong) but, it felt like there was no auto-saving whatsoever, which led to a lot of frustration towards the end of the game on the last boss. This resulted in respawning back in Needle-Eye, having to spam my controller to skip through dialogue and cut-scenes multiple times so that I could race back to the final boss, and skimming by with half health at the start of the boss fight.  	All in all,  is a wonderful game, the story is beautiful and one that I have thoroughly enjoyed but some updates need to be made. The atmosphere is gorgeous, the music is beautiful and the aesthetic of it all made me feel happy. I loved exploring the world and discovering secrets, unlocking achievements, and solving puzzles. Solving the puzzles was possibly one of the favorite aspects of the game because they left me feeling satisfied after solving them as I'm not amazing at puzzles LOL.  	I would suggest to whoever is reading this to wait until  is smoothed out and polished a little bit more until purchasing this. But this is a fantastic game and a must purchase, for the uniqueness of it alone.  Rating: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to give this game a shot despite the negative reviews, and I regret it. _childDocuments_.review: The camera is waaay too far back and removed from the gameplay. As such, items that are dropped by enemies or boxes are incredibly small and easy to overlook. Because of the camera's distance you'll also encounter many moments where the player is obscured by the environment completely, this also happens with enemies and it can also make progression confusing. This is a perplexing choice and easily the biggest reason I can't recommend this. Events frequently triggered too early, for example dialogue about a button started well before I even arrived at the button. There's something clunky about the combat and the hit boxes. Overall the aesthic is fine. The main character wouldn't look out of place in a super generic Dreamworks animated movie. The "homages" to Zelda are frequent and on-the-nose in a way that is a bit tiresome (XEL is pronounced "Zel", right away you have a Navi sidekick, and the first boss is ripped right out of Breath of the Wild).  Gameplay is very similar to "Hob", though it feels a little less imaginative.
