_childDocuments_.review: Sovereign Syndicate is a Victorian steampunk CRPG developed and published by Crimson Herring Studios. The game is set in a steampunk-inspired Victorian London and features a tarot card system instead of dice rolls. You play as three different characters, each with their own skills and motivations, and customize their personality through narrative choices that unlock new tarot cards. The gameplay is essentially a mix of  within a steampunk world similar to  where magic, technology and supernatural creatures coexist. First, you will play as Atticus Daley, an orphaned minotaur and skilled magician who prefers to live away from society. Next, you will play as Clara Reed, a corsair and rebellious woman who is trying to leave London but gets involved in an investigation about missing people. And finally, you will play as Teddy Redgrave, an engineer who is building Otto, an automaton who gradually acquires more consciousness and questions the nature of existence. You will alternate between these protagonists through different chapters. Their personal stories are linked by one big main quest and some of their actions can influence the world they live in (for example, I unlocked a door with one character and that door was unlocked for the other characters too). NPCs also react to your gender, race and appearance with different dialogues; for example, when playing as the minotaur Atticus I casted an illusion that made him look like a human and NPCs changed their behavior towards him. This can be very important to solve certain quests in more subtle and diplomatic ways.When playing with a new character for the first time, you will be asked to choose their archetype, which defines their starting attributes, traits and major arcana. The latter can also be obtained throughout the story and are very important because they unlock new personality traits, which in turn allow you to select some unique dialogue choices that otherwise would be locked. The main attributes are: Animal Instinct, Wit, Self-Discipline and Spryness. As you play, you also accumulate humours points through the choices you make; these are divided into phlegm, yellow bile, black bile and blood, which are tied to one of the attributes listed above. When a humour bar is filled, the associated attribute levels up and your personality changes according to which attribute you have developed the most. Similarly to Disco Elysium, you have some inner voices that constantly talk inside your head. Choosing one voice over another will drastically change the balance of your humours and with time some voices will become stronger than others. Temperament is also another key aspect of your characters as it represents their mental state, which can move between Desperate, Weary, Content, Optimistic and Hopeful. Similarly to humours, your choices can also change your temperament (for example by giving you +5 Hope) and some special dialogue choices will only be available depending on your temperament score. Last but not least, instead of a DnD dice roll system, you have a Tarot Cards system that basically replaces it. To make a skill check, you draw a card from one of the four Minor Arcana decks (Cups, Wands, Swords and Coins). Each deck includes cards numbered from 1 (Ace) to 14 (King), as well as special ones like The World (which automatically grants 100% success on skill checks) and The Fool (which will always fail the check). All this may seem complex to understand at first, but if you have some experience with CRPGs you will be at home. The progression system is complex but also rewarding because it allows you to change your character’s personality and, depending on the personality, dialogues provide multiple ways to complete quests. The writing is great too, with a lot of description about environments and situations, plus the inner voices in your head that constantly question your choices. The game is only available in English right now, but it’s not as complex as in Disco Elysium. Compared to the latter, it lacks the deep philosophical, political and surreal themes that made me think even when I was not playing the game. This is more like a fictional narrative focused on characters’ personal dramas that are linked together by a long and intriguing main quest.The game’s open world is rich and immersive, filled with interesting characters and locations. The main setting is East London, divided into multiple streets and lanes that host minor locations of interest. You can fast travel to each of these streets, but you can’t fast travel when you are inside a building or in a particularly restrained area. There is great diversity in the environments that reflects the social status of the people who live there: from luxurious districts filled with exclusive clubs and high-class buildings to dark alleys and brothels, each location provides plenty of content, characters and side quests. One thing that I noticed though is that some outdoors environments feel empty and lack detail compared to closed areas, and some basic NPCs also walk through these areas but you can’t talk or interact with them, which is something I have rarely seen in CRPGs games, fortunately.As you can see from the trailers, graphics look pretty good and the PC version runs great even at max settings. Minor bugs and glitches are present, for example sometimes my character got stuck near a wall and could not move or fast travel (because I was inside a building), so I had to reload my last save, which fortunately wasn’t very old, but I was able to replicate the glitch on the same walls, so it’s probably something that needs to be addressed through patches. There are also some sudden frame drops in a few areas (from 60 to 45 fps), but they don’t ruin the experience. What partially ruins it, at least for me, is the angle of the camera, which constantly moves to follow the character’s movements. Despite having an isometric view, the angle of the camera often moves overhead on top of your character (like a bird’s eye view), which becomes annoying while exploring, especially on certain locations where the camera seems to be fighting with walls. I think that a more classic and fixed isometric view would have been a lot better for exploration. Overall, Sovereign Syndicate is a very intriguing CRPG that offers a distinctive and immersive experience. The game’s world feels interesting to explore thanks to the wonderful mix of steampunk technology and supernatural creatures, narrated through well-written and highly descriptive dialogues. The tarot card system works really well and allows you to define your character’s personality through in-game choices that also unlock new options to complete quests. Recommended if you are fluent in English (which is the only available language right now) and you enjoyed .

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, good story. Sound is a bit boring, graphics are decent, considering the price everything is fine. If you like CRPGs this game is worth it for the world alone... Think of Arcanum. The writing is good, but not as in depth as Disco... Yes, you hear your voices, but failing never felt rewarding or peaked the interest to find new ways.Playtime: First playtrough without any guides: ~15hOne thing to mention... I would enjoy a iron man/ one save feature, the tarot system is basically die meaning it lends itself to savescumming.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: This is everything I have wanted in a game since I played Disco Elysium, the steampunk aesthetic, the seedy narrative, the tarot cards, the art, every part of this game fills a niche for me.This won't be the same opinion for everyone naturally, but to my personal tastes this game is a masterpiece, I will be recommending this to all of my RPG loving friends, and recommend anyone reading this, if your on the edge of buying this, you won't regret it.(Also woohoo a canadian developer!)
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: So I came across this game when saw some post about "New Disco Elysium like game".  And here is my crude comparison of those:Advantages: 1) Camera movent in Sovereign Syndicate feels more alive and responsive.2) In my opinion 3d art for the game is better.3) No restrictions in game time. Great.Disadvantages:1) Plot is rather uninteresting. 2) The amount of mechanics in game are laking. They are very simple and doesn't contribute to game all that much.3) Loading between every location.So, overall - I did gave a chance to game, I finished it to see if anything interesting story-wise happens, or if some mechanics would drasticlly influence the game ending, but unfortunatelly it never happened. The system of character mood is unimportant for the most part, and could be easily moved to close to optimistic just by eating fruit. Whatever. The Tarot cards system, altho interestingly looking, grants only ability to choose some options in dialogue, but is also rarely important. Personage characteristics - same deal, you choose one which will be predominant, and then mostly use it, because it has highest probability to pass those dialog variants check. Also about these checks - In Disco Elysium there were red (one time) and white(could be repeated after upping corresponding skill) checks. In this game - seems like only red, cause you cannot repeat anything. And I would like to discuss also this "steampunk and magic world" statement. Magical beast - yeah, ok. But what can you do as *magical minotaur* - disquise yourself as human with illusion. That's it. No other fancy tricks, no other magic involved anywhere. Same goes to the steampunk - game gives you a good look at walking automaton and mentions some other steam inventions, but not a lot of this is involved in the game itself.Overall, I am dissapointed with game, it didn't bring any fealings except for boredom and  feeling that I just wasted my money and time at unimportant stuff.Knowing that game is the first game of studio, hope they will reconsider their decisions and come up with something more interesting and unique. As it seems there might be continuation to this, plotwise
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: Yes for the story, The rest is clunky.Incredible well written story with twist and turns and meaningful choices. Multiple aspect of your personality talking to you was great to give context. Multiple endings.I just think the game should have been made into a visual novel instead of the iso RPG here's why;The exploration for gears doesn't bring much and the world is fairly empty. We could have collected the gin and the fans through dialogue anyway.Graphic wise it's not the prettiest game we would have been better off with full screen well draw characters that show facial expression instead of the tiny portrait next to the dialogue box.All the text is on the right side of the screen in a narrow box, once again, it would have been better if they had taken all the real estate available on the screen.Waste a lot of time to fast travel to a location to then walk to a store to then have another loading screen.The Whole Tarot card system is good but we are not active with it, they should have given us 3-4 cards to pick from instead of RNG that we have no control over.Hope a for a sequel with improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: Sovereign Syndicate treads the well-worn path paved by Disco Elysium, attempting to replicate its success. While it achieves a solid result, it falls short in several key areas.Positive aspects:- Victorian steampunk setting- Diverse character perspectives, departing from Disco Elysium's single viewpoint - The art style is ok, though it doesn't compete with the oil painting style of Disco Elysium- The narrative is also decent, spanning approximately 10-11 hours of gameplay: it holds its ground without reaching the pinnacle set by Disco Elysium- Twitch integration for social engagement (I did not test it though, as I played it entirely offline)Negative aspects:- Lack of originality and innovation, as it echoes Disco Elysium too closely- Simplified mechanics: the absence of features like the Thought Cabinet/tech tree and the inability to assign points to character traits result in a somewhat watered-down gameplay experience- No voice acting: in a text-heavy game, the absence of voice acting is a missed opportunity to enhance the immersive experience- No hardcore modeIn conclusion, for a fair price tag it is recommended for those seeking a narrative-focused experience, but be prepared for a game that falls slightly short compared to Disco Elysium.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible journey through a beautifully dark and intricate steampunk world. Sovereign Syndicate brings a fresh twist to the RPG genre with its complex characters, branching narrative, and Victorian-inspired setting. The game masterfully combines choice-driven storytelling with compelling RPG mechanics, making each decision feel significant. Each character is unique, and their individual story arcs are engaging and add so much depth to the world. From intense dialogues to exploring the gritty streets of a steampunk city, every moment kept me captivated. The choices really make a difference, creating a highly replayable experience that fans of story-driven games will love. Highly recommended for anyone seeking a deep and atmospheric RPG!
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Sovereign Syndicate even more than I anticipated in my preview; it was my Christmas game over several hours. After eighteen chapters playing as Atticus, Clara, Teddy, and a couple as Otto, I saw the credits roll and wanted to keep playing. Now, halfway through a second playthrough, I hope we will see much more of this Victorian steampunk London in sequels, and more strange stories of Minotaurs, Dwarves, Cyclopes, and others—a league of extraordinary fantasy folk.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: I never review games but want to help give this one a boost. It's a great little RPG that's got Disco Elysium DNA but obviously never hits those highs. Regardless, it's a fun 8-10hrs with three good protagonists and a murder mystery which pulls you through nicely. A few design quirks aside, it's hard to find many faults, especially for what is clearly a small team and (presumably) small budget.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Not sure why others are so critical of the writing - It would be odd if this sort of game wasn't verbose and descriptive. Personally I think it's great, each character has a definite voice and the narrative writing is top-notch.Like others are saying, this isn't really exactly like Disco Elysium, although it draws heavily on it for inspiration. It's shorter and more linear, but I think it serves a story like this well. It's sort of like a RPG-lite/adventure/visual novel combo, which in my eyes is perfect. I hope there's a sequel down the road!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll say yes on this one, but there are a few things to list:- Story - Decent and what made me finish the game- Game - It's more a storybook than a game so pay heed- Walking/Running - There is a lot of going back and fort and fetching and such. _childDocuments_.review: Very "budget" version of Disco Elisium.Neat detective story in the fantasy steampunk noir setting of early 20th century London, narrated by a drunkard, a prostitute and a bounty hunter.It has non-linear development, RPG system, "inner dialogues" and lots of sidequests.If you liked Disco Elisium, then I recommend it, for there is nothing else now. Game is good, story is nice, but it lacks Disco Elisium's "mojo", that unexplainable crazy vibes.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Great story driven game. Worth the $20.If you are expecting Disco Elysium, it's not, so might want to look elsewhere.If you were expecting shoot em up action, look elsewhere.If you are into reading and a good narrative, you'll enjoy the 12 hours or so it takes to get almost everything in game done.Ending seems to setup sequels, please deliver!
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: Need a brush up on Cockney and Victorian Slang before Dickens Faire? look no furtherSOVEREIGN SYNDICATEAn Excellent Dialog based CRPG. Using Quaint English the dialog has unusual terms and nouns highlighted in yellow so you can mouse over for a definition. Great if you don’t know the difference between “dosh” and “cosh” considering the Desperate states of this London one may happen to you to remove you of the other. Sadly only one character will speak to you with rhyming slang, but many others have just as interesting dialecticals native or not to England, yet common none the less, ya ken. I fell in love with game the moment I played the demo. By far one of the most exciting chapters, as its supposed to be, the bait to to catch you hook line and sinker. When you begin you are given a choice of Archeytype to stack the attributes  used in conversation and challenges from Strong, Uncommon, Good to Fair. This is the Only Similarity this game has to Disco Elysium other than being an entirely Dialog Based Narrative Adventure Game other than the occasional gin bibing and opiomania. Your Archetype also gives you your first Major Arcana granting you a Disposition usable in conversation. All Major Arcana are available to each of the three characters you play can be acquired through chance or circumstance. The challenge system is based on the suits of Tarot, each one of your attributes governed by a particular suit when you draw a card that is added to your attribute to determine success. Whenever you have a dialog you are given choices based on your attributes favoring an attribute choice adds a point to your humors, as like to the swelling of Hippocratic fluids, that levels up your attributes. The only other Stat in the game is Temperament a gauge from Hope to Despair, your actions and perspectives will influence this giving you different dialog choices.Being a veteran CRPGer I know you may want to Min/Max or Stat Balance and possibly SaveScum, which is easy since the game autosaves before every interaction. However I recommend against it, rather RolePlay the Archetype and consider a temperament you choose and enjoy the consequences. Sometimes a fail has better results than a success. You cant 100% the achievements on a single play through without save scumming the ending so enjoy the game your first run.I’d only call this game Steampunk as much as you can call Shadowrun Cyberpunk. Its an alternate Victorian London populated with mythical creatures, like centaurs, minotaurs, and cyclops, as well as automatons. and Cybernetic augmentation is as common as Werewolves.  For 18 Chapters it still seems short to me… I really want to see this game flourish and spawn offspring because this is a world I want to play in often. As well The Ending sets it up to be a Saga. Try the demo and Fall in Love with this Dame like I did.I'd like to see setting flourish
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Disco Elysium but with a different story, which is exactly what I was hoping it would be.I love the Victorian London setting, and the addition of a glossary is really nice. Also love the writing, the music and the visuals so far.But I was hoping that this game would also be pretty much an interactive audio book, like Disco Elysium, and I was a bit sad to see that there isn't a narrator, or any voice acting so far. That was the main reason why I fell in love with DE. But oh well. I am still very much interested in the game and you should definitely try it if you want more DE.The tarot cards are very pretty also. And I did not yet have any performance issues or anything so that's great too!
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting game and one I played to completion.  Probably around a 65-75/100 game.  Characters walk annoyingly slowly, you will repeat a lot of the same locations many times.  It takes a while to figure out you should be using the map in the bottom right to fast-travel.  The constant perspective switching between characters means that every time a story gets interesting you cut to a different character doing something else.  I would have preferred to just play as Atticus the whole time, he was easily the strongest character.The film Canada/Alberta financing explains why one of the characters is part of the expulsion of the Acadians to Louisiana.  The ending was strong until the very end.  Having the characters join the Sovereign Syndicate at the end made the whole came feel like a prologue to something along the lines of the League of Extraordinary Gentlemen rather than a complete story in its own right.  Not finding out who the Masked Gentleman was was also a bit of a disappointment.The Tarot card system was cool and worked well, as did the various humours.  The illustrations and comics at key moments were very cool and I only wish there were more of them in the middle.  Worth a play through, particularly if you like steampunk.  You'll get faster at navigating the city over time; even if I would have loved an ostrich mount to make everyone move much quicker than their glacial pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: Sovereign Syndicate is a good game, but I had to rush it in the end. In a few words, the story is great, the writing is far from Disco Elysium's Genius BUT is still fine (even if I do hate some characters), the setting is cool... But the pacing, the narration and the whole slugginess of the game really drags it down. Everything is slow and boring in Sovereign Syndicate, moving in the small city is a chore and you can only use fast travel from outside locations to outside locations. That means you have to walk ALL THE WAY to every single location et exit them to move around.Most of the quests are just fetch quests, and I would have been OK with this if only the game let me fast travel everywhere. The way the game is cut into chapters is also... clumsy. Sometimes you want to progress a quest, only to find out that there is nothing to do except waiting for 3 or 4 chapters. I wish the instructions were clearer, because the whole chapter things kinda remove the RPG vibe (the game railroads you a lot).I'm not a huge fan of the 3 protagonists solo progression, but that is just me. It's kinda frustrating when 3 characters have the same quests, and you have to progress on it knowing you already found intel that makes it worthless. Weird West for example was handling it a lot better.I could forgive a lot of this if the game was respecting my time, but it is not...
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: Not really one to leave reviews but I wanted to help increase other potential players willingness to give this one a go. I mainly play RPGs and some narrative and action adventure games for context. I loved the aesthetic, dialogue, and narrative themes of the game. Is it a AAA game? No, but not everything needs to be. It is an intelligent, unique experience that I for one deeply prefer over mass produced mind numbing shooters and empty open worlds with a multitude of fetch quests.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only a few hours into Sovereign Syndicate, but I'm hooked! The steampunk London setting is atmospheric and gritty, and the characters are complex and compelling. The writing is top-notch, pulling you right into this world of mystery and intrigue. The tarot card system adds a unique layer of chance and strategy that feels fresh for the genre. If you love story-driven RPGs, give Sovereign Syndicate a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: The story itself is quite interesting and did caught my interest. I enjoyed the game.Gameplaywise, I believe a fail forward approach would have been great, as sometimes I was just stuck into reloading, reloading, reloading the save game till I did pass a skill check - that was just time waste and not so enjoying.Luckily that happened not too often and there were quite a lot of awesome things to explore, I sometimes felt like I was in a victorian Version of Shadowrun! :)Thank you for this rough gem of a game!
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying this allot so far.  The writing has pulled me in. There's a feature to mouse over and define some old London slang and phrases which I was unfamiliar with and appreciate (really helps me to get a better feel and understanding for the setting). I really like the artwork, I actually take longer to read stuff because I have to admire the artwork first :DSo far I'd say this is DEFINITELY worth buying!
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game that wears its Disco Elysium inspiration on its sleeve.The story-telling is supported by some strong worldbuilding and is tight without sacrificing complexity. The game mechanics themselves are relatively thin but not in a way that particularly detracts from the intended role-playing experience. The shifting PoV between the player characters really gels with the narrative structure, letting you experience the same zones from different perspectives. A full playthrough including side content is pretty short (10-15 hours), but the experience justifies the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: If you like DIsco Elysium, you'd probably like this game. You can feel the game has lower budget, there is jankiness in many aspect of the game, but the core story of the game is quite intriguing. The game's got heart, I can recommend for 20 bucks.Some technique issues, no native V-sync and the camera movement can be disorienting at times, hopefully something the devs can address in a future patch.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: An intriguing role-playing game, without combat but with stats rolls. The story is engaging. Every interactive spot is worth checking out, always worth it to satisfy your curiosity and gain trait points. You have to be careful, however, because unsuccessful choices or throws weaken the character's mental state and may block more sensible choices. The game has a save system on request, so if you like, you can load and try again ;> Well, curiosity kills the cat...Works well on Steam Deck.However, I prefer playing on PC because the fonts look better - 95% of the gaming time is spent reading. In options you can increase the main font, so it's not a big problem. Tooltips are an important and useful feature, especially for non-native English speakers. On Steam Deck, tooltips have a dedicated key (on PC you use a mouse).
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only 3 hours in, but so far I'm utterly hooked to the world and story. Top notch writing and characters. Cannot wait to see how this all comes together.*Edit* Just finished the game, due to some IRL medical issues I wasn't able to finish it earlier in February like I would have liked. In the end though I highly recommend this game, absolutely loved all of the characters, the lore and world created. It truly came together for me in the end and I feel like there's something special here for future games.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: I was an avid fan of Disco Elysium, and sought to find a similar experience in any capacity. This game was brought to my attention as a similar format with compelling storytelling, however, I began to realize just HOW much it borrowed from DE in the opening sequence. It is so close to a cut-and-paste that I found it extremely distasteful and very underwhelming.This game plays more like a fan fiction of Disco Elysium in a steampunk fantasy world than anything that deserves to be considered in its own right. I am very disappointed because I know this is an unpopular genre with a tight-nit community, and I am sure the devs care a lot about this IP, but it is extremely lacking in any form of originality. They have already hinted at some sort of "Definitive Edition", so maybe I will return to try that. At this point I have refunded the game and cannot recommend it at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: I'm amazed this game isn't more popular. Anyone who enjoyed Disco Elysium or classic point-and-click adventure games like The Longest Journey should give this one a try. Fun characters, good writing, and a very interesting steampunk fantasy world. The plot advances quickly and it doesn't outstay its welcome. Really good game and one that I hope to see sequels to!
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: A Point n' Click with RPG ambitions, inspired, for our benefit, by the success of the good (if vastly overrated) Disco Elysium 5 years ago.Comparisons with the other game are inevitable:- appealing visuals and music;- dialogue-based interactions on every hot spot;- small geographical setting with rich lore and worldbuilding;- tons of reading, the vast majority of it optional and well hidden;- struggling protagonists;- even the main flaw is the same: dice rolls.Having to reload and blindly click through 100 lines of dialogue you've already read, 6 times, until the toss of a coin is finally in your favour... that was tiresome 40 years ago, that was fixed 25 years ago with smart mechanics and, for unfathomable reasons, the annoyance is trending again these days.One could expect the RNG to work if Sovereign Syndicate made failures valuable, which it doesn't; still, DE did, and proved that wrong: you had to reload and reroll 20 times more to satisfy your curiosity about both failure and success.Randomised skill checks are just a nuisance.Fortunately, the save system is fully fledged. You can explore at whim, and your choices do matter (the store page keyword is uncharacteristically used correctly.)Auto-saves, right before each interaction, are particularly useful.The rest of the UI is equally good.Including text legibility, which is paramount in a text-heavy game.All well suited for comfortable gamepad use.The one weakness of the interface would be the running speed, too slow, especially for the dwarf character. I suppose it is so to avoid looking silly, fair enough, but the game does rely heavily on backtracking, and sometimes I'd choose silly over lengthy.Partially addressed with instant access to the fast travel map (not from every cell, unfortunately) so at least you are spared a lot of running to the free Floating Tram stations (if not all the intermediate, cell-constrained, redundant loading screens.)Technical quality has room for improvement, but is good.Abundant loading screens, some of them long.Some visual glitches, notably with the camera in specific spots, some of them leading to navigation issues.And a few crashes, annoying of course, but harmless thanks to the pervasive autosaves.No broken quests, no softlocks (unlike in DE,) and I really didn't mind the invisible walls (though I would mind their removal even less.)Now the story and the storytelling are what make or break such a game.Easily a thumb up, a pleasure to explore, and to investigate, from start to finish.A good hook (the demo is still accessible for you to check it out,) consistent (slow) pace and wealth of details, welcome twists along the way, up to a very satisfying finish (when DE, for example, completely dropped the ball in its last stretch.)Sometimes too contrived (the serial killer quest, in my opinion,) a few points still unclear (that's fair,) but a bloody good job overall, especially when hunting for intricacies and minute impacts between parallel character storylines.Indeed, you play as several characters, in compartmentalised chapters.What the writers are going for ultimately works, but I found it a flaw early on.Each time the flow broke, I actually quit the game; I took my break right there.Multiple times, until an addictive game kept me away for months.When I came back, I finally got used to it and kept playing on chapter changes.Might actually be seen as a quality, by those having a hard time stepping away from their monitor.Still, all these jumps don't help in remembering all the characters and mini-stories.A who's who tab would have been a welcome addition to the GUI indeed.I'll welcome a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: In Sovereign Syndicate, a steampunk RPG set in a grim Victorian-era London, mysterious murders and missing children set the stage for a dark narrative. I initially hesitated to dive into this game because steampunk isn’t my favorite genre, and the minotaur character didn’t appeal to me. But after playing, I realized I was wrong—this game is a must-try for anyone who loves story-rich, immersive experiences.The game revolves around three unlikely heroes, each with their unique backgrounds and struggles. You switch between them across 18 chapters, exploring the same areas from different perspectives. The narrative is the game’s core, with plenty of text, dialogue, and internal monologues shaping your decisions and the story’s outcome.While the game has no traditional combat, the mechanics are engaging, relying on character attributes and tarot card-based skill checks. The setting is well-crafted, with a focus on the harsh realities of the Victorian era, populated by mythological beings like centaur bobbies and minotaur mobsters. Despite some minor issues, like screen tearing and limited character pathfinding with stairs, the game is well-polished, especially for an indie studio’s first release.I found the story intriguing, with its Jack the Ripper-like mystery, and appreciated the depth and replayability offered by different character builds. Though there’s no voice acting, the sound design and soundtrack perfectly capture the steampunk atmosphere. The game isn’t a CRPG in the traditional sense, so adjust your expectations accordingly—it’s a narrative-driven RPG with a great story, relatable characters, and a solid soundtrack.Overall, Sovereign Syndicate is a hidden gem worth checking out, especially considering its price. If you’re into narrative games with RPG elements, I highly recommend giving it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Note regarding "received game for free": I won the key giveaway from their mailing list.Just finished the game and I loved it. If you like narrative games like Disco Elysium and/or Citizen Sleeper, this game is for you, although it's not quite as complex or variable as either. The trait priority you pick at the start determines the approach you can take to situations that require a conflict resolution (roughly social/mental/physical). Your temperament acts as overall outlook on life. Certain dialogue options or decisions are only available at certain temperament levels (between weary and hopeful). Each of the three (and a half) main characters has their own main agenda which occasionally overlap, as well as personal substories. The setting is an alternative Victorian London in which certain mythological creatures live side by side with humans. It certainly made me want to explore more of it. While you can move freely between the set locations, it is NOT an open world, it's far to small for that.  While nothing particularly original, the main stories are interesting enough to pursue them. The writing is great, atmospheric and archaic enough to give it character. A few bullet points: - there is NO voice acting and there is a lot of text. There is, however, atmospheric music that changes from location to location, as well as some sound effects. - I encountered ONE progression bug I was able to circumvent by choosing a different dialogue option. I believe this has already been fixed. There were also some very minor things like a couple of options reappearing despite them already being resolved, or the same option being listed twice. - the use of tarot cards instead of dice for trait checks added atmosphere - my actual playing game was roughly 25 hours. I often get distracted or do other things while a game is running so the Steam count isn't accurate. - I can only hope this game sells well enough that they can a) add voice acting down the line and b) make another game that actually features the Sovereign Syndicate (odd for the thing in the title only getting mentioned in the last five minutes).TL;DR: If you like narrative RPGs/interactive novels, picking this up is a no-brainer, especially at the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I should have listened to the reviews saying that if you like Disco Elysium, you might be disappointed with this one. Like that game, it is a text-heavy narrative in an intriguing alt-European setting. But unlike that game, very little seems to happen, and still less is influenced by the player. There are seemingly different starting 'classes' and different facets of your personality that sometimes pop up as options in dialogue, but they have practically no effect on how you progress through the game. What stopped me from playing was the absence of any hook or tension in the narrative. The game follows three protagonists, a novel idea, but which in practice only dilutes the story. While the writing is clearly very competent when  it comes to environment descriptions or character descriptions, it's not in service of anything gripping. Whatever the overarching plot even is, it is drip fed to the player. If someone told me to watch a TV show because it gets good after a couple of seasons, I'd pass. Here, too, I recommend that you pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Let us start with why I am downvoting this:1. I do not have the dialogue choices I need to pursue tasks that have been given to me. This happened to me in Chapter 1, and now again in Chapter 2. If I cannot pursue a task, do not give it to me. I can gain it later, when I have the chance to actually pursue it.2. Names are thrown into the game before we have any idea who these people are, and used as if we should know them. Please introduce the people somehow first.3. Some of the dialogue I completely lose the thread of it. As I was streaming, I would stop, quite confused, and say "I lost the thread". I think it is a Germanism. It means that the golden thread that makes this make sense has slipped from my hands. Eg, what the devil is this conversation about??? Now, to the good stuff. I hate to give this a downvote, but until the issue with the tasks is fixed, it will remain a downvote. I REALLY like this game!! It becomes frustrating, when I'm supposed to find a police officer or detective to confer with, and none exists - and neither does Scotland Yards in the game at that point.The setting is wonderful. The faces they draw are very compelling. I love them!!! Especially the engineer we meet in the docks. This game as real atmosphere.The dialect of the time feels forced sometimes.You start-out with a character given to you. You can control the personality a bit. For example: in Chapter 1, you always start out with a Minotaur. You can decide, however, whether he is more inclined toward his animalistic nature, spryness, wit, or self-discipline. You then make certain choices to move the story-line along. The end result is, however, the same.In Chapter 2, you are given a new character, and she has certain aspects of her personality you can choose, too. The dialogue choices develop your character's personality. Your character also has a disposition - how hopeful or full of despair they are. You will uncover major Arcana cards on your journey. You will be given tasks, or can accept tasks. You can explore the area and dialogue choices. Take anything that isn't nailed down, like our beloved, older games. You never know what might come in handy.Thus, you move along in the story. I have sadly not finished the game. I was streaming it to show people what it looks like, but found it frustrating to continually have tasks that I could not pursue, and having nothing else to do but move onto the next chapter.It is otherwise a FANTASTIC game! I hope the devs will fix this issue. If I cannot work a task, I should not be able to take the task.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this game, and it's not for the mechanics, style, or atmosphere generally all of which I rather enjoy.However in different chapters you are made to play different characters. This I do not like, this is something I've never liked in almost any game, as you always just want to rush through and get back to the protagonist. The first story is interesting, and seemingly with several paths one can take. However it ends shortly after getting into it. Seemingly because the character they're really interesting in you playing is Clara. A Mary Sue, wannabe girl boss. She's a sexist and gynophile, and really more repulsive than interesting. I'm fine with having characters that have their own character, I'm not fine with being forced to playing someone who is so bigoted and insufferable. They simultaneously want you to think she's amazing while at the same time representing her as completely loathsome. What's worse is they fall into the same pitfall that most modern media does today. Every woman, everywhere, is excessively complemented, and spoken of complementary as though they're all angels, with the morality of devils, come down to grace us all with their existence. Women did not used to be written so poorly and one-dimensional. All that said remember how I said that first chapter was very short, the second one you're given a much larger area and more to do.  Though things get worse. You are forced to aid in an abortion. This is disgusting, and beyond the pale to force a player to engage in.Having this character could have been fine, if they could have separated the characters. Allowed you to play each through individually. The choices one would make in said chapter as that character could be randomly generated until you play as that character which would actual make this a decent game. So at this time I can not recommend this game as I'm made to want to rush through a portion of it to get to the actual story i'm interested in.

_childDocuments_.review: (I haven't played nearly 70 hours. I always tab out of the games and leave them running in the background.)Sovereign Syndicate is a narrative-driven role-playing game in the iso-perspective.It is set in an alternative SteamPunk London, which is populated by humans, mythical creatures (minotaurs, centaurs) and fantasy creatures (dwarves and werewolves). There are also machines called Automata, which have no will of their own.The corpses of badly mangled prostitutes are found and the three playable protagonists set off in search of the murderer.- That would be ATTICUS DALEY, a magically gifted minotaur. Constantly drunk or otherwise drugged up, he has reached the bottom of the gutter.- CLARA REED is a prostitute who is kept by her rich lovers and knows how to move in high society as well as in the dives and dark alleys of London.- The dwarf TEDDY REDGRAVE is a monster hunter and engineer who earns his living by hunting down evil creatures and spends his time tinkering with his automaton named OTTO.In addition to the series of murders, however, all three have their own agendas and stories to follow.You control the three protagonists alternately (not simultaneously as in Baldur's Gate, for example).The plot is divided into chapters, with each chapter being dedicated to one of them.London is made up of various locations that can be freely explored.Each location is represented by an iso-map, from which you can access up to five different secondary locations.The locations are always slightly different for Clara, Atticus and Teddy. Things that one of them notices another doesn't see at all. Some areas cannot be entered by everyone and some residents react completely differently depending on who approaches them.It can even happen that you bump into one of the other two protagonists.As soon as you interact with people or objects, a conversation window opens. Here you can have a conversation or an inner monologue.Depending on how you behave, you increase one of your 4 individual character values:If you are tactful as Clara, you increase your “Tact”. If you behave wildly and quick-tempered like an animal, you increase your “Animal Instinct” as Atticus. And if Teddy examines a device in detail, his “Analysis” value improves.In some situations, you have to make rolls for these attributes. With a high “Animal Instinct”, it is much easier to intimidate a gang member and if you have a certain “Intellect”, this allows Clara to meet a wiseguy at eye level.Even if the perspective would suggest it, there are no iso tactical battles or anything similar, the entire game is told in this way, i.e. in the conversation windows.This is what the creators CRIMSON HERRING want: To tell a story!And this leads to the game's main problem: the chosen perspective and the creators' intentions do not match at all.An iso-perspective is far removed from the characters and locations, but gives you an overview. This makes sense when you need it. Because, for example, you need to see what is happening on the top left when you are on the bottom right, or you need to get your people into formation for the next conflict.In Sovereign Syndicate, however, there are no (tactical) battles or anything similar. Instead, the chosen perspective means that you spend an endless amount of time running over rather empty maps again and again.When a new chapter begins (and you usually change protagonists), it's an endless slog just following the current quests.You would like to rely on the fact that nothing has changed in the other locations and that the people standing there have nothing new to say. And that's usually the case.But not always!Sometimes there is something to discover away from the places you have to visit for the quests. And that drove me crazy! I don't want to miss out on anything potentially important!So: chapter change - walk through all the locations - talk to all the people - complete one or two quests - chapter change - walk through all the locations - talk to all the people - (etc.)This game could have been a really great visual novel! All the action takes place in the conversation windows anyway. Why I was forced to walk endless distances instead is beyond me.And it would have been much easier for me to immerse myself in the various locations, the posh brothel, the nasty harbor tavern, the filthy sewers, etc., if the really talented artists had produced great pictures instead.As it is, the camera hovers far above the action and a hotspot has to tell me that there's a pile of broken bottles somewhere. So small that I can barely identify them in the iso view...However:Sovereign Syndicate offers a good story in a great, beautifully crafted setting. The dialog and the story are extensive and superbly written. All this makes me hope for more games from Crimson Herring in this exciting world they created.I didn't regret persevering to the end screen, but I was on the verge of quitting several times due to the endless, pointless running.As a focused, tight visual novel, Sovereign Syndicate would have been much better in my opinion.-P.S.: I almost forgot one thing. There's one part of the game that's so great that I wish the developers had given it a lot more space (or maybe even made it its own game):

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't completed the game just yet.  The 3d camera views and the way you need to look close at the screen kind of make it difficult to play in long stretches for me.  That said, this has been compared to disco elysium.  However it is a good bit different.  I saw in another comment that the card that is drawn from a deck is not returned.  That changes my thoughts on how I will play through the game.  The writing is okay but the way they keep trying to use victorian vernacular kind of makes it a little bit hard to follow.  Luckily they do let you see a translation by hovering over it.I think the system of using social skills to pass through the game.  In that way it is very similar to disco elysium.  However there are only 4 of them but they are 4 different ones for each character.I find that I like it.  I would give it a 6.5 or 7 out of 10 given that 5.5 is average.  Definitely looked for something like that because it kind of scratches the Disco Elysium itch that nothing else really has satisfied for a while now.  Plays kind of like a point and click visual novel.  They said in the discussion that if they are able to make a 2nd game there will be more character leveling up if they get the chance.  I think that would add a deal of replayability.It was done on a budget so I don't remember if there was voice acting but most of the words spoken don't have voice acting.  Which is expensive so I don't know if I hold that against them.EDIT:  I completed it.  18 chapters and about 10 hours though I think that steam went back an hour, (if you can believe that) so it is 11 possibly.    I would say that this was work the buy.  I want to see if different playthrough will yield different stories.  Kind of like... disco elysium.  I want to play the successor to this game so I would appreciate it if you purchased it so their studio could make the next one.  I just didn't like the ending all too much but it is ambitious.  Maybe a 7.5 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a couple of frustrating moments. You never know in which act a quest ends and if you have collected everything needed to move on to the next. At times, you lose the narrative thread, and you just run around London hoping to find it again.In the end, the whole story comes together. And some form of catharsis does occur. Nonetheless, writing such a complex, multi-threaded story is challenging, and the story is a bit shallow in some spots.Generally, I would fancy a bit more darkness, like in the Penny Dreadful series. It's there and even of a similar level, but it doesn't quite grip you. Perhaps due to the somewhat cartoonish design. Especially the characters.The game can be played many times. At least, once for optimists, another for cynics through the optimism mechanic. Plus, several more times to pass all the dialogue checks. I think it's impossible to complete all checks in one playthrough. It's not even about randomness, but because when a card is drawn for a check (they use cards instead of dice), that card is not returned to the deck. So, you literally have just a couple of high cards for the entire game to cover the unlikely checks.If you like Disco Elysium - definitely try, but the story itself is not that deep.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun, charming and - at times - moving game. Loved the art direction, the setting (steampunk London with gin-soused Minotaurs, tinkering-obsessed dwarves, courtesans with a heart of gold, and - of course - the most adorable automaton in the form of Otto) is brilliant. Especially enjoyed the dark humour and characterisation!There are a few moments where it is not clear where you need to go to progress the story along, but apart from that I was really impressed with how many side things there are to do. The different skills (or attributes) also clearly change certain narrative outcomes, so there is scope for replayability. Particularly chuffed, as a Londoner, to see the attention to detail with the old-school slang of the era.Recommend if you want a fun and engaging CRPG with a narrative that comes together in a fun conclusion.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll not spend time talking to this game's influences (chief among them, Disco Elysium), as I believe it does a disservice to the unique aspects of it. Chief among them, what is colloquially known as the 'zapping' system. Basically, the game takes place in a persistent world and items, interactions, etc. are acknowledged and affect the other characters you play as. It's so rare to see that tackled by a game, that the novelty alone is worth the price of admission. Overall, Sovereign does a capital job navigating you through its multiple central mysteries. The aesthetic, gorgeous, and the writing is quite good. My chief complaint, and where it unfortunately differs greatly from Disco, is that skill checks are regressed to the classic CPRG pitfall of failure simply meaning that opportunity is gone. In Disco, many checks can be reattempted, and those that can't have failure leading to unique, interesting content. With Sovereign, failing a stat check simply means a narrative dead end, and it's sad to see that, as it simply meant I felt inclined to save scum until I succeeded. Hopefully, the next game by these developers reflects a better execution of that type of "failing into content" that makes Disco such a magnificent game.Beyond that, a few bugs, and somewhat forgettable music (save the vocal performance, which was fantastic), this game was still absolutely worth the time and cost of admission.

It isn't as good as Disco Elysium but it is a good game which can be recommended to anyone who really like to read. Pricing was For me it is distracting how characters are changed every chapter and I actually prefer to have three distinct story told one after each other and not simultaneously. But after some time I get used to this. Anyway interesting story, Victorian steampunk atmosphere and resemblance to Disco Elysium and books of Terry Pratchett made this game unique. _childDocuments_.review: Game is okay, kinda similar to older TTRPG type video games. I just have a few gripes with how some things are handled, mainly with the characters and progression.The story feels stretched thin trying to encompass the three main characters, what I would recommend is set focus to one and have the others perspective take less focus. This takes away a lot of the information overload that all the characters stories have and doesn't make it easy to connect to some characters on a more personal level, a maybe easier way to solve this issue from a developer perspective might be to have the character choose a starting character and either go through their story one at a time or set Acts that need you to switch to other characters for a bit if the story relies on pieces from every story coming together, instead of the character pass along train.Quest wise, things aren't too obvious? I can't tell where I'm meant to go for some of them besides scouring everything (which can get a bit tedious at times) or quests just progressing in strange ways, so far I've only really had that problem with the journalist quest, and the locked door in the first area where you can only interact with once each character even if you find an item (like a magic lockpick for example) and still not have a new interaction.Not really big gripes and I've only just started so not sure if these will get more fleshed out as the story goes on but hearing that it's an indie game I'm well impressed with the effort that went in at least while maintaining a fair price. Overall it is an interesting game.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game that is well worth the price.Set in an Alt reality Steampunk London you follow the story of three main characters with different backgrounds and vices.It is mostly a story-heavy game, influenced by your choices in dialogueThe world it is set in is interesting and most of the characters you meet are unique, drawing you into this world.There is little to no VA in the game so if you do not like reading, this game won't be for you. If you like a good story and a new setting to get interested in I would highly recommend Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a surprise gem that might wind up being one of my favourites of 2024.I rarely play indie RPGs, but I stumbled across a review, thought it looked interesting and had a bit of spare time - and then I played it for seven hours on the first day alone because I couldn't put it down.The character writing in this is great, with some characters having a depth missing even in many AAA games - very impressive for a small-studio release. The characters can interact with most people in their small part of the world in interesting ways, and come from different backgrounds in ways that mean that people respond to them differently and some characters have access others lack (and vice versa). The characters are fleshed out and believable in a way that I'd have to go back years to think of an equivalent example of, and the dialogue is consistently good. Based on what I've seen so far, I would play the hell out of anything with Clara and Teddy in it for a lot longer than what I presume it will take to 100% this.It also takes some interesting approaches with the games systems (such as tarot cards instead of dice for success chance) that work well.One of my prevailing reactions to this game so far is that I just wish someone had thrown a bunch more funding at them - it it is a great game and I would recommend it without hesitation, but it could have caught on a lot more widely and gotten a lot more well-deserved attention if they'd had the budget for voice acting, a rotating camera, and such.I will say that I don't quite get why they started the game the way they did, because the first fifteen minutes really scream "Disco Elysium in steampunk England" - and then the rest of the game is far better and more original than that descriptor would let on.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: I am still very early on, but I fell in love IMMEDIATELY. The writing and aesthetic is fantastic, its nice to finally see some other games looking at what Disco Elysium did and applying it to other worlds and places. I can't wait to dig even deeper, and I foresee myself playing this multiple times to see just how it can play out differently based on my choices!

_childDocuments_.review: What a pleasant surprise to start the year off. _childDocuments_.review: If you liked Disco Elysium, you'll probably enjoy Sovereign Syndicate. That said, there are some key differences here.The mental narration and abilities are split between three characters, which does make for more interesting gameplay, but less interesting characters. That's true across the board - there are more transparent game systems here than in Elysium, but that overall makes for what I find to be a less interesting world. Characters are less complicated (and overall less unique!), which makes getting what you want from them easier but also less satisfying - a bookseller who believes her shop is haunted is to me far more compelling than a laundress who also operates on the black market. There's a lot less personality here, even in the early hours of the game.That's reflected visually as well - the 3D animations are jerky and the backgrounds are fine, but there's none of the artistic flair that the painted backgrounds had. I'll certainly play more - I like the systems and the world enough that I'd like to see more of it - but I don't feel compelled the way I did in Disco Elysium to chase down every little thing. Maybe that will change as I get into more of the world and its secrets, but so far this is an enjoyable but distant second to Disco Elysium.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good so far. Only gripe I have is there's no narration which I loved in Disco Elysium. The writing is good however, so it's not a huge gripe. Basically, if you enjoyed Disco Elysium, you're going to love this game. You choose dialog options from the four humors, yellow bile, black bile, phlegm, and blood that shape who your character is, just in a steampunk setting in London.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

_childDocuments_.review:
Explore an open world in this Victorian steampunk cRPG. Play as three characters with branching stories that intertwine. Investigate, interact, and take action to leave your mark on the world and its inhabitants. No random stat points here, use your skills to level them up, and trust your fate to our tarot card chance system.

So, how will you solve your problems? Combat, persuasion, magic, explosives? The choice is yours and all your cards are on the table; but be careful, the docklands aren't for the faint of heart.

Explore the back alleys, opium dens, brothels, and more at your peril, or relax and enjoy their simple pleasures. Investigate, interact, and take action to forge your own path.
_childDocuments_.name: Sovereign Syndicate

name: 1000xRESIST
detailed_description: Buzz "1000xRESIST nails what it's going for—a blend of "big idea" sci-fi and coming-of-age story." - PC Gamer "At its heights, it achieves the cerebral complexity I expect from the likes of Hideo Kojima or Yoko Taro..." - PC GamesN "It’s a lucid dream, hand crafted for you. It’s extraordinary. It’s something really very special. In a world plagued by extruded content emanating vacuously from every screen, we should be so lucky." - Giant Bomb About the Game The three time IGF award nominated 1000xRESIST is a thrilling sci-fi adventure. 1000 years in the future, humanity is all but extinguished and a disease spread by an alien occupation keeps the survivors underground. You are Watcher. You dutifully fulfil your purpose in service of the ALLMOTHER, until the day you learn a shocking secret that changes everything. In the near future we learn we are not alone in the universe. A mysterious alien race of giant entities arrives. We call them the Occupants. They are not hostile, but it doesn’t matter. Their arrival is a death sentence. Humanity is wiped out in a matter of months, succumbing to a disease the Occupants have brought to our planet. There is one survivor, a teenage girl called Iris. Somehow she is immune. 1000 years later. Iris is not only immune but immortal. She has birthed a new society consisting exclusively of her own clones. She calls them Sisters. They call her the ALLMOTHER. Unlike the ALLMOTHER, the sisters are not immune. They must wear masks 24/7 to avoid breathing the diseased air even in the Orchard - an underground bunker where they live in constant fear of an Occupant attack. The ALLMOTHER lives in her own compound on the front line of the war with the Occupants. All Sisters dream of one day being able to take the train and join her in the fight. Within the Orchard, every sister has an assigned function, while six sisters have special roles to play… Principal - Head of administration and oversight of the Orchard Bang Bang Fire - Head of military Knower - Head of knowledge preservation Fixer - Head of engineering Healer - Head of medical and cloning And you - the new Watcher . Your role is unique. You have the great privilege of reliving and interpreting the memories of the ALLMOTHER through a process known as Communion, made possible by Secretary, your floating AI companion. As the game begins, you are excited to embark on your first Communion. But all is not well. Your closest sister, Fixer, comes to you with a dangerous revelation. You have been lied to. The ALLMOTHER is not what she claims to be. Fixer’s claims rock the foundations of your world, throwing everything you know and believe into doubt. After Fixer is executed for her treason, it falls to you to discover the truth. Dive into the memories of the ALLMOTHER. Explore pivotal moments in her life from high school days and the arrival of the Occupants to the creation of the Orchard and the birth of the first sisters. Jump back and forth through moments in time within these memories to solve puzzles and access locked off areas and secrets. In between Communions, explore the Orchard - a large underground hub area which houses you and your sisters, has many characters to speak to, and holds many things to uncover. Find the truth and reclaim your legacy. Experience perspective shifts both literal and metaphorical as the game blends between 3rd person adventure, visual novel and first person walking simulator while throwing twists, turns and revelations at you until you question everything you think you know. Born from an eclectic set of inspirations, including the games of Yoko Taro (NieR:Automata), the anime of Satoshi Kon (Perfect Blue) and Naoko Yamada (A Silent Voice), and even the theatre of Robert Wilson (Einstein on the Beach), 1000xRESIST tells a story in ways only a game can while simultaneously bringing fresh ideas to interactive storytelling from theatre, dance, performance art, and cinema. Enjoy more than 10 hours of playtime brought to life with over 15,000 lines of fully voiced dialogue from a brilliant cast of Asian-Canadian actors and an incredible soundtrack from two composers. ABOUT THE DEVELOPER 1000xRESIST is created by sunset visitor 斜陽過客, an independent studio based in Vancouver (Canada) dedicated to telling diverse stories through the lens of speculative fiction. We are a group of majority Asian-Canadian diaspora creators with a decade of experience in dance, theatre, music, film, visual arts, and new media arts, bringing our background in the experimental performing arts to interactive media.
