short_description: 1000xRESIST is a thrilling sci-fi adventure. The year is unknown, and a disease spread by an alien invasion keeps you underground. You are Watcher. You dutifully fulfil your purpose in serving the ALLMOTHER, until the day you discover a shocking secret that changes everything.

_childDocuments_.review: not quite finished yet, but this has been a really spectacular ride -- one of the year's most resonant, stylish, ambitious story games. the high concept is alluring, the more personal story underlying that high concept is beautiful and thorny, and I can't wait to see how they bring this thing to its conclusion. really amazing game. jump on it!
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: I was honestly having a really good time with this game and enjoying the post-COVID story. Unfortunately I fell through the floor in Chapter 2 and now I can't progress anymore as my autosave just takes me back to a point where I fall through the floor over and over again. Not fun. I'd hope to see how this story plays out, but I'll probably just refund and watch a play through on Youtube.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST had me hooked from start to finish. This game takes full advantage of the medium to tell a beautifully rich and dense story. It’s by far one of the best sci-fi stories I’ve ever experienced and I cannot recommend it enough. The game explores themes of control, immigration, intergenerational trauma and the different ways facism can take root in a society through the lens of this settlement of clones and their relationship to the ALLMOTHER: the sole human survivor of the apocalypse. There’s more to it but I feel like describing the game’s plot any further than that would be doing it a disservice. I could happily spend hours more with this game, in it’s world and with it’s characters, but I think it’s paced perfectly. It pulls you in layer by layer, each chapter just as poignant, intriguing and heartfelt as the next and took me by surprise again and again with each revelation and explosive twist. It’s masterfully done and extremely evocative. I would say that one critique I have would be that the hub world can be difficult to navigate, especially at the beginning when you’re unfamiliar with your surroundings. A map would have been appreciated at the time however by the end of the game I was able to navigate it fairly easily by memory alone and I wouldn’t have been able to do that if the game had given me a map so I’m on the fence about it. The ending left me wanting more in the same way a good meal makes you want to keep eating after you’re full. There were several scenes I could have kept chewing on for days if the game had let me but I think they balanced it well, giving you just enough to read between the lines and keep you thinking. The game is fully voice acted and has a wonderful soundtrack, I think it’s worth every penny and fully encourage you to comb through it hair to hair.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: It is not an easy thing to describe what makes this game so compelling. While playing this game I have likened it to inspiring the same existential feelings that Evangelion did but the truth is they aren't all that similar besides telling the story of a character thrust into a role of much responsibility, and made to endure struggles and suffering that aren't their due, for no reason other than being born.Plot twist after plot twist; questions piling up with each answer; turn after turn that just keeps you hooked, always wanting to know more, always wanting to know why, how, when, WHY? Putting it down didn't help - I desperately wanted to keep playing to find out more, to continue the story, Now, having played through each of the endings, I'm finally satisfied... Which is good, because I don't think any other game, movie, or book will inspire the same feelings in me that this game does. Writing, game mechanics, art style, music, voice acting, and more, all crafted together to build a fantastic story that will keep you up at night!
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Great narrative experience. There's not much "gameplay" per se, as most of this is a visual novel with some degree of player agency (mostly dialogue). The story is deeply engaging with intrigue all the way through, with the Communion segments being an enjoyable way of exploring the mystery of the story. The pacing felt good too, plus if you're a busy person, the game has chapters that nicely wrap up so you can comfortably play the game over several sessions (I binged a few chapters nonetheless). If you want an immersive and poignant story, this is a game worth giving a go. A pleasant surprise.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely the best game I've played this year. The high points are the characters, story, and beautiful music. I don't think I've played a game this deeply sad in a while. Every character is sympathetic and flawed in some way. The way it links themes of dysfunctional families, diaspora, sci-fi concepts, loss, and the failings of structures of power is truly a wonder. One thing I really enjoyed about the writing is how it uses minor characters and dialogue that did not have much importance and calls back to them in a way that has high emotional impact. In the same vein, the game creates its own lexicon that you learn by osmosis and uses it to convey the feelings of the characters in a lot of unexpected ways.I'm grateful that there are still people out there making games with emotional resonance. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: I never even expected to like this as much as I do now.I played the demo and found it… cringe? Pretentious? Too weird for my liking? Too “anime”?I decided to give the game another chance. Everything changed the 2nd time I booted it up. I could barely even stop. The character writing, the symbolism, the *vibes*, man… I started seeing so much of myself in some characters too.It all makes a wonderful game. I thoroughly enjoyed everything.I did feel a little empty in the epilogue, but I think it’s supposed to be that way.Unbelievable experience with an unforgettable story.I recommend it to everyone, yet I know, I won’t be able to share it with anyone.Thank you, sunset visitor.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most engrossing stories I've experienced in a long time. A grand marriage of big sci-fi ideas and extremely human themes that never loses sight of either side despite the wild places that the plot takes you. Also an audiovisual treat, with consistently great scene composition and moody, evocative music.  A wildly ambitious and well-executed debut title for Sunset Visitor and I can not wait to see what they do next.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of the most heartfelt and touching stories in a video game, certainly of the past few years.Really the only negative I can think of is that I imagine what it could be with a much larger budget. It's such a shame that major companies invest so much more money in so much more terrible games when actually important and well written games like this have to make do with less.You're seriously missing out if you don't experience this game. I don't ever leave reviews generally, but it's worth it for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: I had about a million thoughts playing this game, and after finishing it, they feel impossible to summarize. This game is an all encompassing piece, it cannot be summarized, but it should be experienced. If you love sci-fi, thinking about stuff, if you love dense narrative experiences, play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: So far the concept seems interesting, but there seems to be too much about personal/national identity conflicts in the Hong Kong/China divide that frankly, I at least could do without. You know "The Last Human" trope? The final icon of our species, beloved by a future society of succesors (be it robots, clones, other races) for being an impeccable embodiment of our virtues, an icon of what made us great? Yeah, what if she was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥? And you had to bear witness to their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and how that revelation could impact your fragile society that is all that remains after an Arrival/Roadside Picnic style alien aproximation to earth killed all of humanity.It's an interesting 3d exploration adventure narrative game with a few dialogue options that so far have not offered me any control of the narrative. Will update when I finish it
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is a deeply evocative, interpretive, and allegorical piece of art. I find it very hard to talk about, not because it’s easy to spoil, but because, where do you begin with this game? Not even the game itself seems to know. Every sequence of events seems to be designed to elicit more questions than answers, every line of dialogue seems to hint at information beyond your reach yet still begs you to dissect it, often times the game feels like it's talking to you in riddles. It's a slow burn that keeps hypnotizing you with its seemingly insurmountable abstract concepts and ethereal art direction, getting lost in a maze of sci-fi warfare, interpersonal relationships that go too far and not far enough, the desperate fight for better things, but, amidst the chaos, (in my read, at least) stands a message so pristinely clear, so important and fervent, and eventually, what was once confusing starts to click. There is so much thematic depth about family, order, identity, purpose, there is love and spite and everything in-between, there is the you that remains, that remains and remains.Here's a bit of a caveat; if you don't enjoy visual novels, or at least walking simulators, you may not like this game. Almost all of it is walking around and reading/listening to dialogue, and while it has more than enough surprises in store, I think that fact remains. Pretty much all of the game is voiced, an incredible task considering the staggering amount of dialogue, and the performances are as strange and fantastic as the game itself.I feel like a story like this doesn't come too often. One that cares as deeply about its own presentation and artistry as it does about the things it has to say. There is a palpable weight in every action, every line of dialogue, every character. You just have to decide whether to carry it or leave it.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: No words.I got interested in this game some time before its release because of its visual presentation. At some point afterward, reading people's comments and reviews, I became afraid it was some sort of vacuous, pseudo-intellectual, wannabe-artsy mumbo-jumbo; you know, the sort of pretentious nonsense liked by BAs in literature who think that Metal Gear Solid is too mainstream and that whatever unoriginal doodle comes out from indie studios is the ultimate Great American Novel of our time.But no. This game is actually great—legitimately artistic and intellectual. It's my GOTY pick for 2024 so far, and one of my favorite games altogether.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: "We do not get to choose what we inherit."First couple hours I figured this game was going to be intriguing. Within six hours I thought this game was going to be pretty special.By the end I knew I would be thinking about this game for a long time to come.Avoid spoilers, go in blind. Just know that you're in for a ride.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: This is a heavy story-focused game in which you mostly run around and talk to people to advance the game, and it's damn good at what it's going for. The story was a bit hard to get into at first and it kind of meanders at times, but it is genuinely thought-provoking and emotional. Just be prepared for it being very sci-fi and very weird.Despite it mostly being a walking sim, it does do various things throughout each chapter to mix it up a bit. The graphics are simple and flawed at times and occasionally break immersion, but this game is also an example of not needing AAA graphics to have beautiful imagery.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: One of the more complicated narrative themes I've seen tackled masterfully. 1000XResist is less of a game and more of an interactive story. The story does a great job of feeding you narratives from different sources, forcing you to look and evaluate what it is you hold dear. I encountered two noclip bugs but none so big that cannot be fixed by reloading an auto save. Definitely a worthwhile story
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Finally finished, and absolutely can recommend. Complex, emotional, with a great soundtrack and voice acting.  Amazingly put together narrative that I will most likely be thinking about for some time.While there is no combat, which might turn some away, if that doesn't bother you, and you're looking for something deep, I think this would be a great choice. HEKKI ALLMO
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, remember the ladder climb in MGS3, and how despite it having absolutely bland gameplay but somehow being a highlight of the game? Imagine that as a whole game, but it somehow not getting old. Gameplay peaks in the first chapter and only gets worse as the game goes on, and yet the further I played, the more in love with it I fell. It's also not something I could really see working as a movie or even a visual novel with how the gameplay, as bare as it is, is an active part of the storytelling. It's a fantastic story with incredible worldbuilding, and I don't really want to say much more than that.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Is the narrative compelling enough to carry the game on its own?  Yes. The game's focus is the story, as told in interesting and unconventional ways that video games allow. It feels like a groundbreaking way to tell a story.I have one bone to pick with the storytelling: in many ways the story is very forcefully crammed into the contemporary dynamic between Hong Kong and mainland China and the 2019 Hong Kong protests.  It feels cheap whenever we are reminded that this game isn't about intergenerational trauma and power dynamics in general, but rather it is specifically about separatist protests stemming from Hong Kong's colonial ties to England.  Hong Kong's colonial history is a chapter that this game omits in its telling of intergenerational and diasporic trauma.  The metaphor for Hong Kong's relationship to mainland China is crudely underdeveloped, making the references all seem hamfisted (like, okay so the miscellaneous rebel is carrying an umbrella and the evil government is all colored red ... so what other comparisons are we supposed to draw? Is the ALLMOTHER England?)Even with the immersion-breaking effect of being repeatedly reminded that the game is a metaphor for Chinese regional politics, I still enjoyed the experience and would recommend. The narrative escapes the historical trappings that it is occasionally forced into, and is so rich and rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: I very rarely write reviews, but I also very rarely have the chance to experience a story like this. 1000xRESIST centers its speculative sci-fi story's heartbeat on a hyper specific character, a Canadian teenage daughter of Hong Konger ex-pats, and all her complexities and infinite possibilities. The expert weaving of multiple elements — the unique pain of those who lost the Hong Kong they spilled blood to fight for, the messy realities of different types of ethnic minorities (child of immigrants vs recent immigrant), exploration of nature versus nurture within the context of genetic information, parent-child relationships!, history's role in building the future, and good ol' Original Sin — miraculously works together use its specificity to tell a broadly relevant and relatable narrative. Gameplay is largely minimal but generally used effectively. The main space where the game takes place can be confusing to navigate, but never to the point of making me want to quit playing. The game is largely structured around running around and interacting with people and objects, with some interesting segments of time traversal (like Dishonored 2's Timepiece mechanic) and word riddles. There are many obvious comparisons to Nier Automata to be made, but the most notable to me is that this is truly a story that could only have been told via the medium of video games.As the American child of Taiwanese immigrants, 1000xRESIST hits me hard. There is a heartache I feel for Hong Kongers and a fear of losing the Taiwan we and I have in this moment. I thank all those responsible for bringing 1000xRESIST into existence and reminding me that despite how hopeless it all may seem, there is meaning in making our voices known and heard.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: 10/101000xRESIST is, without a doubt, one of the most beautifully unique storytelling experiences I’ve come across. It somehow manages to perfectly weave real-life events into an insane sci-fi narrative, full of brilliant twists and turns. While it’s not going to blow your mind in terms of gameplay, this is a story that simply couldn’t be told as effectively in any other medium whether that’s a book, movie, or comic. The fact that it’s a game allows you to step directly into the shoes of its characters, to experience time as they do, to feel the weight and distance of the world around you. It makes everything feel real in a way other media couldn’t achieve. It’s easily one of the most ambitious and thought out blends of fiction and reality I’ve ever seen. If you’re looking for a powerful narrative experience PLEASE play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Every so often a game comes along that exudes such self-confidence in its story, its themes and presentation. 1000xRESIST is one of those games. I've reached the end now, and I've been thinking about it all evening. I get the feeling this is a story that's going to sit with a lot of players for a long time to come.Truly a fantastic example of games as an art form.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: There are very few games that can be said to match either the narrative excellence of the best literature or the aesthetic impact of visual arts, yet 1000xRESIST manages to achieve both things in an incredible 15-hour adventure. If you consider yourself a "narrative gamer", this is the real deal; nothing comes close.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: wow, what a lovely experience~the whole way through, I was marvelling at just how much sunset visitor has managed to do here with so little. there is no sense of scarcity, just a true approach of abundance in the myriad of creative ways they reuse assets to create unique and stunning scenes, fully embracing the limitations of being a small studio and weaving something grand with what they have. truly impressive <3i love the aesthetics, the music is fitting, just... overall this is a such a treat to experience. it is essentially a visual novel/walking sim so one needs to approach this game as a narrative-first experience. you're mostly just being in/moving through scenes and running from one place to another, with a few surreal parts where you fly between different floating points in space. i really liked how often the traversal was woven into the story somehow, or simply provided you with space to really sink into what was going on in the story and stew in it's complications.the voice-acting is pretty decent, it has some amateur vibes at times but there's a care, earnestness and spaciousness to it all that I really liked. having mentioned spaciousness, i have to comment on the intriguing mix of headyness and embodiedness they manage here: though the story and dialogue is very philosophical, abstract and poetic, there is a sense of embodiedness that they manage to convey in the spaciousness of the characters, between characters, the many moments of quiet contemplation, the scenes that force you to slow down by taking away the ability to run, the ones that let you run but give you a vast distance to sit with... very impressive. often with these heady philosophical kind of stories, like Evangelion for instance (which I don't find nearly as similar to this as many seem to?) or Nier (to a slightly lesser extent) can get caught up in a kind of separation from the body, and while this does have a little bit of that element, it manages to ground you into the experience in a way that resonated with my bodymind in a way that all my favourite art does <3 you will feel things!there is a constant shifting of perspective going on throughout, one minute being third person, the other first person, then top-down, then side-scrolling, then you're flying around a bit, then you're maybe a different character... these are all used in very creative ways to complement the narrative and get you to shift the way you look at everything, offering a kind of complexity through constant change.And all throughout there is an emphasis on time: on past/present/future and how it all unfolds in one gloriously messy whole. the way we carry things from our ancestors, and the decisions we make or are unaware we have made and how that carries forward into the future. There is a literal time-shifting mechanic at many points where you can shift between different points in time to piece together memories and narratives that have become disconnected in their present moment. I really loved this a lot <3in all, this is a story about oppression, trauma, ancestry, time, revolution... decisions on what we want to carry with us and what we want to set aside~ all wrapped up in an incredibly cinematic package, dipped into the fabric of spacetime and recited to you as surreal poetry and prose. beautiful stuff! <3aphantasia-wise, thankfully they added a map for the Orchard, it would've been a nightmare to navigate without. that being said, the map only helps so much... i still got lost many times, including one time where i got frustrated and had to look up where something was. the waymarkers are helpful, but they are sometimes hard to see, especially if you happen to be far away from your destination (they shrink), as they are kind of transparent grey diamonds that can get lost against the background of the Orchard itself. i eventually just got the hang of the layout of everything, but ya even in the epilogue i managed to get a little bit lost, so this game has some slightly tricky elements with navigation in the Orchard if you are in any way like me and get easily lost. however, every other scene is fairly linear and clearly marked, so i didn't run into any issues outside of that one area. The game is so good though that I can forgive it for this one thing!i won't spoil anything, but i will say i got the Red ending and i loved it (it's my fave), and went back to watch all the other ones which didn't take long at all. the way the ending is structured is incredibly unique and really had me thinking and feeling through different possibilities before making any decisions. wonderful stuffso yeah, needless to say, I absolutely love this game and am v excited to see what sunset visitor does next. And in general, I'm taking this as another nod to dig more into Fellow Traveller, seeing as they also published Citizen Sleeper (one my favourite games ever!!) and others i either have backlogged or wishlisted that i'm very curious to check out (In Other Waters, The Stillness Of The Wind, Genesis Noir, Paradise Killer...)highly recommended if you want a wild yet meditative scifi that fiercely plants it's feet and doesn't just point toward the future, but to the past and present too! meeting at the messy middle that is humanity

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so, so much. It focuses on and describes experiences that I haven't lived myself, but it does so in such an enthralling, visually engaging way that I basically couldn't put it down. For a game that operates in high-concept sci-fi, with deliberately obtuse story concepts and a winding, timeline-spanning narrative for much of its runtime, the themes it explores are painfully human, knowing exactly when to twist the knife and up the agony factor and when to grant the player a little bit of a reprieve. 1000xRESIST is a triumph of a story and an amazing game.That said, gameplay is sparse - calling it a walking simulator feels a little dismissive, a little inaccurate, but the puzzle elements of the gameplay aren't especially prominent, and you spend the vast majority of your time walking around the map, talking to characters to advance the story. With so little focus on the gameplay, the story and aesthetic need to carry the experience, and 1000xRESIST delivers on this in spades. I love the core concept of a society built from ruins on the back of a single moody teenage girl, where flippant remarks and stray thoughts become the basis for scripture and holy rituals. It's a great way of conveying the alienness of the world and social structure, and the way it informs every single little thing about the world while being, in many ways, entirely impenetrable is impressive.Equally impressive to me is how those elements are used to cast back to the past and tell a much more grounded story of discrimination, "other"ness, and reactive cruelty. Like I said, it's not an experience I've lived myself, but I always greatly appreciate a game that teaches me about lives that aren't my own, and I think that 1000xRESIST's themes end up hitting extremely hard for the people who DO have first-hand knowledge and experience with what it explores. It's the kind of thing that reinforces how important it is for minority voices to be elevated, for opportunities to be granted to tell stories you don't typically see in Western media.I still have gripes, minor as they are - the in-game navigation is truly a horror show, with no in-game maps to reference for a main hub design that feels deliberately confusing, with multiple ways to access the upper levels of the main map that don't connect to each other. Objective markers are on a 2D plane separated by elevation, but it takes forever to understand how this system actually works, and it eats up a lot of time when you're trying to find how to get to a specific character with no easy reference points. I do also think that the game could stand to have a little bit more diversity in terms of its gameplay loop, but that's a relatively minor critique compared to the map thing.On the whole, 1000xRESIST was a beautiful experience, and I came away from it feeling deeply enriched. Games that are built with the purpose of telling specific life experiences don't always hit for people who haven't lived those experiences, and sometimes it can feel either like the game wasn't made for you at all or that it's preaching its message a little too hard, but 1000xRESIST manages to avoid both of these pitfalls without flinching away from the more uncomfortable elements of its subject matter. Huge recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is a game that speculates about the children of the 2019 Hong Kong protests in a Nier Automata-like setting. You jump between time periods to solve light adventure puzzles, but thematically it's all about how people remember and suffer. It's one of the most lucid expressions of generational trauma being passed on and on, making people reproduce the violence and suffering of the past.I love this game, even if I think it is too much. It's a wonderful title that resonates with me, and I still have conversations with friends who are familiar and unfamiliar with the events it depicts. The whole game is mostly just you walking and talking and remembering. Each level changes perspectives and storytelling techniques, reminding me of Kentucky Route Zero. The ultimate message of the game is something personal and local to the hearts of anyone who identifies as Chinese and/or Hong Kong.For people who aren't sure if they will get the message of the game, I would say that this game is part of an ongoing conversation that the Chinese and Hong Kong diasporas are having with each other. We don't have a good answer. In fact, I would argue that none of us are ready to have the discussion that this game raises. It's okay if you don't get it, because some of us don't.But I think it will help you understand why diasporic people can feel a certain way. It's also about understanding the legacy of a protest generation from another country. There are many parallels to our current world that we can make to understand the game, even without the context. Thanks to this game, I've had a lot of cool conversations with people who don't know much, but are willing to learn about the struggles around the world.That said, I have a few issues with the game:1) Motion sicknessI'm not sure what makes this game so exhausting for me, but the way the camera works, the frame rate, and the screen transitions in the hub world make me sick. I can only play this game in two-hour chunks. My guess is low depth-of-field.2) The waypoint system/lack of mapsThe Orchard is the hub world of the game, and it's designed to look more like a real building than a game map. This would be fine if the navigation system wasn't so unintuitive. The game gives you waypoints to talk to characters, but navigating to where they are is a chore. Sometimes you have to find the stairs hidden in the corner. Other times, I didn't realize that I had to go underground to get to a certain place. There are signs in the game, but they are confusing and vague to me -- the arrow pointing down indicates a U-turn, which I would have gotten if the game didn't have an underground level. I think I need a map or something to ground myself in these large levels because I ended up not talking to every NPC in the game. Too bad, because they say some funny things and are fully voiced.3) The zippingThere's this section of the game where you have to aim the camera and "zip" to a target node. It's weird, and it's also irritating to find the nodes because they're hidden somewhere. I'm not sure what the point of this gameplay is. I would rather the game was just a walking sim.Anyway, these are all minor complaints about a game that speaks provocatively about current events and dilemmas in diaspora life. I seriously recommend getting this game if anything in this review and others sounds interesting to you. It's a game that will stay with you and remind you the world is full of people who are suffering in their own way.

_childDocuments_.review: (TLDR; 9.5/10, buy this if you enjoy interactive fiction and sci-fi)1000xRESIST is simply an incredible experience from start to finish. I would honestly suggest going in completely blind, or perhaps only reading the short description to see if this is a game that would pique your interest in general. Be aware that it is mostly a work of interactive fiction where only your final choice determines the ending, but you still have plenty of freedom to explore the exquisitely designed scenes and talk to characters as much or as little as you want. While some of the later chapters felt comparatively slow and I encountered some confusing moments, the ending was still absolutely worth it. I really enjoyed talking to most of the characters, even if I didn't them all that likeable. The only thing that really annoyed me was the design of the Orchard - the map was very helpful, but it still took a lot of running around to get where I wanted to be, which was mildly frustrating. _childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible game that uses the medium to tell a powerful story in a way that would not work in any other medium. Sadly to talk about said story would involve much too many spoilers, so let's talk about reasons why you should play 1000xRESIST.Firstly: The design is amazing, there are unique character designs even though most of the characters you interact with are all clones of the same person (this is not a spoiler, it literally says so on the Store page).Secondly: The music is haunting, beautiful, atmospheric, tense and all helps to build on the story too, adding another element that pulls you deeper.Thirdly: The story itself, which while can't be discussed unless with someone else who has also played it, is about you being one clone out of many many others, but is also about choices, consequences, dispossession, grief, anger, love, questions, more love, and also hope.I played through this game solidly over a weekend being pulled in by the story, the way the UI changes, how the story shifts, how it uses the medium to add depth and weight, so much weight, to the story, and then leaves you with an ending that is neither right or wrong, just your ending.This game rocketed to the top of my games of all time and I will NOT SHUT UP about people playing this game if I feel like this is going to be something that they will even just get a little bit of something out of. Because ultimately this is not so much a game, but a story told using video games as a medium and an example of how games can and should be used to tell unique stories that no other medium can.

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is a brilliant game with fantastic writing and storytelling, and I would say I cannot recommend it enough, but that would probably be irresponsible.This is a game about grief, trauma, and many other things that hit incredibly hard. It is emotional, heavy, and while these aspects are not purposeless and are both in service of and served by the narrative, they are also a warning. If you are looking for a game that is short and easy to digest, this is not one of them. This is a game that will make you feel, think, and lay on the floor processing when you finish it.1000xRESIST is beautiful, haunting, heart-rending, and everything else at once. It is incredible and pulls no punches. It is a game that is nearly perfect if not for some very minor gameplay nitpicks that mean nothing in the grand scheme of things.I believe this is a story that should be experienced, but I do not recommend playing this if you struggle with stories about subjects like grief, trauma, diaspora, and mortality. If you believe that a story that focuses heavily on these topics, and in such a direct and heavy-yet precise way, hold off on it until you're ready.It is brilliant, it is beautiful, and it hurts.

_childDocuments_.review: For me, It's hard to talk about 1000xResist to a would be player without feeling like you're taking away from the experience, this is a 10h-or-so hours long narrative game, it is brisk paced, it doesnt rush the story but also doesnt never stops hitting you with hooks to reel you in back into the experience, the musical score is emotional and gripping, the voice acting is stellar and the art design is off the charts.On a more complicated topic, the gameplay; this is a fully 3D "Adventure" narrative game, it is quite simple, you run around, maybe zip around in some abstract platforming stages, interact with people and objects, sometimes in creative and unexpected ways, and thats it, there is no big emphasis on puzzles and there is no combat, however interacting and exploring 3D spaces, in my opinion, can be interesting on its own right.There is an intense care for structural detail in this game, environments are lovingly detailed and quite varied, from mundane to surreal, and in turn, you feel a duty to explore, to navigate your way thru, and to  the events that transpire there, such is your role as the player, and such is the protagonist's function, I greatly recommend talking with everyone as well, nothing in this game is filler.So if you like narrative adventures you're in the correct place, what motivates you here is the desire to know what happened, to see if theres a way to fix or heal this world, or to set it on fire. The principal challenge is to understand what you're watching and the game is not as cryptic or surreal as it may present itself, just dont expect an action or puzzle game, you're here for a story.A tagline the developers have used is  is actually quite descriptive of the game, at first I thought maybe they could be telling too much, but it is only the surface, and hearing about 1000 years of pain is not the same as experiencing them.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the more unique and intriguing stories I’ve experienced in games in recent years. An unforgettable gem! It’s a narrative focused & dialogue-heavy game (100% voiced), so don’t expect complex gameplay - you’re here for the story. I finished my playthrough after around 17 hours, but there are multiple endings. Everything in it was so high quality & well put together. It’s a fascinating sci-fi tale with many twists and turns with great writing, characters and lore, all neatly wrapped up in cool art direction with abstract/surreal elements. DO NOT spoil yourself on it, it’s best experienced fresh. Just watch the launch trailer, if you’re unsure. I paid close attention to the story & found it fairly comprehensible despite many plots & turns. It was really cool to put pieces of lore and mystery together & experience the twists. Audio is phenomenal here too. The voice acting was amazing, full of emotions and character. The OST has both beautiful & haunting compositions that fit each scene perfectly. This game kept me gripped throughout & I can’t stop thinking about it. It’s wild to think that it’s this studio’s debut. I cannot wait for their next creation. Hekki Allmo!
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: I can't state enough how happy I am that this game is doing really well! This game is gorgeous and a wild ride from start to finish, with so many little details to love and admire. Someone likened it to the experience of playing Neir: Automata for the first time and knowing that this is a story that will stick with you and will mean more to you the more you come back to it, and I can't agree more. Personally it reminds me more of the feeling of playing Signalis, with its focus on love across unfathomable time and what it means to be. I love this game, I love that both of the endings that get you to the credits are focused on whether forgiveness is possible, and neither choice is framed as bad. I love how both endings get you meaningfully different information, despite ending up in the same place. (I'm trying so hard to talk about this without spoiling anything) Those two endings being different in the way they were was such a small touch, they didn't have to do that, but I really loved it and playing through the second one got me crying all over again because of it. Basically, what I'm trying to say is; thank you Jacob Geller for making a video essay that pointed me at this game and thank you devs for making it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely phenomenal piece of storytelling from start to finish. _childDocuments_.review: You should play this game. High concept sci-fi + generational drama that unfolds like a well written play. Game play is mostly just talking to characters and exploring environments, but the way it all comes together is amazing. Touching story with a myriad of themes that i will be untangling in my head long after seeing credits. Initially seems like some things are going to be symbolic and unexplained, but by the end I understood everything that was happening and why. One thing I want to highlight is the camera. This game has one of the most expressive camera's i've ever seen. The way that it changes depending on the scene and emotion is amazing. The largest criticism i can give is that you can get lost in the free roam sections. I didn't mind because I loved the architectural design, but I could see someone getting annoyed at it. There is a map, but still.Please play this game. This is a capital L literature game.

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is a game that will leave you confused, amazed, and frightened in all the best ways possible. Once you think you've gotten it all figured out, it throws ten more curveballs at you. The characters all feel extremely real, and their development is written magnificently. The voice acting is extremely on-point, and the soundtrack never fails to set the mood while remaining an absolute bop. With fantastic characterization, a soundtrack like no other, and a truly unique art style, 1000xRESIST is ALMOST perfect.Unfortunately, it is held back by a few things. Save files don't actually save the current moment you're in - when you load a save file, you might be kicked back anywhere from a few seconds to several minutes. Additionally, the lack of graphical settings on PC leaves a game that, while unique in its art style, is downright ugly to look at at times. This is mostly due to the complete lack of antialiasing. You can tell this game was designed with the Nintendo Switch in mind first.  EDIT: The latest patch adds a map to The Orchard, which addresses my complaint for the most part.Overall, I still highly recommend 1000xRESIST, despite its few shortcomings. You'll still have a fantastic time from beginning to end. Stay as spoiler free as you possibly can, because I promise you, this is 1000% better when you have no idea what's coming your way. Hair to hair.

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is beautiful, dense, hopeful and downright horrifying. It's a shining example of how to weave interactivity and storytelling to deliver an experience like none other. There hasn't been a game that explores control, historic recurrence and intergenerational trauma as effectively as this, and there likely won't be for a very long time, if ever. The game serves as a stark reminder that those who don't learn from history are doomed to repeat it. Over and over again in an endless cycle.The way this game toys with structure, genre and gameplay conventions with absolute confidence to bring these deeply flawed, broken, complex characters and their struggles to life is just fantastic. I think the greatest thing any piece of art can do is make you feel. Make you feel enough to the point that you become inspired. Inspired to reach on out and make something of your own. To touch someone in a way that piece of art touched you. Whether it's to terrify, to move and/or amaze.I've been in a creative slump but playing this game was absolutely the kick in the ass I needed. To be reminded of just how powerful video games can be and that we've barely scratched the surface of just how cool storytelling in this medium can get.1000xRESIST is one of the greatest studio debuts ever. This is one of the greatest video game stories ever. It's not every day a developer releases their first game and it is GOAT-tier. It might be too early, but I hope sunset visitor 斜陽過客 plan to keep making games. I will be there day 0 if so. We need more voices and creators like you all in games. Phenomenal job from everyone involved.

_childDocuments_.review: After binging the entire game and 100%ing it over the course of two days, I can say with confidence that this is possibly my favorite game of all time. I certainly can't think of any other game that has had such a profound effect on me emotionally. Where I was so immersed and invested in the story that at times I lost awareness that I was even playing a game.Although the animation and controls may lack a little bit of polish at times, I got used to the controls very quickly. The gameplay is simple, revolving primarily around exploration and talking to other characters. The simplistic gameplay allows the true focus of the game to take center stage: the story and writing. I honestly can't capture how something that seems simple on the surface can hold such a wealth of complexity and meaning beyond almost any piece of fiction I have ever consumed.I've always been a sucker for post-apocalyptic settings, and this game delivers such an amazing and unique story within that genre. From almost the first moment, I was hooked by this sense of mystery and wonder. I HAD to know what happened next, what I was missing. As you progress through the story, once cryptic phrases become increasingly layered with meaning. There's so many motifs layered within one another, so many twists and backtwists, moments of intense sadness and joy, revelation and despair. Countless themes including memory, loss, generational trauma, the pandemic, and discrimination faced by Asian people.I'm not even someone that tends to gravitate towards walking simulator types games, but this game truly opened my eyes to what I might be missing out on. To the creators, I can only say thank you for producing such an incredible work of interactive fiction. This is a game that I will be thinking about for a long time...and returning to to ascertain all that I may have missed the first time around. You can return again and again, but it's never going to be the same as the first time. And that's ok.

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is one of those genuinely beautiful indie experiences that are few and far between. I'm glad the  Jacob Geller video essay "Nothing Ever Stops Existing"  convinced me to play it. I'm not too proud to admit that this game made me cry. This is a deeply emotional story that tackles a lot of deep subjects. Though it is not integral per se to the narrative, it tells the story of issues faced by Asian immigrants and the children of immigrants in North America. It deals extensively with the Hong Kong protests that garnered world-wide attention in 2019. It asks us what happens when childhood is cut short by catastrophe? It asks how important is the fight for freedom, successful or otherwise? It asks how far we would or wouldn't go for our family or mankind, especially when the choice pits the two against each other. It asks if the ends truly justify the means, and it shows that even in our darkest night, there is hope. The Sci Fi element is definitely interesting in its own right, but it serves as a great vehicle to study time, humanity, and memory. Hekki grace to the sunset visitor 斜陽過客 team! May you all be able to create even greater games in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: If I go over every feeling that this game gave me I would spoil too much. I'm not talking simple things like sad, you probably expect it to be a bit sad. It's not just surreal, you know that too already. It's not just metaphorical, you can probably guess there's a lot of that. If you're reading this review, you should play it so that you can feel what it made me feel.There's so many voices that went into the making of this game and there are so many thoughts and ideas that come through in it. There's a single unifying theme, but that theme is so multilayered that it is frankly astounding just how in-depth this game explores that theme, That theme is not just a theme, it is something that has been experienced, and deserves you to experience it. Just remember to remember and be the witness it needs.Thanks to my friend for making sure I witness this story myself. I've been given a story to remember.

_childDocuments_.review: A storytelling and artistic masterpiece. If you've ever wanted to play a game that will make you cry from witnessing the pure beauty of a story about love, loss, bonds, family, reflection, and the power of choice and the complexity of morality, this game is one that hits that nail on the head. When you feel like you are the main character of the game, that's how you know they've done it right. To call this game poetic is an understatement.

_childDocuments_.review: A narrative focused adventure game where you play as a clone that worships an immortal human called the “ALLMOTHER”, living underground (along with other clones) 1000 years after the rest of humanity was wiped out. You spend the game jumping into the ALLMOTHER’s memories, learning more about her life and gradually realizing she’s not quite the divine being she assumes herself asI will say initial impressions weren’t exactly great, it’s a bit lacking in presentation more than I’d like (though understandable given it’s the first game from this studio) and I feel like the first few chapters were somewhat boring. It isn’t really helped by the sections where you need to run around the Orchard talking to the other Sisters, which I just found annoying after a while since it’s a pain to navigate. The voice acting is… fine, though I won’t deny the flatter delivery took me out of some scenes at times. Aside for those gripes though, it does reveal itself to be a pretty ambitious sci-fi story worth sticking through, and it builds on its initial premise in a really interesting way by its end (if making it somewhat long winded)

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST defies easy labels.  It's a walking simulator/visual novel.  It's a story about apocalypse.  It's a story about family.  It's a story about inheritance, and what is passed on across generations.  It's a story about betrayal.  It's a story about truth and justice.  It's a story about the malleability of history.What 1000xRESIST is, however, is one of the most striking examples I've ever seen of gameplay being used to present and augment a narrative, and it excels.  Absolutely incredible work with striking visuals, incredible music, simple yet emotional voice acting, and dead certainty about what story it's telling and how it's going to accomplish it.1000xRESIST is an easy top-flight GOTY candidate and should not be overlooked.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best story in a game I've experienced this year, and definitely an all-timer.This game should be experienced completely blind, so I don't want to talk about the themes this game covers - but I can almost guarantee the scope is  than you think it is, based on the trailers etc. that you've seen on this store page.Recommending this game comes with a few caveats though, that really should be mentioned (spoiler free):1) This game is essentially a third person 'walking sim', or maybe more accurately, a visual novel where you can freely walk around spaces and interact with things.90% of the time you spend in 1000xRESIST will be walking around and talking to people. There is no combat, and only some very light puzzling.The story is more than strong enough to carry this in my opinion, but this might be a dealbreaker for some.2) You might have the impression based on the game's marketing and overall aesthetic that it is heavy on the standard anime tropes and stylings - I know I thought this going in.This isn't the case whatsoever. It might look reminiscent of anime such as Evangelion, but that's where the similarities end.To clarify, this wouldn't have inherently been a bad thing anyway, but different people have different tastes and tolerances for this sort of thing, so just wanted to put that out there. If you normally avoid those types of games and stories, I would still recommend this to you.3) The game's opening act isn't , but it's the weakest part of the package and takes a bit to properly get going. I urge you to give the game some time if you're not feeling it in the intro (I wasn't). Let it cook.Mark my words, 1000xRESIST is a game we will be talking about years from now. It is a true modern classic and a landmark achievement for narrative in the medium of videogames.If you're the kind of person that seeks out strong stories and/or unique experiences in your games, you owe it to yourself to play this. _childDocuments_.review: A phenomenally well-written adventure. Obviously won't be for you if you don't like games where reading is the main course but if you do - this is a real treat. It's really more of a visual novel that allows for 3D movement. I thought the story was fantastic, and the way it interweaves the themes of motherhood, the tribulations of the Hong Kong diaspora, freedom vs conformity, hanging onto the past vs embracing the future - it's all very impressive. And it packages it all up in a science fiction thriller/mystery that never runs out of twists and turns. If I had one criticism, its that, while being a relatively short game (8 hours for me) it does feel a little overlong/self-indulgent at parts - particularly towards the end where I felt a slightly more abbreviated conclusion would have had greater effect. Still, it's hard to begrudge a game that is partly about the temptation to linger in the past a little extra lingering with its characters. If I had a second criticism its that the "game" parts of the game can be a bit of an annoyance at times. I did like that by the end of the game I had an intimacy with the hub area you return to over and over - but it didn't alleviate the often tedious and confusing time I had navigating it for the first half of the game. And I honestly don't know what they were thinking throwing in a single timed section at the game's close. It's not difficult but it does feel wildly out of place with everything else.Still, those quibbles aside - this is one of the most memorable game stories I've ever played - I look forward to whatever they create next with great anticipation.

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xResist is a well-crafted but somewhat obtuse VN-style experience that I generally enjoyed.The narrative is split up into three parts - "Watcher" and her daily life in the Orchard, Iris and her struggles with her family / friends before the events of the game, and a third part that requires spoilers to say. The stuff with Iris, Jiao, and her family was the strongest here in my opinion, a very deep narrative that has the potential to impact people on a personal level. The stuff with Watcher was also good, but it was much closer to "generic, vague, lore-heavy sci-fi" than the other part.The game plays out like a "walking simulator" with more dialogue. Go to a place, talk to a person, go to another place, talk to the "right" person, advance the story. Very simple.However, the layout of the Orchard is completely nonsensical and wastes the player's time, even with a map. Waypoints don't help a whole lot because a waypoint could be directly ahead of you, but you still have to go halfway around the circle, then come back around, to reach it. Unfortunately this isn't something that can be fixed, it's an integral part of the game.The game's narrative is presented somewhat non-linearly. This makes it interesting and intriguing, but very hard to keep track of. In a future update, I would love to see some sort of "recall" feature where you can just view summaries of what Watcher has experienced, and the communions you've went through. There were lots of times when an old plot point was brought up and my first reaction was, "huh?" because I didn't note other plot points down.The game is visually distinctive, though falls short in some lighting scenarios, especially in the Orchard. Some of the cinematic scenes are very successful. The character designs are appropriately urban-punk. But what took me out of it sometimes was that characters' mouths do not move when they speak. That's not a problem when all but a few of the characters in the game wear face masks, but for Watcher, Iris, Jiao, and the parents, it breaks the immersion for sure.I'd be interested in going through the game again after more updates have been made, and I certainly intend on snagging a physical copy once one is released. But in its current state, 1000xResist is a good but flawed 3D visual novel with an interesting hook.

_childDocuments_.review: As a local Hong Konger who witnessed and somewhat overcame my fear of potentially being brutally beaten to death and imprisoned for years by actually joining the protests in 2019, I have never been able, and I believe I still am unable, to watch any documentaries capturing what happened in the second half of that year. I was essentially traumatized in the aftermath, a fate I think also befell most who joined or experienced the protests in one way or another. Imagine how "peaceful" Hong Kong once was and, all of a sudden, the police were heavily armed, wearing black masks that covered their entire faces and removing their identification numbers. They were intentionally depersonalized, and we were strategically dehumanized by being called "cockroaches," a pest fated to be eradicated. The rest is history. We used to joke that everyone in Hong Kong knows what tear gas smells like after around 10,000 rounds were fired in total. And we all know what the masks in the game are protecting the characters from.That being said, I eventually played this game, as a "veteran gamer" who thought a game was "less real" than reality itself. I was half-right (I won't spoil the story), but I was surprised at how it managed to rewind what happened in Hong Kong in a way that evokes memories without unnecessarily rubbing salt in the wound. Of course, I imagine it must be much easier for a Hong Konger to spot the subtext behind the storylines, but I still have to admit that at times, I had little idea what the story "definitely" allude to (yeah I know this statement is absurd). Curiously, the distance from—or space created outside of—"reality" is actually therapeutic for me, allowing me to genuinely catch my breath in the prison of traumatic memory. In a sense, this game, which may be classified as a "walking simulator" (I assure you there is more to it than just "walking" though :)), does a wonderful job of granting me the psychological space, with scenes thoughtfully and intricately crafted, that allows me to navigate the experience of hopes, fears, and desires (and, unfortunately, also sporadic verbal or physical violence directed at those who were seen to "stand in our way") shared by most protesters and many Hong Kongers. Seen this way, this is a game that offered me the privilege to "replay" pieces of memories of what we went through, but at my own pace. With the "just-enough" contextual cues, the buried hopes came alive again, and I was also able to confront my fears once more. I shed a tear midway through the game, but that was more of a catharsis than sadness.Obviously, I am heavily biased when it comes to evaluating this game, but I think it doesn't really matter whether you are familiar with what happened in Hong Kong in 2019. There are themes that are universal and seen everywhere in the world, particularly at this moment when the desire to live life to the fullest is systematically punished, if not trampled. There are many people out there who have strived to defend their homeland from ruthless invasions or persecutions of overwhelming forces masquerading as "self-defense" or "maintaining national security." If you can even remotely relate to these sufferings or can imagine what they might be like, then I wholeheartedly recommend this game to you. It is not just a very well-made and polished game but also features tiny delicate touches that resonate with gamers here and there. I would like to express my deepest gratitude to the developer of the game, which has become integral to my personal narrative of what my fellow Hong Kongers and I have experienced. Game on and fight on.

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea what the reviews were talking about this game has no hook or drive to make you want to play it. One review I saw said "I walked into this game knowing nothing about it (and you should too!)" and that was a terrible recommendation. The opening scene is a murder and there's sad music playing with the characters are waxing poetic, but I have no idea who these people are. They're introducing these characters like I missed a 300 page manga prologue or something. Why would I care if this person died or that person left or what have you when I have no idea what's going on."....Don't forget to clean that ♥♥♥♥ from under your bed," "....I wont...." are actual lines said in dramatic suspense not 5 minutes into the game. Like some sort of inside joke I'm supposed to be laughing my ass off about.In my time playing, I had a few  dialogue tree options I could choose one of three choices from. *Literally* only the first choice did she actually say anything remotely similar to what I selected. It's entirely possible that the game intended these to be internal monologues that I'm having to select but the way they were presented at first makes them seem like choices and they weren't at all. It was just filler in order to get you to press A once every few minutes. You don't have to give me a false sense of input only to ignore my choices. There's games I've played that have literally no dialogue choices that are more interesting than this one.This runs like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ PC port. Like I saw the reviews say it's a Switch game and it FEELS like it. Like full minute loading screens for literally 5 lines of dialogue before another full minute loading screen. ALSO THE LAG IS BAD. I'm walking around doing nothing and I can see the whole environment lagging like I'm playing some mmo on my phone.I had issues with the camera and got so fed up at one point I just started sprinting through the levels trying to get past all the dialogues that I have no input in or care for. _childDocuments_.review: You already know that something titled  is going to be some pretentious, existential ♥♥♥♥ à la Evangelion, so if that isn't your vibe turn back now. Fortunately that is my vibe, so I dig this a lot. And if the title doesn't tick you off that this game is weird, then the Steam description definitely will; this game has the kind of lore, story, and world that would make Hideo Kojima and Suda51 blush. It's 1000 years in the future and everyone's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dead. Well, not  One girl managed to survive the infection which led to human extinction: Iris, a living, breathing Mary Sue who's not only immune to the disease, but is also immortal too. Developing a God complex larger than Kanye West's, she renames herself Allmother. Since she's the only one in an underground bunker called the Orchard, the Allmother creates new life - because she can do that now apparently. Deciding that men are cringe, she creates six sisters to assist her: Knower, Fixer, Bang Bang Fire (lol), Healer, Principal, and Watcher. Each of them have their own role and function in the Orchard.You are Watcher. As Watcher, you get to be a peeping Tom and explore the Allmother's memories through a process called  Through communions, you find the answers and truths to  world and characters, but you'll also be asking yourself many new questions as well. These mysteries are what drives the game's narrative, and it's very well paced throughout - it is incredibly hard to predict what will happen next in the story (in a good way).And if it isn't obvious, this is a very story-focused game. In fact, calling this a  is almost a little too loose. This is basically a visual novel with some walking simulator elements. You definitely don't want to boot this up with gamer brain enabled, because if all you care about in games is shooty-shooty bang-bang, you're going to be disappointed. The game description mentions there are puzzles in this game, but that's honestly a bit of a stretch too. You should be buying this game for the crazy dystopian world and narrative, and nothing more.There are a handful of issues with the game worth noting. Many of the issues derive from a general feeling that the budget for this game was lower than a pub crawl for me on a Friday night. Art and animation feels amateurish, and occasionally the voice actors deliver lines poorly (though for the most part they did a great job). Environments and assets are often recycled and reused in the game, and although the narrative supports this, it's still clear that this was a clever and purposeful way to cut down on the budget.These issues are easily overlooked however because the world and story is so fantastic. I was mildly disappointed by the ending (I felt like the epilogue could have been longer), but other than that I was completely hooked throughout. There's a lot of themes in here not explored very often in game stories (existentialism, diaspora, crazy sci-fi settings), so it's always great to see cool and unique ♥♥♥♥ like this being created.Hekki grace to the developers. I hope they get the opportunity to make more games in the future - they're clearly very talented at what they do.Overall: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Everybody already said that the narrative is amazing, I can only confirm that. One of the all time best game narratives. _childDocuments_.review: I could try to thinkpiece this out, but I'm no English Major and it'd probably read like word salad. Watch me give it a shot anyway!For some people, this is going to be a game where 90% of your playtime is spent going "Okay wait back up, what's happening" even when you do your best to pay attention. I was there for a while, but really getting stuck in and absorbing every bit of the world presented, linear as it is, actually reveals it to be wildly interesting. What's shocking is that it succeeds in doing something that I haven't really felt 'worked' since the Star Wars: Clone Wars tv series - it gives you an expansive cast of clones and manages to make you actually care about them. They all have opinions, are flawed people, don't communicate perfectly and very much experience love imperfectly in a society that probably shouldn't have been able to spring up in the way it did (and is pretty horrible to think about once you know *how* it did) And yet, you *do* see them as people, even the ones who are standoffish or even go off the deep end. But that's just in the roughly present-based time period of the narrative. There's so much beyond that, so much pain to process, missed chances, bad decisions each character makes... It's a heavy work, and I love it for that. _childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST tells an incredible story full of very heavy themes - parenthood, generational trauma, alienation, loss, totalitarianism, and more. It does this using an incredibly intriguing world that hooked me from the start, trying to figure out what was going on. It delivers multiple strong messages throughout its chapters, and not least with its ending. And yet, despite this, I never felt like the game was preaching to me or telling me what to think. It simply presents a people, circumstances, and their actions, and trusts the player to make up their own opinions along the way. Any fans of visual novels, walking simulators or "choice games" will not regret playing this game.It even manages to defy some common pitfalls with "choice games", specifically endings - not by avoiding them or throwing infinite budget at them, but by leaning into them, which I found really cool.My only criticism of 1000xRESIST is that it does fall a bit short in the gameplay department. It has a few mechanics to break it away from being a total "walking simulator", but I ultimately feel like they are necessary to tell the story.Sunset Visitor has gained a fan in me with this game, and it deserves it's Overwhelmingly Positive - as of writing - label 100%.

_childDocuments_.review: What a creative and original story, just wow. Only marred by its gameplay, which is ambitious at times but can be tedious, unfocused, literally directionless as it oftentimes doesn't tell you what you need to do or where anything is, which is extremely compounded by the byzantine level design of its main setting. All that aside though it's a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ interesting story! Finished in under eight hours, and a solid hour of that was "c'mon game just get me to the next plot point". Still, that's a pretty good ratio of good:badVery pointed critiques/explorations of global crisis responses, authoritarianism vs individualism, survival vs dignity, generational trauma, etc all in a cool sci-fi setting through a deeply personal lens of the child of Hong Kong expats (you can litcrit it as a subtle anti-CCP text). It kind of felt like Everything Everywhere All At Once at times, SCP at others, What Remains of Edith Finch in random places. The story, gameplay, and art style all deftly switch genres throughout to fulfill a very deliberate vision. I don't want to give away too much here but I already have!Despite the genre fluidity, the work as a whole is cohesive and sharply thematic, clearly something where everyone working on it was on the same page. I want to give the lead writer in particular their flowers because man this really felt like a magnum opus communication of their lived experience and a vivid exploration of identity/personality. Parts of it reached high art.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never struggled more on recommending a game, but 1000xRESIST's story is just too good for me not to. I can't say much about the specific things I loved without spoiling, so I'll just say 11/10 on the story front, no notes. The humor is super up my alley, I love how campy it can be while also having really genuine and vulnerable moments as well. So, why then do I struggle to recommend it as I sing its' praises? If you get ANY kind of motion sickness or migraines from games you're going to have to plan recovery time after playing into the equation. There were multiple times I had to stop playing and lie down (especially the singular timed section of the game; I can compensate a lot of times for the motion sickness, but not when I have to rush too! And replaying a challenging section of a game is only fun if it's not actually hurting to do it, you know), or avert my gaze and fumble around using my peripheral vision because an effect on the screen was making me sick. It makes it hard to want to replay a game that is practically BEGGING to be replayed multiple times for better enjoyment of the story. The ability to turn a few visual effects off would be a game changer for me, personally.Devs DO get bonus points for giving us the option to turn off high pitched sounds though. That was really appreciated and thoughtful. I wish all media had this option.In the end I decided to give it the thumbs up because, as important as accessibility is to me, it's sunset visitor's first game it seems, and they already did more with that one accessibility option than a lot of other games do. I'll cross my fingers and hope they consider adding more accessibility options in the future.Plus, not everyone has these particular struggles of course, and those who don't SHOULD 100% try this game, there's no other good reason not to in my humble opinion. The story is even BETTER than you expect it to be, I promise you.Ultimately I'm left with a lot of hope and excitement for future sunset visitor games! I'm very hopeful the next game might have more accessibility options so even MORE people can experience the incredible storytelling they're capable of. Congrats to everyone involved on your well earned acclaim!

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is an incredibly ambitious narrative adventure game I will be thinking about for many years to come. It toes the line between being visually and narratively experimental without (for the most part) going too far such the player is left adrift. Its universe is unbelievably well thought out and the characters are all very distinct from each other, which is a real feat given how many there are. I'd also like to pay special attention to the game's unbelievably diverse and affecting soundtrack, which does a lot of heavy lifting to bring the scenes and ambiance of the game home. I did have a few qualms with the game: I think it can feel a bit overwritten at times, and after what are IMO the game's highlights in chapters 6 and 7 which really do a lot to bring home the game's idea of how generations of people fight different versions of similar conflicts (the Hong Kong riots dovetail nicely with what's going on with the main characters in the "present"), the last few chapters felt a bit meandery to me; I often didn't feel that I was getting much new information or different perspectives on existing information, and I'm not completely sold on the way the game wraps up. I also just never loved the mechanic of flinging Watcher to the floating rings to get over gaps, it always seemed a bit out of place and gets overused. I also found navigating the Orchard to talk to all NPCs very cumbersome and feel it could have a lot better designed so that getting new opportunities to discover what's going on with all the NPCs feels exciting rather than a chore. All that said, I would highly recommend this game to anyone who's looking for an experience that in many ways attempts to push the boundaries of storytelling in games, that clearly wears influences like NieR and Evangelion on its sleeve without ever feeling like an homage or, worse, derivative.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best narrative-focused games made in years, and up there in my favorite stories in almost all media in general. Great soundtrack, VAs, and amazing use of camera angles, close ups, lighting, and more, to convey all emotions you can think of despite the lack of facial animation. If anyone wants to get immerse in an amazing story, where you feel and go through the same struggles as your protagonist this is the game for you. This game is deeply intimate and emotional, and at the same time tackled many, grand scale issues that any generation could feel relating to.I recommend going in blind into this game, as once finished you will see previous actions by all the characters in a different light, or understand more the subtext behind their words, and maybe that can ruin the experience of being just like the protagonist, Watcher, in search for answers and knowledge that everyone seems to know but you.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid, dramatic, beautiful. Think of it mostly as a visual novel with some walking.Definitely slow at times, but makes up for it with some well-constructed and delivered emotional punches. A bit of storytelling whiplash mid-way through (with a whiff of DDLC) but it does come together.The experience is a magical-realism mash-up of political protests in Hong Kong; a feeling of immigrant displacement; the calamity and rebirth of Neon Genesis Evangelion; and the archetype-based characterization (reminds me particularly of the play "Tamara", but I'm sure it's a trope used in many other places).The whole thing is a good length (not too long unless you achievement-hunt it, which I did, but you probably shouldn't). The ending is pleasantly open, and interesting to explore, though more variety would have been cool.All that said, the darn glasses just strike me as impractical.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot give this game higher praise than that I was so enthralled by its narrative, I played all 10 hours in one sitting. The fact the game hasn't blown up to the scale of other indie darlings is baffling to me just as much as with In Stars And Time.The storytelling is masterful, balancing themes such as the Hong Kong protests, generational trauma, always living in the fear of becoming a totalitarian state with such personal stories. It doesn't insult the player with false platitudes and presents the world as it is - but with hope for creating something better for those who come after us.The story takes you through beautiful vistas, dreams and memories of the so-called Allmother. And even though you might notice some corner-cutting (such as no animation for lips or reused assets and levels), I don't think they could warrant any sort of harsh criticism. The game is still gorgeous and the fact every single line is voice acted brings out the character in every scene. This is truly one of the best games of the year that no fan of deep narratives should miss.
