_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so if I could I would give this game something in between thumbs up and thumbs down.But as that is not possible, I chose the thumbs up option. However, this is a little more nuanced than a simple "game good" or "game bad".The setup of this game is unique, and quite intriguing at first. You play as Watcher and connect with different people to relive their memories. From there, you learn a lot about the status of the world, how it came to be and about different characters.All of this is more than heavily inspired by NieR:Automata. The vibe is similar, and some major plot beats are the same (A2 in NieR:Automata when you meet her for the first time:  ) which is apparent from chapter 1.All of this is very good! If not predictable, if you played NieR:A.The gameplay is basically just walking around, talking to people or inspecting the environment.The problem in all of this is that it is not consize. The dialogue with characters is really great, as long as they are talking about events or locations or characters in the game world. One characters start talking to each other about their feelings, the dialogue becomes honestly just a mess. Gibberish. In a normal conversation, two people will react through spoken words to what the other person has just said. In this game, the dialogue is disjointed. As if two people are having a monologue alternately, without even reacting to whatever another character has just said. It is just weird. Here is an example, that I (partially) made up to prove this point:Character A: "What is there left for you? They gave up everything... just for you"Character B: "A dull knive isn't really a knive."Character A: "I see. Would this have given them peace, knowing you performed your function after all? I wonder."This could be directly from the game, I am not kidding.This dialogue is so bad, even AI could have done it better. But this critisizm weirdly only applies when characters talk about abstract topics however.A second thing I quite dislike are some of the walking sections, that just feel designed to waste time.Ex: You are exploring a room, rewinding time to see what transpired. You rewind time once. The interaction prompt is in the middle of the room. You rewind it again. This time, you need to go to upstairs to trigger the event.Third rewind. Downstairs again. Fourth. Upstairs. Fith, downstairs. You get the point.All of this could have been done with significantly less running from A to B.Then, in chapter six or so there are some "quizzes", in which you have to answer a gibberish question in the style I detailed above with an equally gibberish answer. Good luck figuring that out. Basically trial and error.Lastly, the motivation of a big, big big big character is left unknown - you get their backstory, but none of that helps creating any morivation for their future acts whatsoever, making all of this essentially feel really random, add to that some large plotholes and there you go. In the end, this is very unsatisfying.As a final verdict, I'd say play it for the atmosphere and not the plot. Unraveling the mystery is well done, but once you are past the mystery everything falls apart. In the end, the game felt weird - the good kind of weird. Yet, not good enough to fully recommend this game.Six to one.

_childDocuments_.review: Very rarely do I encounter a Visual Novel that draws me in line. By line. By line. Let alone one that raptly makes use of its 3D environment to provide stunning visuals and cinematography. It is staggering to me the depths with which it feels every spoken word, every press of the A button, is in itself a form of art. I can't remember the last time a Visual Novel stuck with me in such a way that I cannot get the words out of my brain. Not just the overarching themes or the aesthetics, but the  themselves. That I find me repeating it to myself so I won't forget. Brains are so good at holding onto clutter. And yet I am filled with this game's words. Its poetry. I really cannot speak too much of the story because to do so would be to spoil your experience of it. But it is a masterclass of narrative expertise.To put it another way, at times 1000xRESIST feels like a bowl of noodles. Its concepts, its themes, are these noodles. You take a bit, and someone comes along and pours in more noodles to replace what you already ate. And you feel so engorged by the midpoint that you're not sure you can handle any more noodles, that the bowl will overfill and spill out everywhere, but somehow it remains and remains and it's still a giant ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bowl of noodles.A really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good giant ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bowl of noodles.It's not without flaws. The hub world can be excruciatingly difficult and frustrating to navigate. There aren't many gameplay elements, and the ones that do exist are minimal. The opening is long and I had a headache trying to bite into too much at once. But once you hit a certain point in the story, you'll be so enraptured it will be difficult to put the game down. And when you do, you'll still be thinking about it.Absolutely one of my favorite, most well-crafted stories of all time. The developers should be proud.------There is a you that remains and remains.There is a nearness and its gravity is echoing.There is a truth and a choice that must be made.Resist. Resist. Resist. A thousand times, resist.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this even if you aren't a fan of narrative driven walking simulators. There were twists and turns that I wasn't expecting and kept me wondering where the story was going. I experienced two different endings, I don't know how many there are in total. I'll be keeping an eye on this developers future projects.I do have two complaints; navigation in the hub city is a challenge that probably inflated my playtime by a few hours. The other is after completing one of the chapters you get shown a splash screen with the developer and publisher logo and  thrown back to the main menu which was confusing. _childDocuments_.review: so many things to say...where do i starti love narrative games like this, so i knew going in that i would at the very least enjoy this game.i did, more so than i expected.this game is less so a game, and more so an experience, allowing you to walk around in memories and scenes from the past, and letting you commune with ghosts from another time. the compositions of these scenes were what stuck out to me the most, packed with so much detail and environmental storytelling. you get a sense of the place and the people of that time, the internal landscape of the characters and the oddly beautiful artistry of the world's destruction. this story just couldn't have been told in any other medium, and i mean that in the best way possible. this game doesn't hold your hand when it comes to understanding or interpreting the story. though it can be overwhelming at times, it strings you on through these dreamlike scenes  packed with vague dialogue that seemingly allude to things we aren't aware of yet. even as you reach the end and things begin to clear up, the narrative never fully explains itself, only becoming more interpretive as we descend deeper into the past. this is a game that pushes the medium to its limits in how it presents its story to us, with so much subtext, poetry and ultimately interpretation left up to us, the watcher of these memories. while little is truly explained to us by the end, i still can't shake the overall impression this game has left on me. namely: hope, forgiveness, love, nostalgia, tragedy, faith. there's so many themes relating to intergenerational trauma, familial angst, the asian diaspora, loss and love, hardships and tragedy. this is a generational story deeply imbued with a sense of humanity throughout and a sort of wistfulness. an unnameable longing for the small, mundane things in life such as a bowl of noodle or brazenly running down train tracks to nowhere while the world around you has irrevocably changed and nothing's quite the same as it used to be. there is a very human portrayal of the characters in this game, despite the traditional human conventions and etiquettes of the past being lost on most of our characters, they act as any flawed individual would when put in bleak situations. they hurt each other, run away, fight but also reconcile. by the end, we are shown that no one is beyond forgiveness. there are no true villains in this game, just people who've been deeply hurt and wronged by a world that couldn't care less about them. having finished the game, i was left with a profound emptiness by the end. i felt like i had been on a journey alongside these characters, and i remembered everything. when i think of this game now, i remember this quote: it didn't matter how things turned out in the end. it didn't change anything. but it still matters that the love was there.

_childDocuments_.review: I put this in the same league as those "Once in a generation" types of games we get every once in awhile. Games fueled by a ton of talent with tons and tons of passion for the story they have to tell. The game has tons of twists to keep it interesting, but it kept me interested with every chapter as you're slowly unraveling its plot. I found myself just so invested in what it had to tell.The game is so clearly inspired by the developers' experience with the COVID-19 pandemic, Hong Kong protests, authoritarianism, and generational trauma. It's such a beautiful story that doesn't necessarily try to answers questions like, how do we govern ourselves? When is somebody past the point of forgiveness? At what point do we let go of the past? But it does put you in a position where you can try to answer that for yourself. It's a game that feels so much like the developers love humanity, for all the pain and joy we create. I just know this will be a game that will sit with me for quite a while and I will continue to annoy my friends until they play it.There is a choice. And we will not make it.

_childDocuments_.review: Insane feat in storytelling from an indie team and for games in general. Literally some of the smoothest, realistic, readable/understandable dialogue I've seen in a narrative based game (especially in such a non-linear and wild story like this one). The voice acting is A++, some of the best I have heard in any game ever honestly. 80% of the words coming out of characters mouth felt profound even when it wasn't. Zero of the lines ever really hit me in a way that took me out of the immersion of the story, with no awkward writing or deliveries that this sort of game can be prone to. All while still retaining that feeling and vibe of experimental indie originality. What an achievement this game is honestly.::: Things I liked :::- The whole thing was so interesting from start to end. Really one of those games you go tunnel vision on for the last 3-4 chapters where nothing else in your life exists again until you see how it plays out.- Controls and movement are super responsive. Character traverses the levels fast enough and has enough things to interact with or talk to along the way that you never feel like you are spending hours just walking from point A to point B.- Again, incredible narrative design, characters, dialogue.- About 3 times as much story as I thought I was getting myself into.- Crazy narrative design that is actually follow-able thanks to the care that's gone into the dialogue.- Hits you in the existentialism bones real hard- The music (Fixer's Song extended is 10/10, probably one of my favorite game tracks going forward)::: Things that could have been improved :::- The levels at times felt a little like VRchat worlds at times. That's kind of just a byproduct of using Unity 3D unfortunately. Unless you have a whole team dedicated to hours of detailing and tweaking the look of things it will always kind of have that Unity look to it. That being said it really doesn't matter and the levels still communicate the vibe and story convincingly.- Felt the game opened stronger than it finished. The first half is pretty much a perfect game/story. The second half starts going off the rails (not necessarily in a bad way) and doesn't feel as concise(?) and starts to feel a little more chaotic narrative design wise. It adds a lot of new stuff and layers very quickly (vague to avoid spoilers). Its definitely a much different game that maybe what you thought it was when you started. But unlike a tonne of narrative focused games, it actually does have an ending for the buildup it created which is so important. Could it have tied it up a bit better? Maybe? Do I have any recommendations of how? Not at all.::: End :::An absolute sleeper hit. So much care has been put into this game across the board and it all pays off. Saw it back when it released and thought it looked interesting, I am so glad I got round to playing it. When people ask me what are good story-focused games, this makes a top spot on the list easy. No question.

_childDocuments_.review: An unequivocally beautiful piece of art. If you're reading the reviews here wondering if or not to play this, just do it. read nothing more, go in blind and experience it. I am only jealous I can never do the same again. Now please excuse me while I gush for a bit.If you need more info, 1000xRESIST is a wonderfully creative story telling experience that will suck you in with intrigue, but ultimately win you over with its heartwrenchingly personal but of course relatable tale that juxtaposes the clinical sci-fi setting it places it in. That's not to say the visuals are bland at all, the level of cinematography on show in some scenes is is sublime with a masterful attention to lighting and framing, all in service to elevate this already gripping tale. Oh and don't forget the soundtrack; with a particular focus on emotive piano sores and spashes of synths & reverb (in keeping with the sci-fi setting), these tracks will be on repeat for me long after the credits roll. This story is also admittedly dialoge heavy, but my god did the voice cast deliver here. The direction here must have been on point because the emotion dripping over every line perfectly fits the scene in which it is delivered. The only factor that may be considered a downside to some is the actual gameplay; its simple exploring and light puzzle solving that's unlikely to fluster anyone, but i'm sure its by design. If you want deeply personal, emotionally conflicted but unforgettable story with little else to distract you from that, then try this.To everyone at sunset visitor, thank you. You've made something special that will leave a lasting mark on myself and many others. I wish you all the success and hope you get to continue creating experiences like this for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a moment that came perhaps eight or nine hours into my 20 hour experience... I was standing in the corner of an apartment, looking back and forth between a piano and a shelf. Outside, a heavy rain fell. One of my sisters stood at the window, transfixed by what any of us players would take for granted, perhaps even as a nuisance. But here was a character who saw this rather familiar event as mesmerizing; a fantasia come to life. Even if it was just in a memory we were both witnessing. It's the small, seemingly mundane, ultimately sublime moments like this that I search for and savor in games. They are rare, but signify the accumulative and immersive power of the medium like nothing else.  It's something that hinges so much on the developers making the space for the player to just stop and ponder; to look, taking a breath in, suddenly realizing that the tears are swelling up.  By this measure, Sunset Visitor's debut is a staggering work, standing out in this era of beige sci-fi (near-future, corporate whateverness) and going for something with the scope, depth and humanity of authors like Samuel R. Delany, Ursula K. Le Guin and Octavia E. Butler. Of course, this is a video game, and so its nesting-doll narrative flows within that accumulative effect this medium does best, rendering mechanics and POVs quite clearly and lovingly adapted from Nier: Automata. Its exploration of the Asian diaspora, and specifically the 2019 Hong Kong movement in a tale that spans a thousand years and a new frontier for the heirs of humanity, is densely layered and always compelling. It's also one of the first great COVID-era pieces of art; something that reflects the paradigm shift of the last four years with a great knowing and empathy, infusing real world feeling into another world entirely with grace and melancholy. If you're a fan of the surreal, wistful road-tripping sci-fi of Kentucky Route Zero, the scum-encrusted sadness of Norco, or the intimate and epic scope of Citizen Sleeper, than 1000xRESIST should lift your spirits and remind you why narrative-rich games are a saving grace of a medium swallowed by an industry that so often feels fueled by gimmicks and bloat.

_childDocuments_.review: An engaging story full of wild ideas and turns, great cinematography with a strong use of colour and geometry, and game mechanics that while used sparingly still strongly support its emotional angle, making it so much more than just an interactive movie....All of which, while accurate praise, is burying the lede that as a migrant child having lived within the legacy of political violence and generational trauma, the way 1000xRESIST approaches its themes has left me shaken in a way no other game ever has before. _childDocuments_.review: Without exaggeration, I think this is one of the most beautiful stories I've ever experienced, and by far my favorite story of 2024.  Where to even start?  It’s cyberpunk.  It's post-human.  It's maximalist and existential.  It tells a very personal and heartfelt story about generational trauma, totalitarianism, and interpersonal relationships.  I feel like even describing it that way isn't doing it jsuticI laughed, I cried (a LOT), and got so terribly attached to every single character and all their complexities.The gameplay can be described as a visual novel meets walking simulator.  I can understand how that might not be for everyone, but if you're even remotely curious or open-minded enough to try that genre, this is an instant recommend. The beautifully written dialogue felt natural, organic, and appropriate for each in-game setting. And though the graphics are limited, it really worked in the game's favor (in my opinion), for example, by having character models serve as set pieces for the larger picture being painted. Some spoilers ahead! Here’s where it gets really personal for me. I am a child of Hong Kong immigrants and visited that beautiful city a good number of times. Even though the 2019 protests were well after my parents left, I still saw them reflected in Iris's parents.  I saw their hopelessness, shaking their heads at the news and decrying the futility of it all.  I eventually felt that same hopelessness myself, as days turned to weeks turned to months… There is a scene in 1000xResist with the father and mother, after so many years, talking over drinks about the protests. That it had to be this way.  Because the world will see that Hong Kong had fought. Otherwise, history will say we had always wanted this. Iris’s departure also marks the end of the 50 years “one country, two systems” agreement, with her father begging her to give them hope simply by saying she’ll eventually return… even if that hope is false. This game so beautifully spoke about and reflected back at me so many things that have lived in the back of my mind, but I have never been able to express.  This is a maximalist gem, and in a world of constant political unrest, it tells us to not give up, to keep moving forward, and to let go lightly of the things we cannot take with us. This is a work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: This is legitimately one of the best video games story experiences I've ever seen. I spent 90% of this game completely lost and trying to find my objective because there's no map or even a minimap, there's just a compass that vaguely tells you there's someone to talk to west of you. However, despite spending 90 percent of the game lost, I was never bored or frustrated because every nook and cranny and corner had either an extremely interesting chatacter to speak to, or some huge piece of lore to give you a better grasp of the world and what got it to this point. Please don't think that's an exaggeration, I genuinely mean it, every corner. I have never seen a game so ingeniously wrap up the world building into the navigation of the game like this before. It's incredible. A writing Master class. Buy and play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never feel compelled to write reviews for games, but after beating it at 1:30 in the morning I felt like I should sing its praises. 1000xResist is very light on gameplay (and what gameplay *is* there can be tedious and slightly annoying at times), but the story, presentation, and overall style more than make up for its shortcomings. _childDocuments_.review: In an era dominated by games created purely for profit, "1000xRESIST" stands out as a refreshing exception, truly aiming to tell a story. And what a story it tells – more complex, sensible, and engaging than almost any game I've played.This is more than just a game. The developers masterfully play with the medium, never letting technical limitations hinder the narrative. Technically, it looks good and sounds even better, with an aesthetic that's nothing short of perfect. It's a beautiful experience from start to finish.The game's inspirations, including "Signalis" and "In the Mood for Love," initially caught my attention. While I expected to like it, I didn't anticipate loving it as much as I do. The influence of Asian cinema enriches the storytelling, adding depth and nuance.That said, "1000xRESIST" might not be for everyone. Some players might not appreciate its narrative-driven approach, and honestly, I feel sorry for those who can't. For me, it's the game of the year and a new addition to my all-time favorites.In conclusion, "1000xRESIST" is a humbling reminder of what games can achieve when they prioritize storytelling. It's a must-play for anyone who values narrative depth and artistic expression in gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, this not my kind of game. _childDocuments_.review: I can’t stop thinking about 1000xResist since playing it, and have struggled to put into words everything that the game made me feel. I think it is safe to say that it is a modern masterpiece, and I struggle to imagine another game dethroning it for my game of the year this year.While the game absolutely holds up in its own right, and does not feel derivative of any particular other piece of media, I keep trying to think about it in relation to other works. Perhaps that started with a tweet from @Buliaros which is both very funny, and very apt “They should have called 1000xResist ‘Venba X Evangelion’”. There is a part of 1000xResist that feels very tied to grounded narratives about family, generational trauma, coming of age, and specifically immigrant experiences, things like Venba, Everything Everywhere All At Once, All Our Asias, or even 100 Years of Solitude come to mind. The game’s weaving between the mundane and the metaphorical, the plain and the poetic, the real and the magically real feels acutely linked to that particular vein of media, but it never quite feels as high brow as that connection may seem.Kentucky Route Zero and Norco also come to mind as the game weaves in and out of various literary modes, but never quite feels highfalutin or pretentious in that process, instead using the literary language to better convey a simpler truth. Or to just be funny.The games other influences within the speculative fiction and sci-fi are the other half of the picture. The comparisons to NeiR: Automata and Evangelion are openly invited by the developers. I also found myself thinking about Transistor and Umurangi Generation. While 1000xResist engages with the apocalyptic melancholy of those first three, it is the apocalyptic anger of Umurangi Generation Macro and End of Evangelion that you can feel rising throughout. An anger that is sometimes righteous, sometimes furious, and other times just outright cruel. It is that cruelty that makes it effective as a non-combat game, that is conversely the most violent game I have played. In that when violence happens here, it is harsh and brutal and real in a way that a game where you are killing thousands of fodder enemies could never be. The game actively resists equating all violence. As in the real world, violence in 1000xResist is a powerful social and political force. Something that can be wielded on an individual, group, or state level, and with each comes different considerations in its use, its justification and its cruelty.There are other themes and narrative threads that the game explores that I hesitate to even mention for fear of spoiling them, and the narrative construction is perhaps where the comparisons to NeiR are most apparent, as each layer deep you find yourself thinking “well there is no way this can go and further down” and each time you are proven wrong.In summary: Play 1000xResist. It is genuinely one of the greatest narrative video games I have ever played and I need more people to play it so I can talk with more people about it.

_childDocuments_.review: "There is a choice and we will not make it."1000xRESIST is one of the best narratives I've experienced in gaming. The story explores many complicated and multilayered themes that is sure to leave an impact on you both emotionally and even politically. It's a story that takes place in the future, but also in the past, that examines characters so different from us but also so human. You can clearly see the inspiration from great stories like Nier, Evangelion, and Attack on Titan, but it tells its own story beautifully.While I initially struggled to get into the story because of the way it drops you straight in (literally starting at the climax), I found it to be one of the best parts of the game. You slowly piece together everything yourself based on what you are presented with, including the overall themes of the game and what remains (and remains and remains...) with you personally, especially with the final segment. I was always intrigued by the story, but it did take a sizable portion of the game for me to finally be hooked in because of this.The gameplay and mechanics are quite simple and almost nonexistent, the graphics are alright but nothing amazing, and the map design of the main area is a bit confusing, but I can't imagine this masterfully written experience as anything other than a game with the way it presents itself. A game that is worth playing for the narrative alone.

_childDocuments_.review: The time for indie narrative games that are metaphors for depression is over. Now is the age of indie narrative games about generational trauma. This is a game best-experienced spoiler-free, but I found the first chapter to be a weak sales pitch of what the game can achieve. It's easy to see the opening sections and think it's a walking simulator about breaking cult indoctrination. The trailers lean into this for the sake of not spoiling anything. I went in expecting an anime rendition of The Giver: A somewhat generic sci-fi about a society where everyone is the same, but the super special main character is allowed to know about what exists outside those walls and they discover that the utopia is dystopian. 1000xResist exceeded those expectations by leagues, but any articulation of how changes how a new player would experience the game. The narrative isn't entirely hinged on its spoilers. This isn't some tacky serial drama stringing you along to earn one more season's worth of funding. I believe you could go in with full knowledge of the game's narrative and have an emotionally resonant experience. It wouldn't be the same experience, but a meaningful one. One of the great selling points I can say that doesn't spoil anything is that so much narrative is packed into minor characters in the background that are completely optional to engage with. Many of them don't even have names when you meet them and you have to construct the timelines for how they become who they end up.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely compelling and with a whole lot to say. Being more of a visual novel than a standard game there is little gameplay and it is simple, almost all of it is walking around and talking to other characters. Occasionally a “zip” segment will come up, a sort of navigation puzzle where you have to lock on to points and zip to them to get around to a location, nothing too complex. The style is strong with both an anime look and beautiful vistas, the use of color and lighting in direct correlation with the story makes for some truly memorable moments.The meat of it is in the story. It starts with quite an engaging start and then builds to it for the first half. The game tells the story of a sister Watcher who learns the truth beyond her existence and everything about the world and the god-like ALLMOTHER or Iris that seems to control it all, unveiling some ugly truths and difficult choices, often a person is portrayed in one way, and then with added context a more complex picture emerges. Two events strongly make up the base of the game, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the 2019/20 Hong Kong protests. There is a virus in the game that causes apocalyptic things and even mask-wearing, isolation becomes explored through this, and the burden of caregiving, sometimes is too much to handle. Here characters are allowed to engage in some of both the best and worst aspects of themselves. In general, the Hong Kong protests and aftermath(most notably the diaspora that followed) make up the main themes of the game. Iris’s parents were heavily involved in them and fled to seek a different life. Authority is constantly questioned and is something to be skeptical of here with heavy allegories especially as the game goes on. We see firsthand how stories have emerged that are untrue, that paint things in a light to serve power purpose and downplay atrocities, this is also wrapped up in faith and worship intensifying these feelings even more and their perceived power. History is a lie, something that is morphed to fit a purpose, the old is burned to make way for what “works better”.Emotionally the game can be a lot to take in as it is all in some ways a tragedy and what you see will make you question everything about what you both the player and the character of Watcher know. Parts don’t feel good and that is intentional. In line with this color plays a huge part, there are 5 sisters and each one has a distinct color, there is also a principal with a distinct color and these are important to telling where things are at in the story. Memory plays a big part and in these memories, some are much more colorful than others as age or happiness plays a part in them. Perspective plays another role as frequently you will change perspectives both figuratively and literally, much of the game is played standard third-person over-the-shoulder but on occasion, this might switch to first-person for a more intimate experience, or side-scrolling to show off more of the world, or even bird’s eye view.Having great ambition the game is able to deliver on this and create a unique experience in a genre that is so often stuck in doing the same things, it’s experiments with perspective and color as well as an overwhelming story make it a special thing with much to ponder over.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: A game I've been obsessed with since I finished it weeks ago. Time and time again I find myself watching playthroughs of this game to see people experience it for the first time. To relive that rollercoaster of joy, horror, anxiety, and hope.The game itself tells a story that felt incredibly personal, and yet circled a subject that I truly did not know much about, and balanced that intimacy and unfamiliarity with such skill that I was truly transported, and brought to tears, multiple times.If you are a fan of Sci-Fi, this game is for you. If you are a first or second generation immigrant, this game is for you. If you are interested in world events, this game is for you. _childDocuments_.review: Extraordinary, trippy storytelling that had me genuinely captivated across an entire weekend, practically glued to the Steam Deck I was playing it on.It’s a very expertly crafted bit of scifi that explores how memory and perception shape our ability to act on the future. In particular, it takes aim at its titular theme, ”Resist”, and how memory endures, and this motivates how we mark our actions in the larger canon of memory. The science fiction storytelling around this concept is pretty sharp, and interesting in its own right, but I’ll avoid spoiling.A key element of the game is experiencing scenes spread throughout time. In an immediate sense, this is a kind of “detective” mode like Arkham, Cyberpunk 2077, etc…but it’s used very effectively as way to deliver some genuinely stunning story moments. Some feel like flipping through storyboards and seeing moments frozen in time. Others are languishing exploration of environments as they change with the passing events of people’s lives. Near the end, it’s used to parallel events you should be drawing as parallels, in several key sections.Overall, how this game explores how ideas, memories and words shape our perception of the past and future —and how we manipulate them for good and ill— represent its greatest accomplishment.I can see the comparisons to Nier Automata, although I think these elements are comparatively weaker parts of the larger package. There are also a handful of sequences that rely a bit too much on repetitive tasks spaced through time manipulation sequences that get a bit tedious. Overall, very little to gripe about, despite its heady scope and long runtime, this has very little fat on its bones —and what fat there is—well, is mostly worthwhile stylistic flourishing.Easily one of my favorite games of the year (so far)

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely floored. 1000xResist is one of my favorite games in years and quite possibly my Game of The Year for 2024!Without question, it is the story that shines here. In terms of gameplay, it's a pretty straightforward walking sim with some light dialogue choice systems and a bit of Adventure game dna. That story though?1000xResist is a scifi narrative game that explores themes of Pandemic, authoritarianism, and the Hong Kong protests. Its world, shaped by the last living human -- a teenage girl -- and her many clones is bleak and uncomfortable. There is a sense of artifice to everything, because their world has no opportunity for anything else. Everything is fake, everything is a lie, and you the Watcher, the one person in the world who gets to know the truth.The magic of this story is in the execution; every layer and twisting thread is handled perfectly. Far better than I would have dared hope for, and boldly enough to nourish a need that I've had for years.If you are someone who doesn't mind a walking sim, and if that story description above interests you at all, you MUST play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is an astounding narrative game that touches on themes and topics like COVID, the Hong Kong protests of 2019, and diaspora within a strange sci-fi setting. _childDocuments_.review: [SPOILER - FREE[I had no expectations upon starting up 1000xResist for the first time. This is one of the greatest games ever made. A true masterpiece in gaming. Do not fret that it is a "walking simulator" -- this sits atop the genre, passing other classics like What Remains of Edith Finch and Firewatch. This is my guarantee: if you can understand what is happening, you WILL be entertained.I have not felt this profoundly SHOCKED by a gaming experience's novelty and uniqueness since Disco Elysium. I remember when I played Disco for the first time, my initial epiphany was "every other game I have ever played has been for children." This game undoubtedly presents an even more original, profound experience; it has left me thinking "every other game I have ever played has lacked the conviction to see its ideas through." This game's greatest strength is that it is bewilderingly and confidently strange. In my mind, it is a sci-fi epic of Vonnegut proportions.Another point of comparison I have for it is the webcomic Homestuck, which itself was a sort of textual precursor to the wildly popular Undertale/Deltarune. 1000xRESIST, like those stories, is aggressively original, elaborate, soulful, and MODERN. This is a new experience. The game takes itself seriously as art just as it is irreverent in the face of previous conceptions of "games as art." Like a high-art novel, the text folds in, on, and over itself -- it meanders in self-referential analysis and milks every theme and idea for all the poetry within. Simultaneously, 1000xRESIST also makes bad knock-knock jokes. There were moments of extreme tension in which levity were deployed, which never undercut the tension. Such maneuvers were almost jarringly virtuosic. It astonishes me that something so vulnerable and singular was created by a team of people.I felt every emotion playing this game. I was moved to tears on several occasions. I hope this game achieves ascendant success and injects its brilliance into our gaming ecosystem; we would all benefit from more of THIS in the world.10 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of my most anticipated games, and fortunately it lived up to my expectations. 1000xResist is one of freshest stories I've experienced.Some will look down their nose at the simplistic gameplay mechanics, but seeking out every bit of writing is more than worth it. The presentation is excellent too. The art direction is strong and moody, evocative of Nier but with a clear vision.The abstract writing seems intimidating at first, but it becomes understandable the more you learn about the world. The game doesn't always stop to explain, the gameplay loop is largely seeking out more information yourself as you please. The sci fi elements are admittedly high concept, but it so effectively weaves pathos into everything. In this regard, the storytelling is very similar to Evangelion and Hello Charlotte. Like those works, the complicated large scale stuff gives the drama weight. What surprised me most was how self aware the writing is. It pokes fun at the dialogue without undercutting itself. The cast is strongly characterized and likable. The writing can be poignant, biting, and funny, and even side characters have distinct voices.While I enjoyed the second half of the game less than the first, it feels cohesive as a drama and allegory, and the ending will stick with me for a long time. I encourage anyone with even a passing interest in sci fi or stories about generational trauma to give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Story-driven gamers assemble! This is my best experience with narrative-driven games in a long while. The last time I was so immersed in a game was with Prey (2017). It took me almost 30 hours to complete the game while talking with every character and seeing all the content offered in a single playthrough. This game is not shy about showing its aspirations and benefits a lot from doing it this way. The constant existential dread as in Nier: Automata. The solitude and the difficulties in building bridges between people are similar to The End of Evangelion. The fear of the unknown and the search for a way to build a bridge between past and future, as in The Arrival by Denis Villeneuve. How do you deal with a tragedy? How can you stop past mistakes to impair the happiness of your future? How do you know that someone is beyond forgiveness? These were just some of the questions that I was asking myself while playing the final sequence of this game. There are some other themes that I'm not capable of talking about, e.g., the Asian diaspora and Hong Kong independence, but that play a significant part in the whole story (We are playing with the descendants of immigrants, after all).One other major aspect of this game is the direction. You can feel how diverse the background of the team responsible for this game is. The last time I experienced something with a direction as bold and unique as this game was when I played Nier: Automata and Undertale in 2017 and 2019, respectively. Ultimately, I went fully blind on this game just because I found the name funny (and someone on Reddit commented that this game was like Nier meets Evangelion), and it ended being one of my favorite games of all time. I hope the TGA this year does justice to the artistic vision that this game represents. It's a breath of fresh air in the game industry, and I only hope more games like this will be made in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely might be one of my favorites in the recent years.If I was to do an elevator pitch for this game it would be - "Life is Strange 1 meets Nier Automata with a dose of Evangelion & Signalis".If you love heartfelt narrative games (there is no combat in this game, just story, conversations, some platforming and time manipulations) I absolutely recommend it. Extremely good writing here. It mixes sci fi epic and human melancholy beautifully. Explores so many themes, great dialogue. Top tier soundtrack.Really strong world building and lore, nuanced characters. The more you play the more you uncover, just as a good mystery story should do - slowly expand, explain, reframe, recontextualize past events in a new light, add in the missing pieces, while still retaining the ethereal dreamy like moments.The game is actually way bigger than i expected, It took me 18 hours to beat it (granted I talked to every NPC in the game , which I advise by the way, it enhances the immersion).Amazing artistry on display with creative shots, framing, composition, stellar soundtrack, beautiful natural voice acting (the game is fully voice acted).All these aspects elevate this indie game a tier about its weight.Absolutely recommend.As for the Cons: I would say that the walls and floors in the Orchard would benefit from some more pronounced AO, some surfaces there look rather flat. _childDocuments_.review: I'd like to keep this review simple, as opposed to most of my reviews, because I really think this game needs to speak for itself. There is nothing in this game I can describe to you better than the game will show you on it's own, so instead let me try to explain why you should buy this game and let it take you on one of the craziest narrative experiences in media.First let me start by saying this, and while I hate to even tell you this much I think it's really important to know so some people don't walk into this game unprepared: this game is all about generational trauma. There are heavy themes of abuse throughout the entire narrative, so if you're not in the right head space, give yourself some time before playing this. I streamed this and my first night I sobbed during one of the sequences. Obviously these themes will not hit everyone the same, but I wanted to put the warning out there just in case.That said, the way this narrative is weaved into the world and every single thing you do and/or experience is just... breath-taking. I have honestly never been so enthralled by a story; or at least, I haven't in any recent memory. (As we know, memory is a funny thing.) This story is BEGGING to be told. It is BEGGING to be experienced. This story needs to be known. Please give it a chance, there is a lot in here and so much to feel, experience, and unpack. The visuals are stunning. Some of the best character design I've seen in a while and a truly beautiful and inspiring sci-fi setting, which imo is really hard to find nowadays. The music is also fantastic; there are quite a few mixes of other songs within the game to change up the atmosphere and I really adore that. Voice acting was killer and they reused certain VAs in such intelligent ways. Lovely. Everything about this game was so lovely. It's also only $20 and I got over 20 hours out of the game and that was only my FIRST playthrough. There are multiple endings AND achievements to go along with almost everything you do in the game. I mean seriously, if you're used to playing indie games you should know how phenomenal a lot of these talking points are. This is a small team with, what I think is, their debut game and it is better than almost any game I've played the last five, maybe even ten years. Impressive, beautiful, haunting, and my (current) GOTY. This team should be SO proud of what they have put forward here. I can't wait for some years to pass, for me to grow as a person, come back to this, and experience something new, yet familiar. I have been completely and utterly blown away. Thank you so much Sunset Visitor, this game was a treat and I would buy it 10 times over just to experience this story.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything I just wrote is either a direct quote, a paraphrase or an echo from the game. It's all from different chapters, timestamps, from miscellaneous contexts, but arranged to fit together, be evocative and make emotional sense. I even toyed with the idea of writing the whole review with nothing but phrases from the game. If there ever was a piece of media where over-citing would make a perfect referential fit, it's this one. Its narrative is literally built on the power of repeated words. The main storytelling device, the pivotal means of communication, the central theme - words echoing back and forth... back and forth... through generations, time and memories, putting you in a constant state of déjà vu. Imagine if you had an intergalactic library of stored memories of all time and all history - would you even need new words? Everything has already been said, you can only repeat it... back and forth... A dangerous gravity, this game. From the very start, from the sight of the dark still water, I was caught in it. This has been a thoroughly cathartic experience and I was thinking why it had such a profoundly dehydrating effect on me, why I'd become so flooded as to just start... spilling... and spilling... "Bodies have so much water." Is it sickness or just sadness? The answer is complex and multifaceted just like the game. I'll try to capture some of its most resonant strands. The story isn't a tearjerker though, it doesn't need such cheap tricks, but it's one deeply human, heartfelt sci-fi, built on the bones of its ancestors, on remembering those that remain, and remain, and remain... A postapocalyptic speculative fiction about past, history, time, reminiscing. Hauntingly nostalgic, reflective and impressionistic, looking back from the future, while trying to move foreword. "Swirly... Like a ballet of possibilities twists beneath its surface..."Fragmented yet linear, monumental in scope yet poignantly intimate and personal, spanning generations across time and spaces, diving head on into a messy yarn of swirling timelines; traversing huge bodies of water and intergalactic dust alike, searching for a home, looking for new memories. From Hong Kong to Canada to the Orchard; from two stars to one star; from sphere to square; from dangerous nearness whose gravity is echoing to a landing and a remaining. "A diagonal slice through time, place and form" - to quote another piece of gaming art whose migratory ghosts I couldn't help but see wandering about.From immigrants to aliens, from blue to red, one to six, from allfather to allmother, mothers to daughters, shell to sister, hair to hair, from theocracy to red terror, from individualism to collectivism, sphere to square, names to functions, from traditionalism to progressivism, grace to gratitude, doublespeak to common tongue, pandemic to Sinophobia, discordance to concordance, fire to water, resistance to survival, from apocalypse to ascension, from decoupling of substances to fundamental reordering, history to myth, from a mean high school girl to a hallowed saint, from ancient sins to bleeding wounds, traumas to oceans of tears, from the last supper of a family that eats together to the mass communion with a new family, from city to obsession... "The us is a weave that can be unpicked."Narrative threading is incredibly complex, but the game plays it tight and loose with exceptional confidence, using mirroring, patterns and associations to connect all the assorted strands. Because underneath them all, this is a game about memory. And what better means to weave a story through, because that's what (hi)story essentially is. Or rather, her story. The game tackles herstory through generations of women, their sacrifices, fighting spirit and survival. It's a story of her, and a her, and a her: Iris, and her mother, and her mother's mother, and all the sisters. It's matrilineal like that. It's a game about abandoning your mother, overcoming her while honouring her. Mothers as authority figures, overbearing, controlling mothers, mothers as perpetual martyrs, always serving others. Mothers carrying severe post-traumatic paranoia together with the thanklessness of parenting, and passing it on down the line. Daughters becoming like their mothers even though they swore not to, mommy issues galore. Ancient sins and traumas get propagated and perpetuated; same patterns repeat throughout herstory. "There is an us with a pattern we are threading." The repeating patterns are very familiar from our real world history and culture; they resonate with stark clarity, as this individual herstory becomes collective by slowly turning into myth, a hagiography, a gospel. Religious imagery and allusions are strong in this one: from the original sin and loss of innocence, to departure from the Garden, to the Ancient Sister's pride, to allowing your gods to die... To Ascension and Mass Communion. Through it all, cultural, social and political strands tighten into a knot. I already mentioned some, it felt like watching mini history unfold within a small enclosure. "There is a choice and you will make it." - but only at the very end of the game; otherwise, player 'choices' are either flavour or dialogue options, means of conversation. Still, complex societal themes and currents are expressed, dilemmas and messy decisions hard to reconcile: to be water and survive at all costs, regardless of the soul, or to burn for justice and keep your anger close in order to right the past wrongs; to find comfort in tradition which can be a dangerous gravity, or to move so fast to notice there are things worth remembering; to keep an open bleeding wound or to cauterise it; to forgive... or forget. To carry baggage and clutter constantly with us because we're scared of loss, or to choose what to inherit and what to let go, to learn that we can't hold onto everything, because... "Sometimes, you just don't fit in the backpack." Are we still talking about societal things or have we ventured into a personal space? It started to feel too close to home somehow. That's what the game does constantly; it echoes, resembles, implies... It resonates.* The foreshadowing, mirroring, parallels are masterfully done, they hit you in tidal waves. Truly, this game works like water, and water is a recurring visual and symbolic motif; it creates such strong murmur.

_childDocuments_.review: A quiet masterpiece of videogame storytelling. Absolutely worth it at full price and an experience I do recommend if you ended up on this steam page for the game. My full, more nuanced thoughts are as follows:"All that I am...is now in you"We have so many coming of age stories, but very few about coming to terms with the environment we were raised in. For each of us there is a unique and invisible familial legacy that shapes our understanding of the world and how we fit into it. How we give love, how we accept love, and our deepest, most personal fears are frequently echoes of people long past, unintentionally and yet carefully preserved and handed down to us.The term "generational trauma" has been used to describe this game and I agree that trauma is passed down, but so is everything else. It's not just the fears and the hurt, it's also the desires and behavior. Often what makes us feel the most powerful is the exact thing we are most afraid of never having. "We do not get to choose what we inherit", a line of dialogue from the game. We get everything. All that our parents are, is now in us.1000xRESIST tells a uniquely mature story that explores this concept, and many others, in a futuristic apocalyptic science fiction setting. There are many comparisons that can be made to NieR Replicant/Automata, Neon Genesis Evangelion, Land of the Lustrous, and even Tron to a certain extent. However, I implore you to take these comparisons as a means to get in the door of experiencing this game, but leave them at the entrance and embark with a mentally clean slate when you begin your journey with it.The more I consider this game, the more I am impressed with it. The multilayered narrative and evocative immersion of 1000xRESIST create a game that is absolutely worth experiencing if you value the medium of gaming as a thought provoking and artistic form of expression and communication. If games like Firewatch and What Remains of Edith Finch are your speed, this one is a must play. What is increasingly impressive is how far 1000xRESIST stands above its contemporaries in both ambition and scope.The presentation lulls you into a hypnotic state of calm (and excellent) voice acting, a tonal and atmospheric (yet still melodic) soundtrack, and environments that are frustratingly difficult to screenshot as the beauty is in the crafted experience of inhabiting the space, not in how it uses a 16:9 rectangle to frame it.I have been praising this game quite heavily, but it is not perfect so I want to address some of its weaker aspects. As the debut work of brand new game studio Sunset Visitor (consisting of 3-5 people) it can't quite break away from feeling like a sophomore effort unity engine project reminding me somewhat of That Dragon Cancer. 1000xRESIST falls solidly into the small indie team making a first 3d unity game, and within that tier they have gone above and beyond in terms of unique art direction and polish. What they have achieved is extremely commendable and beautiful, but must be understood for the scale of development access and tools available to the team. The animation, modeling, and overall navigation/interactivity of the game feel somewhat limited by these constraints, but only serve as infrequent speed bumps that quickly melt away once the story gets going. The first chapter especially does wonders to immerse the player in a thickly atmospheric and intriguing world. Some areas (especially the orchard, even with the provided map) can be difficult to mentally navigate and was a frustration I had with the game. It usually didn't take too long to eventually get where I was trying to go, but I never felt I fully grasped the layout of the larger environments. I can't wait to see what they do for a second game, and I hope this one provides the funding and exposure necessary to round off these harsher edges going forward.Overall, 1000xRESIST is a landmark in narrative excellence for the medium as a whole. The fact that this size of team with limited tools was able to create such a multifaceted and complex experience is a crowning achievement for the indie space. While the overwhelming praise for the game may seem bordering on hyperbole, the longer I consider my experience with the game, the more I want to join the chorus of its proponents. I would advise that the game is primarily a quiet and thought provoking experience, far from the bombastic image that such high praise may be conjuring in your head. If you approach the game on its own terms and give it time to digest, I assure you it will be time well spent. I highly recommend this game for fans of the stereotypical walking simulator, and everyone that is willing to push a little beyond their comfort zone to try something that feels narratively fresh in the gaming medium.---------I spent ~14 hours to complete the game, trying to exhaust all available dialogue options and see every possible area. Took ~2 hours more to get the remaining achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: A modern masterpiece. I don't throw around that phrase lightly but it fits here. 1000xResist is brimming with the creativity and boldness you only find in indie games these days. It has a strong voice and it knows what its doing, letting a story unfold that effortlessly balances on the edge of horrific and heartwarming. This is a Sci-Fi, this is a horror story, this is a family drama, this is a political thriller, this is a first context story, this is a diaspora narrative. There is so much that all adds up to this mystifying final package that is 1000xResist.The gameplay is not full of complex systems, but it has enough interaction and thought to it that it is far from the basic form of "walking sim" that many like to deride. You'll also find stellar voice acting, and some of the most cinematic shot composition I've ever seen in a video game. This is the sort of game that comes by only once in a while, one so absolutely gravitational that you cannot help but get sucked in as hours bleed away as you pour through its chapters. The team at Sunset Visitor has bottled lightning. This is a game that people need to play, with characters and set pieces I doubt you'll forget for a long while once you see them. It's a game that will keep you guessing, eager to unravel just a bit more of its narrative. And just when you think you've got it figured out, that's when the floor really drops out from under you. Don't let this game pass you by, give it a shot, and see what awaits you in communion. Hekki grace.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim on release day after seeing it on a twitter thread, and proceeded to not do anything else that weekend until I finished the game. It was an exceptional experience for a game I'd never even head of before then.This game is surprisingly well written and has a great concept. While it is pretty much a walking simulator with light gameplay elements, it still makes really good use of them to tell an extremely compelling story. I especially liked a level at the beginning where you explore an earlier and later version of an environment, where some areas were blocked off in one time but not the other forcing you to switch back and forth and experience the contrast between the two.If you're a fan of the stories of games like Nier Automata and AI Somnium Files, I think you'll enjoy this one. It has the high concept sci-fi story of those games but also a great focus on the characters' experiences that can sometimes be lacking in other games of that type. The hub area can be pretty confusing to get around, and I personally thought some of the vocal performances were a bit weak. However, given this is an indie game I think these are minor sins that can be forgiven in an otherwise excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: Rough around the edges, but truly an uncut gem. If you can appreciate its artstyle and sometimes clunky gameplay mechanics, 1000xRESIST is quite a unique way to tell a story, and it tells quite the unique story in doing so. There's a lot of mystery and nuance throughout the game, the voice acting is nice (save for a few exceptions) and overall the experience that this game delivers is something you can't really explain in a review, you can only really experience for yourself. By that I don't mean I can't tell you what happens or what it is about, but rather, the way you feel about it will be wholly your own.It tackles a variety of subjects, from childhood to parenthood, what it means to be yourself, and concepts such as "good" or "bad". If there's two themes that are most consistently found throughout the game are "regret" and "hope". It has a lot of grace when it broaches each of these topics, and never once did I feel like the game forced a certain viewpoint, instead it had a free-form way of simply presenting information and leaving me to ponder on its deeper meanings. It's refreshing, really, and difficult, too, for a game such as this to be mostly avoid of choice and yet still feel like your playthrough will be unique simply because of the way you interpret things as they are told. I will likely always remember this game and frequently recommend it to any future friends and acquaintances to come, simply because of how much of a great piece of media it is.If you're even remotely interested in visual novels or sci-fi subjects, get this game. Don't read about it, don't watch any videos, just play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally wait until I've played through an entire game before I leave a review. But I need to replay the first half a few times before I let myself enjoy the second. _childDocuments_.review: As you're probably already aware if you're reading this, this isn't a game, it's a slightly interactive story. You won't be challenged and you won't, for the most part, be making meaningful choices - you'll be walking from A to B to trigger the next piece of dialogue. Graphics are pretty basicThat's okay. I don't mind that. I prefer when a phenomenal story can be woven with great gameplay, like Horizon: Zero Dawn, but I've nothing against walking simulators - Life Is Strange was fantastic, after all. But that means that it lives and dies by how much the story grabs you... and this didn't do it for me. I couldn't get invested in the characters, and while it did a decent job of keeping me playing to find out what happens next, what happened next was consistently underwhelming for me. Reading other reviews, lots of other people were floored by it, and it *looks* to me like that winds up primarily dependent on how much it resonates with your own personal experiences - and sadly this review might not be very useful as I can't really elaborate on that without spoilers. What I will say is that I consider this to be much more "drama in a sci-fi setting" than the "sci-fi adventure" it's billed as.

_childDocuments_.review: It is extremely difficult to describe what I've gone through without selling it short or spoiling too much. 1000xRESIST is a narrative adventure that tackles grand, ambitious speculative fiction, surreal scifi, bleak, dark existential dread, political allegory, generational trauma, cycles of neglect and violence, the pains of simply connecting with other people. Learning to live with regret. With grief. With yourself.It is both massive in scale and incredibly intimate and raw. The splintered narrative structure can be a bit bewildering at times, but if you get emotionally invested in stories, this is both encouragement but also severe warning. This game will absolutely wreck you. I tear up at engaging stories all the time, but this thing made me ugly cry several times. It will break your heart. It's bleak, it's cruel, it's poetic and beautiful and cuts you like a piece of glass. Special mention must be given both to the gorgeous soundtrack and the absolutely stellar voice acting. The writing is impossibly strong already, but combined with some incredibly natural and heartfelt delivery, the dialogue just elevates the whole thing and really makes you feel for even the briefest exhale. I really recommend taking your time in exploring all the environments to catch all the incidental dialogue, the world building is incredibly restrained but strong.Thoroughly devastating, the developer has created something so raw and sincere, I can't wait to see what they might do next. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game was definitely not what I had at all expected. But it has been a wild ride all the same, this has to be the most immersive game I've played excluding Nier Automata (which I absolutely love). It constantly plays with your understanding of everything in the game from the physics to, the environment, to the emotional tone. it is all masterfully done. And in doing so it crafts a deep and complex multi polar narrative that shows the deepest motivations and emotions of all the cast. At times it can be disorienting, other times beautiful, other times incredibly emotionally brutal. over the course of 2 days I was just emotionally compelled to play it. And after it all was finished had me crying heavily out of the shear emotional catharsis of it all. The game is an absolute masterpiece easily on par with something like Automata, it's definitely not for everyone, but if you like complex and engaging story narratives with a similar to Nier vibe but with its own unique would and storytelling, I would highly recommend this,

_childDocuments_.review: *100xRESIST*  (PC / Switch) by Sunset Traveler is a really special narrative-driven game. With only light gameplay, the focus is _squarely_ (that's a joke, but you don't know it yet) on the unique and complex characters, themes, and stellar voice acting. It just doesn't feel or sound like _anything_ I've ever played before.While the focus is largely on characters living in the Asian diaspora of Western Canada, the themes of mother-daughter generational trauma, politics of protest (and their familial consequences), surviving a global pandemic (this was clearly written during covid), are universal and profoundly impactful and thought-provoking, nearly insisting I complete it's ~10hr runtime in one weekend.While the characters and world are stylistically animesque (and there's some clear visual inspiration from Evangelion), there is nary an anime trope (or any other kind of trope, to be honest) to be found. Indeed, some elements reminded me more of The Three Body Problem, but to say more would reveal too much.All in all, it's just _fresh_. Not a single character or story beat brought on an eye-roll, and the dialogue and voice acting is nuanced excellently delivered. If you like sci-fi in any medium that simultaneously tackles the "big picture" stuff while deftly weaving in interesting characters, I think you'll enjoy it. Hekki grace.Hekki allmo.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet again, I found myself playing an indie game I knew nothing about, that I bought only because it was in a bundle with one that I wanted - Cryptmaster - to get a better price-per-item value. I already feel like the bundle gave me my money's worth twice over. And I haven't even touched Cryptmaster yet.When it comes to games like this one, I think it's more important for a person potentially interested in playing them to know what they aren't rather than what they are. That is what I'm going to focus on.1. When you look at the art style, you may think "ah, this is one of those cheap anime games ironic weebs buy by the hundreds to show the world how weeb they are". Well, it isn't. It's just an art style. The game doesn't have any anime tropes, unnecessary fan service or anything like that.2. Upon closer inspection of screenshots provided on the game's store page, you'll probably notice those cool combat suits. Except, they're not combat suits and there is no combat in the game at all. No platforming either. Puzzles, there are, scarce and simple.What do you do then? Run around and talk, mainly. It doesn't feel like a "walking simulator" at all, however. The game doesn't try to buy time by making you travel. You run fast and locations aren't that big.Considering the pacing and the amount - and weight - of things that happen in the story, adding more gameplay would ironically make the game feel slower. Like adding water to your drink of choice to make it last longer.3. If you scrolled down the store page, you might have already learned that 1000xRESIST was a part of something called "LudoNarraCon". That could make you think of those super artistic games pretending to be deep by purposely serving you stories so convoluted, that if you ask their authors to explain them, they typically mutter something about a "dissonance", "depression" or "existence" while avoiding eye contact and sweating profusely.1000xRESIST does have a sensible amount of symbolism and metaphors - mostly pertaining to the game's lore, I'm pleased to add - but the story it tells is completely solid. In both senses: being good and being concrete. You won't have to google "1000xRESIST plot summary" after finishing the game either. Everything is explained - and without walls of text to boot.Yes, this is what you play this game for: fantastic story, writing and presentation. I'm not going to talk about the story itself at all, the official description is good enough to give you an idea, and I recommend going in completely blind, just like I did. You do have two hours to change your mind anyway.Presentation, on the other hand, is something worth a mention. Direction of cutscenes, framing, work of camera, use of colours. These aren't things I think about a lot while playing video games, but 1000xRESIST does them so well, I couldn't help but notice. I never thought they were this important in conveying information and emotions. I sincerely believe the game is worth playing for this alone.4. Looking at screenshots and watching videos, you may feel like characters are somehow... similar. And don't even have real names. It's not laziness, it's a part of the story. And believe me, you will soon start not only to recognize those characters, but even care about them.I think these would be the biggest misconceptions one could have about 1000xRESIST.Of course, nothing is perfect. There aren't any big problems I have with the game, but I'll name a couple of minor ones:- Optimization - it's not that bad, but I don't see the reason why my RTX2070 - outdated as it is - would need to work so hard to keep 75fps in a game that should run on a PS3.- Faces could use some work. It would be especially nice if characters moved their lips when talking.To summarize, 1000xRESIST is a must-play for those who like good stories. Other preferences don't really matter. Even if you like action, you won't be bored. More can happen in five minutes here than in most entire action games.I would say we got a solid GOTY candidate, but all those awards are in fact popularity contests, so that's not very likely. 9.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a "video" novel  than a game but I feel this is the best media this story could be told. _childDocuments_.review: Story-Driven Game: A Tale of Eternal ClonesMind the rough edges (small dev limited budget = limited polish) and Embark on a loooong journey through a world where individuals and groups, all exact clones, have lived in isolation for thousands of years. Dive deep into the conflicts and stories, from the distant past (before the isolation) to the present and future, that have shaped their existence. Explore and come to understand the complex decisions of several characters, learn how their identities have been influenced by their experiences. Take your time; just when you think you're nearing the end, you'll find yourself playing for hours more, falsely expecting the end to be around the corner.Tip for New Players:Navigating the world hub can be very challenging. SAVE yourself TIME and use your compass to guide you and focus on the story content, as there are no collectibles outside of it. don't bother with the empty underground.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely incredible experience. The comparisons to Nier/Yoko Taro are not overblown one bit. In some ways, this story even exceeds those comparisons - notably with the references to recent history. The gameplay is simple - mostly walking and exploring - and it works well with the story and worldbuilding without becoming obtrusive or burdensome.There is some slight roughness here and there - no lip syncing for voice acting, occasional rough voice acting from minor NPCs - but the former is typically a non-issue due to worldbuilding reasons, and the latter felt less "cringey" and more like this was clearly a work of love. The hardest part was finding a stopping point when I needed to go to bed or grab some food! I never wanted to stop! My playtime was 17 hours for a very complete playthrough - a bit too long to go without a break here and there :) a good problem to have!I would say go in blind, but frankly I don't know if spoiling yourself would even have much of an effect. Certainly there's some intrigue and surprises here and there, but the most enjoyable part of this game was how the story weaves throughout history and from the individual to the societal and back again - it's something that feels special and difficult to spoil.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't know how to summarize this game. It's not just that the narrative and characters are fantastic and multi-layered - it's not just that their low-concept science fictional world is incredible - it's also the staging, the framing of every scene, the shifts in gameplay, the cuts...this game uses visuals to heighten and enhance the story being told. _childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is one of the best "walking simulator" narrative type games I've played.  It wears its NieR:Automata, Signalis, 13 Sentinels, and Satoshi Kon inspirations on it sleeve, but rather than outright copying those works, paints the canvas with its own unique colors.  It's a stylish, deeply rich, and textured sci-fi story that serves as the framing for a story deeply tied to transgenerational diaspora trauma with splashes of PTSD, identity, and surviving/living through global catastrophes rounding things out.  It's a story that has a lot on its plate and it does a fantastic job of pulling all of its themes together and marrying them to a narrative that also remembers to be entertaining as well.As a player, you're given an endlessly fascinating world to explore.  Whether it's the fragmented communion segments (which feel inspired by AI: The Somnium Files at times) or exploring the Orchard, there's always something interesting to see and many engaging conversations to be had.  This is a game where it's absolutely worth exploring the world to talk to not only the main characters who are milling about, but also nameless NPCs that you'll find scattered around.  There's a lot of personalty and smaller personal stories you can dig up if you take the time and it only makes the game's world richer.  The gameplay portions, featuring some light puzzle solving with time manipulation and Gravity Rush-inspired platforming segments are a good way to break up the walk and talk, though I do wish the former was used maybe just a little more for puzzle solving and that the latter felt a little more guided at times.  During the zip sequences it can sometimes be hard to really know where you're going and interactables don't always stand out easily.  Navigating the Orchard can also be a little tedious at times with the waypoint system not being as useful as it could be, but none of this is ever gamebreaking and is mildly irritating at worst.  1000xRESIST is a heavy and heady narrative that's brutally honest and real.  It doesn't shy away from the uncomfortable, but it doesn't wallow or revel in it either. Even if the dialogue can be a bit self-indulgent at times and maybe the layers of metaphor run a layer or two too deep, there's still an immense amount of heart at the center of the story that keeps the game from ever jumping the track, and it's a narrative experience I'll be thinking about for a good while to come.

_childDocuments_.review: In reflecting on 1000xRESIST, I'm reminded of the title of a book - one that I've never read, but that was so evocative I've never forgotten it: "The Knife of Never Letting Go."The phrase encapsulates this game perfectly. 1000xRESIST is a triumphant work of science fiction, with the sharpness and sincerity of a knife. I'm loathe to say anything about it beyond what sunset visitor 斜陽過客 have chosen to share, other than to say the blade they have forged cuts with precision. It is exceptionally written, both in terms of the overall narrative and the characterisation of its cast. Human foible and fondness intermingles with the cold gaze of millennia and neither feel at odds with the other.Visually, it can lean on tableau, but has a strong sense of direction and composition that makes many of the scenes striking. The most minor of complaints I have is that I wish it were more animated, that motion accompanied the emotion, but it does make those times where the characters launch into life so much more impactful. Also, please, sunset visitor 斜陽過客, an option to have dialog automatically advance, I beg you.I have experienced very few tales like this - games or otherwise. Take a chance on a stranger and 1000xRESIST. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that all the praise this game is getting is  well earned.I'm still  and gushing over this story, and I'm pretty sure it'll stay with me for a while. A strong contender for best one I've experienced in years.It's very much an arthouse game, it's not afraid to be whatever its creators wanted it to be and doesn't shy away of spelling out very clearly what real world parallels it is trying to harness.Some of the themes it explores are incredibly complex (diasporic and generational trauma are just a couple of them), and some people will have a deeper personal connection to them than I did, but even as an "outsider" they hit me hard.They're wrapped in the best kind of sci-fi, the kind that holds up a mirror at humanity, with a plot that lets you make sense of things on your own until it throws the next wham line, subtle insinuation, not-so-subtle reveal or assumption-breaker your way. The surface-level aspects like graphics, UI, animations, and "gameplay" may be criticizable by their...excessive simplicity, but the deeper ones - the strong art direction, the camerawork, the mise-en-scène, the sound design, the amazingly consistently amazing voice acting, the stellar writing, are all masterfully done and work together to form a  that says a lot even without words and just elevates the whole. I often found myself awestruck by some setpieces, just trying to absorb everything.On that note, everything seems designed with intent and significance, so being immersed and engaged and taking it all in will greatly enhance the experience. There's a lot of optional conversations to be had, but the game rewards you very handsomely for just walking around and getting to know other characters' relationships, personalities and wishes. Some beats both major and minor wouldn't have had the same impact if I hadn't engaged with them. I do have a couple critiques in my head, but the positives more than outweigh the negatives.Can't wait to get into the written essays and hours-long analysis videos and podcasts people will create about it and see how others connected with it (that's what you do with art, isn't it?).It's not for everyone, but if you're even slightly into meaty narrative walking simulators, give it a try when the mood next strikes. I'm glad I did.
