_childDocuments_.review: 1000xResist is an absolute gem. It's a third person narrative adventure game with a riveting story that draws its inspiration from NieR:Automata, Evangelion, the COVID pandemic, migration, and the Hong Kong protests. Set in a futuristic habitat that protects the ALLMOTHER and her colony of clones from the Occupants, the story and setting bear more than a little resemblance to NieR:Automata, and I think fans of that game - as well as other abstract, visionary games like Signalis - will undoubtedly enjoy it (provided they're on-board with the absence of combat).Honestly, I could not put this down. Every part of the experience is impeccably composed: the way that the story is delivered through exploration of the ALLMOTHER's memories, the depth of world-building through NPC dialogue and atmospheric, beautifully-rendered environments, and a gorgeously evocative, emotional soundtrack. The voiceovers are wonderful too, each ASMR-worthy performance best enjoyed via earphones (where you'll also get the most out of the OST's subtler moments). The plot is an original, heart-rending story of both sisterhood and individuality, of history and the future and the cost of shaping both.Most of the game is spent exploring each chapter's locations, talking to NPCs to unveil the story. There are occasional "grappling hook" sections where you zip around a stage, but generally little action to participate in outside of exploration. There is plenty to witness, though, and weighty decisions to be made; and the compelling plot - along with its breathtaking artistic direction - is more than enough to carry it.With a playtime of around 9 hours, there were a few points where I thought the game could have wrapped up a bit sooner without sacrificing anything, and I encountered one bug where I fell through a floor, but these are minor gripes. The fact is, this is a wonderful piece of visual storytelling, and I really recommend it to fans of narrative-rich games exploring the nature of humanity.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on release day and I am only in the middle of Chapter 6. So like not done a full playthrough.But man this game, its intense. It switches perspectives so often that it keeps you engaged but the storytelling is emotionally brutal, it never veers into narm territory, its paced perfectly but getting emotionally gut punched when I least expect it is oof. Had to step away a couple of times. I played it nearly all night haha. I will be honest, there was one scene so far that froze for me but like it froze only for 10 seconds or so aaand I have a GTX 1060, make of that what you will. The models and some of the animations are slightly rough looking but it honestly adds to the charm of the game for me.The voice acting is superb. It really pulls the game together, soundtrack is good but like no giant bangers that stick in my head, that said it complements the game nicely and doesnt detract from the splendid voice acting.QOL suggestions? I will say the game doesnt have an auto-play kind of function for dialogue so it gets a little frustrating to have to keep clicking. Similarly if you're scrolling through time periods you have to hold down the mouse and click, then hold down again, and again. At one point the game makes you do this 40 times and it really detracted from my experience, so perhaps an auto time scroller for that particular section (the one with healer?) Additionally there's no way to remap the key bindings on the keyboard. If that could be added I'd have zero complains with the UI, its just those three things. _childDocuments_.review: Maybe the best-realized video game narrative experience I've enjoyed since Grim Fandango. Not just in terms of compelling story, which tons of games have, but in terms of the skillful way it uses its wonderful art direction and great vocal performances to tell a very compelling story--not "compelling for a video game" but just plain good by any standard. The game is not "cinematic," because it is definitely a video game--more so than your average VN, it is "game-y" even if it lacks combat--though it is a lot like a really good season of television, in how it gives life and personality to its well-realized ensemble cast, and the way it briefly and fruitfully experiments with different forms of storytelling throughout its run. Like Grim Fandango, it is occasionally clunky or obtuse--the maze-like hub world here taking the place of GF's more maddening puzzles--but in a way that ends up a sort of essential part of the experience. A more polished game wouldn't attempt half of what this one does. More experienced developers might've reined in the scope and "perfected" a smaller chunk of this story. I'm glad these ones were too inexperienced to know how impossible their ambitions were.Anyway if you are put off by so many reviewers' mentions of Serious Themes like Generational Trauma and The Immigrant Experience, because you don't want to play something didactic or "Message-y," I promise you that while this game does indeed take those themes very seriously it is also a Rip-Roaring SciFi Adventure that is frequently Very Funny. It is fun, in other words.

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is one of the best narrative adventure games I've played in a long time, and I don't say that lightly. It interleaves the contemporary stresses of the protests in Hong Kong with a time-hopping sci-fi story of clones, memories, incomprehensible aliens, revolutions, and betrayal, and it ultimately comes together into a rich exploration of generational trauma. Characters confront how they have been unwittingly scarred by the pain their ancestors experienced, and must decide what to take from the past and what to attempt to leave behind. It's largely a game of exploring spaces, talking to other characters, and doing some very light platforming or puzzles. However, the interactivity drew me into protagonist Watcher's mindset, with smartly-chosen camera perspectives (the game moves between first-person, free control third person, and fixed camera angles), environments, and lighting heightening the emotional impact of each sequence. Almost the entire way through, every time you think you have a handle on where the game is headed and what it is capable of, it adds new layers, uses new techniques, and throws in new twists. Days later, I'm still sitting with what I experienced.This is a shockingly confident debut from the talented team at sunset visitor, who make the absolute most of a limited amount of environments, character models, and animation budget to punch well above their weight. The main voice cast does an incredible job. The end result feels personal and deeply affecting. It's one of those games that I want to bring up to anyone who will listen because of how meaningful playing it to me.

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is a game about a cult of clones that worship their original. It's about humanity struggling against an invasion by cosmic horrors that bring with them an incurable disease. It's about finding out who the "man behind the curtain" really is. It's about generational trauma, and the way its dangerous gravity pulls at those who try to escape it. It's about the things people are willing to do to survive. It's about being haunted by longing for a home you never knew, that no longer exists. It's about the way you end up becoming your mother even after everything you did to escape her. It's about the violence of assimilation. It's about hurting the people you love. It's about revolution. It's about the terrible weight of memories, and how precious they are. It's about a lot more than I've written here.It'll raise your standards for how narratives can be delivered in this medium. There is truly nothing else like it.

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is an absolutely attention-hoarding game; its story, its style, its characters, the devices through which they are represented. They made me glued to the screen until I reached the end of the journey."Watch", they told me. And watch I did.I watched a story about the apocalypse. I watched a story about aliens. I watched a story about a group of sisters. I watched a story about their ALLMOTHER. I watched a story about a friendship. I watched a story about intergenerational trauma. I watched a story about systematic oppresion. I watched a story about the weight of expectation, about the dangers of fanatism and blind faith. I watched a story about leaving things behind, but never letting yourself forget the truths they taught you. A narrative experience that will haunt me in the best of ways for a good while.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that I can't really describe because it does so many things in so many ways that trying to contain it with comparisons feels like it does it a disservice.So, no comparisons. Instead, this game tells a story about home, and families, and trauma, and rebellion, and memory, and rage, and forgiveness, and the messiness of the world. _childDocuments_.review: 1000xResist is probably best described as a visual novel or walking simulator (a loaded term, but it's accurate mechanically) with light puzzle and platforming elements.That probably doesn't sound very interesting, and it wouldn't be if it weren't for the story being really really good. I think you should go into it without much research, but I think the closest thing I could compare the story to is Neon Genesis Evangelion, complicated and about some pretty heavy stuff. But also told in an extremely engaging and thought-provoking way.The voice acting is really good. The music is pretty good. You might be hesitant about the graphics. In fairness the game does not look high budget. But it's put together with a director's eye and a painter's hand. It's not going to win any rewards for fidelity, or make all that money you spent on your graphics card worth it. It's probably going to stay with you for longer than any game that did.Ultimately, I think you should buy this because it's a good game, and you should play it. But maybe more because I want to see what this studio puts out with more funding, I want to see the people who made this be rewarded for putting this into the world. Easily worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: I like being very critical of stories that I love so I'm going to start by saying this game is a strong contender for game of the decade so far and I'm not saying that lightly 1000xRESIST is a story that you can tell was deeply personal to the people writing, discussing political Ideology, the concept of family, home, love and indeed, resistance in a way that can only be expressed from a first hand perspective. It manages to craft a beautiful thought-provoking story while also still managing to tell a thrilling sci-fi dystopia about aliens, cloning and to top it all off, doomed Yuri.Spoilery part of the review ahead:Chapter 2 of 1000xRESIST could be packaged as a single product and sold and I wholeheartedly believe this. The story of Iris and rebellion from a first generation migrant who's parents had fled war is some of the tightest writing in fiction. It is followed up by a solid stream of hard hitting writing up until it fumbles a little in chapter 6There's an inherent problem in dystopia stories. You start by going for the head, your characters succeed in cutting off the head, but there's still a dystopia. I'm reminded of mistborn, attack on titan, Gurren Lagaan. 1kR tackles this in a very interesting way with a new figurehead immediately taking place and a new protagonist. Which is a brave and novel perspective, you're introduced to this "new normal" in a way that immediately draws parallel between our two protagonists. Again, I think "blues" awakening is amazing.The issue being, the game seems to backpedal slightly, bringing back the old protagonist for a while (and eventually killing her off again) which is again, interesting. The Blue/Watcher twist is novel and surprising, but the game absolutely suffers with pacing in the third quarter. Timeskips galore makes sense when you learn about watchers condition, but something making sense doesn't make it feel good.But absolutely brings it back for the finale, only to stumble with an ending. The problem with having a "and now it is up to you, player, to rewrite society." In a game inherently about politics, is you lose out on relationship complexities. My opinions on fixer and BBF don't really matter because I'm building a new world, characters don't get closure because you choose if they live or die in a single moment.Ideally, the final chapter would be thrice as long, but I understand that's not indicative of the story they wanted to tell so it just confuses me why the approach was taken at all. In a story where no character is perfect and manipulation is a core theme where the question of governance is so core, the ending of "okay wise guy, why don't you give it a shot?" With some timeskippy nonsense feels cheap. I was busy wiping the tears from my eyes after the emotional scene with secretary only to be told "ok, now build a government."Again, these are minor complaints. The story more than makes up for it and any pacing issues are outmatched by the quality of both world and character building surrounding it. I only critique issues this harshly when I truly love an artpiece and that's what 1000xRESIST is, art. Despite everything negative I have said, the game made me cry on multiple occasions and it is not an experience I will soon forget.I don't like number scores, but 96/100

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Don't look at the low playtime, I had some internet issues.Being the pretentious hipster supreme that I am, I expected to like this game since it was immediately apparent that it is made for pretentious hipsters. I expected it to be something like Nier, except more avant-garde and something I could feel superior for liking and recommending to other people despite knowing that they wouldn't ever be interested in playing something like this. That kind of thing, you probably know the feeling.Well this "game", if I can even call it that, isn't anything like Nier or anything good. The first thing I noticed is the absolutely atrocious voice acting that made me bleed from the ears just from listening to it. I was incredibly surprised when I was perusing the reviews and reading that voice acting was apparently very good. It almost made me doubt my sanity, but after playing further I was convinced that I am not insane and voice acting is in fact terrible.The environments and the general look-and-feel are hard to describe. The best analogy I can come up with is that "it's like something you would see in a Suda51 game if Suda51 was a talentless hack". They are insanely boring and unremarkable and look like a test level in the engine that had a couple of objects thrown into it. My memory could be failing me, but I think early versions of Yandere Simulator had more effort put into the levels.The writing is probably the worst part. The dialogues made me remember my childhood in Russia when I didn't have good internet and didn't know English. Back then I used to rent video games from shady dealers much like I rented VHS tapes from a a video salon. Those games were obviously illegal cracked copies that most of the time had terrible localization that made it seem like every line of dialogue was an amalgamation of incoherent word salad (in fairness, it was entertaining and even memetic in retrospect). The dialogue in this game is a lot like that, except it takes itself incredibly seriously. In fact, the quality of writing in this review is probably a lot more engaging and entertaining than anything you could hope to find in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth going in blind. It oozes with originality and creativity, crafting a unique and poignant story, with equally stunning visuals. While I certainly did not mind, be advised that the gameplay is mostly about exploration, light puzzles, and dialogue choices. The game as a whole feels like an interactive play, with heavy focus on storytelling. As such, it may not be for everyone. But if you are even a little bit curious, just take the plunge, it is that good.This is one of the few games that every time I played, my wife would either stop whatever she did so she could watch, or ask me for a recap after. We spent plenty of my playtime discussing our theories as the story unfolded. The last time this happened was while playing 13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim, and I rate 1000xRESIST just as high.To the devs, thank you for making this game, as a longtime gamer, this was a breath of fresh air. Looking forward to any and all of your future endeavours!Hekki grace!

I need everyone in the world to experience what 1000xRESIST has to offer. I have never loved a game more than I've loved this game, and I'm not even fully finished yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros* Decent length for a single player experience (8-10 hours), especially for $20* Interesting setting, since clone society stories that delve very deep into the relationship clones have with each other and with their progenitor are very rare* Compelling narrative (you get to experience the past, present, and future of this society) with strong characters* Incredibly varied voiceover cast for a story about clones; some really help carry the performance* Reaches ambitiously for some parallels with the chaos of the government changeover in Hong Kong from Britain to China - and mostly succeeds at doing soCons* Little in the way of gameplay* Graphics are about 15 years old* Animations aren't much better - some have the rigidness of being slight T-pose variations* Metaphor for revolution and oppression will be hard to connect with for many. I still found it interesting, just not moving.Verdict: If you're only into games for the gameplay, definitely skip this. If your true purpose in single player gaming is to find exceptional narratives and experience them, then get this. It'll hit the spot.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xResist is masterful by any metric. It's a sci-fi story, but it's my favorite kind of sci-fi story because it quickly stops being about sci-fi. It's one of the best stories in any game I've played in a long time, and it's certainly one of the densest. There are narrative choices that I disagree with or don't understand, but I cannot condemn them, because I recognize that they are part and parcel with the greater whole that I love so much. This is an entirely narrative-focused game, so keep that in mind, but if you're interested in a story that will make you feel a little too human, don't let this game pass you by.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. 1000 X Resist is one of my top games of 2024. I just finished it and everything from the visuals, to the writing, to the unique mechanics of the individual levels amazed me. Only complaint is with the quality of some of the audio voices but with writing and performances of this caliber that's basically just a nitpick.If it looks at all interesting to you and you like any of their inspirations they have listed at the bottom of the game description, I can't recommend it enough!
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Challenger to Disco Elysium and Citizen Sleeper for the position of best written game in recent years.  How this gem unveiled the mysteries gradually throughout the game, slowly filling in the missing pieces is phenomenal. Pacing is just top notch.Even after finishing, the characters are still on my mind. That rarely happens to me anymore.And how can a small game have such phenomenal dubbing ? The voice actors are so, so fresh. Especially JIAO! Such a beautiful soft voice and wonderful diction. Sunny Daydream Chen is amazing.Hekki grace
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: This was an unexpected gem. I purchased this game on sale not knowing how much I would end up loving it. The story, the art style, the music has me in a chokehold. A great game to play when you're not trying to do too much, but just want something kind of low maintenance as the mechanics are not difficult at all to maneuver. It also gives you a chance to explore a bit on your own which I like. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Great game to play when you want to relax and enjoy a good story.One thousand times resist is a story about, well, resisting. As you go with the story you must resist and continue going to it's complete conclusion, hair to hair. It's a story about passed-down trauma, standing your ground, experiencing life, and remembrance. Despite it's simplistic gameplay and graphics it manages to very quickly grasp your full attention, forcing you, in some sense, to see it's story through the end, hair to hair and sphere to square. It truly is an unexpected gem of a game and an example going forwards of what can truly be accomplished in terms of the "videogame" or "interactive-medium" of storytelling. It is a game, and story, to be experienced and surely paves the way of what is possible with limited means with this medium.Hekki allmo in all its grace. Can't wait to forget the story to replay it all again.TLDR; 10/10 game to be experienced and strong GOTY contender. Hekki Allmo.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: What 1000x resist's sci fi narrative adventure game brings to the table is that its not only dense as hell plot and theme wise, feeling almost like an adaptation of some acclaimed novel, whilst also having stylistic flourishes that are both impressive and also feel purposeful in a way that a higher budget game probably wouldn't. They made a game this visually striking with what feels like cardboard sets and a few unity shaders. The starkness of the environment design and the various shifts of perspective from over the shoulder to first person to top down to side scroller in a way that feels elegant rather than whiplash to the extreme. Its the kind of game where I want to replay again with a notebook or something to try and make sense of it, but not in a tiresome "lore game" way of your dark souls of the world, but in a "rewatching Satoshi Kon's paprika to notice all the foreshadowing and symbolism better" way. Absolute banger and strong personal GOTY contender
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: The story is phenomenal, and easily the standout part of the game. The themes of memory, generational trauma, and existentialism are eloquently conveyed through the story and heightened by the excellent voice acting and striking art design. I found it difficult to put down through the entire 5-6 hour story.However, I can't help but feel like the game didn't take enough advantage of its medium. Most of the gameplay is walking around and interacting with things and people, which is made tedious by the barebones navigation UX, labyrinthine structure of some of the maps, and sections where you are made to walk back and forth between a handful of characters. There is minimal character animation and no lip movement- which is a completely valid artistic choice, but in combination with everthing else, gives me the feeling that this story could have easily been told in the form of a movie or a graphic novel.P.S: Note that there are no options to adjust graphics settings- though the game runs fine on lower end PCs and the steam deck.Overall, I recommend this game- a great 5-hour experience worth $15.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the 'walking around and talking to people and light dialogue options' of games like 13 Sentinels and Nier Automata, you will like this game.If you want high action gameplay, you will not find that in this game.  This game has really good writing, voice acting and use of cinematography.  Probably the big indie narrative hit of 2024.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say the story is great, the art direction is cool too, but it feels really lacking in so many areas, the voice acting is boring and unexpressive, the writing pace is suuuuper slow and there is so much filler, the animations are non existant and the environment design is very boring and not memorable. I really liked the story (even if it's veeeeery easy to guess after just 1 hour) but this game didn't feel like a game at all, would have been better as a show or movie (there is no gameplay anyway so it wouldn't change anything at all)It makes me sad to say it wasn't worth it to spend the time I spent playing it since this kind of game would have been better experienced if I just watched it on youtube instead of playing it myself
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those tactical downvotes. The game isn't bad by any means, but I think the store description and the near 100% percent positive rate give a misleading impression of what this actually is.First of all, there is talk about puzzles, switching between time periods and stuff. Let's get this out of the way, this is 100% a walking simulator. not 99% walking simulator, 100%. There is nothing here can be called a puzzle or actual gameplay at any point of the game and by the third time you are told to talk to every single NPC in the game in that maze they call a hub area, you start kinda getting annoyed.Second, the story while pretty good is not always up to its own complexity. This game rather reminds me of 13 Sentinels in narrative structure, but a game with this many twists needs a very high standard of storytelling; merely "good" unfortunately is not always "good enough" if you're trying to hit me with the fifth consecutive "everything you thought you knew is a lie".Third, while I think a nuanced view of stuff like character motivations, protagonist vs antagonist instead of good vs evil is very important for narrative games with deep themes, unfortunately some of the characters do fall flat in here. Yes, they did get screwed over by circumstances and/or either people, but at the end of the day a lot of the people in here are just fundamentally complete psychopaths with how they react to ♥♥♥♥♥♥ events happening to them and this drives too much of the conflict in this game to truly feel some of the poignant moments.And fourth, while I always expected the alien part of the plot to take a backseat to everything else in the game, as is customary in these character driven dramas, I can't help but be disappointed that the Occupants don't take a backseat to the main plot: They are utterly irrelevant except for setting up the structure of "humanity has died out and everyone lives underground because of aliens", which is kind of a bummer, especially considering which what a weirdly large amount of time they take up, despite contributing essentially nothing to the story.All in all, if you asked me a vacuum, I would probably recommend this game, but I would like to make sure people go into this with their expectations correctly calibrated. This is a good game, but is nowhere close to something like NIer or 13 Sentinels, despite what a 100% positive rating and rave critic reviews (of which there are very few) would tell you and you will enjoy what is here a lot more if you keep that in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: This game is huge in narrative scope. The game itself is walking around and talking to people; there's some light puzzling and grappling-hook usage but it's all about the dialogue. Inter-generational trauma, diasporic disconnection, social formations, religious and cultural production being used to reinforce (or rebel against) social formations, aliens and apocalypse, teenage bullying. It all really gels together and completely works, but it makes the game hard to write about because there's so much you could choose to focus on.The constant stories within the story (characters are always rehearsing, staging plays, singing songs, reciting poems)  are a huge part of the world. You get to see every character thinking their history and trying to arrive at some kind of truth. I think the game itself is another such effort by the game's creators and cast of actors. Since we can't arrive at a perfect knowledge of each other's experiences, we have to do things like reading, creating art, practicing religion, or thinking about how political power is structured, to get as close as we can. And in these (necessary) processes there's a lot of potential failures and inadequacies and compromises that will inevitably create consequences for the people trying to communicate with each other.TL;DR play the dang game! Hekki ALLMO
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough thumbs down, I think the game is close to being really good but falls flat.The story is really good... for the first half. I found after the big event, the narrative pacing becomes completely staccato, disorienting, and like there's no real direction. I also took time to read all of the extra dialogue but still found the characters motivations and feelings unclear, given the numerous twists and lies. There's also several fakeout endings. I had assumed it ended at Chapter 6, for the six sisters and that's what the achievements showed, and for every successive chapter I felt the narrative dragging on more and more.I also thought the gameplay fell flat a lot. The Orchard is extremely confusing to navigate in an uninteresting way. I spent probably half of this playtime running in circles trying to find out where it is I'm supposed to be going. While the dialogue does a superb job of making the world feel real and lived-in, like a society of clones isolated for a thousand years would really be like that, the actual physical game space was not. It's empty and uninteresting. I thought the only space that reflected that was Oldtown which you spend very little time in, and the area is also poorly explained? The gameplay itself is largely the same, empty, repetitive, and borderline frustrating. The production quality, in terms of what's animated and what's not, which areas get detailed, also felt extremely inconsistent, where each scene could range from beautifully animated and scored to feeling like I'm playing some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Unity asset flip shovelware.Speaking of, I was completely hooked on the different characters, mysteries, and the nature of the world and the Occupants. My answer, time after time, was: Oh, this is just X from Y good movie/game/anime. It just got more derivative as time went on. I think also part-of this comes from my lack of clicking with the Hong Kong storyline as I am not an immigrant myself and live in an area with little Chinese population, so I don't really know much about the subject. So I think it's also just not for me. I also thought the topic of faith and its one-way nature was really interesting, and then felt like it really abruptly became a "God is fake and bad" atheist bash fest narrative #983489, and then had little to say on it otherwise. I came out on the ending thinking, "Wow, a lot happened! So much to think about." then realized I had very little to think about that couldn't have been said halfway throughout the game.So, shame because I really enjoyed it! It was really entertaining. I would buy it on sale if this is your type of game because I think the highlights and unique story is pretty good. I think most of its issues would be fixed if it were a VN.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful. One of the most brilliantly engaging sci-fi narratives I've ever consumed and I'm so glad that I took a go at a genre (interactive story) I'm usually not particularly interested in.The voice acting alone sold me on the game and should win awards. The entire cast (Watcher, Iris, Principal) deliver such emotion and the writing embodies such a distinct style... I was just completely smitten by both. I don't think I've ever taken as many screenshots of locales and lines of dialogue that I just knew I wanted to return to - some of the writing is absolute poetry. 'Hekki grace' may be etched into my mind forever.Gameplay wise, you are navigating between characters to progress dialogue. There is not much here that will challenge you mechanically, but the game uses its medium to deliver a beautiful story, masterfully. This is a somber, melancholic science fiction story that has deeper meanings and parallels but can also be enjoyed at face value. When you feel confused... you're supposed to be confused. An absolute 10/10 that will stay with me for years to come. Sometimes, you just don't fit into the backpack.

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is a terrific and somber game that does what many great stories do, speak of the times. The game is fearless with its unique perspective, expressing many difficult themes that some will find uncomfortable or controversial. In 1000xResist, you play as the Watcher, a woman tasked with observing daily life in the Orchard, an underground bunker ruled by the ALLMOTHER, hidden from the dangerous alien “Occupants”. The ALLMOTHER is elusive and controlling, never revealing herself to those in the Orchard until she deems it the right time. The story is incredibly ambitious and satisfies this notion to every degree.In essence, 1000xRESIST is a story of revolt, not only against a tyrannical government but of fate itself. Taking much inspiration from sci-fi hits such as Neon Genesis Evangelion and Nier: Automata, the game tells a fantastic story on a personal and social scale. It examines the psychology and philosophy of its characters and details how they affect the ALLMOTHER’s underground society. 1000xRESIST is a thousand year odyssey that chronicles the origins of the story’s central society, unraveling the traumatic events and philosophies that shaped the Orchard. The times change, people come and go, nations rise and fall, and traumatic scars grow. Witness the end of a world and the birth of a new one. The path paved here is new and unique in the video game medium.Despite being a science fiction game seemingly far removed from the present day, that is not the case. At the heart of this story lies the 2019-2020 Hong Kong protests, where millions marched to resist against the epitome of tyranny itself. From this narrative core is where we see the game at its most real and personal, seeping into every part of the story and subsuming it as a greater whole. 1000xRESIST becomes a generational story of the torch of resistance being passed from one generation to the next. It's a resonant narrative for every nation that ever resisted against tyranny. The gameplay of 1000xRESIST is minimal, the game deliberately lacks combat, opting to focus on exploration, puzzles, and fun movement. Explore underground cities, schools, caves, and apartments. The game gives everything it has within its narrative ambitions, impressing with its visual moods. Notably its endings remain as the strongest gameplay aspect, providing its players with many choices and several impactful endings. The fate of the Orchard is in your hands.Speaking of visuals, the graphics are stylized to a great degree. Sometimes, the game does look strange, but remains fitting to the story of 1000xRESIST. There’s a great use of color, typically used for character associations and symbolism. It's very good stuff.The soundtrack is also super amazing, evoking all the mood it wants. Every track fits with each scene, creating an even better game.Overall, 1000xRESIST is a modern masterpiece. The story is amazing, original, intellectually interesting and emotionally challenging. The characters are well-defined and its setting is fully realized. But most importantly, it's a game with a voice worth listening to. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most tightly written, impactful, moving, cerebral and deeply heartfelt stories I have experienced in gaming, period. It was made by Canadian devised theatre creators who got their projects shelved during the pandemic, and then got money from the Canada Media Fund to make this. Their immersive theatre experience shows in how they beautifully frame their plot moments, and amazing story crafting. The art direction is top notch! The plot draws on real events like the Umbrella Revolution and Covid, as well as themes of bullying, xenophobia, the immigrant experience, and political unrest to create a tightly woven plot that had me hooked from the beginning. It's a gripping sci-fi, but at it's innermost core, 1000xResist is about mothers and daughters, memories, and what trauma we pass down from generation to generation. The voice acting is tight, there is no line of dialogue wasted, and the music is also amazing.  Don't spoil it for yourself by looking up videos. Just play it blind. You wont regret it If you like Nier or Evangelion, you'll love this.Hekki Allmo Sunset Visitor. Make more great art!
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: This game proves that you don't need hundreds of people and dollars to create a story experience that will stick in your head long after you've finished it. (I think the core team was 6 people after watching a documentary on Youtube about it's development.)First off, this is NOT an action game. If anything it shares more DNA with visual novels and you will do a lot of talking and listening with static characters dotted around a number of enclosed areas. However, when it's over it feels like you have experienced something way more than the sum of it's parts.The story spans from near present day to the far future, and essentially shows the ramifications of a bit of selfishness and bullying between two schoolgirls and it's impact across multiple post-apocalyptic timelines, including alien invasion, world ending viruses, underground bunkers full of senseless murder and a LOT of clones. The last section of the game gave me some real 'To The Moon' vibes as well, as you dip into a character's mind to re-live sections of their past.Can't really explain any more, yet magically all these themes tie together and you come away with an understanding of why this sits at overwhelmingly positive on Steam. Hekki Allmo!
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: landmark achievement when it comes to narrative adventure games. character writing paired with the voice acting is incredible, you really love to see a game clearly trying to be meaningful and interesting written by people who 1) actually have interesting things to say and 2) can actually writebeyond that what really sets this game apart is its clarity of vision -- no hamfisted RPG mechanics or overly complicated "choices matter" stuff, it truly just lets you loose in a weird ass world filled with fun characters you wanna learn more about and delivers on all fronts. another huge point in its favor is its willingness to not shy away from real life politics, not going to spoil anything in a review but its a breath of fresh air especially since i think the narrative could have suffered heavily from being too abstract if they hadn't really expertly grounded it in real events people can emotionally connect with
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is truly something special. I was initially put off by the visuals - the quality of the models is low to the point of occasionally being uncanny, especially side characters. However, as all the reviews on the store page say, the writing in this game is phenomenal. The subject matter is heavy, but there are important lessons and insights to be gained from as early as chapter 1. A truly unique work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay 3/10 Story 10/10This is what would happen if you blended Nier, The Matrix, M Dot Strange, V for Vendetta, Bladerunner, Death Stranding, Deadly Premonition, Eternal Threads, a philosophy 101 course, a Jacob Geller video essay, Promised Neverland, Evangelion, and a bunch of closeted clone lesbians together. I cried very much at this milkshake of an indie game. It's worth experiencing for sure but only at the right time and that's maybe the most meta thing about it. Very cool that it exists and very cool that I got to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: This game, man. It's so hard for me to give praises to a game based on its story alone, specially when I try to avoid spoiling it to encourage more people into playing it.I think the trailer speaks for itself showing how much potential this experience has going for itself. And, just in its first minutes I knew there was something great waiting for me. Now, when I finished chapter 2 at the two hour mark, I knew something unique was waiting for me. I don't believe there will be a better game this year or in a couple of years to come since this one is the best game I have played in ages. Yes, is THAT good.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: A very poignant story in a stylish package. Special mention to the voice acting which is superb all the way through and very endearing to the characters. This is particularly noteworthy as this is very much a dialogue and text driven game. The amount and the quality of the voice lines for such a relatively small game is honestly very impressive. Also of note is the music, constantly accompanying the narration, that does a lot to elevate the game's emotions.This game covers a lot of ground thematically, with references to real life events both explicitly and by analogy, which makes for a really heartfelt and gripping story to follow along. It's clear that this a story that means a lot to the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: This is a deeply narrative game that is ready to take you on an emotional journey.I loved this game. It took me deep into a rich world with complex characters that I came to love (then hate, then love again). I really felt the flaws that made them who they are and why they do what they do. I felt quite a lot in fact, they are some incredibly sad and beautiful sequences that I'm still thinking about.I think its really cool that a game would take risks in telling its story, and when I thought I knew how things would go I was sure to get a surprise.If you're into a big story with big feels then this games for you.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful and interesting slow burn story that has a lot of coming-of-age tropes packed into a neat sci-fi "end of the world" scenario. Think Logan's Run meets Evangelion and a sprinkling of Fight Club. If you like Suda51 titles, this might fulfill a certain craving for something new along those lines visually but not thematically (not really any moons to speak of). A couple of little puzzles here and there to keep the gameplay relevant to what is essentially a robust visual novel.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so stylish, and really engaging to play -- there's lots to discover and cool details, and the game play gets really active in certain sections; so many surprises! The voiced texts are a really cool feature, and add an additional depth -- super satisfying. I love point and click adventure games, and this one does NOT disappoint! The content is also really cool and relevant.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played the demo section but will update my review as I proceed. Even in the opening hour or so, this game is extremely compelling. A blend of all-too-familiar modern school life in the middle of a terrifying pandemic, and a bizarre far future society of clone girls. The art is striking and beautiful. The music is earthy and intense. The dialogue is oozing with character. And while the gameplay is obviously not the main focus, I do like how you navigate obstacles by jumping between different time periods, which means as you solve the (very simple) puzzles, your also forcing yourself to experience parallel stories.Definitely looking forward to more.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: More of a visual novel with minimal gameplay. One of the best-written, if not THE best-written, narratives I have ever seen in a video game. Very innovative storytelling that covers themes of dispossession, familial estrangement, and diaspora politics with the gravity they deserve in a sci-fi setting. Does not treat the player like an idiot. Deserves to be more well-known. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: + Beautiful and haunting narrative centered around the morality different "humans" post-apocalypse, woven from many threads, this tale is unforgettable. Messaging is fantastic, incredible ambiguity at every turn.+ Characters that feel real in every way despite being as unreal as they come, the act like people despite their inhumanity and feel believable in every way.+ Aesthetically incredible, while it appears to be yet another basic anime game on the surface, it transcends what's typically done in this space and ends up in the highest echelon of quality+ Music is truly spectacular- Game play was as boring as it gets, running around and talking for 11 hours is essentially all you do, there's an argument to be made this game should have been 5-6 hours of cut scenes where you just click to forward dialogue, more like a visual novelThis game receives my maximum rating: S
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is the most interesting piece of media from 2024 that I've experienced so far in any medium. I've already written an entire blog post about it and only barely scratched the surface of my thoughts on it, and I expect it's going to stick with me for a while.If anything you've seen or heard about it sounds at all interesting or like it might be your kind of thing I can say it's extremely worth the price and dozen or so hours of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: This is what I play games for, hell, this is what I experience art for. An absolute masterclass in narrative design. Confident in every decision. A complex and layered sci-fi story built on a deeply personal and focused foundation, mastering the challenge of evoking strong emotions while navigating heady concepts and world building.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: 1000xRESIST is nothing short of a masterpiece. Incredible narrative, voice acting, world building. Despite most characters being clones of each other the voice actors were able to deliver performances that really set them apart from each other. And each character was filled with personality that really made them feel unique. The game play can be a little repetitive but everything else was more than enough to hold my interest. Oh and DEVS please add a map to the main hub area lmao.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review: On a technical level, this game is bordering on being an absolutely hellish experience, but from a narrative perspective, the game more than delivers. A story with themes of Generational Trauma, Existentialism, Diaspora, Letting go of the past and finding hope in the uncertainty of the future. Only complaint is that this game is a walking simulator, and the game tries to make the "walking" a chore from time to time with a nearly impossible to navigate hub world, and a compass that is invisible 50% of the time because the color matches the environment around you. But other than that, the narrative had me hooked from beginning to end. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

_childDocuments_.review:
The year is unknown and the air is unbreathable. All that remains are you and your sisters, living under the shadow of a mysterious disease, cloning one another into eternity. In the safety of the Garden, survival is simple. Stay inside. Serve your function.

Your name and function: WATCHER. You relive the memories of the ALLMOTHER and uphold her glory. When your closest sister, FIXER, comes to you with a dangerous rumour, you phase through time, and discover a devastating truth: someone has tampered with history.

1000xRESIST is a hyper-cinematic, narrative adventure. Shift through time. Experience the past, present, and future. Examine memory, identity, and inherited histories, whilst exploring dynamic environments, each with their own distinct style and feel.
_childDocuments_.name: 1000xRESIST

name: Warlander
detailed_description: DISCORD Jump into Discord with us and become directly involved in our community-focused game development! FEATURE SUGGESTIONS AND BUG REPORTING We are using a public feature upvoter and bug tracker to allow the community to help identify potential bugs and also have a voice in determining which features will make it into the game. About the Game Sharpen your blades and ready your warhammers. Join an army of up to 100 players and battle each other in action-packed, player vs. player skirmishes and epic castle sieges with the ultimate goal of breaking into the enemy's stronghold, destroying their Core, and claiming victory for you and your allies! Combining elements of MOBA, RPG and Hack & Slash, Warlander offers an action-packed battle experience you haven’t seen before. Compete with up to 100 players in a stylish medieval fantasy world, marked by war over magical entities, known as Cores. Capture towers for faster redeployment and awaken cataclysmic idols such as scale meteors, storms and battle robots to turn the tides of war in your favor. Control tactical choke points, destroy the enemy's defenses and build mighty siege weapons. A true Warlander maneuvers skillfully across the battlefield and works in unison with their squad to outsmart and overpower any resistance. A deep combat system turns every encounter into a battle of wits. Make use of blocks, guard breaks, parry counters, critical strikes and combo attacks at the right time to overcome any opponent. Your chances of victory greatly depend on how well you perform as a team. Vote on your preferred strategy before each battle and join a squad, each with its own mission. Defense squads protect your castle, build anti-siege weaponry and pay close attention to enemy positions and movement - dealing with each timely and appropriately. Assault squads are all about infiltrating enemy castles. Find a way through your foes’ defenses and destroy the enemy Core. As part of the Special Ops squad, you continuously analyze the state of battle and react flexibly to new threats and opportunities. You are an immortal champion fighting under your Warlord’s banner for control over magical lands and powers. For each battle, you have the ability to inhabit one of up to five different vessels of your design both in appearance and battle skills, otherwise known as your deck. Each deck is different and unique. Build your decks according to your personal strategy and pick the one that best suits your army before the start of each battle. Your successes on the battlefield will not go unnoticed and each display of valor is rewarded. Gaining new valor titles allows you to use better armor, weapons, skills, and talents and diversify your unique selection of decks.

A true Warlander maneuvers skillfully across the battlefield and works in unison with their squad to outsmart and overpower any resistance. A deep combat system turns every encounter into a battle of wits. Make use of blocks, guard breaks, parry counters, critical strikes and combo attacks at the right time to overcome any opponent. Your chances of victory greatly depend on how well you perform as a team. Vote on your preferred strategy before each battle and join a squad, each with its own mission. Defense squads protect your castle, build anti-siege weaponry and pay close attention to enemy positions and movement - dealing with each timely and appropriately. Assault squads are all about infiltrating enemy castles. Find a way through your foes’ defenses and destroy the enemy Core. As part of the Special Ops squad, you continuously analyze the state of battle and react flexibly to new threats and opportunities. You are an immortal champion fighting under your Warlord’s banner for control over magical lands and powers. For each battle, you have the ability to inhabit one of up to five different vessels of your design both in appearance and battle skills, otherwise known as your deck. Each deck is different and unique. Build your decks according to your personal strategy and pick the one that best suits your army before the start of each battle. Your successes on the battlefield will not go unnoticed and each display of valor is rewarded. Gaining new valor titles allows you to use better armor, weapons, skills, and talents and diversify your unique selection of decks.
short_description: Harness the almighty powers of god-like Warriors, Clerics, and Mages, with a unique style that mashes a Medieval-inspired setting, Fantastical items and abilities…and…EVEN POWERFUL ROBOTS! Master siege weapons and cataclysmic spells to control the battlefield and destroy the enemy's core!

_childDocuments_.review: Update 2: I've been banned, because I told them it's "a very bad idea to keep adding maps when your player base is only a few hundred people" in the comment section of their roadmap post. I'll have the proof and message screenshot uploaded under "Artwork".Update: Absolutely stay away. They're deleting everything with even a trace amount of criticism. They outlined a horrible content roadmap that's obviously going to end up splitting their non-existing player base, to which some of us respectfully commented "Pretty bad idea" and explained why. They just deleted all of those, and left only one comment asking for an extra feature.Unfortunately, this feels like a cashgrab that is inches away from being fun.Even if we ignore the blatent pay to win (to the point where someone can literally 1 tap you with a basic attack), there are some bad issues.- Very few players, matchmaking takes ~5 minutes sometimes.- Feels very clunky on all levels. Movement is weird, eg. you can only sprint forward. Using skills locks your camera and I don't like it, personally. Skills and attacks have no queue, so your inputs are ignored if you do anything while already in an animation. You can't chain stuff. The UI is clunky, eg. getting out of a match takes about 30 seconds after it ends because you go through like 5 animated screens. The game has a weird filter on it, I don't know what it is, but all contrast is missing, and it makes it hard to see stuff, together with visual clutter, it's bad. - If your core takes any damage, you might as well give up and let them take it, because if no cores get destroyed the team with the lower core health loses. Now this could be good, but the balance is so bad, either you gate-r**e the enemy team or they gate-r**e you. For... a.. long while. And you don't get a chance to go for theirs. No one can leave the defense.- At the start of a round you can vote one of 3 tactics, Offensive, Balanced, Defensive. Might as well remove this, as only Balanced works.- A LOT of people ignore the tactics and their squads' jobs.- No one plays Clerics (healer) because it's just not fun. It feels like they forgot to add a healer class and just threw it in without any imagination. Clerics only have 2 useful skills, heal, and a clunky movement speed buff, that places an acceleration area below you. So you have to be the first one to charge to buff your team. That gets you killed, because you're the squishiest class. They can also.. place a wall?! Perfect to annoy allies. Heal is also undertuned....- You can become a commander without wanting to (even though you can explicitly chose to become one at the menu, if you want to - also I don't think anyone knows about this - ) because if no one chooses so, it'll be a random person, who will not give a damn about it.- Being a commander is clunky. eg. the map you see to command squads is exactly the same that you see when you die, but sometimes you can't choose respawn point on one, and can't command others on the other (makes sense, but it's hard to even know which one's in front of you). When giving orders the click is sometimes just not recognized.... your orders most of the times are overridden somehow, by other random objectives.... While not being a commander, it's very hard to see what your squad's objectives are, so some people just ignore it.- Respawn times feel too long and you have to sit there through most of it looking at your own corpse.- Catastrophe mechanics and others are not well explained at all, and are just annoying because of weird camera angles, visibility, and limited movement. eg. a tornado completely squashes everyone into a wall, and you can't move, can't see anything, and you'll lift up and be thrown around by it for like 10 seconds. Not really fun time.- Defenses are way too easily broken by anyone, but especially mages. And most people play mage.I think that'd be all.

_childDocuments_.review: Depending on when you get on, the player base is really small. I often find myself in (the normal game mode) 20vs20 with about 8 or so players and the rest being filled with bots. After a while this broke the fun and immersion of the game. Like groups of bots will automatically run into walls and get stuck, or will auto target you so you can't sneak by them. It's not fun with the amount of bots and the maps are not optimized in size for the fun had.The gain for coins and consumables is very slow and it's a trickle. Selling/dismantling items returns little to no value and isn't worth it unless you have too many items that you have to make room for it.This Game have achieved this amazing feat of frustrating balance, just when the game gets good and hits it's critical point of being fun (like really really fun), it ends. The beginning stages are somewhat fun, and then it ramps up when people unlock their higher tiered combatants with game changing moves, and then the game typically ends before people really shine in combat.As it sits, it's not fun to play with bots, and they should probably invent a new player mode for like 8vs8 or 5vs5 combat. It would make for a sort of better moba if the map scaling wasn't so large.The range combat in this game is well balanced and arguably god tier standard to what should be expected in a game, so there's a lot of good here.The battles are fun, but the meta progression is a slow crawl and a grind.The biggest issue is that I find myself in the loading screen or waiting for a game for about less than a quarter of my play time, resulting in this frustrating loop of not being able to fully enjoy the game while also wanting more play time.The gameplay is fine, it's just short and doesn't feel rewarding. Placing consistently top two in a battle sounds nice, but if the lobby of 40 player slots is mainly bots, it's kind of pointless. Then the rewards for placing high does not do much.I want to give this a good rating, but it doesn't feel rewarding to play. And Toylogic has made a banger of a game before, so I was just hoping they could make a spiritual successor to that one game people know and love. This just isn't it chief.

_childDocuments_.review: On the positive side, this game can be fun. Unlike many others, I like the idea of having to level up individual characters and the pay-to-win factor is limited by the amount of gear points you can spend on characters. Many of the minor mechanics and features are nice but I don't want to spend too much time listing them.On the other hand, Warlander really has some problems. 1. Just as other reviews say: Progressing the battle pass takes ages and is unrewarding, especially with the TWO premium passes.2. The commander role is terrible. The interface does not respond ~30% of the time/of my clicks and resetting all participating squads to their "default" commands once their objective has been achieved is aweful. No, I do not want my castle guards to fall back from the middle of the map if our half is untouched by the enemy! Also, there neither is a reward for following orders nor for making sensible ones. Therefore, you cannot expect to ever get any other order than to stay at home when playing castle guard. This role should either be dropped or completely revamped.3. Just as other reviews say: Many games feel like a question of either stomp or getting stomped. 2 team games also often end too quickly for them to really be exciting and try different strategies if the teams are rather evenly matched. Additionally, once the fight gets to the core, the game just looses all fun; it's just blindly smashing everything, casting everything, playing roulette whether you die or not and not being able to distinguish between friend and foe because the screen is overloaded with effects.I still enjoy it most of the time and I will continue playing it. I really hope to change my review and wholeheartedly recommend the game in the future. Please make it so.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone with over 1000 hours in the game, I had high hopes for this game. I was praising the developers when the game was first introduced, and thought that the game would be heading down a good path for consumers based on their willingness to interact, and change the game. Ultimately, along the way the developers have lost all passion for the game, and have stopped interacting with the community in the ways the once did.It feels as if all of the funds for the servers to play the game, have been shifted to another project. The game runs horribly on the server side, and most of the time you can't even block without your enemy hitting straight through your shield. In the beginning you could tell that they were focused, and were trying to ensure that Warlander was the best game that it would be for the community. They kept their voices loud, and it was clear what they were doing for us next. As of now, most of the changes that are being made to the game are minor or haven't shifted the game. We had one major change at the end of last season that to shift the game in any sort of regard, and all that was done was squishing EVERYTHING down based on a set percentile across the board. This change stripped veterans of hard earned items that played an advantage into the game, which took several hundreds of hours to earn, away from them in order to cater to new players. The very next change, they make it so that skill cool-downs don't reset on death, requiring level 5 skills in most slots disregarding everything that they said about catering to new players.We are now over a month into Season 1, and the only content that we have received is content that was planned for launch of the season and needed to be pushed back. They focus more on things like making sure that their Discord is clean, and ensuring that they give creator spotlights while somehow managing to ignore some of their biggest creators that have followed them the longest in said spotlights.They pretend that they care about everything that the community points out in the game, but at the end of the day, bug reports that are submitted from March are still unaddressed. The Feature Suggestion page which is supposed to be an area for the community to voice changes that should come to the game, is completely ignored. There are so many Features that have been suggested since last September when the game first went into closed Beta, and they still haven't even acknowledged them. It's to the point that it's clear, it's all customer facing. You reach out to the support team directly, you get an automated response, and they close your ticket. Everything that they do for the community seems to be ensuring that they don't have a negative backlash, which is why a large bulk of the things seem to get ignored. I believe in doing so they have created some of the most negative relationships between developer and consumer I have had the displeasure of being a part of.Ultimately at the highest level, Warlander is just a large game of who can abuse the mechanics that the developers have left unaddressed and unpolished for so long. Overwhelmed by the fact the bots are all on the same code, perform the most optimal strategies without any human factors, and all target the same individual? Just jump out of their reach, and go AFK. They aren't programmed to do anything but sit and stare at you. You'll be providing a huge service to your team, all while giving you extra time to hate the AI and developers for leaving it unaddressed since before game release.Tired of Cataclysms not spawning in an area you can receive them? Feed the enemy the towers, and you'll be able to ensure game shifting Cataclysms spawn in your base completely uncontested for the rest of the game.   You want to beat your opponent without them getting to play the game? Just destroy their stairs so they can't reach the counter siege they should always have access to. As a bonus, you can stand outside of their Keep walls after destroying their stairs and thanks to the changes in PATCH 1.2.1.1004 they won't even be able to open their doors! Congratulations! You've successfully made it so the enemy can't play the game.The funniest part about all of it is that it constantly gets complained about in the highest level streams for the game, and Plaion Developers have witnessed this several times. At the end of the day, nothing is done for the game. They just accept the negative publicity. They don't even speak to the community to address the issues. They simply ignore them as if they don't exist. They are continuing down a path where they are going to implement some sort of competitive guild system, but the game is still in shambles with all of the glaring flaws. It's going to be the same thing as the public game mode currently. Who can abuse the most mechanics that the developers have left unaddressed since Closed Beta? As of now, your number 1 player in Warlander has abused a catapult glitch that doubles points which was in the game since Console release. They go so far to lose games, but continue to abuse the glitch to ensure that they get 60 points per game on the ladder regardless. The only hope that this game even seemingly had was the 4 vs 4 arena mode which I had no care for. Sadly, even the videos that they have released previewing the mode, it's very clear that the developers are currently just too disconnected from their own game. I hope that it's something that they are able to address and fix in the future, but as of now I wouldn't recommend Warlander. You'll enjoy it for the first few hundred hours, get attached to the fact that it's new and there isn't any game like it right now, but then the lack of balance changes, glaring flaws, and getting ghosted by the developers will just leave you sad that you've invested the time in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing over 30 hours of this game I wanted to share my experience a remove some of the stigma that I think overflowed from the beta. The Boost can be purchased with in game currency, they are not locked behind a paywall, and all they do is boost exp, items, and rarity. I use them all the time, and I buy them from selling items in game. I wanted to also comment on some of the posts I've seen:Well not in this game, your items are soft locked on your characters by Title/CP and every battle is soft locked by your Valor you earn through out the match. /e facepalm... maybe a bit... but isn't that the point, Yes if you play more, and have boosts on more, you're going to have better gear... but you start the battle out just like everyone else valor capped as a basic Mage/Warrior/Cleric... you have to get valor and spawn other characters just like everyone else, and guess what, there have been countless times as a CP capped 250 cleric I've killed every class at higher valor/title, the items are balance so they don't completely make you a god... but even if they do.. its temporary and also time-gated, even if you have max valor in the battle.I have several mythical, items now at this point, some I got even when boosts were off, but guess what... Now that that is out of the way do I like this game?Yes, it is great, teamwork is a must, and you need to pay attention to the beginning quests to fully understand what is going on. Also check out the steam community Guides, A lot of people have put together some very useful information.Give the game a chance, play with friends*UPDATE 3/23/2024Game seems to be pretty dead (Peak 250ish people), some of the initial changes really broke the classes, the barrier to entry and the CP/Valor/Deck building was admittedly confusing initially so I can see that being a barrier for a lot of people who tried the game for a small play session. _childDocuments_.review: Good stuff. All three roles are enjoyable and impactful. I recommend it. A lot of players are on console which makes the game more fun since PC master race. Each game is only 15 minutes too.20v20 MOBA break enemy core to win. You're in a squad of four. Vote to be Defense, Assault, or Special Ops. Defend your castle with cannons, ballista and oil. Assault enemy castle with catapult, siege towers, and rams (and sometimes robots, tornadoes, and meteor showers). Special Ops focuses on capturing towers which are spawn points for your side. Its nice spontaneously working together with people as a team to get your role done. Warrior: Highest health, great defense, good damage. Can't push forward without them.Cleric: Medium health, Medium defense, low damage. Heals & revives.Mage: Lowest health, no shield, good damage. Many ways to play, I love ignition for the fire bowling ball and ice spear for sniping people.Playing a specific character will grant exp to that character (you can make 5 characters). _childDocuments_.review: Really a shame they got rid of Happy Wars and tried to replace it with this. Maybe if you're not coming here from Happy Wars you'll find a bit of enjoyment here, but the harsher emphasis on microtransactions still leads me to believe this might be objectively inferior. Unlike Happy Wars where getting a nice variety of weapons and hats to customize with, even with just free currency, isn't too hard, Warlander will just give you boring realistic stuff and put any funnier more outlandish cosmetics behind a paywall, but even then, the more realistic artstyle makes them actually look kind of jarring.Back to the microtransactions though, they're pretty oppressive. You can't even make two characters of every class, which I feel like should be standard so you can make one class that needs no deploy points and one that does, but no. You'll have to tediously go to a character and manually change their title (and possible gear and abilities) if you ever feel like switching something as basically as that up. If you're not someone coming from Happy Wars, then you can ignore what's below, this is just my perspective on stuff I find inferior to Happy Wars.------------------------------------------I think my biggest issue with this game is how some of the more fun team skills are now relegated to randomly spawning "idols" that appear around the map and are team specific. Tornado, meteor storm, and I think a few others are now locked to these. Every class can use them, they only take one person to use them now, and they're on a timer, so if you don't get to them or use them in time they're just gone. I don't like this. I think team skills were more fun since they didn't limit your strategy with a timer, and getting your team to help you out with them really emphasizes the team aspect of the game. The timer just makes it feel more like a chore than good strategy or anything fun like that. As someone who played mostly mage in Happy Wars, I don't like how mage plays now. Because mage doesn't get a hand held weapon, made pretty much plays like a TPS zombies game, hoping everyone else stays far away from you while you're shooting them. It's a big departure from how warriors and clerics play, both having weapons and shields. I also don't really like how the higher titles have abilities they can do on their own. If I choose the highest title for mage, it doesn't really matter that it costs a ton of deploy points, it feels wrong to be able to just walk to an enemy tower, cast a lightning storm all by myself, and just totally lock it down and kill anyone who approaches, floating in the air so most things can't even hit me. Something that good should require at least a few people to execute in my opinion, even with the deploy points.The high title warrior ability where he grows is kind of cool, but I still feel like that should also be a team skill. Strategy altogether is kind of different for this game. I think this is because everything's larger scale. People are less likely to be packed together, and abilities (for the most part) don't target as large a range as their Happy Wars counterparts, so the focus feels a lot like it's shifted more towards many small 1v1s than team fights if that makes sense, and that just makes you lean towards Warrior because in most situations you'll feel like you were better off as a warrior class. This is a subjective point, but I also just don't like the aesthetics. Happy Wars was so fun and cartoony, and this new aesthetic is just so standard and generic. It also makes the few fun cosmetics there are really clash with the artstyle, especially considering how boring your default stuff is, so your character can look like a baseball player amongst a bunch of knights and it just feels really weird. Happy Wars' artstyle lent itself well to having a wide range of both stereotypical and more bizarre cosmetics because the artstyle made everything already at least a little cartoony, so nothing really looked out of place as outlandish as it might've been. Here you have most people with a realistic shield and then for some reason someone's going to have an emoji shield that looks so jarring. I have a few more complaints, both subjective and what I feel are objective complaints, but I think I got my point across. If I ever get an Xbox One I'll probably just play Happy Wars on that instead of playing this on Steam. I wish they'd just bring it back honestly because it was very fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is generally alright. The core idea is there and there is fun to be had. Since it's free, you lose absolutely nothing picking it up with your friends for a few matches and then uninstalling right after.Based on my own experience I would say that it's not pay to win. I've also had zero issues with the game's anti-cheat.It does however have a few key issues that Is holding the game back by a substantial margin. I don't believe this game will ever reach general popularity because of it's issues and can see the game dying pretty quick down the road.-Combat is clunky, VERY clunky. The way staggers work and combat's reliance on staggers means there's very little mobility in combat and it feels awful. Duels consists of little more than trying to stagger-lock eachother and when you are stagger locked and unable to do anything about the button mashing your opponent is unleashing on you, it feels like you're just sitting there waiting for death. I Must emphasise this as my current biggest issue I have with the game. Being staggered feels horrible. It's just not fun. Everything else about the game is fun. But being staggered, something that the combat system is built around, just simply isn't fun.-The game's netcode makes combat extremely inconsistent. You can time your block-stagger-crit combo perfectly only for your opponent to blow through your guard. 75% of the time the crit markers don't even appear for me. I regularly knock opponents out of my basic attack range with the charge attack resulting in frustration as I swing into the air, locking myself into an animation during which my opponent just runs away.-No dodging. Most of the issues I have with combat can be fixed with a stagger-breaking dodge. The fact that there is no dodging in a fast-paced third person melee game like this is complete developer oversight. So long as it lacks this key bit of common functionality combat will continue to be nothing more than button mashing after an engage with little mobility and no way to break staggers or avoid engages. See the above two points.-Game runs like crap. I've got a fairly decent pc, but can't get beyond 40 fps and very regularly drop to 20 fps on the lowest settings.-Little content. The content that is there is fun enough, but you're doing the same thing again and again and again. You don't need to split the playerbase with different gamemodes, but some map-specific features akin to Heroes of the Storm would do a lot for the game.-No chat? In a competitive multiplayer game focused around teamwork? Really? The reasons for this is beyond my comprehension. until some form of chat is introduced whether voice or text, people will continue to ignore the roles that they are assigned and will continue to do nought but try to rush through the middle of the map every match. Despite heavy incentives to work as a team, everybody currently just sort of does their own thing, and it's infuriating.-Little equipment variety (Nitpick). The gear needs to vary more both mechanically and visually. My tier 5 cleric looks near identical to my tier 2 cleric. Clerics only use maces, Warriors only use swords. Having a visual and mechanical variety in gear adds a lot to a game's depth and also simply makes the game look more interesting.-Gender locked classes (Nitpick). I want to play as a sexy knight lady with a zweihander. Pls let me.

Everything is OP in its own way, which means nothing is OP and it's just over all annoying to fight against enemies.I can't reiterate how much this game needs a voice chat, or at least text chat. There's a whole line that describes a game mode as making and breaking alliances, but the fun of that would be between players talking to each other about it.Progression seems pretty favored towards spending some cash. That's fine, but not very fun, and I feel like it'll hamper new players getting into the game; the items that you can get, and the perks on them, do make a whole world of difference.Prices also seem a bit high. I understand you have to make the cash, but you should bleed through paper cuts and not gouges - this game has no esports or competitive angle, so I don't see myself spending the cash for skins or loot in the way that I would League of Legends, a game that has confirmed staying power.Game is also poorly optimized.Game has quite a few noticeable bugs.Team play is virtually non-existent.After reading all of this you may think I'm only resentful for the game. Quite the opposite in fact - it is probably one of the better multiplayer experiences in a while. It has very solid bones. Again, this is a middling review even if I call it negative here. Do I recommend it? Technically yes. In its current state? Not a whole lot.
