_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:Gambling Simulator with no resemblance of balance!!!As time goes on, new players will be in even bigger disadvantage than those who start week after launch.Month after launch, only people who enjoy self flagellation should join this game.= = = =Itemization is everything in this game. And you are at mercy of randomized items you get, and random results of recrafting perks on items.For example:Basic Tier.0 Mage starts with 100HP, if you manage to get all random trashy T.1 items, 160HP. If you get HP bonus items 220HP.Tier.1 Mage still starts with 100HP, too. But can get up to 340HP through proper items.Tiers got up to 5.Looks OK? Intend to use highest unlocked Character Tier? Sorry: "NO!!!"At start of each game, you can only use Tier.0 character. And as you get match points, Tier.1 unlocks. In mid game Tier.2. Tier.3 will become available at mid-late game. And so on.And when you die on that higher than T.0 character, it gets cool down. Which means you can't use items you put on higher Tier.And we are back on itemization. By time you have available Tier.1 character, you do not have even one Appropriate item for it. You can cannibalize your T.0 character for half decent experience. But then you'll start game with very underwhelming T.0 garbage to which you'll have to return every time your T.1 dies.By time you have T.2, situation is even worse.And here comes business model. No, you do not buy good items, that would be one time payment. You'll have to pay constantly for higher drop rate of items after match. Why?Because F2P player gets 1-2 garbage items per match. If it is armor you can sell it for 30, if it is shield 50, weapon 60.Want to buy basic garbage weapon of your choice? 900. So sell:buy ratio is 1:15.Not that bad? Weapon for Tier.1 costs 2700. For Tier.2 6300.===> So, you better pay for consumables increasing drop rate.On top, you may have noticed mention of recrafting. Higher the weapon grade, more slots for perks. More space for gambling.Chance to get perk you want on T.0 weapon is 1 in 5 as it has one perk slot. On T.1 it is 1 in 25 as it has 2 slots. With T.2, you go to 1 in 125.===> Pay for few hundred reroll crystals, just for your T.2 (mid tier) character.= = = =So, what's proper strategy? Max out T.0 character. Never cannibalize it. Slowly keep improving T.1 character even at time you have T.3 available. From what I have seen, you can start considering use of T.2 after 80~100 matches depending on luck.= = = =Character Balance: As shown above, important player's stats go up 2~4 times even at lower tiers based on gear. As such, Mage which is meant to be glass cannon can have higher survivability than Warrior who is meant to be tanky. Don't be surprised that min-maxed mage one shots you, it is not hack, it is game design.So in situation when there is nothing like balance within one Class. (Not even within one Tier of one class.) There simply can't be balance between classes.Perk Balance: Perks you can roll differ greatly. For example, on T.1 weapon with 2 perks, you can roll 2x attack boost which equals to +15% DPS.Or you can roll 2x ammo boost which equals +75% magazine capacity. For weapon which empties magazine in second and half, but reloads 2 seconds. You not only increase burst damage by 75% before you need to take cover, but total DPS in long run goes up by 45%.Other example can be armor with HP rolls vs damage against specific class rolls. T.1 perks for T.1 character can get you up to 30% extra damage against one specific class, or general 10% damage to all, if you put each class at 2 armor pieces. Or you can get extra 120 life. So you can be tanky mage without 10% damage bonus on armor. Or you can sacrifice 35% of your life to get that 10% damage bonus which is nothing in comparison to what you ca get from weapon perks.= = = =Many things in this game exist only to keep you down with useless stats/functionality. For example heal on Cleric. Basic heal is single target, you have 3 charges. Can't self heal. Then, if lucky you can obtain AoE heal with long duration, in which Cleric heals even herself. And objective power of this heal is like 3~4 times in 1v1 situation. And like 15~20 times in group fights. Cleric without this AoE heal is nobody.= = = =Battle Pass: Free vs PaidFree mostly gives you one time consumable version of what you obtain as permanent in Paid Battle Pass. Free is basically advertisement for Paid Battle Pass.Same way as bad match rewards are advertisement for reward improving consumables.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to review Neutral since the game needs some work on QOL changes and ingame changes.The game is very simple to understand and play. There are no hitting keys for combos outside setting your skills up for more synergy between them.The game has 3 classes or characters to choose from; the warrior, the cleric, and the mage.The Warrior and Cleric are the melee focused classes but they are can have a secondary weapon for range attack. The mage can have some close range Spell Weapons but that class is more for AOE damage and long range attacks, he dies fast.There is Points system for equipment that is tied to your Title. Titles come from Tier 1 to Tier 5, and you unlock them by playing and doing objectives. The higher the Tier Title you use the more CP(for the inventory points) you have to equip better gear, weapons, spells, skills, or talents. The Equipment system is a balance in how you want to go equipped into battle.You start the matches with as a 0 Tier character, as you get more points you raise your Tier so you can start using the better and higher Tier characters you have. As soon as you start using a higher tier character you start the cooldown to that character in case you die with it. It goes from 180 seconds to about 5 minutes of cooldown, don't die.At the moment all ingame purchases are for cosmetics using the Premium coin or extra character slots, or extra XP type boosts. You can also buy the boosts with regular game coins.The Premium coin uses the scamming system where you buy more points than you need and then you are left with 20 or 30 coins that wont get you anything. You can't buy the coins exactly as you need them.The combat is a smash buttons to attack and hope you as the warrior stun lock your opponent so he wont retaliate. Clerics spam AOE heals, and mages spam lightning attacks, fire walls, and sniper from afar.There is no ingame chat or way to communicate with team mates except to spam the Ping system and hope the idiot understand what you mean.

_childDocuments_.review: (It's worth noting that my initial gameplay was on PC, but I've since been playing on PS5 and any additions/modifications I make to this review will be from that perspective)Game's fine.Gameplay wise, at least. I don't wanna delve into the store and micro-transactions so early, because everyone else here has already talked it to the core and I wanna talk about the gameplay first.There is a real game to be found here. It really is solid all around and by all accounts is a relatively enjoyable experience.Team Placements are understandable, but practically RNG since you're playing with almost exclusively random people it's impossible to ensure you get the role you want.The maps are fine, unique though sometimes highly confusing. The castle layouts are also fine, but due to the castle layout being large most of the time it was a little more confusing as to where I was supposed to go to build certain ballistas but it's just something you'd have to play and learn.Combat is pretty good. Simple, in most regards, far from your Chivalry and whatnot. But For what it's worth I reckon it alongside the characters abilities adds just enough depth to give you enjoyable moments in large and hectic fights.I think giving your classes cooldowns after a death is a really solid idea, it changes a lot of how you'd normally play and makes you have to develop strategies to both how you build your classes and how/when you use them in battle. The rank system is just terrible. It has been changed since this initial review and is now absolutely horrid. The system was already troublesome for making rather snowballed games by essentially keeping you behind and not letting you progress before the enemy would essentially overrun the first line of defense. But the new system relies on a CURRENCY to KEEP you in your higher ranks to play as your stronger characters. So if you're preforming poorly, or even get unlucky, you'll almost never advance. It is a miserable experience and I just cannot even imagine what they were thinking with this. Graphics, although are good by objective standards, aren't very interesting? Looking at the game and promotional art, I'd never have looked into this game if it wasn't for my prior history. It's just basic realistic medieval fantasy fights with a burly man warrior, a dainty woman cleric, and an old bearded wizard with the game's only interest being the magical flare+effects of the maps and abilities. The maps look great, I will say. Some equally realistic and bland, but still look good. The layouts are fun, lots of open spaces and routes to flank and fight with, I think they got a good grasp on this one.Menu's are fine. Some things were a little confusing and took a second or two of rummaging around to make sense of but nothing ever made me genuinely question it's intent, some to my dismayThis game quite honestly has an AMAZING foundation. Gameplay is solid, controls are simple, premise is easy. If this was just what it was, I'd happily recommend this game and play with friends.But, inevitably, I'm can't recommend this to anyone. As the game is egregiously monetized. From "Progression Boost"ers, making the game pay-to-win, to making decorative customization (the best and most enjoyable part of any F2P) of your equipment convoluted and predatory. Loss, after loss, after loss as I can only sit and watch my enemies with visibly far better equipment just roll my team no matter how much effort I put in. I would practically support two entire teamfights on opposite sides of my castle and fending off waves, but it would never matter since my team just didn't have the ability to push in. And since the enemies took 1% off our core we'd lose to a time-out.The game has interesting mechanics and gameplay loops that can offer a unique and enjoyable experience, But the store and it's payed high-tier players will always rear it's ugly head around and remind you the harsher aspects of this game.A part of me really does want to see this game succeed, as it could 100% be the evolution of a small but beloved game IP that gave me and thousands of others countless hours of joy and entertainment. But I can only sit and see what the ToyLogic and the others have plans for this game.Or they could just bring back Happy Wars. That'd be great too.(I'd like to note once again, I am playing on PS5, however I have since uninstalled this game from my device and will not be playing it again for the foreseeable future. This edit for my review could be my last, though I still hope ToyLogic and those behind them can still have it in their heart to turn their sails and pull this game in a direction I would be more than happy to play. Though unless someone would like to personally message me and tell me to try again, this game may as well have never existed in my life. I wish you all the utmost luck and thank you to whoever has read this far. I've only said so much because I care.)

_childDocuments_.review: Please read to the end for how this game can become significantly less hot garbage; skip to it if you have to. In the mean time, here's some scathing remarks.All it's good mechanics are stolen directly from MOBA's. The map design, the bots (probably unintentionally close to the weak bots in games like LoL, but yeah around 40-75% of any given team are bots), even the microtransactions are taken from other games. Much of it's game "balance" and mechanics is stolen from happy wars. The spells, attacks, every one of the 'cataclysms' and 'group spells'. Even the 'armor style' is clearly a poor imitation of the bonus class system. A vast majority are from happy wars and the ones that are wildly different, to nobody's surprise, tend to be overpowered; Crows, Powerbomb, Colossus Form for god's sake. Meanwhile, they poorly apply a lot of Happy Wars' old abilities, from Ressurect to Smash to Dispel, which are wet blankets when you compare them to other things that could be in their slot. The resulting system is slipshod and patched together, with things feeling oddly disjointed at times.My theory regarding the rank system is, they designed it originally to be far more flexible than it currently is, then realized that if it was how I would much prefer it to be- 5 individual title and loadout selections for each character- these players might be overwhelmed by the amount of options or, worse, complain about the small selection of spells compared to how much the loadouts offer you by means of changing strategy. Let me explaine exactly how bad this is;This thing, the rank system, has become the most problematic issue when it comes to advancing my characters. Limitations surrounding titles mean you can advance all you want but if you don't want to spend most of the match with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ character because the higher tiers can take more than four minutes to regenerate once they die (and they will) you will be restricted to more reasonable one stars. You're basically rendered ineffective because being more bold would leave you playing the rest of the game with a handicap if you're killed; a recipe for a major steamroll. You can't play the game how you want and can't benefit from most of your grinding because they wanted to balance the OP characters. Truth is, this idea is sound on paper. In Happy Wars you had huge bullet sponges of endgame characters that could make the game unfun if you get targeted by them, your only possible reprieve being cliffs that these vetera players are far too smart to risk getting anywhere near. Issue is, OP is still OP. In fact, all they did was pivot most of the strength from the equipment to the abilities. As a result, have ruined their veneer of balance by shooting themselves in the foot. Remember how respawn times for characters get insanely high? Well, if you happen to be a four star fighting a five star, get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ I guess because they have some of the most OP spells in the game and they have cooldowns barely longer than the average group spell. Take Collossus Form as an example. Instant full heal, 300 max health bonus, 30% more damage, 36% faster movement speed while guarding, an insanely annoying group stun attack that can be casted ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incessantly, plus an automatic level 5 Barrier, all with a duration of 15 seconds.The cooldown? . Do you know how high a TIER 3 CHARACTER's respawn is? 280. They can wipe teams because they shut down your highest level characters faster than you can respawn, and this is FAR from okay. You are already restricted to just 5 characters. The moment you die, that goes down by 20% for what can be a quarter of the match. It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous.How they SHOULD have done it, is make it so that you can select 5 different loadouts for each character. One for each title. Respawn for that particular character increases up to a full minute at 5 stars, but the super abilities themselves have a use limit per game. And, once you advance a character to their 5 star form, you can't advance the others. One character can use the same items across their multiple tiers, but different ones can't. To balance the OP abilities that are far simpler, like Powerbomb and Crow, simply make them part of titles. Currently, one Centurion or the rare Souleater is literally all it takes to win a game. They can just ignore your entire team if they want and prioritize the core during their 15 seconds. If they have good items, they can even one-wave the core on their own due to how OP Roar is for crowd control, and how good their guard is. The defenses are just too weak to support the level of abilities offered in Warlander; as a Commander for most battles, the Attack formation wins far, FAR more frequently than the other two. The reason why? The ♥♥♥♥♥♥ automarker system. It constantly overrides your orders based off of the stratagem of the units, and in defensive teams it basically leaves your team twiddling your thumbs most of the time without considering the threats like catapults or siege towers unless you manually do so; it often GOES OUT of it's way to change them from what you want. The bots literally are useless without proper orders, so get bent I guess if you are trying to defend and need help, because the automarker will basically tell you to get ♥♥♥♥♥♥. After all, doing 1% more damage to it is how you win, and if an enemy team gets in? The automarker doesn't care.Oh right, yeah, the royally ♥♥♥♥♥♥, anticlimactic, annoying version of the tower system. See, in Happy Wars, you were locked in place and were restricted by build speed to destroy and rebuild towers, something that gave some actual nuance to taking respawn towers and 'core' health from the enemy team. You couldn't just sit in a corner of the room and spam spells at it. Now, it's ridiculously easy to get a win just by doing 2% damage and hardlining the enemy team. In Happy Wars, it actually felt like you were building up to a victory. Breaking the gate and the castle was an ordeal that needed all hands on deck, and you actually had to put yourself at risk for a win condition; one sole individual could get spawned on at base and countered with numbers before they could get too much damage in. Additionally, by tying the weaker health Clerics and Engineers to the highest tower damage, they encouraged team pushes. In Warlander, all it takes is one lucky individual to win or lose the game for you. Which is all too common when your Commander isn't watching the enemy markers. Sure, the singular path with only handful of branching ones helped, but the lack of unnecessary vastness stripped away the possibility of someone cheesing the game through luck alone. You actually needed to think about stats, items, abilities, strategy. The upgrade system was rewarding, the grinding gave actual immediate benefits, and the matchmaking was reasonable, even if you could get crushed by high levels still. In that game, you mostly lost because you had the wrong mixture of classes. In this game, you lose because you weren't picked as commander and the doofus on your team picked Defensive, rendering 60% of your team (bots) practically useless for the duration of the match. This isn't good game design, This is an aesthetically-pleasing moba using the corpse of a loved one to masquerade as an actually decent game. But, it could be better. Way better. _childDocuments_.review: The anti-cheat is bad, though almost everything else about the game is pretty great.  The game is a large scale 3rd person multiplayer combat game.  The combat plays out sort of like a 3rd person MOBA like say SMITE.  You are put into a squad of other players and together your squad is given a role.  Your teams objective is to destroy the enemies castle/core and to protect your own.  The roles are divided up as assaulter squads which try to destroy the enemy core, defenders who try to protect their core, and spec ops who try to capture/control neutral objectives (think sort of like a jungler form a traditional MOBA).  The gameplay is pretty smooth, I've had no real graphical hickups, loading issues, or similar.  The monetization is mostly a non-issue it has a multi-tiered battlepass but seemingly nothing super important gameplay wise is in the battlepass, at best its going to give you boosted drops so you "level up" faster on an account level not in game.  If it wasn't for the anti-cheat it would be a very easy slam dunk 100% recommend.  With the anti-cheat as it is I'd still generally recommend it.  Valorant has terrible anti-cheat too and people still love it and I think the same will hold true with Warlander aswell if people give it a shot, though not coming from a major company/major marketing is going to hold it back some.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great fun casual game just to turn your brain off and enjoy the chaos. Each team is a 20 man army with either warriors, healers, or mages that try to siege the enemies castle in a tug-o-war fashion. The maps are limited and on a rotation at the moment but it makes up for the fact that they have destructible structures, build-able artillery, and event items like a meteor shower or a massive tornado giving it a fun chaotic presentation.Classes do need to be leveled individually for each character created and all units share equipment among the characters. And creating a stronger character is only playable in the battlefield if you earn enough Valor points (participation points). Getting gear and spells are all random drops from the end of the match or purchasable with in-game currency earned from matches or selling equipment (not Premium currency). -Common in-game currency-Gear, Spells, apply Glamour (Cosmetics), Boosters, Perk re-roll, and limited cosmetics-Premium Currency-Glamour (Cosmetics), Boosters [~$2], perk re-roll [~$2], +5 character slots [~$5], +1 Character Deck [~$6], Battlepass [~$10 or ~$20]The game is for sure rewarding long time players that grind for better gear and being able to use them late in the games match  due to the Valor Point system and having new players only being on an equal playing field at the start of the match. But the advantage seems small (at the moment) since that game wants the players to move and fight as a squad instead of as a solo hero. Even going in solo with the best gear against a 2 man or a squad will get them killed.The game is incredibly fun chaotic siege with only making it feel unbalanced on 1v1 fights, but as whole its a great side game to play if you feel burnt from your main game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR version: Class and "Valor" system deliberately made laughably grindy to squeeze as much cash out of you as possible leading to a game where spenders DOMINATE non spenders.The "Valor" System in this game is complete garbage. On the face it seems like a kind of "kill streak" system, where doing pretty much anything productive in a game grants you points towards valor levels. These valor levels are thresholds that once passed allow you to deploy character that have higher ranked valor titles. Titles in this game are very important as having a higher grade title on a character bestows powerful benefits such as more hp or more damage to buildings, but also more equip load. all characters have a set equipment capacity. Things like armor, weapons, active skills, and passive traits all count towards this capacity. All of the equipment directly effects character stats, a low level new character with no valor title and the basic equipment is FAR weaker than a well equipped Valor five character. On paper the devs seem to want you to have a character that starts at valor level zero and then as the game goes on progressively grows stronger as you do productive things, but the system is intentionally designed to get you to pay as much money as possible to get ahead. The first issue is that the system requires you to make five separate characters its not class based, its character based. so if you wanted to have a cleric at each level of valor then you would have to create and level up individually five separate clerics. And although armor and weapons are class specific characters of the same class do not share them so of those five separate clerics you only star with one set of non-default equipment meaning you have to earn the the better skills armor and weapons for the other four. This is done through complete random chance after every game. After each game you are awarded completely random gear and skills. The game does not seem to take into account what class you played as I only played as the cleric and was only ever was given wizard gear and skills. This is where the pay to win element comes in. In the in game real money shop there are boosters that give your characters increased experience but also allow you to buy boosters that increase not only the rarity of item but the amount of items gained per match. There is also 2 levels of the paid "season pass" (Battle pass)  the normal level which is 10$ USD and the "Premium Pass" which is 20$ USD. The "Premium pass" and normal pass  not only contain some of the boosting consumables but also passive increases to the drop rates of equipment. All these random chance laden grind-a-thon systems that are radically accelerated past by using real money leads to an experience, and I'm not joking or being hyperbolic when I say this, in every single match there is one or two people that have a Valor five well equipped character that can and does take out entire enemy teams with ease.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick summary:  A mashup of the Battlefield/StarWarsBattlefront/MOBAs.  Pick roles, drop into large scale, fast paced combat. Great for people that don't want to dedicate large amounts of time to playing a game, but won't mind if they do get sucked in for awhile. 6 or 7 out of 10.  With potential updates and patches, the game could very well become an 8/10 or 9/10.Pros: Core gameplay is solid. Very fun. Easy to get sucked into the "one more round mentality". Progression system keeps you wanting to play more to unlock more gear and class ranks.Cons: Game has some issues with  loot, matchmaking and balance. Issues with lag and hitbox collisions can result in stun-locking even when there's a delay in hits. Balance wise- every class is needed, but Mages and Warriors are definitely stronger and more fun to play than the support Cleric. Games often feel like a one-sided stomp in favor of one team due the way that the in-battle progression system works. Winning the first large battle snowballs experience points in favor of the winning side, which in turn allows them to re-deploy as a higher rank character faster than the losing team. Matchmaking means that your team might all be new players, while the opposing team is all experienced veterans who know how to play the game. RNG loot drops at the end of each match can result in frustratingly slow progression of character builds.There's far more issues that need to be addressed, like the Pay 2 Win item shop and Battle Passes and communication UIs, but I've been F2P this whole time and still find the game enjoyable. I do hope they update and rectify some of these issues, but it may be too late since launch.  The small player base is just large enough to get consistent matches queued quickly, but a larger player base could solve some of the 1-sided stomping issues.

_childDocuments_.review: So. I didn't even know this game existed until it popped up on my PS5, so I came here, and found it on steam! Great! I was pumped. It looked fun! It looked exciting, and a good siege type game! Tutorial done, and played my first round, and had a blast!Then... Then came all the faults... War... War never changes...THE BAD.So the first thing I noticed was the utter lack of balance in the matchmaking. Don't get me wrong. it's nice that you can hire mercenaries, but it's taking time away from building your own characters, and play style. It's kinda like the Splatoon effect. Everyone's got the big boy weapons, and gear, and you're there getting ready to be defeated in one shot, or one combo.The hit detection is... Off. Like really off. I'll be holding up my shield, and pointing it towards my enemy, and their regular attacks are coming through. I'll shield bash someone, and they won't get stunned even though it connected, or enemies will swing their swords, and hammer 2 character lengths away from you, and it will connect, but when you're right next to them, and you swing. It almost feels like RNG.Speaking of RNG... The end game rewards feels absolutely underwhelming if you're not using boosters. You could be 1st place, 1st squad, and be lucky to get a blue named item, so even though I CAN have a character be a 4-star, or above. there's no point, because I don't have the gear, or abilities to make it worth it. So even after 26 hours of playing I still feel about as weak as I did 5 hours in. Whilst other players can 1 shot kill with ease. Meaning for new players. they have to get beat down for a lengthy period of time, before they too have the gear to contend, and beat up newer players.This is just a minor nitpick, but seriously? Can we not chose different genders for roles? Male Cleric, Female Wizard, Female Warrior? Would be kind of nice for that sweet sweet character customization.THE GOOD.Even though it's buggy, and sometimes a right mess of cheaters capturing towers from the comfort of their own keep. The game is a fun sieging experience. Rushing down points, capturing objectives. Using catapults, and battering rams.When you're a premade squad of 4. You get a rush of camaraderie Even when helping other squads if feels so cooperative that it just feels RIGHT! The maps are neat. the way everything is positioned is good.Fights feel chaotic, and all over which makes sense for the setting!FINAL THOUGHTS.I'm not going to say this game is trash, or pay to win, but I will say that... You might only start to feel progress after you put in 50-60 hours to have stats to keep up with other people. Sure you can buy mercenaries, but that just doesn't feel good. But hey. if you want extra bonus rewards, and drop chance, and rarity chance. you can buy the season pass, or the SUPER season pass. I can't fault them. They have to make money somehow, but that feels a little dirty. I'll check back in a couple of weeks to see if things stabilises, but until then. I hope the game gets better, because I can't recommend it with all it's flaws/

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun.Definitely gives the Happy Wars vibes. It's like jumping into MMO PvP without all the bullspit. You don't have to spend a cent and it's fun. People are wildin' in the reviews about the p2w and hackers, but it hasn't impacted my ability to enjoy the game at all. As in, I haven't noticed any of it, if happens at all. It did take a few games to start to get some loots and titles for my characters. Like, there was a bit of a startup phase, I guess. I do like the squad tactics and the extra rewards you get for completing your squad role's objectives. It is a neat way to incentivize people to play their roles.Big fan of how much in the shop is purchaseable with in game currency as well as how fast you earn it. I play all three classes regularly and they all feel great and are fun.The game looks and runs great on my 5700XT (except when I streamed it, it got a bit chunky, but I suspect that was my OBS encoder settings as it streamed and ran fine the night before via Discord). When I ran into my first battle and the skill effects were popping off everywhere, I immediately went "WOW" out loud xD One big con for me is that for some reason, the game keeps picking up my joystick as a controller input and then locking to that input. As in, I can't get my M&K inputs back until I alt+F4 and restart the game. Not sure if this is the game behavior or Steam controller settings being wonky, but it doesn't happen in any other game I can think of. The lack of voice/text comms was disturbing at first, but I found I only wanted to use it when I wanted to call my team donkeybrains so in the end I stopped missing it pretty quickly. Overall, I'd give it like a 7.5/10 and for a free game, that's pretty satisfying imo. tl;drPretty fun. Takes a few games to get going. Unplug your joystick? Decent shop. Pretty. Free. 7.5/10 IMO

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent tens of hours playing Warlander in open/closed beta since mid 2022. I've grown a love for the game and very much anticipated its release, but unfortunately it has been a massive disappointment. Here are the reasons why:1. It is safe to say that  the "full release" (if it can even be called that) is beyond underwhelming. It is simply the beta tests with a shop and battle pass added.2. (FIXED ITEM IN BRACKETS 5-26-2023) [The Battle Pass takes an ungodly amount of time to progress, and with rewards that don't make it feel as if that effort was worth anything.] An egregious example of this is the TIMED skins for the free battle pass which expire in 3 days. This means your 88 hours you spent to receive a mediocre skin (I'm looking at you, Cactus Kid) are almost entirely for naught if you're a free player.3. Even if you paid for the battle pass that isn't the end of it. There are TWO paid battle passes, a normal and a premium one each with different items. This is such a maddeningly goofy idea that I don't want to waste keystrokes typing about it.4. You are given 5 character slots in the beginning, which is enough to make 2 of... wait, oh yeah you CAN'T make 2 of each character by default. You have to pay real money for more character slots.5. Patches for the game consist of the occasional positive fix but mostly buffs/nerfs attacks and items which unfortunately do not improve the balance of the game. This has been an issue since beta, and it hasn't changed a bit since. Every balancing fix just causes a new problem which very well could potentially break the dynamics of the characters you play. 6. There are no ways to earn Goldings (the premium currency) in-game or in the battle pass. I am not counting that one weekend login bonus thing because to call that peanuts would be insulting to peanuts.7. There currently aren't many accessibility options in the game, which could be a big minus to some people. I have protan colorblindness, and this makes playing 5-army battle a struggle. The yellow and green team are indistinguishable to me, which causes a confusion that makes playing frustrating and I haven't touched the mode for some time.  8. The lack of players have resulted in a rise of the dreaded "Bot Lane" tactic seen in the lower player count moments of the beta tests. A person can use the commander role to give direct instructions to bots that fill in for missing players to harass one of the lanes. This can allow one player to wield a considerable amount of power, and it's really annoying to be on the receiving end.There are probably many other little bits i could've put here but the main point of all this is that I'm very disappointed in how the game released and how it is being currently run. I've had many fun times and met awesome players during the beta and I really want to see a day where Warlander is another F2P gem. Sadly, today is not that day.EDIT (3-6-2023): I'd thought this review would be the last time addressing this product, but it must be noted that the community for this game is ROTFUL and DEFENSIVE as all hell. If you happen to make any minor criticism in the Warlander discord, you will be deemed "toxic" and "passive-agressive" by the mods. I was timed out for a week for making at best a mildly sarcastic remark about the game.    Do not expect your voice to be heard. If you make anything that resembles a complaint about the current state of the game, you will either be directed to send it to the bottomless pit that is the feature-suggestion channel, or be timed out because "we don't need that kind of negativity, the devs are very hard at work optimizing [the shop]."    Those who remain in the discord are known to the underground as "Yeslanders" because they are simply yesmen for the game and are willing to put up with insane amounts of mediocrity in the form of half-baked patches and new skins which are just color changes of old skins.   Any dissenting voice, even in Steam at times, can and will likely be deleted if Warlander has the ability to do so. I can not support these actions and it is only a reminder that instead of working to improve the game in a way that will change minds to be more positive, they will instead listen to the ever-shrinking amount of Yeslanders for guidance.  I did not mean to write a paragraph about this, but my salt meter is high today. I, a very loyal and patient player of this game, am entirely fed up. Please just play something else.MAJOR EDIT 4-16-2023: In the last 3 days there have been some major developments in the state of Warlander, albeit not in the actual game itself. In spite of everything said above, for better or for worse, I remain an active member of the Warlander community as well as keep track of all developments for...well I don't know i guess it's a good entertainment. That being said the heartbreaking news was revealed that console release has been delayed and a official announcement will come upon the end of Season 0.   While, if the reactions were anything to go against, half of the active Warlander discord were reeling from the disappointment, a scandal has been brewing in the background. One of the highest rated reviews of the game has been deleted by Steam moderation, and as a result all (nearly 2,500) individuals who found the review helpful were penalized. The topic of the review was about the anti-cheat, which to the current administration, is an absolute no-no to talk about when discussing the game.   It is an allegation to say this, but there is absolutely no doubt in my mind that Plaion/Toylogic have had a hand in conducting this action. In what amounts to a blatant act of censorship, they have targeted that review and all who upvoted it. If actions like this are enabled, it will be a matter of time before more nuanced reviews are targeted as well, possibly including mine. The word has to be spread this course of action is absolutely unacceptable no matter the size of the publisher or the content of a review. If the goal of this was to save face in the midst of a continuous decline in reception for the game, then I hope that it is a catastrophic failure for Plaion/Toylogic.   Thankfully, after investigation, Steam is reversing some of the action taken. If you have been affected by this, PLEASE MAKE YOUR VOICE HEARD. The fact that I have to talk about something as petty as this is absolutely ridiculous. To those in charge of Warlander, please get your **** together.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been enjoying my time in the game because it's fun when it works. Range combat feels good, but melee is a mess. Melee in a pinch is attack spam and win.There's no chat feature probably for toxicity, they don't show players connected or counts alive in a match. So no clue if there are bots or actual players. For the most part it feels like players, but some look like they're scripted.Melee staggers and knock backs are too ridiculous. I find myself avoiding melee at all costs until you hit 5 star warrior which grants you juggernaut, that will let you ignore staggers and knock downs. Their latency is poor. You'll notice melee is not fair when you're running and not taking staggered hits, but you're dying because they attacked you on their end. Melee shouldn't have stagger and movement constrictions, because up close range is still a very good alternative to being melee locked into a swing. Stagger on skill use makes sense, but auto attacks don't deserve it. The trade off is that you're stuck in your melee swing action, but in doing so you can stagger your opponent or knock them back too far if they jump. Blocking is barely worth it, unless you're taking range hits from a far. Rarely will you block melee attacks due to lag or skills guard breaking, or if they just hit you at an angle that strikes right through your defensive block. The lag. You'll be connected with one of their three servers to get matches. People who have good connection to the game's server can block well enough for it to register and counter even after being attacked with a staggering hit. So it takes a lot out of melee. If your connection is good with their servers you're basically in god mode. Ignore staggers, attack priority registration, block and counter priority. Meaning it's great when the mechanics work, but half the players jump into battle and die due to lack of actions being registered on their end. Don't waste your money here, enjoy the game for it's f2p. You'll get enough loot roll and spend coins on the skills you want. For the p2w aspect it's really not that bad, I bought a 25 level pack and premium battle pass. I can't recommend this game for it's bad optimization and poor connection.

Great graphics, decent loot, fluid gameplay(melee stuns are annoying at first but you adapt), servers are extremely stable (for me), and an overall satisfying gameplay loop.Set PC frame limit and the game runs quietly with even my 20+ other tabs open as well as simultaneous streaming. It's a phenomenal game once you start unlocking all of the different skills and abilities. At first it feels very tedious and like you're just going to get one-shotted by everything but that quickly falls away within an hour. Make sure you equip the full armor set you get for each class right off the gate. Like, really, I am having a blast and that's something I can't often say given my experiences with most free-to-play/"indie" titles. The 2 army mode is awesome once people figured out how to actually defend. The 5 army mode is hectic, but ridiculously fun once you and your squad get to coordinating. Only real cons are things that can be ironed out: Weapon variety could be better, but that comes with time. Gender-locked classes don't matter. It's not an MMO and they will likely add more classes per gender so you can fulfill whatever fantasy you have for a less than 30 minute engagement where classes are on a cooldown anyway TO PREVENT EVERYONE JUST SPAMMING KNIGHT/MAGE (which people did do right out the gate).Don't like that you need to start with an un-Titled characters in 2 army mode, but it makes sense so sweats don't just rain BS they've earned from unlocks on you from the jump. Easy way to circumvent this is to always have an un-Titled cleric in your deck. Heal and dps with even a legendary crossbow and you should be able to play whoever you want by the first time you die.

_childDocuments_.review: --------------------------------------------------The game feels like it could be fun, however, due to the technical issues, I can't really experience it completely.The battlefield offers a standard MOBA type flow - capture towers, build defenses, destroy the opponent's core, all while earning valor for every action. Draw is an option.There are only three classes - warrior, mage, and cleric - which is OK because it's easier to balance, but it can also get stale. From what I could tell, however, the classes/skills feel unbalanced which immediately ruins the flow of the battlefield.The combat is OK-ish, however, it requires some rough and fine tuning.Melee combat doesn't feel fluid and is oftentimes aggravating due to its clunkiness (esp. in large group fights).Ranged attacks don't feel precise no matter the sensitivity. It just doesn't provide the fluid aiming I'm used to in other games (could be due to point No.2 above).I can't tell yet, but some people feel way too overpowered, killing me with one or two hits. Are they already sporting much powerful gear, or if it's something else...? I don't know... I'm also 94% sure I saw some players teleport a greater-than-normal distance, need more time to confirm.The character upgrade system seems interesting. You need to level your character and do specific tasks in order to gain titles, in order to increase your character rating, in order to equip more powerful items/skills. The higher the character level and title, the more valor is required so you can deploy it, and it takes more time for the character to re-deploy if defeated, however, you're more powerful in return. Always keep a titleless character in a deck, otherwise you can't play.Decks contain 5 slots for characters, presumably for different play styles, however, due to the titles and levels, that implies that you need different characters (of the same class), which means you need to buy character slots in order to create and level up new characters, as there is no option to have several load-outs for a single character.----------The general design style is nothing new, it looks nice, however, the armors don't really look good. Not even the exclusive store-bought ones look like something I would spend money on. Sadly there are only a few armor types and weapon types, along with small armor accessories.Right off the bat - It's on the  spectrum, which makes this a "not recommended" for me, for now.The featured battle pass provides P2W items such as +% to gain extra item/talent/skill (also earnable through quests). For both earnable and paid currency (5 items for 3000 earnable or 180 paid) you get to boost your XP gain, number of items gained, or a chance for a higher rarity item (1 item per battle). You can also buy crystals to change a perk to a random perk on your item. Character slots and Deck slots are paid currency only. You get 5 character slots and 2 deck slots from the start.The game offers real-money currency packs, however, it doesn't provide a pack with the exact amount needed for either battle pass, or a specific item - a common predatory practice (leaves you with change you can't use for anything else, baiting you to buy just a bit more).Standard battle pass just unlocks the pass and gives you one extra item as per ususal.Premium battle pass instantly unlocks 25 levels, and you get an extra item on top of a Standard pass item, however, only on some of the levels.Overall, it doesn't feel good nor rewarding due to the amount of XP required for one pass level (150.000). If you have an average match, you'll get an average of 5.000 XP which means 30 matches. One match lasts between 10 and 15 minutes. That's way too much for a single level (out of 100). The daily quests don't seem to contribute to the progress at all.The weapon/armor skins you gain from it are OK-ish and some are just re-colors of themselves. Additionally, it looks like the free pass skins have a 3-day expiration timer (?!) and can only be applied once, while paid pass skins can be applied infinitely and indefinitely.You can also use the earnable currency to buy mild re-colors of the armor and accessories, but with a random perk. For reference, I've earned 950 coins in 6 average matches, and you need between 500 and 10500 for an item depending on its size, type, and rarity. You can also sell the items you were rewarded from the matches for some pocket money.On top of that, the pass doesn't reward real-money currency, like other good games do. It offers 30.000 earnable currency over the course of 100 levels.The battle pass has 85 days remaining.

_childDocuments_.review: I played it on console. Bought the season pass, completed the pass, and deleted it. I got a computer and tried on computer. Deleted it. Literally has good games if its casual people, but theres a glitch in the system to where the person just hits you once, shield break or stun, hits once or twice, shield stun/break, rinse and repeat until the person is dead. Leaving you standing there eating every hit with little to nothing to do unless the person messes up the rotation. I get the mechanics so people cant sit there behind their shield, but if there was a CD to how often a person can shield break that wouldnt be to bad. Just so it can break the endless loop and give people that little second to put up a fight. It has a great concept but, its long run of a good feeling dies really fast thanks to that.Its very hard to understand how the item system works for new guys. We get nice things and cant even equip 3/4s of them. when a person gets his "High Tier" champ we of course get to equip more, and better things, but you spend 10 mins of a 15min game to use them, and you die within the minute due to some exploit, or random situation on the map. Theres no satisfaction of playtime for the hard work you put into collecting the items, and building your guy to use half the things we get. Conclusion the Tier system is a nice touch, but it can really damper the collection process.I noticed that there seemed to be games where people were 100% built to defend, and etc. I then noticed by paying a little money i can make more decks, but to fill the decks i had to spend more money on getting  the characters.  I know theres gotta be some kind of income, and if people could build an attack/defence off the bat they wouldnt make that little bit. Though I wouldnt want to pay money for extra content where  i just get combo'd to death my whole game from unbalanced servers. Conclusion its not expensive, and if you enjoy the game its worth the extra set, but its annoying when one side is all P2P and the ally side is just a bunch of random F2P mercs...All in all its a great game, its a fun Attack/Defend the castle and all. Though as soon as you get them unbalance exploit games it kills a whole vibe. Its a very simple rotation, and i hate getting my combos cuz i feel for the person on the other side who cant react to the broken mix.

_childDocuments_.review: **Major edit, 2024 Nov 7**Still a high rating. I have over 1000 hours in this game and have reached the Top 10. The previous "Sentry Anti Cheat" issue has been completely solved by ToyLogic completely removing Sentry. The common problem now seems to be that beginners are often matched with experienced players.I have been trying to help by showing people how to play on Streams and by guiding other beginners, and often times I hear from beginners that they don't even know **why** they're winning or losing.At the same time many people complain about "gear" or "titles". Now the most powerful 5 stars are available to all players from the very beginning without any work neccesary, and yet those beginners are still unable to win- it shows it's not about "gear" or "titles".Long time players simply have a much better strategy, and beginner players will continue to get smashed unless they learn the meta. That's the current state of the game.-----Original Review below------The game is really fun and not very rough on beginners as long as you play it smart. Sentry Anti Cheat does not remain on after the game is closed and Toylogic are very clear about how they collect and use your info in their privacy policy. If you use any other social media platform, there should be no privacy concerns here.EDIT** I am now 370 hours in and currently am the 200th ranked player.The game is extremely F2P friendly as most of the stuff that affect gameplay can also be bought using the free currency. The only stuff that F2P players DON'T have access to that actually affect gameplay is the increase RNG% that good stuff drop from battles, the increase is about 10% or less.If you see any reviews saying that the game is "P2W" because the paid players can "buy legendary characters", know that those are fake reviews because there are no such things as "legendary characters". The closest things to "legendary characters" are the 5 star characters which can ONLY be bought using the FREE CURRENCY and there is NO WAY to convert the paid currency to the free one.Furthermore, the game is extremely beginner friendly as you start with the extremely strong skills and equipment. For reference, most high level players of this game still play a level 2-3 character for 90% of the match. They simply optimize each character for a specific job and can outperform a beginner who is unfamiliar with these jobs.For example, a valor 2 warrior class called the "brigand" allows the warrior to climb ladders extremely quickly. This class can easily be used to sneak into the enemy castle and hit the core. Noobs may not see the value of this class and may not try to optimize a warrior specifically for this one role. That's the difference between a noobie player trying to sneak into the castle vs a pro player trying to sneak into the castle.

_childDocuments_.review: Warlander is a wretched hive of cheats, deception and censorship.As a long time Steam game player and collector, I take pride in providing well-informed, comprehensive reviews when I need to. However, it is with a heavy heart that I must emphatically dissuade you from partaking in the disaster that is Warlander. This game, once a promising venture with balanced, challenging, and thrilling combat, has devolved into an abysmal cesspool of hackers, cheaters, and unresponsive developers.Initially, Warlander's simplistic and captivating design drew players in, myself included. But as time passed, the game's once-enjoyable matches morphed into one-sided slaughters. The disparity between the dominating and losing teams became insurmountable, leaving the enjoyment of gameplay to pure chance.Upon investing a considerable sum of money into Warlander's largest gold package, I naively hoped for an improved experience. Instead, I was met with continuous losses, prompting me to take a hiatus. Returning to the game a week later, I encountered a barrage of technical issues, ranging from mid-game disconnects to login and matchmaking errors.When Warlander announced improvements to their matchmaking system, I optimistically anticipated the resolution of these issues. Alas, the nightmare persisted; queue times became unbearable, and matches remained elusive. Desperate for answers, I contacted Warlander Support, only to receive generic troubleshooting advice and an incomprehensible request for video proof of my inability to join matches.The situation took a turn for the worse when I was banned from both the Warlander discussion threads and the game itself. My crime? A respectful inquiry into the game's ban policy. Throughout this ordeal, the support team remained unresponsive, leaving me with no answers, a poor-quality gaming experience, and a $120 hole in my wallet.This game, now a mere shadow of its former self, (Which is sad considering it is so new) has devolved into a farcical spectacle overrun by AI bots and max-level players, who effortlessly crush their opponents by mid-game. The developers have exhibited a blatant disregard for their customers, falsely accusing genuine players of cheating while rewarding actual cheaters. This, coupled with their non-existent communication, demonstrates a profound lack of respect for their player base.I implore you to avoid Warlander and its tyrannical practices. This game is a disgrace to the gaming community, and supporting it would only perpetuate its malevolent existence. If there were a means to report such deplorable developers to Steam, I would not hesitate to do so.Warlander is a calamitous concoction of deceit, exploitation, and disappointment. _childDocuments_.review: The game is fun. The graphics are very pleasing and easy on the system. Combat is fun, energetic and can be fast paced, but it's easy to lose track of what's going on when there are large battles taking place in smaller areas. Even when it's only a few combatants, magic from wizards or clerics can easily cloud your vision, but that's part of the game I suppose.Battles can be super intense and you will most likely find yourself getting sucked into the action.The menu system is a bit.. janky. What I mean is that not everything is terribly intuitive and some of the design choices and placements are just awful. Such as the equipment/skills/weapon windows of the character screen. Early on in the game you are taken through the tutorial which does a decent job of getting you ready. HOWEVER. There is a GLARING mechanic that they just GLOSSED over. That is, while playing, when you level up your units, eventually you may get Titles for them. This is essentially leveling them up, allowing you to put better gear, stronger skills, etc.. equipped on your unit. Nice right? Not done yet though.  There is the 'Deck' system, which basically allows you to create your roster of units available to you in-game. No biggie. However, what they don't mention early on is that you MUST have one character that DOES NOT have a title in order to play on game start. If you don't you don't play. Because higher level units in your roster require VALOR to be able to use, which you get by playing, killing, etc, during a match. That was annoying to figure out on my own.The last issue is that THERE IS SO MUCH PAY TO WIN ITS ABSURD. The first day my buddy and I were doing really, really well and having a blast. We came back 2 days later and were just getting obliterated by WHALES who spent absurd amounts to get better gear. The fact that the game is Pay-To-Win is an instant turn off. Which sucks cuz I really do enjoy the game. But there's just no way to compete with teams of people who are kitted the heck out.Overall the game has way more pros than cons, but the P2W aspect makes it a 'Do Not Recommend.'

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves better than mixed reviews. If you played happy wars when you were younger or just love team based games then you'll gonna love this game. Sure the matches can be tough at times, because the palyerbase is small and high levels are getting mixed into low level matches... But once you get to know the ropes, actually stick to playing your role and get better items and upgrade your heroes, the slow rise to power becomes really satysfying, turning from just a useless grunt, to actually being able to do something to contribute to your team. This game plays pretty much like a MOBA or atleast i think it the best way to play Warlander. Dont rush mindlessly into fights you cant win (especially when you're newbie). The default gamemode is 20v20, the teams are divided into 5 squads, each being able to choose their role like Castle Guard, Assault team and Recon Team (or spec ops)At the start of the match your team gets to vote the strategy, that means types of squads there will be, but the default most people vote for is balanced - 2 assault squads, 2 castle guard squads and one recon squad. The castle guard is tasked with managing the fortress; building defenses, repelling attackers or if the need arises, sallying out to battle enemies preparing to siege the fortress Assault squads are tasked with breaching the castle defenses, fighting their way into the keep and destroying the enemy core. Sounds like simple job, but this is the hardest role which many newbies chooseThe recon squad is tasked with capturing control points and keeping the catapult in your team hands. Holding the catapult is often a matter of win and lose and you'll see lenghty battles over which team gets the cata. Recon squad also joins the assault squads if there's nothing left to doThe map is usually two castles on each side of the map with 2 lines of defense and 3 lanes with control points acting as respawn pointsLeveling in this game is something most people seem to not understand. I suggest looking it up on yt but im just gonna explain it real quick.You create your own characters, but to play the stronger ones, you'll have to level up with your weaker ones first. TL;DR alot of fun, hard to get into but very rewarding if you do

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun.  The fighting could be a little little less janky, but the objective based gameplay is fairly smooth -- squad cooperation and combat is really enjoyable, even as a solo player.  There's a lot of quality of life fixes in this game that have been needed in other games of this type, such as casual role enforcement through pre-game role voting without being a tyrant about it, and by reward players by playing those roles.  The team ally system in the 5 army (100 player) battles is a lot of fun, too.The people complaining seem to be mainly disappointed that character abilities are also equippable items with rarity, and only obtainable through random rewards at the end of matches.  This makes it so people who play the game longer will have an edge over people who are new, or who don't play as much.  I can see why this would disappoint the purely "skill" based players, but this game is about teamwork anyway, not about the average solo cowboy (I use skill in quotations, because this has more to due with perception than actual skill).  This is compensated for in game with the tiered characters equip rating and the in match valor system, so it seems pretty balanced to me.  Even if you get a mythic level skill early, you can't equip it until you a solid title on a character.  I guess this does make the game a bit grindy before you can "git gud" -- but honestly I prefer that anyway.  If the game is fun, and this one is, I'm going to play it a lot.I may edit this review after I play a bit more and decide if people who play the game a lot "inherently ruin the game for others" as other people have claimed, but so far I haven't seen even a tier 5 geared out character that couldn't be taken down by a squad of tier 1 players -- so we shall see!

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing free to play title for those who like the castle siege defend and attack game play. There are three classes, a warrior which is your tank, a cleric which is a medium tank medium damage healer, and the mage which is high dps insanity glass cannon play style. The match starts by allocating a commander for your team who is in charge of giving the squads of 4 people each direction during the game by simply telling them where to move to next. Each side is defending a core in their castle, behind walls and turrets which can be built and reinforced by the team as the game progresses. There is alot of curve balls though, some maps have certain places for catapults/trebuchets that can wipe out defenses from a far. And there is often a siege ram in the middle lane and a siege tower in another lane, so the maps follow the 3 lane design. Therefore it is easier to push certain lanes than others with siege, which can permanently remove a wall or gate in that area.The battlefield is chaos, with towers around the place which act as spawn ins for your squad and team, and players can teleport freely around the map, with some minor regression to their equipped class. Classes can be built to alter between your two weapons usually a melee and ranged weapon, or spells in the mages case. These are highly customisation, and there are alot of play styles. You can have 5 loadouts to call into battle. The game uses a title system which is where you start the game at rank 0 and by earning points from building, fighting or taking towers on the field, slowly levels you up to level 5. This lets you call in one of those 5 loadouts you make, which have a level (insert level) loadout of that class, scaling up their attributes as you set them. However, if you have higher "title" loadouts, they take longer to be selected during the battle as you need to reach that level. And they have a longer cool down should you die as that loadout. So its like a moba in a sense, except there is no buying items, you just set the loadout before hand and go from there.After each battle you have a chance to find new armour, weapons or spells, and or other abilities, and so the game is free-to-play for a reason, its going to require alot of time and grind, and just RNG to really get the stuff you want, but its alot of fun pushing through enemy squads as a team or making insane solo plays for the enemy core. Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Most negative reviews seem to focus solely on either the anti-cheat software that comes with this game or with its supposed Pay-2-Win monetization model. I won't go into the spyware debate at all and as far as Pay-2-Win is concerned, it doesn't seem too bad.Yes, the game aggressively pushes in-app purchases such as the already existing season pass or the outrageously overpriced cosmetics that you need to buy before they rotate out. It's disappointing, but not totally P2W. There are consumables that allow for the use of a high level hero in one match, but with the way the game works, everyone must initially spawn in with a very basic hero and get points before they can start using their higher tier characters. You are supposed to build a balanced hero selection with options for every stage of a match, but enough about that.Is the game good?Not particularly. It's flashy, it's noisy, it's chaotic. Think old school WoW battlegrounds, or maybe Guild Wars 2's World v World v World. Lots of characters using all sorts of colourful abilities until one side overruns the other. This does, in principle, sound like fun and this style of game is very successful especially in MMOs and some Battle Royales, but crucially, Warlander's action lacks impact, depth and feedback.Melee fights between two knights often devolve into wild slashing whilst using abilities immediately on cooldown. Ranged attacks plink away at your health without you even realising. Hits don't feel like they have any weight, neither for you as the attacker, nor for the defender. If you don't keep looking at your health bar all the time, it is almost impossible to know just how close to death you are.Which is somewhat pointless anyhow, as the time-to-kill is incredibly short, especially if using wizards and some knight builds. Sadly, this wasn't changed all that much since beta, despite many opinions having been voiced. The poor balancing turns what could have been a strategic MOBA-esque game into a spam and rush fest that ultimately does not feel satisfying. Siege battles, Warlander's main game mode, do not feel like sieges at all, but rather like a MOBA without minions, on a smaller map, with only three hero classes to choose from who kill each other very quickly, with the first snowball usually spelling the end for the other team as there is no inherent base defense outside of the need to break down gates or build ladders.The lack of strategic or mechanical depth is made worse by the sometimes clunky controls and random bits of terrain you seem to get stuck on while running, which in a game where you're sprinting at full speed toward the enemy for most of the time, is quite jarring. Melee has a wonky lock-on feature that kicks in when you're close enough to an enemy, which also doesn't always feel smooth.Overall, it's disappointing, doubly so because the balancing remains as bad as it was during the beta test.If you're looking for a game you can just hop onto and play a couple of quick matches without stressing out, maybe give Warlander a try - It's Free-to-Play, after all. If you prefer games that reward your time with meaningful progression, engaging game mechanics and strategic depth, I would give it a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: Shockingly excellent gameplay ruined by extremely basic mistakes.   Firstly, and most importantly. there are ZERO excuses for having no way to communicate with each other.  Full stop.  You might as well make it a singe player game with bots.  You MUST be on a discord call with your team, it is literally a requirement.  EVEN THEN, you can only squad up with 4 people.  You can have a team of 20, but if you are in a friend group of 5, one of you is not going to be able to play.  That is not acceptable.  There is no reason for it.  It's not more difficult to code for, it is literally a pointless limitation with no benefit.  The lack of chat is as well.  I'm sure their idea is "tHaTs ToO tOxIC, sOmEoNe WiLl CaLl SoMeOne BaAaAaD!!" because you cannot see your K/D either.  It kneecaps the whole experience.  This is effectively NOT a multiplayer game.The Bad: -  The performance is unacceptable.  It's not a great looking game and a 3080 is unable to keep a stable 60 FPS.  both the minimum and recommended requirements are laughable.  It is bordering on unplayable.-  The commander role sucks.  You can ask players to go certain places but they never do.  You don't build buildings or research upgrades or manage resources.  You just... Tell people "go here" and they promptly ignore you.  That is the gameplay loop for the commander. -  The way stun locking and blocks work is kind of odd. -  There's only 3 classes -  You get better items that make you objectively stronger than new players.  However these ARE only gained through playing the game instead of buying them, which is good.-  Feels like Savage XR or Natural selection  (Good) but dumbed down and worse.------------------------------------------------------------------The Good:  + The gameplay loop is exciting, It's fun wiping out a squad and taking a point. +  Hits feel decently meaty.  +  It is not pay to win. +  Theme is fun. +  I like the art style.Conclusion:Could be amazing but there's A LOT of work to be done here.  In the meantime, just go look up Savage XR and play that.  You're welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Try it for 30min and you'll see!     It's been a while since a game has captivated my group's attention for dozens of hours and still have room to progress. What I appreciate most is the balanced starts slowly unfolding into chaos as players bring out their higher level characters. Progress is fast and transparent, providing a reward I've been craving with more min-maxing around the corner.• F2P vs P2W: You can buy boosters that give you one extra item drop and one extra item rarity per game. The microtransactions are reasonable and RNG in-game is not that bad to reroll a perk. I didn't mind 'donating' $40 to support the team, get the BATTLE PASS ($10 for 90 days!), and unlock more characters to play (you start with 5).• STARTING OUT: You will only need two characters for the first couple hours, although, some matches will only use 2-4 characters depending on play-style and competition. PLEASE... complete your beginner quests. They will unlock daily/weekly missions to progress 'battle pass'. Totally optional, though (my friend has over 100 hours and has yet to complete them).• Solo vs Group - play: The game includes plenty of pings. Yet, the players are still a bit clueless to pings and neglect attack buffs when starting the game. Having a group for voice chat is always my preference -- luckily, the official Discord is full of team-oriented players.     I look forward to more classes and minor balancing as the game rises in popularity.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun. It's free. Why the reviews are "Mixed" right now I couldn't tell ya. No issues finding a game, seems to be plenty of activity. As solo, you join a randomly assigned squad where you vote on your objective as a squad. Defending the castle is just as fun as being assigned to the assault teams.*Update* - You can be a warrior, mage, or cleric. Each with their own abilities and play style. You can swap between them during the castle siege. You have to earn points through various objectives (build siege equipment, kill enemies, heal allies etc) to unlock your higher level characters. You level your characters by playing them, unlocking more equipment, skills and ranks. In a way you lock yourself out of playing your favored class in the beginning by increasing their level and gear, but you get to swap to them once you accumulate enough points. Think of Star Wars Battlefront, make it medieval, add magic. The only game mode however is siege where both teams have castles they must defend, while simultaneously attacking their opponents castle. Defending the castle is fun. Various siege equipment that must be built to defend your multiple walls keep you running around laughing as you slaughter the enemy. If the enemy mages manage to wipe out your siege equipment you can jump down and join the fray or attempt to rebuild. If you clear the enemy and see your castle being attacked on another front, you can simply hit "B" and warp over there to help defend. Don't want to defend? Attack that castle; build different siege equipment to break their walls and fight your way to their core. The more pressure you apply, the more attention you draw. It's fun lol not sure why its not mostly positive / very positive reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never heard of Toylogic or Playon. P2W meaning boosters that increase the items dropped after a match by 1, and the rarity of an item by 1 (Which can also be purchased for silverlings). And silverlings, the games currency was difficult to acquire and locked mostly to the Season Pass. Also in the season pass is a total of 30% boost to drop rates of (Skills, equipment, etc) - I can say now while this has not changed, with the recent boost to silverlings. With the ability to purchase equipment, and skills for silverlings and having a season pass that offers silverlings, the game will at least for this season pass be P2W.Pros: The game is a gem, even with the p2w aspects the power differences will be negligible. The way the game is designed makes it so someone cannot have a higher threshold of CP then others. Allowing at maximum 800 CP which a F2p player should be able to attain in 35-50 hours on one or 2 classes vs a p2w player who will do it in 25-45. The p2w aspect probably only matters at the first 50-100 hours while you do not have anything. However, every game will net you 3-7 or (8) items of variable rarity, your performance also seems to affect this. You can also rent heroes, for mercenaries for fairly cheap to perform at a higher level. Though despite being high level you might prefer your character more given the situation.     The game is incredibly fun, the developers seem to be listening, ranking is performance based.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh Warlander! I wanted so much to make you a constant loop in my library of games... I said early on that you were like a cross between SMITE! and Dark Age of Camelot's RvR. The best of 3D MOBA and large scale siege skirmishes...Early on the game was great. They paired me with other new players and bots. The bots were a nice challenge, but not godlike. The biggest issue was if you attacked an undefended lane, there would be 4 to 8 bots that instantly knew a tower was under attack and teleported to defend the tower, ending up with 1:4 odds at best. They would kill me and then all teleport in unison back to the main lane of combat. No sneaky tower caps for me. :(I pushed on, hoping to get to games with more players. As I ranked up, more and more players were in the 20 vs 20 matches and things were looking up.Got slightly higher in the ranks, more people ended up in the match instead of bots. But now we have the try-hard-bunny-hoppers. These wizards jump through groups with lighting auto attack that has zero recoil and thus never miss. Able to take out groups of non-wizards in short order with the tiniest of a flank, or double teleport before cool downs were exhausted.I suddenly wanted the bots back as I realize that they never jumped around like a chicken with their head cut off shooting lightning. Defeating a bot was more pure requiring strategy on when to attack, block, or break their defenses.I cannot recommend the game in its current state. If they reduce jumping to once every 10 seconds, adjust troublesome skills, and remove most of the cliffs to get knocked off of, I might come back. That is highly unlikely to change.Thanks for reading and I wish you well in your search for the next game to sink hours into.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun.  It doesn't overload you with impossible mechanics and it doesn't bore you with simplicity and repetition.   It has that MOBA feel in that the same map feels very different depending on the dynamics of the game.  The progression feels meaningful as well with gear drops after every victory, and you can buy items with the free currency as well, or through the battle pass system.  Just as a heads up, there is a small amount of P2W in this game, but it's irrelevant beause you can't buy your way to victory.  You get RNG advantages when getting items (I think), get battle pass which has in-game items, character slots, and XP boosts.  It's about as P2W as League in that regard.  No whale can buy themselves victories and that's further cemented by the fact that your epic and legendary items can't be equipped by low level characters.  At the same time, this game is worth about $20 for what it is, so if that means they get that money through conveniences, that's fine with me.  While the game is fun, there's a LOT of work to do with optimization, connection issues, bugs, a sketchy anticheat program,   All of these are fixable though so I'm not going to judge on this yet.  I haven't seen any bugs but I have seen lots of connection issues.  I've been disconnected from 3 games.  The game needs to allow you to rejoin games if you drop out.  Yes it's probably an issue  with cheaters abusing lag but being kicked out of a game is so frustrating.
