_childDocuments_.review: Straight-up I need to convey 2 things:1. You need to watch  It has a lot of neat information & a trick that I think the game forgot to mention in its tutorial.2. I  rogue-lites. You're welcome to read  as to why...Many of the flaws I have with the general rogue-lite formula still continues within this game, I'm not going to deny that. That is a truth.And while it isn't a constant daunt upon me, it is something of which I am occasionally peskily reminded of.Deadlink has been perfectly constructed by folks whom know exactly what they're trying to achieve, and have an actual vision for a game. That's bold, and that's sad such has be stated; because I feel a lot of games nowadays don't.Yet the developers at Gruby Entertainment has successfully made a grand entrance to the entire market, and I'm so proud of them.You've made me straight-up love a rogue-lite. That's only the 2nd time that has ever happened.What a glamorous inaugural. Bravo!If you love DOOM Eternal, you'll love this game.If you love rogue-lites, you'll love this game.If you love both of the aforementioned things, you'll adore this game.The mere game-play for Deadlink has been so refined & perfected by actual maestros of the industry, and sheer titans already. I have nothing but respect for what they've pulled-off here.At first, for my ~30-or-so minutes of my playtime I hated the game-play... A little bit of an overstatement, but I found it really weird & uncomfortable; in the negative perspective. I hated how I always ran out of ammo, and how I had to keep reloading my shotgun... But then I finally watched the aforementioned video listed above, and that changed ! The sheer act of how to get ammo like a pro using 'Marked' enemies was entirely world changing for me in this game -- it twisted my head around, just like my perspective of this game.So basically 'Marked' enemies are enemies you've triggered the 'Marked' effect on, using either your grapple-hook, your push field, or your grenades; ignore the wrong names, I forgot them, as I am on meth and feda mine right now.But you activate it like that, and thereafter if you kill them during their short 'Marked' state, they'll replenish your ammo for both your shotgun & rocket launcher by 1 ammo count, respectively. And you don't have to reload them, they're just instantly there. That's ! I love it, I adore it, I squeal & piss over it. That's downright beautiful -- what a wonderful system.Such means that if you're playing good; by 'Marking' enemies commonly & weapon-switching, you won't ever even need to reload, nor keep track of your ammo counts. Wow. That's a really cool enforcer!The maps are really well-made as well. I feel the 1st level's map are maybe a little too flat in retrospective. But The 2nd level's map are straight-up fantastic! I love how many unique ideas there's been thrown in there, with ideologies within the maps which I've never seen replicated truly akin in any other games. I adore how many platforms there typically are, and how many unique layers & heights there are to them. Many parts of the 2nd level's maps are so beautifully constructed as to push truly special game-play scenarios, with its more airborne drone enemies as well. All very cool!The guns feel great as well, they have a lot of punch & kick in them. I love how devastating the rocket launcher is... for my corpses that is. That's just crazy!... ass... frog...They all look & feel great in every way.How the guns represent their unique weapon mods you've chosen to adapt to them are very cool; as that both looks cool & is very useful as a reminder.Albeit I feel like sometimes my shotgun blasts -- specifically & exclusively -- just goes through enemies sometimes. I'm not sure if it's a glitch or what's up. Maybe I just need to call my dad & admit that I'm a no good gamer? Who knows?It's just not something I feel I experience in many other games.But over-all, such a banger.As said previously above, I'm like rogue-lite hater #1. I've never been a fan of the formula, and I feel like like it's a lazy & safe formula typically adapted only to tack as much play-time unto games -- as to raise the play-time; with less work than making an actual 8-10 hour static campaign. You're welcome to argue with me in the comments. Cya!But here... here I don't mind too much.Compared to something like Hades; in its current state Deadlink is 1000% more enjoyable for me. That's mostly due to how it's not as grindy; as I've already unlocked most of the upgrades for my character within my first 4 hours, from maybe only ~8 runs. And as of now -- in 'Early Access' -- the campaign is very short, and very straightforward. I can appreciate that. There's only 2 levels to beat, and runs seem much faster & less RNG-focused. Cool!So once you die (and you  die), it really won't be the same amount of hassle, at least not for me. And a majour part of that is also due to how great the combat itself is, it's not just 'good', it's not just 'great. It's 'fantastic'!It's so darn brilliant, that I feel inclined to mostly overlook it, because what I love about the game heftily overshadows the parts I do not.The world of Deadlink is beautiful & immensely gorgeous. There are a ton of scenic vistas, which feel almost like screenshot-bait to focus on in-between fights... and I accept it... because I adapt it. lolIt's so freaking awesome & amazing! Both of the levels so far are wonderfully constructed visually, and are very instantaneously distinctive. I was really thrown a curve-ball, cause I did not expect the 2nd level to be in a science lab of some sorts, not whatsoever. It's a really crazy twist -- yet it just works so well. It's a huge contrast to the former level, but it still works alongside it.Deadlink's soundtrack is just straight-up... "wow." I'm shocked, I'm surprised.The soundtrack for Deadlink truly blew me away with its score, and I'm simply amazed.Ivory Tower Soundworks did such brilliant works on it all, and there's not a single bad song. All of them are true bonerjams & extraordinary headbangers! They're on-par with something like Cyberpunk 2077's in-game combat music as well -- which is insane!Great stuff, man. I'd utmost recommend everyone to check the soundtrack out!I'm so glad Gruby Entertainment themselves upload their own tracks, instead of us having to rely on compressed sound-files extracted from the game files, lol.Deadlink blew me away. I played the short-time demo & thought it was 'alright'. Then I bought it upon release... didn't really care... meh. 30 minutes later & I'm standing up, sweating, headbanging, and grinning from the sheer amount of pure joy I'm experiencing! recommendations for all those interested! Even as a rogue-lite hater, this stands as a likely GOTY candidate for me.I can't wait to see what's next for this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Deadlink is a fun roguelite, but it isn't without it's flaws. It's a cyberpunk arena shooter built on a roguelite formula with some pretty cool weapons, items, classes & builds, but I have a couple of issues with the game.So, if they can fix these, maybe alt heavy weapons, I think this game would be a hard recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: this is an okay game and I wouldnt usually give a negative review for that, buit since it has a over 90% positive rating, that I dont agree with, I will.So here is a list of problems:-the upgrades are not build defining at all, nothing makes you change your playstyle, you just stack buffs (the most creative is turning full auto fire to burst)-the early game is very grindy (might be because I suck)-the mark mechanic which you get from using spells on enemys and gives you shields has to be spammed so there is not tactic on when to use abilities at all, you just press them on cooldown-Bosses are boring and bland- most enemies are just dude that shot at you and arnt particulary distinctive from each other- there isnt really a way to dodge most enemy atacks, you tank them with the mark mechanic or walk backwards- melee is straight up underpowered and useless (which I would consider to be an essential part of a game like this)-loading times are long, there are a lot of transitions that take 10+ seconds, which really adds up when you start chaining runs (some floors which you just need to walk though also do that and its just annoying every time after the third)-secondary weapons are boring, so theres essentially only 4 weapons in the game -the art style is... lots of colors, im not a fanagain I wanna point out that this is not a terrible game, it certainly isnt for me but I think there are people who will have a reasonable amount of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: this game is better than Destiny 2 in literally every way. That is all.First Impressions:I can't really explain exactly how perfectly this game hits the sweet spot for me. I'm a massive cyberpunk nerd who writes and composes around the genre. I'm obsessed with dense lore and excellent writing (50k words deep into my own cyberpunk worldbuilding project, but that's not really important) and even more than that, I make and love the exact genre of the OST. I would've played this game for these three alone, regardless of gameplay.But it goes deeper than that. I've played Destiny 2 for wayyyy too long. I found Deadlink at a time when I was quitting D2, but in need of the same things that lead me to fall in love with Destiny to begin with: the gunplay, movement, and buildcrafting. This game nails all 3. Granted, I've only played the Soldier so far, but this is first impressions hahaha. Once I'm done writing this, I'm going to go try out the Hunter.Okay, maybe I can explain it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I love the idea of DOOM: Eternal's gameplay in a rogue-like skin. The graphics and audio are great, and the game definitely captures that Cyberpunk feel.Right now the gameplay is frustrating. A major issue is the limited ammo. DOOM fully succeeds at a "push forward" combat system by making killing enemies and moving ALWAYS be the best option. With the primary weapons of both characters requiring reloading in Deadlink, there's a constant flow-killing effect. It is not fun at all running out of ammo, trying to hide while being unable to do anything useful while reloading. If they had a limited max ammo without requiring reloading like DOOM, then the game would instantly feel much better. As it stands right now, this game is frustrating and annoying due to this, not to mention how extremely low the magazine size is. This would be fine if the game were designed around a more tactical gameplay style, but every other part of this game demands the player move forward and kill enemies. Reloading does not fit here.In general I find that enemy attacks aren't projected well. It's hard to tell what's happening and I find myself dying without really understanding why. Compare this to DOOM: Eternal which even on Nightmare difficulty, it always feels like there was some clear mistake I made on death. I can see how the enemy got me and which attack I failed to dodge. I don't know how specifically this could be fixed, but I know it's a problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Deadlink

_childDocuments_.review: Deadlink is a decent but flawed rogue-like FPS. The game has an impressive soundtrack, art style, and the performance is really good. I enjoyed playing the fast-paced gameplay for the first couple of hours.Unfortunately, after the first completed run there's not much else different to experience, and as a rogue-like that's not a good thing. Replayability suffers due to the lack of variety of enemies, arenas, and impactful implants. The rogue-like build options like the elemental upgrades have hardly any effect on how the game plays. There are implants to choose from during runs, but they're small upgrades that don't drastically change the way you play throughout. Meta upgrades can be purchased outside of the simulation. I also didn't really care for the additional armor that enemies have at higher difficulty as this just made the combat feel more tedious.Ultimately, I think Deadlink is worth playing, but not for very long as the combat loop wasn't designed well enough to keep me playing over and over again. Purchase on sale if you're interested.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves way more popularity. Its satisfyingly fun gameplay loop is the next best thing since Doom Eternal. Be warned, though: Once you get to Neuromancy difficulty, you can't just rely on your pure reflex and aim anymore; clever selections of implants and a bit of RNG will be key here.I just wish there were more variety and randomness to each run like in Hades, maybe change some encounters a bit, add more characters and places to interact with, tweak the area bosses, etc. I'd never play another game for months otherwise.Oh, and the soundtrack is banger, too. You know what, just play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really fun, fast paced, polished, personality-filled, cyberpunk-themed movement / arena-shooter. Voice acting is good, characters are good, boss fights and boss personalities are diverse and fun.On or off sale, it's a good deal. The only downside is it is lacking in variety and does feel a bit shallow once you experience the content. The levels are the same and only minimally randomized by what upgrades you can choose and what the vendors have. While there is multiple classes that afford you different abilities and play styles, the weapons are very limited as each class gets 1 primary weapon with infinite reserve ammo, and all classes get the same potential options of (limited reserve ammo) secondary weapons. For each character you'll notice that you can unlock what appear to be different weapons by completing challenges. Unfortunately, they're only weapon skins.It's a fun ride, but it's also a fast and short ride. Personally I was ready to put it down indefinitely around the 8-10 hr mark. I literally have zero complaints about this game other than I wish it had more content and depth.
_childDocuments_.name: Deadlink

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is fluid, fast and rewards constantly marking enemies to ensure you survive the combat long enough. With ample means to upgrade and enhance yourself to be a fine-tuned killing machine while listening to a fantastic music track that does not distract from the gameplay and the enjoyment...keeping you immersed....And this is where the good points kind of falls off a cliff.While the combat is fluid and can be challenging, certain aspects prove to be overwhelming or tedious.Examples are as follows:1. The second boss, upon entering the second phase, is less capable of being hit. Not a big deal, enemies keep spawning in to keep your shields up. Good. But then there is that ship that spews out homing fast-moving mines that, while you can shoot them and the ship to destroy it, chances are the moment you killed it and turn your attention to the boss...within 3 seconds another of that ship has spawned in and is making more mines and you still can't hit the boss. It's not a hard fight but it is horrendously  and drags out the fight with artificial difficulty where because you have dedicated a lot of time to fight this thing it gives the illusion of being hard rather than seen for what it actually is: micromanaging.2. The third boss is a good challenge, but the only part of it that is brutal is the very first phase where most of the floor ends up electrified and then the boss itself shoots out a wide-arc attack. If it wasn't for me playing Soldier a lot and having a grapple to pull myself up off the ground away from it all using the flying robots...I can't help but wonder how well the other combat shells would do. But also there are times the momentum of the grapple will launch me out so far that I land in electrified terrain and end up dying anyway. This wasn't a huge deal, but then the rest of the fight is just maintaining shields and shooting until it dies. The difficulty curve turns into a cliffside and nosedives after the first phase which is the literal only hurdle in that fight.3. This was the point that was the last straw that broke the camel's back, as one would say. In the fourth zone, every room you go to has a miniboss challenge. Not a big deal at face value, except when one of those minibosses is a teleporting enemy who pops up, attacks, then shortly teleports again. Not a big deal, just stun and shoot...right? Sure. But then there's lots of enemies rushing you, sniping enemies stuck to the walls that keep coming in even after you kill them. And if you take time to try regain shields, you better hope the miniboss hasn't teleported away and is nowhere to be seen. This happened several times, and when she is just gone...she shows up after she has regenerated from being half-dead to about 90% healthy with rapidly regenerating health.After doing this endless battle with me replenishing shields but unable to kill her despite every shot I do being over 500 damage or so to the face with every element on that shotgun, doing more damage on the first shot when I grapple in on her...I quite literally just got frustrated at the stupidity of the entire fight and closed out of the game with no intention of ever picking the game back up in its present state.Play this game if you want to just chill and mindlessly kill things, but don't expect to get far anytime soon without countless hours of grinding and dumb luck.

_childDocuments_.review: Deadlink is really surprising, it created many new ideas as well as using other ideas and gameplay features from other games to form a really solid roguelike shooter. The gameplay is really the fun focus here, it's more on the speedy/movement shooter side of things with your character having plenty of mobility the weapons feel really solid and overall all of the general movement is really tight it's just fun interacting with the game. Where i think the gameplay shines is its abilities and weapons, you have 3 abilities on each of the 3 and tied in to these abilities are your modifiers, all kinds of things like adding more crit damage to even adding passive increased movement speed. I don't want to make too many major comparisons here but this was a popular mechanic that was used very well in DOOM Eternal which is very successful and popular and here with Deadlink they have made their own rendition of abilities proving more than that single purpose. You go from room to room building up your equipment and improving your gear and it's all really fun. Each upgrade really makes a change on your gameplay experience. One of the main things that keeps this game fun is how you can suddenly change your weapons and gear upgrades. The weapons are really cool, you have standard weapons and heavy weapons which you start off by selecting from the 3 characters available at this current point of early access. I expect we might see maybe one or two more but currently the 3 that are here are very fun. Gunplay is really good and the weapons and equipment have so much flair and power, apart from the revolver, that feels kinda pathetic, it's really fun and powerful to use but visually it doesn't have the same kick like the others, minor but I thought it's worth bringing up. The level design here is very creative and it gives off similar vibes to the old school arena shooters like Quake and Unreal tournament. The gameplay objectives are all pretty basic, mainly just kill everything in the room or survive for a little while however there is this one room objective where you have to break these 3 floating balls, this one sucks and what makes its even worse is how little the game does to let you know it's the objective, with all the chaos on the screen i found it really hard to keep up with the objective because i was so busy avoiding enemy attacks and incoming damage. I think this objective is worth removing, it kinda feels like it pulls you away from the speedy frantic killing you are normally doing, this game has so much cool stuff in it like flying from enemy to enemy via grapple hook i just dont think it needs objectives that leave you looking away from the enemy. I wouldn't say this makes the game unplayable or even bad; it's just worth bringing up for the sake of feedback. The runs you take part in also include NPC’s that sell and offer you things and also things like shops which are a staple of rouge-likes. Outside of the normal gameplay loop you have your permanent upgrades which allow you to become stronger, these upgrades will very quickly make the game much easier if you are struggling. Fortunately there are also 3 difficulties, you start on the default and the others open up as you progress in the game. You also have plenty of lore to read plus some very light story features, there is a surprising amount of well crafted story telling for a game in this manner which is a nice addition there is also a whole codex if you choose to learn further about the games features and characters. The art is very stylish, very cell shaded and sharp, everything is very frantic looking. It can sometimes be a little tough to read what's going on during all the chaos and action but the more you play you begin to understand how the visuals present themselves. The sounds here are all really crisp and good, however the music is average, nothing crazy but its not bad by any standard, it fits very nicely into the game's theme and overall tone. As for performance the game runs pretty well for what's going on in the game, the game is pretty performance heavy though so if you are not running super high specs expect to possibly be playing at a lower visual quality or a more traditional/console level frame rate. It does run just fine though, it's a very smooth running game. As for bugs, i think it took me a whole 7 hours to run into my first issue which was a minor collision issue, it was resolved very quickly by moving my player model. There was also a very small UI bug that started after a new update but it did not hinder my experience at all. Overall this is a solid upcoming game with a very bright future, its surprising to see how little coverage this game is getting, it's really fun and chaotic and has so much passion, its only in early access currently and it's still evolving very quickly. Hopefully the game will soon find some more deserved popularity. It's a very well priced and truly very promising game. I'd definitely recommend picking this game up! Looking forward to further updates and improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Cool art style and fluid gameplay -performance is great for me.Cons:Sadly, the grind after each death has gotten too tedious kinda fast.Unlocking passives is super expensive so each run (30-60 min) provides you with a couple of them at best and then you have to go through the whole thing once again; the first levels and the first boss get quite easy and it feels like a chore going through those phases.The skills you get are triggered upon certain actions such as weapon swap or cell break, so it's honestly quite hard to keep track of what activates what during each run in such a hectic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid base of a game that quickly becomes repetitive due to limited content.Pros:+ Solid movement and gunplay strongly inspired by the new Doom games+ Worldbuilding is strong and makes you want to explore more than the game allows you to+ Clean, crisp UI and exceptional game presentation overall+ The game loop of fighting through connected arenas before a boss encounter is ok, but there are very few rooms and I started losing interest after about 10 hours+ Good variety of skills to augment your guns, shell, and neural statsCons:- Way too repetitive. Very few rooms for each 'biome' and you get to know them all very soon. Moreover, the order of the 'biomes' is not randomized and you'll get to see the first one over and over again- Extremely grindy. Grind is to be expected in a roguelite, but Deadlink goes a bit too far with it. 15 hours in and only unlocked the cheapest half of the base skills and the starting class abilities (out of 4 classes total)- The lore, while interesting, is only tangentially delivered via item/enemy info and short NPC lines in the home base- That one stereotypical gen-Z NPC, Argentea, is annoying as ♥♥♥♥

_childDocuments_.review: Deadlink is in the most fortunate situation a rogue-lite can be in. Its flaws are in the lack of depth of the rogue-lite mechanics and its strengths are in the core gameplay. The best news is the update history already shows a track record of that depth being improved upon. There's only one direction Deadlink is moving in. Up.This is some of the best single player FPS gameplay I've experienced. The animations, sound design, movement, and the tightly designed weapon & class ability interactions are simply a pleasure.If you enjoy single player FPS games and/or rogue-lites this is as straightforward a pickup as they come.

_childDocuments_.review: The best worst game I've played in a while. I was mega hyped for it, love Roguelites and Doom and through something that's both of those should be amazing. Sadly, the game is great but frustratingly ♥♥♥♥, for a few clear reasons. Gun play feels and looks good, loot is generally satisfying, and the game looks and sounds great. 1) Core mechanic creates its own bag of problems. The game *requires* you to mark and kill marked enemies to regenerate shield and ammo. At high difficulties, mark time is very low, and only your abilities and grenades can mark things. Cooldowns on your abilities are all absurdly long (unless you're lucky with a cooldown implant or cheesing with a reset item/implant/shell upgrade). This leads not to incredibly engaged gameplay where you're weaving in and out from enemies, soaking up damage but taking them on to regenerate at risk, but instead blowing all your cooldowns, gathering a bit of shield, and then running away to ledges and temp sheilf pick-ups until your abilities are back. Entirely antifun. Especially terrible at higher levels when enemies tank rockets to the face like they're popcorn balls and marks last a second or two. 2) Difficult spike is a flat wall that drops off if you've been godtier lucky enough to get your "build" online. The cooldown/mark/run around loop means that in high difficulties where dozens of enemies spawn all at once, your ass is toast. Once in a blue moon, however, you'll get a cheese combo of shell upgrades, implants, etc that make the game AFK easy. Then you go back to dying for 100 runs in a row. I finished the last boss on the hardest difficulty without even realising it, because my engineer turret had ability power, fire+elec+toxic, and burst down the boss in, I kid you not, literal seconds. 3) The game is far too RNG reliant. See above. You'll go literally hundreds of runs not seeing a certain implant because you only have three rerolls (oh and your rerolls are shared between any choice, so you'll get a ♥♥♥♥ weapon but can't reroll cos you want to spend it on rerolling an implant). 4) Enemies either swarm the ♥♥♥♥ out of you . It goes beyond Chaotic to simply stupid, especially when their tankiness comes up in higher difficulties. Then three mortar tanks spawn, plus three charger shield guys, plus two teleport witches, basically there's no where to go (oh don't stop moving because the tanks will obliterate you, but also don't run out of dashes or jumps because the witch will get you, but also don't even think about touching the ground because the chargers take no damage and are faster than you). Oh, "just hit them from behind!" lmao, sure, just jump over them and stand there while witches and tanks take their turns with your exposed cheeks. 5) you're so slow. Sure, you can move faster, but then all your implants and shell upgrades are no longer giving you damage. So you can choose to be fast and do zero dps, or slow and enemies take three rockets to kill. lol.6) certain Characters/frames/robots are just not really viable. At higher difficulties the hunter is fun but not viable. You need to mark enemies to survive, remember? But your swap ability MUST be reserved for traversal (nice cooldown penalty if you use it on an enemy, oh and it swaps you INTO the enemies on the ground). You can go invisible every 16 seconds or whatever, hope you enjoy your one attack you get that does double damage (so you still need to shoot the enemy once more to kill it). 7) meta progression is the slowest thing on earth. After nearly 30 hours I still don't have all the upgrade paths unlocked. Some of the late upgrades seem core parts of the characters kit, why would they be locked away behind 5000 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ credits? 8) nerfs. Why would you nerf anything in a PVE single-player game? Especially when disgusting cheese strats and builds still exists, it's not just gated behind some of the most unforgiving RNG in roguelite history. All in all, a fantastic game that's been put together with real love, but severe flaws in the design that end up making it a pure slog. I'd highly recommend it if you're looking for something to enjoy and a few dozen hours before realising you actually are having no fun, really, and dropping it entirely. You'll definitely get caught by the "this is fun, and I'm sure with just one more upgrade and some good RNG I'll get the C-ball invisibility implant or the one that restores 40% of my cooldown. Just one more run".

_childDocuments_.review: Wish there were neutral reviews, but as it is im more inclined on the thumbs down than the thumbs up.As a shooter? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing, easily in my top 10 FPS just by the gunplay alone, even in comparison to it's roguelite peers, it's way above every single one of them, the flow of the combat, the enemy reactions when being shot, the particles and effects of your bullets meeting flesh/steel is insanely satisfying.As a roguelite? Not gonna sugarcoat it, this is NOT it, 3 hours in and i've already seen everything the game has to offer (bar the last difficulty but i'm 100% sure it will just be enemies have extra health and you get ♥♥♥♥ on in seconds) there's only 4 levels with a single boss each, it gets REALLY repetitive since the "roguelite" aspect of it boils down to "your weapon can sometimes burn/shock/corrode enemies and you get +10% damage on your revolver" and the most "outlandish" upgrades i've gotten are stuff like "Spawn a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ turret drone when you do X" Everything else like the story, characters, music, etc is also good, the soundtrack in Tora legit made me stare at the exit of a room just so i could keep listenting to it.Only way i can recommend the game is with a DEEP discount, and im talking 50-60%, the devs have a LOT of talent but they somehow made one of the LEAST replayable roguelites i've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: Gave this game a fair try but it's just not good enough for what it is. The bosses and mini bosses after the first one are super tough and you're going to die over and over. This is mostly due to the laziest boss game design of all with tons of constantly spawning enemies on the boss all around you meaning you need to juggle them while getting shot from all sides which is super annoying and poorly designed. So then you restart and go again. The problem is the game is super repetitive. Of the 3 total shells available after 10 hrs, each one uses the same 2 guns and the same two abilities. You can unlock a few new guns from RNG but you mostly use the same ones. You fight the same enemies in the same boring rooms and fight the same bosses in the same order. So no new guns or abilities or anything. Then theres all the unlocks and upgrades. The chip system is kind of stupid meaning you only get a few temporary boosts when you use an ability  a few times a room, and some boring passive bonuses. Most upgrades are just getting different damage types. The shell upgrades are mostly just more damage or health and you rarely see those. So its mostly common rarity boring chips which change nothing and you can only use a few and sell the others. But all the items in the shops are boring common chips, and theres nothing else to buy. Then after you spend 30-40 min finishing a run because the game requires insane grinding, you'll  get a 5% boost in damage reduction and thats it, or unlock a single added thing to start the run. Once you see how high the requirements are for small upgrades it takes away all fun, since you know you'll be using the same guns with the same boring upgrades fighting  the same enemies in the same room. The ripoff doom system is also just done worse and extra stupid and convoluted. You can only get ammo from smashing random few things around the room, that you can't shoot  but have to melee. Then you can only get armor back from hitting an enemy with a grenade or using a certain special ability.  Its just annoying and obtrusive for the sake of being so and youre getting hit from all sides while waiting for weapon cooldowns or grenade respawns to get armor back that disappears so quickly. Then you can't even get health back without spending money. Theres just not enough variety in classes, weapons, encounters, enemies, upgrades, or anything to make the incessant grind worth it. The game isn't all bad as the action can be fun when it works and some guns and abilities are cool and so is the fast paced movement. But mostly failed potential. 5.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Deadlink

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good. Very fun and dynamic I like it a lot and it ate a big chunk of my summer vacation time.A number of my personal gripes if I may. They are mostly related to Neuromancy difficulty.- Rikishi in Tora with increased speed are way too oppressive if you are not playing Hunter- A lot of enemies (like tachikomas or pincers) are too projectile happy, 2-3 of them at the same time in different locations turn game into bullet hell and often damage you take feels unfair - Phoenix pounders and shielders need to chill. It's almost impossible to break distance with them even if you constantly stun them. Same goes to bosses of stage 4 that share similar traits, especially Laika.- Trash dude is useless. Amount of times he actually given me something worthy I can count on one hand. Add on top of that lottery cost which increases with each attempt and amount of XP you need to upgrade your combat shells and in the end we are getting NPC which I rather ignore than use more than once per run ever. On the other hand hackerman is too useful. You get plenty of tokens per run and can get a lot of implants and upgrades if you feel like it. No dowsides except of  RNG. Not saying that hackerman needs to be nerfed, but trash dude just has to feel worthy of interacting with. - Iskra's fight is too chaotic and messy. Too many things you need to keep track on. 4th phase initiates too early. So you need to manage constantly damaging ground, aoe zones which block out c-balls (you have to break them again too), constant stream of lasers, constant assault of drones, changing terrain. I would be happy if changing terrain aspect would just go away and laser phase would be delayed as it turns fight into DPS race. I would also like to add that without  good corrosion damage this fight is practically unwinnable. Which brings me to the next gripe.- Corrosion / toxic damage is too good. At the beginning you have clear distinction between enemy types and what they represent. On Neuromancy difficulty EVERY enemy has armor. So you need to have corrosion and toxic damage ASAP. Locust swarm is by far the best weapon choice for secondary gun, without it you might as well just restart the run. - Liz Watson's second stage is extremely mechanic busy while not providing enough opportunities to refill your shield- Not enough ways to restore HP between stages.This is  just how I feel in general. Looking forward for future updates, game has great potential and awesome soundtrack. Good luck!
_childDocuments_.name: Deadlink

_childDocuments_.review: Now, I very rarely ever review games. I think it's an exercise in futility trying to espouse my subjective recommendations on to others only to be mildly annoyed later when I'm blown off like chop liver and talkative Detroit gangsters. However, this game is different. Where do I start? This game is TIGHT. Tight like 3'11" Nun snatch, aroused before big J.C. himself. This game is so smooth and easy to play, and flows so well its absolutely unreasonable. Each "frame" fills its own unique game-play loop and combat never seems to drag at all. From bursting into the action with your Gripwire Rappel (grappling hook) and blasting an enemy into a fine dust a la meat chunks with your "Scrapper" shotgun, or "trans-locating" behind your enemy letting out a, "nothing personnel kid" and blowing a structurally superfluous ventilation hole into his braincase before tossing down a decoy and zipping around to do the same thing over again, this game has it all. All this is kept funky fresh by the variety of upgrades you can get in the field and permanent upgrades you can get at homebase; and boy let me tell you: this thing polished, I think Dracula can see his reflection in this thing. From the subtle "chunka-chunka-chunk" noise your frame makes while walking to indicate how heavy you are, to the absolutely beautiful art-style, to the HUD so well designed you basically forget its there. This game is so sleek and sheen and it's not even done yet -- with more content being promised later down the line. If I'm allowed, I'd also like to drop a little anecdote. Whilst playing this game, I was so ensconced in my game-play experience that I legitimately forgot to blink, and my eyes began watering, and yet, I still soldiered on; that's right, this game is so good, it quite literally brought me to tears. Like John Carmack said, "Lore in shooters is like the story in p*rn", but honestly? If that is the case, this is one of those hilariously entertaining cuckold videos where he gets on a Segway and starts doing wheelies while the bull dominates his wife pleading with him to stop. Deadlink's lore is Cyberpunk dystopia with a sort of tongue-and-cheek pitch-black humour that doesn't take itself too seriously, whilst still providing some valid critiques of systems of capital like a good piece of Cyberpunk media should. Its competently written, and I actually wanted to read the lore entries so if that's not testament enough I don't know what is. Anyways, with all that being said, go buy and play Deadlink if you have the financial wherewithal to do so, I know I'm sure as Shinola getting back in the simulation.

_childDocuments_.review: With no gun variation it feels very stale just after a couple runs. _childDocuments_.review: Very early impression but this game is great !The gunplay and movement feel just right and it's clear the developers understand how to make building a character interesting: if you like games like Hades and Dead Cells where you're constantly on the lookout for that one upgrade that will make all the pieces of your build fit together, this game is great at that.Initially, it's awkward to deal with the ability cooldowns but once you understand the game's flow, everything becomes very natural. This game takes clear inspiration from Doom Eternal's combat system where you would refill your ressources by killing enemies in certain ways: the biggest difference here is that instead of using "glory kills" that are just fancy animations, Deadlink forces you to use abilities to "tag" enemies, who will then spawn ressources when killed. This system is fantastic and really forces the player to think about how to approach each fight.I've only done a handful of runs so far and i can't find of any significant problems i have with the game, i might update this review later when i have more experience !

_childDocuments_.review: So far this has been an incredibly enjoyable Rogue-lite FPS with combat that reminds me of doom 2016 in both it's high emphasis on mobility and resource management involving incredibly aggressive play. The cyberpunk aesthetic and cell-shaded art-style mixing both strong pastels and vibrant neon's really appeals to me and I've enjoyed challenging myself with the higher difficulties. My main complaints are mostly to do with it's limited content offerings. The game currently only has two classes (although I truly love how different their kits are) and two locations (with many arenas between them, but they are becoming repetitive at 10 hours of play, especially the Japanese levels. However as this is so close to the early access release, I fully expect this to become rectified as development progresses. One problem more content will not necessarily fix is the game's unfortunate, in my opinion, over-reliance on persistent upgrades as progression. Obviously these are a source of contention for discussions of the Rogue like and lite subgenres, and I have personally really enjoyed games with persistent stat increases to their game loops like Hades and Gunfire Reborn. However persistent upgrades in Deadlink go from the convenient like expanded pick up radius, new abilities, and getting a loadout after spawning just to mix up each run more fully and experiment early, to the compulsory persistent damage, resistance, and health sometimes totaling at buffs of nearly 25%. This feels like it is compensating for the game's speed (projectiles, player, and enemy) instead of making other ways the player can keep up with enemy health and dps. Altogether I really have enjoyed this title and look forward to future updates and content.

_childDocuments_.review: If I never played another minute of Deadlink, I would still be able to consider it one of my favorite games of 2024 and one of the best FPS Roguelike games I have every played. I only have 2 of the 4 classes unlocked and wouldn't even need anymore to be happy with my purchase (though knowing there are more is nice lol)I love the cyberpunk aesthetic a lot and I think Deadlink does it justice. Overall visuals are fine. Nothing amazing but the visuals do look great. The gameplay is very fun and fast paced. It's fast, frantic (with a short breather in between each section of the map), and the control are very tight (which you need in those life or death moments). The guns are punchy and feel varied between the classes and the weapon mods you can get along the way, seemingly making for a ton of varied runs before the game gets to that same-y feel. Each of the mods also feel fun to use and none have really felt pointless or bland.The two classes I have unlocked so far feel very different from one another and really does open up the options for runs and adds a lot of replay value. So far, the basic shot gunner has been my main but the second more stealth based class has been really enjoyable for someone who is more of a "so I started blasting" kind of player. I'm confident that the other 2 classes will offer more unique play styles and build to extend the games life even more.The level (really more arena design) is where the game really shines. For me, this is a master class of design. Each area feels built from the ground up to keep you on your toes and give you enough space to and freedom to really tackle each area how you want. They also feel designed with the classes abilities in mind. Truly, I can't say enough (or have the words this morning) to truly gush enough about this.The level up system for your classes seems well thought out. Because I am pretty bad at Deadlink I haven't been able to touch this too much yet so I don't want to touch on this too much. If you enjoy the single player side of Roboquest, Deadlink will be right up your ally.
_childDocuments_.name: Deadlink

_childDocuments_.review: ...It's ok, I guess. Deadlink, at it's core, is a unique take on the roguelike genre. Instead of upgrades being passive or activating on hit/kill, your upgrades activate after swapping weapons, using abilities, or smashing a 'c-ball' which are ammo crates. The upgrades also have a battery meter, which means that the ability's active ability cannot be used unless you equip it on an ability that does not have the correct battery meter. This is a pretty unique balancing system that I like a lot. It stops you from getting too strong too fast, but the issue is that you never really feel like you're getting stronger. Not only is there a lack of that feeling, every run plays systematical the same. There's hasn't been a run where I've gotten an upgrade and it's changed the entire way I play the game. With other games in the genre like Gunfire that DOES have upgrades that dramatically change a run, it feels bad to do the same thing for 25 minutes straight.Deadlink is also far more skill-based than other roguelikes, which is enjoyable until you realize you have no clue where you're being hit from or where the enemies are. Half the time you don't even realize you're taking damage then BOOM you're dead. There is no healing in this game other than medkits you get after completing a room. Your survivability is based entirely on 'marking' enemies with your abilities and grenades then killing them for shield. This is done well but you get a minuscule amount of shields from enemies that can be way too sponge-y.Deadlink has so much potential but not only does this not feel like a full release, there is nothing here that isn't done better by other games. Roboquest has waaay better feeling gunplay and Gunfire Reborn has waaay better roguelike elements. I want to like this game, but when you have ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ deaths from who knows where and when runs feel stale and boring after the first area, you're doing something wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: Received with a humble bundle.I'd recommend Roboquest or Gunfire Reborn before playing this.The theme of the game is pretty neat and the shooting feels decent are what stick out initially.My immediate issue is as a roguelite we don't see significant differences between runs which I think is truly one of the greatest mistakes a roguelite/like can make. Since you're going to frequently and constantly repeating the same content it better feel different to play through. In Deadlink it does not feel different. I get that I'm supposed to have multiple runs to unlock more meta progression so you can easily push the higher difficulties but it doesn't feel good doing it.I'm fighting the same basic enemies with my minimally changing guns and my very very slightly altered abilities if I'm lucky to get the right drops between rooms. The explosiveness and excitement just isn't there.As of late I've become very jaded with the rogue-genre. I feel like it's a really great excuse to make a small amount of content that is decently polished and call it a game because you'll run through it over and over again. Enter Deadlink.

_childDocuments_.review: While you won't be playing this for the story - don't get me wrong, there is one, even if it is just a wrapper - you will be playing this for the gameplay, the play styles and the upgrades, which are all interesting and surprisingly refreshing.This is rogue-lite, so you expect ever changing levels and map variety, which you won't really get, but that's not a bad thing. On the third successful run, you will notice that the bosses are the same, the levels are the same - just shuffled - and that things become familiar. What makes this roguelite stand out is its character classes, weapons, upgrades and mods, which change the entire playstyle quite a bit. While I feel there are 2 strong and 2 weaker characters, based on their long vs short range capabilities, they all have their place. Especially when you get the right upgrades with the correct elements (corrode, fire, electricity) then you will feel it.You may consider this a spoiler, but the game has 3 ways of playing: You finish the last boss, you finish the last boss 7 times or you actually go higher than the default difficulty (pretty tough) and then finish the game on both higher difficulties. I went the second route and then lost interest due to the repetition of the same levels, but given that this was after 15 hours, I could not be happier about it.If you like faster-paced FPS and rogue-lite, but do not care too much about story, but like the vibe of the world in the trailers, then go ahead. You will have quite a few hours of fun with this!

_childDocuments_.review: For now, I can't get into this game. Its got decent gunplay, but the movement feels restrictive with the grapple hook needing a cooldown and all the abilities are tied to using an ability on cooldown. Plus, all the movement you can do to avoid damage seems to move you into another form of damage you can't track or see because enemies can just spawn randomly. In the later levels there is so much AI that the damage vectors are everywhere and you just collide with it all. The grind feels slow and not effective, being very minimal impact. If the vertical movement was better and you could better avoid damage that is your blindspots, maybe. _childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a middling option for reviews, I'm very conflicted about this game, I'll just spit out a pros and cons list and you can make of it what you will.PROS:-Gamefeel is incredible. The movement, the way the guns shoot, the sounds, the animations, it all comes together in a way that's just immaculate. This game scratches a movement shooter itch that only ultrakill has previously scratched for me.-Related to gamefeel, class mechanics are fun and feel really good. A lot of these mechanics are versatile and have many use cases, allowing the player to have a lot of freedom in their gameplay. For example the hunter shell's switchback, which lets you switch places with an enemy, stunning them in the process. Pretty simple and yet very versatile. -The combat music is great, banger high energy synths that roll with the fighting.CONS:-While the enemy design is usually great, the boss design can feel crusty at times, certain class abilities just don't work on them, meaning shells which rely more on these abilities have a harder time. The game also can fall in the pit of "more health = harder", leading to boss encounters that can feel like a slog to get through, and something that has to be endured to get to the fun part that's after them rather than part of the fun themselves. Trinary Iskra for example, while a very interesting concept (3 AI cores in one machine which are constantly bickering with each other) basically just boils down to a parkour challenge, it spins lasers around in patterns and makes platforms you have to jump between while you whittle away at its health bar. Its not particularly difficult but it takes a while and isn't very engaging the way the rest of the game is.-Repetition, it all kinda gets old after a while. The gameplay feels good enough to stay fresh, but the rooms and enemies start to feel stale. There is one preset boss per region, it never changes. You can fight optional bosses as challenges, but they are just re-skins of already existing enemies.-Finally, the writing. It's not good. Now its a rouge-lite, the focus and appeal is on the gameplay, the story is secondary, this is a given. Unfortunately, the lore often drifts from being poorly written into straight up being gross, to the point it makes it harder to enjoy the rest of the game. I will explain, now as is par for the course with poorly written cyberpunk there is an unhealthy dose of techno-orientalism, and at a glance one might think that's as bad as it gets. It is not. i.e. the codex entry of one of the basic yakuza enemies in the japan region describes them as "trying to outdo each other in their show of suicidal dedication". Subtle. There is also the megacorps, the story is about taking down megacorps. Sick right? Unfortunately it turns out the megacorps are written less like actual corporations and more like what your politically illiterate conservative grandfather would criticize as "the elite", in that they for example, employ women. No I'm not kidding. The final region has two kinds of basic enemies, one is all guys and one is all girls. The women 'caste' or whatever are described in the codex as a "propaganda force." Because they're women. The company hires 50% women. And it's framed by the writing as like, dystopian. Do you get what I mean now?TL:DRFeels incredible to play most of the time, very engaging gameplay that rewards quick thinking and creativity, music slaps, however the bosses can be a slog, surroundings feel stale after a few hours, and you have to actively tune out the really gross writing.
_childDocuments_.name: Deadlink

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, oh boy! This game reminds me of when I was playing Unreal Tournament 3 competitions back in the ''barely alive in a hospital bed'' days of LAN parties (which is all I got to witness of that era, sadly)! They're such good memories and it's good to have a new game to fill that gap, even though in a singleplayer way.Deadlink is far from being an uninspired tribute or ''boomer shooter'' though. It surely takes influence from that stuff (Painkiller?), but it also puts its own spin onto it, giving it a contemporary edge too. How do you make it in step with the times? Well, you do by making it rogue-lite and by taking inspiration from the biggest games in the modern arena shooter revival scene as well.As a result, Deadlink is a super-fast arena shooter that feels relentless and unforgiving, but never unfair! It's got the right amount of challenge (easy enough to get far, unlock stuff and get excited, while at the same time tough enough to make you work hard and truly earn your achievements). This is what I meant with reviving that ol' PvP arena FPS thrill! The combination of constant practice + long-term upgrades makes you feel like you're constantly improving... and it's true! This is a nice contrast to other rogue-lite games which just keep on smashing you and keeping you to the ground, despite all your best efforts and improved skills!Once you get the hang of things you're going to feel like a cyber-augmented John Wick!It's the kind of game that builds character in the best way possible, being 100% fun throughout... I've never felt so motivated by a rogue-lite game and I don't think I ever lied to myself this much about ''ok, just ONE more run!'' (to then play 5-6 more instead). It gets you having lots of fun and leaves you always desiring to come back for more (and to further improve yourself). Admittedly it takes a while to get used to its gameplay loop (particularly if you haven't played many recent FPS games), but once you do it just feels mindblowingly great!For this reason, Deadlink is the definition of addictive: most of the hours I played so far have been in the span of a week... I was totally hooked in! Obsessed until I beat it the first (and so far only) time at roughly 19 hours (27 runs). I don't remember feeling this satisfied about my personal growth with a game (or anything else) ever before! So yeah... the gameplay definitely checks out!Even from a presentation standpoint, the game looks awesome! And it's the only rogue-lite I know in which the premise, lore, characters and dialogue are genuinely interesting and well-developed. Of the hours I've played so far, a considerable deal have been spent reading the codex entries to get some insight into the game world! The, dare I say, ''plot'' also serves as the perfect excuse for the rogue-lite mechanic. Overall the devs created an engaging and very captivating surrounding to all the cyberpunk mayhem you're going to unleash inside the simulation! I just hope someday we'll see the actual strike to the megacorporation (maybe in a PvP multiplayer format...).Being able to save mid-run to then resume playing later on is a nice touch! Definitely a quality of life inclusion that more rogue-lites should have. What's weird, though, is warning you before saving the match, but instantly killing yourself (with no warning) as soon as you click ''abandon run'' when you're not allowed to save. The only  other downside I can point out is that the framerate goes down a bit during the most action-packed moments, even though luckily it never goes to unplayable levels, with my system at least. Still a pretty demanding game, hardware-wise!Ultimately, Deadlink is an exciting, modern and fresh take on the old arena FPS formula of the likes of Unreal Tournament, Painkiller and Quake 3 Arena. The cyberpunk world, the great sound design and a banging soundtrack ensure that everything (from the gunplay to the immersion factor) feels convincing and addictive. You can really feel the passion, talent and creativity involved in the game's development in every little thing! So... miss that frantic feeling of speed and excitement that you used to experience playing Quake 3 Arena and Unreal Tournament? No worries! Deadlink (particularly as the soldier) will surely bring back that old, long lost familiar feeling that you cherish so much! If I were you (and into fast arena FPS gameplay), I'd make sure not to miss this!

_childDocuments_.review: Deadlink is an average game. It isn't terrible. It isn't great. If the game space it was working in was less crowded, it would be more interesting. _childDocuments_.review: There is a lack of build diversity and changes between runs. Generally you have very limited options between runs. While it is a skill-based game, frequently there is not enough time or feedback to see what is happening around you. You are encouraged to move quickly and mark enemies (this game's way of having enemies drop vital resources) but due to how enemies warp in and a lack of a distinct sense of space, it can be very hard to tell where enemies are and where your threat is coming from. This usually means that you will be dashing, running and gunning but without a good sense of flow. The game either needs better feedback or it needs better build diversity. Until then there is nothing that makes it stand out from other fast-paced FPS shooters

_childDocuments_.review: A very solidly constructed roguelite that falls into a lot of the pitfalls of roguelites; spongy enemies, repetitive runs, grindy progression and a string of drops that just isn't that fun to play. The core mechanics are solid but limited by cooldowns and locked behind random picks, so it never quite feels like a true movement shooter, fights become more a question of stacking damage from mod picks than moment to moment fps combat.Presentation is good visually and musically, but the writing is completely uninteresting, not helped kinda flat or downright grating delivery from the voice cast, fair enough the plot isn't pretending to be much more than an excuse but if it's not going to be important then minimise it more, I don't want to keep hearing these non-characters in my ear. The Boss fights are a particular low point, all of them feeling more like a DPS check than a real back and forth, with no variation between runs to add interest. I repeatedly entertained thoughts of rummaging through the game's files to try and Half the Phoenix Alpha's HP, because fighting him is deeply unfun and significantly harder than all following fights.This is a very negative review mostly because there are just better options for this kind of thing, if you're not looking for specifically a cyberpunk aesthetic r/l fps you could be playing a better game, but if that is specifically what you want, this game is fine.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game, I'd have more hours in it if I wasn't worried about playing it to death before the full launch. the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ reductive take is that its doom eternal-esque acrobatic shooting + a cyberpunk setting + roguelite replayability. But Deadlink does a really good job of expanding beyond its inspiration, the currently 3 character classes all play genuinely very differently, which is quite rare for an FPS game, since kind of the core of the genre is that everyone is some kind of shooting man. The deadlink classes though have like completely different toolkits, it's not just different guns or different starting gear, it changes the way you engage with the entire playspace bc of the emphasis on movement and positioning. You start the game feeling like a moron who sucks, and as you get better and better you start to feel like a real badass. Then you put the difficulty up and feel like a moron who sucks again. It's an oddly compelling loop.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth every penny, amazing gun play and abilities are fun and splashy. Highly recommend to anyone looking for something "high octane". Story isn't anything awful compelling but it has a great understanding of what it is and makes you laugh. Plenty of replay ability with secrets, achievements, and unlocks. Each run feels pleasantly unique and builds can make you feel godlike if put together properly.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm utterly addicted, only stopping when my back and hands hurt. Satisfying and fast paced gunplay. Banging soundtrack. Great artstyle. Like others have stated, the roguelike elements are a bit on the weak side as there are minimal interesting perk/upgrade choices that don't boil down to optimal damage upgrades, but this can be fixed easily down the road. (I'm also sick of the cyberpunk trend continuing to conflate capitalism and asian culture, but that's more of a genre problem)

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah I've bounced off this game hard as its likely just not for me. I'd refund it but I got it as part of humble bundle so whatevs. Still, my short time with this game has already produced enough notes for a rant. So here's that I guess.Quite immediately I hate the rogue-lite elements. They appear shockingly shallow and uninteresting. The arenas are small and blocky, existing only as a space to fight yet not even being very fun to fight in. Feedback in this game seems quite bad as I never could figure out what was happening to my health until the shooting stopped and I was able to actively look down and see how bad or good I did in the last room. I hate the priority placed on using everything all at once all the time, but then having 8 second cool downs on those things and the occasional reload that always seems to come out of nowhere cause there is no way in hell I'm counting my bullets. Also how in the world does a game of this pace have a 2 second cool down on the dash. Gunfire Reborn has the same but unlike here that game is paced for it. Enemy projectiles may as well not exist with how small and quiet they are. Dodging damage in this game seems to be entirely about staying on the move but then they put half the ledges at a height you have to awkwardly clamber to. Having the health system be based on both "marking" enemies and then still having to pick up the drops feels like trash to play around and being able to run out of ammo on the secondary is just another case of not being able to do what I wanna do because I haven't made use of some forced feeling mechanic in the last 30 seconds. I mean seriously, you get ammo back by picking it up off the ground from re-spawning ammo points like your playing quake online or by punching random floating orbs. It's bizarre and annoying. The first boss fight is also a real stinker cause the dude just spends the whole fight spawning in more enemies. I will say the first person animations are wonderful and satisfying and the game has a great art style overall. Would have been put to better use in a game with actual unique and varied locations instead of this amalgamation of other products of the time that doesn't seem to hold a candle to any one of them.I'll probably try it again when I don't have 10 other games to play that I'm more interested in.
_childDocuments_.name: Deadlink

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand games that make design decisions that actively drag the player out of the core experience, and this game truly suffers from that. If I'm playing a fast paced shooter with rougelite elements I want to be able to shoot fast, dodge quickly, and kill lots of enemies and that's pretty much all I want to be focusing on during intense moments. Adding mechanics that are like "Hey you have to break these floating balls in the sky in order to activate your powerups" is mind boggling to me. Not only that the powerups in this game sadly feel terrible and the shield regeneration mechanic is poorly thought out. Most of the powerups are your typical increase damage by 10%, increase shields by 10%, increase health by 10% and while those kind of upgrades are certainly necessary in rougelike/lite games, almost every upgrade in this game is some kind of variant of that. As for the shields, you have to mark enemies by using your abilities almost constantly. This makes it feel like you are required to use your abilities all the time in order to keep your health up, rather then being able to make more strategic choices for when to use them. Overall, the game feels like a solid fps shooter with rougelike elements added at the last moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I like this game, and wish I'd put a positive review on it. But it relies waaaaaaay too much on "Loot Pinata" mechanic from new Doom as only way to reliably gain armor/ammo, which I absolutely hated. Sometimes it feels like game has an identity crisis as It tries to be a fast paced shooter, but because you need to rely on abilities to "Pinatafy" enemies you have to play it safe and pick enemies one by one as abilities recharge. Then game says "you should keep away from enemies because they damage you more in CQC". But pretty much every ability only works at point blank. Another thing is bosses, on which abilities dont work at all so they give you no armor and you have to waste time on henchmen to gain armor/ammo.Also it has these "Ammo orbs" which mostly serve as annoyance, because abilities target them instead of enemies when next to each other (which happens often). So in crucial moment when you need to stun someone to get out of sticky situation you instead jump to one of these useless orbs.Its worth a try, especialy as it has a free demo, but unless you love that Doom's mechanic, you wont enjoy this game much.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game all around, super stylish, fast-paced fun. Four classes to choose from with random modifiers offered in each run for a bit of build variety and combat that pushes you to go fast and go deep. If you like roguelikes and FPS, this is a game for you with a cyberpunk spin. Even the world is pretty neat, plenty of little details added to flesh it out and make you feel a bit more like it is something that could be. There's plenty of humor, both good and bad tossed in for fun as well. I had a lot of fun with the original mode and now there is an endless mode which I'm having a blast with and a time trial mode. Overall this is a great game for a decent price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is, in a word, weak. The rogue "lite" nature is laughably lackluster for upgrades at a glance, which is fine enough, but the combat itself is by far the most lacking part. The difficulty is non existent until bosses, at which point it manufactures it in the most dreadful way that is all too common among games made by inexperienced developers. Enemy spam. When you do end up beating the boss, it just falls over silently. That experience sums up the game pretty well. I got two levels in, and that's just how it goes. You steam roll enemies that only offer a bit of resistance because of how many there are, not because they're well designed or difficult on their own. You then get to the boss, fight it without damage until you get to phase 2, then enemies just keep pouring in as the boss just speeds up its attacks. It just keeps attacking faster until phase 3, where the entire lack of developmental expertise shines brightly and the bosses just attack non stop. The first boss pretty much never stops shooting 3 laser beams at you while enemies spawn without falter. Since the machine guns and lasers never stop shooting, along with the mortars that go behind cover, it's actually not even worth your time to kill enemies for getting back the meager amount of shield offered. It's genuinely far more viable to just bounce around and keep shooting the boss to reach its soundless death more quickly. When you beat a massive spider robot, it just...falls apart like a lego. No sound at all.The next boss is a juggernaut of a thing that uses a shield. it just slams the ground over and over until you get to phase 3, at which point the strongest and tankiest AI spawn non stop, and then he goes berserk. He just jumps and jumps, pounding the ground to shoot lightning everywhere. It's just boring, predictable, and very poorly made. It's got every last telltale sign of poor design for a lackluster boss fight. Can't make a unique, difficult fight? Spam enemies. That not enough? Spam attacks from the boss without stopping. The mediocre combat leading up to even more disappointing boss fights would be fine if it were more than just passably fun. The combat is quick...kinda, but is still somehow stale despite everything in motion. The grapple is by far the worst part. It has a 3 second cool down if you grapple to an ammo orb, but to an enemy? 7 seconds. This drastically slows the pace of the game, and makes it...boring. It's just not fun. The game clearly struggles to form even a semblance of difficulty, so they solve that with two very trashy choices. Longer cooldowns and enemy spam. The game would be drastically more fun if it just leaned  into being fast. If you could grapple with a 3 second cool down from one enemy to another, that would add far more fun than this game is willing to allow. The dashing is also pretty much tied to the same sinking ship. Its cooldown is just too long to fun, but just short enough to be functional. The game ties the player down with mediocre systems to fabricate difficulty instead of allowing them to have fun and just making do. In essence, the game punishes the player for not knowing how to make difficult encounters. It doesn't ever embrace being a fast cyberpunk shooter, but tries to be a tough rouge lite first, and a fun shooter second. It falls short on both accounts. The generous sale on launch was enough to make me pick it up despite  the lackluster demo, but nothing really improved since then. Enemies just shoot at you like drones and eat bullets like sponges. The myriad systems in place to spice up the combat flow are all just so woefully lackluster that everything is just a tedious blur. If this game is to get somewhere worth buying, it's got a good few tweaks to make. As it stands, its only saving grace is filling a niche that not many others have tried. Rogue lite shooters are rare enough, and cyberpunk ones? Practically non existent. That's all it has going for it. That, and the graphics. They're pretty nice.

With 4 classes each with there own unique abilities and playstyles, player's also have the freedom to build themselves in a way that suites the fast paced action they face in the later levels.Overall a really fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, trigger-happy action game. Get it if you're after a fast-paced, neon-coloured session of making the baddies pay for their crimes. Lore and story is there and is written well; it won't get in your way if all you want is 10 minutes of jump-dash-grapple-headshot fun. I don't know if the authors were inspired by it, but the core mechanics here are as tight as in DOOM (2017). Separate compliments to the composer of in-game music. Heated action is matched with soundtrack that could fit even a triple A game like Cyberpunk 2077. Transitions to downtime music when using shops or moving to the next area are smooth, calming you down before you jump into action again. Sweet AF!Definitely recommend, even at the full price!

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Cells roguelike structure with Doom Eternal combat mechanics.From someone who did not like Doom Eternal, this game is what I wish it was. It relies on the same quick movement and weapon swapping mechanics to generate shield and ammo to make sure you never reload, but by limiting it to 2 weapons, you can focus on your mechanics instead of hitting one of 12 keys for the right weapon.Haven't gotten past the third boss yet and I don't feel like the game is slowing down at all for me. Solid pickup I did not expect to like

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best rougelikes I've played in years. Every gameplay feature ties back into the others giving the gameplay a very engaging and thrilling rythm, the main idea is that you have to use your abilities to mark enemies so they'll refill your shield bar (secondary health bar) upon death as the close range nature of the combat and the aggressiveness of the enemy ai makes it unlikely that you'll be able to dodge every attack. All this makes for a very fun combat system where you're constantly racing to recharge your health faster than you lose it.The rougelite elements are used well to simplify the gameplay while you're still getting the hang of it, there are still a handful of upgrades that are just stat ups and a couple of times I did feel like I had lost because I hadn't unlocked enough stuff yet, though personally this didn't bother me as I still had a great time and unlocking new upgrades and features was always exciting.There is a story, though it is not the focus of the game, it more so serves to enhance the settingThere are four playable characters and the three I've played as so far have each had their own distinct playstyles which get more emphasized as you unlock their respective upgrades.It's a very well made game and it saddened me seeing how little reviews it has, so if you're interested in a fast-paced fps rougelike I highly recommend this game, the devs created a wonderful experience that deserves a lot more love in my opinion

_childDocuments_.review: Deadlink is very promising, being a surpisingly polished, tight feeling demo.There isn't much content yet, but what is there has good replayability value, and feels tightly designed. As an elevator pitch, call it Doom Eternal meets Hades game-play wise.You select your weapons at the start of a run, and go from room to room, selecting doors dependent on the rewards they offer. After a set ammount of encounters, you will face a boss and go to the next stage.Rewards are always a question of either helping you current run, or getting resources to make future runs better while unlocking more content.And between runs, you can learn more about the world while unlocking permanent upgrades for future runs.Regaining health is also reminiscent of gaining armor in Doom Eternal: you need to tag the enemy with an abilitiy to make them drop shield shards when you defeat them. Health itself is much more limited, regaining it usually forces you to either pay an upgrades-worth of money at a store, or choose health over another reward. Overall, it's a pretty decent translation of well known rogue-lite elements into a modern take on arena-style FPS.What differs Deadlink is the augment system your upgrades are build arround:Your abilities have power slots in which augments can be inserted; you can select augments as a reward after most rooms.When you use an abilitiy, it also triggers the effect of any augment slotted into it.These provide synergisitc bonus effects and can be swapped onthe fly, letting you try to make your abilities and weapons as synergystic as possible.While each system in the game is not incredibly deep, they all combine into one concise expereience and allows for fun experimentation. Offering 1 of 3 rewards is a good way to keep things random enough to force players to adapt to each run, while still giving the player choice in how to proceed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games I played at first and thought "this is okay but it's really lacking in comparison to other things I played, I might refund this", but after giving it another honest chance I started unlocking a LOT of incredibly important features that made the game actually fun and THEN it became an absolute blast! Kinda wish games like this would at least give you all the core features from the first run because the opening slough almost killed it for me. I'm all for unlocks and skill trees, but it's stuff like "you can't upgrade your implants until 5 runs in" that makes it a drag.Also 3rd character gets a machine gun and a turret. They're my favorite, I love them.

_childDocuments_.review: Deadlink is an FPS rogue-lite set in a cyberpunk universe and I'm  that this game isn't getting the recognition it deserves like other titles of its genre such as Roboquest and Gunfire Reborn.Deadlink has an incredible gameplay loop and fun progression system that makes it stand out amongst its competitors. In fact, I think the gameplay is peak here out of the other games out there. Despite some problems I have, I still highly recommend that you give it a try, especially for those who want that DOOM fix but don’t want to play DOOM. It’s incredible at what it does, has a great soundtrack to back it up and the dynamic is fun enough to where you’ll feel right at home. The difficulty settings give ease of accessibility and the game looks and runs great!

_childDocuments_.review:
Deadlink is a cyberpunk FPS with roguelite elements. You're the first operative to be recruited to the experimental Deadlink project. Pilot an autonomous combat shell, fighting your way through cramped slums, twisted labs, grimy warehouses, and sleek office buildings on a mission to thwart the schemes of the most powerful corporations in the world.

Wield a deadly arsenal, upgrade your skills and tech, devastate destructible environments, and slash corporate profit margins - all at the same time.
